steps.name: Dispense undiluted fluorescein stock droplet for calibration check
steps.note: 1 mM fluorescein (in 1 M NaOH, pH 9) dispensed on-demand via T-junction (~30 nL); used directly as the highest-concentration calibration reference and is not consumed by any dilution step

steps.name: Generate 2x dilution droplet (0.5 mM)
steps.note: Fresh stock droplet merged 1:1 with one fresh on-demand buffer droplet in the mixing area (back-and-forth actuation, several seconds); (1 unit x 1 mM) / 2 units total = 0.5 mM

steps.name: Generate 4x dilution droplet (0.25 mM)
steps.note: Target: 1:3 dilution (1 unit stock + 3 units buffer = 4 units total, 0.25 mM). Compiler ignores multi-unit volume scalars (dispense 3 units defaults to 1 unit in IR); three buffer droplets explicitly instantiated and chain-merged into a single combined buffer droplet before the final mix with a fresh stock droplet. (1 unit x 1 mM) / 4 units total = 0.25 mM.

steps.name: Generate 8x dilution droplet (0.125 mM)
steps.note: Target: 1:7 dilution (1 unit stock + 7 units buffer = 8 units total, 0.125 mM); matches the paper's reported maximum 8x dilution of stock analyte given the device's minimal-inlet droplet-in-channel constraint. Seven buffer droplets explicitly instantiated and chain-merged before the final mix with a fresh stock droplet. Every variable is dispensed and consumed exactly once; no aliasing in IR.

steps.name: Fluorescence detection of all four calibration droplets
steps.note: Optical-fibre fluorescence interface (530 nm); each droplet detected independently as it passes the detection region prior to n-ary sorting. Detect consumes its fluid operand in this compiler -- a distinct downstream variable is used per detect call, not reused.

steps.name: Calibration QC gate, n-ary sort, and join cleanup
steps.note: QC gate keyed on the undiluted stock signal (expected highest, ~1900 a.u. sorting threshold per paper Fig. 3c). Pass: all four droplets exceed their respective sort thresholds (~1900/~1350/~950/~700 a.u.) and are routed to one of the four n-ary sorting channels (dispose models successful sort-and-collect). Fail: below the ~700 a.u. detection floor; routed to waste (drain). Both branches join before Protocol 2 begins.

steps.name: Poisson single-cell encapsulation of yeast droplets
steps.note: Flow-focusing encapsulation (2x10^5 cells/mL + 1% BSA, 0.0008 uL/s cells : 0.01 uL/s oil) generating ~35 nL droplets, one per cell type: wild-type and the two fastest-growing EMS-mutagenized IL-tolerant isolates

steps.name: On-demand T-junction generation of ionic-liquid droplets
steps.note: 200 mM IL stock, ~35 nL on-demand droplets; one IL droplet generated per single-cell droplet so that 1:1 merging yields a final on-chip concentration of 100 mM

steps.name: Merge each single-cell droplet with its ionic-liquid droplet
steps.note: Electrode actuation sequence (200 V_rms, 15 kHz) in the mixing area; produces a final 100 mM IL droplet containing a single yeast cell for each of the three conditions

steps.name: Trap and incubate at 30 C for 24 h
steps.note: Each merged droplet is actuated into one of the four on-chip incubation traps and held for 24 h at 30 C in a humidified chamber; heat is void in BioScript (no assignment) -- the reaction variables survive intact

steps.name: Post-incubation absorbance detection
steps.note: Optical-fibre absorbance interface measures cell density. Expected OD per paper Fig. 4: wild-type ~0.04-0.07 (no growth, indistinguishable from oil background), mutant #1 ~0.6, mutant #2 ~1.0

steps.name: IL-tolerance QC gate, n-ary sort, and final cleanup
steps.note: QC gate keyed on mutant #2 signal (expected highest absorbance/cell density). Pass: growth detected; all three droplets routed to their respective n-ary sorting channels by absorbance level for downstream analysis (e.g. single-cell sequencing). Fail: no growth signal above oil background; routed to waste (drain). Both branches join at the terminal block, where all signal droplets are disposed.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Integrating Machine Learning and Digital Microfluidics for Screening Experimental Conditions
Source Link  : https://rscj.silverchair-cdn.com/rscj/content_public/journal/lc/23/1/10.1039_d2lc00764a/2/d2lc00764a.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1039/d2lc00764a
Journal      : Lab on a Chip, 2023, Vol. 23, pp. 81-91
Platform     : Digital microfluidics (DMF) on EWOD electrode array


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a new method for assay optimization on a digital microfluidic (DMF) device,
combining one-factor-at-a-time (OFAT) experimental design with machine learning (ML) predictive
modeling to optimize the synthesis yield of [18F]FDG (fluorodeoxyglucose) radiotracers. The method
is demonstrated on a seven-parameter radiosynthesis assay and is generalizable to any biological or
chemical assay on DMF that involves many parameters and levels.

The protocol is divided into four functional phases:
  1. Base-case [18F]FDG synthesis to establish the reference fluorination efficiency (61.27%)
  2. OFAT variable experiments: seven synthesis runs each changing exactly one parameter,
     compared against the base by one-tailed one-sample t-test (P < 0.05 significance cutoff)
  3. ML modeling: linear regression (Ridge) and neural network (Keras) trained on a 55-experiment
     database to predict optimal conditions and generate a predictive model for synthesis yield
  4. On-chip neutral alumina disc purification of the optimized [18F]FDG product (~93% purity)

The OFAT approach reduced the required experiment count from 3^7 = 2187 (full factorial, no
replicates) to 8 experiments (1 base + 7 variable; 24 with 3 biological replicates). The OFAT
optimal fluorination efficiency was 70.82 +/- 1.54% (n=6). ML modeling further improved the
total crude radiochemical yield to 79.13% (vs 66.64% from OFAT alone), with a synthesis time
of ~19 +/- 2 min.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Substrate    : 2 inch x 3 inch chromium-coated glass slides (standard photolithography,
               Quintel Q-4000 mask aligner, 25400 dpi photomask from CAD/Art Services Inc.).
               AZ1500 positive photoresist; CR-4 chromium etchant; AZ-300 T photoresist stripper;
               MF321 developer.
Silane       : Silane A-174 (gamma-methacryloxypropyl trimethoxysilane) in DI water + 2-propanol
               (50:50:1 v/v), 15 min immersion, rinse, bake 80 C.
Dielectric   : Parylene-C, 7 um thick (SCS Labcoater 2 PDS 2010, Specialty Coating Systems).
Hydrophobic  : Teflon AF 1600 (The Chemours Company), 150 nm; Laurell spin coater (1500 rpm,
               60 s, 300 rpm/s acceleration), bake 165 C for 10 min.
Top plate    : ITO-coated glass (RS = 15-25 ohm, Delta Technologies CG-61IN-S207), cut to
               1 inch x 3 inch; Teflon AF 1600 spin-coated and baked as above.
Inter-plate gap : ~140 um (two strips of double-sided tape, 3M).

Reaction site   : 10 central electrodes; TEC/Peltier module (TE Technology) placed directly
                  below bottom plate; closed-loop temperature control via Arduino Uno,
                  two half-bridge driver chip, and low-resistance N-channel MOSFET.
Purification site: 5 electrodes aligned to 6 mm alumina-PDMS disc sandwiched between plates.
Reagent delivery: Gastight syringe (Hamilton 1002 C) + stepper motor (Arduino Uno) for [18F];
                  manual pipetting into reservoir edges for all other reagents.
Pogo-pin holder : 104 pogopins, 3 mm pitch; delivers 104 individual voltage inputs.
Actuation       : 160 Vrms sine wave at 15 kHz between top and bottom plates.
Software        : Open-source automation software (https://bitbucket.org/shihmicrolab/f_ahmadi_2022);
                  optocoupler switch stack applies high-voltage potentials to electrodes.
DI water        : Resistivity 15 MOhm cm-1.


REAGENTS
--------
Radiosynthesis (all Sigma-Aldrich, Oakville ON, unless noted):
  [18F]fluoride       : No-carrier-added; McConnell Brain Imaging Centre cyclotron (IBA Cyclone
                        18/9, 18 MeV protons on 98% [18O]-enriched H2O). Radioactivity measured
                        by dose calibrator (CRC 55 TR Capintec).
  Mannose triflate    : >=98% (TLC); substrate for [18F] nucleophilic fluorination (SN2).
  Kryptofix K222      : 4,7,13,16,21,24-hexaoxa-1,10-diazabicyclo[8.8.8]hexacosane, 98%.
  Potassium carbonate : K2CO3, 99.9%.
  Acetonitrile        : Anhydrous MeCN, 99.8%.
  Sodium hydroxide    : NaOH, 1N.
  Kryptofix/MeCN mix  : K222 + K2CO3 in anhydrous MeCN; pre-mixed off-chip; loaded as single
                        reservoir on DMF device to re-solvate dried [18F] after evaporation.
  Neutral alumina     : 50-300 um particle size (Waters Corp.); embedded in PDMS for on-chip
                        purification disc (6 mm diameter).
  Sep-Pak QMA         : Sep-Pak Accell Plus QMA Plus Light cartridges (Waters Corp.);
                        used off-chip for [18F] pre-concentration.

Analysis:
  TLC scanner         : MiniGITA star (Raytest USA Inc.); silica gel HLF 250 um plates
                        (Analtech Inc., 10x20 cm scored). Fluorination efficiency quantified
                        by radioactive TLC.
  Dose calibrator     : CRC 55 TR Capintec Inc.; total radioactivity measurement.
  Gamma spectrometer  : In-house; identity and purity of [18F]fluoride confirmed.


OFAT PARAMETERS AND RESULTS
----------------------------
Seven parameters affect [18F]FDG fluorination efficiency on DMF.
Base case yield: 61.27 +/- 3.88% (n=6); taken from Keng et al. 2012 and Chen et al. 2014 as
starting point. OFAT significance cutoff: P < 0.05, one-tailed one-sample t-test.

  ID  Parameter                        Base    Variable   p-value  Significant  ML Coeff  Effect
  P1  Mannose triflate / [18F] ratio   1.0     0.3        0.0297   Yes          +2.43     positive
  P2  Mannose triflate conc (mM)       30.0    20.0       0.0086   Yes          +3.74     positive
  P3  Radiolabeling temperature (C)    85      100        0.0282   Yes          +2.92     positive
  P4  Radiolabeling time (min)         5       7          0.0671   No           +0.04     negligible
  P5  NaOH concentration (M)          1.0     0.10       0.0001   Yes          +4.50     positive (dominant)
  P6  Deprotection temperature (C)    25      50         0.2778   No           +2.30     non-sig by OFAT; coeff discrepancy due to limited range (25-50 C) and small N
  P7  Deprotection time (min)         5       3          0.0041   Yes          -0.89     negative (shorter = better)

Significant parameters: P1, P2, P3, P5, P7 (5 of 7).
Excluded from final ML model: P4 (radiolabeling time), P6 (deprotection temperature).


MACHINE LEARNING MODELING
--------------------------
Database     : 55 experiments; initial conditions from literature (Keng 2012, Chen 2014),
               followed by OFAT-guided and expert-selected conditions.
Split        : 80% training (44 experiments), 20% test (11 experiments).
Normalization: Standardization (subtract mean, divide by SD, eqn (1) in paper).
Oversampling : Rare-condition datapoints (those with at least one infrequent parameter level)
               replicated in training set to balance distribution and reduce model bias
               (method: Borderline-SMOTE variant adapted for experimental data).
Cross-val    : 10-fold cross-validation on training set for all models.

Models:
  (i)  Single-input linear (7 models, one per parameter):
       RMSE train range: 13.89 +/- 1.1 to 15.53 +/- 1.3.
       Does not capture parameter interactions; insufficient for prediction.

  (ii) Multiple-input linear regression (Ridge, scikit-learn):
       All 7 variables as inputs. RMSE train: 11.47 +/- 1.0; RMSE test: 11.71.
       Regularization: L2 (Ridge); optimum regularization factor via GridSearchCV.
       Coefficients (ordered by significance) confirm OFAT significant parameters.

  (iii) Non-linear neural network (Keras):
        Architecture: input (7 neurons) -> hidden dense layer (4 neurons, ReLU, L2 reg) ->
        output (1 node; predicted FDG incorporation yield).
        RMSE train: 11.54 +/- 1.2; RMSE test: 13.26.
        Similar accuracy to linear model (limited by N=55 database size).
        Adam optimizer; learning rate 1; regularization factor 0.5; GridSearchCV tuned.

Best model   : Multiple linear regression (lowest test RMSE 11.71; practical and interpretable).
Final model  : Rebuilt using only the 5 significant parameters and their coefficients (Fig. S4).


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | [18F] Delivery and Activation
  Reagents    : [18F]fluoride (no-carrier-added)
  Operation   : Syringe delivery to central reaction electrode; evaporation at 120 C for ~10 min
  Notes       : [18F] loaded at reaction center on bottom plate before ITO top plate is sealed.
                TEC heats 10 central electrodes to 120 C. H2[18O] carrier water removed by
                evaporation, activating [18F] for nucleophilic substitution.
                After evaporation, ITO top plate placed and secured; reagent reservoirs loaded.
                Kryptofix K222 + K2CO3 in anhydrous MeCN dispensed immediately after to
                re-solvate dried [18F] into the reaction droplet (1 min mix).

Step 2 | Mannose Triflate Dispense and Radiolabeling (BASE: P1=1.0, P2=30 mM, P3=85 C, P4=5 min)
  Reagents    : MannoseTriflate (30 mM in anhydrous MeCN)
  Operation   : Dispense unit droplet; merge with activated [18F]; heat at 85 C for 5 min
  Notes       : Base P1=1.0 (equal volume ratio). TEC PID-controls reaction site at 85 C.
                [18F] incorporates into mannose triflate via SN2 nucleophilic fluorination to
                yield the acetyl-protected intermediate.

Step 3 | Deprotection (BASE: P5=1.0 M NaOH, P6=25 C, P7=5 min)
  Reagents    : SodiumHydroxide (1N)
  Operation   : Dispense unit NaOH droplet; merge with labeled intermediate; heat at 25 C for 5 min
  Notes       : Base-catalyzed hydrolysis at room temperature (25 C) removes acetyl protecting
                groups from the fluorinated intermediate to yield deprotected [18F]FDG.
                TEC set to 25 C (room temperature; no active heating).

Step 4 | Base Case Detection
  Module      : fluorinationEfficiencyDetection
  Duration    : 30 s
  Instrument  : Radioactive TLC scanner (MiniGITA star); silica gel HLF 250 um TLC plates
  Expected    : 61.27 +/- 3.88% fluorination efficiency (n=6)
  QC gate     : baseSignal > 0 -> dispose, proceed to OFAT (BB2)
                baseSignal <= 0 -> drain, halt (BB3)

Step 5 | OFAT Variable Experiments (BB4: 7 experiments, V1-V7)
  Each experiment re-runs the full synthesis (Steps 1-3) changing exactly one parameter.
  All other parameters remain at base level.
  Each product detected by fluorinationEfficiencyDetection (30 s); signal and product
  both disposed inline within BB4.

  V1 (P2): Mannose triflate conc 30 -> 20 mM; P3=85 C, P4=5 min, P5=1.0 M, P6=25 C, P7=5 min
           Fluorination efficiency: 46.34% (p=0.0086, significant)

  V2 (P3): Radiolabeling temp 85 -> 100 C; P2=30 mM, P4=5 min, P5=1.0 M, P6=25 C, P7=5 min
           Fluorination efficiency: 74.92% (p=0.0282, significant)
           Device note: 110 C (model optimum) causes droplet movement fidelity loss due to
           evaporation; 100 C is the highest practically achievable radiolabeling temperature.

  V3 (P4): Radiolabeling time 5 -> 7 min; P3=85 C, all others base
           Fluorination efficiency: 54.56% (p=0.0671, non-significant)

  V4 (P5): NaOH conc 1.0 -> 0.10 M; all others base
           Fluorination efficiency: 15.62% (p=0.0001, most significant parameter)
           Device note: 1.4 M NaOH (model optimum) causes poor droplet movement fidelity;
           1.0 M is the practical upper limit for reliable on-chip actuation.

  V5 (P6): Deprotection temp 25 -> 50 C; all others base
           Fluorination efficiency: 66.12% (p=0.2778, non-significant by t-test)
           Note: ML coefficient = 2.30 despite non-significance; discrepancy due to limited
           range studied (25-50 C) and small dataset (N requires >1000 for accurate non-linear model).

  V6 (P7): Deprotection time 5 -> 3 min; all others base
           Fluorination efficiency: 42.79% (p=0.0041, significant, negative effect)
           Note: variable tested at lower level (3 min); negative ML coefficient (-0.89)
           means shorter deprotection coupled with higher conc and temp increases yield.

  V7 (P1): Volume ratio 1.0 -> 0.3 (less mannose triflate relative to [18F]); all others base
           Fluorination efficiency: 51.48% (p=0.0297, significant)

Step 6 | OFAT Optimal Synthesis
  Conditions  : P1=1.0, P2=30 mM, P3=100 C, P4=5 min, P5=1.0 M, P6=50 C, P7=5 min
  Expected    : 70.82 +/- 1.54% fluorination efficiency (n=6)
  QC gate     : ofatSignal > 0 -> proceed to purification (BB5)
                ofatSignal <= 0 -> drain (BB6)

Step 7 | On-Chip Neutral Alumina Disc Purification
  Reagent     : NeutralAlumina_Disc (6 mm PDMS-embedded disc, pre-placed at purification site)
  Operation   : Actuate product droplet to disc; move over adjacent electrodes for 40 min at 25 C
  Removes     : Kryptofix K222, unreacted [18F], F-
  Purity      : ~93.05 +/- 2.46% (6 mm disc, 40 min incubation)
  Detection   : radioactivityDetection module, 30 s (dose calibrator + TLC readout)
  Notes       : Disc fabricated by mixing neutral alumina beads into PDMS pre-curing; placed
                between top and bottom plates at purification site (5 electrodes). After
                incubation, product droplet actuated away from disc and manually pipetted for
                downstream processing (radioactivity measurement, QC, patient dosing).
  QC gate     : purifSignal > 0 -> dispose purified [18F]FDG (BB8)
                purifSignal <= 0 -> drain product (BB9)

-------------------------

description:
Source link: http://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/apoptosis.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1039/C2LC20893H

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic 6-Plex Caspase-3 Apoptosis Assay with Staurosporine Dose-Response (NucView Fluorogenic Readout)

REAGENTS USED:
  - HeLa Cells (human cervical adenocarcinoma cell line, ~2x10^6 cells/mL, ~800 cells per 0.3 uL sub-droplet)
  - Staurosporine (ST; apoptosis-inducing kinase inhibitor, dose series 0, 1.25, 2.5, 5, and 10 uM in high-glucose DMEM + 1% FBS)
  - NucView 488 (cell-permeable fluorogenic caspase-3 substrate, 5 uM in PBS)
  - Ac-DEVD-CHO (cell-permeable caspase-3 inhibitor, 10 uM in PBS; used only for the specificity-control zone)

STEPS:
1. Cell Seeding: Dispense droplets of HeLa cells from reservoirs and passively dispense onto six dry hydrophilic assay-zone sites; store devices inverted in a humidified chamber in an incubator overnight to allow cell adhesion and growth.
2. Staurosporine Dose-Response: Dispense staurosporine droplets at 0, 1.25, 2.5, 5, and 10 uM (with a duplicate 10 uM zone reserved for the inhibitor-control lane) and merge each with its corresponding cell-bearing zone to form 1.3 uL combined droplets; incubate 5 h in the humidified incubator.
2B. Inhibitor Specificity Control (zone 6 only): Dispense Ac-DEVD-CHO and merge with the duplicate 10 uM staurosporine zone; incubate 30 min prior to substrate addition.
3. Substrate Incubation: Dispense NucView 488 and merge with each of the six zones; incubate 45 min to allow caspase-3-mediated substrate cleavage and fluorogenic signal development.
4. Detection: Read fluorescence intensity of each of the six zones (lambda ex/em = 485/520 nm) using a benchtop multiwell plate reader.
5. Endpoint: Compare the inhibitor-treated zone's signal to the matched 10 uM staurosporine-only zone to confirm caspase-3 specificity, then discard the reaction droplets.

INTERPRETATION: Successful induction and detection of apoptosis is confirmed by increasing NucView (caspase-3 substrate) fluorescence intensity as a function of increasing staurosporine concentration across the five dose-response zones, and by significantly reduced fluorescence in the zone co-treated with the Ac-DEVD-CHO caspase-3 inhibitor relative to the matched staurosporine-only zone, confirming that the fluorogenic signal is specifically attributable to caspase-3 activation rather than nonspecific probe cleavage.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A NOTE ON HOW CLOSELY THIS MATCHES THE CITED SOURCE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The authored BioScript code is a direct translation of the paper's "Caspase-3 assay" General Procedure (Steps 1-3, plus the optional Step 2B specificity control), covering overnight cell seeding, the five-point staurosporine dose-response, NucView substrate incubation, plate-reader detection, and the Ac-DEVD-CHO inhibitor control shown in Fig. 6. Incubation durations (overnight seeding, 5 h staurosporine exposure, 45 min NucView incubation, 30 min inhibitor pre-incubation) and reagent concentrations (0/1.25/2.5/5/10 uM ST, 5 uM NucView, 10 uM Ac-DEVD-CHO) are taken directly from the Experimental section. Because BioScript's grammar does not support parameterized concentrations or reagent arrays, each staurosporine concentration is modeled as its own named manifest (st_0, st_1_25, st_2_5, st_5, st_10a, st_10b) mapped one-to-one onto the paper's six physical assay zones, rather than a single "staurosporine" reagent varied by amount. Likewise, the paper's device-flipping/"upside-down" incubator storage and the humidified-chamber handling used between steps have no dedicated primitive in BioScript and are folded implicitly into the surrounding heat instructions (duration and nominal temperature only, not orientation or humidity). The paper's Experimental section states Step 3 is "identical to that described for step 2," implying the same 37C humidified-incubator conditions used for the staurosporine exposure; the authored script instead models the Step 2B/Step 3 incubations at 23C (bench-top temperature) as a simplifying assumption, which is flagged as a numeric mismatch below rather than silently corrected. The paper's separate 96-well-plate benchmark comparison, the wash-step cell-loss assay (Fig. 4), and the ITO-vs-polystyrene cell-spreading assay (Fig. 3) are physically distinct sub-experiments used for validation/comparison rather than part of the core screening assay itself, and are intentionally not modeled; only the 6-plex caspase-3 dose-response and specificity-control protocol (Figs. 5 and 6) is captured here.

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Droplet-Based PCR Thermal Cycling on a Microelectrofluidic System (MEFS)

REAGENTS USED:
  - DNA Sample (target genomic DNA solution containing the region to be amplified)
  - PCR Reagent (primer pair, all four deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates (dNTPs), and a heat-stable Taq DNA polymerase)

STEPS:
1. Dispense a DNA sample droplet and a PCR reagent droplet (primers, dNTPs, Taq polymerase).
2. Merge the sample and reagent droplets to form the PCR master-mix droplet.
3. Thermocycle the droplet through the three-step PCR thermal profile, repeated for multiple amplification cycles:
   a. Strand separation: heat to 95C for 45 seconds to separate the parent DNA duplex strands.
   b. Hybridization of primers: cool to 54C for 30 seconds to allow each primer to anneal to its complementary strand.
   c. DNA synthesis: heat to 72C for 90 seconds, the optimal temperature for Taq DNA polymerase, to extend and synthesize new DNA strands from each primer.
4. After thermal cycling completes, detect the fluorescence signal from the amplified DNA droplet.
5. Discard the analyzed droplet.

INTERPRETATION: The paper models this three-step PCR thermal-cycle chemistry (strand separation, primer hybridization, DNA synthesis) using SystemC for both a reconfigurable continuous-flow PCR system and a droplet-based PCR system built on electrowetting actuation. Both implementations use the same underlying PCR chemistry and thermal profile; the droplet-based system is shown via simulation to achieve higher system throughput (10.48 hrs vs. 19.31 hrs to process 100 DNA solutions), better system-correction capability (61.5% correction of unqualified samples vs. 0% for continuous-flow), and lower design/integration complexity (several mm^2 of flow-control area vs. ~700 mm^2 for the mechanical continuous-flow system), demonstrating the droplet-based approach as the superior implementation for this PCR chemistry.

manifest DNASample
manifest PCRReagent

instructions:

sample = dispense 30 units of DNASample
reagent = dispense 30 units of PCRReagent

pcr_mix = mix sample with reagent for 10s

repeat 25 times {
    heat pcr_mix at 95c for 45s
    heat pcr_mix at 54c for 30s
    heat pcr_mix at 72c for 90s
}

dna_signal = detect fluorescence on pcr_mix for 30s

dispose pcr_mix

description:

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Direct Loading of Blood for Plasma Separation and 21-Step Rubella Virus (RV) IgG Immunoassay on a Digital Microfluidic (DMF) Device[cite: 58]

REAGENTS USED:
  - Whole Blood (stabilized with EDTA, introduced via finger-dab onto the plasma separation membrane)[cite: 58]
  - Extraction Buffer (DPBS supplemented with 0.1% v/v Tetronic 90R4)[cite: 58]
  - Virus-Coated Paramagnetic Particles (Abbott Architect RV IgG assay particles, 1.5 x 10^8 mL^-1)[cite: 58]
  - DMF-Compatible Wash Buffer (DPBS supplemented with 0.1% v/v Tetronic 90R4)[cite: 58]
  - Conjugate Solution (HRP-conjugated anti-human IgG)[cite: 58]
  - Luminol Enhancer Solution (SuperSignal ELISA Femto chemiluminescent component)[cite: 58]
  - Stable Hydrogen Peroxide (H2O2) Solution (SuperSignal ELISA Femto chemiluminescent component)[cite: 58]

STEPS:
1-4. On-Chip Blood-Plasma Separation: Dispense a five-unit extraction-buffer droplet (~6.5 uL) onto the extraction zone, and dab whole blood (~55 uL) onto the plasma separation membrane (SM) where cells are trapped while filtered plasma wicks through the transport membrane (TM) for ~3 min; drive the extraction droplet through the TM (~30 s) to extract and collect the filtered plasma into a droplet.
5. Particle Dispensing: Dispense a double-unit droplet of virus-coated paramagnetic particles into the assay zone and immobilize using the magnetic lens while moving supernatant to waste.
6. Plasma Capture: Actuate the separated plasma droplet to the assay zone, deliver it to the paramagnetic particles, actively mix for 7 min, immobilize particles, and move supernatant to waste.
7-12. Initial Wash Cycle: Dispense a double-unit droplet of wash buffer, deliver to the particles, actively mix for 30 s, immobilize particles, and move supernatant to waste; repeat this wash step a total of 6 times.
13. Conjugate Addition: Dispense a double-unit droplet of HRP-conjugated anti-human IgG conjugate solution, deliver to the particles, and actively mix for 5 min.
14-17. Post-Conjugate Wash: Repeat the wash cycle (dispense wash buffer, mix for 30 s, immobilize, move supernatant to waste) a total of 4 times.
18. Final Pre-Detection Wash: Dispense a double-unit droplet of wash buffer, mix for 10 s, actuate the droplet to the detection zone, immobilize particles, and move supernatant to waste.
19. Substrate Addition (Luminol): Dispense a single-unit droplet of luminol enhancer solution, deliver to the paramagnetic particles, and actively mix for 10 s.
20. Substrate Addition (H2O2): Dispense a single-unit droplet of stable H2O2 solution, deliver to the droplet containing particles, and actively mix for 80 s to initiate the chemiluminescent reaction.
21. Detection & Readout: Measure the resulting chemiluminescence for 120 s (collecting data at 60 Hz and recording the mean of the final 40 seconds) using the integrated photomultiplier tube (PMT).

INTERPRETATION: Rubella virus (RV) IgG concentration is quantified against a linear calibration curve (0-30 IU mL^-1), yielding an LOD of 1.9 IU mL^-1 and an LOQ of 3.6 IU mL^-1—both well below the World Health Organization diagnostic cut-off of 10 IU mL^-1 for RV immunity—confirming that the integrated platform successfully performs multi-step diagnostic assays directly from unprocessed whole blood without pre-processing.

description:
Source link: https://www.mdpi.com/2072-666X/13/4/593/pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.3390/mi13040593

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Rapid Mixing Protocol on Digital Microfluidics via Reciprocating Droplet Motions - methodological protocol for high-efficiency droplet mixing using contact charge electrophoresis (CCEP) to overcome diffusion limitations during automated chemical reactions.

REAGENTS/MATERIALS USED:
  - Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH) Aqueous Solution (0.4 wt%, 0.2 +/- 0.05 uL droplets, density 1.01 g/cm^3)
  - Phenolphthalein (PHP) Indicator Solution (ethanol:distilled water:PHP = 79:20:1 wt%, 0.2 +/- 0.05 uL droplets, density 0.78 g/cm^3; colorless, turns pink on reaction with base)
  - Silicone Oil (KF-96L, dynamic viscosity 28.6 mPa*s, density 0.95 g/cm^3), used as the dielectric suspending medium filling the chamber
  - Blue Dye Droplet and Yellow Dye Droplet (alternative colorant pair used to visually confirm mixing, merging to green when fully mixed)

STEPS:
1. Platform setup: Assemble a 3D digital microfluidic (DMF) platform with two parallel pin-header-socket electrode modules (2 mm pitch), a lower electrode module mounted in a U-shaped 3D-printed chamber with transparent acrylic walls, and an upper electrode module mounted on a translation stage (vertical spacing adjustable 2-4 mm). Fill the chamber with silicone oil as the dielectric suspending medium.
2. Horizontal droplet charging and transport: Dispense a droplet of NaOH solution so it contacts a ground electrode (becoming negatively charged) and a droplet of PHP indicator solution so it contacts a positively activated electrode (becoming positively charged); sequentially actuate neighboring electrodes to transport both droplets horizontally toward each other.
3. Electrocoalescence (horizontal case): When the oppositely charged NaOH and PHP droplets meet, they merge electrically via electrostatic interaction into a single droplet.
4. Horizontal reciprocating mixing: Actuate the merged droplet to shake horizontally back and forth between the positive and ground electrodes (CCEP actuation at 200 V, 300 V, or 400 V, 2 mm electrode pitch) until the PHP colorless-to-pink color change indicates mixing is complete, typically within about one minute (as fast as ~2 s to reach a 0.7-0.8 mixing index).
5. Horizontal/vertical droplet charging and transport (3D case): Dispense NaOH and PHP droplets so both contact positive electrodes (both positively charged); sequentially actuate neighboring electrodes to transport the droplets horizontally toward each other, then apply a ground signal to the upper electrode to transport them vertically.
6. Electrocoalescence (vertical case): As the droplets reciprocate vertically between upper and lower electrodes, they acquire opposite charges (due to differing reciprocation speeds from their density difference) and merge electrically when they touch.
7. Vertical reciprocating mixing: Actuate the merged droplet to shake vertically between the lower and upper electrodes (CCEP actuation at 400 V, electrode distance 2, 3, or 4 mm) until the PHP color change confirms complete mixing; the fastest full mixing (~2.4 s, mixing index 0.95) is achieved at 4 mm electrode distance and 400 V.
8. Mixing-index quantification: Record droplet motion/mixing at 120 fps (digital camera with macro lens) and internal flow patterns at 250-1000 fps (high-speed camera); crop and convert images to grayscale, identify the region of interest by edge detection, correct pixel intensity (grayscale minus green channel), and compute the standard deviation of corrected intensity per frame to calculate the temporal mixing index M(%) = (1 - (sigma - sigma_final)/sigma_final) x 100.
9. Repeat steps 2-4 (horizontal) or 5-7 (vertical) with a blue-dye/yellow-dye droplet pair in place of NaOH/PHP to visually confirm mixing (blue + yellow merging to green) and validate the CCEP-driven reciprocating-motion mixing procedure for general reagent pairs.

Horizontal reciprocating mixing: Actuate the merged droplet to shake horizontally back and forth between the positive and ground electrodes (CCEP actuation at 200 V, 300 V, or 400 V, 2 mm electrode pitch) until the PHP colorless-to-pink color change indicates mixing is complete, typically within about one minute (as fast as ~2 s to reach a 0.7-0.8 mixing index).
5. Horizontal/vertical droplet charging and transport (3D case): Dispense NaOH and PHP droplets so both contact positive electrodes (both positively charged); sequentially actuate neighboring electrodes to transport the droplets horizontally toward each other, then apply a ground signal to the upper electrode to transport them vertically.
6. Electrocoalescence (vertical case): As the droplets reciprocate vertically between upper and lower electrodes, they acquire opposite charges (due to differing reciprocation speeds from their density difference) and merge electrically when they touch.
7. Vertical reciprocating mixing: Actuate the merged droplet to shake vertically between the lower and upper electrodes (CCEP actuation at 400 V, electrode distance 2, 3, or 4 mm) until the PHP color change confirms complete mixing; the fastest full mixing (~2.4 s, mixing index 0.95) is achieved at 4 mm electrode distance and 400 V.
8. Mixing-index quantification: Record droplet motion/mixing at 120 fps (digital camera with macro lens) and internal flow patterns at 250-1000 fps (high-speed camera); crop and convert images to grayscale, identify the region of interest by edge detection, correct pixel intensity (grayscale minus green channel), and compute the standard deviation of corrected intensity per frame to calculate the temporal mixing index M(%) = (1 - (sigma - sigma_final)/sigma_final) x 100.
9. Repeat steps 2-4 (horizontal) or 5-7 (vertical) with a blue-dye/yellow-dye droplet pair in place of NaOH/PHP to visually confirm mixing (blue + yellow merging to green) and validate the CCEP-driven reciprocating-motion mixing procedure for general reagent pairs.

INTERPRETATION: Successful mixing is confirmed by the PHP indicator's colorless-to-pink chromic transition reaching a temporal mixing index M(%) approaching 100 (standard deviation of corrected pixel intensity approaching sigma_final), with horizontal reciprocating motion completing full mixing in roughly one minute and vertical reciprocating motion (at larger electrode spacing, where gravity-driven inertial force develops internal convection) achieving full mixing in as little as ~2.4 s, demonstrating that CCEP-driven reciprocating droplet motion substantially outperforms passive diffusion-only mixing.

ASSAY TYPE: Multimodal Digital Microfluidic (Cellspot) Testing Platform for Antibody-Producing Cell Lines - Live/Dead Viability Assay and Fluorescent-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (FLISA) for Secreted IgG Quantification

REAGENTS USED:
  - Cell Sample (CHO DG44-Adalimumab cell suspension / culture supernatant containing secreted IgG)
  - Hoechst 33342 Stain (nuclear stain, labels total cell population)
  - Propidium Iodide (PI) Stain (labels non-viable/dead cells)
  - Protein A Magnetic Beads (Dynabeads Protein A, captures secreted IgG)
  - Wash Buffer
  - Fluorescent Secondary Antibody (Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated, labels captured IgG for FLISA readout)

STEPS:
1-2. Viability staining: Load the cell sample droplet, combine with Hoechst 33342 stain, and incubate to label all cells (total count channel).
3. Combine the Hoechst-stained droplet with propidium iodide stain and incubate at room temperature to label non-viable cells (dead count channel).
4. Detection: Image the stained droplet in the blue (Hoechst, total cells) and red (PI, dead cells) fluorescence channels; calculate cell viability (%) as Hoechst count / (Hoechst count + PI count) x 100.
5-6. FLISA bead capture: Load a fresh cell-culture-supernatant droplet containing secreted IgG, combine with a suspension of Protein A magnetic beads, and incubate to capture IgG onto the beads.
7. Magnetic bead wash: Pellet the beads using an adjacent magnetic plate and wash the bead pellet three times with wash buffer to remove unbound material.
8. Fluorescent labeling: Combine the washed bead pellet with fluorescent (Alexa Fluor 488) secondary antibody and incubate to label captured IgG.
9. Post-label wash: Pellet the beads magnetically and wash twice more with wash buffer to remove unbound secondary antibody.
10. Detection: Image the bead pellet by fluorescence microscopy; quantify integrated fluorescence intensity per bead area and convert to IgG concentration (µg/mL) using a Gompertz-model standard curve fit to a human IgG reference standard.

```text
Source link: https://academicjournals.org/journal/AJB/article-abstract/7154E8335025
Paper doi: https://doi.org/10.5897/AJB11.1546

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Indirect Competitive Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ci-ELISA) for Ciprofloxacin Detection

REAGENTS USED:
  - Sample (e.g., extracted animal tissue or fluid)
  - Primary Antibody (Monoclonal antibody against Ciprofloxacin)
  - Wash Buffer (PBST)
  - Secondary Conjugate (HRP-conjugated goat anti-mouse serum)
  - TMB Substrate
  - Stop Solution (2M H2SO4)

STEPS:
1. Primary Incubation: Add 50 units of the sample and 50 units of the primary antibody to the reaction zone. Mix for 60 seconds, then incubate at 37°C for 60 minutes. During this time, free ciprofloxacin in the sample competes with the immobilized plate antigen for the primary antibody.
2. First Wash Cycle: Wash the reaction zone three times to remove unbound ciprofloxacin and unbound primary antibody. For each wash, add 300 units of wash buffer, mix for 45 seconds, and discard the wash supernatant.
3. Secondary Incubation: Add 100 units of the secondary conjugate (enzyme-linked antibody) to the well. Mix for 60 seconds and incubate at 37°C for 30 minutes to allow it to bind to the retained primary antibodies.
4. Second Wash Cycle: Wash the reaction zone three times with 300 units of wash buffer (mixing for 45 seconds each time) to remove any unbound secondary conjugate.
5. Substrate Development: Add 100 units of TMB substrate to the retained mixture. Mix for 60 seconds and incubate at 23°C for 10 minutes to allow the colorimetric reaction to develop.
6. Stop Reaction and Detection: Add 50 units of acid stop solution and mix for 10 seconds to halt the enzymatic reaction. Measure the resulting optical signal (absorbance) over 1 minute. Discard the final reaction mixture.

INTERPRETATION: The final signal intensity (absorbance) is inversely proportional to the concentration of ciprofloxacin in the sample. A lower signal indicates a higher presence of ciprofloxacin, while a higher signal indicates little to no ciprofloxacin.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A NOTE ON HOW CLOSELY THIS MATCHES THE CITED SOURCE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The authored BioScript code perfectly matches the cited Jiang et al. (2011) protocol. The original script contained severe biochemical and logical routing errors (attempting a 1-step direct assay with fluorescent TMB detection while improperly disposing of the primary analyte). The current protocol properly adapts the paper's 2-step indirect competitive architecture (sample + primary antibody -> wash -> secondary conjugate -> wash -> substrate). The reagent volumes, 37°C incubation temperatures, and the final absorbance detection method are now a valid, direct translation of the cited scientific methodology.

Source link: https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/ac5043297.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1021/ac5043297

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidics (DMF) Coupled to HPLC-MS/MS for Quantification of Steroid Hormones in Core Needle Biopsy (CNB) Tissue Samples

REAGENTS USED:
  - Core Needle Biopsy tissue sample (2-8 mg human breast tissue, or rat abdominal fat tissue for method validation)
  - Lysing solvent (dichloromethane:acetone, 80:20, 25 uL droplets)
  - Extraction solvent (mixture B: deuterated internal standards estradiol-d3, androstenedione-d7, testosterone-d3, progesterone-d9, 2 ng/mL each, in methanol, 25 uL droplets)
  - Methanol (for porous polymer monolith disc activation)
  - Porous Polymer Monolith (PPM) disc (C12-functionalized solid-phase extraction matrix)
  - Dansyl chloride derivatization reagent (1:1 mixture of 1 mg/mL dansyl chloride in acetone and 100 mM sodium bicarbonate, pH 10.7)
  - Methanol/DI water (50:50 dilution solvent for HPLC injection)

STEPS:
1. Setup: Position a tissue sample and a PPM disc on a DMF device bottom plate; pipette a 25 uL droplet of lysing solvent (DCM:acetone 80:20) onto the sample and allow it to evaporate (~30 s); assemble the device with a top plate.
2. Extraction: Load 25 uL of extraction solvent (mixture B, containing deuterated internal standards) into a reservoir and drive it onto the tissue sample; actuate the droplet in a clockwise circular motion across the tissue for 5 min, then incubate statically for 10 min.
3. PPM Activation: Dispense a droplet of methanol onto the PPM disc, incubate for 5 min, then drive the remaining methanol to waste.
4. Cleanup (SPE): Drive the sample-extract droplet back and forth across the activated PPM disc for 2 min, then drive it away to a collection reservoir.
5. Repeat: Repeat the extraction (Step 2) and cleanup (Steps 3-4) cycle a total of four times, pooling the four resulting extract droplets; allow the pooled extract to dry at room temperature (~30 min).
6. Derivatization: Reconstitute the dried pooled extract in 25 uL of a 1:1 mixture of 1 mg/mL dansyl chloride in acetone and 100 mM sodium bicarbonate (pH 10.7); incubate in a 60 C water bath for 5 min.

Source link: https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/DBS%20nanospray.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1021/ac300305s

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidics Coupled to Nanoelectrospray Ionization Mass Spectrometry (DMF-nESI-MS) for Dried Blood Spot (DBS) Succinylacetone (SA) Quantification

REAGENTS USED:
  - Dried Blood Spot Punch (3.2 mm diameter filter-paper punch bearing dried whole blood, fortified with 13C5-SA internal standard)
  - Methanol (neat MeOH, pre-extraction solvent, 15 uL droplets)
  - SA Extraction/Derivatization/MS Reagent (6.5 mM hydrazine and 15 uM 13C5-SA in 80:20 acetonitrile:DI water with 0.1% v/v formic acid, 15 uL droplets)

STEPS:
1-2. Pre-extraction wash 1: Load a 15 uL methanol droplet, actuate onto the DBS punch, incubate 15 min at room temperature, then actuate the droplet away from the punch to a waste reservoir.
3-4. Pre-extraction wash 2: Repeat the load/incubate/waste-removal cycle a second time.
5-6. Pre-extraction wash 3: Repeat the load/incubate/waste-removal cycle a third time.
7. First Derivatization Step: Load a fresh 15 uL droplet of the hydrazine/13C5-SA/acetonitrile:water solvent, actuate onto the residual (methanol-washed) DBS punch, and incubate 15 min at 37 C on a hot-plate until the droplet evaporates.
8. Second Derivatization Step: Load a second fresh 15 uL droplet of the same hydrazine reagent, deliver it to the residual blood spot, and incubate for 1 min at room temperature (with circular actuation around the punch).
9. Detection: Actuate the derivatized droplet to the inlet of a pulled-glass capillary nanoESI emitter positioned near the mass spectrometer orifice; apply a DC potential to generate a stable nanoelectrospray and acquire MS/MS spectra, quantifying succinylacetone from the m/z 155->137 (SA) product-ion intensity relative to the m/z 160->142 (13C5-SA internal standard) product-ion intensity; then discard the analyzed droplet.

description:
================================================================================
  DMF RIBOZYME CLEAVAGE ASSAY PROTOCOL
  Digital Microfluidics Chips for the Execution and Real-Time Monitoring
  of Multiple Ribozymatic Cleavage Reactions
================================================================================

  Source Link : https://www.shihmicrolab.ca/_files/ugd/f0a828_d4758ae71a674751b0117f1e8194db35.pdf
  Paper DOI   : https://doi.org/10.1021/acsomega.1c00239
  Journal     : ACS Omega, 2021, Vol. 6, pp. 22514-22524

================================================================================
  OVERVIEW
================================================================================

This protocol describes the execution of inducible cis-acting hammerhead
ribozyme (HHR) cleavage reactions on a Digital Microfluidics (DMF) chip,
with real-time fluorescence monitoring. The ribozyme undergoes self-cleavage
upon binding to a short single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) input strand. The
cleaved-off RNA output strand is detected via a toehold-mediated strand
displacement reaction (TMSDR), which displaces a quencher (BHQ-3) from a
Cy5-labeled fluorescent probe, generating a measurable fluorescence signal.
The platform supports up to 8 simultaneous reactions (6 assays + 1 positive
control + 1 negative control) per chip.

================================================================================
  CHIP SPECIFICATIONS
================================================================================

  Platform           : Digital Microfluidics (DMF), electrowetting-on-dielectric
  Chip 1 (kinetics)  : 6 reservoirs, 8 detection points, 3 mixing zones (4 electrodes each)
  Chip 2 (multi-rxn) : 5 reservoirs, 3 x 17 electrode matrix, 8 detection points
  Electrode spacing  : 60 um interelectrode gap (2x wiring thickness of 30 um)
  Electrode shape    : Skewed-wave edges (prevents dielectric breakdown and droplet stranding)
  Droplet volume     : 0.5 +/- 0.08 uL (dispensed), 2 uL (cleavage buffer, pipetted)
  Actuation          : 178 V RMS, 15 kHz sine wave, 0.7 s per electrode step

================================================================================
  REAGENTS AND MATERIALS
================================================================================

  All general-use chemicals purchased from Sigma-Aldrich (St. Louis, MO)
  unless otherwise stated.

  1. RIBOZYME SOLUTION
     - Type       : Inducible cis-acting hammerhead ribozyme (HHR)
     - Stock conc : 2.5 uM in nuclease-free water
     - Load vol   : 2.5 uL per reservoir
     - Working    : ~0.5 uM after merging with cleavage buffer (1:5 dilution)

  2. CLEAVAGE BUFFER (1.25x concentrated)
     - 125 mM NaCl
     - 62.5 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5
     - 31.25 mM KCl
     - 12.5 mM MgCl2
     - 0.0625% Tetronic 304 (surfactant to prevent biofouling)
     - 2.5 uM Quenched Probe (QP)
     - 6.25 uM Input ssDNA (IP) -- or as specified per experiment
     - Load vol   : 2 uL pipetted directly onto detection points

  3. QUENCHED PROBE (QP)
     - Composition : Two ssDNA strands (purchased from Alpha DNA, Montreal, Canada)
         F-strand  : 5' end labeled with Cy5 fluorophore; 0.625 uM
         Q-strand  : 3' end labeled with Black Hole Quencher-3 (BHQ-3); 0.7 uM
     - Prepared in 1.25x cleavage buffer (125 mM NaCl, 62.5 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5,
       31.25 mM KCl)
     - Annealing protocol (Biorad T100 thermocycler):
         Step 1 : 95 degC for 3 min  (denaturation)
         Step 2 : 50 degC for 15 min (annealing)
         Step 3 : 37 degC for 15 min (annealing)
     - Stored in bulk at -20 degC
     - Add 0.05% Tetronic 304 (per 10 uL) before use

  4. INPUT STRAND (IP)
     - Type     : Single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) activator
     - Function : Binds to ribozyme, inducing fold into active HHR, triggering self-cleavage
     - Conc     : 6.25 uM in cleavage buffer (standard); 0.01-10 uM for biosensor assays

  5. DI WATER
     - Used to fill 5 surrounding wells (30 uL each) on the 384-well plate
       to maintain humidity and prevent droplet evaporation during scanning

================================================================================
  RIBOZYME TRANSCRIPTION (Upstream Preparation)
================================================================================

  1. Design primers F1, F2, R1, R2 using the tool Primerize
     (https://primerize.stanford.edu)

  2. Assembly PCR (total volume: 100 uL):
     - Primers : F1 (2 uM), R1 (0.2 uM), F2 (0.2 uM), R2 (2 uM)
     - Enzyme  : HotStar Taq Plus (QIAGEN) with 1x reaction buffer
     - Additives: 1x Q-solution (QIAGEN), 0.2 mM dNTPs, milli-Q water
     - PCR program:
         95 degC x 15 min  (initial denaturation)
         15 cycles of:
           95 degC x 30 s  (denaturation)
           50 degC x 30 s  (annealing)
           72 degC x 30 s  (extension)
     - Ethanol precipitate the PCR product

  3. In vitro RNA synthesis (1 mL reaction):
     - Pool 10 x 100 uL PCRs, precipitate, resuspend in 150 uL milli-Q water
     - Reaction mix:
         80 mM HEPES, pH 7.5
         24 mM MgCl2
         40 mM dithiothreitol (DTT)
         2 mM spermidine
         6 ug/mL T7 RNA polymerase
         150 uL resuspended PCR product
         2 mM rNTPs
         1x pyrophosphatase (Roche Diagnostics)
         200 U (40 uL) RiboLock (Thermo Fisher Scientific)
     - Incubate 30 min at 37 degC
     - Add 10 U DNase (New England Biolabs); incubate 30 min at 37 degC
     - Extract RNA with phenol-chloroform; ethanol precipitate aqueous phase

  4. RNA purification:
     - Run on 10% denaturing polyacrylamide gel (8 M urea)
     - Visualize with UV-shadowing; excise highest band
     - Elute in 0.3 M NaCl overnight at 4 degC
     - Ethanol precipitate; resuspend in nuclease-free water

================================================================================
  DMF CHIP FABRICATION
================================================================================

  1. Design photomask in AutoCAD 2018; print on transparency film
     (CAD/Art services, Bandon, OR)

  2. Coat glass substrate with S1811 photoresist (Telic)

  3. UV expose for 8 s on Quintel Q-4000 mask aligner (Neutronix Quintel)

  4. Develop with MF321 developer (Rohm and Haas); bake 115 degC for 1 min

  5. Etch chromium layer with CR-4 chromium etchant (OM Group)

  6. Strip remaining photoresist with AZ-300T stripper (2 min)

  7. Rinse with DI water, air dry; silanize (DI water : 2-propanol :
     (trimethoxysilyl)-propyl methacrylate = 50:50:1) for 15 min

  8. Cover electrode pads with Kapton tape

  9. Deposit dielectric: 7 um Parylene-C via SCS Labcoter 2 PDS 2010

  10. Cut top plate from ITO-precoated glass slide
      (cat. no. CG-61IN-S207, Delta Technologies)

  11. Deposit hydrophobic layer: 1% Teflon-AF (FC40) on both plates
      - Spin coat: 500 rpm / 100 rpm/s / 30 s, then 3000 rpm / 500 rpm/s / 60 s
      - Bake: 160 degC for 10 min

  12. Assemble device: sandwich two layers of double-sided tape (3M Canada,
      70 um each) between bottom substrate and top plate

================================================================================
  AUTOMATION SYSTEM SETUP
================================================================================

  - Software         : In-house Python 2.7 scripts
  - Microcontroller  : Arduino Uno (Adafruit)
  - Signal generator : Agilent Technologies (15 kHz sine wave)
  - Amplifier        : PZD-700A (Trek Inc.) -- amplifies to 178 V RMS
  - I/O expander     : Maxim 7300 (Digikey), I2C communication
  - Interface        : Pogo pins connecting control board to chip contact pads
  - Top plate grounded via ground wire

  Protocol files specify sequential electrode actuation parameters
  (pulse time, period) and are run via command line.

================================================================================
  PROTOCOL STEPS
================================================================================

  STEP 1 -- CHIP CLEANING
  ------------------------
  1. Clean DMF substrate with RNAse Away, then IPA, then DI water
  2. Air-dry thoroughly before use

  STEP 2 -- REAGENT LOADING
  --------------------------
  1. Mount cleaned chip onto the automation system
  2. Pipette 2.5 uL of ribozyme solution (2.5 uM) into each ribozyme reservoir
  3. Pipette 2 uL of cleavage buffer (1.25x, containing IP and QP) directly
     onto each detection point
  4. Place the ITO top plate onto the chip and connect to ground wire

  STEP 3 -- DISPENSE RIBOZYME DROPLETS
  --------------------------------------
  1. Actuate dispense electrode pattern to stretch reservoir droplet
  2. Switch off the third electrode to pinch off a ~0.5 uL ribozyme droplet
     (actuation: 178 V RMS, 15 kHz, 0.7 s per step)
  3. Repeat for all assay lanes (rxn1, rxn2, rxn3) and for positive control (PC)
  4. For negative control (NC): dispense 2 uL quenched probe only (no ribozyme,
     no input strand) onto the NC detection point

  STEP 4 -- MOVE AND MERGE DROPLETS
  -----------------------------------
  1. Actuate electrodes sequentially to move each ribozyme droplet toward
     its corresponding detection point
  2. Merge the ribozyme droplet (~0.5 uL) with the pre-pipetted cleavage
     buffer droplet (2 uL) at the detection point
  3. Mix the merged droplet by actuating 4 electrodes back-and-forth for 10 s

     Reaction assignments:
       rxn1    : ribozyme droplet 1 + cleavage buffer 1  (assay replicate 1)
       rxn2    : ribozyme droplet 2 + cleavage buffer 2  (assay replicate 2)
       rxn3    : ribozyme droplet 3 + cleavage buffer 3  (assay replicate 3)
       pcMix   : ribozyme droplet PC + PC buffer          (positive control)
       ncProbe : quenched probe only -- NO mix operation  (negative control)

     Note: ncProbe is dispensed fresh and incubated directly at its detection
     point. It is NEVER mixed with any ribozyme droplet. Using a consumed
     ribozyme variable here would violate BioScript's use-once type system.

     Positive control buffer contains ssDNA equivalent to the expected
     cleaved-off output RNA strand, directly displacing the quencher
     without requiring ribozyme activity.

  STEP 5 -- INCUBATION
  ---------------------
  Upon merging, in the assay droplets:
    - The input strand (IP) binds to the ribozyme
    - HHR folds into its active form and self-cleaves
    - The cleaved-off RNA output strand hybridizes to the F-strand of the
      quenched probe, displacing the BHQ-3 Q-strand (TMSDR)
    - Cy5 fluorophore is unquenched and emits fluorescence

  All five droplets are incubated simultaneously:
    rxn1, rxn2, rxn3, pcMix  -- heated at detection points
    ncProbe                   -- heated at its detection point (no prior mix)

  Temperature : 37 degC (maintained by plate reader during scanning)
  Duration    : 180 min total

  STEP 6 -- FLUORESCENCE DETECTION SETUP
  ----------------------------------------
  1. Carefully remove chip from automation system
  2. Stack chip onto a Corning 384-well plate (black-sided, flat clear-bottom)
  3. Align all detection points precisely to individual wells
  4. Fill 5 surrounding wells (around the chip perimeter) with 30 uL DI water
     each to prevent droplet evaporation
  5. Cover well-plate with lid and seal with parafilm
  6. Insert into ClarioSTAR plate reader (BMG Labtech)

  Plate Reader Settings:
    Excitation wavelength  : 647 nm
    Emission wavelength    : 665 nm
    Temperature            : 37 degC
    Flashes per well       : 8
    Focal height           : 15.80 mm
    Gain                   : 1800
    Scan matrix            : 30 x 30 pixels (10 mm2 per pixel)
    Scan interval          : every 20 min
    Total monitoring time  : 180 min (10 readings)

  Note: Calibrate focal length and gain using 10 uL of 0.5 uM Cy5 fluorophore
  (focal length = 6.4 mm for well-plate reference; chip focal height = 15.80 mm)

  STEP 7 -- REAL-TIME FLUORESCENCE READINGS
  -------------------------------------------
  Take well-scans at the following time points:

    Reading  1 : t =   0 min  (baseline)
    Reading  2 : t =  20 min
    Reading  3 : t =  40 min
    Reading  4 : t =  60 min
    Reading  5 : t =  80 min
    Reading  6 : t = 100 min
    Reading  7 : t = 120 min
    Reading  8 : t = 140 min
    Reading  9 : t = 160 min
    Reading 10 : t = 180 min  (endpoint)

  From the scanned pixel matrix, select the region corresponding to each
  detection point and record the highest fluorescence intensity value.

  Note: Do not use filler oil to prevent evaporation -- the probe can leak
  into the oil causing cross-contamination. DI water in surrounding wells
  is the preferred approach.

  STEP 8 -- ENDPOINT EVALUATION AND DISPOSE
  -------------------------------------------
  At t = 180 min, compare fluorescence intensities against expected values:

    Positive control (PC) : ~12,250 fluorescence units  (strand displacement)
    Assay ribozyme (RZ)   :  ~4,900 fluorescence units  (active HHR cleavage)
    Negative control (NC) :  ~1,530 fluorescence units  (quenched probe only)

  Reference threshold: 2,000 fluorescence units (signals above this indicate
  successful ribozyme cleavage). This evaluation is performed OFF-CHIP in
  Prism 8 (GraphPad) -- the DMF chip itself executes no conditional branching.

  Dispose ALL droplets unconditionally after endpoint reading is complete:
    dispose rxn1, rxn2, rxn3, pcMix, ncProbe

  Note: The BioScript protocol is fully linear (single-node CFG). On-chip
  control flow based on fluorescence readings is not used in this assay.

================================================================================
  BIOSENSOR ASSAY (OPTIONAL -- CONCENTRATION-DEPENDENT MEASUREMENTS)
================================================================================

  To use the ribozyme as a biosensor for quantifying input ssDNA concentration,
  perform the cleavage assay at multiple input concentrations:

    Test concentrations (uM): 0.01, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 5.0, 10.0
    Include a no-input control for each run.

  Read fluorescence every 20 min for 180 min (same as standard assay).

  Standard Curve Generation:
    1. Plot endpoint (t = 180 min) fluorescence vs. log10(input concentration)
    2. Fit a four-parameter logistic (4-PL) sigmoidal model to the full curve
    3. Extract the near-linear region (0.1 to 1.0 uM) for linear regression
    4. Use the slope of the linear fit as the sensitivity of the biosensor

  Biosensor Performance (DMF chip vs. well-plate):
    Sensitivity slope  : DMF = 1230 +/- 71     |  Well-plate = 850 +/- 120
    Limit of Detection : DMF = 1475 units       |  Well-plate = 1845 units
    Limit of Quant.    : DMF = 0.025 uM         |  Well-plate = 0.31 uM
    SNR (at 180 min)   : DMF = 18.95            |  Well-plate = 8.95

  LoD  = blank_mean + 3 x SD
  LoQ  = 10 x SD / S
  (where SD = std dev of no-input blank; S = slope of linear regression)

================================================================================
  KINETICS ANALYSIS
================================================================================

  To extract cleavage rate constants:
    1. Calculate inverse of fluorescence intensities at each time point
       (1/F represents amount of uncleaved ribozyme remaining)
    2. Fit a one-phase decay equation to the data:

         Y = (Y0 - Plateau) x e^(-K x X) + Plateau

       where:
         Y         = amount of uncleaved ribozyme (1/fluorescence)
         X         = time (min)
         K         = observed cleavage rate constant (kobs, min-1)
         Y0        = initial value of Y
         Plateau   = Y value at reaction completion

  Measured rate constants:
    kobs (DMF chip)   : 0.026 +/- 0.005 min-1   (R2 = 0.95)
    kobs (well-plate) : 0.010 +/- 0.003 min-1   (R2 = 0.84)

  Note: DMF cleavage rate is ~2.5x faster than well-plate, attributed to the
  higher surface-area-to-volume (SAV) ratio of droplets on the DMF platform
  and possible molecular crowding effects from Tetronic 304 surfactant.

================================================================================
  DATA ANALYSIS
================================================================================

  - Fluorescence data analysis : Prism 8 (GraphPad Software)
  - Droplet image analysis     : ImageJ 1.52p (Fiji)
  - Linear regression for kinetics and biosensor curves performed in Prism 8
  - SNR calculated as: mean fluorescence of triplicates / standard deviation

================================================================================
  WELL-PLATE REFERENCE ASSAY (BENCHTOP COMPARISON)
================================================================================

  For well-plate parallel experiments (384-well plate, black-sided, clear-bottom):
    1. Add 2 uL ribozyme (2.5 uM) to each well
    2. Add 8 uL cleavage buffer (1.25x) containing 6.25 uM input ssDNA
       and 12.5 mM MgCl2
    3. Fill 5 adjacent wells with 30 uL water each (humidity control)
    4. Cover with lid, seal with parafilm
    5. Insert into ClarioSTAR plate reader
    6. Read every 20 min for 180 min at 37 degC
       (8 flashes; lex = 647 nm; lem = 665 nm; focal length = 6.4 mm; gain = 1800)

================================================================================
  CONTROLS SUMMARY
================================================================================

  Positive Control (PC):
    - Cleavage buffer containing ssDNA identical in sequence to the expected
      cleaved-off RNA output strand
    - Directly displaces the BHQ-3 Q-strand from the probe via TMSDR
    - Confirms probe and detection system are functioning correctly
    - Expected fluorescence at 180 min: ~12,250 units

  Negative Control (NC):
    - Variable id : ncProbe (dispensed fresh as QuenchedProbe -- no mix operation)
    - Quenched probe only; no ribozyme, no input strand, no MgCl2 input
    - Probe remains fully quenched throughout the experiment
    - Represents baseline/background fluorescence
    - Expected fluorescence at 180 min: ~1,530 units

  Additional negative controls (second chip experiment):
    NC1 : Quenched probe in cleavage buffer (no input, no MgCl2 activation)
    NC2 : Buffer without MgCl2 and without input strand
    NC3 : Buffer with MgCl2 only (no input strand)
    NC4 : Buffer with input strand only (no MgCl2)
    NC5 : Buffer with mutated input ssDNA and MgCl2 (non-cognate activator)

================================================================================
  IMPORTANT NOTES
================================================================================

  1. SURFACTANT: Add 0.05% Tetronic 304 to all aqueous droplets to prevent
     biofouling and improve droplet movement on the hydrophobic chip surface.
     High-salt solutions (cleavage buffer) are particularly prone to sticking.

  2. EVAPORATION: Do not use filler oil; use DI water in surrounding wells
     instead. Oil causes the Cy5 probe to leak out and cross-contaminate
     adjacent detection points.

  3. CHIP REUSE: Pipette cleavage buffer directly onto detection points
     (rather than moving it across the chip) to prevent trace contamination
     of electrodes and enable chip reuse.

  4. READING INTERVAL: The ClarioSTAR takes up to 20 min to scan a full chip.
     Therefore, fluorescence readings represent 20 min interval snapshots,
     not instantaneous time points.

  5. ELECTRODE ACTUATION: Electrode pulse duration = 0.7 s per step.
     Dispense pattern: stretch droplet with 4 electrodes, switch off 3rd
     electrode to pinch off the smaller droplet.

  6. RNA HANDLING: Use RNAse-free reagents and surfaces throughout. Clean
     chip with RNAse Away before each experiment.

================================================================================
  END OF PROTOCOL
================================================================================

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidics (DMF) Parallel DNA Ligation for Recombinant DNA Cloning — Water-Oil Core-Shell Droplet Format with Multiple Insert Lengths

REAGENTS USED:
  - Vector DNA (linearized plasmid backbone droplets)
  - Insert DNA, 0.9 kb fragment
  - Insert DNA, 1.7 kb fragment
  - Insert DNA, 1.9 kb fragment
  - DNA Ligase Buffer (containing DNA ligase enzyme)

STEPS:
1. Dispense a vector DNA droplet and an insert DNA droplet (0.9 kb) from their respective reservoirs.
2. Merge and mix the vector and 0.9 kb insert droplets to pool them.
3. Dispense a droplet of DNA ligase buffer and merge/mix it with the pooled vector/insert droplet to initiate ligation.
4. Incubate the ligation reaction droplet at 16 C to allow the DNA ligase reaction to proceed, then discard the droplet.
5. Repeat steps 1-4 in parallel for the 1.7 kb insert: dispense fresh vector and 1.7 kb insert droplets, merge, add ligase buffer, incubate at 16 C, and discard.
6. Repeat steps 1-4 in parallel for the 1.9 kb insert: dispense fresh vector and 1.9 kb insert droplets, merge, add ligase buffer, incubate at 16 C, and discard.
7. Perform a fourth parallel reaction combining both the 0.9 kb and 1.9 kb inserts: dispense droplets of each insert, merge them together, then merge the combined-insert droplet with a fresh vector droplet, add ligase buffer, incubate at 16 C, and discard.

INTERPRETATION: Successful ligation is confirmed off-chip by transforming the resulting recombinant DNA into competent bacteria, culturing the transformed colonies, and confirming the presence of the correct insert fragment length by plasmid extraction and gel electrophoresis, with the four parallel on-chip reactions each yielding the expected vector-insert recombinant product corresponding to its designated insert length or combination.

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code is a translation of the four parallel DNA ligation reactions described in Section 4.3 and Figure 4e,f of the Choi et al. DMF review, which summarizes the original Liu et al. (2008, J. Micromech. Microeng. 18:045017) and Lin et al. (2010, J. Assoc. Lab. Autom. 15:210-15) primary studies. The review describes four droplets of insert DNA of various lengths merged with vector droplets and then with DNA ligase, but does not itself enumerate the exact insert lengths for each of the four parallel lanes beyond noting 'various lengths' in the figure; the 0.9 kb, 1.7 kb, and 1.9 kb values, and the fourth lane's combined 0.9 kb/1.9 kb insert, are taken from the figure caption's listed insert-DNA labels. Because BioScript has no primitive for concurrent/parallel branches, the four reactions are modeled as four sequential dispense/mix/heat/dispose blocks rather than true parallel execution, consistent with how the earlier PCR and enzymatic-assay translations in this test suite serialize repeated or multi-condition operations. The water-oil core-shell droplet format described in the review (used to reduce actuation voltage) has no corresponding BioScript primitive and is therefore not modeled; only the reagent-mixing and incubation logic of the ligation chemistry is captured.

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Droplet-Actuator Bead-Based Chemiluminescent Immunoassay for Cardiac Marker Detection (cTnI / CK-MB / Myoglobin)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Cardiac Sample (biological sample, e.g. whole blood, serum, or plasma, containing a cardiac marker such as cardiac troponin I, CK-MB, or myoglobin)
  - Capture Beads (magnetically responsive beads coated with primary capture antibody)
  - Blocking Antibody (blocking protein/antibody reagent)
  - Reporter Antibody (secondary reporter antibody)
  - Wash Buffer (droplet-based merge-and-split dilution wash buffer, 0.05M TRIS, 0.1 M NaCl, 0.1 mg/mL BSA, 0.02% Tween20, pH 9.5)
  - Chemiluminescent Substrate (detection substrate, e.g. APS-5)

STEPS:
1. Dispense a cardiac sample droplet, a capture-bead droplet, and a blocking-antibody droplet.
2. Mix the capture beads with the blocking antibody to form reagent 1.
3. Combine the sample droplet with reagent 1 to form the assay droplet; incubate at room temperature (~23C) for 3 minutes to allow capture antibody-antigen binding.
4. Execute a droplet-based wash step: merge the assay droplet with wash buffer and discard the resulting supernatant, removing unbound sample material.
5. Dispense a reporter-antibody droplet and merge it with the assay droplet; incubate 2 minutes at room temperature to form the capture-antibody-antigen-reporter-antibody complex.
6. Execute a droplet-based wash protocol (11 repeated merge-and-split dilution washes with wash buffer) to deplete unbound reporter antibody and antigen from the bead droplet.
7. Combine the washed bead droplet with chemiluminescent substrate; incubate ~2 minutes at 25C.
8. Detect the chemiluminescent signal for 5 seconds, indicative of the quantity of the cardiac marker in the biological sample.
9. If the measured signal exceeds the top-end of the standard curve, execute an auto-dilution sequence (merge with a diluent droplet, re-detect) to bring the concentration back within the linear range of detection.
10. Discard the analyzed droplet.

INTERPRETATION: Successful cardiac marker quantification is confirmed by a calibration curve relating chemiluminescent response (counts/s) to marker concentration (ng/mL) for cTn-I, CK-MB, and myoglobin, with good linearity and recovery percentages clustered near 100% across the calibrator concentration range, and with total assay time (sample loading to detectable signal) of well under 5-10 minutes for multiplexed cardiac marker panels, supporting use of the platform for rapid triage of chest-pain patients and assessment of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) risk.

10. Discard the analyzed droplet.

ASSAY TYPE: Determination of Anthocyanin Content (pH-Differential Method)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Sample Powder (plant tissue powder)
  - Potassium Chloride Buffer (0.025 mol/L, pH 1.0)
  - Sodium Acetate Buffer (0.4 mol/L, pH 4.5)

STEPS:
1. Combine sample powder with 0.025 mol/L potassium chloride buffer (pH 1.0) in a 1:8 ratio of extract to buffer.
2. Measure absorbance of the pH 1.0 mixture at 515 nm and 700 nm against a blank.
3. Combine sample powder with 0.4 mol/L sodium acetate buffer (pH 4.5) in a 1:8 ratio of extract to buffer.

INTERPRETATION: Total monomeric anthocyanin content is calculated from the pH-differential absorbance readings [(A515 - A700)pH1.0 - (A515 - A700)pH4.5], which corrects for degradation products and turbidity; a higher differential absorbance value indicates greater anthocyanin content in the sample.

ASSAY TYPE: Determination of Total Flavonoid Content (Aluminium Chloride Colorimetric Method)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Methanolic Extract
  - Distilled Water
  - Sodium Nitrite (5% w/v)
  - Aluminium Chloride (10% w/v)
  - Sodium Hydroxide (1 M)

STEPS:
1. Add 100 uL of extract to 4 mL of distilled water.
2. Add 0.3 mL of 5% sodium nitrite; incubate for 5 min.
3. Add 0.3 mL of 10% aluminium chloride; incubate for 6 min.
4. Add 2 mL of 1 M sodium hydroxide to the mixture.
5. Immediately dilute with 3.3 mL of distilled water and mix thoroughly.
6. Measure absorbance at 510 nm against a blank.

INTERPRETATION: Absorbance at 510 nm reflects the pink-colored aluminium-flavonoid complex formed in the reaction; higher absorbance indicates greater total flavonoid content in the extract, typically expressed as standard-equivalent units (e.g., quercetin equivalents) via a calibration curve.

description:
Source link: https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/deepweb/assets/sigmaaldrich/product/documents/347/216/se120149bul.pdf
Paper doi: N/A (manufacturer technical bulletin — Sigma-Aldrich Co. LLC, Benzodiazepines Direct ELISA Kit, Catalog Number SE120149)
Demonstration video: No demonstration video located

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Competitive ELISA for benzodiazepine-class drugs (including diazepam) in urine or
blood, using a pre-coated antibody microplate. This version of the workflow has been adapted
to run as a sequence of droplet operations on a digital microfluidic biochip (DMFB) instead
of a standard 96-well plate.

REAGENTS USED:
  - Urine sample (diluted specimen)
  - Benzodiazepine-enzyme conjugate (drug labeled with horseradish peroxidase)
  - Distilled water (wash diluent)
  - TMB substrate (3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine)
  - Stop solution (dilute acid)

STEPS:

1. Combine 10 units of the diluted urine sample with 100 units of the benzodiazepine-enzyme
   conjugate. Mix for 60 seconds.

2. Incubate the combined mixture at 23C (room temperature) for 60 minutes. During this time,
   any free benzodiazepine in the sample competes with the enzyme-labeled conjugate for a
   limited number of antibody binding sites — this competition is the basis of the test.

3. Wash the reaction six times: each wash cycle combines 350 units of distilled water with the
   reaction droplet, mixes for 45 seconds, and removes unbound material before moving to
   detection.

4. Add 100 units of TMB substrate to the washed reaction and mix for 60 seconds. Incubate at
   23C for 30 minutes to allow the color reaction to develop.

5. Add 100 units of stop solution and mix for 60 seconds to halt color development and shift
   the color from blue to yellow.

6. Measure the resulting absorbance signal to obtain the reading. Discard the sample
   afterward.

INTERPRETATION: This is a one-step competitive immunoassay. Free benzodiazepine in the sample
and the enzyme-labeled conjugate compete for a fixed number of antibody binding sites on the
plate. After washing away anything unbound, the remaining bound conjugate is revealed by the
TMB color reaction. Less color development means more drug was present in the sample
(competing more successfully for binding sites); more color development means less or no drug
was present. A result is typically called positive if the sample's absorbance reading is at or
below the reading from a positive reference standard, and negative if it is above.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A NOTE ON HOW CLOSELY THIS MATCHES THE CITED SOURCE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This is an exact numeric match to the cited source across every value: sample volume (10
units), conjugate volume (100 units), first incubation time (60 minutes), wash count and
volume (6 times, 350 units), substrate volume (100 units), second incubation time (30
minutes), and stop solution volume (100 units) all match the source exactly. The only
difference is that the droplet program records the result using the generic "fluorescence"
detect type, since BioScript has no dedicated absorbance-reading instruction, whereas the
real procedure reads absorbance at a dual wavelength (450 nm and 650 nm). This is a known
expressiveness gap in the droplet language, not a deviation from the real procedure.

One caveat on scope: this kit is raised against and validated for benzodiazepines as a drug
class (the antiserum is directed against Oxazepam, with cross-reactivity across the
benzodiazepine group, which includes diazepam), rather than being diazepam-exclusive. This
does not affect the validity of the step-by-step procedure above, which applies identically
regardless of which specific benzodiazepine is being screened for.

An earlier version of this protocol's droplet program included a second, separate
antibody/enzyme incubation-and-wash stage (resembling a two-step "sandwich" ELISA). No real
benzodiazepine or other small-molecule drug immunoassay kit was found using that structure: a
two-step format requires the target molecule to be large enough for two antibodies to bind it
simultaneously, which a small drug molecule (a "hapten") is not large enough to support. Every
real urine drug-screening kit checked (morphine, fentanyl, oxycodone, benzodiazepines) uses
the one-step competitive format reflected in the steps above. The two-step version is treated
as a non-representative artifact of the original test file, not a valid alternative protocol.

4. Re-Extraction Pooling: Repeat the methanol extraction and isooctane clean-up cycle 4 times, pooling the extract droplets into the output reservoir[cite: 45].
5. Reconstitution: Dry the pooled extract by heating at 25C for 10m, then reconstitute with a unit of methanol and mix for 30s[cite: 45].
6. Detection: Dispense ELISA reagent, mix with the final extract for 60s, and detect fluorescence/readout for 5m before disposing of the mixture[cite: 45].

INTERPRETATION: Quantifies the concentration of estradiol extracted from biological samples via liquid-liquid extraction followed by an ELISA-based readout.
