description:
Source link: https://www.mdpi.com/2079-6374/13/4/419/pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.3390/bios13040419

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Electrowetting-on-Dielectric (EWOD) Digital Microfluidics for In Vitro Maturation, Fertilization, and Individual On-Chip Culture/Manipulation of Bovine Embryos

REAGENTS USED:
  - Cumulus Oocyte Complexes (COCs), abattoir-derived, aspirated from 4-8 mm follicles
  - TCM-199 maturation medium (bicarbonate-buffered, supplemented with gentamycin and EGF)
  - Gentamycin (50 mg/mL)
  - Epidermal Growth Factor, EGF (20 ng/mL)
  - HEPES-TALP medium (oocyte/gamete wash buffer)
  - IVF-TALP medium (bicarbonate-buffered Tyrode solution for sperm preparation/fertilization)
  - Bovine Serum Albumin, BSA (6 mg/mL in sperm medium; 4 mg/mL in culture medium)
  - Heparin (25 ug/mL, sperm capacitation agent)
  - Frozen-thawed bull spermatozoa (Percoll-gradient selected, 1x10^6 cells/mL)
  - SOFaa-ITS-BSA culture medium (synthetic oviductal fluid with amino acids, insulin, transferrin, selenium, BSA)
  - Tween 80 surfactant (0.01% v/v, added to on-chip droplets to prevent protein fouling of the EWOD surface)
  - Fresh/pre-equilibrated top-up culture medium droplet (2-5 uL, merged on-chip at 96 hpi)

STEPS:
1. In Vitro Maturation (IVM): Wash and culture COCs in groups of 60 per 500 uL modified TCM-199 medium supplemented with gentamycin and EGF; incubate 22 h at 38.5 C in 5% CO2.
2. Sperm preparation: Segregate frozen-thawed bull semen on a 45:90% Percoll gradient; wash the viable-sperm pellet in IVF-TALP and adjust to 1x10^6 cells/mL in IVF-TALP supplemented with BSA and heparin.
3. In Vitro Fertilization (IVF): Wash matured oocytes in HEPES-TALP, then co-incubate with the prepared spermatozoa for 21 h in IVF-TALP at 38.5 C in 5% CO2.
4. Denudation: Vortex the presumed zygotes to remove surrounding cumulus cells.
5. On-chip droplet loading: At 48 hpi, select 2- to 4-cell stage zygotes, wash in SOFaa-ITS-BSA medium supplemented with 0.01% Tween 80, and suspend each embryo individually in a 5 uL droplet of this medium; pipette the droplet between the top (ground) and bottom (driving-electrode) plates of the EWOD chip, surrounded by oil.
6. Droplet actuation off the loading edge: Apply 70-90 V DC to the driving electrode (top electrode grounded) to move the embryo-containing droplet away from the chip edge and the oil/air interface.
7. Cleavage assessment: At 48 hpi, evaluate embryo cleavage by morphological grading under a stereomicroscope.
8. Dynamic on-chip manipulation: Every 24 h, move the embryo-containing droplet to the next electrode pair by manual charging of the corresponding contact pad, keeping the embryo individually tracked on-chip through the 2-cell, 4-cell, 8-cell, and morula stages.
9. On-chip medium supply: At 72 hpi, pipette a 2 uL pre-equilibrated droplet of SOFaa-ITS-BSA-Tween 80 medium onto the chip; at 96 hpi, actuate the embryo-containing droplet toward this on-chip droplet and merge them by contact to refresh the culture medium.
10. Continued culture and blastocyst assessment: Continue on-chip incubation with periodic electrode-pair moves through 192 hpi; assess blastocyst formation by morphological grading under a stereomicroscope; discard/dispose of the droplet after assessment.

INTERPRETATION: Successful on-chip embryo manipulation is indicated by comparable cleavage rates (~48 hpi) and blastocyst rates (~192 hpi) between individually cultured droplet embryos (static Petri-dish droplets and on-chip "squeezed" droplets) and conventional static controls, together with visual confirmation that individual embryos progress through successive cleavage stages (2-cell to morula) while being moved and supplied with fresh medium on the EWOD chip, supporting digital microfluidics as a viable platform for non-invasive, individual embryo handling in assisted reproductive technologies.

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code is a direct translation of the paper's IVM/IVF/IVC and on-chip EWOD manipulation workflow (Sections 2.2.2 and 3.2), covering oocyte maturation and sperm preparation (steps 1-2), fertilization and denudation (steps 3-4), on-chip droplet loading and edge actuation (steps 5-6), the 48 hpi cleavage check (step 7), the every-24h electrode-pair movement through the 2-cell to morula stages (step 8), the 96 hpi on-chip medium-merge refresh (step 9), and continued culture to the 192 hpi blastocyst assessment (step 10). Incubation durations and temperatures (22 h IVM, 21 h IVF, 38.5c throughout) are taken directly from the Materials and Methods section; hour-scale durations were converted to minutes/seconds since BioScript's grammar exposes only m/s time units. ASSAY TYPE: Electrowetting-Based Digital Microfluidics Coupled to Real-Time (TaqMan) PCR for Human SNP Allelic Discrimination

REAGENTS USED:
  - Allele 1 Control Template (human genomic DNA control containing allele 1 template only, targeted by the VIC-labeled probe)
  - Allele 2 Control Template (human genomic DNA control containing allele 2 template only, targeted by the FAM-labeled probe)
  - Both-Alleles Control Template (heterozygous control containing both allele 1 and allele 2 templates)
  - No-Template Control (no DNA)
  - TaqMan Allelic Discrimination Master Mix (commercially available TaqMan allelic discrimination kit reagent, ABI PN:4312559, for the C440T mutation of the CYC2C9*2 gene; contains differentially labeled FAM/VIC fluorescent probes, primers, dNTPs, and Taq polymerase; ~300 nL droplets)

STEPS:
1. For each of the four allelic controls (allele 1 only, allele 2 only, both alleles, no template), dispense a ~300 nL droplet of the control template onto the electrowetting chip.
2. Dispense a matching ~300 nL droplet of TaqMan master mix reagent for each control.
3. Actuate and merge each control droplet with its corresponding master mix droplet on the electrowetting chip to form four complete PCR reaction droplets.
4. Transport each droplet back and forth several hundred times under electrowetting control to verify standard droplet manipulations (transport, mixing, splitting, dispensing) are unaffected by the PCR reagents, then position the droplets at opposite ends of the electrode array.
5. Remove the electrowetting control voltage and thermocycle the entire chip inside the custom-built hot-air thermocycler mounted on the fluorescence microscope.
6. After each thermal cycle, read out FAM and VIC fluorescence intensity from each droplet in real time to build per-cycle amplification time-courses.
7. Discard each droplet after the thermocycling/detection run is complete.

INTERPRETATION: Successful allelic discrimination is confirmed by real-time fluorescence amplification curves showing successful DNA amplification within the droplets, and by end-point FAM/VIC intensity plots that cleanly separate droplets bearing allele 1 only, allele 2 only, both alleles, and no template, demonstrating that the addition of PCR reagents has little effect on electrowetting droplet manipulation, that the electrowetting chip environment does not inhibit PCR, and that the platform can discriminate a human SNP differing by only one base pair.

mastermix1 = dispense 300 units of TaqManMasterMix
mastermix2 = dispense 300 units of TaqManMasterMix
mastermix3 = dispense 300 units of TaqManMasterMix
mastermix4 = dispense 300 units of TaqManMasterMix

droplet1 = mix allele1 with mastermix1 for 5s
droplet2 = mix allele2 with mastermix2 for 5s

    heat droplet4 at 95c for 15s
    heat droplet4 at 60c for 60s
    signal4 = detect fluorescence on droplet4 for 5s
}

dispose droplet1
dispose droplet2
dispose droplet3
dispose droplet4

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidics (DMF) Oil-Free Homogeneous Enzyme Kinetics Assay — Alkaline Phosphatase (AP) Activity and Inorganic-Phosphate Product Inhibition, Monitored via Fluorescein Diphosphate (FDP) Fluorogenic Substrate

REAGENTS USED:
  - Alkaline Phosphatase (AP) enzyme droplets
  - Fluorescein Diphosphate (FDP) fluorogenic substrate droplets
  - Inorganic Phosphate solution (product-inhibition titrant)
  - Distilled Water (dilution/quench droplets)

STEPS:
1. Dispense an AP droplet and an FDP droplet on an oil-free DMF device.
2. Merge and actively mix the AP and FDP droplets to initiate the enzymatic reaction, converting FDP into fluorescent fluorescein.
3. Incubate the merged droplet at room temperature to allow the reaction to proceed.
4. Measure the baseline fluorescence intensity of the fluorescein product to establish uninhibited AP reaction kinetics.
5. Titrate inorganic phosphate into the reaction droplet across a series of points to assess product inhibition: for each point, dispense a fresh phosphate droplet, merge/mix it with the reaction droplet, incubate, and re-measure fluorescence intensity.
6. Repeat the phosphate titration/measurement cycle across multiple points to build a dose-response inhibition curve.
7. Dilute/quench the final reaction droplet with distilled water and discard it.

INTERPRETATION: Successful assay performance is confirmed by AP enzyme kinetic constants (e.g., Km, Vmax) that are consistent with values reported in the literature for conventional macroscale assays, and by a phosphate-concentration-dependent decrease in fluorescence signal consistent with competitive product inhibition — demonstrating that an oil-free DMF platform supports quantitative homogeneous enzyme kinetics studies without partitioning of hydrophobic reagents into a carrier-oil phase.

module fluorescence

manifest alkaline_phosphatase
manifest fluorescein_diphosphate
manifest inorganic_phosphate
manifest distilled_water

instructions:

ap = dispense 10 units of alkaline_phosphatase
fdp = dispense 10 units of fluorescein_diphosphate

rxn = mix ap with fdp for 30s
heat rxn at 25c for 5m

baseline_reading = detect fluorescence on rxn for 30s

repeat 4 times {
    phosphate = dispense 5 units of inorganic_phosphate
    rxn = mix rxn with phosphate for 20s
    heat rxn at 25c for 5m
    inhibition_reading = detect fluorescence on rxn for 30s
}

water = dispense 20 units of distilled_water
rxn = mix rxn with water for 15s
dispose rxn

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Estimation of Ascorbic Acid Content (2,6-Dichloroindophenol Method)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Apple Fruit Tissue
  - Meta-Phosphoric Acid (1% w/v)
  - 2,6-Dichloroindophenol Reagent

STEPS:
1. Cut apple fruit into small pieces; homogenize 1 g of tissue in 10 mL of 1% meta-phosphoric acid for 1 min.
2. Agitate the mixture slowly at room temperature for 45 min, then vortex.
3. Centrifuge at 1370 x g for 10 min.
4. Filter the supernatant using Whatman No. 1 filter paper.
5. Mix 1 mL of filtrate with 9 mL of 2,6-dichloro-indophenol reagent.
6. Measure absorbance at 515 nm.

INTERPRETATION: Absorbance at 515 nm reflects the reduction of the blue 2,6-dichloroindophenol dye by ascorbic acid (vitamin C) in the extract; a greater decrease in dye absorbance corresponds to higher ascorbic acid content, typically quantified against an ascorbic acid standard calibration curve.

  - Potassium Iodide (KI)

STEPS:
1. Crush 100 mg of leaf tissue (control or infected) with liquid nitrogen and mix with 1 mL reaction mixture comprising 0.25 mL TCA, 0.5 mL KI, and 0.25 mL potassium phosphate buffer (10 mM, pH 6.5).

description:
Source link: Bioscience Lab, IITR
Paper DOI: N/A

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Estimation of Lipid Peroxides (TBARS) in Plant Leaf Tissue

REAGENTS USED:
  - Leaf Tissue (control and infected samples, ground in liquid nitrogen)
  - Trichloroacetic Acid (TCA), 0.1% (w/v) for extraction
  - TBA Reagent (0.5% thiobarbituric acid in 20% trichloroacetic acid)

STEPS:
1. Grind leaf tissue (control or infected) with liquid nitrogen into a fine powder; homogenize 100 mg of powder with 1 mL of 0.1% (w/v) TCA.
2. Centrifuge the extract at 12,000 x g for 15 min at 4 C; collect the supernatant.
3. Mix 1 mL of 0.5% TBA in 20% TCA with 0.5 mL of the supernatant.
4. Heat the mixture at 95 C for 30 min in a dry bath, then cool at ice-cold temperature.
5. Centrifuge the mixture at 14,000 x g for 15 min at 4 C.
6. Measure absorbance at 532 nm, then measure absorbance at 600 nm to correct for unspecific turbidity; subtract A600 from A532 to obtain corrected absorbance.

INTERPRETATION: The corrected absorbance (A532 - A600) reflects malondialdehyde (MDA)-TBA complex formation and is used as a measure of lipid peroxidation (TBARS); higher corrected absorbance indicates greater oxidative membrane damage, with infected-tissue readings typically compared against control-tissue readings.

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Estimation of Total Phenolic Content (TPC) by the Folin-Ciocalteu Colorimetric Assay

REAGENTS USED:
  - Methanolic Extract (plant tissue extract in methanol)
  - Folin-Ciocalteu Reagent (diluted 1:9 with water)
  - Sodium Carbonate Solution (5% w/v)

STEPS:
1. Combine 100 uL of methanolic extract with 500 uL of diluted Folin-Ciocalteu reagent (1:9 diluted with water); keep the mixture at room temperature (~28-30 C).
2. After 5 min incubation, add 400 uL of 5% sodium carbonate to the mixture.
3. Incubate the mixture for 20 min in the dark.
4. Measure absorbance at 765 nm.

INTERPRETATION: The developed blue color is proportional to the total phenolic content of the extract; absorbance at 765 nm is compared against a gallic-acid (or equivalent standard) calibration curve to express TPC in standard-equivalent units per gram of tissue, with higher absorbance indicating greater phenolic content.

description:
Source link: Bioscience Lab, IITR
Paper DOI: N/A

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Estimation of Total Soluble Sugar (Anthrone Method)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Apple Fruit Tissue
  - Methanol (extraction solvent)
  - Deionized Water
  - Anthrone Reagent (0.1 g anthrone dissolved in concentrated sulfuric acid, 0.2% v/v)

STEPS:
1. Crush 3 g of apple fruit tissue into 10 mL of methanol; homogenize for 2 min at room temperature.
2. Centrifuge the homogenate at 10,000 x g for 15 min; collect the supernatant.
3. Add 100 uL of supernatant to 900 uL of deionized water (final volume 1 mL); keep in an ice bath.
4. After 2 min of incubation, add 2 mL of cold anthrone reagent to the mixture.
5. Heat the reaction for 10 min in a boiling water bath.
6. Cool the reaction, then measure absorbance at 620 nm.

INTERPRETATION: Absorbance at 620 nm reflects the anthrone-sulfuric acid colorimetric reaction with soluble carbohydrates; higher absorbance indicates greater total soluble sugar content in the fruit tissue extract, typically compared against a glucose (or equivalent standard) calibration curve.

description:
Source link: https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/c7lc00170c.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1039/C7LC00170C

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic (DMF) Tissue Extraction Coupled to Magnetic Bead-Based Chemiluminescent Immunoassay for Estradiol (E2) Quantification in Core-Needle Biopsy (CNB) Samples

REAGENTS USED:
  - Core Needle Biopsy (CNB) tissue homogenate (~5 mg breast tissue sample)
  - Methanol (neat, extraction solvent, 4.8 uL droplets)
  - Immunoassay Reconstitution Buffer (BSA in DPBS with Tetronic 90R4, 4.8 uL droplet)
  - Anti-E2 Coated Paramagnetic Microparticles (1.6 uL droplet)
  - Wash Buffer (Tris-based DMF wash buffer, 1.6 uL droplets)
  - Estradiol-HRP Conjugate (E2 conjugated to horseradish peroxidase via 6-CMO, 1.6 uL droplet)
  - Hydrogen Peroxide (H2O2) substrate solution (0.8 uL droplet)
  - Luminol/Enhancer Solution (0.8 uL droplet)

STEPS:
1. Load the CNB tissue homogenate onto the bottom plate and affix the top plate bearing the hydrophilic anchor.
2-3. Dispense a 4.8 uL methanol extraction-solvent droplet, deliver it to the CNB tissue sample, and extract by moving the droplet in a circular pattern around the tissue for 5 min.
4. Drive the sample-extract droplet away from the tissue to the hydrophilic anchor and evaporate at room temperature for 5 min.
5-6. Repeat steps 2-4 once more (second extraction/evaporation cycle onto the anchor).
7. Redissolve the dried analyte on the anchor: dispense a 4.8 uL droplet of immunoassay reconstitution buffer onto the anchor and actuate for 30 s.
8. Dispense a 1.6 uL droplet of anti-E2 paramagnetic microparticles and engage the magnet to separate the particles from the diluent.
9. Deliver the 4.8 uL reconstituted sample extract to the immobilized particles for resuspension.
10. Actively mix the particles with the sample for 6 min, then engage the magnet and drive the supernatant to waste.
11-13. Wash cycle: dispense a 1.6 uL wash-buffer droplet, deliver it to the particles, resuspend/mix for 10 s, engage the magnet, and drive the supernatant to waste; repeat this cycle a total of 4 times.
14. Dispense a 1.6 uL droplet of E2-HRP conjugate and deliver it to the immobilized particles for resuspension.
15. Actively mix for 2 min.
16-18. Repeat the wash cycle (steps 11-13) a total of 4 times.
19. Dispense a 0.8 uL droplet of H2O2 and deliver it to the immobilized particles.
20. Dispense a 0.8 uL droplet of luminol/enhancer solution and deliver it to the immobilized particles, combining with the H2O2 droplet.
21. Actively mix the combined droplet for 10 min and measure chemiluminescence using the integrated photomultiplier tube (PMT); then discard the droplet.

INTERPRETATION: E2 concentration in each tissue extract is determined against a four-parameter logistic calibration curve built from ten E2 standards (0-20,000 pg/mL), and reported as the amount of analyte detected relative to sample mass. REAGENTS USED:
  - Core Needle Biopsy (CNB) tissue homogenate (~5 mg breast tissue sample)
  - Methanol (neat, extraction solvent, 4.8 uL droplets)
  - Immunoassay Reconstitution Buffer (BSA in DPBS with Tetronic 90R4, 4.8 uL droplet)
  - Anti-E2 Coated Paramagnetic Microparticles (1.6 uL droplet)
  - Wash Buffer (Tris-based DMF wash buffer, 1.6 uL droplets)
  - Estradiol-HRP Conjugate (E2 conjugated to horseradish peroxidase via 6-CMO, 1.6 uL droplet)
  - Hydrogen Peroxide (H2O2) substrate solution (0.8 uL droplet)
  - Luminol/Enhancer Solution (0.8 uL droplet)

STEPS:
1. Load the CNB tissue homogenate onto the bottom plate and affix the top plate bearing the hydrophilic anchor.
2-3. Dispense a 4.8 uL methanol extraction-solvent droplet, deliver it to the CNB tissue sample, and extract by moving the droplet in a circular pattern around the tissue for 5 min.
4. Drive the sample-extract droplet away from the tissue to the hydrophilic anchor and evaporate at room temperature for 5 min.
5-6. Repeat steps 2-4 once more (second extraction/evaporation cycle onto the anchor).
7. Redissolve the dried analyte on the anchor: dispense a 4.8 uL droplet of immunoassay reconstitution buffer onto the anchor and actuate for 30 s.
8. Dispense a 1.6 uL droplet of anti-E2 paramagnetic microparticles and engage the magnet to separate the particles from the diluent.
9. Deliver the 4.8 uL reconstituted sample extract to the immobilized particles for resuspension.
10. Actively mix the particles with the sample for 6 min, then engage the magnet and drive the supernatant to waste.
11-13. Wash cycle: dispense a 1.6 uL wash-buffer droplet, deliver it to the particles, resuspend/mix for 10 s, engage the magnet, and drive the supernatant to waste; repeat this cycle a total of 4 times.
14. Dispense a 1.6 uL droplet of E2-HRP conjugate and deliver it to the immobilized particles for resuspension.
15. Actively mix for 2 min.
16-18. Repeat the wash cycle (steps 11-13) a total of 4 times.
19. Dispense a 0.8 uL droplet of H2O2 and deliver it to the immobilized particles.
20. Dispense a 0.8 uL droplet of luminol/enhancer solution and deliver it to the immobilized particles, combining with the H2O2 droplet.
21. Actively mix the combined droplet for 10 min and measure chemiluminescence using the integrated photomultiplier tube (PMT); then discard the droplet.

description:
================================================================================
PROTOCOL: [18F]FDG Radiosynthesis on Digital Microfluidics (OFAT-Optimized)
================================================================================

Source Link : https://www.shihmicrolab.ca/_files/ugd/f0a828_ab1a29cf1f1a4c74999bfd94b207f38b.pdf
Paper DOI   : https://doi.org/10.1039/d2lc00764a
BioScript   : fdg_radiosynthesis_ofat.bs
Platform    : Digital Microfluidics (EWOD / DMFB electrode-array device)
Optimization: One-Factor-At-A-Time (OFAT) + Machine Learning (Ridge Regression)
Product     : [18F]FDG (2-[18F]fluoro-2-deoxy-D-glucose)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
OFAT-OPTIMAL PARAMETERS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Parameter                          Optimal Value
  ---------------------------------  ----------------
  Mannose triflate / [18F] volume    1.0 (equal ratio)
  Mannose triflate concentration     30 mM
  Radiolabeling temperature          100 C
  Radiolabeling time                 5 min
  NaOH concentration                 1.0 M
  Deprotection temperature           50 C
  Deprotection time                  5 min

  Fluorination efficiency (OFAT)   : 70.82 +/- 1.54%
  Overall synthesis yield (OFAT)   : 66.64%
  Overall synthesis yield (ML)     : 79.13%
  Total synthesis time             : ~19 +/- 2 min
  Post-purification purity         : ~93.05 +/- 2.46%

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
REAGENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  1. [18F]Fluoride         - No-carrier-added [18F]fluoride ion in [18O]-enriched H2O
  2. Mannose Triflate      - 30 mM in anhydrous acetonitrile (MeCN); substrate for
                             [18F] fluorination
  3. Kryptofix K222        - K222 / K2CO3 complex; activates [18F]fluoride for
                             nucleophilic substitution
  4. NaOH                  - 1.0 M sodium hydroxide; deprotection agent

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVICE SETUP
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  - DMF bottom plate: chromium-coated glass, standard photolithographic fabrication
  - Dielectric layer : parylene-C (7 um)
  - Hydrophobic layer: Teflon AF 1600 (150 nm), spin-coated at 1500 rpm
  - Top plate        : ITO-coated glass, Teflon AF 1600 coated
  - Inter-plate gap  : ~140 um (2x double-sided tape spacer)
  - Actuation        : 160 V_RMS sine wave at 15 kHz; 104 pogo-pin holder
  - Heating/cooling  : 14.8 x 14.8 mm TEC/Peltier module (10 central electrodes
                       defined as reaction site)
  - Reagent delivery : stepper-motor-driven syringe system
  - Purification site: alumina disc (6 mm dia., neutral alumina 50-300 um in PDMS)
                       sandwiched between top and bottom plates

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 1 - Deliver [18F]Fluoride
  - Dispense no-carrier-added [18F]fluoride to the reaction site via syringe.

STEP 2 - Activate [18F] (Carrier Evaporation)
  - Heat [18F]fluoride droplet at 120 C for 10 min.
  - Evaporates [18O]-H2O carrier; TEC/Peltier heater used.

STEP 3 - Resuspend with Kryptofix K222 / K2CO3
  - Dispense Kryptofix K222 droplet and mix with activated [18F] for 5 s.
  - Perform MeCN azeotropic dry: heat at 120 C for 5 min to remove residual water.

STEP 4 - Merge Mannose Triflate with Activated [18F]
  - Dispense 30 mM mannose triflate droplet (volume ratio 1:1 with [18F]).
  - Mix with activated [18F] droplet for 10 s to form reaction droplet.

STEP 5 - Fluorination (Radiolabeling)
  - Heat reaction droplet at 100 C for 5 min.
  - Nucleophilic substitution incorporates [18F] into mannose triflate scaffold.

STEP 6 - Deprotection (NaOH Hydrolysis)
  - Dispense 1.0 M NaOH droplet; mix with reaction droplet for 5 s.
  - Heat at 50 C for 5 min.
  - Hydrolyses the intermediate to yield crude [18F]FDG at room temperature.

STEP 7 - On-Chip Alumina Disc Purification
  - Actuate crude [18F]FDG droplet to the purification site (6 mm alumina disc).
  - Incubate at 25 C for 40 min; move droplet around adjacent electrodes to
    enhance contact with disc.
  - Removes Kryptofix K222, unreacted [18F]fluoride, and free F-.
  - Expected purity: ~93.05 +/- 2.46%.
  - After incubation, actuate purified droplet away from disc; collect manually
    by pipette for downstream processing.

STEP 8 - Detect Fluorination Efficiency (Quality Gate)
  - Analyse purified product by radioactive TLC (silica gel HLF plates).
  - Detection time: 30 s.
  - Quality threshold: fluorination efficiency >= 70%.
    PASS (>= 70%) -> drain / collect product for use.
    FAIL (< 70%)  -> do not collect; dispose.

STEP 9 - Waste Disposal
  - Dispose all final merged droplet variables:
    protected18F (crude [18F]FDG), activatedF18 (activated [18F] intermediate),
    reactionDroplet (fluorination intermediate).
  - Note: precursor variables (f18Drop, k222Drop, mannoseTriflate, naohDrop)
    were consumed into these during mix operations and no longer exist.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DETECTION & ANALYSIS INSTRUMENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  - Dose calibrator         : CRC 55 TR (Capintec) - radioactivity measurement
  - TLC scanner             : MiniGITA star (Raytest) - fluorination efficiency
  - TLC plates              : Silica Gel HLF 250 um, 10x20 cm scored (Analtech)
  - Gamma spectrometer      : in-house; identity and purity of [18F]fluoride

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
NOTES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  - The OFAT method requires only 8 experiments (1 base + 7 variable) compared
    to 2187 experiments needed for a full 3^7 factorial design.
  - Significant parameters identified by OFAT (p < 0.05, t-test):
      mannose triflate concentration, NaOH concentration, radiolabeling
      temperature, deprotection time, mannose triflate / [18F] volume ratio.
  - Non-significant parameters: radiolabeling time, deprotection temperature.
  - ML model (Ridge regression, 55-experiment database, 80/20 train/test split,
    10-fold cross-validation) further improved overall yield to 79.13%.
  - Conditions predicted for 100% incorporation (110 C, 1.4 M NaOH, 90 mM
    mannose triflate) were not practically achievable on-chip due to poor droplet
    movement fidelity at extreme concentrations and temperatures.

================================================================================

description:
Source link: [https://www.neogen.com/globalassets/pim/assets/original/10006/d131519.pdf](https://www.google.com/search?q=https://www.neogen.com/globalassets/pim/assets/original/10006/d131519.pdf)
Paper doi: N/A (manufacturer technical bulletin — Neogen Corporation, Fentanyl ELISA Kit Instructions, Product #131519)
Demonstration video: https://1drv.ms/v/s!AqwZF7jQGx_IgahJFK519Id1HCad4g

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Competitive ELISA for trace quantities of fentanyl and/or other metabolites in human urine, blood, or oral fluid. This version of the workflow has been adapted to run as a sequence of droplet operations on a digital microfluidic biochip (DMFB) instead of a standard 96-well plate.

REAGENTS USED:

* Sample (urine, blood, or oral fluid)
* Drug-enzyme conjugate (fentanyl labeled with horseradish peroxidase)
* Wash buffer (diluted 10X phosphate buffered saline with surfactant)
* K-Blue Substrate (stabilized 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine / TMB)
* Acid stop solution (1N H2SO4)

STEPS:

1. Combine 20 units of the sample with 100 units of the drug-enzyme conjugate. Mix for 60 seconds.
2. Incubate the combined mixture at 23C (room temperature) for 45 minutes. During this time, any free fentanyl in the sample competes with the enzyme-labeled conjugate for a limited number of antibody binding sites — this competition is the basis of the test.
3. Wash the reaction three times: each wash cycle combines 300 units of wash buffer with the reaction droplet, mixes for 45 seconds, and removes unbound material before moving to detection.
4. Add 100 units of K-Blue (TMB) substrate to the washed reaction and mix for 60 seconds. Incubate at 23C for 30 minutes to allow the color reaction to develop.
5. Add 100 units of acid stop solution and mix for 10 seconds to halt color development and shift the color from blue to yellow.
6. Measure the resulting absorbance signal to obtain the reading. Discard the sample afterward.

INTERPRETATION: This is a one-step competitive immunoassay. Free fentanyl in the sample and the enzyme-labeled conjugate compete for a fixed number of antibody binding sites on the plate. After washing away anything unbound, the remaining bound conjugate is revealed by the K-Blue (TMB) color reaction. Less color development means more drug was present in the sample (competing more successfully for binding sites); more color development means less or no drug was present. A result is typically called positive if the sample's absorbance reading is at or below the laboratory's designated cutoff calibrator, and negative if it is above.

---

## A NOTE ON HOW CLOSELY THIS MATCHES THE CITED SOURCE

This is an exact numeric match to the cited Neogen protocol across every value: sample volume (20 units), conjugate volume (100 units), first incubation time (45 minutes), wash count and volume (3 times, 300 units), substrate volume (100 units), second incubation time (30 minutes), and stop solution volume (100 units) all match the source exactly.

An earlier version of this protocol's droplet program included a second, separate antibody/enzyme incubation-and-wash stage (resembling a two-step "sandwich" ELISA) and attempted to record the result using a "fluorescence" detect type. No real fentanyl or other small-molecule drug immunoassay kit was found using that structure: a two-step format requires the target molecule to be large enough for two antibodies to bind it simultaneously, which a small drug molecule (a "hapten") is not large enough to support. Every real urine drug-screening kit checked uses the one-step competitive format reflected in the steps above. Furthermore, TMB is a strictly colorimetric substrate requiring absorbance detection. The two-step fluorescent version is treated as a non-representative artifact of the original test file, while this corrected protocol represents the valid, biologically sound real-world assay.

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Flexible & Transparent Digital Microfluidics Fabrication Protocol (Droplet Manipulation and Actuation Characterization on an ITO/PET/PE EWOD Device)

REAGENTS USED:
  - DI Water (droplet manipulation demo and contact-angle/leakage/driving-voltage characterization, 8-10 uL droplets)
  - 0.1 M Sodium Chloride Solution (contact-angle characterization, 10 uL droplets)
  - 1 M Sodium Chloride Solution (contact-angle characterization, 10 uL droplets)

STEPS:
1. Droplet Manipulation Demo: A DI water droplet is dispensed onto the transparent ITO/PET electrode array (2 mm x 2 mm electrodes, 0.5 mm spacing) and actuated by electrowetting to move straight and turn across the array.
2. Droplet Merging Demo: A second DI water droplet is dispensed and actuated to merge with the first droplet on the same electrode array.
3. Contact Angle Characterization: DI water, 0.1 M NaCl, and 1 M NaCl droplets (10 uL each) are individually dispensed and actuated under increasing AC voltage (1 kHz); the contact angle of each droplet is measured, decreasing nearly linearly with voltage before reaching saturation.
4. Leakage Current Characterization: A droplet is dispensed and held between two electrodes on the Rain-X-treated PE film and PET substrate; the AC voltage supply is swept from 250 Vrms to 450 Vrms in 25 V increments, with the leakage current density measured five times at each voltage step.
5. Minimum Driving Voltage Characterization: DI water droplets of 8, 10, and 12 uL are each dispensed and actuated with electrode on/off switching times of 1, 2, 3, and 4 s, and the minimum voltage required for reliable droplet movement is measured at each combination.

INTERPRETATION: Successful device performance is confirmed by reliable droplet dispensing, translocation, and merging on the thin (less than 200 um), flexible, and optically transparent ITO/PET/PE device; a water contact angle increase from 78.3 to 103.2 degrees after Rain-X treatment; leakage current densities that remain low (tens to ~190 nA/mm2) across the 250-450 Vrms operating range, confirming the PE film is an acceptable thin dielectric; contact angles for DI water and NaCl solutions that decrease with increasing voltage toward saturation; and minimum driving voltages that decrease with slower electrode on/off switching and increase with droplet volume, together validating the device as a low-cost, transparent alternative to conventional glass/silicon EWOD chips for colorimetric and optical droplet-based assays.

metadata.notes: This paper is primarily a device-fabrication study (laser ablation of ITO on PET, PE film dielectric lamination, Rain-X hydrophobic surface treatment); those steps have no BioScript equivalent since they are substrate/electrode manufacturing operations, not droplet operations, and are intentionally not modeled. The authored BioScript code instead captures the paper's on-chip droplet-manipulation and actuation-characterization experiments, which are the only parts of the paper expressed as chip-level droplet actions: the droplet movement/merging demo (Figure 1b,c), the contact-angle test across three solutions (Figure 9a), the leakage-current voltage sweep (Figure 8), and the minimum-driving-voltage test across droplet volumes and electrode on/off times (Figure 9b). Because BioScript has no primitive for droplet translocation, spatial movement (straight/turn) is approximated as a self-mix, consistent with how droplet transport was modeled in other translated protocols. Because BioScript has no primitive for AC voltage, voltage magnitude, or contact-angle optical measurement, 'detect fluorescence' is used as a generic stand-in readout for the contact-angle, leakage-current, and minimum-driving-voltage measurements, and the specific voltage/current values themselves are not encoded -- only the repeat-loop structure (9 voltage steps x 5 repeats for leakage; 3 volumes x 4 on/off times for minimum voltage) approximates the paper's test matrices.

description:
================================================================================
  PROTOCOL: FUCOSYLTRANSFERASE INHIBITION ASSAY USING IMAGE-ANALYSIS
             AND DIGITAL MICROFLUIDICS (DMF)
================================================================================

  Source Link : https://www.shihmicrolab.ca/_files/ugd/f0a828_fb291b4dee6147cd9c47c11d6308710c.pdf
  Paper DOI   : https://doi.org/10.1063/1.5088517
  Journal     : Biomicrofluidics 13, 034106 (2019)

================================================================================
  OVERVIEW
================================================================================

This protocol describes a fluorescence-based inhibition assay for
H. pylori alpha(1,3)-fucosyltransferase (FucT) performed on a digital
microfluidic (DMF) device. The assay uses the labeled synthetic disaccharide
4-methylumbelliferyl beta-N-acetyllactosaminide (MU-beta-LacNAc) as a
substrate. When FucT is active, it fucosylates MU-beta-LacNAc, preventing
its hydrolysis by glycoside hydrolases and resulting in low fluorescence.
When FucT is inhibited (e.g., by GDP), the substrate remains unfucosylated,
gets cleaved by BgaA and SpHex, and releases fluorescent 4-methylumbelliferone
(4-MU). Inhibition curves spanning four orders of magnitude are generated
on-device via serial dilution, with concentrations verified by an image-based
"pixel count" method.

================================================================================
  PLATFORM & DEVICE SPECIFICATIONS
================================================================================

  Platform        : Two-plate digital microfluidic (DMF) chip
  Chip dimensions : 3 x 2 in. (75 x 50 mm)
  Electrodes      : 93 actuation electrodes (avg. width ~1 mm) +
                    10 reservoir electrodes (4.1 x 3 mm^2 each) +
                    1 waste collection electrode
                    Total: 103 electrodes
  Electrode shape : "Skewed-wave" (sinusoidal intercalating, ~4.0 x 0.87 mm^2)
                    Minimum angles ~90 deg to prevent dielectric breakdown
  Electrode gap   : 30 um (interelectrode average)
  Plate gap       : ~140 um (two layers of double-sided tape)
  Top plate       : ITO-coated glass (Rs = 15-25 ohm)
  Bottom plate    : Chromium electrode-bearing glass with FluoroPel PFC1601V
                    hydrophobic coating
  Driving voltage : 120-160 VRMS at 15 kHz
  Automation      : Arduino Uno + PCB relay board + PaseMaker software
                    (Python 2.7, LLGUI.exe interface)
                    GitHub: https://github.com/shihmicrolab/Automation
  Imaging         : 3.0 MP CMOS USB camera (EO-3112C, Edmund Optics) +
                    10x C-mount close focus zoom lens (54363, Edmund Optics)
  Unit droplet    : ~500 nL

================================================================================
  REAGENTS & SOLUTION PREPARATION
================================================================================

  All solutions contain 0.05% Pluronics F-68 to prevent protein biofouling.
  All solutions are covered with a thin layer of silicone oil (applied by
  touching the droplet surface with an oil-coated pipette tip).

  1. HEPES BUFFER
     - 25 mM HEPES, pH 7.0
     - 0.05% Pluronics F-68
     - Use: diluent for serial dilutions and blank control

  2. GDP INHIBITOR STOCK
     - 80 mM GDP (guanosine 5'-diphosphate) in 25 mM HEPES pH 7.0
     - 0.05% Pluronics F-68
     - Use: inhibitor stock for serial dilution

  3. FucT ENZYME SOLUTION
     - 0.135 mg/mL H. pylori FucT stock
     - Working concentration: 0.03 mg/mL (0.6 nM) after dilution on-chip
     - Buffer: 25 mM HEPES pH 7.0, 0.05% Pluronics F-68
     - Note: Recombinant FucT expression follows previously described
       procedures (see supplementary material of source paper)

  4. GLYCOSYLATION MIX (reaction-initiating solution)
     Stock concentrations (2x, before on-chip dilution):
     - 40 mM MgCl2
     - 0.04 mM MU-beta-LacNAc
     - 0.08 mM GDP-fucose
     - 25 mM HEPES pH 7.0, 0.05% Pluronics F-68
     Final on-chip concentrations (after 1:2 dilution):
     - 10 mM MgCl2
     - 0.01 mM MU-beta-LacNAc
     - 0.02 mM GDP-fucose

  5. HYDROLYSIS MIX (reaction-stopping solution)
     Stock concentrations (5x, before on-chip dilution):
     - 125 mM EDTA
     - 0.25 mM BgaA (beta-galactosidase from S. pneumoniae, ~247 kDa)
     - 0.25 mM SpHex (N-acetylhexosaminidase from S. plicatus)
     - 25 mM HEPES pH 7.0, 0.05% Pluronics F-68
     Final on-chip concentrations (after 1:5 dilution):
     - 25 mM EDTA
     - 0.05 mM BgaA
     - 0.05 mM SpHex
     Note: BgaA and SpHex sequentially cleave unfucosylated MU-beta-LacNAc
     to release fluorescent 4-MU. Both enzymes must be present for signal.

  6. GLYCINE SOLUTION (optional, for bell-curve correction)
     - 1 M glycine, pH 10.4
     - Use: 5-fold dilution of final reaction droplets if a bell-shaped
       dose-response curve is observed (caused by GDP quenching of 4-MU)

================================================================================
  ASSAY PRINCIPLE
================================================================================

  UNINHIBITED (low/no GDP):
    MU-beta-LacNAc --[FucT + GDP-fucose]--> Fucosylated-MU-beta-LacNAc
    Fucosylated substrate is NOT cleaved by BgaA/SpHex --> LOW fluorescence

  INHIBITED (high GDP):
    GDP competes with GDP-fucose at FucT active site --> FucT blocked
    MU-beta-LacNAc remains unfucosylated
    Unfucosylated MU-beta-LacNAc --[BgaA then SpHex]--> 4-MU (fluorescent)
    --> HIGH fluorescence

  Fluorescence readout: lambda_ex = 365 nm, lambda_em = 460 nm

================================================================================
  ON-DEVICE PROTOCOL (42-STEP DMF PROCEDURE)
================================================================================

------------------------------------------------------------------------
  STEP 1 — Prime HEPES Buffer Reservoirs
------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - Manually pipette five droplets (~2.7 uL each) of 25 mM HEPES buffer
    onto five separate reservoirs on the DMF chip.
  - Place the ITO top plate on top of the device.
  - Apply silicone oil shell to each droplet using an oil-coated pipette tip.
  - These reservoirs serve as diluents for the serial dilution (Steps 3-10).

------------------------------------------------------------------------
  STEP 2 — Load GDP Inhibitor Stock
------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - Pipette a ~3.1 uL droplet of 80 mM GDP solution to one of the five
    pipetting inlet electrodes (aligned to the edge of the ITO).
  - Apply a driving potential to the inlet electrode to pull the droplet
    under the ITO into the reservoir gap.
  - Apply silicone oil shell.
  - This minimizes time on-chip before use, reducing biofouling risk.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
  STEPS 3-10 — Serial ~5.5-Fold Dilution of GDP (6 Concentrations)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Each dilution step:
    a. Dispense one unit droplet (~500 nL) of the current GDP solution.
    b. Move the unit droplet into the adjacent buffer-primed reservoir.
    c. Mix by pulling the merged volume along the linear path and actuating
       the reservoir electrode to pull it back (creates ~1:5 dilution).
    d. Dispense one unit droplet of the resulting dilution for the next step.

  Resulting GDP concentrations (calculated by pixel count method):
    Concentration 1: 36.0 +/- 4.25 mM
    Concentration 2:  6.2 +/- 0.40 mM
    Concentration 3:  1.1 +/- 0.01 mM
    Concentration 4:  0.22 +/- 0.01 mM
    Concentration 5:  0.04 +/- 0.006 mM
    Concentration 6:  0.006 +/- 0.001 mM

------------------------------------------------------------------------
  STEP 11 — Load Negative Control (Blank)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - Pipette a ~3.1 uL droplet of 25 mM HEPES buffer (no GDP) to an
    empty reservoir via pipetting inlet (same method as Step 2).
  - This serves as the 0 mM GDP blank control.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
  STEPS 12-19 — Prepare 1 uL Reaction Droplets for Each Concentration
------------------------------------------------------------------------
  For each of the 7 GDP concentrations (including blank):
    a. Dispense two unit droplets (~500 nL each) from the reservoir.
    b. Merge the two unit droplets into one ~1 uL droplet.
    c. Actuate the merged droplet away from the reservoir path.
    d. Actuate the remaining excess droplet in the reservoir to the waste
       electrode and wick away using a paper strip.
    e. Return the merged 1 uL droplet to its reservoir.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
  STEPS 20-26 — Add FucT Enzyme to Each GDP Droplet
------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - Pipette a ~3.1 uL droplet of 0.135 mg/mL FucT stock to a reservoir
    inlet (as in Step 2).
  - For each of the 7 GDP concentrations:
    a. Dispense one unit droplet (~500 nL) of FucT from the reservoir.
    b. Merge and mix the FucT droplet with the 1 uL GDP droplet
       in its respective reservoir (mix time: 5 s).
  - Incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
    Purpose: GDP competitively binds to the FucT active site.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
  STEPS 27-33 — Add Glycosylation Mix (Initiate Fucosylation Reaction)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - For each of the 7 reaction droplets:
    a. Dispense one unit droplet (~500 nL) of glycosylation mix.
    b. Merge and mix with the FucT + GDP droplet (mix time: 5 s).
  - Incubate for 10 minutes at room temperature.
    Purpose: FucT transfers fucose from GDP-fucose onto MU-beta-LacNAc.
    If GDP has inhibited FucT, MU-beta-LacNAc remains unfucosylated.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
  STEPS 34-41 — Add Hydrolysis Mix (Stop Reaction / Reveal Signal)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - For each of the 7 reaction droplets:
    a. Dispense one unit droplet (~500 nL) of hydrolysis mix.
    b. Merge and mix with the reaction droplet (mix time: 5 s).
  - Incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
    Purpose: BgaA cleaves galactose, then SpHex cleaves N-acetylglucosamine
    from unfucosylated MU-beta-LacNAc, releasing fluorescent 4-MU.
    Fucosylated substrate is sterically blocked and yields no signal.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
  STEP 42 — Fluorescence Detection
------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - Align and mount the DMF device onto a Nunc 384-well black polystyrene
    microplate.
  - Scan the device surface using a ClarioSTAR monochromator microplate
    reader (BMG Labtech):
      lambda_ex  : 360-365 nm
      lambda_em  : 450-460 nm
      Gain       : 750
      Focal height: 15.80 mm
      Flashes    : 40
      Scan step  : 30 x 30 pixel increments (each pixel = 10 mm^2)
  - Output: fluorescence heatmap of the entire chip surface.

================================================================================
  PIXEL COUNT (PC) — IMAGE-BASED CONCENTRATION METHOD
================================================================================

  The "pixel count" (PC) method calculates droplet volumes and inhibitor
  concentrations directly from on-device images, without requiring external
  detectors or plate readers at the dilution step.

  Procedure:
    1. Capture an image of the droplet using the on-board CMOS camera.
    2. Binarize the image (convert to 1s and 0s) to enhance droplet boundaries.
    3. Apply edge-finding algorithm to trace the droplet boundary.
    4. Calculate droplet area from the traced boundary.
    5. Calculate droplet volume:
         Volume = droplet area x 140 um (plate gap height)
    6. Apply C1V1 = C2V2 to calculate the concentration after each dilution.

  Validation: PC volumes agree more closely with micropipette readings than
  gravimetric (precision balance) measurements. Fluorescence deviation
  between PC-calculated and direct fluorescence measurements is <0.05%.
  Homogeneity of dispensed droplets from the same mixed source: <3% CV.

================================================================================
  OPTIONAL: GLYCINE DILUTION (Bell-Curve Correction)
================================================================================

  If the dose-response curve shows a bell-shaped (non-sigmoidal) profile
  at the highest GDP concentrations (~40 mM), this is likely due to
  GDP quenching of 4-MU fluorescence rather than a true inhibition effect.

  Correction procedure:
    - After the hydrolysis incubation (Step 41), dilute each reaction
      droplet 5-fold into 1 M glycine, pH 10.4.
    - This restores the sigmoidal curve shape and improves reproducibility
      by reducing solution viscosity.
    - Expected IC50 after glycine dilution:
        DMF device  : 0.093 +/- 0.037 mM GDP
        Well plate  : 0.114 +/- 0.086 mM GDP
        (Not significantly different: p = 0.53, alpha = 0.05)

================================================================================
  DATA ANALYSIS — IC50 CALCULATION
================================================================================

  Fluorescence values are blank-corrected (subtract buffer-only signal).

  GDP concentrations are determined using the pixel count method.

  4-MU concentrations are calculated using a linear calibration curve
  derived from 4-MU standards pipetted and measured on-device.

  Dose-response curve fit (least squares):
    y = b + ((a - b) / (1 + (x / c)^d))

    where:
      y = fluorescence signal
      x = GDP concentration (mM)
      a = maximum signal (top plateau)
      b = minimum signal (bottom plateau)
      c = IC50 value
      d = Hill coefficient

  Note: Exclude ~40 mM GDP data points if bell-shaped behavior is observed
  before glycine dilution, as they represent artefactual signal quenching.

================================================================================
  ASSAY PERFORMANCE METRICS
================================================================================

  Z-factor (well-plate validation)   : 0.78  (n = 8)
  Droplet dispensing variability     : ~9% CV
  On-chip fluorescence homogeneity   : <3% CV
  PC vs. fluorescence deviation      : <0.05%
  Orders of magnitude of dilution    : 4 (10,000-fold range)
  Silicone oil effect on 4-MU signal : Not significant (p = 0.143)

================================================================================
  CONTROLS
================================================================================

  Positive control (max signal):
    - 0 nM FucT + full hydrolysis mix
    - Expected: ~6 uM 4-MU released from 10 uM MU-beta-LacNAc

  Negative control (min signal):
    - 0.6 nM FucT, no hydrolysis mix
    - Expected: minimal fluorescence (~1 uM 4-MU baseline)

  Blank:
    - 0 mM GDP + 0.6 nM FucT + full glycosylation and hydrolysis mix
    - Expected: low fluorescence (FucT fully active, substrate fucosylated)

================================================================================
  CRITICAL NOTES
================================================================================

  1. BIOFOULING PREVENTION
     - Add 0.05% Pluronics F-68 to ALL solutions containing proteins
       (FucT, BgaA, SpHex).
     - Apply silicone oil shell to all droplets; this is the single most
       effective measure: it allows >24 consecutive droplet movements vs.
       failure within 4-8 movements without oil.
     - Use HEPES buffer (not Tris): Tris caused fouling after ~4 movements
       even with Pluronics; HEPES lasted ~8 movements. With oil + HEPES +
       Pluronics, >24 movements were achieved without slowing.
     - Load protein solutions via pipetting inlet electrodes and use
       immediately; avoid long dwell times on the reservoir surface.

  2. ELECTRODE DESIGN
     - Use "skewed-wave" shaped electrodes. Conventional square electrodes
       of equivalent area require 9-13 electrodes to span the same distance
       and require 27% larger minimum droplet volumes to avoid stranding.
     - Sinusoidal curves with minimum ~90 deg angles prevent dielectric
       breakdown (which occurs at >10^8 V/cm with pointed electrode shapes).

  3. DROPLET VOLUME CONSISTENCY
     - Consistent dispensing is critical for accurate inhibition curves.
     - Verify all droplet volumes using the pixel count method at each
       serial dilution step.

  4. 4-MU FLUORESCENCE SENSITIVITY
     - 4-MU fluorescence is sensitive to ionic conditions, pH, and water
       content. Prepare all 4-MU standards in the same buffer and surfactant
       conditions as the reaction samples.
     - The reaction components (buffer + Pluronics) may enhance 4-MU
       fluorescence above the theoretical maximum; account for this when
       interpreting absolute signal values.

  5. GDP QUENCHING ARTEFACT
     - At GDP concentrations of ~40 mM, a false drop in fluorescence signal
       may be observed. This is NOT inhibition reversal but rather
       concentration-dependent quenching of 4-MU by GDP.
     - Apply glycine dilution (see above) to correct this effect.

================================================================================
END OF PROTOCOL
================================================================================

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidics (DMF) Colorimetric Two-Enzyme Glucose Assay with Integrated Absorbance Detection, on an Oil-Filled Two-Plate Device

REAGENTS USED:
  - Glucose Oxidase/Peroxidase Colorimetric Reagent (two-enzyme reaction mixture)
  - Physiological Sample (e.g., whole blood, serum, urine, or saliva)

STEPS:
1. Dispense a droplet of the glucose oxidase/peroxidase colorimetric reagent.
2. Dispense a droplet of the physiological sample to be tested.
3. Merge and mix the reagent and sample droplets to initiate the two-enzyme colorimetric reaction.
4. Incubate the merged reaction droplet at 37 C to allow the coupled glucose oxidase/peroxidase reaction to develop a color change proportional to glucose concentration.
5. Measure the absorbance of the reaction droplet with the integrated LED/photodiode absorbance detector.
6. Discard the analyzed reaction droplet.

INTERPRETATION: Successful glucose quantification is confirmed by a linear absorbance response over the clinically relevant range of approximately 25-300 mg/dl glucose, with glucose values obtained from physiological samples (whole blood, serum, urine, saliva) that agree with reference measurements — except in the case of urine, where endogenous uric acid can interfere with the enzymatic reaction, underscoring the importance of sample pretreatment for clinical diagnostic use.

Paper doi: 10.1016/j.aca.2003.12.030
Demonstration video: No demonstration video located

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Colorimetric enzyme test strip reaction for measuring glucose concentration in a fluid sample, run as a series of small droplet reactions on a lab-on-a-chip device.

REAGENTS USED:
  - glucose sample: the fluid being tested; five separate portions are used, one per trial, so a small calibration-style series of readings can be built up
  - enzyme reagent: a ready-mixed reagent containing glucose oxidase and peroxidase along with a color-forming dye; it reacts with glucose to produce a colored product, with more color developing as more glucose is present
  - distilled water: used in a side reaction alongside the reagent, prepared and set aside for each trial but not measured

STEPS:
1. Place a small portion of the glucose sample on the chip.
2. Add a small portion of the enzyme reagent next to it.
3. Bring the two together and mix them for about 10 seconds so the reaction can begin.
4. Hold the combined droplet in place and measure the color/light signal it gives off for 30 seconds. This reading reflects how much glucose was in the sample.
5. Separately, combine a portion of distilled water with a portion of the enzyme reagent, mix for 30 seconds, and discard it.
6. Repeat steps 1-5 four more times, for a total of five trials. In each trial the amount of glucose sample stays the same, but the amount of enzyme reagent added is changed (first a small amount, then twice as much, then twice as much again, then twice as much again, before returning to the original small amount for the fifth trial).
7. After all five trials are complete, discard the reacted droplets from each trial.

INTERPRETATION: Each of the five trials produces a signal reading whose strength corresponds to how much glucose was present in that sample. Comparing the five readings against each other (or against known glucose standards run the same way) lets a technician build a calibration curve and estimate the glucose concentration of an unknown sample. A stronger signal generally means more glucose reacted with the reagent.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
A NOTE ON HOW CLOSELY THIS MATCHES THE CITED SOURCE
----------------------------------------------------------------------
The cited paper (Srinivasan, Pamula & Fair, 2004) describes an electrowetting droplet-chip glucose assay using a colorimetric enzyme-kinetic method (Trinder's reaction): a glucose oxidase/peroxidase/dye reagent droplet is merged with a sample droplet, mixed for about 15 seconds, and the color signal is read continuously for at least 30 seconds. That final step - a mix, then a 30-second optical read whose strength scales with glucose concentration - matches this .bs file's five detect steps exactly on timing (30s) and closely on mixing time (10s in the code vs. 15s in the paper).

Two things differ and are worth being upfront about:

1. In the real protocol, the five (or more) calibration points are made by varying the GLUCOSE CONCENTRATION of the sample while keeping the reagent-to-sample ratio fixed. In this .bs file, the glucose amount is held constant across all five trials and it is instead the REAGENT amount that is varied (10, 20, 40, 80, then back to 10 units). This is a different way of generating a multi-point series, and it does not exactly reproduce the paper's dilution method, though the end goal (multiple readings to compare against each other) is the same. This is a benchmark-authoring choice, not something we changed.

2. The paper explicitly states that this kinetic method "does not require a blank reading." This .bs file nonetheless prepares a water+reagent droplet in every trial and discards it without ever reading it. It does not affect the final glucose readings (it is disposed of and never feeds into any detect step), but it is an extra, scientifically unnecessary step relative to the cited source. We are documenting it rather than silently removing it, since it is part of the original benchmark code.

No structural/dependency bugs were found in this file - each of the five glucose+reagent reaction droplets is read via detect before being discarded, so every reported reading is genuinely derived from its corresponding glucose sample. The .bs file also declares a "Sample" material that is never dispensed or used anywhere in the code; this appears to be a leftover/unused declaration from the original benchmark authoring and has no effect on execution.

Overall: the reaction chemistry, the fixed 30-second read, and the multi-trial calibration-style structure all point to this being an adaptation of the Srinivasan et al. 2004 droplet glucose assay for the BioScript benchmark suite, with the two documented differences above (what is varied per trial, and the extra unread blank step).

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Cell-Free Glycoprotein Biosynthesis Protocol on Digital Microfluidic Chips (Flow-Based Microfluidic System for Cell-Free Glycoprotein Biosynthesis)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Plasmid DNA Stream (pJL1-sfGFP-DQNAT-6xHis acceptor protein plasmid, energy mix, salts, and metabolites)
  - S30 Cell-Free Extract Stream (E. coli BL21 Star (DE3) S30 crude extract plus T7 RNA polymerase)
  - CjLLOs Reagent (C. jejuni lipid-linked oligosaccharides bearing the GalNAc5(Glc)Bac heptasaccharide, glycan donor for the surface-tethered CjPglB oligosaccharyltransferase)
  - Wash Buffer (PBS with 10 mM imidazole, for IMAC resin washing)
  - Elution Buffer (PBS with 300 mM imidazole, for IMAC product recovery)

STEPS:
1. Protein Synthesis Module: A plasmid/energy/salts/metabolites stream and an S30 extract/T7 RNA polymerase stream are combined at the inlet of a serpentine microfluidic chip and mixed by diffusion as they travel through the channel; each chip provides a 30 min reaction residence time, and multiple chips are linked in series (up to four chips for a 2 h total residence time) to continuously synthesize sfGFP-DQNAT-6xHis.
2. Protein Glycosylation Module: The synthesized protein stream is continuously flowed over CjPglB oligosaccharyltransferase that is site-specifically biotinylated and tethered to the channel surface (via silane-PEG5000-biotin/NeutrAvidin/biotin chemistry), together with CjLLO glycan donor; the device is held at 30 C and the reaction proceeds across a series of chips at 30 min residence time per chip, achieving up to 100% glycosylation efficiency within 2 h.
3. Protein Purification Module (Loading/Flowthrough): The glycosylated protein stream is passed through a channel packed with Ni2+-charged affinity resin held in place by an array of posts at the outlet; hexahistidine-tagged glycoprotein binds the resin while unbound material exits as the flowthrough fraction.
4. Protein Purification Module (Wash): The inlet stream is switched to wash buffer (PBS + 10 mM imidazole) at 2 uL/min to remove non-specifically bound proteins and cellular debris from the resin bed; the wash fraction is collected.
5. Protein Purification Module (Elution): The inlet stream is switched to elution buffer (PBS + 300 mM imidazole) at 2 uL/min to recover the purified hexahistidine-tagged glycoprotein product as the elution fraction; the resin-bound flowthrough droplet is then discarded.

INTERPRETATION: Successful glycoprotein biosynthesis is confirmed by significantly increased sfGFP titers under continuous flow relative to batch/off-chip CFPS (Figure 2A), immunoblot detection of the monoglycosylated (g1) product with anti-His and hR6 (anti-heptasaccharide) antibodies confirming efficient on-chip glycosylation comparable to off-chip untethered reactions (Figure 3C), and recovery of purified glycoprotein product at 78 +/- 10% purity with 45 +/- 14% capture efficiency via the on-chip IMAC module (Figure 4), together demonstrating a first-in-kind modular glycosylation-on-a-chip platform for continuous, decentralized glycoprotein biomanufacturing.

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code is a direct translation of the paper's three-module continuous-flow architecture (Figure 1): protein synthesis (module 1), glycosylation (module 2), and IMAC purification (module 3). Because BioScript's grammar has no primitives for flow rate, serially-linked chip chaining, or surface-tethered enzymes/resin (all central to this paper's design), several structural approximations were made. The four-chip, 2 h CFPS residence time (Figure 2C) is modeled as one initial mix plus a repeat-3 loop of 30 min mixes (four total 30 min stages). The surface-tethered CjPglB enzyme is not itself a dispensable manifest -- since BioScript cannot represent an immobilized catalyst distinct from the reaction volume -- so glycosylation is modeled as mixing the CFPS product with the cjllos_reagent manifest at 30c, repeated to approximate the multi-chip flow-through described for the tethered-enzyme system. Likewise, the Ni2+-charged IMAC resin bed is a fixed solid phase within the device (Figure 4A) with no corresponding manifest; only the wash_buffer and elution_buffer streams that flow over it are dispensed, and binding/flowthrough is represented as a self-mix step rather than a true solid-phase capture operation. The detection modality in the paper is fluorescence imaging and immunoblotting of sfGFP (Figures 2, 3), so 'detect fluorescence' is used directly and is not a stand-in for a different modality, unlike in some other translated protocols.

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic Hemagglutination Assays for Blood Typing, Donor Compatibility Testing, and Hematocrit Analysis

REAGENTS USED:
  - Whole Blood
  - Reconstitution Solvent
  - Anti-A, Anti-B, Anti-AB, and Anti-D Blood Typing Antibodies (lyophilized)
  - Hematocrit Reagent (chemical agglutination agent)

STEPS:
1. Reconstitute lyophilized antibodies and hematocrit reagents using the reconstitution solvent and mix for 5s.
2. Meter whole-blood unit-droplets for each parallel test channel (A, B, AB, D, and hematocrit).
3. Merge each whole-blood droplet with its respective reconstituted reagent and mix for 10s to form the test droplet.
4. Perform digital aperture absorbance detection (DAAD) imaging readout to score agglutination states for the ABO/RhD blood-typing panel.
5. Apply threshold conditions to selectively dispose of nonagglutinated (negative) droplets, and perform quantitative DAAD scoring for hematocrit.
6. Clear all remaining test droplets from the array.

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic (DMF) Screening of Hepatotoxicity Using 3D Self-Assembled Hepatic Organoids (HepG2/NIH-3T3 Spheroids)

REAGENTS USED:
  - HepG2/NIH-3T3 Collagen Organoid Suspension (free-floating hepatic organoids self-assembled from HepG2 hepatocyte-like cells and NIH-3T3 fibroblasts in a collagen hydrogel matrix, confined on-chip by SU-8 pillars)
  - Culture Media (standard growth media used for organoid maintenance and as diluent for the on-chip acetaminophen dilution series)
  - Acetaminophen (cytotoxic hepatotoxin, used to generate a dose-response dilution series on-chip)
  - Hoechst 33342 (nuclear stain, labels total cell population)
  - Caspase-3 Activity Reporter / NucView488 (fluorogenic apoptosis marker)
  - Ethidium Homodimer-1 (necrosis marker, labels compromised-membrane/dead cells)

STEPS:
1. Organoid Seeding: Dispense the HepG2/NIH-3T3 collagen organoid suspension and merge with culture media; incubate 60 min at 37 C to allow the organoids to settle and equilibrate on-chip (confined by SU-8 pillars).
2-6. Dose-Response Loop (repeated once per acetaminophen concentration in the on-chip dilution series):
   a. Dispense a fresh acetaminophen droplet and a culture-media diluent droplet; merge to form one dose of the dilution series.
   b. Merge the diluted acetaminophen dose with the seeded organoid droplet; incubate 24 h at 37 C to expose the organoids to the hepatotoxin.
   c. Dispense Hoechst 33342 and merge with the treated organoid droplet to stain total nuclei.
   d. Dispense the caspase-3 activity reporter and merge with the Hoechst-stained droplet; incubate 30 min at 37 C to develop the apoptosis signal.
   e. Dispense ethidium homodimer-1 and merge with the apoptosis-stained droplet; incubate 15 min at 37 C to develop the necrosis signal.
   f. Detect apoptotic-marker fluorescence on the fully stained droplet. If the apoptotic signal is at or above a defined toxicity threshold, discard the droplet (organoid scored as apoptotic/toxic response).
   g. Otherwise, detect necrotic-marker fluorescence on the same droplet to score the necrotic fraction, then discard the droplet.
7. Repeat the dose-response loop across the acetaminophen concentration series to build the apoptotic-versus-necrotic population profile as a function of acetaminophen concentration.
8. End of Assay: Discard the residual seeded-organoid reservoir droplet.

INTERPRETATION: Successful hepatotoxicity screening is confirmed by a dose-dependent shift from an apoptotic-dominant response at intermediate acetaminophen concentrations (peaking near 10 mM) to a necrotic-dominant response at higher concentrations (e.g., 20 mM), consistent with 3D organoid culture recapitulating in vivo-like hepatotoxic responses not observed in comparable 2D (96-well plate) assays, supporting use of the DMF organ-on-a-chip platform for drug/toxicity screening.

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic (DMF) Screening of Hepatotoxicity Using 3D Self-Assembled Hepatic Organoids (HepG2/NIH-3T3 Spheroids)

REAGENTS USED:
  - HepG2/NIH-3T3 Collagen Organoid Suspension (free-floating hepatic organoids self-assembled from HepG2 hepatocyte-like cells and NIH-3T3 fibroblasts in a collagen hydrogel matrix, confined on-chip by SU-8 pillars)
  - Culture Media (standard growth media used for organoid maintenance and as diluent for the on-chip acetaminophen dilution series)
  - Acetaminophen (cytotoxic hepatotoxin, used to generate a dose-response dilution series on-chip)
  - Hoechst 33342 (nuclear stain, labels total cell population)
  - Caspase-3 Activity Reporter / NucView488 (fluorogenic apoptosis marker)
  - Ethidium Homodimer-1 (necrosis marker, labels compromised-membrane/dead cells)

STEPS:
1. Organoid Seeding: Dispense the HepG2/NIH-3T3 collagen organoid suspension and merge with culture media; incubate 60 min at 37 C to allow the organoids to settle and equilibrate on-chip (confined by SU-8 pillars).
2-6. Dose-Response Loop (repeated once per acetaminophen concentration in the on-chip dilution series):
   a. Dispense a fresh acetaminophen droplet and a culture-media diluent droplet; merge to form one dose of the dilution series.
   b. Merge the diluted acetaminophen dose with the seeded organoid droplet; incubate 24 h at 37 C to expose the organoids to the hepatotoxin.
   c. Dispense Hoechst 33342 and merge with the treated organoid droplet to stain total nuclei.
   d. Dispense the caspase-3 activity reporter and merge with the Hoechst-stained droplet; incubate 30 min at 37 C to develop the apoptosis signal.
   e. Dispense ethidium homodimer-1 and merge with the apoptosis-stained droplet; incubate 15 min at 37 C to develop the necrosis signal.
   f. Detect apoptotic-marker fluorescence on the fully stained droplet. If the apoptotic signal is at or above a defined toxicity threshold, discard the droplet (organoid scored as apoptotic/toxic response).
   g. Otherwise, detect necrotic-marker fluorescence on the same droplet to score the necrotic fraction, then discard the droplet.
7. Repeat the dose-response loop across the acetaminophen concentration series to build the apoptotic-versus-necrotic population profile as a function of acetaminophen concentration.
8. End of Assay: Discard the residual seeded-organoid reservoir droplet.

INTERPRETATION: Successful hepatotoxicity screening is confirmed by a dose-dependent shift from an apoptotic-dominant response at intermediate acetaminophen concentrations (peaking near 10 mM) to a necrotic-dominant response at higher concentrations (e.g., 20 mM), consistent with 3D organoid culture recapitulating in vivo-like hepatotoxic responses not observed in comparable 2D (96-well plate) assays, supporting use of the DMF organ-on-a-chip platform for drug/toxicity screening.

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Direct Competitive Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA) for Opiate (Heroin) Detection

REAGENTS USED:
  - Sample (Urine)
  - Immobilized Capture Antigen (Heroin enzyme)
  - Drug-Enzyme Conjugate (Heroin conjugate)
  - Wash Buffer
  - TMB Substrate (K-Blue substrate)
  - Stop Solution

STEPS:
1. Primary Incubation: Add 10 units of the urine sample and mix with the immobilized heroin enzyme. Add 100 units of the heroin drug-enzyme conjugate and mix for 60 seconds. Incubate the mixture at 23°C (room temperature) for 45 minutes to allow free heroin/opiates in the sample to compete with the conjugate for antibody binding sites. Discard the supernatant droplet.
2. Wash Cycle: Wash the reaction zone three times to remove any unbound sample and unbound conjugate. For each wash cycle, add 300 units of wash buffer, mix with the retained enzyme for 45 seconds, and discard the wash supernatant.
3. Substrate Development: Add 100 units of K-Blue substrate to the retained enzyme. Mix and incubate at 23°C for 30 minutes to allow the colorimetric reaction to develop.
4. Stop Reaction and Detection: Add 100 units of stop solution and mix for 60 seconds to halt the enzymatic reaction. Measure the resulting optical signal (absorbance) of the final droplet. Discard the final reaction mixture.

INTERPRETATION: The final signal intensity (absorbance) is inversely proportional to the concentration of heroin/opiates in the sample. A lower signal indicates a higher presence of heroin, while a higher signal indicates little to no heroin (as more conjugate successfully bound to the antibodies).

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A NOTE ON HOW CLOSELY THIS MATCHES THE CITED SOURCE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The authored BioScript code closely matches the Neogen Corporation commercial Opiate Group Forensic ELISA kit protocol. The standard microplate-based competitive ELISA for opiates (including heroin) has been adapted for a Digital Microfluidic Biochip (DMFB). Volumetric mismatches and optical detection errors (measuring fluorescence instead of absorbance) present in earlier iterations were corrected. The standard room temperature incubations are explicitly set to 23°C, the wash cycles reflect the discrete 3-cycle loop with 300 µL volumes, and the continuous multi-well reading has been successfully translated into a singular droplet absorbance detection step.

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic (Electrowetting) Colorimetric Enzyme-Kinetic Glucose Assay on Human Physiological Fluids (Serum, Plasma, Urine, Saliva)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Calibrant (100 mg dL-1 glucose standard solution, 1.5 uL droplets)
  - Glucose Reagent (6 U mL-1 glucose oxidase, 6 U mL-1 peroxidase, 6 mM 4-aminoantipyrine, 6 mM TOPS, in 0.1 M phosphate buffered saline pH 7.0, 1.5 uL droplets)
  - Plasma Sample (1.5 uL droplets)
  - Serum Sample (1.5 uL droplets)
  - Saliva Sample (spiked with glucose, 1.5 uL droplets)
  - Urine Sample (spiked with glucose, 1.5 uL droplets; subject to uric acid interference with the Trinder reaction)

STEPS:
1. Calibration run: Dispense a 1.5 uL calibrant droplet (100 mg/dL glucose standard) and a 1.5 uL glucose reagent droplet onto adjacent electrodes (electrode pitch 1.5 mm, spacer height 500 um).
2. Merge and mix the calibrant/reagent droplet by shuttling across multiple electrodes for 15 s.
3. Measure absorbance continuously for at least 30 s using the LED-photodiode setup (545 nm green LED, TSL257 photodiode) and compute RateCALIB from the slope of the absorbance-vs-time curve.
4. Plasma assay: Dispense a 1.5 uL plasma droplet and a 1.5 uL glucose reagent droplet, merge/mix for 15 s, and measure absorbance for at least 30 s to obtain RatePLASMA.
5. Serum assay: Repeat the same dispense/merge-mix/absorbance-read cycle using serum in place of plasma to obtain RateSERUM.
6. Saliva assay: Repeat the same cycle using (glucose-spiked) saliva to obtain RateSALIVA.
7. Urine assay: Repeat the same cycle using (glucose-spiked) urine to obtain RateURINE.
8. Concentration calculation: For each sample, compute CSAMPLE = (RateSAMPLE / RateCALIB) x 100 mg dL-1.
9. Reference comparison: Compare each on-chip concentration against a reference value obtained on a bench-top spectrophotometer (Gensys 20) using a conventional 100-fold dilution; note that the urine result shows a significant deviation from the reference value, attributed to interference by uric acid reacting with hydrogen peroxide in the Trinder reaction (interference that the 100-fold dilution in the reference method suppresses but the digital-microfluidic chip's 2-fold dilution does not).

INTERPRETATION: Successful glucose quantification is confirmed by close agreement between the on-chip and reference concentrations for plasma, serum, and saliva (total error 3, 8, and 3 mg dL-1 respectively), demonstrating basic feasibility of colorimetric enzyme-kinetic bioassays on real physiological samples using an electrowetting-based digital microfluidic lab-on-a-chip; the larger urine discrepancy (16 mg dL-1) highlights a matrix-specific interference (uric acid) that must be addressed (e.g., via additional sample dilution/wash) for that fluid type.

calib_rate = detect absorbance on calib_mix for 30s
dispose calib_mix

reg_p = dispense 15 units of glucose_reagent

plasma_rate = detect absorbance on plasma_mix for 30s
dispose plasma_mix

Protocol Details
ASSAY TYPE

Digital Microfluidic Platform for Human Plasma Protein Depletion (HSA and Immunoglobulin Depletion using Magnetic Beads)

REAGENTS USED
Protein Sample (human plasma containing target and high-abundance proteins)
Protein A/G Beads (superparamagnetic particles for immunoglobulin capture)
Anti-HSA Beads (superparamagnetic particles coated with anti-human serum albumin antibodies)
Working Buffer
STEPS
Bead Preparation: Dispense 4 units of Protein A/G beads and 4 units of Anti-HSA beads, then mix them together.
Initial Depletion: Dispense 4 units of the protein sample, merge and mix with the mixed bead suspension, and incubate at 25°C for 10 minutes to deplete high-abundance proteins.
Initial Detection: Measure the fluorescence signal of the depleted sample for 30 seconds.
Conditional Secondary Depletion: If the residual signal exceeds the threshold (> 5), perform a secondary depletion cycle by dispensing fresh Protein A/G and Anti-HSA beads, mixing them with the primary depleted sample, incubating at 25°C for 10 minutes, measuring the secondary signal, and disposing of the initial depletion mixture.

    beadsHSA2 = dispense 4 units of AntiHSABeads
    beads2 = mix beadsAG2 with beadsHSA2

    depletion2 = mix beads2 with depletion1
    heat depletion2 at 25c for 10m

    dispose depletion1

Perform a digital microfluidic human plasma protein depletion assay using Protein A/G and Anti-HSA magnetic beads. First, mix Protein A/G beads and Anti-HSA beads, then combine with the protein sample and incubate at 25C for 10 minutes. Detect the signal; if it exceeds 5, perform a secondary depletion cycle with fresh beads, incubate at 25C for 10 minutes, detect the new signal, and dispose of the first depletion mixture.

manifest ProteinAGBeads
manifest AntiHSABeads
manifest WorkingBuffer

instructions:

beadsAG = dispense 4 units of ProteinAGBeads
beadsHSA = dispense 4 units of AntiHSABeads
beads = mix beadsAG with beadsHSA

sample = dispense 4 units of ProteinSample

depletion1 = mix beads with sample
heat depletion1 at 25c for 10m

signal1 = detect fluorescence on depletion1 for 30s

if (signal1 > 5) {
    beadsAG2 = dispense 4 units of ProteinAGBeads
    beadsHSA2 = dispense 4 units of AntiHSABeads
    beads2 = mix beadsAG2 with beadsHSA2

    depletion2 = mix beads2 with depletion1
    heat depletion2 at 25c for 10m

    signal2 = detect fluorescence on depletion2 for 30s
    dispose depletion1
}
