description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : An Automated Induction Microfluidics System for Synthetic Biology
Source Link  : https://www.shihmicrolab.ca/_files/ugd/f0a828_dff8587cf80c488aa25077207e571507.pdf
Paper DOI    : http://dx.doi.org/10.1021/acssynbio.8b00025
Journal      : ACS Synthetic Biology, 2018, Vol. 7, pp. 933-944
Platform     : Digital microfluidics (DMF) with integrated 600 nm LED absorbance reader,
               TSL2561 lux sensor, Arduino Uno controller, and MATLAB-based GUI automation


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes the Automated Induction Microfluidics System (AIMS), a digital
microfluidic platform for automating bacterial cell culture, OD-triggered IPTG induction,
and on-chip protein expression analysis without manual intervention. The system integrates:
  (1) A DMF device for droplet-based cell culture, induction, and enzymatic assays
  (2) A 600 nm LED + TSL2561 lux sensor for real-time OD monitoring at 280 um gap height
  (3) An Arduino Uno + MATLAB GUI for automated droplet movement and induction triggering
  (4) CLARIOStar plate reader for end-point fluorescence detection (off-chip)

Three protocols are encoded sequentially in the BioScript file:
  P1 - Growth Curve: Semicontinuous mixing of E. coli mother culture with OD monitoring
       until the induction threshold (OD = 0.4) is reached.
  P2 - Inducer Concentration Optimisation: On-chip 2:1 serial dilution of IPTG to generate
       a dose-response curve for RFP expression using a pET16b-RFP reporter construct.
  P3A - BGL Single-Point Screening: Three thermophilic beta-glucosidases (BGL1: T. roseum,
        BGL2: T. terrenum, BGL3: R. marinus) screened for MUG hydrolysis activity after
        4 h induction; time-course fluorescence assay (0, 15, 30, 45, 60 min).
  P3B - BGL3 Multi-Point Optimisation: BGL3 (highest activity, >=6x BGL1/BGL2) optimised
        across five post-induction incubation times (0, 2, 3, 5, 6 h); fixed 30 min MUG
        assay per time point.

Volume reduction: 10,000x in culture (15 uL vs 150 mL); 40x in assay (5 uL vs 200 uL).
Hands-on time at 5-plex: 18 min (AIMS) vs 35 min (bench-top).
IPTG cost at 5-plex: $0.01 reagents (AIMS) vs $2.52 reagents (bench-top).


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Substrate     : Chromium electrodes patterned on glass (S1811 photoresist, Telic Valencia CA)
                Mask resolution: 25,400 dpi (CAD/Art services)
Dielectric    : Parylene-C, 7.2 um thick (SCS Labcoter 2 PDS 2010, Specialty Coating Systems)
Hydrophobic   : FluoroPel PFC1601 V (Cytonix, Beltsville MD); spin-coated 1500 rpm 30 s,
coating         500 rpm/s acceleration; baked 180 C 10 min (Laurell spin coater)
Top plate     : ITO-coated glass (RS = 15-25 Ohm, Delta Technologies CG-61IN-S207)
Gap height    : 280 um (chosen; tested: 210, 280, 350 um)
Design tool   : AutoCAD 2016 (Autodesk)
Fabrication   : Concordia Silicon Microfabrication Lab (ConSIM)

Device sections:
  - Mother culture area: 4 x 4.5x4.5 mm square electrodes
  - Absorbance reading electrode: small middle square 2 (electrode 4); transparent window
    0.25 mm; slope = 0.998, R^2 = 0.999; limit of detection = 0.029 OD units
  - Reservoirs: LB media, IPTG, lysis solution, MUG substrate, stop solution, waste
  - 5 assay/incubation areas
  - 32 actuation electrodes total

Absorbance window selection (7 electrodes tested):
  Electrode 4 (small middle square 2) chosen: reliable droplet movement, slope 0.998,
  R^2 = 0.999. Electrode 1 (large middle square) failed: droplet movement unreliable.
  Star/central/spaced arrays showed non-linear OD response due to small transparent regions.

AIMS hardware:
  LED           : 600 nm (Digikey cat no. 1497-1021-ND); 8 mm above device
  Lux sensor    : TSL2561 (Adafruit); 4 mm below device
  Controller    : Arduino Uno
  Relays        : AQW216 Panasonic (Digikey, Winnipeg MB)
  Function gen. : 33201A Agilent (Allied Electronics, Ottawa ON)
  Amplifier     : PZD-700A Trek Inc. (Lockport NY); delivers 130-270 Vrms sinusoidal
  Communication : I2C protocol (Maxim 7300 I/O expander, Digikey)
  Enclosure     : 3D printed PLA top cover and bottom holder
  Software      : MATLAB (GUI) + Arduino firmware (available at github.com/shihmicrolab/AIMS)


ORGANISM AND STRAINS
--------------------
Host          : E. coli BL21(DE3) (donated by Dr. Vincent Martin, Concordia University)
Vector        : pET16b (T7 promoter + lacI coding sequence)
Reporter      : RFP (BBa_E1010, iGEM registry); cloned via XbaI/BamHI into pET16b
BGL enzymes   :
  BGL1 - Thermomicrobium roseum        (accession YP_002522957.1; synthesised by IDT)
  BGL2 - Thermobaculum terrenum        (accession WP_041425608.1; synthesised by Gen9/Ginkgo)
  BGL3 - Rhodothermus marinus DSM4252  (accession WP_012844561.1; synthesised by Gen9/Ginkgo)
  All BGL genes cloned via XbaI/BamHI into pET16b; transformed into BL21(DE3)
Selection     : LB agar + 100 ug/mL ampicillin (37 C overnight)


REAGENTS
--------
Culture media       : LB broth + 100 ug/mL ampicillin
Anti-biofouling     : 0.05% Pluronics F-68 (added to all cell-containing droplets;
                      prevents protein/cell adsorption on DMF device surfaces)
IPTG stock (P2)     : 3.24 mM; 0.3 uL per dispensed droplet
IPTG stock (P3)     : 11 mM; 2 uL per induction event
Lysis buffer        : 1x (BugBuster-based); 1.42 uL per assay droplet; 10 min RT
MUG substrate       : 6 mM 4-methylumbelliferyl beta-D-glucopyranoside (Carbosynth EM05983)
                      in 150 mM sodium-citrate; 1.42 uL per assay droplet
Stop solution       : 0.4 M glycine-NaOH; 1.42 uL per assay droplet
OD blank            : LB media + 0.05% F-68, no cells (I0 reference reading)
Restriction enzymes : XbaI, BamHI (Thermo, Waltham MA)
Ligase              : T4 ligase (Thermo, Waltham MA); 1 h at RT
Polymerase          : Phusion; 10 uL 5X buffer, 1 uL DMSO, 200 uM dNTPs, 0.5 uM primers,
                      0.5 uL enzyme; PCR: 98 C 30s; 35x (98 C 10s, 55 C 30s, 72 C 30s/kb);
                      72 C 10 min final extension


OD MEASUREMENT
--------------
Formula      : A = log(I0 / I) / 0.028
               A  = absorbance (OD units)
               I0 = blank lux intensity (LB media, no cells)
               I  = sample lux intensity
               0.028 = path length correction factor for 280 um gap height
Threshold    : OD = 0.4 (triggers IPTG induction)
LOD          : 0.035 OD units (at 280 um gap height)
Mixing cycle : one actuation every 45 s; 700 ms actuation time; horizontal + vertical
               4-step sequence; prevents biofouling while maintaining cell homogeneity
Re-check     : If OD < 0.4, continue mixing for 10 min before next OD measurement
Doubling time: AIMS: 72.88 +/- 2.30 min; bench-top: 36.80 +/- 0.36 min
               (two-tailed paired t-test; P = 0.018)
               Difference attributed to semicontinuous vs continuous mixing efficiency
               and shorter path length (280 um vs 1 cm)


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Device Preparation and Blank Acquisition
  Reagents  : LB_Media, PluronicF68
  Operation : mix, 30 s
  Purpose   : Dispense blank droplet (LB + 0.05% F-68, no cells) to acquire I0 lux reading.
              Device inserted into AIMS slot: 8 mm below LED, 4 mm above lux sensor.
              Alignment marks on device and bottom holder used to centre absorbance window
              on lux sensor and minimise lux measurement fluctuations.

Step 2 | Mother Culture Loading
  Organism  : E. coli BL21(DE3) [pET16b]
  Starting OD : 0.1 (overnight culture diluted in LB + 0.05% F-68)
  Volume    : 14 uL loaded onto mother culture area (4 x 4.5x4.5 mm electrodes)
  Operation : mix, 30 s
  Setup     : Bottom plate mated with ITO top plate (grounding). Device placed in incubator
              at 37 C with open water container for humidity; prevents droplet evaporation.

Step 3 | Semicontinuous Mixing and OD Monitoring (P1)
  Mixing    : One actuation every 45 s; 700 ms actuation time; horizontal + vertical
              4-step movement sequence. Continuous mixing caused biofouling within 2 h;
              700 ms actuation time is the minimum for reliable movement without biofouling.
  OD check  : Every 10 min; mother droplet extended to absorbance window electrode.
              If OD < 0.4: return to mixing area; wait 10 min; re-measure.
              If OD >= 0.4: trigger induction program.
  Detection : odMeasurement module; 10 s read duration.
  IR note   : 600 s (10 min) mixing encoded in bsbbif_3_f fail branch.

Step 4 | IPTG Serial Dilution Preparation (P2)
  IPTG stock : 3.24 mM; 0.3 uL per droplet
  Culture    : 1.42 uL unit droplets of RFP-transformed BL21(DE3)
  Method     : 2:1 serial dilution on-chip; explicit dispense + mix steps (no split)
  Concentrations : 200, 133.3, 88.9, 59.3, 40, 26.7, 17.8, 11.9 uM
  Assay spots : 5 (matching device 5-plex layout)
  Macroscale : 45 mL culture induced at 200 uM; diluted with fresh media for series;
               200 uL loaded onto 96-well plate; triplicates + noninduced control.

Step 5 | RFP Induction and Incubation (P2)
  Temperature : 37 C
  Duration    : 4 h (240 min; IR: 14400.0 SECOND)
  Droplets    : 5 daughter droplets actuated to respective assay spots

Step 6 | RFP Fluorescence Detection (P2)
  Plate reader : CLARIOStar (BGM Labtech, Ortenberg, Germany)
  Excitation   : 582 nm; Emission: 612 nm
  Settings     : scan 30x30, width 6 mm, focal height 7.2 mm, gain 2905
  QC gate      : rfpAssay1 (200 uM IPTG, highest expected signal)
  Results      : Dose-response follows sigmoidal (Hill function) profile;
                 max expression at IPTG >= 200 uM; basal levels below 30 uM.
                 Differences in curve steepness vs macroscale attributed to E-field
                 actuation, mixing efficiency, and volume differences between systems.
  Pass (BB5)   : rfpSignal1 > 0 -> dispose all 5 RFP droplets
  Fail (BB6)   : rfpSignal1 <= 0 -> drain all 5 RFP droplets

Step 7 | BGL Culture Growth and Induction - Single-Point (P3A)
  Strains   : BGL1 (T. roseum), BGL2 (T. terrenum), BGL3 (R. marinus)
  Starting OD : 0.4 (triggered by OD monitoring loop from P1)
  IPTG      : 2 uL of 11 mM IPTG mixed with single culture droplet; returned to mixing
              area to uniformly distribute inducer before daughter dispensing.
  Droplets  : 5 daughter droplets per strain (15 total)

Step 8 | Post-Induction Incubation - Single-Point (P3A)
  Temperature : 37 C
  Duration    : 4 h (240 min; IR: 14400.0 SECOND per droplet)
  Total droplets : 15 (5 per strain)

Step 9 | Cell Lysis (P3A)
  Reagent   : 1x lysis buffer, 1.42 uL per droplet
  Temperature : 25 C (room temperature)
  Duration  : 10 min (600 s; IR: 600.0 SECOND)
  Total lysis droplets : 15

Step 10 | MUG Substrate Addition and Incubation - Single-Point (P3A)
  Substrate : 1.42 uL of 6 mM MUG in 150 mM sodium-citrate per droplet
  Temperature : 25 C
  Time points : 0, 15, 30, 45, 60 min
  IR durations : 1.0, 900.0, 1800.0, 2700.0, 3600.0 SECOND
  Note      : t=0 modelled as heat for 1s (no-op compiler token)
  Total assay droplets : 15 (5 time points x 3 strains)

Step 11 | Reaction Stop - Single-Point (P3A)
  Reagent   : 0.4 M glycine-NaOH, 1.42 uL per droplet
  Duration  : 5 s mix
  Total stop droplets : 15

Step 12 | BGL Activity Detection - Single-Point (P3A)
  Plate reader : CLARIOStar
  Excitation   : 368 nm; Emission: 449 nm (MUF fluorescence)
  Settings     : focal height 4.0 mm, gain 664
  QC gates (keyed on t=60 min droplet per strain):
    BGL1 : bgl1Signal; pass BB8, fail BB9, join BB10
    BGL2 : bgl2Signal; pass BB11, fail BB12, join BB13
    BGL3 : bgl3Signal; pass BB14, fail BB15, join BB16
  Results   : BGL3 activity >= 6x BGL1 and BGL2 (rate comparison, Fig 6C).
              BGL1 and BGL2 nearly identical. High BGL3 activity attributed to
              thermostability and salt tolerance of R. marinus enzymes.

Step 13 | BGL3 Multi-Point Induction and Incubation (P3B)
  Strain    : BGL3_Cells (R. marinus DSM4252)
  Starting OD : ~0.1 (low OD; OD monitoring loop bypassed for this subroutine)
  IPTG      : 2 uL of 11 mM IPTG; same volume and concentration as single-point
  Subcultures : 5 daughter droplets induced simultaneously
  Post-induction incubation time points:
    t0h : 0 h  (immediate lysis; 1 s no-op heat token)
    t2h : 2 h  (120 min; IR: 7200.0 SECOND)
    t3h : 3 h  (180 min; IR: 10800.0 SECOND)
    t5h : 5 h  (300 min; IR: 18000.0 SECOND)
    t6h : 6 h  (360 min; IR: 21600.0 SECOND)
  Temperature : 37 C

Step 14 | Cell Lysis - Multi-Point (P3B)
  Reagent   : 1x lysis buffer, 1.42 uL per droplet
  Temperature : 25 C
  Duration  : 10 min (600 s; IR: 600.0 SECOND)
  Total lysis droplets : 5

Step 15 | MUG Substrate Addition and Incubation - Multi-Point (P3B)
  Substrate : 1.42 uL of 6 mM MUG in 150 mM sodium-citrate per droplet
  Temperature : 25 C
  Fixed duration : 30 min for all 5 time points (IR: 1800.0 SECOND each)
  Total assay droplets : 5

Step 16 | Reaction Stop - Multi-Point (P3B)
  Reagent   : 0.4 M glycine-NaOH, 1.42 uL per droplet
  Duration  : 5 s mix
  Total stop droplets : 5

Step 17 | BGL3 Multi-Point Fluorescence Detection (P3B)
  Plate reader : CLARIOStar
  Excitation   : 368 nm; Emission: 449 nm
  Settings     : focal height 4.0 mm, gain 664
  QC gate      : bgl3mpSignal_t6 (6 h; highest expected expression)
  Results      : BGL3 expression at 6 h >= 3x expression at 0 h (Fig 6D).
                 Longer post-induction incubation (>1 h) improves protein folding,
                 accumulation, and productivity in E. coli BL21(DE3). 6 h is optimal.
  Pass (BB17)  : bgl3mpSignal_t6 > 0 -> dispose all 5 MP droplets
  Fail (BB18)  : bgl3mpSignal_t6 <= 0 -> drain all 5 MP droplets
  Terminal     : BB19 disposes all 5 MP QC signals; NOP


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : husser_aims_induction_bgl_synbio.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based, GitHub: https://github.com/lilott8/BioScript)
IR output      : 19 basic blocks (BB1-BB19); 9 if/else gates; 24 CFG edges
DAG            : husser_aims_induction_bgl_synbio_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations converted to minutes (m) or seconds (s) for compiler
                 compatibility (BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported)
                 4 h   -> 240m   (RFP incubation; IR: 14400.0 SECOND)
                 10 min -> 10m   (lysis; IR: 600.0 SECOND)
                 30 min -> 30m   (MUG assay; IR: 1800.0 SECOND)
                 2 h   -> 120m   (BGL3 MP t2h; IR: 7200.0 SECOND)
                 3 h   -> 180m   (BGL3 MP t3h; IR: 10800.0 SECOND)
                 5 h   -> 300m   (BGL3 MP t5h; IR: 18000.0 SECOND)
                 6 h   -> 360m   (BGL3 MP t6h; IR: 21600.0 SECOND)
                 t=0h  -> 1s     (no-op heat token for compiler; IR: 1.0 SECOND)
                 600s  -> 600s   (10 min OD fail branch mixing; IR: 600.0 SECOND)
Modules        : odMeasurement, rfpFluorescenceDetection, bglActivityDetection
No split       : split operation avoided throughout; all dilution series and parallel
                 droplets use explicit dispense + mix scalar variables to prevent
                 stranded-droplet compiler issues (documented in moazami reference file)
drain vs dispose : lilott8 compiler maps both to dispose in IR output; this is expected
                   compiler behaviour, not a source error
Verification   : .bs, .ir, and .dot outputs independently reviewed and confirmed correct
                 (see husser_aims_review.txt for full verification report)

protocol.title: An Automated Induction Microfluidics System for Synthetic Biology
protocol.platform: Digital microfluidics (DMF) with integrated OD reader and automation system
protocol.objective: Automated bacterial cell culture, OD-triggered IPTG induction, inducer concentration optimisation (RFP reporter), and expression screening of thermophilic beta-glucosidase (BGL) enzymes for biomass hydrolysis

device.hydrophobic_coating: FluoroPel PFC1601 V (Cytonix), spin-coated at 1500 rpm, 30 s, baked 180 C 10 min

Absorbance reading electrode (transparent window, small middle square 2, 0.25 mm)

steps.notes: Overnight culture diluted to OD 0.1 in LB + 0.05% F-68. 14 uL loaded onto mother culture area (four 4.5x4.5 mm electrodes). Bottom plate mated with ITO top plate for grounding.

steps.name: Semicontinuous mixing and OD monitoring

description:
Source link: https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/ncomms8513.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms8513

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital microfluidic Immunocytochemistry in Single Cells (DISC) for high-time-resolution analysis of PDGFR/PI3K/Akt phosphorylation signalling in adherent fibroblasts and breast cancer cells

REAGENTS USED:
  - Cell Suspension (NIH-3T3 fibroblasts, MCF-7, or MDA-MB-231 cells at 500,000 cells per mL in culture media; passively dispensed to form virtual microwells (VMs) on the patterned top-plate hydrophilic sites)
  - Starving Media (0.5% serum, 0.05% v/v Pluronic F68 in DMEM)
  - Serum-Free DMEM (0.05% v/v Pluronic F68 rinse/wash medium)
  - PDGF-BB Ligand (human recombinant PDGF-BB stimulant in serum-free DMEM, delivered as single-bolus or brief pulse doses)
  - Fixing Solution (4% paraformaldehyde, 0.05% v/v F68 in DPBS)
  - Wash Buffer 1 (0.05% v/v F68 in DPBS, post-fixation rinse)
  - Permeabilization Solution (0.2% v/v Tween-20 in DPBS)
  - Wash Buffer 2 (0.05% v/v Brij 35 in DPBS, post-permeabilization/antibody rinse)
  - Blocking Solution (1% bovine non-fat dried milk, 0.05% v/v Brij 35 in DPBS)
  - Primary Antibody Solution (anti-PDGFR/anti-phospho-PDGFR or anti-Akt/anti-phospho-Akt mouse and rabbit antibodies in blocking solution)
  - Secondary Antibody Solution (Alexa Fluor 647 anti-mouse and Alexa Fluor 555 anti-rabbit conjugates in blocking solution)

STEPS:
1. Seeding: Passively dispense cell suspension droplets onto the top-plate hydrophilic sites to form virtual microwells; incubate 24 h at 37 C to allow cell adherence.
2. Starving: Dispense starving media to the VM; incubate 24 h at 37 C to serum-starve adherent cells.
3. Rinse: Passively dispense six successive serum-free DMEM droplets across the VM to wash out starving media.
4. Stimulation: Deliver PDGF-BB ligand droplet(s) to the VM for a defined stimulation duration (single bolus of 1 s to 120 s, or a brief 3-40 s pulse followed by ligand-free wash-away, depending on experiment).
5. Fixation: Immediately after stimulation, dispense fixing solution to the VM and incubate 10 min at room temperature to arrest the signalling state.
6. Rinse: Passively dispense six successive Wash Buffer 1 droplets to remove residual fixing solution.
7. Permeabilization: Dispense permeabilization solution to the VM and incubate 10 min at room temperature.
8. Rinse: Passively dispense nine successive Wash Buffer 2 droplets to remove permeabilization solution.
9. Blocking: Dispense blocking solution to the VM and incubate 1 h at room temperature.
10. Primary Antibody Staining: Dispense primary antibody solution (target protein + phosphoprotein antibodies) to the VM and incubate overnight at 4 C.
11. Rinse: Passively dispense six successive Wash Buffer 2 droplets to remove unbound primary antibody.
12. Secondary Antibody Staining: Dispense secondary antibody solution to the VM and incubate 2 h at room temperature.
13. Detection: Disassemble the top plate and scan on a microarray/laser-scanning cytometer; analyze images in CellProfiler to compute, for each single cell, the ratio of phosphorylated-protein to total-protein (phosphorylated + non-phosphorylated) fluorescence intensity, normalized to unstimulated control cells on the same device, yielding a per-cell phosphorylation fold-change used to classify normal vs. hyperactive responders.

PULSE-STIMULATION VARIANT (time-resolved wash-away experiments, Fig. 6):
After seeding, starving, and rinsing as above, cells are stimulated with a brief PDGF-BB pulse (as short as 3 s) and then washed with ligand-free medium to terminate ligand exposure. Cells are held for a defined post-stimulation interval (1-5 min, in 1 min increments) before fixation, so that phosphorylation state is captured at successive time points after the pulse. Steps 5-12 (fixation, permeabilization, blocking, primary/secondary antibody staining, and washes) are then performed identically to the standard protocol, followed by detection/classification of Akt activation.

INTERPRETATION: Successful DISC operation is confirmed by dose-dependent, bulk-averaged PDGFR/Akt phosphorylation curves matching conventional (western blot) measurements of the PDGFR/PI3K/Akt pathway, Hill-coefficient/half-maximal-activation values consistent with prior literature, no significant signalling perturbation from droplet-movement shear stress, and single-cell-resolved histograms/scatter plots revealing heterogeneous "hyperactive responder" subpopulations (e.g., in MDA-MB-231 vs. MCF-7 breast cancer cells) and fast pulse-stimulation kinetics (e.g., a 10 s PDGF pulse committing >30% of cells to Akt activation) not resolvable by traditional bulk assays.

messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

ASSAY TYPE: Digital microfluidic Immunocytochemistry in Single Cells (DISC) for high-time-resolution analysis of PDGFR/PI3K/Akt phosphorylation signalling in adherent fibroblasts and breast cancer cells

REAGENTS USED:
  - Cell Suspension (NIH-3T3 fibroblasts, MCF-7, or MDA-MB-231 cells at 500,000 cells per mL in culture media; passively dispensed to form virtual microwells (VMs) on the patterned top-plate hydrophilic sites)
  - Starving Media (0.5% serum, 0.05% v/v Pluronic F68 in DMEM)
  - Serum-Free DMEM (0.05% v/v Pluronic F68 rinse/wash medium)
  - PDGF-BB Ligand (human recombinant PDGF-BB stimulant in serum-free DMEM, delivered as single-bolus or brief pulse doses)
  - Fixing Solution (4% paraformaldehyde, 0.05% v/v F68 in DPBS)
  - Wash Buffer 1 (0.05% v/v F68 in DPBS, post-fixation rinse)
  - Permeabilization Solution (0.2% v/v Tween-20 in DPBS)
  - Wash Buffer 2 (0.05% v/v Brij 35 in DPBS, post-permeabilization/antibody rinse)
  - Blocking Solution (1% bovine non-fat dried milk, 0.05% v/v Brij 35 in DPBS)
  - Primary Antibody Solution (anti-PDGFR/anti-phospho-PDGFR or anti-Akt/anti-phospho-Akt mouse and rabbit antibodies in blocking solution)
  - Secondary Antibody Solution (Alexa Fluor 647 anti-mouse and Alexa Fluor 555 anti-rabbit conjugates in blocking solution)

STEPS:
1. Seeding: Passively dispense cell suspension droplets onto the top-plate hydrophilic sites to form virtual microwells; incubate 24 h at 37 C to allow cell adherence.
2. Starving: Dispense starving media to the VM; incubate 24 h at 37 C to serum-starve adherent cells.
3. Rinse: Passively dispense six successive serum-free DMEM droplets across the VM to wash out starving media.
4. Stimulation: Deliver PDGF-BB ligand droplet(s) to the VM for a defined stimulation duration (single bolus of 1 s to 120 s, or a brief 3-40 s pulse followed by ligand-free wash-away, depending on experiment).
5. Fixation: Immediately after stimulation, dispense fixing solution to the VM and incubate 10 min at room temperature to arrest the signalling state.
6. Rinse: Passively dispense six successive Wash Buffer 1 droplets to remove residual fixing solution.
7. Permeabilization: Dispense permeabilization solution to the VM and incubate 10 min at room temperature.
8. Rinse: Passively dispense nine successive Wash Buffer 2 droplets to remove permeabilization solution.
9. Blocking: Dispense blocking solution to the VM and incubate 1 h at room temperature.
10. Primary Antibody Staining: Dispense primary antibody solution (target protein + phosphoprotein antibodies) to the VM and incubate overnight at 4 C.
11. Rinse: Passively dispense six successive Wash Buffer 2 droplets to remove unbound primary antibody.
12. Secondary Antibody Staining: Dispense secondary antibody solution to the VM and incubate 2 h at room temperature.
13. Detection: Disassemble the top plate and scan on a microarray/laser-scanning cytometer; analyze images in CellProfiler to compute, for each single cell, the ratio of phosphorylated-protein to total-protein (phosphorylated + non-phosphorylated) fluorescence intensity, normalized to unstimulated control cells on the same device, yielding a per-cell phosphorylation fold-change used to classify normal vs. hyperactive responders.

PULSE-STIMULATION VARIANT (time-resolved wash-away experiments, Fig. 6): After seeding, starving, and rinsing as above, cells are stimulated with a brief PDGF-BB pulse (as short as 3 s) and then washed with ligand-free medium to terminate ligand exposure. Cells are held for a defined post-stimulation interval (1-5 min, in 1 min increments) before fixation, so that phosphorylation state is captured at successive time points after the pulse. Steps 5-12 (fixation, permeabilization, blocking, primary/secondary antibody staining, and washes) are then performed identically to the standard protocol, followed by detection/classification of Akt activation.

INTERPRETATION: Successful DISC operation is confirmed by dose-dependent, bulk-averaged PDGFR/Akt phosphorylation curves matching conventional (western blot) measurements of the PDGFR/PI3K/Akt pathway, Hill-coefficient/half-maximal-activation values consistent with prior literature, no significant signalling perturbation from droplet-movement shear stress, and single-cell-resolved histograms/scatter plots revealing heterogeneous 'hyperactive responder' subpopulations (e.g., in MDA-MB-231 vs. MCF-7 breast cancer cells) and fast pulse-stimulation kinetics (e.g., a 10 s PDGF pulse committing >30% of cells to Akt activation) not resolvable by traditional bulk assays.

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code is a direct translation of the paper's automated 11-step DMF cell-culture and immunocytochemistry procedure (Methods, 'DMF cell culture and immunocytochemistry'), covering cell seeding/adherence, serum starvation, PDGF-BB ligand stimulation, paraformaldehyde fixation, permeabilization, blocking, primary/secondary antibody staining, and the intervening wash cycles, as depicted in Fig. 1b. A second block translates the time-resolved pulse-stimulation wash-away variant (Fig. 6), where a brief ligand pulse (as short as 3 s) is followed by a ligand-free wash droplet and a delay before fixation, capturing Akt phosphorylation at successive post-pulse time points. Incubation durations, temperatures, and droplet counts (e.g., 6x900nl serum-free DMEM rinse, 9x900nl WB2 rinse, 10 min fixation/permeabilization, 1 h blocking, overnight primary antibody at 4C, 2 h secondary antibody) are taken directly from the Methods section's step-by-step reagent volumes. Because BioScript's 'dispense'/'mix' primitives model discrete reagent-exchange droplets rather than a persistent adherent-cell substrate, the virtual microwell is represented by a single continuously-updated droplet handle ('vm' / 'pulse_vm') that is repeatedly re-mixed with each new reagent droplet, consistent with the paper's own description of sequential passive-dispensing reagent exchange over a fixed virtual microwell. Likewise, because the paper's readout is a CellProfiler-derived phosphorylated:total-protein fluorescence intensity ratio (immunofluorescence, not a fluorogenic enzymatic assay), the 'detect fluorescence' primitive is used directly, since this is the genuine detection modality of the assay (unlike protocols using LC-MS/nESI-MS readouts, which must borrow the same primitive as a stand-in). The classification 'if/else' block after each detect step models the paper's post hoc single-cell classification into normal vs. hyperactive responder populations (Fig. 4) and disposes the droplet on both branches. The device fabrication/actuation-voltage control system (DropBot, Methods 'Device fabrication and operation'), the CellProfiler image-analysis pipeline and shape/neighbour-distance statistics (Fig. 4b, Supplementary Figs. 12-15), the microarray-scanner/live-cell-imaging hardware setup, the shear-stress/orthovanadate control experiments (Supplementary Figs. 8, 16), and the double-bolus ligand-renewal kinetics experiment (Fig. 5b) are hardware-control, image-analysis, or separate control/validation sub-experiments with no corresponding BioScript primitive, and are intentionally not modeled; only the core 11-step seed/stimulate/fix/stain/detect protocol and its pulse-stimulation variant are captured here.

description:
Source link: https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/6b02915.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.analchem.6b02915

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic Immunoprecipitation (DMF-IP) for Targeted Protein Purification with Mass Spectrometry Readout

REAGENTS USED:
  - Magnetic Particles (superparamagnetic particles coated with an antibody against the target protein)
  - Sample (complex biological matrix, e.g., serum, containing the target analyte)
  - Wash Buffer (Tris-HCl, pH 7.6)
  - Elution Buffer (100 mM citric acid)

STEPS:
1. Particle Loading: Dispense a droplet of antibody-functionalized magnetic particles onto the device.
2. Capture: Dispense a droplet of sample and merge it with the immobilized particles. Actively resuspend and mix for 10 minutes to allow the target analyte to bind the antibody-coated particles.
3. Wash Cycle: Repeat twice - dispense a droplet of Tris-HCl wash buffer, merge with the particle-bound complex, and mix for approximately 3 minutes to remove unbound sample matrix.
4. Elution: Dispense a droplet of 100 mM citric acid elution buffer and merge with the washed particles. Mix for 5 minutes to release the purified target from the particles.
5. Detection: Recover the eluted droplet and analyze the purified target by direct-infusion tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) for 1 minute. Discard the final reaction mixture.

INTERPRETATION: Successful immunoprecipitation is confirmed by a strong mass spectrometry signal for the target protein's diagnostic tryptic peptide transition in the eluted droplet, in contrast to the low signal observed for the same transition in unprocessed sample matrix, demonstrating effective removal of background matrix and preconcentration of the target analyte.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A NOTE ON HOW CLOSELY THIS MATCHES THE CITED SOURCE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The authored BioScript code is a direct translation of the core, small-volume (3-5 uL) eight-step DMF-IP procedure described by Seale et al. (2016): particle loading, sample capture, a two-cycle wash, elution, and MS detection. Wash and elution mixing durations (10 min capture, ~3 min per wash, 5 min elution) and the elution buffer identity (100 mM citric acid) are taken directly from the paper's DMF-IP General Procedure, and the 5-minute elution time matches the value the authors settled on after their own optimization experiments (Figure 2), rather than an arbitrarily chosen number. Because BioScript's instruction set exposes only dispense, mix, heat, repeat, detect, and dispose, the paper's explicit magnet-engage/particle-isolation steps (steps 2, 4, and 8, in which a magnet immobilizes particles so the supernatant can be exchanged) have no dedicated primitive and are folded implicitly into the surrounding dispense/mix pairs - the same abstraction already used for wash cycles in the ELISA-style scripts in this test suite. The paper's second technique, P-CLIP (a macro-to-microscale paper-wicking preconcentration interface for samples >=100 uL), is a physically distinct workflow involving passive lateral-flow pumping and sequential electrode deactivation with no analog in this instruction set, and is intentionally not modeled; only the core small-volume DMF-IP protocol shown in Figure 1 is captured here.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Digital Microfluidics for Automated Proteomic Processing
Source Link  : https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3157851/pdf/jove-33-1603.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.3791/1603
Journal      : Journal of Visualized Experiments (JoVE), 2009, Vol. 33
Platform     : Digital Microfluidics (DMF) -- two-plate EWOD configuration


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a digital microfluidics (DMF) based method for fully automated,
integrated proteomic sample processing on a single miniaturised device. The workflow covers
all major biochemical processing steps required in clinical proteomics prior to mass
spectrometric analysis: protein extraction by precipitation, resolubilization, reduction,
alkylation, and enzymatic (tryptic) digestion.

DMF is a microscale fluid-handling technique in which nanoliter-to-microliter droplets are
manipulated on an open surface coated with a dielectric layer and electrodes. Applying an
electrical potential to the droplet causes charges to accumulate on either side of the
dielectric, creating electrostatic handles that allow droplets to be dispensed, moved, merged,
mixed, and split. This makes DMF a natural fit for rapid, sequential, multistep, miniaturised
automated biochemical assays.

The paper demonstrates the method using bovine serum albumin (BSA) as a model protein,
achieving identification of 25 distinct peptides (99.9% confidence interval) with 44% sequence
coverage by nano-HPLC-MS/MS after on-chip processing. The approach eliminates the human error
inherent in conventional macroscale pipetting-based or robot-based proteomic sample handling
and enables precise duplication of conditions across laboratories.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Configuration : Two-plate DMF device
Bottom plate  : Patterned chromium (Cr) electrodes (250 nm) on glass substrate.
                Dielectric: Parylene-C (2-5 um, chemical vapor deposition).
                Hydrophobic layer: Teflon-AF (50 nm, 1% wt/wt in Fluorinert FC-40,
                spin-coated at 2000 rpm for 60 s, post-baked at 160 C for 10 min).
Top plate     : Unpatterned indium tin oxide (ITO) glass (transparent contiguous electrode).
                Hydrophobic layer: Teflon-AF (50 nm, same conditions as bottom plate).
Gap           : 140 um total (set by two pieces of double-sided tape on bottom plate edges).
Actuation     : 100 V_rms / 18 kHz AC signals applied via 40-pin connectors.
Control       : LabView (National Instruments, Austin, TX) with in-house calibration program.
                Home-built control box: high-voltage relay array (NI DaqPad), function
                generator, and amplifier. Feedback control calibrated at startup.
Droplet vol.  : ~600 nL per dispensed droplet (defined by 1 mm square electrode dimensions,
                50 um gaps, 2.5 mm square reservoirs).

Fabrication (Part 1):
  1. Clean glass in Piranha solution (3:1 H2SO4:H2O2, 30%) for 10 min with agitation.
  2. Rinse in DI water, dry with N2, deposit 250 nm Cr by electron beam evaporation.
  3. Dehydrate Cr-coated substrate: rinse in isopropanol, bake 5 min at 115 C.
  4. Spin-coat HMDS (30 s, 3000 rpm) then Shipley S1811 photoresist (same parameters).
  5. Pre-bake (100 C, 2 min); expose to UV for 5 s through photomask.
  6. Develop in Shipley MF 321 developer (3 min); wash in DI water; post-bake 100 C, 1 min.
  7. Etch exposed Cr in Cr etchant (30 s); strip photoresist in AZ300T (10 min); rinse DI/N2.
  8. Deposit Parylene-C (2-5 um, CVD); spin-coat Teflon-AF 50 nm; post-bake 160 C, 10 min.
  9. Coat ITO glass top plate with Teflon-AF 50 nm; post-bake 160 C, 10 min.


RESERVOIR MAP (Figure 1b)
--------------------------
R-1  : Protein sample (serum or purified protein dissolved in working buffer WB)
R-2  : Precipitant -- 20% Trichloroacetic acid (TCA) in DI water
R-3  : Waste reservoir (receives supernatant after precipitation and wash eluates)
R-4  : Wash buffer -- 70/30 Chloroform/Acetonitrile (ACN)
R-5  : Resolubilizing buffer -- 100 mM Ammonium Bicarbonate pH 8.0, 0.08% Pluronic F127 w/v
R-6  : Reductant -- 10 mM TCEP (tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine) in WB
R-7  : Alkylating agent -- 12 mM Iodoacetamide (IAM) in WB
R-8  : Trypsin -- dissolved in WB at 1/5 of total protein sample concentration


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Device Set-up (Part 2)
  - Remove polymer coatings from bottom substrate contact pads by scraping with scalpel.
  - Couple exposed pads to 40-pin connectors.
  - Power on LabView computer, control box, function generator, and amplifier.
  - Assemble device: position two pieces of double-sided tape (140 um total) on bottom
    substrate edges; complete with unpatterned ITO top plate (Teflon side facing down).
  - Attach ground connector to top substrate.
  - Run LabView calibration program to initialise feedback control.
  - Load sample and reagents into reservoirs R-1 through R-8.
  - Load and execute LabView actuation code to initiate droplet actuation.

Step 2 | Sample and Reagent Preparation (Part 3)
  Working buffer  : 100 mM TrisHCl pH 7.8, 0.08% Pluronic F127 w/v.
  R-1 (sample)    : Dissolve protein(s) in WB; pipette into R-1.
  R-2 (TCA)       : 20% TCA in DI water; pipette into R-2.
  R-4 (wash)      : 70/30 Chloroform/ACN; pipette into R-4.
  R-5 (resolub.)  : 100 mM AmBic pH 8.0, 0.08% Pluronic F127; pipette into R-5.
  R-6 (TCEP)      : 10 mM TCEP in WB; pipette into R-6.
  R-7 (IAM)       : 12 mM Iodoacetamide in WB; pipette into R-7.
  R-8 (trypsin)   : Trypsin in WB at 1/5 total protein concentration; pipette into R-8.

Step 3 | Protein Extraction by Precipitation (Part 4, Steps 2)
  Inputs     : ProteinSample (R-1), TrichloroaceticAcid (R-2)
  Operation  : Dispense ~600 nL protein droplet from R-1 and ~600 nL TCA droplet from R-2.
               Merge droplets on device surface (Figure 2, Frame 1).
               Incubate 5 min at room temperature; proteins precipitate onto surface
               (Figure 2, Frames 2-3).
               Actuate supernatant away to waste reservoir R-3 (Figure 2, Frame 4).
  Duration   : 5 min (300 s)
  Temperature: Room temperature (~25 C)

Step 4 | Precipitate Washing (Part 4, Step 3)
  Inputs     : WashBuffer (R-4) -- 70/30 Chloroform/ACN
  Operation  : Dispense 3 sequential ~600 nL wash buffer droplets from R-4.
               Drive each droplet across the precipitated protein to waste reservoir R-3
               (Figure 2, Frame 5).
  Wash cycles: 3 (unrolled as 3 independent dispense/drain operations in BioScript)
  Purpose    : Removes residual TCA, soluble contaminants, and lipids from precipitate.

Step 5 | Protein Resolubilization (Part 4, Step 4)
  Input      : ResolubilizingBuffer (R-5)
  Operation  : Allow precipitate to dry on device surface.
               Dispense ~600 nL resolubilizing buffer droplet from R-5 onto precipitate.
               Incubate 20 min until precipitate fully dissolves (Figure 2, Frame 6).
  Duration   : 20 min (1200 s)
  Temperature: Room temperature (~25 C)
  Notes      : AmBic buffer (pH 8.0) is trypsin-compatible. Pluronic F127 prevents biofouling.

Step 6 | Reduction (Part 4, Step 5)
  Inputs     : TCEP_Reductant (R-6), resolubilizedSample
  Operation  : Dispense ~600 nL TCEP droplet from R-6 and merge with sample droplet.
               Mix combined droplet by circular actuation across 6 electrodes.
               Incubate 1 h at room temperature in a humidified chamber (Figure 3, Frames 1-2).
  Duration   : 60 min (3600 s)
  Temperature: 25 C (room temperature, humidified chamber)
  Purpose    : TCEP reduces disulfide bonds between cysteine residues.

Step 7 | Alkylation (Part 4, Step 6)
  Inputs     : Iodoacetamide (R-7), reducedSample
  Operation  : Dispense ~600 nL IAM droplet from R-7 and merge with sample droplet.
               Mix combined droplet by circular actuation across 6 electrodes (same as Step 6).
               Incubate 15 min at room temperature in a humidified chamber, protected from
               light (Figure 3, Frames 2-3).
  Duration   : 15 min (900 s)
  Temperature: 25 C (room temperature, humidified chamber, light-protected)
  Purpose    : IAM alkylates free thiols on cysteines to prevent re-oxidation of disulfides.

Step 8 | Tryptic Digestion (Part 4, Step 7)
  Inputs     : Trypsin (R-8), alkylatedSample
  Operation  : Dispense ~600 nL trypsin droplet from R-8 and merge with sample droplet.
               Mix combined droplet by circular actuation across 6 electrodes (same as Step 6).
               Incubate 3 h at 37 C on a hot plate in a humidified chamber
               (Figure 3, Frames 3-4).
  Duration   : 180 min (10800 s)
  Temperature: 37 C (hot plate, humidified chamber)
  Purpose    : Trypsin cleaves at Lys-X and Arg-X peptide bonds.

Step 9 | Post-Processing Sample Preparation (Part 5, off-chip)
  1. Remove top substrate; quench digestion by adding 0.6 mL of 2.5% TFA in water.
  2. Purify quenched product using C18 ZipTips (Millipore, Billerica, MA) per manufacturer
     instructions.
  3. Dilute purified sample in DI water to a final volume of 100 mL.
  Notes      : TFA quenches trypsin enzymatic activity. C18 ZipTip SPE desalts and
               concentrates peptides for MS injection.

Step 10 | Mass Spectrometry Analysis (Part 6)
  HPLC system : Eksigent Technologies nano-HPLC
  Trap column : 3 mm dia. C18 beads, 150 um ID x 2.5 cm
  Sep. column : 3 um dia. C18 beads, 75 um ID x 15 cm (reversed-phase)
  MS          : LTQ (Thermo-Fisher Scientific)
  Emitter     : Nanoelectrospray emitter, 20 um ID tapered to 10 um ID (NewObjective)
  LC method   :
    Loading    -- 2 uL sample at 5 uL/min in 5% acetonitrile/water onto trap column
    Separation -- 0.5 uL/min; linear gradient 20% to 80% ACN over 25 min
    Hold       -- 80% ACN for additional 10 min
  DB search   : SEQUEST (Bioworks v3.01, Thermo-Fisher Scientific)
                Probability threshold: < 1.0E-03 (99.9% confidence interval)
                Sequence coverage threshold: >= 30%
  Results     : BSA model protein; 25 distinct peptides identified; 44% sequence coverage
                (Figure 4)


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : jebrail_dmf_proteomic_processing.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 4 basic blocks (BB1-BB4), 1 if/else gate, 4 CFG edges
DAG file       : jebrail_dmf_proteomic_processing_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations converted to minutes (m) or seconds (s);
                 BioScript supports s and m only (no h token).
                 1h  (reduction)  -> 60m  (IR: 3600.0 SECOND)
                 3h  (digestion)  -> 180m (IR: 10800.0 SECOND)
Modules        : proteinPrecipitationDetection, digestCompletionDetection
Manifests      : ProteinSample, TrichloroaceticAcid, WashBuffer, ResolubilizingBuffer,
                 TCEP_Reductant, Iodoacetamide, Trypsin

CFG structure  :
  BB1  main         -- entry: precipitation, wash, resolubilization, reduction,
                        alkylation, digestion, QC detect
  BB2  bsbbif_2_t   -- digestSignal > 0: digest complete; dispose(digestedSample)
  BB3  bsbbif_3_f   -- digestSignal <= 0: digest incomplete; drain(digestedSample)
  BB4  bsbbif_4_j   -- terminal: dispose(digestSignal)

  CFG edges: BB1->BB2, BB1->BB3, BB2->BB4, BB3->BB4 (diamond shape)

Abstraction notes:
  Precipitation  : mix + drain abstracts TCA-driven protein precipitation and
                   supernatant removal to R-3. No native precipitate primitive in BioScript.
  Wash unrolling : 3 wash steps unrolled as 3 explicit dispense/drain pairs.
                   No loop construct supported in lilott8/BioScript compiler.
  Resolubilization: Second ProteinSample dispense abstracts the on-surface dried
                   precipitate being re-contacted with the buffer droplet (compiler
                   requires a live variable to mix into).
  Circular mixing: BioScript mix abstracts both the circular 6-electrode electrode
                   actuation and the subsequent timed incubation in a single statement.
  Temperature    : heat at 25c models room-temperature incubation steps;
                   heat at 37c models hot plate used for trypsin digestion.
  drain vs dispose: drain used for waste removal and failed QC paths;
                   dispose used for successfully processed sample at QC pass branch.

protocol.objective: Fully automated, integrated proteomic sample processing on a DMF device: protein extraction by precipitation, resolubilization, reduction, alkylation, and tryptic digestion, followed by nano-HPLC-MS/MS identification

working_buffer.notes: Pluronic F127 surfactant prevents biofouling on device surface

precipitant.name: TCA
precipitant.notes: Denatures and precipitates proteins by pH drop and hydration shell disruption

waste_reservoir.name: R-3
waste_reservoir.notes: Receives supernatant after precipitation and wash eluates

wash_buffer.name: WashBuffer
wash_buffer.notes: Removes residual TCA and non-protein contaminants from precipitate

resolubilizing_buffer.name: AmBic buffer
resolubilizing_buffer.composition: 100 mM Ammonium Bicarbonate pH 8.0, 0.08% Pluronic F127 w/v
resolubilizing_buffer.notes: Redissolves protein precipitate after drying; compatible with trypsin digestion

alkylating_agent.name: IAM
alkylating_agent.notes: Alkylates free thiols to prevent re-oxidation; incubation protected from light

sub_steps.action: Prepare working buffer (WB): 100 mM TrisHCl pH 7.8, 0.08% Pluronic F127 w/v
Dissolve protein(s) in WB; pipette into R-1 on device
Prepare 20% TCA in DI water; pipette into R-2
Prepare 70/30 Chloroform/ACN wash buffer; pipette into R-4
Prepare 100 mM AmBic pH 8.0, 0.08% Pluronic F127 resolubilizing buffer; pipette into R-5
Dissolve TCEP at 10 mM in WB; pipette into R-6
Dissolve IAM at 12 mM in WB; pipette into R-7
Dissolve trypsin in WB at 1/5 of total protein concentration; pipette into R-8

steps.name: Protein Extraction by Precipitation
steps.notes: Protein droplet (R-1) and TCA precipitant droplet (R-2) merged. Combined droplet incubates 5 min; proteins precipitate onto device surface. Supernatant actuated to waste reservoir R-3 (Figure 2, Frame 4).

steps.name: Precipitate Washing
steps.operation: dispense + drive across precipitate + drain to R-3
steps.notes: Three sequential wash buffer droplets dispensed from R-4 and driven across precipitated protein to waste R-3. Removes residual TCA and non-protein contaminants. Modelled in BioScript as 3 unrolled dispense/drain pairs (no loop construct in compiler).

steps.name: Protein Resolubilization
steps.operation: allow precipitate to dry + dispense buffer + incubate
steps.notes: Precipitate allowed to dry on surface. Resolubilizing buffer (AmBic + Pluronic) dispensed from R-5 and incubated 20 min until precipitate fully dissolves. In BioScript, a second ProteinSample dispense abstracts the on-surface precipitate re-contacted with buffer.

steps.name: Reduction
steps.notes: TCEP droplet (R-6) merged with sample. Mixed in circular 6-electrode pattern. Incubated 1 h at room temperature in humidified chamber to reduce disulfide bonds.

steps.name: Alkylation
steps.operation: dispense + merge + circular mix (6-electrode) + incubate in dark
steps.mixing_pattern: Circular actuation across 6 electrodes (same as reduction)
steps.notes: IAM droplet (R-7) merged with reduced sample. Mixed as in S5. Incubated 15 min at room temperature protected from light to alkylate free thiols.

steps.name: Tryptic Digestion
steps.operation: dispense + merge + circular mix (6-electrode) + incubate on hot plate
steps.mixing_pattern: Circular actuation across 6 electrodes (same as reduction)
steps.notes: Trypsin droplet (R-8) merged with alkylated sample. Mixed as in S5. Incubated 3 h at 37 C on hot plate in humidified chamber. Trypsin cleaves at Lys-X and Arg-X.

steps.name: Post-Processing Sample Preparation (off-chip)

sub_steps.action: Remove top substrate; quench digestion by adding 0.6 mL of 2.5% trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) in water
Purify quenched product using C18 ZipTips (Millipore, Billerica, MA) per manufacturer instructions
Dilute purified sample in DI water to a final volume of 100 mL

steps.notes: Off-chip post-processing. TFA quenches trypsin activity. C18 ZipTip SPE desalts and concentrates peptides.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : A Microfluidic Multiplex Sorter for Strain Development
Source Link  : https://advanced.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdfdirect/10.1002/admt.202401209
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1002/admt.202401209
Journal      : Advanced Materials Technologies, 2025, Vol. 10, Article 2401209
Platform     : Droplet-digital microfluidics with multiplex co-planar electrostatic sorting


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a droplet-digital high-throughput screening (HTS) workflow for strain
improvement of Saccharomyces cerevisiae var. diastaticus, a diastatic yeast used in beverage
fermentation for its ability to convert starch and dextrin into fermentable sugars via the
secreted glucoamylase enzyme encoded by the STA1 gene.

The core innovation is a multiplexed electrostatic droplet sorter capable of partitioning a
single genome-shuffled yeast library into two fitness sub-populations simultaneously:
  GT1 (high glucoamylase activity, SC1 channel, 95th fluorescence percentile)
  GT2 (mid glucoamylase activity, SC2 channel, 85th fluorescence percentile)

This avoids the non-uniform sampling bias of binary sorting (which would target only the
top-performing population) and reduces the post-analysis sample size by approximately 14-fold
compared to a binary approach at equivalent 95% confidence. The key finding is that mid-level
sorted strains (IDY1-M23, IDY2-M9) outperform high-level sorted strains in beverage
fermentation, an outcome only discoverable through multiplex screening.

The protocol consists of four sequential phases:
  1. Generation of a diversified genome-shuffled library (>10^7 variants) by self-mating
  2. Single-cell encapsulation in 30 pL droplets, off-chip incubation, and multiplex sorting
  3. Post-HTS colony recovery and maltodextrin growth screening
  4. Beverage fermentation evaluation of selected strains in synthetic media


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Layer i   : Chromium co-planar electrodes patterned on 50 x 75 mm glass slide;
            ground and activated electrodes on same plane (<25 um gap).
Layer ii  : SU-8 5 dielectric, 7 um thick; spin-coated and hard-baked.
Layer iii : PDMS channel layer fabricated by soft lithography;
            channel height 75 um, 100 um width for 30 pL droplet sorting.
            Additional channel heights: 35 um (for 30 pL), 50 um (for 110 pL).

Sorter design:
  - Symmetrical co-planar electrode geometry with three outlets:
      SC1: sorting channel 1 (high-fitness, GT1, SE1 actuation)
      SC2: sorting channel 2 (mid-fitness, GT2, SE2 actuation)
      WC:  central waste channel (non-selected droplets)
  - Two sorting electrodes: SE1 (lateral deflection to SC1) and SE2 (lateral deflection to SC2)
  - No pressure rebalancing or device redesign required for droplet volumes 30-1000 pL
  - Droplet and plug morphologies both sortable (co-planar field intersects both)

Droplet generator: T-junction with 2% fluorosurfactant in HFE7500 oil

Actuation: 15 kHz AC sine wave, 105 Vrms, applied via in-house automation
           software and graphical user interface (Python-based, previously described)
           Software repository: https://bitbucket.org/shihmicrolab/f_ahmadi_2023_uflowcontrol


ORGANISMS
---------
- S. cerevisiae var. diastaticus IDY1: isolated from high-sugar, high-alcohol beverage
  industry setting. More robust and better suited for elevated sugar levels. Grows well
  in all droplet volumes (30, 110, 1000 pL). Peak glucoamylase fluorescence ~3 a.u. at 48 h.
- S. cerevisiae var. diastaticus IDY2: isolated from low-sugar, low-alcohol beverage
  setting. Less adaptable to high sugar; only 30 pL droplets show significant growth.
  Peak glucoamylase fluorescence ~1 a.u. at 48 h.
- IY1: non-diastatic S. cerevisiae (STA1-); negative control; does not secrete glucoamylase.
- IRY1: recombinant S. cerevisiae with heterologous glucoamylase gene; positive control.

Both strains sourced from Lallemand Inc. (Montreal, QC, Canada).


FLUORESCENT SUBSTRATE
---------------------
Substrate : 4-methylumbelliferyl-alpha-D-glucopyranoside (4-MUG-a)
            Validated using commercial Aspergillus niger glucoamylase at pH 7.5 and 11.
            Fluorescent signal distinguishable at neutral pH (pH 7.5) between IDY1/IDY2
            and negative control IY1.
            Previous substrate candidates 4-NPM (absorbance) and 4-NPG rejected:
              4-NPM requires pH >10 (reduces cell viability); absorbance less sensitive.
              4-NPG showed no distinguishable signal for diastatic strains.
Stock     : 4 mM in 0.1 M phosphate buffer pH 7.5
Final     : 2 mM per droplet (1:1 co-encapsulation with cell suspension)
Excitation: 360 nm (ex) / 450 nm (em); measured on CLARIOstar Plus (BMG LABTECH)
BSA       : 10% (w/w) bovine serum albumin added to cell suspension to reduce
            protein adsorption to droplet interface and PDMS walls


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Genome Shuffling Library Generation
  Strains        : IDY1 and IDY2 (independent libraries)
  Method         : Sporulation and self-mating (genome shuffling)
  Sporulation    : Inoculate saturated cultures into sporulation medium (1 g/L yeast
                   extract, 10 g/L KOAc, 0.5 g/L glucose); OD600 start = 0.3
                   Incubate 5 days at 23 C, 150 rpm
  Spore prep     : Ether-zymolyase ascospore technique
  Germination    : ~50 uL YPD 2% glucose, 30 C overnight; then 5 mL 2% YPD, 30 C overnight
  Library size   : >10^7 variants
  Freezer stocks : 25% glycerol (final) added to saturated YPD culture; multiple single-use vials
  Notes          : Non-GMO technique; compliant with agro-food regulatory requirements.
                   IDY2 starts with enhanced growth phenotype in maltodextrin relative to IDY1.

Step 2 | Cell Suspension Preparation
  Preculture     : Overnight YPD broth at 30 C, 200 rpm
  Wash           : Sonicate and wash 3x with PBS by centrifugation
  Resuspend      : 2x YPD broth buffered at pH 7.5
  Cell density   : Adjusted for Poisson lambda=0.3 per droplet size:
                     30 pL  -> 2x10^7 cells/mL
                     110 pL -> 5x10^6 cells/mL
                     1 nL   -> 6x10^5 cells/mL
  BSA            : 10% (w/w) added to cell solution before encapsulation

Step 3 | Single-Cell Encapsulation in 30 pL Droplets
  Generator      : T-junction droplet generator
  Oil            : HFE7500 + 2% PEG fluorosurfactant
  Encapsulation  : 1:1 cell suspension : substrate solution co-flow
  Droplet size   : 30 pL (D = 40 um channel)
  Collection     : PCR tube with 50 uL 2% fluorosurfactant in HFE7500
  Monitoring     : Droplet generation monitored by Fiji (ImageJ) for size verification

Step 4 | Off-Chip Incubation (48 h at 30 C)
  Temperature    : 30 C in the dark
  Duration       : 48 h (= 2880 min = 172800 s)
  Imaging        : Fluorescence + bright-field every 24 h
  Cell growth    : Counted by in-droplet cell counting (Fiji ROI)
  Fluorescence   : CTDF (corrected total droplet fluorescence) quantified per droplet:
                     CTDF = DF/(DA x Mean_BR) - DF_t0/(DA_t0 x Mean_BR_t0)
                     where DF = integrated density, DA = droplet area, BR = background reading
  Optimal volume : 30 pL selected for highest fluorescence and fastest throughput
  Results        : IDY1 peak ~3 a.u. at 48 h (30 pL); IDY2 peak ~1 a.u. at 48 h (30 pL)

Step 5 | Droplet Re-injection and Fluorescence Histogram Gating
  Re-injection   : 3 nL/s droplet flow rate; 300 nL/s spacer oil flow rate
  Tubing         : 1/32" OD, 0.381 mm ID PEEK (re-injection syringe)
  Throughput     : 160 Hz for 30 pL droplets
  Detection      : In-line optical fiber (ex: 470 nm LED, em: 450 nm bandpass filter)
                   Spectrometer: FLAME-S UV-VIS (Ocean Insight)
  Droplets screened: ~720,000 total
  Histogram      : Gaussian fluorescence distribution plotted; gates set as:
                     GT1 (gate-SC1): high fluorescence 95th percentile
                     GT2 (gate-SC2): mid fluorescence 85th percentile

Step 6 | Multiplex Electrostatic Sorting
  Mechanism      : Co-planar electrode actuation laterally deflects droplets into SC1 or SC2.
                   Without actuation: all droplets flow to WC (central waste channel).
  GT1 (SC1)      : SE1 actuated at 15 kHz, 105 Vrms -> high-fitness droplets deflect to SC1
  GT2 (SC2)      : SE2 actuated at 15 kHz, 105 Vrms -> mid-fitness droplets deflect to SC2
  WC (waste)     : Neither electrode actuated; droplet flows undeflected to central channel
  Sorting efficiency: >90.2% true positive; ~3% false negative; no significant difference
                      between SC1 and SC2 channels
  Multiplex efficiency at 30 pL:
    1 mM fluorescein: 100% (SC1), ~3% FN
    0.1 mM fluorescein: 98.6% (SC2), ~3% FN
  Droplets sorted : ~108,000 total (from ~720,000 screened)
  Sorted strains:
    IDY1 GT1 (high): H2, H3
    IDY1 GT2 (mid):  M2, M23
    IDY2 GT1 (high): H13, H23
    IDY2 GT2 (mid):  M9, M22

Step 7 | Colony Recovery and Plating
  Recovery       : Pipette top layer of oil emulsion from pipette tip at SC1 or SC2 outlet
  Aliquot        : 5 uL from sorted population diluted into 50 uL YPD broth
  Plating        : YPD agar plates; incubate 30 C for 48 h
  Colony count   : 24 single colonies picked per gate (GT1 and GT2)
  Glycerol stocks: Remaining emulsion pipetted into YPD broth; grow overnight;
                   add 25% glycerol (final); store at -80 C

Step 8 | Post-HTS Maltodextrin Growth Screening
  Preculture     : Colonies grown in YPD broth, 48 h at 30 C / 300 rpm
  Inoculation    : 5 uL into 1 mL maltodextrin media per well (96-well plate)
  Media          : 2 g/L yeast extract, 4 g/L bacto peptone, 20 g/L maltodextrin
  Incubation     : 30 C, 48 h; OD600 measured at 24 h and 48 h (Tecan Sunrise microplate reader)
  Metric         : Maltodextrin growth fold improvement = Mutant OD600 / Wild type OD600
  Results:
    IDY1 GT1 (high): only H2 showed significant improvement (~2.5x at 48 h)
    IDY1 GT2 (mid):  M2 ~1.4x improvement
    IDY2 GT1 (high): average 2.2x growth improvement vs WT
    IDY2 GT2 (mid):  average 1.7x growth improvement vs WT
  Notes          : IDY2 genome-shuffled populations show enhanced growth baseline vs IDY1
                   in maltodextrin due to starting phenotype advantage.

Step 9 | Enzyme Activity Measurement (parallel to maltodextrin screening)
  Preculture     : 48 h in YPD broth, 30 C, 300 rpm
  Substrate      : 4-MUG-a, 2 mM final concentration
  Protocol       : 20 uL culture + 150 uL YPD broth + 30 uL 4-MUG-a (2 mM);
                   incubate 30 C, 200 rpm; measure fluorescence every 1 h for 15 h
                   (CLARIOstar Plus, ex 360 nm / em 450 nm)
  End-point      : 96-well plate; 50 uL enzyme substrate (2 mM) + 50 uL supernatant;
                   incubate 30 C for 2 h; stop buffer pH 11; read fluorescence
  Metric         : Enzyme activity fold improvement = Mutant Activity (U/mL OD) / WT Activity (U/mL OD)
  Results:
    IDY1 GT1: ~3.7x fold improvement (average) vs WT; only H2 statistically significant (~3x)
    IDY1 GT2: ~1.2x fold improvement (average)
    IDY2 GT1: ~2x fold improvement (7 high strains showed improvement)
    IDY2 GT2: ~2x fold improvement (13 mid strains showed improvement at 24 h and 48 h)

Step 10 | Beverage Fermentation Evaluation
  Preculture     : YPD broth 48 h at 30 C, 300 rpm
  Inoculum       : 100 uL into 3 mL synthetic beverage media
  Synthetic media: 125 g/L maltose, 60 g/L maltodextrin, 1 mL ethanol,
                   1.25 mL 50% glycerol (in water), 3 mL 85% lactic acid,
                   2 g/L yeast extract, 6.4 g/L bactopeptone,
                   pH 5.9, 25 mg/mL chloramphenicol
  Vials          : 6 mL mini vials sealed with rubber caps; needles for gas exchange
  Mixing         : 180 rpm for 5 min; then without agitation
  Temperature    : Phase 1: 20 C for 22 h; Phase 2: 30 C until 72 h endpoint
  Weight loss    : Measured at 0, 18, 24, 42, 48, 66, 72 h (precision scale)
  Fermentation complete: 72 h (final mass loss point)
  Dry biomass    : Pellet cells; dry at 60 C overnight; weigh
  Metrics:
    CO2 released per mg dry biomass (mg CO2/mg yeast)
    Ethanol content normalised to dry biomass (mg ethanol/mL per mg yeast)
    Fermentation rate (mass loss rate h^-1)
  Statistical    : One-way ANOVA at 95% CI, N=3; p-values vs WT:
                   ns: p=0.1234, *: p=0.0332, **: p=0.0021, ***: p=0.0002, ****: p<0.0001
  Key results:
    IDY1-M23 (GT2/mid): highest CO2 mass loss ~7.8 mg CO2/mg biomass at 72 h
                         (vs ~5.01 mg CO2/mg biomass for WT IDY1)
                         Only IDY1 strain to show significant ethanol content improvement
    IDY2-M9  (GT2/mid): mass loss rate ~0.128 h^-1; highest CO2 and ethanol yield for IDY2
    IDY2-H13 (GT1/high): mass loss rate ~0.105 h^-1; second best for IDY2
    Top ethanol producers: IDY1-M23, IDY2-M9 (both mid-level sorted)
  Key finding    : Mid-level sorted strains outperform high-level sorted strains in fermentation.
                   Hypothesised mechanism: high-level strains incur increased metabolic burden
                   from elevated glucoamylase expression (higher ATP demand, amino acid
                   consumption for protein synthesis, diversion from fermentation).
                   Mid-level strains balance enzyme secretion with metabolic load, maintaining
                   fermentation efficiency. This is consistent with metabolic burden literature
                   in heterologous protein production.


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : leal_alves_multiplex_sorter_strain_development.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 13 basic blocks (BB1-BB13), 4 if/else gates, 16 CFG edges
DAG            : leal_alves_multiplex_sorter_strain_development_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations converted to minutes (m) for compiler compatibility
                 (BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported)
                 48 h incubation    -> 2880m  (IR: 172800.0 SECOND)
                 22 h ferment ph1   -> 1320m  (IR: 79200.0 SECOND)
                 50 h ferment ph2   -> 3000m  (IR: 180000.0 SECOND)
                 48 h preculture    -> 2880m  (IR: 172800.0 SECOND)
                 5 min mixing       -> 5m     (IR: 300.0 SECOND)
Modules        : glucoamylaseDetection, maltodextrinGrowthDetection, fermentationDetection
Manifests      : IDY1_Cells, IDY2_Cells, YPD_Media, MUG_Alpha_Substrate,
                 PhosphateBuffer_pH7_5, BSA_Solution, HFE7500_Surfactant, SpacerOil,
                 MaltodextrinMedia, SyntheticBeverageMedia
Biological scope note : This .bs file encodes the IDY1 arm as representative.
                 The IDY2 arm requires a separate .bs file with IDY2_Cells manifest.
                 Sorter parameters, droplet conditions, and assay protocol are identical.
IR verified    : All 13 BBs present; all fluid variables consumed (no stranded variables);
                 two-phase fermentation heat modelled as sequential heat statements on same
                 fluid variable; drain normalised to dispose in IR (compiler behaviour).
DAG verified   : Correct diamond-pattern topology; 4 gates; single terminal node (BB13/NOP).

steps.name: Droplet re-injection and flow-through fluorescence detection
steps.operation: re-injection into sorter (abstracted as mix in BioScript)
steps.detection_method: In-line optical fiber fluorescence (ex 470 nm LED, em 450 nm bandpass)
steps.histogram_gating: Gaussian fluorescence distribution used to set GT1 and GT2 thresholds
steps.notes: Fluorescence intensity measured by in-house automation software to route each droplet to SE1, SE2, or WC.

steps.name: Multiplex sorting - high-fitness gate (GT1)
steps.operation: electrostatic sorting (abstracted as detect + if/else in BioScript)

steps.name: Multiplex sorting - mid-fitness gate (GT2)
steps.key_finding: Mid-level sorted strains (IDY1-M23, IDY2-M9) showed superior fermentation performance vs high-level sorted strains; would have been missed by binary screening

steps.name: Colony recovery and plating
recovery_steps: Pipette top layer of oil emulsion from pipette tips at SC1 or SC2 outlets
Take 5 uL aliquots from sorted population
Pick 24 single colonies per gate (GT1 and GT2) for post-HTS analysis
Prepare glycerol freezer stocks from remaining emulsion (YPD broth overnight)

steps.preculture: YPD broth 48 h at 30 C / 300 rpm

steps.measurement: OD600 at 24 h and 48 h (Tecan Sunrise microplate reader)
steps.metric: Maltodextrin growth fold improvement = Mutant OD / Wild type OD

steps.vial: 6 mL mini vials sealed with rubber caps pierced with needles for gas exchange
steps.synthetic_media_composition: 125 g/L maltose, 60 g/L maltodextrin, 1 mL ethanol, 1.25 mL 50% glycerol, 3 mL 85% lactic acid, 2 g/L yeast extract, 6.4 g/L bactopeptone, pH 5.9, 25 mg/mL chloramphenicol
steps.mixing: 180 rpm for 5 min at start; then without agitation
steps.dry_biomass: Pellet cells; dry at 60 C overnight

metrics.primary: CO2 released per mg dry biomass (mg CO2/mg yeast)
metrics.secondary: Ethanol content normalised to dry biomass (mg ethanol/mL per mg yeast)

results.key_finding: Mid-level sorted strains outperformed high-level sorted strains in fermentation; attributed to balanced glucoamylase expression avoiding metabolic burden

design_efficiency_without_actuation.result: 100% droplets directed to WC regardless of droplet volume

sorting_efficiency_with_actuation.channel_difference: no significant difference between SC1 and SC2 efficiency

binary_vs_multiplex_comparison.sampling_overhead_vs_multiplex: at least 14x more strains needed for equivalent 95% confidence
binary_vs_multiplex_comparison.conclusion: Multiplex reduces sample size ~14x for post-analysis; avoids non-uniform exploration of fitness landscape
