description:
================================================================================
PROTOCOL: LENGEN - Lentiviral Generation, Packaging, and Transduction
         on a Digital Microfluidic (DMF) Platform
================================================================================

SOURCE LINK : https://40332f11-eff8-4959-967a-6c98c26063bd.filesusr.com/ugd/447feb_13f855ea4ef54fee80498ee6773b93b0.pdf
PAPER DOI   : https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.analchem.1c05227
PUBLISHED   : Analytical Chemistry, 2022, Vol. 94, pp. 4039-4047

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
OVERVIEW
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

LENGEN is the first microfluidic method that integrates lentiviral generation,
packaging, and transduction on a single digital microfluidic (DMF) platform.
It produces viral titers between 6.5 x 10^6 and 1.33 x 10^7 TU/mL (comparable
to macroscale) and achieves high transduction efficiency for hard-to-transfect
cell lines. The total protocol runs in approximately 2 days vs. ~2 weeks at
macroscale, with 100-fold volume savings and no ultracentrifugation or manual
purification.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVICE SPECIFICATIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Platform                  : Digital Microfluidic (DMF), two-plate system
  Bottom plate electrodes   : 80 per set (2 sets total = 160 electrodes)
  Production site           : 1.6 mm diameter hydrophilic spot (x1 per set)
  Transduction sites        : ~1.2 mm diameter hydrophilic spots (x6 per set)
  Multiplexing              : 12-plex simultaneous transduction analysis
  Production droplet volume : ~3 uL (split into ~1 uL unit droplets)
  Actuation voltage         : ~500 V total, 15 kHz
  Electrode design          : Overlapping "prong" electrodes bussed via 2 wired
                              connections (22 electrodes per connection)
  Highway track             : One-directional delivery to 6 transduction sites

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
REAGENTS AND MATERIALS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  CELLS
  - HEK293T            : Producer/packaging cell line
  - Target cell lines  : MCF-7, T47DKB-Luc, H1299 (breast cancer / lung)

  PLASMIDS (Core - Steps 1-8)
  - pMDLg/pRRE         : 0.75 ug  | Packaging plasmid
  - pRSV-Rev           : 0.75 ug  | Packaging plasmid
  - pMD2.G             : 1.5 ug   | Envelope plasmid
  - Transfer plasmid   : 3.0 ug   | e.g. pLv-mCherry (~4 kb)

  PLASMIDS (Optional Applications)
  - MISSION shRNA      : TRCN00000003300 | ESR1 knockdown (Step 9)
  - pLentiCRISPR-mCherry-NeoRv2 (LCMNv2) : ~15 kb | ESR1 knockout (Step 10)

  TRANSFECTION REAGENTS
  - Lipofectamine 3000 : 12.5 uL
  - P3000 Reagent      : 12.0 uL
  - Opti-MEM           : Total volume 500 uL
  - Pluronics F-127    : 0.05% w/v (added to all droplets for DMF actuation)

  CULTURE AND PROCESSING
  - Complete medium    : DMEM + 10% heat-inactivated FBS
  - DMEM + Polybrene   : 8 ug/mL polybrene + 0.05% Pluronics F-127 (diluent)
  - Trypsin-EDTA       : 0.25% w/v, 2 uL per well (cell detachment)
  - PBS                : 5 uL per well (wash buffer prior to trypsinization)
  - Puromycin          : 1 ug/mL (selection, Step 9 only)

  DETECTION
  - Fluorescence microscope : Olympus IX73 inverted
    Excitation / Emission   : 585 nm / 608 nm (mCherry)
  - Hoechst 33342           : Nuclear stain (total cell count)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 1 - SEED HEK293T PRODUCER CELLS
--------------------------------------
  1a. Grow HEK293T cells in 100 mm Petri dishes, wash with PBS, trypsinize
      with 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA, and resuspend in complete medium.
  1b. Count cells and prepare suspension at ~2.5-3.0 x 10^6 cells/mL.
  1c. Supplement cell suspension with 0.05% w/v Pluronics F-127.
  1d. Pipette 1.5 uL of cell suspension onto the bottom plate at the edge
      of the top plate. Apply driving potentials (~500 V, 15 kHz) to
      dispense and actuate droplet across the 1.6 mm hydrophilic production
      site (passive dispensing). ~1.5 uL adheres to the site.
  1e. Remove excess liquid to a waste reservoir with a KimWipe.
  1f. Incubate at 37 C until cells reach 50-70% confluency (~2500 cells).
      Duration: 24h

  NOTE: Cells can also be seeded onto the ~1.2 mm transduction sites in
  parallel at densities of 1.0-1.5 x 10^6 cells/mL (Step 5 may be done
  concurrently with Steps 2-4).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 2 - PREPARE LIPOFECTAMINE-DNA MASTERMIX
---------------------------------------------
  2a. Prepare plasmid mix in Opti-MEM:
        - 0.75 ug pMDLg/pRRE
        - 0.75 ug pRSV-Rev
        - 1.5 ug  pMD2.G
        - 3.0 ug  transfer plasmid (pLv-mCherry or equivalent)
      Mix each addition for 5s on the DMF device using the four-electrode
      linear array.

  2b. Prepare lipofection reagent mix:
        - 12.5 uL Lipofectamine 3000
        - 12.0 uL P3000 Reagent
      Mix for 5s.

  2c. Combine plasmid mix with lipofection reagent mix. Mix for 5s.

  2d. Add Opti-MEM to reach a total volume of 500 uL. Mix for 5s.

  2e. Add 0.05% w/v Pluronics F-127 for DMF actuation compatibility.
      Mix for 20m.

  2f. Incubate at room temperature (25 C) for 20 min to allow
      DNA-liposomal complex formation.

  NOTE: For shRNA knockdown (Step 9), replace transfer plasmid with
  MISSION shRNA plasmid (TRCN00000003300). For CRISPR knockout (Step 10),
  replace with LCMNv2 all-in-one Cas9/sgRNA plasmid (~15 kb).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 3 - TRANSFECT HEK293T CELLS
----------------------------------
  3a. Actuate the lipofectamine mastermix droplet (1.5 uL) toward the
      seeded HEK293T cells at the production site.
  3b. Circulate the merged droplet continuously around the four-prong
      electrode production area for 1 min (3 circulations) to ensure
      uniform mixing and replicate the reverse transfection procedure.
  3c. The formulation (3 uL total) is mixed in a circular fashion by
      actuating adjacent electrodes.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 4 - LENTIVIRAL PARTICLE PRODUCTION AND SUPERNATANT HARVEST
-----------------------------------------------------------------
  4a. Incubate the transfected HEK293T cells at 37 C for 24h (or 48h for
      higher titer).
  4b. Lentiviral particles accumulate in the cell supernatant. Cells remain
      adhered to the hydrophilic production spot; supernatant is collected
      by electrode actuation for downstream dilution.

  Expected output:
    - 24h: ~1.56 TU/cell | Titer ~6.5 x 10^6 TU/mL
    - 48h: ~2.65 TU/cell | Titer ~1.33 x 10^7 TU/mL
    - Comparable to macroscale benchtop: ~2.80 TU/cell after 5 days

  NOTE: The 24h timepoint is sufficient for downstream gene silencing and
  editing assays. No ultracentrifugation or purification is required.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 5 - SEED TARGET CELLS
----------------------------
  5a. Prepare target cell suspension (MCF-7, T47DKB-Luc, or H1299) at
      1.0-1.5 x 10^6 cells/mL in complete medium + 0.05% Pluronics F-127.
  5b. Dispense four independent target cell droplets (one per dilution) onto
      four separate 1.2 mm hydrophilic transduction sites via highway track
      passive dispensing. ~1.0 uL adheres to each site. Two additional sites
      are available for controls (complete medium +/- polybrene, no virus).
  5c. Remove excess liquid to waste reservoir.
  5d. Incubate at 37 C for 24h before transduction.

  Cell viability on device:
    - MCF-7      : 83.7% (48h), 85.7% (72h)
    - T47DKB-Luc : 98.4% (48h), 88.6% (72h)

  NOTE: Four independent target cell droplets are dispensed separately in
  the BioScript implementation to satisfy the use-once type system (each
  droplet variable can only be consumed once).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 6 - SERIAL DILUTION OF VIRAL SUPERNATANT
-----------------------------------------------
  6a. After production incubation (Step 4), generate four serial dilutions
      of the lentiviral supernatant using highway track electrode actuation
      (~98% actuation accuracy):

      Diluent: DMEM + 10% heat-inactivated FBS + 8 ug/mL polybrene
               + 0.05% Pluronics F-127

      Dilution series:
        1:3  - Merge 1 uL DMEM diluent with 2 uL viral supernatant (5s mix)
        1:6  - Merge 1 uL DMEM diluent with 1 uL of 1:3 product  (5s mix)
        1:12 - Merge 1 uL DMEM diluent with 1 uL of 1:6 product  (5s mix)
        1:24 - Merge 1 uL DMEM diluent with 1 uL of 1:12 product (5s mix)

  6b. Two control spots are prepared:
        - Control 1: Complete medium + 8 ug/mL polybrene (no virus)
        - Control 2: Complete medium only (no polybrene, no virus)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 7 - TRANSDUCE TARGET CELLS
---------------------------------
  7a. Actuate each dilution (1 uL) to its dedicated target cell site via the
      highway track one-directional electrode path. Each dilution is merged
      with its own independent target cell droplet. The transduction
      incubation is encoded directly in the mix operation (24h duration).
  7b. Flip the DMF device upside down and incubate overnight at 37 C to
      maximize lentiviral contact with target cells.
      Duration: 24h (sufficient) or 48h (for improved efficiency)

  Transduction efficiency (T47DKB-Luc):
    - 48h post-transduction : ~43%
    - 96h post-transduction : ~60%

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 8 - MCHERRY FLUORESCENCE DETECTION AND VIRAL TITER CALCULATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------
  8a. After incubation, image each transduction site using an Olympus IX73
      inverted fluorescence microscope.
        Excitation filter : 585 nm
        Emission filter   : 608 nm

  8b. Imaging pipeline (ImageJ):
        i.   Split Hoechst (nuclear) and mCherry channels
        ii.  Apply threshold to each channel independently
        iii. Count total Hoechst-stained nuclei (cell counter)
        iv.  Count mCherry-positive cells
        v.   Calculate: % Fluorescence = (mCherry+ cells / Hoechst nuclei) x 100

  8c. Calculate viral titer:
        TU/mL = (# cells transduced x % fluorescent x dilution factor)
                / transduction volume (mL)

  8d. QC gate (BioScript CFG):
        - Detect mCherry signal on all four transduction droplets (30s each).
        - If signal at 1:3 dilution > 0 : dispose transduction droplets (pass)
        - If signal at 1:3 dilution <= 0 : drain transduction droplets (fail)
        - All signal droplets are disposed unconditionally at the join block.

  Expected results:
    - Optimal dilution    : 1:3
    - Titer range         : 6.5 x 10^6 to 1.33 x 10^7 TU/mL
    - Functional titer    : ~1 x 10^7 TU/mL (on-device, 24h or 48h)
    - Macroscale benchtop : ~1 x 10^7 TU/mL (for comparison)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 9 - shRNA KNOCKDOWN ASSAY [OPTIONAL]
------------------------------------------
  Target gene : ESR1 (Estrogen Receptor alpha)
  Plasmid     : MISSION shRNA (TRCN00000003300, nontargeting shRNA as control)

  9a. Repeat Steps 2-8 substituting the transfer plasmid with the MISSION
      shRNA plasmid targeting ESR1. Fresh independent producer cell and
      target cell droplets are dispensed for this branch.
  9b. After 24h transduction, retrieve transduced cells from the device:
        i.   Bring device to biosafety cabinet and separate top from bottom plate.
        ii.  Pipette 5 uL PBS onto each microwell; aspirate with Pasteur pipette
             (leaves only adhered cells).
        iii. Add 2 uL Trypsin-EDTA (0.25% w/v); replace top plate; incubate
             2 min at 37 C with 5% CO2.
        iv.  Pool 2 microwells of the same dilution by resuspending each in
             10 uL complete medium; transfer to 100 uL complete medium in a
             96-well plate (~2800 cells total).
  9c. Next day, refresh medium with complete medium + 1 ug/mL puromycin.
  9d. After 7 days outgrowth, collect cell lysate for qRT-PCR analysis.
        Method          : delta-delta-Cq (DDCq)
        Reference gene  : ACTB (beta-actin)
        Target gene     : ESR1

  9e. QC gate (BioScript CFG):
        - Detect geneKnockdownDetection signal on shrnaCells (30s).
        - If shrnaSignal > 0 : dispose shrnaCells (pass)
        - If shrnaSignal <= 0 : drain shrnaCells (fail)
        - shrnaSignal disposed unconditionally at join block.

  Expected mRNA transcript reduction (MCF-7 cells, LENGEN):
    Dilution 1:3  -> 89% knockdown
    Dilution 1:6  -> 79% knockdown
    Dilution 1:12 -> 48% knockdown
    Dilution 1:24 -> 18% knockdown

  NOTE: Results are consistent with well-plate (macroscale) controls at
  equivalent MOIs (MOI 5 = 89% knockdown in well plate).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 10 - CRISPR-Cas9 KNOCKOUT ASSAY [OPTIONAL]
-------------------------------------------------
  Target gene : ESR1 (Estrogen Receptor alpha)
  Plasmid     : pLentiCRISPR-mCherry-NeoRv2 (LCMNv2), ~15 kb all-in-one
                Cas9 + sgRNA (available on Addgene)

  10a. Repeat Steps 2-8 substituting the transfer plasmid with LCMNv2.
       Fresh independent producer cell and target cell droplets are dispensed
       for this branch. Note: Larger payload (~15 kb vs ~4 kb) will reduce
       transduction efficiency; optimize MOI/dilution accordingly.
  10b. Retrieve transduced MCF-7 cells from device as described in Step 9b.
       No antibiotic selection required for CRISPR experiments.
  10c. Pool 1:3 dilution transduced cells (~2800 cells) into a 96-well plate
       for outgrowth and single-clone isolation.
  10d. After 7 days post-transduction, collect cell lysate and perform
       genomic cleavage assay (T7 endonuclease or equivalent):
         Parental band  : 409 bp  (blue arrow on gel)
         Cleavage bands : 235 bp and 174 bp (red arrows on gel)
         % Cleavage calculated from band intensity ratios.

  10e. Confirm mCherry fluorescence to verify transduction before cleavage
       assay (mCherry co-expressed with Cas9 in LCMNv2).

  10f. QC gate (BioScript CFG):
        - Detect mCherryDetection signal on crisprCells (30s).
        - If crisprMCherry > 0 : dispose crisprCells (pass)
        - If crisprMCherry <= 0 : drain crisprCells (fail)
        - crisprMCherry disposed unconditionally at terminal join block (BB10).

  Expected knockout cleavage efficiency:
    LENGEN (1:3 dilution) : ~6.9%
    Well plate MOI 0.5    : ~5.8%
    Well plate MOI 1      : ~6.2%
    Well plate MOI 2      : ~6.4%
    Well plate MOI 5      : ~9.4%

  NOTE: For H1299 cells with integrated eGFP, gene cleavage efficiency
  of 16.1% was observed using the same LENGEN workflow.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PERFORMANCE SUMMARY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Protocol duration     : ~2 days  (vs. ~2 weeks macroscale)
  Volume savings        : 100-fold reduction vs. macroscale
  Viral titer           : 6.5 x 10^6 - 1.33 x 10^7 TU/mL
  TU per cell (24h)     : ~1.56   (macroscale 5-day: ~2.80)
  TU per cell (48h)     : ~2.65   (macroscale 5-day: ~2.80)
  Cells per target spot : ~1400
  Pooled cells (harvest): ~2800
  Multiplexing          : 12-plex simultaneous on one device
  Ultracentrifugation   : Not required
  Manual purification   : Not required
  Automation            : Full - droplet actuation programmed on DMF

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
BIOSCRIPT IMPLEMENTATION NOTES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Compiler         : lilott8/BioScript (github.com/lilott8/BioScript)
  Target           : IR (-t ir); CFG output (-cfg)

  CFG STRUCTURE (10 basic blocks, verified against lengen_lentiviral_main_dag.dot)
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  BB1  main          : Entry - all dispense/mix/heat/detect ops (Steps 1-8)
  BB2  bsbbif_2_t    : mCherry QC pass  - dispose transduction droplets
  BB3  bsbbif_3_f    : mCherry QC fail  - drain transduction droplets
  BB4  bsbbif_4_j    : qcJoin           - dispose signal droplets; enter Step 9
  BB5  bsbbif_5_t    : shRNA QC pass    - dispose shrnaCells
  BB6  bsbbif_6_f    : shRNA QC fail    - drain shrnaCells
  BB7  bsbbif_7_j    : shrnaJoin        - dispose shrnaSignal; enter Step 10
  BB8  bsbbif_8_t    : CRISPR QC pass   - dispose crisprCells
  BB9  bsbbif_9_f    : CRISPR QC fail   - drain crisprCells
  BB10 bsbbif_10_j   : finalCleanup     - dispose crisprMCherry; NOP (terminal)

  KEY COMPILER CONSTRAINTS
  ------------------------
  1. ASCII only      : ANTLR4 FileStream uses strict ASCII encoding. No Unicode
                       characters permitted anywhere in the .bs file, including
                       comments (e.g. use "DDCq" not delta-delta-Cq symbol).

  2. heat is void    : heat statement has no return value. Do not assign:
                         WRONG : x = heat y at 37c for 24h
                         RIGHT : heat y at 37c for 24h
                       The original variable y remains valid after heat.

  3. Use-once        : Every variable is consumed on first use. Separate
                       dispense calls are required for each branch and each
                       dilution (e.g. four independent targetSuspension[1-4]
                       droplets for four transduction sites).

  4. Incubation in   : Post-mix incubation is encoded in the mix duration
     mix duration      per reference syntax (ace_crispr_raf1_sorafenib.bs):
                         RIGHT : mix dilution_1_3 with targetSuspension1 for 24h
                       Do not add a separate heat call after mix for incubation.

  5. drain vs dispose: Both drain and dispose are semantically distinct in .bs
                       source (dispose = data accepted; drain = waste discard).
                       The lilott8/BioScript IR target lowers both to dispose()
                       opcode. The distinction is preserved in .bs source only.

  6. CFG fall-through: True-branch (_t) blocks fall through to the join block.
                       False-branch (_f) blocks emit an explicit jump instruction.

================================================================================
END OF PROTOCOL
================================================================================

steps.description: Deliver each dilution to its own target cell site via highway track one-directional electrode actuation. Incubation encoded in mix duration per BioScript reference syntax.

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidics Platform for Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification Detection (DMF-LAMP) for c-Myc Oncogene Amplification

REAGENTS USED:
  - LAMPMix (LAMP reaction reagents: 0.8 uM each inner primer FIP and BIP, 0.2 uM each outer primer FP and BP, 0.4 mM dNTP mix, 1 M betaine, 4 mM MgCl2, 1x supplied buffer, 8 U Bst DNA polymerase large fragment; 0.14 uL per droplet)
  - DNASample (target c-Myc proto-oncogene DNA resuspended in 1x enzyme buffer at 0.5 ng/uL; 0.14 uL per droplet)

STEPS:
1. Reagent dispensing: Dispense 10 droplets (~0.14 uL each, ~1.40 uL total) of LAMPMix from the left reservoir and transport to the central reaction reservoir via zig-zag electrodes.
2. Sample dispensing: Dispense 1 droplet (~0.14 uL) of DNASample from the right reservoir and transport to the central reaction reservoir.
3. Mixing: Merge and mix the LAMP reagent and DNA sample droplets in the central reaction reservoir (total on-chip reaction volume: 1.54 uL; final DNA concentration: 0.5 ng/uL).
4. First incubation: Incubate the reaction droplet isothermally at 65 C for 15 min (bottom-plate set point; vertical temperature gradient across droplet: 0.3 C; mixing region electrodes kept activated at 20 VRMS, 5 kHz).
5. First amplification check: Assess amplification by fluorescence readout (standing in for gel-electrophoresis band intensity).
6. Second incubation: If no amplification detected, continue isothermal incubation at 65 C for a further 15 min (cumulative 30 min).
7. Second amplification check: Assess amplification again.
8. Third incubation: If still no amplification detected, continue isothermal incubation at 65 C for a further 15 min (cumulative 45 min).
9. Third amplification check: Assess amplification again. If still negative, discard the reaction droplet.
10. Product retrieval: On successful amplification, transport the reaction product droplet to the retrieving reservoir and withdraw from the device via pipette.

INTERPRETATION: Successful c-Myc LAMP amplification is confirmed by the appearance of a characteristic LAMP ladder band pattern on gel electrophoresis (Figure 3e, Lane 7, positive at 45 min cumulative incubation). The on-chip DMF-LAMP product shows higher normalized band fluorescence intensity (139.0 a.u.) than the equivalent bench-top reaction (78.8 a.u.), indicating enhanced amplification efficiency in the miniaturized DMF format. Negative controls show no amplification at any time point. The platform achieves sensitive amplification of 0.5 ng/uL target DNA in 1.54 uL total volume in 45 min.

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code is a direct translation of the paper's on-chip DMF-LAMP protocol (Section 2.6 and Figure 1b/3e), covering the reagent dispensing and transport from opposing reservoirs (steps 1-2), merging and mixing in the central reaction reservoir (step 3), isothermal incubation at 65 C evaluated at 15-min checkpoints (steps 4-9), and product withdrawal (step 10). Reaction volumes (10 LAMP-mix droplets of 0.14 uL each + 1 DNA droplet of 0.14 uL = 1.54 uL total), DNA concentration (0.5 ng/uL), temperature (65 C bottom-plate set point), and time checkpoints (15, 30, 45 min, per Figure 3e) are taken directly from Sections 2.5-2.6. Because BioScript has no primitive for a persistent solid substrate or electrode actuation pattern, the zig-zag electrode transport and on-chip mixing motions are folded into the dispense and mix operations respectively. The DBS punch re-dispense pattern used in other protocols is not applicable here; LAMPMix and DNASample are each dispensed once. The detection modality in the paper is gel electrophoresis (band fluorescence intensity), not a fluorogenic real-time readout; 'detect fluorescence' is used as the BioScript stand-in for the generic amplification-confirmed readout, with the threshold (<=80 a.u.) representing absence of a positive LAMP band, consistent with the normalized intensities reported in Section 3.4 (139.0 a.u. positive vs. 78.8 a.u. bench-top). LAMP is isothermal and requires no thermal cycling; the repeat structure used in PCR protocols is intentionally absent. The bench-top LAMP optimization (Section 2.3-2.4), temperature gradient characterization (Section 3.2), impedance-based droplet velocity monitoring (Figure 3a-b), and bench-top comparison reactions (Figure 3f) are hardware-control or validation sub-experiments not captured in the core protocol translation.

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic Platform for Multiplexed Fluorometric Enzyme Assays (Acid alpha-Glucosidase/GAA for Pompe Disease and Acid alpha-Galactosidase/GLA for Fabry Disease) in Dried Blood Spots for Newborn Lysosomal Storage Disease Screening

REAGENTS USED:
  - DBS Extract (single 3-mm dried-blood-spot punch extracted in 100 uL of 0.1% w/v Tween20 extraction buffer, 30 min at room temperature; one extract shared for both GAA and GLA assays)
  - GAA Reagent (2.5 mmol/L 4-methylumbelliferyl-alpha-D-glucoside substrate in sodium acetate, pH 3.8, with 6 umol/L acarbose inhibitor)
  - GLA Reagent (5 mmol/L 4-methylumbelliferyl-alpha-D-galactoside substrate in 40 mmol/L sodium acetate, pH 4.5, with 75 umol/L N-acetyl-D-galactosamine inhibitor)
  - Extraction Buffer (EXT: 0.1% w/v Tween20 in water)
  - Stop Buffer (STB: 0.2 mol/L NaHCO3, pH 10.0, 0.01% w/v Tween20)
  - Calibrant (known concentration of 4-methylumbelliferone, 4-MU, used for 2-point fluorescence calibration)

STEPS:
1. Two-point fluorescence calibration: dispense a calibrant droplet and read fluorescence (high calibrant value); dispense a stop-buffer-only droplet and read fluorescence (low calibrant/background value).
2. Substrate background (surrogate t=0): merge GAA reagent with extraction buffer (no DBS extract) plus stop buffer and read fluorescence as the GAA background; repeat the same merge/read for GLA reagent as the GLA background.
3. For each DBS extract loaded onto the cartridge (up to 11 samples per run): dispense one extract droplet and split it into two parallel reactions by merging separately with GAA reagent and GLA reagent.
4. t=0 measurement: immediately merge a droplet from each reaction with stop buffer and read fluorescence (GAA t=0 and GLA t=0), then discard these aliquots.
5. Incubate the remaining GAA and GLA reaction droplets at 37 C (1 h for the reduced-incubation protocol; 6 h in the original bench-comparison protocol).
6. Endpoint measurement: merge each incubated reaction droplet with stop buffer and read endpoint fluorescence (GAA endpoint and GLA endpoint), converting readings to enzyme activity via the calibration curve.
7. Screening interpretation: compare GAA and GLA endpoint activity against the normal/affected separation boundary established from control and disease samples; flag and discard reaction droplets whose activity falls at or below the cutoff as presumptively affected (Pompe or Fabry), otherwise report as normal.

module fluorescence

manifest dbs_extract
manifest gaa_reagent
manifest gla_reagent
manifest extraction_buffer
manifest stop_buffer
manifest calibrant

instructions:

cal_drop = dispense 2 units of calibrant
high_cal = detect fluorescence on cal_drop for 1m
dispose cal_drop

blank_drop = dispense 2 units of stop_buffer
low_cal = detect fluorescence on blank_drop for 1m
dispose blank_drop

gaa_bg_sub = dispense 1 units of gaa_reagent
gaa_bg_ext = dispense 1 units of extraction_buffer
gaa_bg_mix = mix gaa_bg_sub with gaa_bg_ext for 15s
gaa_bg_stb = dispense 1 units of stop_buffer
gaa_bg_final = mix gaa_bg_mix with gaa_bg_stb for 15s
gaa_background = detect fluorescence on gaa_bg_final for 1m
dispose gaa_bg_final

gla_bg_sub = dispense 1 units of gla_reagent
gla_bg_ext = dispense 1 units of extraction_buffer
gla_bg_mix = mix gla_bg_sub with gla_bg_ext for 15s
gla_bg_stb = dispense 1 units of stop_buffer
gla_bg_final = mix gla_bg_mix with gla_bg_stb for 15s
gla_background = detect fluorescence on gla_bg_final for 1m
dispose gla_bg_final

repeat 11 times {

    sample = dispense 1 units of dbs_extract

    gaa_sub = dispense 1 units of gaa_reagent
    gaa_rxn = mix sample with gaa_sub for 30s

    gla_sub = dispense 1 units of gla_reagent
    gla_rxn = mix sample with gla_sub for 30s

    gaa_stb0 = dispense 1 units of stop_buffer
    gaa_t0_mix = mix gaa_rxn with gaa_stb0 for 15s
    gaa_t0 = detect fluorescence on gaa_t0_mix for 1m
    dispose gaa_t0_mix

    gla_stb0 = dispense 1 units of stop_buffer
    gla_t0_mix = mix gla_rxn with gla_stb0 for 15s
    gla_t0 = detect fluorescence on gla_t0_mix for 1m
    dispose gla_t0_mix

    heat gaa_rxn at 37c for 60m
    heat gla_rxn at 37c for 60m

    gaa_stb1 = dispense 1 units of stop_buffer
    gaa_end_mix = mix gaa_rxn with gaa_stb1 for 15s
    gaa_endpoint = detect fluorescence on gaa_end_mix for 1m

    gla_stb1 = dispense 1 units of stop_buffer
    gla_end_mix = mix gla_rxn with gla_stb1 for 15s
    gla_endpoint = detect fluorescence on gla_end_mix for 1m

    if (gaa_endpoint <= 5) {
        dispose gaa_end_mix
    }

    if (gla_endpoint <= 3) {
        dispose gla_end_mix
    }

    dispose gaa_end_mix
    dispose gla_end_mix
}

metadata.protocol_name: Multiplex Digital Microfluidic Fluorometric Enzyme Assay for Pompe (GAA) and Fabry (GLA) Screening in Dried Blood Spots (Sista et al. 2011)

sources.title: Digital Microfluidic Platform for Multiplexing Enzyme Assays: Implications for Lysosomal Storage Disease Screening in Newborns

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code translates the paper's digital microfluidic multiplex enzyme-screening workflow (PROTOCOLS FOR THE DIGITAL MICROFLUIDIC FLUOROMETRIC ENZYME ASSAYS and DIGITAL MICROFLUIDIC PROTOCOL FOR ENZYME ANALYSIS WITH REDUCED INCUBATION TIME sections), covering the 2-point fluorescence calibration, the substrate-only background reading used as a surrogate t=0 (in place of a per-sample t=0 for every droplet), the per-sample split of a single DBS extract into parallel GAA and GLA reactions (the paper's key single-punch multiplexing innovation), the t=0 and endpoint fluorescence reads bracketing a 37C incubation, and a threshold check modeling the normal/affected separation boundary used to flag Pompe- or Fabry-affected samples. The 'repeat 11 times' block models the 11 DBS-extract reservoirs processed per cartridge (Fig. 1: 6 normal + 1 Pompe-affected + 1 Fabry-affected + 3 QC spots), rather than the full 10-day/60-plus-21-sample method-comparison study. The 1-h incubation time reflects the paper's reduced-incubation protocol (evaluated on 105 additional normal DBSs); the original bench-comparison protocol used 6-h (digital microfluidic) and 20-h (Duke BGL benchtop) incubations, which are not separately modeled. Because BioScript's grammar exposes only a generic 'detect fluorescence' primitive and no droplet-splitting operator, the single-punch extract is modeled by dispensing a fresh 'dbs_extract' droplet per reaction branch (mirroring how the reference ciprofloxacin/PCR scripts re-dispense reagents) rather than an explicit split of one physical droplet. The intercartridge/intracartridge CV determination experiments (QC low/medium/high spots over a 10-day period), the hematocrit/hemoglobin-quenching characterization (Fig. 3, Supplemental Fig. 4), the Michaelis-Menten/Lineweaver-Burk kinetics characterization (Fig. 2, Supplemental Fig. 1), and the head-to-head statistical comparison against the Duke BGL benchtop method (Table 2, Fig. 2) are validation or characterization sub-experiments with no corresponding BioScript primitive, and are intentionally not modeled; only the core multiplexed calibration/background/reaction/incubation/detection screening protocol is captured here.

description:
Source link: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5291792/pdf/1.4975391.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4975391

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Automated Electrotransformation of Escherichia coli on a Digital Microfluidic Platform Using Bioactivated Magnetic Beads (bead-based preparation of electrocompetent cells, heat-shock induction, DI-water media exchange, oligonucleotide loading, on-cartridge electroporation, and recovery for a multiplex automated genome engineering, MAGE, cycle)

REAGENTS USED:
  - E. coli Culture (EcNR2 DmutS lambda-Red+ strain, grown to stationary phase then sampled at mid-log phase, OD600 4.5-6.0)
  - Magnetic Beads (Wheat Germ Agglutinin, WGA, lectin-coated streptavidin superparamagnetic beads, 1 um diameter, for cell binding)
  - Blocking Agent (fat-free powdered milk, 2.5 mg/mL, to prevent in-droplet bead-cell clumping)
  - Growth Medium (defined MOPS EZ medium supplemented with biotin, or LB, used for growth, heat shock, and recovery)
  - Wash Buffer (DI water with 0.05% Tween 20, used for repeated media-exchange washes to make cells electrocompetent)
  - Oligo Reagent (90-nucleotide single-stranded oligodeoxynucleotide, e.g. bla-restore ODN, introduced for lambda-Red-mediated allelic replacement)
  - Recovery Medium (growth medium added immediately after the electroporation pulse for cell recovery and outgrowth)

STEPS:
1. Bead binding: mix the mid-log-phase E. coli culture with WGA-lectin-coated magnetic beads and rotate/incubate for 15 minutes to bind cells to beads (approximately one bead per cell).
2. Bead blocking: mix the bead-bound cells with fat-free powdered milk blocking agent for 1 minute to prevent bead-cell aggregation and promote uniform dispersion.
3. Media exchange: pull bound cells out of suspension with a magnet, remove the supernatant, and resuspend the bead-bound cells in growth medium.
4. Heat-shock induction: incubate the resuspended, bead-bound cells at 42 C for 15 minutes to induce expression of the lambda-Red recombination proteins (Exo, Beta, Gam).
5. Electrocompetence washes: for each of 3 wash cycles, magnetically pellet the bound cells, remove the supernatant, and replace it with DI water (with 0.05% Tween 20) without resuspension, to render the cells electrocompetent.
6. Oligo loading: suspend the washed, bead-bound cells in DI water, add the single-stranded oligodeoxynucleotide, and incubate briefly (about 30 seconds) to allow oligo uptake.
7. Temperature control and electroporation: hold the sample at the target pulse temperature (4 C or room temperature, depending on protocol variant) and apply a high-field-strength electroporation pulse (up to 24-26 kV/cm, RC time constant approximately 5-6 ms) to transiently permeabilize the cell membrane and deliver the oligonucleotide into the cells.
8. Recovery: immediately merge the pulsed sample with recovery growth medium and incubate at 30 C for 2.5 hours to allow the cells to recover and express any successfully incorporated genetic changes.
9. Transformation frequency readout: plate (or otherwise assay) the recovered cell sample on selective and non-selective media to determine the transformation frequency as the ratio of colony-forming units on the selective condition to the total colony-forming units.

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code translates the paper's Figure 4 benchtop electroporation-optimization protocol (Section II.C, 'Electrotransformation optimization'), which was designed to be reproducible using available digital microfluidic platform functions and was subsequently ported on-cartridge (Section III.C, 'Microfluidic trials'). It covers WGA-lectin magnetic-bead binding of mid-log E. coli (15 min), fat-free-powdered-milk bead blocking (1 min), magnet-based media exchange into growth medium, 42C/15-min heat-shock induction of lambda-Red recombination proteins, three DI-water electrocompetence washes with magnetic pelleting, oligo loading and brief incubation, an electroporation pulse, and a 30C/2.5h recovery step. description:
Source link: https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/completecellculture.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1039/c002147d

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic (DMF) Platform for Complete Mammalian Cell Culture — Adherent Cell Seeding, Growth, Media Exchange, Subculture, and On-Demand Transfection

REAGENTS USED:
  - Fibronectin (ECM protein, dispensed and dried to form an "adhesion pad" on the Teflon-AF electrode surface)
  - Cell Suspension (CHO-K1, HeLa, NIH-3T3, or INS-1 cells, 20-100 cells seeded per 150 nL droplet)
  - Growth Media (DMEM, F-12/DMEM, or RPMI 1640, supplemented with 10% FBS)
  - Fresh Media (used for daily passive-dispensing media exchange, three source droplets per exchange)
  - Trypsin/EDTA (0.25% vol/vol trypsin, 1 mM EDTA, used to detach cells from the adhesion pad)
  - Harvest Media (1 uL droplet passed over the primary pad to collect detached cells and deliver them to the secondary pad; ~2-3% of cells transferred per pass, four passes per subculture)
  - Transfection Mix (pCAG-GFP plasmid DNA complexed with Dreamfect cationic lipid, diluted in culture media)

STEPS:
1. Adhesion pad preparation: Dispense a droplet of fibronectin onto the electrode and allow it to dry, forming an ECM-coated adhesion pad on the hydrophobic Teflon-AF surface.
2. Cell seeding: Dispense a 150 nL droplet of cell suspension (20-100 cells) onto the primary (1 deg) adhesion pad and mix with growth media.
3. Growth incubation: Incubate the seeded droplet at 37 C (5% CO2 humidified chamber) for 24 h, allowing cells to shift from round to spread morphology.
4. Daily media exchange (passive dispensing): Every 24 h, drive three successive 1 uL source droplets of fresh media across the adhesion pad; each passing droplet sweeps away old media and leaves a fresh ~150 nL droplet behind (<3% carryover after one exchange, background level after three). Repeat this daily exchange/incubation cycle across the culture period.
5. Confluency check: Monitor cell density; once cells reach the second half of exponential growth (high density, e.g. 200-300 cells on the pad), proceed to subculture.
6. Cell detachment: Passively exchange the old media on the primary pad with a 150 nL droplet of trypsin/EDTA (three source-droplet exchanges) and allow cells to dissociate for 3-5 min.
7. Harvest and delivery to secondary pad: Translate a 1 uL droplet of fresh media over the primary pad to collect dissociated cells (blocking further trypsin activity), then drive the droplet to the secondary (2 deg) adhesion pad, where a passive-dispensing step deposits some of the cells. Repeat four times (collect + deliver) so that ~10% of the primary-pad cells are transferred to the secondary pad, then discard the depleted primary-pad droplet.
8. Secondary-pad growth: Incubate the newly seeded secondary pad at 37 C for 72 h, with daily passive-dispensing media exchange as in step 4, before subculturing again onto a subsequent generation.
9. On-demand transfection: Passively exchange the media on a subcultured (2 deg) pad with a 150 nL droplet of transfection mix (pCAG-GFP plasmid + Dreamfect lipid, ~5 ng DNA/~20 nL lipid per droplet) and incubate 3 h at 37 C.
10. Post-transfection recovery: Passively exchange the transfection solution for fresh media (three source droplets) and incubate overnight (24 h) at 37 C to allow GFP expression.
11. Detection: Image/quantify GFP fluorescence on the droplet to determine transfection efficiency, then discard the analyzed droplet.

INTERPRETATION: Successful implementation of complete on-chip mammalian cell culture is confirmed by growth/proliferation rates and morphology in droplets comparable to conventional multiwell-plate culture across multiple cell lines and subculture generations, and by transfection efficiencies (~20% GFP-positive cells) comparable to macro-scale transfection, supporting the DMF platform as an automated, miniaturized alternative to conventional mammalian cell seeding, feeding, passaging, and on-demand genetic transformation.

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code translates the paper's four-part complete cell-culture workflow (Results and Discussion): (1) adhesion-pad formation and cell seeding/growth on the primary pad (Fig. 2), (2) daily passive-dispensing media exchange using three source droplets (Fig. 3), (3) trypsin-mediated detachment and passive-dispensing harvest/delivery of cells to a secondary adhesion pad over four collection passes (Fig. 4), and (4) on-demand transient GFP transfection of the subcultured generation (Fig. 6). Incubation temperatures/durations (37C growth, 25C fibronectin drying, 3-5 min trypsinization, 3 h transfection exposure, 24h media-exchange cycles, 72h secondary-pad growth window) and droplet volumes (150 nL culture droplets, 1 uL source/harvest droplets) are taken directly from the Experimental section. BioScript has no primitive for a persistent adhered droplet/pad that is only partially exchanged, so 'passive dispensing' (a source droplet crossing a pad and leaving fresh solution behind while removing old solution) is approximated as a short 'mix' operation between the resident pad droplet and each dispensed source droplet, repeated three times per exchange, consistent with the paper's own finding that three passive exchanges reduce carryover to background. Likewise, the paper's continuous multigenerational passaging ('subcultured ad nauseam' for up to 4 subcultures) is modeled as a single representative 1st-to-2nd-pad subculture event (rather than an arbitrary/unbounded generation count), and the density-based decision to subculture ('second half of exponential growth phase') is modeled with an explicit if/else gated on a detected confluency reading rather than a continuous density sensor. Because BioScript's grammar exposes only a 'detect fluorescence' module, this primitive is reused both as a stand-in for optical/microscopy-based confluency monitoring (which is not fluorescence-based in the paper) and for its literal, correct use in quantifying GFP transfection efficiency in the final step.

description:
Source link: https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/paper%20microproteomic.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jproteome.3c00281

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidics for Microproteomic Analysis of Minute Mammalian Tissue Samples Enabled by a Photocleavable Surfactant

REAGENTS USED:
  - Tissue Sample (murine brain tissue biopsies, ~3 ug, 2 mm diameter punch)
  - Azo-TEAB Buffer (0.5% w/w 4-hexylphenylazosulfonate in 25 mM aqueous tetraethylammonium bicarbonate)
  - TCEP Reagent (tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine, reduction buffer)
  - IAA Reagent (iodoacetamide, alkylation buffer)
  - Digestive Enzyme Mixture (trypsin and Lys-C)
  - Formic Acid / Azo Quench Reagent

STEPS:
1. Tissue Suspension: Dispense the tissue sample and mix with Azo-TEAB buffer to suspend the tissue matrix and extract proteins on-chip.
2. Reduction: Dispense TCEP reagent, mix with the suspended tissue droplet, and incubate at 70 C for 10 min to reduce disulfide bonds.
3. Alkylation: Dispense IAA reagent, mix with the reduced sample droplet, and incubate at 25 C for 30 min in the dark to alkylate free thiols.
4. Digestion: Dispense the digestive enzyme mixture (trypsin/Lys-C), mix with the alkylated sample droplet, and incubate at 37 C for 240 min (4 h) to proteolytically digest proteins into peptides.
5. Quenching: Dispense the formic acid/azo quench reagent, mix with the digested peptide droplet, and incubate at 25 C for 10 min to quench digestion.
6. Detection / Clean-up: Measure peptide fluorescence or absorbance-based readouts to verify sample processing, then discard the analyzed droplet prior to downstream LC-MS/MS proteomic analysis.

INTERPRETATION: Successful microproteomic processing is confirmed by the identification of thousands of proteins (e.g., nearly 2,000 proteins including neural biomarkers and synaptic signaling proteins from minute 3 ug tissue punches) with high peptide sequence coverage and robust droplet actuation enabled by the Azo photocleavable surfactant, demonstrating that Azo-enabled digital microfluidics effectively automates the handling and preparation of size-limited clinical and biological tissue samples for advanced bottom-up proteomics.

description:
================================================================================
PROTOCOL: World-to-Chip DMF -- Bacterial Transformation and Enzymatic Assay
================================================================================

SOURCE LINK : https://www.shihmicrolab.ca/_files/ugd/f0a828_18be169d68164b85b204ed067c7dc1f5.pdf
PAPER DOI   : http://dx.doi.org/10.1021/acs.analchem.8b05754
JOURNAL     : Analytical Chemistry, 2019, Vol. 91, pp. 5159-5168
PLATFORM    : Digital Microfluidic (DMF) -- ITO-well-DMF configuration
TARGET      : E. coli DH5alpha (Protocol 1); Endoglucanase enzyme (Protocol 2)
APPLICATION : Bacterial co-transformation and enzymatic endoglucanase activity assay

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
OVERVIEW
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This paper describes two "world-to-chip" interface features integrated on a DMF
platform and demonstrates them with two biological protocols:

  (1) A 3D-printed reagent delivery system: a cylindrical PLA well (400 uL
      capacity) mated to the ITO top plate via a drilled-hole inlet, with a
      threaded screw to deliver fluid to an ancillary reservoir on-chip. The
      ancillary reservoir refills the main reservoir (7 uL target) after every
      dispense, improving droplet dispensing reproducibility:
        - RSD with well    : 11.62% (LB), 16.78% (water), 15.32% (methanol)
        - RSD without well : 19.61% (LB), 49.29% (water), 35.41% (methanol)

  (2) A closed-loop PID thermoelectric cooler (TEC): a 20x40 mm Peltier module
      integrated below the DMF chip with an aluminum heat block, RTD sensor,
      and Arduino Uno microcontroller. PID parameters (Kp=15, Ki=1.2, Kd=0.5)
      modelled in MATLAB/Simulink:
        - Rise to 42 C    : 2.1 C/s
        - Drop to 4 C     : 1.01 C/s
        - Steady-state    : high stability, low fluctuation

  PROTOCOL 1 -- Bacterial Co-Transformation results:
    - No control (open-loop)       : 3.67e3 CFU/ug (single), 3.17e3 (co-)
    - PID control (ITO-DMF)        : 2.03e4 CFU/ug (single), 9.00e3 (co-)
    - PID + well (ITO-well-DMF)    : 1.48e5 CFU/ug (single), 9.27e4 (co-)
    - 7-fold improvement with reagent well over PID alone (p=0.007)
    - Antibiotic selection: kanamycin (50 ug/mL) + chloramphenicol (35 ug/mL)

  PROTOCOL 2 -- Enzymatic Endoglucanase Assay results:
    - Higher temperature (30 C) produces higher MUF fluorescence vs 23 C
    - ITO-well-DMF fluorescence significantly higher than ITO-DMF (p<0.05,
      ANOVA two-way test) across all three substrate concentrations
    - Enzyme: endoglucanase cleaves beta-(1,4) glycosidic bond in MUC
    - Product: 4-methylumbelliferone (MUF); emission 449 nm, excitation 368 nm

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
REAGENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  ID                    DESCRIPTION                           QUANTITY / SPEC
  --------------------  ------------------------------------  ----------------------
  CompetentCells        E. coli DH5alpha competent cells      1 unit per droplet
                        Thawed on ice 10 min before use
  pFAB4876              Plasmid; GFP reporter; KanR           1 unit; 100 ng/rxn
                        Diluted to 1 ug/uL stock              1 ug/uL stock
  pSB1C3_RFP            Plasmid; RFP (BBa_J04450); CamR       1 unit; 100 ng/rxn
                        Diluted to 1 ug/uL stock              1 ug/uL stock
  CaCl2_Stock           Calcium chloride                      1 unit per droplet
                        150 mM stock; 75 mM final on-chip
  MUC_Substrate         4-methylumbelliferyl beta-D-          1 unit per droplet
                        cellobioside (MUC); 40 uM stock       40 uM stock
                        in 50 mM sodium-phosphate pH 7.0
                        + 0.05% Pluronics F-68
  EndoglucanaseEnzyme   Endoglucanase; cleaves beta-(1,4)     1 unit per assay area
                        glycosidic bonds; concentration        (constant across all
                        held constant across all conditions    three conditions)
                        + 0.05% Pluronics F-68
  QuenchingSolution     0.3 M glycine-NaOH pH 11.0            1 unit per assay area
                        Stops reaction; enhances MUF
                        fluorescence at alkaline pH
  Buffer                50 mM sodium-phosphate pH 7.0         1 unit per droplet
                        + 0.05% Pluronics F-68
                        Used for MUC serial dilution
  PluronicF68           0.05% Pluronics F-68 additive         Dissolved in all
                        Prevents biofouling; maintains         assay solutions;
                        droplet actuation on device            not a standalone
                                                               dispense

  NOTE: All droplet volumes are ~1 uL, dispensed at 160 V_rms, 15 kHz.
  Reservoir target volume: 7 uL (measured by impedance, Vread = 12.9 V).
  ITO-well-DMF: 400 uL bulk reagent per well; ancillary reservoir refills
  main reservoir after every unit droplet dispense.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
MODULES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  transformationQC      : Abstracts off-chip colony count QC step (Kan+Cam agar
                          plate, 37 C overnight incubation); used as on-chip
                          proxy for post-heat-shock cell viability signal

  endoglucanaseDetection: Abstracts CLARIOStar plate reader fluorescence readout
                          (off-chip; device placed on 96-well plate);
                          MUF emission 449 nm, excitation 368 nm;
                          well-scan: 15x15 matrix, 6 mm diameter, focal height
                          4.0 mm, gain 1180; max fluorescence per droplet recorded

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TEMPERATURE CONTROL PARAMETERS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  TEC module     : 20x40 mm Peltier (TE technology, Texas, USA)
  Heat block     : 20x40x5 mm aluminum; 1.5 mm drilled hole for RTD sensor
  Controller     : Arduino Uno with H-bridge driver and N-channel MOSFET
  Control type   : Closed-loop PID (negative feedback)
  PID parameters : Kp=15, Ki=1.2, Kd=0.5 (optimised in MATLAB/Simulink)

  Thermal zones used in this protocol:
    42 C  -- heat shock (transformation Phase 1); rise rate 2.1 C/s
     4 C  -- cold recovery (transformation Phase 2); drop rate 1.01 C/s
    30 C  -- enzymatic assay incubation; steady-state maintained by PID

  NOTE: heat primitive in BioScript is void (no assignment). Temperature
  control is modelled as heat statements acting on fluid variables in-place.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PROTOCOL 1: MICROSCALE BACTERIAL CO-TRANSFORMATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 1 -- Dispense Competent Cells
  Operations:
    cellDroplet = dispense 1 units of CompetentCells
  Notes:
    - E. coli DH5alpha thawed on ice 10 min before use
    - In ITO-well-DMF: 400 uL bulk cells in 3D-printed well
    - Ancillary reservoir refills main reservoir after each dispense

STEP 2 -- Dispense Plasmid DNA Droplets
  Operations:
    dna1Droplet = dispense 1 units of pFAB4876
    dna2Droplet = dispense 1 units of pSB1C3_RFP
  Notes:
    - pFAB4876: kanamycin selection (50 ug/mL); GFP reporter
    - pSB1C3-RFP: chloramphenicol selection (35 ug/mL); RFP insert BBa_J04450
    - Both diluted to 1 ug/uL; 100 ng per plasmid per reaction on-chip
    - Co-transformation: both plasmids present simultaneously

STEP 3 -- Dispense CaCl2 Solution
  Operations:
    cacl2Droplet = dispense 1 units of CaCl2_Stock
  Notes:
    - Stock 150 mM; final concentration on-chip 75 mM (after 1:1 merge)
    - CaCl2 critical for chemical competence and DNA uptake efficiency

STEP 4 -- Merge DNA Plasmids
  Operations:
    dnaMix = mix dna1Droplet with dna2Droplet for 5s
  Notes:
    - Sequential merging required for DMF electrode actuation
    - Paper states "equal volume ratio" merge of all four components

STEP 5 -- Merge Cells with DNA Mix
  Operations:
    cellDnaMix = mix cellDroplet with dnaMix for 5s

STEP 6 -- Add CaCl2 to Complete Transformation Mix
  Operations:
    transformMix = mix cellDnaMix with cacl2Droplet for 10s
  Notes:
    - Final droplet contains cells, pFAB4876, pSB1C3-RFP, CaCl2 at 75 mM
    - All four components merged in equal ~1 uL volume ratio

STEP 7 -- Heat Shock Phase 1 (42 C, 60 s)
  Operations:
    heat transformMix at 42c for 60s
  Notes:
    - Closed-loop PID TEC; rise rate 2.1 C/s
    - Drives transient membrane pore formation for DNA uptake in DH5alpha
    - Temperature fluctuations affect transformation efficiency (refs 37, 38)

STEP 8 -- Heat Shock Phase 2 (4 C, 180 s)
  Operations:
    heat transformMix at 4c for 180s
  Notes:
    - TEC drops to 4 C at 1.01 C/s; stops membrane disruption
    - Stabilises DNA-cell complex; 180 s = 3 min cold recovery
    - heat is void in BioScript; transformMix variable survives intact

STEP 9 -- Post-Transformation QC Detection and Branch
  Operations:
    transformSignal = detect transformationQC on transformMix for 30s
    if (transformSignal > 0) {
        dispose transformMix
    } else {
        drain transformMix
    }
    dispose transformSignal
  Notes:
    - Pass (BB2): transformSignal > 0 -> viable transformed cells detected
    - Fail (BB3): transformSignal <= 0 -> no viable signal; drain
    - Both branches join at BB4; enzymatic assay protocol begins after join
    - Expected (PID + well): ~9.27e4 CFU/ug DNA for co-transformation
    - drain vs dispose: functionally identical in lilott8/BioScript IR
      (both emit as dispose() hardware instruction); source code uses drain
      for fail path to preserve biological intent in dataset documentation

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PROTOCOL 2: ENZYMATIC ENDOGLUCANASE ASSAY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 10 -- Dispense 40 uM MUC Substrate Assay Droplet
  Operations:
    muc40uM_Assay = dispense 1 units of MUC_Substrate
  Notes:
    - Dispensed first and stored untouched in assay area 1
    - Not consumed by any dilution step
    - All solutions contain 0.05% Pluronics F-68 additive

STEP 11 -- Prepare 20 uM MUC Assay Droplet (Direct Dilution)
  Operations:
    muc40_for20   = dispense 1 units of MUC_Substrate
    buffer_for20  = dispense 1 units of Buffer
    muc20uM_Assay = mix muc40_for20 with buffer_for20 for 5s
  Notes:
    - 1:1 mix: (1 unit x 40 uM) / 2 units total = 20 uM. Correct.
    - No split used; avoids compiler split-array stranding bug (lilott8/BioScript
      does not support array indexing; stranded split elements cause hardware
      collision by blocking electrode routing paths)
    - Scalar mix produces single scalar droplet; all downstream ops are 1-to-1

STEP 12 -- Prepare 10 uM MUC Assay Droplet (Explicit Buffer Chaining)
  Operations:
    muc40_for10 = dispense 1 units of MUC_Substrate
    b1          = dispense 1 units of Buffer
    b2          = dispense 1 units of Buffer
    b3          = dispense 1 units of Buffer
    b_mix_2     = mix b1 with b2 for 5s
    b_mix_3     = mix b_mix_2 with b3 for 5s
    muc10uM_Assay = mix muc40_for10 with b_mix_3 for 5s
  Notes:
    - Target: 1:3 dilution for 10 uM; (1 unit x 40 uM) / 4 units = 10 uM. Correct.
    - Compiler ignores multi-unit volume scalars: "dispense 3 units of Buffer"
      defaults silently to a 1-unit dispense in the IR, yielding a second 20 uM
      droplet instead of 10 uM -- a critical concentration error.
    - Fix: three buffer droplets (b1, b2, b3) explicitly instantiated and merged
      into a 3-unit buffer blob (b_mix_3) before final mix with substrate.
    - Every variable assigned and consumed exactly once; no aliasing in IR.

STEP 13 -- Dispense Enzyme Droplets
  Operations:
    enzymeDrop40 = dispense 1 units of EndoglucanaseEnzyme
    enzymeDrop20 = dispense 1 units of EndoglucanaseEnzyme
    enzymeDrop10 = dispense 1 units of EndoglucanaseEnzyme
  Notes:
    - Paper M&M: "a unit droplet of enzyme solution (~1 uL) was dispensed into
      one of three assay areas"
    - Enzyme concentration held constant across all three substrate conditions
      (paper Fig. 5 caption: "enzyme concentration remaining constant")
    - 1 unit per assay area regardless of substrate droplet volume
    - In ITO-well-DMF: enzyme reservoir refilled from 3D well after each dispense

STEP 14 -- Start Reactions
  Operations:
    reaction40uM = mix muc40uM_Assay with enzymeDrop40 for 5s
    reaction20uM = mix muc20uM_Assay with enzymeDrop20 for 5s
    reaction10uM = mix muc10uM_Assay with enzymeDrop10 for 5s
  Notes:
    - Paper M&M: "all three substrate-containing droplets were simultaneously
      mixed with the enzyme droplets in the assay areas"
    - TEC activates at this point for closed-loop 30 C control

STEP 15 -- Incubate at 30 C for 30 min
  Operations:
    heat reaction40uM at 30c for 30m
    heat reaction20uM at 30c for 30m
    heat reaction10uM at 30c for 30m
  Notes:
    - Endoglucanase cleaves beta-(1,4) glycosidic bond in MUC
    - Releases 4-methylumbelliferone (MUF) fluorophore
    - Closed-loop PID TEC maintains 30 C steady-state
    - All three reactions run concurrently in separate assay areas on device
    - heat is void in BioScript; reaction variables survive intact

STEP 16 -- Quench Reactions
  Operations:
    quench40     = dispense 1 units of QuenchingSolution
    quench20     = dispense 1 units of QuenchingSolution
    quench10     = dispense 1 units of QuenchingSolution
    quenched40uM = mix reaction40uM with quench40 for 5s
    quenched20uM = mix reaction20uM with quench20 for 5s
    quenched10uM = mix reaction10uM with quench10 for 5s
  Notes:
    - Paper M&M: "a unit droplet of quenching solution (0.3 M glycine-NaOH,
      pH 11.0) was mixed with each reaction droplet in the assay area"
    - 1 unit quench per assay area; enzyme concentration held constant so
      quench volume is not scaled with substrate volume

STEP 17 -- Fluorescence Detection and Cleanup
  Operations:
    assaySignal40 = detect endoglucanaseDetection on quenched40uM for 30s
    assaySignal20 = detect endoglucanaseDetection on quenched20uM for 30s
    assaySignal10 = detect endoglucanaseDetection on quenched10uM for 30s
    if (assaySignal40 > 0) {
        dispose quenched40uM
        dispose quenched20uM
        dispose quenched10uM
    } else {
        drain quenched40uM
        drain quenched20uM
        drain quenched10uM
    }
    dispose assaySignal40
    dispose assaySignal20
    dispose assaySignal10
  Notes:
    - Off-chip readout: device placed on 96-well plate in CLARIOStar reader
    - MUF emission 449 nm, excitation 368 nm; well-scan 15x15 matrix,
      6 mm diameter, focal height 4.0 mm, gain 1180
    - Maximum fluorescence intensity per droplet recorded
    - QC gate keyed on 40 uM signal (highest expected MUF output)
    - Pass (BB5): assaySignal40 > 0 -> valid fluorescence; dispose all
    - Fail (BB6): assaySignal40 <= 0 -> no signal (enzyme inactive or reagent
      failure); drain all
    - Both branches join at BB7 (terminal); all three signal droplets disposed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Compiler    : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based, Python 3)
  Target      : -t ir (Intermediate Representation + Control Flow Graph)
  Command     : python3 main.py -d -i <file.bs> -t ir -o ./output -cfg

  KNOWN COMPILER BEHAVIOURS (relevant to this protocol):

  1. heat is void -- no assignment allowed.
     WRONG : result = heat transformMix at 42c for 60s
     RIGHT : heat transformMix at 42c for 60s

  2. detect consumes its fluid operand -- variable is spent after detect.
     Must use a distinct variable per detect call; do not reuse.

  3. Multi-unit volume scalars are silently ignored.
     "dispense 3 units of Buffer" generates dispense(Buffer) [0] in IR --
     a single 1-unit dispense. To accumulate N units of a reagent, explicitly
     instantiate N separate 1-unit dispense variables and chain with mix.

world_to_chip_interfaces.description: 3D-printed cylindrical well (8 mm OD, 45 mm height, 1 mm inlet hole; PLA material) mated to ITO top plate; 400 uL bulk reagent capacity; threaded screw delivers fluid to ancillary reservoir on-chip; ancillary reservoir refills main reservoir (7 uL target volume) via impedance-controlled actuation sequence after every dispense; eliminates manual reservoir refilling and improves droplet dispensing reproducibility (RSD reduced from 19.61% to 11.62% for LB media)

20x40 mm thermoelectric cooler (TEC/Peltier module) integrated below DMF chip; aluminum heat block (20x40x5 mm) with RTD sensor; closed-loop PID control implemented in MATLAB/Simulink; PID parameters: Kp=15, Ki=1.2, Kd=0.5; heat-shock zone: 42 C (rise rate 2.1 C/s); cold zone: 4 C (drop rate 1.01 C/s); assay zone: 30 C steady-state; 12V DC cooling fan on heat sink

steps.name: Dispense competent cells
steps.note: E. coli DH5alpha thawed on ice 10 min before use; in ITO-well-DMF configuration, 400 uL bulk cells loaded in 3D-printed well; ancillary reservoir refills main after each dispense

steps.name: Dispense plasmid DNA droplets
steps.note: pFAB4876 (KanR, GFP) and pSB1C3-RFP (CamR) each diluted to 1 ug/uL; 100 ng per plasmid per reaction; co-transformation uses both plasmids simultaneously

steps.name: Dispense CaCl2 solution
steps.note: CaCl2 stock 150 mM; final on-chip concentration 75 mM after merging with cells and DNA in equal volume ratio

steps.name: Merge DNA plasmids
steps.note: Sequential merging is required for DMF; paper summarises as 'equal volume ratio' merge of all four components

steps.name: Add CaCl2 to complete transformation mix
steps.note: Final droplet contains cells, pFAB4876, pSB1C3-RFP, and CaCl2 at 75 mM; all four components in equal 1 uL volume ratio

steps.name: Heat shock Phase 1 -- 42 C for 60 s
steps.note: Closed-loop PID TEC (Kp=15, Ki=1.2, Kd=0.5); rise rate 2.1 C/s; drives transient membrane pore formation for DNA uptake in chemically competent DH5alpha

steps.name: Heat shock Phase 2 -- 4 C for 180 s
steps.note: TEC cools to 4 C at 1.01 C/s; stops membrane disruption and stabilises DNA-cell complex; 180 s = 3 min cold recovery

steps.name: Post-transformation QC detection and branch
steps.note: transformationQC module abstracts off-chip colony count (Kan+Cam agar plate, 37 C overnight); on-chip proxy: post-heat-shock viability signal; expected efficiency with PID+well: ~9.27e4 CFU/ug DNA for co-transformation

steps.name: Dispense 40 uM MUC substrate assay droplet
steps.note: Dispensed first and stored untouched in assay area 1; not consumed by any dilution step; 0.05% Pluronics F-68 in all solutions

steps.name: Prepare 20 uM MUC assay droplet by direct dilution
steps.note: 1 unit 40 uM stock + 1 unit buffer mixed 1:1; (1 unit x 40 uM) / 2 units total = 20 uM; scalar mix, no split needed; avoids compiler split-array stranding bug

steps.name: Prepare 10 uM MUC assay droplet by explicit buffer chaining
steps.note: Target: 1:3 dilution (1 unit 40 uM stock + 3 units buffer = 10 uM). Compiler ignores multi-unit volume scalars (dispense 3 units defaults to 1 unit in IR); three buffer droplets explicitly instantiated and chained before final mix. (1 unit x 40 uM) / 4 units total = 10 uM.

steps.name: Dispense enzyme droplets
steps.note: One unit droplet per assay area; enzyme concentration held constant across all three substrate concentration conditions (paper Fig. 5 caption); in ITO-well-DMF: enzyme reservoir refilled from 3D well after each dispense

steps.name: Start reactions -- merge enzyme with substrate in each assay area
steps.note: Paper M&M: 'all three substrate-containing droplets were simultaneously mixed with the enzyme droplets in the assay areas'; TEC activates for closed-loop 30 C control

steps.name: Incubate at 30 C for 30 min
steps.note: Endoglucanase cleaves beta-(1,4) glycosidic bond in MUC releasing MUF fluorophore; closed-loop PID TEC holds 30 C steady-state; all three reactions run concurrently in separate assay areas

Protocol details:

This is a competitive enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for screening morphine in urine.

REAGENTS USED:
  - Urine Sample
  - Morphine Enzyme Conjugate
  - Distilled Water (Wash Buffer)
  - TMB Substrate
  - Stop Reagent

STEPS:
1. Sample Preparation: Add 20 units of the urine sample to the reaction zone. 
2. Conjugate Incubation: Add 100 units of morphine enzyme conjugate to the sample. Mix the solution for 60 seconds to allow competitive binding between free morphine in the sample and the conjugate.
3. Primary Incubation: Incubate the mixture at 23°C (room temperature) for 60 minutes to reach equilibrium. 
4. Wash Cycle: Wash the reaction zone six times to remove unbound conjugate. For each wash cycle, add 350 units of distilled water, mix for 45 seconds, and discard the wash supernatant.
5. Substrate Development: Add 100 units of TMB substrate to the retained mixture. Mix for 60 seconds, then incubate at 23°C for 30 minutes to allow the colorimetric reaction to develop.
6. Stop Reaction: Add 100 units of acid stop reagent. Mix with the developed substrate for 60 seconds to halt the enzymatic reaction and change the color from blue to yellow.
7. Detection: Measure the resulting optical signal (absorbance) over 1 minute to obtain the reading. Discard the final reaction mixture.

INTERPRETATION: The final signal intensity (absorbance) is inversely proportional to the concentration of morphine in the urine sample. A lower signal indicates a higher presence of morphine, while a higher signal indicates little to no morphine.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A NOTE ON HOW CLOSELY THIS MATCHES THE CITED SOURCE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The overall logic and final output of the BioScript code perfectly match the cited Sigma-Aldrich SE120079 Morphine ELISA protocol. The author has corrected the detection method to "absorbance", resolving the previous biochemical contradiction with the TMB substrate. The reagent volumes (20 units sample, 100 units conjugate, 6 washes of 350 units water, 100 units TMB, 100 units stop reagent) and incubation times (60m and 30m at 23°C) are strictly identical to the bench protocol. The final output is verified as a valid, direct translation of the cited assay.

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic 5-Plex Fluorometric Enzyme Assay for Newborn Screening of Pompe, Fabry, Hunter, Gaucher, and Hurler Lysosomal Storage Diseases from a Single Dried Blood Spot Punch

REAGENTS USED:
  - DBS Extract (single 3-mm dried-blood-spot punch eluted in 100 uL of 0.1% w/v Tween20 extraction buffer, 30 min on an orbital shaker at ambient temperature; one extract shared across all 5 assays)
  - GAA Reagent (Pompe assay: 4-methylumbelliferyl-alpha-D-glucoside substrate with acarbose inhibitor and 20.0 mmol/L methyl-beta-cyclodextrin)
  - GLA Reagent (Fabry assay: 4-methylumbelliferyl-alpha-D-galactoside substrate with N-acetyl-D-galactosamine inhibitor and 20.0 mmol/L methyl-beta-cyclodextrin)
  - IDS Reagent (Hunter assay: 4-methylumbelliferyl-alpha-L-iduronate-2-sulfate substrate with 20.0 mmol/L methyl-beta-cyclodextrin)
  - GBA Reagent (Gaucher assay: 16 mmol/L 4-methylumbelliferyl-beta-D-glucoside substrate with 1.5% sodium taurocholate, no inhibitor)
  - IDU Reagent (Hurler assay: 2 mmol/L 4-methylumbelliferyl-alpha-L-iduronide substrate with 3.0 mmol/L D-saccharic acid 1,4-lactone inhibitor and 20 mmol/L methyl-beta-cyclodextrin)
  - Extraction Buffer (EXT: 0.1% w/v Tween20 in water)
  - Stop Buffer (STB: 0.2 mol/L NaHCO3, pH 10.0, 0.01% w/v Tween20)
  - Calibrant (4-methylumbelliferone, 4-MU, standard used for a 4-point calibration curve run in duplicate)

STEPS:
1. Four-point fluorescence calibration (in duplicate): dispense triple-sized calibrant droplets from each of 4 calibrant reservoirs and read fluorescence for each, giving 8 calibration readings used to build a linear-regression calibration curve.
2. Substrate/reagent background: for 2 of the 44 sample positions, use extraction buffer alone (no DBS extract) merged with each of the 5 reagents, incubate under the same conditions as sample reactions, and read background fluorescence for each of the 5 assays.
3. For each of the remaining DBS extracts loaded onto the cartridge (up to 42 additional samples): dispense one extract droplet and merge it separately with each of the 5 reagents (GAA, GLA, IDS, GBA, IDU) to form 5 parallel reaction droplets from the single punch.
4. Incubate all 5 reaction droplets per sample at 37 C for 1 h.
5. Stop and read: merge each incubated reaction droplet with its corresponding stop buffer droplet and measure endpoint fluorescence for each of the 5 assays (excitation 370 nm / emission 460 nm), converting readings to enzymatic activity via the calibration curve after subtracting background.
6. Screening interpretation: compare each of the 5 endpoint activities against the normal/affected separation boundary established from presumed-normal and confirmed-affected samples; flag and discard reaction droplets whose activity falls at or below the cutoff as presumptively affected (Pompe, Fabry, Hunter, Gaucher, or Hurler), otherwise report as normal.

module fluorescence

manifest dbs_extract
manifest extraction_buffer
manifest stop_buffer
manifest calibrant
manifest gaa_reagent
manifest gla_reagent
manifest ids_reagent
manifest gba_reagent
manifest idu_reagent

instructions:

repeat 8 times {
    cal = dispense 3 units of calibrant
    cal_reading = detect fluorescence on cal for 1m
    dispose cal
}

gaa_bg_sample = dispense 1 units of extraction_buffer
gaa_bg_reagent = dispense 1 units of gaa_reagent
gaa_bg_rxn = mix gaa_bg_sample with gaa_bg_reagent for 15s
heat gaa_bg_rxn at 37c for 60m
gaa_bg_stb = dispense 1 units of stop_buffer
gaa_bg_final = mix gaa_bg_rxn with gaa_bg_stb for 15s
gaa_background = detect fluorescence on gaa_bg_final for 1m
dispose gaa_bg_final

gla_bg_sample = dispense 1 units of extraction_buffer
gla_bg_reagent = dispense 1 units of gla_reagent
gla_bg_rxn = mix gla_bg_sample with gla_bg_reagent for 15s
heat gla_bg_rxn at 37c for 60m
gla_bg_stb = dispense 1 units of stop_buffer
gla_bg_final = mix gla_bg_rxn with gla_bg_stb for 15s
gla_background = detect fluorescence on gla_bg_final for 1m
dispose gla_bg_final

ids_bg_sample = dispense 1 units of extraction_buffer
ids_bg_reagent = dispense 1 units of ids_reagent
ids_bg_rxn = mix ids_bg_sample with ids_bg_reagent for 15s
heat ids_bg_rxn at 37c for 60m
ids_bg_stb = dispense 1 units of stop_buffer
ids_bg_final = mix ids_bg_rxn with ids_bg_stb for 15s
ids_background = detect fluorescence on ids_bg_final for 1m
dispose ids_bg_final

gba_bg_sample = dispense 1 units of extraction_buffer
gba_bg_reagent = dispense 1 units of gba_reagent
gba_bg_rxn = mix gba_bg_sample with gba_bg_reagent for 15s
heat gba_bg_rxn at 37c for 60m
gba_bg_stb = dispense 1 units of stop_buffer
gba_bg_final = mix gba_bg_rxn with gba_bg_stb for 15s
gba_background = detect fluorescence on gba_bg_final for 1m
dispose gba_bg_final

idu_bg_sample = dispense 1 units of extraction_buffer
idu_bg_reagent = dispense 1 units of idu_reagent
idu_bg_rxn = mix idu_bg_sample with idu_bg_reagent for 15s
heat idu_bg_rxn at 37c for 60m
idu_bg_stb = dispense 1 units of stop_buffer
idu_bg_final = mix idu_bg_rxn with idu_bg_stb for 15s
idu_background = detect fluorescence on idu_bg_final for 1m
dispose idu_bg_final

repeat 42 times {

    sample = dispense 1 units of dbs_extract

    gaa_reagent_drop = dispense 1 units of gaa_reagent
    gaa_rxn = mix sample with gaa_reagent_drop for 15s

    gla_reagent_drop = dispense 1 units of gla_reagent
    gla_rxn = mix sample with gla_reagent_drop for 15s

    ids_reagent_drop = dispense 1 units of ids_reagent
    ids_rxn = mix sample with ids_reagent_drop for 15s

    gba_reagent_drop = dispense 1 units of gba_reagent
    gba_rxn = mix sample with gba_reagent_drop for 15s

    idu_reagent_drop = dispense 1 units of idu_reagent
    idu_rxn = mix sample with idu_reagent_drop for 15s

    heat gaa_rxn at 37c for 60m
    heat gla_rxn at 37c for 60m
    heat ids_rxn at 37c for 60m
    heat gba_rxn at 37c for 60m
    heat idu_rxn at 37c for 60m

    gaa_stb = dispense 1 units of stop_buffer
    gaa_final = mix gaa_rxn with gaa_stb for 15s
    gaa_activity = detect fluorescence on gaa_final for 1m

    gla_stb = dispense 1 units of stop_buffer
    gla_final = mix gla_rxn with gla_stb for 15s
    gla_activity = detect fluorescence on gla_final for 1m

    ids_stb = dispense 1 units of stop_buffer
    ids_final = mix ids_rxn with ids_stb for 15s
    ids_activity = detect fluorescence on ids_final for 1m

    gba_stb = dispense 1 units of stop_buffer
    gba_final = mix gba_rxn with gba_stb for 15s
    gba_activity = detect fluorescence on gba_final for 1m

    idu_stb = dispense 1 units of stop_buffer
    idu_final = mix idu_rxn with idu_stb for 15s
    idu_activity = detect fluorescence on idu_final for 1m

    if (gaa_activity <= 8) {
        dispose gaa_final
    }

    if (gla_activity <= 6) {
        dispose gla_final
    }

    if (ids_activity <= 6) {
        dispose ids_final
    }

    if (gba_activity <= 7) {
        dispose gba_final
    }

    if (idu_activity <= 5) {
        dispose idu_final
    }

    dispose gaa_final
    dispose gla_final
    dispose ids_final
    dispose gba_final
    dispose idu_final
}

SOURCE LINK: https://bio-protocol.org/en/bpdetail?id=5722
PAPER DOI: https://doi.org/10.21769/BioProtoc.5722

ASSAY TYPE:
Enzymatic activity assay of 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase (NADH-Dependent Oxidoreductase Activity).

REAGENTS USED:
- Reaction Buffer (contains acetoacetyl-CoA substrate, 30 uM final)
- NADH Solution (10 mM)
- Purified OsAIM1 Enzyme (0.5 ug)
- Purified GST Protein (0.5 ug, negative control)

STEPS:
1. Primary Preparation (Sample): Dispense 100 units of the reaction buffer containing the acetoacetyl-CoA substrate at 25 degrees C. Dispense 1 unit of the 10 mM NADH solution to obtain a final NADH concentration of 0.1 mM. Mix thoroughly to ensure homogenization.
2. Enzymatic Reaction (Sample): Initiate the reaction by dispensing 1 unit of the purified OsAIM1 protein. Mix immediately to ensure uniform distribution of the enzyme in the reaction solution.
3. Detection (Sample): Measure the absorbance at 340 nm, corresponding to the characteristic absorption peak of NADH. Record absorbance values every 15 seconds in a 4-cycle loop (60 seconds) to monitor continuous oxidation. Discard the droplet.
4. Control Branch: Dispense 100 units of reaction buffer and 1 unit of NADH solution, then mix. Dispense 1 unit of purified GST protein as a negative control to account for non-enzymatic NADH oxidation. Mix and measure absorbance every 15 seconds for 4 cycles, then discard.

INTERPRETATION:
The enzymatic reaction rate is determined from the linear decrease in absorbance at 340 nm over time, reflecting NADH oxidation during the reaction. This accompanies the reversible NADH-dependent reduction of acetoacetyl-CoA to 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A NOTE ON HOW CLOSELY THIS MATCHES THE CITED SOURCE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The authored BioScript code closely matches the cited Hu et al. (2026) protocol. The continuous microplate spectrophotometric reading has been adapted to discrete droplet absorbance detection using a timed multi-read loop. Standard reaction volumes (100 uL buffer, 1 uL NADH) map cleanly to discrete volume units, and the parallel negative control branch utilizing GST protein ensures high-fidelity translation to the digital microfluidic biochip (DMFB) architecture.

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Tissue-Digital Microfluidic Isolation of Single Cells for -Omics (tDISCO) for Spatially-Resolved Single-Cell Transcriptomic and Proteomic Profiling of Proximal vs. Distal Astrocytes after Ischemic Stroke

REAGENTS USED:
  - Cryosectioned Brain Tissue Biopsy (2 mm diameter punch from a cortical stroke tissue section, mounted on the tDISCO top-plate)
  - Fixation Reagent (paraformaldehyde-based fixative, applied on-chip)
  - DAPI Nuclear Stain (marks all nuclei)
  - Anti-GFAP Antibody (fluorescent astrocyte marker)
  - Anti-NEUN Antibody (fluorescent neuronal marker)
  - Cell Lysis/Receiving Buffer (droplet positioned above the tissue for laser-induced single-cell lysis and lysate collection)

STEPS:
1. Mount a 2 mm cryosectioned cortical tissue biopsy onto the tDISCO top-plate.
2. Fix the mounted tissue biopsy in place on-chip using the fixation reagent.
3. Stain the fixed tissue on-chip with DAPI, anti-GFAP, and anti-NEUN to mark nuclei, astrocytes, and neurons, respectively.
4. Image the stained tissue at low magnification (20X) to map DAPI+/GFAP+ and DAPI+/NEUN+ cells and record their distance from the stroke lesion.
5. Select a single target cell (e.g., a GFAP+ astrocyte at a defined distance from the injury site) and re-image at high magnification (100X) to confirm its identity and position before lysis.
6. Dispense a receiving-buffer droplet and use digital microfluidic actuation to position it directly over the selected single cell.
7. Fire the focused laser at the targeted cell to induce a cavitation bubble that mechanically lyses the cell, releasing its contents into the overlying receiving-buffer droplet.
8. Actuate the single-cell lysate droplet away from the tissue for downstream -omics processing (library preparation for transcriptomics, or digestion for proteomics).
9. Replenish a fresh receiving-buffer droplet over the same tissue section and repeat steps 5-8 to iteratively isolate additional single cells (e.g., a second GFAP+ astrocyte at a different lesion distance, or a DAPI+/NEUN+ neuron) from the same biopsy.
10. Pool/queue the collected single-cell lysate droplets for transcriptomic (RNA-seq) and proteomic (LC-MS/MS) analysis, comparing molecular profiles across cells at varying distances from the stroke lesion to resolve the spatial boundaries of the astrocyte response.
