module fluorescence

manifest cell_lysate
manifest nhsl1_antibody
manifest control_igg
manifest protein_a_beads
manifest wash_buffer
manifest laemmli_buffer
manifest secondary_hrp_antibody
manifest ecl_substrate

instructions:

// Preclear lysate with Protein A beads to remove non-specific binders
lysate = dispense 100 units of cell_lysate
preclear_beads = dispense 30 units of protein_a_beads
precleared = mix lysate with preclear_beads
heat precleared at 4c for 30m
dispose preclear_beads

// Negative control IP with non-immune IgG
igg = dispense 5 units of control_igg
igg_mix = mix precleared with igg
heat igg_mix at 4c for 120m

igg_beads = dispense 30 units of protein_a_beads
igg_complex = mix igg_mix with igg_beads
heat igg_complex at 4c for 60m

repeat 3 times {
    igg_wash = dispense 200 units of wash_buffer
    igg_washed = mix igg_complex with igg_wash
    dispose igg_washed
}

igg_elution_buffer = dispense 30 units of laemmli_buffer
igg_eluate = mix igg_complex with igg_elution_buffer
heat igg_eluate at 95c for 5m
dispose igg_eluate

// Specific IP with anti-NHSL1 antibody (pAb 4457)
ab = dispense 5 units of nhsl1_antibody
ip_mix = mix precleared with ab
heat ip_mix at 4c for 120m

ip_beads = dispense 30 units of protein_a_beads
ip_complex = mix ip_mix with ip_beads
heat ip_complex at 4c for 60m

repeat 3 times {
    ip_wash = dispense 200 units of wash_buffer
    ip_washed = mix ip_complex with ip_wash
    dispose ip_washed
}

elution_buffer = dispense 30 units of laemmli_buffer
eluate = mix ip_complex with elution_buffer
heat eluate at 95c for 5m

// Western blot detection step (anti-Abi1 / anti-WAVE2, HRP-ECL)
secondary = dispense secondary_hrp_antibody
substrate = dispense 20 units of ecl_substrate
detection_mix = mix eluate with secondary
blot_mix = mix detection_mix with substrate

coip_signal = detect fluorescence on blot_mix for 60s

if (coip_signal >= 80) {
    dispose blot_mix
} else {
    repeat 2 times {
        rewash = dispense 200 units of wash_buffer
        rewashed = mix blot_mix with rewash
        dispose rewashed
    }
    dispose blot_mix
}

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidics with Distance-Based Detection (DMF-DBD) for RT-LAMP-Based Nucleic Acid Diagnostics — Detection of SARS-CoV-2 RNA in Saliva

REAGENTS USED:
  - Extracted SARS-CoV-2 RNA (viral RNA extracted from saliva; blank, low viral load ~10 PFU/mL, and high viral load ~4.6x10^4 PFU/mL samples)
  - RT-LAMP Master Mix (WarmStart colorimetric/fluorescent RT-LAMP reagents with SARS-CoV-2-specific primers, guanidine hydrochloride, and nuclease-free water)
  - Capto(TM) Adhere Agarose Bead Suspension (solid-phase clean-up beads that selectively bind low molecular-weight LAMP by-products, e.g. primer-dimers, leaving high-molecular-weight LAMP amplicons in solution)
  - SYBR(R) Safe Intercalating Dye (100x, fluorescent reporter used for distance-based detection readout)

STEPS:
1. Amplification: Load an aliquot of extracted RNA and RT-LAMP master mix onto the DMF array, merge and mix the two droplets, then heat the merged droplet at 65 C for 17 minutes (reduced-duration amplification, selected to preserve discrimination between high and low viral loads).
2. Bead Clean-Up: Load a droplet of washed Capto(TM) adhere bead suspension, merge it with the amplified LAMP product, and actively mix (rotate in a circular pattern) for approximately 1 minute to deplete low molecular-weight background species.
3. Dye Addition: Load a droplet of 100x SYBR(R) Safe solution, merge it with the bead-cleaned amplicon droplet, and mix for approximately 2 minutes to intercalate the dye into the high-molecular-weight LAMP amplicons.
4. Detection: Drive the resultant droplet to the on-chip distance-based detection (DBD) paper substrate, where it touches the loading zone and wicks by capillary action through the flowing zone; the fluorescent signal travel distance is imaged/read (by eye or camera) over several minutes and correlates with the amount of amplified target present, then the analyzed droplet is discarded.

Steps 1-4 are repeated independently for each of the three sample conditions (blank/no virus, low viral load, and high viral load saliva) to generate the semi-quantitative comparison reported in the paper.

INTERPRETATION: Successful detection is confirmed when the normalized DBD travel distance (and corresponding fluorescent signal) increases monotonically with viral load, allowing statistically significant discrimination between blank, low (~10 PFU/mL, ~4.9x10^4 copies/mL), and high (~4.6x10^4 PFU/mL, ~2.2x10^8 copies/mL) SARS-CoV-2-spiked saliva samples (two-sided t-test, p_blank-low = 0.02863, p_low-high = 0.00077) using a 17-minute reduced amplification time, all performed in a single automated DMF cartridge without any dedicated optical detection apparatus.

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidics with Distance-Based Detection (DMF-DBD) for RT-LAMP-Based Nucleic Acid Diagnostics — Detection of SARS-CoV-2 RNA in Saliva

REAGENTS USED:
  - Extracted SARS-CoV-2 RNA (viral RNA extracted from saliva; blank, low viral load ~10 PFU/mL, and high viral load ~4.6x10^4 PFU/mL samples)
  - RT-LAMP Master Mix (WarmStart colorimetric/fluorescent RT-LAMP reagents with SARS-CoV-2-specific primers, guanidine hydrochloride, and nuclease-free water)
  - Capto(TM) Adhere Agarose Bead Suspension (solid-phase clean-up beads that selectively bind low molecular-weight LAMP by-products, e.g. primer-dimers, leaving high-molecular-weight LAMP amplicons in solution)
  - SYBR(R) Safe Intercalating Dye (100x, fluorescent reporter used for distance-based detection readout)

STEPS:
1. Amplification: Load an aliquot of extracted RNA and RT-LAMP master mix onto the DMF array, merge and mix the two droplets, then heat the merged droplet at 65 C for 17 minutes (reduced-duration amplification, selected to preserve discrimination between high and low viral loads).
2. Bead Clean-Up: Load a droplet of washed Capto(TM) adhere bead suspension, merge it with the amplified LAMP product, and actively mix (rotate in a circular pattern) for approximately 1 minute to deplete low molecular-weight background species.
3. Dye Addition: Load a droplet of 100x SYBR(R) Safe solution, merge it with the bead-cleaned amplicon droplet, and mix for approximately 2 minutes to intercalate the dye into the high-molecular-weight LAMP amplicons.
4. Detection: Drive the resultant droplet to the on-chip distance-based detection (DBD) paper substrate, where it touches the loading zone and wicks by capillary action through the flowing zone; the fluorescent signal travel distance is imaged/read (by eye or camera) over several minutes and correlates with the amount of amplified target present, then the analyzed droplet is discarded.

Steps 1-4 are repeated independently for each of the three sample conditions (blank/no virus, low viral load, and high viral load saliva) to generate the semi-quantitative comparison reported in the paper.

INTERPRETATION: Successful detection is confirmed when the normalized DBD travel distance (and corresponding fluorescent signal) increases monotonically with viral load, allowing statistically significant discrimination between blank, low (~10 PFU/mL, ~4.9x10^4 copies/mL), and high (~4.6x10^4 PFU/mL, ~2.2x10^8 copies/mL) SARS-CoV-2-spiked saliva samples (two-sided t-test, p_blank-low = 0.02863, p_low-high = 0.00077) using a 17-minute reduced amplification time, all performed in a single automated DMF cartridge without any dedicated optical detection apparatus.

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Nucleosome Immunoprecipitation (NuIP) with Fluorescent Detection on Functionalized Magnetic Beads (Digital Microfluidic Device)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Biotinylated Nucleosome Sample (purified human H3K4me2 nucleosomes)
  - Streptavidin-Coated Magnetic Beads
  - Primary Antibody (anti-H3K4me2, raised in rabbit)
  - Secondary Antibody (Alexa Fluor 405 Goat Anti-Rabbit, fluorescent-conjugated)
  - Wash Buffer

STEPS:
1. Capture: Mix the biotinylated H3K4me2 nucleosome sample with streptavidin-coated magnetic beads; incubate for 6 hours with agitation at 4 C.
2. Wash: Wash away unbound nucleosome species from the beads.
3. Detection Complex Preparation: Separately and simultaneously, under the same conditions (6 hours, 4 C, agitation), incubate the primary antibody (anti-H3K4me2) with the Alexa Fluor 405 Goat Anti-Rabbit secondary antibody to form the fluorescent detection complex.
4. Labeling: Add the detection complex to the washed, nucleosome-bound beads and incubate again.
5. Final Wash: Wash away unbound antibody species.
6. Detection: Re-suspend the beads and place a droplet on the digital microfluidic device; electrowet the droplet to the current wires to concentrate the beads magnetically, then image/detect via fluorescence (Alexa Fluor 405: ~395 nm excitation, ~421 nm emission, 420 nm longpass emission filter, CCD camera).

INTERPRETATION: Fluorescence signal on the concentrated magnetic beads confirms successful capture and antibody labeling of the target nucleosome modification (H3K4me2); a nucleosome-containing sample droplet shows clear fluorescence versus a negative control droplet, and fluorescence localizes to the beads (not the supernatant) when tested against an external magnet. In a semiquantitative dose-response series (0-20 uL of stock H3K4me2 nucleosomes), normalized pixel intensity (via ImageJ blue-channel analysis) increases with nucleosome volume, with a linear response observed between 0-10 uL, establishing this on-chip NuIP assay as a confirmatory checkpoint for antibody specificity/sensitivity prior to downstream analyses such as PCR, gel electrophoresis, or sequencing.

Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-19394-5

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic Isolation of Single Cells for -Omics (DISCO) — Single-Cell Genomics Pipeline

REAGENTS USED:
  - Adherent Cell Suspension (U87 human glioblastoma or B16 murine melanoma cells cultured on a DISCO top-plate, ~0.5x10^6 cells/mL loading density)
  - Wash Buffer (DPBS with 0.05% v/v Pluronic F68)
  - Fixative Solution (HOPE Fixative solution I)
  - Permeabilization Buffer (ice-cold acetone)
  - Immunostaining Reagents (CD47-APC antibody, clone CC2C6; Hoechst 33342 nuclear stain)
  - Collection Buffer (DPBS with 0.05% v/v F68, used as the virtual-microwell collection droplet)
  - Whole Genome Amplification Reagent (Repli-g single cell kit, Qiagen)
  - QC-1 PCR Mix (Taq DNA Polymerase, primers for conserved loci on chromosomes 4, 12, 13, 22)
  - DNA Cleanup Reagent (DNA Clean and Concentrator columns, Zymo Research)
  - QC-2 PCR Mix (AmpFlSTR Identifiler PCR Amplification Kit, STR + Amelogenin loci)
  - Library Prep Reagent (Nextera DNA Flex Library Prep Kit, Illumina)

STEPS:
1. Cell seeding and culture: Adherent cells are loaded onto the DISCO top plate at a density of ~0.5x10^6 cells/mL and incubated for 24 h at 37 C in a humidified atmosphere.
2. Fixation: A fixative droplet is delivered to the virtual microwell and incubated 20 min at 4 C, followed by a wash step with DPBS/F68.
3. Permeabilization: An ice-cold acetone droplet is delivered to the fixed cells and incubated at -20 C for 10 min, followed by a wash step.
4. Immunofluorescent staining: The permeabilized cells are labeled with an anti-CD47-APC antibody and Hoechst 33342 nuclear stain to enable phenotype-based, AI-driven cell selection (CNN-based image segmentation, AUC = 0.991).
5. Cell selection and laser lysis: The user (manually or via the trained CNN) selects a single cell of interest; a focused Q-switched Nd:YAG laser pulse (532 nm, ~0.8 um spot size) lyses the targeted cell, releasing its contents into a collection droplet (virtual microwell). Cells with insufficient/ambiguous phenotype signal are excluded from downstream processing.
6. Whole genome amplification (WGA): The single-cell lysate is combined with the Repli-g multiple displacement amplification (MDA) reagent and incubated isothermally (~30 C) to amplify the genome.
7. Quality control 1 (QC-1): The amplified product is PCR-amplified at four conserved loci (chromosomes 4, 12, 13, 22) via standard thermal cycling (94 C denature / 55 C anneal / 72 C extend) and evaluated by gel electrophoresis; samples with fewer than 3 of 4 expected loci are discarded.
8. DNA cleanup: The QC-1-passing product is purified/concentrated using DNA Clean and Concentrator columns.
9. Quality control 2 (QC-2): The cleaned DNA is PCR-amplified at 15 short tandem repeat (STR) loci plus Amelogenin (94 C denature / 59 C anneal / 72 C extend) and evaluated by microfluidic gel electrophoresis; samples with fewer than 12 of 16 expected loci are discarded.
10. Sequencing library preparation: The QC-2-passing DNA is tagmented and library-prepped using the Nextera DNA Flex kit, then the finished single-cell whole-genome sequencing library is collected off-chip for storage (-20 C/-80 C) and downstream next-generation sequencing (Illumina MiSeq).

INTERPRETATION: Successful single-cell genomic analysis by DISCO is confirmed by high sequencing uniformity (Lorenz curve near-theoretical distribution), minimal amplification bias from MDA, negligible background DNA contamination from non-selected cells (<5% vs. bulk), copy-number-variant (CNV) profiles concordant between single cells and bulk samples (R^2 = 0.843), and strong agreement between AI-selected and manually-selected single-cell genomes (R^2 = 0.894), supporting use of DISCO for deep single-cell -omics analysis of heterogeneous or rare adherent cell populations, including detection of single-nucleotide-level CRISPR-induced variants.

// Step 1: cell seeding and culture (24 h, 37c)
cells = dispense 5 units of CellSuspension
heat cells at 37c for 1440m

// Step 2: fixation (HOPE fixative, 4c, 20 min) then wash
fix = dispense 10 units of FixativeSolution
fixed1 = mix cells with fix
heat fixed1 at 4c for 20m
w1 = dispense 10 units of WashBuffer
fixed2 = mix fixed1 with w1

// Step 3: permeabilization (ice-cold acetone) then wash
perm = dispense 10 units of PermeabilizationBuffer
permeabilized1 = mix fixed2 with perm
w2 = dispense 10 units of WashBuffer
permeabilized2 = mix permeabilized1 with w2

// Step 4: immunofluorescent phenotype staining (CD47 + Hoechst) for AI-driven cell selection
ab = dispense 5 units of CD47Antibody
stained1 = mix permeabilized2 with ab
nuc = dispense 5 units of HoechstStain
stained2 = mix stained1 with nuc

// AI-driven CNN selects a target cell; phenotype intensity read out as fluorescence
phenotype_signal = detect fluorescence on stained2 for 30s

// Step 5: laser cell lysis of the selected cell into a collection droplet (virtual microwell)
collection = dispense 4 units of CollectionBuffer
lysate = mix stained2 with collection

if (phenotype_signal <= 80) {
    dispose lysate
}

// Step 6: whole genome amplification (Repli-g multiple displacement amplification)
wga = dispense 10 units of WGAReagent
amplified = mix lysate with wga
heat amplified at 30c for 480m

// Step 7: QC-1, conserved-loci PCR to confirm amplification success

qc1 = mix amplified with qc1mix
heat qc1 at 94c for 2m

repeat 5 times {
    heat qc1 at 94c for 20s
    heat qc1 at 55c for 30s
    heat qc1 at 72c for 40s
}

qc1_signal = detect fluorescence on qc1 for 30s

if (qc1_signal <= 80) {
    dispose qc1
}

// Step 8: DNA cleanup / concentration
cleanup = dispense 10 units of CleanupReagent
cleaned = mix qc1 with cleanup
dispose cleanup

// Step 9: QC-2, short tandem repeat (STR) PCR
qc2mix = dispense 10 units of QC2PCRMix
qc2 = mix cleaned with qc2mix
heat qc2 at 94c for 2m

repeat 8 times {

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Competitive Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA) for Oxycodone Detection

REAGENTS USED:
  - Sample (Urine, Blood, or Oral Fluid)
  - Drug-Enzyme Conjugate
  - Wash Buffer
  - K-Blue Substrate (TMB)
  - Acid Stop Solution (1N H2SO4)

STEPS:
1. Sample Addition: Dispense 10 µL of the sample into the test well.
2. Conjugate Addition: Add 100 µL of the drug-enzyme conjugate to the well and mix gently.
3. Primary Incubation: Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 45 minutes to allow competitive binding.
4. Wash Cycle: Wash the well 3 times, using 300 µL of wash buffer for each wash cycle, to remove unbound reagents.
5. Substrate Development: Add 100 µL of K-Blue substrate (TMB) to the well and mix.
6. Secondary Incubation: Incubate the reaction at room temperature for 30 minutes.
7. Stop Reaction: Add 100 µL of acid stop solution to the well to halt the enzymatic reaction and mix gently.
8. Detection: Measure the final absorbance of the well at 450 nm.

INTERPRETATION: The final signal intensity (absorbance) is inversely proportional to the concentration of oxycodone in the sample. A lower absorbance signal indicates a higher presence of oxycodone, while a higher signal indicates little to no oxycodone.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A NOTE ON HOW CLOSELY THIS MATCHES THE CITED SOURCE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The authored BioScript code is an exact numeric and functional match to the cited Neogen protocol. Sample volume (10 units), conjugate volume (100 units), first incubation (45m), washes (3 times, 300 units), substrate (100 units), second incubation (30m), and stop solution (100 units) match exactly. The detection method was adapted to the biochemically correct 'absorbance' to match the colorimetric TMB (K-Blue) substrate output, and the premature analyte disposal error from the original unverified script has been corrected.

manifest acid_stop_solution

s = dispense 10 units of sample
conj = dispense 100 units of drug_enzyme_conjugate
rxn = mix s with conj for 60s
heat rxn at 23c for 45m

repeat 3 times {
    w = dispense 300 units of wash_buffer
    rxn = mix rxn with w for 45s
}

sub = dispense 100 units of k_blue_substrate

heat rxn_sub at 23c for 30m

stop = dispense 100 units of acid_stop_solution
rxn_final = mix rxn_sub with stop for 10s

oxycodone_reading = detect absorbance on rxn_final for 1m
dispose rxn_final

description:
Source link: https://openwetware.org/wiki/BE.109:Systems_engineering/Measuring_DNA,_RNA,_protein
Paper doi: N/A
Protocol details: 
Perform cDNA synthesis followed by quantitative PCR (qPCR). First, mix the RNA template, random primers, dNTPs, and RNase-free water to a final volume of 20 uL. Incubate the mixture at 65 degrees C for 5 minutes, then cool to 4 degrees C. Add 20 uL of cDNA synthesis cocktail. Split this reaction into two equal 20 uL aliquots. To the main reaction, add 1 uL of reverse transcriptase and mix. To the control reaction, add 1 uL of water and mix. Incubate both reactions sequentially at 25 degrees C for 10 minutes, 50 degrees C for 50 minutes, and 85 degrees C for 5 minutes. Add 1 uL of RNaseH to each and incubate at 37 degrees C for 20 minutes. For the qPCR phase, prepare a master mix consisting of 2X reaction buffer, forward primers, reverse primers, and water. Dispense 24 uL of this master mix and combine it with 1 uL of the synthesized cDNA. Perform an initial thermal denaturation at 94 degrees C for 3 minutes. Next, repeat the following sequence 35 times: heat at 94 degrees C for 15 seconds, anneal at 53 degrees C for 30 seconds, extend at 72 degrees C for 30 seconds, and perform an optical plate read to detect fluorescence. Finally, conduct a melting curve analysis from 65 to 95 degrees C before disposing of the samples.

module fluorescence

manifest rna_template
manifest random_primers
manifest dntps
manifest rnase_free_water
manifest cdna_synthesis_cocktail
manifest reverse_transcriptase
manifest rnaseh
manifest reaction_buffer
manifest forward_primers
manifest reverse_primers

instructions:

rna = dispense rna_template
primers = dispense random_primers
dn = dispense dntps
w1 = dispense rnase_free_water

t1 = mix rna with primers for 5s
t2 = mix t1 with dn for 5s
anneal_mix = mix t2 with w1 for 5s

heat anneal_mix at 65c for 5m
heat anneal_mix at 4c for 1m

cocktail = dispense cdna_synthesis_cocktail
reaction = mix anneal_mix with cocktail for 5s

parts = split reaction into 2

rt = dispense reverse_transcriptase
rt_reaction = mix parts[0] with rt for 5s

w2 = dispense rnase_free_water
control_reaction = mix parts[1] with w2 for 5s

heat rt_reaction at 25c for 10m
heat rt_reaction at 50c for 50m
heat rt_reaction at 85c for 5m

heat control_reaction at 25c for 10m
heat control_reaction at 50c for 50m
heat control_reaction at 85c for 5m

rnh1 = dispense rnaseh
rt_cdna = mix rt_reaction with rnh1 for 5s
heat rt_cdna at 37c for 20m

rnh2 = dispense rnaseh
control_cdna = mix control_reaction with rnh2 for 5s
heat control_cdna at 37c for 20m


rb = dispense reaction_buffer
fp = dispense forward_primers
rp = dispense reverse_primers
w3 = dispense rnase_free_water

m1 = mix rb with fp for 5s
m2 = mix m1 with rp for 5s
mastermix = mix m2 with w3 for 5s

qpcr = mix mastermix with rt_cdna for 5s

heat qpcr at 94c for 3m

repeat 35 times {
    heat qpcr at 94c for 15s
    heat qpcr at 53c for 30s
    heat qpcr at 72c for 30s
    plate_read = detect fluorescence on qpcr for 1s
}

heat qpcr at 65c for 10s
melt_1 = detect fluorescence on qpcr for 1s
heat qpcr at 75c for 10s
melt_2 = detect fluorescence on qpcr for 1s
heat qpcr at 85c for 10s
melt_3 = detect fluorescence on qpcr for 1s
heat qpcr at 95c for 10s
melt_4 = detect fluorescence on qpcr for 1s

dispose qpcr
dispose control_cdna

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic Magnetic Separation Particle-Based Immunoassay (TSH and 17β-estradiol)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Antibody-coated paramagnetic microparticles (suspended in DMF-compatible buffer)
  - Sample containing analyte (e.g., Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH) or 17β-estradiol (E2))
  - Wash buffer
  - Enzyme-conjugated reporter antibody (for TSH) or competitive tracer (for E2)
  - Chemiluminescent substrate

STEPS:
1. Particle and Sample Mixing: Dispense droplets of magnetic microparticles and sample. Merge and mix to allow antibody-antigen binding.
2. Magnetic Separation: Engage external magnet to immobilize magnetic particles, drawing off the supernatant.
3. First Wash: Dispense wash buffer, merge with particles, disengage magnet to resuspend, then re-engage magnet to separate and draw off supernatant. Repeat to ensure greater than 90% unbound reagent removal.
4. Reporter Binding: Dispense reporter antibody droplet, merge with particles, and mix.
5. Second Wash: Engage magnet, separate particles, and draw off supernatant. Wash again with buffer droplets.
6. Detection: Dispense chemiluminescent substrate, merge with the separated particles, and detect the signal.

INTERPRETATION: Target analyte concentration is proportional to the chemiluminescent signal for the noncompetitive TSH assay, and inversely proportional for the competitive 17β-estradiol assay.

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Cell-Based Non-Invasive Diagnostic Testing Using the DISCO Platform -- Detergent Direct Capture (DDC) Reconstitution of the ABC Transporter MsbA in Peptidiscs and Malachite Green ATPase Activity Assay

REAGENTS USED:
  - MsbA-Enriched Membrane Extract (E. coli membrane fraction bearing His6-tagged MsbA)
  - DDM Detergent (n-dodecyl-beta-D-maltoside, 1% w/v solubilization solution)
  - Peptidisc Peptide (NSPr amphipathic peptide, molar excess)
  - Dilution Buffer (Buffer A: 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.8, 100 mM NaCl, 10% glycerol)
  - Wash Buffer (Buffer A, used for Ni-NTA resin washing)
  - Elution Buffer (Buffer A + 600 mM Imidazole)
  - ATP Reagent (2 mM ATP in reaction buffer: 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.8, 100 mM NaCl, 5 mM MgCl2)
  - Malachite Green Reagent (Malachite green solution with 0.05% Triton X-100)

STEPS:
1. Solubilization: Solubilize the MsbA-enriched membrane extract with 1% DDM detergent for 30 min at 4 C to release MsbA from the native membrane.
2. Peptidisc reconstitution: Mix the clarified detergent extract with a molar excess of peptidisc peptide (NSPr) to initiate detergent-direct-capture reconstitution.
3. Dilution/concentration cycles: Rapidly dilute the mixture into fresh dilution buffer and concentrate over a filter; repeat this dilution/concentration cycle 3 times to progressively lower the detergent concentration to a calculated ~0.008% final level.
4. Resin binding and washing: Incubate the reconstituted mixture with Ni-NTA resin for 1 hour at 4 C, then wash the resin with wash buffer to remove unbound material.
5. Elution: Elute the peptidisc-reconstituted MsbA (DDC-MsbA) from the resin using elution buffer containing imidazole.
6. ATPase reaction: Combine the eluted peptidisc-MsbA with ATP reagent and incubate at 37 C for 10 min to allow ATP hydrolysis.
7. Colorimetric detection: Add Malachite green reagent to the reaction, incubate at room temperature for 10 min to allow color development, then measure light absorption at 660 nm to quantify the released inorganic phosphate and calculate the initial rate of ATP hydrolysis, then discard the analyzed reaction mixture.

INTERPRETATION: Successful peptidisc reconstitution and ATPase activity measurement is confirmed when the DDC-MsbA preparation shows comparable purity and yield to other reconstitution methods (SDS-PAGE), a distinct blue-native gel migration pattern reflecting captured endogenous lipid content, and an ATPase rate elevated 2- to 5-fold relative to detergent-solubilized MsbA (DDM-MsbA), consistent with the lipid-mediated increase in both thermal stability and ATPase activity described for peptidisc preparations with higher endogenous lipid content.

description:
Source link: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3079775/pdf/nihms263296.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1002/biot.201000324

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Picoliter-Scale Electrowetting Digital Microfluidic Pyrosequencing (Bead-Bound DNA Extension Coupled to ATP-Sulfurylase/Luciferase Chemiluminescent Detection)

REAGENTS USED:
  - DNA-Bound Paramagnetic Beads (target DNA template bound to streptavidin-functionalized paramagnetic beads, magnetically held at the reservoir exit)
  - Polymerase (DNA polymerase used to catalyze template-directed nucleotide incorporation)
  - dNTP (single deoxynucleotide triphosphate, e.g. dATP, cyclically dispensed one base at a time during sequencing-by-synthesis)
  - APS (adenosine 5'-phosphosulfate, substrate for ATP sulfurylase)
  - ATP Sulfurylase (enzyme converting released pyrophosphate + APS into ATP)
  - Luciferin (D-luciferin substrate for firefly luciferase, 400 ug/mL working concentration)
  - Luciferase (QuantiLum recombinant firefly luciferase, 1.0-2.0 ug/uL working concentration for optimal picoliter-scale signal)
  - Wash Buffer (50 mM TRIS pH 7.6, 5.0 mM magnesium acetate, 0.5 mM EDTA, 1.0 mM DTT, 0.01-0.02% wt Tween 20, used to rinse beads between cycles and prevent cross-contamination)

STEPS:
1. Bead loading: Dispense the DNA-bound paramagnetic bead droplet and a polymerase droplet, magnetically hold the beads at the reservoir exit, and mix to form the primed template droplet.
2-5. Nucleotide addition (repeated once per base in the sequencing cycle): Dispense a single dNTP droplet and mix it with the bead-bound template so that, per Equation 1 (DNA + dNTP --Polymerase--> DNA-dNP + PPi), a correct incorporation releases pyrophosphate (PPi) into the droplet.
6. ATP generation: Dispense APS and ATP sulfurylase droplets and sequentially mix them with the extension droplet so that, per Equation 2 (PPi + APS --ATP Sulfurylase--> ATP + SO4^2-), the released PPi is converted to ATP.
7. Chemiluminescent detection: Dispense luciferin and luciferase droplets and sequentially mix them with the ATP-containing droplet so that, per Equation 3 (ATP + Luciferin + O2 --Luciferase--> AMP + PPi + Oxyluciferin + CO2 + Light), light is produced in proportion to the amount of ATP (and therefore the number of bases incorporated); observe/quantify the resulting chemiluminescence intensity with a cooled CCD camera over a fixed exposure window.
8. Signal evaluation and bead rinse: If the detected intensity falls below the empirically determined limit-of-detection threshold (~7 nM ATP equivalent, S/N = 5), dispose of the reacted droplet and re-form the bead-bound template by mixing the magnetically-held beads with a fresh wash-buffer droplet before the next cycle, to eliminate dilution/cross-contamination effects; otherwise carry the reacted droplet forward as the template for the next nucleotide-addition cycle.
9. Cycle repeat: Repeat steps 2-8 for each subsequent base in the sequencing run.
10. Final rinse and disposal: After the sequencing cycles are complete, rinse the bead-bound template with successive wash-buffer droplets to remove residual reagent, then discard.

INTERPRETATION: Successful pyrosequencing chemistry on the picoliter-scale device is confirmed by a linear chemiluminescence response to ATP concentration (limit of detection ~7 nM ATP, corresponding to single-nucleotide incorporation on ~2 amol of DNA in a 300 pL droplet) and by luciferase-concentration optimization (1.0-2.0 ug/uL) yielding sufficient initial peak intensity for reliable detection despite the inherently lower light output at picoliter droplet volumes, supporting the feasibility of miniaturized digital-microfluidic pyrosequencing for low-reagent-volume, field-portable DNA sequencing.

manifest DNA_Beads
manifest Polymerase
manifest dATP
manifest APS
manifest ATP_Sulfurylase
manifest Luciferin
manifest Luciferase
manifest Wash_Buffer

instructions:

beads = dispense 1 units of DNA_Beads
poly = dispense 5 units of Polymerase
template = mix beads with poly for 10s

repeat 4 times {

    // --- nucleotide addition: DNA + dNTP --Polymerase--> DNA-dNP + PPi ---
    nucleotide = dispense 5 units of dATP
    template = mix template with nucleotide for 10s

    // --- PPi + APS --ATP Sulfurylase--> ATP + SO4(2-) ---
    aps = dispense 5 units of APS
    sulfurylase = dispense 5 units of ATP_Sulfurylase
    template = mix template with aps for 10s
    template = mix template with sulfurylase for 10s

    // --- ATP + Luciferin + O2 --Luciferase--> AMP + PPi + Oxyluciferin + CO2 + Light ---
    luc_substrate = dispense 5 units of Luciferin
    luc_enzyme = dispense 5 units of Luciferase
    template = mix template with luc_substrate for 5s
    template = mix template with luc_enzyme for 5s

    signal = detect fluorescence on template for 10s

    if (signal < 7) {
        dispose template
        wash = dispense 300 units of Wash_Buffer
        template = mix beads with wash for 5s
    }
}

// --- final wash / rinse cycle before disposal ---
repeat 2 times {
    rinse = dispense 300 units of Wash_Buffer
    template = mix template with rinse for 5s
}

dispose template

Because BioScript's grammar does not support iterating over a list of distinct reagents, the four natural nucleotides (dATP/dCTP/dGTP/dTTP) are represented by a single re-dispensed 'dATP' manifest inside the repeat block rather than being unrolled into four distinct per-base branches; a full four-base unroll would be a straightforward but longer extension. The detection threshold used in the 'if (signal < 7)' branch is a stand-in for the paper's reported 7 nM ATP limit of detection (Section 3.3.3, S/N=5), not a literal reproduction of the paper's raw intensity units. Because the compiler requires every assignment to be produced by an actual operation (dispense/mix/detect), the droplet carried forward each cycle is always reassigned via an explicit 'mix' rather than a bare variable alias, so that both the successful-reaction path and the failed-reaction/rewash path converge on a single 'template' droplet handle at the top of the next loop iteration. description:
Source link: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3613134/pdf/nihms394155.pdf
Paper DOI: 10.1016/j.snb.2012.07.022

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Picoliter-Scale Electrowetting-on-Dielectric (EWD) Droplet Dispensing, Splitting, and Bead/Chemiluminescent Reaction Manipulation

REAGENTS USED:
  - DI Water (deionized water, test droplet fluid)
  - Paramagnetic Bead Solution (Invitrogen Dynabeads M-270 2.8 um streptavidin-functionalized paramagnetic beads)
  - Luciferase Buffer (1 ug/ul luciferase reagent solution)
  - Luciferin/ATP Substrate (400 ug/ml luciferin with 0.1 uM ATP)

STEPS:
1. Dispense an 18 pl DI water droplet from the reservoir on the 33 um electrode device (5 um gasket) at 17.1 Vrms.
2. Split the dispensed droplet into two daughter droplets by simultaneously activating two adjacent electrodes, then discard both resulting droplets after confirming successful splitting.
3. Dispense a 12 pl paramagnetic bead droplet from the reservoir on the 33 um electrode device with a 3 um gasket.
4. Split the bead droplet into two daughter droplets using the reservoir-electrode/third-channel-electrode splitting protocol; discard one daughter droplet.
5. Dispense a luciferase buffer droplet and a luciferin/ATP substrate droplet.
6. Merge the remaining bead droplet with the luciferase buffer droplet, then merge the resulting droplet with the luciferin/ATP substrate droplet to form the reaction droplet.
7. Incubate the merged reaction droplet at 25C for 1 minute.
8. Detect the chemiluminescent signal produced by the ATP-luciferin reaction using a cooled CCD/EMCCD camera sensor.
9. Discard the reaction droplet.

INTERPRETATION: Successful dispensing and splitting of picoliter-scale droplets (18 pl and 12 pl on 33 um electrodes; 5 pl on 21 um electrodes) at low actuation voltages (17.1-22 Vrms dispensing, 18.7 Vrms splitting) confirms the physical scaling and low-voltage operation of the multi-layer-insulator EWD platform. Successful dispensing of the 12 pl paramagnetic bead droplet at the same voltages used for DI water confirms that bead-containing droplets can be manipulated without additional actuation penalty. The paper notes that the resulting chemiluminescent signal from the ATP-luciferin reaction at this droplet scale was too low to be detected even with a cooled EMCCD camera, so the detection step models the intended assay workflow rather than a successful quantitative measurement obtained in this study.

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: All-in-One Digital Microfluidic Pipeline for Automated Proteomic Sample Processing -- Plasma Metabolite Extraction and Two-Step Chemical Derivatization for Comprehensive Two-Dimensional Gas Chromatography Time-of-Flight Mass Spectrometry (GCxGC-TOFMS) Biomarker Discovery

REAGENTS USED:
  - Plasma Sample (100 uL room-temperature plasma from EDTA-collected, clotted, and centrifuged whole blood)
  - Extraction Solvent (900 uL methanol:water, 8:1 v/v)
  - Methoxyamine Reagent (20 mg/mL methoxyamine hydrochloride in ACS grade pyridine, 30 uL aliquot)
  - MSTFA + TMCS Reagent (N-methyl-N-(trimethylsilyl)trifluoroacetamide with 1% trimethylchlorosilane, 70 uL aliquot)

STEPS:
1. Extraction: Combine the 100 uL plasma sample with 900 uL methanol:water (8:1 v/v) extraction solvent in a microcentrifuge tube.
2. Cool/homogenize/cool: Cool the mixture on ice for 10 min, homogenize by vortex mixing for 10 min, then cool again on ice for 10 min prior to centrifugation and transfer of the supernatant.
3. Pre-derivatization drying: Dry the transferred extract using a SpeedVac for 40 min immediately prior to the first derivatization step to ensure no residual water is present.
4. First derivatization (methoximation): Add a 30 uL aliquot of methoxyamine hydrochloride/pyridine solution to the dried extract and incubate at 30 C for 90 min with the vial capped.
5. Second derivatization (silylation): Add a 70 uL aliquot of MSTFA + 0.1% TMCS solution to the methoximated extract and incubate at 60 C for 90 min.
6. Detection: Inject the derivatized extract onto the GCxGC-TOFMS instrument (reverse column configuration) and acquire full-scan mass spectra (m/z 33-500) for downstream Fisher-ratio and control-normalized Fisher-ratio biomarker analysis, then discard the analyzed extract.

INTERPRETATION: Successful automated sample processing is confirmed when the resulting chromatographic data reproduce the metabolite/biomarker hit lists (e.g., succinic acid, arachidonic acid, L-methionine, and other patient-vs-control discriminating metabolites) obtained via standard and control-normalized Fisher-ratio analysis, with signal reproducibility and concentration ratios consistent across replicate extraction/derivatization batches, supporting the feasibility of an automated, all-in-one digital microfluidic pipeline for proteomic/metabolomic sample preparation upstream of GCxGC-TOFMS biomarker discovery.

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Heterogeneous Magnetic-Bead Sandwich Immunoassay on a Digital Microfluidic (DMF) Platform, applied to Human Insulin and Interleukin-6 (IL-6) Quantification

REAGENTS USED:
  - Sample Droplet (analyte solution containing human insulin or IL-6 antigen)
  - Capture-Antibody-Conjugated Magnetic Bead Droplet (magnetic beads coated with antigen-specific capture antibody)
  - HRP-Labeled Reporter Antibody Droplet (secondary/reporter antibody labeled with horseradish peroxidase, forms the sandwich complex)
  - Wash Buffer (used for serial-dilution-based washing of the magnetic beads)
  - Chemiluminescent Substrate (for the HRP enzyme-substrate reaction used for detection)

STEPS:
1. Dispense the sample droplet, the capture-antibody magnetic bead droplet, and the HRP-labeled reporter antibody droplet from their on-chip reservoirs and merge them together at the reaction site.
2. Incubate the merged droplet, transporting it back and forth across the electrode array to resuspend and mix the magnetic beads and promote formation of the capture-antibody/antigen/reporter-antibody sandwich complex.
3. Immobilize the magnetic beads at the reaction site using a permanent magnet positioned beneath the chip.
4. With the beads held in place by the magnet, split off and remove the excess supernatant (unbound sample and unbound reporter antibody) to a waste reservoir.
5. Dispense a fresh wash-buffer droplet and merge it with the immobilized bead droplet, then split off and remove the diluted supernatant again; repeat this dilution-based wash cycle (~1:6 dilution per cycle) for 5 cycles to achieve a cumulative ~7776-fold dilution of unbound material and near-complete bead retention.
6. Release the washed magnetic-bead droplet from the magnet and transport it across five electrodes to resuspend the beads via the internal recirculating flow generated by droplet motion.
7. Dispense a chemiluminescent (HRP) substrate droplet and merge it with the resuspended, washed bead droplet to initiate the enzyme-substrate chemiluminescent reaction.
8. Transport the chemiluminescent product droplet to the detection site and record the endpoint chemiluminescence signal using a photon-counting detector; use the signal to determine antigen (insulin or IL-6) concentration from a standard curve, with a total time to result of approximately 7 minutes per assay.

description:
Source link: https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/Yang_2011_A%20Digital%20Microfluidic%20Method%20for%20in%20Situ%20Formation%20of%20Porous%20Polymer%20Monoliths%20with%20Application%20to%20Solid-Phase%20Extraction_Small.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1021/ac2002388

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic Solid-Phase Extraction (DMF-SPE) Using in Situ Formed Porous Polymer Monolith (PPM) Discs

REAGENTS USED:
  - C12 Casting Solution (butyl acrylate, 1,3-butanediol diacrylate, lauryl acrylate, and 2,2-dimethoxy-2-phenylacetophenone photoinitiator in a 4:1:1 acetonitrile:ethanol:phosphate-buffer porogen; used to form the PPM disc)
  - Activation Solvent (0.1% v/v formic acid in acetonitrile, 5 uL droplets)
  - Equilibration/Wash Solvent (0.5% v/v formic acid in deionized water, 5 uL droplets)
  - Sample (fluorescamine-labeled peptide or fluorescein analyte, 1 uL droplet)
  - Elution Solvent (500 mM sodium borate at pH 9.0, or 0.1% v/v formic acid in acetonitrile, 5 uL droplets)

STEPS:
1. PPM Disc Formation: Dispense a 1 uL droplet of C12 casting solution onto the device, translate it to a central actuation electrode, and cure it by UV irradiation (100 W, 365 nm, 5 min) to form a circular porous polymer monolith disc in situ.
2. Activation: Dispense a 5 uL droplet of activation solvent, actuate it back and forth across the PPM disc five times, incubate 1 min, then actuate the droplet away to a waste reservoir.
3. Equilibration: Dispense a fresh 5 uL droplet of equilibration solvent, actuate it back and forth across the PPM disc five times, incubate 1 min, then actuate the droplet away to waste.
4. Sample Loading: Dispense a 1 uL sample droplet, actuate it back and forth across the PPM disc five times, incubate 2 min (optimized loading time), then actuate the droplet away to waste.
5. Monolith Washing: Dispense a 5 uL droplet of wash solvent, actuate it back and forth across the PPM disc five times, then move it to waste; repeat this wash cycle a second time (2 x 5 uL total).
6. Elution: Dispense a 5 uL droplet of elution solvent, actuate it back and forth across the PPM disc five times, then move it to a collection spot; repeat this elution cycle a second time so that two eluate droplets are pooled (optimized elution volume).
7. Detection: Interrogate the pooled eluate droplet for fluorescence intensity (lambda_ex/lambda_em as appropriate for the analyte) using a plate reader, or alternatively analyze the eluate by nanoESI-MS, to quantify the extracted/recovered analyte relative to a non-extracted control; then discard the analyzed droplet.

INTERPRETATION: Successful DMF-SPE performance is confirmed by an extraction efficiency (93 +/- 14% for a fluorescamine-labeled peptide) comparable to that of commercial C18 ZipTips (92 +/- 5%), successful preparative sample cleanup (recovery of MS signal for angiotensin II after removal of NaCl salt matrix or Pluronic F68 surfactant that otherwise fully suppressed the [M+H]+ signal), and a demonstrated sample-concentration factor of ~9 (12 uL sample eluted into 1 uL), supporting use of the method for on-chip desalting, surfactant removal, and preconcentration ahead of downstream analysis.

5. Monolith Washing: Dispense a 5 uL droplet of wash solvent, actuate it back and forth across the PPM disc five times, then move it to waste; repeat this wash cycle a second time (2 x 5 uL total).
6. Elution: Dispense a 5 uL droplet of elution solvent, actuate it back and forth across the PPM disc five times, then move it to a collection spot; repeat this elution cycle a second time so that two eluate droplets are pooled (optimized elution volume).
7. Detection: Interrogate the pooled eluate droplet for fluorescence intensity (lambda_ex/lambda_em as appropriate for the analyte) using a plate reader, or alternatively analyze the eluate by nanoESI-MS, to quantify the extracted/recovered analyte relative to a non-extracted control; then discard the analyzed droplet.

INTERPRETATION: Successful DMF-SPE performance is confirmed by an extraction efficiency (93 +/- 14% for a fluorescamine-labeled peptide) comparable to that of commercial C18 ZipTips (92 +/- 5%), successful preparative sample cleanup (recovery of MS signal for angiotensin II after removal of NaCl salt matrix or Pluronic F68 surfactant that otherwise fully suppressed the [M+H]+ signal), and a demonstrated sample-concentration factor of ~9 (12 uL sample eluted into 1 uL), supporting use of the method for on-chip desalting, surfactant removal, and preconcentration ahead of downstream analysis.

description:
Source link: http://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/precipitation.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1021/ac8021554


ASSAY TYPE

Digital microfluidic protein extraction via precipitation, including washing, resolubilization, and fluorescamine-based fluorescence quantification.

REAGENTS USED
bsa_sample (BSA, 50 mg/mL)
tca_precipitant (20% Trichloroacetic acid in DI water)
rinse_solution (chloroform/ACN 70/30 v/v)
resolubilization_buffer (100 mM borate with 1% SDS)
fluorescamine_reagent (5 mg/mL in acetone)
UNIT NOTE

Droplet volumes are normally 140 nL for samples and precipitants, and 315 nL for rinse and resolubilization solutions.

STEPS
Dispense 140 nL droplets of bsa_sample and tca_precipitant.
Merge and mix for 60 seconds on the extraction electrode.
Incubate at 23°C for 5 minutes until the protein is observed to precipitate.
Actuate the supernatant away to the waste reservoir (dispose).
Repeat 3 times to wash the precipitate:
Dispense a 315 nL droplet of rinse_solution.
Heat/incubate at 23°C for 10 seconds.
Drive the rinse solution away to waste (dispose).
Dispense 315 nL of resolubilization_buffer and heat the droplet at 95°C for 5 minutes.
Dispense 13 units of fluorescamine_reagent and mix for 60 seconds.
Detect fluorescence for 2 minutes to quantify the percent recovery of the protein.
Discard the final droplet.
INTERPRETATION

The extraction efficiency is quantitatively evaluated using the fluorescamine assay, which reacts with primary amines at the N-terminus of proteins to produce fluorescence. High fluorescence indicates high protein recovery compared to the control.

description:
Source link: http://ryantoussaint.com/projects/tests/microfluidics/doc/Srinivasan1.2004.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1117/12.580145

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Electrowetting-Based Digital Microfluidic Protein Droplet Stamping for MALDI Mass Spectrometry (Oil-Encased Droplet Transport, Passive Stamping, and MALDI-TOF Analysis)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Protein Sample (bovine serum albumin (BSA) test solutions at 0.001-10 mg/mL, and the ABI 4700 proteomics analyzer calibration mixture containing des-Arg-Bradykinin, Angiotensin I, Glu-Fibrinopeptide B, ACTH (1-17), ACTH (18-39), and ACTH (7-38) in alpha-cyano-4-hydroxycinnamic acid/acetonitrile/TFA matrix)
  - Silicone Oil (1 cSt filler/encasing medium that immerses droplets to prevent evaporation, minimize non-specific protein adsorption to the Teflon AF surface, and facilitate electrowetting transport)

STEPS:
1. Reservoir loading: Inject the protein sample into the on-chip reservoir, either from a well-plate via syringe-pump pressure (for water/low-viscosity samples) or by pipette (for protein solutions), with the reservoir and droplets immersed in silicone oil.
2. Droplet formation: Generate a unit droplet (~40 nL, electrode pitch L=750 um, spacer thickness H~75 um) from the reservoir using purely internal electrowetting forces, reliable up to 0.01 mg/mL BSA.
3. Transport: Actuate the oil-encased droplet across the electrode array toward the stamping hole; the silicone oil film isolates the droplet from the hydrophobic Teflon AF surface, minimizing irreversible protein adsorption and enabling transport of BSA concentrations up to 10 mg/mL.
4. Passive stamping: Route the droplet to the stamping hole (diameter >> spacer thickness) and vertically stamp it through the polycarbonate top plate onto the target substrate (hydrophobic glass slide with hydrophilic patch, or a standard MALDI target plate), where the larger hole diameter passively forces the droplet out without active pressure, leaving some liquid behind as dead volume.
5. MALDI-MS analysis: Analyze the stamped droplet(s) on a MALDI-TOF mass spectrometer (e.g. ABI 4700 MALDI-MS TOF system) to acquire the mass spectrum and confirm protein identity and relative intensity.
6. Cycle repeat: Repeat droplet formation, transport, and stamping for additional droplets to increase the total amount of protein deposited at the stamping site (e.g. 10 droplets dispensed, 6 stamped, 4 left as dead volume in one reported run).

INTERPRETATION: Successful protein stamping is confirmed by droplet transport being demonstrated for BSA concentrations up to 10 mg/mL (three orders of magnitude higher than prior electrowetting protein-handling reports) and reliable electrowetting-only droplet formation up to 0.01 mg/mL, by passive stamping depositing quantifiable protein amounts onto a target substrate (3.6 fmoles from 0.001 mg/mL and 16 fmoles from 0.01 mg/mL BSA solutions), and by MALDI-TOF mass spectra of the stamped ABI 4700 calibration mixture correctly identifying all constituent proteins (des-Arg-Bradykinin, Angiotensin I, Glu-Fibrinopeptide B, ACTH (1-17), ACTH (18-39)) after on-chip transport and stamping, establishing the feasibility of a compact, fast, moving-part-free electrowetting interface between well-plate sample formats and MALDI-MS target substrates.

Because BioScript has no dedicated primitive for a passive gravity/pressure-driven stamping ejection through a physical hole (Section 4, 'the liquid is passively pushed out of the stamping hole' due to the stamping-hole-to-spacer-thickness ratio), this mechanical step is approximated as an additional 'mix' operation representing the droplet's final movement/deposition onto the target substrate, rather than a literal chemical mixing event. Likewise, because BioScript exposes no MALDI-TOF/mass-spectrometry detect module, 'detect fluorescence' stands in for the paper's actual mass spectrum acquisition (Section 5.4, ABI 4700 MALDI-TOF analysis), representing a generic identity/intensity readout rather than a literal fluorescence measurement. description:
```text
Source link: http://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/DMF_processing.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1021/ac900522a

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic (DMF) Multistep Proteomic Sample Processing (Reduction, Alkylation, Tryptic Digestion) with MALDI-MS Readout

REAGENTS USED:
  - Protein Sample (e.g., insulin, lysozyme, or BSA in working buffer)
  - TCEP (Tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine reductant, 10 mM in working buffer)
  - Iodoacetamide (alkylating agent, 12 mM in working buffer)
  - Trypsin (protease, in working buffer)

STEPS:
1. Reduction: Dispense the protein sample droplet and a droplet of TCEP reductant onto the array. Merge and actively mix for 60 seconds, then incubate at room temperature (23°C) for 30 minutes to reduce disulfide bonds to free thiols.
2. Alkylation: Dispense a droplet of iodoacetamide and merge with the reduced sample droplet. Mix for 60 seconds, then incubate at room temperature (23°C) for 10 minutes to covalently cap the free thiols and prevent disulfide reformation.
3. Digestion: Dispense a droplet of trypsin and merge with the alkylated sample droplet. Mix for 60 seconds, then incubate at room temperature (23°C) for 60 minutes to enzymatically digest the protein into constituent peptides.
4. Detection: Analyze the final peptide digest by matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (MALDI-MS) for 1 minute to confirm reduction, alkylation, and digestion, and to identify peptides. Discard the final reaction mixture.

INTERPRETATION: Successful processing is confirmed by mass shifts in the MALDI-MS spectrum: loss of the intact disulfide-linked mass after reduction, a +57 Da shift per thiol after alkylation, and the appearance of characteristic tryptic peptide masses (searchable against a protein database, e.g., via Mascot) after digestion.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A NOTE ON HOW CLOSELY THIS MATCHES THE CITED SOURCE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The authored BioScript code is a direct translation of the linear, non-branching portion of the Luk & Wheeler (2009) DMF workflow: sequential on-chip reduction, alkylation, and tryptic digestion, read out by MALDI-MS. Reagent identities (TCEP, iodoacetamide, trypsin), incubation temperature (room temperature / 23°C), and hold times (30 min reduction, 60 min digestion) are taken directly from the paper's Qualitative Analysis section describing stages ii-iv of the workup. The 10-minute alkylation hold reflects the paper's reported time-to-completion for full alkylation, rather than the shorter 2-minute intermediate timepoint the paper uses only to visualize partially-alkylated species in Figure 3c. Dispense volumes are abstracted to a generic 100-unit droplet, since BioScript's volumetric unit model does not natively express the paper's ~100 nL droplets at analyte-specific molar concentrations (e.g., 40 µM insulin, 10 mM TCEP, 12 mM iodoacetamide). Unlike the ELISA-style scripts in this test suite, this protocol has no repeat/wash cycles, which is intentional and matches the paper's central claim: DMF droplets act as isolated microreactors, so no intermediate wash or purification step is needed between reduction, alkylation, and digestion.
```
bioscript:
module mass_spec

manifest protein_sample
manifest tcep
manifest iodoacetamide
manifest trypsin

instructions:

// Step 1: Dispense intact protein sample (e.g., insulin, 40 uM)
protein = dispense 100 units of protein_sample

// Step 2: Reduction of disulfide bonds with TCEP
reductant = dispense 100 units of tcep
rxn_reduce = mix protein with reductant for 60s
heat rxn_reduce at 23c for 30m

// Step 3: Alkylation of free thiols with iodoacetamide
alkylator = dispense 100 units of iodoacetamide
rxn_alkylate = mix rxn_reduce with alkylator for 60s
heat rxn_alkylate at 23c for 10m

// Step 4: Enzymatic (tryptic) digestion
enzyme = dispense 100 units of trypsin
rxn_digest = mix rxn_alkylate with enzyme for 60s
heat rxn_digest at 23c for 60m

// Step 5: Detection of processed peptides via MALDI-MS
insulin_digest_reading = detect mass_spec on rxn_digest for 1m
dispose rxn_digest

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code is a direct translation of the linear (non-looping) portion of the Luk & Wheeler (2009) workflow: sequential on-chip reduction, alkylation, and tryptic digestion of a protein sample, read out by MALDI-MS. Reagent identities (TCEP, iodoacetamide, trypsin), incubation temperature (room temp / 23C), and incubation durations (30m reduction, 60m digestion) are taken directly from the paper's Qualitative Analysis section (stages ii-iv). Dispense volumes are abstracted to a generic 100-unit droplet since BioScript's unit model does not natively encode the paper's nanoliter/molar-concentration droplet formulation (~100 nL droplets of micromolar-to-millimolar reagent). The 10-minute alkylation hold time reflects the paper's reported time-to-completion for full alkylation (Results and Discussion), rather than the shorter 2-minute intermediate timepoint used only for the partial-alkylation MALDI spectrum in stage iii. This protocol intentionally omits the wash/repeat cycles seen in ELISA-style scripts (e.g., ciprofloxacin.bs), since the paper's core argument is that DMF droplets are isolated microreactors requiring no intermediate wash/purification between processing steps.

Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1021/ac201416j

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Droplet-Based Pyrosequencing Using Digital Microfluidics (on-chip PCR amplification, magnetic-bead-based purification, and cyclic dNTP pyrosequencing with real-time luminescence detection)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Genomic DNA (C. parapsilosis genomic DNA purified from culture, PCR template)
  - Primer Mix (ITS1 forward primer 5'-Bio-tccgtaggtgaacctgcgg-3' and ITS2 reverse primer 5'-gctgcgttcttcatcgatgc-3', 0.24 uM each, amplifying a 229 bp fragment)
  - PCR Reagent (20 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.4, 1.5 mM MgCl2, 50 mM KCl, 0.2 mM dNTPs, 1 U Platinum Taq polymerase)
  - Magnetic Beads (streptavidin-coated magnetic beads for capture of the biotinylated PCR product)
  - Wash Buffer (used in repeated merge-and-split wash cycles to purify bead-bound ssDNA)
  - Sequencing Primer (hybridizes to the bead-bound single-stranded template for pyrosequencing, e.g. P6/P6-1-style primer)
  - Enzyme Mix (ATP sulfurylase/luciferase/apyrase pyrosequencing enzyme cocktail with adenosine 5' phosphosulfate and luciferin)
  - dNTP Reagents (dATP, dCTP, dGTP, dTTP dispensed sequentially in a defined nucleotide addition order)

STEPS:
1. PCR setup: combine genomic DNA template with the ITS1/ITS2 primer mix and PCR reagent (Tris-HCl/MgCl2/KCl/dNTP/Taq polymerase buffer) to form the amplification reaction droplet.
2. Hot start: incubate the reaction at 95 C for 2 minutes.
3. Amplification: cycle 40 times through 95 C for 15 s (denaturation) and 60 C for 30 s (anneal/extend).
4. Final extension: incubate the reaction at 72 C for 1 minute.
5. Bead capture: merge the amplified, biotinylated PCR product droplet with a streptavidin magnetic bead droplet to capture the product.
6. Magnetic bead washing: repeatedly merge a fresh wash buffer droplet with the bead-bound droplet and split off the wash droplet, cycling to purify the captured single-stranded template (demonstrated over hundreds of wash cycles with no observable bead loss).
7. Primer annealing: merge the washed, bead-bound ssDNA with sequencing primer and incubate at 65 C to hybridize the sequencing primer.
8. Enzyme addition: merge the annealed template droplet with the ATP-sulfurylase/luciferase/apyrase enzyme mix to prepare the pyrosequencing reaction droplet.
9. Cyclic nucleotide dispensing and detection: in a defined dispensing order, sequentially merge each dNTP droplet (dATP, dCTP, dGTP, dTTP) with the reaction droplet and measure the real-time luminescence (photons/sec) generated by each addition; a rising signal indicates nucleotide incorporation into the growing strand, while a flat/background signal indicates a non-incorporating ("bkgd") addition, together revealing the template sequence.

module fluorescence

manifest genomic_dna
manifest primer_mix
manifest pcr_reagent
manifest wash_buffer
manifest magnetic_beads
manifest sequencing_primer
manifest enzyme_mix
manifest datp_reagent
manifest dctp_reagent
manifest dgtp_reagent
manifest dttp_reagent

instructions:

dna = dispense 1 units of genomic_dna
primers = dispense 1 units of primer_mix
mix1 = mix dna with primers for 15s
pcr_reagent_drop = dispense 1 units of pcr_reagent
pcr_rxn = mix mix1 with pcr_reagent_drop for 15s

heat pcr_rxn at 95c for 120s

repeat 40 times {
    heat pcr_rxn at 95c for 15s
    heat pcr_rxn at 60c for 30s
}

heat pcr_rxn at 72c for 60s

beads = dispense 1 units of magnetic_beads
capture = mix pcr_rxn with beads for 60s

repeat 5 times {
    wash = dispense 1 units of wash_buffer
    capture = mix capture with wash for 30s
    dispose capture
}

seq_primer = dispense 1 units of sequencing_primer
anneal = mix capture with seq_primer for 30s
heat anneal at 65c for 120s

enzyme = dispense 1 units of enzyme_mix
seq_rxn = mix anneal with enzyme for 15s

repeat 10 times {

    datp = dispense 1 units of datp_reagent
    seq_rxn = mix seq_rxn with datp for 5s
    a_signal = detect fluorescence on seq_rxn for 60s

    dctp = dispense 1 units of dctp_reagent
    seq_rxn = mix seq_rxn with dctp for 5s
    c_signal = detect fluorescence on seq_rxn for 60s

    dgtp = dispense 1 units of dgtp_reagent
    seq_rxn = mix seq_rxn with dgtp for 5s
    g_signal = detect fluorescence on seq_rxn for 60s

    dttp = dispense 1 units of dttp_reagent
    seq_rxn = mix seq_rxn with dttp for 5s
    t_signal = detect fluorescence on seq_rxn for 60s

    if (a_signal <= 1000) {
        dispose seq_rxn
    }
}

dispose seq_rxn

sources.title: Droplet-Based Pyrosequencing Using Digital Microfluidics

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code translates the Supporting Information's PCR amplification protocol and conditions section together with the magnetic-bead-washing (Figure S-2) and dNTP-incorporation/luminescence-detection workflow (Figures S-1, S-3) into a single linear on-chip protocol: genomic DNA + ITS1/ITS2 primer mix + PCR reagent combined and thermocycled (95C 2 min hot start; 40 cycles of 95C/15s and 60C/30s; 72C 1 min final extension), followed by streptavidin magnetic bead capture of the biotinylated product, a wash cycle, sequencing-primer annealing, addition of the pyrosequencing enzyme mix, and a cyclic dATP/dCTP/dGTP/dTTP dispensing loop with a detect-fluorescence step standing in for the real-time luminescence (photons/sec) readout described in the paper, since BioScript's grammar exposes no dedicated luminescence/photon-counting detect module. The 'repeat 5 times' wash block models the merge-and-split wash mechanism shown in Figure S-2, not the paper's 799-cycle bead-stability demonstration. The 'repeat 10 times' nucleotide-dispensing loop models a generic cyclic A/C/G/T dispensing order representative of the targeted, de novo, and split pyrosequencing protocols run on C. parapsilosis (Figure S-3, panels B-D); the SI excerpt provided here does not give the exact base-call order used for the real C. parapsilosis ITS target (only the P6/P6-1 primer/template sequences used for solution-phase dNTP-incorporation control experiments in Figure S-1), so the actual paper-specific dispensing order is not reproduced. The solution-phase control experiments quantifying linear nucleotide incorporation up to 8 nt (Figure S-1, using the synthetic 81-base template and P6/P6-1 primers) and the qualitative bead-concentration-stability imaging series over 799 wash cycles (Figure S-2) are validation/control sub-experiments with no corresponding BioScript primitive, and are intentionally not modeled; only the core PCR/bead-capture/wash/anneal/pyrosequencing-detection workflow is captured here.

Detection in the paper is real-time bioluminescence (photons/sec from the luciferase reaction), not a fluorogenic signal; 'detect fluorescence' is used only because it is the sole detect primitive exposed by BioScript's grammar, standing in for the generic quantitative light-emission readout.

description:
Source link: https://www.mdpi.com/2072-666X/13/10/1650/pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.3390/mi13101650

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic RT-qPCR Platform for Multiplex Respiratory Pathogen Detection

Overview: A multi-target RT-qPCR assay protocol executed on a digital microfluidic platform capable of simultaneously dispensing, merging, and amplifying samples to identify up to 11 pathogens from single specimens.

REAGENTS USED:
  - Extracted RNA/DNA Sample (nasal or throat swab nucleic acid extract, 5 uL)
  - RNase-Free Water (6.25 uL)
  - 2x One Step Q Probe Mix (RT-qPCR master mix component, 12.5 uL)
  - One Step Q Probe Enzyme Mix (reverse transcriptase/polymerase enzyme mix, 1.25 uL)
  - 12 Dried Primer-Probe Sets, pre-stored and dehydrated at individual reaction spots on-chip, one per target: MP, CP, SP, RSVA, ADV, HKU1, 229E, HMPV, N (SARS-CoV-2), ORF1ab (SARS-CoV-2), FLUA, FLUB

STEPS:
1. Master Mix Preparation: Dispense 5 uL RNA/DNA sample, 6.25 uL RNase-free water, 12.5 uL 2x One Step Q Probe Mix, and 1.25 uL One Step Q Probe Enzyme Mix; combine sequentially into a single 25 uL RT-qPCR amplification master mix.
2. Droplet Splitting to Reaction Spots: Transport and split the master mix (2 uL per spot) onto each of the 12 on-chip reaction spots, rehydrating the pre-stored dried primer-probe set at each spot to form 12 independent reaction mixtures (one per pathogen target).
3. Reverse Transcription: Heat each of the 12 reaction mixtures at 50 C for 15 min to reverse-transcribe viral/bacterial RNA into cDNA.
4. Initial Denaturation: Heat each of the 12 reaction mixtures at 95 C for 30 s.
5. Thermal Cycling (Amplification): For each of the 12 reaction mixtures independently, cycle 45 times through 95 C for 10 s (denaturation) then 60 C for 30 s (annealing/extension), with real-time fluorescence acquisition during the anneal/extend step of each cycle.
6. Detection: Acquire the real-time fluorescence signal (delta Rn) from each of the 12 reaction spots over the amplification run; a Ct value is computed per spot from the cycle at which fluorescence crosses ten times the standard deviation above the mean baseline (cycles 3-15), and each spot's reading is compared against its corresponding detection-limit threshold to call the sample positive or negative for that target.
7. Disposal: Dispose of each of the 12 analyzed reaction droplets after the amplification/detection run completes.

INTERPRETATION: Successful multiplex detection is confirmed by pathogen-specific amplification curves crossing threshold within 45 cycles for true positives, no amplification (or amplification only after 45 cycles) for true negatives, and reported diagnostic performance (versus off-chip benchtop RT-qPCR) of TPR 93.33%, TNR 100%, PPV 100%, NPV 99.56%, ACC 99.85% (on the plasmid/clinical validation panel), and a Kappa value of 0.963, supporting use of the DMF RT-qPCR platform for field and point-of-care respiratory pathogen screening in medical resource-limited settings.

module fluorescence

manifest RNA_Sample
manifest RNase_Free_Water
manifest OneStep_Q_Probe_Mix
manifest OneStep_Q_Probe_Enzyme_Mix
manifest MP_Primer_Probe
manifest CP_Primer_Probe
manifest SP_Primer_Probe
manifest RSVA_Primer_Probe
manifest ADV_Primer_Probe
manifest HKU1_Primer_Probe
manifest E229_Primer_Probe
manifest HMPV_Primer_Probe
manifest N_Primer_Probe
manifest ORF1ab_Primer_Probe
manifest FLUA_Primer_Probe
manifest FLUB_Primer_Probe

instructions:

// ---- Prepare common RT-qPCR amplification master mix ----
// 5uL RNA, 6.25uL water, 12.5uL 2x Probe Mix, 1.25uL Probe Enzyme Mix (25uL total)
rna = dispense 5 units of RNA_Sample
water = dispense 6 units of RNase_Free_Water
probemix = dispense 13 units of OneStep_Q_Probe_Mix
enzymemix = dispense 1 units of OneStep_Q_Probe_Enzyme_Mix

mix1 = mix rna with water
mix2 = mix mix1 with probemix
master_mix = mix mix2 with enzymemix

// ---- Split master mix into the 12 reaction spots pre-loaded with dried primer/probe sets ----

mp_probe = dispense MP_Primer_Probe
mp_mix = mix master_mix with mp_probe

cp_probe = dispense CP_Primer_Probe
cp_mix = mix master_mix with cp_probe

sp_probe = dispense SP_Primer_Probe
sp_mix = mix master_mix with sp_probe

rsva_probe = dispense RSVA_Primer_Probe
rsva_mix = mix master_mix with rsva_probe

adv_probe = dispense ADV_Primer_Probe
adv_mix = mix master_mix with adv_probe

hku1_probe = dispense HKU1_Primer_Probe
hku1_mix = mix master_mix with hku1_probe

e229_probe = dispense E229_Primer_Probe
e229_mix = mix master_mix with e229_probe

hmpv_mix = mix master_mix with hmpv_probe

n_mix = mix master_mix with n_probe

orf1ab_mix = mix master_mix with orf1ab_probe

flua_probe = dispense FLUA_Primer_Probe
flua_mix = mix master_mix with flua_probe

flub_probe = dispense FLUB_Primer_Probe
flub_mix = mix master_mix with flub_probe

// ---- Reverse transcription step: 50C for 15m ----
heat mp_mix at 50c for 15m
heat cp_mix at 50c for 15m
heat sp_mix at 50c for 15m
heat rsva_mix at 50c for 15m
heat adv_mix at 50c for 15m
heat hku1_mix at 50c for 15m
heat e229_mix at 50c for 15m
heat hmpv_mix at 50c for 15m
heat n_mix at 50c for 15m
heat orf1ab_mix at 50c for 15m
heat flua_mix at 50c for 15m
heat flub_mix at 50c for 15m

// ---- Initial denaturation: 95C for 30s ----
heat mp_mix at 95c for 30s
heat cp_mix at 95c for 30s
heat sp_mix at 95c for 30s
heat rsva_mix at 95c for 30s
heat adv_mix at 95c for 30s
heat hku1_mix at 95c for 30s
heat e229_mix at 95c for 30s
heat hmpv_mix at 95c for 30s
heat n_mix at 95c for 30s
heat orf1ab_mix at 95c for 30s
heat flua_mix at 95c for 30s
heat flub_mix at 95c for 30s

// ---- 45 cycles of 95C 10s / 60C 30s amplification for each reaction spot ----
repeat 45 times {
    heat mp_mix at 95c for 10s
    heat mp_mix at 60c for 30s
}

repeat 45 times {
    heat cp_mix at 95c for 10s
    heat cp_mix at 60c for 30s
}

repeat 45 times {
    heat sp_mix at 95c for 10s
    heat sp_mix at 60c for 30s
}

repeat 45 times {
    heat rsva_mix at 95c for 10s
    heat rsva_mix at 60c for 30s
}

repeat 45 times {
    heat adv_mix at 95c for 10s
    heat adv_mix at 60c for 30s
}

repeat 45 times {
    heat hku1_mix at 95c for 10s
    heat hku1_mix at 60c for 30s
}

repeat 45 times {
    heat e229_mix at 95c for 10s
    heat e229_mix at 60c for 30s
}

repeat 45 times {
    heat hmpv_mix at 95c for 10s
    heat hmpv_mix at 60c for 30s
}

repeat 45 times {
    heat n_mix at 95c for 10s
    heat n_mix at 60c for 30s
}

repeat 45 times {
    heat orf1ab_mix at 95c for 10s
    heat orf1ab_mix at 60c for 30s
}

repeat 45 times {
    heat flua_mix at 95c for 10s
    heat flua_mix at 60c for 30s
}

repeat 45 times {
    heat flub_mix at 95c for 10s
    heat flub_mix at 60c for 30s
}

// ---- Real-time fluorescence detection on each reaction spot ----
mp_result = detect fluorescence on mp_mix for 10s
cp_result = detect fluorescence on cp_mix for 10s
sp_result = detect fluorescence on sp_mix for 10s
rsva_result = detect fluorescence on rsva_mix for 10s
adv_result = detect fluorescence on adv_mix for 10s
hku1_result = detect fluorescence on hku1_mix for 10s
e229_result = detect fluorescence on e229_mix for 10s
hmpv_result = detect fluorescence on hmpv_mix for 10s
n_result = detect fluorescence on n_mix for 10s
orf1ab_result = detect fluorescence on orf1ab_mix for 10s
flua_result = detect fluorescence on flua_mix for 10s
flub_result = detect fluorescence on flub_mix for 10s

// ---- Threshold-based positive/negative calls (Ct-based cutoff, illustrative threshold) ----
if (mp_result >= 100) {
    dispose mp_mix
}

if (cp_result >= 100) {
    dispose cp_mix
}

if (sp_result >= 100) {
    dispose sp_mix
}

if (rsva_result >= 100) {
    dispose rsva_mix
}

if (adv_result >= 100) {
    dispose adv_mix
}

if (hku1_result >= 100) {
    dispose hku1_mix
}

if (e229_result >= 100) {
    dispose e229_mix
}

if (hmpv_result >= 100) {
    dispose hmpv_mix
}

if (n_result >= 100) {
    dispose n_mix
}

if (orf1ab_result >= 100) {
    dispose orf1ab_mix
}

if (flua_result >= 100) {
    dispose flua_mix
}

if (flub_result >= 100) {
    dispose flub_mix
}

dispose mp_mix
dispose cp_mix
dispose sp_mix
dispose rsva_mix
dispose adv_mix
dispose hku1_mix
dispose e229_mix
dispose hmpv_mix
dispose n_mix
dispose orf1ab_mix

Overview: A multi-target RT-qPCR assay protocol executed on a digital microfluidic platform capable of simultaneously dispensing, merging, and amplifying samples to identify up to 11 pathogens from single specimens.

REAGENTS USED:
  - Extracted RNA/DNA Sample (nasal or throat swab nucleic acid extract, 5 uL)
  - RNase-Free Water (6.25 uL)
  - 2x One Step Q Probe Mix (RT-qPCR master mix component, 12.5 uL)
  - One Step Q Probe Enzyme Mix (reverse transcriptase/polymerase enzyme mix, 1.25 uL)
  - 12 Dried Primer-Probe Sets, pre-stored and dehydrated at individual reaction spots on-chip, one per target: MP, CP, SP, RSVA, ADV, HKU1, 229E, HMPV, N (SARS-CoV-2), ORF1ab (SARS-CoV-2), FLUA, FLUB

STEPS:
1. Master Mix Preparation: Dispense 5 uL RNA/DNA sample, 6.25 uL RNase-free water, 12.5 uL 2x One Step Q Probe Mix, and 1.25 uL One Step Q Probe Enzyme Mix; combine sequentially into a single 25 uL RT-qPCR amplification master mix.
2. Droplet Splitting to Reaction Spots: Transport and split the master mix (2 uL per spot) onto each of the 12 on-chip reaction spots, rehydrating the pre-stored dried primer-probe set at each spot to form 12 independent reaction mixtures (one per pathogen target).
3. Reverse Transcription: Heat each of the 12 reaction mixtures at 50 C for 15 min to reverse-transcribe viral/bacterial RNA into cDNA.
4. Initial Denaturation: Heat each of the 12 reaction mixtures at 95 C for 30 s.
5. Thermal Cycling (Amplification): For each of the 12 reaction mixtures independently, cycle 45 times through 95 C for 10 s (denaturation) then 60 C for 30 s (annealing/extension), with real-time fluorescence acquisition during the anneal/extend step of each cycle.
6. Detection: Acquire the real-time fluorescence signal (delta Rn) from each of the 12 reaction spots over the amplification run; a Ct value is computed per spot from the cycle at which fluorescence crosses ten times the standard deviation above the mean baseline (cycles 3-15), and each spot's reading is compared against its corresponding detection-limit threshold to call the sample positive or negative for that target.
7. Disposal: Dispose of each of the 12 analyzed reaction droplets after the amplification/detection run completes.

INTERPRETATION: Successful multiplex detection is confirmed by pathogen-specific amplification curves crossing threshold within 45 cycles for true positives, no amplification (or amplification only after 45 cycles) for true negatives, and reported diagnostic performance (versus off-chip benchtop RT-qPCR) of TPR 93.33%, TNR 100%, PPV 100%, NPV 99.56%, ACC 99.85% (on the plasmid/clinical validation panel), and a Kappa value of 0.963, supporting use of the DMF RT-qPCR platform for field and point-of-care respiratory pathogen screening in medical resource-limited settings.

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic (DMF) Platform for Chemiluminescent Detection of Rubella Virus (RV) IgG and IgM by Indirect ELISA

REAGENTS USED:
  - RV-Coated Paramagnetic Particle Suspension (virus-immobilized magnetic microparticles for antigen capture, 1.8 uL droplets)
  - Patient Sample (serum or plasma, pre-diluted, containing RV IgG and/or RV IgM, 1.8 uL droplets)
  - DMF-Compatible Wash Buffer (1.8 uL droplets, used in 4x wash cycles after each binding step)
  - HRP-Conjugated Goat Anti-Human IgG (detection conjugate for the RV IgG assay, 1.8 uL droplets)
  - HRP-Conjugated Goat Anti-Human IgM (detection conjugate for the RV IgM assay, 1.8 uL droplets)
  - Goat Anti-Human IgG Pretreatment Reagent (blocks endogenous RV IgG/rheumatoid-factor IgM interference before the IgM assay, 0.9 uL droplets)
  - Hydrogen Peroxide, H2O2 (chemiluminescent substrate component, 0.9 uL droplets)
  - Luminol-Enhancer Solution (chemiluminescent substrate component, 0.9 uL droplets)

STEPS:

RV IgG Immunoassay (7-step indirect ELISA):
1. Dispense a droplet of RV-coated paramagnetic particle suspension (1.8 uL) and separate the particles from the storage diluent.
2. Dispense a sample droplet (1.8 uL), deliver it to the particles, mix for 3 min, then magnetically separate particles from the supernatant.
3. Wash the particles in 4 successive 1.8 uL wash-buffer droplets, mixing and then separating from the supernatant each time.
4. Dispense a droplet of HRP-conjugated anti-human IgG (1.8 uL), deliver to the particles, and mix for 2 min.
5. Repeat the 4x wash cycle from step 3.
6. Dispense one droplet each of H2O2 (0.9 uL) and luminol-enhancer solution (0.9 uL), merge them with the particles, and mix for 2 min.
7. Measure the mean chemiluminescent signal over 10 s with the integrated photomultiplier tube (PMT).

RV IgM Immunoassay (identical 7-step assay, preceded by an IgG-blocking pretreatment):
0. Pretreatment: Mix a 1.8 uL sample droplet with a 0.9 uL droplet of goat anti-human IgG pretreatment reagent for 7 min to block endogenous RV IgG and rheumatoid-factor IgM before analysis.
1-7. Repeat the same capture -> 4x wash -> conjugate (HRP-anti-human IgM in place of anti-IgG) -> 4x wash -> substrate -> PMT-detect sequence described above.

INTERPRETATION: Results are reported as a signal-to-cutoff (s/co) ratio, calculated by normalizing the mean chemiluminescent signal of each assay to the mean signal of the corresponding cutoff control (a 10 IU/mL RV IgG calibrator for the IgG assay; the RV IgM cutoff Cal 1 reagent for the IgM assay). An s/co >= 1 is interpreted as positive; an s/co in the gray zone (0.69-0.99 for IgG, 0.75-0.99 for IgM) is interpreted as equivocal; an s/co below the gray zone is interpreted as negative. Diagnostic sensitivity and specificity of 100%/100% for both RV IgG and RV IgM were obtained against a commercial mixed-titer performance panel referenced against an Abbott EIA platform, supporting use of the method as a portable, decentralized alternative to central-laboratory rubella serology for identifying pregnant women at risk of transmitting rubella to their offspring.

instructions:

particles_igg = dispense 18 units of rv_particles
sample_igg = dispense 18 units of patient_sample
capture_igg = mix particles_igg with sample_igg for 3m

repeat 4 times {
    wash_igg = dispense 18 units of wash_buffer
    capture_igg = mix capture_igg with wash_igg for 30s
    dispose wash_igg

if (igg_signal >= 10) {

    dispose rxn_igg

Source link: https://www.mdpi.com/2072-666X/13/2/196/pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.3390/mi13020196

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic qPCR Cartridge Protocol for Viral Detection (SARS-CoV-2)

REAGENTS USED:
  - cDNA template of the SARS-CoV-2 N gene (SARS-CoV-2 RUO plasmid control, ten-fold serial dilutions from 10,000 to 1 copy/uL)
  - N1 primer-probe mix (U.S. CDC-referenced, IDT)
  - N2 primer-probe mix (U.S. CDC-referenced, IDT)
  - RNase P (RP) primer-probe mix (human internal control gene)
  - TaqMan Fast Advanced Master Mix (2X, Applied Biosystems)
  - Nuclease-free water (diluent, and NTC substitute for template)
  - Positive control template
  - Hexadecane (environmental oil filling the cartridge to prevent droplet evaporation and reduce friction)
  - Tween-20 surfactant (0.1% final concentration in aqueous reagents, reduces surface tension/biofouling)

STEPS:
1. Reaction assembly: On the DMF cartridge, generate a 1.5 uL droplet-scale reaction for each of five parallel tracks/reservoirs (N1, N2, RP, positive control, NTC) by combining 1 uL cDNA template (or nuclease-free water for the NTC), 1.5 uL primer-probe mix, 10 uL TaqMan Fast Advanced Master Mix, and 7.5 uL nuclease-free water (20 uL bulk reaction mix, scaled down on-chip).
2. Enzyme activation: Heat each reaction droplet at 95 C for 2 min (1 cycle) to activate the polymerase.
3. Thermal cycling (40 cycles): For each cycle, denature at 95 C for 1 s, then anneal/extend at 60 C for 20 s, with droplets electrowetting-actuated between the two on-chip temperature zones (~1.75 C/s ramp rate, ~42 min total for 40 cycles).
4. Real-time fluorescence detection: After every thermal cycle, capture the FAM fluorescence intensity of each droplet using the optical module (camera, fluorescence filter cube, LED) to build real-time amplification curves.
5. Data analysis / dispose: Subtract baseline intensity to obtain delta fluorescence intensity (dFI), determine threshold cycle (Ct) values via LinRegPCR, and evaluate qPCR efficiency from the Ct-vs-log(concentration) standard curve; discard analyzed droplets once data collection is complete.

INTERPRETATION: Successful SARS-CoV-2 N gene detection is confirmed by sigmoidal amplification curves resembling standard benchtop qPCR, a limit of detection down to 10 copies/uL (15 copies/droplet) for both N1 and N2 target regions, and standard-curve qPCR efficiencies within the acceptable 90-110% range (92.8% for N1, 101.2% for N2), supporting use of the DMF cartridge as a point-of-care NAAT platform for COVID-19 diagnosis.
