mixa_n1 = mix template_n1 with pp_n1
mixb_n1 = mix mixa_n1 with mm_n1
N1_mix = mix mixb_n1 with water_n1

template_n2 = dispense 1 units of cDNA_template
pp_n2 = dispense 2 units of primer_probe_N2
mm_n2 = dispense 10 units of master_mix
water_n2 = dispense 8 units of nuclease_free_water

mixa_n2 = mix template_n2 with pp_n2
mixb_n2 = mix mixa_n2 with mm_n2
N2_mix = mix mixb_n2 with water_n2

template_rp = dispense 1 units of cDNA_template
pp_rp = dispense 2 units of primer_probe_RP
mm_rp = dispense 10 units of master_mix
water_rp = dispense 8 units of nuclease_free_water

mixa_rp = mix template_rp with pp_rp
mixb_rp = mix mixa_rp with mm_rp
RP_mix = mix mixb_rp with water_rp

pos = dispense 1 units of positive_control
pp_pos = dispense 2 units of primer_probe_N1
mm_pos = dispense 10 units of master_mix
water_pos = dispense 8 units of nuclease_free_water

mixa_pos = mix pos with pp_pos
mixb_pos = mix mixa_pos with mm_pos
PC_mix = mix mixb_pos with water_pos

ntc = dispense 1 units of ntc_sample
pp_ntc = dispense 2 units of primer_probe_N1
mm_ntc = dispense 10 units of master_mix
water_ntc = dispense 8 units of nuclease_free_water

mixa_ntc = mix ntc with pp_ntc
mixb_ntc = mix mixa_ntc with mm_ntc
NTC_mix = mix mixb_ntc with water_ntc

heat N1_mix at 95c for 2m
heat N2_mix at 95c for 2m
heat RP_mix at 95c for 2m
heat PC_mix at 95c for 2m
heat NTC_mix at 95c for 2m

repeat 40 times {
    heat N1_mix at 95c for 1s
    heat N1_mix at 60c for 20s
    N1_signal = detect fluorescence on N1_mix for 1s

    heat N2_mix at 95c for 1s
    heat N2_mix at 60c for 20s
    N2_signal = detect fluorescence on N2_mix for 1s

    heat RP_mix at 95c for 1s
    heat RP_mix at 60c for 20s
    RP_signal = detect fluorescence on RP_mix for 1s

    heat PC_mix at 95c for 1s
    heat PC_mix at 60c for 20s
    PC_signal = detect fluorescence on PC_mix for 1s

    heat NTC_mix at 95c for 1s
    heat NTC_mix at 60c for 20s
    NTC_signal = detect fluorescence on NTC_mix for 1s
}

if (N1_signal >= 40000) {
    dispose N1_mix
}

if (N2_signal >= 40000) {
    dispose N2_mix
}

if (NTC_signal >= 8000) {
    dispose NTC_mix
}

dispose RP_mix
dispose PC_mix

metadata.protocol_name: Digital Microfluidic qPCR Cartridge for SARS-CoV-2 Detection (Ho et al. 2022)

sources.title: Digital Microfluidic qPCR Cartridge for SARS-CoV-2 Detection

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code is a direct translation of the paper's on-chip qPCR procedure (Sections 2.2 'Sample Preparation' and 2.6 'On-Chip qPCR Procedure of SARS-CoV-2 N Gene'), modeling the five parallel reservoirs/tracks (N1, N2, RP, positive control, NTC) described in the Discussion section, the 95C/2min enzyme activation, the 40-cycle 95C-1s/60C-20s thermal profile, per-cycle fluorescence detection matching the real-time optical module (Section 2.4), and threshold-based dispose logic standing in for the paper's Ct/deltaFI-based positive/negative call (Section 2.7). This script was compiled with the lilott8/BioScript compiler and produced a valid IR (with correctly phi-noded loop and if/else basic blocks for the 40-cycle repeat and the three threshold checks) and a valid control-flow DAG (.dot), confirming syntactic and structural correctness.

chemical_evidence.source_quote: the N gene cDNA template (SARS-CoV-2 RUO plasmid controls) of SARS-CoV-2 with a stock concentration of 200,000 copies/uL
The qPCR primer-probe mix for N1 and N2 referring to the U.S. CDC were from IDT
The TaqMan Fast Advanced Master Mix (2X) for two-step qPCR
1.5 uL primer-probe mix, 10 uL of DNA master mix, and 7.5 uL nuclease-free water
a human RNase P gene (RP) control, a positive control, and a no template control (NTC) altogether on the same DMF qPCR cartridge

operation_evidence.bs_operation: template/pp/mm/water dispense + mix chain per track
operation_evidence.source_quote: we prepared a 20 uL reaction mix that contained 1 uL cDNA template of varied concentration, 1.5 uL primer-probe mix, 10 uL of DNA master mix, and 7.5 uL nuclease-free water

operation_evidence.bs_operation: heat ..._mix at 95c for 2m
operation_evidence.source_quote: 1 cycle of enzyme activation at 95C for 2 min

operation_evidence.bs_operation: repeat 40 times { heat 95c 1s, heat 60c 20s, detect fluorescence }
operation_evidence.source_quote: followed by 40 cycles of a thermal profile of 1 s at 95C for denaturation, and 20 s at 60C for annealing and extension

operation_evidence.bs_operation: N1_signal/N2_signal/... = detect fluorescence on ..._mix for 1s
operation_evidence.source_quote: the optical module automatically recorded the fluorescence after each cycle, which enabled real-time analysis

operation_evidence.bs_operation: if (...signal >= threshold) { dispose ...mix }
operation_evidence.source_quote: By expressing dFI on the logarithmic scale, the threshold cycle (Ct) was determined for quantification analysis

numeric_mismatches.note: BioScript's dispense grammar in the reference examples only uses integer unit counts, so the paper's exact 1 uL / 1.5 uL / 10 uL / 7.5 uL reaction volumes are approximated as 1/2/10/8 integer units rather than exact fractional microliter amounts.

The paper calls positives via Ct value derived from log-scale deltaFI and LinRegPCR baseline/threshold fitting, not a single-timepoint raw fluorescence-intensity cutoff. BioScript exposes only scalar comparison operators in its if-statement, so a plausible raw-intensity threshold (drawn from the ~7500-50000 a.u. range seen in Figure 3b) is used as a stand-in for the paper's Ct-based quantification logic.

The paper's thermal cycling is physically implemented by driving the droplet back and forth between two fixed-temperature zones on the cartridge (~1.75C/s effective ramp via droplet speed), not by ramping a single heater. BioScript has no droplet-transport/actuation primitive distinct from 'heat', so the zone-shuttling mechanism is represented simply as sequential 'heat at Tc' calls.

numeric_mismatches.field: droplet volume consistency / temperature uniformity / fluorescence linearity characterization (Figures 2 and 3)
numeric_mismatches.note: Not modeled. These are hardware/instrument characterization experiments (electric, thermal, and optical module validation) run separately from the N1/N2 qPCR assay itself, and fall outside the scope of this translation.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : One Cell, One Drop, One Click: Hybrid Microfluidics for Mammalian Single Cell Isolation
Source Link  : https://www.shihmicrolab.ca/_files/ugd/f0a828_20644bba5a194fc0966d7bba24bbc451.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1002/smll.202002400
Journal      : Small, 2020, Vol. 16, Article 2002400
Platform     : Hybrid DMF (digital microfluidics + droplet-in-channel microfluidics) on EWOD/electrode array


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a hybrid microfluidics method for deterministic single-cell isolation,
encapsulation, on-demand droplet manipulation, and isoclonal recovery for mammalian gene-editing
workflows. The device integrates a bottom digital microfluidic (DMF) layer (chromium co-planar
electrodes on glass + 7 um SU-8 5 dielectric) with a top PDMS channel layer (35 um height,
50-75 um width), enabling individual electrode-addressable control of droplets flowing inside
microfluidic channels -- a configuration referred to as "hybrid" microfluidics.

The protocol is divided into four functional phases:
  1. Hydrodynamic single-cell trapping in serpentine channel traps (8 um constrictions)
  2. In situ deterministic single-cell encapsulation by phase change (no Poisson statistics)
  3. On-demand droplet operations: forward/reverse release, keep, on-demand generation, and merge
  4. CRISPR-Cas9 gene-editing pipeline: transfection, on-chip fluorescence screening,
     isoclone sorting, capillary recovery, and clonal expansion in a 96-well plate

The complete trap-to-recovery workflow takes approximately 45 minutes, compared to hours
or days required by standard FACS or limited dilution methods.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Layer i   : Chromium electrodes patterned on glass (50 x 75 mm); electrode size ~100 um,
            area 0.06 mm2; co-planar ground and activated electrodes on same plate.
Layer ii  : SU-8 5 dielectric, 7 um thick; spin-coated and hard-baked to 180 C.
Layer iii : PDMS channel layer; channel height 35 um, main channel width 50 um,
            bypass channel width ~50 um; fabricated by soft lithography on SU-8 2035 master.

Device sections:
  - T-junction on-demand droplet generator (2 T-junctions, multiple sub-electrodes)
  - Serpentine single-cell trapping array: 12 traps total, 6 electrode-equipped;
    each trap has 4 co-planar electrodes (2 below main channel, 2 below trap)

Inlets  : I1 (oil + droplets), I2 (cells + priming), I3 (PBS/media for generator),
          I4 (HFE7500 for generator)
Outlets : O1 (waste), O2 (sample recovery / flow reversal), O3 (bridge to encapsulation)

Actuation: 15 kHz AC, 126 Vrms applied via optocoupler switches controlled through
           an in-house Python-based GUI automation framework.


CELL LINES
----------
- MCF-7 (human breast cancer): model cell line for trapping, encapsulation, and viability assays.
  Cultured in DMEM + 10% FBS, no antibiotics, 37 C, 5% CO2.
- NCI-H1299 (human lung squamous cell carcinoma, eGFP+/Luciferase dual-labelled stable line):
  used for gene-editing, isoclone sorting, and expansion.
  Cultured in RPMI-1640 + 10% FBS, no antibiotics, 37 C, 5% CO2.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Device Priming
  Reagents : PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free), Pluronics F-127
  Mix      : 2% Pluronics F-127 in PBS
  Duration : 5 min at 0.8-8 nL/s via inlet I1
  Purpose  : Reduces MCF-7 cell adhesion to PDMS channel walls.

Step 2 | Hydrodynamic Single-Cell Trapping
  Cell line      : MCF-7
  Concentration  : 1e5-1e6 cells/mL in PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free), stirred continuously in syringe
  Flow rate      : 1-4 nL/s (optimal); 5 nL/s tested at ~88.3% single-cell efficiency
  Trap design    : 8 um constriction (smaller than MCF-7 cell diameter); positioned at
                   curvature of serpentine channel so Qtrap > Qbypass when trap is empty.
                   Slanted overhang along main channel steers flow into trap.
  Multi-occupancy: >54 consecutive single-cell events confirmed; second cell does not enter
                   occupied trap (increased Rtrap reduces Qtrap).
  Filtering      : Cells passed through 40 um cell strainer before loading to remove clumps.

Step 3 | In Situ Deterministic Single-Cell Encapsulation
  Method         : Phase change from single-phase (aqueous) to two-phase (water-in-oil) flow.
  Oil            : HFE7500 + 2% w/v PEG fluoro-surfactant (Ran Biotechnologies), 4 nL/s
  Electrode      : 15 kHz, 126 Vrms; electric field density ~5x10^6 V/m between main channel
                   and trap; electrostatic force pulls aqueous phase into trap when oil shears.
  Droplet volume : 150.3 +/- 5.6 pL (N=11); monodisperse, no Poisson-based encapsulation.
  Frame sequence : Frame I: trap electrode activated, oil enters main channel.
                   Frame II: trap electrode active, other electrodes grounded; oil cuts aqueous
                             phase at both trap ends; cell remains inside.
                   Frame III: all potentials grounded; oil continues to next trap.

Step 4 | On-Demand Droplet Operations
  Forward release : Actuate electrodes below trap then main channel (15 kHz, 126 Vrms).
                    Flow rate <1 nL/s → >95% release probability.
                    Without actuation: droplet never released at any flow rate.
  Reverse release : Same actuation sequence under reverse oil flow.
                    Hydrodynamic only: >10.92 nL/s needed; with actuation: 100% at any rate.
  Keep            : 4 electrodes activated; field centred at trap opening.
                    Flow rates <45.4 nL/s → >95% keep probability (Ph < Felec).
                    Above 45.4 nL/s: Ph > Felec; droplet escapes.
  On-demand gen.  : T-junction; oil 2-2.5 nL/s, aqueous 0.6 nL/s; 15 kHz 126 Vrms.
                    Droplet volume 250.9 +/- 39 pL.
  Merge           : Incoming droplets merged with trapped droplets on demand; no stream
                    synchronisation required.

Step 5 | Cell Viability Assay
  Cells          : MCF-7 (fresh trap), PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free)
  Actuation      : 15 kHz, 126 Vrms for 30 s total (two top electrodes 10 s each,
                   ground electrode 10 s, two bottom electrodes 10 s)
  Stain          : FDA/PI 1X; 10 uL PI stock (2 ug/mL) + 2.5 uL FDA stock (5 ug/mL)
                   FDA: ex 490 nm / em 526 nm (live cells, green)
                   PI : ex 488 nm / em 617 nm (dead cells, red)
  Incubation     : 10 min on device in dark; imaged at 4x or 10x on inverted fluorescence
                   microscope (Olympus IX73)
  Results        : Control 87.5 +/- 7.2% viability; potentiated 82.5 +/- 8.1% viability
                   (p = 0.6687, unpaired t-test, N=3). No significant difference.
                   ~18% loss attributed to pre-processing handling outside culture environment.

Step 6 | Off-Chip CRISPR-Cas9 Transfection (eGFP KO arm)
  Cell line      : NCI-H1299 (eGFP+/Luciferase stable)
  Plasmid        : pCRISPR_eGFP_314 (Cas9 + mCherry reporter + eGFP sgRNA)
                   eGFP sgRNA sequence: GCAACTACAAGACCCGCGCCG
  Reagent        : Lipofectamine 3000, 5 ug DNA/well
  Format         : 24-well plate; Day 0: subculture; Day 1: transfect; Day 3: harvest
  Incubation     : 48 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 (= 2880 min = 172800 s)
  Results        : ~25.3% transfection efficiency (mCherry+); ~4.95% KO efficiency (GCD assay)
  KO confirm     : Genomic Cleavage Detection assay (GeneArt GCD kit, Thermo Scientific);
                   ~500 bp PCR fragments re-annealed and cleaved; resolved on 2% LAB gel at 220 V.
  Note           : RAF1 KO is an independent parallel experiment (pCRISPR_RAF1_94;
                   RAF1 sgRNA: GCCGCCCGAGAGTCTTAATCG; 13.7% transfection, 8.3% KO efficiency).

Step 7 | On-Chip Isoclone Trapping, Screening, and Encapsulation
  Cells          : Transfected NCI-H1299, resuspended in PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free)
  Trapping rate  : 4 nL/s
  Screening      : Fluorescence microscopy
                   mCherry (ex ~565 nm): positive = successful transfection
                   eGFP   (ex ~460 nm): loss of signal = eGFP knocked out
  Expected hits  : ~1 in 6 traps (~16.7%) contain a mCherry+ isoclone
  Re-trapping    : If trap contains no transfected clone, increase forward flow rate to
                   squeeze cell through trap and load a new cell iteratively.
  Encapsulation  : HFE7500 + 2% fluorosurfactant at 4 nL/s; 15 kHz, 126 Vrms
  Detection      : mCherryGFPDetection module; 30 s fluorescence read
  Sorting        : Positive clone released on-demand toward outlet (forward release)
  Total time     : ~45 min from trapping to release

Step 8 | Isoclone Recovery and Clonal Expansion
  Recovery method:
    1. Positive droplet forward-released on demand to outlet
    2. Loaded into glass capillary pre-filled with HFE7500 2% fluorosurfactant
    3. Capillary tip placed onto 20 uL conditioned media on hydrophobic PTFE membrane
       (0.22 um) on custom 3D-printed holder at 37 C
    4. Capillary flushed with 10 uL FC-40 oil; oil absorbs HFE7500, releasing aqueous droplet
    5. 1 min incubation; isoclone released into conditioned media droplet
    6. Transferred to 96-well plate with 50 uL conditioned media/well at 37 C

  Conditioned media: 50% RPMI-1640 10% FBS 1% pen/strep collected from 1-day 80%-confluent
                     H1299 cells + 50% fresh complete growth media; filter-sterilised; -80 C storage.
  Expansion        : 37 C, 5% CO2; 7 days (= 10080 min = 604800 s)
                     Day 1   : Single adherent clones visible
                     Day 2-3 : mCherry reporter lost (transient transfection, plasmid diluted)
                     Day 5   : Image eGFP-negative clones (460 nm channel)
                     Day 7   : Confirm clonal expansion; media changed with fresh complete media
  Format           : 96-well plate; expand to 50% confluency


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : samlali_hybrid_microfluidics_isoclone.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
DAG            : samlali_hybrid_microfluidics_isoclone_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations converted to minutes (m) for compiler compatibility
                 (BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported)
                 48h  -> 2880m  (transfection incubation; IR: 172800.0 SECOND)
                 168h -> 10080m (expansion; IR: 604800.0 SECOND)
Modules        : viabilityDetection, dropletReleaseDetection,
                 mCherryGFPDetection, genomicCleavageDetection
Biological scope note: This .bs file encodes the eGFP KO arm only.
                 The RAF1 KO arm requires a separate .bs file with Cas9_RAF1_sgRNA_Plasmid.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : A Droplet-Based Screen for Wavelength-Dependent Lipid Production in Algae
Source Link  : https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Steve-Shih/publication/262874413_A_droplet-based_screen_for_wavelength-dependent_lipid_production_in_algae/links/00b7d53909cf950ec1000000/A-droplet-based-screen-for-wavelength-dependent-lipid-production-in-algae.pdf?__cf_chl_f_tk=N2GSHFBauUsIm5B8xwZxkkXn_LuBAACs9pC5GteCtAg-1782901072-1.0.1.1-e0TB_oLJRbhpUUI8lmO01R0_1wpK5AF10F3ILeZ6Fv4
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1039/c4ee01123f
Journal      : Energy & Environmental Science, 2014, DOI: 10.1039/c4ee01123f
Platform     : Digital microfluidics (DMF) on open electrode array with custom LED illumination


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes the first microfluidic method applied to discovery of algae culture
conditions favourable for generating high-energy lipids. The platform uses digital microfluidics
(DMF) — where droplets are manipulated on an open electrode array by application of electric
fields — to perform automated, multiplexed long-term culture and analysis of Cyclotella cryptica
(CCMP 332), a diatom widely used as a model organism for biofuel lipid research.

The protocol is divided into three functional phases:
  1. Multicolour illumination screen: 7 LED wavelengths + dark control at two intensities,
     screening neutral lipid production and biomass accumulation simultaneously over 24 h.
  2. Blue/yellow cycling screen: 8 timed combinations of blue (~450 nm) and yellow (~580 nm)
     illumination at high intensity, identifying the optimal condition for biofuel production.
  3. ROS mechanistic assay: DCFDA fluorescence quantification of reactive oxygen species under
     yellow, blue, and ascorbate-treated conditions to elucidate the photooxidative stress
     mechanism underlying wavelength-dependent lipid accumulation.

The method reduces manual intervention from >600 pipette steps (conventional multiwell screen)
to fewer than 20, while generating equivalent or greater data density. Two pipette steps are
sufficient to run a single device for 24 h, producing 48 measurements (24 absorbance + 24
fluorescence) across 8 culture conditions at 3 time points.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Open-array DMF device; no pumps, valves, or mechanical mixers required.

Electrode layout (per device):
  - 2 four-electrode active reservoirs (algae suspension + LipidTOX dye)
  - 8 algae culture zone electrodes
  - 8 bussed dye dispensing electrodes
  - 8 absorbance detection electrodes (L-shaped, for daughter droplet routing)
  - 8 fluorescence detection electrodes
  - 8 waste reservoir electrodes with 1 mm-diameter through-holes

Dispensing: All dispenser electrode modules feature narrow central electrodes
  (>= 0.5:1 ratio relative to destination electrode) to facilitate necking during
  droplet formation; critical for reliable parallel dispensing on bussed electrodes.

Detection zones: 9 mm pitch; compatible with standard 384-well multiwell plate reader.
  Transparent windows for transmission (absorbance) and opaque-bottom wells for fluorescence.

Waste management: Spent reagents driven to waste electrodes; fluid wicks through 1 mm
  through-holes onto absorbent tissue below device after each measurement cycle.

Droplet volumes: 150 uL to 2 uL (wide range controlled by varying electrode sizes/shapes
  and bussed groupings).

Automation: Impedance sensing with feedback control over droplet position; programmed
  actuation sequences for culture, dispensing, detection, and waste routing.

Illumination: Custom LED arrays positioned below device; multicolour array (7 peak
  wavelengths: red ~625 nm, orange ~590 nm, yellow ~580 nm, green ~525 nm, blue ~450 nm,
  purple ~400 nm, white broadband) and blue/yellow dual-LED arrays for cycling experiments.
  Intensities: 50 and 250 umol/m2/s (low and high).


ORGANISM AND REAGENTS
---------------------
Organism    : Cyclotella cryptica (CCMP 332); purchased from National Center for Marine
              Algae and Microbiota (NCMA, East Boothbay, ME).
Culture     : f/2 medium (NCMA, Maine, NE) supplemented with biotin and cyanocobalamin
              (2 nM each, NCMA) and 0.02% w/v Pluronic F68; Pyrex media bottles (max 200 mL);
              20 C; 12 h white light / 12 h dark alternating cycle; weekly subculture 1:10.
              Inoculation density ~9.0e5 cells/mL (exponential phase).
On-chip     : 1.5e6 cells/mL in complete media; 150 uL loaded into algae active reservoir.
              LipidTOX working solution: 200x dilution in complete media; 120 uL loaded.

LipidTOX    : HCS LipidTOX Green neutral lipid stain (Life Technologies, Burlington, ON,
              Canada); fluorogenic reporter fluorescing in presence of neutral lipids (TAG);
              ex 488 nm / em 520 nm.

DCFDA       : DCFDA cellular reactive oxygen species detection assay kit (ab113851, Abcam,
              Cambridge, MA); reporter fluorescing in presence of ROS; ex 490 nm / em 526 nm.

Ascorbic    : 50 ug/mL ascorbic acid in complete media; antioxidant for ROS rescue arm.
acid


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Device Sterilisation and Algae Preparation (off-chip)
  Sterilise   : DMF devices incubated in 70% ethanol for 10 min prior to use.
  Algae prep  : Maintained by weekly subculture at 1:10 ratio; density confirmed by
                absorbance at 660 nm in 200 uL aliquots in clear-bottom 96-well plates
                using a plate reader. Exponential growth phase confirmed before loading.
  Absorbance  : 1 mL media aliquot (no cells) as reference; 1 mL culture aliquot measured
  spectrum    : by UV/Vis spectrophotometer (Eppendorf, Westbury, NY). C. cryptica
                absorbance maxima at blue (strong) and red (weak) wavelengths, consistent
                with primary photosynthetic pigment chlorophyll c.

Step 2 | Device Loading — Active Reservoir Initialisation
  Inputs      : Algae suspension (150 uL, 1.5e6 cells/mL) and LipidTOX solution (120 uL,
                200x stock dilution in complete media) pipetted into their respective
                active reservoirs.
  Pipette steps: 2 (only manual steps required for entire 24 h run).
  Circulation : Each active reservoir continuously circulates on its four electrodes in a
                circular mixing pattern to prevent cell settling and maintain homogeneous
                density before each dispense step. In BioScript, abstracted as a mix loop
                on the reservoir droplets prior to dispensing.

Step 3 | Culture Droplet Dispensing (Screening Step 2)
  Operation   : 8 culture droplets (12 uL each) dispensed from algae active reservoir to
                8 algae culture zone electrodes in series via bussed electrode actuation.
  Notes       : Representative single droplet lineage encoded in BioScript; hardware
                bussing handles 8 simultaneous culture droplets per device.

Step 4 | Label Droplet Dispensing (Screening Step 3)
  Operation   : ~15 uL source droplet dispensed from LipidTOX active reservoir to dye
                dispensing bus; 8 label droplets (2 uL each) formed simultaneously.
                If source volume insufficient, second source droplet dispensed from reservoir.

Step 5 | Absorbance Measurement — Cell Density (Screening Step 4)
  Operation   : 8 daughter culture droplets (2 uL each) dispensed from culture zones and
                actuated to L-shaped absorbance detection electrodes.
  Detection   : Device placed on transparent 384-well plate; PHERAstar plate reader
                (BMG Labtech, Durham, NC); 660 nm; scan matrix 15x15; scan width 3 mm;
                focal height 8.7 mm. Records cell density at each time point.
  Time points : t = 0 h (baseline), t = 6 h, t = 24 h.

Step 6 | Fluorescence Measurement — Neutral Lipid (Screening Step 5)
  Operation   : 8 daughter culture droplets merged 1:1 with 8 label droplets; incubated
                5 min for LipidTOX staining; mixed droplets driven to fluorescence
                detection electrodes.
  Detection   : Device placed on black 384-well plate; PHERAstar plate reader; 488 nm
                excitation / 520 nm emission; scan matrix 20x20; scan width 3 mm;
                focal height 8.7 mm; gain 550. Records neutral lipid content per droplet.
  Waste       : Mixed droplets driven to waste reservoirs after measurement; fluid wicks
                through 1 mm through-holes onto tissue below device.
  Time points : t = 0 h, t = 6 h, t = 24 h.
  Notes       : Screening Steps 3-5 (Steps 4-6 here) repeated after each illumination
                incubation phase (after 6 h and after 18 h additional incubation).

Step 7 | Multicolour Illumination Screen (Protocol 1)
  Conditions  : 7 LED wavelengths (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, white) +
                dark control; low (50 umol/m2/s) and high (250 umol/m2/s) intensity.
                All LEDs on continuously for 24 h; n=3 devices per condition.
  Schedule    : Load device (Step 2) → dispense and measure t=0 (Steps 3-6) →
                6 h illumination → repeat Steps 3-6 (t=6h) →
                18 h illumination → repeat Steps 3-6 (t=24h).
  Key finding : Yellow LEDs (~580 nm) produce the highest neutral lipid accumulation
                per cell (>2x vs. dark control) at high intensity (Fig. 3d/f).
                Blue LEDs (~450 nm) produce the highest biomass growth rate (Fig. 3b).
                First report of culture wavelength dependence of algal neutral lipid
                production; mechanism correlates with oxidative stress (see Step 9).
  QC gate     : absorbSignal1 > 0 → fluorescence measurement (BB2/pass);
                absorbSignal1 <= 0 → drain culture droplet (BB3/fail).

Step 8 | Blue/Yellow Cycling Screen (Protocol 2)
  Conditions  : 8 timed combinations of blue (~450 nm) and yellow (~580 nm) LEDs at
                high intensity (250 umol/m2/s), 24 h total; n=3 devices per condition.
                Combinations (h blue / h yellow): 24/0, 0/24, 1/23, 3/21, 6/18,
                12/12, 15/9, 20/4.
  Schedule    : Blue phase (900m = 15h) → measure t=15h → yellow phase (540m = 9h)
                → measure t=24h. Baseline t=0h measured before illumination.
  Optimal     : 15h blue / 9h yellow → ~4-fold lipid increase vs. dark control;
  condition   : ~2-fold vs. yellow or blue alone (Fig. 4b). Growth rates remain high
                (above any single colour other than blue) due to blue phase proliferation.
  Macroscale  : Best condition (15h blue / 9h yellow), 24h yellow, and 24h blue validated
  validation  : in 200 mL Pyrex flasks (n=5). Trends identical to DMF microscale (Fig. 4c/d).
                Confirms microfluidic screen hits translate to conventional-scale cultures.
  QC gate     : absorbSignal2 > 0 → fluorescence measurement (BB5/pass);
                absorbSignal2 <= 0 → drain culture droplet (BB6/fail).

Step 9 | ROS Mechanistic Assay (Protocol 3)
  Purpose     : Determine whether wavelength-dependent lipid accumulation correlates with
                reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, consistent with a photooxidative
                stress mechanism (analogous to nutrient-deprivation stress).
  Conditions  :
    Arm A     : Yellow illumination 24h — expected high ROS (positive arm).
    Arm B     : Blue illumination 24h — expected low ROS (negative control).
    Arm C     : Yellow illumination 24h + 50 ug/mL ascorbic acid — antioxidant rescue;
                expected ROS reversal to near-blue levels.
    Arm D     : Silicon deprivation (off-chip, macroscale positive control; known ROS
                inducer in C. cryptica via silicon-deficiency stress).
  DCFDA       : Algae grown at 5.0e6 cells/mL in 200 mL Pyrex flasks for >=1.5 weeks
  protocol    : under standard conditions (12h light/dark). Centrifuged 3000 rpm, 5 min;
                resuspended in 50 mL appropriate media variant. Illuminated 24h under
                assigned condition. Cells evaluated with DCFDA kit per manufacturer
                instructions: 5 mL aliquots centrifuged, washed 1x in buffer, resuspended
                in 500 uL DCFDA solution or complete media (control); incubated 37 C 30 min
                dark; centrifuged, washed, resuspended in 1x buffer. 150 uL aliquots placed
                in black-bottom 96-well plates; read at ex 490 nm / em 526 nm; n=5 per arm.
  Result      : Yellow light and silicon deprivation produce significantly higher ROS than
                blue light or normal conditions; ascorbate reverses the yellow-light ROS
                elevation (Fig. 5c). Supports hypothesis that yellow light causes
                photooxidative stress — when photosynthesis cannot keep pace with photon
                absorption, excited chlorophyll states (1Chl* and 3Chl*) form singlet-state
                oxygen (1O2*) and other ROS. Blue-light-specific antioxidant synthesis
                (xanthophyll cycle genes ZEP, VDE) may explain the wavelength specificity.
  QC gate     : rosSignalYellow > 0 → dispose all ROS arm droplets (BB8/pass);
                rosSignalYellow <= 0 → drain all ROS arm droplets (BB9/fail).


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : shih_algae_lipid_dmf_screen.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
DAG            : shih_algae_lipid_dmf_screen_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations converted to minutes (m) for compiler compatibility
                 (BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported)
                 6h   -> 360m   (first illumination phase; IR: 21600.0 SECOND)
                 18h  -> 1080m  (second illumination phase; IR: 64800.0 SECOND)
                 15h  -> 900m   (blue phase; IR: 54000.0 SECOND)
                 9h   -> 540m   (yellow phase; IR: 32400.0 SECOND)
                 24h  -> 1440m  (ROS illumination arms; IR: 86400.0 SECOND)
                 30m  -> 30m    (DCFDA incubation; IR: 1800.0 SECOND)
Modules        : absorbanceDetection, lipidTOXFluorescenceDetection,
                 rosFluorescenceDetection
Manifests      : CyclotellaCryptica, LipidTOX_Stock, DCFDA_Kit,
                 AscorbicAcid, FC_Medium, FC_Medium_NoSilicon,
                 LED_BlueArray, LED_YellowArray
Parallelism    : 8 culture droplets per condition handled via bussed electrode hardware;
                 BioScript encodes single representative droplet lineage per protocol arm.
Active         : Continuous circulation on four-electrode active reservoirs abstracted as
reservoir      : self-mix loop (mix algaeReservoir with algaeReservoir) in BioScript.
Drain vs.      : lilott8/BioScript compiler maps drain -> dispose in IR output for fail
dispose        : branches (BB3, BB6, BB9); behaviourally equivalent at compiler level.
                 Hardware-level waste routing distinction should be handled at scheduler.
Biological     : Protocol 1 encodes yellow LED arm at high intensity as representative
scope          : single-colour condition. Full multicolour screen requires 8 separate
                 device runs (one per colour/control). Low intensity arm is a separate run.
                 Protocol 2 encodes optimal 15h blue / 9h yellow condition only; other
                 7 timing variants follow identical BioScript structure with different
                 heat durations. Protocol 3 ROS arm D (silicon deprivation) is off-chip
                 macroscale only and is not encoded in the DMF BioScript.

device.waste_management: Vertical through-holes (1 mm dia.) in waste reservoir electrodes; spent fluid wicks away from device onto absorbent tissue below
device.automation: Impedance sensing and feedback control over droplet position; automated actuation sequence management

steps.notes: Device placed on black 384-well plate for fluorescence measurement. Steps 3-5 repeated after each illumination incubation phase.

steps.key_finding: Yellow LEDs (~580 nm) produce highest neutral lipid accumulation per cell (>2x vs. control) at high intensity; blue LEDs (~450 nm) produce highest biomass growth

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Dried Blood Spot Analysis by Digital Microfluidics Coupled to Nanoelectrospray Ionization Mass Spectrometry
Source Link  : https://pubs.acs.org/doi/pdf/10.1021/ac300305s?ref=article_openPDF
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/ac300305s
Journal      : Analytical Chemistry, 2012, Vol. 84, pp. 3731-3738
Platform     : Digital microfluidics (DMF) coupled to nanoelectrospray ionization mass spectrometry (nESI-MS) on EWOD electrode array


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes an automated digital microfluidic (DMF) method for the extraction,
derivatization, and nanoelectrospray ionization tandem mass spectrometry (nESI-MS/MS)
quantification of succinylacetone (SA), a biomarker for hepatorenal tyrosinemia (HT,
tyrosinemia type 1), from 3.2 mm dried blood spot (DBS) punches on Whatman 903 filter paper.

The system integrates a standard two-plate DMF device (patterned chromium electrodes on glass
bottom plate + unpatterned ITO-coated glass top plate, both Teflon-AF coated) with a pulled-glass
capillary nanoESI emitter inserted between the two plates. This "sandwich" configuration
immobilizes the emitter without external seals or gaskets, and allows emitters to be exchanged
in seconds without disassembling the device.

A key innovation is an impedance-based automated feedback control system (RBBB Arduino
microcontroller) that detects droplet movement failures and automatically escalates driving
voltage (50 Vrms steps up to 350 Vrms) until movement succeeds -- achieving 100% droplet
movement success across DBS punches versus 60% without feedback.

The protocol is divided into three functional phases:
  1. Sequential methanol pre-extraction (3 cycles) to remove non-SA analytes
  2. SA extraction and hydrazine derivatization (two-step: evaporate then re-dissolve)
  3. On-chip nESI-MS/MS quantification with internal standard normalization

An extended protocol (Fig. 6) additionally enables parallel amino acid (AA) analysis from
the methanol pre-extractate using a second capillary emitter and n-butanol HCl derivatization,
demonstrating compatibility with multi-analyte newborn screening panels.

The DMF method was validated against the gold-standard NSO technique (paired t-test,
p = 0.05, t = 0.8177) with no statistically significant difference at 95% CI, using
75 uL total reagent volume vs 200-310 uL conventionally.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Bottom plate : Chromium electrodes patterned on glass (photolithography + wet etching);
               22 square actuation electrodes (2.2 x 2.2 mm), 7 reservoir electrodes (5 x 5 mm);
               interelectrode gaps 30 um; contact pads interface with 40-pin connector.
               Coated with 7 um Parylene-C (vapor deposition) + 50 nm Teflon-AF (spin-coated).

Top plate    : Unpatterned ITO-coated glass (Delta Technologies Ltd.);
               37.5 x 25 mm; coated with 50 nm Teflon-AF.

Assembly     : 5 layers double-sided tape spacer (~450 um total gap).
               Gap > DBS punch thickness (~430 um including blood) to allow punch insertion.
               15 uL droplets span approximately two 2.2 x 2.2 mm electrodes.

nESI interface: Pulled-glass capillary emitter (New Objective Inc.); 360 um o.d., 50 um i.d.,
               30 um tip i.d., ~5 cm long; inserted ~2.7 cm between the two plates.
               Emitter tip positioned ~3 mm from LTQ MS orifice.
               Droplet fills capillary (~100 nL) by capillary action on contact.
               DC 1.7-2.2 kV applied to ITO top plate for nanoelectrospray generation.
               Spray stable >200 s, RSD = 7.3%, fluid consumption ~800 nL/min.
               Extended protocol uses two emitters (one per end of device, Fig. 6a).

Fabrication  : University of Toronto ECTI cleanroom facility.
               Photomask printed at Pacific Arts and Design (Markham, ON).


REAGENTS
--------
- MeOH (neat methanol):
    Pre-extraction solvent; 15 uL droplets x 3 cycles = 45 uL total.
    Extracts amino acids and acylcarnitines; SA remains in residual spot.

- HydrazineReagent (SA extraction/derivatization/MS solvent):
    6.5 mM hydrazine + 15 uM 13C5-SA in 80:20 acetonitrile:H2O + 0.1% v/v formic acid.
    15 uL droplets x 2 steps = 30 uL total.
    Derivatizes SA to hydrazone; 13C5-SA serves as internal standard.

- InternalStandard_13C5_SA (3,4,5,6,7-13C-succinylacetone):
    Supplier: Cambridge Isotope Laboratories (Andover, MA).
    Concentration: 15 uM. MS transition: m/z 160 -> 142.
    Co-formulated in HydrazineReagent (modelled separately in BioScript).

- AADerivatizationReagent (extended protocol only):
    3 N HCl in n-butanol; butyl ester derivatization at 75 C.

- AASolvent (extended protocol only):
    Acetonitrile:H2O 4:1 v/v; re-dissolution of dried AA derivatives.

- DBSPunch:
    3.2 mm diameter punch from Whatman 903 filter paper bearing dried blood.
    Toronto samples: male EDTA blood (Biochemed Services) spiked with SA (5-80 uM) and 13C5-SA.
    Ottawa samples: NSO standard technique; stored -20 C; pre-fortified with 13C5-SA before use.
    Note: DBSPunch is a solid-phase persistent object on the DMF bottom plate, not a liquid
    reagent. Declared as a BioScript manifest to allow mix step referencing.


ACTUATION AND FEEDBACK CONTROL
-------------------------------
Waveform     : Sine wave, 15 kHz, 150-350 Vrms
Source       : Function generator (Agilent Technologies) + amplifier
Contact pads : 40-pin connector; automated droplet control via C++ software / Arduino USB

Feedback control system (new, Table 1):
  - Buffered impedance measurement circuit managed by RBBB Arduino (Modern Device)
  - Digital potentiometer (1-10 kOhm) for automatic thresholding per liquid type
  - Actuation pulse: 505 ms (500 ms drive + 5 ms measure)
  - Failure response: step-up 50 Vrms per failed pulse (max 350 Vrms)
  - Relays: 80 AQV259H Panasonic solid-state relays, 2 per output (40 outputs)
  - Control software: custom C++ program via USB to Arduino
  - Result: 100% success rate (avg 4.8 +/- 1.3 pulses) vs 60% success (avg 25.6 +/- 4.8
    pulses) at constant 150 Vrms without feedback. First system with automated
    feedback-controlled variation of actuation potentials.


MS/MS DETECTION
---------------
Instrument   : LTQ linear ion trap mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific)
Ionization   : Nanoelectrospray (nESI), positive mode

SA quantification (MS/MS):
  Derivatization   : Hydrazine -> SA hydrazone (reaction: Sander et al. Clin. Chem. 2006)
  Parent ion scan  : 25% collision-induced dissociation (CID)
  Scan range       : m/z 100-300
  SA transition    : m/z 155 -> 137 (neutral loss H2O, -18 m/z)
  IS transition    : m/z 160 -> 142 (neutral loss H2O, -18 m/z; 13C5-SA)
  Averaging        : 50 acquisitions per spectrum; >=3 samples per condition
  Calibration      : SA/13C5-SA intensity ratio vs SA concentration (linear regression)
  R^2              : 0.9923
  LOD              : 4.95 uM (2.43 ng)
  Extraction efficiency: 85.2% (CV = 6.85%)
  Spray RSD        : 7.3% (TIC, Fig. 1d)
  HT clinical range: 16-150 uM (well above LOD)
  Tip washing      : 4-5 rinse droplets reduce SA signal to <LOD (Fig. 5)

AA analysis (extended protocol, MS1, Fig. 6b):
  Derivatization   : 3 N HCl in n-butanol, 75 C (butyl esters)
  AAs detected     : VAL, MET, TYR, HIS, GLN, PRO, PHE, ASP
  Mode             : Proof-of-concept, non-quantitative; primary MS (MS1)


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | MeOH Pre-Extraction Cycle 1
  Reagents  : MeOH (15 uL), DBSPunch
  Operation : mix (droplet actuated to DBS punch)
  Duration  : 15 min (900 s) at room temperature
  IR op     : preExtract11[0] = mix(meoh11[0], dbsPunch11[0]) @ 900.0SECOND
  Purpose   : First methanol wash; extracts amino acids, acylcarnitines, and small
              molecules. SA not efficiently extracted by MeOH; retained in spot.
  Outcome   : MeOH extractate actuated to waste reservoir (drain).

Step 2 | MeOH Pre-Extraction Cycle 2
  Reagents  : MeOH (15 uL), DBSPunch (persistent)
  Operation : mix
  Duration  : 15 min (900 s) at room temperature
  IR op     : preExtract21[0] = mix(meoh21[0], dbsPunch11[0]) @ 900.0SECOND
  Purpose   : Second MeOH wash; DBSPunch reused (solid-phase persistent object).
  Outcome   : Drain to waste.

Step 3 | MeOH Pre-Extraction Cycle 3
  Reagents  : MeOH (15 uL), DBSPunch (persistent)
  Operation : mix
  Duration  : 15 min (900 s) at room temperature
  IR op     : preExtract31[0] = mix(meoh31[0], dbsPunch11[0]) @ 900.0SECOND
  Purpose   : Third and final MeOH wash. Residual punch now ready for SA extraction.
  Outcome   : Drain to waste.

Step 4 | SA Extraction and Derivatization - Part A (evaporation step)
  Reagents  : HydrazineReagent (15 uL), InternalStandard_13C5_SA, DBSPunch (persistent)
  Operation : mix + heat
  Mix duration  : 15 min (900 s) contact with DBS punch
  Heat          : 37 C for 15 min (900 s) on hot-plate until evaporation
  IR ops    : extractionMix11[0] = mix(hydrazineReagent11[0], is11[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
              saExtraction11[0] = mix(extractionMix11[0], dbsPunch11[0]) @ 900.0SECOND
              heat(saExtraction11[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 900.0SECOND
  Purpose   : 6.5 mM hydrazine extracts SA from residual DBS and derivatizes it to
              hydrazone. Incubation at 37 C drives evaporation, concentrating product.
              Internal standard co-dispensed for ratio-metric quantification.

Step 5 | SA Extraction and Derivatization - Part B (circular re-dissolution)
  Reagents  : HydrazineReagent (15 uL), InternalStandard_13C5_SA, saExtraction1
  Operation : mix (circular 5-electrode actuation pattern)
  Duration  : 1 min (60 s) at room temperature
  IR ops    : extractionMix21[0] = mix(hydrazineReagent21[0], is21[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
              derivatizedSA1[0] = mix(extractionMix21[0], saExtraction11[0]) @ 60.0SECOND
  Purpose   : Fresh hydrazine droplet re-dissolves and collects evaporated SA hydrazone.
              Circular actuation around 5 adjacent electrodes maximises recovery.

Step 6 | nESI-MS/MS Quantification of Derivatized SA
  Inputs    : derivatizedSA
  Operation : detect (saAnalysis module)
  Duration  : 200 s
  IR op     : saSignal1[0] = detect(saAnalysis, derivatizedSA1[0]) @ 200.0SECOND
  Purpose   : Droplet driven to capillary emitter inlet; fills by capillary action (~100 nL).
              DC 1.7-2.2 kV applied to ITO top plate; stable nESI generated into LTQ.
              MS/MS: 25% CID, neutral loss 18, transitions m/z 155->137 (SA) and 160->142 (IS).
              SA/IS ratio used for calibration curve quantification (R^2 = 0.9923, LOD 4.95 uM).
  Branch    :
    Pass (BB2) : saSignal > 0  -> SA detected above LOD; dispose(derivatizedSA)
    Fail (BB3) : saSignal <= 0 -> signal below LOD or spray failure; drain(derivatizedSA)

Step 2a | AA Extended Protocol - MeOH Extraction and Evaporation (BB4, post-SA join)
  Reagents  : MeOH (15 uL), DBSPunch (second punch / conceptual extractate)
  Operation : mix + heat
  Mix duration  : 5 min (300 s) [shorter than SA protocol]
  Heat          : 25 C for 15 min (900 s) [ambient evaporation to dryness]
  IR ops    : aaExtract1[0] = mix(meoh_aa1[0], dbsPunch21[0]) @ 300.0SECOND
              heat(aaExtract1[0]) @ 25.0CELSIUS @ 900.0SECOND
  Purpose   : Isolates MeOH pre-extractate for AA analysis. In paper this is performed
              concurrently (Fig. 6 setup); linearized in BioScript after SA QC join.

Step 2b | AA Extended Protocol - Butyl Ester Derivatization
  Reagents  : AADerivatizationReagent (15 uL), aaExtract
  Operation : mix + heat
  Mix duration  : 5 s
  Heat          : 75 C for 15 min (900 s) until dryness
  IR ops    : aaDerivMix1[0] = mix(aaDerivReagent1[0], aaExtract1[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
              heat(aaDerivMix1[0]) @ 75.0CELSIUS @ 900.0SECOND
  Purpose   : 3 N HCl in n-butanol derivatizes amino acids to n-butyl esters at 75 C.

Step 2c | AA Extended Protocol - Re-dissolution and nESI-MS Analysis
  Reagents  : AASolvent (15 uL), aaDerivMix
  Operation : mix + detect (aminoAcidAnalysis module)
  Mix duration  : 1 min (60 s)
  Detect duration: 200 s
  IR ops    : aaReadySample1[0] = mix(aaSolventDrop1[0], aaDerivMix1[0]) @ 60.0SECOND
              aaSignal1[0] = detect(aminoAcidAnalysis, aaReadySample1[0]) @ 200.0SECOND
  Purpose   : ACN:H2O re-dissolves dry butyl ester derivatives; droplet actuated to
              second nESI emitter (Fig. 6a, top-left). Primary MS spectrum collected.
              AAs detected: VAL, MET, TYR, HIS, GLN, PRO, PHE, ASP (Fig. 6b).
  Branch    :
    Pass (BB5) : aaSignal > 0  -> AA peaks detected; dispose(aaReadySample)
    Fail (BB6) : aaSignal <= 0 -> no signal; drain(aaReadySample)


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : shih_dbs_dmf_nesi_ms.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG            : shih_dbs_dmf_nesi_ms_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations expressed in seconds (s) or minutes (m)
                 15 min incubations -> 15m  (IR: 900.0 SECOND)
                 1 min re-dissolution -> 1m (IR: 60.0 SECOND)
                 200 s detect windows -> 200s (IR: 200.0 SECOND)
Modules        : saAnalysis, aminoAcidAnalysis
Manifests      : MeOH, HydrazineReagent, AADerivatizationReagent, AASolvent,
                 DBSPunch, InternalStandard_13C5_SA
drain vs dispose note:
                 lilott8/BioScript emits dispose() for both drain and dispose in IR.
                 Semantic intent preserved in .bs source comments only.
DBS abstraction note:
                 DBSPunch is a solid-phase persistent object, not a liquid reagent.
                 Declared as manifest and reused across all mix steps in BB1 (dbsPunch11[0]).
                 Second DBSPunch dispense (dbsPunch21[0]) in BB4 represents the conceptual
                 MeOH extractate isolated for AA analysis (linearization of parallel branch).
AA branch note:
                 In the paper, AA extraction runs concurrently with SA extraction (Fig. 6).
                 BioScript's linear execution model requires sequential encoding; AA branch
                 is placed after the SA QC join (BB4) as the correct approximation.

protocol.platform: Digital microfluidics (DMF) coupled to nanoelectrospray ionization mass spectrometry (nESI-MS)
protocol.sample_type: Dried blood spot (DBS) on Whatman 903 filter paper
protocol.objective: Automated on-chip extraction, derivatization, and nESI-MS/MS quantification of succinylacetone (SA) as a biomarker for hepatorenal tyrosinemia (HT, tyrosinemia type 1) from 3.2 mm DBS punches; extended protocol also enables parallel amino acid analysis

layers: Patterned chromium electrodes on glass bottom plate (photolithography + etching)
7 um Parylene-C dielectric layer (vapor deposition)
50 nm Teflon-AF hydrophobic coating (spin-coated, 1% wt/wt in Fluorinert FC-40, 1000 rpm, 30 s, post-baked 160 C 10 min)
Unpatterned ITO-coated glass top plate (50 nm Teflon-AF coated)

bottom_plate.electrode_array: 22 square actuation electrodes (2.2 x 2.2 mm each)

assembly.note: Gap > DBS punch thickness (~430 um) to allow punch insertion without crushing

nesi_interface.emitter_type: Pulled-glass capillary nanoESI emitter (New Objective Inc.)
nesi_interface.spray_voltage_kV: 1.7-2.2 DC applied to ITO top plate
nesi_interface.extended_protocol: Two capillary emitters (one per end of device) used for parallel SA and AA analysis (Fig. 6)

pre_extraction_solvent.name: Methanol (MeOH)
pre_extraction_solvent.purpose: Sequential pre-extraction to remove amino acids, acylcarnitines, and other small molecules that interfere with SA derivatization. SA remains in residual blood spot.

sa_extraction_derivatization_ms_solvent.name: HydrazineReagent
sa_extraction_derivatization_ms_solvent.composition: 6.5 mM hydrazine + 15 uM 13C5-SA internal standard in 80:20 acetonitrile:H2O + 0.1% v/v formic acid
sa_extraction_derivatization_ms_solvent.purpose: SA extraction from residual DBS; hydrazine derivatization to hydrazone; formic acid for MS ionization; 13C5-SA as internal standard for quantification

internal_standard.name: 3,4,5,6,7-13C-succinylacetone (13C5-SA)
internal_standard.note: Co-dispensed in HydrazineReagent; modelled as separate manifest InternalStandard_13C5_SA in BioScript

aa_derivatization_reagent.name: AADerivatizationReagent
aa_derivatization_reagent.purpose: Butyl ester derivatization of amino acids for ESI-MS/MS (standard NBS method)

aa_ms_solvent.name: AASolvent
aa_ms_solvent.purpose: Re-dissolution of dried butyl-ester AA derivatives prior to nESI-MS

dbs_sample.name: DBSPunch
dbs_sample.toronto_samples: Male blood units in EDTA (K3) from Biochemed Services; fortified with SA (5, 10, 20, 50, 80 uM) and 15 uM 13C5-SA; 100 uL aliquots spotted; dried overnight at ambient temperature
dbs_sample.ottawa_samples: NSO standard technique (Mei et al. J. Nutr. 2001); stored at -20 C; pre-fortified with 10 uL 13C5-SA (15 uM) and air-dried 2 h at RT before analysis

reagent_total_volume_uL.reduction_note: DMF reduces reagent use by 2.7-4.1x vs conventional technique

feedback_control.system: Impedance-based feedback control (RBBB Arduino microcontroller, Modern Device)
feedback_control.circuit: Buffered voltage measurement with digital potentiometer (Radj = 1-10 kOhm)
feedback_control.failure_response: Step-up 50 Vrms per failed attempt (max 350 Vrms)
feedback_control.relays: 80 AQV259H Panasonic solid-state relays, 2 per output (40 outputs total)
feedback_control.control_software: Custom C++ program interfaced via USB to Arduino
feedback_control.note: First system to implement automated feedback-controlled variation of actuation potentials

ms_detection.instrument: LTQ linear ion trap mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific)

sa_analysis.tip_washing: 4-5 rinse droplets reduce SA signal below LOD (Fig. 5)

aa_analysis.note: Proof-of-concept, non-quantitative (Fig. 6b); same spray parameters as SA analysis

validation.method: Paired t-test vs NSO gold standard
validation.conclusion: No statistically significant difference between DMF and NSO standard technique
validation.note: Different extraction volumes, techniques, mass spectrometers (different manufacturers), locations, and operators

steps.name: MeOH pre-extraction cycle 1
steps.notes: 15 min incubation at room temperature. Methanol extracts amino acids, acylcarnitines. SA remains in residual spot. MeOH extractate actuated to waste reservoir after incubation.

steps.name: Drain MeOH pre-extractate 1 to waste
steps.notes: In extended AA protocol (Fig. 6), this extractate is retained and diverted for AA derivatization instead. In main SA-only protocol it is discarded.

steps.name: MeOH pre-extraction cycle 2
steps.notes: Second sequential MeOH wash. DBSPunch object reused (persistent solid phase).

steps.name: MeOH pre-extraction cycle 3
steps.notes: Third and final MeOH pre-extraction. Residual punch now ready for hydrazine SA extraction.

steps.name: SA extraction and derivatization - Part A (evaporation)
steps.notes: 6.5 mM hydrazine reagent actuated to residual DBS punch. Incubated at 37 C on hot-plate until evaporation (~15 min). Hydrazine reacts with SA to form hydrazone derivative. Evaporation concentrates derivatized analyte. Reaction mechanism: Sander et al. Clin. Chem. 2006.

steps.name: SA extraction and derivatization - Part B (circular re-dissolution)
steps.notes: Fresh 15 uL hydrazine reagent droplet loaded and actuated to evaporated residual. Incubated 1 min at RT. Droplet actuated in circular pattern around 5 electrodes adjacent to DBS punch to maximise re-dissolution of derivatized SA hydrazone.

steps.name: nESI-MS/MS analysis of derivatized SA
steps.notes: Droplet driven to capillary emitter inlet; fills by capillary action. DC 1.7-2.2 kV applied to ITO top plate. MS/MS: 25% CID, scan m/z 100-300, neutral loss 18 (m/z 155->137 for SA, 160->142 for 13C5-SA). 50 acquisitions averaged.

steps.name: AA extended protocol - MeOH extraction and evaporation
steps.notes: In extended protocol, first MeOH incubation is 5 min (not 15 min). Extractate evaporated to dryness at RT (~15 min) on non-reservoir electrode to concentrate AAs. In BioScript, fresh DBSPunch dispense represents the isolated MeOH extractate (linearization of parallel branch).

steps.name: AA extended protocol - Butyl ester derivatization
steps.notes: 3 N HCl in n-butanol actuated to dried AA extract. Heated to 75 C until dryness. Forms n-butyl ester derivatives of amino acids for ESI-MS/MS.

steps.name: AA extended protocol - Re-dissolution and nESI-MS analysis
steps.notes: ACN:H2O 4:1 solvent re-dissolves dried derivatives. Droplet actuated to second nESI emitter (opposite end of device, Fig. 6a). Primary MS spectrum. AAs detected: VAL, MET, TYR, HIS, GLN, PRO, PHE, ASP.

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.contents: Steps S1-S9: three MeOH pre-extractions, SA extraction/derivatization Parts A+B, nESI-MS/MS detection, AA extended branch (S2a-S2c)

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_4_j
basic_blocks.contents: dispose(saSignal); AA extended protocol S2a-S2c; aaSignal gate

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_7_j
basic_blocks.contents: dispose(aaSignal); NOP

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Digital Microfluidics with Impedance Sensing for Integrated Cell Culture and Analysis
Source Link  : https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0956566312007105
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bios.2012.10.035
Journal      : Biosensors and Bioelectronics, 2013, Vol. 42, pp. 314-320
Platform     : Digital microfluidics (DMF) with integrated label-free impedance sensing on EWOD/electrode array


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes the first digital microfluidic system capable of impedance-based sensing
of mammalian cells, integrating cell seeding, long-term culture, and multiplexed label-free analysis
on a single DMF device. The approach repurposes the feedback-control impedance circuit already used
for high-fidelity droplet position sensing (Vsense loop) to simultaneously measure cell density
as a function of impedance -- eliminating the need for fluorescent dyes, enzymatic stripping,
fixatives, or imaging for routine cell population analysis.

Three assays are validated in sequence on the same device platform:
  1. Calibration -- impedance vs. surface density regression for three cell lines
  2. Proliferation -- 4-day growth curve monitoring by periodic impedance measurement
  3. Serum screening -- 5-plex on-chip FCS dilution series with 4-day growth readout

The system achieves approximately 1000-fold reduction in reagent use compared to commercial
multiwell-plate impedance systems (e.g. Applied Biophysics ECIS: 1.5-4 mL per assay vs.
1-10 uL per assay in DMF format). Automated media exchange without intervention enables
uninterrupted long-term culture and analysis.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Bottom plate : 66 electrodes on glass substrate; coated with Parylene-C dielectric + Teflon-AF
               hydrophobic layer. Electrode types: reservoir, driving, active dispensing,
               and cell-sensor (ITO, patterned). Device dimensions: 50 x 100 mm.
Top plate    : ITO-coated glass with Teflon-AF hydrophobic coating; 6 hydrophilic cell-culture
               sites (1 mm diameter, exposed ITO) patterned for cell attachment and virtual
               microwell formation.

Droplet volumes:
  Unit droplet    : ~1 uL (covers area over single driving electrode)
  Virtual microwell: ~0.2 uL (sub-droplet spontaneously formed when unit droplet is translated
                     across hydrophilic ITO culture site; passive dispensing, S1-S3 program)

Reagent exchange (E1-E3 program): three-droplet sequential wash sequence replaces virtual
microwell contents (e.g. cell media -> sucrose buffer) without disturbing the adherent cell
monolayer on the hydrophilic ITO surface.

Feedback control: Vsense loop (Fig S1) repeatedly measures droplet impedance to enable
high-fidelity automated droplet movement (104 movements per full protocol run).
Same hardware repurposed for cell density measurement by detecting Vsense as a function
of cell surface density in low-conductivity sucrose medium.


IMPEDANCE SENSING SYSTEM
-------------------------
Sensing voltage  : 100 Vrms AC pulse, 1 s duration
Sensing frequency: 15 kHz (optimal; selected from 5, 15, 30 kHz characterisation)
Measurement medium: 500 mM aqueous sucrose (10 mM HEPES, 0.05% Pluronic F68, pH 7.4)
Rationale        : Low-conductivity sucrose resolves density-dependent Vsense differences
                   that are indistinguishable in full cell media (p=0.101 in media vs.
                   p=2.36e-7 in sucrose at 15 kHz for NIH-3T3 low vs. high density).
Sucrose exposure : ~10 min per measurement cycle; no impact on proliferation for any cell type.
LOD              : 20-25 cells/mm2 (improvable by thinner insulator, smaller electrode, reduced gap).
Circuit model    : Modified from Morgan et al. 2007; adds capacitor element for DMF insulator
                   and bottom sub-circuit for electrode-adhered cell interface.


CELL LINES
----------
- HeLa (human cervical carcinoma): DMEM + 10% FCS + penicillin (100 IU/mL) +
  streptomycin (100 ug/mL) + 0.05% w/v Pluronic F68. 37 C, 5% CO2.
- NIH-3T3 (mouse embryonic fibroblast): same media as HeLa.
- CHO-K1 (Chinese hamster ovary): 50/50 v/v F-12/DMEM + 10% FCS + penicillin +
  streptomycin + 0.05% w/v Pluronic F68. 37 C, 5% CO2.

All cell suspensions supplemented with 0.05% Pluronic F68 (w/v) to prevent biofouling
during DMF electrode actuation. Cells detached with 0.25% w/v trypsin + 1 mM EDTA
before each DMF experiment, centrifuged, and resuspended at target density.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Cell Seeding and Culture -- Calibration Assay
  Cell lines     : HeLa, NIH-3T3, CHO-K1
  Densities      : 0.5 x 10^6, 1.0 x 10^6, 2.0 x 10^6 cells/mL (9 conditions total; 3 lines x 3 densities)
  Operation      : Passive dispensing (S1-S3): unit droplet driven over hydrophilic ITO site
                   leaves 0.2 uL virtual microwell containing cell suspension.
                   Abstracted as mix in BioScript (no DMF electrode mixing implied).
  Incubation     : 24 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 (= 1440 min = 86400 s)
  Media          : HeLa/NIH-3T3: complete DMEM; CHO-K1: complete F-12/DMEM (50/50)
  Replicates     : 5 per condition

Step 2 | Sucrose Exchange and Vsense Measurement -- Calibration Assay
  Exchange medium : 500 mM sucrose buffer (E1-E3 three-droplet wash; ~10 min sucrose exposure)
  Sensing         : 100 Vrms, 15 kHz, 1 s pulse; Vsense recorded
  Validation      : ImageJ microscopy cell count: surface density (cells/mm2) and area (mm2)
                    calculated for each virtual microwell; used to generate regression curves.
  Regression      : Vsense vs. surface density linear over >= 1 order of magnitude:
                    HeLa R2=0.9965; NIH-3T3 R2=0.9935; CHO-K1 R2=0.9920
  QC gate         : NIH-3T3 high-density Vsense (nih3t3High_Vsense) used as gate signal.
                    Pass (BB2): dispose all calibration droplets.
                    Fail (BB3): drain all calibration droplets.

Step 3 | Cell Seeding and 4-Day Proliferation Monitoring
  Cell lines      : HeLa, NIH-3T3, CHO-K1
  Seeding density : 0.25 x 10^6 cells/mL (all three lines)
  Operation cycle : For each 24h timepoint (24h, 48h, 72h, 96h):
                    (a) Exchange media with sucrose (E1-E3)
                    (b) Vsense at 15 kHz, 1 s; translate to surface density via calibration curves
                    (c) Exchange sucrose with fresh complete media (E1-E3)
                    (d) Culture 24h at 37 C, 5% CO2
  Replicates      : 5 per cell line
  Results         : Day 1: all lines below LOD (~20-25 cells/mm2).
                    Days 2-4: measurable densities; NIH-3T3 and HeLa proliferate faster
                    than CHO-K1, consistent with standard macroscale culture conditions.
  QC gate         : NIH-3T3 Day 4 Vsense (nih_vsense_d4) used as gate signal.
                    Pass (BB5): dispose Day 4 sucrose droplets.
                    Fail (BB6): drain Day 4 sucrose droplets.

Step 4 | Serum Screening Assay (5-Plex FCS Dilution Series)
  Cell line       : NIH-3T3
  Seeding density : 0.25 x 10^5 cells/mL (10x lower than proliferation assay)
  Initial culture : 6 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 in complete DMEM (= 360 min = 21600 s) for attachment
  FCS concentrations: 0.625%, 1.25%, 2.5%, 5%, 10% (5-plex, 6 virtual microwells on device)
  Dilution method : On-chip serial dilution (D1-D9 program); 20% FCS in serum-free DMEM as
                    concentrated stock; serum-free DMEM as diluent.
                    Dilution chain:
                      10%    FCS: 1 part FCS_Stock (20%) + 1 part diluent
                      5%     FCS: 1 part 10% mix    + 1 part diluent
                      2.5%   FCS: 1 part 5% mix     + 1 part diluent
                      1.25%  FCS: 1 part 2.5% mix   + 1 part diluent
                      0.625% FCS: 1 part 1.25% mix  + 1 part diluent
  Operation cycle : Same as proliferation assay (Steps 3 cycle) except FCS-specific media
                    regenerated on-chip (D1-D9) for each daily refresh instead of plain DMEM.
  Measurement points: 24h, 48h, 72h, 96h
  Replicates      : 5 per concentration
  Results         : 5% and 10% FCS: sigmoidal growth profiles.
                    0.625%-2.5% FCS: flat or declining profiles; poor proliferation.
                    Max surface density ~200 cells/mm2 at 10% FCS on Day 4.
  QC gate         : 10% FCS Day 4 Vsense (vsense_10_d4) used as gate signal (highest serum,
                    highest expected Vsense).
                    Pass (BB8): dispose all 5 concentration Day 4 sucrose droplets.
                    Fail (BB9): drain all 5 concentration Day 4 sucrose droplets.


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : shih_dmf_cell_impedance_sensing.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
DAG file       : shih_dmf_cell_impedance_sensing_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations in s or m only (h token not supported by compiler)
                 1440m = 86400.0 SECOND (24h culture/incubation cycles)
                 360m  = 21600.0 SECOND (6h initial attachment in serum assay)
Modules        : impedanceSensing, cellCountDetection
Virtual microwell abstraction:
                 mix steps labelled "seeding" abstract passive dispensing (S1-S3) event;
                 not DMF electrode mixing. No reagent mixing occurs at these steps.
Sucrose exchange abstraction:
                 mix steps labelled "exchange" abstract E1-E3 three-droplet sequential wash;
                 single mix statement represents the full exchange program.
Serial dilution note:
                 BioScript has no loop or parametric dilution support. All 5 FCS concentration
                 chains are fully unrolled for the initial dilution and each of 3 daily refresh
                 cycles (Days 1, 2, 3), resulting in explicit variable chains per concentration.
QC gate note   : Variable alias assignment (e.g. calibSignal = nih3t3High_Vsense) is not
                 registered in the compiler symbol table and causes UndefinedVariable error
                 at dispose. Detect result variables used directly in if conditions.
drain vs dispose: drain and dispose both lower to dispose() in IR; semantically equivalent
                 at the lilott8/BioScript compiler level.

protocol.title: Digital Microfluidics with Impedance Sensing for Integrated Cell Culture and Analysis
protocol.platform: Digital microfluidics (DMF) with integrated impedance sensing
protocol.objective: Label-free impedance-based cell density sensing integrated with DMF for cell seeding, long-term culture, and multiplexed analysis via three assays: calibration, proliferation, and serum screening

top_plate.coating: Teflon-AF hydrophobic coating (patterned; hydrophilic ITO exposed at culture sites)

device.passive_dispensing: Unit droplet translated across hydrophilic ITO site -> spontaneous 0.2 uL virtual microwell formation (S1-S3 program)
device.reagent_exchange: Three-droplet sequential wash sequence (E1-E3 program) replaces microwell contents without disturbing cell monolayer
device.feedback_control: Impedance-based droplet position sensing (Vsense loop, Fig S1) repurposed for cell density measurement

impedance_system.measurement_medium: 500 mM aqueous sucrose (10 mM HEPES, 0.05% w/v Pluronic F68, pH 7.4)
impedance_system.rationale_for_sucrose: Low-conductivity medium separates density-dependent Vsense values; full cell media shows no statistically significant difference between densities
impedance_system.sucrose_viability_impact: None observed for any cell type tested
impedance_system.circuit_model: Capacitor (insulator) in series with parallel R-C (medium) and cell membrane/cytoplasm sub-circuit; modified from Morgan et al. 2007 to account for DMF insulator layer and electrode-adhered cells

cell_media.HeLa: DMEM + 10% FCS + 100 IU/mL penicillin + 100 ug/mL streptomycin + 0.05% w/v Pluronic F68
cell_media.NIH3T3: DMEM + 10% FCS + 100 IU/mL penicillin + 100 ug/mL streptomycin + 0.05% w/v Pluronic F68
cell_media.CHO_K1: 50/50 v/v F-12/DMEM + 10% FCS + 100 IU/mL penicillin + 100 ug/mL streptomycin + 0.05% w/v Pluronic F68

reagents.sucrose_buffer: 500 mM sucrose in DI water (18 MOhm cm), 10 mM HEPES, 0.05% w/v Pluronic F68, pH 7.4
reagents.trypsin_edta: 0.25% w/v trypsin + 1 mM EDTA (cell detachment before DMF experiments)
reagents.pluronic_f68_additive: 0.05% w/v Pluronic F68 in all cell suspensions (biofouling prevention)
reagents.fcs_stock_for_serum_assay: 20% FCS in serum-free DMEM (used as concentrated stock for on-chip serial dilution in serum screening assay)

steps.name: Cell seeding into virtual microwells (calibration)
steps.operation: passive dispensing (abstracted as mix in BioScript)
steps.notes: S1-S3 passive dispensing: unit droplet (1 uL) driven over hydrophilic ITO site leaves 0.2 uL virtual microwell. Each of 9 conditions (3 lines x 3 densities) seeded in separate virtual microwells.

steps.name: Sucrose exchange and Vsense measurement (calibration)
steps.microscopy_validation: ImageJ cell count of surface density (Nc) and area occupied (Ac) for regression validation
steps.notes: QC gate keyed on NIH-3T3 high-density Vsense (highest expected signal; R2=0.9935). Sucrose exchange (E1-E3) is three-droplet wash abstracted as single mix step in BioScript.

steps.name: Cell seeding and 4-day proliferation monitoring
steps.operation: passive dispensing + periodic sucrose exchange + Vsense + media refresh
steps.cycle_per_timepoint: sucrose exchange (E1-E3) -> Vsense at 15 kHz -> media exchange (E1-E3) -> 24h culture at 37C

results.day_1: All cell lines below LOD (~20-25 cells/mm2)
results.days_2_to_4: Measurable surface densities obtained for all lines
results.ranking: NIH-3T3 and HeLa proliferate faster than CHO-K1; consistent with macroscale culture

steps.notes: QC gate keyed on NIH-3T3 Day 4 Vsense (highest expected surface density at experiment end). Vsense translated to surface density (cells/mm2) via calibration regression curves from S2.

steps.name: Serum screening assay (5-plex FCS dilution series)
steps.dilution_scheme: On-chip serial dilution (D1-D9 program): 20% FCS stock + serum-free DMEM diluent; each concentration independently dispensed and verified
steps.cycle_per_timepoint: sucrose exchange (E1-E3) -> Vsense at 15 kHz -> regenerate FCS droplets (D1-D9) -> media exchange -> 24h culture at 37C

results.5_pct_and_10_pct: Sigmoidal growth profiles; cells proliferate well
results.0_625_to_2_5_pct: Flat or declining profiles; poor proliferation

steps.notes: QC gate keyed on 10% FCS Day 4 Vsense (highest serum concentration; highest expected surface density). Serial dilution fully unrolled in BioScript (no loop support). Serum-free DMEM used as diluent throughout.
