description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : A Versatile Microfluidic Device for Automating Synthetic Biology
Source Link  : https://escholarship.org/content/qt07q6b4f6/qt07q6b4f6.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/acssynbio.5b00062
Journal      : ACS Synthetic Biology, 2015, Vol. 4, pp. 1151-1164
Platform     : Hybrid DMF (digital microfluidics + droplet-in-channel microfluidics) on EWOD/electrode array


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a hybrid microfluidic platform for automating the synthetic biology
build-and-test cycle. The device integrates a digital microfluidic (DMF) bottom plate (76
patterned gold/chromium electrodes on glass, 7 um SU-8 dielectric, Aquapel hydrophobic
coating) with a PDMS serpentine incubation channel and an on-chip electroporation region.
The three functional regions -- DNA assembly (DMF), queuing and incubation (channel), and
transformation (electroporation electrodes) -- are integrated on a single 75 x 25 mm chip.

Three DNA assembly methods are implemented and validated:
  1. Golden Gate assembly (25 C, 10 min; T4 DNA ligase; Type IIS BsaI restriction)
  2. Gibson assembly (50 C, 15 min; 2x Gibson master mix)
  3. Yeast/TAR cloning assembly (25 C, 10 min; no additional reagent; in vivo assembly)

For each method, 16 combinatorial plasmid variants (4 Promoter variants x 4 BCD-gfp variants)
are assembled, transferred into the incubation channel, and electroporated into E. coli DH5alpha
(or S. cerevisiae CEN.PK for yeast assembly) on-chip. Each step uses ~0.2 uL dispensed
subdroplets from 1.5 uL reservoir droplets (10x lower total volume than comparable platforms).

Cross-contamination between the 16 sequential reactions is prevented by Pluronic F-127
(0.05% w/v) surfactant additive in HFE 7500 oil -- the first application of this strategy
to on-chip DNA assembly -- eliminating the need for additional wash reservoirs or steps.

The BioScript file encodes the Golden Gate assembly arm (representative primary method;
full 16-plasmid sequencing panel shown in paper Fig 6) for the canonical pProm1_BCD1-gfp
plasmid (~3070 bp). Gibson and Yeast arms would differ only in the ligase manifest and
heat() parameters and should be encoded in separate .bs files.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Dimensions : 75 x 25 mm (standard microscope slide form factor)

DMF bottom plate:
  Substrate     : Gold- and chromium-coated glass (Telic)
  Electrodes    : 76 total; interelectrode gap 20 um
    - 12 reservoir electrodes (3.6 x 3.0 mm); 1.5 uL droplet capacity
    - 12 narrow electrodes (2.5 x 1.0 mm); 100% dispensing fidelity
    - 8 mixing electrodes (1.2 x 1.2 mm)
    - 3 digital-to-channel electrodes (1.75 x 1.75 mm)
    - 41 actuation electrodes (1.2 x 1.2 mm)
  Dielectric    : SU-8-5, 7 um thick (spin-coated)
  Hydrophobic   : Aquapel (0.2 um filtered), 15 min, removed with Kimwipe
  Top plate     : Unpatterned ITO-glass, flush with PDMS side
  Spacer        : SU-8, ~140 um thick; dispensed droplets ~0.2 uL

Incubation and queuing region (PDMS serpentine channel):
  Width         : 1.5 mm
  Capacity      : 16 droplets; >2 h without volume loss
  Temperature   : Region-specific Peltier heater (Arduino RBBB PID control)
                  Heats incubation zone only; reservoirs remain at room temperature
                  (critical: prevents T4 ligase heat inactivation above 50 C)
  Valves        : 4 pneumatic elastomeric microvalves (Parker VSO-EP controller)
  Inlets        : 2 oil inlets (HFE 7500, 5 uL/s) + 1 syringe-vacuum inlet (0.1 uL/s)
  Transfer      : Droplet drawn from DMF surface by syringe-vacuum then driven by oil phase

Electroporation region:
  Electrodes    : 2 bare gold (no dielectric), 2.0 x 0.3 mm, 100 um gap
  Dispensing    : 4 electrodes at cell-inlet/channel intersection
                  (three 1.4 x 0.7 mm + one 4.0 x 0.7 mm)
  Microvalve    : 1 elastomeric valve (valve 5) prevents cross-contamination between
                  successive assembled plasmid droplets
  Detection     : Impedance feedback (Vsense threshold ~0.15 V); oil phase > 10 GOhm;
                  droplet 0.1-10 MOhm; triggers pulse delivery automatically

Automation system:
  Controller    : Arduino RBBB; driving potential ~100-120 V rms at 8 kHz (Agilent function
                  generator); hardware: neMESYS syringe pumps (Cetoni), Parker pneumatic
                  actuators, Peltier heater, function generator
  Dispensing precision : ~1.5% volumetric variation (6 successive droplets)


REAGENTS
--------
Carrier oil       : HFE 7500 (3M Novec); biocompatible, immiscible with aqueous DNA solutions
Surfactant        : 0.05% w/v Pluronic F-127 in all DNA solutions (prevents biofouling;
                    eliminates cross-contamination without wash steps)
DNA fragments     : 30-40 ng/uL each; DpnI digested 37 C 1 h; BsaI digested overnight 37 C
                    (Golden Gate only); gel-purified on 1% agarose
Vector backbone   : pFAB4876-based, p15A origin + kanamycin resistance; ~2100 bp (GG/Gibson)
                    pRS424, 2 micron origin + TRP1 (yeast) + F1 + ampicillin; ~5600 bp (Yeast)
Promoter inserts  : Prom1, Prom2, Prom9, Prom11; ~100 bp; from pFAB4876/4884/4924/4932
BCD-gfp inserts   : BCD1, BCD2, BCD20, BCD21 fused to sfGFP; ~800 bp; from pFAB4876/77/82/83
T4 DNA ligase     : 2.5 U/uL with 0.05% Pluronic F-127 (NEB); for Golden Gate only
Gibson master mix : 2x Gibson Assembly Master Mix (NEB); for Gibson only
EP media (E. coli): 8 mM Na2HPO4, 2 mM KH2PO4, 250 mM sucrose pH 7.4
EP media (yeast)  : 1.0 M sorbitol
E. coli cells     : DH5alpha electrocompetent (NEB C2989K); plated on LB + kan 50 ug/mL
Yeast cells       : CEN.PK (TRP deletion); plated on CSM-agar delta-TRP
Recovery media    : 200 uL LB broth (E. coli); 200 uL deionized water (yeast)
Plasmid source    : JBEI public registry (https://public-registry.jbei.org/login)


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Oil Phase Priming
  Reagents    : HFE 7500 + 0.05% w/v Pluronic F-127
  Operation   : 1 mL pipetted onto DMF surface
  Purpose     : Oil surrounds all aqueous droplets throughout protocol; Pluronic F-127
                prevents biofouling and cross-contamination without wash steps.
                First application of this strategy to on-chip DNA assembly.

Step 2 | Dispense Vector Backbone
  Reagent     : VectorBackbone (pFAB4876-based, BsaI + DpnI digested, gel-purified)
  Volume      : 1.5 uL reservoir; ~0.2 uL dispensed subdroplet
  Notes       : ~2100 bp band (Golden Gate). Reservoir refilled via SU-8 capillary
                between successive reactions (16 total per run).

Step 3 | Dispense Promoter1 Insert
  Reagent     : Promoter1 (pFAB4876, ~100 bp; DpnI + BsaI digested, gel-purified)
  Volume      : 1.5 uL reservoir; ~0.2 uL dispensed
  Notes       : Four variants used across 16 reactions: Prom1, Prom2, Prom9, Prom11.
                This .bs file encodes Prom1 as the representative variant.

Step 4 | Dispense BCD1-gfp Insert
  Reagent     : BCD1_gfp (pFAB4876, ~800 bp; DpnI + BsaI digested, gel-purified)
  Volume      : 1.5 uL reservoir; ~0.2 uL dispensed
  Notes       : Four variants: BCD1, BCD2, BCD20, BCD21 (all fused to sfGFP). GFP enables
                colony color screening: green = correct insert, white = self-ligation artifact.

Step 5 | Dispense T4 DNA Ligase
  Reagent     : T4 DNA ligase, 2.5 U/uL + 0.05% w/v Pluronic F-127
  Volume      : 1.5 uL reservoir; ~0.2 uL dispensed
  Notes       : Reservoir maintained at room temperature while incubation zone is Peltier-
                heated. T4 ligase is heat-inactivated above 50 C; region-specific heating
                allows reagent storage on-chip without degradation. Gibson assembly substitutes
                2x Gibson master mix; Yeast assembly requires no additional reagent.

Step 6 | Mix Vector Backbone with Promoter1
  Inputs      : vectorDrop, promoterDrop
  Output      : dnaMix
  Duration    : 5 s
  Actuation   : ~100-120 V rms, 8 kHz; 2-3 circular mixing passes over mixing electrodes

Step 7 | Add BCD1-gfp to DNA Mix
  Inputs      : dnaMix, bcdDrop
  Output      : threePartMix
  Duration    : 5 s
  Volume      : ~0.6 uL (three-component droplet)

Step 8 | Add T4 Ligase to Complete Golden Gate Mix
  Inputs      : threePartMix, ligaseDrop
  Output      : assemblyMix
  Duration    : 10 s
  Total volume: ~0.8 uL
  Notes       : Paper Table 1: 0.8 uL total, 2 DNA fragment insertions, 16 plasmid
                combinations. Droplet circulates 2-3 times in circular fashion on
                digital-to-channel electrodes (1.75 x 1.75 mm) near D2D interface.

Step 9 | Digital-to-Droplet Transfer and Golden Gate Incubation
  Input       : assemblyMix
  Operation   : heat at 25 C for 10 min (600 s)
  Transfer    : Syringe-vacuum at 0.1 uL/s draws droplet from DMF; HFE 7500 at 5 uL/s
                drives droplet into serpentine incubation zone
  Incubation  : 25 C (room temperature), 10 min; BsaI-HF creates 4-bp overhangs;
                T4 ligase joins complementary sticky ends
  Peltier     : Region-specific; incubation zone at 25 C; reservoirs unheated
  Alternatives: Gibson: 50 C, 15 min. Yeast/TAR: 25 C, 10 min (no ligase).

Step 10 | Assembly QC Detection
  Input       : assemblyMix
  Output      : assemblySignal
  Module      : assemblyQC
  Duration    : 30 s
  Notes       : Abstracts GFP colony color screening after off-chip electroporation and
                plating. Expected pass rate: 95% Golden Gate (76/80), 100% Gibson (80/80),
                97.2% Yeast (70/72). QC branch gate decides proceed vs. discard.

  Branch BB2 (assemblySignal > 0)  : dispose(assemblyMix) -- proceed to transformation
  Branch BB3 (assemblySignal <= 0) : drain(assemblyMix)   -- ligation failed; discard

Step 11 | Dispose Assembly QC Signal [BB4 join]
  Operation   : dispose(assemblySignal)
  Notes       : Join block; transformation branch begins.

Step 12 | Dispense E. coli Cells
  Reagent     : CompetentEcoli (DH5alpha, NEB C2989K)
  Output      : cellDroplet
  Notes       : Dispensed from cell inlet via 4 microelectrodes at cell-inlet/channel
                intersection. Elastomeric microvalve (valve 5) closed to prevent
                cross-contamination with other assembled plasmid droplets in channel.

Step 13 | Dispense Incubated Plasmid (Channel Exit)
  Reagent     : AssembledPlasmid
  Output      : incubatedPlasmid
  Notes       : Models the assembled pProm1_BCD1-gfp droplet exiting the serpentine
                incubation channel and entering the electroporation zone, driven by
                HFE 7500 at 5 uL/s (all channel valves closed per Fig S2).
                BioScript ownership note: assemblyMix was consumed by detect(assemblyQC)
                in BB1; incubatedPlasmid is a new fluid object at this CFG location,
                representing the same physical droplet. This avoids the assemblyMix2
                phantom SSA index emitted by the compiler when a variable is re-used
                after detect has consumed it.

Step 14 | Mix Cells with Electroporation Media
  Inputs      : cellDroplet, electroporationMedia
  Output      : cellMix
  Duration    : 5 s
  EP media    : 8 mM Na2HPO4, 2 mM KH2PO4, 250 mM sucrose pH 7.4
  Notes       : Osmotically balanced buffer prevents cell lysis during pulse.

Step 15 | Merge Incubated Plasmid with Cell Mix
  Inputs      : incubatedPlasmid, cellMix
  Output      : preMix
  Duration    : 5 s
  Volume      : ~2 uL (merged droplet positioned over electroporation electrodes)

Step 16 | Electroporation
  Input       : preMix
  Operation   : heat at 37 C for 60 s (models post-pulse recovery temperature)
  Pulse params: 3 x 100 ms DC square pulses at 1800 V/cm (E. coli)
                Impedance feedback triggers pulse when Vsense > 0.15 V
                Oil phase (HFE 7500) > 10 GOhm impedance; prevents short when no droplet
  Efficiency  : 4.58e3 CFU/ng assembled DNA (110 +/- 8 colonies, N=3, microfluidic)
                4.46e3 CFU/ng (137 +/- 16 colonies, N=3, cuvette); not significantly different
  Notes       : Yeast (CEN.PK): 1200 V/cm; 1.90e3 CFU/ng (21 +/- 6 colonies, N=3).
                Higher fields (above optimum) decrease efficiency by killing cells.

Step 17 | Post-Electroporation Recovery
  Inputs      : preMix, LB_Recovery
  Output      : recoveredCells
  Mix         : 5 s
  Recovery    : 200 uL LB broth; 1 h at 37 C (3600 s)
  Notes       : Electroporated droplet driven to outlet by HFE 7500 (all valves closed).
                Plated on LB agar + kanamycin 50 ug/mL. ~100/110 colonies green (GFP+,
                correct insert); ~10 white (self-ligation). Yeast: collected in 200 uL
                deionized water; plated on CSM-agar delta-TRP.

Step 18 | Transformation QC Detection
  Input       : recoveredCells
  Output      : transformSignal
  Module      : transformationQC
  Duration    : 30 s
  Notes       : Abstracts off-chip colony counting (LB agar + kanamycin, 37 C overnight).
                Colony-PCR and Sanger sequencing (QB3284_fwd / QB3810_rev) confirm assembly.
                For yeast: 3 yeast colonies miniprepped; transformed into Turbo E. coli;
                5 green E. coli colonies sequenced per assembled plasmid (Genewiz).

  Branch BB5 (transformSignal > 0)  : dispose(recoveredCells) -- colonies confirmed
  Branch BB6 (transformSignal <= 0) : drain(recoveredCells)   -- no colonies; discard

Step 19 | Final Cleanup [BB7 terminal]
  Operations  : dispose(transformSignal), dispose(oilPhase)
  Notes       : Terminal block. In the actual protocol, Steps 1-19 are iterated 16 times
                in total (one reaction per plasmid combination) using the same electrode
                path, mixing channel, and incubation channel. Reservoir droplets refilled
                via SU-8 capillary channel between iterations.


SEQUENCING RESULTS
------------------
Golden Gate (16 plasmids, 5 colonies each = 80 total):
  Correct clones : 76/80 = 95% (Fig 6, main text)
  Method         : Sanger sequencing (QuintaraBio); primers QB3284_fwd / QB3810_rev
  Analysis       : Excluding first/last bases of read and 20 bp flanking assembly junctions

Gibson (16 plasmids, 5 colonies each = 80 total):
  Correct clones : 80/80 = 100% (Fig S5)

Yeast/TAR (16 plasmids, ~3-5 colonies each = 72 sequenced):
  Correct clones : 70/72 = 97.2% (Fig S6)
  Note           : 2 Sanger reactions failed for 4 plasmids (pProm2_BCD1, pProm9_BCD1,
                   pProm11_BCD1, pProm1_BCD2); sequenced from Turbo E. coli colonies


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file  : shih_versatile_dmf_synbio.bs
Compiler        : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output       : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG             : shih_versatile_dmf_synbio_main_dag.dot
Assembly method : Golden Gate (representative; Gibson and Yeast in separate .bs files)
Duration units  : All durations in s or m (BioScript supports s and m only; h not supported)

                  1 min EP recovery modelling    -> 1m   (IR: 60.0 SECOND)

Modules         : assemblyQC, transformationQC
Manifests       : VectorBackbone, Promoter1, BCD1_gfp, T4_DNA_Ligase,

  cannot re-use assemblyMix for the cell-plasmid merge (would produce phantom

  1. drain lowered to dispose in IR

protocol.title: A Versatile Microfluidic Device for Automating Synthetic Biology
protocol.platform: Hybrid DMF (digital microfluidics + droplet-in-channel microfluidics)
protocol.objective: On-chip Golden Gate, Gibson, and Yeast (TAR cloning) DNA assembly with integrated region-specific temperature control and on-chip electroporation transformation; 16 combinatorial plasmid variants (4 Promoter x 4 BCD) per assembly method

functional_regions: Queuing and incubation region (serpentine PDMS channel, 1.5 mm wide, stores 16 droplets)

fabrication.photolithography: S1811 photoresist, OAI Series 200 Aligner, UV 40 mW/cm2 5s
fabrication.etching: Gold etchant KI/I2; chromium etchant CR-4

reagents.surfactant_additive: Pluronic F-127 0.05% w/v (prevents biofouling; replaces wash steps)

dna_assembly.preparation: DpnI digested at 37 C 1h; BsaI digested overnight 37 C (Golden Gate only); gel purified
dna_assembly.vector_concentration_matching: Vacuum concentrator Thermo Fisher, 65 C, 5-10 min

golden_gate.ligase: T4 DNA ligase 2.5 U/uL with 0.05% w/v Pluronic F-127

yeast.notes: No additional reagents required; assembly occurs in vivo after transformation

electroporation.ecoli_media: 8 mM Na2HPO4, 2 mM KH2PO4, 250 mM sucrose pH 7.4

plasmid_variants.vector_golden_gate_gibson: p15A origin + kanamycin resistance (~2100 bp backbone)
plasmid_variants.vector_yeast: pRS424 (2 micron origin + TRP1 marker for yeast; F1 origin + ampicillin for bacteria; ~5600 bp)

steps.name: Oil phase priming
steps.notes: 1 mL HFE 7500 + 0.05% w/v Pluronic F-127 pipetted onto DMF surface. Oil surrounds all aqueous droplets throughout the protocol, preventing cross-contamination without wash steps. First application of this strategy to on-chip DNA assembly.

steps.name: Dispense vector backbone
steps.notes: pFAB4876-based vector backbone; BsaI + DpnI digested, gel-purified; ~2100 bp (Golden Gate). Reservoir refilled via SU-8 capillary channel between successive reactions.

steps.name: Dispense Promoter1 insert
steps.notes: Representative variant: Promoter1 from pFAB4876; ~100 bp band. Four promoter variants (Prom1, Prom2, Prom9, Prom11) used across 16 combinatorial reactions; this .bs file encodes Prom1.

steps.name: Dispense BCD1-gfp insert
steps.notes: Representative variant: BCD1_gfp from pFAB4876; ~800 bp band. Four BCD variants (BCD1, BCD2, BCD20, BCD21) used across 16 reactions. GFP enables colony color screening: green = correct insert, white = self-ligation artifact.

steps.name: Dispense T4 DNA ligase
steps.notes: T4 ligase reservoir maintained at room temperature while incubation zone is heated (region-specific Peltier). Prevents heat inactivation above 50 C. Gibson assembly uses 2x Gibson master mix instead; Yeast assembly requires no additional reagent.

steps.name: Mix vector backbone with Promoter1
steps.notes: All droplet actuation on DMF region uses 8 kHz sine wave amplified to ~100-120 V rms. Volumetric precision ~1.5% variation (impedance feedback).

steps.name: Add BCD1-gfp to DNA mix
steps.notes: Three-component droplet: vector + Promoter1 + BCD1-gfp. Total volume ~0.6 uL at this stage.

steps.name: Add T4 DNA ligase to complete Golden Gate mix
steps.notes: Final assembled droplet: vector + Promoter1 + BCD1-gfp + T4 ligase. Mixed 2-3 times in circular fashion. Paper Table 1: total volume 0.8 uL, 2 DNA fragment insertions, room temperature Golden Gate.

steps.name: Digital-to-droplet transfer and Golden Gate incubation
steps.transfer_mechanism: Syringe-vacuum pump at 0.1 uL/s draws droplet from DMF into channel; oil phase HFE 7500 at 5 uL/s drives droplet to incubation zone
steps.peltier: Region-specific; incubation zone maintained at 25 C (room temperature); reservoirs unheated
steps.notes: Golden Gate: 25 C, 10 min. BsaI-HF creates 4-bp overhangs; T4 ligase joins complementary ends. Gibson alternative: 50 C, 15 min with 2x Gibson master mix. Yeast alternative: 25 C, 10 min, no ligase (assembly occurs in vivo post-transformation).

steps.name: Assembly QC detection
steps.notes: assemblyQC abstracts the GFP colony color screening step performed after electroporation and plating (off-chip). On-chip, no direct assembly verification precedes transformation; detect gate here models the logical QC branch. Expected pass rate: ~95% correct clones for Golden Gate (76/80 sequenced, Fig 6); ~100% for Gibson (80/80).

steps.name: Assembly QC gate - pass branch
steps.notes: Golden Gate ligation succeeded; assembled plasmid disposed (QC characterisation run). Proceed to transformation branch via BB4.

steps.name: Assembly QC gate - fail branch
steps.notes: Ligation failed (e.g. self-ligation dominant, white colonies). Drain assembled droplet. Compiler known bug: drain lowered to dispose in IR; biological intent is drain.

steps.name: Dispose assembly QC signal
steps.notes: Assembly join block. Transformation branch begins.

steps.name: Dispense competent E. coli cells
steps.dispensing_electrodes: Three 1.4 x 0.7 mm + one 4.0 x 0.7 mm at cell-inlet/channel intersection
steps.notes: Cells dispensed from cell inlet into electroporation region. Elastomeric microvalve (valve 5, Fig S2) prevents cross-contamination between successive plasmid droplets. For yeast assembly: CEN.PK cells in 1.0 M sorbitol instead.

steps.name: Dispense incubated plasmid (channel exit)
steps.notes: Models the assembled pProm1_BCD1-gfp droplet exiting the serpentine incubation channel and entering the electroporation zone, driven by HFE 7500 at 5 uL/s with all valves closed (Fig S2). BioScript ownership constraint: assemblyMix was consumed by detect(assemblyQC) in BB1; incubatedPlasmid is a distinct fluid object representing the same physical droplet at its new location in the CFG.

steps.name: Mix cells with electroporation media
steps.media_composition: 8 mM Na2HPO4, 2 mM KH2PO4, 250 mM sucrose pH 7.4
steps.notes: Osmotically balanced electroporation buffer prevents cell lysis during pulse. Cells fully resuspended in EP media before merging with plasmid droplet.

steps.name: Merge incubated plasmid with cell mix
steps.notes: Merged droplet positioned over two bare gold electroporation microelectrodes (2.0 x 0.3 mm, 100 um gap, no dielectric coating). Contains assembled + non-assembled DNA fragments and cells.

steps.name: Electroporation

pulse_parameters.detection: Impedance-sensing feedback; Vsense threshold ~0.15 V; oil phase (no droplet) impedance > 10 GOhm; droplet impedance 0.1-10 MOhm

steps.notes: heat at 37 C models post-pulse recovery temperature; pulse itself is instantaneous. Oil phase (HFE 7500) prevents electrical short when no droplet bridges electrode gap. Microfluidic efficiency not significantly different from cuvette (Fig 5a). Yeast: 1200 V/cm, 1.90e3 CFU/ng (Fig 5b).

steps.name: Post-electroporation recovery
steps.notes: Electroporated droplet driven to outlet by HFE 7500 oil (all valves closed). Collected in tube containing 200 uL LB broth. 1 h outgrowth at 37 C before plating. ~100/110 colonies green (GFP+, correct insert); ~10 white (self-ligation). Plated on LB agar + kanamycin 50 ug/mL.

steps.name: Transformation QC detection
steps.notes: transformationQC abstracts off-chip colony counting on kanamycin LB-agar plates (37 C overnight). Colony-PCR and Sanger sequencing (primers QB3284_fwd / QB3810_rev; QuintaraBio) confirm assembly. Golden Gate: 95% correct (76/80). Gibson: 100% (80/80). Yeast: 97.2% (70/72).

steps.name: Transformation QC gate - pass branch
steps.notes: Transformed colonies confirmed; dispose recovery droplet.

steps.name: Transformation QC gate - fail branch
steps.notes: No viable transformed cells detected (electroporation failure or no assembly). Drain recovery droplet. Compiler known bug: drain lowered to dispose in IR.

steps.name: Final cleanup
steps.notes: Dispose transformation QC signal and oil phase droplet. Terminal block. In the actual protocol, Steps S1-S19 are repeated 15 more times (16 total iterations) using the same electrode path, mixing channel, and incubation channel. Reservoir droplets refilled via SU-8 capillary between iterations.

golden_gate.additional_reagent: T4 DNA ligase 2.5 U/uL + 0.05% Pluronic F-127

cross_contamination.strategy: HFE 7500 biocompatible oil + 0.05% w/v Pluronic F-127 surfactant additive (no wash steps)
cross_contamination.validation: 30 colonies picked from pProm1_BCD2-gfp plate; all 30 showed BCD2 banding pattern (Fig 4c); statistical analysis in Supporting Information

automation_system.feedback: Impedance sensing; Vsense threshold ~0.15 V for ~0.2 uL droplets
automation_system.software: In-house automation; controls droplet movement, feedback sensing, syringe pumps, valves, Peltier, function generator (Fig S3)

description:
Source link: https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/d4lc01002g.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1039/D4LC00962B

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic Bead Densification and Processing Coupled to Single-Molecule Array (DMF-Simoa) for Tumor Necrosis Factor-alpha (TNF-alpha) Quantification

REAGENTS USED:
  - TNF-alpha Sample (solution of TNF-alpha antigen, 100 uL aliquot)
  - Simoa Capture Beads (anti-TNF-alpha antibody-coated superparamagnetic beads, 25 uL suspension containing 15000 functionalized beads)
  - Biotinylated Detection Antibody (anti-TNF-alpha detection antibody, 20 uL aliquot)
  - Wash Buffer (PBS containing 0.01% w/v Tetronic 90R4 surfactant)
  - Streptavidin-beta-Galactosidase (SbG) Reagent (enzyme label conjugate)
  - RGP Substrate (resorufin-beta-D-galactopyranoside fluorogenic substrate)

STEPS:
1. Off-chip pre-incubation: Mix the 100 uL TNF-alpha sample, 25 uL bead suspension (15000 beads), and 20 uL detection antibody together; incubate for 20 min off-chip on a shaker at 800 rpm to form antibody-antigen-bead sandwich immunocomplexes.
2. Stepwise sample loading onto DMF: Dispense the entire pre-incubated sample-bead mixture onto the sample reservoir electrode; sequentially load, split, and remove waste from ~9 uL segments over ~12 closed-loop, capacitance-monitored cycles to fully transfer the sample into the device while retaining beads on the densifying electrode (>98% bead retention).
3. Bead washing: Wash the densified beads with fresh wash buffer over multiple wash cycles (5 repeats) to remove unbound sample components.
4. SbG incubation: Deliver the streptavidin-beta-galactosidase reagent to the densified beads and incubate for 5 min at 25C to label captured immunocomplexes with enzyme.
5. Post-SbG washing: Wash the labeled beads again with fresh wash buffer over multiple wash cycles (5 repeats) to remove excess unbound SbG.
6. Substrate addition and detection: Deliver the RGP (resorufin-beta-D-galactopyranoside) substrate to the washed, labeled beads and incubate for 30 min at 25C to allow enzymatic conversion to fluorescent resorufin; the processed bead suspension is then collected and transferred to a microtiter plate/SR-X imager, where beads are loaded into femtoliter-sized microwells and imaged to determine the average number of enzyme labels per bead (digital single-molecule readout), then the analyzed droplet is discarded.

INTERPRETATION: Successful DMF-Simoa TNF-alpha quantification is confirmed by calibration curves of average enzyme labels per bead vs. TNF-alpha concentration obtained via the DMF-processed workflow that are comparable to those obtained via conventional manual microtiter-plate Simoa processing, with more than 98% bead retention during stepwise sample loading and no significant loss of assay sensitivity, supporting the feasibility of a miniaturized, automated DMF-Simoa platform for ultrasensitive biomarker detection.

module fluorescence

manifest tnf_sample
manifest simoa_beads
manifest detection_antibody
manifest wash_buffer
manifest sbg_reagent
manifest rgp_substrate

instructions:

sample = dispense 100 units of tnf_sample
beads = dispense 25 units of simoa_beads
dab = dispense 20 units of detection_antibody

a = mix sample with beads
b = mix a with dab for 60s
heat b at 23c for 20m
dispose b

repeat 12 times {
    sample2 = dispense 9 units of tnf_sample
    beads2 = dispense 25 units of simoa_beads
    c = mix sample2 with beads2 for 5s
    dispose c
}

repeat 5 times {
    wash = dispense 250 units of wash_buffer
    beads3 = dispense 25 units of simoa_beads
    d = mix wash with beads3 for 45s
    dispose d
}

sbg = dispense 20 units of sbg_reagent
beads4 = dispense 25 units of simoa_beads
e = mix beads4 with sbg for 60s
heat e at 25c for 5m

repeat 5 times {
    wash2 = dispense 250 units of wash_buffer
    beads5 = dispense 25 units of simoa_beads
    f = mix wash2 with beads5 for 45s
    dispose f
}

rgp = dispense 50 units of rgp_substrate
beads6 = dispense 25 units of simoa_beads
g = mix beads6 with rgp
heat g at 25c for 30m

tnf_reading = detect fluorescence on g for 5m
dispose g

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic Colorimetric Detection of Nitroaromatic Explosive Particles (TNT/DNT) via Reaction with KOH

REAGENTS USED:
  - TNT Sample (commercial grade 2,4,6-trinitrotoluene, or pure 2,4-dinitrotoluene, dispensed by pipette onto the electrowetting chip)
  - KOH Reagent (potassium hydroxide solution that reacts with nitroaromatic explosives to form colored complexes)

STEPS:
1. Dispensing: Manually pipette a droplet of TNT (or DNT) sample and a droplet of KOH reagent onto the electrowetting chip.
2. Merging: Merge the two droplets by applying voltages to the appropriate electrodes.
3. Mixing: Electrowetting-enabled mixing -- transport/shuttle the merged droplet across electrodes to enhance mixing flow, forming the colored reaction complex.
4. Detection: At the completion of mixing, measure the absorbance of the colored complex at room temperature using an on-chip LED (with characteristic absorbance peaks reported at 336 nm and 510 nm for TNT-KOH and 407 nm and 657 nm for DNT-KOH complexes).
5. Disposal: Discard the analyzed droplet after the absorbance reading is taken.

INTERPRETATION: Successful colorimetric explosive detection is confirmed by a linear calibration curve of absorbance versus TNT concentration (y = 0.0056x + 0.0145, R^2 = 0.9863) over the 4-20 ug/mL range, yielding a calculated detection limit of approximately 2.6 ug/mL -- competitive with antibody-based surface plasmon resonance competition assays (7.8 ug/mL). Because the TNT and DNT colored complexes produce mutually independent absorbance peaks, TNT can be quantitatively estimated even in the presence of DNT, a combination common in contaminated soil, supporting on-site, automated colorimetric detection of land-mine and munitions-related nitroaromatic contamination without requiring an experienced chemical analyst.

manifest KOH_Reagent

instructions:

// --- dispensing: TNT/DNT sample and KOH reagent droplets ---
tnt = dispense TNT_Sample
koh = dispense KOH_Reagent

// --- electrowetting-enabled mixing: merge and shuttle across electrodes ---
reaction = mix tnt with koh for 5s

// --- colorimetric detection: LED absorbance measurement of colored complex ---
absorbance = detect fluorescence on reaction for 30s

dispose reaction

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Automated Digital Microfluidic Magnetic-Particle-Based Chemiluminescent Immunoassay for Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone (TSH), DOE-Optimized Protocol

REAGENTS USED:
  - Antibody-Coated Paramagnetic Microparticles (Abbott Laboratories; ~3.0 x 10^8 particles/mL in DMF-compatible particle diluent, pH 10, 5 um diameter, magnetic susceptibility 1.05)
  - TSH Standards (0, 0.4, and 4 uIU/mL, supplemented with 0.05% v/v Pluronic L64)
  - DMF-Compatible Wash Buffer (custom-prepared, used for post-capture and post-conjugate particle washing)
  - HRP-Conjugated Anti-TSH Detection Antibody (mouse monoclonal, 2 ug/mL working solution in conjugate diluent)
  - Hydrogen Peroxide / Stable Peroxide Substrate Component (SuperSignal ELISA Femto, supplemented with 0.025% v/v Pluronic L64)
  - Luminol-Enhancer Solution (SuperSignal ELISA Femto chemiluminescent substrate, second component)

STEPS (Optimized Immunoassay protocol, as validated against the pilot/DOE-derived parameters):
1. Particle Capture: Dispense antibody-coated paramagnetic particles from a reservoir and separate from the particle diluent using the magnetic lens; deliver five pooled sample droplets (~4 uL) of TSH standard to the immobilized particles and mix for 3 min (the DOE-optimized incubation time).
2. First Wash: Wash the particles four times in wash buffer, separating particles from the supernatant after each wash using the magnetic lens.
3. Conjugate Binding: Dispense HRP-conjugated anti-TSH detection antibody, deliver to the immobilized particles, and mix for 2 min.
4. Second Wash: Wash the particles four times in wash buffer, separating from the supernatant; unlike the pilot protocol, the chemiluminescent reaction is initiated immediately after the final wash rather than queuing particles in wash buffer, to avoid signal loss from unequal wait times.
5. Chemiluminescent Reaction: Resuspend the washed particles in one droplet of H2O2 substrate component, merge with one droplet of luminol-enhancer solution, and mix for 4 min until the chemiluminescent signal saturates.
6. Detection: Using the integrated, motorized photomultiplier tube (PMT), collect the chemiluminescent signal ~10 s after the substrate mixing step, for each of the four replicate measurements per concentration.
7. Endpoint: Average the four replicate measurements at each TSH concentration and fit to a linear equation; the limit of detection (LOD) is defined as the concentration corresponding to the blank (0 uIU/mL) signal plus 3 standard deviations of the blank measurements. Dispose of the reacted droplet after measurement.

INTERPRETATION: A successful, correctly optimized assay is confirmed by a chemiluminescent signal that increases monotonically with TSH concentration (0, 0.4, 4 uIU/mL) with low inter-replicate variability (CV 6-10%), yielding a linear calibration curve with an LOD of ~0.15 uIU/mL -- sufficiently low to screen for hyperthyroidism (TSH < 0.3 uIU/mL) -- and reduced sample incubation time (3 min) relative to the non-optimized prototype protocol (6 min), demonstrating that the DOE-derived parameters (five sample droplets, 3 min capture incubation) improve both sensitivity and speed relative to previous non-automated work.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A NOTE ON HOW CLOSELY THIS MATCHES THE CITED SOURCE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The authored BioScript code is a direct translation of the paper's "Optimized Immunoassays" procedure (Experimental Section, p. 9641), which itself modifies the seven-step pilot protocol described immediately prior in the same section. It captures the particle-capture incubation (3 min, five pooled droplets), the two four-cycle wash stages bracketing conjugate addition, the HRP-conjugate incubation (2 min), the H2O2/luminol-enhancer chemiluminescent reaction (4 min mix), and the ~10 s PMT signal-collection window, using the optimized (not pilot) timing values throughout. Because BioScript's grammar has no primitive for magnetic separation, particle pelleting/supernatant removal is folded implicitly into each wash-loop's dispense-mix-dispose cycle (mirroring the wash-loop pattern used in the ciprofloxacin reference script) rather than being modeled as a distinct operation. Because BioScript does not support explicit droplet-count or merged-volume parameters, the paper's "five pooled unit droplets (~4 uL)" sample delivery is represented as a single nominal "dispense 20 units of tsh_standard" rather than five discrete droplet-merge operations; the "20 units" figure is an arbitrary placeholder volume, not a value sourced from the paper. The two four-times wash loops are modeled with BioScript's repeat construct rather than as four explicit unrolled dispense/mix/dispose steps. A "heat f at 25c for 10s" instruction was added immediately before detection as a scripting convenience to explicitly stage the substrate at a nominal bench-top temperature prior to signal collection; this step is a modeling addition and is not described in the paper, which specifies only mixing followed directly by PMT measurement with no explicit thermal-control step at this point. Source link: https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/3e68/c4204aa7be83590b2fbb4e51db36dcdc64f3.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1007/s10404-007-0161-8

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Open-Surface Digital Microfluidic Potentiometric/Conductometric Titration

REAGENTS USED:
  - Analyte solution (sample droplet, created from an on-chip analyte reservoir)
  - Titrant solution (diluent droplet, created from an on-chip titrant reservoir)

STEPS:
1-2. Droplet creation: Create one droplet from the analyte reservoir and one droplet from the titrant reservoir.
3-4. Splitting: Split each of the two droplets into two smaller droplets.
5-6. First merge: Merge one analyte half with one titrant half to form a 50:50 mixture; return the unused titrant half to the reservoir.
7. Mixing: Mix the merged 50:50 droplet by rotating it clockwise then counterclockwise over four grid electrodes.
8. First split-for-detection: Split the mixed 50:50 droplet into two. Send one half to the detection site to record its pH or conductivity reading.
9. Second dilution: Merge the retained half with a fresh analyte droplet to form a 75:25 (analyte:titrant) mixture; mix by rotation and split again.
10. Second split-for-detection: Send one half to the detection site to record its pH or conductivity reading; create and split another fresh analyte droplet.
11. Third dilution: Merge the retained half with the fresh analyte droplet to form an 88:12 (analyte:titrant) mixture.
12. Final detection: Send the resulting droplet to the detection site to record its pH or conductivity reading.

INTERPRETATION: The protocol demonstrates that serial dilution/titration -- normally requiring continuous titrant addition on a benchtop potentiometer or conductometer -- can instead be reprogrammed as a sequence of droplet splitting, merging, and rotational mixing steps on an open-surface digital microfluidic array. Each detection-site reading (pH or conductivity) at the 50:50, 75:25, and 88:12 dilution stages allows the assay to be halted once the target endpoint is reached, illustrating the reprogrammability advantage of open-surface droplet manipulation over fixed-channel or continuous-flow microfluidics.

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code is a direct translation of the paper's proposed potentiometric/conductometric titration protocol (Fig. 9), which builds a serial dilution series (50:50, 75:25, 88:12 analyte:titrant) through repeated droplet splitting, merging, and rotational mixing, with a detection-site reading taken at each stage. Because BioScript's confirmed grammar exposes no explicit 'split' primitive (droplet transport/splitting is compiler-inferred rather than an authored instruction, per the reference PCR and ciprofloxacin scripts), each 'split-then-merge-to-a-new-ratio' step in the paper is instead modeled as a freshly weighted 'dispense' of analyte/titrant at the target ratio, which reproduces the same dilution-refinement outcome without depending on unconfirmed syntax. Nested 'if' blocks are used to model the paper's iterative refine-until-endpoint logic: a dilution stage's droplet is only disposed and replaced by the next, more concentrated mixture if its detection reading has not yet reached a target threshold. Only the core titration sequence (Fig. 9) is captured; the paper's separate EWOD/magnetofluidics/wire-guide actuation mechanisms, contact-angle and work-of-adhesion theory, and other applications (glucose sensing, immunoassays, PCR, single-cell analysis) described elsewhere in the paper are not modeled.

Detection in the paper is potentiometric (pH meter) or conductometric, not fluorescent. 'fluorescence' is used only because it is the sole detect module confirmed working in the reference BioScript files; it stands in for a generic quantitative pH/conductivity signal read.

The paper does not specify a numeric pH/conductivity endpoint value; 40 is a placeholder threshold used to demonstrate the iterative refine-until-endpoint control flow described qualitatively in the text, and should be replaced with the analyte's real target reading.

description:
================================================================================
PROTOCOL: triDrop Digital Microfluidic Electroporation for CAR-T Cell Therapy
================================================================================

SOURCE LINK : https://www.shihmicrolab.ca/_files/ugd/f0a828_07554e20c82e469c9608111c6af47aa0.pdf
PAPER DOI   : https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.analchem.4c06911
JOURNAL     : Analytical Chemistry, 2025, Vol. 97, pp. 11026-11034
PLATFORM    : Digital Microfluidic (DMF) -- triDrop system
TARGET CELL : Primary Human T Cells
APPLICATION : CAR-T cell therapy production and functional immune cell engineering

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
OVERVIEW
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The triDrop system is a three-droplet digital microfluidic electroporation
platform designed to transfect primary human T cells while minimizing cellular
harm. It achieves:

  - Transfection efficiency : >95% (mRNA delivery)
  - Cell viability (18h)    : 80-85% post-EP (vs ~65% for Neon/Nucleofector)
  - Payload requirement     : 50 ng mRNA per reaction (10x less than Nucleofector)
  - Cell input              : 0.5 x 10^5 cells per reaction
  - Cost reduction          : up to 20-fold vs gold standard methods
  - CAR-T killing efficacy  : up to 2-fold improvement vs conventional EP systems
  - Gene dysregulation      : only 32 genes dysregulated (vs 105 Neon, 89 NF)

The key advantage of triDrop is its three-droplet geometry: a cell+payload
droplet is flanked by buffer droplets, physically separating cells from the
anode and cathode. This limits exposure to Joule heating, pH changes, metal
ion contamination, and electrolytic byproducts that cause cell death and
transcriptomic dysregulation in conventional EP systems.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
REAGENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  ID                    DESCRIPTION                         QUANTITY / SPEC
  --------------------  ----------------------------------  ----------------------
  tCells                Primary human T cells               0.5 x 10^5 per rxn
  electroporationBuffer Electroporation buffer              1 unit per rxn
  mrnaPayload           mRNA payload                        50 ng per rxn
                        (alt: Cas9 RNP for CRISPR KO/KI)  (alt: 2.5 pmol RNP)
                        (alt: CAR construct for CAR-T)
  recoveryBuffer        Recovery buffer                     1 unit per rxn
  il2Media              Culture media with IL-2             400 IU/mL; 1 unit
  rajiCells             Raji cells (CD19-positive target)   1 unit per rxn
  mcf7Cells             MCF-7 cells (CD19-negative ctrl)    1 unit per rxn

  NOTE: T cells must be electroporated within 24h after removal of activation
  beads. Cells must remain in EP buffer for no more than 15 min before
  transfer to recovery buffer.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
MODULES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  electroporationAssay  : Handles the electroporation procedure on DMF chip
  cytokineDetection     : Handles IFN-gamma and TNF-alpha ELISA detection

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ELECTROPORATION PARAMETERS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Pulse count    : 3 pulses
  Voltage        : 1600 V_DC
  Pulse duration : 10 ms each                [FIX: was incorrectly 10s in old file]
  Temperature    : 37 degrees C

  NOTE: These parameters correspond to Neon-equivalent settings used in the
  paper. The triDrop DMF platform applies these pulses across the merged
  three-droplet structure, with the cell+payload droplet isolated from direct
  electrode contact by flanking buffer droplets.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 1 -- Prepare Cell Droplet in Electroporation Buffer
  Operations:
    cellDrop      = dispense 1 units of tCells
    epBuffer1     = dispense 1 units of electroporationBuffer
    cellsInBuffer = mix cellDrop with epBuffer1 for 2s
  Notes:
    - Cell count: 0.5 x 10^5 per reaction (triDrop optimum)
    - Mixing ensures uniform cell suspension in EP buffer

STEP 2 -- Prepare Payload Droplet
  Operations:
    payloadDrop   = dispense 1 units of mrnaPayload
  Notes:
    - mRNA payload at 50 ng per reaction for transfection experiments
    - Substitute with cas9_rnp (2.5 pmol) for CRISPR knockout/knock-in
    - Substitute with car_construct for CAR-T production runs

STEP 3 -- triDrop Three-Droplet Fusion
  Operations:
    bufferFlank    = dispense 1 units of electroporationBuffer
    cellPayloadMix = mix cellsInBuffer with payloadDrop for 5s
    triDropMerged  = mix cellPayloadMix with bufferFlank for 3s
  Notes:
    - The flanking buffer droplet is the defining feature of triDrop geometry
    - It physically separates the cell+payload volume from electrode surfaces
    - Limits Joule heating and electrolytic byproduct (pH, metal ions, gas
      bubbles) exposure that cause cellular dysfunction in conventional EP

STEP 4 -- Electroporation Pulse
  Operations:
    heat triDropMerged at 37c for 10ms       [FIX: was 10s; correct value is 10ms]
  Notes:
    - Maps to DMF energy delivery: 3 x 1600 V_DC pulses, 10 ms each
    - The heat primitive in BioScript is void (no return value / no assignment)
    - triDrop geometry minimizes current-induced cell damage vs Neon/NF

STEP 5 -- Transfer to IL-2 Recovery Buffer
  Operations:
    recoveryDrop   = dispense 1 units of recoveryBuffer
    il2Drop        = dispense 1 units of il2Media
    recoveryMix    = mix recoveryDrop with il2Drop for 5s
    recoveredCells = mix triDropMerged with recoveryMix for 10s
  Notes:
    - Transfer must occur within 15 min of pulse application
    - Recovery buffer: culture media containing 400 IU/mL IL-2
    - Prompt transfer is critical for achieving 80-85% viability at 18h

STEP 6 -- Post-EP Incubation
  Operations:
    heat recoveredCells at 37c for 18h
  Notes:
    - Incubation at 37 degrees C post-electroporation
    - heat is void in BioScript -- recoveredCells variable survives intact
    - triDrop achieves 80-85% viability at 18h (vs ~60% for Neon/NF)
    - All three systems recover to >80% viability only after 72h post-EP
    - triDrop cells show no significant dysregulation of IL-2, TNF-alpha,
      or IFN-gamma (critical cytokines for cellular therapy functionality)

STEP 7 -- Binary Split Tree on recoveredCells            [NEW: replaces old step 7]
  Operations:
    rcA  = split recoveredCells into 2
    rcB  = split recoveredCells into 2
    rcA0 = split rcA into 2
    rcA1 = split rcA into 2
    rcB0 = split rcB into 2
    rcB1 = split rcB into 2
  Notes:
    - Required because this compiler greedily assigns index [0] to every use
      of a split variable when the same name appears more than once as an
      operand, causing index collisions on same-type operations (e.g. two mix
      calls consuming the same split result both get assigned [0]).
    - Fix: full binary tree of 3 splits produces 4 uniquely-named leaf
      variables (rcA0, rcA1, rcB0, rcB1), each used exactly once downstream.
    - rcA0 -> Raji 24h detect arm
    - rcA1 -> Raji 48h continuation arm
    - rcB0 -> MCF-7 (neg ctrl) 24h detect arm
    - rcB1 -> MCF-7 (neg ctrl) 48h continuation arm

STEP 8 -- Start Raji (CD19+) Co-Culture -- Positive Arm  [NEW: replaces old step 7]
  Operations:
    rajiDrop1          = dispense 1 units of rajiCells
    rajiDrop2          = dispense 1 units of rajiCells
    coculture24hDetect   = mix rcA0 with rajiDrop1 for 24h
    coculture24hContinue = mix rcA1 with rajiDrop2 for 24h
  Notes:
    - Anti-CD19 CAR-T cells co-cultured with Raji (CD19-positive) target cells
    - E:T ratio 1:1 (paper Fig. 4c)
    - CAR expression peaks at 24h post-EP, >80% expression at 6h post-EP
    - Two dedicated droplets: one for 24h detect, one for 48h continuation
      (single variable used per operation -- no index collision)

STEP 9 -- Start MCF-7 (CD19-) Co-Culture -- Negative Control Arm  [NEW]
  Operations:
    mcf7Drop1              = dispense 1 units of mcf7Cells
    mcf7Drop2              = dispense 1 units of mcf7Cells
    negControl24hDetect    = mix rcB0 with mcf7Drop1 for 24h
    negControl24hContinue  = mix rcB1 with mcf7Drop2 for 24h
  Notes:
    - MCF-7 cells are CD19-negative; engineered CAR-T cells should produce
      no cytokine signal here (confirms CAR specificity)
    - Matches paper Fig. 4a,b "T/M" (T cells with MCF-7) condition
    - Two dedicated droplets: one for 24h detect, one for 48h continuation

STEP 10 -- Detect Cytokine Secretion at 24h             [FIX: replaces old step 8]
  Operations:
    result24h    = detect cytokineDetection on coculture24hDetect for 30s
    negResult24h = detect cytokineDetection on negControl24hDetect for 30s
  Notes:
    - Detects IFN-gamma and TNF-alpha in supernatant via ELISA
    - triDrop CAR-T cells secrete ~2-fold more antitumor cytokines than
      Nucleofector-engineered cells when cultured with CD19+ targets
    - IFN-gamma: p=0.006 (24h), p=0.05 (48h) vs Nucleofector
    - TNF-alpha:  p=0.02  (24h), p=0.016 (48h) vs Nucleofector
    - No cytokine production observed with CD19-negative MCF-7 cells
      (confirms high CAR specificity)
    - Each detect consumes one dedicated droplet (no index collision)

STEP 11 -- Extend Co-Culture to 48h                     [FIX: replaces old step 9]
  Operations:
    il2Extend1    = dispense 1 units of il2Media
    il2Extend2    = dispense 1 units of il2Media
    coculture48h  = mix coculture24hContinue with il2Extend1 for 24h
    negControl48h = mix negControl24hContinue with il2Extend2 for 24h
  Notes:
    - heat is void in BioScript and cannot produce a new fluid variable;
      mix with fresh il2Media is used as the timed-hold primitive instead
    - This is the compiler-legal pattern for multi-stage incubation
      (cf. ace_crispr_raf1_sorafenib.bs: maintainCtrl* = mix fresh* with
      cell* for 24h)
    - Old step 9 incorrectly used "heat coculture24h" then re-detected on
      the same variable, causing an UndefinedVariable compiler crash

STEP 12 -- Detect Cytokine Secretion at 48h             [NEW: replaces old step 9]
  Operations:
    result48h    = detect cytokineDetection on coculture48h for 30s
    negResult48h = detect cytokineDetection on negControl48h for 30s
  Notes:
    - Second cytokine readout at 48h timepoint (paper Fig. 4a,b)
    - Killing efficiency at 4:1 E:T ratio:
        24h: ~61% relative target cell killing
        48h: ~85% relative target cell killing
    - Activated Pan T cells (control): ~23% (24h) and ~45% (48h) at 4:1 ratio

STEP 13 -- Evaluate Killing Efficiency and Cleanup       [FIX: replaces old step 10]
  Operations:
    if (result48h > 0) {
        dispose coculture48h
        dispose negControl48h
    } else {
        drain coculture48h
        drain negControl48h
    }
    dispose result24h
    dispose result48h
    dispose negResult24h
    dispose negResult48h
  Notes:
    - QC gate: result48h > 0 confirms valid cytokine signal at 48h
      (old file used >= 85 which is a simulation-level threshold not
      appropriate as a BioScript conditional gate variable)
    - Both arms (Raji + MCF-7) cleaned up in both branches
    - Old step 10 had a double-free bug: dispose inside if-branch followed
      by unconditional drain on the same variable; fixed by using a proper
      if/else with dispose vs drain, no variable used twice
    - negResult24h and negResult48h disposed unconditionally after branch

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
OPTIONAL BRANCH -- CRISPR KNOCKOUT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Substitute STEP 2 payload with:
    payloadDrop = dispense 1 units of cas9Rnp   (2.5 pmol Cas9 RNP)

  triDrop CRISPR knockout results (TRAC locus, 0.5 x 10^5 cells):
    - Knockout efficiency : 68-75%
    - Viability           : ~80%
    - RNP required        : 2.5 pmol (vs 50 pmol for Nucleofector)
    - No significant difference vs Neon (p=0.26)
    - Nucleofector achieves only 14% KO under same low-cell conditions

  Volumetric normalization of RNP (not cellular normalization) is critical
  for achieving high delivery efficiency in the triDrop system.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
OPTIONAL BRANCH -- CRISPR KNOCK-IN
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Co-deliver with STEP 2:
    ssODN donor template (90bp) + Cas9 RNP + p53 siRNA

  triDrop knock-in results:
    - Knock-in efficiency       : >60%, up to 80% insertion efficiency
    - Proliferative capacity    : 2.5-fold cell increase (vs 3.3-fold control)
    - Neon/Nucleofector show impaired proliferation post-KI
    - Payload requirement       : at least 10-fold less than Nucleofector

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TRANSCRIPTOMIC PROFILE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Dysregulated genes 6h post-EP (log fold change >1 or <-1, p<0.05):
    triDrop      : 32 genes   (most similar to no-EP control)
    Nucleofector : 89 genes
    Neon         : 105 genes

  Dysregulated Reactome pathways (average Z-score >2.0 or <-2.0):
    triDrop      : 79 pathways
    Nucleofector : 134 pathways
    Neon         : 130 pathways

  34 genes commonly dysregulated in Neon+Nucleofector but NOT in triDrop,
  including stress response genes PPP1R15A, SESN2 and immunotherapy-relevant
  genes TSC22D3 and CD48.

  triDrop does NOT upregulate apoptosis, cellular stress, or inflammation
  pathways -- preserving full T cell functionality for immunotherapy.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Compiler    : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based, Python 3)
  Target      : -t ir (Intermediate Representation + Control Flow Graph)
  Command     : python3 main.py -d -i <file.bs> -t ir -o ./output -cfg

  KNOWN COMPILER BEHAVIOURS (relevant to this protocol):

  1. heat is void -- no assignment allowed.
     WRONG : coculture48h = heat coculture24h at 37c for 24h
     RIGHT : heat coculture24h at 37c for 24h
             coculture48h = mix coculture24h with il2Media for 24h

  2. detect consumes its fluid operand -- variable is spent after detect.
     Must split before detect if fluid is needed downstream.

  3. Greedy index collision on split arrays -- when the same split variable
     name appears as operand to N operations of the same type, the compiler
     assigns index [0] to ALL of them instead of [0]..[N-1].
     Fix: each split variable must appear exactly once as an operand.
     Use a binary split tree to produce unique leaf variables for each consumer.

  4. ASCII-only source files -- ANTLR4 FileStream rejects non-ASCII bytes.
     All comments must use ASCII characters only. No Unicode arrows (->),
     box-drawing characters, degree symbols, or em-dashes in source files.

  CFG STRUCTURE (this protocol):
    BB1  main         -- entry block: all operations through detect at 48h
    BB2  bsbbif_2_t   -- if-true branch: dispose coculture48h, negControl48h
    BB3  bsbbif_3_f   -- if-false branch: drain coculture48h, negControl48h
    BB4  bsbbif_4_j   -- join block: dispose all result variables, NOP

  CFG EDGES:
    BB1 -> BB2 (result48h > 0)
    BB1 -> BB3 (result48h <= 0)
    BB2 -> BB4
    BB3 -> BB4

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
BIOSCRIPT FILES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  .bs file  : triDrop_electroporation.bs   (BioScript source)
  .json file: triDrop_electroporation.json (protocol in JSON format)
  .txt file : triDrop_electroporation.txt  (this file)
  .dot file : triDrop_electroporation_main_dag.dot (CFG output)
  .ir file  : triDrop_electroporation.ir   (IR output)

================================================================================
END OF PROTOCOL
================================================================================

description:
Source Link: https://www.shihmicrolab.ca/_files/ugd/f0a828_d655eb72036446bb9a7b585b7ad3212f.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1002/admt.202300719

Protocol Details:

Title: A Tri-Droplet Liquid Structure for Highly Efficient Intracellular Delivery in Primary Mammalian Cells Using Digital Microfluidics (triDrop Transfection)

Overview:
The triDrop protocol uses digital microfluidics (DMF) to electroporate mammalian cells with biological payloads (dextran, plasmids, mRNA, or Cas9 ribonucleoproteins) using a three-droplet liquid structure. Two outer "liquid electrode" droplets of high-conductivity buffer flank a central sample droplet of low-conductivity buffer containing cells and payload. Applying voltage to the outer droplets generates a focused, homogeneous electric field through the central droplet, enabling efficient electroporation while protecting cells from electrochemical damage and excessive current.

1. Reagents and Materials
- High conductivity buffer (liquid electrode): PBS with 0.05% Pluronics F-68, conductivity ~16 mS/cm (immortalized cells) or ~32 mS/cm custom buffer (primary T cells in RPMI)
- Low conductivity buffer (sample/electroporation buffer): Type T electroporation buffer with 0.05% Pluronics F-68, conductivity ~8 mS/cm
- Cell types: HEK293, HeLa, Jurkat cells, and primary human CD4+ T cells
- Payloads: FITC-tagged dextran (70, 250, 2000 kDa), eGFP plasmid (~5 kb), eGFP mRNA (~1 kb), Cas9 ribonucleoprotein (RNP) with gRNA
- DMF device: bottom plate with chromium driving/reservoir electrodes, dielectric (SU-8 5) and hydrophobic (Teflon-AF) coating; top plate with gold electroporation electrodes and grounding plane

2. Cell Preparation
- Resuspend cells in low-conductivity electroporation buffer containing the desired payload
- Target concentration: at least 2 x 10^7 cells/mL
- Cell number per reaction: 20,000-40,000 cells (low-cell-number workflow)
- For plasmid/mRNA experiments: resuspend at 4 x 10^7 cells/mL with payload at 1.275 pg/cell (plasmid) or 2 pg/cell (mRNA)
- For CRISPR experiments: form Cas9 RNP by combining sgRNA (100 pmol per 1 million cells) with Cas9 protein (50 pmol per 1 million cells), incubate 10 min at room temperature before adding to cells

3. Reservoir Loading
- Load three reservoirs on the DMF device:
  - Two outer reservoirs: high-conductivity buffer (6 microliters each)
  - Middle reservoir: cells + payload in low-conductivity buffer (6 microliters)
- Reservoirs filled by pipetting fluid onto the bottom plate edge and applying driving potentials to draw fluid in

4. Droplet Dispensing and Actuation
- Dispense three ~1 microliter droplets (one from each reservoir) via pulling/necking
- Actuate the cell-containing droplet to the center of the electroporation site
- Actuate the two high-conductivity droplets to the outer edges of the electroporation site
- Actuation achieved via AC potentials of 300-400 V RMS at 15 kHz

5. triDrop Formation (Merging)
- Merge the three droplets into a continuous tri-droplet chain by actuating the high-conductivity droplets toward the central sample droplet
- Mixing between droplets is limited to diffusion; three discrete regions remain distinguishable for over 30 seconds post-merge

6. Electroporation Pulse
- Immediately upon merging, apply high-voltage DC square-wave pulses to the gold electrodes in contact with the flanking droplets
- Standard conditions (immortalized cell lines, e.g., HEK293/HeLa): 3 pulses, 200 VDC, 10 ms duration; effective field range 0.5-0.63 kV/cm
- Jurkat/HeLa optimized range: 0.75-0.90 kV/cm
- Primary T cells: 3 pulses, 450 V, reduced pulse duration of 1-3 ms (shorter durations improve viability)
- Electroporation pulse circuit: 8-pin optocoupler, DC power source, Arduino Uno-controlled pulse generator (100-450 VDC, 1-10 ms duration range)
- Total electroporation process completes within 5 seconds of droplet merging
- Total time from reservoir loading to electroporation: ~3 minutes for three triDrop structures

7. Off-Chip Transfer
- Remove the top plate immediately after electroporation
- Pipette the total tri-droplet volume (~3 microliters) off-chip into a well plate pre-loaded with warmed culture media
- Maximum cell exposure time in electroporation buffer: 20 minutes (to preserve viability)
- HEK293/HeLa cells: recovered in flat-bottom 48-well plates
- Jurkat/primary T cells: recovered in U-bottom 96-well plates

8. Post-Electroporation Recovery and Culture
- Incubate cells for recovery for more than 24 hours at 37 C in a humidified chamber with 5% CO2
- Primary T cells monitored daily for up to 7 days post-electroporation; viability becomes comparable to non-electroporated controls by day 5
- For CRISPR knockout experiments, cells are cultured for 72-96 hours post-electroporation prior to analysis

9. Analysis and Validation
- Flow cytometry (e.g., BD FACS Melody) to measure:
  - Viability ratio (VR): ratio of viable (DAPI-negative) electroporated cells to non-electroporated control
  - Transfection efficiency (TE): percentage of fluorescent living cells above threshold relative to total living cells
  - Mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) fold-change: ratio of MFI in transfected cells to non-transfected control
  - Knockout efficiency: percentage of living cells below a fluorescence threshold (for gene knockout assays)
- Fluorescence microscopy (bright-field and fluorescent imaging) for morphology and expression confirmation
- For CRISPR knockout validation (e.g., beta-2-microglobulin or TRAC locus): stain with FITC-tagged antibody and analyze fluorescence shift via flow cytometry

10. Key Reported Outcomes
- Transfection efficiency: greater than 95% with greater than 95% viability for dextran delivery in immortalized cells (HEK293, HeLa, Jurkat)
- Plasmid delivery: TE 71% / VR 90% (HEK293); TE 60% / VR 99% (HeLa)
- mRNA delivery in Jurkat: TE 95%, VR 98%, MFI fold-change greater than 500, using only 2 pg mRNA/cell
- Primary CD4+ T cells: plasmid TE >38%, VR 81%; mRNA TE 89%, VR 90% (using high-conductivity culture media flanks)
- CRISPR knockout efficiency: 35% average (beta2M, Jurkat); 70% average, up to 80% peak per introduction (beta2M, primary T cells); average 30-67% (TRAC locus, 10-condition arrayed primary T-cell experiment using fewer than 1,000,000 total cells)
- Comparable performance to Neon, Lonza, and Celetrix benchtop electroporation systems, while requiring substantially fewer cells (20,000-40,000 vs. 200,000-1,000,000+)

description:
Source link: https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/d1lc01068a%20paper.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1039/D1LC01068A

Protocol Details
ASSAY TYPE

Portable Sample Processing for Molecular Assays: Application to Zika Virus Diagnostics (Integrated Extraction, NASBA Amplification, and Cell-Free Toehold Switch Detection on Digital Microfluidics)

REAGENTS USED
Plasma Sample (human blood plasma containing Zika virus RNA)
Lysis Buffer
Proteinase K
Carrier RNA
Magnetic Beads (silica-coated paramagnetic particles for nucleic acid capture)
Wash Buffer
Ethanol Wash Buffer
Elution Water
NASBA Master Mix
NASBA Enzymes
Cell-Free (CF) Master Mix (cell-free protein expression system components)
Toehold Switch DNA (synthetic riboregulator circuit for Zika RNA detection)
STEPS
Lysis & Digestion: Mix the plasma sample with lysis buffer, heat at 95°C for 2 minutes, add Proteinase K and mix for 30 seconds, add carrier RNA and mix for 30 seconds, then incubate at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Nucleic Acid Capture: Dispense and mix magnetic beads with the lysed sample for 5 minutes to bind viral RNA.
Primary Washes: Perform 4 successive wash cycles using wash buffer, mixing for 1 minute per wash followed by supernatant disposal.
Secondary Washes: Perform 2 successive wash cycles using ethanol wash buffer, mixing for 1 minute per wash followed by disposal.
Elution: Dispense elution water and mix with the captured beads for 3 minutes to recover purified RNA.
NASBA Amplification: Mix the RNA eluate with NASBA master mix, heat at 65°C for 2 minutes, cool to 41°C for 10 minutes, add NASBA enzymes, and incubate at 41°C for 90 minutes.
Cell-Free Detection: Mix cell-free master mix with toehold switch DNA for 30 seconds, combine with the NASBA amplification product, incubate at 37°C for 175 minutes, and detect fluorescence/colorimetric signal for 5 minutes.
Endpoint: Evaluate the Zika detection result against a threshold (≤ 50) to selectively dispose of the reaction mixture.
INTERPRETATION

Successful Zika virus detection is confirmed by robust target amplification through NASBA, followed by cell-free toehold switch expression of a reporter protein, producing a measurable fluorescent or colorimetric signal that indicates the presence of viral RNA in the plasma sample.

module fluorescence

manifest plasma_sample

manifest proteinase_k

manifest magnetic_beads

manifest ethanol_wash_buffer
manifest elution_water

manifest nasba_enzymes
manifest cf_master_mix

instructions:

// ---- Pre-processing (P): lysis and reversible RNA capture on magnetic beads ----
sample = dispense 5 units of plasma_sample
lysis = dispense 5 units of lysis_buffer
lysed = mix sample with lysis for 30s
heat lysed at 95c for 2m

pk = dispense 1 units of proteinase_k
lysed_pk = mix lysed with pk for 30s

carrier = dispense 1 units of carrier_rna
lysed_carrier = mix lysed_pk with carrier for 30s
heat lysed_carrier at 23c for 15m

beads = dispense 12 units of magnetic_beads
captured = mix lysed_carrier with beads for 5m

// ---- DMF Extraction (E_DMF): bead wash cycles (optimized to 6 washes) ----
repeat 4 times {
    wash = dispense 6 units of wash_buffer
    washed = mix captured with wash for 1m
    dispose wash
}

repeat 2 times {
    ewash = dispense 6 units of ethanol_wash_buffer
    ewashed = mix captured with ewash for 1m
    dispose ewash
}

eluent = dispense 5 units of elution_water
rna_eluate = mix captured with eluent for 3m

// ---- DMF Amplification (A_DMF): NASBA anneal, cool/equilibrate, amplify ----
mmix = dispense 3 units of nasba_master_mix
anneal_mix = mix rna_eluate with mmix
heat anneal_mix at 65c for 2m
heat anneal_mix at 41c for 10m

enzymes = dispense 1 units of nasba_enzymes
amp_mix = mix anneal_mix with enzymes
heat amp_mix at 41c for 90m

// ---- Cell-free protein expression assay (C): toehold switch colorimetric detection ----
cfmix = dispense 6 units of cf_master_mix
switch = dispense 1 units of toehold_switch_dna
cf_reaction = mix cfmix with switch for 30s

detection_mix = mix cf_reaction with amp_mix for 60s
heat detection_mix at 37c for 175m

zika_result = detect fluorescence on detection_mix for 5m

if (zika_result <= 50) {
    dispose detection_mix
}

dispose detection_mix
