description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Sensitive Detection and Quantification of SARS-CoV-2 in Saliva
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-021-91835-7
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-021-91835-7
Journal      : Scientific Reports, 2021, Vol. 11, Article 12425
Platform     : Saliva-based nucleic acid testing pipeline; BSL3 TRIzol RNA extraction,
               BSL1 RT-PCR (CFX384, Bio-Rad) and ddPCR (QX200, Bio-Rad) analysis
Institution  : University of Chicago Medical Center (IRB 20-0520)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a comprehensive saliva-based SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid testing pipeline
developed and validated at the University of Chicago Medical Center. It provides a complete
alternative to nasal or nasopharyngeal swab testing using two parallel molecular readouts:
real-time reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR) and droplet digital PCR (ddPCR), both targeting
the nucleocapsid N1 and N2 genes and the RnaseP internal control.

Specimens were prospectively collected from 137 curbside outpatients (92 symptomatic, 45
asymptomatic pre-operative) and 29 COVID-19 inpatients, with paired nasal swab (NS) results
from the CLIA-certified clinical microbiology laboratory (CML) using the FDA-EUA Cepheid
Xpert Xpress system as the comparator gold standard.

The protocol is divided into three sequential phases:
  1. TRIzol-based RNA extraction (TRE method) from saliva specimens in a BSL3 facility
  2. RT-PCR assay (relative quantification; positive calling Ct < 40 for N1 or N2)
  3. ddPCR assay (absolute quantification; empirical threshold from 45 pre-op negatives)

Key outcomes:
  - RT-PCR saliva: 100% concordance with CML-positive cases (curbside and inpatient cohorts)
  - ddPCR saliva: 93.75% concordance (curbside); potential for higher sensitivity at low
    viral loads vs nasal swabs and RT-PCR (15 additional positives vs CML NS assay)
  - Viral load range: 10^6-fold across patients; saliva shows more uniform distribution
    than nasal swabs (less operator variability in volume collection)


COHORTS
-------
Curbside outpatients (N = 137):
  - Symptomatic (COVID-19 testing): N = 92
  - Asymptomatic (pre-operative screening, used as ddPCR threshold derivation cohort): N = 45
  - All SARS-CoV-2 negative by CML nasal swab (pre-op cohort)

Inpatients (N = 29):
  - All confirmed SARS-CoV-2 positive on hospital admission by CML
  - NS and saliva collected several days after admission (post-diagnosis)
  - CML identified 14/29 NS samples as positive at research collection timepoint


SPECIMEN COLLECTION
-------------------
Saliva:
  - Self-collection by drool technique (spitting into sterile tube to the 2 mL line)
  - 2 mL Zymo DNA/RNA Shield (ZymoR1100-50) added immediately at point of collection
  - Transported to BSL3 facility for RNA extraction

Nasal Swab (NS):
  - Anterior nares nasal swab collected by research team into 1 mL Amies transport solution
    (Thermo Scientific)
  - One NS sent to CML for standard-of-care analysis using FDA-EUA Cepheid Xpert Xpress
    (targets: N2 and envelope E gene; positive if Ct < 45 for either)
  - Second NS sent to BSL3 for research RT-PCR and ddPCR analysis alongside saliva


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Saliva Specimen Receipt
  Input      : SalivaSpecimen (1 mL pre-stabilised aliquot)
  Operation  : dispense
  Notes      : 1 mL aliquot of Zymo-stabilised saliva enters the TRIzol extraction
               protocol. BioScript `dispense` abstracts receipt into the workflow.

Step 2 | TRIzol LS Addition
  Reagents   : TRIzol LS (Thermo Fisher Scientific, #10296010), 3 mL
  Operation  : mix (30 s)
  Volumes    : 1 mL sample + 3 mL TRIzol LS
  Notes      : Brief vortexing to homogenise. Guanidinium thiocyanate in TRIzol
               denatures proteins and protects RNA from RNases during extraction.

Step 3 | Chloroform Addition and Phase Emulsification
  Reagents   : Chloroform, 0.6 mL
  Operation  : mix (15 s)
  Notes      : 0.6 mL chloroform added to TRIzol lysate; brief vortexing creates
               water-in-organic emulsion. Separates RNA (aqueous upper phase) from
               proteins and DNA (organic phase and interphase).

Step 4 | Phase Separation Centrifugation
  Condition  : 12,000 x g, 4 C, 15 min
  Operation  : heat at 4c for 15m (BioScript abstraction for centrifugation)
  IR output  : heat(phaseMixture) @ 4.0 CELSIUS @ 900.0 SECOND
  Phases     : (1) Colourless upper aqueous phase (RNA)
               (2) White interphase (DNA/protein)
               (3) Red-pink organic phase (protein/lipid)
  Notes      : BioScript has no centrifugation primitive. `heat at 4c` models the
               cold centrifuge condition, consistent with the samlali and moazami
               reference .bs files' use of `heat` for non-heating physical operations.

Step 5 | Aqueous Phase Transfer and Precipitation Setup
  Reagents   : Isopropanol (1 mL), Glycogen (1 uL)
  Operation  : mix x2 (10 s each)
  Volumes    : 0.8 mL upper aqueous phase + 1 mL isopropanol + 1 uL glycogen
  Notes      : Aqueous phase carefully transferred to new tube (interphase avoided).
               Glycogen acts as co-precipitant to improve RNA pellet visibility and
               yield at low concentrations typical of saliva samples.

Step 6 | Overnight RNA Precipitation
  Condition  : -20 C overnight (minimum 12 h)
  Operation  : heat at 4c for 720m (BioScript abstraction; IR: 43200.0 SECOND)
  Notes      : Paper states "-20 C overnight or room temperature for 10 min."
               Cold overnight path encoded for maximum yield. Negative temperatures
               not tested in lilott8/BioScript compiler; 4 C used as functional
               cold abstraction. The compiler correctly emits 43200.0 SECOND (12 h).

Step 7 | RNA Pellet Collection Centrifugation
  Condition  : 12,000 x g, 4 C, 10 min
  Operation  : heat at 4c for 10m (IR: 600.0 SECOND)
  Notes      : RNA pellet collected; supernatant discarded.

Step 8 | 75% Ethanol Wash
  Reagents   : 75% ethanol, 2 mL
  Operation  : mix (30 s)
  Notes      : Washes residual isopropanol and salts from pellet. Salivary fluids
               are known PCR inhibitors (Ochert et al., PCR Methods Appl. 1994,
               cited as ref. 14 in paper); ethanol wash removes inhibitory substances.

Step 9 | Ethanol Wash Centrifugation
  Condition  : 7,500 g, 4 C, 5 min
  Operation  : heat at 4c for 5m (IR: 300.0 SECOND)
  Notes      : Re-pellets RNA; ethanol supernatant discarded.

Step 10 | Ethanol Evaporation
  Condition  : Room temperature (25 C), 5-10 min
  Operation  : heat at 25c for 10m (IR: 600.0 SECOND)
  Notes      : Upper bound (10 min) encoded. Over-drying reduces RNA solubility;
               under-drying causes ethanol carry-over PCR inhibition.

Step 11 | RNA Resuspension and QC
  Reagents   : RNase-free water (50 uL), Qubit RNA HS Kit
  Operation  : mix (2 min) + detect (30 s)
  Storage    : -80 C
  QC module  : ddPCR_RnaseP_Detection (proxy for Qubit fluorometric measurement)
  Notes      : Final RNA extract resuspended in 50 uL RNase-free water. Qubit RNA
               HS Kit used to assess quantity and quality before PCR. rnaQcMix
               disposed after QC signal detected; rnaExtract used in steps 12-18.
               TRE method relative efficiency vs QVK (QIAmp Viral RNA Mini Kit): 17%.
               High assay sensitivity (LOD: 1 copy/reaction) compensates for lower yield.

Step 12 | RT-PCR Reaction Assembly (N1, N2, RnaseP channels)
  Reagents   : TaqPath One-Step RT-PCR Master Mix (ThermoFisher), N1/N2/RnaseP probe/
               primer sets (IDT #10006770), Precision Blue Real-Time PCR Dye (Bio-Rad)
  Operation  : mix (sequential; 3 parallel channels)
  Reaction   : 20 uL total per channel
               5 uL TaqPath Master Mix
               2 uL probe/primer set (N1, N2, or RnaseP)
               0.1 uL Precision Blue Real-Time PCR Dye
               6.4 uL RNA extract
               6.5 uL PCR-grade water
  Controls   : Serial dilution of SARS-CoV-2 RNA Standard (Exact Diagnostics #COV019)
               run alongside each RT-PCR plate. DNA positive control: IDT #10006625.
               Negative control: Millipore nuclease-free water (extraction-processed).
  Notes      : Three parallel reactions targeting N1, N2, and RnaseP assembled from
               the same RNA extract. BioScript `dispense SalivaSpecimen` (x3) models
               aliquoting identical RNA into three separate reaction tubes.
               Assembly order: masterMix + primerSet (5s) -> add RT dye (5s)
               -> add RNA aliquot (10s).

Step 13 | RT-PCR Thermocycling
  Instrument : CFX384 Touch Real-time PCR Detection System (Bio-Rad)
  Software   : CFX Maestro
  Protocol   : CDC 2019-nCoV RT-PCR diagnostic panel (Revision 3, 2020)
  Stages     :
               Stage 1: Reverse transcription    25 C / 2 min   (IR: 120.0 s)
               Stage 2: RT incubation            50 C / 15 min  (IR: 900.0 s)
               Stage 3: Polymerase activation    95 C / 2 min   (IR: 120.0 s)
               Stage 4: 45 cycles (compressed)   55 C / 45 min  (IR: 2700.0 s)
                 [actual cycle: 95 C / 3 s denaturation + 55 C / 30 s anneal/extension]
  Performance:
               Efficiency: >99.25% for N1 and N2 (Supplementary Fig. 1)
               LOD: 1 copy/reaction (Ct ~38.2 for N1, ~38.6 for N2)
  Notes      : 45-cycle PCR amplification compressed into a single `heat at 55c for 45m`
               block (2700 s in IR). BioScript has no cycle-loop primitive; each isothermal
               stage is emitted as a discrete heat instruction in the IR. This is the same
               thermocycler abstraction used in the moazami reference .bs file (heat-shock
               stages encoded as separate heat calls).

Step 14 | RT-PCR Fluorescence Readout and Positive Calling
  Modules    : rtPCR_N1_Detection, rtPCR_N2_Detection, rtPCR_RnaseP_Detection
  Duration   : 30 s per channel
  Channels   : FAM (N1, N2 TaqMan probes); RnaseP (internal extraction control)
  Rule       : Positive if Ct < 40 for N1 OR N2 (CDC recommendation)
               Ct = 45 assigned to undetermined (no amplification) reactions
  Results    :
               Curbside: 16/16 CML-positive samples detected (100%); +7 additional
               positives vs CML NS assay (Fig. 2c,d)
               Inpatients: 14/14 CML positives detected (100%); +9 additional (Fig. 5)
  CFG gate   :
               Pass (BB2, bsbbif_2_t): rtPCR_N1_Signal > 0
                 -> dispose(rtPCR_rxn_N1, N2, RnaseP)
               Fail (BB3, bsbbif_3_f): rtPCR_N1_Signal <= 0
                 -> drain(rtPCR_rxn_N1, N2, RnaseP)
               Join (BB4, bsbbif_4_j): dispose RT-PCR signals; enter ddPCR branch
  Notes      : N1 used as primary gate (stronger LOD). BioScript does not support compound
               OR conditionals in a single if statement. RnaseP confirms extraction quality
               but is not part of the positive/negative QC gate.

Step 15 | ddPCR Reaction Assembly (N1, N2, RnaseP channels)
  Reagents   : One-step ddPCR Supermix (Bio-Rad), Reverse Transcriptase + DTT (Bio-Rad),
               N1/N2/RnaseP probe/primer sets (IDT #10006770, same as RT-PCR)
  Operation  : mix (sequential; 3 parallel channels)
  Reaction   : 20 uL total per channel
               5 uL One-step ddPCR Supermix
               2 uL reverse transcriptase
               1 uL 300 mM DTT
               2 uL probe/primer set (N1, N2, or RnaseP)
               6.4 uL RNA extract
  Notes      : Identical IDT probe/primer sets used for both RT-PCR and ddPCR (same primers
               and probes combination per paper Methods). Assembly order: supermix + RT/DTT
               (5s) -> add primer set (5s) -> add RNA aliquot (10s).

Step 16 | Droplet Generation
  Equipment  : Bio-Rad QX200 droplet generator (manual or automated)
  Oil        : Bio-Rad ddPCR droplet generation oil for probes (#1863005)
  Output     : ~20,000 nanoliter-sized water-in-oil droplets per reaction
  Operation  : mix with DropletGeneratorOil for 2m (abstracts emulsification)
  Notes      : Each droplet contains zero or one target RNA molecule, enabling absolute
               digital quantification without a standard curve (Hindson et al., Nat.
               Methods 2013, ref. 19 in paper). After generation, emulsion transferred to
               sealed 96-well plate for thermocycling.

Step 17 | ddPCR Thermocycling
  Instrument : C-1000 Thermal Cycler (Bio-Rad)
  Ramping    : 2.5 C/s between all stages
  Stages     :
               Stage 1: Initial hold                25 C / 2 min    (IR: 120.0 s)
               Stage 2: Reverse transcription        50 C / 60 min   (IR: 3600.0 s)
               Stage 3: Polymerase activation        95 C / 10 min   (IR: 600.0 s)
               Stage 4: 45 cycles (compressed)       55 C / 45 min   (IR: 2700.0 s)
                 [actual cycle: 95 C / 30 s denaturation + 55 C / 60 s anneal/extension]
               Stage 5: Signal stabilisation         98 C / 10 min   (IR: 600.0 s)
               Stage 6: Hold                          4 C / 60 min   (IR: 3600.0 s)
  Performance:
               LOD (N1): 0.06 CN/uL (Supplementary Fig. 2)
               LOD (N2): 0.21 CN/uL
               Dilution LOD: N1 detected at 1:1,000,000 dilution in pool of negatives
               (10x more sensitive than RT-PCR at 1:100,000; Supplementary Table 1)
               Inhibitor resistance: ddPCR concentrates targets per droplet, reducing
               bias from salivary PCR inhibitors (refs 20-22)
  Notes      : 4 C hold approximated as 60 m (3600 s in IR); paper allows overnight hold.
               45-cycle PCR compressed to single heat block (2700 s). Ramping speed 2.5 C/s
               maintained between all stages per paper Methods.

Step 18 | Droplet Reading and Positive Calling
  Equipment  : Bio-Rad QX200 droplet reader
  Software   : Quantasoft (Bio-Rad); raw fluorescence amplitude -> CN/uL + droplet count
  Modules    : ddPCR_N1_Detection, ddPCR_N2_Detection, ddPCR_RnaseP_Detection
  Duration   : 30 s per channel
  Rule (NS)  : CN/uL > 0.1 AND > 2 positive droplets for N1 OR N2 (Bio-Rad recommendation)
  Rule (saliva): BOTH CN/uL AND positive droplet count must exceed empirical threshold
               (mean + 2*SD from 45 pre-operative SARS-CoV-2 negative individuals;
               Supplementary Table 2; data distribution in Supplementary Fig. 7)
  Results    :
               Curbside: 15/16 CML-positive samples detected (93.75%); 31/92 total
               positives vs 16/92 by CML NS assay (Fig. 2e,f)
               Inpatients: 11/14 CML positives; 17 total positives (Fig. 5)
               Reproducibility: 91.3% concordance on re-test of 46 saliva specimens
               (Supplementary Fig. 8); 4 discordant samples attributed to RNA
               degradation after ~5 months storage
  CFG gate   :
               Pass (BB5, bsbbif_5_t): ddPCR_N1_Signal > 0
                 -> dispose(ddEmulsion_N1, N2, RnaseP)
               Fail (BB6, bsbbif_6_f): ddPCR_N1_Signal <= 0
                 -> drain(ddEmulsion_N1, N2, RnaseP)
               Terminal (BB7, bsbbif_7_j): dispose(ddPCR signals, rnaQcSignal, rnaExtract)
                 -> NOP (compiler standard exit node)
  Notes      : N1 used as primary gate (LOD 0.06 CN/uL vs N2 0.21 CN/uL).
               Saliva shows more uniform viral load distribution vs nasal swabs (less
               operator variability in collection volume). Supercarriers (>10,000 CN/mL)
               and their link to superspreading identified as key clinical application
               (refs 32, 33 in paper; Fig. 4).


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : abasiyanik2021_sars_cov2_saliva_detection.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG shape      : Diamond-diamond (two sequential QC gates)
               BB1 -> BB2/BB3 -> BB4 -> BB5/BB6 -> BB7
Duration units : All durations converted to seconds (s) or minutes (m) only
               (BioScript supports s and m; h token not supported)
               15 min centrifugation  ->  15m  (IR: 900.0 SECOND)
               Overnight -20 C        -> 720m  (IR: 43200.0 SECOND, 12 h minimum)
               RT-PCR 45 cycles       ->  45m  (IR: 2700.0 SECOND, compressed)
               ddPCR RT step          ->  60m  (IR: 3600.0 SECOND)
               ddPCR 45 cycles        ->  45m  (IR: 2700.0 SECOND, compressed)
               ddPCR 4 C hold         ->  60m  (IR: 3600.0 SECOND, approximated)
Modules (6)    : rtPCR_N1_Detection, rtPCR_N2_Detection, rtPCR_RnaseP_Detection,
                 ddPCR_N1_Detection, ddPCR_N2_Detection, ddPCR_RnaseP_Detection
Manifests (18) : SalivaSpecimen, NasalSwabSpecimen, TrizolLS_Reagent, Chloroform,
                 Isopropanol, Glycogen, Ethanol_75pct, RNaseFreeWater,
                 TaqPath_MasterMix, N1_ProbePrimerSet, N2_ProbePrimerSet,
                 RnaseP_ProbePrimerSet, PrecisionBlue_RTDye, SARS_CoV2_RNA_Standard,
                 ddPCR_Supermix_OneStep, ReverseTranscriptase_DTT,
                 DropletGeneratorOil, QubitRNA_HS_Reagent
Key abstractions:
  - Centrifugation (no BioScript primitive) -> `heat at 4c for <duration>`
    Consistent with reference .bs files: samlali uses `heat at 25c` for 30 s
    electrode actuation; moazami uses `heat at 42c` / `heat at 4c` for heat-shock.
  - -20 C overnight precipitation -> `heat at 4c for 720m` (compiler-safe cold approx.)
  - 45-cycle PCR thermocycle -> single `heat at 55c for 45m` block (no cycle-loop
    primitive in BioScript; same compression used in moazami for heat-shock phases)

    conditional per BioScript grammar (no compound OR in if statement)

    BioScript behaviour; not a protocol error)

    correctly emitted with @ time annotations, correct BB labels and jump targets

protocol.title: Sensitive Detection and Quantification of SARS-CoV-2 in Saliva
protocol.platform: Saliva-based nucleic acid testing pipeline (RT-PCR + ddPCR); BSL3 RNA extraction, BSL1 analysis
protocol.objective: Validate saliva as an alternative specimen for sensitive SARS-CoV-2 detection using RT-PCR and ddPCR, benchmarked against EUA-certified nasal swab testing by a CLIA-certified clinical microbiology laboratory (CML)

saliva.method: Self-collection by drool technique (spitting into sterile tube to 2 mL line)
saliva.stabilisation: 2 mL Zymo DNA/RNA Shield (ZymoR1100-50) added immediately at collection
saliva.transport: To BSL3 facility for RNA extraction

nasal_swab.method: Anterior nares nasal swab (NS) collected by research team
nasal_swab.clinical_analysis: CML using FDA-EUA Cepheid Xpert Xpress (targets N2 + E gene; positive if Ct < 45 for either)

rna_extraction.primary_method: TRIzol-based RNA extraction (TRE); 17% relative efficiency vs QVK
rna_extraction.glycogen: 1 uL co-precipitant for improved pellet recovery at low RNA concentrations
alternative_kits_evaluated: QIAmp MinElute Virus DNA/RNA Spin Kit (QVDRK)

rt_pcr.master_mix: TaqPath One-Step RT-PCR Master Mix (Thermo Fisher Scientific)
rt_pcr.probe_primer_sets: IDT 2019-nCoV CDC EUA (#10006770): N1, N2, RnaseP
rt_pcr.precision_blue_dye: Precision Blue Real-Time PCR Dye (Bio-Rad), 0.1 uL per reaction
rt_pcr.negative_control: Millipore nuclease-free water processed with RNA extraction methods
rt_pcr.instrument: CFX384 Touch Real-time PCR Detection System (Bio-Rad)

ddpcr.supermix: One-step ddPCR Supermix (Bio-Rad), 5 uL per reaction
ddpcr.probe_primer_sets: IDT (#10006770): N1, N2, RnaseP (same as RT-PCR)
ddpcr.droplet_generator: Bio-Rad QX200 (manual or automated); ~20,000 nanoliter-sized droplets per reaction

steps.name: Saliva specimen receipt
steps.notes: 1 mL aliquot of pre-stabilised saliva (already combined with Zymo DNA/RNA Shield at collection) enters TRIzol extraction protocol. BioScript `dispense` abstracts receipt of specimen into the extraction workflow.

steps.name: TRIzol LS addition
steps.notes: 3 mL TRIzol LS added to 1 mL sample (saliva or nasal swab per paper Methods). Brief vortexing to homogenise. Guanidinium thiocyanate denatures proteins and protects RNA from RNases.

steps.name: Chloroform addition and phase emulsification
steps.notes: 0.6 mL chloroform added; brief vortexing creates water-in-organic emulsion for phase separation. Chloroform separates RNA (aqueous upper phase) from protein and DNA (organic/interphase lower phases).

steps.name: Phase separation centrifugation
steps.notes: Centrifuge 15 min at 12,000xg, 4 C. Three phases form: (1) colourless upper aqueous phase (RNA), (2) white interphase (DNA/protein), (3) red-pink organic phase (protein/lipid). BioScript `heat at 4c for 15m` abstracts centrifugation (no native primitive in BioScript).

steps.name: Aqueous phase transfer and RNA precipitation setup
steps.notes: 0.8 mL colourless upper aqueous phase carefully transferred to new tube (avoid interphase). 1 mL isopropanol and 1 uL glycogen added. Glycogen acts as co-precipitant to improve RNA pellet visibility and yield at low concentrations. BioScript `mix` abstracts manual transfer and addition.

steps.name: Overnight RNA precipitation at -20 C
steps.notes: Paper states 'kept at -20 C overnight or at room temperature for 10 min.' Cold path encoded (higher yield). BioScript encodes as `heat at 4c for 720m` (43200 s in IR). Negative temperatures not tested with lilott8/BioScript compiler; 4 C used as functional cold abstraction.

steps.name: RNA pellet collection centrifugation
steps.notes: Centrifuge 10 min at 12,000xg, 4 C to pellet RNA. Supernatant discarded. BioScript `heat at 4c for 10m` (600 s in IR).

steps.name: 75% ethanol wash
steps.notes: 2 mL 75% ethanol added to pellet; vortexed to wash away residual isopropanol and salts. Salivary fluids are known PCR inhibitors (paper ref. 14: Ochert et al., PCR Methods Appl. 1994). Ethanol wash removes inhibitory substances.

steps.name: Ethanol wash centrifugation
steps.notes: Centrifuge 5 min at 7500g, 4 C to re-pellet RNA. Supernatant discarded. BioScript `heat at 4c for 5m` (300 s in IR).

steps.name: Ethanol evaporation
steps.notes: Pellet air-dried at room temperature for 5-10 min to evaporate residual ethanol. Over-drying reduces solubility; under-drying causes ethanol carry-over PCR inhibition. Upper bound (10 min) encoded. BioScript `heat at 25c for 10m` (600 s in IR).

steps.name: RNA resuspension and QC
steps.qc_module: ddPCR_RnaseP_Detection (used as proxy for Qubit fluorometric QC)
steps.notes: Pellet resuspended in 50 uL RNase-free water. Quantity and quality assessed by Qubit RNA HS Kit. BioScript models Qubit QC as a detect step using the RnaseP module as a proxy for RNA integrity. rnaQcMix disposed after detection; rnaExtract used in downstream PCR steps.

steps.name: RT-PCR reaction assembly (N1, N2, RnaseP channels)
steps.notes: Three parallel RT-PCR reactions assembled targeting N1, N2, and RnaseP (internal control). Serial dilution of SARS-CoV-2 RNA Standard run alongside each plate as positive control. BioScript `dispense SalivaSpecimen` (x3) models aliquoting from the same RNA extract into three separate reactions. Assembly sequence: masterMix + primerSet (5s) -> add RT dye (5s) -> add RNA aliquot (10s).

steps.name: RT-PCR thermocycling (CFX384 Touch, Bio-Rad)
steps.notes: 45-cycle PCR amplification compressed into single `heat at 55c for 45m` block (2700 s in IR). This is a standard BioScript thermocycler abstraction: the compiler has no cycle-loop primitive; each isothermal stage is emitted as a separate heat instruction. Same pattern used in moazami reference file (heat-shock stages encoded as discrete heat calls).

steps.name: RT-PCR fluorescence readout and positive calling
steps.positive_calling_rule: Ct < 40 for N1 OR N2 (CDC recommendation; same threshold for saliva and NS)

channels.FAM: N1 and N2 TaqMan probes (SARS-CoV-2 targets)

steps.notes: N1 used as primary gate (stronger LOD). BioScript does not support compound OR conditionals in a single if statement; N1 is primary signal per CDC positive-calling logic (positive if N1 OR N2 < 40). RnaseP result not used in QC gate but encoded for completeness.

steps.name: ddPCR reaction assembly (N1, N2, RnaseP channels)
steps.notes: Same IDT probe/primer sets (#10006770) as RT-PCR. Three parallel reactions targeting N1, N2, and RnaseP assembled from the same RNA extract. BioScript `dispense SalivaSpecimen` (x3) models aliquoting. Assembly sequence: supermix + RT/DTT (5s) -> add primer set (5s) -> add RNA aliquot (10s).

steps.name: Droplet generation (~20,000 droplets per reaction)
steps.oil: Bio-Rad ddPCR droplet generation oil for probes (#1863005)
steps.notes: Each assembled reaction fractionated into ~20,000 nanoliter-sized droplets at the QX200 droplet generator. Each droplet contains zero or one target RNA molecule, enabling absolute digital quantification without standard curve. `mix ddPCR_rxn with DropletGeneratorOil for 2m` abstracts emulsification at droplet generator.

steps.name: ddPCR thermocycling (C-1000 thermal cycler, Bio-Rad)

performance.dilution_series_lod: N1 target detected at 1:1,000,000 dilution in pool of negatives (Supplementary Table 1)
performance.inhibitor_resistance: ddPCR concentrates targets in smaller reactions, reducing bias from salivary PCR inhibitors (refs 20-22)

steps.notes: 4 C hold encoded as `heat at 4c for 60m` (3600 s in IR); paper protocol allows overnight hold. 45-cycle PCR compressed to single heat block at 55 C (2700 s). Ramping speed 2.5 C/s applied between all stages.

steps.name: Droplet reading and positive calling (QX200, Quantasoft)
steps.positive_calling_rule_NS: CN/uL > 0.1 AND > 2 positive droplets for N1 OR N2 (Bio-Rad manufacturer recommendation for nasal swab)
steps.positive_calling_rule_saliva: BOTH CN/uL AND positive droplet count exceed empirical threshold (mean + 2*SD from 45 pre-operative SARS-CoV-2 negative individuals; Supplementary Table 2)
steps.empirical_threshold_derivation: 45 asymptomatic pre-operative participants, all SARS-CoV-2 negative by CML nasal swab; standard formula: mean + 2*SD (Supplementary Fig. 7)

channels.FAM: N1 and N2 TaqMan probes (SARS-CoV-2 targets)

pass.result_curbside: 15/16 CML-positive samples detected (93.75% concordance); 31/92 total positives vs 16/92 by CML NS assay (Fig. 2e,f)

steps.reproducibility: Independent re-test of 46 saliva specimens (19 positive, 27 negative) confirmed 91.3% concordance (Supplementary Fig. 8). RNA degradation after ~5 months storage explains 4 discordant samples.
steps.notes: N1 used as primary QC gate (LOD 0.06 CN/uL vs N2 at 0.21 CN/uL). ddPCR identified 15 more positives than CML NS assay (curbside cohort), especially at low viral copy numbers (black circles, Fig. 2b). Viral load range spans 10^6-fold across patients (Supplementary Table 4); supercarriers defined as >10,000 CN/mL.

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.content: TRIzol RNA extraction (S1-S11) + RT-PCR assembly and thermocycle (S12-S14) + ddPCR assembly and thermocycle (S15-S17)

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_4_j
basic_blocks.content: dispose RT-PCR signals; ddPCR reaction assembly + droplet generation + thermocycle + readout (S15-S18)

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_7_j
basic_blocks.content: dispose(ddPCR_N1_Signal, ddPCR_N2_Signal, ddPCR_RnaseP_Signal, rnaQcSignal, rnaExtract); NOP

cfg.cfg_shape: Diamond-diamond (two sequential QC gates, each with true/false branches converging at a join node)

results_summary.saliva_distribution: More uniform viral load distribution vs nasal swabs (less operator variability in collection volume)

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Ultrasensitive Digital Quantification of Cytokines and Bacteria Predicts Septic Shock Outcomes
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-020-16124-9
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-16124-9
Journal      : Nature Communications, 2020, Vol. 11, Article 2607
Platform     : Digital proximity ligation assay (dPLA) + droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) on Bio-Rad QX200


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a combined dPLA and ddPCR pipeline for simultaneous femtomolar-sensitivity
quantification of host cytokines (IL-6 and TNF-alpha) and bacterial DNA biomarkers (gram-negative
(GN) 16S rRNA gene, gram-positive (GP) 16S rRNA gene, and the antibiotic-resistance gene blaTEM)
from human biological samples (BALF and plasma). The method overcomes the limitations of conventional
ELISA (poor sensitivity, incompatibility with simultaneous nucleic acid measurement) by combining
proximity ligation assay (PLA) with droplet digital PCR (ddPCR), achieving sub-femtomolar protein
detection and single-copy DNA resolution.

The protocol is divided into three functional phases:
  1. DNA extraction (QIAamp cador Pathogen Mini Kit) from human BALF or plasma
  2. dPLA for IL-6 and TNF-alpha quantification with ddPCR readout
  3. Triplex ddPCR for simultaneous GN + GP + blaTEM quantification

Results are applied to two clinical cohorts:
  - Cohort 1 (BALF): 23 asthma patients vs 11 healthy subjects
    Finding: elevated GN bacteria and IL-6 in asthma vs healthy (p<0.01 and p<0.01)
  - Cohort 2 (Plasma/ICU): 32 septic shock patients at time points t1 and t2 (t3 for Group B)
    Finding: temporal changes in IL-6 and GN bacteria predict mortality; decision-tree
    classifier achieves >90% accuracy using only t1 measurements of GN and TNF-alpha

Assay performance outperforms many commercial ELISA kits:
  IL-6 LOD  : 0.02 pg/mL (0.73 fM) in BALF; 0.84 pg/mL (40 fM) in plasma (SDB-II)
  TNF-alpha LOD : 0.08 pg/mL in both BALF and plasma (HMB)
  GN LOD    : 0.06 CPN/uL (0.09 aM); GP LOD: 0.06 CPN/uL (0.09 aM)
  blaTEM LOD: 0.9 CPN/uL (1.57 aM); CV as low as 1.3%; stable >100 days


INSTRUMENT AND PLATFORM
-----------------------
ddPCR System   : Bio-Rad QX200 droplet digital PCR system
Droplet Gen.   : Bio-Rad QX200 AutoDG (#1864002)
Droplet Reader : Bio-Rad QX200 droplet reader (#1864003)
Analysis       : QuantaSoft Analysis Pro v1.0.596
Plates         : Eppendorf 96-Well twin.tec PCR plates (#951020362)
Tubes          : 0.2 uL thin-walled PCR tubes (Thermo Fisher #AB-0620 / #AB-1182)
Centrifuge     : 500 g for plasma; 6000 g and 20000 g for DNA extraction columns


REAGENTS
--------
Antibodies:
  - Biotinylated anti-human IL-6 polyclonal goat antibody (R&D Systems #BAF206)
  - Biotinylated anti-human TNF-alpha polyclonal goat antibody (R&D Systems #BAF210)

Recombinant Standards:
  - Recombinant human IL-6 (R&D Systems #206-IL-010)
  - Recombinant human TNF-alpha (R&D Systems #210-TA-020)
  - Recombinant human IL-10 (R&D Systems #217-IL-005) [cross-reactivity control]

Proximity Probe Kits:
  - TaqMan Protein Assays Open Kit (Thermo Fisher #4453745) [IL-6 / TNF-alpha in plasma]
  - TaqMan Protein Assay-II kit (Thermo Fisher #4483013) [triplex BALF assay]

Sample Dilution Buffers:
  - SDB-II (Thermo Fisher #4483013): IL-6 quantification in plasma
  - HMB (homemade Nong's buffer): TNF-alpha quantification in plasma
    Composition: 1x PBS, 1 mM d-biotin (Sigma #47868), 0.1% gelatin (Aurion #900.03),
    0.05% Tween-20 (Sigma #P9416), 100 nM goat IgG (Thermo Fisher #50643345),
    0.1 mg/mL salmon sperm DNA (Invitrogen #15632-011), 4 mM EDTA (Invitrogen #AM9261)
  - 0.1x TM Buffer (Biochain #K3011010-1) + 0.5% gelatin: IL-6 and TNF-alpha in BALF

ddPCR Supermix:
  - ddPCR EvaGreen Supermix (Bio-Rad #186-4033) [simplex EvaGreen assays]
  - ddPCR Supermix for Probes (Bio-Rad #186-3023) [TaqMan probe assays; required for multiplex]

DNA Extraction: QIAamp cador Pathogen Mini Kit (Qiagen #54104)

Primers and Probes (sequences in Supplementary Table 5):
  - Bac_fwd / Bac_rev: universal forward/reverse primers targeting 16S rRNA conserved region
  - GN_probe: HEX-labeled hydrolysis probe (GN-specific 16S rRNA region)
  - GP_probe: FAM-labeled hydrolysis probe (GP-specific 16S rRNA region)
  - TEM_fwd / TEM_rev / TEM_probe: FAM-labeled blaTEM primers and probe
  Simplex concentrations: 900 nM primers; 200 nM TaqMan probes
  Triplex concentrations: 900 nM all primers; 340 nM GN probe; 180 nM GP probe; 380 nM blaTEM probe

gBlock Standards (IDT): GN 16S rRNA, GP 16S rRNA, blaTEM; diluted in AVE + 0.1 mg/mL salmon sperm DNA


SAMPLE COHORTS
--------------

Cohort 1 — BALF (Asthma vs Healthy):
  Asthma (n=23): Average age 46 [38-53]; 53% female; 65% white, 30% black, 4% other.
                 Criteria: EPR 3 Guidelines on Asthma. Bronchoscopy within 4 weeks of visit.
  Healthy (n=11): No respiratory medication; good health.
  IRB: University of Chicago; written informed consent.

Cohort 2 — Plasma/ICU (Septic Shock):
  Protocol IRB: 18-1163 (University of Chicago); Declaration of Helsinki.
  Total (n=32): Adults >18 y; Medical ICU; vasoactive medication; suspected infection;
                enrolled within first 24h of Sepsis-3 shock diagnosis.
  Blood collection: 30 mL sodium citrate tubes; plasma isolated within 2h (500 g, 15 min);
                    stored at -80 C. All patients received antibiotics prior to collection.
  Time points:
    t1 = within first 24h of diagnosis (enrollment)
    t2 = 24-48h after t1 (all patients)
    t3 = upon resolution of septic shock (Group B only)
  Clinical scores: APACHE-II and SOFA on day of enrollment.
  Patient groups:
    Group A (n=7):  Early recovery. Shock resolved within 48h (no vasopressors; MAP >65 mmHg).
                    Samples at t1 and t2.
    Group B (n=13): Late recovery. Shock resolved after 48h.
                    Samples at t1, t2, and t3.
    Group C (n=12): Death. Never resolved shock. Died in ICU on vasopressors.
                    Samples at t1 and t2.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | DNA Extraction from Human Sample
  Input          : 100 uL human plasma or BALF
  Kit            : QIAamp cador Pathogen Mini Kit (Qiagen #54104)
  Protocol       :
    1. Combine 100 uL sample + 100 uL PBS + 20 uL proteinase K
    2. Add 100 uL buffer VXL; incubate RT for 15 min
    3. Add 350 uL buffer ACB; mix thoroughly
    4. Load lysate to QIAamp Mini column; centrifuge 6000 g, 1 min
    5. Wash with AW1 buffer; centrifuge 6000 g, 1 min
    6. Wash with AW2 buffer; centrifuge 6000 g, 1 min
    7. Add 100 uL AVE elution buffer; incubate 1 min; centrifuge 20000 g, 1 min
    8. Collect eluate; store at -20 C until ddPCR
  Background correction: PBS blank extraction performed in parallel; average background
                         signal subtracted from all human sample measurements.
  Note           : Preconcentration of sample during DNA extraction further improves LOD.

Step 2 | IL-6 dPLA — Proximity Probe Preparation and Incubation
  Inputs         : Human plasma or BALF (diluted 5-fold in SDB-II or 0.1x TM buffer)
                   IL-6 proximity probes A and B (200 pM each; from TaqMan Protein Assays Open Kit)
  Probe prep     : 2 uL 1 mg/mL biotinylated antibody diluted to 200 nM in ADB; combine 5 uL
                   200 nM 5'/3' prox-oligos with 5 uL 200 nM antibody (1 h, RT); dilute to 10 nM.
  Reaction setup : 2 uL protein solution + 2 uL APS (200 pM/probe)
  Incubation     : 37 C, 60 min (antibody binds IL-6; oligonucleotides brought into proximity)
  Specificity    : IL-6-specific signal 1-2 orders of magnitude above cross-reactive IL-10 / TNF-alpha signal

Step 3 | IL-6 dPLA — Ligation and Stop
  Ligation mix   : 50 uL 20x ligation reaction buffer + 909 uL nuclease-free water + 1 uL DNA ligase (1x)
  Reaction       : Add 96 uL ligation solution to 4 uL protein/probe solution; 37 C, 10 min
  Stop           : Heat 95 C, 5 min (heat denaturation; IL-6 protocol)
  Output         : Ligated PLA product ready for ddPCR amplification

Step 4 | IL-6 dPLA — ddPCR Reaction Setup and Thermal Cycling
  Reaction setup : 9 uL PLA eluate + 10 uL 2x ddPCR Supermix for Probes + 1 uL 20x Universal PCR Assay
                   Total volume: 20 uL; emulsified per Bio-Rad QX200 protocol
  Thermal cycling:
    Preheat   : 95 C, 10 min
    Cycles    : 40x [94 C 30s / 60 C 1min]
    Final ext : 98 C, 10 min; ramp rate 2.5 C/s
  Readout        : Bio-Rad QX200 droplet reader; QuantaSoft Pro v1.0.596
  Quantification : CPN/uL converted to pg/mL via IL-6 calibration curve (R2 = 0.99)
  LOD            : 0.84 pg/mL (40 fM) in plasma SDB-II; 0.02 pg/mL (0.73 fM) in BALF
  Resolution     : ~0.04 pg/mL (patient-dependent)
  Total time     : ~2 h

Step 5 | TNF-alpha dPLA — Proximity Probe Incubation
  Buffer         : HMB (homemade Nong's buffer) — SDB-II incompatible with TNF-alpha
  Reaction setup : 2 uL plasma (5-fold diluted in HMB) + 2 uL APS (200 pM/probe)
  Incubation     : 4 C, overnight (~12 h; modelled as 720 min in BioScript)
  Critical note  : TNF-alpha degrades rapidly and is sensitive to storage and buffer conditions.
                   Overnight incubation required to maximise signal with HMB.
                   For BALF samples: 0.1x TM buffer + 0.5% gelatin used instead.

Step 6 | TNF-alpha dPLA — Ligation and Protease Stop
  Ligation       : 96 uL ligation solution added to 4 uL probe/sample; 37 C, 10 min
  Stop method    : Protease digestion (NOT heat, unlike IL-6)
                   2 uL 1x protease (in PBS) -> 37 C 10 min -> 95 C 15 min for inactivation
  Note           : Protease stop avoids non-specific signal from TNF-alpha antibody denaturation.

Step 7 | TNF-alpha dPLA — ddPCR Reaction Setup and Thermal Cycling
  Setup and cycling: Identical to IL-6 ddPCR (Step 4)
  LOD            : 0.08 pg/mL in plasma (HMB); 0.08 pg/mL in BALF (TM buffer); 4.58 fM undiluted
  Calibration    : R2 = 0.92
  Total time     : ~7 h (dominated by overnight probe incubation step)

Step 8 | Triplex ddPCR — GN Bacteria + GP Bacteria + blaTEM
  Inputs         : Extracted DNA (from Step 1)
                   GN primers/probe (Bac_fwd + Bac_rev + HEX-GN_probe)
                   GP primers/probe (Bac_fwd + Bac_rev + FAM-GP_probe)
                   blaTEM primers/probe (TEM_fwd + TEM_rev + FAM-blaTEM_probe)
  Reaction setup : 1x ddPCR Supermix for Probes; 900 nM each primer;
                   340 nM GN probe (HEX); 180 nM GP probe (FAM-medium);
                   380 nM blaTEM probe (FAM-high); total volume 20 uL
  Thermal cycling (GN/GP/blaTEM):
    Preheat   : 95 C, 10 min
    Cycles    : 40x [94 C 30s / 62 C 1min]
    Final ext : 98 C, 10 min; ramp rate 2.5 C/s
  Alternative cycling (blaTEM simplex):
    95 C 10 min; 40x [94 C 30s / 50 C 15s / 70 C 20s]; 98 C 10 min
  Cluster readout: 2D amplitude plot; 4 clusters:
    HEX-positive  = GN signal
    FAM-medium    = GP signal
    FAM-high      = blaTEM signal
    No fluorescence = empty droplets
  LODs           : GN 0.06 CPN/uL (0.09 aM); GP 0.06 CPN/uL (0.09 aM); blaTEM 0.9 CPN/uL (1.57 aM)
                   Bacteria: GN 1.76 CFU/uL; GP 12.19 CFU/uL
  Total time     : ~2 h (vs days for conventional blood culture)
  Note           : Detects both pathogenic bacteria and endogenous microbiota.
                   Duplex (GN+GP) also validated; agrees with triplex (Supplementary Fig. 6).
                   blaTEM detects 1-copy-number difference per uL.

Step 9 | Decision-Tree Classification of Patient Outcome
  Inputs         : GN bacteria (CPN/uL) and TNF-alpha (pg/mL) at t1
  Classifier     : DecisionTreeClassifier (scikit-learn, Python); max_depth=2
  Validation     : StratifiedKFold cross-validation (n_splits=5); standardised features
  Thresholds     : GN <85 CPN/uL at t1 -> Group C (death); 100% accuracy
                   GN >=85 CPN/uL + TNF-alpha threshold -> Group A or B
  Accuracy       : Group A 85.71%; Group B 92.31%; Group C 100%; k-fold average >90%
  Comparison     : Decision tree outperforms LDA and logistic regression (less overfitting
                   at n=32; controlled by max_depth)
  Key finding    : Counterintuitive relationship: lower GN at t1 predicts death.
                   Supports the hypothesis that mortality is driven by excessive host
                   cytokine response (increasing IL-6), not by direct bacterial burden.
                   IL-6 temporal change (not absolute level) is the strongest predictor:
                   89% of patients with IL-6 increase at t2 were in Group C (death);
                   85% of patients with IL-6 decrease at t2 were in Group A or B.
  Note           : Patient group classification was performed by independent clinicians
                   without access to molecular measurements (no classification-related confounders).


KEY BIOLOGICAL FINDINGS
-----------------------

BALF (Asthma):
  - Almost all asthma patients had elevated GN bacteria; only 55% of healthy individuals did.
  - IL-6 significantly elevated in asthma vs healthy (p<0.01); supports IL-6 as airway
    inflammation biomarker and potential asthma phenotype marker (IL-6-high phenotype).
  - TNF-alpha uniformly low in all BALF samples (<0.5 pg/mL, near assay LOD).
  - Two GN subpopulations observed in both groups (~20 CPN/uL and ~2 CPN/uL).

Plasma (Septic Shock):
  - GN: Group A decreased rapidly (avg -157 CPN/uL, t1->t2); Group B increased (avg +108 CPN/uL);
    Group C decreased slightly — counterintuitively predicts death.
  - GP: Groups A and C decreased to nondetectable at t2; Group B remained at moderate levels
    (13-36 CPN/uL) across all 3 time points — surprising since Group B ultimately recovered.
  - blaTEM: Most patients below LOD. One Group B patient showed blaTEM rise from 0 to >300
    CPN/uL at t3; confirmed by blood culture (beta-lactam-producing bacteria). Digital assay
    result available same day vs days for culture.
  - TNF-alpha: Group B had highest levels at t1 and t2; dropped to <10 pg/mL by t3 (resolution).
    Group C had very low TNF-alpha (progressed beyond initial cytokine secretion peak by t1).
  - IL-6 absolute levels not correlated with outcome; temporal changes strongly correlated.
    Increasing IL-6 -> death; decreasing IL-6 -> recovery (Fig. 5c-e).
  - dPLA resolution (~0.04 pg/mL) allows detection of IL-6 changes too small for conventional ELISA.

-------------------------

DAG            : abasiyanik_dpla_ddpcr_septic_shock_main_dag.dot

                 (BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported)
                 TNF-alpha overnight incubation: 720m  -> IR: 43200.0 SECOND
                 IL-6 probe incubation: 60m            -> IR: 3600.0 SECOND
                 PCR cycling (40x, abstracted): 60m    -> IR: 3600.0 SECOND

                 TNF-alpha protease inactivation: 15m  -> IR: 900.0 SECOND

                 Both nested branches (BB11, BB12) converge at BB13, which jumps to terminal BB10.

protocol.title: Ultrasensitive Digital Quantification of Cytokines and Bacteria Predicts Septic Shock Outcomes
protocol.platform: Digital proximity ligation assay (dPLA) + droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) on Bio-Rad QX200

universal_bacteria.Bac_rev: Reverse primer targeting 16S rRNA conserved region (GN and GP)

steps.name: IL-6 dPLA — ddPCR reaction setup and thermal cycling
TNF-alpha dPLA — Proximity probe incubation

Triplex ddPCR — GN bacteria + GP bacteria + blaTEM

steps.notes: Detects both pathogenic bacteria and endogenous microbiota. Duplex assay (GN + GP only) also validated and shown to agree with triplex (Supplementary Fig. 6). blaTEM resolves 1-copy-number difference per uL; result available within 2h vs days for blood culture.

inputs: ddpcrSignal (GN CPN/uL, TNF-alpha pg/mL at t1)

steps.notes: Counterintuitive finding: lower GN at t1 correlates with death (excessive cytokine response, not bacterial burden, drives mortality). IL-6 temporal change (t1->t2), not absolute level, is the strongest individual mortality predictor: 89% of patients with increasing IL-6 were Group C; 85% with decreasing IL-6 were Group A or B.

BALF_asthma.GN_elevation: Almost all asthma patients had high GN levels vs 55% of healthy individuals
BALF_asthma.IL6_elevation: IL-6 levels significantly higher in asthma patients than healthy (p<0.01)
BALF_asthma.TNFa: Uniformly low in all BALF samples (<0.5 pg/mL, near LOD)

GN_dynamics.Group_B: GN increased quickly t1->t2 (average +108 CPN/uL); late recovery
GN_dynamics.Group_C: GN decreased slightly by t2; counterintuitively associated with death

GP_dynamics.Group_B: GP remained at moderate level (13-36 CPN/uL) across all 3 time points

plasma_septic_shock.IL6_dynamics: Temporal change (not absolute level) correlates with mortality: increase -> death; decrease -> recovery
plasma_septic_shock.blaTEM_detection: One Group B patient showed blaTEM increase from 0 to >300 CPN/uL at t3; confirmed beta-lactam-producing bacteria on blood culture same day — detected on day of collection vs days for culture
plasma_septic_shock.TNFa: Group B had highest TNF-alpha at t1 and t2; dropped to <10 pg/mL at t3 (shock resolution). Group C showed very low TNF-alpha (progressed past initial cytokine peak).

LOD_calculation.method: LOD = background signal + 2x SD of background signal, or intercept of linear regression curve (whichever higher)
LOD_calculation.IL6_resolution_method: Two measurements distinguishable if absolute difference > 2x SD of both measurements; ~0.04 pg/mL in two patients (one Group A, one Group C)

statistical_analysis.BALF_test: Two-part statistical test (zero-inflated) with Benjamini-Hochberg correction (twopart_statistics.R, Supplementary Software 1)
statistical_analysis.septic_shock_test: Two-sided Mann-Whitney U test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction
statistical_analysis.decision_tree: scikit-learn DecisionTreeClassifier (max_depth=2); StratifiedKFold (n_splits=5); compared with LDA and logistic regression (decision tree superior, less prone to overfitting at this sample size)

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : An Automated Single-Cell Droplet-Digital Microfluidic Platform for Monoclonal Antibody Discovery
Source Link  : https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdf/10.1002/smll.202308950
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1002/smll.202308950
Journal      : Small, 2024, Vol. 20, Article 2308950
Authors      : Fatemeh Ahmadi, Hao Tran, Natasha Letourneau, Samuel R. Little,
               Annie Fortin, Anna N. Moraitis, Steve C. C. Shih
Platform     : Droplet-Digital (D2) microfluidics (digital microfluidics + droplet-in-channel
               microfluidics) on EWOD/electrode array


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a Droplet-Digital (D2) microfluidic platform for automated monoclonal
antibody (mAb) discovery. The platform integrates a bottom digital microfluidic (DMF) electrode
layer (chromium co-planar electrodes on glass + 7 um SU-8 dielectric) with three stacked
PDMS-based microchannel devices, enabling individual electrode-addressable control of droplets
flowing inside microfluidic channels -- a configuration combining "droplet-in-flow" techniques
with digital microfluidics for on-demand droplet generation and manipulation.

The protocol is divided into five functional phases:
  1. Target cell encapsulation and single-cell sorting (Devices 2 and 3)
  2. Hybridoma cell staining and hydrodynamic single-cell trapping (Device 1)
  3. In situ deterministic co-encapsulation by phase change and electrode-actuated merge
  4. On-chip incubation, droplet disruption, and PBS/Alexa Fluor 647 wash (Device 1)
  5. Fluorescence-based antibody binding detection and positive hybridoma recovery

The complete workflow from trapping to recovery processes 100 doublets in ~60 min, achieving
co-encapsulation efficiency of 95 +/- 3.2% -- the highest reported without preliminary sorting
of both cell types or microvalve-based capture systems. This surpasses the Poisson-based
nondeterministic co-encapsulation efficiency of ~16%, which is the limit of conventional
flow-focusing droplet microfluidic approaches.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Layer i   : Chromium electrodes patterned on glass; co-planar ground and actuation electrodes.
Layer ii  : SU-8 dielectric, 7 um thick; spin-coated and hard-baked.
Layer iii : Three stacked PDMS-based microchannel devices adhered to the dielectric layer.

Device 1 -- Trapping array:
  100 traps total (50 per serpentine side); channel height 20 um, channel width 50-75 um;
  7 um constriction per trap; 2 actuation electrodes + 1 ground electrode per trap;
  sets of 5 traps bussed together to one potential circuit to reduce electrode density
  and operational complexity.

Device 2 -- Flow-focusing droplet generator:
  Generates ~30 pL monodisperse droplets at ~3 kHz throughput;
  used for target cell encapsulation following Poisson distribution.

Device 3 -- Co-planar binary electrode sorter:
  Selects single-target-cell droplets by CFSE fluorescence (ex 470 nm / em 520 nm);
  PMT photon-counting head triggers electrode actuation to sort droplets above single-cell
  fluorescence threshold and below two-cell threshold.

Inlets  : Inlet 1 (HFE7500 oil, main channel), Inlet 2 (PBS / Alexa647 Ab / target droplets),
          Inlet 3 (hybridoma cell suspension in IMDM)
Outlets : Outlet 1 (sample recovery via reverse oil flow, 4 nL/s)

Actuation: 15 kHz AC; 32 Vrms for encapsulation/merge; 64 Vrms for droplet disruption/wash.
           Electrode actuation controlled through in-house Python-based GUI automation software
           (open-source: https://bitbucket.org/shihmicrolab/f_ahmadi_2023_uflowcontrol).


CELL LINES
----------
- Hybridoma cells (confidential line, provided by NRC Canada):
  Produces monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) that bind to specific membrane-bound antigens on target
  cells. Cultured in IMDM + 10% heat-inactivated FBS + mouse IL-6 (1 ng/mL) + pen/strep;
  37 C, 5% CO2. Passaged every 3 days at 8e6 cells/mL. Loaded at 1e6 cells/mL in IMDM
  (10% FBS + IL-6, no antibiotic). Stained with CellTrace Calcein Red-Orange AM
  (ex 577 nm / em 590 nm) prior to chip loading.

- Target cells (confidential line, provided by NRC Canada):
  Express membrane-bound antigens recognised by the desired antigen-specific mAbs.
  Cultured in DMEM + 10% heat-inactivated FBS + G418 (0.4 mg/mL); 37 C, 5% CO2.
  Passaged every 3 days at 3e6 cells/mL. Loaded at 1e6 cells/mL in IMDM
  (10% FBS + IL-6, no antibiotic). Stained with CellTrace CFSE (ex 470 nm / em 520 nm)
  prior to chip loading for Device 3 sorting.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Device Priming
  Reagents  : PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free), Pluronics F-127
  Mix       : 2% Pluronics F-127 in PBS
  Flow rate : 50 nL/s from inlet 3 for 5 min (outlet 1 closed); then reduced to 1 nL/s
              and outlet 1 opened
  Duration  : 5 min (300 s)
  Purpose   : Reduces non-specific hybridoma cell adhesion to PDMS channel walls.

Step 2 | Target Cell Staining and Encapsulation (Device 2)
  Cell line      : Target cells
  Stain          : CellTrace CFSE (5 uM, 1e6 cells/mL in PBS, Ca2+/Mg2+ free)
  Stain time     : 20 min at 37 C; wash with PBS to remove excess dye
  Resuspension   : IMDM (10% FBS + mouse IL-6 1 ng/mL, no antibiotic, 1e6 cells/mL)
  Operation      : Flow-focusing encapsulation (Poisson distribution)
  Oil            : HFE7500 + 2% Ran Fluoro-surfactant
  Droplet size   : ~30 pL monodisperse
  Throughput     : ~3 kHz
  Purpose        : Encapsulate target cells in small droplets for downstream sorting (Device 3).

Step 3 | Single Target-Cell Droplet Sorting (Device 3)
  Detection      : CFSE fluorescence (ex 470 nm / em 520 nm) via PMT photon-counting head
  Sorting gate   : Fluorescence counts above single-cell threshold and below two-cell threshold
  Action (pass)  : Single-target-cell droplet collected into gas-tight glass syringe with HFE7500
  Action (fail)  : Empty or multi-cell droplets sent to waste channel
  Transfer       : Collected droplets bridged to Device 1 inlet 2 via 0.014" OD / 0.006" ID tubing
  Purpose        : Ensure only droplets with exactly one target cell are used for co-encapsulation.

Step 4 | Hybridoma Cell Staining and Hydrodynamic Trapping (Device 1)
  Cell line      : Hybridoma cells
  Stain          : CellTrace Calcein Red-Orange AM (1e6 cells/mL, 20 min at 37 C; PBS wash)
  Resuspension   : IMDM (10% FBS + IL-6, no antibiotic, 1e6 cells/mL)
  Flow rate      : 1-5 nL/s; optimal 1 nL/s
  Trapping eff.  : 98 +/- 3.92% at 1 nL/s (N=5 repeats, n=10 replicates per flow rate)
  Trap design    : 7 um constriction (smaller than hybridoma cell diameter); hydrodynamic
                   confinement by fluidic resistance. Open trap Rtrap < Rbypass; when occupied
                   Rtrap increases, directing flow to next open trap.
  Trap count     : 100 traps (50 per serpentine side per device)
  Occupancy check: singleCellTrapDetection module; fluorescence threshold gates single occupancy
  Purpose        : Isolate single hybridoma cells in addressable traps for deterministic
                   co-encapsulation and individual droplet-level screening.

Step 5 | In Situ Droplet Generation (Device 1)
  Method         : Phase change from single-phase aqueous (IMDM) to two-phase (water-in-oil)
  Oil            : HFE7500 + 2% Ran Fluoro-surfactant, 1 nL/s from inlet 1
  Electrode      : 32 Vrms, 15 kHz; electrodes below traps actuated to shear aqueous phase
  Droplet volume : 40-150 pL (varies with oil flow rate)
  Success rate   : >95% at 1 nL/s
  Frame sequence : Oil enters main channel while trap electrode holds aqueous phase.
                   Oil shears aqueous at both trap ends; cell remains inside.
                   Droplet pinches off; oil continues to next trap.
  Purpose        : Deterministic encapsulation of single hybridoma cell per trap.
                   No Poisson statistics. No preliminary sorting of hybridoma cells required.

Step 6 | Deterministic Co-Encapsulation (Droplet Merge, Device 1)
  Operation      : On-demand electrode-actuated droplet merge
  Re-injection   : Sorted single-target-cell droplets re-injected from inlet 2 at 5 nL/s
  Oil spacer     : HFE7500 from a separate inlet at 1 nL/s (spaces droplets entering traps)
  Electrode      : 32 Vrms, 15 kHz; actuated when target-cell droplet reaches trap proximity
  Efficiency     : 95 +/- 3.2% co-encapsulation at 5 nL/s re-injection flow rate
                   (N=5 repeats, n=10 replicates; highest reported without microvalves)
  Time for 100   : 60 min for 100 two-cell doublets with automated system
  Notes          : Two separate inlets avoid merging of sequential target-cell droplets.
                   Electrode actuation pattern detailed in Figure S6 of paper.
                   Failure mode at >10 nL/s: target droplet coalesces with empty trap droplet.

Step 7 | On-Chip Co-Incubation
  Temperature    : 25 C (room temperature; no external heating element)
  Duration       : 30 min (1800 s)
  Events         : Hybridoma cells secrete mAbs into confined droplet volume.
                   Antigen-specific mAbs diffuse and bind to membrane-bound antigens on
                   co-encapsulated target cell surface.
                   Non-specific mAbs remain free in droplet volume.

Step 8 | Droplet Disruption and PBS / Alexa Fluor 647 Wash (Device 1)
  Wash solution  : PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free) + Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated goat anti-mouse
                   IgG (H+L) secondary antibody; loaded from inlet 2 at 1-5 nL/s
  Electrode      : 64 Vrms, 15 kHz; field intensity 2-4 x 10^5 V/m; electrodes below traps
  Duration       : ~5 min to wash all 50 traps
  Mechanism      : Electrostatic force perpendicular to droplet interface (Figure S7 of paper)
                   disrupts IMDM droplet; non-specific mAbs washed out through 7 um constriction.
                   Hybridoma + target cell retained in trap (antigen-Ab bond maintains target cell;
                   hybridoma remains by hydrodynamic confinement).
  Wash efficiency: 96.8% reduction in normalised fluorescence intensity after 1 wash step
                   (N=15 replicates; Figure 4C of paper)
  Cell retention : 96 +/- 9.6% at 1-5 nL/s (N=5 repeats, n=10 replicates; Figure 4D)
  Re-formation   : PBS/Alexa647 flow reduced to 0.1 nL/s; HFE7500 oil flow increased to
                   5 nL/s to re-form PBS droplet around both cells in situ.
  Advantage      : Individual droplet disruption by electrostatic forces avoids chemical
                   demulsifiers (which compromise cell viability) and acoustic/magnetic methods
                   (which have device material limitations).

Step 9 | Fluorescence Detection and Antibody Binding Screening
  Channel        : Alexa Fluor 647 (ex 627 nm / em 665 nm); 300 ms exposure
  Camera         : Hamamatsu ORCA-Flash 4.0 (Township, NJ, USA)
  Detection      : antibodyBindingDetection module gates on mean fluorescence of cell >
                   mean fluorescence of surrounding droplet (SNR threshold)
  Result (pass)  : Localised red fluorescent signal around target cell membrane =
                   antigen-specific mAb detected; hybridoma is a positive producer
  Result (fail)  : No localised signal = non-specific mAb producer; droplet drained
  SNR            : Significant improvement post-wash for antigen-specific vs non-specific
                   hybridomas (P < 0.05); without washing both types have similar SNR (P > 0.05)
  Selection rate : 94.00 +/- 1.41% at 100:0 ratio (100% desired); 1.60% at 1:50 ratio
                   (platform detects rare-cell populations at biologically relevant concentrations
                   of ~2% antigen-specific B cells from immunised donors)
  Purpose        : Distinguish antigen-specific from non-specific mAb-producing hybridomas
                   at the single-cell level without requiring pre-sorting or bulk assays.

Step 10 | Positive Hybridoma Recovery
  Condition      : antibodySignal > 0 only (antigen-specific mAb detected)
  Recovery steps :
    1. Positive droplet released by reverse oil flow at 4 nL/s from outlet 1
       (inlet 3 briefly opened to remove previously accumulated droplets in that channel)
    2. Droplet collected into glass capillary pre-filled with HFE7500 2% Ran Fluoro-surfactant
    3. Capillary contents expelled onto 10-20 uL IMDM complete medium placed on hydrophobic
       PTFE membrane (0.22 um, Thomas Scientific) secured in custom 3D-printed holder
    4. ~1 mL Fluorinert FC-40 oil added; FC-40 disrupts surfactant-stabilised emulsion
       and PTFE membrane absorbs HFE7500 and surfactant
    5. Aqueous cell droplet released into IMDM complete medium
    6. Merged droplet transferred to well-plate (e.g. 96-well) using pipette for downstream
       antibody characterisation (sequencing, ELISA, binding kinetics, SPR, etc.)
  Downstream     : Antibody characterisation assays (off-chip; not encoded in BioScript).


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : ahmadi_2024_mab_discovery.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges

Manifests      : HybridomaCells, TargetCells, IMDM_Medium, PBS, PluronicF127,

Fixes applied  :

protocol.title: An Automated Single-Cell Droplet-Digital Microfluidic Platform for Monoclonal Antibody Discovery
protocol.platform: Droplet-Digital (D2) microfluidics (digital microfluidics + droplet-in-channel microfluidics)
cell_lines: Hybridoma cells (antigen-specific mAb producer, NRC Canada, confidential line)
Target cells (membrane-bound antigen-expressing, NRC Canada, confidential line)
protocol.objective: Deterministic single-cell co-encapsulation of hybridoma and target cells, on-demand droplet disruption and media exchange, antigen-specific mAb screening by fluorescence, and recovery of positive hybridoma cells for downstream antibody characterisation

layers: Chromium electrodes on glass (layer i)
SU-8 dielectric layer, 7 um thick (layer ii)
PDMS-based microchannel devices x3 (layer iii)
sections: Device 1 -- Trapping array (100 traps, 50 per serpentine side)
Device 2 -- Flow-focusing droplet generator (target cells, ~30 pL, ~3 kHz)
Device 3 -- Co-planar binary electrode sorter (single target-cell selection)

inlets.inlet_2: PBS / Alexa Fluor 647 secondary Ab solution / target-cell droplets (re-injection)

outlets.outlet_1: Sample recovery (positive hybridoma droplets via reverse oil flow)

reagents.carrier_oil: HFE7500 + 2% Ran Fluoro-surfactant (2% w/v PEG fluoro-surfactant in HFE7500)
reagents.recovery_oil: Fluorinert FC-40 (~1 mL for PTFE membrane wash)

cell_media.hybridoma: IMDM + 10% heat-inactivated FBS + mouse IL-6 (1 ng/mL) + pen/strep; 37 C, 5% CO2
cell_media.target_cells: DMEM + 10% heat-inactivated FBS + G418 (0.4 mg/mL); 37 C, 5% CO2

secondary_antibody.purpose: Labels membrane-bound antigen-specific mAbs on target cell surface post-wash

reagents.wash_solution: PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free) containing Alexa Fluor 647 secondary antibody
reagents.capillary: Glass capillary pre-filled with HFE7500 2% Ran Fluoro-surfactant

steps.name: Device priming
steps.notes: 2% Pluronics F-127 in PBS flowed at 50 nL/s for 5 min (outlet 1 closed). Flow rate then reduced to 1 nL/s and outlet 1 opened. Reduces non-specific cell adhesion to PDMS channel walls.

steps.name: Target cell staining and encapsulation (Device 2)
steps.stain: CellTrace CFSE (5 uM, 1e6 cells/mL in PBS)
steps.resuspension: IMDM (10% FBS + IL-6, no antibiotic, 1e6 cells/mL)
steps.notes: Device 2 generates monodisperse ~30 pL droplets at ~3 kHz. Target cells stained with CFSE before loading to enable fluorescence-based sorting in Device 3.

steps.name: Single target-cell droplet sorting (Device 3)
steps.operation: co-planar binary electrode sorting by fluorescence
steps.sorting_threshold: Fluorescence above single-cell threshold and below two-cell threshold
steps.collection: Gas-tight glass syringe filled with HFE7500 oil

pass.action: mix oil spacer, hold for re-injection

steps.notes: PMT-based photon counting triggers electrode actuation. Only droplets containing exactly 1 target cell are collected. Multi-cell and empty droplets sent to waste.

steps.name: Hybridoma cell staining and trapping (Device 1)
steps.stain: CellTrace Calcein Red-Orange AM (1e6 cells/mL in IMDM)
steps.resuspension: IMDM (10% FBS + IL-6, no antibiotic, 1e6 cells/mL)
steps.operation: hydrodynamic single-cell trapping (abstracted as mix in BioScript)
steps.trap_design: 7 um constriction; fluidic resistance blocks outlet when cell occupies trap

pass.action: dispense fresh IMDM, proceed to encapsulation

steps.notes: Hydrodynamic confinement by fluidic resistance. Open trap Rtrap < Rbypass; when occupied Rtrap increases, next cell flows to next open trap. Device primed with Pluronics F-127 to reduce cell adhesion. Cell concentration kept at 1e6/mL in IMDM.

steps.name: In situ droplet generation around trapped hybridoma (Device 1)
steps.notes: IMDM medium replaced by oil flowing at 1 nL/s. Electrodes actuated at 32 Vrms / 15 kHz to shear aqueous phase and generate in situ droplet around trapped single hybridoma cell. Deterministic -- no Poisson statistics.

steps.name: Deterministic co-encapsulation (droplet merge, Device 1)
steps.notes: Sorted single-target-cell droplets re-injected from inlet 2 at 5 nL/s, interleaved with oil spacer at 1 nL/s from a separate inlet. When target-cell droplet arrives at a trap, electrode beneath is actuated (32 Vrms / 15 kHz) to merge it with in situ hybridoma droplet. 95 +/- 3.2% efficiency at 5 nL/s -- highest reported co-encapsulation efficiency without preliminary sorting of both cell types or microvalve systems.

steps.name: On-chip co-incubation
steps.notes: Two-cell droplets incubated on-chip for 30 min at room temperature. Hybridoma secretes mAbs into confined droplet. Antigen-specific mAbs diffuse and bind to membrane-bound antigens on co-encapsulated target cell. Non-specific mAbs remain free in droplet volume.

steps.name: Droplet disruption and PBS/Alexa Fluor 647 wash (Device 1)
steps.wash_solution: PBS + Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated goat anti-mouse IgG (H+L)
steps.notes: PBS/Alexa647 solution flowed at 1-5 nL/s. Electrode beneath traps actuated at 64 Vrms / 15 kHz to disrupt droplet interface via electrostatic force. Non-specific mAbs washed out through constriction. Antigen-specific mAbs retained on target cell membrane. After wash, PBS flow reduced to 0.1 nL/s and oil flow increased to 5 nL/s to re-form droplet in situ around both cells. 96.8% fluorescence reduction after 1 wash step (~5 min for 50 traps).

steps.name: Fluorescence detection and antibody binding screening
steps.detection_channel: Alexa Fluor 647 (ex 627 nm / em 665 nm, 300 ms exposure)
steps.signal_definition: Mean fluorescence intensity of target cell membrane > mean fluorescence of surrounding droplet
steps.snr_improvement_post_wash: Significant (P < 0.05 between binding and non-binding hybridomas)
steps.notes: Antigen-specific mAbs bound to target cell membrane are labelled by Alexa Fluor 647 secondary antibody, generating localised red fluorescence around target cell. Non-specific mAbs washed away in S8. SNR significantly higher post-wash for antigen-specific hybridomas. PMT photon-counting head triggers on-demand reverse-flow release of positive droplets.

steps.name: Positive hybridoma recovery
recovery_steps: Positive droplet released by reverse oil flow at 4 nL/s from outlet 1 (inlet 3 briefly opened to clear channel)
Droplet collected into glass capillary pre-filled with HFE7500 2% Ran Fluoro-surfactant
Glass capillary contents expelled onto 10-20 uL IMDM complete medium on hydrophobic PTFE membrane secured in 3D-printed holder
~1 mL FC-40 oil added to disrupt surfactant-stabilised emulsion; PTFE membrane absorbs HFE7500 and surfactant
Aqueous cell droplet released into IMDM complete medium
Merged droplet transferred to well-plate (e.g. 96-well) using pipette for downstream expansion or antibody characterisation assays
steps.downstream: Antibody characterisation (ELISA, sequencing, binding kinetics, etc.)

in_situ_generation.method: Phase change (single-phase aqueous to two-phase water-in-oil)
in_situ_generation.notes: Flow rate must be >1 nL/s to provide hydraulic pressure for phase exchange; not so high as to squeeze cell through constriction.

merge.notes: Two separate inlets used -- one for re-injected target droplets, one for oil spacer. No stream synchronisation required.

disruption.method: Electrostatic force (electrode actuation without emulsion destabiliser)
disruption.notes: Individual droplet disruption by electrostatic forces; avoids chemical demulsifiers that compromise cell viability. Droplets disrupted individually per trap -- no coalescence. Surfactant concentration in oil phase: 0.001% wt (no chemical emulsion destabiliser added).

release.electrode_actuation: none required (hydrodynamic release after wash droplet re-formation)
release.notes: Reverse flow of 2% Ran-HFE oil from outlet 1 at 4 nL/s. Inlet 3 briefly opened to clear previously accumulated droplets in that channel before collection.

performance.notes: Co-encapsulation efficiency of 95% is the highest reported without requiring preliminary sorting of both cell types or microvalve-based capture systems.

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.content: Device priming; target cell stain + encapsulation (Device 2); hybridoma stain; trapping (Device 1); sortSignal detect

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_4_j
basic_blocks.content: PHI merge; dispose sortSignal; stain hybridoma; trap; trapOccupancySignal detect

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_7_j
basic_blocks.content: PHI merge; dispose trapOccupancySignal; in situ droplet generation; merge; incubate 30 min; wash; re-form droplet; antibodySignal detect

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_8_t
basic_blocks.action: dispense IMDM recovery medium; mix reforumDroplet -> recoveredCells; dispose recoveredCells

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_10_j
basic_blocks.content: dispose antibodySignal; NOP

bioscript_notes.ir_output: 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
bioscript_notes.duration_units: All durations in seconds (s) or minutes (m); h token not supported by compiler
modules: singleCellTrapDetection (used for both sort gate and trap occupancy gate)
antibodyBindingDetection (Alexa Fluor 647 channel, post-wash SNR gate)
fixes_applied: Removed dead module declaration: targetCellSortDetection (declared but never called; singleCellTrapDetection covers both sort and trap occupancy gates)

Fixed imdmForHybridoma double-consumption: added imdmForHybridoma2 = dispense 1 units of IMDM_Medium inside BB5 (trap-pass branch) so each mix has its own fresh dispense unit; SSA compiler emits PHI imdmForHybridoma22 in BB7 join
bioscript_notes.ascii_compliance: All non-ASCII characters (em-dashes U+2014, arrow U+2192) replaced with ASCII equivalents (-- and ->) for ANTLR4 FileStream compatibility
