description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Digital Quantification of Proteins and mRNA in Single Mammalian Cells
Source Link  : https://www.cell.com/molecular-cell/pdfExtended/S1097-2765(16)00174-X
Paper DOI    : http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.molcel.2016.02.030
Journal      : Molecular Cell, 2016, Vol. 61, pp. 914-924
Platform     : Digital PLA (proximity ligation assay + droplet digital PCR) combined with
               two-step RT-ddPCR; bench-top Bio-Rad QX100 microfluidic droplet system


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a practical, commercially available workflow for the absolute and
simultaneous quantification of both protein and mRNA copy numbers from the same single
mammalian cell. The method combines proximity ligation assay (PLA) with droplet digital PCR
(ddPCR) to achieve femtomolar sensitivity for protein detection (digital PLA), and integrates
a two-step reverse transcription ddPCR (RT-ddPCR) for absolute mRNA quantification from the
same single-cell lysate.

The protocol is divided into two parallel arms operating on split lysate from one cell:
  1. Digital PLA arm (protein): proximity probes bind target protein -> connector
     oligonucleotide hybridises -> ligation forms dsDNA -> protease digestion ->
     ddPCR in 20,000 droplets -> absolute protein copy number via calibration curve.
  2. RT-ddPCR arm (mRNA): two-step GoScript RT (42 C, 60 min) -> ddPCR (40 cycles,
     60 C annealing, TaqMan Probe 2) -> mRNA copy number corrected for 87.6% RT recovery.

The joint dataset was used to construct and validate a stochastic two-state model of CD147
transcription and translation in single HEK293T cells. Key findings: CD147 mRNA and protein
are poorly correlated at the single-cell level (Spearman R = 0.10); approximately 1,000
proteins are produced per mRNA molecule; transcription occurs in bursts of ~40 mRNAs at
a rate of 3.78 bursts/day.

The entire assay uses commercially available reagents and equipment; no genetic manipulation
of host cells or custom microfluidic device fabrication is required. A single researcher can
process 100 single-cell samples in one day.


ASSAY SPECIFICATIONS
--------------------
Digital PLA:
  Target proteins   : CD147 (endogenous, HEK293T), GFP-p65 (exogenous, RAW264.7), ICAM-1
  LOD (CD147)       : 0.14 fM assay / 16.2 fM sample / 86 proteins per uL ddPCR solution
  LOD (single cell) : 29,300 CD147 molecules per cell (from 2 uL lysate fraction)
  Sensitivity       : 70 proteins per DNA count (CD147); 95 (GFP); 565 (ICAM-1)
  Dynamic range     : 2-3 orders of magnitude (linear)
  Calibration curve : CD147: y = 0.0142x + 12.4, R2 = 0.9997
                      GFP  : y = 0.0094x + 10.6, R2 = 0.9982
                      ICAM-1: y = 0.00177x + 1.30, R2 = 0.9993
  Droplets          : ~20,000 per reaction at ~0.85 nL each (limiting dilution; 0 or 1 dsDNA)
  Concentration eq. : C = (1000/Vd) * ln(1 - P/R)

RT-ddPCR:
  Target            : CD147 mRNA (NM_198589.2)
  Primer/probe      : TaqMan Gene Expression Assay Hs00174305_m1 (Probe 2; FAM/MGB)
                      Exon-exon junction spanning; excludes genomic DNA signal
  PCR cycles        : 40; fluorescence threshold 3200 RFU
  RT recovery rate  : 87.6% (validated against T7 in-vitro transcribed CD147 mRNA standard)
  LOD               : 52.5 copies/cell (87 aM); corrected for RT recovery
  Expected output   : Mean 188.2 +/- 90 CD147 mRNA copies per HEK293T cell


CELL LINES
----------
- HEK293T (human embryonic kidney; Tlr4-GFP stable line, gift from Prof. Kensuke Miyake,
  University of Tokyo): primary cell line for joint CD147 protein and mRNA measurements.
  Media: high-glucose DMEM (Gibco 41965-039) + 10% FCS (Gibco 26010-066) + 100 U/mL
  penicillin G + 100 ug/mL streptomycin (Gibco 15070063).
  Conditions: 37 C, 5% CO2; passage every 3-4 days to 1e5 cells/mL; max 30 passages.

- RAW 264.7 (murine macrophage; GFP-p65 h2b-mCherry dual-fluorescent stable line):
  used for GFP-p65 single-cell protein quantification only.
  Media: DMEM (Sigma D6429) + 8.8% FBS (Sigma F9665) + 0.88X GlutaMAX + 17.7 mM HEPES.
  Conditions: 37 C, 5% CO2; passage every 2-3 days to 1e5 cells/mL; max 15 passages.


REAGENTS
--------
Lysis buffer     : 0.1X TM lysis buffer (10-fold diluted TM Buffer, Biochain) +
                   protease inhibitor cocktail (Biochain) + CRB (Life Technologies) +
                   RNaseOUT (Invitrogen). Compatible with both digital PLA and RT-ddPCR.
                   Alternative for RAW264.7: 1X standard lysis buffer (2X Cell Lysis Reagent,
                   Life Technologies + Protease Inhibitor Cocktail I + Phosphatase Inhibitor
                   Cocktail II + CRB).

Proximity probes : Anti-human CD147 biotinylated polyclonal goat antibody (R&D Systems,
                   BAF972; oligonucleotide-conjugated; 400 pM each stock, 200 pM final).
                   Anti-GFP biotinylated polyclonal goat antibody (Abcam, AB6658).
                   Anti-murine ICAM-1 biotinylated polyclonal goat antibody (R&D Systems,
                   BAF796).

Connector oligo  : Custom DNA oligonucleotide (Microsynth, Switzerland); hybridises to
                   both proximity probe oligonucleotides to template ligation.

Ligation         : T4 DNA ligase + ligation buffer (Life Technologies TaqMan Protein Assay);
                   25-fold dilution of probe-bound sample; 10 min at 37 C.

Protease         : Diluted protease solution (Life Technologies TaqMan Protein Assay);
                   10 min at 37 C; inactivated 15 min at 95 C.

ddPCR reagents   : 2X ddPCR Supermix for Probes (Bio-Rad); 20X Universal PCR Assay
                   (Life Technologies); DG8 cartridges; QX100 Droplet Generator;
                   QX100 Droplet Reader; QuantaSoft v1.3.2.0.

RT reagents      : GoScript Reverse Transcription System (Promega); random primers;
                   dNTPs 0.5 mM each; MgCl2 3.1 mM; RNaseOUT 1 U/uL (Invitrogen).

Protein standards: Human CD147 (R&D Systems, 972-EMN); pure GFP (Abcam, AB84191);
                   murine ICAM-1 (R&D Systems, 796-IC).

Containers       : Low-adsorption 8-well PCR strips (Thermo Fisher, AB-0266);
                   1.5 mL low-adsorption microfuge tubes (Ambion, AM12450).
                   Used for ALL steps to minimise protein loss.


FACS SORTING
------------
Instrument       : MoFlo XDP (Beckman-Coulter); 70 um nozzle; 60 psi sheath fluid
Lasers/filters   : 488 nm blue + 561 nm yellow-green; 529/28, 613/20, 785/60 nm bandpass
Viability dye    : DRAQ7 (BioStatus, DR71000) at 600 nM; stains dead cell nuclei (high signal)
HEK293T gates    : 4 nested gates (SSC-H/FSC-H, SSC-H/SSC-W, FSC-H/FSC-W, DRAQ7/GFP);
                   R4 gate selects single viable Tlr4-GFP-positive cells
RAW264.7 gates   : 3 nested gates (FSC/SSC, DRAQ7/FSC-W, GFP/mCherry);
                   R3 gate selects dual-fluorescent GFP-p65 mCherry-positive macrophages
Sort volumes     : 2 uL (RAW264.7 protein only); 2 uL (HEK293T protein only);
                   3 uL (HEK293T joint protein + mRNA)
Post-sort        : Plates centrifuged briefly; sealed with clear adhesive sheet + Parafilm;
                   stored at -80 C until processing. Software: Summit (Beckman Coulter).


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Single-Cell FACS Sort and Lysis
  Cell line      : HEK293T (Tlr4-GFP stable)
  Buffer         : 0.1X TM lysis buffer (3 uL per well)
  Operation      : Single viable cell sorted by FACS (R4 gate) directly into well containing
                   3 uL 0.1X TM lysis buffer; cell contacts buffer and lyses immediately.
  Duration       : 5 min mixing (BioScript abstraction: mix for 5m; IR: 300.0 SECOND)
  Notes          : 0.1X TM buffer confirmed compatible with both PLA and RT-ddPCR (Fig S4G-H).
                   Cell strainer (40 um) used before loading to remove clumps. DRAQ7 excludes
                   dead cells. Tlr4-GFP expression used as sort marker.

Step 2 | Lysate Split: Protein Fraction (2 uL) and mRNA Fraction (1 uL)
  Total lysate   : 3 uL
  Protein arm    : 2 uL (2/3 of lysate) -> digital PLA workflow
  mRNA arm       : 1 uL (1/3 of lysate) -> RT-ddPCR workflow
  Notes          : Physical 1:2 ratio split; no BioScript native split operator; modelled as
                   two independent dispense+mix variables (proteinLysate, mRNALysate).
                   LOD for CD147 protein in the 2 uL fraction: 29,300 molecules/cell.

Step 3 | Proximity Probe Adsorption  [DIGITAL PLA ARM]
  Inputs         : 2 uL protein lysate + 2 uL assay probe solution (200 pM each probe final)
  Temperature    : 37 C
  Duration       : 60 min
                   (BioScript: heat at 37c for 60m; IR: 3600.0 SECOND)
  Mechanism      : Both anti-CD147 antibody-oligonucleotide probes bind distinct epitopes on
                   the same CD147 molecule; tethered oligonucleotides come into ~40 nm
                   proximity enabling connector hybridisation in the next step.
  Notes          : Probe specificity confirmed: human CD147 probes show no signal with mouse
                   3T3 bulk lysate (Fig S3A). GFP-negative cell lysate background comparable
                   to PBS buffer (Fig S3C).

Step 4 | Connector Oligonucleotide Hybridisation and Ligation  [DIGITAL PLA ARM]
  Inputs         : Probe-bound sample + 96 uL ligation solution (25-fold dilution)
  Temperature    : 37 C
  Duration       : 10 min
                   (BioScript: heat at 37c for 10m; IR: 600.0 SECOND)
  Mechanism      : Connector oligonucleotide hybridises to both paired probe oligonucleotides;
                   T4 DNA ligase seals nicks; three-oligonucleotide complex becomes a dsDNA
                   molecule encoding one protein detection event.

Step 5 | Protease Digestion and Inactivation  [DIGITAL PLA ARM]
  Inputs         : Ligated sample + 2 uL diluted protease solution
  Digestion      : 37 C for 10 min (IR: 600.0 SECOND); removes antibody-oligo conjugates,
                   leaving only dsDNA amplicons in solution.
  Inactivation   : 95 C for 15 min (IR: 900.0 SECOND)
  Notes          : BioScript: two sequential heat steps (heat at 37c for 10m;
                   heat at 95c for 15m).

Step 6 | ddPCR Droplet Generation and Amplification  [DIGITAL PLA ARM]
  Inputs         : 9 uL PLA solution + 10 uL 2X ddPCR Supermix + 1 uL 20X Universal PCR Assay
  Total volume   : 20 uL; emulsified into ~20,000 droplets (~0.85 nL each)
  Device         : Bio-Rad QX100 Droplet Generator (DG8 cartridges); Veriti thermal cycler
  PCR schedule   :
    Hot-start        : 95 C for 10 min  (IR: 600.0 SECOND)
    40 cycles        : 94 C 30 s / 60 C 1 min (total ~35 min; IR: 2100.0 SECOND abstracted)
    Final extension  : 98 C for 10 min  (IR: 600.0 SECOND)
    Ramp speed       : 2.5 C/s
  Readout        : QX100 Droplet Reader; QuantaSoft v1.3.2.0 Absolute Quantification setting;
                   threshold set from most concentrated standard (applied to all wells).
  Concentration  : C = (1000/Vd) * ln(1 - P/R); where Vd = droplet volume (nL),
                   P = positive droplets, R = total droplets.
  Protein count  : Converted via daily calibration curve (accounts for day-to-day variation;
                   CV of DNA concentration used as error for each single-cell measurement).
  Notes          : QuantaSoft v1.3.2.0 uses 0.91 nL droplet volume (incorrect; true = 0.85 nL);
                   calibration curve construction corrects for this systematic 10% error.
                   BioScript: three sequential heat steps (95c/10m, 94c/35m, 98c/10m).

Step 7 | Protein ddPCR Detection and QC Gate  [DIGITAL PLA ARM]
  Module         : ddpcrDetection (abstracts QX100 readout + calibration curve conversion)
  Detection      : 30 s
  Pass gate      : proteinSignal > 0 -> CD147 protein detected above LOD -> dispose (BB2)
  Fail gate      : proteinSignal <= 0 -> below LOD -> drain (BB3)
  Join           : BB4 (both branches converge; mRNA arm begins)
  Results        : 138 of 186 sorted HEK293T cells had CD147 protein above LOD.
                   Range: 35,900 +/- 2,900 to 636,000 +/- 36,000 proteins/cell (18-fold).
                   Population mean: ~218,000 CD147 molecules/cell.
                   Poisson CV: 6-8% (fundamental ddPCR error).

Step 8 | RT Primer Annealing  [RT-ddPCR ARM]
  Inputs         : 1 uL mRNA lysate + 1 uL random primers + 2.95 uL nuclease-free water
  Denaturation   : 70 C for 5 min (IR: 300.0 SECOND); denatures RNA secondary structure
  Chilling       : 4 C for 5 min (IR: 300.0 SECOND); prevents re-folding before RT
  Notes          : BioScript: heat at 70c for 5m then heat at 4c for 5m.

Step 9 | Reverse Transcription (cDNA Synthesis)  [RT-ddPCR ARM]
  System         : GoScript Reverse Transcription System (Promega)
  Additives      : RNaseOUT 1 U/uL; dNTPs 0.5 mM each; MgCl2 3.1 mM; 1X GoScript buffer
  Total volume   : 9 uL
  RT schedule    :
    Primer annealing : 25 C for 5 min  (IR: 300.0 SECOND)
    cDNA synthesis   : 42 C for 60 min (IR: 3600.0 SECOND)
    RT inactivation  : 70 C for 15 min (IR: 900.0 SECOND)
  Recovery rate  : 87.6% (validated by T7 in-vitro transcribed CD147 mRNA standard;
                   linear fit y = 0.876x, R2 = 0.988; Fig S5C). All single-cell reads
                   divided by 0.876 to obtain true copy numbers.
  Notes          : BioScript: three sequential heat steps (25c/5m, 42c/60m, 70c/15m).

Step 10 | ddPCR Amplification of cDNA  [RT-ddPCR ARM]
  Inputs         : RT product + 10 uL 2X ddPCR Supermix + 1 uL 20X TaqMan Probe 2 assay
  Total volume   : 20 uL; emulsified into ~20,000 droplets
  TaqMan assay   : Hs00174305_m1 (Probe 2); FAM/MGB; exon-exon junction spanning;
                   excludes amplification of genomic CD147 DNA.
  PCR schedule   :
    Hot-start        : 95 C for 10 min  (IR: 600.0 SECOND)
    40 cycles        : 94 C 30 s / 60 C 1 min (~35 min; IR: 2100.0 SECOND abstracted)
    Final extension  : 98 C for 10 min  (IR: 600.0 SECOND)
    Ramp speed       : 2.5 C/s
  Threshold      : 3200 RFU (separates CD147 amplicon-positive from negative droplets;
                   confirmed in Fig S4C). QuantaSoft Absolute Quantification setting.
  Notes          : BioScript: three sequential heat steps (95c/10m, 94c/35m, 98c/10m).

Step 11 | mRNA RT-ddPCR Detection and QC Gate  [RT-ddPCR ARM]
  Module         : rtddpcrDetection (abstracts QX100 readout + 87.6% RT recovery correction)
  Detection      : 30 s
  Pass gate      : mRNASignal > 0 -> CD147 mRNA detected above LOD -> dispose (BB5)
  Fail gate      : mRNASignal <= 0 -> below LOD -> drain (BB6)
  Terminal       : BB7 (both branches converge; dispose mRNASignal; NOP; experiment ends)
  Results        : Single-cell range: 57 +/- 18 to 2,651 +/- 121 CD147 mRNA copies/cell.
                   Population mean: 188.2 copies/cell; SD: 90 copies/cell.
                   100-cell averages: 106 +/- 2 to 215 +/- 3 copies/cell (narrower range).
                   ~1,000 proteins translated per CD147 mRNA molecule.
                   Spearman R = 0.10 with protein (poor correlation; n=131 cells).
                   mRNA distribution fits gamma pdf (p=0.65; two-state stochastic process).
                   Transcription burst size: 40 +/- 4 mRNAs/burst; rate: 3.78 +/- 0.38/day.


DOWNSTREAM ANALYSIS
-------------------

mRNA-Protein Correlation
  Method         : Spearman rank correlation
  Result         : R = 0.10 (n=131 HEK293T cells; Fig 4B)
  Interpretation : Poor single-cell correlation; bulk analyses (Pearson R = 0.41-0.59) overestimate
                   correlation due to noise averaging. mRNA abundance is a poor surrogate for
                   protein copy number in single mammalian cells.

Distribution Fitting
  Software       : R v3.1.0; fitdist / fitdistcens (fitdistrplus package; Delignette-Muller 2015)
  mRNA           : Gamma pdf fit; p=0.65 (chi-squared); bins of 40 copies/cell.
                   Inconsistent with Poisson (one-step birth-death process).
  Protein        : Gamma pdf fit; p=0.24; bins of 65,000 copies/cell.
  Conclusion     : Both distributions consistent with two-state stochastic gene expression.

Stochastic Two-State Model
  Model          : Promoter stochastically switches between Off and On states.
                   mRNA transcribed only from On state; translated into protein.
                   Six kinetic parameters (c1-c6) + extrinsic noise parameter.
  Inference      : Moment-based MCMC (Zechner et al. 2012); fitted to E[M], E[P],
                   E[M^2], E[P^2] at steady state. Five independent MCMC runs per dataset.
  Validation     : E[M(t)P(t)] (mRNA-protein covariance) computed from model parameters
                   and compared against experimentally measured correlation (not used in fit).
                   4 of 5 experimental repeats: predicted and measured E[M(t)P(t)] agree.
  mRNA half-life : 20.97 hr (from Schwanhausser et al. 2011; mouse fibroblasts)
  Protein half-life: 33.48 hr (from Schwanhausser et al. 2011)
  Parameters     : See Table S1 in paper for posterior MCMC estimates.


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : albayrak_digital_pla_rtddpcr.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG            : albayrak_digital_pla_rtddpcr_main_dag.dot
               : strict digraph with nodes: main, bsbbif_2_t, bsbbif_3_f, bsbbif_4_j,
                 bsbbif_5_t, bsbbif_6_f, bsbbif_7_j
               : edges: 1->2, 1->3, 2->4, 3->4, 4->5, 4->6, 5->7, 6->7

Duration units : All durations in minutes (m) for compiler compatibility
                 (BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported)
                 Time conversions used:
                   5 min   lysis/split mix    ->  5m  (IR: 300.0 SECOND)
                   60 min  probe adsorption   -> 60m  (IR: 3600.0 SECOND)  [corrected from 25m]
                   10 min  ligation           -> 10m  (IR: 600.0 SECOND)
                   10 min  protease digest    -> 10m  (IR: 600.0 SECOND)
                   15 min  protease inact.    -> 15m  (IR: 900.0 SECOND)
                   10 min  PCR hot-start      -> 10m  (IR: 600.0 SECOND)
                   35 min  40-cycle PCR block -> 35m  (IR: 2100.0 SECOND; abstracted)
                   10 min  final extension    -> 10m  (IR: 600.0 SECOND)
                   5 min   RT denaturation    ->  5m  (IR: 300.0 SECOND)
                   5 min   RT chilling (4 C)  ->  5m  (IR: 300.0 SECOND)
                   5 min   primer annealing   ->  5m  (IR: 300.0 SECOND)
                   60 min  cDNA synthesis     -> 60m  (IR: 3600.0 SECOND)
                   15 min  RT inactivation    -> 15m  (IR: 900.0 SECOND)

Modules        : ddpcrDetection  (QX100 readout + calibration curve -> protein copy number)
                 rtddpcrDetection (QX100 readout + 87.6% RT recovery correction -> mRNA copies)

Lysate split   : BioScript has no native ratio-split operator. The 1 uL mRNA fraction and
                 2 uL protein fraction are modelled as two independent dispense+mix events
                 from the same manifest, each representing the respective volume fraction.

PCR abstraction: 40 amplification cycles (94 C 30 s / 60 C 1 min) collapsed into a single
                 heat step at 94c for 35m. Hot-start (95c/10m) and final extension (98c/10m)
                 are separate heat instructions. Applied identically to both PLA ddPCR (Step 6)
                 and RT-ddPCR (Step 10) arms.

Compiler fix   : Probe adsorption duration corrected from 25m (1500 SECOND) to 60m
                 (3600 SECOND) following biological review against Albayrak et al. Experimental
                 Procedures: "the mixture was incubated at 37 C for 1 hr". Both the mix and
                 heat instructions for probeBindingRxn updated accordingly.

Biological scope: This .bs file encodes the joint CD147 protein + mRNA quantification
                 workflow from single HEK293T cells. GFP-p65 quantification from RAW264.7
                 macrophages (Fig 3C-D) follows the digital PLA arm only (no RT-ddPCR) and
                 requires a separate .bs file with GFP_p65_Proximity_Probe manifests and
                 a 2 uL sort volume into standard 1X lysis buffer.

protocol.title: Digital Quantification of Proteins and mRNA in Single Mammalian Cells
protocol.platform: Digital PLA (proximity ligation assay) + droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) + two-step RT-ddPCR; bench-top microfluidic droplet platform (Bio-Rad QX100)
cell_lines: HEK293T (human embryonic kidney; Tlr4-GFP stable, gift from Prof. Kensuke Miyake)
protocol.objective: Absolute and simultaneous quantification of CD147 protein (digital PLA) and CD147 mRNA (two-step RT-ddPCR) copy numbers from the same single mammalian cell; parameterisation of a stochastic two-state model of gene expression

rt_ddpcr.primer_probe: TaqMan Gene Expression Assay Hs00174305_m1 (Probe 2; FAM/MGB; exon-exon spanning)

reagents.lysis_buffer: 0.1X TM lysis buffer (10-fold diluted TM Buffer, Biochain) + protease inhibitor cocktail (Biochain) + CRB (Cell Resuspension Buffer, Life Technologies) + RNaseOUT (Invitrogen)

proximity_probes.CD147: Biotinylated anti-human CD147 polyclonal goat antibody (R&D Systems, BAF972); oligonucleotide-conjugated; 400 pM each probe stock, 200 pM final
proximity_probes.GFP: Biotinylated anti-GFP polyclonal goat antibody (Abcam, AB6658)
proximity_probes.ICAM1: Biotinylated anti-murine ICAM-1 polyclonal goat antibody (R&D Systems, BAF796)

reagents.connector_oligonucleotide: Custom DNA oligo (Microsynth, Switzerland); hybridises to both proximity probe oligonucleotides to template ligation
reagents.ligation_solution: T4 DNA ligase + ligation buffer; 25-fold dilution of probe-bound sample
reagents.protease_solution: Diluted protease (Life Technologies TaqMan Protein Assay); inactivated at 95 C for 15 min
reagents.rt_system: GoScript Reverse Transcription System (Promega); random primers, dNTPs 0.5 mM each, MgCl2 3.1 mM, 1 U/uL RNaseOUT

protein_standards.CD147: Human CD147 recombinant protein (R&D Systems, 972-EMN); diluted in 0.1X TM buffer or LDB
protein_standards.GFP: Pure GFP protein (Abcam, AB84191); diluted in 1X PBS
protein_standards.ICAM1: Pure murine ICAM-1 (R&D Systems, 796-IC); diluted in 1X PBS

reagents.containers: Low-adsorption 8-well PCR strips (Thermo Fisher, AB-0266); 1.5 mL low-adsorption microfuge tubes (Ambion, AM12450)

HEK293T.media: High-glucose DMEM (Gibco, 41965-039) + 10% FCS (Gibco, 26010-066) + 100 U/mL penicillin G + 100 ug/mL streptomycin sulfate (Gibco, 15070063)
HEK293T.conditions: 37 C, 5% CO2; passage every 3-4 days to 1e5 cells/mL; max 30 passages
HEK293T.sort_marker: Tlr4-GFP fusion protein (DRAQ7 for viability; R4 gate)

RAW264.7.media: DMEM (Sigma, D6429) + 8.8% FBS (Sigma, F9665) + 0.88X GlutaMAX + 17.7 mM HEPES
RAW264.7.conditions: 37 C, 5% CO2; passage every 2-3 days to 1e5 cells/mL; max 15 passages
RAW264.7.reporter: GFP-p65 h2b-mCherry dual fluorescent stable line; sorted by FACS (GFP/mCherry gates)

facs_sorting.viability_dye: DRAQ7 (BioStatus, DR71000) at 600 nM; stains dead cell nuclei
facs_sorting.sort_target_HEK293T: Single viable Tlr4-GFP cells; 4 nested gates (SSC-H/FSC-H, SSC-H/SSC-W, FSC-H/FSC-W, DRAQ7/GFP)
facs_sorting.sort_target_RAW264.7: Single viable GFP-p65 mCherry+ macrophages; 3 nested gates (FSC/SSC, DRAQ7/FSC, GFP/mCherry)
facs_sorting.storage: Sealed with clear adhesive sheet + Parafilm; -80 C until processing

steps.name: Single-cell FACS sort and lysis
steps.notes: Single cell sorted by FACS into 3 uL 0.1X TM buffer in 8-well PCR strip; plate centrifuged briefly, sealed, stored at -80 C. 0.1X TM buffer is compatible with both digital PLA and RT-ddPCR (confirmed in Fig S4G-H). BioScript mix duration: 5m (300s in IR).

steps.name: Lysate split: protein fraction (2 uL) and mRNA fraction (1 uL)
steps.operation: split 1:2 (abstracted as two independent dispense+mix events in BioScript)
steps.notes: Physical 1:2 split; protein fraction (2 uL) into digital PLA arm; mRNA fraction (1 uL) into RT-ddPCR arm. BioScript has no native ratio-split; modelled as two variables (proteinLysate, mRNALysate) derived from lysate. LOD for CD147 protein in 2 uL fraction: 29,300 molecules/cell.

steps.name: Proximity probe adsorption
steps.notes: Both proximity probes (anti-CD147 antibody-oligonucleotide conjugates) combined in assay probe solution; bind distinct CD147 epitopes simultaneously. When bound to same molecule, oligonucleotides come into ~40 nm proximity enabling connector hybridisation. BioScript: heat at 37c for 60m (IR: 3600.0 SECOND).

steps.name: Connector oligonucleotide hybridisation and ligation
steps.notes: 96 uL ligation solution added to 4 uL probe-bound sample (25-fold dilution). Connector oligo hybridises to paired probe oligonucleotides; T4 ligase seals nicks forming dsDNA. dsDNA molecule encodes one protein detection event. BioScript: heat at 37c for 10m (IR: 600.0 SECOND).

steps.name: Protease digestion and inactivation
steps.notes: Protease digests antibody-oligonucleotide conjugates, leaving only dsDNA amplicons in solution. Inactivated at 95 C for 15 min. BioScript: heat at 37c for 10m then heat at 95c for 15m (IR: 600.0 SECOND, 900.0 SECOND).

steps.name: ddPCR droplet generation and amplification (protein)
steps.readout: QX100 Droplet Reader + QuantaSoft v1.3.2.0 Absolute Quantification; threshold set from most concentrated standard
steps.notes: Positive droplets contain one amplified dsDNA molecule (fluorescent); negative droplets do not. Concentration: C = (1000/Vd) * ln(1 - P/R). Absolute protein count from calibration curve. BioScript: three sequential heat steps (95c/10m, 94c/35m, 98c/10m). IR: 600s, 2100s, 600s.

steps.name: Protein ddPCR detection and QC gate

pass.interpretation: CD147 protein detected above LOD (29,300 molecules/cell)

fail.interpretation: Below LOD; cell had insufficient CD147 protein

expected_results.single_cell_range: 35,900 to 636,000 CD147 proteins per cell (138 HEK293T cells)

steps.name: RT primer annealing
steps.notes: RNA secondary structure denatured at 70 C for 5 min; immediately chilled on ice (4 C, 5 min) to prevent re-folding before RT. BioScript: heat at 70c for 5m then heat at 4c for 5m (IR: 300.0 SECOND each).

steps.name: Reverse transcription (cDNA synthesis)
steps.recovery_validation: T7 in-vitro transcribed CD147 mRNA standard measured by A260 vs RT-ddPCR (y=0.876x, R2=0.988); all single-cell reads corrected by 0.876 factor
steps.notes: BioScript: heat at 25c for 5m, heat at 42c for 60m, heat at 70c for 15m (IR: 300s, 3600s, 900s).

steps.name: ddPCR amplification of cDNA (mRNA)
steps.taqman_assay: Hs00174305_m1 (Probe 2); FAM/MGB; exon-exon junction spanning; excludes genomic DNA
steps.notes: BioScript: heat at 95c for 10m, heat at 94c for 35m, heat at 98c for 10m (IR: 600s, 2100s, 600s). Concentrations converted to mRNA copies/cell with 87.6% RT recovery correction.

steps.name: mRNA RT-ddPCR detection and QC gate

pass.interpretation: CD147 mRNA detected above corrected LOD (52.5 copies/cell = 87 aM)

fail.interpretation: Below LOD; mRNA undetectable in this cell

expected_results.distribution_fit: Gamma pdf (p=0.65 by chi-squared test); two-state stochastic gene expression

mRNA_protein_correlation.conclusion: Poor correlation at single-cell level; contrasts with bulk estimates (Pearson R = 0.41-0.59). mRNA is a poor surrogate for protein abundance.

distribution_fitting.mRNA_fit: Gamma pdf (shape=alpha, rate=beta); p=0.65 chi-squared goodness-of-fit
distribution_fitting.conclusion: Distributions inconsistent with Poisson (one-step birth-death); consistent with two-state stochastic process

stochastic_model.type: Two-state promoter switching model (Peccoud and Ycart 1995; Paulsson 2005)
stochastic_model.inference_method: Markov-chain Monte Carlo (MCMC); moment-based analysis (Zechner et al. 2012)
stochastic_model.validation_term: E[M(t)P(t)] (mRNA-protein covariance; not used in fitting)
stochastic_model.model_validation: 4 out of 5 experimental repeats: predicted E[M(t)P(t)] agrees with measured correlation

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.description: Cell lysis, lysate split, digital PLA arm (S1-S7), RT-ddPCR arm (S8-S11)

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_4_j
basic_blocks.description: Dispose proteinSignal; mRNA RT-ddPCR arm begins

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_7_j
basic_blocks.description: Dispose mRNASignal; NOP; experiment ends

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Sperm-seq wet lab protocol: sperm preparation and droplet-based sequencing library generation
Source Link  : https://www.protocols.io/view/sperm-seq-wet-lab-protocol-sperm-preparation-and-d-j8nlk9q81v5r/v1
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.pex-823/v1
Journal      : Research Square (preprint), posted June 3rd, 2020
Authors      : Avery Davis Bell, Curtis J. Mello, Steven A. McCarroll
Affiliations : Department of Genetics, Harvard Medical School;
               Program in Medical and Population Genetics, Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
Platform     : Droplet-based single-sperm sequencing (10X Genomics GemCode, Option 1)


OVERVIEW
--------
Sperm-seq is a high-throughput, droplet-based single-sperm sequencing technology capable of
generating thousands of cell-barcoded single-sperm sequencing libraries in a single run. This
protocol encodes the complete wet-lab workflow: sperm preparation (decondensation), fluorescence-
based cell quantification, and 10X Genomics GemCode droplet library generation.

The protocol is divided into three phases:
  1. Sperm preparation (~3.5 h): PBS washes, Buffer SMT freeze-thaw cycling, chromatin
     decondensation in Buffer DB (heparin + BME), and heparinase treatment to remove PCR inhibitor
  2. Sperm quantification (~15 min): SYBR Green I fluorescent staining (1:100 dilution),
     hemocytometer counting, and concentration-based QC gate
  3. Library generation (1-3 days): dilution to target cell number, GemCode master mix assembly,
     droplet generation on chip, GEM barcoding incubation, and library QC

Sequencing output is processed using the Bell et al. Nature 2020 pipeline (31,228 human sperm
genomes; "Insights about variation in meiosis from 31,228 human sperm genomes").


REAGENTS
--------

Buffer SMT (freeze-thaw buffer; adapted from Montag et al. 1992; Samocha-Bone et al. 1998):
  250 mM sucrose (from 1 M sucrose, Sigma S7903)
  5 mM MgCl2 (from 1 M MgCl2, Sigma M8266)
  10 mM Tris pH 7.5 (from 1 M Tris pH 7.5, ThermoFisher Scientific 15567027)
  Example 10 mL recipe: 2500 uL sucrose + 50 uL MgCl2 + 100 uL Tris pH 7.5 + 7350 uL ultrapure water

Buffer DB (salt decondensation buffer; adapted from Montag et al. 1992; Samocha-Bone et al. 1998):
  113 mM KCl (from 1 M KCl, Sigma P5405)
  12.5 mM KH2PO4 (from 1 M KH2PO4, Sigma P9791)
  2.5 mM Na2HPO4 (from 1 M Na2HPO4, Sigma S3264)
  2.5 mM MgCl2 (from 1 M MgCl2, Sigma M8266)
  20 mM Tris pH 7.5 (from 1 M Tris pH 7.5, ThermoFisher Scientific 15567027)
  Freshly added per 100 uL (4 samples): 1.5 uL 10 mM heparin + 2 uL 100 mM BME + 96.5 uL Buffer DB base

Other reagents:
  1X PBS pH 7.4 (Life Technologies 10010023)
  10 mM heparin (Heparin Sodium Salt from Porcine, Sigma H3393; diluted in ultrapure water)
  100 mM beta-mercaptoethanol / BME (diluted from 14.3 M, Sigma M6250; used in fume hood)
  0.1 units/uL Heparinase 1 (Sigma H2519; diluted in ultrapure water; stored at -20 C)
  10X SYBR Green I (diluted from 10000X, ThermoFisher Scientific S7563)

10X GemCode reagents (Option 1):
  GemCode Gel-Bead Kit
  GemCode Chip Kit
  GemCode Library Kit
  Master mix per sample (60 uL total): 32.5 uL GemCode reagent mix + 1.5 uL primer release agent
    + 9.2 uL GemCode polymerase + 16.8 uL ultrapure water
  Beads: vortex full speed 25 s; dilute 1:11 in ultrapure water (>=90 uL per sample)
  Chip loading: 60 uL sample / 85 uL diluted beads / 150 uL droplet generation oil


EQUIPMENT
---------
  Nonstick 1.5 mL microfuge tubes (ThermoFisher Scientific AM12450)
  Fuchs-Rosenthal C-chip hemocytometer (VitaScientific NANC07005)
  10X GemCode controller and accessories (per GemCode User Guide Rev C)
  Centrifuge capable of 400g at 4C
  Fluorescence microscope (green channel for SYBR Green I counting)
  Liquid nitrogen (for freeze-thaw cycles)


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Thaw and Transfer Sperm Aliquot
  Input    : SpermAliquot (>=250,000 cells; typically 10 uL)
  Procedure: Thaw at room temperature. Quick spin. Transfer to nonstick 1.5 mL tube.
  Notes    : Nonstick tubes minimise cell loss during subsequent centrifugation steps.

Step 2 | First PBS Wash
  Inputs   : spermRaw, PBS
  Procedure: Spin 400g, 4C, 10 min. Remove supernatant. Resuspend pellet in 10 uL PBS.
  BioScript: heat at 4c for 10m abstracts cold centrifugation (in-place, no variable assignment).

Step 3 | Second PBS Wash
  Inputs   : spermPellet1, PBS
  Procedure: Spin 400g, 4C, 10 min. Remove supernatant.
  BioScript: heat at 4c for 10m.

Step 4 | Resuspend in Buffer SMT
  Inputs   : spermPellet2, BufferSMT
  Volume   : 2.5 uL Buffer SMT
  Purpose  : Osmotic protection of sperm membrane during freeze-thaw cycles.

Step 5 | Freeze-Thaw Cycles x3
  Input    : spermInSMT
  Procedure: Submerge tube in liquid nitrogen 5-10 s. Uncap to de-pressurise.
             Hold in fist until thawed. Repeat for a total of 3 cycles.
  Purpose  : Mechanical disruption of sperm membrane to aid chromatin release.
  BioScript: 3 cycles unrolled as 6 sequential heat calls (no loop constructs):
             heat at 4c for 10s (freeze) / heat at 37c for 30s (thaw) x3.

Step 6 | Prepare Buffer DB with Heparin and BME
  Inputs   : BufferDB_Base, Heparin_10mM, BME_100mM
  Recipe   : 1.5 uL 10 mM heparin + 2 uL 100 mM BME + 96.5 uL Buffer DB base per 100 uL (4 samples)
  Notes    : Prepare fresh immediately before use. BME handled in fume hood.
  BioScript: Two sequential mix steps (heparin into DB base, then BME).

Step 7 | Chromatin Decondensation in Buffer DB
  Inputs   : spermInSMT, bufferDBReady
  Volume   : 22.5 uL Buffer DB per sample
  Incubation: 37C for 45 min
  Purpose  : BME reduces protamine disulfide crosslinks; heparin prevents chromatin aggregation.
  BioScript: heat at 37c for 45m (in-place on spermDecondensing).

Step 8 | Heparinase Treatment
  Inputs   : spermDecondensing, Heparinase (0.1 units/uL)
  Volume   : 5 uL freshly-thawed heparinase per sample
  Thaw     : On ice during last half of 37C incubation (Step 7)
  Incubation: Room temperature, 2 h (120 min)
  Purpose  : Removes heparin to eliminate PCR inhibition in downstream library amplification.
  BioScript: heat at 25c for 120m abstracts RT incubation.
  Dataflow : spermDecondensed is the terminal output of the full prep chain; consumed at Step 11.

Step 9 | SYBR Green I Staining for Cell Counting
  Inputs   : SpermCountAliquot_Decondensed (1 uL sub-sample), SYBRGreenI_10X, PBS
  Dilution : 1:100 (1 uL sperm + 10 uL 10X SYBR Green I + 89 uL PBS)
  Incubation: 5-10 min in dark at room temperature (with or without gentle rotation)
  Morphology: Decondensed sperm appear as large bright fluorescent circles under green light;
              non-decondensed sperm appear as compact dots.
  BioScript abstraction note: BioScript has no split operation. The 1 uL counting sub-sample is
    physically pipetted from the post-heparinase decondensed tube before the bulk stock is used
    for library prep. In BioScript this sub-sample is modelled as a single dispense of
    SpermCountAliquot_Decondensed -- a manifest explicitly named to identify its physical source.
    The bulk stock (spermDecondensed) flows unbroken into Step 11 to preserve end-to-end dataflow.

Step 10 | Hemocytometer Cell Count
  Input    : stainedSperm
  Instrument: Fuchs-Rosenthal C-chip hemocytometer (VitaScientific NANC07005)
  Procedure: Load 20 uL stained sperm into C-chip. Count sperm in 5 big squares under
             green fluorescent light. Concentration (cells/uL) = count in 5 squares x 100.
  Target   : 10,833 cells in 5 uL for GemCode loading.
  Detection: spermCountDetection module; 5 min detect duration.
  QC gate:
    Pass (spermCountSignal > 0): sufficient cells confirmed; dispose stain aliquot; proceed to library.
    Fail (spermCountSignal <= 0): insufficient count (failed decondensation or too few cells); drain.

Step 11 | Dilute Sperm to Target Concentration
  Inputs   : spermDecondensed (full prep chain output), UltrapureWater
  Target   : 10,833 cells in 5 uL ultrapure water
  Notes    : This step is the primary consumption of spermDecondensed; the main dataflow is intact.

Step 12 | GemCode Master Mix Assembly
  Inputs   : GemCodeReagentMix, PrimerReleaseAgent, GemCodePolymerase, UltrapureWater
  Volumes  : 32.5 uL reagent mix + 1.5 uL primer release agent + 9.2 uL polymerase + 16.8 uL water
  Total    : 60 uL per sample
  BioScript: Three sequential mix steps in component addition order.

Step 13 | Combine Sperm with Master Mix
  Inputs   : spermDiluted (5 uL), masterMix (60 uL)
  Total    : 65 uL
  Notes    : Pipette gently with wide-bore tips; decondensed chromatin is fragile.

Step 14 | Prepare GemCode Beads
  Inputs   : GemCodeBeads, UltrapureWater
  Procedure: Vortex beads at full speed for 25 s. Dilute 1:11 in ultrapure water (>=90 uL per sample).
  BioScript: Two sequential mix steps chain to accumulate dilution water.

Step 15 | Load GemCode Chip
  Inputs   : spermMasterMix, beadsDiluted, DropletGenerationOil
  Wells    : Sample 60 uL / Beads 85 uL / Oil 150 uL
  Notes    : GemCode controller partitions mixture into GEMs; single sperm barcoded per GEM.

Step 16 | GEM Incubation and Library Construction
  Input    : chipLoaded
  Incubation: 37C, 180 min (3h GEM incubation; BioScript: heat at 37c for 180m)
  Library  : Adapter ligation and indexing per GemCode User Guide Rev C Steps 5.36-6.2.6
  QC       : libraryQCDetection module (Bioanalyzer/qPCR fragment size and yield); 30 s detect.
  Sequencing: Illumina sequencer per 10X Genomics instructions; slightly increased input
              concentration improves yield.
  Analysis : Bell et al. Nature 2020 pipeline.
  QC gate:
    Pass (libraryQCSignal > 0): valid library; dispose chipLoaded.
    Fail (libraryQCSignal <= 0): library prep failed; drain chipLoaded.


TROUBLESHOOTING
---------------
If sequence data shows uneven genome coverage or unclear bead/ambient DNA boundary:
  - Make fresh Buffer SMT and Buffer DB before Step 1
  - Vary BME: try 1 mM final concentration (reduce BME_100mM from 2 uL to 1 uL per 100 uL DB)
  - Decrease freeze-thaw cycles (try 2 instead of 3)
  - Use wide-bore pipette tips and gentle pipetting at all mixing steps


TIMING
------
  Sperm preparation    : ~3.5 hours
  Sperm quantification : ~15 minutes (more for multiple samples)
  Library preparation  : 1-3 days (depending on kit/approach and break points taken)


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : bell_sperm_seq_library_generation.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG file       : bell_sperm_seq_library_generation_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations in s or m (BioScript supports s and m only; h not supported)
                 45 min decondensation  -> 45m   (IR: 2700.0 SECOND)
                 120 min heparinase RT  -> 120m  (IR: 7200.0 SECOND)
                 7 min SYBR stain       -> 7m    (IR: 420.0 SECOND)
                 5 min detect count     -> 5m    (IR: 300.0 SECOND)
                 180 min GEM incubation -> 180m  (IR: 10800.0 SECOND)
Modules        : spermCountDetection, libraryQCDetection
Compiler notes :
  - heat is in-place throughout; never assigned to a variable
  - 3 freeze-thaw cycles unrolled as 6 sequential heat calls (no loop constructs)
  - drain lowered to dispose in IR; this is known compiler behaviour; .bs source is correct
  - SpermCountAliquot_Decondensed manifest models the 1 uL sub-sample from the decondensed stock;
    spermDecondensed flows unbroken into the library dilution step (Step 11)

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Enhancing Protease Activity Assay in Droplet-Based Microfluidics Using a Biomolecule Concentrator
Source Link  : https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3165005/pdf/nihms305699.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/ja2036628
Journal      : J. Am. Chem. Soc., 2011, Vol. 133, No. 27, pp. 10368-10371
Platform     : Integrated nanofluidic ICP biomolecule concentrator + flow-focusing droplet generator (PDMS chip)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes an integrated microfluidic platform that combines a nanofluidic
biomolecule concentrator based on ion concentration polarization (ICP) with a flow-focusing
microdroplet generator on a single PDMS chip. The concentrator pre-concentrates low-abundance
enzyme molecules from a diluted physiological sample into a pL-scale plug before encapsulating
them into water-in-oil droplet microreactors. This addresses two fundamental limitations of
droplet-based enzyme assays: low assay sensitivity from low-abundance analytes, and long
reaction times required to turn over sufficient substrate for detection.

The platform was validated on:
  1. beta-galactosidase (platform characterisation)
  2. Kinase MK2 (platform characterisation)
  3. Recombinant MMP-9 at 0.2-3.2 nM (primary assay; kinetics determination)
  4. MMP activity in MEF cellular supernatant -- stimulated vs. untreated conditions

Key achievements vs. conventional droplet assays:
  - ~10-fold reduction in assay reaction time
  - ~100-fold reduction in sample volume (<25 uL total for up to 10 conditions)
  - ~100-fold concentration enhancement in the ICP plug (~20-fold at encapsulation)
  - kcat/Km = 7.81e4 M^-1 s^-1 for MMP-9, consistent with plate-reader and prior literature
  - Stimulated vs. untreated MEF differentiation in 5 min (concentrated) vs. >50 min
    (unconcentrated)


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Fabrication  : PDMS chip bonded to PDMS-coated glass slide; standard soft lithography.
               Three syringe pumps (Harvard PHD2000) drive fluid flow.

Concentrator section:
  - Polymeric nanoporous ion-selective junctions flanking the main sample channel
  - Buffer side channels on either side of the junction for voltage application
  - Applied voltage: ~50 V (main channel at +50 V, buffer channels at GND)
  - Sample flow rate: 0.03 uL/min (middle channel, pressure-driven)
  - Mechanism: electrokinetic force opposes pressure-driven flow; negatively charged
    molecules accumulate at depletion boundary into a continuously growing pL-scale plug
  - Enhancement: ~100-fold in plug; reduces to ~20-fold at encapsulation due to Gaussian
    diffusion during ~200 um transport to droplet generator
  - Enhancement factor tunable by adjusting accumulation time and flow rate

Mixing zone:
  - Released plug merges 1:1 with substrate from two flanking side channels
  - Enzyme:substrate ratio controlled by balancing three aqueous stream flow rates

Droplet generator section:
  - Flow-focusing geometry; hydrophobic PDMS surfaces cause aqueous phase to lift off
    into oil and encapsulate
  - Carrier fluid: HFE7500 fluorocarbon oil at 1.0 uL/min
  - Surfactant: biocompatible perfluorinated surfactant (synthesised in-house) in oil phase
  - Droplet volume: ~40 pL; generation rate: ~2.5 kHz; monodisperse W/O emulsion
  - Gaussian plug divided into train of droplets with graded enzyme concentrations
    (0.2-3.2 nM from tail to centre) enabling parallel kinetics screening in one run

Channels:
  - Middle channel   : Sample stream (enzyme + Alexa Fluor-546 tracer)
  - Side channels    : Substrate streams (two flanking); converge at mixing zone
  - Buffer channels  : PBS flanking main channel on either side of ion-selective membrane


REAGENTS
--------
Tracer dye       : Alexa Fluor-546 phalloidin; ex 561 nm / em 572 nm
                   Co-loaded with enzyme; monitors plug in real time; intensity ratio
                   vs. enzyme-free droplet infers local enzyme concentration per droplet.
Carrier oil      : 3M Novec HFE7500 fluorocarbon oil
Surfactant       : Synthesised biocompatible perfluorinated surfactant in oil phase
Priming agent    : Pluronics F-127 (2% in PBS)
MMP buffer       : Standard MMP assay buffer
Enzyme (recomb.) : MMP-9 (recombinant); 0.2 nM in MMP buffer; screened 0.2-3.2 nM
Substrate        : FRET-based polypeptide MMP substrate; 5 uM; fluoresces upon cleavage
Cellular samples : Mouse embryonic fibroblast (MEF) conditioned media;
                   0.5x dilution in MMP buffer; stimulated (cytokine-treated) and untreated;
                   <25 uL total consumed across both conditions


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Device Priming and Surface Passivation
  Reagents  : PBS, Pluronics F-127
  Mix       : 2% Pluronics F-127 in PBS
  Duration  : 5 min
  Purpose   : Reduces nonspecific adsorption of biomolecules to PDMS channel walls
              and to droplet interfaces; critical for low-abundance analyte recovery.

Step 2 | Enzyme Sample Stream Preparation
  Reagents  : MMP-9 (0.2 nM), Alexa Fluor-546 tracer, MMP buffer
  Operation : Mix enzyme with tracer, then dilute in MMP buffer
  Channel   : Middle channel, flow rate 0.03 uL/min
  Notes     : Tracer fluorescence (ex 561 nm / em 572 nm) monitors plug accumulation and
              allows per-droplet enzyme concentration to be inferred post-encapsulation
              by comparing to tracer intensity of enzyme-free droplet (0.2 nM reference).

Step 3 | Substrate Side-Channel Stream Preparation
  Reagents  : FRET MMP polypeptide substrate (5 uM in MMP buffer)
  Operation : Dispense into left and right flanking side channels
  Notes     : Substrate streams merge with enzyme plug at mixing zone just before droplet
              formation. Enzyme:substrate ratio set to 1:1 by balancing aqueous flow rates.

Step 4 | ICP Biomolecule Concentrator -- Accumulation Phase
  Operation : Electrokinetic trapping (voltage-on)
              Modelled as heat at 25 C (ambient; no external heating) in BioScript.
  Voltage   : ~50 V across ion-selective nanoporous junction
  Flow rate : 0.03 uL/min (sample); PBS in buffer side channels at GND
  Duration  : ~10 min (accumulation time; primary handle for tuning enhancement factor)
  Output    : ~100-fold concentration enhancement in the pL-scale plug
  Notes     : Voltage-off releases plug by pressure-driven flow. Negatively charged enzyme
              molecules and tracer trap at the ICP depletion boundary and accumulate
              continuously. Enhancement factor adjustable by concentration time.

Step 5 | Plug Transport and Substrate Mixing
  Operation : mix (plug + substrate)
  Distance  : ~200 um from concentrator to droplet generator
  Output    : ~20-fold enhancement at encapsulation point (Gaussian diffusion during transport
              reduces peak from ~100-fold). Enzyme and substrate mixed 1:1 in mixing zone.

Step 6 | Flow-Focusing Droplet Encapsulation
  Operation : mix assay plug with HFE7500 + surfactant carrier phase
  Oil flow  : 1.0 uL/min
  Droplets  : ~40 pL; ~2.5 kHz generation rate; monodisperse W/O emulsion
  Bins      : Gaussian plug divided into droplet train spanning 0.2-3.2 nM enzyme:
                High bin  : ~20-fold enhancement; ~3.2 nM MMP-9 (plug centre)
                Mid bin   : ~10-fold enhancement; ~1.6 nM MMP-9 (plug shoulder)
                Low bin   : ~1-fold;              ~0.2 nM MMP-9 (plug tail; baseline)
  Notes     : Vortices induced inside droplets ensure rapid enzyme-substrate mixing
              post-encapsulation. Surfactant stabilises emulsion; contents isolated for
              individual reactions. Simultaneous observation of multiple concentrations
              enables high-throughput kinetics determination in a single run.

Step 7 | Droplet Incubation and Fluorescence Monitoring (Recombinant MMP-9)
  Operation      : heat at 37 C for 35 min; detect mmpActivityDetection
  Readout        : Product fluorescence increases linearly with time per droplet (Fig. 2A)
                   Tracer channel reports local enzyme concentration per droplet
  Kinetics       : Reaction rates vs. concentration fitted to Michaelis-Menten (Fig. 2B)
                   kcat/Km = 7.81e4 M^-1 s^-1 (consistent with plate-reader and literature)
  Neg. control   : ~25 a.u. fluorescence change (no protease); flat baseline
  Enhancement    : Concentrated droplets show 15-fold higher reaction rate vs. unconcentrated
  QC gate        : assaySignal > 0 -> dispose (BB2); <= 0 -> drain (BB3); join at BB4

Step 8 | Cellular Supernatant Sample Preparation
  Reagents  : MEF conditioned media (stimulated and untreated), 0.5x in MMP buffer,
              Alexa Fluor-546 tracer, MMP buffer
  Operation : Mix each condition with tracer, then with buffer
  Volume    : <25 uL total across both conditions
  Notes     : Both conditions run in sequence on same chip platform.

Step 9 | ICP Concentration of Cellular Supernatant
  Operation : Electrokinetic trapping; same conditions as Step 4
              Modelled as heat at 25 C for 10 min in BioScript
  Output    : ~10-20x enhancement at encapsulation
  Notes     : Concentration step amplifies activity difference between stimulated and
              untreated ~10-fold relative to unconcentrated samples. Enables detection
              of biologically relevant MMP activity differences from physiological samples.

Step 10 | Cellular Assay Droplet Encapsulation
  Operation  : mix concentrated plugs with FRET substrate + carrier oil phase
  Substrate  : FRET MMP substrate (5 uM)
  Carrier    : HFE7500 + fluorocarbon surfactant
  Notes      : Same flow-focusing geometry as Step 6. Stimulated and untreated samples
               run as separate droplet populations.

Step 11 | Cellular Proteolytic Activity Detection
  Operation      : heat at 37 C for 5 min; detect mmpActivityDetection
  Key timepoint  : 5 min sufficient to differentiate stimulated vs. untreated (concentrated)
                   Concentrated  -- stimulated: slope 2.14 a.u./s (line-1)
                                 -- untreated:  slope 0.95 a.u./s (line-3)
                   Unconcentrated requires >50 min:
                                    stimulated: slope 0.32 a.u./s (line-2)
                                    untreated:  slope 0.22 a.u./s (line-4)  (Fig. 3A)
  Kinetics       : Linear relation between reaction rate and concentration (Fig. 3B)
                   Stimulated:  (kcat/KM)[E] = 1.61e-4 s^-1
                   Untreated:   (kcat/KM)[E] = 4.68e-5 s^-1
  QC gate        : cellSignal > 0 -> dispose (BB5); <= 0 -> drain (BB6); join at BB7


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : chen_concentrator_droplet_mmp_assay.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG            : chen_concentrator_droplet_mmp_assay_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations in s or m (BioScript supports s and m only; no h token)
                 10 min accumulation -> 10m  (IR: 600.0 SECOND)
                 35 min incubation   -> 35m  (IR: 2100.0 SECOND)
                  5 min cell assay   ->  5m  (IR: 300.0 SECOND)
Modules        : fluorescenceDetection, tracerFluorescenceDetection, mmpActivityDetection
Manifests      : PBS, PluronicF127, AlexaFluor546_Tracer, MMPBuffer, MMP9_Enzyme,
                 FRET_MMP_Substrate, CellularSupernatant_Stimulated,
                 CellularSupernatant_Untreated, HFE7500_FluorocarbonOil, FluorocarbonSurfactant

ICP concentrator abstraction:
  The electrokinetic trapping (voltage-on accumulation) step has no native BioScript
  primitive. It is modelled as heat at 25 C (room temperature; no external heating applied
  in the paper). Duration encodes accumulation time, which is the primary experimental
  handle for controlling the enhancement factor. Voltage-off plug release is implicit at
  the end of the heat block. Buffer side-channel flows are represented as dispense + mix
  steps converging at the junction, consistent with the three-stream chip geometry.

Droplet encapsulation abstraction:
  Flow-focusing encapsulation is modelled as mix with carrier oil phase. The Gaussian
  plug producing a graded enzyme concentration across the droplet train is represented
  as three discrete scalar droplet variables (high/mid/low bins). This encodes the
  parallel kinetics screening experiment (Fig. 2B) within BioScript's scalar variable model.

Compiler behaviour notes:
  - drain statements are lowered to dispose at IR level; expected BioScript behaviour,
    not a source error.
  - BB5 (pass branch of second if gate) has no explicit jump instruction in IR; the
    compiler infers the edge 5->7 via fall-through. The DAG edge is present and correct.
    No source fix is required; behaviour is consistent with reference files
    (samlali_hybrid_microfluidics_isoclone.bs, moazami_world_to_chip_dmf.bs).

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Automated Digital Microfluidic Platform for Magnetic-Particle-Based Immunoassays with Optimization by Design of Experiments
Source Link  : https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/ac401847x.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/ac401847x
Journal      : Analytical Chemistry, 2013, Vol. 85, pp. 9638-9646
Platform     : Automated DMF (digital microfluidics) with integrated motorized PMT and magnetic lens assembly on Pogo-pin electrode array


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a fully automated digital microfluidic (DMF) platform for performing
magnetic-particle-based sandwich immunoassays from sample to analysis with minimal manual
intervention. The target analyte is thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), clinically relevant for
thyroid disease screening (normal range 0.3-4 uIU/mL; hyperthyroidism: <0.3 uIU/mL).

The platform integrates three core hardware components:
  1. A 90 Pogo pin interface (two 15x3 arrays, 100 mil spacing) for digital microfluidic control,
     enabling 15 high-voltage inputs per square inch on a 3x2 in. DMF device.
  2. A motorized Hamamatsu H10682-110 PMT for chemiluminescent detection, with motor-driven
     engage/disengage and a light-blocking shutter (dark count < 50 counts/s in enclosure).
  3. A "magnetic lens" assembly: a neodymium bar magnet (3 x 0.5 x 0.25 in., Br=1.32 T)
     flanked by two AISI 1080 steel machined armatures acting as triangular field directors.
     Motor-driven vertical engagement (~150 um gap, ~600 uN vertical force) focuses the
     magnetic field to a narrow zone, enabling up to 8 simultaneous parallel magnetic
     separations -- vs. a maximum of 2 with the prior neodymium disc geometry.

The protocol implements a 3^3 full factorial Design of Experiments (DOE) optimization --
the first reported DOE optimization for immunoassays in any microfluidic system -- varying
three factors: sample volume (1, 3, 5 unit droplets), sample incubation time (3, 6, 9 min),
and TSH concentration (0, 0.4, 4 uIU/mL), totalling 108 discrete experiments. The resulting
optimized protocol achieves a 5-fold lower limit of detection (0.15 uIU/mL) and a 2-fold
reduction in sample incubation time relative to the prior prototype setup (Ng et al., 2012).


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Bottom plate : 80 actuation electrodes (2.2 x 2.2 mm each), interdigitated borders
               (140 um peak-to-peak sinusoids), interelectrode gaps 30-80 um.
               8 reagent reservoirs (16.4 x 6.7 mm), 4 waste reservoirs (16.4 x 6.4 mm).
               Substrate thickness ~1.15 mm. Contact pads on periphery for Pogo pin interface.
Top plate    : Grounded brass leaflets connected at device hinge on loading.

Unit droplet volume  : ~800 nL
Reservoir volume     : ~3.5 uL
Actuation            : Sine wave AC, 100-120 Vrms, 10 kHz; Microdrop software + Arduino-based
                       high-voltage switching instrument.
Mixing mode          : Unit droplet shuttled in circular motion across 4+ electrodes.

Magnetic lens positions:
  Disengaged : ~3.8 cm below device (no field influence on droplets)
  Engaged    : ~150 um below device; vertical force ~600 uN (>470 uN minimum for immobilization)
  Field decay: <35 uN at >4 mm from magnet center (minimizes stray particle attraction outside
               separation zone; contrast with disc magnet where stray force at 10 mm = ~50/100 uN)

PMT positions:
  Disengaged : ~5 cm above device; shutter closed
  Engaged    : Several hundred micrometers above device; shutter open; collects emitted light


REAGENTS
--------
Paramagnetic particles  : Anti-TSH antibody-coated (Abbott Laboratories, Abbott Park, IL)
                          Working solution: ~3.0e8 particles/mL in DMF-compatible particle
                          diluent (pH 10): Tris base 6.1 g/L, NaCl 5.8 g/L, BSA 1% w/v,
                          thimerosal 0.05% w/v, Pluronic L64 0.05% v/v.

TSH standards           : Abbott Laboratories (Abbott Park, IL)
                          Concentrations: 0, 0.4, 4 uIU/mL
                          Supplemented with Pluronic L64 0.05% v/v prior to use.

HRP conjugate           : HRP-conjugated mouse monoclonal anti-TSH (Abcam Inc., Cambridge, MA)
                          Working solution: 2 ug/mL in DMF-compatible conjugate diluent.

Chemiluminescent substrate : SuperSignal ELISA Femto (Thermo Fischer Scientific, Rockford, IL)
                             Components: stable peroxide (H2O2) + luminol-enhancer solution.
                             Both supplemented with Pluronic L64 0.025% v/v prior to use.

Wash buffer             : DMF-compatible custom wash buffer (composition per Ng et al. 2012).
Pluronic L64            : BASF Corp., Germany; donated by Brenntag Canada (Toronto, ON).
Deionized water         : 18 MOhm-cm at 25 C.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Paramagnetic Particle Dispense and Immobilization
  Reagents        : ParamagneticParticles
  Operation       : dispense 1 unit droplet (~800 nL)
  Magnetic lens   : Engaged (~150 um gap); particles pellet on device surface above magnet.
  Separation      : Particle diluent supernatant moved away by electrode actuation (magnetic sep.).
  Purpose         : Immobilize antibody-coated particles for sample delivery.
  Notes           : Magnetic lens supports 8 simultaneous separations across device width.
                    Particle pellet radius example: ~155 um at 3.0e8 particles/mL in 800 nL droplet.

Step 2 | TSH Sample Dispense and Pooling (5 unit droplets = 4 uL)
  Reagents        : TSH_Standard (0, 0.4, or 4 uIU/mL)
  Operation       : dispense x5 (individual scalars) + sequential merge
  Unit volume nL  : 800
  Pooled volume   : 4 uL (5 x 800 nL)
  DOE result      : 5 droplets selected as optimal across all concentrations; maximum Sqrt(SBR)
                    response at 5 droplets x 3 min (Fig 4D, response surface).
  Notes           : Five droplets dispensed as five independent scalar variables and accumulated
                    via chained mix operations (compiler constraint: multi-unit dispense does not
                    produce discrete indexed elements suitable for downstream scalar operations).

Step 3 | Sample Incubation with Immobilized Particles
  Reagents        : tshSample (pooled), particleDrop (immobilized)
  Operation       : mix
  Duration        : 3 min (optimized; pilot protocol midlevel was 6 min)
  Mixing mode     : Continuous circular shuttle, 100-120 Vrms, 10 kHz
  DOE finding     : Negative vol x inc and con x inc interaction coefficients show longer
                    incubation at high TSH or high volume reduces Sqrt(SBR). Optimum is
                    5 droplets x 3 min. The integrated platform achieves faster analyte binding
                    than the prototype due to continuous uniform mixing (hand-held probes in
                    prototype could not provide controlled continuous mixing).

Step 4 | Post-Sample Wash Series (4 cycles)
  Reagents        : WashBuffer
  Wash cycles     : 4
  Per cycle       : dispense wash buffer -> mix with particles (30 s, resuspend) ->
                    dispense additional wash buffer -> mix (10 s, transfer) ->
                    drain supernatant to waste.
  Magnetic lens   : Engaged for pellet immobilization; disengaged for resuspension each cycle.
  Purpose         : Remove unbound TSH and non-specific binders.
  QC gate         : detect chemiluminescenceDetection on particlesWashed for 5 s.
                    washSignal > 0  -> particle pellets confirmed; proceed to conjugate step (BB4).
                    washSignal <= 0 -> pellets lost during wash; drain and abort (BB3).

Step 5 | HRP-Conjugate Delivery and Incubation
  Reagents        : HRP_AntiTSH_Conjugate
  Operation       : dispense 1 unit droplet (~800 nL) + mix
  Duration        : 2 min
  Mixing mode     : Active electrode mixing, 100-120 Vrms, 10 kHz
  Purpose         : HRP-conjugated anti-TSH binds to TSH captured on particle surface
                    (completes the sandwich: particle-antibody -- TSH -- HRP-antibody).

Step 6 | Post-Conjugate Wash Series (4 cycles)
  Reagents        : WashBuffer
  Wash cycles     : 4
  Per cycle       : Same as Step 4 (dispense -> mix -> drain).
  Critical note   : Supernatant removed IMMEDIATELY after final wash cycle. No queue-wait in
                    wash buffer. Pilot assays demonstrated up to 45% chemiluminescent signal
                    decay when particles queued in wash buffer (2+ min extra for second-in-queue
                    pair). Optimized protocol eliminates this delay entirely.
  Variable threading : cwash4a (final resuspension droplet carrying particles) fed directly
                    into H2O2 resuspension step without intermediate drain.

Step 7 | Chemiluminescent Substrate Reaction
  Reagents        : H2O2_StablePeroxide, LuminolEnhancer (SuperSignal ELISA Femto)
  Operation       : dispense H2O2 (800 nL) -> mix with particles (10 s, resuspend in H2O2) ->
                    dispense LuminolEnhancer (800 nL) -> mix pooled substrate (4 min)
  Pooled volume   : ~1600 nL
  Mix duration    : 4 min (optimized; pilot used 40 s mix + 100 s static incubation)
  Stable window   : ~1 min after 4 min mixing (HRP-catalysed luminol oxidation reaches plateau)
  Purpose         : Mixing duration creates a stable chemiluminescent measurement window,
                    allowing all parallel droplets (up to 8) to be read sequentially by the
                    single PMT within ~1 min without signal drift between measurements.

Step 8 | PMT Chemiluminescence Detection
  Operation       : detect chemiluminescenceDetection on substratePool for 10 s
  PMT state       : Engaged (motor-lowered, shutter open, several hundred um above device)
  Integration     : 10 s within the stable measurement window
  Replicates      : 4 per concentration; results averaged
  Calibration     : Linear fit to averaged signal; LOD = mean(blank) + 3 x SD(blank)
  LOD achieved    : 0.15 uIU/mL (5-fold lower than prototype 0.83 uIU/mL)
  QC gate         : detectionSignal > 0  -> dispose(substratePool) (BB5)
                    detectionSignal <= 0 -> drain(substratePool) (BB6)
  Cleanup         : dispose(detectionSignal); PMT returns to disengaged position (BB7, terminal)


PERFORMANCE COMPARISON
----------------------

Metric                        Prototype (Ng 2012)    Integrated Platform    Improvement
----------------------------  ---------------------  ---------------------  -----------
Coefficient of variation (%)  9-21                   6-10                   Lower / better
LOD absolute (nIU)            2.0                    0.6                    3-fold lower
LOD concentration (uIU/mL)    0.83                   0.15                   5-fold lower
Sample volume (uL)            2.4                    4.0                    Larger (optimized)
Sample incubation time (min)  6                      3                      2-fold reduction
Parallel magnetic separations 2 (disc magnet)        8 (magnetic lens)      4-fold increase
PMT CV (%)                    0.63-21 (well-plate)   0.56-9.3 (integrated)  Lower / better
PMT LOD (uU/mL)               7.97 (well-plate)      4.88 (integrated)      Better

Clinical note: LOD of 0.15 uIU/mL provides capability to screen for hyperthyroidism
([TSH] < 0.3 uIU/mL), which the prototype setup (LOD 0.83 uIU/mL) could not achieve.


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : choi_dmf_tsh_immunoassay.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else QC gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG file       : choi_dmf_tsh_immunoassay_main_dag.dot
Modules        : chemiluminescenceDetection

Duration conversions (all verified against IR output):
  3 min  (sample incubation)   -> 180.0 SECOND
  2 min  (conjugate incubation)-> 120.0 SECOND
  4 min  (substrate mixing)    -> 240.0 SECOND
  30 s   (wash resuspend)      -> 30.0 SECOND
  10 s   (wash transfer)       -> 10.0 SECOND
  10 s   (PMT integration)     -> 10.0 SECOND
  5 s    (TSH pool merging)    -> 5.0 SECOND
  5 s    (wash QC detection)   -> 5.0 SECOND

Compiler behaviours documented:
  - drain and dispose both map to dispose opcode in IR; semantically correct,
    no structural issue; drain/dispose distinction is at the biology level only.
  - False branch (BB3, BB6) carries explicit jump to join block.
  - True branch (BB2, BB5) falls through to join block implicitly.
  - Multi-unit dispense not supported as indexed array: 5 TSH unit droplets
    dispensed as 5 independent scalar variables (tsh1-tsh5) and accumulated
    via chained mix operations (tshPool_2 -> tshPool_3 -> tshPool_4 -> tshSample).
  - Wash variable threading: wash_Na variables carry the particle-containing
    resuspension droplet at each wash cycle; washSup variables carry the
    supernatant and are drained. cwash4a feeds directly into particlesInH2O2,
    verified in IR output.

IR / DAG verified clean:
  - All 7 BB labels present; all 8 CFG edges confirmed in DAG.
  - No dangling edges, no missing joins, no unreachable blocks.
  - All time conversions confirmed against IR SECOND values.
  - cwash4a1[0] correctly resolves as input to particlesInH2O21[0] in IR.

protocol.title: Automated Digital Microfluidic Platform for Magnetic-Particle-Based Immunoassays with Optimization by Design of Experiments
protocol.platform: Automated DMF (digital microfluidics) with integrated PMT and magnetic lens
protocol.objective: Automated magnetic-particle-based sandwich immunoassay for TSH with DOE-optimized protocol; first report of DOE optimization for immunoassays in any microfluidic system

device.form_factor: Benchtop enclosure, approx. 18 x 23 x 30 cm, light-tight

electronic_interface.loading: motor-driven lowering onto device contact pads

positions.engaged: several hundred micrometers above device surface

integrated_pmt.shutter: closed in disengaged state; opens on engagement
integrated_pmt.actuation: motor-driven with two optical limit switches
integrated_pmt.software: EM6 counter timer software via CT2 counter timer module (ET Enterprises)

magnetic_lens.name: magnetic lens

armatures.function: field directors focusing flux to pole tips

magnetic_lens.actuation: motor-driven vertical with two optical limit switches
magnetic_lens.modeling_software: COMSOL (Burlington, MA); 3D model, magnetic fields and no currents

particle_model.pellet_geometry: sphere with volume = single particle volume x particle count

advantages_over_disc_magnet: Localized field (<35 uN force at >4 mm from center); minimizes unintended particle attraction
Stronger vertical force in separation zone (exponential increase as gap decreases)
Vertical motor engagement eliminates horizontal disc movement that causes stray attraction
Supports up to 8 simultaneous parallel magnetic separations vs. 2 for disc magnet

paramagnetic_particles.diluent: DMF-compatible particle diluent (pH 10): Tris base 6.1 g/L, NaCl 5.8 g/L, BSA 1% w/v, thimerosal 0.05% w/v, Pluronic L64 0.05% v/v

tsh_standards.additive: Pluronic L64 0.05% v/v (added prior to use)

chemiluminescent_substrate.additive: Pluronic L64 0.025% v/v (added prior to use)

pluronic_l64.supplier: BASF Corp., Germany (donated by Brenntag Canada, Toronto, ON)
pluronic_l64.use: DMF compatibility additive in standards and substrate

steps.name: Paramagnetic particle dispense and immobilization
steps.magnetic_lens: engaged (~150 um gap); particles pellet on device surface above magnet
steps.notes: Particle diluent supernatant moved away by electrode actuation; pellet immobilized for sample delivery. Magnetic lens facilitates up to 8 simultaneous separations across device.

steps.name: TSH sample dispense and pooling (5 unit droplets)
steps.doe_optimization: 5 droplets selected as optimal by 3^3 full factorial DOE (highest Sqrt(SBR) across all concentrations)
steps.notes: Five unit droplets dispensed individually and chained via sequential mix operations to accumulate 4 uL pooled sample.

steps.name: Sample incubation with immobilized particles
steps.mixing_mode: circular shuttle across 4+ electrodes (continuous active mixing, 100-120 Vrms, 10 kHz)
steps.doe_optimization: 3 min selected as optimal (not 6 min from prototype); negative vol x inc interaction means longer incubation at high volume reduces Sqrt(SBR)
steps.notes: Rapid continuous mixing enables faster analyte binding kinetics than prototype setup (hand-held probes). Key DOE result: con x inc negative coefficient at high TSH; 3 min outperforms 6-9 min across all concentrations when volume is maximized.

steps.name: Post-sample wash series (4 cycles)
steps.magnetic_lens_state: engaged for pellet immobilization; disengaged for resuspension
steps.purpose: Remove unbound TSH and non-specific binders from particle surface

steps.name: HRP-conjugate delivery and incubation
steps.purpose: HRP-antibody binds to TSH captured on particle surface (sandwich formation)

steps.name: Post-conjugate wash series (4 cycles)
steps.critical_note: Supernatant removed IMMEDIATELY after final wash (no queue wait). Pilot assays showed up to 45% signal decay when particles queued in wash buffer before measurement. Optimized protocol eliminates this delay entirely.
steps.purpose: Remove unbound HRP-conjugate

steps.name: Chemiluminescent substrate reaction
steps.mixing_mode: active electrode mixing (replaces pilot: 40 s mix + 100 s static incubation)
steps.purpose: HRP catalyses luminol oxidation by H2O2; signal reaches stable plateau after 4 min continuous mixing, enabling sequential PMT reads within ~1 min window without signal drift

steps.name: PMT chemiluminescence detection
steps.pmt_state: engaged (motor-lowered, shutter open, several hundred um above device)
steps.calibration: linear fit; LOD = mean(blank) + 3 x SD(blank)

doe_analysis.midlevels_rationale: vol=3 droplets and inc=6 min match prototype setup optimal parameters (Ng et al. 2012)
doe_analysis.response_transform: square-root (Box-Cox confirmed power ~0.5 minimizes sum of squares error)
doe_analysis.model: Modified second-order centered polynomial regression (eq 1 in paper)

fit_statistics.residual_normality: confirmed by Shapiro-Wilk test and normal probability plot

significant_factors.effect: negative quadratic; plateaus at high vol
negative quadratic; plateaus at high con
longer incubation at high vol reduces Sqrt(SBR)
longer incubation at high con reduces Sqrt(SBR)

optimal_parameters.rationale: Maximum Sqrt(SBR) at 4 uIU/mL and at 0.4 uIU/mL (critical for sensitivity); response surface peak at 5 droplets x 3 min (Fig 4D)

performance.clinical_significance: LOD of 0.15 uIU/mL enables screening for hyperthyroidism ([TSH] < 0.3 uIU/mL)

pmt_vs_well_plate_reader.dynamic_range: at least 2 orders of magnitude (both methods)
pmt_vs_well_plate_reader.advantage: Reproducible fixed positioning of PMT relative to device eliminates manual insertion variability
