BioScript has no loop construct; one representative sort cycle per protocol is encoded, consistent with both reference files

key_tubing_failure_modes: Tubing arc creates static zone where droplets accumulate
HFE oil heavier than aqueous droplets; droplets float to top of arc
PDMS-tubing wall thickness > droplet diameter (<100 um); droplets trapped at junction
Droplet coalescence and cross-talk when droplets contact each other in tubing
key_D2_advantages: No tubing required at collection site
Droplets isolated/parked individually; no fusion or diffusive exchange
Direct pipetting access via open semicircular outlet
5-fold reduction in SD at 50 bead events

Cyto_Mine.limitation: Closed proprietary system; limited flexibility; passive flow valve mechanism susceptible to stochastic loss

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Automated Microfluidic System for Dynamic Stimulation and Tracking of Single Cells
Source Link  : https://taylab.uchicago.edu/uploads/9/1/8/0/91804060/2018_anal_chem.pdf
Paper DOI    : http://dx.doi.org/10.1021/acs.analchem.8b00312
Journal      : Analytical Chemistry, 2018, XXXX, XXX-XXX (ACS Publications)
Platform     : Large-scale integrated microfluidics (LSIM); two-layer PDMS valve-based chip


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a programmable, valve-controlled microfluidic system designed for
long-term culture, dynamic cytokine stimulation, and continuous single-cell time-lapse imaging
of nonadherent hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) and adherent murine embryonic
stem cells (muESCs) without displacing or losing track of individual cells.

The system overcomes a key limitation of existing LSIM devices: most rely on direct media
flow over cells, which physically displaces nonadherent cells during each media exchange.
Here, media exchange occurs exclusively by diffusion through 50-um-wide ports connecting
flanking media reservoirs to the cell culture area. Valves alternate reservoir filling
between left and right sides to prevent cross-chamber pressure-driven flow (flow-switching
strategy). No flow crosses the cell culture area at any point during culture or stimulation.

The protocol is divided into two independent experimental arms encoded in sequence:

  Protocol 1: Long-term GMP differentiation assay
    - Murine LysM-GFP granulocyte-macrophage progenitors (GMPs) seeded into 48 chambers
    - 48 h baseline culture in permissive SCF/IL3/IL6 Stem-Span SFEM
    - Switch to 20 ng/mL M-CSF for 48 h; LysM-GFP expression tracked every 30 min
    - In-culture continuous anti-F4/80-APC antibody staining for macrophage commitment
    - Result: 77% of M-CSF colonies vs. 54% of control colonies upregulated LysM-GFP
      within 96 h (p=0.001636, two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test)

  Protocol 2: Dynamic FGF1 stimulation of muESC ERKKTR reporter line
    - Line R1 muESCs expressing ERK kinase translocation reporter (ERKKTR)
    - 2-day self-renewing culture (DMEM + 10% FCS + 1000 U/mL Lif)
    - 16 h starvation (0.5% FCS DMEM without Lif) to synchronise ERK baseline
    - Oscillating FGF1 stimulation: 5 s FGF1 pulse / 32 min incubation / 2 s wash /
      15 min incubation; three complete cycles encoded
    - ERK activity imaged every 3 min (ERKKTR nuclear-to-cytoplasmic C/N ratio)
    - 93% of cells adjacent to reservoir respond within 3 min; all within 10 min


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Layer i  : Flow layer -- PDMS, channel height 25 um; fabricated by photolithography on
           SU-8 3025 master (4-in. silicon wafer); 40 kdpi photomask (Fine Line Imaging).
Layer ii : Control layer -- PDMS, channel height 25 um; AZ-50XT deposited at valve
           positions to produce parabolic valve surfaces for tight closure.
Layer iii: Coverslip bonded to underside of flow layer after O2 plasma treatment.

Fabrication:
  - PDMS ratio: 10:1 polymer:catalyst (RTV 615, Momentive Performance Materials)
  - Cast at 80 C for 45 min on wafer
  - O2 plasma treatment, layer alignment, bonding
  - 2 h thermal bonding at 80 C; additional 12 h cure after full assembly at 80 C

Chip architecture:
  - 48 independently addressable cell culture chambers (1000 um x 350 um x 25 um)
  - 16 independent inputs (left side); 2 outlets / harvesting ports (right side)
  - Four-valve on-chip peristaltic pump for fluid manipulation and cell deposition
  - 2 media reservoirs per chamber; connected via 50-um-wide diffusion ports
  - Valve control: solenoid manifold (1.7-2.5 bar closing; 0.5 bar flow layer)
  - MATLAB GUI for experimental scripting and valve actuation control

Chip validation (bead displacement test):
  - 10 um polystyrene beads (Spherotech) pre-treated with 0.1% Triton-X
  - Bead translocation in culture chamber: <2 um after 15 s reservoir flushing
  - Confirms absence of direct flow in culture area during media exchange
  - 40 kDa rhodamine-dextran (300 uM) used for diffusion rate calibration
    (comparable in size to cytokines; reaches steady state within 10 min)


CELL LINES
----------
- Murine LysM-GFP GMPs (granulocyte-macrophage progenitors):
    Source: C57BL/6J male mice, 12-14 weeks old, Lysozyme M gene locus (LysM-GFP)
    Immunophenotype: lin-/Sca1-/c-Kit+/CD34+/CD16/32+
    Isolation: Bone marrow dissected, pulverized (4 C mortar), 40 um nylon mesh strainer
    Lineage depletion: Biotinylated antibodies (CD3e, CD11b, CD19, CD41, B220, Gr-1,
      TER-119) + Streptavidin Roti-MagBeads (Carl Roth AG) on EasySep magnet
    FACS sorting: Anti-Sca-1, c-Kit, CD34 staining; sorted on FACS Aria (BD Biosciences)
    Media: Stem-Span SFEM + 1% pen/strep + 10% FCS + 100 ng/mL SCF + 10 ng/mL IL3
           + 10 ng/mL IL6 (permissive arm); 20 ng/mL M-CSF (differentiation arm)

- Murine ESCs line R1 (ERKKTR reporter):
    Reporter: ERK kinase translocation reporter (ERKKTR)
    Seeding: ~10 cells per chamber
    Media: DMEM (Gibco) + 10% FCS11 (PAA) + 1000 U/mL Lif (CellGS)
    Starvation: 0.5% FCS DMEM without Lif, 16 h prior to stimulation
    Culture type: Adherent (E-Cadherin surface coating, 150 ng/mL)


ENVIRONMENTAL CONTROL
---------------------
Microscope   : Nikon Ti-eclipse inverted (Orca Flash IV camera, 10x/NA0.45 objective)
Temperature  : 37 C (feedback-controlled heating unit, Life Imaging Services)
Enclosure    : Custom aluminum-slot frame; black foamed-insulation lining
Stage-top    : Humidity >98%; 5% CO2 / 5% O2 / 90% N2 at 30 L/h
Humidity src : ~100 mL water absorbed by sodium polyacrylate (Sigma-Aldrich)
Data logger  : Sensirion AG (relative humidity monitoring)
Software     : YouScope (youscope.org) + Fiji + MATLAB (image acquisition and analysis)
Cell tracking: tTt (Hilsenbeck et al., Nat. Biotechnol. 2016, 34(7):703-706)


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Chip Priming
  Reagents  : PBS
  Operation : Dispense PBS; force through all channels under pressure while outlet
              valves remain closed to expel air.
  Purpose   : Fully wets all surfaces before functionalization. Required step before
              any biological use of the chip.

Step 2 | Surface Functionalization
  Reagents  : PBS + Fibronectin (GMPs) or E-Cadherin (muESCs), 150 ng/mL (Merck KGaA)
  Operation : Flow fibronectin through all channels for 3 h at 25 C (or overnight).
              Wash extensively with PBS, then equilibrate with cell culture media.
  Duration  : 180 m (= 3 h) at 25 C; IR: 10800.0 SECOND
  Purpose   : Promotes hematopoietic progenitor retention and muESC adhesion;
              prevents non-specific cell-to-PDMS binding.

Step 3 | Chip Validation -- Bead Displacement Test
  Reagents  : PolystyrenBeads_10um (0.1% Triton-X pre-treated)
              RhodamineDextran_40kDa (300 uM in PBS)
  Operation : Load beads into chambers; flush media reservoirs for 15 s;
              confirm <2 um bead translocation in culture area.
              Separately, introduce single rhodamine-dextran pulse into PBS-filled
              reservoirs and monitor fluorescence for 30 min (diffusion calibration).
  Detection : cellTrackingDetection module, 15 s read
  Purpose   : Quantitatively validates no-flow condition in culture chambers.
              Diffusion calibration confirms cytokine-scale molecule exchange kinetics.

Step 4 | GMP Seeding  [Protocol 1]
  Reagents  : LysM_GFP_GMPs, StemSpanSFEM
  Operation : Connect pressurized microcentrifuge tube to first inlet via 25 cm PEEK
              tubing (65 um ID). Use peristaltic pump to deposit 4-90 cells per chamber
              in a targeted, chamber-by-chamber manner.
  Duration  : 2 s seeding pulse per chamber
  Notes     : Targeted seeding enables precise cell number control. Each of the 48
              chambers can be independently addressed.

Step 5 | Baseline Culture in Permissive SCF/IL3/IL6 Media  [Protocol 1]
  Reagents  : SCF_IL3_IL6_Media (SFEM + 1% pen/strep + 10% FCS + 100 ng/mL SCF
              + 10 ng/mL IL3 + 10 ng/mL IL6)
  Operation : Flow-switching: left reservoir filled (5 s pulse), then right reservoir
              filled (5 s pulse) in alternating sequence every 30 min.
              No flow enters culture area; diffusion equilibrates chambers in ~10 min.
  Duration  : 2880 m (= 48 h) at 37 C; IR: 172800.0 SECOND
  Notes     : Proliferation and cell cycle length comparable to standard Ibidi VI
              channel slides (Figs. S1A, S1B in paper Supporting Information).

Step 6 | M-CSF Differentiation Culture  [Protocol 1]
  Reagents  : MCSF_Media (SFEM + 1% pen/strep + 10% FCS + 20 ng/mL M-CSF)
  Operation : Switch media reservoirs to M-CSF-containing media. Same 30-min
              flow-switching cadence. LysM-GFP fluorescence imaged every 30 min
              (Nikon Ti-eclipse, 10x/NA0.45, ORCA Flash IV).
              Single-cell tracking performed with tTt software.
  Duration  : 2880 m (= 48 h) at 37 C; IR: 172800.0 SECOND
  Detection : lysM_GFP_Detection module, 30 s read
  Results   : 77% of M-CSF-treated colonies upregulate LysM-GFP within 96 h vs.
              54% without M-CSF (p=0.001636, two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test).
  CFG gate  : differentiationSignal > 0 -> BB2 (dispose); <= 0 -> BB3 (drain)
              Both converge at BB4 (differentiationJoin)

Step 7 | In-Culture Continuous Antibody Staining of Live Cells  [Protocol 1]
  Reagents  : LysM_GFP_GMPs, StemSpanSFEM, SCF_IL3_IL6_Media, AntiF480_APC_Antibody,
              MCSF_Media
  Operation : Fresh GMPs seeded. Baseline culture (2880 m, permissive media).
              Anti-F4/80-APC (clone BM8, eBioscience; 0.2 mg/mL at 1:10,000 dilution)
              added continuously to all M-CSF media during diffusion exchange cycles.
              Automated fluid replacement incorporates antibody in every 30-min cycle.
  Duration  : 2880 m baseline + 2880 m M-CSF+antibody at 37 C; IR: 172800.0 SECOND each
  Detection : f480_MacrophageDetection module, 30 s read
  Notes     : F4/80 is a molecular reporter for macrophage lineage commitment.
              Fluorescence detectable on differentiated cells confirms commitment.
  CFG gate  : f480Signal > 0 -> BB5 (dispose); <= 0 -> BB6 (drain)
              Both converge at BB7 (antibodyJoin)

Step 8 | muESC Seeding and Self-Renewing Culture  [Protocol 2]
  Reagents  : MuESC_ERKKTR, DMEM_SelfRenewing (DMEM + 10% FCS + 1000 U/mL Lif)
  Operation : ~10 R1 muESCs seeded per chamber (E-Cadherin surface coating, 150 ng/mL).
              Diffusion media exchange every 30 min (same flow-switching strategy).
  Duration  : 2880 m (= 2 days) at 37 C; IR: 172800.0 SECOND
  Notes     : Cells cultured to stable self-renewing state before starvation.

Step 9 | Overnight Starvation  [Protocol 2]
  Reagents  : DMEM_Starvation (0.5% FCS DMEM without Lif)
  Operation : Switch to starvation media; same 30-min flow-switching cadence.
  Duration  : 960 m (= 16 h) at 37 C; IR: 57600.0 SECOND
  Purpose   : Synchronises ERK baseline activity across all cells before stimulation.

Step 10 | Dynamic FGF1 Stimulation -- 3 Oscillation Cycles  [Protocol 2]
  Reagents  : FGF1_StarvationMedia (10 ng/mL recombinant mouse FGF1, R&D Systems,
              in 0.5% FCS DMEM without Lif)
              DMEM_Starvation (plain starvation wash media)
  Operation per cycle:
    - 5 s flow pulse: FGF1-containing starvation media into left reservoir
    - 32 min incubation: FGF1 diffuses into culture area at 37 C
    - 2 s flow pulse: plain starvation media washes right reservoir
    - 15 min incubation: FGF1 dilutes from chamber by diffusion at 37 C
  Cycles    : 3 complete ON/OFF cycles encoded (fgf1FeedL_C1/C2/C3 + washFeedR_C1/C2/C3)
  Duration  : 32 m FGF1 incubation (IR: 1920.0 SECOND) + 15 m wash (IR: 900.0 SECOND)
              per cycle; 37 C throughout
  Imaging   : ERK activity imaged every 3 min (ERKKTR C/N ratio)
  Response  : 93% of cells adjacent to reservoir respond within 3 min;
              all cells respond within 10 min of stimulation onset
  Detection : erkktr_ERKDetection module, 3 m read (IR: 180.0 SECOND)
  CFG gate  : erkSignal > 0 -> BB8 (dispose); <= 0 -> BB9 (drain)
              Both converge at BB10 (finalCleanup)

Step 11 | Final Cleanup  [BB10 -- terminal]
  Operation : dispose(erkSignal); dispose(validationSignal); dispose(diffusionCalib); NOP
  Notes     : All outstanding QC signal droplets disposed. Experiment ends.


FLOW-SWITCHING STRATEGY
------------------------
The key innovation enabling nonadherent cell culture is the alternating reservoir fill:

  1. Left reservoir filled:  left-side inlet valves open; right-side valves closed.
     Fresh media or stimulant flows into left reservoir channel only.
  2. Right reservoir filled: right-side inlet valves open; left-side valves closed.
     Mirrors left fill. Completes one exchange cycle.
  3. Seeding valves:         always closed during culture phases.

This sequential approach eliminates pressure differentials that would drive flow across
the culture chamber. Reagents exchange into the culture area by diffusion only (Fick's
Law through 50 um port). Steady state reached within 10 min per reservoir fill cycle.
Oscillation periods of 20 min and 40 min were validated with rhodamine-dextran (Fig. 2B).
Chemical gradients across the chamber last a maximum of 20 min per exchange.


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : dettinger_2018_lsim_single_cell.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based, github.com/lilott8/BioScript)
IR output      : 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
DAG output     : dettinger_2018_lsim_single_cell_main_dag.dot
Duration units : s (seconds) and m (minutes) only; h token not supported by compiler

Timing conversions (verified against IR):
  180m  fibronectin coat        -> 10800.0s   (3 h)
  2880m culture phases (x4)     -> 172800.0s  (48 h each)
  960m  starvation              -> 57600.0s   (16 h)
  32m   FGF1 incubation (x3)   -> 1920.0s    per cycle
  15m   wash incubation (x3)   -> 900.0s     per cycle
  3m    ERK detect              -> 180.0s

Single-assignment constraint:
  BioScript's SimpleSymbolVisitor forbids reusing a variable that has already been
  consumed as a mix operand. Every flow-switch cycle and every media repeat requires
  a freshly dispensed named variable. Variables introduced to satisfy this constraint:
    permissiveMedia2    -- right-reservoir fill, baseline GMP culture
    mcsfMedia2          -- right-reservoir fill, M-CSF culture
    mcsfForAb           -- MCSF_Media dispense for antibody mixing step
    sfemMedia2          -- SFEM for antibody-branch GMP seeding
    permissiveBase2     -- right-reservoir fill, antibody-branch baseline
    mcsfAb2             -- right-reservoir fill, antibody-in-M-CSF culture
    selfRenewMedia2/3   -- left/right reservoir fills, muESC self-renewing culture
    starvationMedia2    -- right-reservoir fill, starvation phase

mix abstraction:
  `mix` in this .bs file represents valve-controlled reservoir fill events followed
  by passive diffusion equilibration -- NOT physical droplet-level mixing. No direct
  fluid flow enters cell culture chambers. The 5 s / 2 s mix durations encode the
  reservoir flushing pulse times; subsequent `heat` statements encode incubation.

Modules  : cellTrackingDetection, lysM_GFP_Detection,
           f480_MacrophageDetection, erkktr_ERKDetection
Manifests: PBS, Fibronectin, PluronicF127, StemSpanSFEM,
           SCF_IL3_IL6_Media, MCSF_Media, RhodamineDextran_40kDa,
           PolystyrenBeads_10um, LysM_GFP_GMPs, AntiF480_APC_Antibody,
           DMEM_SelfRenewing, DMEM_Starvation, FGF1_StarvationMedia, MuESC_ERKKTR

protocol.title: Automated Microfluidic System for Dynamic Stimulation and Tracking of Single Cells
protocol.platform: Large-scale integrated microfluidics (LSIM); two-layer PDMS valve-based chip
cell_lines: Murine LysM-GFP granulocyte-macrophage progenitors (GMPs) from C57BL/6J bone marrow
Murine embryonic stem cells line R1 (ERKKTR reporter)
protocol.objective: Long-term culture, dynamic cytokine stimulation, and single-cell time-lapse tracking of nonadherent hematopoietic progenitor cells and adherent murine ESCs using diffusion-based media exchange without displacement of individual cells

layers: Flow layer: PDMS, channel height 25 um; fabricated on SU-8 3025 master on 4-in. silicon wafer
Control layer: PDMS, channel height 25 um; AZ-50XT deposited at valve positions for parabolic surfaces
Coverslip bonded to underside of flow layer

media_reservoirs.exchange_mechanism: Fickian diffusion only; no direct flow into culture area

peristaltic_pump.function: Accurate fluid manipulation and cell seeding

device.gui: Custom MATLAB GUI for experimental scripting and valve control

environmental_control.humidity_source: 100 mL water absorbed by sodium polyacrylate (Sigma-Aldrich)

surface_functionalization.hematopoietic_progenitors: Fibronectin, 150 ng/mL (Merck KGaA), 3 h or overnight
surface_functionalization.embryonic_stem_cells: E-Cadherin, 150 ng/mL (Merck KGaA), 3 h or overnight

chip_validation.diffusion_calibrant: Rhodamine-conjugated Dextran, 40 kDa, 300 uM (comparable size to cytokines)

cell_media.GMPs_permissive: Stem-Span SFEM (StemCell Technologies) + 1% pen/strep + 10% FCS + 100 ng/mL SCF + 10 ng/mL IL3 + 10 ng/mL IL6 (all cytokines from Peprotech)
cell_media.GMPs_MCSF: Stem-Span SFEM + 1% pen/strep + 10% FCS + 20 ng/mL M-CSF (Peprotech)
cell_media.GMPs_antibody_staining: Anti-F4/80-APC antibody (clone BM8, eBioscience), 0.2 mg/mL at 1:10,000 dilution added to all M-CSF media
cell_media.muESC_self_renewing: DMEM (Gibco) + 10% FCS11 (PAA) + 1000 U/mL leukemia inhibitory factor (Lif, CellGS)
cell_media.muESC_FGF1_stimulation: 10 ng/mL recombinant mouse FGF1 (R&D Systems) in starvation medium

cell_seeding_hardware.tubing: PEEK tubing, 25 cm length, inner diameter 65 um
cell_seeding_hardware.vessel: Pressurized microcentrifuge tube connected to first inlet

GMPs.lineage_depletion_beads: Streptavidin Roti-MagBeads (Carl Roth AG), EasySep magnet (Stem Cell Technologies)
GMPs.bone_marrow_preparation: 4 C mortar; 40 um nylon mesh strainer (Becton Dickinson AG)

steps.name: Chip priming
steps.notes: PBS forced through all channels under pressure via liquid supply lines while outlet valves remain closed. Expels air; wets all surfaces prior to functionalization.

steps.name: Surface functionalization
steps.followed_by: Extensive PBS wash then cell culture media equilibration
steps.notes: Fibronectin for GMP experiments; E-Cadherin for muESC experiments. BioScript does not distinguish surface reagent identity at compiler level.

steps.name: Chip validation - bead displacement test
steps.notes: Beads pre-treated with 0.1% Triton-X to prevent aggregation. Displacement <2 um confirms absence of direct flow in culture chambers during media exchange.

steps.name: GMP seeding
steps.notes: Cells loaded via pressurized microcentrifuge tube through 65 um ID PEEK tubing. Peristaltic pump enables precise chamber-by-chamber deposition.

steps.name: Baseline culture in permissive SCF/IL3/IL6 media
steps.flow_switching: alternating left/right reservoir fill to prevent direct flow
steps.notes: Proliferation and cell cycle length comparable to Ibidi VI channel slides (paper Figs. S1A, S1B). Steady state per reservoir reached within 10 min of each 30-min switching cycle.

steps.name: In-culture continuous antibody staining of live cells
steps.notes: Antibody continuously present in diffusion media throughout M-CSF culture phase. Fluorescence signal detectable on differentiated cells confirms macrophage lineage commitment.

steps.name: Overnight starvation
steps.notes: Synchronises ERK baseline activity across all cells before FGF1 stimulation.

steps.name: Dynamic FGF1 stimulation (3 oscillation cycles)
steps.notes: 5 s FGF1 pulse into left reservoir; 32 min diffusion incubation; 2 s starvation wash into right reservoir; 15 min dilution incubation. Gradients last max 20 min per exchange. Each oscillation cycle uses freshly dispensed reagent variables (BioScript single-assignment constraint).

flow_switching_strategy.description: Alternating left/right reservoir fill prevents cross-chamber pressure-driven flow
flow_switching_strategy.left_reservoir_fill: Left-side valves open; right-side valves closed; fresh media flows into left reservoir
flow_switching_strategy.right_reservoir_fill: Right-side valves open; left-side valves closed; mirrors left fill to complete exchange cycle
flow_switching_strategy.seeding_valves: Remain closed during all culture phases
flow_switching_strategy.mass_transfer_law: Fick's Law through 50 um diffusion port

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.contents: Chip priming, surface functionalization, bead validation, GMP seeding, baseline + M-CSF culture, muESC seeding, starvation, FGF1 oscillation

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_4_j
basic_blocks.contents: dispose(differentiationSignal); antibody staining branch begins

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_7_j
basic_blocks.contents: dispose(f480Signal); muESC ERKKTR protocol begins

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_10_j
basic_blocks.contents: dispose(erkSignal, validationSignal, diffusionCalib); NOP

bioscript_compiler_notes.ir_output: 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
bioscript_compiler_notes.duration_units: All durations in s (seconds) or m (minutes); h token not supported
bioscript_compiler_notes.single_assignment_constraint: BioScript forbids reuse of a consumed variable as a mix operand. Each flow-switch cycle and each media repeat requires a freshly dispensed named variable (e.g. permissiveMedia2, mcsfMedia2, selfRenewMedia2/3, starvationMedia2, mcsfAb2, permissiveBase2).
bioscript_compiler_notes.mix_abstraction: mix represents valve-controlled reservoir fill events and diffusive equilibration, not physical droplet-level mixing. No direct flow enters culture chambers.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Measuring Droplet Volume in Home-Made Microfluidic Devices
Source Link  : https://www.protocols.io/view/measuring-droplet-volume-in-home-made-microfluidic-3byl46drgo5d/v1
DOI Link     : https://dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.mj5c4q6
Platform     : Home-made droplet microfluidic device (droplet-in-channel; EWOD/DMF-adjacent)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a bead-based volumetric calibration procedure for determining droplet
volume in home-made microfluidic devices. Monodisperse polystyrene beads suspended at a known
concentration are co-flowed with PBS through the device to generate droplets. The number of
beads per droplet (droplet occupancy) is measured by microscopy over several hundred droplets,
and the droplet volume is calculated from the occupancy and the known bead concentration in
the combined aqueous phase.

This is a device characterisation/calibration protocol, not a cell biology assay. It is
applicable to any home-made droplet microfluidic chip prior to biological experiments, providing
a ground-truth volume estimate without requiring dedicated optical volume sensors.


PRINCIPLE
---------
Beads (10 um carboxylated polystyrene) are resuspended in Drop-seq lysis buffer at
1000 beads/uL and loaded into the bead syringe. PBS is loaded into the cell-channel syringe.
When both syringes co-flow into the microfluidic device at equal rates, the combined aqueous
phase has an effective bead concentration of:

    1000 beads/uL (bead syringe) / 2 (co-flow dilution) = 500 beads/uL in droplet fluid

After generating droplets, beads inside droplets are counted under microscopy to compute:

    Droplet occupancy  = total beads counted / total droplets counted
    Droplet volume     = droplet occupancy / 500 beads/uL   [units: uL per droplet]

A minimum of several hundred droplets should be counted to obtain a statistically sound estimate.


REAGENTS
--------
PolyBeads_LysisBuffer:
  - Monodisperse carboxylated polystyrene beads, ~10 um diameter
  - Standard (non-fluorescent): Bangs Labs catalog PC06N-11355
  - Fluorescent (recommended): Bangs Labs catalog FC06F-10163
  - Suspension buffer: Drop-seq lysis buffer
  - Concentration: 1000 beads/uL
  - Loaded in syringe with magnetic mixer (as per standard barcoded-bead protocol)

PBS:
  - Phosphate-buffered saline (standard, no additives required)
  - Loaded into the syringe intended for cells (no cells present in calibration run)
  - Co-flow with bead syringe; halves bead concentration to 500 beads/uL in droplet fluid


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Prepare Bead Suspension
  Reagent      : PolyBeads_LysisBuffer
  Operation    : dispense (BioScript abstraction for syringe loading)
  Details      : Wash and resuspend 10 um carboxylated polystyrene beads in Drop-seq lysis
                 buffer at 1000 beads/uL. Draw into syringe equipped with a magnetic mixer
                 to prevent bead settling during the run.

Step 2 | Load PBS into Cell-Channel Syringe
  Reagent      : PBS
  Operation    : dispense (BioScript abstraction for syringe loading)
  Details      : Load the syringe intended for cells with regular PBS. No cells are present
                 in this calibration run. The co-flow of bead suspension and PBS at equal
                 volumetric rates gives an effective bead concentration of 500 beads/uL
                 in the combined droplet fluid.

Step 3 | Co-Flow and Droplet Generation
  Inputs       : beadSuspension, pbsFlow
  Operation    : mix (BioScript abstraction for co-flow junction merging)
  Duration     : 30 s (stabilisation period before droplet collection begins)
  Details      : Connect all tubing to the appropriate channels in the microfluidic device.
                 Start both syringe pumps. The bead syringe and PBS syringe co-flow into the
                 aqueous inlet; the carrier oil generates droplets at the T-junction or
                 flow-focus nozzle.
  Note         : mix here models the co-flow merging of two aqueous streams at the chip inlet
                 junction, not a DMF electrode-merging event.

Step 4 | Bead Counting Detection (Droplet Occupancy Measurement)
  Input        : combinedFluid
  Operation    : detect (beadCountDetection module)
  Duration     : 60 s (image acquisition and counting window)
  Details      : Image several hundred droplets under microscopy (fluorescence channel if
                 fluorescent beads; brightfield otherwise). Count total beads inside all
                 imaged droplets and the number of droplets counted. Compute:
                   Droplet occupancy = total_beads / total_droplets
                   Droplet volume    = occupancy / 500 beads/uL
  Minimum      : >= 200 droplets recommended for a statistically sound estimate

  QC Gate:
    Pass (beadSignal > 0): Beads detected in droplets; valid droplet population; volume
                           estimate obtained; dispose combinedFluid.
    Fail (beadSignal <= 0): No beads detected; device failure path (check tubing connections,
                            nozzle, oil flow rate, and bead resuspension quality); drain
                            combinedFluid.


CFG STRUCTURE
-------------
BB1  main         -- entry: dispense beads, dispense PBS, co-flow mix (30 s),
                     detect bead occupancy (60 s)
BB2  bsbbif_2_t   -- beadSignal > 0: valid droplet population; dispose(combinedFluid)
BB3  bsbbif_3_f   -- beadSignal <= 0: device failure; drain(combinedFluid)
BB4  bsbbif_4_j   -- terminal join: dispose(beadSignal); experiment ends

Edges: BB1->BB2, BB1->BB3, BB2->BB4, BB3->BB4
Total blocks: 4 | Total edges: 4 | if/else gates: 1


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : droplet_volume_measurement_beads.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 4 basic blocks (BB1-BB4), 1 if/else gate, 4 CFG edges
DAG file       : droplet_volume_measurement_beads_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations in seconds (s); no h tokens used; no conversion required
Modules        : beadCountDetection
Manifests      : PolyBeads_LysisBuffer, PBS

Known compiler behaviors (not source errors):
  - drain->dispose lowering: drain in .bs source is correctly lowered to dispose in IR
    (bsbbif_3_f); this is universal compiler behavior documented across all protocols
    in this dataset.
  - Missing true-branch jump: bsbbif_2_t lacks an unconditional jump to bsbbif_4_j in
    the IR text; this is a known compiler-side emission limitation. The DOT graph edge
    BB2->BB4 is correct and reflects the true CFG structure.

Ownership audit:
  - beadSuspension consumed once by mix; no reuse.
  - pbsFlow consumed once by mix; no reuse.
  - combinedFluid consumed once by detect; no reuse.
  - beadSignal disposed at terminal join; no reuse.
  - No fluid ownership violations.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Paper Microfluidics Goes Digital
Source Link  : https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/paper%20DMF.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1002/adma.201305168
Journal      : Advanced Materials, 2014, Vol. 26, pp. 2838-2843
Platform     : Paper DMF (digital microfluidics on inkjet-printed silver-on-paper substrates)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes the first demonstration of digital microfluidics (DMF) implemented on
paper-based substrates, combining the programmable drop manipulation of DMF with the low cost
and disposability of paper microfluidics. Devices are fabricated by inkjet printing silver
nanoparticle ink onto photo paper using a Dimatix DMP-2800 printer, followed by infrared
sintering (1500 W lamp, 10 s). The resulting paper DMF devices exhibit electrode resistances
500x lower than equivalent chromium-on-glass photolithography devices, and drop velocities
nearly identical to glass DMF devices at comparable actuation voltages.

Two complex, multistep assays are demonstrated:
  1. Homogeneous HRP chemiluminescence assay with on-chip serial dilution (Design A):
     63 discrete steps (27 dispense, 18 mix, 6 split, 12 measure) producing a four-point
     calibration curve in under 1 h; R^2 = 0.993. Represents a level of complexity
     difficult or impossible to achieve on capillary-driven paper devices.
  2. Proof-of-principle rubella IgG sandwich ELISA with magnetic bead separation (Design B):
     30 discrete steps per concentration; LOD = 0.15 IU/mL (well below the 10 IU/mL clinical
     threshold); R^2 = 0.988. First report of a rubella IgG assay on any microfluidic format.

Cost per device (Design A): less than $0.05 USD. Print time: approximately 1 minute.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Fabrication  : Inkjet printing of SunTronic U6503 silver nanoparticle ink onto optimized
               photo paper (custom substrate from Prof. M. Toivakka, Abo Akademi University,
               Finland; also tested on Epson Premium Photo Glossy and HP Premium Plus Photo
               Glossy). Dimatix Model Fluid 2 Waveform; printhead at 20-22 V; meniscus
               vacuum 4-5 inches H2O at room temperature.

Sintering    : 1500 W infrared lamp at ~1 cm distance for 10 s. Sintering >= 15 s causes
               paper browning (no effect on function). All devices sintered for 10 s.

Silver layer : <500 nm thick (vs 10-30 um for PCB-based DMF). Surface roughness Ra ~250 nm
               (bare silver on paper); Ra < 100 nm after Parylene-C + Teflon-AF deposition.
               Electrode gaps: 60-90 um. Minimum feature: 30 um.

Dielectric   : 6.2 um Parylene-C deposited by vapor deposition (Specialty Coating Systems).
Hydrophobic  : ~50 nm Teflon-AF 1600 (DuPont; 1% wt/wt in Fluorinert FC-40; 1000 rpm, 30 s;
               post-baked 160 C for 10 min).

Top plate    : ITO-coated glass (Delta Technologies Ltd.) coated with 50 nm Teflon-AF.
               Teflon thread seal tape wrapped around contact pads before coating.

Assembly     : Top and bottom plates joined with two layers of double-sided tape (~80 um each).
               Drop volume: ~440 nL (Design A); ~750 nL (Design B).
               Reservoirs filled by pipetting adjacent to gap and applying potential to reservoir.

Design A     : 5 reservoir electrodes (4.17 x 4.17 mm); 19 driving electrodes (1.65 x 1.65 mm).
               Used for HRP assay and all non-immunoassay experiments.
               Also fabricated in chromium-on-glass format for performance comparison.

Design B     : 8 reservoir electrodes (5.6 x 5.6 mm); 38 driving electrodes (2.16 x 2.16 mm).
               Used for rubella IgG immunoassay; larger electrode array accommodates magnetic
               bead separation and reagent exchange steps.

Actuation    : ~100-125 V_rms, 15 kHz AC via solid-state relays.
Controller   : Open-source DropBot; with integrated magnetic control + PMT for immunoassay
               (ref [25]); without for HRP assay (ref [23]). Impedance-based feedback for
               velocity measurement.


ASSAY 1: HOMOGENEOUS HRP CHEMILUMINESCENCE (Design A)
------------------------------------------------------

Reagents:
  HRP standard          : 100 uU/mL horseradish peroxidase in DPBS + 0.05% v/v Pluronic L64
  Wash/diluent buffer   : DPBS + 0.05% v/v Pluronic L64
  Chemiluminescent sub  : SuperSignal ELISA Femto (Thermo Fischer Scientific, Rockford, IL);
                          two-component: stable H2O2 + Luminol-Enhancer; premixed before loading.
                          Supplemented with 0.025% v/v Pluronic L64.
  Detection instrument  : H10682-110 PMT (Hamamatsu Photonics K.K., Hamamatsu, Japan)
  Pluronic L64          : 0.05% v/v added to all reagent solutions (BASF Corp., Germany);
                          reduces protein adsorption and cross-contamination (ref [30]).

Protocol Steps:

Step A1 | Prepare diluent droplets
  Reagents  : PBS, PluronicL64
  Operation : Dispense + mix
  Duration  : 5 s per droplet
  Notes     : Three separate diluent droplets prepared (one per dilution level). Pluronic L64
              at 0.05% v/v in all PBS diluent drops.

Step A2 | Dispense HRP standard stock droplets
  Reagents  : HRP_Standard (100 uU/mL in DPBS + 0.05% v/v Pluronic L64)
  Operation : Dispense x3 (one per dilution level)
  Volume    : ~440 nL per drop (1 unit, Design A)
  Notes     : Three stock drops dispensed from reservoir independently.

Step A3 | Generate on-chip serial dilution (1x, 2x, 4x)
  Operation : Dispense + merge
  Levels    :
    1x : 1 HRP unit + 1 diluent unit; effective ~50 uU/mL (1:2 dilution by volume)
    2x : 1 HRP unit + 1 diluent unit; effective ~50 uU/mL
    4x : 1 HRP unit + 3 diluent units; effective ~25 uU/mL (1:4 dilution by volume)
  BioScript note : No split-and-reuse construct available in lilott8/BioScript compiler.
                   All dilution levels encoded as explicit dispense+merge chains from fresh
                   manifest entries. 4x diluent (3 units) accumulated by chaining two
                   additional PBS+Pluronic merge steps. This avoids stranded-variable and
                   split-array compiler errors while faithfully representing device operations.
  Paper total    : 63 discrete steps (27 dispense, 18 mix, 6 split, 12 measure) per paper.

Step A4 | Merge HRP dilutions with SuperSignal substrate and mix 60 s
  Reagents  : SuperSignalSubstrate (1 drop per dilution level)
  Operation : Dispense + mix
  Mix time  : 60 s
  Notes     : Paper M&M: 'One drop of SuperSignal chemiluminescent substrate was then
              dispensed, mixed, and merged with each diluted drop of HRP, and the pooled
              drop was mixed for 60 s, driven to the detection area.'

Step A5 | Pre-measurement incubation at room temperature
  Operation      : heat
  Temperature    : 25 C
  Duration       : 120 s (2 min)
  Notes          : Paper M&M: 'emitted light was measured after 2 min with an H10682-110 PMT.'
                   heat step models 2 min dwell in detection zone before PMT readout.

Step A6 | PMT chemiluminescence detection
  Module         : chemiluminescenceDetection
  Duration       : 30 s per droplet
  Instrument     : H10682-110 PMT (Hamamatsu Photonics K.K., Japan); emission ~425-500 nm
  Calibration    : 4-point curve; R^2 = 0.993; each condition repeated 3 times
  QC gate        : hrpSignal1x (1x dilution = highest HRP concentration = highest signal)
    Pass (BB2)   : hrpSignal1x > 0; dispose all three reaction droplets
    Fail (BB3)   : hrpSignal1x <= 0; drain all three reaction droplets
  Join (BB4)     : dispose HRP signal droplets; proceed to Rubella ELISA branch


ASSAY 2: RUBELLA IgG SANDWICH ELISA (Design B)
-----------------------------------------------

Immunocomplex architecture:
  Magnetic bead coated with inactivated rubella virus (solid phase)
  Primary antibody: rubella IgG (analyte)
  Secondary antibody: HRP-conjugated goat anti-human IgG (detection)
  Readout: luminol/H2O2 chemiluminescence

Note: Unlike conventional ELISAs using a capture antibody specific to a target analyte,
this assay uses a bead coated with inactivated virus as the solid phase; the primary
antibody (rubella IgG) is the analyte. LOD = 0.15 IU/mL (clinical threshold: 10 IU/mL).

Concentrations tested: 0 IU/mL (blank), 1.56 IU/mL, 3.125 IU/mL
Steps per concentration: 30 (11 dispense, 10 mix, 8 magnetic separation, 1 measure)
Time per concentration: ~10 min; each condition repeated 2 times.

Reagents:
  Paramagnetic particles : Rubella-virus-coated microparticles (Abbott Laboratories);
                           ~1.5e8 particles/mL in Superblock Tris-buffered saline
  Rubella IgG standards  : 0, 1.56, 3.125 IU/mL (Abbott Laboratories);
                           diluted in DPBS + 4% BSA + 0.05% v/v Pluronic L64
  HRP conjugate          : HRP-conjugated goat polyclonal Anti-Human IgG, 16 ng/mL
                           in custom DMF-compatible conjugate diluent
  Wash buffer            : Custom DMF-compatible wash buffer (refs [25,27])
  H2O2 solution          : Stable peroxide component of SuperSignal ELISA Femto substrate
  Luminol-Enhancer       : Luminol-Enhancer component of SuperSignal ELISA Femto substrate
                           + 0.025% v/v Pluronic L64
  Magnetic separation    : Motorized magnet integrated with DropBot controller (ref [25])

Protocol Steps (identical sequence for all three IgG concentrations):

Step B1 | Dispense paramagnetic bead suspension
  Reagents  : ParamagneticParticles
  Operation : Dispense x2 + merge
  Volume    : 2 unit volumes (~1.5 uL total; Design B unit = 750 nL)
  Notes     : Paper M&M: 'A ca. 1.6 uL drop (2 unit volumes) containing paramagnetic
              particles was dispensed from a reservoir and separated from the diluent.'
              Encoded as two 1-unit dispenses merged to produce the 2-unit-volume drop.

Step B2 | Dispense rubella IgG standard and incubate with beads
  Reagents  : RubellaIgG_Std_0 / RubellaIgG_Std_156 / RubellaIgG_Std_3125
  Operation : Dispense + mix
  Duration  : 180 s (3 min)
  Notes     : Paper M&M: 'One drop of rubella IgG standard (0, 1.56 or 3.125 IU/mL) was
              dispensed, delivered to the immobilized particles, and mixed for 3 min.'
              Three separate manifest entries encode the three concentrations.

Step B3 | Primary antibody wash x3 with magnetic separation
  Reagents  : WashBuffer (1 drop per wash cycle)
  Operation : Dispense + mix (30 s) + detect rubellaMagneticSeparation (30 s) x3
  Notes     : Paper M&M: 'The particles were washed three times in wash buffer and separated
              from the supernatant.' rubellaMagneticSeparation module abstracts motorized
              magnet engagement + DMF electrode switching that pellets the bead fraction and
              moves the supernatant droplet to waste electrode. Three explicit wash cycles
              unrolled (BioScript has no loop construct).

Step B4 | Dispense HRP conjugate and incubate with beads
  Reagents  : HRP_Conjugate (goat anti-human IgG, 16 ng/mL)
  Operation : Dispense + mix
  Duration  : 120 s (2 min)
  Notes     : Paper M&M: 'One drop of HRP conjugate solution was dispensed, delivered to
              the immobilized particles, and mixed for 2 min.'

Step B5 | Post-conjugate wash x3 with magnetic separation
  Reagents  : WashBuffer (1 drop per wash cycle)
  Operation : Dispense + mix (30 s) + detect rubellaMagneticSeparation (30 s) x3
  Notes     : Paper M&M: 'The particles were washed three times in wash buffer [after
              conjugate incubation].' Identical sequence to Step B3.

Step B6 | Resuspend beads in H2O2 and merge with luminol-enhancer
  Reagents  : H2O2_Solution, LuminolEnhancer
  Operation : Dispense + mix (30 s) + merge + mix (30 s)
  Notes     : Paper M&M: 'The particles were separated from the wash buffer and resuspended
              in one drop of H2O2, and this drop was merged and mixed with one drop of
              luminol-enhancer solution.' Two-component substrate merge encoded as sequential
              resuspend then luminol merge steps.

Step B7 | Pre-detection incubation and PMT readout
  Operation      : heat + detect
  Temperature    : 25 C
  Incubation     : 120 s (2 min)
  Module         : rubellaCLDetection
  Duration       : 30 s
  Instrument     : H10682-110 PMT (Hamamatsu Photonics K.K., Japan)
  LOD            : 0.15 IU/mL (clinical threshold: 10 IU/mL); R^2 = 0.988
  Notes          : Paper M&M: 'The pooled drop was incubated for 2 min and the
                   chemiluminescent signal was recorded using the PMT.'
  QC gate        : elisaSignal3125 (3.125 IU/mL = highest tested = highest expected signal)
    Pass (BB5)   : elisaSignal3125 > 0; dispose elisa0Pool, elisa156Pool, elisa3125Pool
    Fail (BB6)   : elisaSignal3125 <= 0; drain elisa0Pool, elisa156Pool, elisa3125Pool
  Terminal (BB7) : dispose elisaSignal0, elisaSignal156, elisaSignal3125; NOP


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : fobel_paper_dmf_digital_microfluidics.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else gates, 7 CFG edges
DAG            : fobel_paper_dmf_digital_microfluidics_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations in s or m (BioScript supports s and m only; h not supported)
                 2 min incubation  -> 2m  (IR: 120.0 SECOND)
                 3 min incubation  -> 3m  (IR: 180.0 SECOND)
Modules        : chemiluminescenceDetection, rubellaMagneticSeparation, rubellaCLDetection

Serial dilution note:
  BioScript has no split-and-reuse construct. The 1x/2x/4x HRP serial dilution is encoded
  as explicit dispense+merge chains from fresh manifest entries to avoid split-array and
  stranded-variable compiler errors. The 4x diluent (3 units) is accumulated by chaining
  two additional PBS+Pluronic merge steps.

Magnetic wash note:
  The rubellaMagneticSeparation detect variables (sep*, csep*) produced during wash cycles
  are intermediate separation signals; they are not used as QC gate inputs and are not
  explicitly disposed. The lilott8/BioScript compiler accepts unconsumed detect intermediates
  without error. If future compiler versions flag these, add dispose statements for each
  sep* variable after the final wash in each concentration arm.

drain normalization:
  Both if/else gate false branches use drain in .bs source. The compiler normalizes drain
  to dispose in the IR output -- expected behavior consistent with all prior encoded protocols.

Manifest entries (13):
  PBS, HRP_Standard, SuperSignalSubstrate, WashBuffer, ParamagneticParticles,
  RubellaIgG_Std_0, RubellaIgG_Std_156, RubellaIgG_Std_3125, HRP_Conjugate,
  H2O2_Solution, LuminolEnhancer, PluronicL64

  Note: Three separate manifest entries encode the three IgG concentrations because
  BioScript dispense must reference a named manifest entry; concentration cannot be
  parameterized at runtime.

assay_1_hrp_chemiluminescence.wash_buffer: DPBS supplemented with 0.05% v/v Pluronic L64

steps.name: Prepare PBS diluent droplets with Pluronic L64
steps.notes: Three independent diluent droplets prepared (one per dilution level). Pluronic L64 at 0.05% v/v added to all reagent solutions to prevent protein adsorption.

steps.name: Dispense HRP standard stock droplets
steps.notes: 100 uU/mL HRP in DPBS + 0.05% v/v Pluronic L64. Three stock drops dispensed from reservoir, one per dilution level.

steps.name: Generate 1x, 2x, and 4x HRP dilution series

4x.notes: 1:4 dilution; 3 diluent units accumulated by explicit chaining (compiler constraint: no multi-unit dispense)

steps.bioscript_note: BioScript has no split-and-reuse construct; serial dilution encoded as explicit dispense+merge chains to avoid stranded-variable compiler errors. All three dilution levels instantiated from fresh manifest dispenses.

steps.name: Merge HRP dilutions with SuperSignal substrate and mix
steps.notes: One SuperSignal substrate drop merged with each diluted HRP drop. Mixed for 60 s on electrode array. Paper M&M: 'pooled drop was mixed for 60 s, driven to the detection area.'

steps.name: Pre-measurement incubation at room temperature
steps.notes: 2 min dwell at ambient temperature in detection zone before PMT readout. Paper M&M: 'emitted light was measured after 2 min with an H10682-110 PMT.'

qc_gate.rationale: 1x (undiluted equivalent) has highest expected HRP concentration and signal

steps.name: Dispense paramagnetic bead suspension
steps.notes: Paper M&M: 'A ca. 1.6 uL drop (2 unit volumes) containing paramagnetic particles was dispensed from a reservoir.' Modelled as two 1-unit dispenses merged to approximate 2-unit-volume drop.

steps.name: Dispense rubella IgG standard and incubate with beads
steps.notes: Paper M&M: 'One drop of rubella IgG standard (0, 1.56 or 3.125 IU/mL) was dispensed, delivered to the immobilized particles, and mixed for 3 min.' Three separate manifest entries used for three IgG concentrations.

steps.name: Primary antibody wash (3x) with magnetic separation
steps.notes: Paper M&M: 'The particles were washed three times in wash buffer and separated from the supernatant.' rubellaMagneticSeparation module abstracts motorized magnet engagement + DMF electrode switching for bead pellet/supernatant separation after each wash cycle.

steps.name: Dispense HRP conjugate and incubate with beads
steps.notes: Paper M&M: 'One drop of HRP conjugate solution was dispensed, delivered to the immobilized particles, and mixed for 2 min.' Conjugate: HRP-conjugated goat anti-human IgG at 16 ng/mL.

steps.name: Post-conjugate wash (3x) with magnetic separation
steps.notes: Paper M&M: 'The particles were washed three times in wash buffer [after conjugate incubation].' Identical wash/separate sequence as B3.

steps.name: Resuspend beads in H2O2 and merge with luminol-enhancer
steps.notes: Paper M&M: 'The particles were separated from the wash buffer and resuspended in one drop of H2O2, and this drop was merged and mixed with one drop of luminol-enhancer solution.' SuperSignal ELISA Femto components loaded separately in BioScript to reflect two-component merge.

qc_gate.rationale: 3.125 IU/mL is the highest tested concentration with highest expected chemiluminescent signal

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Droplet On Tape: Protocol
Source Link  : https://www.protocols.io/view/droplet-on-tape-protocol-n2bvj9wzblk5/v1
DOI Link     : https://dx.doi.org/10.1038/protex.2017.017
Journal      : Nature Protocols Exchange, February 28, 2017
Platform     : Acoustic Droplet Ejection (ADE) onto Kapton conveyor belt (DOT system) for XFEL sample delivery
Associated   : Fuller et al., Nature Methods, 2017; DOI: 10.1038/nmeth.4195


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes the Droplet On Tape (DOT) system, a flexible sample delivery platform
coupling Acoustic Droplet Ejection (ADE) with a moving Kapton conveyor belt for time-resolved
X-ray studies at X-ray Free Electron Lasers (XFELs). DOT enables simultaneous X-ray Diffraction
(XRD) and X-ray Emission Spectroscopy (XES) from protein microcrystal slurry or protein
solution, along with ancillary signals (transmission, fluorescence). It supports multiple
reaction initiation schemes: laser flash photolysis (single-excitation free-space timing and
multi-step fiber excitation) and gas-phase activation (differential pumping of reactive gas).

The platform is designed for restricted-access beamline environments and is operated entirely
via remote control (EPICS framework). The DOT system is comprised of five main sub-systems:
the ADE injector, control systems, the conveyor belt, the sample environment (Helium enclosure),
and reaction initiation systems.

Typical beamline deployment: 5 days setup (3 people); 4-5 days data collection per experiment.
Custom fabrication of all components: ~1 month (machining) + ~1 month (assembly, 2 people).


SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Five integrated sub-systems:

Sub-system 1 | ADE Injector
  Transducer   : Olympus V319-SU, 1 inch spherical focus, 15 MHz resonance frequency
                 (developed for ultrasonic imaging applications)
  Waveform gen.: Agilent 33612A; tone-burst at 15 MHz, controllable amplitude and duration
  Amplifier    : Amplifier Research 500A250C RF amplifier; final driving voltage ~40 V
  Ejection     : Tone-burst <100 us ejects nano-liter droplet from sample-air interface
  Coupling     : BNC cable -> bi-directional coupler (30 dB) -> transducer
                 Bi-directional coupler samples forward and reverse signals
  Echo probe   : "probe" spike (few hundred ns) sent a few ms before ejection burst
                 Sonar principle: echo return at ~35 us delay (1 inch focal length transducer)
                 at correct focus; fluid level monitored with <50 um accuracy
                 Oscilloscope monitored remotely via remote desktop (critical at beamline hutch)
  Sample path  : Polymicro tubing (360 um O.D., 180-250 um I.D.) from Legato 130 syringe pump
                 to ADE reservoir; coupling water column isolates sample from transducer

Sub-system 2 | Control Systems
  Framework    : EPICS (Experimental Physics Industrial Control Software)
  Hardware     : Syringe pump (Legato 130), Waveform generator (Agilent 33612A),
                 Actuator motors (Newport XPS-Q8), Tape drive motor (Lexium M-Drive),
                 Cameras (Allied Vision Manta-style)
  Custom IOCs  : Syringe pump: https://github.com/fullerf/LEGATO130
                 Waveform generator: https://github.com/fullerf/Agilent33600A
  Dependencies : EPICS base, StreamDevice, Asyn
  Tape drive   : Lexium M-Drive connected via built-in serial terminal; telnet from Linux/Mac
                 Speed controlled via motor slew rate adjustments (infrequently needed after
                 initial calibration)

Sub-system 3 | Conveyor Belt System
  Belt type    : Seamless Kapton (polyimide, Kapton 100H, C22H10O2N5, DuPont)
                 0.063-0.125 inch width; 31-36 inch diameter; 50 micron thickness
                 Supplier: BPB Inc., Bay Area, CA (custom request)
  Why seamless : Ultrasonically welded belts skip at weld over rollers, disrupting XFEL
                 synchronisation. Seamless belts eliminate this problem.
  Alternative  : Mylar film (used early in development; inferior x-ray scattering vs Kapton)
  Consumable   : Yes; one belt lasts several shifts if XFEL beam does not directly hit it
  Surface tmt  : FAS (1H,1H,2H,2H-Perfluorodecyltriethoxysilane, 97%, Sigma-Aldrich) in
                 n-octane; WCA increased from ~60 deg to 100 +/- 5 deg (see protocol below)
  Tensioner    : Hanging weight on rotating arm; two crowned rollers; adjustable by adding or
                 removing weights; over-tension indicator: belt curls when tension released
  Rollers      : ABEC 5 low-friction ball bearings with CNC-machined crown cap (3 inch radius
                 of curvature); crown keeps belt centred during operation
  Electrostatic: Passive: steel anti-static brushes near drive mechanism
                 Active: Transforming Technologies IN3425 static gun (ionised air) near ADE
                 deposition point; both required to avoid disrupting ADE ejection
  Mounting     : Newport UTS-100 motorised stage; modified Thorlabs aluminium breadboards
  Drive motor  : Lexium M-Drive LMDCE423 micro-stepping stepper motor; direct drive to 1 inch
                 stainless steel shaft; <4 revolutions/s typical operating speed
                 (geared mechanism abandoned due to velocity error introduction)

Sub-system 4 | Sample Environment
  Enclosure    : Custom acrylic (0.5 inch) helium chamber; Professional Plastics Inc.
  Door         : Large inflatable door with wide aperture at X-ray interaction region
  Joints       : Solvent welded (where possible); rubber foam gaskets elsewhere
  Feed-through : 0.125 inch aluminium panel, water-jet cut; handles all electronic, gas,
                 water, and fibre connections into the chamber
  Helium path  : Thin inflatable polyethylene bags extend helium environment from sample to
                 detector; second bag between XES crystal spectrometer and main chamber;
                 minimises scatter from heavier atoms in air during XRD/XES

Sub-system 5 | Reaction Initiation Systems
  Laser (fiber): High-precision CNC-machined grid (tolerance 0.0005 inch); holds 3 excitation
                 fibre-coupled laser inputs and 2 IR gate fibres
                 IR gate separation: 60 mm; each gate 30 mm from nearest excitation point
                 Each excitation fibre: 5 degrees of freedom for coupling optimisation
                 Droplet arrival monitored via IR scatter onto photodiode
                 All 5 fibres monitored on remote-accessible oscilloscopes
  Laser (free) : Single-excitation; movable 1 m focal-length motorised lens upstream of XFEL
                 Max laser advance: 6 mm upstream of XFEL interaction
                 Time delay range: 20-100 ms (at 300-60 mm/s belt speed)
                 Spatial overlap: 100 um accuracy (laser spot: ~400 um diameter)
                 Temporal overlap: 200 us accuracy (camera exposure); ns via photodiode
  Gas reaction : Conveyor belt passes through limited-extent reactive gas region (O2 example)
                 Confinement: differential pumping via series of small orifices
                 Exposure time: L / v_tape; Dead time: L_xfel / v_tape
                 Sealing: vacuum grease on all openings except belt entry and exit holes


BELT SURFACE TREATMENT PROTOCOL
---------------------------------

Step 1 | Belt Cleaning
  Reagents  : Milli-Q water, isopropanol
  Action    : Sonicate in Milli-Q water for 10 min; then sonicate in isopropanol for 10 min
  Notes     : Removes surface contaminants before hydrophobicity treatment

Step 2 | Vacuum Drying (pre-FAS)
  Equipment : Precision vacuum oven, model 19
  Condition : 50 C, 1 hour
  Notes     : Belt must be fully dry before FAS treatment; moisture interferes with silane
              bonding chemistry

Step 3 | FAS Hydrophobicity Treatment
  Reagent   : 0.25% (w/v) FAS (1H,1H,2H,2H-Perfluorodecyltriethoxysilane, Sigma-Aldrich)
              in n-octane
  Action    : Reflux belt in FAS/n-octane solution for 2 hours
  Result    : Water contact angle (WCA) increases from ~60 deg to 100 +/- 5 deg
  Purpose   : Aqueous droplets bead up on belt surface and do not spread; critical for
              maintaining droplet integrity during transport to XFEL interaction region

Step 4 | Vacuum Drying (post-FAS)
  Equipment : Precision vacuum oven, model 19
  Condition : 150 C, 3 hours
  Notes     : Removes all residual unreacted FAS from belt surface


BELT CLEANING PROCEDURE (in-experiment)
-----------------------------------------
  Method    : Drive belt through 4 high-pressure water jets (200+ psi, 500 um I.D.)
  Drying    : 2 compressed Helium blow-off nozzles (top and bottom of belt)
  Gas supply: 3 x KNF Neuberger N145.1.2AN.18 gas-tight diaphragm pumps draw Helium from
              the Helium chamber and recirculate it to power the blow-off nozzles
  Residue QC: Run belt dry (no sample injected); probe XES signal; accumulated residue
              detected as XES background above baseline; performed periodically during beamtimes


FIBER EXCITATION TIMING (Multi-excitation, e.g. Photosystem II)
-----------------------------------------------------------------
  Principle : Space-time diagram representation; constant belt velocity -> trajectories are
              straight lines with slope = velocity; excitation positions fixed in space/time
  Two DOF   : (1) deposition delay (Delta_tau_dep): when droplet is ejected onto belt
              (2) laser delay (Delta_tau_laser): when each fibre excitation fires
  Setup     :
    1. Adjust deposition delay until droplet appears in XFEL crosshairs (stroboscopic monitor)
    2. Fine-adjust deposition delay until droplet observed to explode (camera synced to XFEL)
    3. Confirm via solvent scatter in forward detector or emission signal in XES detector
    4. Adjust belt velocity until IR gate signals coincide in time
       (confirms droplets simultaneously present on all excitation points)
    5. Laser delay must be time-coincident with IR gate signals
  Allowed speeds at 10 Hz rep rate: 30, 60, 150, 300 mm/s
  (droplet spacing must be integer multiple or divisor of both 30 mm and 60 mm)
  Note      : Deposition delay and belt speed are coupled; adjust both incrementally


PROTOCOL STEPS (BioScript encoding)
--------------------------------------

Step 1 | Kapton Belt Cleaning (BB1 / main)
  Inputs    : MQWater, Isopropanol
  Operation : mix (sonication abstracted); 10 min
  Notes     : Sequential sonication in Milli-Q water then isopropanol

Step 2 | Vacuum Drying Before FAS (BB1 / main)
  Operation : heat at 50 C for 60 min (3600 s in IR)
  Equipment : Precision vacuum oven

Step 3 | FAS Reflux Treatment (BB1 / main)
  Inputs    : FAS_NOctane (0.25% w/v FAS in n-octane)
  Operation : mix (reflux abstracted); 120 min (7200 s in IR)

Step 4 | Vacuum Drying After FAS (BB1 / main)
  Operation : heat at 150 C for 180 min (10800 s in IR)
  Notes     : Residual FAS removal

Step 5 | ADE Injector Setup and Sample Loading (BB1 / main)
  Inputs    : SampleSolution, CouplingWater
  Operation : mix (reservoir loading abstracted); 2 s
  Notes     : Legato 130 syringe pump controls sample influx rate; coupling water column
              isolates sample from transducer

Step 6 | Acoustic Echo Probe — Fluid Level QC (BB1 -> BB2/BB3)
  Operation : detect echoLevelDetection for 10 s
  Pass (BB2): echoSignal > 0 -> fluid level and focus confirmed; eject droplet; dispose
  Fail (BB3): echoSignal <= 0 -> echo out of range; drain; re-adjust sample influx rate
  Join (BB4): dispose(echoSignal)

Step 7 | Laser Zone Droplet Transport (BB4 / echoJoin)
  Inputs    : ProteinCrystalSlurry, HeliumGas
  Operation : mix (belt transport through Helium enclosure abstracted); 5 s
  Notes     : Belt carries droplet from ADE deposition point through Helium chamber to laser
              excitation zone; belt speed 30-300 mm/s; time delays 20-100 ms

Step 8 | Droplet-Hit and Timing Confirmation (BB4 -> BB5/BB6)
  Operation : detect dropletHitDetection for 30 s
  Methods   : stroboscopic camera (sync'd to XFEL), forward scatter detector, XES detector,
              IR gate photodiode coincidence
  Pass (BB5): laserHitSignal > 0 -> overlap confirmed; dispose; proceed to XRD
  Fail (BB6): laserHitSignal <= 0 -> droplet missed; drain; re-adjust delay/belt speed
  Join (BB7): dispose(laserHitSignal)

Step 9 | XFEL Data Collection - XRD (BB7 -> BB8/BB9)
  Inputs    : ProteinCrystalSlurry, HeliumGas
  Operation : detect xrdSignalDetection for 30 s
  Motor     : Lexium M-Drive LMDCE423 direct drive; <4 rps
  Pass (BB8): xrdSignal > 0 -> valid diffraction; dispose; proceed to XES
  Fail (BB9): xrdSignal <= 0 -> beam miss or crystal failure; drain
  Join(BB10): dispose(xrdSignal)

Step 10 | Simultaneous XES Data Collection (BB10 -> BB11/BB12)
  Inputs    : ProteinCrystalSlurry, HeliumGas
  Operation : detect xesSignalDetection for 30 s
  Notes     : Second Helium bag between XES crystal spectrometer and main Helium chamber
  Pass(BB11): xesSignal > 0 -> valid emission spectrum; dispose; proceed to belt residue check
  Fail(BB12): xesSignal <= 0 -> no emission; drain
  Join(BB13): dispose(xesSignal)

Step 11 | Belt Cleaning Run (BB13 / xesJoin)
  Inputs    : MQWater, HeliumGas
  Operation : mix (water jet pass abstracted); 5 min cleaning; 2 min blow-off drying
  Water jets: 4 x 200+ psi jets; 500 um I.D.
  Drying    : 2 compressed Helium blow-off nozzles (KNF Neuberger pump system)

Step 12 | Belt Residue QC Check (BB13 -> BB14/BB15)
  Operation : detect residueDetection for 30 s
  Method    : dry belt run; XES background monitoring
  Pass(BB14): residueSignal > 0 -> residue above baseline; dispose; repeat cleaning cycle
  Fail(BB15): residueSignal <= 0 -> belt clean; dispose; ready for next shift
  Join(BB16): dispose(residueSignal); NOP [terminal]


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : fuller_droplet_on_tape_dot.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 16 basic blocks (BB1-BB16), 5 if/else QC gates, 20 CFG edges
DAG file       : fuller_droplet_on_tape_dot_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations converted to minutes (m) for compiler compatibility
                 (BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported)
                 60 min  (50 C dry)    -> 60m   -> IR: 3600.0 SECOND   [verified]
                 120 min (FAS reflux)  -> 120m  -> IR: 7200.0 SECOND   [verified]
                 180 min (150 C dry)   -> 180m  -> IR: 10800.0 SECOND  [verified]
                 sonication            -> 10m   -> IR: 600.0 SECOND    [verified]
Modules        : echoLevelDetection, dropletHitDetection, xrdSignalDetection,
                 xesSignalDetection, residueDetection
Platform notes : mix steps abstract ADE acoustic ejection, belt transport through Helium
                 enclosure, and surface chemistry (reflux, sonication); not DMF electrode mixing
                 heat steps cover vacuum oven drying (50 C, 150 C) and FAS reflux chemistry
                 treatedBelt variable carried from BB1 (FAS treatment) -> BB13 (cleaning),
                 confirmed in IR line 59: mix(treatedBelt1[0], cleaningWater1[0])
                 drain -> dispose compiler mapping confirmed in bsbbif_6_f (IR line 30)
IR anomaly     : bsbbif_3_f (BB3 echo fail) emits dispose() for drain; standard compiler
                 behaviour for non-DMF targets; functionally correct
CFG verified   : strict digraph with 16 nodes and 20 edges; diamond-chain structure;
                 no stray edges, no missing joins, no cycles; NOP terminal at BB16 confirmed
