description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : On-chip Integration of Droplet Microfluidics and Nanostructure-Initiator
               Mass Spectrometry for Enzyme Screening
Source Link  : https://ipo.lbl.gov/wp-content/uploads/sites/8/2017/05/2016-049_pub.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1039/c6lc01182a
Journal      : Lab on a Chip, 2016 (Royal Society of Chemistry)
Authors      : Joshua Heinemann, Kai Deng, Steve C. C. Shih, Jian Gao, Paul D. Adams,
               Anup K. Singh, Trent R. Northen
Platform     : uNIMS (digital droplet microfluidics + NIMS array, EWOD-actuated)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes the uNIMS platform -- a first-of-its-kind integration of droplet
microfluidics with nanostructure-initiator mass spectrometry (NIMS) for label-free,
time-resolved enzyme kinetics screening at the 150 nL droplet scale. The system couples
a digital microfluidics (DMF) chip (electrowetting-on-dielectric, EWOD) with a patterned
silicon NIMS array (640 pads, 5x5 cm wafer), enabling programmable droplet deposition
onto discrete NIMS elements for subsequent mass spectrometry (MS) imaging.

The protocol is divided into two functional parts:
  PART 1: Dextromethorphan (DXM) standard validation -- confirms droplet actuation
          onto NIMS pads and analyte sorption at m/z 272.
  PART 2: CelE-CBM3a enzyme kinetics -- two independent pH conditions:
    2A: pH 6.0 (phosphate buffer, 50 mM) -- parallel droplet loading, 5 time points
        (10, 20, 30, 40, 50 min), G4 substrate degraded to G3, G2, G1.
    2B: pH 5.0 (acetate buffer, 100 mM) -- continuous series loading, 3 time points
        (10, 20, 40 min), similar product distribution to pH 6 demonstrating CelE
        robustness to process conditions.

Key advantages over conventional NIMS screening:
  - 150 nL droplets vs 20 uL dead volume from 384-well acoustic printing (~133x reagent
    reduction)
  - Programmable time resolution for kinetics (droplets deposited and removed at defined
    intervals via EWOD)
  - Fluorous probe and products remain adsorbed on NIMS surface after droplet removal,
    enabling off-line MS imaging
  - Scalable: demonstrated 20 assays per NIMS array; protocol modification enables 620
    individual assays (1 pad per enzyme); theoretical maximum >100,000 pads per 5 cm2
    at 50 um grid resolution


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
The uNIMS stack consists of five layers held together in a 3D-printed chassis:

Layer i   : 3D-printed PLA top cover (Ultimaker 2, 215 C, Blender.org design)
Layer ii  : PDMS mounting gasket for PEEK tubing interfacing (upper gasket)
Layer iii : DMF chip -- glass substrate; 128 chrome electrodes (5 cm L x 500 um W x
            375 um H); 5 um SU-8-5 dielectric; PDMS fluidics channel (500 um W x 225 um H);
            31 digital arrayers for droplet actuation over NIMS pads;
            1 T-junction for pressure-driven droplet generation (~150 nL droplets)
Layer iv  : NIMS array chip -- 5 x 5 cm silicon wafer; 640 patterned NIMS pads
            (photopatternable PDMS protective gasket, laser-cut wafer, ICP-RIE etching)
Layer v   : 3D-printed PETG bottom piece with Dropbot PCB adapter (pogo pins)

Seal      : Reversible PDMS compression seal between DMF chip (layer iii) and NIMS array
            (layer iv) -- allows NIMS array removal and mounting in mass spectrometer
            after experiment, without disturbing adsorbed analytes.

DMF chip fabrication:
  - Photolithography on chrome Telic wafers (AZ1500 positive resist, OAI Series 200 aligner,
    16 mW/cm2, 15 s exposure; MF-321 developer ~1 min)
  - Chrome etch: CR-4 chromium etchant, 5 min agitation
  - Post-bake: 120 C, 10 min
  - Plasma treatment: 20% O2, 20 W RF, 5 min
  - Dielectric: 5 um SU-8-5 (Microchem protocol)
  - Channel layer: SU-8-2075 master mold (140 um height); PDMS (20:1, cured 100 C 1 h);
    sealed against glass slide with 100 uL Picoglide, rinsed with Novec HFE-7500

NIMS array fabrication:
  - Photopatternable PDMS (10:1 ratio, 3% benzophenone, degassed by centrifugation)
  - Spin-coat on silicon wafer: 2500 rpm, 30 s
  - UV exposure: <365 nm, 10 min; photomask ~100 um above substrate
  - Post-exposure bake: 120 C, 2.5 min (vacuum oven)
  - Development: toluene, 10 s; rinse IPA and H2O
  - ICP-RIE etching (PlasmaLab 100, Oxford Instrument):
      Gas: SF6/O2 at 30/20 ratio; pressure: 6 mTorr; temperature: -80 C (cryogenic)
      Etching chamber power: 5 W; plasma generator power: 1000 W
  - Result: silicon nanostructures for NIMS-based laser desorption/ionisation

Dropbot control:
  - Hold voltage: 20 V (maintains droplet position during flow halt)
  - Actuation: 90 V, 10 kHz, 250 ms bursts (moves droplets in/out of NIMS pad pockets)
  - Impedance detection: used to detect actuation failure
  - Software: Dropbot + microdrop GUI; monitoring and validation visual (limitation noted)


REAGENTS
--------

Carrier oil      : Novec HFE-7500 (3M, US); 100 uL Picoglide (Dolomite Microfluidics, UK)
                   pumped through channel for 30 min for surface preparation.
                   Flow rates: 0.05 uL/s reaction cocktail, 0.2 uL/s HFE-7500 oil.

Enzyme           : CelE-CBM3a (CelE); chimeric endoglucanase; GH family 5 (GH5) domain
                   from Clostridium thermocellum (Cthe_0797) fused to carbohydrate binding
                   module CBM3a. Deconstructs plant hemicellulose via beta-1,4 glycosidic
                   bond cleavage. Concentration: 240 ug/mL. (Ref: Deng et al., ACS Chem.
                   Biol. 2014, 9(7), 1470-1479)

Substrate probe  : 1,4-beta-D-cellotetraose-probe (G4). Fluorous-tagged (perfluorocarbon)
                   for NIMS surface affinity. MW 1515.48; formula C55H78F17N5O24.
                   Detected at m/z 1516.43 (H+). Volume: 1 uL per reaction.

Degradation      :
products           G3 (cellotriose-probe)  -- MW 1353.42; C49H68F17N5O19; m/z 1354.37 (H+)
                   G2 (cellobiose-probe)   -- MW 1191.37; C43H58F17N5O14; m/z 1192.32 (H+)
                   G1 (glucose-probe)      -- MW 1029.32; C37H48F17N5O9;  m/z 1030.28 (H+)

Buffers          : pH 6: Phosphate buffer, 50 mM, pH 6.0 (4 uL per 6 uL reaction)
                   pH 5: Acetate buffer, 100 mM, pH 5.0 (4 uL per 6 uL reaction)

Validation std   : Dextromethorphan (DXM); 1 mg/mL in H2O; detected at m/z 272 (H+);
                   matrix-free ionisation; no signal on non-NIMS surrounding structures.

MALDI matrix     : Universal MALDI matrix; 20 mg/mL in MeOH; applied to NIMS array after
                   removal from uNIMS system prior to MS imaging.

General reagents : SU-8-5, SU-8-2075, SU-8 Developer (Microchem, Newton, MA); gold and
                   chromium-coated glass slides (Telic, Valencia, CA); ITO-coated glass slides
                   and silicon wafers (Delta Technologies, Stillwater, MN); Aquapel (TCP Global,
                   San Diego, CA); MF-321 developer (Rohm and Haas); CR-4 chromium etchant
                   (OM Group); AZ-300 T photoresist stripper (AZ Electronic Materials);
                   Sylgard 184 PDMS (Dow Corning); benzophenone and mixed xylenes (Sigma);
                   TPS (Trichloro(1H,1H,2H-perfluorooctyl)silane) for master mold silanisation.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

-- PART 1: DXM STANDARD VALIDATION --

Step 1 | Device Surface Preparation and Oil Phase Loading
  Reagent  : Novec HFE-7500 (with 100 uL Picoglide surfactant)
  Operation: Dispense oilPhase; pump through PDMS channel for 30 min
  Purpose  : Coats channel surfaces; stabilises droplets at T-junction; enables EWOD
             actuation; primes reversible PDMS seal interface with NIMS array.

Step 2 | Dextromethorphan Standard Preparation
  Reagent  : DXM, 1 mg/mL in H2O; 5 uL plug prefilled into syringe tubing
  Operation: Dispense dxmDroplet (1 unit = ~150 nL droplet abstraction)
  Purpose  : Validates microfluidic droplet actuation and NIMS pad analyte sorption before
             enzymatic assay. DXM detected at m/z 272 (H+); matrix-free ionisation.

Step 3 | DXM Droplet Generation at T-Junction
  Inputs   : dxmDroplet + oilPhase
  Operation: mix for 5 s (abstracts T-junction droplet generation)
  Flow rate: 0.05 uL/s reaction cocktail; 0.2 uL/s HFE-7500 oil
  Result   : ~150 nL DXM droplets in HFE-7500 oil train; synchronised with electrode
             actuation for uniform spacing along central fluidics chamber.

Step 4 | DXM Droplet Loading and Incubation on NIMS Pads
  Input    : dxmDropletInOil
  Operation: heat at 25 C for 10 m (600 s; room temperature)
  Actuation: Flow halted; 20 V electrode hold. 31 arrayers actuate droplets at 90 V,
             10 kHz, 250 ms bursts into NIMS pad pockets.
  Incubate : DXM sorbs onto NIMS surface during contact. Fluorous-tagged substrates
             confirmed to remain adsorbed in microfluidic environment (consistent with
             traditional NIMzyme execution).
  Eject    : Droplets ejected from pocket after incubation; evacuated via central chamber.

Step 5 | MALDI Matrix Coating
  Inputs   : dxmDropletInOil + UniversalMALDI_Matrix
  Operation: mix for 1 m (60 s; abstracts matrix co-crystallisation)
  Procedure: NIMS array physically removed from uNIMS system after experiment completion.
             Universal MALDI matrix (20 mg/mL MeOH) applied to array surface.
             Array mounted in ABSciex 5800 MALDI-TOF for MS imaging.

Step 6 | MS Imaging QC -- DXM Deposition Detection (Branch Gate 1)
  Input    : dxmNimsArray
  Module   : nimsImagingDetection
  Duration : 30 s
  MS scan  : ABSciex 5800 MALDI-TOF; positive mode; laser intensity 4150; focus m/z 1200;
             50 um laser step; m/z 272 ion map; OpenMSI spot set analysis.
  Branch:
    Pass (depositionSignal > 0)  --> BB2: dispose(dxmNimsArray); proceed to pH 6 kinetics
    Fail (depositionSignal <= 0) --> BB3: drain(dxmNimsArray); no sorption (surfactant
                                         suppression or actuation failure)
  Join: BB4 (validationJoin) -- dispose(depositionSignal); pH 6 kinetics branch begins.


-- PART 2A: CelE KINETICS AT pH 6.0 (PHOSPHATE BUFFER) --

Step 7 | Reaction Cocktail Preparation (pH 6)
  Buffer   : Phosphate buffer, 50 mM, pH 6.0 (4 uL)
  Substrate: G4 substrate-probe (1 uL)
  Enzyme   : CelE-CBM3a, 240 ug/mL (1 uL)
  Total    : 6 uL; premixed off-chip in 0.5 mL eppendorf tube
  Operation: 4 buffer units dispensed individually, chained via sequential mix in BioScript
             (ph6_buf_12, ph6_buf_34, ph6_bufBulk); substrate and enzyme then merged.
             [Compiler constraint: explicit sequential merging required; no multi-unit
             dispense; same pattern as b1/b2/b3 in Moazami et al. reference.]
  Loading  : 5 uL plug drawn into syringe tubing and injected onto uNIMS.

Step 8 | Reaction Droplet Generation at T-Junction (pH 6)
  Inputs   : ph6_reactionCocktail + HFE7500_Surfactant
  Operation: mix for 5 s
  Flow rate: 0.05 uL/s cocktail; 0.2 uL/s HFE-7500
  Loading  : Parallel mode (Fig. 4A) -- flow halted after chamber fills; all 31 arrayer
             electrodes actuated simultaneously; droplets loaded in parallel onto all
             corresponding NIMS pads.

Step 9 | Sequential Incubation on NIMS Pads -- 5 Time Points (pH 6)
  Input    : ph6_dropletsInOil
  Operation: 5 sequential heat blocks at 25 C (room temperature)
  Time pts : 10 min (600 s) -- cumulative: 10 min
             10 min (600 s) -- cumulative: 20 min
             10 min (600 s) -- cumulative: 30 min
             10 min (600 s) -- cumulative: 40 min
             10 min (600 s) -- cumulative: 50 min
  Pads     : 6 pads per time point; 31 total pads used
  Ejection : At each 10 min interval, 6 droplets synchronously ejected from NIMS pocket
             into central chamber and evacuated. Fresh droplets actuated for next interval.
  Products : G4 (m/z 1516.43) degraded to G3 (m/z 1354.37), G2 (m/z 1192.32),
             G1 (m/z 1030.28) over 50 min. Probe and products remain adsorbed on NIMS
             surface after droplet removal.

Step 10 | MALDI Matrix Coating and MS Imaging (pH 6) (Branch Gate 2)
  Inputs   : ph6_dropletsInOil + UniversalMALDI_Matrix
  Mix      : 1 m (60 s); array coated after removal from uNIMS system
  Detect   : nimsImagingDetection; 30 s; same MS parameters as Step 6
  Analysis : OpenMSI spot set analysis; fractional conversion:
             [G1] / ([G4] + [G3] + [G2] + [G1]) for each time point pad.
  Note     : MS imaging required (not simple spot analysis) because HFE-7500 surfactant
             adheres to NIMS surface and suppresses ionisation; surfactant causes
             heterogeneous ions at high concentration, reducing sensitivity.
             NIMS surface acts as capture substrate for substrates and products.
  Branch:
    Pass (ph6Signal > 0)  --> BB5: dispose(ph6_nimsArray); G3/G2/G1 detected; proceed to pH 5
    Fail (ph6Signal <= 0) --> BB6: drain(ph6_nimsArray); no product signal
  Join: BB7 (pH6Join) -- dispose(ph6Signal); pH 5 kinetics branch begins.


-- PART 2B: CelE KINETICS AT pH 5.0 (ACETATE BUFFER) --

Step 11 | Reaction Cocktail Preparation (pH 5)
  Buffer   : Acetate buffer, 100 mM, pH 5.0 (4 uL)
  Substrate: G4 substrate-probe (1 uL)
  Enzyme   : CelE-CBM3a, 240 ug/mL (1 uL)
  Total    : 6 uL; premixed off-chip in 0.5 mL eppendorf tube
  Operation: Identical chaining pattern to pH 6 (ph5_buf_12, ph5_buf_34, ph5_bufBulk);
             acetate buffer replaces phosphate buffer.

Step 12 | Reaction Droplet Generation at T-Junction (pH 5)
  Inputs   : ph5_reactionCocktail + HFE7500_Surfactant
  Operation: mix for 5 s
  Flow rate: 0.05 uL/s cocktail; 0.2 uL/s HFE-7500
  Loading  : Continuous series mode (Fig. 4B) -- droplets removed directly from flow without
             halting; successive pads occupied and cleared continuously.

Step 13 | Sequential Incubation on NIMS Pads -- 3 Time Points (pH 5)
  Input    : ph5_dropletsInOil
  Operation: 3 sequential heat blocks at 25 C (room temperature)
  Time pts : 10 min (600 s)  -- cumulative: 10 min
             10 min (600 s)  -- cumulative: 20 min
             20 min (1200 s) -- cumulative: 40 min
  Note     : Three time points vs five for pH 6; final heat block is 20 m (600 s gap
             between 20 min and 40 min time points). CelE produces similar product
             distributions at pH 5 and pH 6, demonstrating enzyme robustness to process
             conditions (reaction profile consistent with Deng, Front. Bioeng. Biotechnol. 2015).

Step 14 | MALDI Matrix Coating and MS Imaging (pH 5) (Branch Gate 3 + Terminal)
  Inputs   : ph5_dropletsInOil + UniversalMALDI_Matrix
  Mix      : 1 m (60 s); NIMS array removed and matrix-coated as before
  Detect   : nimsImagingDetection; 30 s; same MS parameters
  Branch:
    Pass (ph5Signal > 0)  --> BB8: dispose(ph5_nimsArray); kinetics confirmed
    Fail (ph5Signal <= 0) --> BB9: drain(ph5_nimsArray); no product signal
  Terminal : BB10 -- dispose(ph5Signal); NOP. Experiment ends.
             NIMS array placed in ABSciex 5800 MALDI-TOF for final MS imaging session.


QUANTIFICATION
--------------
Method   : Fractional conversion (internal normalisation)
Formula  : [Gx] / ([G4] + [G3] + [G2] + [G1]) for each product Gx at each time point
Rationale: Internal normalisation eliminates sensitivity to droplet volume variation
           (device maintains +/-10% SD in droplet size; turbulent mixing at t-junction
           causes initially larger droplets). Less sensitive to concentration measurement
           errors than direct quantification approaches.
Software : OpenMSI spot set analysis tools (Rubel et al., Anal. Chem. 2013, 85(21),
           10354-10361)


MASS SPECTROMETRY
-----------------
Instrument  : ABSciex 5800 MALDI-TOF
Mode        : Positive ionisation
Laser int.  : 4150
Focus m/z   : 1200
Laser step  : 50 um
Matrix      : Universal MALDI matrix, 20 mg/mL in MeOH
Analysis    : OpenMSI spot set analysis


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : heinemann_uNIMS_enzyme_screening.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
DAG            : heinemann_uNIMS_enzyme_screening_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations in minutes (m) or seconds (s); h token not supported.
                 pH 6 incubation: 5 x heat 10m (IR: 5 x 600.0 SECOND)
                 pH 5 incubation: 2 x heat 10m + 1 x heat 20m (IR: 600, 600, 1200 SECOND)
ASCII note     : File uses only ASCII characters. Non-ASCII symbols replaced:
                 'u' for mu (micro); '+/-' for plus-minus; 'beta' for Greek beta.
                 Required because ANTLR4 FileStream uses ASCII codec and rejects bytes >127.
Modules        : dropletDepositionDetection, nimsImagingDetection
Manifests      : CelE_CBM3a_Enzyme, G4_Substrate_Probe, PhosphateBuffer_pH6,
                 AcetateBuffer_pH5, HFE7500_Surfactant, DextromethorphanStandard,
                 UniversalMALDI_Matrix
Buffer chaining: 4 units of buffer (4:1:1 volume ratio) built via explicit sequential
                 mix chain (ph6_buf_12 -> ph6_buf_34 -> ph6_bufBulk); same compiler
                 constraint pattern as Moazami et al. b1/b2/b3 reference.
Surfactant note: HFE-7500 suppresses NIMS ionisation; MS imaging required over spot
                 analysis to detect all degradation products. NIMS-compatible surfactants
                 identified as a key future direction.

steps.notes: MS imaging required (not spot analysis) due to ion suppression from HFE-7500 surfactant. Surfactant adheres to NIMS surface and reduces sensitivity; MS imaging detects all degradation products despite suppression. Fractional conversion: [G1]/([G4]+[G3]+[G2]+[G1]).

steps.name: Reaction cocktail preparation (pH 5)
steps.notes: Identical composition to pH 6 run with acetate buffer replacing phosphate buffer. Same off-chip premix procedure. Loaded continuously in series onto uNIMS (Fig. 4B).

steps.name: Reaction droplet generation at T-junction (pH 5)
steps.loading_mode: Continuous series (droplets removed from pad directly from flow; Supplementary Video)
steps.notes: Series loading used for pH 5 run. Droplets can also be removed directly from flow without pausing (vs parallel loading which requires flow halt for pH 6 run).

steps.name: Sequential incubation on NIMS pads (pH 5) -- 3 time points
steps.notes: Three time points vs five for pH 6. Final heat block is 20 m (600s gap from 20 to 40 min). CelE produces similar product distributions at pH 5 and pH 6, demonstrating enzyme robustness to process conditions (reaction profile consistent with Deng, 2015).

steps.name: MALDI matrix coating and MS imaging (pH 5)

pass.meaning: G3/G2/G1 hydrolysis products detected; experiment complete

fail.meaning: No product signal; surfactant suppression or enzyme inactivity

terminal.notes: NIMS array removed for final MS imaging. Terminal node; NOP in IR.

dxm_validation.outcome: DXM (m/z 272) detected exclusively on NIMS pads, not surrounding structures
dxm_validation.ionisation: Matrix-free; NIMS surface sufficient for ionisation
dxm_validation.ms_imaging: OpenMSI confirmed successful analyte deposition pattern

pH6_kinetics.observation: G4 rapidly degraded to G3, G2, G1 over 50 min
pH6_kinetics.note: Ion intensities low vs DXM; MS imaging required to detect all degradation products due to surfactant suppression

pH5_kinetics.observation: Similar product distributions to pH 6; CelE robust across both pH conditions

device_capacity.reagent_reduction: 150 nL droplets vs 20 uL dead volume in acoustic printing from 384-well plates
device_capacity.scalability_note: Grid of 50 um resolution gives >100,000 pads per 5 cm2 NIMS array when scaled to lower bounds of digital microfluidics; compatible with ABSciex MALDI-TOF highest scan resolution

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Direct Detection and Drug-Resistance Profiling of Bacteremias Using Inertial Microfluidics
Source Link  : https://pubs.rsc.org/lc/article/15/10/2297/1246161/Direct-detection-and-drug-resistance-profiling-of
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1039/c5lc00311c
Journal      : Lab on a Chip, 2015, Vol. 15, pp. 2297-2307
Platform     : Inertial microfluidics (Dean Flow Fractionation) + NanoString hybridization-based RNA detection


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a method for rapid isolation of bacteria from whole blood using a PDMS
spiral microchannel device operating on the principle of Dean Flow Fractionation (DFF), coupled
to hybridization-based RNA detection (NanoString nCounter) for direct pathogen identification
and antibiotic susceptibility determination without bacterial culture or enzymatic amplification.

The protocol encodes two sequential diagnostic workflows:

  Workflow 1 | Species identification via rRNA detection:
    Bacteria (~100 cfu/mL) isolated from 3x-diluted whole blood by DFF; rRNA probes targeting
    species-variable regions of 16S and 23S rRNA identify E. coli, K. pneumoniae, and
    P. aeruginosa from concentrated bacterial eluate. Sensitivity approaches clinically relevant
    uncultured bacteremia loads without PCR or enzymatic amplification.

  Workflow 2 | Antibiotic susceptibility via mRNA detection:
    E. coli clinical isolates at ~10^5 cfu/mL (direct spike or 7.5 h BACTEC pre-enrichment
    from 1 cfu/mL) processed by DFF; recovered bacteria exposed to ciprofloxacin (2.5 mcg/mL,
    37 C, 30 min); mRNA transcriptional response profiled by NanoString. Transcriptional
    Susceptibility Score discriminates susceptible (score ~0) from resistant (score ~1) strains.

Total workflow time: ~8 hours including DFF separation, RNA hybridization, and ciprofloxacin
exposure. This represents a >6-fold acceleration over standard culture-based methods (48-72 h).


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Material  : Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) cast from silanized silicon wafer master; bonded
            irreversibly to glass slide by air plasma (Harrick Plasma Cleaner).
Channel   : Spiral geometry; 500 um (w) x 80 um (h); total length ~10 cm.
            Height fixed at 80 um so that blood cells (ap/h > 0.07) experience inertial
            lift (F_L) while bacteria (<1 um, ap/h << 0.07) are governed by Dean drag (F_D) only.

Inlets:
  Outer inlet (75 um wide)  : 3x diluted whole blood sample (~15% hematocrit)
  Inner inlet (425 um wide) : PBS + 0.1% BSA sheath fluid at ~10x sample flow rate

Outlets:
  Bacterial outlet (200 um) : Bacteria and platelets (Dean-migrated to outer wall, DC1 complete)
  Waste outlet              : RBCs and leukocytes (inertially focused at inner wall)

Separation principle:
  Dean drag (F_D) migrates all particles toward the inner wall. RBCs (~6-8 um) and leukocytes
  (~7-12 um) satisfy ap/h > 0.07 and are arrested at the inner wall by inertial lift forces (F_L).
  Bacteria (<1 um) and platelets (~2-3 um) are unaffected by F_L; they complete one full Dean
  Cycle (DC1), recirculating from inner to outer wall, and exit at the bacterial outlet.
  Separation is label-free, species-independent, and based solely on physical size.

Equipment:
  Syringe pumps : PHD 2000 (Harvard Apparatus) x2 (separate pumps for sample and sheath)
  Microscope    : Olympus IX71 inverted phase contrast + Hamamatsu CCD camera
  High-speed camera : Phantom v9 (Vision Research) for blood cell imaging
  Flow cytometer : BD Accuri C6 (BD Biosciences) for separation efficiency quantification
  Centrifuge    : 16,000 x g for bacterial eluate pelleting


BACTERIAL STRAINS AND CULTURE
------------------------------
- E. coli (clinical isolate)       : LB broth, mid-log phase
- Klebsiella pneumoniae            : LB broth, mid-log phase
- Pseudomonas aeruginosa           : LB broth, mid-log phase
- Staphylococcus aureus            : LB broth, mid-log phase
- Enterococcus faecalis            : Todd-Hewitt Broth (THB), mid-log phase

All organisms cultured to mid-log phase; diluted to target concentration based on OD measurements.
Concentration verified by plating serial dilutions for cfu counting. Bacteria spiked into whole
blood immediately before loading onto the DFF device.

Blood culture route (mRNA workflow only):
  BACTEC blood culture bottle inoculated at 1 cfu/mL of E. coli; incubated at 37 C for 7.5 hours
  to reach >10^5 cfu/mL (verified by plating). Cultured blood diluted 1:5 (v/v) with culture
  media before loading.


REAGENTS
--------
Sample buffer       : 1x PBS + 0.1% BSA (Miltenyi Biotec); prevents non-specific adsorption
Sheath fluid        : 1x PBS + 0.1% BSA
Lysis buffer        : RLT (Qiagen) + beta-mercaptoethanol (4x excess); 5 min RT incubation
Ciprofloxacin stock : 2.5 mcg/mL working concentration (fluoroquinolone; inhibits DNA gyrase)
Blood anticoagulant : EDTA (fresh human whole blood; Research Blood Components, Brighton MA)
Blood culture bottle: BACTEC (identical to clinical microbiology labs)
Immunofluorescence  : CD41a-FITC 1:50 (platelets); CD45-APC 1:100 (leukocytes); BD Biosciences
RBC lysis buffer    : eBioscience (for leukocyte imaging experiments only)
E. coli bioparticles: Alexa Fluor 488 E. coli K-12 BioParticles conjugates (Invitrogen);
                      used for device characterization and separation efficiency measurement


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Blood Sample Preparation
  Reagents    : WholeBlood, PBS_BSA_Buffer, EcoliClinicalIsolate
  Operation   : Dilute whole blood 1:3 (v/v) with PBS + 0.1% BSA to reach ~15% hematocrit.
                Spike bacteria at target concentration immediately before loading.
  rRNA workflow bacteria concentration  : ~100 cfu/mL (3 mL blood processed)
  mRNA workflow bacteria concentration  : ~10^5 cfu/mL (direct spike or blood culture route)
  Blood culture route                   : BACTEC bottle, 1 cfu/mL, 37 C, 7.5 h (450 min)
  Notes       : BSA at 0.1% prevents non-specific adsorption to tubing and PDMS walls.
                Bacteria spiked into diluted blood immediately before device loading.

Step 2 | Device Priming
  Reagents    : SheathFluid (PBS + 0.1% BSA)
  Operation   : Sheath fluid loaded into 60 mL syringe; pumped through inner inlet (425 um)
                at ~10x the sample flow rate to form tight sample stream at outer wall.
  Purpose     : Pins sample stream near outer wall; removes air bubbles; conditions channel walls.

Step 3 | Dean Flow Fractionation Separation
  Reagents    : Diluted spiked blood (outer inlet), SheathFluid (inner inlet)
  Operation   : mix (continuous-flow spiral microchannel separation; abstracted from DMF mixing)
  Total flow rate             : 1700 uL/min
  Sample flow rate            : ~150 uL/min
  Processing time             : ~20 min per mL whole blood (at 45% starting hematocrit)
  Channel height              : 80 um (governs inertial focusing threshold ap/h > 0.07)
  Dean Cycle                  : DC1 (bacteria complete full recirculation to outer wall)
  Bacterial recovery          : >65% across 10^2 to 10^4 cfu/mL
  Platelet recovery at outlet : ~40% (larger size slows Dean migration)
  Leukocyte removal           : Focused inertially at inner wall; exits waste outlet
  Notes       : Separation is label-free and species-independent. Bacteria are recovered
                in PBS+BSA sheath fluid, removing cellular inhibitors of downstream assays.

Step 4 | Bacterial Eluate Concentration
  Operation   : Centrifuge eluate at 16,000 x g; remove supernatant; resuspend pellet in
                50 uL 1x PBS. Modelled as heat at 25 C for 5 min in BioScript.
  Purpose     : Concentrates bacteria ~20-fold for sufficient input to RNA detection assay.

Step 5 | Bacterial Recovery QC
  Module      : bacterialRecoveryQC (abstracts cfu enumeration on LB agar)
  Duration    : 30 s detection
  Expected    : >65% recovery
  Branch      :
    Pass (recoverySignal > 0)  -> BB2: dispose bacterialEluate; proceed to lysis
    Fail (recoverySignal <= 0) -> BB3: drain bacterialEluate; abort

Step 6 | Bacterial Lysis for RNA Extraction
  BB          : BB4 (recovery join)
  Reagents    : bacterialPellet (resuspended in 50 uL PBS), RLT_Lysis_Buffer + BME
  Operation   : Vigorous vortex with 4x excess RLT+BME; 5 min at room temperature (25 C).
  Storage     : Use immediately or store at -80 C.
  Notes       : RLT denatures proteins and inactivates RNases. No RNA purification step;
                crude lysate used directly as NanoString input.

Step 7 | NanoString rRNA Hybridization for Species Identification
  BB          : BB4 (continued)
  Target RNA  : 16S and 23S ribosomal RNA (rRNA)
  Advantage   : rRNA present at >1000-fold excess over most abundant mRNA; enables detection
                of ~100 bacteria/mL without enzymatic amplification.
  Probeset    : 13 discriminatory probes total
                  3 probes specific to E. coli (Ec)
                  1 probe specific to K. pneumoniae (Kp)
                  5 probes specific to P. aeruginosa (PsA)
                  4 probes shared between Ec and Kp (not PsA)
                Probes designed to species-variable regions of 16S/23S by ClustalOmega MSA.
  Hybridization : 65 C for 2 h (shortened from standard protocol with minimal signal loss)
  Readout     : NanoString PrepStation + nCounter Digital Analyzer; nSolver software normalization
  Organism Score: Geometric mean of species-specific probe counts / sum of all geometric means
  Sensitivity : ~100 cfu/mL from 3 mL processed whole blood
  Module      : rRNASpeciesDetection
  Duration    : 30 s detection
  Note        : Unprocessed whole blood gives uninterpretable hybridization due to blood
                product interference. DFF pre-processing is required for valid rRNA signal.
  Branch      :
    Pass (rRNASignal > 0)  -> BB5: dispose bacterialLysate; proceed to mRNA workflow
    Fail (rRNASignal <= 0) -> BB6: drain bacterialLysate

Step 8 | Susceptibility Sample Preparation and Blood Culture Enrichment
  BB          : BB7 (rRNA join)
  Reagents    : EcoliClinicalIsolate_Susceptible, EcoliClinicalIsolate_Resistant,
                WholeBlood, PBS_BSA_Buffer
  Route A (direct spike): Spike at 10^5 cfu/mL into 1 mL whole blood; process immediately.
  Route B (blood culture): BACTEC bottle at 1 cfu/mL; incubate 37 C for 7.5 h (450 min,
                27000 s) to reach >10^5 cfu/mL; dilute 1:5 with culture media before DFF.
  Notes       : Both susceptible and resistant isolates processed identically. Classification
                resolved downstream by Transcriptional Susceptibility Score.
                mRNA detection requires ~10^5 cfu/mL; blood culture bridging step needed
                for typical bacteremia loads (~10-100 cfu/mL).

Step 9 | DFF Separation for Susceptibility Workflow
  Operation   : Same spiral device, same flow conditions (1700 uL/min, 20 min/mL).
  Inputs      : spikedBloodS, spikedBloodR, SheathFluid
  Post-separation: Concentrate eluate by centrifugation at 16,000 x g; resuspend in 50 uL PBS.
                   Modelled as heat at 25 C for 5 min.
  Notes       : Both susceptible and resistant arms processed in parallel.

Step 10 | Ciprofloxacin Exposure
  Reagents    : eluateS, eluateR, Ciprofloxacin_Stock
  Concentration: 2.5 mcg/mL ciprofloxacin
  Temperature : 37 C
  Duration    : 30 min (1800 s)
  Mechanism   : Susceptible organisms upregulate 6 stress-response mRNA transcripts in
                response to DNA gyrase inhibition. Resistant organisms do not show equivalent
                induction at this concentration.
  Notes       : 30 min sufficient for detectable transcriptional differential without
                significant bacterial growth. Susceptible and resistant isolates exposed
                identically; classification is by transcriptional outcome, not treatment.

Step 11 | Lysis and NanoString mRNA Hybridization for Susceptibility Determination
  BB          : BB7 (continued)
  Reagents    : ciproExposure_S, ciproExposure_R, RLT_Lysis_Buffer
  Lysis       : 4x RLT+BME, vortex, 5 min at 25 C (modelled as mix + heat at 25 C for 5 min)
  Target RNA  : mRNA (6 ciprofloxacin-responsive transcripts + 3 non-responsive controls)
  Normalization: Responsive transcripts normalized to geometric mean of control transcript
                 expression from same lysate and same hybridization assay. Controls for
                 cell number variation between samples.
  Transcriptional Susceptibility Score:
    Derivation set of clinical E. coli strains (susceptible and resistant) defines score
    anchors: 0 = centroid of susceptible strains; 1 = centroid of resistant strains.
    Unknown samples projected onto vector between centroids in transcriptional space.
    Threshold: dashed line = 4 SD from susceptible derivation cohort mean.
  Hybridization : 65 C for 2 h
  Sensitivity   : ~10^5 cfu/mL (mRNA less abundant than rRNA; >1 order of magnitude better
                  than VITEK-2 threshold of >10^6 cfu/mL)
  Module      : mRNASusceptibilityDetection
  Duration    : 30 s detection
  Branch      :
    Pass (susceptibilitySignal_S <= 0) -> BB8: dispose lysate_S and lysate_R
                                          Interpretation: susceptible organism
    Fail (susceptibilitySignal_S > 0)  -> BB9: drain lysate_S and lysate_R
                                          Interpretation: resistant organism

Step 12 | Final Cleanup
  BB          : BB10 (terminal)
  Operation   : dispose(susceptibilitySignal_S); dispose(susceptibilitySignal_R); NOP
  Experiment ends.


PERFORMANCE SUMMARY
-------------------
Total workflow time       : ~8 h (vs 48-72 h for standard culture-based methods)
Bacterial recovery        : >65% (vs ~30% by low-speed centrifugation)
rRNA sensitivity          : ~100 cfu/mL (from 3 mL blood; no amplification)
mRNA sensitivity          : ~10^5 cfu/mL (>1 order of magnitude better than VITEK-2)
Species identified        : E. coli, K. pneumoniae, P. aeruginosa (simultaneous or sequential)
Mixed infection detection : All 3 pairwise combinations of pathogens detected at 1000 cfu/mL
Susceptibility metric     : Transcriptional Susceptibility Score 0 (susceptible) to 1 (resistant)
Clinical threshold (VITEK-2): >10^6 cfu/mL; this method operates at >10^5 cfu/mL
Clinical threshold (BACTEC): ~10^8 cfu/mL for positive culture detection


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : hou_2015_dff_bacteremia.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
DAG            : hou_2015_dff_bacteremia_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations converted to seconds (s) or minutes (m) for compiler compatibility
                 (BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported)
                 20 min DFF separation    -> 20m  (IR: 1200.0 SECOND)
                 5 min lysis              -> 5m   (IR: 300.0 SECOND)
                 120 min hybridization    -> 120m (IR: 7200.0 SECOND)
                 30 min ciprofloxacin     -> 30m  (IR: 1800.0 SECOND)
                 450 min blood culture    -> 450m (IR: 27000.0 SECOND)
Modules        : bacterialRecoveryQC, rRNASpeciesDetection, mRNASusceptibilityDetection
Manifests      : WholeBlood, PBS_BSA_Buffer, SheathFluid, EcoliClinicalIsolate,
                 EcoliClinicalIsolate_Susceptible, EcoliClinicalIsolate_Resistant,
                 RLT_Lysis_Buffer, Ciprofloxacin_Stock
Abstraction notes:
  - `mix` steps abstract continuous-flow spiral DFF separation events, not DMF electrode mixing.
    This is consistent with the samlali reference file's treatment of hydrodynamic trapping events.
  - Blood dilution (1:3) encoded as two explicit dispense + chained mix steps to avoid split
    arrays and compiler errors (no array indexing used).
  - Susceptibility gate uses signal <= 0 for susceptible (score near 0) and > 0 for resistant
    (score near 1), mapping the paper's Transcriptional Susceptibility Score to BioScript's
    integer comparison semantics.
  - Both susceptible and resistant isolate arms encoded as scalar variables; processed in
    sequence within BB7 join block.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : A Microfluidics Approach Towards High-Throughput Pathogen Removal from Blood Using Margination
Source Link  : https://pubs.aip.org/aip/bmf/article/6/2/024115/923894
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4710992
Journal      : Biomicrofluidics, 2012, Vol. 6, Article 024115
Platform     : Pressure-driven continuous-flow PDMS microfluidic device; cascaded straight margination channels with bifurcation outlets


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a label-free, high-throughput microfluidic blood filtration technique for
non-specific removal of blood-borne pathogens and inflammatory cellular components from whole blood,
inspired by the in vivo microcirculatory phenomenon of leukocyte margination. The device exploits
the Fahreaus effect: as whole blood flows through narrow 20x20 um microchannels, deformable red
blood cells (RBCs) migrate axially to the channel centre under Poiseuille flow, forming an RBC-rich
core and a cell-free layer adjacent to the channel walls. Mechanical collisions between migrating
RBCs and other cellular components (bacteria, yeast, platelets, and leukocytes) drive their radial
displacement into the cell-free wall region -- a phenomenon termed margination.

At the downstream bifurcation (1:8:1 ratio), marginated cells are skimmed off via narrow side
channels (waste) while RBC-enriched, pathogen-depleted blood exits the large centre outlet. Two
margination channels are cascaded in series: the bacteria-depleted blood from stage 1 enters stage 2
with higher hematocrit, amplifying Fahreaus effect and RBC-bacteria hydrodynamic interactions, and
achieving overall bacterial removal efficiency greater than 80% in a single pass.

The technique requires no sample preparation, no magnetic labelling, and no sheath flow. Whole blood
can be drawn directly from patients and pumped into the device, making it suitable for a blood
dialysis circuit concept for adjunctive sepsis treatment.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Fabrication : PDMS (Sylgard 184, Dow Corning); standard soft lithography; silicon master patterned
              by deep reactive ion etching (DRIE); PDMS 10:1 prepolymer:curing agent, cured 70 C
              for 2 h; bonded to glass slides by air plasma (Harrick Plasma Cleaner); left 2 h at
              70 C to complete bonding; 1.5 mm holes punched for inlets and outlets.
Silanization: Trichloro(1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluorooctyl)silane 1 h (silicon wafer and PDMS master).

Single-channel device:
  - First margination channel : 20 um (W) x 20 um (H) x 5 mm (L); aspect ratio = 1
  - Second margination channel: 20 um (W) x 20 um (H) x 1 mm (L); aspect ratio = 1
  - Bifurcations in series    : 1:8:1 (side:centre:side outlet ratio)
  - Expanded bifurcation      : channel expands to 200 um width to enhance cell-free layer
  - Side outlet width         : 20 um (skims leukocytes 8-15 um; flow ratio 1:4 side:centre)
  - Throughput                : 1 mL/h per channel at 15 uL/min

Parallel 6-channel device:
  - 6 cascaded-design channels in parallel with additional upstream filter region
  - Filter region removes clogs and debris before margination channels
  - Throughput: 6 mL/h (100 uL/min total); performance equivalent to single-channel device

Flow driver  : Syringe pump (NE-1000, New Era Pump Systems Inc.)
Imaging      : Olympus IX71 inverted phase contrast microscope + Hamamatsu C4742-80-12AG CCD;
               IPLAB software (video acquisition); ImageJ (analysis)
Confocal     : LSM 510 meta laser scanning confocal (Carl Zeiss) on Axiovert 100 M Inverted;
               488 nm excitation; 10x objective + 2.5x digital zoom; 1 um z-interval; 512x512 px


SEPARATION PRINCIPLE
--------------------
Aspect ratio : Low aspect ratio (height/width <= 1; 20x20 um square channels) gives isotropic
               shear distribution across the channel cross-section, closely resembling circular
               blood vessels. RBC axial migration distances are equal in all directions, forming
               a well-defined RBC core and enabling efficient margination to all four sidewalls.
               High aspect ratio channels (>1) produce blunt z-direction velocity profiles and
               uneven margination, trapping bacteria at the mid-plane.

Flow rate    : Bacteria margination efficiency increases with flow rate and plateaus above
               10 uL/min. At high flow rates (Re ~4-5), RBCs experience higher shear and
               inertia, accelerating axial migration and RBC-bacteria interactions. Inertial
               focusing is negligible in whole blood at Re << 50.

Cascaded design: Removing plasma and marginated bacteria at stage 1 bifurcation increases
               hematocrit of blood entering stage 2 (~10% increase). Higher hematocrit enhances
               platelet and bacteria diffusivity at the RBC core periphery and increases frequency
               of RBC-bacteria collisions, driving further margination in stage 2.

Yeast vs bacteria: S. cerevisiae (~5 um ovoid; elastic modulus ~1e8 Pa) is larger and stiffer
               than E. coli (~2x0.5 um rod; ~1e7 Pa). Larger size drives stronger margination
               towards all four channel corners, yielding higher removal (~90%) than bacteria (~80%).
               Rod-shaped bacteria also undergo additional tumbling/rotational motion that enhances
               lateral drift across streamlines.


CELL LINES AND PATHOGENS
-------------------------
E. coli      : Strain HB101 K-12; GFP-expressing (arabinose-inducible); cultured overnight at
               37 C in LB Agar + ampicillin 100 ug/mL + arabinose 0.1%; harvested and
               resuspended in 1x PBS before use. Spiked at 1e6-1e7 CFU/mL.
               For device characterisation: Alexa Fluor 488 E. coli K-12 BioParticles
               conjugates (Invitrogen) used for FACS analysis.

S. cerevisiae: Haploid W303-1B strain; YFP-expressing; gift from Dr. Jacquin Niles, MIT
               Department of Biological Engineering. Spiked at 1e6-1e7 per mL.
               Morphology (~5-7 um ovoid) representative of pathogenic Candida albicans.

Human blood  : Whole blood (Research Blood Components, Brighton MA).
               Device characterisation: washed 3x with PBS + 0.5% BSA; resuspended at 45%
               hematocrit in PBS + 0.5% BSA + 3% w/v Dextran-40.
               Whole-blood pathogen removal experiments: fresh unwashed blood used directly.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | RBC Sample Preparation (Device Characterisation)
  Reagents    : Whole blood, PBS + 0.5% v/v BSA (wash buffer),
                PBS + 0.5% v/v BSA + 3% w/v Dextran-40 (sample buffer)
  Operation   : Wash RBCs 3x with wash buffer (centrifuge 300 x g, 5 min each wash).
                Resuspend at 45% hematocrit in sample buffer.
  BioScript   : Centrifugation abstracted as heat at 25c (no centrifuge primitive).
                Each wash cycle: mix 5m + heat at 25c for 5m.
  Notes       : Dextran-40 prevents RBC sedimentation during syringe pump operation.
                For pathogen removal experiments using fresh whole blood, this step is skipped.

Step 2 | Antibody Staining for Cellular Analysis
  Reagents    : Fresh whole blood (unwashed), CD41a-FITC (1:50, BD Biosciences),
                CD45-APC (1:100, BD Biosciences)
  Operation   : Incubate blood with antibodies at 4 C for 40 min without prior washing.
  Purpose     : CD41a-FITC labels platelets; CD45-APC labels leukocytes.
                Staining in fresh blood preserves native cell populations for FACS analysis.

Step 3 | Microbial Spiking
  Reagents    : GFP-E. coli (resuspended in 1x PBS), YFP-S. cerevisiae
  Operation   : Add each microbe to antibody-stained blood at 1e6-1e7 per mL; vortex 30 s.
  Notes       : Both microbe types spiked simultaneously for combined whole-blood analysis.
                Separate experiments performed for E. coli vs S. cerevisiae to quantify
                removal efficiency by CFU counting and haemocytometer independently.

Step 4 | Stage 1 Margination (First Channel, 5 mm)
  Input       : Spiked whole blood loaded at inlet via syringe pump
  Flow rate   : 15 uL/min (Re ~4-5; wall shear rate ~6e4 s-1)
  Operation   : Continuous laminar flow through 20x20 um channel (5 mm). RBCs migrate
                axially to form RBC-rich core; bacteria, yeast, platelets, and leukocytes
                marginate to cell-free wall region via RBC mechanical collisions.
  Bifurcation : 1:8:1; channel expands to 200 um at bifurcation to enhance cell-free layer.
                Marginated cells collected in narrow side channels (20 um; drain/waste).
                RBC-enriched, pathogen-depleted blood exits large centre outlet (ratio 8).
  Stage 1 result: ~50% bacterial removal; hematocrit increases ~10% in centre outlet.
  BioScript   : mix abstracts laminar co-flow through margination channel;
                rbcSuspension supplies RBC hydrodynamic environment.

Step 5 | Stage 2 Margination (Cascaded Channel, 1 mm)
  Input       : Stage-1 filtered blood (higher hematocrit, reduced bacteria)
  Flow rate   : 15 uL/min (continuous from stage 1)
  Operation   : Bacteria-depleted blood undergoes second round of margination. Higher
                post-stage-1 hematocrit amplifies Fahreaus effect and RBC-bacteria
                collision frequency; additional bacteria driven to channel periphery.
  Bifurcation : 1:8:1; second waste stream drained; final filtered blood collected.
  Stage 2 result: cumulative >80% bacterial removal, >80% platelet and leukocyte depletion,
                ~90% S. cerevisiae removal, ~30% increase in RBC concentration at centre outlet.
  Haemolysis  : Negligible (optical absorption 414 nm); RBC transit time < 0.01 s in
                high-shear margination zone.

Step 6 | FACS Analysis of Filtered Blood
  Instrument  : BD LSR II flow cytometer (BD Biosciences)
  Gating      : FSC/SSC + fluorescence: CD41a-FITC (platelets), CD45-APC (leukocytes),
                GFP (E. coli), YFP (S. cerevisiae)
  Normalisation: Concentration at centre outlet / inlet sample concentration (%)
  QC gate     : cellularComponentDetection module; 30 s detect
                Pass (separationSignal > 0): >80% removal confirmed; dispose filtered blood
                Fail (separationSignal <= 0): insufficient removal; drain; re-optimise

Step 7 | Bacterial CFU Quantification
  Operation   : Plate 10 uL aliquots from inlet and centre outlet on LB agar.
                Incubate 24 h at 37 C. Count colony-forming units (CFUs).
  Removal efficiency = 1 - (CFU_outlet / CFU_inlet)
  Yeast count : Haemocytometer (independent of FACS/CFU pipeline).
  BioScript   : 24 h incubation = 1440 min (compiler duration constraint; IR: 86400.0 SECOND)
  QC gate     : bacterialColonyCount module; 30 s detect
                Pass (bacteriaSignal > 0): >80% bacterial removal confirmed; dispose
                Fail (bacteriaSignal <= 0): insufficient removal; drain; flag for re-run

Step 8 | Parallel Device Validation (6-Channel Scale-Up)
  Device      : 6 cascaded-design channels in parallel + upstream filter region
  Flow rate   : 100 uL/min total (6 ml/h)
  Result      : Similar platelet, leukocyte, and bacteria filtration performance to single channel
  Note        : Further parallelisation (100+ channels) or device stacking could approach
                conventional dialysis throughput (~1-2 L/h)


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : hou_margination_pathogen_removal_blood.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG            : hou_margination_pathogen_removal_blood_main_dag.dot

Duration conversions (s/m only; h not supported):
  40 min antibody staining -> 40m  (IR: 2400.0 SECOND)
  24 h agar incubation     -> 1440m (IR: 86400.0 SECOND)
  5 min wash cycles        -> 5m   (IR: 300.0 SECOND)

Platform note  : This is a pressure-driven continuous-flow device, not a DMF platform.
                 `mix` operations abstract laminar co-flow through the margination channel
                 (NOT electrode-driven droplet merging). `rbcSuspension` models the RBC
                 hydrodynamic environment required for margination physics.
                 `drain` and `dispose` both normalise to dispose() in IR output (expected
                 compiler behaviour); physical distinction is preserved in .bs source comments.
                 `heat at 25c` abstracts centrifugation and room-temperature operations.
                 `heat at 4c` abstracts cold/on-ice incubation steps.
                 `heat at 37c` abstracts bacterial culture incubation.

Modules        : bacterialMargination, yeastMargination,
                 cellularComponentDetection, bacterialColonyCount

IR audit note  : BB2 (bsbbif_2_t) true-branch jump to BB4 is implicit in IR (no explicit
                 jump opcode); BB3 (bsbbif_3_f) carries explicit jump -- standard compiler
                 behaviour, does not affect CFG correctness. BB5 and BB6 both dispose
                 platesMix (pass and fail paths identical for physical waste handling;
                 bacteriaSignal differentiates device validation status only).

protocol.title: A Microfluidics Approach Towards High-Throughput Pathogen Removal from Blood Using Margination
protocol.platform: Pressure-driven continuous-flow PDMS microfluidic device (straight margination channels, cascaded bifurcation design)
protocol.objective: Label-free, non-specific removal of blood-borne pathogens (bacteria and fungi) and inflammatory cellular components (platelets and leukocytes) from whole blood via RBC-driven margination in narrow microchannels, for sepsis treatment application

device.fabrication: Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS, Sylgard 184, Dow Corning); standard soft lithography; silicon wafer patterned by deep reactive ion etching (DRIE); PDMS cured 10:1 w/w prepolymer:curing agent at 70 C for 2 h; bonded to glass slides by air plasma (Harrick Plasma Cleaner); 1.5 mm inlet/outlet holes punched
device.silanization: Trichloro(1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluorooctyl)silane (Sigma Aldrich); 1 h for both silicon wafer and PDMS master template
device.channel_design: Two cascaded straight margination channels with two bifurcations (1:8:1) in series

parallel_device.filter_purpose: Remove clogs and debris upstream of margination channels

device.flow_driver: Syringe pump (NE-1000, New Era Pump Systems Inc.)
device.imaging: Inverted phase contrast microscope (Olympus IX71) + Hamamatsu C4742-80-12AG CCD camera; IPLAB software for video acquisition; ImageJ for analysis
device.confocal: LSM 510 meta laser scanning confocal (Carl Zeiss) on Axiovert 100 M; 488 nm excitation; 10x objective + 2.5x digital zoom; 1 um z-slices; 512x512 px

separation_principle.mechanism: Leukocyte margination (in vivo microcirculatory phenomenon adapted to microchannels)
separation_principle.rbc_behaviour: Deformable RBCs migrate axially to channel centre (Fahreaus effect) under Poiseuille flow profile, forming an RBC-rich core and a peripheral cell-free layer adjacent to channel walls
driving_forces: Hydrodynamic RBC-bacteria interactions at high shear
separation_principle.rbc_aggregation: Minimal at high working shear rate; margination proceeds via Fahreaus effect and hydrodynamic interactions rather than rouleaux formation
separation_principle.cascaded_benefit: Stage-2 filtered blood has higher hematocrit (+~10% post-stage-1), enhancing RBC axial migration and RBC-bacteria hydrodynamic interactions for additional margination in the second channel

reagents.whole_blood: Human whole blood (Research Blood Components, Brighton MA); used fresh for whole-blood analysis; washed for device characterisation
reagents.sample_buffer_characterisation: 1x PBS + 0.5% v/v BSA + 3% w/v Dextran-40 (Sigma Aldrich); Dextran-40 prevents cell sedimentation

ecoli.label: GFP (arabinose-inducible)
ecoli.culture: Overnight 37 C in LB Agar + ampicillin 100 ug/mL + arabinose 0.1%

ecoli_bioparticles.product: Alexa Fluor 488 E. coli K-12 BioParticles conjugates (Invitrogen)

saccharomyces.label: YFP
saccharomyces.source: Gift from Dr. Jacquin Niles, MIT Department of Biological Engineering

platelet_marker.incubation: 40 min at 4 C directly in fresh whole blood

leukocyte_marker.incubation: 40 min at 4 C directly in fresh whole blood

reagents.agar_plates: LB agar; 10 uL aliquots plated; CFU counted after 24 h at 37 C

operating_conditions.flow_rate_rationale: PDMS device and tubing connections not rigid enough to withstand pressure drop at higher flow rates for extended operation; bacteria margination efficiency plateaus above 10 uL/min

flow_rate_optimisation.bacteria_margination_onset: Negligible at 1 uL/min; improved with increasing flow rate; constant beyond 10 uL/min

aspect_ratio_optimisation.rationale: Aspect ratio 1 (20x20 um) gives isotropic shear distribution resembling circular blood vessels; efficient RBC core formation across full cross-section; highest throughput at aspect ratio <= 1

channel_length_optimisation.observation: Margination constant across all tested lengths; 5 mm selected to minimise pressure drop and allow higher working flow rate

steps.name: RBC sample preparation (device characterisation)
steps.operation: Wash 3x with PBS + 0.5% BSA; resuspend at 45% hematocrit in PBS + 0.5% BSA + 3% Dextran-40
steps.centrifugation: Abstracted as heat at 25c (no centrifuge primitive in BioScript)
steps.notes: Washing removes plasma proteins and platelets; Dextran-40 prevents RBC sedimentation during syringe pump-driven flow. For whole-blood pathogen removal experiments, unwashed fresh blood is used directly.

steps.name: Antibody staining for cellular component analysis
steps.operation: Incubate fresh whole blood with fluorophore-conjugated antibodies at 4 C for 40 min
steps.notes: No prior washing; staining performed directly in fresh blood to preserve native cell populations. Blood placed at 4 C without washing before antibody addition.

steps.name: Microbial spiking into whole blood
steps.operation: Vortex microbes into antibody-stained blood for 30 s
steps.notes: E. coli (~2 x 0.5 um rod; rigid peptidoglycan wall E' ~1e7 Pa) marginate via size difference and stiffness contrast with RBCs (E' ~1e4 Pa); rod shape confers additional tumbling/rotational motion enhancing lateral drift. S. cerevisiae (~5 um ovoid; E' ~1e8 Pa) undergo complete corner margination to all four channel walls, yielding higher removal efficiency than bacteria.

steps.name: Stage 1 margination
steps.operation: Continuous laminar flow; RBCs migrate axially to form RBC-rich core; bacteria, yeast, platelets, and leukocytes marginate radially to cell-free wall region
steps.bifurcation: 1:8:1; marginated cells collected in narrow side channels (waste); RBC-enriched blood exits large centre outlet
steps.notes: Cell-free layer enhanced at the expanded bifurcation (20 um -> 200 um width). Most marginated bacteria reside in cell-free region next to channel wall, efficiently removed by side channels. Centre outlet (ratio 8) collects densely-packed RBCs with minimal loss.

steps.name: Stage 2 margination (cascaded design)
steps.operation: Bacteria-depleted blood from stage 1 undergoes additional margination; higher hematocrit post-stage-1 amplifies Fahreaus effect and RBC-bacteria hydrodynamic interactions
steps.bifurcation: 1:8:1; second waste stream drained; final filtered blood collected from centre outlet
steps.haemolysis: Negligible; optical absorption at 414 nm; RBC transit time < 0.01 s in high-shear margination zone

steps.name: FACS analysis of filtered blood
steps.instrument: BD LSR II flow cytometer (BD Biosciences)
steps.normalisation: Bacteria/cell concentration at centre outlet / inlet sample concentration

results.rbc_recovery_increase_pct: ~30 (Fahreaus effect; 1:8:1 bifurcation packs RBCs into centre outlet)

steps.name: Bacterial CFU quantification
steps.operation: Plate 10 uL aliquots from inlet and filtered centre outlet on LB agar; count colonies after 24 h at 37 C

theoretical_separation_efficiency.basis: Ratio of wetted perimeter of centre region to total cross-section perimeter at bifurcation
theoretical_separation_efficiency.agreement: Experimental results in good agreement with theoretical values at each stage

basic_blocks.contents: dispose(bacteriaSignal); NOP

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Combinatorial Synthesis of Peptidomimetics Using Digital Microfluidics
Source Link  : https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1556/JFC-D-12-00012.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1556/JFC-D-12-00012
Journal      : J. Flow Chem., 2012, Vol. 2, No. 3, pp. 103-107
Authors      : Mais J. Jebrail, Naila Assem, Jared M. Mudrik, Michael D.M. Dryden,
               Kaixiang Lin, Andrei K. Yudin, Aaron R. Wheeler
Affiliation  : Department of Chemistry, University of Toronto,
               Toronto ON M5S-3H6, Canada
Platform     : Digital microfluidics (DMF) -- two-plate electrowetting-on-dielectric
               (EWOD) device with chromium bottom electrodes and ITO top plate


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes the first reported use of digital microfluidics (DMF) for
combinatorial chemical synthesis. The method performs thioacid-aziridine ligation of
peptidomimetics and their subsequent desulfurization entirely on-chip, with an integrated
magnetic separation step to remove Raney Nickel (RaNi) catalyst from reaction products.
The approach represents a greater than 1000-fold reduction in reagent consumption compared
to macroscale bench synthesis (microlitres vs millilitres) and requires no stir bars,
rotary evaporators, or traditional gloveboxes.

The protocol is divided into two functional parts:
  PART 1 (Steps 1-4, 16 total steps): Combinatorial thioacid-aziridine ligation
    producing 4 peptidomimetic products (A1-B1, A1-B2, A2-B1, A2-B2) under N2
    atmosphere at room temperature for 1 hour in methanol.
  PART 2 (Steps 5-8, 16 total steps): On-chip desulfurization using Raney Nickel
    catalyst at room temperature for 15 minutes, followed by magnetic immobilisation
    of RaNi and solvent evaporation to isolate 4 desulfurized analogues.

Total processing steps: 32 steps producing 8 products on a single DMF device.
Characterisation: ESI-MS (all 8 products, triplicate) and 1H NMR (desulfurized A1-B1,
compared to macroscale synthesis; spectra nearly identical).


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Configuration : Two-plate DMF device
Bottom plate  : Patterned chromium electrodes on glass
                - 88 square actuation electrodes (2.2 x 2.2 mm,
                  140 um peak-to-peak sinusoid interdigitated borders)
                - 10 reservoir electrodes (5 x 5 mm each)
Top plate     : Contiguous indium tin oxide (ITO) electrode
Spacer        : Two layers of double-sided tape, total thickness 180 um
Coating       : Hydrophobic insulator on both plates

Droplet volumes:
  Unit droplet   : ~900 nL
  Reservoir      : ~4.5 uL

Actuation:
  Voltage        : 70-100 V_rms
  Frequency      : 18 kHz (sine wave)
  Generator      : Agilent function generator + amplifier
  Mechanism      : Driving potential applied between top ITO electrode and
                   sequential bottom electrodes; droplets pinched off from
                   reservoirs and actuated across electrode array

Inter-electrode gaps : 40 um
Reagent capacity     : 6 reagents per device


REAGENTS
--------
Starting materials (all at 0.1 M in HPLC-grade MeOH):
  A1 : Boc-Ala-SH  -- Boc-protected Ala thioacid peptide
  A2 : Boc-Val-SH  -- Boc-protected Val thioacid peptide
  B1 : Az-Ala-An   -- NH aziridine-terminated Ala-Anilide amino acid
  B2 : Az-Pro-An   -- NH aziridine-terminated Pro-Anilide amino acid
       (B1 and B2 synthesised from commercially available amphoteric
        aziridine aldehydes; ref Hili & Yudin, JACS 2006)

Catalyst:
  RaNi : Raney Nickel (~5 mg in MeOH per 4.5-uL reservoir droplet)
         Ni-Al alloy grains; ferromagnetic (enables magnetic recovery)

Solvent:
  MeOH : HPLC-grade methanol (reaction solvent and re-dissolution solvent)
         MeOH-d4 (Cambridge Isotope Laboratories) used for NMR analysis

Other:
  Formic acid : 0.1% in MeOH (MS sample preparation)


PRODUCTS
--------
Peptidomimetics (thioacid-aziridine ligation products):
  A1-B1 : Boc-Ala-Cys-rAla-Anilide   m/z 425
  A1-B2 : Boc-Ala-Cys-rPro-Anilide   m/z 451
  A2-B1 : Boc-Val-Cys-rAla-Anilide   m/z 452
  A2-B2 : Boc-Val-Cys-rPro-Anilide   m/z 479

Desulfurized analogues (RaNi-catalysed desulfurization products):
  desulf A1-B1 : m/z 393
  desulf A1-B2 : m/z 419
  desulf A2-B1 : m/z 421
  desulf A2-B2 : m/z 447


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

PART 1 -- COMBINATORIAL LIGATION

Step 1 | Dispense Starting Material Droplets
  Reagents  : Boc_Ala_SH, Boc_Val_SH, Az_Ala_An, Az_Pro_An (all 0.1 M in MeOH)
  Operation : Dispense 2 unit droplets (~900 nL each) per reagent = 8 droplets total
  Actuation : 70-100 V_rms, 18 kHz; reservoir electrode activated to pinch off
              unit droplet onto actuation electrode array
  Notes     : Each device reservoir holds ~4.5 uL; ancillary reservoirs connected
              to main via electrode actuation sequence

Step 2 | Merge Reagent Pairs (Combinatorial Pairing)
  Operation : Mix each A droplet with the corresponding B droplet (4 pairs)
              A1 + B1 -> a1b1_merge
              A1 + B2 -> a1b2_merge
              A2 + B1 -> a2b1_merge
              A2 + B2 -> a2b2_merge
  Duration  : 5 s per merge
  Actuation : 70-100 V_rms, 18 kHz; sequential electrode actuation drives droplets
              to shared electrode where coalescence occurs

Step 3 | Circular Mixing and N2 Atmosphere Ligation Incubation
  Operation : Circular mixing (60 s) then N2 incubation (1 h, RT)
  Mixing    : Droplets actuated in circular motion on 4 electrodes for 60 s
  Incubation: 1 h at room temperature (25 C) under N2 atmosphere
  Atmosphere: Miniaturised Petri-dish glovebox (150 mm o.d. x 15 mm h polystyrene
              Petri dish); purged with N2 at ~50 mL/min for 2 min; sealed with
              parafilm; inlet and outlet tubes fitted in lid (UV-cured epoxy)
  Chemistry : Thioacid-aziridine ligation; installs peptide bond isostere with
              thiol sidechain between peptide fragments
  Products  : A1-B1 (m/z 425), A1-B2 (m/z 451), A2-B1 (m/z 452), A2-B2 (m/z 479)
  BioScript : heat at 25c for 60m (RT incubation; no glovebox primitive)

Step 4 | Solvent Evaporation -- Ligation Product Isolation
  Operation : Remove top plate; allow MeOH to evaporate at RT for 15 min
  Duration  : 15 min at RT (25 C)
  Result    : Dried peptidomimetic solids remain on bottom plate electrode surface
  BioScript : heat at 25c for 15m (no evaporation primitive)

--- LIGATION QC GATE ---
  Detection : ESI-MS on A1-B1 (sentinel product; expected m/z 425)
  Module    : msDetection; 30 s detection
  MS params : Agilent 1200 series quadrupole; positive ion mode; 50 V; 100 C
              capillary; 0.5 mL/min; 2.3 mM in MeOH + 0.1% formic acid;
              average of 67 acquisitions; verified in triplicate
  Pass (BB2): ligationSignal > 0 -> dispose all 4 ligation products; proceed to PART 2
  Fail (BB3): ligationSignal <= 0 -> drain all 4 ligation products

PART 2 -- DESULFURIZATION

Step 5 | Re-dissolve Peptidomimetic Products in MeOH
  Operation : Dispense 900-nL MeOH droplet; drive to each dried product spot
  Duration  : 5 s mixing per product
  Procedure : Top plate replaced; MeOH droplet dispensed from reservoir and driven
              by electrode actuation to re-solubilise each dried peptidomimetic solid
  Notes     : 900-nL droplets sufficient; volumes up to hundreds of uL possible
              depending on compound solubility (ref Au et al., Biomed. Microdevices 2011)

Step 6 | Dispense and Merge RaNi Catalyst with Product Droplets
  Catalyst  : RaneyNickel (~5 mg Ni-Al alloy in MeOH, 4.5-uL reservoir droplet)
  Operation : Dispense 1 RaNi droplet per product; merge with each dissolved product
  Duration  : 5 s per merge
  Pairs     : a1b1_dissolved + rani_a1b1 -> desulf_a1b1_raw
              a1b2_dissolved + rani_a1b2 -> desulf_a1b2_raw
              a2b1_dissolved + rani_a2b1 -> desulf_a2b1_raw
              a2b2_dissolved + rani_a2b2 -> desulf_a2b2_raw
  Chemistry : Raney Nickel catalyses desulfurization: removes -SH from cysteine-
              like sulfa backbone; yields reduced amide bond (confirmed by NMR
              peaks at 4.05 and 4.29 ppm for reduced amide CH protons)

Step 7 | Circular Mixing and RT Desulfurization Incubation
  Operation : Circular mixing (60 s) then RT incubation (15 min)
  Mixing    : Droplets actuated in circular motion on electrodes for 60 s
  Incubation: 15 min at room temperature (25 C)
  BioScript : heat at 25c for 15m
  Products  : desulf A1-B1 (m/z 393), desulf A1-B2 (m/z 419),
              desulf A2-B1 (m/z 421), desulf A2-B2 (m/z 447)

Step 8 | Magnetic RaNi Immobilisation and Product Isolation
  Magnet    : Neodymium Iron Boron (NdFeB) magnet (Main Electronics, BC)
  Procedure :
    1. NdFeB magnet placed beneath device; RaNi grains (ferromagnetic) immobilised
       to device bottom plate surface by magnetic force
    2. Supernatant (desulfurized product in MeOH, now RaNi-free) driven away from
       immobilised RaNi by electrode actuation
    3. Top plate removed; MeOH allowed to evaporate at RT for 30 min
    4. Desulfurized product remains as dried solid; collected by pipette after
       dissolving in appropriate solvent for off-chip analysis
  Duration  : 30 min evaporation at RT (25 C)
  BioScript : drain (magnetic separation) + heat at 25c for 30m (evaporation)
              NOTE: lilott8/BioScript maps drain to dispose() in IR; magnetic-
              separation semantic is preserved in source comments only
  NMR check : Desulf A1-B1; 1H NMR (CD3OD, 400 MHz):
              delta 4.05 and 4.29 ppm (reduced amide bond CH protons)
              delta 1.44 ppm (Boc protecting group)
              delta 7.60-7.17 ppm (phenyl group)
              Nearly identical to macroscale bench synthesis spectrum

--- DESULFURIZATION QC GATE ---
  Detection : ESI-MS and NMR on desulf-A1-B1 (sentinel product; expected m/z 393)
  Module    : nmrDetection; 30 s detection
  Pass (BB5): desulfSignal > 0 -> dispose all 4 desulfurized product droplets
  Fail (BB6): desulfSignal <= 0 -> drain all 4 desulfurized product droplets

--- TERMINAL (BB7) ---
  dispose desulfSignal; NOP
  Experiment ends. 8 products synthesised in 32 steps on a single DMF device.


CHARACTERISATION
----------------

Mass Spectrometry (ESI-MS):
  Instrument        : Agilent 1200 series quadrupole MS (Santa Clara, CA)
  Ionisation        : Electrospray (ESI), positive ion mode
  Applied voltage   : 50 V
  Capillary temp    : 100 C
  Flow rate         : 0.5 mL/min
  Sample prep       : ~2.3 mM in MeOH + 0.1% formic acid, 70 uL aliquot
  Acquisitions      : Average of 67 per spectrum
  Replicates        : Triplicate for all 8 products

1H Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR):
  Instrument (DMF)  : Varian UnityPlus 500 MHz NMR spectrometer
  Instrument (macro) : Varian Mercury 400 MHz NMR spectrometer
  Solvent           : MeOH-d4 (Cambridge Isotope Laboratories, Andover MA)
  Reference         : MeOH-d4 at 3.31 ppm
  Sample tube (DMF) : Capillary tube (100 um i.d.), sealed with hand-held butane
                      torch, positioned in 3-mm Norell S400 NMR tube
  Concentration     : ~1.2 mM in 80-uL MeOH-d4
  Pulse width       : 90 degrees (7.3 us)
  Spectral width    : 16 ppm
  Recycle delay     : 1 s
  Steady states     : 1
  Scans             : 512
  Temperature       : 25 C
  Replicates        : Triplicate

Full 1H NMR data for desulf A1-B1 (CD3OD, 400 MHz):
