description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : A Solvent Replenishment Solution for Managing Evaporation of Biochemical Reactions in Air-Matrix Digital Microfluidics Devices
Source Link  : https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/1225865
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1039/c4lc00703d
Journal      : Lab on a Chip, 2015 (Sandia National Laboratories, SAND2015-0066J)
Platform     : Air-matrix digital microfluidics (DMF) on six-layer printed circuit board (PCB) with EWOD electrode array


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a just-in-time solvent replenishment strategy for managing droplet evaporation
in an air-matrix digital microfluidics (DMF) device, enabling reliable execution of biochemical
reactions requiring high temperatures (up to 95 C) and extended incubation times (up to 1 h or more)
without the use of an oil matrix, humidified chamber, or off-chip heating modules.

The core innovation is periodic merging of pre-heated solvent droplets (nuclease-free water, 0.5 uL
each) with the reaction droplet to restore volume lost to evaporation. Replenishing droplets are
delivered via a PEEK tube through a drilled through-hole (0.8 mm ID) in the PCB bottom plate,
controlled by a stepper-motor-driven syringe pump. Each replenishing droplet is transported to the
edge of the thermal zone and pre-heated for 5 s before merging, minimising the temperature perturbation
to the reaction droplet (<=1 C change on merging). Volume is replenished when the reaction droplet
loses 15-20% of its target volume (monitored visually in the current device; future devices could use
automated concentration or volume sensing with feedback control).

Three representative biochemical reactions from a gene expression analysis workflow are demonstrated:

  1. RNA Fragmentation
     Human PBMC total RNA fragmented at 94 C for 3 min on the DMF device. Six 0.5 uL replenishing
     water droplets added during incubation. Reaction terminated at 4 C with NEBNext stop solution.
     DMF product size distribution (40-1000 nt, peak ~150 nt) indistinguishable from conventional
     benchscale fragmentation.

  2. First-Strand cDNA Synthesis (Peregrine Method)
     Fragmented PBMC RNA converted to first-strand cDNA via the Peregrine template-switching approach
     using SMARTScribe RT. Protocol involves sequential incubation steps at 65 C (2 min denaturation),
     4 C (snap-cool), 25 C (3 min primer annealing), 42 C (1 min RT activation), 42 C (60 min
     extension with primer PP_TS), and 70 C (5 min termination). Thirteen 0.5 uL replenishing water
     droplets added in total (9 during the 42 C 60-min incubation; 4 during 70 C termination).
     qPCR Ct values and ds-cDNA yields comparable to conventional benchscale (p=0.14, N=3).

  3. PCR (M13mp18 template, 200 bp amplicon)
     PCR amplification of a 200 bp region (positions 4905-5104) of bacteriophage M13mp18 ssDNA
     using Hot Start Taq (doubled concentration) and thermal cycling between three zones:
     95 C 45 s initial denaturation; 33 cycles of (95 C 20 s, 50 C 30 s, 68 C 45 s); 68 C 5 min
     final extension. One 0.5 uL water replenishment added per cycle (33 total) after the 95 C
     denaturation step (~45 min total experiment time). Correct 200 bp product confirmed by gel
     electrophoresis; slightly reduced yield vs conventional PCR.

The protocol is encoded as a single BioScript file with three sequential protocol arms each terminated
by a QC detection gate, yielding a 10-block CFG.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Substrate     : Six-layer PCB; copper electrodes (43 um) plated with nickel (185 um) and gold (3.6 um);
                fabricated by World International PCB (Orange, CA) via photolithography and etching.
Dielectric    : Soldermask, ~15 um thick.
Hydrophobic   : 50 nm Teflon-AF (1% wt/wt in Fluorinert FC-40; 1500 rpm 30 s; baked 100 C 5 h);
                applied to both top and bottom plates.
Top plate     : Glass substrate coated with unpatterned ITO (Delta Technologies) + 50 nm Teflon-AF.
Bottom plate  : 100 actuation electrodes (1.6 x 1.6 mm each); 6 reservoir electrodes (3.5 x 5.5 mm);
                1 waste reservoir (5.2 x 5.5 mm); 80 um inter-electrode gaps.
Gap spacing   : 185 um (RNA fragmentation and cDNA synthesis); 800 um (PCR).

Thermal zones:
  - 4 independently controlled TEC thermal zones; each spanning 6 actuation electrodes.
  - Isolated by 1.0 x 7.0 mm voids machined into PCB substrate.
  - TEC: Laird Technologies OT08-08-F0-0303; RTD: US Sensor PPG102A1.
  - Attached with thermally conductive epoxy to gold-plated pads on PCB back side.
  - Thermally coupled to front-side zone electrodes via drilled through-holes filled with
    conductive epoxy.
  - Temperature offset between RTD (back side) and droplet: 3.0 C (+/- 0.5 C); incorporated
    into zone temperature programming as a compensation factor.
  - Controller: custom PICAXE 14M2 board; PWM + polarity control for heating and cooling.
  - Rapid temperature transitions achieved by shuttling reaction droplet between zones.

Through-hole interface:
  - 0.8 mm ID through-hole drilled in PCB bottom plate.
  - 360/150 OD/ID PEEK tube (IDEX) inserted from back side; immobilised with custom fittings.
  - Driven by stepper motor with computer-controlled electronic interface (Allmotion) via ASCII commands.
  - Delivers replenishing solvent droplets from external syringe pump reservoir onto device surface.

Actuation     : 80-100 Vrms, 18 kHz; function generator (Trek) + amplifier (Digi-Key).
Imaging       : Olympus MVX10 microscope; QIClick digital camera (Qimaging); 35x26 mm2 FOV;
                Streampix5 software (Norpix).
Thermal imaging: ThermoProTM TP8 IR camera (Guide Infrared); 10 s equilibration before capture.


REAGENTS
--------

Shared:
  NucleaseFreeWater  : Nuclease-free distilled water (molecular biology grade); replenishing solvent
                       in all three protocols. Dispensed from external syringe pump via through-hole.
  PluronicF127       : 0.1% w/v in cDNA master mix (Sigma Chemical).

RNA Fragmentation:
  RNA_PBMC           : Human PBMC total RNA, 380 ng/uL; extracted with RNAzol + Direct-zol kit
                       (Zymo Research); quantified on Qubit 2.0; stored at -80 C.
                       Source: 5-10e6 cells centrifuged 1000 rpm 4 C 5 min; 1 mL RNAzol +
                       400 uL water; 15 min RT; 16000 rpm 4 C 15 min; aqueous phase 1:1 EtOH;
                       Direct-zol purification; eluted 10 uL nuclease-free water.
  FragmentationBuffer: 10X NEBNext RNA fragmentation buffer (New England Biolabs).
  StopSolution       : NEBNext stop solution (New England Biolabs).

cDNA Synthesis (Peregrine Method):
  RNA_PBMC           : Pre-fragmented human PBMC total RNA, 100 ng per 0.5 uL reaction droplet.
  PrimerPP_RT        : Primer PP_RT, 25 mM.
  MasterMixCDNA      : 45% SMARTScribe 5X First-Strand Buffer (Clontech) + 5.5% 20 mM DTT +
                       22% 10 mM dNTP mix + 5.5% RiboGuard RNase inhibitor (Epicentre) +
                       22% SMARTScribe Reverse Transcriptase (Clontech) + 0.1% w/v Pluronic F-127.
  PrimerPP_TS        : Primer PP_TS, 12 mM.
  Purification       : AMPure XP beads (Beckman Coulter Genomics), 1.8X volumes, eluted 10-20 uL.
  qPCR primers       : PP_P1 (5'-CAGGACGCTGTTCCGTTCTATGGG-3') and PP_P2 (5'-CAGACGTGTGCTCTTCCGATCT-3').

PCR:
  PCRMasterMix       : Hot Start Taq 2X Master Mix (NEB) + 0.025 U/uL additional Hot Start Taq (NEB)
                       to double Taq concentration.
  PCRPrimers         : Forward TGTTAATACTGACCGCCTCAC + Reverse CAGTAATAAAAGGGACATTCTGGC;
                       target M13mp18 positions 4905-5104 (200 bp amplicon; GenBank X02513.1);
                       equimolar mix, 4 uM per primer in 4X stock; 2 uM final concentration.
  M13mp18_Template   : Bacteriophage M13mp18 ssDNA (NEB), 250 pg/uL in nuclease-free water.
  Reservoir volumes  : 4 uL master mix; 2 uL primers; 2 uL template.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

=== PROTOCOL 1: RNA Fragmentation ===

Step 1 | Dispense reagents
  Inputs   : 3 x 0.5 uL RNA_PBMC (380 ng/uL); 1 x 0.5 uL 10X NEBNext fragmentation buffer
  Operation: dispense from respective reservoirs (reservoir volume 3.6 uL each)

Step 2 | Merge into reaction droplet
  Operation: sequential mix; rna1 + rna2 (10 s), + rna3 (10 s), + fragBuffer (10 s)
  Result   : 2 uL reaction droplet; transported to thermal zone

Step 3 | Thermal fragmentation
  Operation: heat at 94 C for 180 s
  Notes    : Without replenishment, droplet dries completely in <2 min at 94 C

Step 4 | Evaporation replenishment (6 water droplets)
  Operation: 6 x (dispense 0.5 uL NucleaseFreeWater + mix 5 s)
  Notes    : Each droplet pre-heated at zone edge 5 s before merge; volume maintained <=20% variation;
             temperature perturbation <=1 C per replenishment

Step 5 | Termination
  Operation: heat at 4 C for 30 s (droplet shuttled to cold zone); then dispense 0.5 uL StopSolution +
             mix 5 s
  Notes    : Stop solution terminates fragmentation reaction

Step 6 | QC detection
  Module   : rnaFragmentationDetection
  Duration : 30 s
  Expected : Fragments 40-1000 nt, peak ~150 nt; no 18S (1868 nt) or 28S (5025 nt) rRNA peaks
  Off-chip : Zymo RNA Clean + Concentrator-5 purification; Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer RNA Nano 6000 Chip
  Gate     : rnaSignal > 0 -> dispose (BB2); rnaSignal <= 0 -> drain (BB3)
  Join     : BB4

=== PROTOCOL 2: First-Strand cDNA Synthesis (Peregrine Method) ===

Step 7 | Dispense and merge RNA + primer PP_RT (Step A)
  Inputs   : 0.5 uL fragmented RNA_PBMC (100 ng); 0.5 uL PrimerPP_RT (25 mM)
  Operation: dispense; mix 10 s -> 1 uL droplet
  Notes    : Begins Peregrine template-switching cDNA synthesis

Step 8 | Denaturation and snap-cool (Step A cont.)
  Operation: heat 65 C 120 s (denaturation); heat 4 C 30 s (snap-cool)
  Notes    : Droplet shuttled between thermal zones for rapid transition

Step 9 | Merge master mix and incubate (Step B)
  Inputs   : 3 x 0.5 uL MasterMixCDNA
  Operation: dispense mm1, mm2, mm3; mix mm1+mm2 (5 s); mix + mm3 (5 s); mix into cdnaRxn (10 s)
  Then     : heat 25 C 180 s (primer annealing); heat 42 C 60 s (RT activation)

Step 10 | Merge primer PP_TS and extend (Step C)
  Input    : 0.5 uL PrimerPP_TS (12 mM)
  Operation: dispense + mix 5 s; heat 42 C 3600 s
  Replenishment: 9 x (dispense 0.5 uL NucleaseFreeWater + mix 5 s) during incubation

Step 11 | Termination (Step D)
  Operation: heat 70 C 300 s
  Replenishment: 4 x (dispense 0.5 uL NucleaseFreeWater + mix 5 s) during incubation
  Notes    : Inactivates SMARTScribe RT; 13 replenishments total across cDNA synthesis protocol

Step 12 | QC detection
  Module   : cdnaSynthesisDetection
  Duration : 30 s
  Expected : Ct comparable to conventional benchscale (p=0.14, N=3); equivalent ds-cDNA yield and size
  Off-chip : AMPure XP bead purification; qPCR Ct assay (SsoFast EvaGreen, CFX96, Bio-Rad);
             Bioanalyzer High Sensitivity DNA Assay Chip
  Gate     : cdnaSignal > 0 -> dispose (BB5); cdnaSignal <= 0 -> drain (BB6)
  Join     : BB7

=== PROTOCOL 3: PCR (M13mp18, 200 bp amplicon) ===

Step 13 | Dispense and merge PCR reagents
  Inputs   : 0.5 uL PCRMasterMix; 0.5 uL PCRPrimers; 0.5 uL M13mp18_Template
  Operation: dispense; mix master mix + primers (5 s); mix + template (5 s) -> 1.5 uL reaction droplet

Step 14 | Initial denaturation
  Operation: heat 95 C 45 s
  Purpose  : Hot Start Taq polymerase activation

Step 15 | 33 PCR cycles with per-cycle replenishment
  Cycle profile per cycle:
    Denaturation : 95 C, 20 s
    Replenishment: dispense 0.5 uL NucleaseFreeWater + mix 5 s (after denaturation, before annealing)
    Annealing    : 50 C, 30 s
    Extension    : 68 C, 45 s
  Total cycles     : 33
  Total water drops: 33 (one per cycle, added after denaturation step as in paper M&M)
  Note             : BioScript has no loop construct; all 33 cycles fully unrolled in source

Step 16 | Final extension
  Operation: heat 68 C 300 s
  Purpose  : Completion of partially extended amplicons

Step 17 | QC detection
  Module   : pcrProductDetection
  Duration : 30 s
  Expected : Single band at 200 bp; slightly reduced yield vs conventional PCR acceptable
  Off-chip : 2% agarose gel electrophoresis (E-Gel system, Life Technologies)
  Gate     : pcrSignal > 0 -> dispose (BB8); pcrSignal <= 0 -> drain (BB9)
  Join     : BB10 (terminal; dispose pcrSignal)


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file    : jebrail_dmf_evaporation_mgmt.bs
Compiler          : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output         : 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
DAG               : jebrail_dmf_evaporation_mgmt_main_dag.dot

Duration encoding : All durations use s (seconds) or m (minutes); h token unsupported by compiler.
                    3 min  -> 180s   (RNA fragmentation at 94 C)
                    2 min  -> 120s   (cDNA denaturation at 65 C)
                    1 h    -> 3600s  (cDNA extension at 42 C)
                    5 min  -> 300s   (cDNA termination at 70 C; PCR final extension)

Evaporation replenishment abstraction:
  Each just-in-time replenishment event is encoded as:
    wN = dispense 1 units of NucleaseFreeWater
    rxnVar = mix rxnVar with wN for 5s
  Variable reassignment (rxnVar = mix rxnVar with wN) correctly tracks fluid ownership through
  each sequential merge. The 5 s mix duration abstracts: (1) dispensing from syringe pump via
  through-hole; (2) transport to thermal zone edge; (3) pre-heating; (4) merge with reaction droplet.
  Total replenishment events: 6 (RNA) + 13 (cDNA) + 33 (PCR) = 52 events across the full file.

PCR cycle unrolling:
  BioScript has no loop primitive. All 33 cycles are fully unrolled as sequential heat/dispense/mix
  blocks. This yields a linear CFG for the PCR section rather than a cyclic graph, which correctly
  captures the sequential electrode actuation and thermal zone shuttle schedule.

heat statement semantics:
  `heat` is void/in-place in BioScript; the fluid variable is NOT consumed and persists after the
  statement. All downstream operations correctly reuse the same variable post-heat.

dispose/drain pattern:
  True branches (QC pass) use `dispose`; else branches (QC fail) use `drain` throughout.
  Known compiler behaviour: `drain` is lowered to `dispose()` in IR output due to visitStore
  routing in the compiler. The .bs source is correct; only IR lowering is affected.

Known compiler limitations (consistent with all other dataset entries):
  1. drain -> dispose lowering in IR (bsbbif_3_f, bsbbif_6_f, bsbbif_9_f): expected behaviour.
  2. True-branch blocks (bsbbif_2_t, bsbbif_5_t, bsbbif_8_t) emit no unconditional jump in IR
     text; DOT edges are correct. Known missing-jump-in-true-branch limitation.

Modules declared:
  rnaFragmentationDetection  : Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer RNA Nano 6000 Chip readout
  cdnaSynthesisDetection     : qPCR Ct assay + Bioanalyzer High Sensitivity DNA Assay Chip
  pcrProductDetection        : Gel electrophoresis (2% agarose E-Gel), 200 bp band

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Digital Microfluidic Method for Protein Extraction by Precipitation
Source Link  : https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/precipitation.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/ac8021554
Journal      : Analytical Chemistry, 2009, Vol. 81, No. 1, pp. 330-335
Authors      : Mais J. Jebrail, Aaron R. Wheeler
Platform     : Digital Microfluidics (DMF) on Parylene-C / Teflon-AF coated glass


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes the first microfluidic method for extracting proteins from
heterogeneous fluids by precipitation. The approach uses digital microfluidics (DMF)
to implement an automated, fully on-chip sequence of protein precipitation, rinsing,
and resolubilization -- without centrifugation. Protein precipitates settle rapidly
in DMF droplets (~0.1 mm path length vs. several mm in centrifuge tubes) and adhere
strongly to the Teflon-AF device surface, enabling clean separation of the liquid
supernatant from the solid precipitate by droplet actuation alone. The overall
extraction time is approximately 15 min, roughly half that of the conventional
macroscale equivalent (~30 min).

The protocol is divided into three functional phases:
  1. Qualitative extraction -- Mb/PC model system evaluated by ESI-MS (Fig. 2)
  2. Quantitative extraction -- protein standards (BSA, Mb, Fb) evaluated by
     fluorescamine assay (Fig. 3); >80% recovery for all three proteins
  3. Complex mixture extraction -- fetal bovine serum (FBS) and Jurkat T-cell
     lysate (CL) evaluated by fluorescamine assay (Fig. 4);
     FBS: 84.0 +/- 7.8%; CL: 82.4 +/- 11.5%

The method is compatible with proteins spanning a wide range of molecular weights
(17-340 kDa) and isoelectric points (pI 4.7-7.3), as well as with complex biological
matrices. Performance is comparable to conventional macroscale precipitation techniques,
with the advantages of automation, reduced reagent/sample consumption, no centrifugation,
and shorter processing time.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Geometry    : Double-T (double cross) electrode layout
Substrate   : Glass wafer
Electrodes  : Chromium (250 nm) patterned by photolithography
              Actuation electrodes: 1x1 mm and 1.5x1.5 mm
              Reservoir electrodes: 2.5x2.5 mm and 3.0x3.0 mm
              Interelectrode gap: 40 um
Dielectric  : Parylene-C, 2.5 um (vapor deposition)
Hydrophobic : Teflon-AF, 50 nm (spin-coated, 1% wt/wt in Fluorinert FC-40,
              2000 rpm / 60 s; post-baked 160 C / 10 min)
Top plate   : Unpatterned ITO-coated glass + Teflon-AF (50 nm)
Spacer      : 1-2 layers double-sided tape (70 um or 140 um interplate spacing)
Actuation   : 70-100 Vrms at 18 kHz (function generator + amplifier)
Key feature : Extraction electrode -- surface above this electrode is where
              precipitation, rinsing, and resolubilization all occur

Reservoirs (4 reagent + 1 waste):
  - Precipitant reservoir
  - Rinse solution reservoir
  - Resolubilizing buffer reservoir
  - Sample reservoir
  - Waste reservoir


REAGENTS AND MATERIALS
----------------------

Precipitants (Table 1):
  Mb, Fb           : Acetonitrile (ACN) -- primary; no secondary
  Mb/PC mixture    : ACN (primary) + saturated ammonium sulfate (secondary)
  BSA, FBS         : 20% trichloroacetic acid (TCA) in DI water
  Cell lysate (CL) : 20% TCA in DI water

Rinse solutions (Table 1):
  Mb, Fb, Mb/PC, BSA : 70/30 v/v chloroform/ACN
  FBS                : Acetone
  Cell lysate        : 60/40 v/v chloroform/acetone
  Note: neat chloroform is not directly actuatable at low driving potentials;
  chloroform/ACN (70/30 v/v) mixtures are readily movable on DMF devices.
  Neat acetone dissolves some CL precipitate; chloroform/acetone (60/40) avoids this.

Resolubilization buffers (Table 1):
  Mb, Fb, Mb/PC, BSA : 10 mM borate buffer (pH 8.5) + 1% SDS
  FBS, CL            : 100 mM borate buffer (pH 8.5) + 10% SDS

Working solutions:
  All protein solutions prepared in 10 mM borate buffer (pH 8.5) + 0.08% Pluronics F127 (w/v)
  Carrier fluid: Fluorinert FC-40

Key reagents (Sigma, unless noted):
  Acetone, ACN, chloroform, methanol, boric acid, 50% formic acid, Fluorinert FC-40,
  NaOH, Pluronics F127, TCA, Triton X-100, PMSF, SDS, fluorescamine, ammonium sulfate,
  BSA, fibrinogen (Fb), myoglobin (Mb)
  PBS, FBS: Invitrogen Canada
  1,2-Dibutyroyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (PC): Avanti Polar Lipids

Fluorescence assay:
  Reagent  : Fluorescamine (5 mg/mL in acetone)
  Platform : Pherastar plate reader (BMG Labtech); 384-well low-volume microplate
  Excitation: 390 nm; Emission: 510 nm
  Reaction : Immediate; fluorescamine non-fluorescent until it reacts with
             primary amines at protein N-terminus
  Controls : Unextracted protein droplets processed identically through device
             (dispense -> extraction electrode -> dry -> resolubilize -> collect)


PROTEIN STANDARDS
-----------------
BSA (bovine serum albumin) : MW 66 kDa, pI 4.7, 50 mg/mL; precipitant = 20% TCA
Mb  (myoglobin)            : MW 17 kDa, pI 7.3, 30 mg/mL; precipitant = ACN
Fb  (fibrinogen)           : MW 340 kDa, pI 5.5, 20 mg/mL; precipitant = ACN

Qualitative model system:
  Analyte     : Mb (0.71 mM)
  Contaminant : PC phospholipid (62 mM) -- 80:1 molar excess
  Analysis    : ESI-MS (LTQ linear ion trap, Thermo Fischer Scientific)
                Positive ion mode; 315 nL sample diluted into 50 uL 50/50 water/ACN
                + 0.1% formic acid; flow rate 0.5 uL/min; 1.7-1.9 kV; 170 C capillary;
                50 acquisitions averaged; triplicate


CELL LINE AND LYSATE
--------------------
Cell line   : Jurkat T-cells
Culture     : RPMI 1640 + 10% FBS + penicillin (100 IU/mL) + streptomycin (100 ug/mL)
              37 C, 5% CO2, humidified; subcultured every 3-4 days at 5e5 cells/mL
Lysis buffer: PBS + 0.08% F127 + 1% Triton X-100 + 1 mM PMSF
Lysis method: Cells washed 1x PBS; suspended at 6e7 cells/mL in lysis buffer;
              incubated on ice 30 min; centrifuged 13,000 rpm 5 min;
              supernatant collected and stored at -80 C


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Device Priming
  Reagent  : 0.08% Pluronics F127 in 10 mM borate buffer (pH 8.5)
  Duration : 5 min at 25 C (room temperature)
  Purpose  : Coat Teflon-AF surfaces with Pluronics surfactant layer to reduce
             non-specific protein adsorption to device surfaces.
  BS model : heat primingDrop at 25c for 5m; dispose

Step 2 | Qualitative Extraction -- Sample and First Precipitant Dispensing
  Sample   : Mb/PC mixture (Mb 0.71 mM, PC 62 mM) in borate buffer + 0.08% F127
  Precipitant 1: ACN (~140 nL)
  Operation: Dispense sample and ACN droplets; merge on extraction electrode
  Duration : 5 min incubation at 25 C (room temperature)
  BS model : mix mbPcSample with precipitant1_Mb for 5m

Step 3 | Qualitative Extraction -- Secondary Precipitant Addition
  Precipitant 2: Saturated ammonium sulfate in DI water (~140 nL)
  Rationale: Required at low Mb concentration (0.71 mM); ACN alone insufficient
             for reproducible precipitation below ~1 mM.
  Duration : Additional 5 min incubation at 25 C
  BS model : mix mbPcPrecip1 with precipitant2_Mb for 5m

Step 4 | Supernatant Removal
  Operation: Actuate supernatant droplet away from extraction electrode to waste
             reservoir. Precipitate remains on electrode; adsorbed to Teflon-AF.
  Key point: No centrifugation required. Path length ~0.1 mm; precipitates settle
             in seconds (2x faster than in centrifuge tubes).
  BS model : drain supernatant1

Step 5 | Rinsing (x3)
  Rinse solution : 70/30 v/v chloroform/ACN (~315 nL per droplet)
  Cycles         : 3 sequential rinse droplets
  Operation      : Each rinse droplet dispensed, driven across extraction electrode,
                   and actuated to waste.
  Purpose        : Remove PC lipid contamination and non-protein constituents.
  BS model       : mix mbPcPrecipFull with rinse1_Mb for 30s; drain (x3)

Step 6 | Drying
  Temperature : 25 C (room temperature air dry)
  Duration    : 5 min
  Purpose     : Remove residual chloroform/ACN before resolubilization.
                No bake step required for chloroform/ACN rinse systems.
                TCA precipitants require bake at 95 C for 5 min (Steps 9a, 9c).
  BS model    : heat mbPcPrecipFull at 25c for 5m

Step 7 | Resolubilization
  Buffer   : 10 mM borate (pH 8.5) + 1% SDS (~315 nL)
  Duration : 5 min incubation at extraction electrode
  Purpose  : Dissolve precipitated protein for downstream analysis.
  BS model : mix mbPcPrecipFull with resolubBuffer_Mb for 5m

Step 8 | Qualitative QC -- ESI-MS Detection
  Module   : precipitationDetection (abstracts LTQ linear ion trap MS)
  Duration : 30 s detection window
  Pass     : Mb multiply charged ions detected (m/z 600-1800, charges +27 to +10);
             PC signal (m/z 398, 795) suppressed to trace levels.
  Fail     : Mb signal absent or PC signal dominant.
  Gate     : precipitationSignal > 0 -> BB2 (pass/dispose); else BB3 (fail/drain)

Step 9a | BSA Extraction (Quantitative -- Protein Standards)
  Sample       : BSA 50 mg/mL (~140 nL)
  Precipitant  : 20% TCA (~140 nL); incubate 5 min at 25 C
  Rinse        : 70/30 v/v chloroform/ACN x3 (~315 nL each); 30 s per rinse
  Bake         : 95 C for 5 min to remove residual TCA before resolubilization
  Resolubilize : 10 mM borate (pH 8.5) + 1% SDS (~315 nL); 5 min
  BS model     : bsaPrecip -> drain supernatant -> rinse x3 -> heat 95c 5m -> resolubBSA

Step 9b | Mb Extraction (Quantitative -- Protein Standards)
  Sample       : Myoglobin 30 mg/mL (~140 nL)
  Precipitant  : ACN (~140 nL); incubate 5 min at 25 C
  Rinse        : 70/30 v/v chloroform/ACN x3 (~315 nL each); 30 s per rinse
  Dry          : 25 C for 5 min (no bake required for ACN precipitant)
  Resolubilize : 10 mM borate (pH 8.5) + 1% SDS (~315 nL); 5 min
  BS model     : mbPrecip -> drain supernatant -> rinse x3 -> heat 25c 5m -> resolubMbQuant

Step 9c | Fb Extraction (Quantitative -- Protein Standards)
  Sample       : Fibrinogen 20 mg/mL (~140 nL)
  Precipitant  : ACN (~140 nL); incubate 5 min at 25 C
  Rinse        : 70/30 v/v chloroform/ACN x3 (~315 nL each); 30 s per rinse
  Dry          : 25 C for 5 min
  Resolubilize : 10 mM borate (pH 8.5) + 1% SDS (~315 nL); 5 min
  BS model     : fbPrecip -> drain supernatant -> rinse x3 -> heat 25c 5m -> resolubFb

Step 9d | Fluorescamine Assay (Quantitative QC)
  Reagent  : Fluorescamine (5 mg/mL in acetone); 1 min reaction at 25 C
  Incubate : 2 min settle at 25 C before plate reader measurement
  Module   : fluorescenceDetection (abstracts Pherastar plate reader readout)
  Gate     : fluorSignal > 0 -> BB5 (pass/dispose all 3); else BB6 (fail/dispose all 3)
  Target   : >80% recovery for BSA, Mb, Fb vs. unextracted control
  Note     : QC gate keyed on BSA signal (highest concentration, most robust)
  Compiler : drain collapsed to dispose by lilott8/BioScript in IR; both branches
             use dispose explicitly for consistent output (BB6 fix).

Step 10a | FBS Extraction (Complex Mixture)
  Sample       : Fetal bovine serum (~140 nL)
  Precipitant  : 20% TCA (~140 nL); incubate 5 min at 25 C
  Rinse        : Acetone x3 (~315 nL each); 30 s per rinse
                 Supplemental rinse strategy: if supernatant is sticky/immovable,
                 dispense rinse solvent to extraction electrode first; combined
                 rinse+supernatant droplet driven to waste together.
  Bake         : 95 C for 5 min to remove residual TCA
  Resolubilize : 100 mM borate (pH 8.5) + 10% SDS (~315 nL); 5 min
  Recovery     : 84.0 +/- 7.8% (mean +/- SD, N=4)
  BS model     : fbsPrecip -> drain supernatant -> rinse x3 -> heat 95c 5m -> resolubFBS

Step 10b | Cell Lysate Extraction (Complex Mixture)
  Sample       : Jurkat T-cell lysate (~70 nL; reduced interplate spacing 70 um
                 to handle high viscosity; standard spacing 140 um not suitable)
  Precipitant  : 20% TCA (~70 nL); incubate 5 min at 25 C
  Rinse        : 60/40 v/v chloroform/acetone x3 (~158 nL each); 30 s per rinse
                 Neat acetone dissolves some CL precipitate; chloroform/acetone avoids this.
  Bake         : 95 C for 5 min to remove residual TCA
  Resolubilize : 100 mM borate (pH 8.5) + 10% SDS (~158 nL); 5 min
  Recovery     : 82.4 +/- 11.5% (mean +/- SD, N=4)
  BS model     : clPrecip -> drain supernatant -> rinse x3 -> heat 95c 5m -> resolubCL

Step 10c | Fluorescamine Assay (Complex Mixture QC)
  Reagent  : Fluorescamine (5 mg/mL in acetone); 1 min reaction at 25 C
  Incubate : 2 min settle at 25 C before plate reader measurement
  Module   : fluorescenceDetection
  Gate     : complexSignal > 0 -> BB8 (pass/dispose both); else BB9 (fail/dispose both)
  Note     : QC gate keyed on FBS signal.
  Compiler : Same drain->dispose fix applied (BB9).


CONVENTIONAL MACROSCALE COMPARISON
------------------------------------
For each protein standard and complex mixture, identical extraction was performed
macroscopically (N=4 replicates each):
  - 10 uL sample + 10 uL chilled precipitant in microcentrifuge tube
  - Incubate 5 min at 4 C; centrifuge 13,000 rpm 5 min; discard supernatant
  - Wash pellet 3x: suspend in 22.5 uL rinse solution; centrifuge 13,000 rpm 5 min; discard
  - Dissolve pellet in 100 uL resolubilization buffer
  - Same precipitants, rinse, and resolubilization solutions as DMF
  - Performance comparable to DMF; DMF is ~2x faster (15 min vs. 30 min)


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
--------------------------
BioScript file : jebrail_dmf_protein_precipitation.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
DAG            : jebrail_dmf_protein_precipitation_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations expressed in s (seconds) or m (minutes).
                 BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported.
                 Key durations in IR:
                   5m  precipitation/resolubilization -> 300.0SECOND
                   30s rinsing                        ->  30.0SECOND
                   5m  drying/baking                  -> 300.0SECOND
                   2m  fluorescamine settle            -> 120.0SECOND
                   30s detection                      ->  30.0SECOND
Modules        : precipitationDetection, fluorescenceDetection
Compiler quirk : drain collapses to dispose in IR output for lilott8/BioScript.
                 All else-branch drain calls in BB6 and BB9 replaced with dispose
                 for consistent IR. BB2/BB3 drain in qualitative branch also
                 collapses; acceptable as both branches dispose resolubMb in IR.
Parallelism    : BSA, Mb, and Fb extractions run in parallel on device (double-T
                 layout). BioScript encodes them sequentially; CFG logical structure
                 is correct.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Synchronized Synthesis of Peptide-Based Macrocycles by Digital Microfluidics
Source Link  : https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/macrocycle_synthesis.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.201001604
Journal      : Angewandte Chemie International Edition, 2010, Vol. 49, pp. 8625-8629
Platform     : Two-plate digital microfluidics (DMF) on EWOD/electrode array
Authors      : Mais J. Jebrail, Alphonsus H. C. Ng, Vishal Rai, Ryan Hili,
               Andrei K. Yudin, Aaron R. Wheeler
Affiliation  : Department of Chemistry and Institute of Biomaterials and Biomedical
               Engineering, University of Toronto, Toronto, ON M5S 3H6, Canada


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes the first two-plate digital microfluidic platform for parallel
multi-component, multi-step chemical synthesis. It implements synchronized on-chip
synthesis of five peptide-based macrocycles (PMs) from three components -- amino acids,
amphoteric aziridine aldehydes, and tert-butyl isocyanide (tBuNC) -- in a one-step
Ugi-type macrocyclization reaction. Products contain aziridine sites that are primed for
late-stage nucleophilic modification.

Downstream processing converts the PMs into macrocyclic peptide thioesters (ring-opened
products, ROPs) by reacting with thiobenzoic acid (PhCOSH). As a further demonstration,
a nine-membered macrocycle is synthesized from a Pro-Leu dipeptide substrate -- a ring
size associated with considerable synthetic difficulty in conventional cyclic peptide
synthesis.

The platform is fully automated, hardware-free (no pumps, tubing, or valves), compatible
with a wide range of organic solvents and corrosive chemicals, and supports critical
steps -- solvent removal and re-dissolution of solids -- that are problematic in
microchannel-based systems. Five products are formed in 30 total processing steps
(6 steps per parallel reaction), verified by ESI-MS and 1H-NMR against macroscale
reference syntheses.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Configuration : Two-plate DMF
Top plate     : Transparent ITO (indium tin oxide) glass; removable for product isolation
Bottom plate  : Electrode array coated with Teflon-based hydrophobic insulator
Reservoirs    : 10 reagent supply reservoirs
Electrodes    : 88 actuation electrodes dedicated to dispensing, merging, and mixing
Droplet volume: 900 nL per unit droplet
Actuation     : Electrical potentials applied to electrode array (EWOD principle);
                discrete nL-to-uL droplets controlled in parallel with no cross-contamination
Surface       : Chemically inert Teflon; compatible with TFE, organic solvents, corrosive
                chemicals -- diversifies reagent scope beyond PDMS-based microchannel systems

Key advantages over microchannel platforms:
  - No pumps, tubing, valves, or 3D channel networks required
  - Individual reagent addressing with no complex microvalve networks
  - Supports solvent removal by evaporation and re-dissolution of solid products
  - Easy off-chip product access (remove top plate; recover by pipette)
  - Scalable: proposed future systems capable of tens to hundreds of simultaneous products


REAGENTS
--------
Amino acids (five tracks):
  Val, Met, Ile, Thr, Pro -- 0.1 M in deionized water; 90 nmol per droplet (900 nL)

Aziridine aldehyde:
  Amphoteric aziridine aldehyde -- 0.05 M in TFE; 45 nmol per droplet (900 nL)
  Role: electrophilic macrocyclization partner; aziridine ring in product is site for
  late-stage modification by nucleophilic ring-opening

tert-Butyl isocyanide (tBuNC):
  0.1 M in TFE; 90 nmol per droplet (900 nL)
  Role: isocyanide component of Ugi-type three-component cyclization

Thiobenzoic acid (PhCOSH):
  0.1 M in TFE; 90 nmol per droplet (900 nL)
  Role: nucleophile for aziridine ring-opening; yields macrocyclic peptide thioesters
  (ROPs); thioesters are precursors to native chemical ligation (S-to-N acyl transfer)

Trifluoroethanol (TFE):
  Re-dissolution solvent; 4 x 900 nL droplets (~3.5 uL) driven to each dried PM spot
  by electrode actuation before ring-opening

Pro-Leu dipeptide (nine-membered macrocycle synthesis):
  0.1 M in TFE; 90 nmol per droplet (900 nL)

Off-chip analysis solvents:
  MS  : 100 uL MeOH + 0.1% formic acid (ESI-MS)
  NMR : 250 uL CD3OD (1H-NMR)


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Phase 1 | Peptide Macrocycle (PM) Synthesis -- Five Parallel Tracks

Step 1 | Amino Acid + Aziridine Aldehyde Merge
  Tracks    : Val, Met, Ile, Thr, Pro (5 simultaneous reactions)
  Inputs    : AminoAcid_X (900 nL, 0.1 M, 90 nmol) + AziridineAldehyde (900 nL, 0.05 M, 45 nmol)
  Operation : Dispense from respective reservoirs; electrode-actuated merging and mixing
  Duration  : 20 s (circular actuation on 4 electrodes)
  Purpose   : Imine formation between amino acid and aziridine aldehyde

Step 2 | tBuNC Addition and Macrocyclization
  Tracks    : Val, Met, Ile, Thr, Pro
  Inputs    : AA+AzAld merged droplet + tBuNC (900 nL, 0.1 M, 90 nmol)
  Operation : Dispense tBuNC; electrode-actuated merging and mixing
  Duration  : 20 s (circular actuation on 4 electrodes)
  Purpose   : Completes three-component Ugi-type macrocyclization

Step 3 | Macrocyclization Incubation
  Tracks      : Val, Met, Ile, Thr, Pro
  Temperature : 25 C (room temperature)
  Duration    : 1 h (60 min; IR: 3600.0 SECOND)
  Enclosure   : Parafilm-sealed Petri dish to minimize evaporation
  Kinetics    : ~70% depletion of initial reagent within 1 h by DMF;
                ~90% by macroscale; anticipated improvement with continuous rapid mixing

Step 4 | PM Isolation by TFE Evaporation
  Tracks      : Val, Met, Ile, Thr, Pro
  Method      : ITO top plate removed; TFE evaporated at RT (25 C) for 15 min
  Result      : Solid PM precipitates on electrode; accessible by pipette after re-dissolution
                in 100 uL MeOH/0.1% formic acid (MS) or 250 uL CD3OD (NMR)

Phase 1 QC Gate | PM Verification (BB1 -> BB2/BB3)
  Representative track : Met
  Detection module     : macrocycleQC (abstracts off-chip ESI-MS + 1H-NMR)
  Detection duration   : 30 s
  MS verification      : m/z 342 (PM-Met; Fig 4b); other PMs in Supporting Information Figs S1-S4
  NMR verification     : 1H-NMR in CD3OD; chemical shifts correlated with macroscale product
                         (Supporting Information Fig S6)
  Pass (BB2)           : macrocycleSignal > 0 -> dispose(rxnMixMet); proceed to Phase 2
  Fail (BB3)           : macrocycleSignal <= 0 -> drain(rxnMixMet)
  Join (BB4)           : dispose(macrocycleSignal); Phase 2 begins


Phase 2 | Aziridine Ring-Opening (ROP) -- Five Parallel Tracks

Step 5 | PM Re-Dissolution in TFE
  Tracks    : Val, Met, Ile, Thr, Pro
  Inputs    : 4 x TFE droplets (4 x 900 nL = ~3.5 uL) per dried PM spot
  Operation : Four sequential TFE dispenses chained via electrode-actuated mixing;
              combined droplet driven to dried solid spot by electrode actuation
  Purpose   : Re-dissolve solid PM for ring-opening reaction
  Notes     : Volume of TFE is not constrained (unlike microchannel platforms);
              flexibility is a key DMF advantage highlighted in Fig 3 frames 1-2

Step 6 | PhCOSH Merge and Ring-Opening Incubation
  Tracks      : Val, Met, Ile, Thr, Pro
  Inputs      : pmSolnX (~3.5 uL) + PhCOSH (900 nL, 0.1 M, 90 nmol)
  Operation   : Dispense PhCOSH; electrode-actuated merging and mixing
  Mixing      : 20 s (circular actuation on 4 electrodes)
  Incubation  : 1 h at 25 C (IR: 3600.0 SECOND); parafilm-sealed Petri dish
  Purpose     : Nucleophilic opening of aziridine by PhCOSH yields macrocyclic
                peptide thioester at defined position

Step 7 | ROP Isolation by TFE Evaporation
  Tracks      : Val, Met, Ile, Thr, Pro
  Method      : TFE evaporated at RT (25 C) for 15 min (IR: 900.0 SECOND)
  Result      : Precipitated macrocyclic peptide thioesters (ROPs) at defined electrode
                positions; spatially resolved on-chip

Phase 2 QC Gate | ROP Verification (BB4 -> BB5/BB6)
  Representative track : Met
  Detection module     : ringOpeningQC (abstracts off-chip ESI-MS + 1H-NMR)
  Detection duration   : 30 s
  MS verification      : m/z 150 (unreacted Met), 342 (PM-Met), 480 (ROP-Met; Fig 4c)
  NMR verification     : 1H-NMR in CD3OD; chemical shifts correlated with macroscale
                         (Supporting Information Fig S7)
  Pass (BB5)           : ringOpeningSignal > 0 -> dispose all 5 ROP droplets
  Fail (BB6)           : ringOpeningSignal <= 0 -> drain all 5 ROP droplets
  Terminal (BB7)       : dispose(ringOpeningSignal); 9-mer sub-protocol follows


Supplementary Protocol | Nine-Membered Macrocycle Synthesis (Fig 5, paper)

Step 8 | Pro-Leu Dipeptide + AziridineAldehyde + tBuNC Merge
  Substrate   : Pro-Leu dipeptide (0.1 M in TFE, 900 nL, 90 nmol)
  Inputs      : Pro-Leu dipeptide + AziridineAldehyde (900 nL, 0.05 M) + tBuNC (900 nL, 0.1 M)
  Operation   : Dispense all three components; sequential electrode-actuated merging and mixing
  Mixing      : 20 s per merge (circular actuation on 4 electrodes)

Step 9 | Nine-Membered Macrocycle Incubation
  Temperature : 25 C (room temperature)
  Duration    : 3 h (180 min; IR: 10800.0 SECOND)
  Mixing      : Every 30 min (6 x 20 s circular actuation events over 3 h)
  BioScript   : Encoded as single heat 180m; periodic mixing is a DMF controller
                firmware operation not representable as a BioScript droplet-level operation
  Notes       : Longer reaction time vs standard PMs due to reduced reactivity of dipeptide
                substrate; nine-membered ring size previously inaccessible by direct
                linear tripeptide cyclization (Failli et al., Can. J. Chem. 1979, 57, 3257)

Step 10 | Nine-Membered Macrocycle Isolation
  Method      : TFE evaporated at 25 C for 15 min (IR: 900.0 SECOND)
  Product     : Compound 8; ESI-MS m/z 421 (Fig 5b, paper)
  Significance: Demonstrates reaction selectivity and scope extension to larger ring sizes
                via dipeptide substrates; Pro-Leu macrocycle contains thioester for
                anticipated native chemical ligation applications


REACTION OUTCOME SUMMARY
------------------------

PM Synthesis (5 parallel tracks):
  PM-Val  : m/z confirmed (Supporting Information Fig S1)
  PM-Met  : m/z 342 (Fig 4b); NMR confirmed (Supporting Information Fig S6)
  PM-Ile  : m/z confirmed (Supporting Information Fig S2)
  PM-Thr  : m/z confirmed (Supporting Information Fig S3)
  PM-Pro  : m/z confirmed (Supporting Information Fig S4)

ROP Synthesis (5 parallel tracks):
  ROP-Met : m/z 480 (Fig 4c); NMR confirmed (Supporting Information Fig S7)
  ROP-Val/Ile/Thr/Pro : confirmed (Supporting Information Figs S1-S4)
  Agreement with macroscale synthesis: near-identical spectra (Supporting Information Fig S5a,b)

Nine-Membered Macrocycle:
  Compound 8 (Pro-Leu derived): m/z 421 (Fig 5b); 9-membered ring confirmed


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : jebrail_macrocycle_dmf.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG file       : jebrail_macrocycle_dmf_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations converted to minutes (m) or seconds (s);
                 BioScript supports only s and m tokens (h token not supported)
                 1h incubation  -> 60m   (IR: 3600.0 SECOND)
                 15min evap     -> 15m   (IR: 900.0 SECOND)
                 3h 9-mer incub -> 180m  (IR: 10800.0 SECOND)
Modules        : macrocycleQC, ringOpeningQC

Compiler constraints and resolutions:
  1. Case-sensitive variables
       Bug  : aaMixMet = mix aamet with azAldMet (lowercase 'aamet' vs declared 'aaMet')
       Error: UndefinedVariable: main.aamet is not defined
       Fix  : corrected to mix aaMet with azAldMet

  2. Self-mix rejected by symbol visitor
       Bug  : rxnMix9mer = mix rxnMix9mer with rxnMix9mer (double-consume of same variable)
       Error: would raise UndefinedVariable or double-consume on next compiler pass
       Fix  : replaced 6 alternating heat(30m)+mix(self) cycles with single heat 180m;
              periodic electrode actuations are firmware-level DMF operations, not
              droplet-level BioScript operations

  3. No parallelism primitive
       Issue: Paper synthesizes 5 PMs simultaneously on-chip
       Resolution: 5 PM tracks and 5 ROP tracks encoded sequentially; concurrent on
                   physical device; documented in comments

  4. drain() normalised to dispose() in IR
       Observation: BioScript compiler emits dispose() opcode for both dispose and drain
                    keywords; distinction is only meaningful at physical execution layer;
                    not a bug in the IR

  5. Multi-unit TFE re-dissolution
       Issue: Compiler does not support multi-unit scalar dispense into solid spot
       Resolution: 4 TFE dispenses chained via sequential mix steps to accumulate ~3.5 uL
                   (pattern from Moazami reference file, lines 222-229)

  6. Pro-Leu dipeptide manifest
       Issue: Pro-Leu dipeptide is a distinct reagent not declared in the manifest block
       Resolution: Mapped to AminoAcid_Pro with prominent comment; separate manifest
                   ProLeu_Dipeptide recommended in a full implementation

  7. Nine-membered macrocycle as post-terminal sub-protocol
       Design: 9-mer synthesis is an independent demonstration (Fig 5), not downstream
               of the five-PM synthesis; runs unconditionally after BB7 terminal node;
               does not introduce additional CFG branches
