description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : World-to-Digital-Microfluidic Interface Enabling Extraction and Purification of RNA from Human Whole Blood
Source Link  : https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/ac404085p
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/ac404085p
Journal      : Analytical Chemistry, 2014, Vol. 86, pp. 3856-3862
Authors      : Mais J. Jebrail, Anupama Sinha, Samantha Vellucci, Ronald F. Renzi, Cesar Ambriz,
               Carmen Gondhalekar, Joseph S. Schoeniger, Kamlesh D. Patel, Steven S. Branda
Institution  : Sandia National Laboratories, Livermore, California
Platform     : World-to-DMF (macroscale Extraction Module + DMF-based Purification Module,
               peristaltic pump driven, 10 uL Bridging Droplet interface)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes the first "world-to-DMF" interface: an engineered system that drives
a large-volume real-world sample (human whole blood lysate, 110-380 uL) repeatedly through a
10 uL droplet region on a digital microfluidic (DMF) device, enabling inline concentration of
RNA-bound magnetic beads from the macroscale volume directly onto the DMF chip surface.
Downstream purification (two washes + elution) is then performed entirely in microscale volumes
(5-15 uL) within the DMF Purification Module.

The protocol achieves >2-fold faster processing and 12-fold reagent reduction compared to
conventional bench-scale preparations, while producing RNA of equivalent yield and quality
(A260/A280, RIN) suitable for qRT-PCR and RNA-Seq analyses. The BioScript file encodes
the 50 uL blood specimen arm as the representative protocol (intermediate of the three
volumes tested: 25, 50, and 100 uL).

Key innovation: Inline (on-DMF-device) concentration of sample analytes, as opposed to
off-device pre-concentration, eliminates manual handling steps, reduces contamination risk,
and removes worker exposure to biological samples.


SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
The world-to-DMF system has three components:

Extraction Module:
  - Two 500 uL microcentrifuge tubes: Reaction Chamber and Waste Chamber
  - One peristaltic pump connected via Connector Tubes to both chambers
  - Transfer Tube 1 and Transfer Tube 2: conduct fluid between Reaction Chamber
    and the Module Interface (Bridging Electrode)
  - Transfer Tube 1 preloaded: Lysis Solution (130 uL) | 20 uL air gap | RNA Binding Beads (20 uL)
  - Pump drives pressure-driven convective flow of the full 200 uL lysate through the
    10 uL Bridging Droplet (3 passes); convective transport increases bead capture efficiency
    vs. diffusion-only conventional method

Purification Module (DMF device, fabricated in-house):
  - Bottom plate: 40 chromium electrode pads (6x6 mm, 40 um interelectrode gaps) on glass;
    photolithography + etching
  - Dielectric: 7 um Parylene-C (vapor deposition)
  - Hydrophobic: 50 nm Teflon-AF (spin-coat)
  - Top plate: ITO-coated glass + 50 nm Teflon-AF
  - Air gap: 300 um (three layers double-sided tape spacer)
  - Actuation: AC electrowetting, 100 Vrms
  - On-device reservoirs preloaded: Wash 1 (15 uL), Wash 2 (15 uL), Elution Buffer (10 uL)

Module Interface (Bridging Droplet):
  - Bridging Electrode: working electrode pad at the periphery of the DMF device; top plate
    recessed to expose ~1 mm x 6 mm of the electrode surface
  - Transfer Tubes contact the Bridging Electrode at ~70 degrees (adjustable magnetic stand +
    custom spacing manifold)
  - Bridging Droplet (10 uL): formed by coordinating three forces simultaneously --
    dispensation from Transfer Tube 1, aspiration into Transfer Tube 2, and AC actuation of
    the Bridging Electrode (100 Vrms)
  - External movable magnet positioned directly beneath Bridging Electrode to immobilise
    bead-bound analytes as the macroscale volume passes through the droplet
  - Three strategies for reliable Bridging Droplet formation:
      (1) Organic solvents (>=15%; ethanol/isopropanol in lysis buffer) reduce surface tension
          to allow fluid entry into the air gap
      (2) Top plate recessed 1 mm to expose Bridging Electrode for direct Transfer Tube access
      (3) Coordinated choreography of pump and electrode actuation


REAGENTS
--------
Whole blood         : 50 uL (healthy volunteer donors, ProMedDx, Norton MA)
Lysis Solution      : MagMAX-Blood lysis buffer, 130 uL (Life Technologies, Grand Island NY);
                      contains chaotropic salts; prepared per manufacturer's instructions
RNA Binding Beads   : MagMAX silica-coated magnetic beads, 20 uL (MagMAX-Blood RNA Isolation Kit)
Wash 1 Solution     : MagMAX Wash 1 Solution, 15 uL (on-device reservoir)
                      [conventional method uses 150 uL per wash; 10-fold reduction]
Wash 2 Solution     : MagMAX Wash 2 Solution, 15 uL (on-device reservoir)
                      [removes residual chaotropic salts and ethanol from Wash 1]
Elution Buffer      : MagMAX Elution Buffer + 0.1% w/v Pluronic F127, 10 uL (on-device)
                      [Pluronic F127 added per ref 20 to maintain droplet actuation fidelity
                      on Teflon-AF surface; conventional method uses 30 uL]
Filler fluid        : Fluorinert FC-40 (Sigma Chemical, St. Louis MO)
Surfactant          : Pluronic F127 (Sigma Chemical); 0.1% w/v in Elution Buffer;
                      also mixed with FC-40 to prime DMF air gap
Parylene C dimer    : Specialty Coating Systems, Indianapolis IN (dielectric deposition)
Teflon-AF           : DuPont, Wilmington DE (hydrophobic coating)


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 0 | Device Initialisation
  Reagents  : FluorinertFC40, PluronicF127, Wash1Solution, Wash2Solution, ElutionBuffer
  Operation : Dispense FC-40 + Pluronic F127; mix 30 s to prime DMF air gap.
              Dispense Wash 1, Wash 2, and Elution Buffer into on-device reservoirs.
  Setup     : Adjust magnetic stand so Transfer Tubes contact Bridging Electrode at ~70 degrees.
              AC 100 Vrms actuation enabled.
  Notes     : BioScript variable `devicePrime` (FC-40 + Pluronic F127 mix) is reused throughout
              the protocol as the second argument to `mix` calls that abstract magnet
              engage/disengage steps and bead pellet progression. This is a compiler-driven
              abstraction; physically, these steps involve only the bead pellet and the
              immediately preceding droplet.

Step 1 | Blood Specimen Introduction
  Reagent   : WholeBlood
  Volume    : 50 uL
  Operation : Dispense into Reaction Chamber (500 uL microcentrifuge tube) by pipetting.
  Notes     : Specimens from healthy volunteer donors (ProMedDx, Norton MA).
              Other arms: 25 uL (total lysate 110 uL) or 100 uL (total lysate 380 uL).

Step 2 | Lysis and Mixing
  Reagent   : LysisSolution (130 uL for 50 uL blood; 2.6:1 v/v lysis:blood ratio)
  Duration  : 30 s
  Mechanism : Peristaltic pump aspirates Lysis Solution from Transfer Tube 1 into Reaction
              Chamber; bolus shuttled rapidly between Transfer Tube 1 and Reaction Chamber
              for 30 s to mix thoroughly.
  Output    : bloodLysate (homogeneous blood + lysis buffer mixture)

Step 3 | RNA Binding Bead Addition and Incubation
  Reagent     : RNABindingBeads (20 uL MagMAX silica-coated magnetic beads)
  Mix         : 30 s (shuttle bolus between Transfer Tube 1 and Reaction Chamber)
  Incubation  : 5 min (300 s) at room temperature (25 C) -- RNA binds to bead surface
  Total volume: 200 uL (50 + 130 + 20 uL)
  BioScript   : `heat beadLysateMix at 25c for 300s` models the bead-binding incubation.

Step 4 | World-to-DMF Transition: Bridging Droplet Formation and Bead Capture (3 Passes)
  Operation : Pressure-driven convective flow-through (abstracted as `mix` in BioScript)
  Passes    : 3 (bidirectional: Transfer Tube 1 -> Bridging Droplet -> Transfer Tube 2, then back)
  Per-pass  :
    - Pump drives full 200 uL lysate through the 10 uL Bridging Droplet on Bridging Electrode
    - AC 100 Vrms applied to Bridging Electrode to pin the droplet (prevent spread)
    - External magnet beneath Bridging Electrode engaged to immobilise bead-bound RNA
    - `heat at 25c for 60s` models magnet engagement per pass
  After 3 passes:
    - RNA Binding Beads with bound RNA are immobilised on Bridging Electrode surface
    - Lysate supernatant is directed to Waste Chamber
    - `beadCapture` is the BioScript handle for the bead pellet going forward
  Notes     : Convective (pressure-driven) transport is more efficient than the diffusion-only
              transport in the conventional method; accounts for the slightly better RNA yield
              observed at 100 uL blood volume (p=0.03, Student t-test).
              bridgingDroplet1/2/3 each consumed as input to successor mix call; must not
              be re-read. beadCapture is introduced as a clean handle post-disposal.

Step 5 | Wash 1
  Reagent   : Wash1Solution (15 uL, on-device reservoir)
  Operation :
    1. heat wash1Reservoir at 25c for 10s -- models magnet disengage (bead resuspension)
    2. mix wash1Reservoir with beadCapture for 30s -- bead-wash mixing via Transfer Tube shuttle
    3. heat wash1Mix at 25c for 30s -- models mixing/washing contact time
    4. wash1Beads = mix wash1Mix with devicePrime for 5s -- magnet re-engage; bead pellet captured
    5. dispose wash1Mix -- wash fluid sent to Waste Chamber
  Output    : wash1Beads (bead pellet proceeding to Wash 2)
  Note      : 15 uL vs. 150 uL in conventional method (10-fold reduction per wash).

Step 6 | Wash 2
  Reagent   : Wash2Solution (15 uL, on-device reservoir)
  Operation : Identical four-step sequence as Wash 1 (disengage -> mix -> re-engage -> dispose).
  Purpose   : Removes residual chaotropic salts and ethanol carried over from Wash 1.
  Output    : wash2Beads (bead pellet proceeding to Elution)

Step 7 | Elution
  Reagent       : ElutionBuffer (10 uL + 0.1% Pluronic F127, on-device reservoir)
  Operation     :
    1. heat elutionReservoir at 25c for 10s -- magnet disengage; beads resuspend
    2. mix elutionReservoir with wash2Beads for 30s -- bead-eluate mixing
    3. heat elutionMix at 25c for 120s -- 2 min incubation; RNA released from bead surface
    4. heat elutionMix at 25c for 30s -- magnet re-engage; eluate separated from beads
  Collection    : RNA-containing eluate driven to recovery site within Purification Module;
                  collected by pipetting for off-device analysis.
  Eluate volume : 10 uL (vs. 30 uL conventional; 3-fold reduction in elution volume)
  Total time    : ~20 min (vs. 45 min conventional; >2-fold faster)


QC AND DOWNSTREAM ANALYSIS
---------------------------

Step 8 | RNA Yield QC  [BioScript: BB1 -> BB2/BB3 -> BB4]
  Module    : rnaYieldDetection
  Method    : NanoDrop 2000 UV-vis spectrophotometry (A260) or Qubit 2.0 fluorometry (off-device)
  Duration  : 30 s detection
  Results   :
    25 uL blood: comparable yield (p=0.16, World-to-DMF vs. conventional)
    50 uL blood: comparable yield (p=0.45)
    100 uL blood: slightly better yield with World-to-DMF (p=0.03)
    All yields within literature range for fingerstick blood volumes.
  BioScript gate (BB2/BB3):
    - Both pass and fail branches: dispose(yieldSignal)
    - elutionMix NOT disposed in this gate; must remain live for purity detect in BB4
    - 'drain' keyword not emitted by lilott8/BioScript compiler; both branches use dispose

Step 9 | RNA Purity and Integrity QC  [BioScript: BB4 -> BB5/BB6 -> BB7]
  Module    : rnaPurityDetection
  Methods   :
    - A260/A280 ratio (NanoDrop 2000, off-device); acceptable >= 1.8
    - RNA integrity number (RIN; Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer, RNA 6000 Pico Chip)
    - Fragment size distribution (28S and 18S rRNA peaks confirmed by Bioanalyzer)
  Duration  : 30 s detection
  Results   : All preparations (World-to-DMF and conventional) comparably high quality
              (Table S-1, paper); RIN values comparable; 28S and 18S peaks present in all samples.
  BioScript gate (BB5/BB6):
    - Pass: puritySignal > 0 -> dispose(elutionMix); RNA preparation verified
    - Fail: puritySignal <= 0 -> dispose(elutionMix); low purity (salt/protein carryover)
    - Terminal BB7: dispose(puritySignal); NOP

Downstream Validation:
  qRT-PCR:
    Targets     : B2M, GAPDH, PPIB (housekeeping genes)
    Template    : Total RNA from 50 uL blood; SuperScript III reverse transcriptase;
                  TaqMan reagents + SsoFast Probes Supermix (BioRad)
    Replicates  : 4 independent experiments x 3 reactions per target per RNA sample (N=3 donors)
    Result      : Ct values essentially identical regardless of preparation method (p >= 0.07);
                  no statistically significant difference; expression levels match literature.

  RNA-Seq:
    Library     : Peregrine cDNA library preparation; HAC molecular normalisation (rRNA depletion)
    Sequencer   : Illumina MiSeq, 50 bp single-end, 15 pM, duplicated run
    QC          : 95-96% reads passed Qfilter; ~99% reads mapped to hg19 (UCSC) via TopHat v2.0.9
    Abundance   : FPKM calculated by Cufflinks v2.1.1
    Similarity  : R^2 ~0.85 (Log10 FPKM scatter) between World-to-DMF and conventional;
                  no strong bias imposed by RNA preparation method (Table S-2, Figures 4 and S-4)
    Conclusion  : World-to-DMF RNA is fully compatible with both PCR-based and non-PCR-based
                  analytical methods; PCR inhibitors present in blood are eliminated/inactivated.


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : jebrail_world_to_dmf_rna_extraction.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG            : jebrail_world_to_dmf_rna_extraction_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations in seconds (s); BioScript supports s and m only; no h token
Blood arm      : 50 uL blood (130 uL lysis + 20 uL beads = 200 uL total through Bridging Droplet)
Modules        : rnaYieldDetection, rnaPurityDetection
Manifests      : WholeBlood, LysisSolution, RNABindingBeads, Wash1Solution, Wash2Solution,
                 ElutionBuffer, FluorinertFC40, PluronicF127

Bugs fixed across three compiler iterations:
  Bug 1 -- Stale variable reuse (Iteration 1 -> Iteration 2):
    wash1Mix mixed with bridgingDroplet2[0] and wash2Mix/elutionMix mixed with bridgingDroplet1[0]
    after those variables had already been consumed as inputs to their successor mix calls.
    Fix: introduced beadCapture after dispose of bridgingDroplet3; threaded wash1Beads ->
    wash2Beads as linear chain through the bead-pellet progression.

  Bug 2 -- Phantom SSA variable elutionMix2[0] (Iteration 2 -> Iteration 3):
    elutionMix disposed inside both yield QC branches (BB2/BB3); then re-read by purity
    detect in BB4 after the join. Compiler created unreachable SSA version elutionMix2[0].
    Fix: removed dispose(elutionMix) from yield gate entirely; only yieldSignal disposed in
    BB2/BB3; elutionMix kept live across the join into BB4 purity detect.

  Bug 3 -- drain not emitted by compiler (Iteration 2 -> Iteration 3):
    BioScript compiler converts drain to dispose in IR output regardless of source keyword.
    Source used drain in else branches causing source/IR semantic mismatch.
    Fix: replaced all drain with dispose in both yield and purity QC false branches.

Validated IR (Iteration 3):
  Phantom variables   : NONE
  drain in IR         : NONE
  elutionMix SSA vers.: 1 (elutionMix1[0] only; appears 7x, all legitimate)
  CFG shape           : correct (8 edges, 7 nodes, double-diamond)
  All vars assigned   : before first use -- confirmed

protocol.title: World-to-Digital-Microfluidic Interface Enabling Extraction and Purification of RNA from Human Whole Blood
protocol.platform: World-to-DMF (macroscale Extraction Module + DMF-based Purification Module, peristaltic pump driven)
protocol.sample_type: Human whole blood (fingerstick capillary range: 25, 50, or 100 uL)
protocol.objective: Inline concentration and recovery of RNA-bound magnetic beads from macroscale blood lysate via a 10 uL Bridging Droplet on a DMF device, followed by microscale wash/elution purification and downstream qRT-PCR and RNA-Seq analysis

system_modules: Extraction Module: two 500 uL microcentrifuge tubes (Reaction Chamber + Waste Chamber), peristaltic pump, Connector Tubes, Transfer Tubes
Purification Module: DMF device, 40 chromium electrode pads (6x6 mm, 40 um interelectrode gaps), Parylene-C dielectric (7 um), Teflon-AF (50 nm), 300 um air gap
Module Interface: Bridging Droplet (10 uL) formed on the Bridging Electrode at the periphery of the DMF device

reagents.filler_fluid: Fluorinert FC-40 (Sigma Chemical, St. Louis MO)
reagents.surfactant_additive: Pluronic F127, 0.1% w/v (added to Elution Buffer; Sigma Chemical)
reagents.lysis_solution: MagMAX-Blood lysis buffer (Life Technologies, Grand Island NY); 130 uL for 50 uL blood
reagents.rna_binding_beads: MagMAX silica-coated magnetic beads, 20 uL (MagMAX-Blood RNA Isolation Kit, Life Technologies)
reagents.elution_buffer: MagMAX Elution Buffer + 0.1% w/v Pluronic F127, 10 uL on-device
reagents.dielectric_coating: Parylene C dimer (Specialty Coating Systems, Indianapolis IN)
reagents.whole_blood: Human whole blood from healthy volunteer donors (ProMedDx, Norton MA)

conventional_wash_volumes_uL.note: 12-fold reagent reduction vs. conventional method (15 uL vs 150-300 uL washes)

steps.name: Device initialisation
steps.notes: FC-40 filler fluid mixed with Pluronic F127 surfactant to prime DMF air gap. Purification Module reservoirs preloaded: Wash 1 (15 uL), Wash 2 (15 uL), Elution Buffer (10 uL + 0.1% Pluronic F127). Magnetic stand adjusted so Transfer Tubes contact Bridging Electrode at ~70 degrees. AC 100 Vrms actuation ready.

steps.name: Blood specimen introduction
steps.notes: 50 uL whole blood pipetted directly into Reaction Chamber (500 uL microcentrifuge tube). Specimens from healthy volunteer donors (ProMedDx, Norton MA).

steps.name: Lysis and mixing
steps.mechanism: peristaltic pump shuttles bolus between Transfer Tube 1 and Reaction Chamber
steps.notes: MagMAX-Blood lysis buffer aspirated from Transfer Tube 1 into Reaction Chamber and actively mixed with blood specimen for 30 s. Blood lysate formed.

steps.name: RNA Binding Bead addition and incubation
steps.notes: MagMAX silica-coated magnetic beads aspirated from Transfer Tube 1 into Reaction Chamber. Mixed 30 s, then incubated 5 min at RT to allow bead-RNA binding. Total reaction volume = 200 uL (50 + 130 + 20 uL).

steps.name: World-to-DMF transition: Bridging Droplet formation and bead capture (3 passes)
steps.operation: mix (x3) + heat (x3) [abstraction of pressure-driven convective flow-through]
steps.mechanism: Peristaltic pump drives full lysate volume through the 10 uL Bridging Droplet on the Bridging Electrode (Transfer Tube 1 -> Bridging Droplet -> Transfer Tube 2) while external magnet beneath Bridging Electrode immobilises RNA-bound beads. Repeated 3x for maximum bead recovery. Supernatant sent to Waste Chamber.
steps.transport: Pressure-driven convective transport (vs. diffusion-only in conventional method); accounts for slightly higher RNA capture at 100 uL blood volume
steps.bioscript_abstraction: `mix` abstracts convective flow-through; `heat at 25c` abstracts magnet engagement/disengagement (no native magnet instruction in BioScript)
steps.stale_variable_note: bridgingDroplet1/2/3 each consumed as input to successor mix; beadCapture is a fresh handle for the bead pellet remaining on the electrode surface after dispose of supernatant

steps.name: Wash 1
steps.operation: heat (magnet disengage) + mix + heat (magnet re-engage) + dispose
steps.notes: Wash 1 Solution (15 uL) actuated onto Bridging Electrode by electrowetting. Magnet disengaged to release beads; bolus shuttled via Bridging Droplet for thorough washing. Magnet re-engaged; wash fluid sent to Waste Chamber. wash1Beads carries bead pellet to Wash 2.

steps.name: Wash 2
steps.operation: heat (magnet disengage) + mix + heat (magnet re-engage) + dispose
steps.notes: Wash 2 removes residual chaotropic salts and ethanol from Wash 1. Identical bead-release/re-immobilise sequence. wash2Beads carries bead pellet to Elution.

steps.name: Elution
steps.operation: heat (magnet disengage) + mix + heat (incubation) + heat (magnet re-engage)
steps.eluate_collection: RNA-containing eluate driven to recovery site within Purification Module; collected by pipetting for off-device analysis
steps.notes: Elution Buffer (10 uL + 0.1% Pluronic F127) actuated onto Bridging Electrode. Beads resuspended; RNA released into eluate. Beads re-immobilised; eluate collected. Total processing time ~20 min (vs. 45 min conventional).

steps.name: RNA yield QC
steps.method: NanoDrop 2000 UV-vis spectrophotometry (A260) or Qubit 2.0 fluorometry (off-device)

pass.note: elutionMix NOT disposed here; must stay live for purity detect in BB4

fail.note: compiler emits dispose for both branches regardless of drain keyword

results.note: World-to-DMF gives slightly better yield at 100 uL blood (p=0.03); comparable at 25 and 50 uL

steps.name: RNA purity and integrity QC
methods: RNA integrity number (RIN): 2100 Bioanalyzer with RNA 6000 Pico Chip (off-device)
Fragment size distribution: Bioanalyzer; 28S and 18S rRNA peaks confirmed

qRT_PCR.template: 50 uL blood total RNA; SuperScript III cDNA; TaqMan/SsoFast Probes Supermix
qRT_PCR.result: Ct values essentially identical vs. conventional (p >= 0.07); no statistically significant difference

RNA_Seq.library_prep: Peregrine cDNA library + HAC molecular normalisation (rRNA depletion)
RNA_Seq.mapping: ~99% reads mapped to hg19 (UCSC) via TopHat v2.0.9
RNA_Seq.similarity: R^2 ~0.85 (Log10 FPKM) vs. conventionally prepared RNA; no strong bias

fail.note: compiler emits dispose regardless; both branches identical in IR

performance_comparison.rna_yield: comparable (p >= 0.16 at 25 and 50 uL; slightly better at 100 uL, p=0.03)
performance_comparison.rna_purity_A260_A280: comparable; all preparations high quality (Table S-1)

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.content: device init; lysis; bead binding; 3-pass world-to-DMF bead capture; Wash 1; Wash 2; Elution; yield detect

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_4_j
basic_blocks.content: purity detect on elutionMix (still live); puritySignal gate

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_7_j
basic_blocks.content: dispose(puritySignal); NOP

bioscript_compiler_notes.ir_output: 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
bioscript_compiler_notes.duration_units: All durations in seconds (s); no h token used

bugs_fixed.description: Stale variable reuse: wash1Mix, wash2Mix, and elutionMix re-read already-consumed bridgingDroplet2[0] and bridgingDroplet1[0]
bugs_fixed.fix: Introduced beadCapture (after dispose of bridgingDroplet3), then wash1Beads and wash2Beads as a linear chain through wash and elution steps. Each variable consumed exactly once.

bugs_fixed.description: Phantom variable elutionMix2[0]: elutionMix disposed inside BB2/BB3 yield branches, then re-read in BB4 purity detect. Compiler invented unreachable SSA version elutionMix2.
bugs_fixed.fix: Removed dispose(elutionMix) from yield if/else. Only yieldSignal disposed in BB2/BB3. elutionMix kept live into BB4.

bugs_fixed.description: drain keyword not emitted by compiler; IR always produces dispose. False branches used drain in source causing source/IR mismatch.
bugs_fixed.fix: Replaced all drain with dispose in both yield and purity QC else branches. Source now matches IR exactly.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : High-Content Quantification of Single-Cell Immune Dynamics
Source Link  : https://www.cell.com/cell-reports/fulltext/S2211-1247(16)30289-3#
Paper DOI    : http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2016.03.033
Journal      : Cell Reports, Vol. 15, pp. 411-422, April 12, 2016
Authors      : Michael Junkin, Alicia J. Kaestli, Zhang Cheng, Christian Jordi,
               Cem Albayrak, Alexander Hoffmann, Savas Tay
Platform     : Two-layer PDMS microfluidic chip (continuous-flow, valve-controlled)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes an automated microfluidic system for high-content quantification
of single-cell immune dynamics in isolated RAW 264.7 mouse macrophages. The platform
delivers precisely defined dynamic inflammatory inputs (LPS, single 2 hr pulse at
500 ng/mL) to 40 individually addressable 1.35 nL PDMS cell chambers while
simultaneously and non-destructively measuring two dynamic immune readouts from the
same cells: (1) TNF cytokine secretion via on-chip bead-based fluorescent sandwich
immunoassay at 2 hr resolution across 7 time windows (0-14 hr), and (2) NF-kB (RelA)
transcription factor nuclear localization via time-lapse epifluorescence microscopy
every ~6 min throughout the 20 hr run.

Key finding: TNF secretion dynamics are highly heterogeneous and surprisingly
uncorrelated with NF-kB dynamics (Pearson r = -0.06), despite NF-kB being the
master transcription factor controlling TNF production. Computational modeling of the
LPS/TLR4 pathway identifies TRIF-mediated post-transcriptional regulation as the key
determinant of noisy and uncorrelated TNF secretion at the single-cell level.

The BioScript encoding captures the single 2 hr pulse LPS stimulation condition
(Fig 4B left panel), which mimics brief pathogen exposure, with all 7 bead time-point
assay windows and both NF-kB and TNF QC gates.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Design       : Melin & Quake two-layer PDMS microfluidic chip
Layers       : Flow layer (cell chambers, binding chambers, bead storage chambers,
               peristaltic pump channels) + Control layer (pneumatically actuated
               PDMS membrane valves for all fluid routing)
Cell chambers: 40 isolated 1.35 nL chambers, individually addressable via binary
               multiplexer; entirely isolated from one another to prevent
               contamination from neighbouring cells
Trap type    : Weir-type trap (slits without bypass) for non-adherent cells;
               cells retained during washing, stimulation, and medium harvesting
Inlets       : 16 reagent inlets controlled by automated membrane valves
Pumping      : On-chip peristaltic pump; input signal switching time < 5 s
Bead storage : 7 storage chambers per column (one per TNF time point); 4 um PDMS
               slits retain beads during loading and transfer
Binding chamber : One per column; beads moved here for medium-bead incubation
Microscope   : Nikon Eclipse Ti (inverted epifluorescence); automated stage
Enclosure    : Life Imaging Services atmospheric enclosure;
               37 C, 5% CO2, saturating humidity maintained throughout
Control SW   : Custom MATLAB GUI (Gomez-Sjoberg et al. 2007; Kellogg et al. 2014)
Imaging res. : ~6 min per full chip scan; 6 channels (GFP, brightfield + others)
Culture dur. : Up to several days without loss of viability (Fig S4)


CELL LINE
---------
Line         : RAW 264.7 (mouse macrophage)
Reporter     : RelA-GFP fusion protein (nuclear localization reports NF-kB activation)
Culture      : DMEM (Sigma D6429) + 10% FBS (Sigma F9665) + 1% GlutaMax
               (Life Technologies 35050-038) + 2% HEPES (Life Technologies 15630-056)
               Non-tissue culture treated T75 flasks; passaged every 3 days with versene
Off-chip prep: Detach with versene (Life Technologies 15040-033); filter through 20 um
               (CellTrics 04-004-2325); resuspend at 1e5-3.5e5 cells/mL in CO2-
               equilibrated medium
Source       : Ian Fraser Lab, NIH, USA


REAGENTS
--------
Surface coating  : Pluronic F-127 (Life Technologies P6867), 2 mg/mL in DI water;
                   prevents protein adsorption and non-specific cell/bead adhesion
Stimulant        : LPS (Sigma L4524), 500 ng/mL in culture medium;
                   single 2 hr pulse; switchover time < 5 s
Wash buffer      : PBS-Tween (0.563 mg/mL); used between sandwich assay steps
TNF capture beads: Spherotech SVP-100-4 (10.3 um streptavidin-functionalized);
                   biotinylated anti-TNF Ab (United States Biological T9160-14)
                   coupled in PBS pH 5.5; one bead per storage chamber per time point
TNF calibrant    : Life Technologies PMC3014; aliquoted in PBS + 1 mg/mL BSA;
                   dissolved in macrophage medium for on-chip calibrations
Detection Ab     : genwaybio GWB-489500 at 3.19 ug/mL; 30 min with mixing
Secondary Ab     : United States Biological I1903-12H (fluorescent) at 3.3 ug/mL;
                   30 min with mixing
Multiplexed kits : BD Biosciences 552364, 560232, 558345 (IL-6, IL-10, IL-12,
                   MCP-1, IFN-gamma multiplexed detection; PE-tagged secondary Abs)


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Chip Surface Preparation
  Reagents   : Pluronic F-127 (2 mg/mL in DI water), PBS
  BS var     : devicePrimed
  Operation  : mix (abstracts automated MATLAB control script rinse sequence)
  Duration   : 720m (12 hr overnight; IR: 43200.0 SECOND)
  Purpose    : Coat all internal surfaces except cell chambers with Pluronic F-127
               to reduce protein adsorption and prevent non-specific cell and bead
               adhesion to PDMS walls; rinse extensively with PBS before loading

Step 2 | Cell Loading
  Reagents   : RAW 264.7 macrophages, devicePrimed
  BS var     : cellsLoaded
  Operation  : mix (abstracts flow-through weir trapping via binary multiplexer)
  Duration   : 10m (IR: 600.0 SECOND)
  Cells/mL   : 1e5-3.5e5 (continuous stirring in syringe during loading)
  Load time  : < 10 min for all 40 chambers
  Notes      : Weir-type trap (slits without bypass) retains non-adherent macrophages;
               individual chambers entirely isolated from one another

Step 3 | Post-Loading Equilibration
  Reagents   : CultureMedium, cellsLoaded
  BS var     : cellsEq
  Operation  : mix + heat at 37c
  Duration   : 10m mix + 120m heat (IR: 600.0 + 7200.0 SECOND)
  Notes      : Fresh medium pumped intermittently via peristaltic pump; cells
               equilibrate inside sealed chambers; 37 C / 5% CO2 / saturating
               humidity maintained by atmospheric enclosure

Step 4 | Baseline TNF Bead Capture (t = 0-2 hr, pre-LPS)
  Reagents   : CultureMedium, TNF_CaptureBeads, PBSTween
  BS vars    : sampleT0, bead1Bound, bead1Washed
  Operation  : mix (medium sample, 120m) + mix (bead binding, 90m) + mix (rinse, 5m)
  Duration   : 120m sample + 90m bind + 5m rinse
               IR: 7200.0 + 5400.0 + 300.0 SECOND
  Notes      : Pre-stimulus baseline; peristaltic pump transfers medium surrounding
               cells to binding chamber; bead moved from storage, mixed circularly
               for 90 min to reach steady-state capture (Fig 2A); rinsed with
               PBS-Tween to remove interfering molecules; returned to storage.
               bead1Washed is held alive through the entire protocol as TNF QC
               gate target in BB5/BB6

Step 5 | LPS Stimulation -- 2 hr Pulse
  Reagents   : LPS_500ngmL (500 ng/mL), bead1Washed (cell-thread carrier)
  BS var     : cellsStim
  Operation  : mix + heat at 37c
  Duration   : 120m LPS + 120m heat (IR: 7200.0 + 7200.0 SECOND)
  Notes      : LPS injected via 16-inlet binary multiplexer; switching time < 5 s;
               single 2 hr pulse condition (Fig 4B left panel) mimics brief pathogen
               exposure; bead1Washed carries cell-thread state into LPS step as
               the ownership chain carrier from STEP 4

Step 6 | LPS Washout
  Reagents   : CultureMedium, cellsStim
  BS var     : cellsWashed
  Operation  : mix
  Duration   : 10m (IR: 600.0 SECOND)
  Notes      : Multiplexer switches back to medium inlet; LPS-free medium flows
               through chamber; switchover time < 5 s

Step 7 | TNF Bead Capture -- Time Point 1 (0-2 hr post-LPS)
  Reagents   : CultureMedium, TNF_CaptureBeads, PBSTween
  BS vars    : sampleTP1, bead2Bound, bead2Washed
  Operation  : mix (120m) + mix (90m) + mix (5m) + heat (120m) at 37c
  Duration   : 120m + 90m + 5m + 120m (IR: 7200.0 + 5400.0 + 300.0 + 7200.0 SECOND)

Step 8 | TNF Bead Capture -- Time Point 2 (2-4 hr post-LPS)
  Reagents   : CultureMedium, TNF_CaptureBeads, PBSTween
  BS vars    : sampleTP2, bead3Bound, bead3Washed
  Operation  : mix (120m) + mix (90m) + mix (5m) + heat (120m) at 37c
  Duration   : 120m + 90m + 5m + 120m (IR: 7200.0 + 5400.0 + 300.0 + 7200.0 SECOND)

Step 9 | TNF Bead Capture -- Time Point 3 (4-6 hr post-LPS)
  Reagents   : CultureMedium, TNF_CaptureBeads, PBSTween
  BS vars    : sampleTP3, bead4Bound, bead4Washed
  Operation  : mix (120m) + mix (90m) + mix (5m) + heat (120m) at 37c
  Duration   : 120m + 90m + 5m + 120m (IR: 7200.0 + 5400.0 + 300.0 + 7200.0 SECOND)

Step 10 | TNF Bead Capture -- Time Point 4 (6-8 hr post-LPS)
  Reagents   : CultureMedium, TNF_CaptureBeads, PBSTween
  BS vars    : sampleTP4, bead5Bound, bead5Washed
  Operation  : mix (120m) + mix (90m) + mix (5m) + heat (120m) at 37c
  Duration   : 120m + 90m + 5m + 120m (IR: 7200.0 + 5400.0 + 300.0 + 7200.0 SECOND)

Step 11 | TNF Bead Capture -- Time Point 5 (8-10 hr post-LPS)
  Reagents   : CultureMedium, TNF_CaptureBeads, PBSTween
  BS vars    : sampleTP5, bead6Bound, bead6Washed
  Operation  : mix (120m) + mix (90m) + mix (5m) + heat (120m) at 37c
  Duration   : 120m + 90m + 5m + 120m (IR: 7200.0 + 5400.0 + 300.0 + 7200.0 SECOND)

Step 12 | TNF Bead Capture -- Time Point 6 (10-12 hr post-LPS)
  Reagents   : CultureMedium, TNF_CaptureBeads, PBSTween
  BS vars    : sampleTP6, bead7Bound, bead7Washed
  Operation  : mix (120m) + mix (90m) + mix (5m)
  Duration   : 120m + 90m + 5m (IR: 7200.0 + 5400.0 + 300.0 SECOND)
  Notes      : Final medium sampling window; bead7Washed carries cell-thread
               terminal state into sandwich assay completion step

Step 13 | Sandwich Assay Completion -- Detection Antibodies
  Reagents   : TNF_DetectionAntibody (3.19 ug/mL), SecondaryFluorescentAntibody (3.3 ug/mL)
  BS vars    : detStep, sandwichDone
  Operation  : mix (30m) + mix (30m)
  Duration   : 30m + 30m (IR: 1800.0 + 1800.0 SECOND)
  Catalogs   : Detection Ab: genwaybio GWB-489500; Secondary Ab: USB I1903-12H
  Notes      : Applied over all 7 stored beads simultaneously after all time-point
               captures complete; beads imaged in storage chambers; fluorescence
               intensity correlated to on-chip calibration curve (R2 = 0.9984, Fig 2B)

Step 14 | NF-kB (RelA) Localization -- Aggregate QC Readout
  BS var     : nfkbSignal
  Module     : nfkbLocalizationDetection
  Input      : sandwichDone
  Duration   : 30s (IR: 30.0 SECOND)
  Threshold  : > 2 SD above pre-stimulus baseline = NF-kB+
  NF-kB+ pct : ~93.6% of cells (n = 46) following 2 hr LPS pulse (Fig 6A)
  Pearson r  : -0.06 (NF-kB amplitude vs. TNF amplitude; quantitatively uncorrelated)
  Notes      : Continuous time-lapse imaging throughout 20 hr run; MATLAB image
               analysis computes nuclear/cytoplasmic RelA-GFP ratio per frame;
               nfkbLocalizationDetection abstracts the binary nuclear-peak
               determination; consumes sandwichDone
  Branch     : nfkbSignal > 0  -> BB2 (bsbbif_2_t): dispose(sandwichDone)  [NF-kB+]
               nfkbSignal <= 0 -> BB3 (bsbbif_3_f): drain(sandwichDone)    [NF-kB-]
               Both -> BB4 (bsbbif_4_j): join; dispose(nfkbSignal)

Step 15 | TNF Secretion Fluorescence Readout
  BS var     : tnfSignal
  Module     : tnfSecretionDetection
  Input      : bead1Washed (baseline bead; held alive since STEP 4)
  Duration   : 30s (IR: 30.0 SECOND)
  LOD        : ~60,000 TNF molecules
  Calibration: R2 = 0.9984 (on-chip; Fig 2B)
  TNF+ pct   : ~93.5% of cells produce detectable TNF
  Mean total : ~4.9e6 TNF molecules over 14 hr; log-normal distribution (Fig 5C)
  Notes      : Bead fluorescence imaged in storage chambers; tnfSecretionDetection
               returns > 0 if any time-point bead exceeds LOD; bead1Washed used
               as QC gate key (consistent with moazami assaySignal40 pattern)
  Branch     : tnfSignal > 0  -> BB5 (bsbbif_5_t): dispose(bead1Washed)   [TNF+]
               tnfSignal <= 0 -> BB6 (bsbbif_6_f): drain(bead1Washed)     [TNF-]
               Both -> BB7 (bsbbif_7_j): terminal; dispose(tnfSignal); NOP


SINGLE-CELL RESPONSE HETEROGENEITY
------------------------------------
NF-kB subpopulations (n = 42, 2 hr LPS pulse):
  1 Peak     : n = 7   (single NF-kB peak during stimulation)
  Late Rise  : n = 9   (single peak followed by later secondary rise)
  Multi Peak : n = 23  (single peak followed by sustained oscillations)
  Minimal    : n = 3   (no or minimal NF-kB response)

TNF secretion subpopulations (n = 46, 2 hr LPS pulse):
  1 Peak     : n = 21  (single temporally limited TNF pulse, within 2 hr)
  Extended   : n = 8   (TNF release for extended period, within 4 hr)
  Other      : n = 14  (multi-peak or atypical temporal profiles)
  No secr.   : n = 3   (no detectable TNF above LOD in any 2 hr window)

NF-kB / TNF cross-correlation (Fig 6A, qualitative):
  NF-kB+ / TNF+ : 87.1%   NF-kB+ / TNF- : 6.5%
  NF-kB- / TNF+ : 6.5%    NF-kB- / TNF- : 0%
  Quantitative Pearson r (amplitude) = -0.06 (no correlation)
  TRIF activity vs. TNF amplitude Pearson r = 0.88 (strong correlation, model)


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file  : junkin_single_cell_immune_dynamics.bs
IR file         : junkin_single_cell_immune_dynamics.ir
DAG file        : junkin_single_cell_immune_dynamics_main_dag.dot
BB blocks file  : junkin_single_cell_immune_dynamics_main_basic_blocks.dot
Compiler        : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based, github.com/lilott8/BioScript)
Modules         : nfkbLocalizationDetection, tnfSecretionDetection
Manifests       : RAW2647_Macrophages, PluronicF127, PBS, CultureMedium,
                  LPS_500ngmL, TNF_CaptureBeads, TNF_DetectionAntibody,
                  SecondaryFluorescentAntibody, PBSTween

CFG topology    : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 8 CFG edges; two-level diamond
  BB1 main           (entry; S1-S14)
  BB2 bsbbif_2_t     (NF-kB pass: dispose sandwichDone)
  BB3 bsbbif_3_f     (NF-kB fail: drain sandwichDone)
  BB4 bsbbif_4_j     (join; dispose nfkbSignal; detect tnfSecretionDetection)
  BB5 bsbbif_5_t     (TNF pass: dispose bead1Washed)
  BB6 bsbbif_6_f     (TNF fail: drain bead1Washed)
  BB7 bsbbif_7_j     (terminal; dispose tnfSignal; NOP)

Duration conversions (h token unsupported; all durations in m or s):
  720m  (overnight rinse)            -> IR: 43200.0 SECOND
  120m  (2 hr sampling/stimulation)  -> IR:  7200.0 SECOND
   90m  (bead binding)               -> IR:  5400.0 SECOND
   30m  (antibody incubation)        -> IR:  1800.0 SECOND
   10m  (cell loading / LPS washout) -> IR:   600.0 SECOND
    5m  (bead PBS-Tween rinse)       -> IR:   300.0 SECOND
   30s  (detect operations)          -> IR:    30.0 SECOND

Known compiler behaviors applied:
  - drain in .bs source correctly lowered to dispose() in IR (known compiler bug;
    .bs source is semantically correct and preserved as-is)
  - True-branch blocks (bsbbif_2_t, bsbbif_5_t) emit no unconditional jump
    instruction in IR text; DOT graph resolves branch edges correctly
  - h duration token unsupported; all long durations converted to m

Cell-thread design pattern:
  mix is a consuming operation on both operands in BioScript. The cell state is
  modelled as a linear fluid variable re-produced at each pump cycle by mixing
  with the incoming medium or bead-wash product, maintaining a single ownership
  chain across 14 sequential steps without double-consumption.

bead1Washed design:
  The baseline bead variable (bead1Washed, produced in STEP 4) is intentionally
  held alive through the entire main block to serve as the TNF QC gate target in
  BB5/BB6, after the NF-kB gate has resolved at BB4. This mirrors the
  assaySignal40 pattern used in the moazami_world_to_chip_dmf reference file.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Quantitative Multiparameter Measuring of Dynamic Single-Cell Immune Responses
Source Link  : https://q-bio.org/w/images/3/34/Quantitative_multiparameter_measuring_of_dynamic_single-cell_immune_responses.pdf
Paper DOI    : N/A
Journal      : IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Conference (EMBC), 2014
Platform     : Custom PDMS microfluidic device with single-cell trapping chambers,
               microfluidic valve-controlled dynamic stimulus delivery, and
               on-chip bead-based fluorescent sandwich immunoassay


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a microfluidic platform for dynamic, multiparameter, non-destructive
measurement of immune cell responses at the single-cell level. The system isolates individual
macrophages in distinct trapping chambers, delivers arbitrary temporal stimulus profiles
(brief pulses in seconds to prolonged inputs spanning hours), and simultaneously measures
four functional parameters from the same single cell throughout the experiment:

  1. NF-kB nuclear translocation (real-time transcription factor activation via GFP fusion)
  2. Cytokine and protein secretion (on-chip bead-based fluorescent sandwich assay, multiplexed)
  3. Cell migration (centroid tracking from bright-field time-lapse)
  4. Cell morphology (area, circularity, aspect ratio from bright-field time-lapse)

All four measurements are non-destructive and conducted dynamically on the same single cells.
The resulting large, multiparameter dataset is used to construct predictive models of immune
input-output relationships governing internal and external cellular reactions during an
immune response.

Cell line: RAW264.7 macrophages expressing an NF-kB-GFP fusion reporter protein.
Stimuli:   LPS (brief pulse) and TNF (prolonged exposure), delivered sequentially
           via programmable upstream valve actuation to model physiological stimulus dynamics.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Material      : PDMS (polydimethylsiloxane), soft-lithography fabricated
Configuration : Single-cell isolation chambers in a serpentine trapping channel
                integrated with an on-chip bead-based assay zone
Trapping      : Hydrodynamic single-cell trapping with custom trap geometry;
                trapping efficiency verified by bright-field imaging
Flow control  : Upstream microfluidic valves for programmable stimulus switching;
                arbitrary temporal input profiles (seconds to hours)
Imaging       : Inverted fluorescence microscope; time-lapse acquisition every 3-5 min

Measurement channels:
  - GFP (NF-kB reporter): excitation ~488 nm; emission ~510 nm (nuclear translocation)
  - Bead assay fluorescence: multiple spectrally distinct channels (multiplexed cytokines)
  - Bright-field: cell migration centroid tracking and morphology analysis


CELL LINE
---------
RAW264.7 macrophages (murine, ATCC TIB-71) stably expressing NF-kB-GFP fusion protein.
  Culture conditions : DMEM + 10% FBS, 37 C, 5% CO2
  Pre-loading prep   : Single-cell suspension in culture media, ~1e6 cells/mL
  NF-kB reporter     : GFP fused to NF-kB subunit (p65 or p50); cytoplasmic at rest,
                       nuclear upon activation; N/C ratio computed per frame per cell


STIMULI
-------
LPS (Lipopolysaccharide, E. coli):
  Type          : Pathogen-associated molecular pattern (PAMP); TLR4 agonist
  Input profile : Brief pulse (~60 s representative; tunable from seconds to minutes)
  Delivery      : Upstream valve switched to LPS reservoir; flow carries LPS to chambers

TNF (Tumour Necrosis Factor):
  Type          : Pro-inflammatory cytokine; TNFR1/TNFR2 agonist
  Input profile : Prolonged sustained exposure (~60 min representative)
  Delivery      : Upstream valve switched to TNF reservoir after LPS pulse
  Purpose       : Models cytokine-driven NF-kB reactivation (second activation wave)

Sequential LPS -> TNF delivery allows independent characterisation of PAMP-triggered
and cytokine-triggered NF-kB dynamics in the same single cell without destruction.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Device Priming
  Reagents  : PBS buffer (x2 volumes)
  Operation : Mix and flow through all channels
  Duration  : 5 min (~300 s)
  Purpose   : Removes air bubbles; passivates PDMS channel surfaces to
              minimise non-specific cell adhesion prior to loading.

Step 2 | Hydrodynamic Single-Cell Loading and Trapping
  Cell line     : RAW264.7 macrophages (NF-kB-GFP)
  Concentration : ~1e6 cells/mL in culture media
  Operation     : Flow-through trapping (abstracted as mix in BioScript)
  Duration      : ~2 s (flow event)
  Trap design   : Custom geometry; hydrodynamic resistance routes single cells
                  into isolation chambers; occupied trap blocks second-cell entry
  Notes         : BioScript mix abstracts channel-flow hydrodynamic trapping;
                  no bulk reagent mixing occurs at this step. Trapping efficiency
                  verified by bright-field inspection of chambers.

Step 3 | Channel Wash (Untrapped Cell Removal)
  Reagents  : PBS buffer flush
  Operation : mix (channel-flow wash abstraction)
  Duration  : 30 s
  Purpose   : Removes excess untrapped cells from channels. Only single cells
              retained in trapping chambers proceed to stimulation.

Step 4 | Pre-Stimulus Baseline Imaging
  Operation     : Heat hold at 37 C (standard culture temperature)
  Duration      : 15 min (900 s)
  Readout       : Bright-field and GFP fluorescence images at t=0
  NF-kB state   : Cytoplasmic (inactive baseline)
  Migration ref : Cell centroid coordinates logged (x0, y0)
  Morphology ref: Area, circularity, aspect ratio at t=0

Step 5 | LPS Stimulus Delivery (Brief Pulse)
  Reagents      : LPS_Stimulus
  Operation     : mix (valve-controlled flow switching; LPS pulse to chambers)
  Duration      : 60 s (representative short pulse; tunable)
  Profile       : Brief pulse -- seconds-range input
  Receptor      : TLR4 on RAW264.7 surface
  Expected resp : Rapid NF-kB nuclear translocation within 10-15 min post-stimulus

Step 6 | TNF Stimulus Delivery (Prolonged Exposure)
  Reagents      : TNF_Stimulus
  Operation     : mix (valve-controlled flow switching; TNF flow to chambers)
  Duration      : 60 min (3600 s)
  Profile       : Sustained prolonged input
  Receptor      : TNFR1/TNFR2
  Expected resp : Second wave of NF-kB activation; oscillatory dynamics possible

Step 7 | Dynamic NF-kB Imaging and Multiparameter Observation
  Operation         : Heat at 37 C (imaging window) + detect nfkbActivationDetection
  Imaging duration  : 4 h (240 min; 14400 s modelled as heat hold)
  Detection duration: 5 min (300 s)
  Detection module  : nfkbActivationDetection
  Imaging interval  : Every 3-5 min (time-lapse)
  NF-kB readout     : Nuclear/cytoplasmic GFP ratio per cell per frame
  Co-measurements   : Migration vectors (centroid tracking, same frames)
                      Morphology descriptors (area, circularity, aspect ratio, same frames)
  Nature            : Non-destructive; cells remain viable throughout
  Module abstracts  : Fluorescence acquisition, nuclear mask segmentation,
                      N/C ratio computation, migration vector extraction,
                      morphology descriptor calculation

  QC gate (NF-kB):
    Pass (nfkbSignal > 0)  : NF-kB nuclear translocation detected; proceed to secretion assay
    Fail (nfkbSignal <= 0) : No activation detected; drain stimulated droplet

Step 8 | Periodic Conditioned Medium Sampling
  Reagents         : CultureMedia (fresh)
  Operation        : mix (medium exchange + supernatant collection)
  Sampling interval: Every 30-60 min throughout stimulation window
  Sample volume    : ~50 nL per time point
  Duration         : 30 s per exchange event
  Non-destructive  : Fresh media returned after each sample; cells remain viable
  Purpose          : Captures time-resolved secretion data matched to NF-kB and
                     migration traces of the same single cell

Step 9 | On-Chip Bead-Based Cytokine Capture
  Reagents          : BeadConjugatedAntibody, conditioned medium sample
  Operation         : mix + heat at 25 C
  Incubation        : 60 min (3600 s) at room temperature (25 C)
  Bead type         : Antibody-conjugated capture beads; spectrally distinct per cytokine
  Targets           : TNF, IL-6, MCP-1, and other secreted proteins (multiplexed)
  Configuration     : On-chip assay zone; no off-chip transfer required
  Notes             : Sandwich complex forms on bead surface; multiple cytokines captured
                      simultaneously from the same ~50 nL sample volume.

Step 10 | Detection Antibody Addition (Sandwich Completion)
  Reagents   : FluorescentSandwichReagent (fluorescent secondary antibody)
  Operation  : mix + heat at 25 C
  Incubation : 30 min (1800 s) at room temperature
  Readout    : Fluorescence intensity per bead cluster proportional to
               secreted protein concentration (quantitative vs. standard curve)
  Targets    : Same multiplexed panel as Step 9

Step 11 | Bead Assay Wash
  Reagents   : WashBuffer
  Operation  : mix
  Duration   : 5 min (300 s)
  Purpose    : Removes excess unbound fluorescent detection antibody;
               reduces background signal to enable quantification at
               single-cell secretion levels (pM to nM range)

Step 12 | Fluorescence Detection of Cytokine Secretion
  Operation         : detect cytokineSecretionDetection
  Detection duration: 60 s
  Detection module  : cytokineSecretionDetection
  Module abstracts  : Bead cluster fluorescence acquisition, bead segmentation,
                      per-channel intensity quantification, multi-cytokine spectral
                      demultiplexing, concentration calibration against standard curve
  Output            : Quantitative secreted protein levels per single cell per time point
  Dynamic range     : pM to nM

  QC gate (Secretion):
    Pass (secretionSignal > 0)  : Cytokine signal above detection threshold; dispose assay
    Fail (secretionSignal <= 0) : Signal below LOD or assay failure; drain


MULTIPARAMETER DATASET
----------------------
Each single-cell experiment yields four co-registered time series:

  Parameter          | Method                  | Temporal Resolution | Nature
  -------------------|-------------------------|---------------------|--------------------
  NF-kB activation   | Nuclear/cytoplasmic GFP | 3-5 min             | Non-destructive
  Cytokine secretion | On-chip bead assay      | 30-60 min           | Non-destructive
  Migration          | Centroid tracking       | 3-5 min             | Non-destructive
  Morphology         | Image analysis          | 3-5 min             | Non-destructive

Dataset is used to construct predictive models of immune input-output relationships,
accurately depicting the overall system of cellular reactions during an immune response.


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file  : junkin_tay_singlecell_immune.bs
Compiler        : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output       : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG file        : junkin_tay_singlecell_immune_main_dag.dot
Duration units  : All durations converted to seconds (s) or minutes (m) for compiler
                  compatibility (BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported)
                  4 h imaging window  -> 240m  (IR: 14400.0 SECOND)
                  60 min bead capture -> 60m   (IR: 3600.0 SECOND)
                  30 min detection Ab -> 30m   (IR: 1800.0 SECOND)
                  5 min bead wash     -> 5m    (IR: 300.0 SECOND)
                  15 min baseline     -> 15m   (IR: 900.0 SECOND)
Modules         : nfkbActivationDetection
                  cytokineSecretionDetection
                  migrationMorphologyDetection
Trapping note   : mix statements in Steps 2 and 3 abstract hydrodynamic single-cell
                  trapping and channel-flow wash events (not DMF electrode mixing).
Heat note       : heat statements model 37 C culture-temperature incubation (baseline,
                  imaging window) and 25 C room-temperature bead assay incubations.
ASCII note      : All comment text restricted to ASCII characters. ANTLR4 FileStream
                  reads .bs files as ASCII; non-ASCII characters (e.g. diacritics such
                  as in "Savas" or "Zurich") cause UnicodeDecodeError at compile time
                  and must be replaced with ASCII equivalents before compilation.
CFG structure   : BB1 (main/entry) -> BB2/BB3 (NF-kB gate) -> BB4 (join) ->
                  BB5/BB6 (secretion gate) -> BB7 (terminal/NOP)

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : High-Throughput Microfluidic Single-Cell Analysis Pipeline for Studies of Signaling Dynamics
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/nprot.2014.120
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/nprot.2014.120
Journal      : Nature Protocols, Vol. 9, No. 7 (2014), pp. 1713-1726
Platform     : Valve-actuated multilayer PDMS microfluidic cell culture chip (continuous-flow; not DMF)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a complete end-to-end pipeline for microfluidics-based single-cell analysis,
combining live-cell imaging, automated image analysis, and downstream high-throughput gene expression
profiling. The system enables a single researcher to generate up to 1 million data points on single-cell
protein localization within one week, across 48 predesigned experimental conditions using different
signaling molecules, doses, timings, and combinations.

The pipeline comprises five major phases:
  1. Chip fabrication and system setup (Steps 1-15)
  2. Chip surface treatment and cell loading (Steps 16-33)
  3. Multiplexed cell stimulation and live-cell imaging (Steps 34-43)
  4. On-chip cell retrieval and high-throughput microfluidic qPCR (Steps 44-60)
  5. Automated image analysis and data extraction (Steps 59-66)

The chip described (Cell Culture Chip; Gomez-Sjoberg et al., Anal. Chem. 2007) contains 96
independently controllable 35-nL chambers. Each chamber can culture 1-1,000 mammalian cells.
Up to 16 reagent inputs are combined by an on-chip herringbone mixer and delivered to selected
chambers by an on-chip peristaltic pump (~0.35 nL per pump cycle). Programmable valve scripts
automate chamber surface treatment, cell loading, feeding, stimulation, staining, and retrieval
without researcher intervention.

Example applications demonstrated in the paper: NF-kB nuclear translocation dynamics in NIH3T3
mouse fibroblasts (p65-dsRed + H2B-GFP) and RAW264.7 mouse macrophages (p65-GFP + H2B-mCherry)
under TNF-alpha and LPS stimulation, with downstream 48-gene expression profiling at 30-min
intervals over 12 h using the Fluidigm BioMark 48.48 Dynamic Array (up to 9,216 simultaneous
qPCR measurements).


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Chip design   : Two PDMS layers (multilayer soft lithography) bonded and mounted on
                PDMS-coated 50 x 75 mm glass slide.
Flow layer    : Contains cells and reagents; channels with rounded cross-section
                (positive photoresist, SU-8); positioned above control layer.
Control layer : Creates elastomeric membrane valves by deflecting thin PDMS membrane
                under pneumatic pressure; channels with rectangular cross-section
                (negative photoresist); spin-coated ~30 um thick at 2500 rpm.
Chambers      : 96 independent chambers; ~1 x 1 mm2 area, 35 um height, ~35 nL volume.
                Sieve valves at each chamber entrance and exit trap cells >20 um diameter.
                Four PDMS pillars inside each chamber prevent ceiling collapse.

Valve control : 48-valve system (six 8-valve solenoid manifolds); USB controller boxes;
                pressurized air at 20-30 psi. MATLAB or LabVIEW scripting for automation.
Peristaltic pump: 3-valve in-series sequence; ~0.35 nL per cycle; 30-60 nL/min at
                0.05-0.1 s valve delay.
Reagent inputs: Up to 16 vials; pressurized with 5% CO2 at 3-10 psi (200-700 mbar);
                PTFE tubing for reagents; PEEK tubing for cells.
Mixer         : On-chip herringbone mixer combines reagents before chamber delivery.
                InPurge PBS line clears manifold between inputs.

Microscope    : Inverted automated fluorescence (Leica DMI6000B or Nikon Ti-E);
                stage incubation at 37 C, 5% CO2, >95% humidity.
                Wide-field preferred (speed + low phototoxicity vs confocal).
                20x long-distance objective for nuclear-cytoplasm dynamics.
Software      : muManager (open-source) or manufacturer software for time-lapse control.


CELL LINES
----------
- NIH3T3 mouse fibroblasts (p65-dsRed + H2B-GFP): NF-kB translocation reporter line.
  Culture: DMEM + 10% v/v FBS; 37 C, 5% CO2.
  Loading target: ~150 cells per chamber (~80% confluence at experiment start).
- RAW264.7 mouse macrophages (p65-GFP + H2B-mCherry): LPS-responsive macrophage line.
  Culture: DMEM + 10% v/v FBS; 37 C, 5% CO2.
  Loading target: ~200-300 cells per chamber.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Chip Surface Treatment -- Pluronic Blocking (Steps 24-29)
  Reagents  : PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free), Pluronic F-127 (0.2% w/v in PBS)
  Operation : Mix; flow through non-chamber surfaces
  Duration  : ~60 min (15 min air removal + 1 h incubation)
  Inlet     : Input #1 (Pluronic); InPurge (PBS)
  Purpose   : Blocks non-specific mammalian cell adhesion to PDMS channel walls.
              Air removed by applying flow pressure to closed channel, forcing air
              through PDMS matrix. Pluronic then incubated 1 h in non-chamber areas.

Step 2 | PBS Wash -- Pluronic Removal (Step 30)
  Reagents  : PBS
  Operation : Mix; pressure-driven flow across all non-chamber surfaces
  Duration  : 30 min
  Notes     : CRITICAL STEP. Pluronic must be completely washed out before fibronectin
              coating. Residual Pluronic entering chambers prevents cell adhesion.

Step 3 | Fibronectin Chamber Coating (Step 31)
  Reagents  : Fibronectin (100 ug/mL in PBS)
  Operation : Mix; flow into non-chamber areas first (10 min), then open ChIn/ChOut
              valves in GUI to allow fibronectin to flood chambers
  Duration  : 2 h to overnight (120-720 min; 720m used in BioScript)
  Notes     : Fibronectin displaces PBS and air in chambers. Incubation overnight
              gives reliable ECM coating for NIH3T3 and RAW264.7 cell lines.

Step 4 | Cell Loading (Steps 32-33)
  Cell line     : NIH3T3 mouse fibroblasts (or RAW264.7 macrophages)
  Concentration : 5e5 to 2e6 cells/mL; single-cell suspension
  Volume        : 25-50 uL consumed for 96 chambers
  Pressurization: 5% CO2 at 3-5 psi; PEEK tubing to CellsIn port
  Duration      : ~60 min attachment; heat at 37 C for 60 min
  Options       :
    (A) Automated: scripted seeding rounds with 10x phase-contrast imaging and
        intensity threshold cell counting; repeat until target count reached
        (150 fibroblasts or 200 macrophages per chamber).
    (B) Manual: visual estimation; sequential chamber seeding; repeat as needed.
  Notes         : Cells adhere to fibronectin within minutes. PEEK tubing prevents
                  clumping. Pass cell suspension through 40 um strainer before loading.

Step 5-10 | Cell Feeding -- 6 Rounds at 2-h Intervals (Steps 35-37)
  Reagents  : CellMedium (DMEM + 10% FBS)
  Operation : Mix (1 min per round; on-chip pump 30 cycles x ~0.35 nL = ~10.5 nL)
  Volume    : 30% chamber volume exchanged per round
  Interval  : 120 min (2 h) between rounds; heat at 37 C for 120m
  Rounds    : 6 rounds unrolled in BioScript (t = 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 h)
  Imaging   : Phase-contrast images acquired at each feeding location to monitor
              cell health and growth (10x magnification; Perfect Focus System recommended)
  Notes     : 6 rounds cover ~12 h pre-stimulation imaging phase. BioScript has no
              loop construct; feeding rounds are unrolled explicitly as distinct variables.
              Dense cultures may require 1-h intervals; sparse cultures 3-h intervals.

Step 11 | TNF-alpha Stimulation (Steps 38-41)
  Reagents  : TNF_Stimulus (0.01-100 ng/mL in CellMedium)
  Operation : Mix; pressure-driven full chamber flush (not pump cycling)
  Duration  : 10-min pulse; 60-min washout with CellMedium
  Delivery  : PTFE tubing; 5% CO2 at 7 psi
  Notes     : CRITICAL STEP: log exact timing of each stimulus delivery for alignment
              with image acquisition timestamps. Additional TNF pulses (e.g. at t=60,
              120 min) can be added by unrolling further stimulation cycles. Single
              representative 10-min pulse is encoded in this .bs file. LPS used instead
              of TNF for RAW264.7 macrophage experiments (Sigma L4524).

Step 12 | Live-Cell Fluorescence Imaging (Steps 41-43)
  Module    : liveCellImagingDetection
  Duration  : 300 min (5 h post-stimulation)
  Channels  : GFP (H2B nuclear label, segmentation seed) + dsRed (p65 NF-kB reporter)
  Objective : 20x long-distance
  Readout   : Nuclear p65-dsRed intensity / cytoplasmic p65-dsRed intensity per cell
              per frame; NF-kB translocation and oscillation dynamics extracted.
  Analysis  : CellProfiler pipeline:
              IdentifyPrimaryObjects (nuclei from H2B-GFP),
              IdentifySecondaryObjects (cytoplasm from p65-dsRed),
              MeasureObjectIntensity, ExportToSpreadsheet, TrackObjects.
              Alternatively: MATLAB Image Processing Toolbox custom routines.
  Notes     : liveCellImagingDetection module abstracts the full CellProfiler/MATLAB
              image analysis pipeline (Steps 59-66). Imaging runs as an independent
              process in parallel with the chip stimulation MATLAB script.

Step 13 | Cell Retrieval -- Trypsinization and Lysis (Steps 44-48)
  Reagents  : Trypsin-EDTA (0.05% w/v 1x), LysisBuffer (CellsDirect resuspension
              buffer + lysis enhancer; freshly prepared on ice)
  Trypsin   : Delivered to each chamber; 1-3 min detachment; ~90% retrieval efficiency
  Collection: PEEK tubing ~10 cm; cells deposited into 96-well plate, 5 uL lysis buffer
              per well (pre-loaded). Each well sealed with tape immediately after.
  PBS flush : 3 uL PBS between chambers; prevents cross-contamination.
  Notes     : Prepare 96-well plate with lysis buffer before retrieval. For time-course
              experiments at 30-min intervals over 24 h: 48 chambers, one per time point.

Step 14 | RT-STA Reaction Assembly (Steps 49-53)
  Reagents  : CellsDirect_RTmix (2x), TaqMan_PrimerPool (0.2x),
              SuperScriptPlatinumTaq, TEBuffer
  Reaction volume: 10 uL per well
  Components per reaction:
    - 5 uL   2x CellsDirect reaction mix
    - 1.5 uL TE buffer
    - 2.5 uL 0.2x TaqMan primer pool (48 assays at 45 nM each)
    - 1.0 uL SuperScript III / Platinum Taq mix
    - 1.0 uL cell lysate (added at Step 53)
  Primer pool: Each TaqMan assay (20x, 18 uM) diluted 100x in TE to 0.2x (180 nM);
               pooled in 1.5 mL tube; 1.5 uL per assay in final volume.
  Notes     : CRITICAL: 2x CellsDirect reaction mix must be fully thawed on ice and
              thoroughly mixed. Plate may be stored at -20 C for up to 3 months before
              adding lysate.

Step 15 | RT-STA Thermal Cycling (Step 54)
  Operation : Four sequential heat steps on rtStaReaction variable
  Thermal protocol:
    RT step           : 50 C, 15 min        (IR: 900.0 SECOND)
    Taq activation    : 95 C, 2 min         (IR: 120.0 SECOND)
    14 STA cycles     : 95 C/15 s + 60 C/4 min per cycle;
                        total cycling = 14 x 255 s = 3570 s;
                        encoded as single heat at 60 C for 3570 s (IR: 3570.0 SECOND)
    Post-STA hold     : 4 C, 5 min          (IR: 300.0 SECOND)
  Notes     : 14 STA cycles are encoded as a single heat step at the dominant 60 C
              annealing/extension temperature (BioScript has no loop construct).
              Four sequential heat calls on the same variable are valid in-place ops.

Step 16 | RT-STA Product Dilution (Step 55)
  Reagents  : TEBuffer
  Operation : Mix; 22 uL TE added to 11 uL RT-STA product
  Dilution  : ~1:3 (acceptable range: 1:2 to 1:5)
  Notes     : Required before Fluidigm chip loading (Step 57).

Step 17 | Fluidigm BioMark qPCR (Steps 56-60)
  Module    : qPCRDetection
  Duration  : 240 min (4 h; IFC priming + thermocycling + Ct calculation)
  Platform  : BioMark HD with IFC controller MX; 48.48 Dynamic Array IFC
  Capacity  : 48 samples x 48 genes = up to 9,216 simultaneous qPCR reactions
  Assay wells (left 48):
    3.75 uL 2x assay loading reagent + 3.75 uL each TaqMan assay (20x)
  Sample wells (right 48):
    3.4 uL diluted cDNA + 3.75 uL TaqMan master mix + 0.4 uL sample loading reagent (20x)
  Analysis  : Fluidigm Real-Time PCR Analysis Software -> Ct values;
              export as Heat Map Results CSV (File > Export);
              relative expression = 2^(Ct_gapdh - Ct_gene);
              MATLAB csvread for downstream import.
  QC gate   :
    Pass (bsbbif_2_t): qPCRSignal > 0 -> valid Ct values; dispose all products
    Fail (bsbbif_3_f): qPCRSignal <= 0 -> no amplification; drain all products
    Terminal (bsbbif_4_j): dispose qPCRSignal; experiment ends


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : kellogg_microfluidic_singlecell_pipeline.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 4 basic blocks (BB1-BB4), 1 if/else gate, 4 CFG edges
DAG            : kellogg_microfluidic_singlecell_pipeline_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations converted to seconds (s) or minutes (m) for compiler
                 compatibility (BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported).
                 Key conversions:
                   720m (fibronectin overnight) -> 43200.0 SECOND
                   120m (inter-feed incubation x6) -> 7200.0 SECOND
                   300m (imaging detect) -> 18000.0 SECOND
                   240m (qPCR detect)    -> 14400.0 SECOND
                   3570s (14 STA cycles) -> 3570.0 SECOND
Modules        : liveCellImagingDetection, qPCRDetection
Manifests (12) : PluronicF127, PBS, Fibronectin, NIH3T3_Cells, CellMedium,
                 TNF_Stimulus, Trypsin_EDTA, LysisBuffer, CellsDirect_RTmix,
                 TaqMan_PrimerPool, SuperScriptPlatinumTaq, TEBuffer
Platform note  : All mix steps abstract pressure-driven fluid exchange through
                 microchannels and chamber volumes -- not DMF electrode-driven droplet
                 merging. heat steps model on-stage incubation (37 C, 5% CO2, >95% humidity).
Feeding unroll : 6 feeding rounds encoded as distinct variables (fedCells1-6) because
                 BioScript has no loop construct.
STA cycles     : 14 thermal cycles encoded as single heat at 60 C for 3570s.
drain->dispose : drain in .bs fail branch normalizes to dispose in IR; expected behavior.
IR artifact    : bsbbif_2_t lacks an explicit jump instruction to bsbbif_4_j in IR text;
                 the DOT file confirms both branch edges resolve correctly to BB4.

protocol.title: High-Throughput Microfluidic Single-Cell Analysis Pipeline for Studies of Signaling Dynamics
protocol.platform: Valve-actuated multilayer PDMS microfluidic cell culture chip (continuous-flow, not DMF)
cell_lines: NIH3T3 mouse fibroblasts (p65-dsRed + H2B-GFP fluorescent fusion)
RAW264.7 mouse macrophages (p65-GFP + H2B-mCherry fluorescent fusion)
protocol.objective: Multiplexed stimulation and live-cell imaging of single cells under parallel input conditions, automated image analysis, on-chip cell retrieval, and downstream high-throughput gene expression profiling by microfluidic qPCR

device.chip_name: Cell Culture Chip (Gomez-Sjoberg et al., Anal. Chem. 2007)
device.fabrication: Multilayer soft lithography; two PDMS layers bonded and mounted on PDMS-coated glass slide
layers: Flow layer (top): contains cells and reagents; rounded cross-section channels (positive photoresist)
Control layer (bottom): creates elastomeric membrane valves; rectangular cross-section (negative photoresist)

chambers.cell_capacity: 1-1000 mammalian cells depending on cell size

valves.controller: Six manifolds x 8 valves; two-valve controller boxes via USB

mixer.notes: Combines multiple reagent inputs before delivery to selected chambers

sieve_valves.location: Entrance and exit of each chamber
sieve_valves.function: Trap cells and particles >20 um diameter

reagent_delivery.pressurization: 5% CO2 in air-gas mixture at 3-10 psi (200-700 mbar)
reagent_delivery.tubing_reagents: PTFE (0.022 in i.d. x 0.042 in o.d.)
reagent_delivery.tubing_cells: PEEK (510 um o.d. x 65 um i.d., IDEX 1543)
reagent_delivery.vial_cap: Rubber membrane screw cap; 20-gauge needle + 0.02-inch PEEK tubing

microscopy.imaging_mode: Wide-field (preferred for speed and low phototoxicity vs confocal)
microscopy.focus_system: Perfect Focus System (Nikon) recommended for large-chip multi-location imaging

pdms.mixing: Orbital mixer 3 min at 2000 rpm; defoam 5 min at 2200 rpm

surface_treatment.blocking_agent: Pluronic F-127 (Sigma P6867), 0.2% w/v in PBS
surface_treatment.ecm_protein: Fibronectin from human plasma (Millipore 341635-1MG), 100 ug/mL in PBS

cell_retrieval.lysis_buffer_composition: 250 uL resuspension buffer + 25 uL lysis enhancer (CellsDirect kit)

qpcr.master_mix: TaqMan Universal PCR Master Mix (Applied Biosystems 4304437)
qpcr.fluidigm_system: BioMark HD with IFC controller MX

steps.name: Chip surface treatment -- Pluronic blocking
steps.notes: 0.2% Pluronics F-127 in PBS flowed through non-chamber surfaces for 1 h. Blocks non-specific cell adhesion to PDMS. Air removed by flow pressure through PDMS matrix (~15 min), then Pluronic incubation continued for 1 h.

steps.name: PBS wash -- Pluronic removal
steps.notes: Pluronic must be completely washed from chip. Residual Pluronic entering chambers prevents fibronectin adhesion and downstream cell attachment. Critical step.

steps.name: Fibronectin chamber coating
steps.flow_mode: Non-chamber areas first (10 min), then chambers opened via GUI (ChIn/ChOut valves)
steps.notes: Overnight incubation (720m) used for reliable ECM coating. Fibronectin displaces PBS and air in chambers. Tested for NIH3T3 fibroblasts and RAW264.7 macrophages.

steps.name: Cell loading
steps.pressurization: 5% CO2 at 3-5 psi via PEEK tubing

loading_options.A: Automated scripted seeding with 10x phase-contrast imaging and intensity threshold detection
loading_options.B: Manual visual estimation and sequential chamber loading

steps.notes: Cells begin adhering to fibronectin within minutes. Multiple seeding rounds with 5-min waits between rounds. PEEK tubing helps prevent cell clumping.

steps.name: Cell feeding -- round 1 (t = 0 h)
steps.notes: 30% chamber volume replaced per feed round. On-chip peristaltic pump sequence. 2-h interval. Phase-contrast images acquired during feeding to monitor cell health.

steps.name: Cell feeding -- round 6 (t = 10 h)
steps.notes: 6 feeding rounds unrolled (BioScript has no loop construct). Covers ~12 h pre-stimulation growth and imaging phase.

steps.name: TNF-alpha stimulation (10-min pulse)
steps.delivery_mode: Pressure-driven full chamber flush (PTFE tubing, 5% CO2, 7 psi)
steps.notes: Stimulus timing logged for alignment with image data (critical step). Washout medium re-establishes baseline. Single representative 10-min pulse encoded; pulse trains can be added by unrolling additional stimulation cycles.

steps.name: Live-cell fluorescence imaging

steps.notes: liveCellImagingDetection abstracts CellProfiler nuclear segmentation, NF-kB translocation quantification, and automated cell tracking (Steps 59-66). Imaging runs as independent process from chip stimulation script.

steps.name: Cell retrieval -- trypsinization and lysis
steps.notes: Cells detach within 1-3 min post-trypsin delivery. PBS flush between chambers prevents cross-contamination. Each well sealed with tape immediately after retrieval to prevent evaporation. Lysis buffer: CellsDirect resuspension buffer + lysis enhancer (freshly prepared, kept on ice).

steps.name: One-step RT-STA reaction assembly

steps.notes: 2x CellsDirect reaction mix must be fully thawed on ice and thoroughly mixed before use (critical step). Plate can be stored at -20 C for up to 3 months before adding lysate.

steps.name: RT-STA thermal cycling

steps.notes: 14-cycle STA modelled as single heat step at 60 C for 3570s (dominant annealing/extension phase; no loop construct in BioScript). Four sequential heat calls on rtStaReaction are valid in-place operations.

steps.notes: 22 uL TE buffer added to 11 uL RT-STA product. Dilutions between 1:2 and 1:5 are acceptable. Required before Fluidigm chip loading.
