description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Digital Signaling Decouples Activation Probability and Population Heterogeneity
Source Link  : https://elifesciences.org/articles/8931
Paper DOI    : http://dx.doi.org/10.7554/eLife.08931
Journal      : eLife 2015, Vol. 4, Article e08931
Authors      : Ryan A Kellogg, Chengzhe Tian, Tomasz Lipniacki, Stephen R Quake, Savas Tay
Platform     : Automated microfluidic cell culture (PDMS chip, Gomez-Sjoberg et al. 2007) +
               widefield fluorescence live-cell microscopy + 96-well bulk RT-qPCR


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol studies how the NF-kB transcription factor system encodes and decodes temporal
information in inflammatory input signals. Using a combination of mathematical modeling and
microfluidic single-cell experiments, the paper demonstrates that NF-kB activates in a
digital (all-or-none) fashion in response to both LPS (pathogen signal) and TNF (host immune
signal), and that this digital switch enables two-dimensional control over population-level
and single-cell-level responses:

  1. Stimulus AREA (concentration x duration) controls the FRACTION of cells that activate
     NF-kB in the population -- the "Area Rule."
  2. Stimulus TEMPORAL PROFILE (shape: short-strong vs. long-low) controls NF-kB DYNAMICS
     and gene expression phenotype in the responding cells.

These two axes are independently tunable: a brief high-dose (SS) stimulus and a sustained
low-dose (LL) stimulus with the same area activate the same responding fraction, but produce
distinct NF-kB dynamics (rapid/uniform vs. delayed/heterogeneous) and therefore distinct
downstream gene expression profiles.

Three experimental protocols are encoded in the BioScript file in sequence:

  Protocol 1 : LPS Dose-Modulation (LL Signal, on-chip microfluidics)
  Protocol 2 : LPS Duration-Modulation (SS Signal, on-chip microfluidics)
  Protocol 3 : NF-kB-Dependent Gene Expression Assay (off-chip, 96-well RT-qPCR)


CELL LINE
---------
p65-knockout NIH 3T3 fibroblasts modified via lentiviral vectors to express:
  - p65-DsRed under the endogenous p65 promoter (NF-kB nuclear translocation reporter)
  - H2B-GFP (nuclear position reporter for cell tracking)
Clonally derived to express p65-DsRed at the lowest detectable level to preserve
near-endogenous expression. (Lee et al., 2009; Tay et al., 2010)


DEVICE AND IMAGING
------------------
Microfluidic chip: PDMS-based automated cell culture system (Gomez-Sjoberg et al. 2007;
  Kellogg et al. 2014 Nat. Protoc. 9:1713). Chamber dimensions: 1.12 mm x 0.9 mm x 0.040 mm.
  ~200 cells/chamber; all LPS doses tested in parallel on a single chip in duplicate chambers.

Microscope  : Leica DMI6000B widefield, 20x magnification
Camera      : Retiga-SRV CCD (QImaging)
Filters     : Leica L5 (GFP channel, H2B-GFP nuclear reporter)
              Leica Y3 (DsRed channel, p65-DsRed NF-kB reporter)
Light source: Leica EL6000 mercury metal halide
Imaging interval: 5-6 min over ~250 min post-stimulation

NF-kB quantification: Mean nuclear DsRed fluorescence / mean cytoplasm DsRed fluorescence.
  Cell tracking: CellProfiler + custom Matlab. Peak detection: Matlab smooth() + mspeaks().
  Peak area integration: Matlab trapz() (baseline-corrected, LPS onset to first minimum).
  Statistics: Unpaired two-sample T-test (Matlab ttest2()). Mitotic cells excluded.


MATHEMATICAL MODEL
------------------
Base model: IKK-NF-kB regulatory module from Tay et al. 2010 (Nature 466:267).
LPS extensions: TLR4 receptor species; TRAF6 activation; cooperative IKK activation
  via Hill kinetics (n=4) to model Myddosome/TRAF6 lattice clustering.
Cell-to-cell variability: TLR4 receptor number drawn from lognormal distribution
  (mu=8.0, sigma=0.8; expected 4.1e3 receptors/cell; median 3.0e3; mode 1.6e3).
Simplifications: CD14 removed (assumed in excess; LPS binds TLR4 directly).
  TLR4-TRIF-dependent branch removed (LPS.TLR4 complexes do not internalize in model).
  Only TLR4-MyD88 (early response) branch modeled.
Parameter estimation: Iterative automatic (L2-norm error on activation fractions,
  log-scale parameter sampling) + manual; 200 simulations per parameter set.
LPS concentration conversion: 1 ng/mL LPS = 2.4e4 molecules/cell
  (MW ~10 kDa; chamber volume 1.12x0.9x0.040 mm; ~100 cells/chamber).

Area Rule (Appendix 1, Equation 2): For high-dose inputs where ligand-receptor
  backward reaction is negligible:
    P([AB] >= [AB]_th) = P(B0 >= [AB]_th / (1 - exp(-k+ * S)))
  where S = integral(concentration dt) = stimulus area, B0 = receptor number (lognormal),
  k+ = forward binding rate. Fraction of activation depends ONLY on input area S.
  Caveat: at sub-threshold doses, the maximal activatable fraction saturates and
  further increases in duration cannot exceed that ceiling.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Fibronectin Coating and Cell Seeding (Protocol 1 + 2)
  Reagents  : FibronectinSolution, CompleteMedia, NIH3T3_NFkB_Cells
  Operations: Mix fibronectin + media for 5 min (300 s) -> coatedChamber
              Load ~200 cells into coatedChamber for 2 s -> loadedChamber
              Incubate at 37 C for 24 h (1440 min = 86400 s) to ~80% confluence
  IR        : coatedChamber1[0] = mix(fibronectin1[0], media_prime1[0]) @ 300.0SECOND
              loadedChamber1[0] = mix(seedCells1[0], coatedChamber1[0]) @ 2.0SECOND
              heat(loadedChamber1[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 86400.0SECOND

Step 2 | LPS Dose-Modulation: High-Dose LL Arm (500 ng/mL, continuous)
  BB        : BB1 (main) -> BB2/BB3 fork
  Stimulus  : Long-duration low-dose (LL) -- high-dose arm: 500 ng/mL continuous LPS
              Delivered as step increase via media exchange; continuous flow replenishes
              internalized ligand. All conditions in parallel, duplicate chambers.
  Duration  : 250 min imaging (250m = 15000 s)
  Expected  : ~100% cells respond; median peak at ~35 min; low timing variability;
              Hill coefficient ~2.3; sustained oscillations under continuous flow
  IR        : llHighChamber1[0] = mix(loadedChamber1[0], lpsHighDose1[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
              heat(llHighChamber1[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 15000.0SECOND
              llHighSignal1[0] = detect(nfkbTranslocationDetection, llHighChamber1[0]) @ 15000.0SECOND

Step 3 | LPS Dose-Modulation: Low-Dose LL Arm (0.25 ng/mL, continuous)
  BB        : BB1 (main) -> BB2/BB3 fork (parallel with Step 2)
  Stimulus  : Long-duration low-dose (LL) -- low-dose arm: 0.25 ng/mL continuous LPS
              Same delivery method; dose pre-diluted in media before chip loading.
  Duration  : 250 min imaging (15000 s)
  Expected  : ~5% cells respond; median peak >80 min; high cell-to-cell timing variability;
              stereotypical peak shape shifted later; heterogeneous dynamics
  IR        : llLowChamber1[0] = mix(loadedChamber1[0], lpsLowDose1[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
              heat(llLowChamber1[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 15000.0SECOND
              llLowSignal1[0] = detect(nfkbTranslocationDetection, llLowChamber1[0]) @ 15000.0SECOND

  QC Gate (LL Dose): if llHighSignal > 0 -> dispose both chambers (pass)
                     else -> dispose both chambers (fail; imaging/reagent failure)
                     Convergence at BB4 (bsbbif_4_j).

Step 4 | LPS Duration-Modulation: 1 s SS Pulse (500 ng/mL, 1 s)
  BB        : BB4 (bsbbif_4_j) -> BB5/BB6 fork
  Stimulus  : Short-duration strong-amplitude (SS) -- 1 s pulse @ 500 ng/mL
              1 s flow of LPS through chamber; immediate media wash terminates
              receptor-ligand contact (no further LPS exposure after wash).
  Fresh cells seeded: 1440m growth at 37 C (86400 s) before stimulation.
  Duration  : 150 min post-pulse imaging (9000 s)
  Expected  : ~3.3% cells respond; median peak ~55 min; low timing variability (uniform).
              Same responding fraction as 0.25 ng/mL continuous LL arm (~3-5%).
              Response dynamics are fast and synchronous, unlike LL low-dose arm.
  IR        : ss1sPulsed1[0] = mix(ssChamber1[0], ssPulseHigh1[0]) @ 1.0SECOND
              ss1sWashed1[0] = mix(ss1sPulsed1[0], mediaWashShort1[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
              heat(ss1sWashed1[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 9000.0SECOND
              ss1sSignal1[0] = detect(nfkbTranslocationDetection, ss1sWashed1[0]) @ 9000.0SECOND

Step 5 | LPS Duration-Modulation: 40 s SS Pulse (500 ng/mL, 40 s)
  BB        : BB4 (bsbbif_4_j) -> BB5/BB6 fork (parallel with Step 4)
  Stimulus  : Short-duration strong-amplitude (SS) -- 40 s pulse @ 500 ng/mL
              Same delivery; post-pulse media wash terminates stimulus.
  Duration  : 150 min post-pulse imaging (9000 s)
  Expected  : ~87.5% cells respond; median peak ~47 min; low timing variability.
              Median peak time changes < 2 min vs. 1 s arm despite >25x difference
              in responding fraction. No significant timing difference (Fig. 5 supp. 2).
              Area Rule: 500 ng/mL x 10 s = 5000 ng·s/mL activates ~55% (validated
              vs. 50 ng/mL x 100 s and 100 ng/mL x 50 s, both ~51-54% responding).
  IR        : ss40sPulsed1[0] = mix(ssChamber1[0], ssPulseLong401[0]) @ 40.0SECOND
              ss40sWashed1[0] = mix(ss40sPulsed1[0], mediaWashLong1[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
              heat(ss40sWashed1[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 9000.0SECOND
              ss40sSignal1[0] = detect(nfkbTranslocationDetection, ss40sWashed1[0]) @ 9000.0SECOND

  QC Gate (SS Pulse): if ss40sSignal > 0 -> dispose both washed chambers (pass)
                      else -> dispose both (fail)
                      Convergence at BB7 (bsbbif_7_j).

Step 6 | Gene Expression Assay -- Cell Seeding (96-well plate)
  BB        : BB7 (bsbbif_7_j)
  Protocol  : Off-chip, 96-well plate
  Reagents  : NIH3T3_NFkB_Cells, CompleteMedia
  Seeding   : 10,000 cells/well; attach overnight (1440m = 86400 s) at 37 C
  IR        : bulkWell1[0] = mix(bulkCells1[0], bulkMedia1[0]) @ 60.0SECOND
              heat(bulkWell1[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 86400.0SECOND

Step 7 | Gene Expression Assay -- LPS Stimulation (500 ng/mL and 50 ng/mL)
  BB        : BB7 (bsbbif_7_j)
  LPS doses : 500 ng/mL (high-dose; early gene peak at 30 min)
              50  ng/mL (low-dose; dose-dependent peak delay to 1-3 h)
              Full screen range: 1-500 ng/mL; two representative doses encoded in CFG.
  Duration  : 8 h stimulation (480m = 28800 s); cells lysed at 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 h
  IR        : stimWell5001[0] = mix(bulkWell1[0], lpsGex5001[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
              heat(stimWell5001[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 28800.0SECOND
              stimWell501[0]  = mix(bulkWell1[0], lpsGex501[0])  @ 5.0SECOND
              heat(stimWell501[0])  @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 28800.0SECOND

Step 8 | Gene Expression Assay -- RNA Extraction and cDNA Preparation
  BB        : BB7 (bsbbif_7_j)
  Reagents  : RNALysisBuffer, cDNA_Primers, GAPDH_Primer
  Operations: Lysis: mix stimWell + RNALysisBuffer for 5 min (300 s)
              RT-PCR: mix RNA + cDNA_Primers for 30 min (1800 s) [Invitrogen One-Step
                      RT-PCR kit with specific target amplification, 24-primer set]
              Normalisation: mix cDNA + GAPDH_Primer for 5 s
  IR        : rna5001[0]      = mix(stimWell5001[0], lysate5001[0]) @ 300.0SECOND
              cdna5001[0]     = mix(rna5001[0], primers5001[0]) @ 1800.0SECOND
              cdnaNorm5001[0] = mix(cdna5001[0], gapdh5001[0]) @ 5.0SECOND

Step 9 | Gene Expression Assay -- Fluidigm qPCR Detection
  BB        : BB7 (bsbbif_7_j) -> BB8/BB9 fork
  Platform  : Fluidigm 48.48 dynamic array; technical duplicates; normalized to GAPDH
  Duration  : 60 min (3600 s)
  IR        : gexSignal5001[0] = detect(geneExpressionDetection, cdnaNorm5001[0]) @ 3600.0SECOND
              gexSignal501[0]  = detect(geneExpressionDetection, cdnaNorm501[0])  @ 3600.0SECOND

  Target genes and dose-dependent response (500 vs. 50 ng/mL LPS):
    Early (peak 30 min -> 1 h)    : nfkbia (IkBa), a20
    Early (peak 1 h -> 2 h)       : nfkbie (IkBe), tnf
    Intermediate (peak 1-2 h -> 3 h) : ccl20, icam1
    Late (slow kinetics; no delay): casp4, ccl5

  QC Gate (GEX): if gexSignal500 > 0 -> dispose both cDNA normalised droplets (pass)
                 else -> dispose both (fail; RT-PCR or Fluidigm failure)
                 Convergence at BB10 (bsbbif_10_j) -> NOP (terminal).

area_rule.description: Stimulus integral (concentration x duration) determines fraction of cells that activate NF-kB in the population. Validated analytically, by simulation, and experimentally.
area_rule.analytical_basis: For high-dose inputs where backward reaction (ligand-receptor dissociation) is negligible, fraction of activation P([AB] >= [AB]_th) depends only on input area S = integral(concentration dt). See Appendix 1, Equation 2.
area_rule.caveat: At sub-threshold doses, increasing duration infinitely does not exceed maximal activation fraction for that dose; Area Rule has a dose-dependent ceiling.

experimental_validation.conclusion: Equal area conditions produce statistically equivalent responding fractions regardless of temporal profile

cooperative_activation.mechanism: Myddosome assembly and TRAF6 lattice clustering

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Cellular Decision Making by Non-Integrative Processing of TLR Inputs
Source Link  : https://www.cell.com/cell-reports/fulltext/S2211-1247(17)30359-5
Paper DOI    : http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2017.03.027
Journal      : Cell Reports, 2017, Vol. 19, pp. 125-135
Platform     : Automated microfluidic cell culture chip + widefield live-cell fluorescence microscopy


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a single-cell live-imaging microfluidic approach to study how cells process
simultaneous inflammatory signalling inputs through a shared downstream pathway. Mouse 3T3 fibroblasts
expressing p65-DsRed at near-endogenous levels are cultured in automated microfluidic chambers and
stimulated with combinatorial TLR4 (LPS) and TLR2 (PAM) agonists across a 3x3 dose matrix. NF-kB
nuclear translocation dynamics are quantified continuously over 8 hours at single-cell resolution.

The protocol is divided into four functional phases:
  1. Automated microfluidic cell culture: fibronectin coating, cell seeding, pre-culture,
     and 9-condition LPS x PAM co-stimulation matrix (step increase via chamber media exchange)
  2. NF-kB live imaging and bagging classifier-based response classification:
     single cells classified as LPS-like, PAM-like, or uncertain/mixed using a
     trained ensemble of N=50 decision-tree classifiers (n=0.6 majority vote threshold)
  3. Sequential cross-tolerance stimulation: two schemes test TLR cross-tolerance mediated
     by shared negative feedback (IkB, A20, miR-146a) at the TRAF6 node
  4. miR-146a TaqMan qPCR validation: bulk stimulation + RNA isolation + two-step
     qPCR confirms miR-146a as the slow, sustained, ultrasensitive negative feedback
     that mediates PAM response shutoff and enables cross-TLR tolerance

The central finding is "non-integrative processing": under TLR2-TLR4 co-stimulation, single cells
respond with an NF-kB dynamic profile characteristic of either TLR4 (LPS-like) or TLR2 (PAM-like)
activation, rather than a mixed or combined response. This is mediated by switch-like NF-kB activation,
receptor-specific processing timescales (endosomal delay for TLR2), cell-to-cell variability in TLR
receptor numbers, and multilayer negative feedback enabling cross-tolerance.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Platform     : Automated microfluidic cell culture system (Gomez-Sjoberg et al. Anal. Chem. 2007;
               Kellogg et al. Nat. Protoc. 2014; Kellogg & Tay, Cell 2015)
Chamber size : 1.12 mm x 0.9 mm x 0.040 mm per chamber
Cells/chamber: ~100 cells at imaging; seeded at 200 cells/chamber
Parallelism  : All 9 LPS-PAM dose combinations run in parallel on a single chip
               Duplicate chambers per condition (2 chambers per LPS-PAM combination)
Atmosphere   : 37 C, 5% CO2; maintained via on-stage incubation chamber
Stimulus     : Delivered as step increase (chamber media exchange); stimulus vials
               pressured with 5% CO2, kept on ice before delivery
Post-stim    : Chambers sealed immediately after stimulus delivery
Imaging      : 5-6 min interval acquisitions for 480 min (8 hours)


CELL LINE
---------
Mouse 3T3 fibroblasts (p65^(-/-) background):
  - Re-express p65-DsRed under control of 1.5 kb endogenous p65 promoter
  - Clonally derived to express p65-DsRed at near-endogenous (lowest detectable) level
  - H2B-GFP nuclear marker driven by ubiquitin promoter (automated cell tracking)
  - Culture: DMEM complete media, 37 C, 5% CO2, no antibiotics
  - Reference: Tay et al. Nature 2010; Lee et al. Sci. Signal. 2009


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Fibronectin Chamber Coating
  Reagents  : Fibronectin, PBS wash
  Operation : Chamber perfusion coating (abstracted as mix in BioScript)
  Duration  : 5 min
  Purpose   : Promotes 3T3 fibroblast adhesion to PDMS chamber surface.
              Excess fibronectin removed with PBS wash.

Step 2 | Cell Seeding and Pre-culture
  Cell line : Mouse 3T3 p65-DsRed (p65^(-/-))
  Density   : 200 cells/chamber (seeding); ~100 cells/chamber at imaging
  Media     : DMEM complete (37 C, 5% CO2)
  Duration  : 24 h (= 1440 min; IR: 86400.0 SECOND)
  Target    : ~80% confluence before stimulation
  Notes     : Periodic media replenishment during pre-culture. Incubation
              chamber maintains 37 C and 5% CO2 on microscope stage.

Step 3 | Pre-stimulation Media Refresh
  Reagents  : DMEM complete (fresh, CO2-equilibrated)
  Duration  : 1 min
  Purpose   : Removes conditioned media; establishes NF-kB baseline before stimulus.

Step 4 | Combinatorial LPS x PAM Co-stimulation (9-condition 3x3 matrix)
  TLR4 agonist : Ultrapure LPS (Invivogen); TLR4-exclusive activation
                 Doses: 100, 33, 11 ng/mL
  TLR2 agonist : Pam3CSK4 (PAM, Invivogen); synthetic triacylated lipopeptide; TLR2 via endosome
                 Doses: 40, 13.3, 4.4 ng/mL
  Conditions   : 9 combinations (C1-C9); 2 duplicate chambers each; 18 chambers total
  Primary cond : C9 (LPS 11 ng/mL + PAM 4.4 ng/mL) -- most distinct LPS/PAM dynamics
                 used as representative condition for bagging classifier CFG gate
  Delivery     : Step increase via microfluidic media exchange; all vials pressured with
                 5% CO2 and kept on ice; delivered to parallel chambers on single chip
  Imaging      : Chambers sealed post-delivery; 5-6 min intervals for 480 min

  Dose matrix (ng/mL):
    LPS\PAM  |  40     |  13.3   |  4.4
    ---------+---------+---------+------
    100      |  C1     |  C2     |  C3
    33       |  C4     |  C5     |  C6
    11       |  C7     |  C8     |  C9*
    (* primary mechanistic condition)

Step 5 | NF-kB Live Imaging and Bagging Classifier Detection
  Microscope   : Leica DMI6000B widefield, 20x magnification
  Camera       : Retiga-SRV CCD (QImaging)
  Light source : Leica EL6000 mercury metal halide
  Channels     : DsRed (Y3 filter, NF-kB signal); GFP (L5 filter, H2B nuclear marker)
  Quantification: Mean nuclear DsRed / mean cytoplasm DsRed intensity ratio
  Tracking     : CellProfiler (automated) + custom MATLAB
  Peak analysis: MATLAB smooth + mspeaks; features: first peak intensity, max peak time
  Classifier   : Bagging classifier (N=50 decision trees, n=0.6 majority vote threshold)
                 Implemented via MATLAB fitensemble ('Bag','Tree','Classification')
                 Training: single-stimulus LPS and PAM trajectories at matched doses
                 Output: LPS-like / PAM-like / Uncertain (mixed) per cell
                 Accuracy: 89% overall; >=85% per condition (10-fold CV)
  Key results  : C9 (LPS 11 + PAM 4.4 ng/mL): ~40-50% LPS-like, ~40-50% PAM-like, ~15% mixed
                 C1 (LPS 100 + PAM 40 ng/mL): ~90% LPS-like
                 C7 (LPS 11 + PAM 40 ng/mL): ~90% PAM-like
  Gate         : classifySignal > 0 -> non-integrative (>80% LPS- or PAM-like) -> BB2 (pass)
                 classifySignal <= 0 -> integrative/mixed dominant -> BB3 (fail)

Step 6 | Sequential Stimulation Scheme A: LPS First, PAM at +2 hr
  Cell line     : Mouse 3T3 p65-DsRed (fresh chambers; parallel chip run)
  First stim    : LPS 11 ng/mL at t=0
  Interval      : 120 min incubation at 37 C, 5% CO2 (heat step in BioScript)
  Second stim   : PAM 13.3 ng/mL at t=120 min (delivered to same chamber)
  Imaging       : Continuous throughout (480 min total window)
  Detection     : nfkbLiveImagingDetection (480 min)
  Results (Fig 5C):
    53% cells responded to LPS only (LPS-induced IkB/A20/miR-146a blocked PAM response)
    30% cells responded to PAM only (LPS-refractory; caught by PAM at +2 hr)
    17% cells responded to both stimuli (incomplete negative feedback suppression)
  Interpretation: Rapid negative feedback induced by LPS sufficient to inhibit subsequent
                 PAM response in majority of pre-activated cells.

Step 7 | Sequential Stimulation Scheme B: PAM First, LPS at +4 hr
  Cell line     : Mouse 3T3 p65-DsRed (fresh chambers; parallel chip run)
  First stim    : PAM 13.3 ng/mL at t=0
  Interval      : 240 min incubation at 37 C, 5% CO2 (ensures miR-146a fully induced;
                  PAM onset ~2 hr; 240 min interval allows sustained expression to build)
  Second stim   : LPS 100 ng/mL at t=240 min (high dose to maximally challenge pre-activated cells)
  Imaging       : Continuous throughout (480 min total window)
  Detection     : nfkbLiveImagingDetection (480 min)
  Cross-tol gate: crossToleranceDetection on Scheme A signal (30 s detection)
                  crossTolSignal > 0 -> cross-tolerance confirmed -> BB5 (pass)
                  crossTolSignal <= 0 -> no cross-tolerance -> BB6 (fail)
  Results (Fig 5D):
    84% cells responded to PAM only (A20/miR-146a fully blocked high-dose LPS response)
    16% cells responded to both stimuli
  Interpretation: Moderate PAM stimulus activated all cells; sustained A20/miR-146a negative
                 feedback mediated cross-TLR tolerance, blocking even high-dose LPS at +4 hr.
                 Cross-tolerance operates via shared TRAF6 node downstream of both TLR2 and TLR4.

Step 8 | miR-146a TaqMan qPCR Validation
  Purpose       : Validate miR-146a as slow, sustained, ultrasensitive negative feedback
                  responsible for PAM response shutoff (Fig 2C) and cross-TLR tolerance
  Cell line     : Mouse 3T3 (bulk flasks; off-chip, not single-cell microfluidics)
  Stimuli       : LPS 10 ng/mL and PAM 10 ng/mL (separate flasks; not co-stimulation)
  Time course   : RNA harvested at 0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 hr post-stimulation (480 min)
  Incubation    : 37 C, 5% CO2 (heat step in BioScript; 480 min per arm)
  RNA isolation : mirVana miRNA isolation kit (Ambion); TrizolReagent abstraction in BioScript
  cDNA synthesis: TaqMan microRNA reverse transcription kit (Applied Biosystems)
  qPCR assay    : TaqMan miRNA-specific assay hsa-miR-146a (cross-reactive with murine miR-146a)
  Normalisation : snoRNA234 snRNA endogenous control (Applied Biosystems)
  Thermocycler  : 95 C denaturation (15 s/cycle) + 60 C annealing/extension (60 s/cycle), 40 cycles
                  Total per arm: 2 x 50 min heat steps (BioScript; 95 C then 60 C)
  Detection     : miR146aExpressionDetection module; representative gate on LPS arm
                  miR146aSignal > 0 -> sustained induction confirmed -> BB8 (pass)
                  miR146aSignal <= 0 -> no induction -> BB9 (fail)
  Results (Fig 2C):
    LPS onset   : ~1 hr post-stimulation
    PAM onset   : ~2 hr post-stimulation
    Profile     : Sustained high expression for >6 hr (unlike IkB/A20 which return to baseline)
    Role        : Slow feedback via TRAF6 mRNA cleavage (also IRAK1/2); Hill coefficient 4
                  in ODE model (ultrasensitivity); explains rising-amplitude PAM oscillations
                  and abrupt shutoff at 300-400 min under low-dose PAM stimulation


MATHEMATICAL MODEL SUMMARY
--------------------------
Type         : ODE system; mass-action / Michaelis-Menten / Hill kinetics
Base         : Extended from Kellogg et al. eLife 2015 (LPS/TLR4 NF-kB model)
               and Tay et al. Nature 2010 (TNF NF-kB model)
Noise        : Receptor-level extrinsic noise only; TLR4 and TLR2 total counts are
               lognormally distributed (mu_R, sigma_R parameters)
Simulation   : 500 cells per condition; only active trajectories considered
Key features :
  - TLR4 (LPS): surface membrane signalling; rapid TRAF6a(LPS) accumulation
  - TLR2 (PAM): endosomal processing modelled as low binding (kf) + low unbinding (kr);
                 slow TRAF6a(PAM) accumulation; integrator-like PAM.TLR2 complex dynamics
  - Fast feedback : IkBa (principal fast feedback); A20
  - Slow feedback : miR-146a (Hill coefficient 4; ultrasensitive); targets TRAF6 mRNA
  - IKK activation: cooperative TRAF6 clustering (Hill term); switch-like NF-kB response
  - Non-integrative mechanism: LPS fires first (no endosomal delay); IkB/A20/miR-146a
    feedback prevents PAM response in TLR4-sensitive cells; TLR4-refractory cells receive
    PAM signal unimpeded. Switch-like activation polarises each cell to one outcome.
  - TRIF pathway excluded: inactive in 3T3 fibroblasts (A. Hoffmann, personal communication)
  - Ligand/cell: 1 ng/mL LPS = 2.4e4 ligands/cell (MW 10 kDa);
                 1 ng/mL PAM = 1.6e5 ligands/cell (MW 1509.6 Da)
                 Chamber: 1.12 x 0.9 x 0.040 mm; ~100 cells/chamber

-------------------------

imaging.analysis_software: CellProfiler (automated tracking) + custom MATLAB (peak detection via mspeaks; smoothing via smooth function)

classifier.training_data: Single-stimulus LPS and PAM NF-kB trajectories at matched doses
classifier.classification_rule: LPS-like if >nu fraction of trees vote LPS; PAM-like if >nu fraction vote PAM; Uncertain otherwise
classifier.artificial_mixed_check: 1000 artificial mixed trajectories (LPS + PAM training trace sums) tested; majority classified as mixed/uncertain confirming classifier validity

steps.name: Fibronectin chamber coating
steps.notes: Fibronectin adsorbed to PDMS chamber surface to promote 3T3 fibroblast adhesion. PBS wash removes excess.

steps.name: Cell seeding and pre-culture
steps.notes: Periodic media replenishment during pre-culture. Cells reach ~80% confluence before stimulation.

steps.name: Pre-stimulation media refresh
steps.notes: Fresh DMEM delivered to remove conditioned media and establish baseline NF-kB level before stimulus.

steps.name: Combinatorial LPS x PAM co-stimulation (9-condition matrix)
steps.delivery: Step increase via microfluidic chamber media exchange
steps.chip_parallelism: All 9 conditions run in parallel on a single chip
steps.notes: Stimulus vials pressured with 5% CO2, kept on ice. Chamber sealed post-delivery. Condition C9 (LPS 11 / PAM 4.4 ng/mL) used as primary CFG gate condition -- most distinct LPS-like vs PAM-like dynamics.

steps.name: NF-kB live imaging and bagging classifier detection

pass.interpretation: Non-integrative processing confirmed; >80% cells are LPS-like or PAM-like, <15-20% uncertain
pass.action: dispose all co-stim chambers; proceed to sequential stimulation arm

steps.name: Sequential stimulation Scheme A: LPS first, PAM at +2 hr

results_fig5c.interpretation: Rapid NF-kB negative feedback (IkB, A20, miR-146a) induced by LPS prevents PAM response in 53% of cells. Remaining 30% were LPS-refractory and caught by PAM at +2 hr.

steps.name: Sequential stimulation Scheme B: PAM first, LPS at +4 hr

second_stimulus.note: High-dose LPS used to maximally challenge PAM-pre-activated cells

steps.rationale_for_240min_interval: Ensures miR-146a is fully induced (onset ~2 hr post-PAM; sustained for several hours) before second stimulus

results_fig5d.interpretation: Moderate PAM 13.3 ng/mL activated all cells. A20 / miR-146a negative feedback sufficient to block even high-dose LPS in 84% of pre-activated cells. Demonstrates cross-TLR tolerance through shared TRAF6 node.

pass.interpretation: Cross-tolerance confirmed; majority of pre-stimulated cells refractory to second stimulus
pass.action: dispose sequential chambers; proceed to miR-146a validation

fail.interpretation: No cross-tolerance; cells respond to both stimuli

steps.name: miR-146a TaqMan qPCR validation
steps.purpose: Mechanistic validation of miR-146a as slow sustained negative feedback mediating PAM response shutoff and TLR cross-tolerance

cdna_synthesis.kit: TaqMan microRNA reverse transcription kit (Applied Biosystems)

qpcr.assay: TaqMan miRNA-specific assay hsa-miR-146a (cross-reactive murine miR-146a)

results_fig2c.expression_profile: Sustained high expression for >6 hr (unlike IkB/A20 which return to baseline)
results_fig2c.feedback_type: Slow, ultrasensitive negative feedback targeting TRAF6 mRNA (IRAK1/2 also targeted)

pass.interpretation: Sustained miR-146a induction confirmed; validates model slow feedback mechanism

mathematical_model.base_model: Extended from Kellogg et al. eLife 2015 (TLR4/LPS) and Tay et al. Nature 2010
mathematical_model.noise_model: Receptor-level extrinsic noise only; TLR4 and TLR2 total counts follow log-normal distributions
key_mechanistic_features: TLR4 (LPS): surface membrane signalling; rapid TRAF6 accumulation
TLR2 (PAM): endosomal processing; slow TRAF6 accumulation (low binding rate kf, low unbinding rate kr models internalization as integrator)
Slow feedback: miR-146a (Hill coefficient 4, ultrasensitive); targets TRAF6 mRNA
Cell-to-cell variability from TLR receptor number lognormal distribution
mathematical_model.chamber_volume_calculation: 1 ng/mL LPS -> 2.4e4 ligands/cell; 1 ng/mL PAM -> 1.6e5 ligands/cell (MW: LPS 10 kDa, PAM 1509.6 Da)
mathematical_model.non_integrative_mechanism: LPS activates first (no endosomal delay); IkB/A20/miR-146a feedback prevents PAM response in TLR4-sensitive cells. TLR4-refractory cells receive PAM signal unimpeded -> PAM-like response. Switch-like NF-kB activation polarises each cell to one outcome.
mathematical_model.excluded_pathway: TRIF-mediated TLR4 pathway excluded (inactive in 3T3 fibroblasts; Alexander Hoffmann personal communication)

basic_blocks.description: Device prep; cell seeding; 9-condition LPS x PAM co-stimulation matrix; NF-kB live imaging

basic_blocks.description: Dispose classifier + imaging QC signals; enter sequential stimulation arm

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_5_t
basic_blocks.action: dispose seqA and seqB chambers; proceed to miR-146a arm

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_7_j
basic_blocks.description: Dispose sequential imaging signals and cross-tolerance QC signal; enter miR-146a arm

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_8_t
basic_blocks.action: dispose LPS and PAM qPCR normalised samples

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_9_f
basic_blocks.action: drain LPS and PAM qPCR normalised samples

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_10_j
basic_blocks.description: Dispose miR146aSignal and remaining cond9a chamber; NOP; experiment ends

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Liquid Biopsy and Therapeutic Response: Circulating Tumor Cell Cultures for Evaluation of Anticancer Treatment
Source Link  : https://www.science.org/doi/pdf/10.1126/sciadv.1600274
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.1600274
Journal      : Science Advances, 2016, Vol. 2, Article e1600274
Platform     : Integrated three-layer PDMS microfluidic device (continuous-flow); tree-like gradient generator + channel barrier + tapered microwell array


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes an integrated microfluidic approach for short-term primary circulating tumor cell
(CTC) culture from patient whole blood and in situ anticancer drug screening. Blood samples from breast
cancer patients are collected via liquid biopsy, lysed to remove red blood cells, and the resulting
nucleated cell fraction (WBCs + CTCs) is seeded directly into a custom device incorporating arrays of
tapered elliptical microwells. No pre-enrichment of CTCs is required before culture.

Cells are cultured under hypoxic conditions (1% O2, mimicking the in vivo tumor microenvironment) for
11 days, during which CTC-containing clusters form in the tapered microwells. Culture positivity is
assessed on Day 11 by bright-field imaging. Positive samples (clusters in >=50% of microwells) proceed
to in situ drug screening: a tree-like serpentine gradient generator simultaneously delivers eight
different doxorubicin concentrations across eight parallel culture channels. After 72 hours of drug
exposure, cell viability is assessed by LIVE/DEAD fluorescence staining (calcein-AM / EtBr / CD45-APC),
and IC50 values are extracted by 4-parameter logistic curve fitting.

The complete procedure from blood collection to IC50 readout takes 14 days. Rapid IC50 feedback
enables immediate clinical intervention upon detection of drug resistance or tolerance.
Clinically validated with 73 blood samples from 55 breast cancer patients.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
The integrated device consists of three bonded PDMS layers assembled by oxygen plasma treatment:

Layer 1 (top)    : Tree-like serpentine gradient generator. Mixes two inlet flows (0% vehicle +
                   100% drug) to produce 8 output concentrations simultaneously at 100 uL/min.
                   Concentration gradient confirmed stable over 24 h (P < 0.05) and independent
                   of input dye concentration across 5 flow rates (25-200 uL/min).
                   Fabricated by standard photolithography on SU-8 2050 / SU-8 2000.5 silicon wafer.

Layer 2 (middle) : Channel barrier. Aluminum mold (Whits Technologies, Singapore). Defines 8
                   parallel culture channels; prevents cross-contamination between concentration zones.

Layer 3 (bottom) : Custom multimicrowell array. Each of the 8 channels contains ~1000 tapered
                   elliptical microwells (250 x 150 um footprint, 150 um depth, 4.7 mm pitch).
                   Fabricated by diffuser back-side lithography: laser direct writing on soda-lime
                   optical mask blank (Heidelberg DWL 66fs, Coherent I326C Ar laser), Cr etching,
                   SU-8 2100 resist (300 um thick, double spin-coat at 1500 rpm), UV exposure
                   through opal diffusing glass (Edmund Optics) at 12 mW/cm2, 365 nm, 9 s.
                   Dome-shaped SU-8 pillars (height 150 um) serve as PDMS casting template.

Microwell geometry: Tapered (dome-bottom) elliptical wells preferred over cylindrical wells because
   the inclined walls allow cells to settle to the center, forming a single dense cluster per well
   rather than multiple small aggregates. Tapered design retains 88 +/- 20% cell viability vs
   31.5 +/- 3% for cylindrical microwells.

Device integration: Assembled device placed in 150-mm dish filled with thin PBS film to limit
   evaporation; incubated in humidified chamber. Syringe pump (NE-1000, New Era Pump Systems)
   connected via BD Luer-Lok syringes for all infusion/withdrawal operations.


CELL SOURCE AND CLINICAL SAMPLES
---------------------------------
- Primary circulating tumor cells (CTCs) from breast cancer patients (n = 73 blood samples,
  55 patients; early-stage, newly diagnosed, locally advanced, or refractory metastatic).
- Study approved by DSRB (references 2012/00105, 2012/00979, 2010/00270, 2010/00691).
  All patients provided informed consent.
- Control validation: MCF-7 (HTB-22TM, ATCC) human breast adenocarcinoma cell line used
  to characterise and validate assay conditions before clinical sample evaluation.
  MCF-7 maintained in high-glucose DMEM (Invitrogen) + 10% FBS + 1% pen/strep;
  37 C, 5% CO2, 80% confluence; subcultured twice weekly; 0.01% trypsin / 5.3 mM EDTA.
- Presence of cancer cells in clinical samples validated by fluorescence in situ hybridization
  (FISH) for breast cancer-associated markers TOP2A (Abbott) and CCND1 (Empire Genomics).


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Blood Collection and RBC Lysis
  Reagents    : Whole blood (EDTA vacutainer, Becton-Dickinson), RBC lysis buffer (Life Technologies)
  Volume      : Equiv. 10 mL whole blood per evaluation run (1.25 mL per channel)
  Procedure   : Blood samples stored in EDTA vacutainer; lysed within 10 h of withdrawal.
                RBC lysis buffer mixed with whole blood for 3-5 min at room temperature (25 C)
                to lyse erythrocytes while retaining nucleated cells (WBCs + CTCs).
  BioScript   : lysateMix = mix bloodSample with lysisBuffer for 5m
                heat lysateMix at 25c for 5m

Step 2 | PBS Wash of Nucleated Cell Fraction
  Reagents    : Sterile PBS
  Procedure   : Lysed sample washed once with sterile PBS at room temperature to remove
                residual lysis buffer and cellular debris. Nucleated cell pellet retained.
  BioScript   : washedCells = mix lysateMix with pbsWash for 2m

Step 3 | Cell Seeding into Microfluidic Device (Day 0)
  Reagents    : Supplemented DMEM (DMEM + 10% FBS + 1% pen/strep)
  Procedure   : Nucleated cells resuspended in 1.6 mL supplemented DMEM; 200 uL added to
                each of 8 channels via syringe pump at 100 uL/min (equiv. 1.25 mL blood/channel).
                Samples diluted and evenly mixed before addition to minimise cell number variation
                between microwells and channels. Device kept in humidified chamber.
  BioScript   : seededCulture = mix washedCells with seedingMedia for 5m
                (BioScript `mix` abstracts the syringe-pump seeding flow-through event)

Step 4 | Day 0-3 Culture (Incubation Cycle 1)
  Conditions  : 37 C, 5% CO2, hypoxia 1% O2 (clinical samples); humidified chamber
  Duration    : 3 days = 4320 min = 259200 s
  BioScript   : heat seededCulture at 37c for 4320m

Step 5 | Media Exchange #1 (Day 3)
  Reagents    : Supplemented DMEM (fresh)
  Procedure   : 150 uL medium withdrawn from each channel via syringe pump (100 uL/min,
                infusion/withdrawal mode, BD Luer-Lok syringe). 150 uL fresh supplemented
                DMEM introduced per channel. Closed system incubated at 37 C / 5% CO2.
  BioScript   : culture_d3 = mix seededCulture with freshMedia1 for 2m

Step 6 | Day 3-6 Culture (Incubation Cycle 2)
  Conditions  : 37 C, 5% CO2, hypoxia 1% O2; humidified chamber
  Duration    : 3 days = 4320 min = 259200 s
  BioScript   : heat culture_d3 at 37c for 4320m

Step 7 | Media Exchange #2 (Day 6)
  Reagents    : Supplemented DMEM (fresh)
  Procedure   : Same as Step 5.
  BioScript   : culture_d6 = mix culture_d3 with freshMedia2 for 2m

Step 8 | Day 6-9 Culture (Incubation Cycle 3)
  Conditions  : 37 C, 5% CO2, hypoxia 1% O2; humidified chamber
  Duration    : 3 days = 4320 min = 259200 s
  BioScript   : heat culture_d6 at 37c for 4320m

Step 9 | Media Exchange #3 (Day 9)
  Reagents    : Supplemented DMEM (fresh)
  Procedure   : Same as Step 5.
  BioScript   : culture_d9 = mix culture_d6 with freshMedia3 for 2m

Step 10 | Day 9-11 Culture (Incubation Cycle 4)
  Conditions  : 37 C, 5% CO2, hypoxia 1% O2; humidified chamber
  Duration    : 2 days = 2880 min = 172800 s
  BioScript   : heat culture_d9 at 37c for 2880m

Step 11 | Day 11 - Culture Positivity Assessment
  Method      : Bright-field imaging at 10x magnification (Olympus inverted confocal microscope).
                Gray-value plot profiles obtained per microwell across maximum diameter (ImageJ).
                Combined scatterplots of gray values normalised to highest count per microwell.
                Microwells with dense cell clusters show gray values consistently <0.5 within
                microwell region. Microwells with debris or sparse monolayers show high gray values.
  Threshold   : Clusters in >=50% of microwells (~500 clusters from 1.25 mL blood) = POSITIVE.
                Debris/sparse monolayers only = NEGATIVE.
  Note        : Cultures should not have RBC contamination (incomplete RBC lysis impairs cluster
                boundary detection by image processing software).
  Branch      : clusterSignal > 0  -> Positive; proceed to drug infusion (BB2 / bsbbif_2_t)
                clusterSignal <= 0 -> Negative; drain culture, experiment ends (BB3 / bsbbif_3_f)
  Efficiency  : Pretreatment: 59.3% positive (n=27); Posttreatment: 19.6% positive (n=46);
                Overall: 34.2% positive (n=73)
  BioScript   : clusterSignal = detect clusterDetection on culture_d9 for 30s

[POSITIVE CULTURE PATH ONLY -- Steps 12-16]

Step 12 | Pre-Drug Medium Priming Flush (Day 11)
  Reagents    : Supplemented DMEM (fresh)
  Procedure   : 150 uL medium withdrawn per channel before drug loading.
                Device briefly primed with fresh DMEM at 100 uL/min prior to drug-containing
                medium introduction to clear existing medium from channels.
  BioScript   : primedCulture = mix culture_d9 with primingFlush for 2m

Step 13 | Doxorubicin Gradient Preparation and Infusion (Day 11)
  Reagents    : DoxorubicinStock (1 mM in DMSO; 1 uL into 1 mL DMEM -> ~1 uM working stock,
                ~0.1% DMSO final), SupplementedDMEM (vehicle control, 0% drug)
  Gradient    : Tree-like gradient generator mixes 0% vehicle and 100% drug inlets at 100 uL/min
                to produce 8 concentrations simultaneously:
                  Channel 0:  0.00 uM  (vehicle control; viability normalisation reference)
                  Channel 1: ~0.14 uM  (~14% of stock)
                  Channel 2: ~0.29 uM  (~29%)
                  Channel 3: ~0.43 uM  (~43%)
                  Channel 4: ~0.57 uM  (~57%)
                  Channel 5: ~0.71 uM  (~71%)
                  Channel 6: ~0.86 uM  (~86%)
                  Channel 7: ~1.00 uM  (100% of working stock)
  Procedure   : Drug loading carried out carefully at 100 uL/min (inward infusion) to avoid
                drug influx upon reinsertion of tubings. Evaporation limited by humidified chamber;
                gradient concentration remains stable over 72 h exposure period.
  BioScript   : 8 dispense calls (1x SupplementedDMEM + 7x DoxorubicinStock) followed by
                binary-tree mix operations representing gradient channel assignments.
                (BioScript abstraction: no native gradient-generator primitive available)

Step 14 | 72-Hour Drug Exposure Incubation (Day 11-14)
  Conditions  : 37 C, 5% CO2, hypoxia 1% O2; humidified chamber
  Duration    : 72 h = 4320 min = 259200 s
  Notes       : Gradient concentration remains constant over time. Vehicle control channel
                (culture_ch0, 0 uM doxorubicin) and drug-treated channels (drug_all)
                incubated simultaneously; treated as separate BioScript fluid variables.
  BioScript   : heat culture_ch0 at 37c for 4320m
                heat drug_all at 37c for 4320m

Step 15 | Day 14 - LIVE/DEAD In Situ Staining
  Reagents    : Calcein-AM (2 uM; Life Technologies), EtBr (ethidium bromide; red),
                CD45-allophycocyanin (APC; 1:100; Miltenyi Biotec Asia Pacific)
  Stain roles : Calcein-AM (green, ex 490 nm / em 526 nm) -> viable cells
                EtBr (red, ex 488 nm / em 617 nm) -> dead/damaged cells
                CD45-APC (red) -> leukocyte marker; gates out WBCs; only CD45- cells (green)
                counted for clinical sample viability rate determination
  Procedure   : Staining cocktail incubated in situ for 45 min at room temperature in dark.
                Samples flushed gently with PBS. Imaged with Olympus inverted confocal
                microscope (emission filters ET460/50m and ET535/50m).
  Notes       : Two separate stain dispenses (stainCtrl for vehicle control channel;
                stainDrug for drug-treated channels) required per BioScript ownership rules.
  BioScript   : stainCtrl = dispense 1 units of CalceinAM_EtBr_CD45APC_Stain
                stainDrug = dispense 1 units of CalceinAM_EtBr_CD45APC_Stain
                stained_ctrl = mix culture_ch0 with stainCtrl for 45m
                stained_drug = mix drug_all with stainDrug for 45m

Step 16 | Day 14 - Fluorescence Detection and IC50 Readout
  Module      : ctcViabilityDetection
  Procedure   :
    1. Z-stack images acquired from 25 microwells per channel at 37 C using confocal microscope.
       Stack slices: 15 um; compiled to max-intensity merged image.
       Microwells at consistent distance from assay inlet selected for evaluation.
    2. Images preprocessed by cropping and thresholding (signals 8-150 um);
       merged images compared to rule out repeated signal counts.
    3. CD45- gating: only green-fluorescent (calcein-AM+, CD45-) cells counted per microwell
       for clinical samples (rules out WBC signal).
    4. Viability % per channel normalised to vehicle control channel (channel 0, lowest drug).
    5. 4-parameter logistic equation curve fitting (Microsoft Excel).
    6. IC50 extracted as drug concentration at 50% normalised cell death (y axis).
  Branch      : viabilitySignal > 0  -> valid readout; dispose stained droplets (BB5)
                viabilitySignal <= 0 -> staining/imaging failure; drain all (BB6)
  BioScript   : viabilitySignal = detect ctcViabilityDetection on stained_ctrl for 45m


KEY RESULTS
-----------
MCF-7 cell line IC50  : 0.78 +/- 0.02 uM doxorubicin (4-parameter logistic fit; n=3 triplicate
                         cultures). Slightly higher than monolayer culture values (~0.5 uM)
                         due to heightened cell density in multilayer clusters reducing drug penetration.

Clinical IC50 values (breast cancer patients):
  Sample CTB039  | Pretreatment  | IC50 = 0.85 uM
  Sample CES021  | Posttreatment | IC50 > 1 uM  (drug resistance suspected)
  Sample CES053  | Posttreatment | IC50 = 0.34 uM
  Sample P2B28   | Posttreatment | IC50 > 1 uM  (drug resistance suspected)
  Sample P2B29   | Pretreatment  | IC50 = 0.94 uM
  Sample P2B29   | Posttreatment | IC50 = 0.86 uM (slight IC50 reduction; possible drug sensitivity
                                                    increase after doxorubicin + sunitinib cycle)

Cluster formation and drug response: Percentage of microwells with clusters decreased with
   increasing doxorubicin concentration (average correlation coefficient -0.71), confirming
   that cluster formation correlates inversely with drug sensitivity (consistent with prior work).
   Macrophage-like cell counts per microwell also correlated negatively with cluster formation
   and may serve as an additional prognostic indicator.


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file  : khoo_ctc_liquid_biopsy_drug_screening.bs
Compiler        : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output       : khoo_ctc_liquid_biopsy_drug_screening.ir
DAG output      : khoo_ctc_liquid_biopsy_drug_screening_main_dag.dot
Basic blocks    : 7 (BB1-BB7); 8 CFG edges
Modules         : clusterDetection, ctcViabilityDetection
Manifests       : WholeBlood, RBC_LysisBuffer, PBS, SupplementedDMEM,
                  CalceinAM_EtBr_CD45APC_Stain, DoxorubicinStock

Duration conversions (h token unsupported; all times in m or s):
  3-day incubation cycles x3  : 4320m -> 259200.0 SECOND (IR)
  2-day incubation (Day 9-11) : 2880m -> 172800.0 SECOND (IR)
  72 h drug exposure           : 4320m -> 259200.0 SECOND (IR)
  45 min staining/detection    : 45m   ->   2700.0 SECOND (IR)

Known compiler behaviours observed in IR:
  - `drain` in .bs source lowered to `dispose()` in IR (known bug; .bs semantics preserved)
  - True-branch blocks (bsbbif_N_t) do not emit unconditional jump in IR text;
    DOT edge bsbbif_5_t -> bsbbif_7_j resolves correctly in DAG
  - `heat` is void/in-place; fluid variable not consumed by heat instructions
  - PHI nodes emitted at bsbbif_4_j (cluster join) for all variables assigned in pass branch only

BioScript abstraction notes:
  - Gradient generator: 8-channel simultaneous concentration gradient abstracted as
    8 discrete DoxorubicinStock dispenses followed by binary-tree mix operations.
    No native gradient-generator primitive exists in BioScript.
  - Hypoxia: 1% O2 chamber condition not expressible in BioScript; documented in comments;
    encoded as heat at 37 C.
  - Media exchange: each cycle modelled as dispense SupplementedDMEM + mix with culture
    variable; fluid ownership re-assigned at each exchange per single-use variable rule.
  - Staining: two separate dispense calls (stainCtrl, stainDrug) to satisfy single-use
    ownership constraint; a single stainReagent variable used in two mix calls would
    constitute a double-consume violation.
  - viabilitySignal scoping: assigned and disposed entirely within the cluster-pass branch (BB2);
    never referenced on the cluster-fail path (BB3); clusterSignal assigned unconditionally
    before its if/else and disposed unconditionally at the join (BB4).

protocol.title: Liquid Biopsy and Therapeutic Response: Circulating Tumor Cell Cultures for Evaluation of Anticancer Treatment
protocol.platform: Integrated three-layer PDMS microfluidic device (continuous-flow, gradient generator + channel barrier + tapered microwell array)
protocol.cell_source: Primary circulating tumor cells (CTCs) from clinical whole blood; breast cancer patients
protocol.objective: Short-term primary CTC culture in tapered microwells, doxorubicin dose-response screening via 8-channel concentration gradient, and IC50 determination without pre-enrichment

layers: Topmost layer: tree-like serpentine gradient generator (PDMS); mixes two inlet flows to produce 8 output concentrations
Intermediate layer: channel barrier (aluminum mold, Whits Technologies); defines 8 parallel culture channels; prevents cross-contamination between concentration zones
Bottommost layer: custom multimicrowell array (PDMS); each channel contains ~1000 tapered elliptical microwells

microwell_geometry.fabrication_method: diffuser back-side lithography; SU-8 2100 resist (300 um), opal diffusing glass, Hg(Xe) arc lamp 12 mW/cm2 at 365 nm, 9 s exposure

gradient_generator.notes: Channel-0 outlet (0% drug) serves as vehicle control and viability normalisation reference. Gradient distribution confirmed by FITC dye fluorescence quantification and COMSOL simulation.

device.assembly: standard oxygen plasma bonding; device placed in 150-mm dish with PBS film to limit evaporation; incubated in humidified chamber
device.pdms_formulation: Sylgard 184 (Dow Corning), 10:1 prepolymer:curing agent, degassed, cured at 80 C for 1 h

culture_media.notes: Supplemented DMEM selected after optimization across medium conditions (fig. S18 of paper)

media_exchange.syringe: BD Luer-Lok 10 mL (Becton, Dickinson and Company)
media_exchange.pump: NE-1000, New Era Pump Systems Inc.

doxorubicin.working_dilution: 1 uL stock into 1 mL supplemented DMEM

cd45_apc.labels: leukocytes (CD45+); used to gate out WBCs
cd45_apc.notes: Only CD45- cells (green fluorescence) counted for clinical sample viability rate

imaging.image_processing: ImageJ (NIH); max-intensity merged Z-stacks; cropping and thresholding 8-150 um; repeated signals ruled out by comparison

culture_conditions.atmosphere_clinical: hypoxia, 1% O2 (mimics in vivo tumor microenvironment)
culture_conditions.dish: 150-mm dish with thin PBS film to limit evaporation
culture_conditions.notes: Clinical CTC samples develop clusters only under hypoxic conditions; MCF-7 cell line forms clusters under both normoxic and hypoxic conditions at high seeding concentrations

positivity_criteria.threshold: CTC-containing clusters in >=50% of microwells per channel
positivity_criteria.method: bright-field imaging at 10x magnification; grey-value plot profiles (ImageJ); low grey values (<0.5) within microwell region indicate dense cluster
positivity_criteria.negative_classification: cell debris or sparse monolayers; grey values consistently high

ic50_determination.normalisation: viability data normalised to results from lowest-drug channel (channel 0, vehicle control)
ic50_determination.ic50_definition: concentration at which curve passes through 50% normalised cell death (y axis)
ic50_determination.imaging: Z-stack confocal images of 25 microwells per channel; 15 um slices; max-intensity merge
ic50_determination.gating: only CD45- cells (green) considered for clinical samples
ic50_determination.notes: IC50 > 1 uM indicates drug tolerance or resistance (above maximum tested range). Posttreatment P2B29 showed higher IC50 vs pretreatment, suggesting onset of drug resistance.

steps.name: Blood collection and RBC lysis
steps.notes: Whole blood (10 mL equiv.) from EDTA vacutainer; lysed within 10 h of withdrawal; 3-5 min lysis at room temperature; retains nucleated cell fraction (WBCs + CTCs)

steps.name: PBS wash of nucleated cell fraction
steps.notes: Single PBS wash to remove residual lysis buffer and debris; nucleated cell pellet retained

steps.name: Cell seeding into microfluidic device
steps.notes: Nucleated cells resuspended in 1.6 mL supplemented DMEM; evenly distributed across 8 channels (~200 uL per channel); BioScript `mix` abstracts on-chip syringe-pump seeding event

steps.name: Day 0-3 incubation
steps.notes: Closed system in humidified chamber; 150-mm dish with PBS film; clinical samples under hypoxia

steps.name: Media exchange #1 (Day 3)
steps.notes: 150 uL withdrawn via syringe pump (infusion/withdrawal mode, 100 uL/min); 150 uL fresh supplemented DMEM added per channel; BioScript models as dispense + mix

steps.name: Day 11 culture positivity assessment
steps.method: bright-field imaging at 10x; grey-value plot profiles per microwell (ImageJ); combined scatterplots normalised to highest count per microwell
steps.positive_threshold: clusters in >=50% of microwells (~500 clusters per 1.25 mL blood)

steps.name: Pre-drug medium priming flush (Day 11)
steps.notes: 150 uL medium withdrawn per channel before drug loading; device briefly primed with fresh DMEM at 100 uL/min to clear existing medium prior to drug infusion

steps.name: Doxorubicin gradient preparation and infusion (Day 11)
steps.notes: Tree-like gradient generator simultaneously delivers 8 concentrations from 0% (DMEM vehicle) and 100% (DoxorubicinStock) inlets. BioScript models as 8 discrete dispenses + binary-tree mix operations. Loading must be carried out carefully to avoid drug influx upon reinsertion of tubings.

steps.name: 72-hour drug exposure incubation (Day 11-14)
steps.notes: Gradient concentration remains constant over time; evaporation limited by humidified chamber. Vehicle control (culture_ch0) and drug-treated channels (drug_all) incubated separately in BioScript representation.

steps.name: Day 14 - LIVE/DEAD in situ staining
steps.notes: Two separate stain dispenses (stainCtrl and stainDrug) required per BioScript single-use variable ownership rule. Vehicle control and drug-treated channels stained independently.

steps.name: Day 14 - Fluorescence detection and IC50 readout
detection_steps: Confocal Z-stack acquisition (25 microwells/channel, 15 um slices, max-intensity merge)
CD45- gating: only green-fluorescent (calcein-AM+, CD45-) cells counted per microwell
Viability % per channel normalised to vehicle control channel (channel 0)
IC50 extracted as drug concentration at 50% normalised cell death

bioscript_compiler_notes.ir_output: khoo_ctc_liquid_biopsy_drug_screening.ir

duration_conversions.note: BioScript supports s and m duration tokens only; h token unsupported

known_compiler_behaviours.drain_to_dispose: `drain` in .bs source is lowered to `dispose()` in IR output; .bs source remains semantically correct
known_compiler_behaviours.true_branch_no_jump: true-branch blocks (bsbbif_N_t) do not emit unconditional jump in IR text; DOT edges resolve correctly
known_compiler_behaviours.heat_is_void: `heat` is void/in-place; fluid variable ownership not consumed by heat instructions

abstraction_notes.gradient_generator: 8-channel continuous-flow gradient generator abstracted as 8 discrete DoxorubicinStock dispenses + binary-tree mix operations; no native gradient primitive in BioScript
abstraction_notes.hypoxia: 1% O2 hypoxic chamber condition not expressible in BioScript; documented in comments only; encoded as heat at 37 C
abstraction_notes.media_exchange: Each 3-day media exchange cycle modelled as dispense SupplementedDMEM + mix with culture variable; fluid ownership re-assigned at each exchange
abstraction_notes.stain_split: Two separate stain dispense calls (stainCtrl, stainDrug) used to avoid single-variable double-consume ownership violation
abstraction_notes.viability_signal_scoping: viabilitySignal assigned and disposed entirely within the cluster-pass branch (BB2); never referenced on the cluster-fail path (BB3)

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.description: RBC lysis, PBS wash, cell seeding, Day 0-11 culture with 3 media exchanges, cluster detection

basic_blocks.label: clusterPass
basic_blocks.description: Pre-drug flush, doxorubicin gradient infusion, 72h exposure, LIVE/DEAD staining, viability detection gate

basic_blocks.label: clusterFail
basic_blocks.description: Culture negative; drain culture_d9; experiment ends

basic_blocks.label: clusterJoin
basic_blocks.description: PHI nodes for branch-diverged variables; dispose clusterSignal; NOP

basic_blocks.label: viabilityPass
basic_blocks.description: Valid LIVE/DEAD signal; dispose stained_ctrl, stained_drug, viabilitySignal

basic_blocks.label: viabilityFail
basic_blocks.description: Staining/imaging failure; drain stained_ctrl, stained_drug; dispose viabilitySignal

basic_blocks.label: finalCleanup
basic_blocks.description: Jump to clusterJoin (bsbbif_4_j); experiment complete

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Expansion of Patient-Derived Circulating Tumor Cells from Liquid Biopsies Using a CTC Microfluidic Culture Device
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/nprot.2017.125
Paper DOI    : http://dx.doi.org/10.1038/nprot.2017.125
Journal      : Nature Protocols, 2018, Vol. 13, No. 1, pp. 34-58
Platform     : Three-layer PDMS microfluidic device (gradient generator / barrier layer / microwell array) fabricated by soft lithography


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a microfluidics-based method for the ex vivo expansion of patient-derived
circulating tumor cells (CTCs) from liquid biopsies (peripheral blood) into CTC clusters, without
prior enrichment or exogenous growth factor supplements. The approach co-cultures CTCs with
patient-derived white blood cells (WBCs) in inverted dome-shaped elliptical microwells under
hypoxia (1% O2, 37 C), mimicking the tumor microenvironment niche. Monocyte-derived macrophages
within the co-culture differentiate into tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and are proposed as
key drivers of cluster formation.

The protocol is divided into five functional phases:
  1. Device priming and gradient generator calibration with FITC fluorescent dye (Steps 53-71)
  2. Blood preparation: RBC lysis and nucleated cell resuspension (Steps 72-77)
  3. CTC cluster culture in microwells under hypoxia for 14 days (Steps 78-79)
  4. Drug screening using the integrated gradient generator (Step 82)
  5. Immunofluorescence staining and imaging of CTC clusters (Steps 83-86)

Optional downstream procedures include post-enrichment with anti-CD45 microbeads (Step 81)
and DNA/RNA FISH for cancer cell identification (Steps 87-99).

Overall cluster formation success rate: >50% of clinical blood samples.
Assay duration from blood draw to cluster read-out: 2 weeks.
Drug screening after cluster formation: 48 h drug exposure + fluorescence read-out.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Layer i   : Concentration gradient generator (uppermost).
            Fabricated by standard PDMS replica molding on silicon wafer / SU-8 master
            (photolithography). Tree-like branched channel network splits two inlet streams
            into 8 output channels with a stable concentration gradient.
            Inlets: 2 (drug / vehicle control). Outlets: 8 channels.

Layer ii  : Barrier layer (middle).
            Fabricated from aluminum mold by machining; PDMS soft replica.
            Millimeter-scale barrier channels compartmentalise the 8 gradient outputs into
            individual cell-culture lanes, preventing cross-mixing at the microwell region.

Layer iii : Microwell layer (bottom).
            Fabricated by diffuser back-side lithography on a 4-inch soda lime mask plate
            coated with SU-8 3050 (double coat, >300 um total thickness).
            Opal diffuser (45 deg) generates dome-shaped exposure profile.
            Results in inverted dome-shaped elliptical microwells:
            150 um (width) x 250 um (length) x 150 um (depth); average diameter 187.5 um.
            1350 microwells per 60-mm Petri dish (laser ablation variant).
            8 columns of microwells aligned to 8 barrier channels.

Assembly   : Layers bonded by oxygen plasma treatment (150 W, 0.05 torr, 90 s) forming
             covalent -O-Si-O- bonds; baked at 80 C for >=1 h.
Material   : PDMS (Sylgard 184, 10:1 base:curing agent); biocompatible, optically
             transparent (240-1100 nm), elastomeric for accurate replica molding.

Alternate microwell fabrication: Laser ablation (CO2 laser, VLS 2.30; 10% speed, 50% power;
             laser-to-substrate distance 3 cm) on 35- or 60-mm Petri dishes (Box 1).


CELL LINES AND CLINICAL SAMPLES
--------------------------------
- MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 (ATCC): commercially available breast cancer cell lines used for
  device characterisation and spheroid formation validation.
  Culture: DMEM + 10% FBS + 1% pen-strep, 37 C, 5% CO2.
- Patient blood samples: 10 mL per patient, EDTA Vacutainer tubes, kept on ice.
  Cancer types validated: breast, lung, spinal cancer; locally advanced, early-stage,
  and refractory metastatic disease.
  Ethical approval: DSRB references 2012/00105, 2012/00979, 2010/00270, 2010/00691.
  All samples processed within 6 h of draw.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 53-56 | Device Priming
  Reagents  : 70% (vol/vol) ethanol, PBS (1x)
  Operation : Two syringes of 70% ethanol injected at 50 uL/min (~5 min) via two syringe pumps
              to prime the gradient generator and remove air bubbles. Followed by two syringes
              of PBS at 100 uL/min (~5 min) to remove ethanol residue.
  Purpose   : Hydrophilise PDMS channels; remove air; sterilise device before cell culture.
  Critical  : Replace syringe by disconnecting from tip (not tubing) to avoid new air bubbles.

Step 57-68 | Gradient Generator Calibration (FITC Dye)
  Reagents  : 100 uM FITC fluorescent dye (fluorescein isothiocyanate isomer I) in PBS,
              deionised (DI) water
  Operation : Syringe 1 (FITC dye) and Syringe 2 (DI water) pumped simultaneously at equal
              flow rates. After 30 min equilibration, 60 uL collected from each of the 8
              channels into a 384-well plate (Tecan Infinite M200 fluorescence plate reader).
  Flow rates : 25, 50, 100, 150, 200 uL/min (5 independent runs per device).
  Additional : 20 uM FITC at 100 uL/min to confirm concentration-independence of gradient.
  Repeats   : Three independent devices (Step 68).
  Results   : Concentration gradients similar across flow rates; close to theoretical values;
              no leakage observed; gradient independent of dye concentration.
  Purpose   : Verify uniform outlet flow rates, stable gradient generation, and device integrity.

Step 72-73 | Blood Preparation - RBC Lysis
  Reagents  : Patient blood (10 mL, EDTA Vacutainer), RBC lysis buffer (G-Bioscience 786650)
  Ratio     : 10 mL blood + 20 mL RBC lysis buffer (1:2 vol/vol)
  Duration  : 3 min at room temperature with gentle mixing (hypotonic hemolysis by osmotic stress)
  Critical  : Both blood and buffer at room temperature before mixing. Do not exceed 5 min.

Step 74-75 | Nucleated Cell Isolation
  Operation : Centrifuge lysed sample 1000g, 5 min, room temperature. Remove supernatant
              (plasma + lysed RBC fragments). Resuspend pellet in 5 mL PBS; centrifuge 335g,
              3 min to wash. Repeat wash if debris remains.
  Result    : Nucleated cell fraction (WBCs + CTCs); RBC lysis does not significantly affect
              nucleated cell viability.
  Storage   : Optional: add 10% (vol/vol) DMSO; cryopreserve at -80 C up to 4 weeks;
              long-term in liquid nitrogen up to 1 year.

Step 76-77 | Cell Resuspension and Seeding
  Reagents  : Supplemented DMEM (10% FBS, 1% pen-strep)
  Volume    : Resuspend in 1 mL per 1000 microwells; add 200-300 uL per channel.
  Seeding   : Volume-based (not count-based); multichannel pipette for simultaneous seeding.
  Culture   : 37 C, 5% CO2, 1% O2 (hypoxia incubator, humidified). Day 0.
  Note      : No surfactant coating required for clinical samples; non-adherent blood cells
              provide cushioning for CTCs in microwells.

Step 78 | Day-3 Media Change
  Operation : Remove 0.2 mL old medium (hand pipette or syringe pump at 200 uL/min).
              Replace with 0.2 mL fresh supplemented DMEM.
  Critical  : Minimal disturbance to microwell clusters to prevent cell loss.
              Increase frequency of media change if media turns yellow before 72 h.

Step 79 | Day-14 Cluster Assessment
  Operation : Phase-contrast microscopy of full microwell array.
  Criteria  :
    Morphological : Multilayered cell aggregate with defined boundaries.
    Cell count    : >=8 cells per 250 um^2 (Hoechst staining, Step 83A/83B).
    Cell density  : Low grayscale values in ImageJ histogram of microwell region.
  Threshold : >=50% microwells contain clusters = positive sample.
  Results   : >50% cluster formation rate across >300 clinical samples screened;
              73.3% in refractory metastatic cohort (n=44); 70/110 in locally advanced cancer.
  Note      : Cultures can be retained up to 2 months; can be passaged as spheroids to
              low-adherence dishes or 3D gels after 2 weeks.

Step 80 | Cluster Harvest
  Reagents  : PBS, trypsin 0.25% (wt/vol) with EDTA
  Operation : Remove media; wash with 1 mL PBS. Add 1 mL trypsin; incubate 37 C for 3 min.
              Neutralise with equal volume fresh supplemented DMEM. Dissociate by gentle
              pipetting. Centrifuge 335g, 3 min; resuspend pellet in 1 mL PBS.

Step 81 | Post-Enrichment (Optional)
  Reagents  : Anti-CD45 microbeads (Miltenyi Biotec, cat. no. 130-045-801)
  Purpose   : Negative selection to deplete CD45+ leukocytes; obtain higher-purity CTC fraction.
  Use case  : Required for downstream genomic sequencing; optional for drug screening.

Step 82 | Drug Screening
  Reagents  : Doxorubicin (Sigma-Aldrich D1515) dissolved in DMSO; supplemented DMEM
  Working concentration : 1 uM doxorubicin in supplemented DMEM (freshly prepared, store on ice)
  Delivery  : Gradient generator delivers 8-point dilution series across 8 channels in parallel
              (inlet 1: drug; inlet 2: DMSO vehicle control). Introduced by hand pipette or
              syringe pump.
  Duration  : 48 h incubation at 37 C (= 2880 min)
  Viability : Calcein AM (1:1000 in PBS; live cells; ex 490 nm, em 526 nm) and
              propidium iodide (1:1000 in PBS; dead cells; ex 488 nm, em 617 nm).
              Incubate 15 min before imaging.
  Read-out  : Cell viability (%) vs. drug concentration (%); IC50 determination.

Step 83-84 | Immunofluorescence Staining (Fixed-Cell Protocol, Option B)
  (i)   Fix cells: 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS, 10 min on ice.
  (ii)  Block: 2.5% (wt/vol) BSA in PBS, 30 min on ice.
  (iii) Permeabilise: 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, 1 min on ice.
  (iv)  Wash with PBS; centrifuge 335g, 3 min.
  (v)   Primary antibody staining in 2.5% BSA/PBS, 30 min on ice (dark):
          - pan-cytokeratin (CK) antibody (FITC, 1:50): epithelial CTC marker
          - CD45 antibody (APC, 1:50): leukocyte marker
          - Hoechst dye (1 M, 1:1000): nuclear counterstain
  Wash  : 5 mL PBS; resuspend in 100 uL PBS for imaging.
  Key phenotypes:
          CK+/CD45-/Hoechst+  = putative CTC
          CD45+/Hoechst+       = leukocyte feeder cell
  Imaging : Transfer to 8-well chamber (Nunc Lab-Tek); Olympus inverted microscope
            (IX71) with filter sets ET460/50m, ET535/50m, ET605/70; automated stage.
            Image entire well or single fields; analyse with IMARIS or ImageJ.

Steps 87-99 | DNA FISH (Optional, 2 days)
  Purpose   : Identify cancer cells by copy number of breast cancer-associated genes
              (CCND1, HER2, FGFR1, MYC, TOP2A, ZNF217; Table 1 in paper).
  Key steps : Fixation (acetic acid:methanol 1:3); RNase treatment (45 min, 37 C);
              denaturation (70% formamide in 2x SSC, 80 C, 10 min); probe hybridisation
              (42 C, 16 h); DAPI counterstain; confocal imaging (Olympus IX71).
  Note      : Not encoded in BioScript (no fluid primitive for FISH hybridisation steps).


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : khoo_ctc_microfluidic_cluster.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
DAG            : khoo_ctc_microfluidic_cluster_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations converted to minutes (m) for compiler compatibility
                 (BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported)
                 72h   ->  4320m  (Day 0 to Day 3 culture;  IR: 259200.0 SECOND)
                 11d   -> 15840m  (Day 3 to Day 14 culture; IR: 950400.0 SECOND)
                 48h   ->  2880m  (drug incubation;         IR: 172800.0 SECOND)
Modules        : clusterFormationDetection, viabilityDetection,
                 immunostainingDetection, drugEfficacyDetection
Omissions      : Photolithography / soft-lithography device fabrication (Steps 1-52)
                 has no BioScript fluid primitive equivalent and is omitted by design.
                 DNA FISH procedure (Steps 87-99) is omitted for the same reason.
                 Anti-CD45 post-enrichment (Step 81) is included as a mix + drain
                 sequence within BB1 (no independent QC gate).
Scoping note   : All QC-gated variables (clusterSignal, drugSignal, stainingSignal)
                 are defined at module scope (BB1/main) to satisfy the lilott8/BioScript
                 requirement that variables consumed by downstream BBs must not be
                 defined inside an if/else block. Inner-block operations are limited to
                 dispose/drain of same-block droplets only (mirrors samlali and moazami
                 reference .bs files).
Drain note     : BioScript `drain` compiles to `dispose(...)` at IR level. Distinction
                 is preserved at .bs source level for human readability only.

protocol.title: Expansion of Patient-Derived Circulating Tumor Cells from Liquid Biopsies Using a CTC Microfluidic Culture Device
protocol.platform: Three-layer PDMS microfluidic device (gradient generator / barrier layer / microwell array); soft lithography + diffuser back-side lithography
cell_lines: MCF-7 (human breast cancer, ATCC HTB-22) - device characterisation and spheroid validation
MDA-MB-231 (human breast cancer, ATCC CRM-HTB-26) - device characterisation
Patient blood samples - clinical CTC cluster formation and drug screening
protocol.objective: Ex vivo expansion of patient-derived CTCs from liquid biopsies into CTC clusters without prior enrichment or growth factor supplements; downstream drug screening and immunofluorescence characterisation

layers: Layer i: Concentration gradient generator (uppermost) - PDMS replica on silicon wafer / SU-8 master; tree-like branched channels; 2 inlets, 8 outputs
Layer ii: Barrier layer (middle) - PDMS soft replica of aluminum mold (machined); compartmentalises 8 gradient outputs into individual culture lanes
Layer iii: Microwell layer (bottom) - PDMS by diffuser back-side lithography; inverted dome-shaped elliptical microwells

material.name: PDMS (Sylgard 184, Dow Corning)
material.bonding: Oxygen plasma treatment (150 W, 0.05 torr, 90 s) + bake at 80 C >=1 h

gradient_calibration.dye: FITC (fluorescein isothiocyanate isomer I, Sigma F7250)
gradient_calibration.reader: Tecan Infinite M200 PRO fluorescence plate reader

surfactant_coatings.pluronic_acid: Pluronics F-127 or Pluronic acid (Sigma 9003-11-6) in PBS; 0.1% vol/vol
surfactant_coatings.purpose: Promote spheroid formation with cancer cell lines; not required for clinical samples

post_enrichment.purpose: Negative selection of CD45+ leukocytes for higher-purity CTC fraction
post_enrichment.use_case: Required for genomic sequencing; optional for drug screening

steps.name: Device priming with ethanol
steps.notes: Two syringes of 70% ethanol on separate syringe pumps; removes air bubbles from gradient generator. Priming ends when no air bubbles remain in channels.

steps.name: PBS flush to remove ethanol
steps.notes: Remove all ethanol residue from gradient generator before cell culture. Replace syringes by disconnecting from tips (not tubing) to prevent new air bubbles.

steps.name: Gradient generator calibration - 25 uL/min
steps.notes: 100 uM FITC dye vs DI water. Collect 60 uL from each of 8 channels after 30 min equilibration. Dispose gradient mix and calibration signal.

steps.name: Gradient generator calibration - 50 uL/min
steps.notes: Identical to S3 at 50 uL/min.

steps.name: Gradient generator calibration - 100 uL/min
steps.notes: Also run separately with 20 uM FITC (Step 67) to confirm concentration-independence.

steps.name: Gradient generator calibration - 150 uL/min
steps.notes: Identical to S3 at 150 uL/min.

steps.name: Gradient generator calibration - 200 uL/min
steps.notes: Final flow rate run. After all five calibration runs, flush device with PBS to clear FITC. Repeat entire calibration on 3 independent devices (Step 68).

steps.name: RBC lysis
steps.notes: RBC lysis buffer is hypotonic; promotes hemolysis by osmotic stress. Both blood and buffer at room temperature before mixing. Do not exceed 5 min lysis. Process within 6 h of blood draw.

steps.name: Nucleated cell wash
steps.notes: Resuspend pellet in 5 mL PBS to remove residual RBC debris. Repeat wash if debris remains (red layer above white/yellowish pellet after centrifugation).

steps.name: Cell resuspension in supplemented DMEM
steps.notes: Volume-based seeding because initial CTC count does not predict cluster-forming potential. Use multichannel pipette for simultaneous seeding across all channels.

steps.name: Cell seeding into microwell device - Day 0 to Day 3
steps.notes: No surfactant coating required for clinical samples; non-adherent blood cells cushion CTCs. Multichannel pipette seeding into 8 channels. Day 0 of culture.

steps.name: Day-3 partial media change and Day 3 to Day 14 culture
steps.operation: drain then mix (partial media removal and replacement) then heat
steps.notes: Minimal disturbance critical to prevent cell loss. Increase media change frequency if media turns yellow before 72 h (highly proliferative culture).

cluster_criteria.morphological: Multilayered cell aggregate with defined boundaries
cluster_criteria.cell_density: Low grayscale values in ImageJ histogram of microwell region

steps.name: Post-enrichment with anti-CD45 microbeads (optional)
steps.notes: Optional. Mix cluster harvest with anti-CD45 microbeads per manufacturer protocol (Miltenyi Biotec). Drain depletes CD45+ leukocytes. Not gated separately in CFG; integrated into BB4 (clusterJoin) before drug screening.

steps.name: Drug exposure - doxorubicin gradient
steps.delivery: Gradient generator 8-point dilution series; syringe pump or hand pipette
steps.notes: Freshly prepare drug solution and store on ice. Gradient generator delivers drug vs. vehicle control across all 8 channels simultaneously.

steps.name: Drug efficacy viability staining and detection
steps.read_out: Cell viability (%) vs. drug concentration (%); IC50 curve

steps.name: Cluster harvest by trypsinisation
steps.operation: mix then heat then mix then drain then mix
steps.notes: Wash with 1 mL PBS. Add 1 mL trypsin; incubate 37 C 3 min. Neutralise with equal volume fresh DMEM. Dissociate by gentle pipetting. Centrifuge 335g, 3 min; resuspend in 1 mL PBS.

steps.name: PFA fixation
steps.operation: mix then heat (on-ice incubation at 4 C)
steps.notes: 4% wt/vol PFA; 10 min on ice. Alternatively, stain CD45 before fixation to prevent loss of membrane antigens.

steps.name: BSA blocking
steps.operation: mix then heat (on-ice incubation at 4 C)
steps.notes: 2.5% wt/vol BSA in PBS; 30 min on ice.

steps.name: Triton X-100 permeabilisation
steps.operation: mix then heat (on-ice incubation at 4 C)
steps.notes: 0.1% vol/vol Triton X-100; 1 min on ice. Enables intracellular antibody penetration (pan-CK).

steps.name: PBS wash after permeabilisation
steps.notes: Wash with PBS; centrifuge 335g, 3 min. Remove Triton X-100 before antibody staining.

steps.name: Primary antibody and nuclear stain incubation
steps.operation: mix then heat (on-ice incubation at 4 C)
steps.notes: pan-CK (FITC, 1:50) + CD45 (APC, 1:50) + Hoechst (1:1000). Protect from light to prevent fluorophore bleaching.

steps.name: Final PBS wash and resuspension for imaging

culture_conditions.cluster_composition: Heterogeneous co-culture; 10-50% epithelial CK+ cancer cells of total cell count
culture_conditions.key_mechanism: Patient WBCs act as feeder cells; monocytes differentiate into tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) within clusters, mimicking tumor microenvironment

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.description: Device priming, gradient calibration, blood prep, seeding, culture, drug screen, harvest, immunostaining

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_4_j
basic_blocks.description: dispose(clusterSignal); anti-CD45 enrichment; drug screen

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_7_j
basic_blocks.description: dispose(drugSignal); cluster harvest; immunostaining

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_10_j
basic_blocks.description: dispose(stainingSignal); experiment ends; NOP

omissions: Photolithography and soft-lithography device fabrication (Steps 1-52): no BioScript fluid primitive equivalent
DNA/RNA FISH procedure (Steps 87-99): no BioScript fluid primitive equivalent
bioscript_compiler_notes.scoping_note: All QC-gated variables (clusterSignal, drugSignal, stainingSignal) defined at BB1/main scope. Inner if/else blocks limited to dispose/drain of same-block droplets only.
bioscript_compiler_notes.drain_note: BioScript `drain` compiles to `dispose(...)` in IR. Source-level distinction preserved for human readability only.

ir_observations.seededDevice_after_drain: seededDevice1[0] is used in mix after drain; BioScript SSA does not enforce consumed semantics after drain. Physically correct: cells remain in device after partial media removal.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : A Microfluidic DNA Library Preparation Platform for Next-Generation Sequencing
Source Link  : https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article/file?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0068988&type=printable
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0068988
Journal      : PLoS ONE, 2013, Vol. 8, Issue 7, Article e68988
Platform     : DMF hub with peripheral capillary-based modules (digital microfluidics +
               continuous-flow off-chip sample preparation modules)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a fully integrated and automated microfluidic system for preparing
Illumina sequencer-ready NGS libraries from nanogram-scale genomic DNA samples. The platform
combines a central digital microfluidic (DMF) hub -- a planar, Teflon-AF-coated ITO electrode
array that actuates discrete droplets via electrowetting -- with peripheral continuous-flow
capillary-based modules that perform each of the four unit operations in the Nextera library
