preparation workflow: DNA tagmentation, magnetic bead-based clean-up, limited-cycle PCR, and
two-stage size selection.

The DMF hub serves as a "fluidic router": it meters reagents, routes droplets between
peripheral modules via in-plane fused-silica capillaries, and integrates all sample
preparation steps into a single, hands-free, programmable protocol. Off-DMF modules are
individually optimised for their respective unit operations, allowing reliable thermocycling,
magnetic bead manipulation, and precise size selection that would be difficult to implement
on the DMF surface alone.

The platform was validated with human genomic DNA, Escherichia coli MG1655 gDNA (5 ng input),
and Klebsiella pneumoniae BAA-2146 (KpnNDM) gDNA. E. coli libraries yielded >99% alignment
to the reference genome, even genome coverage, and mean depth of 168-320X across three
replicates. De novo assembly of KpnNDM revealed at least five beta-lactamase genes including
NDM-1. The protocol reduces hands-on time to ~5 min and total preparation time to ~1 h,
using ~30 uL total reagent volume (vs. 80-650 uL conventional).


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Hub type : Central DMF hub; two gap configurations:
             185 um gap (human gDNA; 1-2 uL droplet volumes)
             400 um gap (bacterial gDNA; 2X volumes)

Bottom plate : ITO-patterned glass (photolithography + etching); coated with 4 um Parylene-C
               + 50 nm Teflon-AF (spin-coated 1% wt/wt Fluorinert FC-40, 2000 rpm, 60 s;
               post-baked at 160 C, 10 min). 48 actuation electrodes: 44 rectangular
               (~2.5 x 2.5 mm and ~6.3 x 9.5 mm), 4 pentagon-shaped (~4.5 x 7.5 x 6.3 mm);
               inter-electrode gap 20 um.
Top plate    : Unpatterned ITO glass; 50 nm Teflon-AF.
Manifold     : Custom-engineered polymer manifold frame with metal compression frames;
               spring-loaded pogo-pin electrical contacts; CapTite fittings.

Capillary interface:
  14 side ports; fused-silica capillaries (Polymicro) coated in-house with Teflon-AF.
  185 um gap:  160/100 um OD/ID capillaries (Part TSU100170); tip ~250 um from
               2.5 x 2.5 mm receiving electrodes.
  400 um gap:  360/100 um OD/ID capillaries (Part TSU100375); directly inserted.
  Module tubing: 750/562 um OD/ID polycarbonate (Part CT562-750-5, Paradigm Optics).
  Short coupling tubes: 500/167 um OD/ID (Part CT250-500-5); glued with optical cement.
  Pumping:     8-port valve manifold syringe pump (Part 59943-01, Hamilton, Reno NV);
               positive displacement; 10 uL/min flow rate. 1-2 uL air gap separates
               reagent bolus from pumping water.

Peripheral modules:
  Tagmentation   : Thermal module; 750 um OD tubing in ~850 x 800 um (D x W) groove in
                   custom-machined Al block; module recessed ~100 um below block surface
                   for temperature match within ~5 C. Closed-loop PID TEC.
  Limited-cycle PCR : Same Al block configuration; OpenPCR benchtop cycler (Saratoga CA).
  Clean-up       : Capillary tube module; external neodymium magnet (3 mm dia x 3 mm,
                   K&J Magnetics, Jamison PA); positive pressure-driven syringe pump for
                   near-complete supernatant removal; bolus shuttle resuspension.
  Size selection : Same magnet/pump configuration as clean-up; two-stage bead:DNA ratio
                   protocol (2.2 uL and 0.45 uL SPRI beads for Stages 1 and 2).
  Waste          : Dedicated waste capillary and reservoir.

Actuation: 80-90 V_rms at 15 kHz generated by function generator (Trek, Medina NY) amplified
           by Digi-Key Corporation (Thief River Falls MN). Computer-controlled electronic
           interface via manual keystrokes or preprogrammed scripts. Droplets visualised with
           MVX10 microscope (Olympus) + QIClick camera (Qimaging); Streampix5 (Norpix) for
           video capture.


REAGENTS
--------
Carrier fluid      : Fluorinert FC-40 (Sigma Chemical, St. Louis MO)
Pluronic additive  : Pluronic F127 (Sigma Chemical); 0.1% w/v in all DNA and reagent solutions.
                     Added to prevent biofouling (protein/enzyme adsorption to Teflon-AF).
                     Validated not to affect Nextera tagmentation efficiency (Fig S1, paper).
Buffer             : 1X Tris-EDTA (TE) pH 8.0 (Sigma Chemical)
Nextera enzyme mix : Nextera DNA Sample Preparation Kit (Illumina, San Diego CA)
                     On-chip mixture: 2 uL High Molecular Weight + 0.5 uL enzyme mix + 0.1% F127
PCR mixture        : 12.5 uL 2X PCR buffer + 0.5 uL primer cocktail + 0.5 uL PCR enzyme
                     + 0.5 uL 50X Adapter 2 (Nextera kit); scaled to 2.8 uL on-chip volume
SPRI beads         : Solid Phase Reversible Immobilisation beads (Beckman Coulter, Danvers MA)
Wash solvent       : Ethanol (HPLC-grade organic solvent)
Elution buffer     : Water + 0.1% Pluronic F127 w/v
Decontamination    : 10% v/v bleach then deionized water rinse between library runs


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | gDNA Sample Dispensing and Nextera Enzyme Mixing
  Reagents        : GenomicDNA (1.8 uL at 5 ng/uL in TE + 0.1% F127); NexteraEnzymeMix (0.6 uL)
  Operation       : Dispense both droplets from pre-loaded capillaries onto 185 um-gap DMF hub;
                    actuate together; mix by continuous aspiration in and out of capillary for 30 s
                    at room temperature (80-90 V_rms, 15 kHz)
  Duration        : 30 s mixing
  Notes           : Bacterial gDNA runs use 400 um-gap hub with 2X volumes of all reagents.

Step 2 | Tagmentation
  Reagents        : tagmentationMix
  Operation       : Aspirate into tagmentation thermal module; incubate at 55 C for 5 min
  Temperature     : 55 C
  Duration        : 5 min (300 s)
  Module          : Tagmentation Al block (closed-loop PID TEC; temperature match within ~5 C)
  Product         : Adapter-tagged DNA fragments; broad 150-1000 bp distribution (Fig 4b);
                    adapter dimers ~45 bp also generated; removed in Step 3
  Notes           : Transposase simultaneously fragments and tags gDNA (Nextera transposition
                    reaction). No mechanical fragmentation or end-repair required.

Step 3 | Magnetic Bead Clean-up -- Capture and Supernatant Removal
  Reagents        : tagmentedProduct; MagneticBeads_SPRI (4.5 uL)
  Operation       : Merge on DMF hub (30 s); aspirate combined droplet into clean-up module;
                    apply external neodymium magnet; immobilise bead pellet on inner tube wall;
                    positive pressure-driven flow removes supernatant; supernatant returned to
                    DMF hub and actuated to waste capillary
  Duration        : 30 s mixing
  Supernatant removed: Excess enzyme, adapter dimers, small DNA fragments
  Notes           : Near-complete supernatant removal achieved by positive pressure-driven syringe
                    pump flow (vs. conventional DMF magnet actuation). Bead pellet not on DMF
                    surface -- preserves Teflon-AF coating (Fig 3, paper).

Step 4 | Ethanol Wash of Bead Pellet (x3)
  Reagents        : EthanolWash (3.0 uL per cycle)
  Operation       : Dispense fresh ethanol droplet onto DMF hub; aspirate into clean-up module;
                    shuttle bolus back-and-forth across immobilised bead pellet for 30 s;
                    return ethanol to DMF hub; actuate to waste module; aspirate off-chip.
                    Repeat for 3 wash cycles total
  Duration        : 30 s per wash cycle; 3 cycles
  Notes           : Chaotic back-and-forth mixing enhances contaminant removal. Each wash
                    uses a fresh 3 uL ethanol droplet dispensed independently.

Step 5 | Elution of Purified Tagmented DNA
  Reagents        : ElutionBuffer (2.2 uL)
  Operation       : Dispense elution buffer onto DMF hub; aspirate into clean-up module;
                    remove external magnet; shuttle bolus for 30 s to resuspend bead pellet;
                    re-apply magnet to immobilise beads; return DNA-containing eluate to DMF hub;
                    actuate to PCR inlet electrode
  Duration        : 30 s resuspension
  Temperature     : Room temperature
  Product         : 2.2 uL purified adapter-tagged DNA fragments (excess enzyme and adapter
                    dimers removed)

Step 6 | PCR Mixture Dispensing and Merging with Eluate
  Reagents        : cleanedDNA (2.2 uL); PCRMixture (2.8 uL)
  Operation       : Dispense PCR Mixture from capillary onto DMF hub; merge with eluate (30 s);
                    aspirate 2.8 uL combined droplet into PCR thermal module inlet;
                    remaining 2.2 uL actuated to waste
  Duration        : 30 s mixing

Step 7 | Limited-Cycle PCR -- Adapter Addition and Library Enrichment
  Reagents        : prePCRDroplet (2.8 uL in PCR module)
  Operation       : Thermocycling in PCR module (Al block, OpenPCR cycler, closed-loop PID TEC)
  PCR conditions  :
    Initial extension  : 72 C for 3 min
    Denaturation       : 95 C for 30 s
    10 cycles          :
      Denaturation     : 95 C for 10 s
      Annealing        : 62 C for 30 s
      Extension        : 72 C for 3 min
    Note: 9 cycles for bacterial gDNA (400 um gap hub)
  Product         : Enriched library ~200-10000 bp; Illumina-specific dual-indexed sequencing
                    adapters incorporated; primer dimers ~55 bp present (removed by size selection)
                    (Fig 4c)
  Notes           : PCR reaction mixture (2.8 uL) cycled in module. After completion, product
                    dispensed back onto DMF hub for size selection.

Step 8 | Size Selection Stage 1 -- Removal of Fragments <200 bp
  Reagents        : prePCRDroplet; MagneticBeads_SPRI (2.2 uL)
  Operation       : Merge PCR product with SPRI beads on DMF hub (30 s); aspirate into
                    size-selection module; apply magnet; immobilise beads;
                    return supernatant to DMF hub
  Bead ratio      : High bead:DNA ratio (binds all DNA fragments including primer dimers
                    and small fragments <200 bp onto beads)
  Supernatant     : Contains desired 200-400 bp library fragments in solution at this ratio
  Notes           : The supernatant -- not the bead-bound fraction -- carries the size-selected
                    library at Stage 1. Bead pellet (small DNA, primer dimers) disposed.

Step 9 | Size Selection Stage 2 -- Removal of Fragments >400 bp
  Reagents        : librarySuper; MagneticBeads_SPRI (0.45 uL); EthanolWash; ElutionBuffer
  Operation       : Merge Stage 1 supernatant with low-volume SPRI beads (30 s); aspirate into
                    size-selection module; apply magnet; immobilise beads containing 200-400 bp
                    library; ethanol wash bead pellet; elute final library (3 uL EB; 5 uL for
                    bacterial gDNA); return eluate to DMF hub as final sequencer-ready library
  Bead ratio      : Low bead:DNA ratio (captures only large fragments >400 bp; desired
                    200-400 bp library bound to pellet after Stage 1 supernatant binds)
  Product         : Final sequencer-ready DNA library; target size distribution 200-400 bp
                    (Fig 4d); small broad hump at high MW indicates trace single-stranded products
  Notes           : At Stage 2 the desired 200-400 bp library IS bead-bound; large fragments
                    remain in solution and are disposed. Final library eluted into 3 uL (human)
                    or 5 uL (bacterial) elution buffer and dispensed to DMF hub.

Step 10 | Library QC Detection and Off-chip Sequencing
  Reagents        : dnaLibrary (3 uL)
  Operation       : detect libraryQC on dnaLibrary for 30 s
  Detection module: libraryQC (abstracts Bioanalyzer size distribution check + Kapa quant)
  Off-chip QC     :
    Size distribution : Bioanalyzer (Agilent); target peak 200-400 bp (Fig 4d)
    Quantitation      : Kapa Library Quantification Kit (KAPA Biosystems, Woburn MA)
    Loading conc.     : 8 pM on MiSeq; primary variability source is ~1000X dilution step
    Sequencing kit    : 300-cycle paired-end 150 bp MiSeq kit (Illumina)
    Read archive      : NCBI SRA accession SAMN02152539 (E. coli); APNN00000000.1 (K. pneumoniae)
  Branch          :
    Pass (BB2)    : librarySignal > 0 -> valid 200-400 bp library at sequencer-compatible
                    concentration; dispose for off-chip MiSeq loading
    Fail (BB3)    : librarySignal <= 0 -> failed library preparation; drain


SEQUENCING RESULTS (E. coli MG1655, 3 replicates)
--------------------------------------------------
Instrument      : Illumina MiSeq (in-house); 300-cycle paired-end 150 bp kit; 8 pM loading
Total bases     : 1.1 GB, 0.7 GB, 1.3 GB
Total reads     : 9.7M, 6.5M, 10.8M
Mean coverage   : 249X, 168X, 320X
Reads mapped    : 99.4%, 99.2%, 99.7% (reference: NC_000913.2; aligner: bowtie2)
GC content      : 50.1%, 49.7%, 50.1%
Coverage        : Even across entire ~4.6 kb E. coli genome; no significant spikes or drops (Fig 5)
De novo assembly: Velvet v1.2.03; k values tested: 25, 27, 29; contig cutoff 200 bp
                  Mean contig count: 249 +/- 27; Mean N50: 62.1 +/- 18.2 kbp

K. pneumoniae BAA-2146 (KpnNDM) de novo assembly:
  1384 contigs; N50 12.4 kbp; expected genome ~5.8 Mbp; GC ~57%
  Findings: multiple plasmids; small high-copy plasmid fully assembled;
            >=5 beta-lactamase genes including NDM-1 (carbapenem resistance);
            large number of transposable elements. Accession: APNN00000000.1


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file  : kim2013_ngs_library_prep_dmf.bs
Compiler        : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output       : 4 basic blocks (BB1-BB4); 1 if/else gate; 4 CFG edges
DAG             : kim2013_ngs_library_prep_dmf_main_dag.dot
                  Diamond CFG: main -> (bsbbif_2_t | bsbbif_3_f) -> bsbbif_4_j
Duration units  : All durations in s (seconds) or m (minutes); h token not supported.
                  5 min tagmentation    -> 5m  (IR: 300.0 SECOND)
                  3 min PCR extension   -> 3m  (IR: 180.0 SECOND)
                  10-cycle PCR block    -> 2200s (10 cycles x 220s per cycle; IR: 2200.0 SECOND)
Modules         : libraryQC, sequencerReadyDetection
Manifests       : GenomicDNA, NexteraEnzymeMix, PCRMixture, MagneticBeads_SPRI,
                  EthanolWash, ElutionBuffer, PluronicF127, FC40_Oil
Compiler notes  : drain in BioScript source (fail branch) is normalised to dispose in IR
                  by the lilott8 backend -- this is a known compiler behaviour, not a source bug.
                  All mix operations use scalar droplet variables (no array indexing) to maintain
                  compatibility with the lilott8/BioScript compiler constraint documented in the
                  moazami reference file.
Biological scope: This .bs file encodes the 185 um-gap hub protocol for human gDNA.
                  Bacterial gDNA (400 um gap, 2X volumes, 9 PCR cycles, 5 uL final elution)
                  requires parameter adjustment; same CFG structure applies.

protocol.title: A Microfluidic DNA Library Preparation Platform for Next-Generation Sequencing
protocol.platform: DMF hub with peripheral capillary-based modules (digital microfluidics + continuous-flow off-chip modules)
samples: Human genomic DNA (peripheral blood mononuclear cells)
protocol.objective: Fully integrated, automated microfluidic system for preparing Illumina sequencer-ready NGS libraries from nanogram-scale genomic DNA via tagmentation, bead-based clean-up, limited-cycle PCR, and two-stage size selection

device.hub_type: Digital microfluidic (DMF) hub with in-plane capillary-to-module interface
gap_configurations: 185 um gap (human gDNA; 1-2 uL droplet volumes)

substrate.bottom_plate: ITO-patterned glass; photolithography and etching; coated with 4 um Parylene-C + 50 nm Teflon-AF
substrate.top_plate: Unpatterned ITO glass; coated with 50 nm Teflon-AF

peripheral_modules.tagmentation: Thermal module; 750 um OD tubing recessed ~100 um in Al block trench (~850 um deep x 800 um wide); closed-loop PID TEC
peripheral_modules.limited_cycle_PCR: Thermal cycling module; OpenPCR benchtop cycler; same Al block configuration
peripheral_modules.cleanup: Magnetic bead module; 3 mm dia x 3 mm neodymium magnet (K&J Magnetics); positive pressure-driven syringe pump for near-complete supernatant removal
peripheral_modules.size_selection: Magnetic bead module; same magnet/pump configuration as clean-up; two-stage bead:DNA ratio protocol

device.manifold_frame: Custom-engineered polymer manifold with metal compression frame; pogo-pin electrical contacts; CapTite fittings (Sandia National Labs)

reagents.surfactant_additive: Pluronic F127, 0.1% w/v in TE buffer (added to all DNA and reagent solutions to prevent biofouling on Teflon-AF surfaces)

dna_sample.human_gDNA: Isolated from peripheral blood mononuclear cells (ATCC); 5 ng/uL in TE + 0.1% F127
dna_sample.ecoli_gDNA: E. coli MG1655 (ATCC); extracted with DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen); quantified by Qubit (Life Technologies)
dna_sample.kpn_gDNA: K. pneumoniae BAA-2146 (KpnNDM) (ATCC); same extraction and quantitation

nextera_enzyme_mix.composition: 2 uL High Molecular Weight component + 0.5 uL enzyme mix (Nextera DNA Sample Preparation Kit, Illumina)
nextera_enzyme_mix.pluronic_additive: 0.1% w/v Pluronic F127 to prevent biofouling (validated not to affect tagmentation efficiency; Fig S1)

pcr_mixture.composition: 12.5 uL 2X PCR buffer + 0.5 uL primer cocktail + 0.5 uL PCR enzyme + 0.5 uL 50X Adapter 2 (Nextera kit)

reagents.magnetic_beads: SPRI beads - Solid Phase Reversible Immobilisation (Beckman Coulter, Danvers MA)
reagents.wash_solvent: Ethanol (HPLC-grade organic solvent; nuclease-free water used throughout)
reagents.decontamination: 10% v/v bleach then deionized water rinse between library runs

steps.name: gDNA sample dispensing and Nextera enzyme mixing
steps.mixing_method: Continuous aspiration and dispensing in and out of capillary for 30 s at room temperature
steps.notes: All droplets prepared in TE + 0.1% Pluronic F127 (w/v). Air gap of 1-2 uL separates reagent bolus from pumping water in syringe. Fluid boluses moved at 10 uL/min.

steps.name: Tagmentation
steps.operation: heat incubation in peripheral thermal module
steps.module: Tagmentation thermal module (Al block, closed-loop PID TEC)
steps.product: Adapter-tagged DNA fragments; broad distribution 150-1000 bp (Fig 4b); adapter dimers ~45 bp also generated
steps.notes: Transposase simultaneously fragments and tags gDNA. Mixture aspirated from DMF hub into module tubing at 10 uL/min.

steps.name: Magnetic bead clean-up - bead capture and supernatant removal
steps.operation: merge on DMF hub + aspirate into clean-up module + magnet immobilisation + supernatant removal
steps.magnet: Neodymium, 3 mm dia x 3 mm thick (K&J Magnetics, Jamison PA)
steps.supernatant_content: Excess enzyme, adapter dimers, small DNA fragments
steps.notes: Bead pellet aggregated on inner tube wall. Positive pressure-driven flow (syringe pump) achieves near-complete supernatant removal (Fig 3, frames 1-3). Supernatant returned to DMF hub, actuated to waste capillary.

steps.name: Ethanol wash of bead pellet (x3)
steps.wash_method: Bolus shuttled back-and-forth across immobilised bead pellet (chaotic mixing effect; removes trace contaminants and salts)
steps.notes: After each shuttle wash: ethanol returned to DMF hub, actuated to waste module, aspirated off-chip. Each wash uses a fresh ethanol droplet dispensed from capillary.

steps.name: Elution of purified tagmented DNA from bead pellet
steps.operation: dispense elution buffer + aspirate into clean-up module + remove magnet + resuspend + re-apply magnet + return eluate to DMF hub
steps.product: 2.2 uL purified adapter-tagged DNA fragments (excess enzyme and adapter dimers removed)
steps.notes: Magnet removed; bolus shuttled to resuspend bead pellet (30 s). Magnet re-applied; DNA-containing eluate droplet returned to DMF hub and actuated to PCR inlet electrode.

steps.name: PCR mixture dispensing and merging with eluate
steps.notes: Combined ~5 uL droplet aspirated into PCR thermal module: 2.8 uL enters the module inlet; remaining 2.2 uL actuated to waste on DMF hub.

steps.name: Limited-cycle PCR - adapter addition and library enrichment
steps.thermocycler: OpenPCR (Saratoga, CA) benchtop cycler; Al block closed-loop PID TEC
steps.product: Enriched library ~200-10000 bp with Illumina-specific sequencing adapters and dual indices; primer dimers ~55 bp present (Fig 4c)
steps.notes: PCR reaction mixture (2.8 uL) cycled in module. After PCR, product dispensed back onto DMF hub for size selection. 9 cycles used for bacterial gDNA (400 um gap hub).

steps.name: Size selection Stage 1 - removal of fragments <200 bp
steps.operation: merge PCR product with SPRI beads + aspirate into size-selection module + magnet immobilisation + supernatant recovery
steps.bead_to_dna_ratio: high (binds all DNA including small fragments and primer dimers)
steps.supernatant_content: Desired 200-400 bp library fragments (remain in solution at this bead:DNA ratio)
steps.notes: Supernatant -- not bead-bound fraction -- carries the size-selected library at this stage. Bead pellet (small DNA <200 bp, primer dimers) disposed.

steps.name: Size selection Stage 2 - removal of fragments >400 bp
steps.operation: merge supernatant with low-volume SPRI beads + aspirate into size-selection module + magnet immobilisation + ethanol wash + elution
steps.bead_to_dna_ratio: low (binds only large fragments >400 bp; desired 200-400 bp library bound to pellet)
steps.product: Final sequencer-ready DNA library; target size 200-400 bp (Fig 4d)
steps.notes: At Stage 2 the desired 200-400 bp library is bead-bound; large fragments (>400 bp) remain in solution and are disposed. 3 uL elution buffer used for human gDNA; 5 uL for bacterial gDNA (400 um gap hub). Library dispensed back to DMF hub for QC and sequencing.

off_chip_qc.quantitation: Kapa Library Quantification Kit (KAPA Biosystems, Woburn MA)
off_chip_qc.read_archive: NCBI Sequence Read Archive accession SAMN02152539 (E. coli); APNN00000000.1 (K. pneumoniae)

kpn_BAA2146.description: First US K. pneumoniae isolate positive for NDM-1 (New Delhi metallo-beta-lactamase); previously unsequenced

notable_findings: Small high-copy number plasmid fully assembled
At least 5 beta-lactamase genes including NDM-1

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.description: Dispense gDNA + Nextera enzyme; tagmentation; bead clean-up + 3x ethanol wash + elution; PCR mix + limited-cycle PCR; two-stage size selection; library elution; QC detect

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_2_t
basic_blocks.action: dispose(dnaLibrary); library ready for MiSeq loading at 8 pM

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_4_j
basic_blocks.description: dispose(librarySignal); experiment ends; library available off-chip for sequencing

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Purification of High Salinity Brine by Multi-Stage Ion Concentration Polarization Desalination
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/srep31850
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/srep31850
Journal      : Scientific Reports, 2016, Vol. 6, Article 31850
Authors      : Bumjoo Kim, Rhokyun Kwak, Hyukjin J. Kwon, Van Sang Pham, Minseok Kim,
               Bader Al-Anzi, Geunbae Lim, Jongyoon Han
Platform     : PDMS-based microfluidic ICP (Ion Concentration Polarization) desalination device
               with cation exchange membranes (CEMs) only — unipolar conduction


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a multi-stage Ion Concentration Polarization (ICP) electrical desalination
method for treating high-salinity brine (>35,000 ppm TDS), including produced water from shale
oil/gas development and brine concentrate from seawater desalination plants. ICP desalination
utilises two cation exchange membranes (CEMs) of the same polarity for unipolar ion conduction,
unlike conventional electrodialysis (ED) which uses both AEM and CEM in bipolar configuration.

The protocol is divided into three characterisation branches:
  1. Multi-stage trifurcated ICP desalination — 3 sequential ICP stages with intermediate
     stream recirculation; salt removal QC by conductivity and ICP-AES measurement
  2. Suspended solids removal — simultaneous TDS and TSS reduction from brine containing
     E. coli bacteria and crude oil emulsions; visualised by fluorescence microscopy
  3. Divalent cation removal — quantitative Na+ and Ca2+ removal confirmed by ICP-AES;
     relevant for produced water recycling and scaling prevention in wellbores

Key advantages of ICP over conventional technologies:
  - Treats brine up to 100,000 ppm TDS with salt rejection up to 70%
  - Removes both dissolved salts and suspended solids simultaneously (no pretreatment)
  - Less susceptible to membrane fouling/scaling (no AEM; pH shift occurs near AEM not CEM)
  - Partial desalination (50-75%) sufficient for EOR recycling and discharge
  - Cost < $1/bbl for source water up to 70,000 mg/L TDS; competitive with MSF and MVR


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Fabrication   : PDMS (Polydimethylsiloxane)-based microfluidic model system
                (for visualisation and concentration distribution tracing)
Membrane gap  : 1.5-2.0 mm
Channel depth : 0.2-0.6 mm
Channel length: 10-100 mm

CEMs          : Fumasep FTCM-E (FuMA-Tech GmbH, Germany)
                Area resistance: ~13.3 Ohm.cm2
                Note: High-resistance membrane used; significant improvement expected with
                lower-resistance membranes (power consumption strongly dependent on resistance)
AEM           : Fumasep FTCM-A (used in electrodialysis comparison experiments only)
Electrodes    : Carbon paper (Fuel Cell Store, Inc., Boulder, CO)
Ref electrodes: Ag/AgCl (A-M Systems, WA); penetrate channels vertically; measure
                membrane voltage drop per cell only (excludes electrode/reaction overpotential)

Plastic scale-up device: Assembled from CEMs, AEMs (ED only), carbon electrodes, and
                          laser-cut plastic components; channel depth 3 mm.

Output streams (trifurcated):
  Concentrate  : Top stream — ion-enriched; receives negatively charged suspended particles
  Intermediate : Middle stream — concentration ~C0; majority fluid; re-fed to next ICP stage
  Diluate      : Bottom stream — ion-depleted; final treated water product


REAGENTS
--------
Feed solutions:
  NaCl brine             : 0.1-1.7 M NaCl (5,800-100,000 mg/L TDS)
  Natural seawater       : Revere Beach, MA; general precipitation only, no prefiltration
                           (used for fouling/scaling durability experiments)

Electrode rinse          : Na2SO4 at same normality as feed NaCl solution
                           Purpose: Exclude electrode/reaction overpotential from
                           cell voltage measurement

Fluorescent tracers:
  ICP zone visualisation : Alexa Fluor 488, 1.5 uM (Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA)
  Fluid tracing          : Fluorescent color coding red dye (Kingscote Chemicals, Inc., OH);
                           1:1000 volumetric ratio
  pH visualisation       : pH indicator dye (Micro Essential Laboratory, Inc., NY); 5 wt%

Bacterial model:
  Strain                 : E. coli K-12 MG1655
  Reporter               : Constitutively expressed GFP
  Purpose                : Visualise bacterial removal from diluate (Fig 7b)

Oil emulsion model:
  Oil                    : Crude oil (Greene, Co., PA)
  Buffer                 : 0.1 M NaCl
  Ratio                  : 1:50 (oil:buffer), sonicated 2 h
  Tracer                 : Fluorescent red dye 1:1000
  Purpose                : Visualise crude oil removal from diluate (Fig 7c)

Demineralised water      : CEM pre-conditioning soak (minimum 48 h before experiments)


EFFICIENCY METRICS
------------------
Current Utilization (CU):
  Formula : CU = zFQ_diluate(C0 - C_diluate) / NI
  Meaning : Fraction of applied current used for salt reduction in diluate flow
            (Ideally unity in ED with no current loss)
  ICP note: CU > 1 achievable with NaCl feed due to diffusivity difference
            DNa+ = 1.33e-9 m2/s; DCl- = 2.03e-9 m2/s; ICP with CEMs enhances
            salt removal ratio up to 20% compared to ED under same current

Energy per Ion Removal (EPIR):
  Formula : EPIR = (IV/Q_diluate) / (zk_BT(C0 - C_diluate)) proportional to V/CU
  Meaning : Specific energy consumed to remove one ion; proportional to voltage/CU
  Key finding: EPIR linearly proportional to salt removal ratio regardless of
               current density, flow velocity, or membrane length (Fig 3c)
               -> Optimal energy efficiency at minimum incremental salt removal ratio
               -> Drives multi-stage (batch) design philosophy


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | CEM Membrane Pre-Conditioning
  Reagents    : Demineralised water
  Operation   : Passive soak (abstracted as mix in BioScript)
  Duration    : Minimum 48 h at room temperature (25 C) = 2880m = 172800 s
  Purpose     : Equilibrate Fumasep FTCM-E CEMs before experiments
  BioScript   : mix cem_membrane with demineralizedWaterPrep for 2880m

Step 2 | Brine Feed Dispense
  Reagent     : NaCl brine, 0.1-1.7 M (5,800-100,000 ppm TDS)
  Flow rate   : ~20 uL/min via syringe pump (Harvard Apparatus PHD 2200), negative pressure
  Note        : Na2SO4 electrode rinse dispensed per-stage at point of use to avoid
                dead-code tokens in BioScript IR (rinse1, rinse2, rinse3)

Step 3 | Stage 1 — ICP Desalination (First Pass)
  Inputs      : Brine feed + conditioned CEM + Na2SO4 rinse (rinse1)
  ICP mix     : 10 s (flow-through separation abstraction)
  Actuation   : 25 C, 60 min = 3600 s (constant-current electrical actuation abstraction)
  Current     : 125-375 A/m2 constant; Keithley 236 source measurement unit
  Mechanism   : Ion depletion zone adjacent to CEMs; Na+ and Cl- separated into
                concentrate (top, enriched) and diluate (bottom, depleted)
  Trifurcated : Small diluate + majority intermediate (~C0) + small concentrate
  Salt removal: 5-20% per stage (optimal EPIR regime; Fig 3c)
  Rinse mix   : 10 s; stage1WithRinse fed to Stage 2
  Monitoring  : Conductivity probe (Microelectrode Inc.); Ag/AgCl reference electrodes

Step 4 | Stage 2 — ICP Desalination (Second Pass)
  Inputs      : stage1WithRinse (intermediate stream ~C0) + conditioned CEM + rinse2
  ICP mix     : 10 s
  Actuation   : 25 C, 60 min = 3600 s
  Current     : Adjusted per dilute production ratio p (506-1175 A/m2; Fig 5a table)
  Key feature : Feed concentration constant at ~C0 at every stage; system always in
                economically favourable high-salinity low-EPIR regime
                (unlike multi-stage ED where concentration drops stage-to-stage)
  Output      : stage2WithRinse fed to Stage 3

Step 5 | Stage 3 — ICP Desalination (Third Pass)
  Inputs      : stage2WithRinse (intermediate stream ~C0) + conditioned CEM + rinse3
  ICP mix     : 10 s
  Actuation   : 25 C, 60 min = 3600 s
  Output      : treatedDiluate (cumulative 50-75% TDS reduction)
  Overall     : System recovery fixed at 50% for cost comparison (SI-section 3.2.1)
  Justification: 3 stages is representative optimised configuration for high-salinity feed;
                 saltier feedwater requires more stages (SI-section 3.2.3)

Step 6 | Salt Removal QC Detection
  Input       : treatedDiluate
  Module      : saltRemovalDetection
  Duration    : 30 s
  Methods     : Flow-through conductivity probe (Microelectrode Inc., NH) for bulk TDS;
                CCD-based ICP-AES (ACTIVA-S, Horiba, Ltd., Japan) for cation quantification
  Pass (BB2)  : saltSignal > 0 -> TDS reduced 50-75%; dispose treatedDiluate
  Fail (BB3)  : saltSignal <= 0 -> TDS target not met; drain treatedDiluate
  Join (BB4)  : dispose saltSignal; proceed to TSS branch

Step 7 | Suspended Solids Removal Characterisation
  Inputs      : E. coli K-12 MG1655 (GFP-expressing) + crude oil emulsion (1:50, sonicated)
                + fresh NaCl brine + demineralised water
  Contaminant mix : 2 s each (sequential)
  ICP mix     : 10 s
  Actuation   : 25 C, 30 min = 1800 s
  Mechanism   : Negatively charged particles (negative zeta potential) migrate en bloc to
                concentrate stream (anode direction) by electrophoretic force + electroconvection
                Diluate exits particle- and salt-free simultaneously
  Module      : suspendedSolidsDetection
  Duration    : 30 s
  Detection   : Fluorescence microscopy (Olympus IX-71)
  Pass (BB5)  : solidsSignal > 0 -> TSS cleared from diluate; dispose tssSeparation
  Fail (BB6)  : solidsSignal <= 0 -> particles remain; drain tssSeparation
  Join (BB7)  : dispose solidsSignal; proceed to divalent cation branch
  Note        : Majority of bio-contaminants and colloidal particles in natural water carry
                negative zeta potentials; simultaneous TDS+TSS removal is key ICP advantage
                over conventional ED (requires separate pretreatment steps for TSS)

Step 8 | Divalent Cation Removal Characterisation
  Inputs      : Fresh NaCl brine + Na2SO4 rinse (rinseDivalent) + demineralised water
  Feed mix    : 5 s
  ICP mix     : 10 s
  Actuation   : 25 C, 30 min = 1800 s
  Target      : Na+ (monovalent) and Ca2+ (divalent) quantified in diluate
  Module      : divalentCationDetection
  Duration    : 30 s
  Method      : CCD-based ICP-AES (ACTIVA-S, Horiba, Ltd., Japan)
  Result      : Divalent cations removed proportionally or in excess of monovalent cations
                (SI-section 8); consistent with electrodialysis literature (refs 41-43)
  Significance: Prevents Ca2+/Mg2+/Ba2+/Sr2+ carbonate/sulfate precipitation in wellbore
                during produced water recycling for hydraulic fracturing reuse
  Pass (BB8)  : divalentSignal > 0 -> Na+/Ca2+ removal confirmed; dispose divalentSeparation
  Fail (BB9)  : divalentSignal <= 0 -> residual divalent ions above threshold; drain
  Terminal (BB10): dispose divalentSignal; NOP


MEMBRANE FOULING AND SCALING
-----------------------------
ICP advantage : Operates without AEMs; pH shift and scale formation (calcium deposits)
                occur near AEM due to water splitting (H+ and OH- production) not near CEM.
                ICP voltage largely constant over extended operation (natural seawater, 3 h,
                500 A/m2, no prefiltration) while ED voltage increases due to organic fouling.
ED comparison : CU reduction ratio higher in ED than ICP (Fig 8e); membrane fouling
                disrupts counter-ion transport and raises resistance.
pH observation: Significant acidification in dilute stream and basification in concentrate
                stream observed near AEM in ED (Fig 8a/b); not observed near CEM in ICP.
Test conditions: Natural seawater (Revere Beach, MA); no prefiltration or chemical
                 precipitation; constant current 500 A/m2; 3-channel stacked devices.


COST ANALYSIS
-------------
ICP target cost : < $1/bbl for source water up to 70,000 mg/L TDS at 70% salt removal;
                  linear dependence of overall cost on feed water salinity (Fig 6)
Capital cost    : Sum of membrane/equipment expenses and maintenance cost
                  (dominated by membrane area; ref 17, 25)
Operating cost  : Power consumption (other minor costs neglected; refs 17, 27, 28)
Optimal staging : More stages -> lower energy cost but higher capital cost;
                  optimum total cost at limit of many stages (incremental desalination)
                  Saltier feedwater -> more stages required (SI-section 3.2.3)

Competitor comparison (Fig 6):
  RO  : Practical limit ~45,000 ppm TDS; not viable for brine; pretreatment > $1/bbl
  MSF : Significant infrastructure; not competitive for partial desalination
  MVR : $3.50-6.25/bbl ($22-39/m3) total; $2-3/bbl operating only; complete desalination
  ICP : Cost (green zone, Fig 6) compares favourably over MSF and MVR for partial
        desalination target (50-75% salt removal)


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------

Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
DAG file       : kim_icp_multistage_brine_desalination_main_dag.dot

Duration conversions:
  48h  membrane conditioning  -> 2880m  (IR: 172800.0 SECOND)
  60m  ICP stage actuation    -> 60m    (IR: 3600.0 SECOND, x3 stages)
  30m  TSS actuation          -> 30m    (IR: 1800.0 SECOND)
  30m  divalent actuation     -> 30m    (IR: 1800.0 SECOND)
Modules        : saltRemovalDetection, suspendedSolidsDetection, divalentCationDetection

                 FDA_PI_ViabilityStain, EcoliBacterialCells, CrudeOilEmulsion, DemineralizedWater

protocol.title: Purification of High Salinity Brine by Multi-Stage Ion Concentration Polarization Desalination
protocol.platform: PDMS-based microfluidic ICP (Ion Concentration Polarization) desalination device
protocol.objective: Multi-stage ICP electrical desalination of high-salinity brine (up to 100,000 ppm TDS) with trifurcated output strategy; simultaneous TDS and TSS removal; divalent cation characterisation; cost-competitive with MSF and MVR

membranes.type: Cation Exchange Membrane (CEM) only — unipolar conduction
membranes.anion_exchange_membrane: Fumasep FTCM-A (used in electrodialysis comparison experiments only)

electrodes.supplier: Fuel Cell Store, Inc., Boulder, CO
electrodes.reference_electrodes: Ag/AgCl (A-M Systems, WA); penetrate channels vertically to measure membrane voltage drop per cell only

plastic_scale_up_device.description: Plastic-based ICP/ED device assembled from CEMs, AEMs (ED only), carbon electrodes, and laser-cut plastic components

output_streams.concentrate: Top stream — ion-enriched; receives negatively charged suspended particles
output_streams.intermediate: Middle stream — concentration ~C0; majority fluid; re-fed to next ICP stage
output_streams.diluate: Bottom stream — ion-depleted; final treated water product

NaCl_brine.notes: Represents seawater, produced water, and high-salinity brine concentrate range

electrode_rinse.purpose: Exclude electrode/reaction overpotential from cell voltage measurement

fluorescent_tracers.fluid_tracing: Fluorescent color coding red dye (Kingscote Chemicals, Inc., OH), 1:1000 volumetric ratio
fluorescent_tracers.pH_indicator: pH indicator dye (Micro Essential Laboratory, Inc., NY), 5 wt%

bacterial_model.purpose: Visualise bacterial removal from diluate stream (Fig 7b)

oil_emulsion_model.tracer: Fluorescent color coding red dye, 1:1000 volumetric ratio
oil_emulsion_model.purpose: Visualise crude oil emulsion removal from diluate stream (Fig 7c)

demineralised_water.use: CEM pre-conditioning soak (minimum 48 h before experiments)

current_utilization_CU.description: Fraction of applied current used for salt removal in diluate flow; ideally unity in ED with no current loss
current_utilization_CU.notes: ICP with CEMs achieves CU > 1 due to diffusivity difference between Na+ and Cl- (DNa+ = 1.33e-9 m2/s, DCl- = 2.03e-9 m2/s)

energy_per_ion_removal_EPIR.description: Specific energy consumed per ion removed; proportional to voltage/CU
energy_per_ion_removal_EPIR.key_finding: EPIR linearly proportional to salt removal ratio regardless of current density, flow velocity, or membrane length (Fig 3c); optimal EPIR at minimum incremental salt removal ratio

multi_stage_strategy.description: Feed stream split into three output flows (concentrate/intermediate/diluate) by concentration distribution between CEMs. Intermediate stream at ~C0 is re-fed to next identical stage.
multi_stage_strategy.advantage_over_electrodialysis: Feed concentration kept constant at every stage; system always operates in economically favourable high-salinity EPIR regime; less inter-channel concentration difference and voltage drop

dilute_production_ratio_p.definition: Fraction of feed volume exiting as diluate output per stage
dilute_production_ratio_p.tradeoff: Lower p -> lower EPIR (energy) but higher stage number and capital cost; optimal p minimises total water cost ($/m3)

multi_stage_strategy.justification: 3 stages is representative optimised configuration for high-salinity range (SI-section 3.2.3); saltier feedwater requires more stages

operating_conditions.flow_driver: Negative pressure syringe pump (Harvard Apparatus PHD 2200)
operating_conditions.voltage_measurement: Keithley 236 source measurement unit; Ag/AgCl reference electrodes; Keithley 2000 Digital Multimeter
operating_conditions.cation_analysis: CCD-based ICP-AES instrument (ACTIVA-S, Horiba, Ltd., Japan)
operating_conditions.numerical_modelling: Coupled Poisson-Nernst-Planck-Navier-Stokes equations; finite volume method; Newton method and GMRES solver

steps.name: CEM membrane pre-conditioning
steps.notes: All Fumasep FTCM-E CEMs soaked in demineralised water (or process solution) for minimum 48 h at room temperature before experiments. BioScript: mix cem_membrane with demineralizedWaterPrep for 2880m.

steps.name: Brine feed dispense
steps.notes: Na2SO4 electrode rinse dispensed per-stage at point of use (rinse1, rinse2, rinse3) to avoid dead-code tokens in IR.

steps.name: Stage 1 — ICP desalination (first pass)
steps.operation: mix (ICP separation abstraction) + heat (electrical actuation abstraction)
steps.notes: Ion depletion zone forms adjacent to CEMs. Na+ and Cl- separated into concentrate (top) and diluate (bottom). Trifurcated: small diluate + majority intermediate (~C0) + small concentrate. heat at 25c abstracts timed constant-current actuation (no thermal processing in paper).

steps.name: Stage 2 — ICP desalination (second pass)
steps.notes: Intermediate stream re-fed at ~C0; feed concentration constant at every stage. System stays in high-salinity low-EPIR regime. No extensive feed concentration change unlike multi-stage electrodialysis.

steps.name: Stage 3 — ICP desalination (third pass)
steps.notes: Third and final ICP stage. Overall recovery fixed at 50% for cost comparison (SI-section 3.2.1). Diluate conductivity confirmed by flow-through probe; cation removal by ICP-AES (ACTIVA-S, Horiba).

steps.name: Salt removal QC detection
steps.detection_method: Flow-through conductivity probe (Microelectrode Inc.) + CCD-based ICP-AES (ACTIVA-S, Horiba)

steps.name: Suspended solids removal characterisation
steps.operation: mix (contaminant loading) + mix (ICP separation) + heat (electrical actuation)

contaminant_preparation.bacteria: E. coli K-12 MG1655 (GFP-expressing); 1.5 uM Alexa Fluor 488 for ICP zone visualisation
contaminant_preparation.oil_emulsion: Crude oil 1:50 in 0.1 M NaCl, sonicated 2 h; fluorescent red dye 1:1000

steps.mechanism: Negatively charged particles (negative zeta potential) migrate to concentrate stream (anode direction) via electrophoretic force en bloc; diluate exits particle-free
steps.notes: Majority of bio-contaminants (bacteria) and colloidal particles (oil emulsions) in nature carry negative zeta potentials; simultaneous TDS+TSS removal is a key ICP differentiator from conventional ED.

steps.name: Divalent cation removal characterisation
steps.result: Divalent cations removed proportionally or in excess of monovalent cations (SI-section 8); consistent with electrodialysis refs 41-43
steps.significance: Divalent cation removal prevents carbonate/sulfate precipitate formation in wellbore during produced water recycling

cost_analysis.ICP_water_cost_target: < $1/bbl for source water up to 70,000 mg/L TDS at 70% salt removal
cost_analysis.cost_dependence: Generally linear with feed water salinity

RO.notes: Not economically viable for brine; rapid power increase and recovery ratio decrease; pretreatment > $1/bbl

MSF.notes: Significant infrastructure and equipment; not competitive for partial desalination

MVR.notes: Currently used for produced water; high capital expense; complete desalination only

cost_analysis.ICP_advantage: Partial desalination (50-75%) sufficient for most applications (EOR, recycling); ICP cost (green zone, Fig 6) compares favourably over MSF and MVR
cost_analysis.capital_cost_basis: Sum of membrane/equipment expenses and maintenance cost dominated by membrane area (amount used)
cost_analysis.operating_cost_basis: Power consumption only (other minor costs neglected)

membrane_fouling_scaling.ICP_advantage: Operates without AEMs; pH shift and scaling occur near AEM not CEM; ICP voltage stable over extended operation vs electrodialysis (Fig 8d)
membrane_fouling_scaling.ED_comparison: ED voltage increases over time due to organic foulants in seawater; ICP voltage largely constant
membrane_fouling_scaling.CU_comparison: ED CU reduction ratio higher than ICP (Fig 8e); more fouling on ED membrane surface disrupts counter-ion transport
membrane_fouling_scaling.pH_observation: Significant pH changes near AEM in ED (acidification in diluate, basification in concentrate); not observed near CEM in ICP (Fig 8a/b)
membrane_fouling_scaling.test_conditions: Constant current density 500 A/m2; natural seawater feed (Revere Beach, MA); no prefiltration; 3 h duration

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Discovery of New States of Immunomodulation for Vaccine Adjuvants via High
               Throughput Screening: Expanding Innate Responses to PRRs
Source Link  : https://pubs.acs.org/doi/pdf/10.1021/acscentsci.2c01351?ref=article_openPDF
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/acscentsci.2c01351
Journal      : ACS Central Science, 2023, Vol. 9, pp. 427-439
Platform     : High-throughput robotic liquid handling (384-well plate, pin-drop dispenser,
               plate reader, AlphaLISA); in vivo murine vaccination model (C57/B6 mice)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a high-throughput screening (HTS) pipeline to discover small-molecule
"immunomodulators" that alter the activity of two key innate immune signalling pathways:
the NF-kB pathway (nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B-cells) and the
IRF pathway (interferon regulatory factors). Immunomodulators act on the signalling network
downstream of pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) rather than binding to the PRR itself,
enabling fine-tuned customisation of innate immune responses.

The pipeline is divided into three sequential phases:
  1. Primary Screen: NF-kB and IRF transcription factor activity in RAW-Dual macrophages
     (murine reporter cell line) across 13 PRR agonists and ~3,147 modulators at 10 uM;
     384-well format; pin-drop robotic dispensing; 24 h readout.
  2. Secondary Screen: Six-plex AlphaLISA cytokine panel in THP-1 monocytes (human);
     720 downselected modulators x 7 PRR agonists; cytokines: IL-1beta, IL-12p40,
     IP-10 (CXCL10), CCL4, TNF-alpha, IFN-beta; quantitative vaccine score computed.
  3. In Vivo Validation: Lead modulators tested in murine prime-boost vaccination model
     (OVA subunit + commercial Fluzone 2021-2022 and Typhim-Vi vaccines); endpoints are
     antigen-specific serum IgG at Day 49 and systemic TNF-alpha at 1 h post-injection.

Key findings:
  - Modulators inhibit and enhance NF-kB and IRF independently by >100-fold.
  - Some modulators are "generalists" (active across nearly all 13 PRR agonists);
    others are "specialists" (active against 1 or a small subset of receptors).
  - Lead antibody-enhancing modulator PME-564 (Lyn kinase / tyrosine kinase inhibitor)
    produces a ~4-fold log AUC increase in anti-HA IgG when combined with Fluzone.
  - Lead cytokine-reducing modulators (PME-1226, PME-397) significantly decrease
    systemic TNF-alpha when combined with CpG (TLR9) agonist.
  - In vivo success rate: ~10-20% of lead candidates validated in murine model.


SCREENING LIBRARY
-----------------
Primary library    : 3,147 compounds total
  Composition      : 246 NF-kB/IRF inhibitors + 2,895 pathway-specific inhibitors
  Many compounds   : Previously studied or FDA-approved in other indications
Compound dose      : 10 uM final concentration (<0.05% DMSO v/v)
Addition method    : Pin-drop (robotic; ~23 nL of 10 mM DMSO stock per 230 uL well)
Downselection      : PCA on 16 variables (NF-kB + IRF activity across 8 high-Z-factor
                     agonists); compounds outside radius 1.75 retained -> 720 compounds
                     for secondary library (SI Appendix Figures S4, Table S3)


PRR AGONISTS
------------
Primary screen : 13 agonists (majority TLRs; SI Appendix Table S2)
  Pam3CSK4     (TLR2/1)      Pam2CSK4    (TLR2/6)
  Poly I:C     (TLR3)        LPS         (TLR4)
  MPLA         (TLR4)        Flagellin   (TLR5)
  Imiquimod    (TLR7)        TL8-506     (TLR8)
  ODN 1826     (TLR9)        3'3'-cGAMP  (STING)
  Tri-DAP      (NOD1)        MDP         (NOD2)
  mIFN-B       (IFNAR1/2)

Agonist concentration : EC50 per agonist (SI Appendix Table S2); occasionally adjusted
                        if modulatory range exceeded dynamic limit

Secondary screen : 7 agonist subset (Pam3CSK4, Pam2CSK4, Poly I:C, LPS, Flagellin,
                   R848 TLR7/8, 3'3'-cGAMP STING)

In vivo subunit model : R848 (TLR7/8), Flagellin (TLR5), CpG 1826 (TLR9)


CELL LINES
----------
- RAW-Dual macrophages (murine): dual NF-kB SEAP / IRF luciferase reporter system;
  both pathways measured in parallel from the same well.
  Primary screen only; cultured in DMEM + 10% FBS, 37 C, 5% CO2.

- THP-1 monocytes (human): secondary screen; selected because human AlphaLISA reagents
  provide higher cytokine multiplexing capacity than murine reagents.
  Cultured in RPMI-1640 + 10% FBS, 37 C, 5% CO2.

- BMDC (murine bone-marrow-derived dendritic cells): off-chip validation of lead compounds
  for cytokine production and cell surface marker expression before in vivo dosing
  (SI Appendix Figure S10).


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Primary Screen -- Cell Seeding
  Cell line    : RAW-Dual macrophages
  Plate format : 384-well
  Operation    : Robotic seeding at optimised cell density
  Incubation   : 24 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 for cell adherence before compound addition
  Purpose      : Establish monolayer with consistent NF-kB/IRF dynamic range
  Reference    : SI Appendix Figure S1

Step 2 | Primary Screen -- Immunomodulator Pin-Drop Addition
  Library size : ~3,147 compounds
  Method       : Pin-drop dispense; ~23 nL of 10 mM DMSO stock -> 10 uM final
  DMSO         : <0.05% v/v final
  Pre-incubation: 1 h at 37 C before agonist addition (equilibration/uptake)
  Notes        : Modulator added before agonist; not co-added

Step 3 | Primary Screen -- PRR Agonist Addition
  Agonists     : 13 PRR agonists at EC50; one agonist per well per modulator
  Method       : Robotic dispense from pre-prepared agonist stocks
  Notes        : Wide range covers TLR, NLR, STING, and IFNAR families; allows detection
                 of generalist vs specialist modulator activity

Step 4 | Primary Screen -- 24 h Co-incubation
  Temperature  : 37 C, 5% CO2
  Duration     : 24 h (= 1440 min; IR: 86400.0 SECOND)
  Outcome      : Transcription factor activity develops; supernatant drawn after incubation

Step 5 | Primary Screen -- Cell Viability QC
  Method       : Live-cell imaging + digital confluency mask (SI Appendix Figure S3)
  Purpose      : Identify and exclude toxic modulator/agonist combinations
  Outcome      : Compounds that reduce confluency below threshold are flagged and removed
                 before TF readout; <1% of library showed inherent pathway activation

Step 6 | Primary Screen -- Dual NF-kB / IRF Transcription Factor Readout
  NF-kB method : SEAP reporter; QUANTI-Blue reagent; absorbance 620 nm
  IRF method   : Luciferase reporter; QUANTI-Luc reagent; luminescence
  Both measured simultaneously from same supernatant well
  Report       : Fold change vs agonist-alone control
  Dynamic range: Inhibition and enhancement observed up to >100-fold in both directions
  Observation  : NF-kB and IRF modulation are largely independent (R2 = 0.0409 for LPS)
  PCA gate     : PC1+PC2 account for 49% of variance; retain outside radius 1.75;
                 3,147 -> 720 compounds advanced to secondary library

Step 7 | Secondary Screen -- THP-1 Cell Seeding
  Cell line    : THP-1 monocytes (human)
  Rationale    : Human AlphaLISA reagents; higher multiplexing than murine RAW-Dual
  Plate format : 384-well; identical robotic workflow to primary screen
  Incubation   : 24 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 for equilibration

Step 8 | Secondary Screen -- Re-apply Lead Modulator
  Compounds    : 720 downselected modulators
  Method       : Same pin-drop protocol; 10 uM final; <0.05% DMSO
  Pre-incubation: 1 h at 37 C before agonist addition
  Scale        : 720 modulators x 7 agonists = 5,040 wells per cytokine

Step 9 | Secondary Screen -- PRR Agonist Addition and 24 h Incubation
  Agonists     : 7-agonist subset of primary screen
  Incubation   : 24 h at 37 C, 5% CO2
  Supernatant  : Collected for AlphaLISA multiplexed measurement

Step 10 | Secondary Screen -- AlphaLISA Six-Plex Cytokine Detection
  Platform     : AlphaLISA (PerkinElmer); no-wash, multiplexed bead assay
  Excitation   : 680 nm; emission 615 nm (channel-switched per bead pair)
  Cytokines    : IL-1beta, IL-12p40, IP-10 (CXCL10), CCL4, TNF-alpha, IFN-beta
  Rationale per cytokine:
    TNF-alpha  : Baseline generalised inflammation; endogenous pyrogen
    IL-1beta   : Partially outside direct NF-kB regulation; enables pathway differentiation
    IFN-beta   : Strong IRF pathway correlate; antiviral type I interferon
    IL-12p40   : Activates NK cells; Th1/Th17 polarisation; adaptive immunity bridge
    IP-10      : Early adjuvant signal; T cell and DC chemoattractant; tolerability correlate
    CCL4       : Monocyte and NK cell chemoattractant; tolerability correlate
  Replicates   : Triplicate duplexed measurements per well
  Standard curves: Per cytokine per agonist (SI Appendix Table S5)
  Normalisation : Fold change vs agonist-alone; transformed to [-1,1] for vaccine score
  Crosstalk    : Corrected per SI Appendix Figure S5D

Step 11 | Secondary Screen -- Vaccine Score Computation and Downselection
  Method       : Weighted normalised cytokine score per modulator/agonist combination;
                 summed across agonists to produce generalist vaccine score
  Weights      : Positive for IFN-beta, IP-10, CCL4, IL-12; negative for TNF-alpha, IL-1beta
  Score range  : -20 (most negative; PME-2988) to +10 (most positive)
  Top generalist threshold: score >= 6 (approximately 20 compounds from 720 pool)
  Reference    : SI Appendix Figure S9

Step 12 | BMDC Validation (off-chip; lead compounds only)
  Cells        : Murine bone-marrow-derived dendritic cells (BMDC)
  Purpose      : Confirm cytokine production and cell surface markers in primary DCs
  Agonists     : Multiple (from primary screen subset)
  Reference    : SI Appendix Figure S10

Step 13 | In Vivo -- Prime Injection (Day 0)
  Model        : C57/B6 mice; i.m. injection
  Modulator dose: 1.5 umol in DMSO:Addavax 1:1 v/v
  Arms         :
    Arm A (Fluzone): Fluzone 2021-2022 (inactivated quadrivalent flu) + modulator
                     Endpoint: anti-HA IgG at Day 49 (log AUC)
    Arm B (Typhim): Typhim-Vi (carbohydrate typhoid vaccine) + modulator
                     Endpoint: systemic TNF-alpha at 1 h post-injection (pg/mL)
    Arm C (OVA):   OVA + R848/Flagellin/CpG1826 + modulator
                     Endpoint: anti-OVA IgG at Day 35 and Day 49 (n=4)
  Early cytokine: Serum collected at 1 h post-injection for TNF-alpha readout

Step 14 | In Vivo -- Boost Injection (Day 21)
  Schedule     : Day 21 post-prime
  Formulation  : Identical to prime; same modulator dose and vehicle
  Interval     : 21 days from prime (= 30240 min; IR: 1814400.0 SECOND)

Step 15 | In Vivo -- Antibody Titer Readout (Day 35 and Day 49)
  Method       : ELISA; antigen-specific serum IgG; log AUC reported
  Fluzone targets: A/Victoria/2570/2019 (HA); B/Phuket/3073/2013 (HA)
  OVA target   : Anti-OVA IgG D49 antibody level
  Timepoints   : Day 35 (14 days post-boost) and Day 49 (28 days post-boost; primary endpoint)
  Interval     : Day 21 to Day 49 = 28 days (= 40320 min; IR: 2419200.0 SECOND)
  Key result   : PME-564 + Fluzone -> ~4-fold log AUC increase vs Fluzone alone (****P<0.0001)
                 PME-564 + OVA subunit -> 2-6x IgG increase across all adjuvants tested
                 PME-1226 + PME-397 + CpG -> significant TNF-alpha reduction (Typhim model)
  n per group  : 4-5 mice


LEAD MODULATORS
---------------
PME-564   : Tyrosine kinase inhibitor (Lyn/Src-family kinase); top generalist vaccine score
            (~8-10). Enhances IP-10, IFN-beta, IL-12 across most agonists; suppresses TNF-alpha
            notably for Pam3CSK4 and R848. In vivo: ~4-fold log AUC IgG increase with Fluzone.
            Clinical precedent: used in myelogenous leukaemia treatment.
            Proposed mechanism: Lyn inhibition alters CpG trafficking from extracellular to
            internal endosomes, changing proinflammatory cytokine and Type I IFN production.

PME-2834  : Pan-WNK kinase inhibitor; originally discovered in hypertension research.
            WNK kinases implicated in NF-kB signalling. Improves antibody titers with Fluzone.

PME-397   : Cytokine reducer; significantly decreases TNF-alpha for CpG and R848 in vivo.

PME-1226  : Cytokine reducer; significantly decreases TNF-alpha for CpG in vivo.

PME-2988  : Negative vaccine score control (~-20). Eliminates IL-12, IFN-beta, IP-10;
            enhances IL-1beta and TNF-alpha ~100-fold. Not suitable as vaccine adjuvant;
            illustrates wide-ranging modulatory landscape.

PME-2539  : Candidate for cancer immunotherapy applications; enhances TNF-alpha ~36-fold
            with cGAMP and upregulates IFN-beta across all agonists tested.


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : kim_immunomodulator_hts.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
DAG            : kim_immunomodulator_hts_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations converted to minutes (m) for compiler compatibility
                 (BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported)
                 24 h  -> 1440m   (cell incubation steps; IR: 86400.0 SECOND)
                 60 min -> 60m    (modulator pre-incubation; IR: 3600.0 SECOND)
                 21 days -> 30240m (prime-to-boost interval; IR: 1814400.0 SECOND)
                 28 days -> 40320m (boost-to-titer interval; IR: 2419200.0 SECOND)
Modules        : nfkbIrfDetection, cytokineDetection, viabilityDetection, vaccinationQC
Variables      : 50 named droplets across 3 phases
Biological scope note: The .bs file encodes all three phases (primary screen, secondary
                 screen, in vivo validation) in a single pipeline. The `mix` primitive
                 abstracts robotic liquid-handling steps (not DMF electrode actuation).
                 The `heat` primitive models both plate incubator steps (37 C cell culture)
                 and in vivo body-temperature distribution windows (37 C murine).
                 drain -> dispose in IR: expected compiler behaviour; drain has no distinct
                 IR opcode in lilott8/BioScript; does not affect CFG correctness.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Massively Parallel Concentration Device for Multiplexed Immunoassays
Source Link  : https://pubs.rsc.org/lc/article/11/7/1351/336806/Massively-parallel-concentration-device-for
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1039/c0lc00349b
Journal      : Lab on a Chip, 2011, Vol. 11, pp. 1351-1358
Platform     : PDMS-glass nanofluidic concentration device with Nafion nanoporous junction


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a massively parallel nanofluidic concentration device for multiplexed
and high-throughput biomolecule detection. By integrating a Nafion nanoporous junction between
a main sample microchannel and a buffer microchannel, ion concentration polarization (ICP) is
generated under an applied dc voltage. This creates an ion depletion zone on the anodic side of
the nanojunction and strongly repels charged biomolecules (CRP, fluorescein) into a concentrated
plug within each microchannel. The key innovation is that a single-inlet/single-outlet reservoir
design allows the device to be massively parallelized: up to 128 individually controlled
concentration channels are operated simultaneously from a single applied voltage bias, without
scaling the number of fluidic connections.

The protocol is divided into two functional sub-protocols:

  1. Multiplexed preconcentration characterisation: up to 128 microchannels operated
     at the same ET (uniform concentration factor, ~4000x in 30 min at 50-100 V) or at
     graded ET values via varying inlet microchannel length (serial concentration, 100-4000x
     in a single 16-channel device). Fluorescein is used as the fluorescent tracer.

  2. Bead-based multiplexed immunoassay: streptavidin microsbeads functionalized with
     biotin-anti-CRP antibody are trapped in DRIE pillar arrays within each microchannel.
     Alexa-488-labeled CRP is loaded into the device and electrokinetically concentrated
     at the bead trap for 30 min (70 V). After buffer wash, fluorescence signal on the
     beads is measured. Serial concentration (ch#1 to ch#16, graded factors) generates
     16 distinct binding curves from a single inlet CRP concentration, extending the
     dynamic range from 44.66 to 2874.60 (ULD/LOD) and improving the LOD from
     162.2 ng/mL (reference) to 2.52 ng/mL (ch#16).


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Fabrication:
  - Positive master mold: SU-8 photoresist patterned on silicon wafer; PDMS cast and cured
    at 65 C for 3 h; peeled from master.
  - Nanojunction: 20 wt% Nafion perflourinated ion-exchange resin (Sigma Aldrich) patterned
    by microflow patterning onto glass using a reversibly bonded PDMS channel
    (200 um wide x 50 um deep x 1 cm long); cured at 95 C for 5 min; PDMS removed.
  - Bonding: PDMS chip with concentration microchannels plasma-bonded onto the Nafion-
    patterned glass substrate.
  - Bead trap: DRIE (deep reactive-ion etching) fabricated pillar array for the bead-based
    immunoassay device (SU-8 resolution insufficient for pillar features).

Channel dimensions : 50 um wide x 15 um deep (sample microchannels)
Bead trap          : 100 um wide x 15 um deep; PDMS micro-pillar array
Nanojunction       : Nafion strip patterned perpendicular to microchannels
Electrodes         : Ag/AgCl (A-M Systems, Inc.)
Power supply       : Keithley 6487 dc power supply
Imaging            : Inverted fluorescence microscope (Olympus IX-51) + SensiCam CCD
                     (Cooke corp.); IPLab 3.6 image analysis (Scanalytics, Fairfax VA)

Multiplexing geometry:
  - Same-length channels (Fig. 2a): all microchannels have identical inlet length;
    same ET across all channels; uniform concentration factor.
  - Variable-length channels (Fig. 2b): inlet channels extended in zigzag pattern with
    different lengths; lower ET for longer channels; serial concentration factors 100-4000x
    across ch#1 (longest) to ch#16 (shortest).
  - Splitting/merging scheme at inlet/outlet matches hydraulic flow resistance.
  - Up to 128 channels demonstrated; single V_H and GND connection only.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Bead Functionalization (off-chip)
  Reagents      : Streptavidin beads (Applied Biosystems, 6-8 um, 35e6 beads/mL),
                  biotin-conjugated anti-CRP (Abcam ab86246)
  Operation     : Mix beads with antibody; stir 18 h at room temperature
  Duration      : 18 h (= 1080 min; encoded as 1080m; h token unsupported in compiler)
  Post-process  : Centrifuge to remove excess antibody; wash 3x with 1x PBS;
                  dilute tenfold before loading
  Notes         : Biotin-streptavidin conjugation links anti-CRP to bead surface.
                  Bead diameter 6-8 um provides optimal trap fit (1-2 beads vertically)
                  and avoids blocking sample flow or requiring sub-micron pillar geometry.

Step 2 | Device Blocking with BSA
  Reagents      : 1% BSA in buffer
  Operation     : Flush through microchannel for 10 min at room temperature
  Duration      : 10 min (600 s)
  Purpose       : Passivates PDMS channel walls; prevents nonspecific CRP adsorption
                  that would produce false-positive fluorescence signal on beads.

Step 3 | Pre-loading Buffer Wash (3x)
  Reagents      : 10 mM sodium phosphate dibasic buffer (pH 8.4)
  Operation     : Positive pressure applied 5 min per wash; 3 cycles
  Purpose       : Remove BSA from channel before bead loading; establish buffer baseline.

Step 4 | Bead Loading into Pillar-Array Traps
  Reagents      : Functionalized bead suspension (diluted tenfold), 10 mM buffer
  Loading       : Positive pressure at anodic reservoir; beads flow into pillar trap zone
  Trap geometry : DRIE pillar array, 100 um x 15 um; traps 6-8 um beads between pillars;
                  1-2 beads per trap stack vertically
  Post-loading wash : Positive pressure at cathodic reservoir; 3x wash to remove clogged
                      (non-trapped) beads from pillar zone; equal bead number per channel
                      confirmed by bright-field microscopy before CRP loading
  Final wash    : 3x additional buffer wash after clog removal
  Preparation time : ~30 min total before CRP concentration step
  BioScript note: `mix` abstracts pressure-driven flow-through bead trapping;
                  no DMF electrode mixing occurs at this step.

Step 5 | Channel Fill with Alexa-488-Labeled CRP
  Reagents      : Alexa-488-labeled CRP (Invitrogen A10235 labeling kit) in 10 mM
                  sodium phosphate dibasic buffer, pH 8.4
  Concentrations tested (5 independent runs):
    run1 : 1 ug/mL
    run2 : 100 ng/mL
    run3 : 10 ng/mL    [representative concentration encoded in BioScript]
    run4 : 1 ng/mL
    run5 : 100 pg/mL
  Operation     : Fill microchannels via positive pressure at anodic reservoir
  Notes         : Two independent channel-arm droplets dispensed in BioScript:
                  ch16 (high-ET arm) and ch1 (low-ET arm), each CRP + buffer.

Step 6 | Electrokinetic Concentration - Channel 16 (ch16, ~4000x factor)
  Voltage       : 70 V dc (also tested at 50 V and 100 V; 70 V for immunoassay runs)
  Duration      : 30 min (1800 s)
  Mechanism     : Applied voltage across Ag/AgCl electrodes drives perm-selective ion
                  current through Nafion nanojunction; ion concentration polarization
                  depletes ions from anodic side, strongly repelling CRP toward anodic wall
                  and forming a concentrated CRP plug at the bead trap.
  Channel       : Ch16 has the shortest inlet microchannel; ET = deltaV / length is
                  maximised; ~4000x concentration factor achieved in 30 min.
  BioScript note: Encoded as `heat ... at 25c for 1800s`; standard abstraction for
                  voltage-driven concentration with no thermal component; 25c = ambient.

Step 7 | Electrokinetic Concentration - Channel 1 (ch1, ~100x factor)
  Voltage       : 70 V dc
  Duration      : 30 min (1800 s)
  Channel       : Ch1 has the longest inlet microchannel; lowest ET; ~100x concentration
                  factor. Represents the low-sensitivity end of the serial concentration
                  gradient and the low end of the extended dynamic range.
  Notes         : In the real device both arms concentrate simultaneously under the same
                  single applied voltage; serial modelling in BioScript reflects CFG
                  linearity constraint (no parallel execution primitives).

Step 8 | Post-Concentration Buffer Wash (3x per channel arm)
  Reagents      : 10 mM sodium phosphate dibasic buffer
  Operation     : Flush buffer through channel after concentration step
  Wash cycles   : 3 per arm (ch16 and ch1 washed independently in BioScript)
  Purpose       : Remove unbound bulk CRP from channel before fluorescence readout;
                  only bead-bound CRP signal is measured.
  Paper quote   : "the sample containing Alexa-488 labeled CRP was removed by flushing
                  sodium phosphate dibasic buffer solution through the device."

Step 9 | Fluorescence Detection of Bead-Bound CRP
  Instrument    : Inverted fluorescence microscope (Olympus IX-51) + SensiCam CCD;
                  IPLab 3.6 image analysis
  Fluorophore   : Alexa-488 (excitation ~490 nm, emission ~525 nm)
  Detection module : crpBindingDetection (BioScript)
  Detection duration : 30 s per channel arm
  Readout       : Fluorescent intensity on trapped beads; signal proportional to
                  amount of CRP bound to anti-CRP antibody on bead surface
  Background    : 40-50 AU (system baseline)
  Signal range  : 56-66 AU (run5, 100 pg/mL) to ~800 AU (run1, 1 ug/mL) at ch16
  QC gate (ch16): bindingSignal > 0 -> dispose; bindingSignal <= 0 -> drain
  QC gate (ch1) : ch1Signal > 0 -> dispose; ch1Signal <= 0 -> drain
  Notes         : Ch16 (shortest channel, ~4000x) gives highest signal and lowest LOD.
                  Ch1 (longest channel, ~100x) gives weakest signal; confirms low end
                  of dynamic range. Five repeats per run for statistical reliability.
                  Data from run2 and run4 omitted from binding curve plot as signal
                  ranges overlapped with neighbour sets.


RESULTS SUMMARY
---------------

Concentration Characterisation (fluorescein tracer, 0.01 ug/mL):
  16-channel uniform (50 V, same-length):
    Concentration factor : ~4000x in 30 min
    Median signal        : 1875.3 AU; SD 66.5 AU; uniformity error <5%
  128-channel uniform (100 V):
    Mean signal          : 1581.3 AU; SD 170.5 AU
  16-channel serial (50 V, variable-length):
    Factor range         : ~100x (ch#1) to ~4000x (ch#16)

Immunoassay Performance (4-parameter logistic fit, R2 > 0.95 for all curves):
  Without concentration (reference):
    LOD    : 162.2 ng/mL
    ULD    : 7244 ng/mL
    Dynamic range (ULD/LOD) : 44.66

  With concentration (ch#16, ~4000x factor):
    LOD    : 2.52 ng/mL
    ULD    : 7244 ng/mL
    Dynamic range (ULD/LOD) : 2874.60
    LOD improvement : ~64x vs reference

  Fitting equation : y = y0 + a / (1 + (x/x0)^b)
    Parameters a, b, x0 within 99% confidence; y0 > 98% confidence (Sigma Plot LSQ fit)


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : ko_multiplexed_nanofluidic_concentration_immunoassay.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG            : ko_multiplexed_nanofluidic_concentration_immunoassay_main_dag.dot

Duration conversions (h token unsupported; all durations in s or m):
  18 h functionalization  -> 1080m  (IR: 64800.0 SECOND)
  10 min BSA blocking     -> 600s   (IR: 600.0 SECOND)
  30 min concentration    -> 1800s  (IR: 1800.0 SECOND)

Known compiler behaviours present in IR:
  - `drain` lowered to dispose() in IR output (known compiler bug; .bs source correct)
  - True-branch blocks (bsbbif_2_t, bsbbif_5_t) emit no unconditional jump (known
    limitation; DOT edges resolve correctly)
  - `heat` is void/in-place; does not consume the fluid variable; fillCh161 and
    fillCh11 correctly appear in subsequent mix calls after their heat statements

Modules        : crpBindingDetection
Manifests      : StreptavidinBeads, BiotinAntiCRP, AlexaCRP, BSA_Block, Buffer, PBS

Serial concentration modelling note:
  The paper operates all 16 channels simultaneously under a single applied voltage.
  BioScript has no parallel execution or loop construct. Two representative channels
  are encoded explicitly: ch16 (shortest inlet, ~4000x, lowest LOD) and ch1 (longest
  inlet, ~100x, highest LOD). These bracket the dynamic range endpoints reported in
  Fig. 5b and Table 1. The QC gate is keyed on ch16 (bindingSignal), consistent with
  the paper's primary performance metric (LOD = 2.52 ng/mL at ch16).

Pellet re-suspension modelling note:
  After each centrifuge wash step the bead pellet is re-suspended in fresh buffer.
  The compiler has no native magnetic-separation or pellet primitive. Each re-suspension
  is modelled as a fresh dispense of StreptavidinBeads, consistent with the established
  convention used across this dataset.
