description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Continuous-Flow Biomolecule and Cell Concentrator by Ion Concentration Polarization
Source Link  : https://pubs.acs.org/ancham/article-pdf/83/19/7348/15036094/ac2012619.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/ac2012619
Journal      : Analytical Chemistry, 2011, Vol. 83, pp. 7348-7355
Platform     : Nanofluidic PDMS microfluidic chip with Nafion nanojunction (cation-selective membrane)
               coupled to syringe pump and high-voltage DC supply


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a continuous-flow nanofluidic concentrator for charged biomolecules
and cells, operating on the principle of ion concentration polarization (ICP) at a Nafion
cation-selective nanojunction. Unlike batch-type preconcentrators that trap analytes in a
stationary plug, this system achieves a steady-state concentrated stream that can be
delivered continuously to downstream sensors or reservoirs.

The device consists of a PDMS microchannel bonded to a Nafion-patterned glass substrate.
The main channel bifurcates into a narrow concentrated channel and a wider filtered channel.
A Nafion line is patterned at 30 degrees along the concentrated channel. When a voltage is
applied across the Nafion (V+) combined with Poiseuille flow (delta-P from a syringe pump),
an ICP depletion zone forms near the nanojunction. Charged biomolecules and cells are
blocked electrostatically by this depletion zone and guided hydrodynamically into the
concentrated channel, while the filtered channel carries essentially target-free buffer.

Concentration factors from 1 to ~200 are achievable by tuning the channel geometry:
  w' = (w1+w2)/w1  (width ratio; tested: 10, 20, 50, 100)
  l' = L1/L2       (length ratio; tested: 0.3, 0.7, 2)
  r  = 1 + R1/R2   (theoretical concentration factor from hydrodynamic resistance ratio)

The protocol is divided into three experimental arms, encoded sequentially in the BioScript:
  1. Fluorescein sodium salt / rGFP continuous-flow concentration demonstration
  2. FITC-lectin polarity assay (negatively charged at pH 8.7; positively charged at pH 7.4)
  3. Red blood cell (RBC) and E. coli co-concentration demonstration


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Substrate    : Clean glass slide; Nafion perfluorinated ion-exchange resin (20 wt%, Sigma-Aldrich)
               patterned using PDMS line mold (width 100 um, height 50 um).
PDMS layer   : Bonded to Nafion-patterned glass by plasma treatment.
               Fabricated by standard photolithography (SU-8 master) and soft lithography.

Channel dimensions (fluorescein/rGFP/cell experiments):
  Main channel width        : 200, 400, 1000, or 2000 um (varied across devices)
  Main channel height       : 15 um
  Inlet length              : 1 cm (inlet to bifurcated point)
  Concentrated channel width: 20 um (fixed; 10 um for FITC-lectin high-factor tests)
  Filtered channel width    : Determined by width ratio w' = (w1+w2)/w1

Channel dimensions (FITC-lectin experiments):
  Concentrated channel width: 10 um
  Concentrated channel height: 15 um
  Main channel width         : 200 or 500 um
  Channel lengths            : 5-10 mm (outlet reservoir location controls length)

Nafion junction angle        : 30 degrees to main channel axis
  Purpose: Generates a straight (not curved) ICP boundary along the junction,
           enabling predictable ICP boundary position and concentrated plug shape.

Voltage application:
  Inlet of main channel (0-150 V) to buffer channel (electrical ground) across Nafion junction.
  Concentrated channel and filtered channel outlets are electrically floated.
  Maximum voltage: 150 V (= 150 V/cm; ~1000x below PDMS breakdown voltage of ~25 V/um).
  Voltage/flow rate values adjusted to balance depletion force and hydrodynamic force.

Flow control:
  Syringe pump: Harvard Apparatus PHD 2200
  Flow rate range: 0-5 uL/min


TARGETS AND REAGENTS
--------------------

Fluorescein sodium salt
  Concentration  : 3 pM
  Buffer         : 1 mM dibasic sodium phosphate (pH 8.7)
  Supplier       : Sigma-Aldrich, St. Louis, MO
  Charge         : Negative at pH 8.7
  Calibration    : 0.03, 0.3, 3, 30 pM and 0.3, 3, 30 nM used as internal references

Recombinant GFP (rGFP)
  Concentration  : 3 pM
  Buffer         : 1 mM dibasic sodium phosphate (pH 8.7)
  Supplier       : BD Bioscience, Palo Alto, CA
  Charge         : Negative at pH 8.7
  Calibration    : 0.3, 3, 30 nM used as internal references

FITC-conjugated lectin from Lens culinaris (lentil)
  Concentration  : 5 ug/mL
  MW             : ~49 kDa
  pI             : ~8.0-8.8
  Supplier       : Sigma-Aldrich, St. Louis, MO
  Zeta potential measurement: Zetasizer nano ZS (Malvern)
  Calibration    : 0.5, 5, 50, 100, 500 ug/mL used as internal references

  Condition A (negatively charged):
    Buffer              : 1 mM dibasic sodium phosphate (pH 8.7)
    Zeta potential      : -18.8 mV
    Electrophoretic mob.: -1.464e-8 m2/V.s
    Charge state        : Negative (lectin is above pI)

  Condition B (positively charged):
    Buffer              : 1 mM dibasic sodium phosphate (pH 7.4)
    Zeta potential      : +3.35 mV
    Electrophoretic mob.: +0.263e-8 m2/V.s
    Charge state        : Positive (lectin is below pI)
    Additive            : 0.1% BSA (Sigma-Aldrich) to prevent nonspecific electrostatic
                          binding to negatively charged PDMS walls and Nafion

Red blood cells (RBCs)
  Source         : Human whole blood (Hoechst, 2000x dilution, Innovative Research)
  Diluent        : 1x PBS (~150 mM)
  Additive       : 0.2% Pluronic F108 (BASF, Cumberland, RI) to reduce osmosis hemolysis,
                   nonspecific binding, and cell aggregation
  Tracker dye    : Cell Tracker Orange CMRA (Molecular Probes, Eugene, OR) at 3 uM
                   (used for fluorescence tracking in Supporting Information video)
  Zeta potential : -13.3 mV (Zetasizer nano ZS, Malvern)
  Input density  : ~1.9e6 cells/mL (RBC-only experiment); ~7.3e5 cells/mL (co-experiment)

E. coli ER2738
  Supplier       : New England BioLabs Inc.
  Culture        : Single colony in LB-Tet medium (50 mL LB + 50 uL tetracycline 50 ug/mL)
                   at 37 C for 24 h; LB-Tet contains ~10 g/L NaCl (~171 mM)
  Buffer on chip : Mixture of RBCs in 1x PBS + E. coli in LB-Tet (1:10 v/v, ~168 mM)
  Zeta potential : -15.5 mV (Zetasizer nano ZS, Malvern)
  Input density  : ~3.2e7 cells/mL
  Note           : PDMS and E. coli share same polarity; nonspecific binding confirmed
                   negligible under experimental conditions

Phosphate buffer (ionic strength series)
  Concentrations tested: 1 mM, 10 mM, 100 mM (dibasic sodium phosphate)
  Purpose: Characterise ICP stability vs. ionic strength (Fig. 3)
  Note: Higher ionic strength expands ICP instability regime; higher electric field
        required to generate ICP boundary at high molar concentrations


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Sample Preparation (fluorescein arm)
  Reagents  : FluoresceinSodiumSalt, Phosphate_Buffer_1mM_pH87
  Operation : mix, 5 s
  Output    : sampleMix (3 pM fluorescein in 1 mM phosphate buffer pH 8.7)
  Note      : rGFP arm is identical; this file encodes fluorescein as primary demonstration.

Step 2 | Device Priming and Channel Equilibration
  Reagents  : Phosphate_Buffer_1mM_pH87, sampleMix
  Operation : mix (abstracts buffer flushing through microchannel), 2 min
  Flow rate : ~2 uL/min
  Purpose   : Equilibrate Nafion nanojunction; remove air bubbles; no chemical reaction.

Step 3 | ICP Continuous-Flow Concentration (fluorescein/rGFP)
  Operation : heat at 25 C for 30 min (models room-temperature voltage operation) +
              mix for 30 min (abstracts electrokinetic + hydrodynamic force balance)
  Voltage   : 80 V
  Flow rate : 5 uL/min
  Geometry  : w' = 50, l' = 0.7 (w1=20 um, w2=980 um, L1=6 mm, L2=9 mm)
  r_theor   : 62
  Results   : Fluorescence intensity 300 -> 800 AU (~50-fold enhancement for fluorescein)
              Filtered channel drops to ~260 AU (near noise; essentially zero target)
              Concentrated plug visible; ICP boundary stable >30 min of operation
  Note      : Experimental factor always lower than theoretical due to ICP-induced
              electroosmotic flow changes in concentrated stream (second electroosmotic
              component boosts concentrated flow velocity; accurate modeling not yet available).

Step 4 | Fluorescence Detection and Concentration Quantification
  Operation : detect (concentrationDetection), 30 s
  Instrument: Olympus IX-71 inverted epifluorescence microscope +
              Hamamatsu thermoelectrically cooled CCD camera
  Software  : Image Pro Plus 5.0 (Media Cybernetics)
  QC gate   : concSignal > 0 -> dispose (BB2, pass)
              concSignal <= 0 -> drain (BB3, fail; ICP unstable or no enhancement)

Step 5 | FITC-Lectin Sample Preparation (both polarities)
  Reagents  : FITC_Lectin_pH87 + Phosphate_Buffer_1mM_pH87 (negative arm)
              FITC_Lectin_pH74 + BSA_Solution + Phosphate_Buffer_1mM_pH74 (positive arm)
  Operation : mix, 5 s each
  Note      : BSA added only for positive (pH 7.4) arm to prevent nonspecific binding.

Step 6 | ICP Concentration of FITC-Lectin (both polarities)
  Operation : mix for 30 min (abstracts ICP concentration for each polarity arm)
  Flow rate : 1 uL/min
  Voltage   : 0-150 V (adjusted per geometry to maintain stable ICP boundary)
  Height    : 15 um (main channel), 10-20 um (concentrated channel)
  Geometries tested:
    12-fold : w'=10, l'=0.7, w1=20 um
    46-fold : w'=20, l'=0.7, w1=10 um  (encoded as representative condition)
    130-fold: w'=50, l'=0.7, w1=10 um
  Key finding:
    Positive FITC-lectin (pH 7.4) shows larger shortfall from theoretical factor than
    negative lectin (pH 8.5), especially at low concentrated flow velocity (130-fold case).
    Cause: Electrostatic nonspecific binding to negatively charged PDMS and Nafion.
    BSA partially mitigates but cannot fully suppress at slow flow rates.
    At faster flow (12-fold case): no significant difference between polarities.
  QC gate   : polaritySignal > 0 -> dispose both (BB5, pass)
              polaritySignal <= 0 -> drain both (BB6, fail)

Step 7 | RBC and E. coli Sample Preparation
  Reagents  : RedBloodCells, EColi_ER2738, PBS_150mM, PluronicF108, LB_Tet_Medium
  Operation : Sequential mix steps, 5 s each
  Outputs   : rbcMix (RBCs in 1x PBS + 0.2% Pluronic F108)
              ecoliMix (E. coli in 1x PBS + LB-Tet 1:10)
              cellMix (RBCs + E. coli co-mixed)
  Input densities: RBC ~7.3e5 cells/mL; E. coli ~3.2e7 cells/mL

Step 8 | ICP-Based Continuous-Flow Cell Concentration
  Operation : heat at 25 C for 2 min + mix for 30 min
              (abstracts ICP concentration of cell stream at Nafion junction)
  Voltage   : 14 V (co-experiment, Fig. 6); 90 V (RBC-only, Fig. 5)
  Flow rate : 0.1 uL/min (co-experiment); 5 uL/min (RBC-only)
  Geometry  : w'=10, l'=1.2 (20-fold concentrator)
  Results (co-experiment, Fig. 6):
    RBC  : 7.3e5 -> 1.4e7 cells/mL (19-fold; matches r_theoretical = 20)
    E. coli: 3.2e7 -> 6.5e8 cells/mL (20-fold; matches r_theoretical = 20)
    Leakage rate: 0% over 120 s live imaging
  Quantification:
    Hemocytometer (SKC Inc.): sample flow and filtered flow density
    ImageJ phase contrast: concentrated channel cell counting
    (Hemocytometer not usable for concentrated channel: ~0.05 uL/min output;
     200 min needed to collect 10 uL minimum volume)
  QC gate   : cellSignal > 0 -> dispose concentratedCells (BB8, pass)
              cellSignal <= 0 -> drain concentratedCells (BB9, fail)


IONIC STRENGTH CHARACTERISATION
--------------------------------
Buffers tested  : 1 mM, 10 mM, 100 mM dibasic sodium phosphate
Analyte         : 3 pM fluorescein sodium salt
Geometry range  : w' = 10, 20, 50, 100; l' = 0.3, 0.7, 2 (30 deg inclined Nafion)
Finding         : Concentration factors proportional to w' and l' as expected.
                  Experimental factors always below theoretical (eq. 3).
                  Higher ionic strength -> ICP instability regime expands (gray zone, Fig. 3).
                  Instability: ICP boundary fluctuations increase with electric field and
                  concentration gradient; disrupts continuous concentrated flow at high w'/l'.
                  1 mM buffer recommended for stable high-factor operation.


COMPARISON: BATCH-TYPE vs CONTINUOUS-FLOW
------------------------------------------
Batch-type preconcentrator:
  Max factor       : ~1e6-fold (Wang et al., 2005)
  Limitation       : Low throughput; unstable after concentration stops; diffusive dispersion
                     makes plug delivery to downstream sensors difficult.

This continuous-flow system:
  Max factor       : ~200-fold (experimental)
  Advantages       : Steady-state concentrated stream maintained continuously in downstream
                     channel or reservoir; no dispersion loss; seamless sensor integration;
                     target-independent (concentration factor set only by channel geometry);
                     sample flow rate ~few uL/min without downstream limitation.


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file  : kwak_icp_continuous_flow_concentrator.bs
Compiler        : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output       : 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else QC gates, 12 CFG edges
DAG             : kwak_icp_continuous_flow_concentrator_main_dag.dot
Duration units  : All durations in seconds (s) or minutes (m) per compiler spec.
                  30 min ICP operation -> 30m (IR: 1800.0 SECOND)
                  2 min priming        -> 2m  (IR: 120.0 SECOND)
Modules         : concentrationDetection, icpBoundaryDetection, cellCountDetection
Abstraction notes:
  `mix`  abstracts hydrodynamic + electrokinetic force balance at Nafion junction
         (continuous-flow ICP concentration event; no reagent mixing in DMF sense).
  `heat at 25c` models room-temperature operation during voltage application
         (no actual thermal step in paper; used to anchor the ICP operation time window).
  `detect` abstracts epifluorescence CCD readout (Olympus IX-71 + Hamamatsu CCD)
         and ImageJ / hemocytometer cell counting.
Protocol scope  : Three sequential experimental arms encoded in one .bs file:
                  (1) Fluorescein/rGFP ICP concentration (primary demonstration)
                  (2) FITC-lectin polarity assay (pH 8.7 negative + pH 7.4 positive)
                  (3) RBC + E. coli co-concentration
                  rGFP arm follows identical protocol to fluorescein; not separately encoded.
                  RBC-only experiment (Fig. 5) shares same geometry as co-experiment (Fig. 6);
                  co-experiment (Fig. 6) encoded as the representative cell concentration arm.

protocol.platform: Nanofluidic PDMS microfluidic chip with Nafion nanojunction (cation-selective membrane)
targets: FITC-lectin from Lens culinaris (positively and negatively charged protein)
protocol.objective: Continuous-flow preconcentration of charged biomolecules and cells using ICP (ion concentration polarization) at a Nafion nanojunction; concentration factors from 1 to ~200 achieved by adjusting channel geometry (width ratio w' and length ratio l')

device.material: PDMS (poly(dimethylsiloxane)) bonded to Nafion-patterned glass substrate by plasma treatment
device.fabrication: Standard soft lithography; PDMS molds for Nafion nanojunction and microchannels by photolithography

nafion.type: Nafion perfluorinated ion-exchange resin, 20 wt% solution (Sigma-Aldrich)
nafion.selectivity: Cation-selective; sulfonate groups provide nanometer-scale ion pathways
nafion.patterning: PDMS line mold (width 100 um, height 50 um) on clean glass substrate
nafion.orientation: Parallel to and along the concentrated channel

main_channel.note: Width varied across devices; bifurcates into concentrated and filtered channels

concentrated_channel.note: Fixed at 20 um for most experiments; 10 um for FITC-lectin high-factor tests

filtered_channel.note: w' = (w1+w2)/w1; l' = L1/L2; both control concentration factor r

channels.buffer_channel: Ground electrode channel; electrical ground for ICP voltage application

concentration_factor.note: Concentration factor is target-independent; same geometry gives same factor for any charged species

voltage_V.note: 150 V/cm ~ 1000x below PDMS breakdown voltage (~25 V/um). Higher voltage causes ICP boundary instability.

flow_rate_uL_min.note: Set by syringe pump (Harvard apparatus PHD 2200). Higher flow rate enables higher concentration factor before instability.

pH_7_4.additive: 0.1% BSA (Sigma-Aldrich) to prevent nonspecific electrostatic binding to PDMS/Nafion

red_blood_cells.tracker_dye: Cell Tracker Orange CMRA (Molecular Probes, Eugene, OR) at 3 uM for fluorescence video tracking

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Microfluidic Cell Retention Device for Perfusion of Mammalian Suspension Culture
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-017-06949-8
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-017-06949-8
Journal      : Scientific Reports, 2017, Vol. 7, Article 6703
Platform     : Inertial microfluidic spiral channel (PDMS) coupled to stirred perfusion bioreactor


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a novel membrane-less cell retention device based on inertial sorting
for continuous perfusion culture of suspended mammalian CHO cells. The spiral microchannel
with trapezoidal cross-section focuses CHO cells (17.7 +/- 2.5 um diameter) near the inner
wall of the channel using a combination of shear gradient-induced and wall-induced lift forces
(F_L proportional to a^4) and Dean drag forces (F_D proportional to a) generated by
counter-rotating Dean vortices in the curved channel geometry. Cells are retained through the
inner outlet (retentate, recycled to bioreactor), while the cell-limited harvest stream exits
through the outer outlet (permeate, collected as IgG1-containing product).

The device eliminates membrane fouling, product retention, and filter replacement contamination
risks associated with conventional tangential flow filtration (TFF) and alternating tangential
flow filtration (ATF) hollow-fiber membrane systems. As a passive operation requiring no active
field (no electric field, no acoustic wave), it is simple, low-maintenance, and biocompatible.
IgG1 recovery exceeds 99% because the smallest channel dimension (~100 um) is far larger than
any antibody molecule, allowing free passage of product into the harvest stream.

Three sequential perfusion cultures of CHO-DG44 cells (IgG1 against CD40 ligand) were run
for 18-25 days each in a 350 mL lab-scale bioreactor at >20 million cells/mL, demonstrating
cell viability >97% throughout and a total IgG1 yield of 263 mg per run.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Material     : Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS, Sylgard 184, Dow Corning); platinum-cured silicone.
               Channel dimensions (~100 um) within limit of injection-moulding (polystyrene).
Fabrication  : Standard soft lithography. Molds designed in Rhinoceros (McNeel North America);
               aluminum molds fabricated by micromachining (Whits Technologies, Singapore).
               PDMS poured into molds; cured at 150 C for 15 min on hotplate. Bonded to flat
               glass slide (260230, Ted Pella) or thin PDMS layer (<500 um) by oxygen plasma
               treatment (Harrick Plasma). Cured at 95 C overnight. Silicone tubings inserted
               (Masterflex, Cole-Parmer). Clamped with binder clips for robust operation.

Single spiral channel:
  Width          : 600 um
  Inner depth    : 80 um
  Outer depth    : 130 um
  Loops          : 8
  Volume         : 28 uL
  Footprint      : 26 x 26 mm
  Outlet width   : 300 um (single channel)

Parallel configuration (used for perfusion cultures):
  Channels per layer : 4 spiral channels combined in single layer
  Inner outlet width : 520 um (enlarged for parallel configuration)
  Perfusion rate     : ~700 mL/day (4-spiral single layer at 1 mL/min input)

Modified high-density channel (Fig. 2d, for 30-40e6 cells/mL):
  Width          : 1000 um
  Inner depth    : 260 um
  Outer depth    : 80 um
  Flow rate      : 4 mL/min input; R_OO/R_IO = 1:0.1
  Retention      : 84% at 43.6e6 cells/mL

Fluidic resistance ratio (R_OO/R_IO):
  Set by attaching small-diameter (510 um ID) tubing (EW-06420-02, Cole-Parmer) of
  adjusted length to outer outlet. Values tested: 4.5, 2.7, 1.5.
  Higher R_OO/R_IO moves streamline boundary toward outer outlet, increasing cell retention.
  Perfusion culture: R_OO/R_IO = 4.0 (inner outlet:outer outlet = 1:4).

Inlets  : 1 (cell culture input from bioreactor via peristaltic pump)
Outlets : 2 -- inner outlet (retentate, cells recycled to bioreactor)
               outer outlet (permeate, harvest: cell-free IgG1-containing stream)

Large-scale stacked device estimate:
  For 1000 L/day perfusion: ~600 channels needed (1000 um x 260 um x 80 um, 4 mL/min/channel).
  Stacked device overall dimensions: 100 mm x 80 mm x 300 mm; single layer 2 mm thick.
  Uniform flow distribution demonstrated in 10-layer simulation (Supplementary Fig. S6).
  Single channel failure reduces stacked device retention by only 1%.


CELL LINE AND BIOREACTOR
-------------------------
Cell line    : CHO-DG44 producing human IgG1 against CD40 ligand
               Gifted from Biogen Idec, MA, USA.
               Diameter: 17.7 +/- 2.5 um (mean +/- s.d., n=19,346).

Culture medium: CD OptiCHO (12681011, CD OptiCHO TM, Thermo Fisher Scientific)
               + 50 uM L-methionine sulfoximine (M5379, Sigma-Aldrich).
               Suspension cultures in autoclaved spinner flask (4500-500, PYREX ProCulture,
               Corning) on magnetic stirrer at 45 RPM.

Bioreactor   : Spinner flask (350 mL working volume) customised for pH/DO control.
               pH setpoint: 7.0; DO setpoint: 40% air saturation.
               Controllers: BioFlo/CelliGen 115 (New Brunswick Scientific, USA);
                            BIOSTAT A (Sartorious, USA).
               Working volume controlled by bioreactor weight via customised software.

Inoculation  : 0.3-0.4e6 cells/mL; batch mode for 4 days before perfusion.

Peristaltic pumps : 07522-20 (Masterflex, USA); 120U/DV (Watson Marlow, USA).


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Device Priming and Sterilisation
  Reagents     : PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free), Pluronics F-127
  Mix          : 2% Pluronics F-127 in PBS
  Duration     : 5 min
  Sterilisation: 10% bleach (min 10 min) then 70% ethanol (min 10 min) via peristaltic pump
                 prior to priming.
  Setup        : Pre-sterilised device, tubings, and bottles connected in biosafety cabinet.
                 400 mL pre-warmed sterile medium transferred into flask.
                 Setup moved into standard CO2 incubator (37 C) after 4-day batch phase.
  Purpose      : Reduces cell adhesion to PDMS surfaces; equilibrates fluidic adaptors.

Step 2 | Batch Growth Phase (Days 0-4, no perfusion)
  Cell line    : CHO-DG44
  Concentration: 0.3-0.4 e6 cells/mL in 350 mL CD OptiCHO + 50 uM MSX
  Operation    : Batch culture (no perfusion); spinner flask at 45 RPM, 37 C, 5% CO2.
  Duration     : 4 days (5760 min; BioScript token: 5760m -> IR: 345600.0 SECOND)
  Notes        : Cells grown in batch mode to establish viable exponential culture before
                 perfusion initiation. Specific growth rate 0.03 h^-1 (same as batch).

Step 3 | Perfusion Initiation and Continuous Cell Retention (Days 4-18/25)
  Input flow rate  : 1 mL/min per single spiral chip (< 1.5 mL/min optimal)
  Perfusion rate   : 2 VVD (vessel volumes per day; 700 mL/day with 4-spiral layer)
  Operation        : Fresh medium supplied continuously at 2 VVD via second peristaltic pump.
                     CHO cell culture pumped continuously through 4-spiral device at 1 mL/min.
                     Cells focused to inner wall by inertial forces (F_L and F_D); retained
                     via inner outlet and recycled to bioreactor.
                     IgG1-containing harvest collected from outer outlet into harvest bottle.
                     Harvest bottle replaced daily.
  Duration         : 18-25 days (min run: 25920 min; BioScript token: 25920m -> IR: 1555200.0 SECOND)
  Cells recycled   : 98.4 +/- 1.1% of total cell number (mean +/- s.d., n=15)
  Temperature      : 37 C / 5% CO2 (modelled as `heat ... at 37c` in BioScript)
  Working volume   : Maintained at ~350 mL by customised weight-control software.

Step 4 | Cell Retention Efficiency Measurement (Daily QC)
  Formula      : R(%) = (X_I - X_OO) / X_I x 100
                 X_I  = cell concentration in bioreactor (inner outlet)
                 X_OO = cell concentration in harvest stream (outer outlet)
  Instrument   : BioProfile CDV Analyzer (Nova Biomedical, USA)
  Aliquots     : 3 per outlet per daily measurement
  Max deviation: 3.8 +/- 2.9% (mean +/- s.d., n=64) for >1e6 cells/mL
  Results:
    At 4.8e6 cells/mL (1 mL/min)  : 99.6 +/- 0.3% (mean +/- s.d., n=9)
    At 15.4e6 cells/mL             : 99.2% (0.1% range, n=3)
    At 22.2e6 cells/mL             : 92.2% (0.8% range, n=3)
    At 20-23e6 cells/mL (perfusion): 82 +/- 3% (mean +/- s.d., n=10)
    Above 26.5e6 cells/mL          : <83% (band broadening; cell-to-cell interaction)
  Detection module (BioScript): cellRetentionDetection
  QC gate:
    Pass (BB2): retentionSignal > 0 -> R > 80% confirmed; dispose bioreactor sample
    Fail (BB3): retentionSignal <= 0 -> retention failure; drain bioreactor sample
    Join (BB4): dispose retentionSignal; proceed to IgG1 branch

Step 5 | IgG1 Product Recovery Measurement (Daily QC)
  Formula      : AR(%) = X_OO / X_I x 100
                 X_I  = IgG1 concentration in bioreactor (feed)
                 X_OO = IgG1 concentration in harvest stream (permeate)
  Instrument   : HPLC affinity chromatography
                 Column: 2-1001-00 (Applied Biosystems, USA)
                 System: 1100 Series (Agilent, USA)
                 Equilibration: 50 mM phosphate + 150 mM NaCl, pH 7.0
                 Elution: 100 mM phosphate + 0.4% (v/v) phosphoric acid (85 wt%), pH 2.5
                 Reference: IgG1-Kappa from human myeloma plasma (I5154, Sigma-Aldrich)
  Results:
    Days 1-2              : ~80% (adsorption to tubing and fluidic adaptors)
    From Day 3 onward     : ~100%
    Peak bioreactor conc. : ~40 ug/mL after Day 9
    Total harvest volume  : 8.16 L per 18-day run
    Total IgG1 yield      : 263 mg per 18-day run
    Production rate       : 26.8 mg/day from Day 9
  Notes        : No membrane = no product retention or concentration polarisation.
                 IgG1 passes freely through ~100 um channel minimum dimension.
  Detection module (BioScript): igG1Quantification
  QC gate:
    Pass (BB5): igG1Signal > 0 -> IgG1 confirmed in harvest; dispose harvest sample
    Fail (BB6): igG1Signal <= 0 -> product loss; drain harvest sample
    Join (BB7): dispose igG1Signal; proceed to viability branch

Step 6 | Cell Viability Assessment (Daily QC)
  Method       : Trypan blue dye exclusion
  Imaging      : 40 images from 40 different fields of view per measurement.
                 Cell diameter by pixel distance. Concentration by cell counting.
                 Calibrants: 6,000 cells -> 5e6 cells/mL; 12,000 cells -> 10e6 cells/mL.
  Instrument   : BioProfile FLEX and CDV Analyzers (Nova Biomedical, USA)
  Stain time   : 2 min (BioScript: 2m -> IR: 120.0 SECOND)
  Results:
    Biocompatibility run : >145 h continuous processing; 98% (1.6% range) avg retention (n=3)
    Viability decrease   : No noticeable decrease observed across 3 independent runs
    Specific growth rate : 0.03 h^-1 (same as batch culture; Supplementary Table S2)
    During perfusion     : Viability maintained >97% throughout
    After Day 10         : 99 +/- 1% (mean +/- s.d., n=9)
  Notes        : Shear stress-related gene not upregulated in CHO cells by spiral sorting
                 (consistent with prior literature: Warkiani et al., Sci. Rep. 2015).
                 No membrane permeability or surface protein changes expected.
  Detection module (BioScript): cellViabilityDetection
  QC gate:
    Pass (BB8): viabilitySignal > 0 -> viability >97% confirmed; dispose stained sample
    Fail (BB9): viabilitySignal <= 0 -> viability drop; drain stained sample
    Join (BB10): dispose viabilitySignal; NOP (terminal)


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : kwon_microfluidic_cell_retention_perfusion.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
DAG            : kwon_microfluidic_cell_retention_perfusion_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations converted to minutes (m) for compiler compatibility.
                 BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported.
                 4 days  -> 5760m   (batch phase;     IR: 345600.0 SECOND)
                 18 days -> 25920m  (perfusion phase; IR: 1555200.0 SECOND)
                 5 min   -> 5m      (channel priming; IR: 300.0 SECOND)
                 2 min   -> 2m      (trypan staining; IR: 120.0 SECOND)
Modules        : cellRetentionDetection, igG1Quantification, cellViabilityDetection
Drain vs Dispose: BioScript compiler normalises `drain` to `dispose` at IR level;
                 distinction is semantic (fail-path waste routing) and does not affect CFG.
Mix abstraction: `mix` steps involving CHO_DG44_Cells model peristaltic pump recirculation
                 through the spiral channel at 1 mL/min; not DMF electrode mixing.
Heat abstraction: `heat ... at 37c` models CO2 incubator dwell and pump operation; not
                 a TEC or hotplate step.
Biological scope: Protocol encodes the full single-run QC workflow (one 18-day perfusion
                 culture). Three sequential runs (18, 25, 25 days) were performed in the
                 paper; the .bs file represents the representative 18-day run (Run 1).
IR verification : All 10 BBs confirmed in .ir output; all 12 CFG edges confirmed in .dot
                 output; all duration conversions verified; no compiler errors or warnings.

protocol.objective: Clog-free, membrane-less cell retention for continuous perfusion culture of suspended mammalian CHO cells using inertial sorting; demonstrated with high cell density (>20e6 cells/mL), long-term run (18-25 days), high IgG1 recovery (>99%), and cell viability (>97%)

forces.dean_drag_FD: Counter-rotating Dean vortices in curved channel; FD proportional to a

Dead cell debris and small non-viable cells can be removed via outer outlet

steps.duration_note: 4 days = 5760 min (BioScript m token; h not supported)

Working volume maintained at ~350 mL by customised weight-based software.

steps.name: Perfusion initiation and continuous cell retention (Days 4-18/25)
steps.operation: mix (inertial sorting recirculation abstraction) + heat (37 C)
steps.notes: Fresh CD OptiCHO medium supplied continuously at 2 VVD. Cell culture continuously pumped through 4-spiral device at 1 mL/min. CHO cells focused near inner wall by inertial forces; retained via inner outlet. Harvest (IgG1) collected from outer outlet. Working volume maintained at ~350 mL. Harvest bottle replaced daily.

steps.name: IgG1 product recovery measurement (daily QC)
steps.instrument: HPLC affinity chromatography (Agilent 1100 Series, Applied Biosystems 2-1001-00 column)
steps.notes: Spiral device has no micro- or nanoporous membrane; IgG1 (smallest channel ~100 um) passes freely into harvest stream. No product retention. Recovery close to 100% from Day 3 onward.

steps.name: Cell viability assessment (daily QC)
steps.imaging: 40 images from 40 different fields of view per measurement; cell diameter by pixel distance
steps.instrument: BioProfile FLEX and CDV Analyzers (Nova Biomedical)

perfusion_culture_results.notes: Peak cell concentration 4x higher than batch cultures using same cell line. Glucose-limited environment maintained stably after Day 10. No noticeable cell accumulation in spiral device.

scalability.modified_chip_quadruple_throughput: width 1000 um, inner depth 260 um, outer depth 80 um; 4 mL/min input

large_scale_estimate.channel_spec: 1000 um width, 260 um inner depth, 80 um outer depth
large_scale_estimate.layers: single layer = 4 channels, 2 mm thick; ~600 channels stacked
large_scale_estimate.notes: Uniform flow distribution demonstrated in 10-layer simulation (Supplementary Fig. S6). If one channel fails, stacked device retention drops by 1% only.

comparison_with_other_technologies.ATF_TFF: Membrane fouling, product retention, contamination risk on filter replacement
comparison_with_other_technologies.acoustic_wave: Requires high-frequency (~2 MHz) ultrasonic transducers; additional active components
comparison_with_other_technologies.centrifugation: High shear stress; high operation and maintenance costs
comparison_with_other_technologies.inclined_sedimentation: Long cell residence time; low retention efficiency at high cell concentration
comparison_with_other_technologies.this_work: Passive, no active field, no membrane, clog-free, benign to cells, scalable by parallelisation; material (PDMS) compatible with pharmaceutical manufacturing; injection-moulding polystyrene feasible for lower unit cost

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Attractive Design: An Elution Solvent Optimization Platform for
               Magnetic-Bead-based Fractionation Using Digital Microfluidics and
               Design of Experiments
Source Link  : https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/attractive_design.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/ac504697r
Journal      : Analytical Chemistry, 2015, Vol. 87, pp. 3902-3910
Platform     : Digital microfluidics (DMF) with C18-functionalized magnetic beads on EWOD electrode array


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a digital microfluidic (DMF) method for solid phase extraction (SPE)
using C18-functionalized magnetic beads manipulated within discrete droplets on an electrode
array. The approach replaces static porous polymer monolith (PPM) sorbents used in prior
DMF-SPE work with reconfigurable C18 magnetic beads, enabling on-the-fly tuning of sorbent
amount and removal of beads after extraction to maintain device reconfigurability.

The protocol is divided into four functional phases:
  1. Six-step C18 magnetic bead SPE (dispense, activate, wash, load, wash, elute)
  2. Loading capacity and equilibrium characterisation (fluorescein model analyte)
  3. Automated on-chip DOE-guided elution solvent optimisation for sitamaquine and angiotensin I
  4. Two-fraction sample fractionation and dried blood spot (DBS) extraction and cleanup

Total extraction time per sample is ~12 min. Throughput is 15 samples/h with 3 parallel
extractions on the current device implementation.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Bottom plate : Glass slide precoated with chromium (200 nm) and photoresist (AZ1500, 530 nm).
               15 x 4 array of driving electrodes (2 x 2 mm each); 8 reservoir electrodes
               (16 x 6 mm each). Patterned by photolithography and wet etching at the Toronto
               Nanofabrication Centre, University of Toronto.
               Dielectric: Parylene C, 7 um, vapor deposited (Specialty Coating Systems).
               Hydrophobic coating: Teflon AF, 50 nm, spin-coated (1000 rpm, 30 s),
               post-baked at 160 C for 10 min.

Top plate    : ITO-coated glass (Delta Technologies Ltd., Stillwater, MN).
               Hydrophobic coating: Teflon AF, 50 nm, spin-coated.

Assembly     : Top and bottom plates sandwiched with three layers of double-sided tape (3M,
               London, Ontario) as spacers; total gap 270 um.

Actuation    : 100-120 V_rms, 10 kHz, applied via automated control system with integrated
               moveable magnetic lens. Successive electrode actuation drives droplets.

Magnetic lens: Motorised vertical step-motor mounted beneath the DMF device.
               Engaged (close to device): immobilises C18 beads on device surface.
               Disengaged (moved away): beads freely suspended in droplet for active mixing.
               Originally developed for immunoassay workflows; repurposed here for SPE.


REAGENTS
--------
C18 Magnetic beads : SiMAG-Octadecyl; 1 um diameter; C18 aliphatic functionality.
                     Chemicell GmbH, Berlin, Germany.
                     Suspension: 5 mg/mL (~9.0e9 beads/mL) in aqueous.
                     Standard bed: 10 uL -> ~9e7 beads, ~9e-5 cm3.
                     Bed size tunable: 6 uL (~5.4e7 beads) to 12 uL (~1.08e8 beads).

Solvents           : HPLC-grade acetonitrile and methanol (Fisher Scientific, Ottawa, Ontario).
                     Deionized (DI) water. 0.1% TFA aqueous (loading capacity experiments).

Sitamaquine        : Antimalarial drug; small-molecule model pharmaceutical analyte.
                     1 ug/mL aqueous working concentration. Provided by GSK, Stevenage, UK.
                     SMILES: CCN(CC)CCCCCCNc1cc(cc2c1nccc2C)OC
                     Molar volume: 332.3 +/- 3.0 cm3; Molar refractivity: 108.7 +/- 0.3 cm3.

Angiotensin I      : Peptide model analyte. 50 ug/mL aqueous working concentration.

Internal standards : 2H10-sitamaquine (500 ng/mL in acetonitrile; from GSK, Stevenage, UK).
                     Bradykinin (10 ug/mL in 1:1 ACN:H2O with 0.1% formic acid).

Fluorescein        : Model analyte for loading capacity; 0.1% TFA aqueous.
                     Concentrations: 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100, 10000, 100000 ug/mL.

DBS reagents       : Human whole blood (BioChemed Services, Winchester, VA) spiked with
                     sitamaquine at 5 ug/mL. Spotted (15 uL) onto PerkinElmer 226 Sample
                     Collection Cards (Greenville, SC). 2 mm biopsy punch for extraction.
                     Methanol (30 uL, 5 min) used for off-chip DBS extraction.

Antifouling note   : Pluronic F-127, commonly used in DMF to reduce nonspecific adsorption,
                     was found to be INCOMPATIBLE with this protocol. Pluronics caused
                     micellar encapsulation of hydrophobic analytes and/or coating of C18
                     bead surfaces, significantly reducing extraction performance.
                     Pluronics are NOT used anywhere in this protocol.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Dispense C18 Magnetic Bead Bed
  Reagent    : C18 magnetic bead suspension, 5 mg/mL in water
  Volume     : 10 uL (~9e7 beads, ~9e-5 cm3 sorbent volume)
  Duration   : ~10 s
  Operation  : Bead suspension pipetted onto DMF device; magnetic lens engaged to form bed.
  Notes      : Sorbent volume tunable on-the-fly -- a key advantage over static PPM systems.
               Larger beds (12 uL) prevent saturation at high analyte concentrations (Fig. 2B).

Step 2 | Activate C18 Stationary Phase
  Reagent    : Acetonitrile (10 uL droplet)
  Duration   : ~30 s
  Operation  : (i) Droplet dispensed and driven to bead bed; beads engulfed.
               (ii) Magnetic lens disengaged; beads mixed via DMF actuation.
               (iii) Magnetic lens engaged; beads immobilised; supernatant driven away.
  Notes      : Solvent activation extends collapsed C18 chains into conformation capable of
               reversed-phase interaction with hydrophobic analytes (paper Fig. 1B).

Step 3 | Wash Beads with Water
  Reagent    : Deionized water (10 uL droplet)
  Duration   : ~30 s
  Operation  : Same three-operation sequence as Step 2.
  Notes      : Equilibrates activated C18 beads to aqueous phase before sample loading.

Step 4 | Load Sample and Incubate
  Reagent    : Analyte sample (10 uL droplet)
  Duration   : 5 min (300 s)
  Operation  : Droplet driven to beads; beads engulfed and actively mixed for 5 min;
               supernatant driven away. Mixing ensured by continuous DMF electrode actuation.
  Notes      : Analyte adsorbs onto C18 stationary phase during incubation.
               Loading equilibrium log K ~6 for sitamaquine (within typical SPE range).

Step 5 | Wash (x2)
  Reagent    : Deionized water (2 x 10 uL droplets)
  Duration   : ~60 s total (2 x 30 s)
  Operation  : Two sequential wash cycles using the three-operation sequence.
  Notes      : Removes unadsorbed matrix components while retaining adsorbed analyte on beads.

Step 6 | Elute
  Reagent    : Optimised elution solvent (10 uL, composed on-chip from unit droplets)
  Duration   : ~5 min (300 s)
  Operation  : Droplet driven to beads; beads engulfed and mixed for 5 min; eluate collected.
  Notes      : Solvent composition determined by DOE (see below). Unit droplets (2.5 uL) of
               neat water, methanol, and acetonitrile are dispensed from reservoirs and
               combined on-chip in the desired proportions to form the elution solvent.


LOADING CAPACITY CHARACTERISATION
----------------------------------
Model analyte : Fluorescein in 0.1% TFA (aqueous); concentrations 0.01-100000 ug/mL.
Measurement   : Fluorescence intensity of supernatant (post-extraction droplet) relative to
                stock solution. PheraStar plate reader (BMG Labtech, Durham, NC);
                ex 480 nm, em 520 nm. Triplicate experiments.

Results (Fig. 2A):
  - ~10% of sample remained unbound for 1-1000 ug/mL (no saturation).
  - At 10 mg/mL and above: saturation detected; >80% of sample remained unbound.

Sitamaquine equilibrium:
  - 1.45% unretained post-extraction at 1 ug/mL (by ESI-MS/MS).
  - Mobile phase volume: 10 uL; stationary phase volume: 6.03e-7 mL
    (shell model: uniform C18 thickness = octadecyl alkane chain length, 2.14 nm).
  - Equilibrium log K ~6; consistent with commonly reported SPE solute-sorbent equilibria.


DOE ELUTION SOLVENT OPTIMISATION
----------------------------------
Design software : JMP (SAS, Cary, NC); simplex-centroid design.
Solvents        : Acetonitrile (ACN), Methanol (MeOH), Deionized Water (H2O).
Combinations    : 7 points: neat ACN, neat MeOH, neat H2O, 1:1 ACN:MeOH, 1:1 ACN:H2O,
                  1:1 MeOH:H2O, 1:1:1 ACN:MeOH:H2O.

On-chip mixing  : Unit droplets (2.5 uL each) dispensed from reservoir electrodes containing
                  neat solvents, then combined and mixed in desired proportions.
                  DMF can automatically generate any composition from the ternary space.

Model           : Three-component special cubic (eq 2 in paper):
                  y_hat = sum(bi*xi) + sum(bij*xi*xj) + sum(bijk*xi*xj*xk)
                  where xi = solvent fraction; bi = linear, bij = binary, bijk = ternary coefficients.
                  Response surface plots generated for each analyte (Fig. 4A/B).

Solubility prediction: Abraham general solvation model (web calculator) used to predict
                  sitamaquine solubilities: MeOH > ACN > H2O; consistent with DOE results.

Results:
  Sitamaquine (1 ug/mL):
    - Optimal elution solvent: 100% Methanol (extraction efficiency ~45-55%; Fig. 4A).
    - General trend: increasing efficiency with increasing organic fraction.
    - MeOH outperforms ACN, consistent with Abraham solvation model prediction.

  Angiotensin I (50 ug/mL):
    - Optimal elution solvent: 1:1 ACN:H2O (extraction efficiency ~45-50%; Fig. 4B).
    - Consistent with common practice for reversed-phase peptide separations by HPLC.

Comparison with ZipTip (Fig. 5):
  - DMF C18 bead extraction comparable to C18 ZipTip (EMD Millipore) for both analytes.
  - Sitamaquine eluted in neat methanol; angiotensin I eluted in 1:1 ACN:H2O.


SAMPLE FRACTIONATION
---------------------
Mixture    : Sitamaquine (1 ug/mL) + angiotensin I (50 ug/mL), co-loaded on C18 beads.
Strategy   : Sequential elution with two solvents of differing polarity:

Elution 1 (Fraction 1) -- Neat methanol:
  Sitamaquine recovery : ~90-95%
  Angiotensin I carry-over : ~5-10%
  Result: Sitamaquine-enriched fraction.

Elution 2 (Fraction 2) -- 1:1 ACN:H2O:
  Angiotensin I recovery : ~85-90%
  Sitamaquine carry-over : ~10-15%
  Result: Angiotensin I-enriched fraction.

Coelution : <10% for both fractions (Fig. 6B).
Detection : ESI-MS/MS (344->271 m/z) for sitamaquine; ESI-MS (433 m/z, [M+3H]3+) for
            angiotensin I. IS: 2H10-sitamaquine (500 ng/mL) + bradykinin (531 m/z, [M+2H]2+).


DRIED BLOOD SPOT EXTRACTION AND CLEANUP
-----------------------------------------
Purpose    : Proof-of-principle for real-world complex matrix sample cleanup.
             Reduce ionisation suppression of sitamaquine in DBS extracts.

DBS preparation:
  - 15 uL human whole blood (BioChemed Services) spiked with sitamaquine (5 ug/mL).
  - Spotted onto PerkinElmer 226 Sample Collection Cards; allowed to dry.
  - 2 mm biopsy punch extracted into methanol (30 uL, 5 min).

On-chip procedure:
  1. Unit droplet (2.5 uL) of DBS extract split off for cleanup.
  2. Combined with water (22.5 uL) on-chip; total 25 uL at diluted aqueous matrix.
     (Aqueous dilution required for C18 reversed-phase compatibility.)
  3. C18 bead SPE cleanup following six-step protocol (elution: neat methanol, 10 uL).
  4. Off-chip: eluate diluted to 100 uL in 1:1 ACN:H2O + 0.5% formic acid.

Detection:
  - API 4000 Triple Quadrupole MS/MS (AB Sciex, Concord, Ontario).
  - Positive ion mode; direct infusion 2 uL/min; spray voltage 5 kV.
  - SRM transition: 344->271 m/z (sitamaquine); 12 scans averaged.

Results (Fig. 7):
  - Raw DBS extract: little signal for sitamaquine at 271 m/z (ionisation suppression).
  - Post C18 bead cleanup: sitamaquine signal (271 m/z) strongly enhanced.
  - Cleanup reduces matrix interferents (lipids, haem, proteins) that suppress ESI ionisation.


MASS SPECTROMETRY PARAMETERS
------------------------------
Sitamaquine (ESI-MS/MS, LTQ, Thermo Scientific, Waltham, MA):
  Mode          : Positive ion, SRM
  Spray voltage : 1.2-1.5 kV (varied)
  Flow rate     : 0.5 uL/min
  Capillary temp: 350 C
  Collision gas : Helium (99.995%) for collision activated dissociation
  Transitions   : 344->271 m/z (sitamaquine); 354->271 m/z (2H10-sitamaquine IS)
  Scans         : 10 acquisitions averaged
  Software      : Thermo Finnigan Xcalibur v2.0

Angiotensin I (ESI-MS, LTQ, Thermo Scientific, Waltham, MA):
  Mode          : Positive ion
  Spray voltage : 1.2-1.5 kV (varied)
  Flow rate     : 0.5 uL/min
  Capillary temp: 200 C
  Monitored     : 433 m/z ([M+3H]3+, angiotensin I)
                  354 m/z ([M+3H]3+, bradykinin IS) for DOE experiments
                  531 m/z ([M+2H]2+, bradykinin IS) for fractionation experiments
  Scans         : 10 acquisitions averaged
  Software      : Thermo Finnigan Xcalibur v2.0


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
--------------------------
BioScript file : lafreniere_attractive_design_dmf_spe.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 13 basic blocks (BB1-BB13), 4 if/else gates, 16 CFG edges
DAG            : lafreniere_attractive_design_dmf_spe_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations in s or m only (compiler supports s and m tokens only)
                 5 min incubations -> 5m (IR: 300.0 SECOND)
                 30 s washes -> 30s (IR: 30.0 SECOND)

Modules        : massSpecDetection, fluorescenceDetection, doeElutionModel

Compiler constraints and workarounds:
  DOE loop     : No loop/array-index semantics in lilott8/BioScript. Seven simplex-centroid
                 points are represented by 3 explicitly encoded runs covering analytically
                 critical conditions (100% MeOH, 1:1 ACN:H2O, 1:1:1 ternary). The
                 doeElutionModel detection module abstracts the special cubic model fitting
                 over all 7 conditions per eq 2 of the paper.
  Elution vol. : Unit droplets are 2.5 uL. Four unit droplets chained via `mix` accumulate
                 10 uL for each elution step; binary-tree mixing avoids long serial chains.
  DBS diluent  : 22.5 uL of water (9 unit droplets) accumulated via 8-way binary tree +
                 final single droplet merge.
  No split     : `split` operator avoided entirely; all dilutions use direct dispense + mix.
  Pluronics    : NOT included in manifests or any dispense operations (incompatible with C18).

Pluronics note : Unlike the Samlali et al. protocol which uses Pluronics F-127 for PDMS
                 antifouling, this protocol explicitly excludes Pluronics due to incompatibility
                 with C18 magnetic beads (micellar encapsulation of hydrophobic analytes).

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Multiplexed Proteomic Sample Preconcentration Device Using Surface-Patterned Ion-Selective Membrane
Source Link  : https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2394188/pdf/nihms46491.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1039/b717900f
Journal      : Lab Chip, 2008, Vol. 8, No. 4, pp. 596-601
Platform     : PDMS microfluidic chip with surface-patterned planar Nafion ion-selective membrane (PDMS/glass)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a high-throughput proteomic sample preconcentration method in PDMS
microfluidic chip format using a surface-patterned submicron Nafion ion-selective membrane.
The key innovation is the direct printing of a Nafion permselective membrane onto a glass
substrate by micro-flow patterning, followed by single-step integration into the device via
standard O2 plasma bonding. This eliminates the need for complicated nanochannel fabrication
(as in prior silicon micro/nanofluidic devices) and cumbersome thin-film integration processes.

The preconcentration mechanism is electrokinetic trapping, exploiting the ion-selectivity of
the Nafion membrane to generate a depletion region in the sample microchannel. Charged
molecules (proteins, peptides, or any charged species regardless of size) are concentrated
in front of the depletion boundary by the combined action of a normal electric field (En)
across the membrane and a tangential electroosmotic flow (EOF) along the sample channel.

Key performance metrics:
  - Concentration factor: ~10^4 in 5 min from 400 pM starting concentration
  - Concentration factor: ~5x10^4 in 10 min from 40 pM starting concentration
  - Concentrated plug volume: ~200 pL per single unit
  - 12x faster than prior PDMS preconcentrator (junction gap breakdown method: ~10^4 in 1 h)
  - 350x larger concentrated volume vs. prior silicon nanochannel device (few pL)
  - 10-unit array: ~2 nL concentrated volume (3500x vs. silicon device); compatible with
    mass spectrometer interfacing via electrospray or droplet dispensing
  - Coefficient of variance: 11.5% across 3 devices (reasonable given pattern alignment inaccuracy)

The Nafion membrane is applicable to any charged molecule; the preconcentration platform is
general and not limited to specific biomarkers or antibody-antigen interactions.


SEPARATION PHYSICS
------------------
The device operates in two sequential electrical phases:

Phase 1 - Depletion mode (V1=50V, V2=50V, buffer GND):
  A voltage difference is applied between the sample channel and the flanking buffer channels
  through the planar Nafion membrane. The normal field component (En) perpendicular to the
  membrane depletes ions in the sample channel and drives charged molecules away from the
  membrane toward the V1 reservoir. A stable depletion region forms and grows with time.

Phase 2 - Concentration mode (V1=50V, V2=25V, buffer GND):
  V2 is reduced to 25V; Vdiff = V1-V2 = 25V (optimum). The tangential field component (Et)
  along the sample channel generates an electroosmotic flow (EOF) that injects molecules from
  the bulk toward the depletion boundary. Molecules stack in front of the depletion zone,
  forming a stable concentrated plug at equilibrium distance Y2 from the Nafion membrane.
  The balance of En (depletion force) and Et (electroosmotic injection) determines plug position.

Optimum Vdiff = 25V: at higher Vdiff, secondary nonlinear electrokinetics near the membrane
destabilize the concentrated zone. Preconcentration factor and depletion region size both
increase monotonically with Vdiff up to 25V (Fig. 5 of paper).

Ion selectivity mechanism: Nafion's cluster network reduces the effective pore size, while
sulfonate groups (-SO3H) provide high negative charge density, achieving permselectivity
superior to prior PDMS nanojunction approaches. No voltage breakdown limit applies (unlike
silicon oxide-gated nanochannels), allowing higher applied voltages and faster concentration.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Material         : PDMS bonded to Nafion-patterned glass substrate (25 mm x 75 mm slides)
Overall size     : 20 mm x 25 mm
Channel geometry : All channels 50 um deep x 50 um wide
Layout           : Dual gate design
                   - Center: sample channel (beta-PE protein in phosphate buffer; red in Fig. 4a)
                   - Flanking left and right: two buffer channels (phosphate buffer; green in Fig. 4a)
                   - Nafion stripe printed on glass connects all three channels at channel bottom
                     as planar permselective junction
Nafion membrane  :
  Material       : Nafion perfluorinated ion-exchange resin (Sigma-Aldrich), 5 wt% in
                   lower aliphatic alcohols/H2O, 15-20% water content
  Target thickness: 191-400 nm; measured 191 nm by SEM (Fig. 4b/c)
  Critical limit : >400 nm causes PDMS sealing failure; leakage at membrane edges compromises
                   ion selectivity and preconcentration efficiency/reproducibility
Electrode config : Pt wire electrodes inserted into channel reservoirs via punched access holes

Array format (10-unit):
  10 single preconcentrators arranged radially around a common collection reservoir (center).
  Sample reservoirs S1-S10 each at V1=50V; common reservoir at V2=25V; individual ground
  reservoirs per buffer channel. Nafion patterned in half-circle shape per unit.
  Concentrated volume: ~2 nL (10 x ~200 pL); sufficient for pipette transfer or direct
  electrospray to mass spectrometer.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Nafion Membrane Patterning - Micro-flow Patterning (Preferred Method)
  Reagents    : Nafion perfluorinated resin (Sigma-Aldrich, 5 wt% in aliphatic alcohols/H2O)
  Volume      : 1 uL per pattern
  Method      : (1) Place 1 uL Nafion resin at reservoir of reversibly bonded temporary PDMS
                    channel (120 um deep x 200 um wide); capillary force fills channel immediately.
                (2) Apply negative pressure via syringe tubing at opposite channel end; flush
                    liquid resin out, leaving thin Nafion residual layer on hydrophilic glass.
                (3) Cure patterned stripe on hotplate at 95 C for 10 min.
  Target      : 191-400 nm; thickness controlled by applied negative pressure magnitude
  Reproducibility: Consistent at constant pressure; CV lower than micro-stamping alternative
  BioScript   : nafionResin self-mix (flow-coat abstraction) + heat at 95c for 10m

  Alternative - Micro-stamping Method:
  (1) Plasma-treat PDMS microstamp surface to improve Nafion wetting.
  (2) Ink PDMS microstamp with Nafion resin.
  (3) Transfer Nafion to clean pre-cleaned glass slide (IPA + DI water wash before printing).
  (4) Cure at 95 C for 10 min on hotplate.
  Thickness 0.5-1 um (less reproducible; pressure-distribution-dependent; risk of leakage).

Step 2 | PDMS Chip Plasma Bonding and Post-Bond Bake
  Method      : Standard O2 plasma bonding; PDMS chip placed on top of Nafion-patterned glass
  Alignment   : Not critical; performed without microscope
  Post-bond   : Hotplate 70 C for 12 h (720 min) to enhance bonding strength
  Result      : Elastic PDMS conforms adequately to rounded Nafion membrane profile at <=400 nm
                thickness (Fig. 4c SEM cross-section confirms membrane sealed between PDMS and glass)
  BioScript   : heat nafionCured at 70c for 720m (IR: 43200.0 SECOND)

Step 3 | Buffer Channel Loading
  Reagents    : 10^-2 M phosphate buffer pH 7
  Channels    : Both flanking buffer channels (dual gate); kept at GND during operation
  Duration    : 30 s loading (encoded as mix)
  Purpose     : Dual buffer channels generate depletion zones from both sides of the sample
                channel simultaneously, improving depletion region stability vs. single buffer
                channel design
  BioScript   : bufferLeft + bufferRight dispensed separately; mixed into bufferDual

Step 4 | Sample Loading
  Reagents    : beta-Phycoerythrin (beta-PE; MW 240 kDa, pI 4.3) in 10^-2 M phosphate buffer pH 7
  Concentrations tested: 40 pM, 400 pM, 4 nM, 40 nM
  Canonical   : 4 nM (Fig. 6 time-course experiment)
  Channel     : Central sample microchannel; both ends accessible for V1/V2 electrode connections
  Internal reference standards: 2 uM, 4 uM, 8 uM beta-PE for concentration factor calculation
  BioScript   : proteinSample dispensed; mixed with bufferDual into loadedSample

Step 5 | Depletion Mode (Phase 1)
  Voltage     : V1=50V (sample inlet), V2=50V (sample outlet), buffer channels GND
  Duration    : 1 min to establish and stabilize depletion region
  Physics     : En (normal field across Nafion) depletes ions in sample channel; negatively
                charged beta-PE (pI 4.3 < pH 7.0) pushed toward V1 reservoir; depletion zone
                visible as dark region by fluorescence microscopy
  BioScript   : mix loadedSample with bufferDual for 1m + heat depletedSample at 50c for 1m
                (50c temperature token encodes V1=50V; BioScript has no electrical primitive)

Step 6 | Concentration Mode (Phase 2)
  Voltage     : V1=50V, V2=25V (Vdiff = 25V optimum), buffer channels GND
  Duration    : 5 min (canonical; ~10^4 fold from 400 pM; extend to 10 min for 40 pM)
  Physics     : Et (tangential field along sample channel) drives EOF injecting molecules toward
                depletion boundary; molecules stack in front of depletion zone; En and Et reach
                equilibrium forming stable concentrated plug at distance Y2 from Nafion membrane
  Performance :
    40 nM     : Saturation in ~2 min
    4 nM      : Plug visible at 1 min; grows to 200 um plug at 10 min
    400 pM    : ~2x10^4 fold increase (8 uM reference) in 5 min
    40 pM     : ~5x10^4 fold increase in 10 min; fluorescence detection enabled
  Plug volume : ~200 pL per single preconcentrator unit
  CV          : 11.5% across 3 devices
  BioScript   : mix depletedSample with bufferDual for 5m + heat concentratedPlug at 25c for 5m
                (25c temperature token encodes V2=25V; unique variable avoids reassignment)

Step 7 | Fluorescence Detection and Quantification
  Platform    : Olympus IX71 inverted epifluorescence microscope
  Camera      : Thermoelectrically cooled CCD (Hamamatsu Co., Japan)
  Software    : IPLab (Scanalytics, Fairfax, VA)
  Acquisition : Every 30 s throughout concentration mode
  Shutter     : Mechanical shutter (Olympus) blocks UV between acquisitions (anti-photobleaching)
  Filter      : Neutral density filter prevents CCD saturation; increases dynamic range
  Reference   : 2, 4, 8 uM beta-PE internal standards for concentration factor calculation
  Pass        : Fluorescence intensity >= 8 uM reference (>=~10^4 fold from 400 pM at 5 min)
  BioScript   : detect preconcentrationDetection on concentratedPlug for 5m
                Branch BB2 (pass/dispose) vs BB3 (fail/drain -> membrane leak or voltage failure)


ARRAY OPERATION (10-Unit Format)
---------------------------------
The surface patterning technique allows deposition of Nafion anywhere on the glass substrate,
enabling massively parallel arrays. For the 10-unit radial array (Fig. 7):
  - 10 identical single preconcentrators oriented radially toward a common collection reservoir
  - Nafion patterned in half-circle shape on glass substrate per unit
  - Sample reservoirs S1-S10 each biased at V1=50V
  - Common reservoir (collection center) at V2=25V
  - Individual ground reservoirs per buffer channel for equal electric field conditions
  - All 10 units operated simultaneously; concentrated plugs released toward center
  - Total concentrated volume: ~2 nL (10 x ~200 pL)
  - 3500x larger than prior silicon nanochannel preconcentrator result
  - Sufficient for direct electrospray ionization to mass spectrometer or pipette transfer

BioScript note: BioScript has no loop construct; the 10-unit array requires explicit unrolling
of 10 identical BB1 blocks. The current .bs file encodes the canonical single-unit protocol.
A separate .bs file with explicit 10-unit unrolled structure is a candidate for future encoding.


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : lee_nafion_proteomic_preconcentrator.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 4 basic blocks (BB1-BB4), 1 if/else gate, 4 CFG edges
DAG            : lee_nafion_proteomic_preconcentrator_main_dag.dot
Module         : preconcentrationDetection

Duration conversions (BioScript supports s and m only; no h token):
  Nafion cure      10 min  ->  10m  (IR: 600.0 SECOND)
  Post-bond bake   12 h    -> 720m  (IR: 43200.0 SECOND)
  Depletion mode    1 min  ->   1m  (IR: 60.0 SECOND)
  Concentration     5 min  ->   5m  (IR: 300.0 SECOND)
  Detection         5 min  ->   5m  (IR: 300.0 SECOND)

Key compiler behavior observed:
  - drain normalizes to dispose in IR output (expected; standard compiler behavior)
  - Self-mix pattern: nafionResin mixed with itself (IR line 11); models single-reagent
    flow-coat step with no second reagent. Same documented pattern as warkiani_spiral_ctc_isolation.bs
    and moazami_world_to_chip_dmf.bs. Compiled without error.
  - Multi-consumption: bufferDual1[0] consumed three times (depletion, concentration, and
    loading mix steps) representing continuous buffer channel presence across all operating phases.
    Compiled without error.
  - Sequential heat calls: two heat calls on nafionCured1[0] (95C/600s then 70C/43200s)
    compiled correctly; compiler permits multiple heat calls on the same live variable.
  - Voltage abstraction: BioScript has no electrical primitive; depletion mode encoded as
    heat at 50c (V1=50V token), concentration mode as heat at 25c (V2=25V token).
  - All 3 manifest entries correctly resolved as dispense sources only; no computed mix
    variable was used as a dispense source.
  - No variable reassignment violations; all intermediate variable names are unique.
  - No non-ASCII characters in comments.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Ultra-sensitive Digital Quantification of Proteins and mRNA in Single Cells
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-019-11531-z
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-11531-z
Journal      : Nature Communications, 2019, Vol. 10, Article 3544
Platform     : Automated microfluidic digital proximity ligation assay (u-dPLA); two-layer
               push-up PDMS device; ddPCR and one-step RT-ddPCR readout (Bio-Rad QX200)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes an automated microfluidic system for ultrasensitive, simultaneous
quantification of protein copy numbers and mRNA in individual mammalian cells, called
microfluidic digital proximity ligation assay (u-dPLA). The device traps and lyses single
cells in 7-nL nanoliter chambers, dramatically reducing the dilution factor relative to
regular well-plate dPLA. All assay steps are executed automatically with nanoliter precision
using Matlab-controlled pneumatic valve actuation, reducing pipetting errors to <0.1% versus
~10% for manual pipetting.

Key innovations over regular dPLA:
  - Up to 55-fold improvement in limit of detection (LOD)
  - 25-fold improvement in detection efficiency
  - 100% of single-cell sample used in ddPCR readout (vs 9% in regular dPLA)
  - Linear dynamic range of 3-4 orders of magnitude
  - Integrated live-cell time-lapse microscopy and chemical stimulation in the same device
  - Simultaneous protein and mRNA quantification via duplex one-step RT-ddPCR

The protocol is divided into three functional assay branches:
  1. Single-cell protein quantification via u-dPLA + ddPCR (FAM channel)
  2. Simultaneous protein/mRNA quantification via duplex u-dPLA + RT-ddPCR (FAM + VIC)
  3. HSV-1 viral infection heterogeneity: live-cell ICP4-YFP imaging + viral protein
     quantification by u-dPLA in the same single cells


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Two-layer push-up PDMS device bonded to glass slide (127.76 mm x 85.48 mm x 1 mm).
Chip capacity: 144 parallel single-cell dPLA assay units.

Fluidic layer (thick, top):
  - AZ40XT photoresist 18 um (rounded channels for valve sealing)
  - SU-8 22 um (medium feature channels)
  - SU-8 70 um two-layer (large reagent channels)

Control layer (thin, bottom):
  - SU-8 22 um; microfluidic push-up valves (Unger et al. Science 2000)
  - Pneumatically actuated via Matlab-controlled solenoid valves

Chamber architecture per assay unit (Chambers I-V):
  Chamber I   : Reagent input and wash channel; reagents introduced via dead-end filling
  Chamber II  : Single-cell trap (50 um constriction); cell imaged here and then lysed
  Chamber III : 7-nL lysis chamber; cell contents lysed and retained here; probe mixing zone
  Chamber IV  : Probe-lysate diffusion mixing extension; valve between III and IV opens
                during 1-h incubation to allow mixing by diffusion
  Chamber V   : Ligation reaction chamber; PLA products generated here
  Output port : 1930 um inner diameter biopsy punch; 9 uL PLA products retrieved per unit

Valve system:
  - Microfluidic valves separate each chamber to prevent contamination between steps
  - Dead-end filling delivers precise reagent volumes to empty chambers
  - Wash channels (MilliQ water) flush channels between reagent steps
  - Chip automation via Matlab program controlling valve open/close sequences


CELL LINES
----------
- HEK293T (human embryonic kidney): model cell for CD147/TNFR1 protein quantification
  and mRNA-protein correlation studies. TNFR1 not detected; consistent with no TNF-a
  response in NF-kB stimulation experiment.
  Cultured in DMEM (Cat. No. 11965-092, Life Technologies) + 10% FBS (F9665, Sigma-Aldrich).

- H1299 (human lung epithelial, NSCLC): primary cell line for TNFR1 protein/mRNA
  co-quantification and Spearman mRNA-protein correlation analysis.
  Cultured in RPMI-1640 (Cat. No. 11835-030, Life Technologies) + 10% FBS.

- A549 (human lung epithelial, adenocarcinoma): used for HSV-1 infection heterogeneity
  assay combined with live-cell ICP4-YFP imaging and viral protein u-dPLA.
  Cultured in DMEM (Cat. No. 86012804, Sigma-Aldrich) + 10% FBS.

All cells dissociated with TrypLE (Cat. No. 12605028, Life Technologies) 5 min at 37C,
resuspended in sterile PBS, filtered through 40 um cell strainer, diluted to 2x10^5
cells/mL for on-chip loading at 5 psi input pressure.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | BSA Surface Blocking
  Reagents    : 10% BSA in PBS (Cat. No. 37525, Thermo Fisher)
  Duration    : 1 h (60 min)
  Temperature : 25C (room temperature)
  Purpose     : Coat PDMS chip surfaces to minimise non-specific adsorption of PLA probes
                and cell-lysate proteins to channel walls.
  Post-block  : Wash with MilliQ water; ventilate with compressed air before cell loading.

Step 2 | On-Chip Calibration Curve
  Reagents    : Purified protein standard (TNFR1, CD147, or CSTB), PBS, PLA Probes,
                Ligation Mix, MilliQ water
  Method      : Serial dilution of pure protein standards loaded into assay chambers via
                dead-end filling from lowest to highest concentration. 8 min wash between
                each concentration via Channel I.
  PLA probes  : 500 pM stock diluted to 2 nM in probe binding buffer (0.1% BSA +
                0.05% Tween-20 + 100 nM goat IgG + 0.1 g/L sheared salmon sperm DNA in PBS).
                Channel I flushed 2 min; Channel II flushed 15 min.
  Probe incub : 37C, 60 min (diffusion mixing)
  Ligation    : On ice 30 min; 37C 10 min; 65C 5 min (heat inactivation of T4 ligase)
  Retrieval   : 9 uL per unit, collected for ddPCR
  Purpose     : Calibration converts ddPCR amplicon counts per uL to absolute protein
                copy numbers. Run in parallel with single-cell experiments on the same chip.
  LOD calc    : 3 SD above background reading or y-intercept of fitted linear curve
                (whichever is higher).

Step 3 | Single-Cell Loading and Hydrodynamic Trapping
  Reagents    : SingleCell suspension in PBS, PBS
  Operation   : Pressure-driven flow-through trapping in Chamber II (50 um constriction)
  Loading     : 5 psi input pressure; 2x10^5 cells/mL
  Occupancy   : ~90% average single-cell occupancy per chip run
  Verification: Cell loading confirmed visually under microscope before proceeding
  Note        : Chip immediately moved to ice after loading confirmed.
                BioScript mix abstraction represents pressure-driven hydrodynamic trapping;
                no DMF electrode actuation is involved.

Step 4 | Single-Cell Lysis
  Reagents    : Lysis buffer (0.3x TM buffer + protease inhibitor in cell resuspension buffer)
  Operation   : Lysis buffer introduced from Chamber I to push and lyse cell from
                Chamber II into Chamber III (7 nL)
  Duration    : 10 min on ice (0C)
  Verification: Lysis confirmed visually under microscope
  Key feature : 100% of 7-nL single-cell lysate retained in Chamber III; zero sample loss.
                Regular dPLA loses 91% of sample (only 9% reaches ddPCR readout).
                This 11-fold increase in effective sample use is the primary driver of the
                55-fold LOD improvement.

Step 5 | PLA Probe Incubation with Cell Lysate
  Reagents    : PLA Probes (2 nM working concentration)
  Chambers    : III and IV (valve between open during incubation)
  Duration    : 60 min at 37C; diffusion-based mixing
  Mechanism   : Each PLA probe pair consists of two oligonucleotide-tagged antibodies
                recognising two distinct epitopes on the target protein. When both probes
                bind the same protein molecule, their oligonucleotides are brought within
                ~3-5 nm, enabling connector-mediated ligation.
  Probes used :
    TNFR1 : Biotinylated BAF225 (R&D Systems), streptavidin-biotin conjugation
    CD147 : Biotinylated BAF972 (R&D Systems), streptavidin-biotin conjugation
    CSTB  : Commercially available (Cat. No. 4405465, Applied Biosystems)
    HSV-1 : Anti-HSV-1 polyclonal ab9533 (Abcam), in-house DBCO-NHS/azide click chemistry;
             detects ~80 HSV-1 viral protein species encoded by HSV-1 genome

Step 6 | Ligation Reaction
  Reagents    : Ligation Mix (89.1 uL MilliQ water + 10 uL 10x ligase buffer +
                0.4 uL 1/500-diluted T4 ligase (EL0011, Thermo Scientific) +
                0.5 uL 1 uM connector oligo TTTCGACACGACACGATTTAGGTC per 100 uL)
  Operation   : Ligation mix pushes probe-lysate mix from Chambers III/IV into Chamber V
  On ice      : 30 min for diffusion mixing
  Ligation    : 37C, 10 min; T4 DNA ligase seals nick in connector-bridged probe pair
  Inactivation: 65C, 5 min; heat inactivation of T4 ligase
  Product     : Circular dsDNA PLA product; each molecule = 1 detected protein

Step 7 | PLA Product Retrieval and ddPCR (Protein Quantification Gate)
  Reagents    : MilliQ water (flush), ddPCR Supermix for Probes (Bio-Rad Cat. No. 1863024),
                Universal PCR Assay (Cat. No. 4405501, Applied Biosystems),
                Droplet Generation Oil (Cat. No. 1863005, Bio-Rad)
  Retrieval   : 9 uL PLA products flushed from Chamber V via water through 1930 um port
  ddPCR setup : 9 uL products + 10 uL 2x Supermix + 1 uL 20x PCR Assay = 20 uL total;
                loaded into DG8 cartridge with 65 uL Droplet Generation Oil (QX200, Bio-Rad)
  PCR program : 95C 10 min; 40x (94C 30s / 60C 1 min); 98C 10 min; ramp 1.5C/s
  Readout     : FAM channel; positive droplet count = absolute protein copy number
  ddPCR primers:
    Forward   : GCATCGTCTCGTGGGCTC
    Reverse   : TTGTACGCATGTGGACTTTAGACACGACACGA
  Detection   : ddPCRProteinDetection module; 30 s
  QC gate     :
    Pass (BB2): proteinSignal > 0 -> above LOD; dispose ddPCR droplets
    Fail (BB3): proteinSignal <= 0 -> below LOD; drain
  Results (selected):
    CD147 mean: HEK293T 197,785 (N=266); H1299 327,609 (N=96); A549 179,513 (N=98)
    TNFR1 mean: H1299 14,807 (N=88, range 6,310-33,541); A549 13,017 (N=84)
    TNFR1 in HEK293T: all below LOD (2,277 molecules); consistent with no NF-kB response
    Cells above TNFR1 LOD: 86% (149/174); first single-cell TNFR1 counts reported

Step 8 | Duplex Protein/mRNA Quantification (Same Single Cell)
  Reagents    : RNaseOUT (Cat. No. 10777019, Invitrogen; 20x dilution in all reagent mixes),
                One-step RT-ddPCR Supermix (5 uL), Reverse Transcriptase (2 uL),
                DTT 300 mM (Cat. No. 1864021, Bio-Rad; 1 uL),
                Universal PCR Assay 20x (1 uL),
                TNFR1 TaqMan Probe 20x (Cat. No. Hs01042313_m1, Applied Biosystems; 1 uL),
                Nuclease-free water (1 uL); Total: 20 uL
  Method      : PLA product retrieval (9 uL) includes protected mRNA; RNaseOUT added to all
                reagent mixes throughout chip steps to protect mRNA integrity
  Duplex      : FAM channel -> protein (PLA ligation products, same as Step 7)
                VIC channel -> mRNA (RT-ddPCR amplicons from TNFR1 mRNA)
  RT program  : 42C 1 h; 95C 10 min; 40x (95C 30s / 60C 1 min); 98C 10 min; ramp 2C/s
  Crosstalk   : VIC/FAM crosstalk negligible (Supplementary Fig. 5a/b)
  Detection   : rtDdPCRmRNADetection module (VIC channel); 30 s
  QC gate     :
    Pass (BB5): mrnaSignal > 0 -> mRNA detected; dispose duplex droplets
    Fail (BB6): mrnaSignal <= 0 -> mRNA below detection; drain
  Results     :
    Spearman rho (TNFR1 protein vs mRNA, H1299): 0.45 (N=38 single cells)
    Previous estimates: ~0.1 (Taniguchi 2010, Albayrak 2016, Darmanis 2016)
    Finding: Including lowly-expressing cells (previously below dPLA LOD) increases
    mRNA-protein correlation significantly. Spearman coefficient rises as low-protein
    cells are included in the calculation (Fig. 3e). High-sensitivity quantification is
    essential for accurate mRNA-protein correlation estimates.

Step 9 | HSV-1 Viral Infection Heterogeneity Assay
  Reagents    : HSV1_InfectedCell (A549 + HSV-1 ICP4-YFP, MOI 2, overnight), ControlCell
                (A549, no virus), PBS, LysisBuffer, PLAProbes (HSV-1), LigationMix,
                MilliQWater, ddPCR_Supermix, UniversalPCRAssay, DropletGenerationOil
  Cell prep   : HSV-1 stock prepared by Vero cell infection (MOI 0.01), harvested Day 3
                by three freeze-thaw cycles; stock concentration by plaque assay.
                A549 infected with 25 uL virus in 2 mL fresh medium overnight (MOI 2).
  Live imaging:
    Reporter  : ICP4-YFP; ICP4 expressed immediately upon viral genome nuclear entry,
                prior to genome replication (DeLuca et al. 1985; 1987).
                Nuclear YFP signal = infection proceeded to nuclear entry (YFP-positive).
    Modality  : Time-lapse fluorescence imaging on chip before lysis (liveCellImagingDetection)
    Calculation: Matlab imfindcircles locates cells; ImageJ Rolling Ball Background
                 Subtraction; total fluorescence = sum of all YFP pixel values within cell
  Lysis       : All cells lysed simultaneously with 0.3x TM buffer, on ice, 10 min
  HSV-1 PLA   : Polyclonal anti-HSV-1 ab9533 (Abcam) conjugated via DBCO-NHS click chemistry;
                detects ~80 viral protein species; both immediate-early, early, and late proteins
  Probe incub : 37C, 60 min
  Ligation    : On ice 30 min; 37C 10 min; 65C 5 min
  ddPCR       : Same protocol as Step 7; FAM channel; viral protein copy number per cell
  Detection   : viralProteinDetection module; 30 s
  QC gate     :
    Pass (BB8): infectionSignal > 0 -> ICP4-YFP+ (nuclear entry confirmed); dispose
    Fail (BB9): infectionSignal <= 0 -> uninfected or control (no YFP); drain
  Results     :
    N infected (YFP+) cells: 27; N control cells: 19
    Group difference p-value: 5.356e-11 (two-sided Welch's t test)
    Spearman rho (ICP4-YFP fluorescence vs total viral protein count): 0.48
    Interpretation: Not all YFP-positive cells progress past immediate-early protein
    synthesis stage; partial correlation (rho=0.48) indicates a sub-population undergoes
    abortive infection. Single-cell viral protein counts span ~5-fold range across
    infected cells, consistent with prior reports of substantial single-cell heterogeneity
    in viral progeny release (Heldt 2015, Russell 2018).


PERFORMANCE SUMMARY
-------------------
Protein target    LOD (on-chip)   LOD (regular)   Det. eff (on-chip)  Det. eff (regular)
TNFR1             2,277 molecules 66,789 molecules 33 proteins/DNA     741 proteins/DNA
CD147             2,795 molecules 55,385 molecules 29 proteins/DNA     70 proteins/DNA
CSTB              18,824 molecules 1,035,991 mol.  304 proteins/DNA    5,024 proteins/DNA

LOD improvement: up to 55-fold  |  Detection efficiency improvement: up to 25-fold
Dynamic range  : 3-4 orders of magnitude
Sample recovery: 100% of 7-nL lysate used (vs 9% in regular dPLA)
Chip capacity  : 144 parallel single-cell assay units

steps.name: Calibration curve loading (on-chip)
steps.operation: serial dead-end filling + probe incubation + ligation
steps.notes: Calibration curve run in parallel with single-cell experiments on same chip. Converts ddPCR amplicon counts per uL to absolute protein copy numbers. LOD defined as 3 SD above background or y-intercept of fitted linear curve (whichever is higher).

steps.name: Single-cell loading and hydrodynamic trapping
steps.operation: pressure-driven flow-through trap (abstracted as mix in BioScript)

steps.mechanism: Oligonucleotide-tagged antibody pairs bind two distinct epitopes on target protein; proximity (<3-5 nm) enables connector-mediated ligation
steps.notes: Channels I and II flushed with probes for 2 min and 15 min respectively before introduction to Chamber III.

steps.notes: T4 ligase seals nick between probe oligonucleotides when both are bound to same protein molecule, generating a circular DNA PLA product quantified by ddPCR.

steps.name: PLA product retrieval and ddPCR readout

results.TNFR1_HEK293T: All below LOD; TNFR1 not expressed or below detection in HEK293T

steps.name: Duplex protein and mRNA quantification (same single cell)

results.comparison_to_previous_estimates: Significantly higher than previous ~0.1 estimates (Taniguchi 2010, Albayrak 2016)
