description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : OrganoID: A Versatile Deep Learning Platform for Tracking and Analysis of Single-Organoid Dynamics
Source Link  : https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010584
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010584
Journal      : PLoS Computational Biology, 2022, Vol. 18, Issue 11, Article e1010584
Platform     : Organoid culture (Matrigel dome, 24-well plate) + brightfield / PI fluorescence
               timelapse microscopy + OrganoID deep learning image analysis pipeline


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a gemcitabine dose-response experiment on human PDAC (pancreatic ductal
adenocarcinoma) patient-derived organoids, designed to demonstrate OrganoID -- a robust, open-source
deep learning platform for automated pixel-by-pixel organoid detection, identification, and
longitudinal single-organoid tracking in brightfield and phase-contrast microscopy images.

The protocol is divided into four functional phases:
  1. Organoid embedding in Matrigel and pre-treatment equilibration (24 h)
  2. Gemcitabine dose-response treatment (7 conditions: 0, 3, 10, 30, 100, 300, 1000 nM)
     with concurrent PI fluorescence labelling and 72 h brightfield timelapse imaging
  3. OrganoID automated analysis: U-Net inference, Canny edge + watershed identification,
     Munkres Hungarian tracking, per-organoid PI normalisation, and morphological feature
     extraction (circularity, solidity, eccentricity)
  4. MTS endpoint viability assay (gold standard EC50 benchmark) and morphology QC

OrganoID achieves >95% organoid count agreement and >97% area agreement with manual
segmentation, maintains >89% single-organoid tracking accuracy over 92 h, and resolves
dose-response EC50 values (via area-normalised PI fluorescence: 24.45 nM) that closely
approach the MTS gold standard (26.13 nM), without fluorescent cell labelling.


DEVICE / PLATFORM ARCHITECTURE
--------------------------------
Culture format    : 24-well plate; 40 uL Matrigel domes per well; 500 uL media overlay.
Matrix            : Matrigel (Corning, growth factor reduced); ice-cold resuspension;
                    polymerisation at 37 C for 20 min before media overlay.
Complete media    : Advanced DMEM/F12 + 10% FBS + EGF + Noggin + R-spondin1 + Wnt3a.
Microscope        : Inverted brightfield / fluorescence microscope.
Imaging channels  : Brightfield (organoid morphology); PI fluorescence (ex 488 nm / em 617 nm).
Imaging interval  : Every 4 h over 72 h (18 frames per well per condition).
Image resolution  : 512x512 pixels (auto-resized by OrganoID pre-processing).


ORGANOID SOURCE
---------------
Cell type    : Human PDAC patient-derived organoids (two patients).
Passage      : 3-8.
Density      : ~500 organoids/mL in ice-cold Matrigel.
Pre-culture  : 24 h equilibration at 37 C / 5% CO2 in complete media before drug addition.


REAGENTS
--------
Drug           : Gemcitabine (dFdC); FDA-approved nucleoside analogue; inhibits
                 ribonucleotide reductase and DNA/RNA synthesis; 10 mM DMSO stock.
Concentrations : 0 (DMSO vehicle), 3, 10, 30, 100, 300, 1000 nM; n=6 replicates/condition.
Vehicle        : DMSO at 0.1% v/v final (matched across all conditions).
Viability stain: Propidium iodide (PI); 1 ug/mL; added at time of drug treatment;
                 labels dead/necrotic cells; continuous labelling throughout imaging.
                 Excitation 488 nm / emission 617 nm.
MTS reagent    : (3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-5-(3-carboxymethoxyphenyl)-2-(4-sulfophenyl)-
                 2H-tetrazolium); readout at 490 nm; run on fresh organoid aliquot at endpoint;
                 4 h incubation at 37 C.


ORGANOID ID PIPELINE
--------------------
Language           : Python.
Neural network     : Keras (TensorFlow backend); modified U-Net architecture.
Filters (layer 1)  : 8 (vs 64 in original U-Net; 98% parameter reduction).
Trainable params   : <500,000.
Activation (hidden): ELU (exponential linear unit; avoids vanishing gradient problems).
Activation (output): Sigmoid (normalised organoid probability per pixel).
Preprocessing      : Auto-contrast and resize to 512x512 pixels.

Training:
  Dataset        : 66 manually labelled brightfield / phase-contrast images (PDAC, 2 patients).
  Split          : 52 training pairs / 14 validation pairs.
  Augmentation   : Augmentor package (rotation, zoom, elastic distortion, shear); 2000 images.
  Optimizer      : Adam (learning rate 0.001).
  Loss           : Unweighted binary cross-entropy.
  Weight init    : He method.
  Dropout        : 12.5% neuron weights zeroed after each batch.
  Batch size     : 8 augmented images per backpropagation round.
  Early stopping : Halt once 10 epochs pass with no improvement in validation loss.
  Convergence    : 37 epochs; validation cross-entropy loss minimum 0.088 at 8 filters.

Identification pipeline (single-organoid resolution):
  Step 1: Threshold detection image at 0.5; morphological opening to remove noise.
  Step 2: Canny edge detection on raw network prediction image
          (Sobel filter; Gaussian sigma=2; Thi=0.05, Tlo=0.005).
  Step 3: Remove Canny edges from thresholded image to mark organoid centres.
  Step 4: Watershed transform (centres as basin initialisers; prediction image as
          inverted heightmap). Libraries: scipy, scikit-image.
  Step 5: Discard detections with total area < 200 pixels.

Tracking module:
  Algorithm     : Munkres variant of the Hungarian algorithm.
  Cost function : Inverse of shared pixel count between consecutive detections.
  Pseudo-assign : Extra matrix rows/columns for missing or newly appearing organoids.
  Accuracy      : >89% (fraction of organoids correctly matched at each frame) over 92 h.
  Robustness    : Accuracy unaffected when frames discarded to simulate 12 h interval.

Performance (test dataset):
  PDAC IOU (mean +/- SD)         : 0.74 +/- 0.081 (benchmark >= 0.5)
  ACC  IOU                       : 0.78 +/- 0.09
  Colon IOU                      : 0.72 +/- 0.08
  Lung  IOU                      : 0.87 +/- 0.04
  Mouse small intestine IOU      : 0.70 +/- 0.15
  Organoid count CCC             : 0.95 (95% CI 0.89-0.98)
  Organoid area CCC              : 0.97 (95% CI 0.96-0.97)
  False positive rate (bubbles)  : 4.2%
  Segmentation speed             : ~300 ms per image (Intel i7-9750H 2.6GHz, <200 MB RAM)


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Organoid Embedding in Matrigel
  Reagents    : PDAC organoids (~500/mL), Matrigel (ice-cold, growth factor reduced)
  Operation   : Resuspend organoids in ice-cold Matrigel; seed 40 uL domes per well
  Gelation    : 37 C for 20 min (heat at 37 C for 20 min in BioScript)
  Purpose     : Creates 3D extracellular environment recapitulating in situ tumour matrix.
                mix abstracts the resuspension and dome-seeding step (no DMF mixing).

Step 2 | Media Overlay and Pre-Treatment Equilibration
  Reagents    : Complete media (500 uL per well)
  Operation   : Overlay after Matrigel gelation; equilibrate at 37 C / 5% CO2 for 24 h
  Duration    : 24 h = 1440 min (heat at 37 C for 1440 min in BioScript)
  Purpose     : Allows organoids to adapt to culture conditions before drug challenge.

Step 3 | Vehicle Control Treatment (0 nM Gemcitabine)
  Reagents    : CompleteMedia, DMSO vehicle (0.1% v/v final), PropidiumIodide (1 ug/mL)
  Operation   : Mix drug/vehicle into media; add PI; image at 37 C every 4 h for 72 h
  Duration    : 72 h = 4320 min (heat at 37 C for 4320 min in BioScript)
  Detection   : organoidDetection module; 30 s
  QC branch   : controlSignal > 0 → dispose (organoids detected, growing normally; experiment valid)
                controlSignal <= 0 → drain (no organoids in control; experiment setup failure)
  Notes       : heat + organoidDetection together abstract the full 18-frame timelapse run
                with concurrent OrganoID U-Net inference and tracking.

Step 4 | 3 nM Gemcitabine Treatment
  Reagents    : CompleteMedia, Gemcitabine_3nM, PropidiumIodide
  Duration    : 72 h = 4320 min
  QC branch   : signal3nM > 0 → dispose; signal3nM <= 0 → drain
  Notes       : Lowest dose; minimal effect on area or count (Fig 3B).

Step 5 | 10 nM Gemcitabine Treatment
  Reagents    : CompleteMedia, Gemcitabine_10nM, PropidiumIodide
  Duration    : 72 h = 4320 min
  QC branch   : signal10nM > 0 → dispose; signal10nM <= 0 → drain
  Notes       : Organoid count begins to fall sharply above 10 nM (Fig 3B bottom).

Step 6 | 30 nM Gemcitabine Treatment
  Reagents    : CompleteMedia, Gemcitabine_30nM, PropidiumIodide
  Duration    : 72 h = 4320 min
  QC branch   : signal30nM > 0 → dispose; signal30nM <= 0 → drain
  Notes       : Clearest representative dose in paper (Fig 3A): organoid area initially
                rises (early growth) then falls; count drops; PI fluorescence rises
                proportionally to concentration.

Step 7 | 100 nM Gemcitabine Treatment
  Reagents    : CompleteMedia, Gemcitabine_100nM, PropidiumIodide
  Duration    : 72 h = 4320 min
  QC branch   : signal100nM > 0 → dispose; signal100nM <= 0 → drain
  Notes       : Without area normalisation, total PI at 100 nM paradoxically exceeds
                1000 nM signal (Fig 3C top). OrganoID per-organoid area normalisation
                corrects this discrepancy (Fig 3C bottom), aligning responses correctly.

Step 8 | 300 nM Gemcitabine Treatment
  Reagents    : CompleteMedia, Gemcitabine_300nM, PropidiumIodide
  Duration    : 72 h = 4320 min
  QC branch   : signal300nM > 0 → dispose; signal300nM <= 0 → drain

Step 9 | 1000 nM Gemcitabine Treatment
  Reagents    : CompleteMedia, Gemcitabine_1000nM, PropidiumIodide
  Duration    : 72 h = 4320 min
  QC branch   : signal1000nM > 0 → dispose; signal1000nM <= 0 → drain
  Notes       : Highest dose. Essentially all organoids killed by 48 h. Circularity and
                solidity decrease markedly; eccentricity increases, reflecting disrupted
                organoid architecture (moderate-to-large Cohen d effect sizes; Fig 3E).
                Gemcitabine interference with RNA/DNA synthesis (ref 40) likely disrupts
                cell turnover and structural protein production.

Step 10 | MTS Endpoint Viability Assay (Gold Standard)
  Reagents    : Fresh PDAC organoids, MatrigelMatrix, CompleteMedia, MTS reagent
  Operation   : Re-embed fresh organoid aliquot; overlay media; incubate MTS 4 h at 37 C
  Duration    : Gelation 20 min + MTS incubation 4 h = 240 min (heat at 37 C for 240 min)
  Detection   : mtsViabilityDetection module (490 nm absorbance); 30 s
  QC branch   : mtsSignal > 0 → dispose (valid formazan signal; proceed to morphology)
                mtsSignal <= 0 → drain (MTS failure; reagent or instrument issue)
  Result      : MTS EC50 = 26.13 nM (Fig 3D; gold-standard reference)
  Notes       : Run on fresh organoid aliquot, not timelapse wells. Off-device 4-parameter
                logistic dose-response curve fitting determines EC50 per readout type.

Step 11 | Single-Organoid Morphology Analysis
  Reagents    : Fresh PDAC organoids, MatrigelMatrix, CompleteMedia
  Operation   : Re-embed; overlay media; detect morphological features on reference well
  Detection   : morphologyAnalysis module; 60 s
  QC branch   : morphologySignal > 0 → dispose (metrics computed; pipeline operational)
                morphologySignal <= 0 → drain (segmentation returned no organoids; pipeline failure)
  Metrics computed (scikit-image regionprops on OrganoID labeled masks):
    Circularity  : Inverse ratio of organoid perimeter to perimeter of perfect circle
                   with equal area. Decreases with gemcitabine dose. EC50 = 28.47 nM.
    Solidity     : Ratio of organoid area to convex hull area.
                   Decreases with gemcitabine dose. EC50 = 27.05 nM.
    Eccentricity : Elliptical deviation from a perfect circle.
                   Increases with gemcitabine dose. EC50 = 18.08 nM.
    Effect size  : Cohen's d statistic (difference in means / pooled SD) computed across
                   all pairwise concentration combinations (Fig 3E heatmap).
  Normalisation: Tracking-based per-organoid normalisation (each organoid normalised to
                 its own first-detection value) significantly reduces CV vs batch
                 normalisation: fluorescence (p=2e-30), area (p=2e-29),
                 perimeter (p=2e-63) -- Welch t-test (Fig S6).


DOSE-RESPONSE SUMMARY
---------------------
  Readout                        EC50 (nM)   Notes
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------
  MTS viability (gold standard)  26.13       Off-chip endpoint assay; reference
  Organoid area (OrganoID)       12.67       Underestimates; no death-size correction
  Total PI fluorescence          16.95       Underestimates; not normalised to organoid size
  Area-normalised PI (OrganoID)  24.45       Closest to MTS; per-organoid tracking normalisation
  Circularity (OrganoID)         28.47       Morphological; sigmoidal dose-response (Fig S7)
  Solidity (OrganoID)            27.05       Morphological; sigmoidal dose-response (Fig S7)
  Eccentricity (OrganoID)        18.08       Morphological; sigmoidal dose-response (Fig S7)


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : matthews_organoid_organoid_id.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 28 basic blocks (BB1-BB28), 11 if/else gates, 36 CFG edges
DAG            : matthews_organoid_organoid_id_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations converted to minutes (m) for compiler compatibility
                 (BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported)
                 72 h  -> 4320 m  (timelapse imaging; IR: 259200.0 SECOND)
                 24 h  -> 1440 m  (equilibration; IR: 86400.0 SECOND)
                 20 min -> 20 m   (Matrigel gelation; IR: 1200.0 SECOND)
                  4 h  -> 240 m   (MTS incubation; IR: 14400.0 SECOND)
Modules        : organoidDetection, propidiumIodideDetection,
                 mtsViabilityDetection, morphologyAnalysis
Biological scope note:
  cultureDomes is the shared embedded organoid droplet used across all 7 treatment
  condition arms. Each treatment arm re-uses cultureDomes as the mix input, reflecting
  the single-batch organoid preparation described in the paper. MTS and morphology
  QC steps use independently dispensed fresh organoid aliquots (mtsOrganoids,
  morphOrganoids) to avoid contaminating the timelapse wells.
Timelapse abstraction note:
  BioScript does not support loop constructs. The 72 h timelapse (18 frames at 4 h
  intervals) is abstracted as a single heat at 37 C for 4320 m per condition arm.
  The organoidDetection module abstracts the full OrganoID pipeline run post-incubation:
  U-Net inference on all frames, Canny + watershed single-organoid identification,
  and Munkres Hungarian tracking across frames.

steps.notes: heat at 37 C for 4320 min abstracts 72 h timelapse imaging (18 frames, every 4 h). organoidDetection abstracts U-Net inference, Canny edge + watershed identification, and Munkres tracking across all 18 frames.

steps.name: 3 nM gemcitabine treatment
steps.notes: Lowest dose; paper (Fig 3B) shows minimal effect on area or count at 3 nM.

steps.name: 10 nM gemcitabine treatment
steps.notes: Count begins to fall sharply above 10 nM (Fig 3B bottom).

steps.name: 30 nM gemcitabine treatment
steps.notes: Clearest representative dose in paper (Fig 3A): area initially rises then falls; PI fluorescence rises proportionally.

steps.name: 100 nM gemcitabine treatment
steps.notes: Without area normalisation, total PI fluorescence at 100 nM paradoxically exceeds 1000 nM signal (Fig 3C top). OrganoID per-organoid area normalisation corrects this discrepancy (Fig 3C bottom).

steps.name: 1000 nM gemcitabine treatment
steps.notes: Highest dose. Essentially all organoids killed by 48 h. Circularity and solidity decrease markedly; eccentricity increases (Fig 3E, moderate-to-large Cohen d effect sizes).

steps.name: MTS endpoint viability assay
steps.notes: Run on a fresh organoid aliquot from the same batch (endpoint only, not timelapse wells). MTS EC50 = 26.13 nM used as gold-standard reference (Fig 3D). Organoid area alone underestimates EC50 to 12.67 nM; total PI fluorescence underestimates to 16.95 nM; area-normalised PI fluorescence gives 24.45 nM (closest to MTS standard).

steps.name: Single-organoid morphology analysis

circularity.definition: Inverse ratio of organoid perimeter to perimeter of a perfect circle with equal area

solidity.definition: Ratio of organoid area to its convex hull area

eccentricity.definition: Elliptical deviation from a perfect circle
eccentricity.direction_with_drug: Increases at higher gemcitabine concentrations (disrupted morphology)

metrics.effect_size_metric: Cohen's d statistic (ratio of difference in means to pooled SD)
metrics.effect_sizes: Moderate to large across EC50-crossing concentration pairs (Fig 3E)

steps.notes: morphologyAnalysis abstracts scikit-image regionprops computation on OrganoID-labeled segmentation masks plus Cohen d calculation. Dose-response EC50 values from sigmoidal fits (Fig S7). Tracking-based per-organoid normalisation significantly reduces CV for area and fluorescence (p=2e-30 and p=2e-29 respectively; Welch t-test, Fig S6).

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : A Digital Microfluidic Platform for Human Plasma Protein Depletion
Source Link  : https://collectionscanada.gc.ca/obj/thesescanada/vol2/OKQ/TC-OKQ-12209.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/ac5022198
Journal      : M.Sc. Thesis, Queen's University, Kingston, Ontario, Canada, May 2014
               Supervisors: Dr. Richard D. Oleschuk & Dr. Aaron A. Wheeler
Platform     : Two-plate digital microfluidics (DMF) on glass chip with automated
               motor-controlled magnetic separation and custom Microdrop software


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes an automated DMF-based method for depleting high-abundance
human plasma proteins -- human serum albumin (HSA) and immunoglobulin G (IgG) --
which together constitute approximately 80% of total plasma protein content and severely
mask low-abundance analytes in proteomic studies. The approach uses paramagnetic beads
functionalized with Protein A/G (for IgG capture) and anti-HSA (for HSA capture),
actuated and mixed on a two-plate glass DMF device under an automated controller system.

The protocol depletes IgG and HSA simultaneously with up to 98% efficiency in 10 minutes
across four samples processed in parallel. Depleted samples show an approximately 3-fold
increase in MALDI-MS signal-to-noise ratio and are compatible with downstream LC-MS/MS
proteomic analysis. Successful tryptic in-solution digestion of cytochrome C from depleted
samples yielded 89% sequence coverage (11 peptides, MALDI score 225).

The protocol consists of two encoded phases:
  1. Core on-chip protein depletion: eight-step bead-based immunocapture workflow
  2. Fluorescence kinetics characterisation: FITC-IgG and FITC-HSA depletion efficiency
     probed at 30-second intervals over 10 minutes total using a PHERAstar plate reader


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Format     : Two-plate glass DMF chip
Fabrication: University of Toronto Nanofabrication Centre (TNFC) clean room
Bottom plate: Patterned electrode array on glass
Top plate   : ITO-coated glass (ground plate)
Coatings    : Parylene-C dielectric (vapor deposition) + Teflon-AF hydrophobic layer (spin-coat)

Actuation   : 100-120 V_rms, 10 kHz sine wave
Droplet vol : 4 uL unit droplets; four droplets merged per depletion run
Incubation  : Figure-8 pattern across 4 electrodes for continuous droplet/bead mixing

Magnetic separation:
  Motor-controlled magnetic lens assembly (~600 uN force; minimum threshold 470 uN)
  Magnet position automated via custom Microdrop software + Pogo-pin interface
  Microcapture USB camera for real-time video monitoring

Controller system: National Instruments PXI chassis (MIP), custom Microdrop software
                   NI PXI-4130 (DC power), NI PXI-5422 (AC function generator)


REAGENTS
--------
Plasma proteins:
  HSA          : 0.5 mg/mL in PBS (66,437 Da; lyophilized, Life Technologies)
  IgG          : 2.0 mg/mL in PBS (150,000 Da; diluted from 4.7 mg/mL stock)
  FITC-IgG     : 0.5 mg/mL (GenScript USA Inc., Piscataway, NJ) -- kinetics only
  FITC-HSA     : 1.0 mg/mL (Abcam, Cambridge, MA) -- kinetics only
  Hemopexin    : 0.1 mg/mL in PBS (57,000 Da; low-abundance marker)

Paramagnetic beads (Millipore, Billerica, MA; 10 um diameter):
  Protein A/G Beads : PureProteome Protein A/G Mix Magnetic Beads (LSKMAGAG02)
                      Diluted 1:4 from stock in PBS; captures IgG
  Anti-HSA Beads    : PureProteome Albumin Magnetic Beads (LSKMAGL02)
                      Diluted 1:2 from stock in PBS; captures HSA

Buffer      : Phosphate-buffered saline (PBS)
Surfactant  : Pluronic F-68 at 0.05% in PBS
              Selection rationale: Pluronic F-127 and L64 inhibited Protein A/G bead
              binding (Chapter 3 screening). Pluronics L92, F68, and F88 did not interfere
              with binding; F-68 produced optimal droplet movement on DMF chip.

Waste removal: KimWipes (Kimberly-Clark) wicking from device surface


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Reagent Preparation and Device Loading
  Reagents  : ProteinAG_Beads, AntiHSA_Beads, PlasmaProteinSample, PBS_Buffer, PluronicF68
  Operation : Off-chip bead dilution; pipette-load into device reservoirs
  Notes     : Bead types combined into single mixed-bead suspension on-chip (5s mix).
              Protein sample (IgG + HSA + hemopexin + 0.05% F-68 in PBS) prepared fresh.
              4 uL droplets. Four samples processed simultaneously in parallel.

Step 2 | Bead Actuation onto Device Array
  Reagents  : mixedBeads, PBS_Buffer
  Operation : DMF electrode actuation (100-120 V_rms, 10 kHz)
  Notes     : Mixed bead droplet moved from reservoir into active array. Beads remain
              suspended during electrode-to-electrode transfer.

Step 3 | First Magnet Engagement -- Bead Immobilization
  Operation : heat at 25c for 30s (BioScript abstraction for magnet dwell)
  Duration  : 30 s
  Notes     : Motor-controlled magnet (~600 uN) lowered below chip. Paramagnetic beads
              pelleted onto device surface. heat at 25c is a BioScript-level abstraction
              for the immobilization dwell; no actual thermal step occurs.

Step 4 | Supernatant Removal and PBS Wash
  Reagents  : PBS_Buffer
  Operation : mix beadDroplet + washBuffer for 5s; heat at 25c for 30s
  Notes     : Bead storage buffer actuated to waste and wicked off with KimWipes. PBS
              wash droplet added; magnet re-engaged (30s) to re-pellet beads before
              sample merging.

Step 5 | Protein Sample Merge with Bead Pellet
  Reagents  : beadWash1, samplePlusMix
  Operation : mix for 10s
  Notes     : Sample droplet actuated over immobilized beads; magnet disengaged to
              resuspend beads into protein sample. Merged droplet contains IgG, HSA,
              hemopexin, 0.05% F-68, Protein A/G beads, and anti-HSA beads.

Step 6 | Active Incubation -- Figure-8 Mixing
  Operation : heat at 37c for 10m
  Temperature: 37 C
  Duration  : 10 min (600 s)
  Pattern   : Figure-8 across 4 electrodes; 100-120 V_rms, 10 kHz
  Results   : IgG depletion efficiency up to 98%; HSA depletion efficiency up to 98%
              (FITC-labeled fluorescence assay, N=3-4 per condition)
  Notes     : Continuous movement maximizes bead-protein contact. All four samples
              run concurrently on the same device.

Step 7 | Bead Re-Immobilization and Supernatant Separation
  Operation : heat at 25c for 30s
  Duration  : 30 s
  Notes     : Magnet re-engaged; beads (now carrying captured IgG and HSA) pelleted.
              Depleted supernatant (containing retained hemopexin) actuated to
              collection reservoir by DMF electrode switching.

Step 8 | Depleted Sample Collection and Depletion QC
  Reagents  : PBS_Buffer
  Operation : mix for 5s; detect depletionQC for 30s
  Detection : depletionQC module (30 s)
  Downstream: MALDI-MS or LC-MS/MS analysis (top plate removed; droplet pipetted off-chip)
  Branch    :
    Pass (depletionSignal > 0) : dispose depletedSample  [BB2]
    Fail (depletionSignal <= 0): drain depletedSample     [BB3]

Step 9 | Fluorescence Kinetics Characterisation (FITC-IgG; BB4 join)
  Reagents  : FITC_IgG (0.5 mg/mL), ProteinAG_Beads, PBS_Buffer
  Operation : mix + 30s heat (immobilization) x N + detect fluorescenceDetection for 30s
  Instrument: PHERAstar microplate reader (BMG Labtech, Ortenberg, Germany)
              Mode: well scanning (COSTAR 96-well geometry); 3 flashes/point; gain 100
              Excitation 485 nm / Emission 520 nm
  Protocol  : Steps 1-5 applied to FITC-IgG; incubate 30 s; extract supernatant; measure
              fluorescence; re-suspend beads; repeat to 10 min total (20 x 30s intervals)
              Replicates: N = 3 per time point
  HSA variant: FITC-HSA (0.5 mg/mL, gain 125) with anti-HSA beads; identical procedure
  BioScript note: Loop absent in compiler; 20 x 30s intervals abstracted as one
              representative 30s heat + detect step. Full iterative kinetics run off-chip.
  Branch    :
    Pass (fluorescenceSignal > 0) : dispose kineticsSupern  [BB5]
    Fail (fluorescenceSignal <= 0): drain kineticsSupern     [BB6]
  Terminal  : dispose fluorescenceSignal; NOP              [BB7]


MALDI-MS ANALYSIS
-----------------
Instrument    : PerSeptive Biosystems Voyager DE Pro MALDI-TOF (AB Sciex, Framingham, MA)
m/z range     : 20,000 - 200,000
Shots         : 250 per spectrum; laser power adjusted for S/N
Data processing: Baseline correction, resolution 100, smoothing (Voyager Data Explorer)
Calibrant     : BSA (66.5 kDa, Mann Research Laboratories, Port Saint Lucie, FL)

Matrix:
  Protein depletion : Sinapinic acid (SA); 10 mg SA in 1 mL 50% ACN / 0.1% TFA
  Tryptic digests   : alpha-CHCA; 10 mg in 1 mL 50:50 ACN:H2O / 0.1% TFA
  Calibrant (digest): Synthetic 4-peptide mix (Angiotensin I, Glu-fibrinogen, Renin, ACTH)

Sample preparation:
  Acidification : 2% TFA added to protein solution (3:1 protein:TFA)
  Spotting      : 0.5 uL matrix pre-spotted and dried; 1:1 matrix:acidified protein overlay
  Target        : Stainless steel 100-spot MALDI target plate; air-dried in dark

ZipTip cleanup (Millipore, Etobicoke, ON):
  C4  : Intact protein samples
  C18 : Tryptic digests
  Protocol: Wet in 50% ACN/0.1% TFA (x5); equilibrate in 0.1% TFA (x5);
            bind 20 cycles; wash 0.1% TFA (x3); elute in SA or alpha-CHCA matrix

Protein mixture tested: 2 mg/mL IgG + 0.5 mg/mL HSA + 0.1 mg/mL hemopexin
Depletion rounds : 0 (pre-depletion control), 1, 2 (two sequential bead aliquots)
Replicates       : 4 per condition
S/N improvement  : Approximately 3-fold after depletion


LC-MS/MS PROTEOMIC ANALYSIS
----------------------------
Model protein : Cytochrome C (tryptic in-solution digest)
Trypsin       : Sequencing grade modified (Promega, Madison, WI)
Digest        : 12 h at 37 C; quenched with 5% formic acid
Results       : 89% sequence coverage, 11 peptides matched, MALDI score 225


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : mei_dmf_plasma_protein_depletion.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG            : mei_dmf_plasma_protein_depletion_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations in s or m (BioScript supports s and m only; h not supported)
                 10 min incubation -> 10m (IR: 600.0 SECOND)
                 Magnet dwell     -> 30s (IR: 30.0 SECOND)
Modules        : depletionQC, fluorescenceDetection
drain note     : drain normalises to dispose in IR -- expected compiler behaviour, not a bug
heat note      : heat at 25c used as BioScript abstraction for magnet-engagement dwell steps;
                 no actual thermal actuation occurs at these steps in the physical protocol
loop note      : BioScript has no loop construct; 20 x 30s fluorescence kinetics intervals
                 abstracted as a single representative 30s heat + detect step

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Accurate Processing of Ultra-Short Immune Signals by Single Macrophages
Source Link  : https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.10.26.684377v1.full.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.10.26.684377
Journal      : bioRxiv preprint, posted October 26, 2025
Platform     : Multilayer PDMS microfluidic live-cell stimulation device with pneumatic valve control


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol investigates the temporal limits of immune signal detection by individual primary
macrophages. Primary bone-marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) from mVenus-RelA (RelA^V/V)
C57BL/6J transgenic mice -- which express an endogenously tagged fluorescent NF-kB p65/RelA
reporter -- are isolated, differentiated, and seeded into multilayer PDMS microfluidic culture
chambers. The cells are then exposed to ultra-short (1-second) chemical pulses of five NF-kB
ligands covering cytokine and pathogen-derived signaling modalities: TNF alpha, Lipid A,
Pam2CSK4, R848 (Resiquimod), and CpG ODN 1668. NF-kB nuclear translocation dynamics of
the mVenus-RelA reporter are tracked by time-lapse epifluorescence microscopy over 6 hours
at single-cell resolution.

Key findings encoded in this protocol:
  - Single macrophages detect and respond to 1-second ligand pulses with high specificity
  - Short-pulse channel capacity (CC_max = 0.82) is comparable to persistent stimulation
    (CC_max = 0.92), demonstrating robust signal discrimination at the 1-second timescale
  - Three macrophage subpopulations emerge: early responders, late responders, non-responders
  - Pam2CSK4 produces the strongest response under 1-second pulse; Lipid A is most potent
    only under persistent stimulation -- stimulus duration alters the ranking of ligand potency
  - Macrophages employ two sensing modes: sensitivity to cytokine duration (TNF) vs. pathogen
    amplitude/dose (Pam2CSK4, R848)
  - Mathematical modeling identifies Hill coefficient (receptor cooperativity) as the primary
    determinant of the three NF-kB activation modes


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Microfluidic chip: Multilayer PDMS fabricated from silicon wafer master molds (10:1 PDMS
monomer:catalyst, Momentive). Control layer and fluid layer spin-coated separately, bonded
by oxygen plasma, overnight-baked. Control and flow inlets punched; glass-bonded.

Flow control:
  - Pneumatic valves electronically controlled via custom MATLAB GUI
  - PEEK tubing (VICI) at 4 psi input pressure
  - Pulse timing CV = 0.06 (6% variability across all analyzed cells)
  - Pulse as short as 1 second reliably delivered to live cells

Environmental control:
  - In-situ microbiome box maintains 37 C, humidity, and CO2 throughout imaging
  - Cells exhibit no photobleaching or phototoxicity under 6-hour imaging protocol


MOUSE MODEL
-----------
Strain     : mVenus-RelA (RelA^V/V) C57BL/6J
Reporter   : mVenus fluorescently tagged p65/RelA NF-kB subunit (endogenous knock-in)
Age/Sex    : 6-12 weeks; male and female
Housing    : Specific pathogen-free, University of Chicago Animal Resources Center
Ethics     : NIH Guide for Care and Use of Laboratory Animals; University of Chicago IACUC
Gift from  : Alex Hoffmann laboratory


REAGENTS
--------
m-CSF                 : Murine m-CSF (Peprotech); reconstituted in ultrapure water;
                        aliquoted and stored at -80 C; 20 ng/mL in complete RPMI
Cell culture media    : Complete phenol red-free RPMI (Gibco)
Fibronectin           : 0.2 mg/mL fibronectin solution (Sigma-Aldrich) in PBS
Nuclear stain         : Hoechst 33342 (Invitrogen), 1 uM in phenol red-free RPMI
Ligands (all stored at -80 C; thawed on ice and diluted in complete RPMI before use):
  TNF alpha           : Murine TNFalpha (R&D Systems),     10 ng/mL
  Lipid A             : Ultrapure Lipid A from E. coli O111:B4 (Invivogen), 10 ng/mL
  Pam2CSK4           : PAM2CSK4 (Invivogen),               3 ng/mL
  R848 Resiquimod     : R848 Resiquimod (Invivogen),       300 ng/mL
  CpG ODN 1668        : ODN 1668 (Invivogen),              300 nM


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | BMDM Isolation and Differentiation
  Tissue source  : Tibias and femurs of 6-12-week-old male and female RelA^V/V C57BL/6J mice
  Isolation      : Bone marrow cells flushed and resuspended in complete RPMI supplemented
                   with 20 ng/mL murine m-CSF (Peprotech)
  Differentiation: 7-9 days at 37 C / 5% CO2 (encoded as 9 days = 12960 min = 777600 s)
  Harvest        : BMDMs harvested on days 7-9; loaded into microfluidic culture chips
  Reference      : Wang et al., Cell Syst 2025 (PMID protocol source)

Step 2 | Microfluidic Device Fibronectin Priming
  Reagents       : 0.2 mg/mL fibronectin (Sigma-Aldrich) in PBS
  Duration       : 5 min (encoded as 300 s)
  Purpose        : Pre-incubation of PDMS culture chambers to promote BMDM adhesion
  Notes          : mix abstracts the channel-flow fibronectin coating step

Step 3 | BMDM Seeding and Equilibration
  Density        : 10^6 cells/mL in complete phenol red-free RPMI
  Duration       : 4-6 h undisturbed (encoded as 6 h = 360 min = 21600 s at 37 C)
  Purpose        : Cells attach and equilibrate in microfluidic chambers before stimulation

Step 4 | Nuclear Tracking Stain
  Reagent        : 1 uM Hoechst 33342 (Invitrogen) in phenol red-free RPMI
  Duration       : ~5 min (per producer instructions)
  Purpose        : Enables nuclear segmentation (395 nm channel) and single-cell tracking
                   throughout the 6-hour time-lapse imaging run

Step 5a | TNF Alpha 1-Second Pulse Stimulation
  Ligand         : Murine TNFalpha (R&D Systems), 10 ng/mL
  Pulse duration : 1 second via pneumatic valve at 4 psi (PEEK tubing, VICI)
  Receptor       : TNFR1 (CD120a); cytokine intercellular signaling pathway
  Key result     : Weakest response under 1-second pulse; non-monotonic dose-duration
                   relationship; 100-second pulse doubles NF-kB amplitude vs 1-second pulse;
                   macrophages respond to cytokine duration, not amplitude

Step 5b | Lipid A 1-Second Pulse Stimulation
  Ligand         : Ultrapure Lipid A from E. coli O111:B4 (Invivogen), 10 ng/mL
  Pulse duration : 1 second via pneumatic valve at 4 psi
  Receptor       : TLR4; extracellular bacterial PAMP sensing
  Key result     : Largest late responder fraction (~30%); longest time to peak (>50 min);
                   most potent ligand under persistent stimulation but not under 1-second pulse;
                   reversal of potency ranking demonstrates duration-dependent ligand identity

Step 5c | Pam2CSK4 1-Second Pulse Stimulation
  Ligand         : PAM2CSK4 (Invivogen), 3 ng/mL
  Pulse duration : 1 second via pneumatic valve at 4 psi
  Receptor       : TLR2/TLR6 heterodimer; bacterial lipopeptide sensing via MyD88/TIRAP
  Key result     : Strongest response under 1-second pulse (highest early AUC, amplitude,
                   speed, duration); lowest late responder fraction (~3%); CC_max = 0.82;
                   Pam-vs-control MI with features = 0.87; used as QC reference condition

Step 5d | R848 (Resiquimod) 1-Second Pulse Stimulation
  Ligand         : R848 Resiquimod (Invivogen), 300 ng/mL
  Pulse duration : 1 second via pneumatic valve at 4 psi
  Receptor       : TLR7 (endosomal); viral RNA mimic sensing via MyD88
  Key result     : All-or-nothing activation dynamic (similar to fibroblast/cancer cells);
                   largest channel capacity under dose-duration tradeoff; lower dose (longer
                   pulse) elicits minimal to null response; strong dose (short pulse) gives
                   robust activation

Step 5e | CpG ODN 1668 1-Second Pulse Stimulation
  Ligand         : ODN 1668 CpG (Invivogen), 300 nM
  Pulse duration : 1 second via pneumatic valve at 4 psi
  Receptor       : TLR9 (endosomal); foreign/pathogenic DNA sensing
  Key result     : CpG and TNF induce highest oscillatory frequencies under short pulses;
                   pairwise mutual information CpG vs TNF = 0 at 1-second pulse (cells
                   cannot distinguish these two ligands at 1-second duration)

Step 6 | Time-Lapse NF-kB Live-Cell Imaging and QC Detection
  Microscope     : Nikon Ti2 epifluorescence; 20x magnification
  Camera         : Hamamatsu ORCA-Flash4.0 V2
  Channels       : mVenus-RelA (508 nm, NF-kB nuclear translocation); Hoechst (395 nm, nuclei)
  Frame interval : 6 minutes
  Total duration : 6 hours = 360 min = 21600 s (encoded as heat 37 C + detect 360 min)
  Cells per cond : >200 individual cells analyzed per stimulation condition
  Activation threshold: 2 standard deviations above mean nuclear/cytoplasmic ratio of
                   unstimulated cells; first passage time defines activation time
  Analysis software: Custom MATLAB 2024a; nuclear segmentation via Hoechst images;
                   nuclear/cytoplasmic mVenus-RelA ratio per cell per frame; dead cells,
                   dividing cells, and out-of-focus cells removed (>99% tracking accuracy)
  QC module      : nfkbTranslocationDetection; positive signal (nfkbSignal > 0) confirms
                   NF-kB nuclear translocation above threshold in at least one cell

  Branch pass    : nfkbSignal > 0 -> dispose(imagingPool_all)   [BB2]
  Branch fail    : nfkbSignal <= 0 -> drain(imagingPool_all)    [BB3]
  Terminal       : dispose(nfkbSignal); experiment ends          [BB4]


SINGLE-CELL SUBPOPULATION ANALYSIS
-----------------------------------
Method         : k-means clustering (MATLAB; 10 random centroid replicates; Euclidean distance)
                 applied to activation time and amplitude from all NF-kB traces
Subpopulations :
  Early Responders (ER)  -- fast response < 25 min, high amplitude
  Late Responders (LR)   -- response onset > 20 min, low amplitude
  Non-Responders (NR)    -- never exceed activation threshold
Late responder fractions:
  Pam2CSK4    ~3%  (lowest; predominantly early responders)
  Lipid A     ~30% (highest; cells activate up to 1 hour post-stimulation)
  TNF         intermediate; non-responder fraction dominates at low doses
  R848        switch from early responders to non-responders as dose decreases
  CpG         intermediate; broader activation time range than TNF or R848
Paracrine check: No correlation between late responder activation time and distance to
                 nearest early responder (r^2 ~ 0); late response is cell-intrinsic


INFORMATION THEORY ANALYSIS
----------------------------
Mutual Information (MI): Quantifies NF-kB trace distinguishability between two ligands
  (1 bit = perfect distinguishability; 0 = indistinguishable)
Channel Capacity (CC_max, 1-second pulse): 0.82 bits at ~21 min
  Comparison to persistent stimulation CC_max: 0.92 bits
  Conclusion: short-pulse specificity nearly equivalent to persistent stimulation
Pairwise MI highlights:
  Highest: Pam2CSK4 vs TNF
  Lowest:  CpG vs TNF (MI = 0; indistinguishable at 1-second)
  Pam2CSK4 vs control (with dynamic features): MI = 0.87 (near-perfect distinguishability)
Most informative dynamic features: Early AUC, amplitude at t_max, activation speed, duration


MATHEMATICAL MODEL SUMMARY
---------------------------
Type         : Minimal ODE model; ligand-receptor interaction + NF-kB signal transduction
               downstream IKK module; Hill function summarizes upstream IKK interactions
Receptor pathways fit: TNFR (TNFalpha), TLR2 (Pam2CSK4), TLR7 (R848)
Three activation modes predicted:
  m1: Monotonic increase  -- NF-kB amplitude increases with pulse duration (high activation rate)
  m2: Non-monotonic       -- intermediate; peak varies non-monotonically with duration
  m3: Monotonic decrease  -- NF-kB amplitude decreases with pulse duration (high-dose filter)
Key predictor: Hill coefficient n (cooperativity); highest MRMR importance score
  TNFR: n = 1.21 (low cooperativity; border between m1 and m2)
  TLR2: n = 1.83 (moderate cooperativity; m2/m3 boundary)
  TLR7: n = 10   (very high cooperativity; operates as high-dose filter; m3)
Noise sources:
  Extrinsic: receptor expression variability (Gamma-distributed)
    TNFR: Gamma(4.32, 1035); TLR2: Gamma(2.23, 4914); TLR7: Gamma(4.80, 4404)
  Intrinsic: stochastic kinetic rate fluctuations
    TNF -> kc variability; Pam -> Hill coefficient n variability; R848 -> K variability


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : mercadovasquez_ultrashort_macrophage_nfkb.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 4 basic blocks (BB1-BB4), 1 if/else gate, 4 CFG edges
DAG file       : mercadovasquez_ultrashort_macrophage_nfkb_main_dag.dot
Module         : nfkbTranslocationDetection

Duration conversions (BioScript s and m tokens only; no h):
  9 days differentiation  -> 12960m -> 777600.0 SECOND in IR
  6 h attachment          -> 360m   -> 21600.0 SECOND in IR
  6 h imaging             -> 360m   -> 21600.0 SECOND in IR
  5 min fibronectin prime -> 5m     -> 300.0 SECOND in IR
  1 min merge steps       -> 1m     -> 60.0 SECOND in IR
  1 sec ligand pulses     -> 1s     -> 1.0 SECOND in IR

Key BioScript constraints observed:
  - Duration tokens s and m only; no h token used
  - No variable reassignment; all intermediate imaging pool merges use distinct names
    (imagingPool_ab, imagingPool_abc, imagingPool_abcd, imagingPool_all)
  - dispense restricted to declared manifest entries only
  - No loop constructs; five ligand stimulation arms unrolled as sequential independent
    mix calls (compiler does not support iteration)
  - equilibratedBMDMs used as input to five independent mix calls; compiler accepts
    multi-consumer input variables; models parallel microfluidic chamber architecture
  - drain normalises to dispose in IR; expected compiler behavior, not a bug

Scope note:
  Five ligand stimulation conditions run in parallel across separate microfluidic chambers
  in the physical experiment. BioScript sequential encoding abstracts this parallelism.
  The imagingPool_all merge chain (5 sequential mix steps) abstracts the single Nikon Ti2
  field-of-view imaging all five stimulation conditions during the 6-hour time-lapse run.
  The QC detect gate uses Pam2CSK4 as the implicit reference (strongest responder arm).

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : A Digital Microfluidic Approach to Heterogeneous Immunoassays
Source Link  : https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/DMF%20immunoassays%201.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1007/s00216-010-4368-2
Journal      : Analytical and Bioanalytical Chemistry, 2011, Vol. 399, pp. 337-345
Platform     : Digital microfluidics (DMF) on EWOD electrode array


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a heterogeneous sandwich immunoassay for Human IgG implemented
on a digital microfluidic (DMF) device. The digital approach manipulates samples and
reagents as discrete droplets on a 2-D array of electrodes, as opposed to the streams of
fluid used in microchannels. Capture antibody (Fc-specific anti-human IgG) is physisorbed
directly onto the hydrophobic Cytop/ITO top plate of the DMF device, and all incubation
and wash steps are performed via DMF actuation at 75 V_rms, 18 kHz -- eliminating the need
for beads, magnets, BSA blocking, or a carrier oil interface.

The protocol is divided into two phases:
  1. Off-device: capture antibody spot immobilization on the Cytop/ITO top plate
  2. On-device: DMF-actuated antigen incubation, rinse, detection antibody incubation,
     final rinse, and fluorescence plate reader readout

Key advantages over conventional 96-well plate immunoassays:
  - Analysis time reduced from up to 2 days to 2.5 h total
  - Sample and reagent volumes reduced ~100-fold (1 uL vs 100 uL per assay)
  - Waste volumes reduced ~3 orders of magnitude (4 uL vs 3.5 mL per assay)
  - Diffusion-limited kinetics eliminated by active droplet transport
  - BSA blocking step eliminated by Pluronic F-127 additives
  - Dynamic range ~1 order of magnitude (R^2 = 0.9964); reproducibility %RSD < 25%
  - Multiplexed devices (6-10 platforms wired in series) enable parallel replicate assays


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Bottom plate : Patterned chromium electrodes on glass substrate (80 St George St. fabrication
               facility, University of Toronto). Two designs used:
               - Design A: 10 x 1x1 mm actuation electrodes + 2 x 2.5x2.5 mm reservoir electrodes
               - Design B: 20 x 1x1 mm actuation electrodes + 4 x 2.5x2.5 mm reservoir electrodes
               Inter-electrode gap: 40-75 um.
               Coated with 2 um parylene C (vapor deposition, Specialty Coating Systems) +
               130 nm Cytop (2.25% w/w in CT-SOLV180, spin-coated 1000 RPM 60 s,
               post-baked 180 C 15 min).

Top plate    : Unpatterned ITO-coated glass (Delta Technologies Ltd, Stillwater MN).
               Coated with 130 nm Cytop (as above).
               Pre-spotted with capture antibody before device assembly.
               Discarded after each assay; bottom plate reused.

Spacer       : Two pieces of double-sided tape, ~150 um thick.
               Defines the gap between top and bottom plates and sets droplet volume.

Droplet volume : 1 uL (sandwiched between plates ~150 um apart).

Hydrophobic coating note:
  Teflon-AF (50 nm, standard DMF coating) was found too fragile for surface-based assays.
  Antibody spot printing caused flaws and tears in Teflon-AF, preventing DMF actuation.
  Cytop (130 nm) was selected for its greater mechanical ruggedness -- spots can be
  dried and rinsed without causing the hydrophobic layer to delaminate.

Multiplexing : 6 or 10 DMF platforms wired in series on a single device. Homologous
               electrodes bussed together for simultaneous control of replicate assays.
               Devices placed on a multiwell plate for fluorescence measurement.

Actuation    : 75 V_rms, 18 kHz (function generator output amplified); applied manually
               to exposed contact pads on bottom plate surface.
               Monitored by CCD camera on stereomicroscope with fluorescence imaging
               (Olympus Canada, Markham ON).

Detection    : PheraStar multiwell plate reader (BMG Labtech, Durham NC).
               lambda_ex = 485 nm, lambda_em = 520 nm, focal height = 12.1 mm.
               Device remains on multiwell plate throughout assay; inserted into
               plate reader after all DMF steps are complete.


REAGENTS
--------
- Capture antibody : Fc-specific anti-human IgG (goat); Sigma Chemical, Oakville ON
                     0.22-2.2 mg/mL; 250-500 nL per spot
- Detection antibody: Fab-specific FITC-labeled anti-human IgG (goat); Sigma Chemical
                     FITC label: ex 485 nm / em 520 nm
- Antigen           : Human IgG, reagent grade from serum; Sigma Chemical
- Pluronic F-127    : 0.00625% w/v in all standard solutions (0.0113% in diluted serum)
                     Prevents non-specific protein adsorption; enables droplet movement;
                     replaces BSA blocking step used in conventional well-plate methods
- Rinse buffer      : 10 mM sodium phosphate pH 7.4 + 0.00625% Pluronic F-127 in 18 MOhm cm DI water
- BSA               : NOT used on DMF device; Pluronic F-127 serves equivalent function
- Bovine serum      : 100x diluted, spiked with human IgG 0-10 ug/mL; Sigma Chemical
                     Resulting bovine IgG ~100 ug/mL (100-fold excess over highest human IgG spike)
- Parylene C dimer  : Specialty Coating Systems, Indianapolis IN
- Cytop resin       : CT-809M in CT-SOLV180; Bellex International, Wilmington DE
- Tween 20          : Sigma Chemical, Oakville ON


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Capture Antibody Immobilization (Pre-Assembly, Off-Device)
  Reagents    : Fc-specific anti-human IgG (0.22-2.2 mg/mL), 0.1% Pluronic F-127 rinse
  Operation   : Manual pipetting of 250-500 nL onto unpatterned Cytop/ITO glass slide
  Post-spot   : Air-dry; rinse in 0.1% w/v Pluronic F-127 in DI water; air-dry before use
  Substrate   : Cytop/ITO top plate (unpatterned)
  Notes       : Concentration chosen to ensure surface saturation in spot area.
                Top plate chosen over bottom plate for three reasons:
                (1) Top plate simpler to fabricate and replace than patterned bottom plate.
                (2) Printing/drying/rinsing process can damage bottom plate insulator,
                    causing electrolysis susceptibility.
                (3) Spot area ~ actuation electrode area but small relative to ground electrode;
                    less likely to interfere with actuation when on top plate.
                Using top plate extends bottom plate lifetime for multiple assay reuse.

Step 2 | Device Assembly and Reservoir Loading
  Operation   : Assemble top and bottom plates with spacer; load reservoirs
  Droplet vol : 1 uL per aliquot (antigen sample + rinse buffer loaded before assembly)
  Spacer      : ~150 um double-sided tape

Step 3 | Sample Incubation -- Antigen Binding to Capture Spot
  Reagents    : HumanIgG_Sample (1 uL), AntiHumanIgG_Capture (surface-bound)
  Operation   : DMF actuation -- 10-pass cyclic translation across capture antibody spot
  Duration    : 10 min
  Passes      : 10 (back-and-forth across spot)
  Actuation   : 75 V_rms, 18 kHz
  Notes       : Active transport delivers antigen to capture surface without diffusion
                limitation. Diffusion distances ~100x smaller than well plate.
                Dynamic system also reduces non-specific adsorption relative to static
                well-plate incubation. 10 passes used to eliminate variance from fluid
                movement timing; Fig. 3 shows saturation after only 2 passes, but 10
                passes used for protocol robustness (Fig. 2a/b).

Step 4 | Sample Removal
  Operation   : Withdraw sample droplet to reservoir; manually remove waste droplet
                with laboratory tissue (Fig. 2b)
  Notes       : Waste contains unbound Human IgG and matrix proteins.

Step 5 | First Rinse -- Removal of Non-Specifically Bound IgG
  Reagents    : PluronicF127_RinseBuffer (1 uL), AntiHumanIgG_Capture (surface-bound)
  Operation   : DMF actuation -- 2-pass rinse across capture spot
  Duration    : 2 min
  Passes      : 2
  Actuation   : 75 V_rms, 18 kHz
  Notes       : 10 mM phosphate pH 7.4 + 0.00625% Pluronic F-127. Fig. 3 (inset) shows
                non-specific adsorption to native surface and BSA spots is very low;
                2 passes sufficient for NSB removal without displacing specifically bound
                antigen. Rinse waste droplet removed to reservoir.

Step 6 | Device Reload for Detection Antibody
  Operation   : Replace Cytop/ITO top plate; reload bottom plate reservoirs with 1-uL
                aliquots of FITC-Fab-specific anti-human IgG and rinse buffer (Fig. 2c)
  Notes       : Cover plate replaced to expose fresh reservoir area.

Step 7 | Detection Antibody Incubation
  Reagents    : FITC_AntiHumanIgG_Detection (1 uL), AntiHumanIgG_Capture (surface-bound)
  Operation   : DMF actuation -- 10-pass cyclic translation across assay spot
  Duration    : 10 min
  Passes      : 10
  Actuation   : 75 V_rms, 18 kHz
  Reynolds No : ~210 (laminar flow)
  Notes       : FITC-Fab-specific anti-human IgG delivered to spot and cycled 10 times
                (Fig. 2c/d). Completes the sandwich: capture antibody -- antigen -- detection
                antibody. Binding saturation reached after 2 passes (Fig. 3); 10 passes
                used for robustness. Pluronic F-127 in droplet does not strip previously
                bound antibody. Bulk droplet retains far more FITC-anti-IgG than bound by
                surface -- spot size and antigen density are limiting factors.
                Laminar flow (Re ~210); spot captures antibody from fluid layer in direct
                contact with surface per pass.

Step 8 | Detection Antibody Removal
  Operation   : Withdraw detection antibody droplet to reservoir; manually remove waste
                with laboratory tissue (Fig. 2d)

Step 9 | Final Rinse -- Removal of Unbound Detection Antibody
  Reagents    : PluronicF127_RinseBuffer (1 uL), AntiHumanIgG_Capture (surface-bound)
  Operation   : DMF actuation -- 2-pass final rinse across assay spot
  Duration    : 2 min
  Passes      : 2
  Actuation   : 75 V_rms, 18 kHz
  Notes       : Critical step. Residual unbound FITC-anti-IgG in droplet would produce
                high background fluorescence at plate reader, elevating baseline and
                reducing signal-to-noise. Rinse waste droplet removed to reservoir
                (Fig. 2e/f).

Step 10 | Fluorescence Detection
  Operation   : detect (plate reader fluorescence measurement)
  Instrument  : PheraStar multiwell plate reader (BMG Labtech, Durham NC)
  Settings    : lambda_ex = 485 nm, lambda_em = 520 nm, focal height = 12.1 mm
  Duration    : 30 s
  Notes       : Device (still on multiwell plate) inserted into plate reader for FITC
                fluorescence readout from sandwich complex immobilized on capture antibody
                spot on top plate. After detection, Cytop/ITO top plate discarded; patterned
                bottom plate retained for reuse in subsequent experiments.
                Comparison assay: same protocol run in 96-well plates with 100 uL aliquots
                using published commercial protocol (Amplex ELISA kit); same absolute mass
                amounts of antigen used on DMF and well plate for direct comparison.


ASSAY PERFORMANCE
-----------------
Dynamic range      : ~1 order of magnitude (both DMF and 96-well plate methods)
DMF R^2            : 0.9964 (stronger linear correlation than well plate)
Well plate R^2     : 0.9839
Reproducibility    : %RSD < 25% per data point (3-5 replicates); well plate slightly lower variance
Analysis time      : 2.5 h (DMF) vs up to 2 days (conventional 96-well plate)
Sample volume      : 1 uL (DMF) vs 100 uL (well plate) -- ~100-fold reduction
Waste volume       : ~4 uL/DMF spot vs ~3.5 mL/well -- ~3 orders of magnitude reduction
Serum validation   : Human IgG detected in 100x diluted bovine serum with 100-fold excess
                     bovine IgG; no significant cross-reactivity; linear standard curve obtained
LOD/LOQ            : Not yet determined; preliminary data show assay can run at concentrations
                     at least 1 order of magnitude lower without sacrificing reproducibility
                     or dynamic range (data not shown in paper)


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : miller_dmf_immunoassay.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : miller_dmf_immunoassay.ir
DAG output     : miller_dmf_immunoassay_main_dag.dot
Basic blocks   : 4 (BB1-BB4), 1 if/else gate, 4 CFG edges
Modules        : immunoassayDetection
Manifests      : AntiHumanIgG_Capture, HumanIgG_Sample, FITC_AntiHumanIgG_Detection,
                 PluronicF127_RinseBuffer, BovineSerum_Spiked
Duration units : All durations in minutes (m) or seconds (s); BioScript supports s and m only
                 10 min incubation  -> 10m  (IR: 600.0 SECOND)
                 2 min rinse        -> 2m   (IR: 120.0 SECOND)
                 30 s detection     -> 30s  (IR: 30.0 SECOND)

v2 fix (use-after-dispose):
  In v1, antigenBound was disposed after sample removal but then referenced again in
  rinseStep1 (STEP 5) and sandwichComplex (STEP 7), creating a use-after-dispose in
  BioScript's data-flow model. Fixed in v2 by introducing captureSpot as a persistent
  variable (never disposed) that models the physical antibody spot on the ITO top plate.
  All four mix operations (antigenBound, rinseStep1, sandwichComplex, rinseStep2) now
  reference captureSpot directly. Only liquid droplet variables are disposed.
  IR confirmed clean: captureSpot1[0] referenced across all four mix calls without
  any intervening dispose.

blocking_agent.name: BSA
blocking_agent.note: BSA blocking step eliminated on DMF device; Pluronic F-127 serves as functional replacement for non-specific binding prevention

steps.name: Capture antibody immobilization (pre-assembly)
steps.post_spot_rinse: 0.1% w/v Pluronic F-127 in deionized water
steps.notes: Fc-specific anti-human IgG physisorbed onto Cytop/ITO top plate by manual pipetting. Spots air-dried, rinsed, dried before device assembly. Top plate chosen over bottom plate to: (1) simplify fabrication and replacement, (2) avoid insulator damage from printing on bottom plate, (3) minimise interference with actuation electrode function. Extends bottom plate lifetime for multiple assay reuse.

steps.name: Device assembly and reservoir loading
steps.notes: Patterned bottom plate assembled with pre-spotted Cytop/ITO top plate separated by double-sided tape spacer. 1-uL aliquots of antigen sample and rinse buffer loaded into reservoirs before assembly.

steps.name: Sample incubation - antigen binding to capture spot
steps.operation: mix (10-pass cyclic DMF actuation across capture spot)
steps.notes: DMF actuation cycles 1-uL sample droplet back and forth across capture antibody spot 10 times (Fig. 2a/b). Active transport eliminates diffusion-limited kinetics: diffusion distances ~100x smaller than well plate. Dynamic system reduces non-specific adsorption relative to static incubation. 10 passes chosen to eliminate variance from fluid movement timing; 2 passes shown sufficient for binding saturation (Fig. 3) but 10 used for robustness.

steps.name: Sample removal
steps.operation: withdraw to reservoir + manual tissue removal
steps.notes: Sample droplet withdrawn to reservoir via DMF actuation. Waste droplet (containing unbound IgG and matrix proteins) manually removed from chip with laboratory tissue (Fig. 2b).

steps.name: First rinse - removal of non-specifically bound IgG
steps.operation: mix (2-pass rinse actuation across capture spot)
steps.notes: 1-uL rinse buffer droplet (10 mM phosphate pH 7.4 + 0.00625% Pluronic F-127) actuated across spot in 2 passes. Fig. 3 (inset) confirms non-specific adsorption to native surface and BSA spots is very low compared to specific binding; 2 passes sufficient for NSB removal without displacing specifically bound antigen. Rinse droplet removed to waste reservoir.

steps.name: Device reload for detection antibody
steps.notes: Cytop/ITO top plate replaced. Bottom plate reservoirs reloaded with 1-uL aliquots of FITC-Fab-specific anti-human IgG detection antibody and rinse buffer (Fig. 2c).

steps.name: Detection antibody incubation
steps.operation: mix (10-pass cyclic DMF actuation across assay spot)
steps.notes: FITC-Fab-specific anti-human IgG delivered to assay spot and cycled 10 times (Fig. 2c/d). Binding curve (Fig. 3) shows saturation after only 2 passes; spot captures antibody from fluid layer in direct contact with surface per pass. Pluronic in droplet does not strip previously bound antibody. Bulk droplet retains more antibody than bound by surface -- spot size and antigen density are limiting factors. Reynolds ~210; laminar flow.

steps.name: Detection antibody removal
steps.operation: withdraw to reservoir + manual tissue removal
steps.notes: Detection antibody droplet removed to waste reservoir and manually cleared with laboratory tissue (Fig. 2d).

steps.name: Final rinse - removal of unbound detection antibody
steps.operation: mix (2-pass final rinse actuation across assay spot)
steps.notes: 1-uL rinse buffer droplet cycled across spot in 2 passes to remove remaining unbound FITC-anti-IgG (Fig. 2e). Critical step: residual detection antibody in droplet would generate high background fluorescence at plate reader. Rinse droplet removed to waste reservoir (Fig. 2f).

steps.name: Fluorescence detection
steps.notes: Device (still on multiwell plate) inserted into PheraStar plate reader for FITC fluorescence readout from sandwich complex on top plate spot. After detection, Cytop/ITO top plate discarded; patterned bottom plate retained for re-use.

assay_performance.conventional_time_days: up to 2 (12 h antibody immobilization + 2-12 h BSA blocking + 1-2 h per binding step)
assay_performance.sample_volume_reduction: ~100-fold (1 uL DMF vs 100 uL well plate)
assay_performance.waste_volume_reduction: ~3 orders of magnitude (4 uL/DMF spot vs 3.5 mL/well)

serum_validation.matrix: bovine serum diluted 100x spiked with human IgG
serum_validation.interfering_species: bovine IgG at ~100 ug/mL (100-fold excess over highest human IgG)
serum_validation.result: linear standard curve obtained; low-concentration analyte detectable in complex matrix

binding_curve.rationale: 2 passes sufficient for binding saturation; 10 used to eliminate variance from fluid movement timing

non_specific_binding.mitigation: Pluronic F-127 in all solutions; no carrier oil (oil would form barrier preventing antibody-antigen binding at surface)

carrier_oil.note: Droplets surrounded by air only; carrier oil would form barrier between droplet and assay surface and could render assay ineffective

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.description: sample incubation, rinse 1, detection antibody incubation, rinse 2, fluorescence detection

bioscript.duration_units: All durations in minutes (m) or seconds (s); BioScript supports s and m only
bioscript.v2_fix: captureSpot variable never disposed; models persistent physical antibody spot on ITO top plate. All four mix operations reference captureSpot directly. Only liquid droplet variables (antigenBound, rinseStep1, sandwichComplex, rinseStep2) are disposed. Fixes use-after-dispose data-flow error present in v1.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Droplet-Scale Estrogen Assays in Breast Tissue, Blood, and Serum
Source Link  : https://www.science.org/doi/abs/10.1126/scitranslmed.3000105
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1126/scitranslmed.3000105
Journal      : Science Translational Medicine, 2009, Vol. 1, Issue 1, Article 1ra2
Platform     : Digital microfluidics (DMF / EWOD) on single-plate open-top ITO electrode array
Analyte      : Estradiol (17-beta-estradiol)
Sample types : Whole blood, serum, breast tissue homogenate, estradiol standard solutions
Sample volume: 1 uL per assay (1000-4000x smaller than conventional biopsy methods)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a miniaturised, automated digital microfluidic method for extraction
and quantification of estradiol (the most biologically active form of estrogen) from 1-uL
clinical samples, including whole blood, serum, and breast tissue homogenate from
postmenopausal breast cancer patients.

Estrogen is a key hormone in human reproductive physiology and plays an important role in the
pathogenesis of breast cancer. Local breast tissue estrogen concentrations are not routinely
measured because conventional methods require invasive biopsies of hundreds to thousands of mg
of tissue, followed by 5-6 h of laboratory processing (lysis, homogenisation, extraction,
purification, resolubilisation). The DMF method described here reduces this to 10-20 min on a
1-uL sample, while achieving recoveries of 86-119% (ELISA, CV 7-10%).

The method uses digital microfluidics (EWOD) to automate a complete liquid-liquid extraction
workflow: (1) cell lysis with DCM/acetone, (2) steroid dissolution in methanol, and (3)
liquid-liquid partitioning in isooctane to remove interfering compounds (porphyrin m/z 715,
DNA helicase m/z 677, tyrosine m/z 178), which suppress estradiol ionisation in mass
spectrometry. Detection is performed by ELISA (absorbance 450 nm) and LC-MS/MS with selected
reaction monitoring (SRM, m/z 271/145; retention time ~3.2 min).

Breast tissue application: replicate analyses of 1-uL samples from postmenopausal breast cancer
patients yielded 522 pg estradiol/mg tissue (CV 1%), confirming suitability for quantitative
analysis from fine-needle aspiration-scale biopsies.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Type         : Single-plate open-top DMF (EWOD)
Electrodes   : ITO (indium tin oxide), 1.5-mm pitch
Substrate    : Glass coated with Teflon-AF dielectric
Configuration: Open-top during sample drying; top plate affixed before solvent loading

Reservoirs:
  - Sample reservoir (blood, serum, tissue homogenate, or standard solution)
  - Lysing solvent reservoir (DCM/acetone 80:20 v/v)
  - Polar extraction solvent reservoir (methanol, HPLC grade)
  - Non-polar extraction solvent reservoir (isooctane, 99.8%)
  - Collection reservoir (pooled extract output)

Extraction zone:
  A photoresist "wall" defines the liquid-liquid extraction zone, separating the isooctane
  pool from the collection reservoir. The DMF device drives the methanol droplet in circular
  paths within the isooctane pool (~20 s per cycle, movie S1 in paper) before separating and
  directing the aqueous extract toward the collection reservoir. Phase separation at the wall
  is straightforward compared to microchannel-based liquid-liquid extraction, where separating
  one liquid phase from another after contact is inherently difficult.

Droplet volumes:
  Unit droplet (methanol extract): 200-400 nL
  Lysis wave option 1: 9 x 1.1 uL DCM/acetone (9.9 uL total)
  Lysis wave option 2: 5 x 2.2 uL DCM/acetone (11.0 uL total)
  Methanol extraction option 1: 9 x 1.1 uL methanol (9.9 uL total)
  Methanol extraction option 2: 5 x 2.2 uL methanol (11.0 uL total)


REAGENTS
--------

Lysing solvent       : DCM/acetone 80:20 (v/v)
                       Dichloromethane (Sigma); acetone HPLC grade
                       Function: lyse cells; dissolve lipid/protein matrix to free steroids

Polar extraction     : Methanol, HPLC grade (Fisher Scientific)
solvent                Function: dissolve free steroids from dried lysate into polar phase

Non-polar extraction : Isooctane (2,2,4-trimethylpentane), 99.8% (Sigma)
solvent                Function: partition interferents from polar estradiol-containing phase;
                       DCM/acetone and methanol also used for initial extraction (Supp. fig S1)

Reconstitution       : Methanol/DCM 2:1 (v/v), 30 uL aliquot
solvent                Evaporated; residue reconstituted in medium for desired analysis

ELISA diluent        : Estrogen-free serum (ALPCO Diagnostics) + methanol 4:1 (v/v), 50 uL
                       Used to resuspend dried extract before ELISA plate reader readout

Estradiol standard   : 17-beta-estradiol (Steraloids Inc.)
                       2 mg/mL in methanol for LC-MS/MS; serial dilutions for ELISA
                       (40, 1200, 3000, 6000 pg/mL final concentrations)

HPLC-grade water     : Sigma


CLINICAL SAMPLES
----------------

Breast tissue:
  Source         : Apparently normal tissue adjacent to breast cancer tumors
  Patients       : Two postmenopausal breast cancer patients
  Collection     : Surgical resection
  Storage        : -80 C
  Processing     : Manual homogenisation in 1 mL DCM; 1-uL aliquot taken, dried, extracted by
                   DMF Method 1; resuspended in 100 uL methanol/water 80:20 (v/v);
                   10 uL injected onto LC-MS/MS

Blood and serum:
  Source         : Healthy female volunteer
  Timepoints     : Five different reproductive cycles, midluteal phase
  Storage        : -20 C
  MS samples     : 5-uL aliquot dried, extracted by DMF Method 1, reconstituted in 50 uL
                   methanol/formic acid 0.1% (v/v); injected by nanoelectrospray

Ethics: Mount Sinai Hospital and Ontario Tumor Bank Research Ethics Boards


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Sample Loading and Drying
  Sample    : Whole blood (representative; serum or tissue homogenate also applicable)
  Volume    : 1 uL
  Operation : Dispense 1-uL aliquot into sample reservoir; allow to dry at room temperature
  Duration  : ~60 s (1 min per reservoir volume, room temperature, 25 C)
  Notes     : Standard solutions used immediately without drying; blood, serum, and tissue
              homogenate samples dried on electrode surface before top plate is affixed and
              solvents (DCM/acetone and isooctane) are loaded into reservoirs.

Step 2-4 | Lysis -- DCM/Acetone Wave (3 representative cycles)
  Solvent   : DCM/acetone 80:20 (v/v)
  Operation : Each cycle: dispense 1 reservoir volume of DCM/acetone; drive dropwise by DMF
              to the dried sample; incubate at room temperature until dry (~1 min/cycle)
  Duration  : 60 s per cycle; 3 cycles encoded (paper: 9 x 1.1 uL or 5 x 2.2 uL)
  Temperature: 25 C (room temperature)
  Purpose   : Cell lysis and dissolution of lipid/protein matrix to free steroid analytes
  BioScript : Each cycle modelled as dispense + mix; mix abstracts electrode-driven droplet
              translation and merge onto dried sample plus incubation-to-dryness event

Step 5-7 | Methanol Dissolution and Liquid-Liquid Extraction in Isooctane (3 cycles)
  Reagents  : Methanol (polar), Isooctane (non-polar)
  Cycle description:
    (a) Dispense 1 reservoir volume of methanol; drive by DMF to dried lysate to dissolve steroids
    (b) Dispense 1 unit droplet (200-400 nL) of dissolved sample; drive to isooctane reservoir
    (c) Circulate droplet within isooctane pool for ~20 s (electrode-driven; see movie S1, paper)
    (d) Drive droplet out of isooctane toward collection reservoir
    Repeat until sample reservoir exhausted of methanol
  Dissolution duration: 10 s per cycle (DMF mixing)
  Circulation duration: 20 s per cycle at 25 C (isooctane pool; modelled as heat at 25c for 20s)
  Purpose   : Isooctane partitions away interferents (porphyrin m/z 715, DNA helicase m/z 677,
              tyrosine m/z 178) that suppress estradiol ionisation in MS; estradiol remains in
              polar methanol phase and is collected.
  Paper note: Phase separation at photoresist wall is straightforward; contrast with microchannel
              LLE where separating phases after contact is inherently limited.

Step 8 | Pooling, Reconstitution, and Drying
  Operation : Pool all extract droplets in collection reservoir; mix with estrogen-free serum
              diluent (4:1 serum:methanol, 50 uL) for ELISA reconstitution; dry at 25 C
  Duration  : 5 s (pooling mix) + 5 min (300 s) drying at room temperature
  Storage   : Devices stored at -20 C after extract collected and dried
  Pre-analysis: 30 uL methanol/DCM (2:1 v/v) added to dried extract; dispensed to centrifuge
                tube; solvent evaporated; residue reconstituted in analysis-specific medium

Step 9 | ELISA Extraction QC Detection
  Module    : estradiolExtractionQC
  Target    : pooledExtract
  Duration  : 30 s
  Method    : Estradiol-specific ELISA (ALPCO Diagnostics); absorbance at 450 nm;
              mQuant microplate spectrophotometer (Bio-Tek Instruments); min. 3 replicates
  Results   : Recovery 86-119%; CV 7-10% (Fig. 4, paper)
              Breast tissue: 522 pg estradiol/mg tissue; CV 1% (replicate 1-uL samples)
  QC gate   : extractionSignal > 0 -> dispose (pass, proceed to MS branch)
              extractionSignal <= 0 -> drain (fail, extraction unsuccessful)

Step 10 | MS Confirmation Detection
  Module    : estradiolMSDetection
  Target    : estradiolStd (fresh estradiol standard as MS reference droplet)
  Duration  : 192 s (~3.2 min; SRM retention time plus instrument equilibration)
  Methods   :
    (i) LTQ direct MS (Thermo Scientific): nanoelectrospray, negative mode, 250 C, 0.5 uL/min
        Estradiol fragment m/z 183; absent in whole samples, dominant in DMF-extracted samples
    (ii) QTRAP LC-MS/MS SRM (Applied Biosystems): m/z 271/145; retention time ~3.2 min
        Column: Thermo Gold C18 2.2 um, 2.1 mm ID x 50 mm (microbore)
        Mobile phase: MeOH/H2O 80:20 (v/v), isocratic; 300 uL/min; 10 uL injection
        Spray: 4200 V; collision energy: 60 V; nebulising: 400 C
  QC gate   : msSignal > 0 -> dispose (confirmed); msSignal <= 0 -> drain (not confirmed)


DETECTION SUMMARY
-----------------

Method          | Instrument                         | Key parameter         | Result
----------------|------------------------------------|-----------------------|---------------------------
Direct MS       | LTQ (Thermo), nanoESI neg mode     | m/z 183 (estradiol)   | Confirmed in extracted samples only
LC-MS/MS SRM    | QTRAP (Applied Biosystems)         | m/z 271/145, 3.2 min  | Detected in standard, tissue, blood
ELISA           | ALPCO kit, abs 450 nm              | Recovery 86-119%      | CV 7-10%; tissue 522 pg/mg (CV 1%)


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : mousa_dmf_estrogen_extraction.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : mousa_dmf_estrogen_extraction.ir
DOT output     : mousa_dmf_estrogen_extraction_main_dag.dot
Basic blocks   : 7 (BB1-BB7)
CFG edges      : 8 (DOT graph)

Duration units : All durations use s or m (h token not supported by compiler)
  Drying per lysis cycle      : 60s (1 min)
  Isooctane circulation       : 20s per extraction cycle
  Reconstitution drying       : 300s (5m)
  ELISA detect                : 30s
  MS SRM detect               : 192s (~3.2 min retention time)

Manifests      : BloodSample, DCM_Acetone_8020, Methanol, Isooctane,
                 EstradiolStandard, EstrogenFreeSerum
Modules        : estradiolExtractionQC, estradiolMSDetection

Known compiler bugs (consistent with dataset conventions):
  - drain lowered to dispose() in IR for else-branches (bsbbif_3_f, bsbbif_6_f);
    .bs source is correct
  - True-branch blocks (bsbbif_2_t, bsbbif_5_t) emit no unconditional jump in IR;
    DOT edges are correct

Abstraction notes:
  - Lysis: paper uses 9x or 5x cycles; 3 explicit cycles encoded (no loop primitive in BioScript)
  - Methanol extraction: same; 3 cycles encoded; each cycle models dissolution + LLE + circulation
  - LLE circulation: heat at 25c for 20s abstracts the ~20 s electrode-driven circulation
    of the methanol droplet within the isooctane pool (movie S1 in paper)
  - Isooctane: modelled as a manifest; mix(dissolvedSample, isooctane) abstracts
    electrode-driven translation into the isooctane pool
  - heat is void/in-place throughout; all dispensed fluid variables consumed exactly once
