description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Digital Microfluidic Magnetic Separation for Particle-Based Immunoassays
Source Link  : https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/estrogen%20and%20TSH%20immunoassay.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/ac3020627
Journal      : Analytical Chemistry, 2012, Vol. 84, pp. 8805-8812
Platform     : Digital microfluidics (DMF), air-matrix (oil-free), EWOD electrode array with movable permanent magnet


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes the first particle-based immunoassay implemented on digital microfluidics
(DMF) without the aid of an oil carrier fluid (i.e., droplets surrounded by air). The air-matrix
format enabled a novel on-chip magnetic particle separation and resuspension method -- the
"supernatant separation" method -- capable of removing greater than 90% of unbound reagents in
a single step. Using this approach, two immunoassays were developed:

  1. Competitive immunoassay for 17beta-estradiol (E2), a small-molecule steroid (272.38 Da).
     This is the first competitive immunoassay implemented on any DMF platform.
  2. Noncompetitive (sandwich) immunoassay for Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH), the most
     commonly performed immunoassay in clinical laboratories.

Compared to conventional well-plate ELISA:
  - 100-fold reduction in reagent volume (11.2 uL vs. 1.2 mL total per assay)
  - 10-fold reduction in analysis time (6 min sample incubation vs. 60 min)
  - Analytical performance retained at a level suitable for clinical screening

The technique has potential for use in fast, low-waste, inexpensive instruments for quantitative
analysis of proteins and small molecules in low sample volumes.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Actuation electrodes : 96
Reservoirs           : 10
Assay regions        : 4 (independent assays per device)
Detection region     : 1 (shared; electrodes rinsed with H2O2 between assays)
Unit droplet volume  : ~800 nL
Droplet environment  : Air (no oil carrier fluid; Pluronic L64 enables oil-free actuation)

Magnet system:
  - Neodymium permanent magnet, N48 grade, 5/8 in diameter x 1/4 in thick, 15.3 lb pull force
  - Positioned in Stripwell microplate manifold (selected wells removed as guides) below device
  - Controlled manually via metal clip; horizontal movement adjusts magnetic force on particles
  - Estimated magnetic force on particle pellet: ~470 uN
  - Minimum particle density for supernatant separation: ~3.0 x 10^8 particles/mL

Detection instrument:
  - Pherastar plate reader (BMG Labtech, Cary, NC)
  - Module: LUM (chemiluminescence); Gain: 3600; Focal height: 8.6 mm
  - Device affixed with tape to empty 96-well Stripwell plate; each droplet aligned to a well
  - Endpoint: 1 min (chemiluminescence signal saturates at 1 min)


IMMUNOASSAY MODES
-----------------
Competitive (E2):
  Exogenous E2-HRP conjugate (labeled antigen) competes with unlabeled E2 in sample for
  binding sites on anti-E2 capture antibodies immobilised on paramagnetic particle surfaces.
  Signal (chemiluminescence, RLU) is INVERSELY proportional to E2 concentration.
  Calibration: 10-1000 pg/mL. Curve fit: 4-parameter logistic equation.

Noncompetitive / Sandwich (TSH):
  Anti-TSH-HRP detection antibody and anti-beta-TSH capture antibody bind TSH at different
  epitopes, forming an antibody-antigen-antibody sandwich complex on the particle surface.
  Signal (chemiluminescence, RLU) is DIRECTLY proportional to TSH concentration.
  Calibration: 0.4-20 uIU/mL. Curve fit: linear equation.


REAGENTS
--------
Fouling mitigation:
  Pluronic L64 (BASF Corp., Germany), donated by Brenntag Canada, at 0.05% (v/v) in all
  solutions. Enables oil-free droplet actuation. Not found to interfere with specific binding
  in well-plate or DMF immunoassays. Custom DMF-compatible particle diluent, conjugate diluent,
  and wash buffer formulated with L64 as sole surfactant (ARCHITECT native surfactants
  cross-reacted with added L64 and prevented reliable droplet movement).

TSH-specific blocking:
  TSH paramagnetic particles blocked with nonfat dried milk prior to use. Required because
  initial TSH immunoassay experiments showed high background noise (nonspecific adsorption of
  anti-TSH-HRP on particle surfaces) preventing differentiation between 0 and 0.4 uIU/mL.
  Blocking significantly reduced background without affecting droplet actuation.

E2 conjugate optimisation:
  E2-HRP (E2 antigen labeled with HRP) at 1 ug/mL optimal concentration. At higher
  concentrations the dynamic range collapses: 50 pg/mL and 500 pg/mL produce similar signals.

Substrates:
  H2O2 (oxidising co-substrate for HRP) + luminol/enhancer solution. Mixed on-chip immediately
  before measurement. Two H2O2 pre-rinse cycles remove residual wash buffer before substrate
  delivery, preventing interference with the chemiluminescent reaction.

ELISA kits:
  Calbiotech (Spring Valley, CA) E2 and TSH kits for well-plate comparison experiments and
  wash-test TMB assays.


WASHING METHODS
---------------

Serial dilution (prior art; NOT used in this protocol):
  Particles immobilised by magnet. Droplet diluted by merging with wash buffer droplet.
  DMF splits pooled droplet; excess removed. Repeated until sufficient dilution.
  Requires >=6 washes (1:1 wash/initial ratio) for 98% unbound reagent removal.
  Drawbacks: slow dilution over many cycles; magnet immobilises particles throughout,
  trapping unbound material between particles.

Supernatant separation (THIS PROTOCOL):
  Magnet focuses particles into pellet on device surface. Supernatant droplet actuated
  away to waste with magnet in place. Magnet removed. Fresh droplet passed over pellet
  and shuttled in circular motion across 4 electrodes to resuspend.
  Achieves 98% unbound reagent removal within 2 wash cycles.
  Requirements:
    (1) Sufficient magnetic force: pellet force (~470 uN) must exceed interfacial force
        pulling particles into droplet. Satisfied for pellets of >=3.0x10^8 particles/mL.
    (2) Adjustable magnetic force: magnet moved horizontally for resuspension.
    (3) Stable particle suspension: ~5% residual liquid retained; particles resuspended
        immediately to prevent aggregation or drying.
  Not compatible with oil-immersed DMF devices.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Particle Separation from Diluent
  Operation  : Dispense 1 unit (800 nL) antibody-coated paramagnetic particle suspension.
               Pluronic L64 pre-mixed to 0.05% (v/v).
  Magnet     : Positioned to immobilise particles as pellet; diluent supernatant actuated to waste.
  Notes      : ~5% residual liquid retained by hydrophilic particles in pellet.
               Performed identically for both E2 and TSH assays (different particles dispensed).

Step 2 | Sample Incubation (3 unit droplets, 6 min)
  Operation  : Three 800 nL sample droplets (2.4 uL total) sequentially dispensed and
               delivered to particle pellet for resuspension and incubation.
  Duration   : 6 min (sufficient to saturate analyte binding; droplets show <5% volume loss
               at >=30 min, so evaporation is not a concern at 6 min).
  E2 (competitive)      : Unlabeled E2 competes for anti-E2 binding sites on particle surface.
  TSH (noncompetitive)  : TSH antigen captured by anti-beta-TSH antibody on particle surface.
  Notes      : 3 unit droplets chosen to improve signal over 1 droplet while remaining
               easily manipulated by DMF (volumes much larger than 1 unit are less reliable).

Step 3 | Post-Sample Wash x4 (Supernatant Separation)
  Operation  : 4 supernatant separation wash cycles with 800 nL wash buffer each.
               Each cycle: magnet immobilises pellet; supernatant to waste; fresh wash buffer
               reconstitutes particles via 4-electrode circular motion.
  Purpose    : Removes unbound sample matrix, excess analyte, and nonspecifically bound proteins.

Step 4 | Conjugate Incubation (2 min)
  Operation  : 1 unit (800 nL) conjugate droplet delivered to washed particles for
               resuspension and incubation.
  Duration   : 2 min
  E2         : E2-HRP (1 ug/mL) competes with sample E2 for remaining anti-E2 binding sites.
  TSH        : Anti-TSH-HRP detection antibody binds TSH at a second epitope, completing
               the antibody-antigen-antibody sandwich complex on the particle.

Step 5 | Post-Conjugate Wash x4 (Supernatant Separation)
  Operation  : 4 supernatant separation wash cycles (same as Step 3).
  Purpose    : Removes unbound HRP-labeled conjugate.

Step 6 | H2O2 Pre-Rinse x2 (Supernatant Separation)
  Operation  : 2 supernatant separation wash cycles with 800 nL H2O2 each.
  Purpose    : Removes residual wash buffer prior to substrate delivery. Prevents dilution
               or quenching of the H2O2/luminol chemiluminescent reaction.
               Replaces manufacturer-recommended H2O2/luminol pre-mix, which caused
               high inter-assay variability.

Step 7 | H2O2 Substrate Incubation (2 min)
  Operation  : Particles delivered to shared detection region. 1 unit (800 nL) H2O2 droplet
               reconstitutes particle pellet and incubates for 2 min.
  Purpose    : H2O2 serves as the oxidising co-substrate for HRP enzyme activity.
  Notes      : Detection region pre-rinsed with H2O2 between successive assays.

Step 8 | Chemiluminescence Activation and Detection
  Operation  : 1 unit (800 nL) luminol/enhancer droplet merged on-chip with the
               H2O2/particle droplet. Incubated 1 min (signal saturates at 1 min endpoint).
  Detection  : Pherastar plate reader, LUM module, gain=3600, focal height=8.6 mm.
               Device taped to empty 96-well Stripwell plate, detection zone per-well aligned.
  E2 signal  : Inversely proportional to E2 concentration (competitive assay).
  TSH signal : Directly proportional to TSH concentration (noncompetitive assay).
  QC gate    : Signal > 0 -> dispose assay droplet (pass). Signal <= 0 -> drain (fail).


PERFORMANCE
-----------

E2 Competitive Immunoassay:
  Calibration range : 10-1000 pg/mL
  Dynamic range     : ~2 orders of magnitude
  LOD (absolute)    : 50 fg         (well-plate ELISA: 152 fg)
  LOD (conc.)       : 21 pg/mL      (well-plate ELISA: 6.1 pg/mL)
  CV range          : 5-14%         (well-plate ELISA: 4-12%)
  Sample volume     : 2.4 uL        (well-plate ELISA: 25 uL)
  Incubation time   : 6 min         (well-plate ELISA: 60 min)
  Clinical use      : Ovarian cancer screening (E2 > 20 pg/mL, age-dependent)
                      E2 serum ranges: males 10-50 pg/mL; premenopausal 30-400 pg/mL;
                      postmenopausal <30 pg/mL

TSH Noncompetitive Immunoassay:
  Calibration range : 0.4-20 uIU/mL
  Dynamic range     : ~2 orders of magnitude
  LOD (absolute)    : 2.0 nIU       (well-plate ELISA: 3.0 nIU)
  LOD (conc.)       : 0.83 uIU/mL   (well-plate ELISA: 0.06 uIU/mL)
  CV range          : 9-21%         (well-plate ELISA: 2-13%)
  Sample volume     : 2.4 uL        (well-plate ELISA: 50 uL)
  Incubation time   : 6 min         (well-plate ELISA: 60 min)
  Clinical use      : Diagnosis of hypothyroidism (TSH > 3.0 uIU/mL);
                      normal serum range: 0.4-3.0 uIU/mL

Reagent consumption comparison (DMF vs. well-plate ELISA):
  Sample       : 2.4 uL vs. 50 uL    (E2) / 25 uL (E2) well-plate
  Conjugate    : 0.80 uL vs. 100 uL
  Wash buffer  : 6.4 uL vs. 900 uL
  Substrate    : 1.6 uL vs. 150 uL
  TOTAL        : 11.2 uL vs. ~1.2 mL  -->  100-fold reduction

Time comparison:
  DMF sample incubation    : 6 min
  ARCHITECT analyzer       : 18 min
  Well-plate ELISA         : 60 min
  --> 10-fold faster vs. ELISA; mechanism: smaller volume packs same particle number
      into smaller space, increasing surface-area-to-volume ratio and reaction kinetics


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : ng2012_dmf_immunoassay.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else QC gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG            : ng2012_dmf_immunoassay_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations in seconds (s) or minutes (m) only (BioScript supports s and m)
                 6 min sample incubation  -> 6m  (IR: 360.0 SECOND)
                 2 min conjugate/H2O2     -> 2m  (IR: 120.0 SECOND)
                 1 min detection          -> 1m  (IR: 60.0 SECOND)
                 5 s wash cycles          -> 5s  (IR: 5.0 SECOND)
Encoding note  : File must be pure ASCII. Greek letters (beta, mu) and special characters
                 (>=, x) must be replaced with ASCII equivalents to avoid ANTLR4
                 FileStream UnicodeDecodeError (byte 0xce in UTF-8 encoding).
Modules        : chemiluminescenceDetection
Manifests      : MagneticParticles, Sample_E2, Sample_TSH, WashBuffer,
                 ConjugateE2_HRP, ConjugateAntiTSH_HRP, H2O2,
                 Luminol_Enhancer, PluronicL64
CFG structure  :
  BB1 (main)     E2 full protocol (S1-S8) + detect + conditional branch
  BB2 (if_2_t)   e2Signal > 0: dispose(e2_detectionMix)
  BB3 (if_3_f)   e2Signal <= 0: drain(e2_detectionMix); jump BB4
  BB4 (if_4_j)   Join; TSH full protocol (S1-S8) + detect + conditional branch
  BB5 (if_5_t)   tshSignal > 0: dispose(tsh_detectionMix)
  BB6 (if_6_f)   tshSignal <= 0: drain(tsh_detectionMix); jump BB7
  BB7 (if_7_j)   Terminal: dispose(tshSignal); NOP
Compiler note  : Both pass (BB2/BB5) and fail (BB3/BB6) branches emit dispose() in the IR;
                 the compiler resolves drain() to dispose() for both conditional paths.
                 Quantitative signal interpretation (calibration curve fitting) occurs off-chip.

protocol.objective: First particle-based immunoassay on DMF without oil carrier fluid; development of supernatant separation washing method; competitive immunoassay for E2 and noncompetitive immunoassay for TSH with 100-fold reagent reduction and 10-fold faster analysis vs. well-plate ELISA

reagents.elisa_kits: Calbiotech (Spring Valley, CA) E2 and TSH well-plate ELISA kits (used for well-plate comparison and TMB wash-test)

serial_dilution.description: Particles immobilised by magnet; droplet diluted by merging with wash buffer droplet; DMF splits pooled droplet; excess solution removed; repeated until sufficient dilution achieved
serial_dilution.efficiency: Inherently inefficient: unbound reagents slowly diluted over many washes; magnet immobilises particles throughout, trapping unbound material between particles
serial_dilution.reference: Previously used in all DMF magnetic particle immunoassays (Sista et al. 2008; Vergauwe et al. 2011)

supernatant_separation.description: Magnet focuses particles into pellet and immobilises on device surface; supernatant droplet actuated away to waste; magnet removed; fresh droplet passed over pellet and shuttled in circular motion across 4 electrodes to resuspend particles

requirements: Sufficient magnetic force: pellet magnetic force (~470 uN) must exceed droplet interfacial force
Adjustable magnetic force: magnet moved horizontally away from device for particle resuspension
Stable particle suspension: ~5% residual liquid retained by hydrophilic particles during pellet phase; immediate resuspension prevents aggregation or drying

steps.notes: Three 800 nL sample droplets (total 2.4 uL) sequentially dispensed and delivered to particle pellet for resuspension and incubation. 6 min sufficient to saturate analyte binding on particle surfaces. Evaporation: <5% volume loss in >=30 min for 1 uL droplet. E2 (competitive): unlabeled E2 in sample occupies anti-E2 binding sites. TSH (noncompetitive): TSH antigen captured by anti-beta-TSH antibody on particle surface.

steps.name: Post-sample wash x4
steps.notes: Four supernatant separation wash cycles remove unbound sample matrix, excess antigen, and non-specifically bound proteins. Each cycle: magnet immobilises pellet, supernatant actuated to waste, fresh wash buffer droplet reconstitutes particles with 4-electrode circular motion.

steps.name: Conjugate incubation
steps.notes: E2 (competitive): E2-HRP at 1 ug/mL competes with sample E2 for residual anti-E2 binding sites. Higher E2-HRP concentrations collapse dynamic range (50 and 500 pg/mL become indistinguishable). TSH (noncompetitive): Anti-TSH-HRP detection antibody binds TSH at a different epitope from capture antibody, forming antibody-antigen-antibody sandwich complex. Milk-blocked TSH particles reduce nonspecific adsorption of anti-TSH-HRP.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Digital Microfluidic Immunocytochemistry in Single Cells (DISC)
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms8513
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms8513
Journal      : Nature Communications, 2015, Vol. 6, Article 7513
Platform     : Digital Microfluidics (DMF) -- two-plate electrowetting-on-dielectric (EWOD)


OVERVIEW
--------
DISC is a DMF-based method that automates all steps required to analyse signalling events in
adherent cells in situ: cell culture, serum starvation, sub-second ligand stimulation, chemical
fixation, and full immunocytochemistry (ICC) for quantitative single-cell phosphorylation profiling.

The platform overcomes two key limitations of existing approaches:
  1. Flow-based microfluidics require high flow rates for fast stimulus switching, producing
     shear stresses (>1 dyn/cm2) that activate unwanted mechanosensitive signalling pathways.
     DISC operates at ~0.5 dyn/cm2 with no moving parts.
  2. Conventional bulk methods (western blot, mass spectrometry) require cell disaggregation
     and cannot resolve single-cell heterogeneity or achieve time resolution below minutes.
     DISC achieves ~1 s reagent exchange and probes individual adherent cells in situ.

The protocol is demonstrated on the well-characterised PDGFR/PI3K/Akt signalling pathway
in NIH-3T3 fibroblasts and extended to breast cancer cell heterogeneity (MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231).
Key finding: a 10 s pulse of PDGF-BB (3.125 ng/mL) is sufficient to commit >32% of cells to
Akt activation -- kinetics far faster than any previously reported method could resolve.

The complete protocol encodes two sequential ICC arms:
  Arm 1 (PDGFR arm): 2 min stimulation; probes PDGFR Y857 / Y1021 phosphorylation.
  Arm 2 (Akt arm):   5 min stimulation; probes Akt S473 phosphorylation.
Both arms run the identical 11-step ICC pipeline with arm-specific antibody panels.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Configuration: Two parallel plates separated by a ~180 um double-sided tape spacer.

Bottom plate:
  Material    : Chromium electrodes on glass (200 x 300 x 1.1 mm, Telic Co.)
  Electrodes  : 80 actuation electrodes, 2.2 x 2.2 mm each; interdigitated borders
                (140 um sinusoidal pattern); inter-electrode gap 30-80 um.
                Reservoir electrodes for reagent loading and waste removal.
  Dielectric  : Parylene C, ~7 um (vapour deposition with A174 silane adhesion primer).
  Hydrophobic : Teflon-AF, ~200 nm (spin-coat 1% w/w in FC-40, 2000 rpm, 60 s; 165 C bake).

Top plate:
  Material    : ITO-coated glass (Delta Technologies Ltd, 300 x 100 mm).
  VM sites    : 8 circular hydrophilic ITO spots (1.75 mm diameter, 4.4 mm pitch) created by
                Teflon-AF lift-off using S1811 photoresist patterning.
  Function    : Cells adhere to the ITO spots; Teflon-AF surrounds spots to confine droplets.

Virtual Microwells (VMs):
  Volume      : ~400 nL per VM (2.4 mm2 footprint).
  Formation   : Passive dispensing -- when a source droplet (~900 nL unit droplet or larger)
                is swept across a vacant ITO spot, a sub-droplet spontaneously forms by
                hydrophobic-hydrophilic interaction (Supplementary Fig. 1).
  Capacity    : 150-300 cells per VM at 500,000 cells/mL seeding density.
  Exchange    : One passive dispense displaces ~93% of VM contents.
                Two successive exchanges displace >99% (Fig. 2b-d).
  Exchange time: ~1 s between successive droplet deliveries (Fig. 2a).

Actuation:
  Waveform    : Sine wave, 80-100 V_rms, 10 kHz.
  Interface   : 90-pin Pogo pin connector.
  Control     : DropBot open-source DMF automation system (http://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/dropbot).
  Orientation : Standard (top plate up) for droplet manipulation; inverted (top plate down)
                for all incubation steps so cells settle onto ITO spots by gravity.


CELL LINES
----------
- NIH-3T3 (mouse embryonic fibroblasts):
  Primary model for PDGFR/PI3K/Akt pathway validation (Figs. 3, 5, 6).
  Cultured in DMEM + 10% calf serum (CS) + 100 U/mL pen G + 100 ug/mL strep, 37 C, 5% CO2.
  Seeded at 500,000 cells/mL; yields ~150-300 cells per VM.

- MCF-7 (human breast cancer):
  Used for Akt single-cell heterogeneity experiments, 0-5 min stimulation
  (Supplementary Figs. 9-11). Cultured in DMEM + 10% FBS + antibiotics.

- MDA-MB-231 (human breast cancer, triple-negative):
  Used for hyperactive-responder single-cell morphology analysis (Fig. 4).
  Higher levels of Akt activation vs MCF-7 after 5 min (Supplementary Fig. 9a).
  Cultured in DMEM + 10% FBS + antibiotics.


PROTOCOL STEPS -- 11-STEP ICC PIPELINE
---------------------------------------
All reagents contain 0.05% v/v Pluronic F-68 (on-chip) to prevent biofouling.
All incubation steps performed at room temperature (25 C) unless otherwise noted.
Device inverted (top plate down) for all incubation steps.

Step 0 | Cell Seeding and Adhesion
  Reagent  : CultureMedia (DMEM + 10% serum + 0.05% F-68 + antibiotics)
  Cells    : NIH-3T3 at 500,000 cells/mL
  Volume   : 3 x 900 nL = 2.7 uL passively dispensed per VM spot
  Duration : 24 h at 37 C in humidified chamber (= 1440 min = 86400 s)
  Notes    : Device inverted after seeding. Cells settle by gravity; adhere to ITO spots.
             10^5-10^6 cells/mL confirmed sufficient for analysis (Supplementary Fig. 4).

Step 1 | Serum Starvation
  Reagent  : StarvedMedia (DMEM + 0.5% serum + 0.05% F-68 + antibiotics)
  Volume   : 6 x 900 nL = 5.4 uL
  Duration : 24 h at 37 C (= 1440 min = 86400 s)
  Notes    : Reduces basal PDGFR and Akt phosphorylation to unstimulated baseline.

Step 2 | Serum-Free Rinse
  Reagent  : SerumFreeMedia (DMEM + 0.05% F-68 + antibiotics)
  Volume   : 6 x 900 nL = 5.4 uL
  Duration : Immediate (passive dispense; ~1 s per exchange)
  Notes    : Two successive exchanges remove >99% of starving media (Fig. 2b-d).

Step 3 | PDGF-BB Ligand Stimulation
  Reagent  : PDGF-BB in SerumFreeMedia (Sigma-Aldrich human recombinant)
  Volume   : 2 x 900 nL = 1.8 uL
  Duration : 2 min for PDGFR arm; 5 min for Akt arm (encoded separately in BioScript)
  Dose     : 0-200 ng/mL (dose-response); 50 ng/mL (time-series); 3.125 ng/mL (pulse)
  Shear    : ~0.5 dyn/cm2 -- below 1 dyn/cm2 threshold for mechanosensitive signalling.
             Validated: 75 continuous back-and-forth movements, P=0.7188, no Akt effect.
  Variants :
    Single bolus  : Continuous PDGF-BB; fix at t = 30-120 s (Fig. 5a)
    Double bolus  : PDGF-BB at t=0 s + second PDGF-BB or vehicle at t=90 s (Fig. 5b)
    Pulse washaway: PDGF-BB for 3-40 s, then SerumFreeMedia wash, then fix at 2-5 min (Fig. 6a/b/c)

Step 4 | Fixation
  Reagent  : 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) + 0.05% F-68 in DPBS
  Volume   : 3 x 900 nL = 2.7 uL
  Duration : 10 min (= 600 s)
  Notes    : Applied within ~1 s of stimulation termination. Arrests signalling at exact
             time point. In time-series experiments, fixation staggered across VMs so
             all VMs are fixed simultaneously.

Step 5 | Post-Fixation Wash
  Reagent  : WashBuffer1 (0.05% v/v F-68 in DPBS)
  Volume   : 6 x 900 nL = 5.4 uL

Step 6 | Permeabilisation
  Reagent  : 0.2% v/v Tween-20 in DPBS
  Volume   : 3 x 900 nL = 2.7 uL
  Duration : 10 min (= 600 s)
  Notes    : Required for intracellular antibody access; essential for pAkt S473 detection.

Step 7 | Post-Permeabilisation Wash
  Reagent  : WashBuffer2 (0.05% v/v Brij 35 in DPBS)
  Volume   : 9 x 900 nL = 8.1 uL
  Notes    : Extended wash volume to fully remove Tween-20 before blocking.

Step 8 | Blocking
  Reagent  : 1% bovine non-fat dried milk + 0.05% Brij 35 in DPBS
  Volume   : 3 x 900 nL = 2.7 uL
  Duration : 60 min (= 3600 s)

Step 9 | Primary Antibody Incubation
  PDGFR arm:
    pan-PDGFR-b : Mouse mAb 1:50, CST sc-19995             [total protein; Cy5 channel]
    p-PDGFR Y857: Rabbit pAb 1:200, SCB sc-12907-R         [phospho; Cy3 channel]
    p-PDGFR Y1021: Rabbit pAb 1:200, SCB sc-12909-R        [phospho; Cy3 channel]
  Akt arm:
    pan-Akt     : Mouse mAb 1:50, CST 2920S                 [total protein; Cy5 channel]
    p-Akt S473  : Rabbit mAb 1:200, CST 4060P               [phospho; Cy3 channel]
  Diluent  : Blocking solution (BS); pre-mixed off-chip before DMF reservoir loading
  Volume   : 3 x 900 nL = 2.7 uL
  Duration : Overnight at 4 C (= 720 min = 43200 s)

Step 10 | Post-Primary Wash
  Reagent  : WashBuffer2 (0.05% Brij 35 in DPBS)
  Volume   : 6 x 900 nL = 5.4 uL

Step 11 | Secondary Antibody Incubation
  Anti-Mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 647 Fab2, 1:500, CST 4410S   [total protein; Cy5 channel]
  Anti-Rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 555 Fab2, 1:500, CST 4413S  [phospho-protein; Cy3 channel]
  Diluent  : Blocking solution (BS); pre-mixed off-chip
  Volume   : 3 x 900 nL = 2.7 uL
  Duration : 2 h at room temperature (25 C) (= 120 min = 7200 s)
  Post     : Top plate removed; rinsed 30 s in 0.05% Tween-20/DPBS; rinsed 30 s in DI water;
             air-dried in dark.


DETECTION AND ANALYSIS
-----------------------
Scanner      : Axon GenePix 4000B microarray scanner.
               Settings: 5 um resolution, 0 mm focus, 532 nm and 635 nm lasers at 100% power,
               PMT 500 V (adjusted per experiment to avoid saturation).
Analysis     : CellProfiler 2.0 r11710 (open-source, http://www.cellprofiler.org/).
               Custom pipeline: image crop, cell identification (Otsu Global thresholding,
               two-class, 0.7 correction factor, 15-100 um diameter), shape and neighbour
               analysis, dual-channel fluorescence measurement.
Quantification: For each cell, fold change = (Cy3 phospho-channel intensity) / (Cy5 total-
               protein intensity), normalised to the no-stimulation control on the same device.
               Data exported for GraphPad Prism (bulk plots) and JMP 10 (single-cell analysis).

PDGFR results (Fig. 3b):
  Dose-response: phosphorylation onset at 3.125 ng/mL; plateau at 50 ng/mL.
  Hill coefficient (Y857): 1.73 +/- 0.33; EC50: 15.89 +/- 1.86 ng/mL.
  Hill coefficient (Y1021): 2.13 +/- 0.44; EC50: 18.33 +/- 1.94 ng/mL.
  Maximal phosphorylation at: Y857 = 75 s; Y1021 = 60 s after stimulation (Fig. 5a).

Akt results (Fig. 3c, Fig. 6):
  Downstream amplification: at 3.125 ng/mL PDGF, ~22% PDGFR phosphorylation drives >70% Akt.
  Pulse commitment (Fig. 6b): 10 s pulse commits >32% of cells to Akt activation.
                               3 s pulse insufficient (indistinguishable from control).
  Noise filtering (Fig. 6c): 3 s pulse induces transient Akt (20% active at 3-4 min)
                              deactivated by 5 min -- enzymatic phosphorylation/dephosphorylation.

Cell heterogeneity (Fig. 4):
  Hyperactive responders defined as: p-Akt fold change > Q3 + 1.5 * IQR.
  MDA-MB-231 peak hyperactivity: 10.2% of cells at 5 min stimulation.
  Hyperactive cell morphology: higher eccentricity (elongated), lower form factor (less spherical),
  more and closer neighbours vs normal cells. Effect attributed to paracrine signalling.
  Cell position in VM: no effect on Akt activation (Supplementary Fig. 15).


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file   : ng2015_DISC_dmf.bs
Compiler         : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based, https://github.com/lilott8/BioScript)
IR target        : ir
IR output        : ng2015_DISC_dmf.ir
DAG output       : ng2015_DISC_dmf_main_dag.dot
Total BB count   : 10 (BB1-BB10)
CFG edge count   : 12
Variables defined: 66 (SSA, all at version [0] or [1] suffix only)
Modules          : phosphorylationDetection, cellViabilityDetection
Manifests        : 18 declared (NIH3T3_Cells, SeumFreeMedia, StarvedMedia, CultureMedia,
                   PluronicF68, PDGFBB_Ligand, Paraformaldehyde, WashBuffer1, WashBuffer2,
                   Tween20, BlockingSolution, PrimaryAntibody_PDGFR, PrimaryAntibody_pPDGFR_Y857,
                   PrimaryAntibody_pPDGFR_Y1021, PrimaryAntibody_Akt, PrimaryAntibody_pAkt_S473,
                   SecondaryAntibody_AlexaFluor647, SecondaryAntibody_AlexaFluor555)

Duration units   : BioScript supports s and m only (h token not supported).
  Cell adhesion (24 h)        -> 1440m  (IR: 86400.0 SECOND)
  Serum starvation (24 h)     -> 1440m  (IR: 86400.0 SECOND)
  PDGFR stimulation (2 min)   -> 2m     (IR: 120.0 SECOND)
  Akt stimulation (5 min)     -> 5m     (IR: 300.0 SECOND)
  Fixation (10 min)           -> 10m    (IR: 600.0 SECOND)
  Permeabilisation (10 min)   -> 10m    (IR: 600.0 SECOND)
  Blocking (60 min)           -> 60m    (IR: 3600.0 SECOND)
  Primary antibody (720 min)  -> 720m   (IR: 43200.0 SECOND)
  Secondary antibody (2 h)    -> 120m   (IR: 7200.0 SECOND)

Issues resolved:
  1. Unicode error (UnicodeDecodeError at position 2598):
     Two UTF-8 degree symbols (0xC2 0xB0) in comment lines 9 and 11 of the ICC protocol
     summary replaced with ASCII hyphen. ANTLR4 FileStream requires strict 7-bit ASCII input.

  2. SSA version-2 undefined variable conflict in BB7_j:
     secondaryStained and aktSecStained were consumed (disposed/drained) in the BB2/BB3 and
     BB5/BB6 gate branches. Re-referencing them in BB7 caused the compiler to emit
     secondaryStained2[0] and aktSecStained2[0] -- undefined SSA names.
     Fix: Replaced mix(secondaryStained, aktSecStained) with a fresh dispense of
     WashBuffer2 as qcCarrier. In the physical experiment, the cellViabilityDetection gate
     is purely computational (CellProfiler on acquired images); the fluid operand is a
     BioScript structural requirement, not a wet-lab step.

BioScript abstractions:
  Passive dispensing    : Modelled as dispense N units + mix. The compiler treats N as a
                          volume scalar; no array elements are generated -- correct because
                          each VM receives the full merged volume.
  Concurrent VMs        : The physical device has 8 VMs; BioScript has no native spatial
                          parallelism. The PDGFR and Akt arms are encoded as sequential BB
                          blocks. For multi-VM or multi-condition runs, replicate the

  Antibody pre-mixing   : Primary and secondary antibodies are pre-mixed off-chip in

  Microarray scan       : Off-chip post-processing step; abstracted as detect

                          cellViabilityDetection on qcCarrier (fresh WashBuffer2 droplet).

protocol.title: Digital Microfluidic Immunocytochemistry in Single Cells (DISC)
protocol.platform: Digital Microfluidics (DMF) — electrowetting-on-dielectric, two-plate configuration
cell_lines: MDA-MB-231 (human breast cancer, triple-negative, hyperactive-responder analysis)
protocol.objective: Automated DMF-based cell culture, serum starvation, sub-second ligand stimulation, fixation, and immunocytochemistry (ICC) for quantitative single-cell phosphorylation profiling of adherent cells in situ

device.configuration: Two parallel plates separated by a spacer

bottom_plate.material: Chromium on glass (200 x 300 x 1.1 mm, Telic Co.)
bottom_plate.reservoir_electrodes: Included for reagent storage and waste removal
bottom_plate.hydrophobic_coating: Teflon-AF, ~200 nm (spin-coat, 1% w/w in FC-40, 2000 rpm, 60 s)

spacer.material: Double-sided tape (3M Scotch or 3M 9965 diagnostic tape)

virtual_microwell.formation: Passive dispensing — hydrophobic-hydrophilic interaction at ITO spot
virtual_microwell.cell_capacity: 150-300 cells per VM at 500,000 cells/mL seeding density

cell_culture.NIH3T3: DMEM + 10% calf serum (CS) + 100 U/mL pen G + 100 ug/mL strep
cell_culture.MCF7_MDA231: DMEM + 10% FBS + 100 U/mL pen G + 100 ug/mL strep

on_chip_media.culture_media: DMEM + 10% serum (CS or FBS) + 0.05% v/v Pluronic F-68 + antibiotics
on_chip_media.starving_media: DMEM + 0.5% serum (CS or FBS) + 0.05% v/v Pluronic F-68 + antibiotics
on_chip_media.pluronic_note: Pluronic F-68 included in all on-chip reagents to prevent droplet biofouling

fixation.reagent: 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) + 0.05% v/v Pluronic F-68 in DPBS

wash_buffers.WB1: 0.05% v/v Pluronic F-68 in DPBS (used after fixation)
wash_buffers.WB2: 0.05% v/v Brij 35 in DPBS (used after permeabilisation, blocking, and antibody steps)

blocking.reagent: 1% bovine non-fat dried milk + 0.05% v/v Brij 35 in DPBS

PDGFR_panel.pan_PDGFR_b: Mouse mAb, 1:50, CST sc-19995 (total PDGFR; Cy5 channel)

Akt_panel.pan_Akt: Mouse mAb, 1:50, CST 2920S (total Akt; Cy5 channel)

secondary_antibodies.anti_mouse_647: Anti-Mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 647 Fab2, 1:500, CST 4410S (total protein, Cy5 ch.)
secondary_antibodies.anti_rabbit_555: Anti-Rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 555 Fab2, 1:500, CST 4413S (phospho-protein, Cy3 ch.)

steps.name: Cell seeding and adhesion
steps.cell_line: NIH-3T3 (or MCF-7 / MDA-MB-231 for heterogeneity experiments)
steps.droplets: 3 x 900 nL CultureMedia + 3 x 900 nL cell suspension
steps.notes: Device inverted after seeding; cells settle by gravity onto hydrophilic ITO spots. 10^5 to 10^6 cells/mL yields 150-300 cells per VM (2.4 mm2).

steps.name: Serum starvation
steps.notes: Reduces basal PDGFR and Akt phosphorylation to unstimulated baseline before ligand addition.

steps.name: Serum-free rinse
steps.notes: Removes residual starving media. Two exchanges displace >99% of VM volume (Fig. 2b-d).

steps.name: PDGF-BB ligand stimulation
steps.shear_note: 0.5 dyn/cm2 — below 1 dyn/cm2 threshold for flow-mediated signalling (Supplementary Note 1). Tested: 75 back-and-forth movements, P=0.7188, no effect on Akt (Supplementary Fig. 8).

pulse_variants.single_bolus: Continuous PDGF-BB; fix at t=30-120 s (Fig. 5a)
pulse_variants.double_bolus: PDGF-BB at t=0; second PDGF-BB or vehicle at t=90 s (Fig. 5b)
pulse_variants.pulse_washaway: PDGF-BB for 3-40 s; wash with SerumFreeMedia; fix at 2-5 min (Fig. 6a/b/c)

steps.name: Fixation
steps.notes: Immediately follows stimulation (~1 s reagent swap). In time-series experiments, fixation is staggered across VMs so all are fixed simultaneously (paper M&M).

steps.name: Post-fixation wash
steps.notes: Removes fixative before permeabilisation.

steps.name: Permeabilisation
steps.notes: Required for intracellular antibody access. Essential for cytoplasmic/membrane pAkt S473 detection.

steps.name: Post-permeabilisation wash
steps.notes: Extended wash volume to fully remove Tween-20 before blocking.

steps.name: Blocking
steps.reagent: 1% non-fat dried milk + 0.05% Brij 35 in DPBS
steps.notes: Reduces non-specific antibody binding. Milk-based blocker compatible with both PDGFR and Akt antibody panels.

steps.name: Primary antibody incubation
steps.bioscript_note: Pre-mixed off-chip before DMF reservoir loading; encoded as sequential dispense + mix steps per arm.

steps.name: Post-primary antibody wash
steps.notes: Removes unbound primary antibodies.

steps.name: Secondary antibody incubation

reagents.anti_mouse_AF647: Fab2, 1:500, CST 4410S — detects total PDGFR or total Akt (Cy5 channel)

steps.notes: Pre-mixed off-chip in blocking solution. Top plate removed after this step, rinsed in 0.05% Tween-20/DPBS, rinsed in DI water, air-dried in dark.

steps.name: PDGFR phosphorylation detection and QC gate
steps.cell_identification: Otsu Global thresholding, 15-100 um diameter, two classes, 0.7 correction factor
steps.quantification: Fold change = (Cy3 phospho intensity) / (Cy5 total intensity), normalised to no-stimulation control on same device

steps.name: Akt S473 phosphorylation detection and QC gate
steps.operation: Full repeat of ICC pipeline (S0-S11) with 5 min stimulation; detect Akt S473

results_Akt.amplification_note: At 3.125 ng/mL PDGF (~22% receptor phosphorylation), Akt activation >70% — downstream signal is amplified
results_Akt.pulse_commitment: 10 s pulse of 3.125 ng/mL PDGF commits >32% of cells to Akt activation (Fig. 6b)
results_Akt.noise_filtering: 3 s pulse: transient Akt activation at 3-4 min deactivated by 5 min (Fig. 6c); consistent with enzymatic phosphorylation/dephosphorylation noise filtering

steps.name: Cell morphology and ICC quality QC gate
steps.operation: detect (CellProfiler computational gate on acquired images)
steps.qc_carrier: WashBuffer2 (1 x 900 nL fresh droplet; fluid operand required by BioScript detect statement; not a wet-lab step)
steps.hyperactive_responder_definition: p-Akt fold change > Q3 + 1.5 * IQR (JMP 10 outlier threshold)
steps.hyperactive_morphology: Elongated (higher eccentricity, lower form factor), more and closer neighbours vs normal cells (Supplementary Figs. 12-14)

signalling_pathway.name: PDGFR/PI3K/Akt
signalling_pathway.description: PDGF-BB binds PDGFR, which auto-phosphorylates (Y857, Y1021), recruiting PI3K. PI3K converts PI(4,5)P2 to PI(3,4,5)P3, which recruits Akt to the plasma membrane where PDK1/PDK2 phosphorylate it at S473. Downstream: proliferation, differentiation, metabolism, migration.
signalling_pathway.reference: Andrae et al. Genes Dev. 22:1276-1312 (2008); Park et al. J. Biol. Chem. 278:37064-37072 (2003)

cell_lines_used.NIH3T3: Validation of PDGFR and Akt dose-response and time-series (Figs. 3, 5, 6)
cell_lines_used.MCF7: Bulk and single-cell Akt response 0-5 min (Supplementary Fig. 9)

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.description: Cell seeding, adhesion, starvation, serum-free rinse, PDGF-BB stimulation, fixation, permeabilisation, blocking, dual primary antibody staining, wash, secondary antibody staining, detect PDGFR phosphorylation signal

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_2_t
basic_blocks.description: PDGFR phosphorylation detected above basal — dispose stained PDGFR VM

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_3_f
basic_blocks.description: No PDGFR phosphorylation — drain (reagent failure or zero stimulation)

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_4_j
basic_blocks.description: Dispose stimulusSignal; begin Akt arm ICC pipeline (separate VM, 5 min stimulation)

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_5_t
basic_blocks.description: Akt S473 phosphorylation detected — dispose stained Akt VM

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_6_f
basic_blocks.description: No Akt activation — drain (below commitment threshold or reagent failure)

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_7_j
basic_blocks.description: Dispose aktSignal; dispense fresh qcCarrier; run cellViabilityDetection QC gate

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_8_t
basic_blocks.description: Valid cell count and S/B ratio — ICC run accepted

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_9_f
basic_blocks.description: Insufficient cells or staining failure — ICC run rejected

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_10_j
basic_blocks.description: Dispose immunoSignal. Experiment ends. Top plate removed for microarray scanning and CellProfiler analysis.

bioscript_compiler_notes.ir_output: ng2015_DISC_dmf.ir
bioscript_compiler_notes.duration_units: All durations in s or m only (BioScript does not support h token)

known_issues_resolved.unicode_error: Two UTF-8 degree symbols (0xC2 0xB0) in comments replaced with ASCII hyphen; ANTLR4 FileStream requires 7-bit ASCII
known_issues_resolved.SSA_version_conflict: secondaryStained and aktSecStained consumed in BB2/BB5 gates; BB7 previously re-mixed them causing SSA version-2 undefined vars. Fixed by dispensing fresh qcCarrier (WashBuffer2) as detect operand in BB7.
known_issues_resolved.passive_dispense_array: Multi-unit dispense (e.g. dispense 6 units) used for all multi-drop steps; avoids array-indexing compiler failure documented in moazami reference

bioscript_abstractions.passive_dispensing: Modelled as dispense N units + mix; compiler treats N as volume scalar
bioscript_abstractions.concurrent_VMs: 8 physical VMs encoded sequentially (BioScript has no native spatial parallelism); PDGFR and Akt arms are sequential BBs
bioscript_abstractions.off_chip_antibody_premix: Primary and secondary antibodies pre-mixed off-chip; encoded as dispense + mix per component before VM application
bioscript_abstractions.microarray_scan: Abstracted as detect phosphorylationDetection; scanner is off-chip post-processing step
bioscript_abstractions.cellprofiler_gate: Abstracted as detect cellViabilityDetection on qcCarrier; purely computational in wet-lab but requires fluid operand in BioScript

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Digital Microfluidic Platform for the Detection of Rubella Infection and Immunity: A Proof of Concept
Source Link  : https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/ClinChemV61I2.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1373/clinchem.2014.232181
Journal      : Clinical Chemistry, 2015, Vol. 61, No. 2, pp. 420-429
Platform     : Digital microfluidics (DMF), two-plate, air-filled, with motorised PMT and magnetic lens assembly


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a shoebox-sized DMF immunoassay platform for the detection of rubella
virus (RV)-specific IgG and IgM antibodies from patient serum, plasma, or whole blood. The
system is motivated by the need for decentralised diagnostics in resource-limited settings to
prevent congenital rubella syndrome (CRS): 100,000 infants are born with CRS each year, and
rural-to-laboratory transport for standard centralised testing is often cost-prohibitive.

Two protocols are encoded in sequence on the same DMF device and .bs file:
  1. RV IgG immunoassay (7-step indirect ELISA): detects immunity or past/current infection.
     Clinical cutoff: 10 IU/mL. LOD: 0.03 IU/mL; LOQ: 0.1 IU/mL.
     Run time: ~25 min per quadruplicate set. Intraassay CVs: 0.3-6.5%.
  2. RV IgM immunoassay (7-step indirect ELISA + on-chip IgG blocking pretreatment):
     the critical test for diagnosing active rubella infection and identifying pregnancies
     at risk for CRS. Run time: ~35 min per quadruplicate set. Intraassay CVs: 1.5-13.4%.

Both assays use rubella-virus-coated paramagnetic microparticles for analyte capture,
HRP-conjugated detection antibodies for signal transduction, and SuperSignal ELISA Femto
chemiluminescent substrate (H2O2 + luminol-enhancer) for readout. Signal is detected by an
integrated motorised PMT (photomultiplier tube); readout is in RLU (relative light units)
over a 10 s integration window.

Diagnostic performance was evaluated against 25 plasma/serum samples from the SeraCare
PTR201 commercial mixed-titer performance panel, using Abbott EIA as the reference standard.
Both assays achieved 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity (AUC = 1.00 for each).


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Configuration  : Two-plate DMF (top plate ground + bottom plate electrode array); air-filled gap.
Gap            : ~140 um between top and bottom plates.
Instrument     : ~7 x 9 x 12 inches (shoebox-sized); computer-controlled via DropBot.
Bottom plate   : 80 actuation electrodes (2.54 x 2.54 mm each); reservoir electrodes for
                 sample/reagent storage and waste removal; chromium electrode layer + insulator
                 + Teflon-AF hydrophobic coating on glass substrate.
Top plate      : ITO ground electrode + Teflon-AF hydrophobic coating on glass.
Unit droplet   : ~900 nL (electrode area x 140 um gap).
Actuation      : 80-100 V_rms, 10 kHz sine wave; Pogo pin interface (90 pins);
                 controlled by DropBot (open-source DMF automation system).

Magnetic lens  : Motorised neodymium magnet assembly.
                 Active position: ~150 um below device; immobilisation force: ~600 uN.
                 Inactive position: 3.8 cm below device (allows droplet resuspension).
                 Minimum release threshold: ~500 uN (exceeds droplet surface tension).
                 Function: concentrates particles into pellet in the separation zone;
                 deactivation allows a fresh droplet to be mixed over the pellet to
                 resuspend particles for subsequent reagent incubation steps.

PMT detector   : Motorised; positioned a few hundred um above device droplet centre when active;
                 5 cm above when inactive (LED + webcam used for droplet monitoring).
                 PMT protection: 2 position sensors, shutter, light-tight enclosure grooves.
                 Integration: 10 s mean signal; output in RLU.
                 Advantage: no excitation source, filters, or lenses required.

Fabrication    : University of Toronto Nanofabrication Centre cleanroom.


REAGENTS
--------
Particles        : RV-coated paramagnetic microparticles (Abbott Architect rubella kit);
                   pre-washed 2x in Superblock, resuspended at ~10x stock (1.5e8 particles/mL).
Wash buffer      : Custom DMF-compatible formulation + 0.05% Pluronic L64.
Conjugate diluent: Custom DMF-compatible formulation + 0.05% Pluronic L64.
HRP conjugate    : (Protocol 1) HRP-conjugated goat polyclonal antihuman IgG, 21 ng/mL.
                   (Protocol 2) HRP-conjugated goat antihuman IgM, 23 ng/mL.
Substrate        : SuperSignal ELISA Femto (Thermo Fischer Scientific):
                   stable peroxide (H2O2) + luminol-enhancer; 900 nL each.
Pretreatment     : Goat antihuman IgG (Abbott Architect IgM pretreatment reagent, 3x dilution
                   in conjugate diluent); 900 nL per IgM assay.
Sample diluent   : Dulbecco PBS + 4% BSA; all samples pre-diluted 10x off-chip before loading.
Pluronic additive: 0.05% Pluronic L64 added to all on-chip reagents; prevents protein
                   adsorption and cross-contamination in the air-filled DMF device.
Calibrators      : RV IgG: 0, 5, 10, 15, 75, 250 IU/mL (Abbott Architect).
                   RV IgM cutoff: Cal 1 (Abbott Architect); RF IgM content 27.0 IU/mL.
Performance panel: SeraCare PTR201-01-25 (25 plasma/serum samples; collected 1994-1995).


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

PROTOCOL 1 | RV IgG IMMUNOASSAY (7 steps, ~25 min per quadruplicate)

Step 1 | Particle dispense and magnetic separation
  Reagents : VirusCoatedParticles
  Volume   : 1.8 uL (2 units); 1.5e8 particles/mL in Superblock
  Operation: Dispense from reservoir; magnetic lens activated (~150 um below device, ~600 uN);
             particles pellet in separation zone; Superblock diluent moved to waste.
  Duration : ~5 s
  Notes    : Particle pellet retained on-chip; resuspended in next step.

Step 2 | Sample incubation
  Reagents : SampleIgG (pre-diluted 10x in DPBS/4% BSA off-chip)
  Volume   : 1.8 uL (2 units)
  Operation: Dispense; deliver to particle pellet; mix in circular motion 3 min.
             RV IgG from sample binds RV-coated particle surface.
             Magnetic lens re-activated; supernatant disposed.
  Duration : 3 min (180 s; IR: 180.0 SECOND)

Step 3 | First wash cycle x4
  Reagents : WashBuffer
  Volume   : 4 x 1.8 uL (4 x 2 units)
  Operation: 4 sequential wash steps. Each: dispense fresh buffer droplet; deliver to pellet;
             mix; magnetic lens activated; supernatant disposed.
             Removes unbound sample antibody and non-specific proteins.
  Duration : 30 s per wash (4 x 30 s; IR: 30.0 SECOND each)

Step 4 | HRP conjugate incubation
  Reagents : HRPConjugateIgG (21 ng/mL HRP-conjugated goat polyclonal antihuman IgG)
  Volume   : 1.8 uL (2 units)
  Operation: Dispense; deliver to particle pellet; mix 2 min.
             HRP-anti-IgG binds RV IgG captured on particles (sandwich immunocomplex).
             Magnetic lens re-activated; unbound conjugate disposed.
  Duration : 2 min (120 s; IR: 120.0 SECOND)

Step 5 | Second wash cycle x4
  Reagents : WashBuffer
  Volume   : 4 x 1.8 uL (4 x 2 units)
  Operation: Identical to Step 3. Removes excess unbound HRP conjugate before substrate.
  Duration : 30 s per wash (4 x 30 s)

Step 6 | Substrate addition, reaction, and chemiluminescent detection
  Reagents : H2O2 (stable peroxide), LuminolEnhancer (SuperSignal ELISA Femto)
  Volume   : 900 nL each (1 unit each)
  Operation: Dispense H2O2 and luminol-enhancer as separate 1-unit droplets; merge (5 s mix);
             deliver substrate mix to particle pellet; mix 2 min. HRP catalyses luminol
             oxidation in H2O2; photons collected by motorised PMT over 10 s.
             Signal reported as RLU; normalised to cutoff calibrator (s/co).
  Substrate mix duration : 5 s
  Reaction duration      : 2 min (120 s)
  Detection duration     : 10 s
  Detection module       : rvIgGDetection
  Interpretation:
    s/co >= 1.0    -> positive  (immune to rubella)
    s/co 0.69-0.99 -> equivocal (gray zone)
    s/co < 0.69    -> negative  (susceptible to rubella)

Step 7 | Diagnostic gate (BB2 / BB3)
  Branch pass (BB2): igGSignal > 0 -> dispose(igGReaction); patient IgG-positive.
  Branch fail (BB3): igGSignal <= 0 -> drain(igGReaction); patient IgG-negative/equivocal.
  Join (BB4): dispose(igGSignal); Protocol 2 begins.


PROTOCOL 2 | RV IgM IMMUNOASSAY + ON-CHIP IgG BLOCKING (7 steps + pretreatment, ~35 min)

Step 8 | On-chip sample pretreatment (IgG blocking)
  Reagents : SampleIgM (pre-diluted 10x in DPBS/4% BSA off-chip),
             PretreatmentReagent (goat antihuman IgG, 3x dilution in conjugate diluent)
  Volumes  : 1.8 uL sample (2 units) + 900 nL pretreatment (1 unit)
  Operation: Dispense both; merge on-chip; mix 7 min.
  Duration : 7 min (420 s; IR: 420.0 SECOND)
  Purpose  : Exogenous antihuman IgG blocks two interference sources in the IgM assay:
               (i)  Endogenous RV IgG competing for particle binding sites
                    -> prevents false negatives (Fig. 3A panel 2).
               (ii) RV IgG / RF IgM immunocomplexes binding non-specifically to particles
                    -> prevents false positives from rheumatoid factor (Fig. 3A panel 3).
  Evidence : Pretreatment significantly suppresses nonspecific signal in IgG+IgM samples
             (P=0.0003); pure IgG (P=0.5) and pure IgM (P=0.6) samples unaffected (Fig. 3B).
             RF IgM in RV IgG calibrators: 1.4-1.85 IU/mL (low).
             RF IgM in RV IgM Cal 1: 27.0 IU/mL (high; pretreatment critical for cutoff use).

Step 9 | Particle dispense and magnetic separation
  Reagents : VirusCoatedParticles
  Volume   : 1.8 uL (2 units); identical stock as Protocol 1.
  Operation: Identical to Protocol 1 Step 1.
  Duration : ~5 s

Step 10 | Pretreated sample incubation
  Reagents : igMPretreatedSample (from Step 8), igMParticles (from Step 9)
  Volume   : (combined pretreated sample droplet delivered to particle pellet)
  Operation: Mix 3 min. RV IgM from pretreated sample binds RV-coated particles;
             IgG/RF IgM competition blocked. Magnetic lens re-activated; supernatant disposed.
  Duration : 3 min (180 s)

Step 11 | First wash cycle x4
  Reagents : WashBuffer
  Volume   : 4 x 1.8 uL (4 x 2 units)
  Operation: Identical to Protocol 1 Step 3. Removes unbound antibody and pretreatment components.
  Duration : 30 s per wash (4 x 30 s)

Step 12 | HRP conjugate incubation
  Reagents : HRPConjugateIgM (23 ng/mL HRP-conjugated goat antihuman IgM)
  Volume   : 1.8 uL (2 units)
  Operation: Dispense; deliver to particle pellet; mix 2 min.
             IgM-specific conjugate; distinguishes this step from Protocol 1 Step 4.
             HRP-anti-IgM binds selectively to RV IgM on particles.
             Magnetic lens re-activated; unbound conjugate disposed.
  Duration : 2 min (120 s)

Step 13 | Second wash cycle x4
  Reagents : WashBuffer
  Volume   : 4 x 1.8 uL (4 x 2 units)
  Operation: Identical to Step 11. Removes excess HRP-anti-IgM before substrate.
  Duration : 30 s per wash (4 x 30 s)

Step 14 | Substrate addition, reaction, and chemiluminescent detection
  Reagents : H2O2 (stable peroxide), LuminolEnhancer (SuperSignal ELISA Femto)
  Volume   : 900 nL each (1 unit each)
  Operation: Identical to Protocol 1 Step 6.
             Cutoff defined by Cal 1 (s/co = 1); s/co = mean signal / mean Cal 1 signal.
  Substrate mix duration : 5 s
  Reaction duration      : 2 min (120 s)
  Detection duration     : 10 s
  Detection module       : rvIgMDetection
  Interpretation:
    s/co >= 1.0    -> positive  (active rubella infection; CRS risk if pregnant)
    s/co 0.75-0.99 -> equivocal (gray zone; retest required per WHO guidance)
    s/co < 0.75    -> negative  (no evidence of acute rubella infection)

Step 15 | Diagnostic gate (BB5 / BB6)
  Branch pass (BB5): igMSignal > 0 -> dispose(igMReaction); active rubella infection confirmed.
  Branch fail (BB6): igMSignal <= 0 -> drain(igMReaction); IgM-negative/equivocal.
  Terminal (BB7): dispose(igMSignal); NOP. Experiment ends.

EQUIVOCAL NOTE: Equivocal results (s/co in gray zone) are interpreted as positive for
sensitivity/specificity calculations per WHO guidance. In clinical practice, all positive or
equivocal patients are retested to confirm final diagnosis. 2 of 25 panel samples produced
positive-equivocal discrepancies between DMF and Abbott EIA at s/co values near the cutoff;
attributed to assay variability (CV ~15%) and 20-year sample age. Final diagnostic accuracy
remained 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity for both assays.


ON-CHIP DILUTION (SUPPLEMENTARY SUB-PROTOCOL)
----------------------------------------------
For patient samples exceeding the linear range (>250 IU/mL) or for whole blood compatibility:

Method   : Serial 2x on-chip dilution.
  Step 1 : Dispense 1 sample droplet (1.8 uL) + 1 diluent droplet (1.8 uL); merge and mix.
  Step 2 : Split pooled droplet into 2 equal sub-droplets.
  Step 3 : Store one sub-droplet; repeat Steps 1-3 with the other.
  4 iterations yield: 2x, 4x, 8x, 16x diluted droplets (125, 62.5, 31.3, 15.6 IU/mL
  from a 250 IU/mL sample).

Blood matrix: Interassay CVs marginally higher for blood samples (10-15%) vs standard (6-9%).
  At 1/4 and 1/8 blood dilutions: signal significantly different from calibrator (P < 0.05).
  At 1/16 and 1/32: indistinguishable from calibrator (P > 0.05).
  Conclusion: 1/16 or 1/32 blood dilution removes matrix interference without reducing
              analyte below LOQ.

BioScript note: Not encoded in this .bs file. BioScript has no loop/repeat construct;
  serial dilution steps would need to be hardcoded per iteration in a separate .bs file.


ASSAY PERFORMANCE SUMMARY
--------------------------
                      RV IgG              RV IgM
LOD (IU/mL)          0.03                --
LOQ (IU/mL)          0.1                 --
Clinical cutoff       10 IU/mL            Cal 1 (s/co = 1)
Dynamic range         ~2 orders magnitude  --
Intraassay CV (%)     0.3-6.5             1.5-13.4
Run time (4 assays)   ~25 min             ~35 min
Parallel assays       4 (aliquoted)       4 (aliquoted)
Sensitivity (95% CI)  100% (98.6-100%)    100% (97.4-100%)
Specificity (95% CI)  100% (95.5-100%)    100% (98.4-100%)
AUC (ROC)             1.00                1.00
Reference standard    Abbott EIA          Abbott EIA
Panel                 SeraCare PTR201     SeraCare PTR201


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file  : ng2015_dmf_rubella_immunoassay.bs
Compiler        : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output       : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG             : ng2015_dmf_rubella_immunoassay_main_dag.dot
Duration units  : All durations in seconds (s) or minutes (m); both supported by compiler.
                  7m pretreatment  -> IR: 420.0 SECOND
                  3m incubations   -> IR: 180.0 SECOND
                  2m incubations   -> IR: 120.0 SECOND
                  30s washes       -> IR: 30.0 SECOND
                  10s detection    -> IR: 10.0 SECOND
                  5s substrate mix -> IR: 5.0 SECOND
Modules         : rvIgGDetection, rvIgMDetection
Manifests       : VirusCoatedParticles, WashBuffer, HRPConjugateIgG, HRPConjugateIgM,
                  H2O2, LuminolEnhancer, PretreatmentReagent, SampleIgG, SampleIgM,
                  SampleIgGplusIgM, DiluentPBSBSA, PluronicL64
Volume encoding : 1.8 uL reagent/sample droplets = 2 units (2 x 900 nL actuation electrodes)
                  900 nL substrate/pretreatment droplets = 1 unit
CFG note        : IR block ordering (bsbbif_2_t listed before main) is compiler serialisation
                  artefact; main is confirmed as entry node (node 1) in .dot output.
                  True branches fall through to join implicitly; only false branches carry
                  explicit jump instructions. This is standard lilott8/BioScript IR behaviour,
                  consistent with samlali and moazami reference files.
Particle sep    : Initial self-mix (igGParticles with igGParticles) abstracts the magnetic
                  separation / diluent removal step; accepted by compiler without error.
Scope note      : On-chip serial dilution sub-protocol not encoded in this .bs file
                  (no loop construct in BioScript). A separate .bs file is required.

steps.name: RV IgG — particle dispense and magnetic separation
steps.operation: dispense + mix (abstracts magnetic separation; supernatant disposed)
steps.notes: Magnetic lens active (~150 um below device, 600 uN); particles pellet in separation zone. Diluent (Superblock) moved to waste. Particle pellet retained on-chip for subsequent steps.

steps.name: RV IgG — sample incubation
steps.notes: Sample pre-diluted 10x in DPBS/4% BSA off-chip before loading. RV IgG from sample binds RV-coated particle surface during 3 min circular mixing. Magnetic lens re-activated; supernatant disposed.

steps.name: RV IgG — first wash cycle x4
steps.notes: Removes unbound sample antibody and non-specific proteins. Each wash: buffer droplet moved over pellet, mixed, magnetic lens activated, supernatant disposed. 4 sequential iterations.

steps.name: RV IgG — HRP conjugate incubation
steps.conjugate: HRP-conjugated goat polyclonal antihuman IgG, 21 ng/mL
steps.notes: HRP-anti-IgG binds to sample RV IgG captured on particles, forming sandwich immunocomplex. Magnetic lens re-activated; unbound conjugate disposed.

steps.name: RV IgG — second wash cycle x4
steps.notes: Removes excess unbound HRP conjugate before substrate addition. Identical procedure to S3.

steps.name: RV IgG — substrate addition, reaction, and detection
steps.readout: RLU integrated over 10 s by motorised PMT
steps.notes: H2O2 and luminol-enhancer dispensed as separate 1-unit (900 nL) droplets, merged, then delivered to particle pellet. HRP catalyses luminol oxidation; photons collected by PMT. No excitation source, filters, or lenses required.

steps.name: RV IgG — diagnostic gate

pass.interpretation: RV IgG detected; s/co >= 1.0; patient immune to rubella (natural or vaccine-acquired)

fail.interpretation: RV IgG not detected; s/co < 0.69; patient susceptible to rubella

steps.notes: Both branches converge at BB4 (igGJoin). igGSignal disposed at join before IgM protocol begins.

steps.pretreatment_reagent: Goat antihuman IgG (3x dilution of Abbott Architect IgM pretreatment reagent in conjugate diluent)
purpose: Blocks endogenous RV IgG from competing for binding sites on RV-coated particles (prevents false negatives; Fig. 3A panel 2)
Blocks RV IgG/RF IgM immunocomplexes from binding non-specifically to particles (prevents false positives from RF IgM; Fig. 3A panel 3)

statistical_evidence.conclusion: Pretreatment significantly suppresses nonspecific signal only in combined IgG+IgM samples (P=0.0003); pure IgG or IgM samples unaffected

steps.notes: Emulates Abbott Architect rubella IgM assay pretreatment procedure. 7 min on-chip mixing. Pretreated sample then delivered to particle pellet in S9.

steps.name: RV IgM — particle dispense and magnetic separation
steps.operation: dispense + mix (abstracts magnetic separation; supernatant disposed)
steps.notes: Identical particle stock and procedure as Protocol 1 S1. Runs concurrently with or immediately after pretreatment step.

steps.name: RV IgM — pretreated sample incubation
steps.notes: Pretreated sample droplet delivered to particle pellet. RV IgM antibodies bind RV-coated particles; IgG/RF IgM competition blocked by pretreatment. Magnetic lens re-activated; supernatant disposed.

steps.name: RV IgM — first wash cycle x4
steps.notes: Identical to Protocol 1 S3. Removes unbound antibody and pretreatment components.

steps.name: RV IgM — HRP conjugate incubation
steps.notes: IgM-specific conjugate; distinguishes from Protocol 1 S4 (antihuman IgG). HRP-anti-IgM binds selectively to RV IgM captured on particles. Magnetic lens re-activated; unbound conjugate disposed.

steps.name: RV IgM — second wash cycle x4
steps.notes: Removes excess HRP-anti-IgM before substrate addition. Identical to S11.

steps.readout: RLU integrated over 10 s by motorised PMT
steps.cutoff_calibrator: RV IgM Cal 1 (Abbott Architect); defines s/co = 1 threshold

interpretation.positive: s/co >= 1.0 (active rubella infection; patient at risk of CRS if pregnant)

steps.notes: Cal 1 contains 27.0 IU/mL RF IgM; on-chip pretreatment (S8) is essential for accurate cutoff calibration with this reagent (Fig. 3C).

steps.name: RV IgM — diagnostic gate

pass.interpretation: RV IgM detected; s/co >= 1.0; active rubella infection confirmed

fail.interpretation: RV IgM not detected; no evidence of acute rubella infection

steps.equivocal_handling: Equivocal results (s/co 0.75-0.99) interpreted as positive per WHO guidance; patient retested to confirm. 2/25 panel samples produced positive-equivocal discrepancies at s/co near cutoff; attributed to assay variability (CV ~15%) and sample age (~20 years).
steps.notes: Both branches converge at BB7 (finalCleanup). igMSignal disposed at terminal.

on_chip_dilution.description: Serial 2x on-chip dilution sub-protocol for samples exceeding the linear range (>250 IU/mL) or for whole blood matrix
on_chip_dilution.method: Iterative 3-step sequence: (1) merge 1 sample droplet + 1 diluent droplet, (2) split into 2 sub-droplets, (3) store one, repeat with other. 4 iterations yield 2x, 4x, 8x, 16x diluted droplets.

blood_matrix_results.conclusion: Dilution to 1/16 or 1/32 removes blood matrix interference (P > 0.05) without reducing analyte below LOQ

on_chip_dilution.bioscript_note: Not encoded in this .bs file. BioScript has no loop/repeat construct; serial dilution requires hardcoded iterations and is best encoded in a separate .bs file.

diagnostic_accuracy.panel: SeraCare PTR201 (25 samples); reference standard: Abbott EIA
diagnostic_accuracy.blinding: Operators blinded to reference result until all data collected

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Development of Digital Microfluidic Heterogeneous Immunoassays
Author       : Alphonsus Hon-Chung Ng
Degree       : Doctor of Philosophy
Institution  : Institute of Biomaterials and Biomedical Engineering, University of Toronto
Year         : 2015
Supervisor   : Prof. Aaron Wheeler
Source Link  : https://utoronto.scholaris.ca/server/api/core/bitstreams/f61c3b5c-993d-4f5e-970d-2bd5634257ee/content
DOI          : N/A
Platform     : Two-plate digital microfluidics (DMF / EWOD), oil-free, air-surrounded droplets


OVERVIEW
--------
This BioScript file encodes two protocols from the PhD thesis of Alphonsus H.C. Ng (University
of Toronto, 2015), which describes the development and validation of digital microfluidic (DMF)
methods for heterogeneous immunoassays. DMF electrostatically manipulates discrete droplets
(pL to uL) on a hydrophobic electrode array without the use of enclosed microchannels or
oil carrier fluid -- a key innovation of this work.

Protocol 1 (Chapter 2) introduces the first oil-free DMF particle-based immunoassay, using a
novel "supernatant separation" washing technique and demonstrating both non-competitive
(thyroid-stimulating hormone, TSH) and competitive (17beta-estradiol, E2) immunoassay modes.
Chapter 3 extends this with a fully automated platform (90 Pogo pin interface, integrated PMT,
magnetic lens) and DOE optimization. Chapter 4 applies the platform to infectious disease
diagnosis (rubella virus IgG and IgM), demonstrating 100% diagnostic sensitivity and specificity.

Protocol 2 (Chapter 5) introduces DISC (Digital Microfluidic Immunocytochemistry in Single-
Cells), which automates all sample preparation steps for in-situ adherent cell immunoassays with
<4 s temporal resolution. Using virtual microwells formed by passive dispensing over hydrophilic
lift-off spots, DISC enables single-cell phosphoprotein quantitation by laser scanning cytometry.

The BioScript encodes representative arms of both protocols and two QC gates per protocol,
yielding 13 basic blocks (BB1-BB13) and 4 if/else gates in the compiled IR/CFG.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Configuration : Two-plate EWOD; patterned chromium bottom-plate + unpatterned ITO top-plate
Spacer        : Two pieces of Scotch double-sided tape (3M); total 180 um gap
Bottom plate  : Chromium electrodes (200 nm) on glass (2 in x 3 in x 1.1 mm, Telic Co.)
                Dielectric: ~7 um Parylene C (vapor deposition)
                Hydrophobic coating: ~200 nm Teflon-AF (1% w/w in FC-40, 2000 rpm, 60 s; post-baked 165 C, 10 min)
                Fabrication: photolithography + CR-4 wet etching at ECTI/TNFC cleanroom, U of T
Top plate     : Unpatterned ITO-coated glass; ~200 nm Teflon-AF
                Chapter 5 modification: hydrophilic lift-off spots (1.75 mm diameter, 4.4 mm pitch)
                by S1811 photoresist fluorocarbon lift-off on ITO (UV expose, develop, Teflon-AF
                spin-coat, acetone liftoff ~5-10 s, exposing ITO hydrophilic pads)

Chapter 2 device:
  - 116 actuation electrodes (2.25 x 2.25 mm ea.); 10 reservoir electrodes (4.5 x 4.5 mm ea.)
  - Interdigitated electrode borders (140 um peak-to-peak sinusoids); inter-electrode gaps 30-80 um
  - Electrode pitch 2.25 mm aligns to 96/384/1536 well-plate format
  - Unit droplet: ~800 nL; reservoir droplet: ~3.5 uL; 4 assay regions + 1 detection region

Chapter 3/4 device:
  - 80 actuation electrodes (2.2 x 2.2 mm Ch3 / 2.54 x 2.54 mm Ch4)
  - 8 sample + 4 waste reservoirs (Ch3); unit droplet ~800 nL (Ch3) / ~900 nL (Ch4)

Chapter 5 (DISC) device:
  - 80 actuation electrodes (2.2 x 2.2 mm); unit droplet ~900 nL
  - Top plate: 8 lift-off spots (1.75 mm diameter, 4.4 mm pitch); virtual microwell ~400 nL

Actuation:
  - Chapter 2: ~150 Vrms, 10 kHz (function generator + TREK amplifier)
  - Chapters 3-5: 80-100 Vrms, 10 kHz sine wave (DropBot + Arduino HV switching; 90 Pogo pin interface)
  - Droplet mixing: circular shuttling across 4 electrodes (unit droplets) or more (larger volumes)

Magnet system:
  - Chapter 2: NdFeB disc (5/8 in dia x 1/4 in, N48, 15.3 lb pull; mu_r=1.05, Br=1.38 T)
    Positioned 1.40 mm below device; manual movement via stripwell manifold + metal clip
    Minimum density for separation: ~3.0e8 particles/mL; estimated force ~470 uN
  - Chapter 3/4: Motorized magnetic lens; >600 uN; up to 8 simultaneous separations;
    deactivated by positioning 3.8 cm below device for resuspension

Detection:
  - Chapter 2: PHERAstar well-plate reader (BMG Labtech); LUM module; gain 3600; focal height 8.6 mm
  - Chapter 3/4: Integrated motorized PMT (CT2 counter timer); LOD 4.88 uU/mL HRP; CV 0.56-9.3%
  - Chapter 5: Axon GenePix 4000B microarray scanner; 532 nm + 635 nm; 5 um resolution;
    PMT 500 V; CellProfiler (Otsu Global, 15-100 um objects, phospho/total protein ratio per cell)


PROTOCOL 1: DMF MAGNETIC PARTICLE IMMUNOASSAY (Chapter 2)
----------------------------------------------------------
Analytes       : Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH, non-competitive sandwich immunoassay)
                 17beta-estradiol (E2, competitive immunoassay)
Anti-fouling   : Pluronic L64 (BASF Corp.), 0.05% v/v in all on-chip reagents
                 Enables air-surrounded droplet movement; prevents protein adsorption

Reagents:
  TSH particles  : Mouse monoclonal Anti-beta TSH coated paramagnetic particles
                   (Abbott ARCHITECT kit 7K62); pre-processed: washed 2x DI water,
                   blocked with 3% NFDM/0.01% Tween-20 buffer pH 7.8 (1 h), washed 2x DI water,
                   resuspended at ~3.0e8 particles/mL in DMF-compatible particle diluent (pH 10:
                   Tris-base 6.1 g/L, NaCl 5.8 g/L, Sucrose 136 g/L, BSA 1% w/v,
                   Thimerosal 0.05% w/v, L64 0.05% v/v)
  E2 particles   : Rabbit monoclonal Anti-E2 coated particles (Abbott ARCHITECT kit 7K72);
                   same prep as TSH but no NFDM blocking step
  TSH conjugate  : Anti-TSH-HRP (goat polyclonal, Fitzgerald Industries), 2 ug/mL in conjugate
                   diluent (pH 7.4: Tris-Base 1.9 g/L, Tris-HCl 13.2 g/L, NaCl 17.5 g/L,
                   BSA 1% w/v, cold fish gelatin 0.1% w/v, Thimerosal 0.05% w/v, L64 0.05% v/v)
  E2 conjugate   : E2-HRP conjugated via 6-CMO (BiosPacific), 1 ug/mL in conjugate diluent
                   (optimal conc. determined empirically; higher conc. loses dynamic range)
  Substrate      : SuperSignal ELISA Femto (Thermo Fisher Scientific): H2O2 + luminol/enhancer
  Wash buffer    : pH 7.7; Tris-base 0.35 g/L, Tris-HCl 1.10 g/L, NaCl 8.367 g/L, L64 0.05% v/v

Supernatant Separation Washing (key innovation vs prior serial dilution method):
  Mechanism      : Magnet positions pellet on device surface; supernatant droplet actuated to waste;
                   magnet removed; fresh wash buffer droplet passed over pellet; circularly mixed
                   (4 electrodes) to resuspend particles
  Efficiency     : >98% unbound reagent removal by wash 2 (benchmark)
                   Serial dilution requires 6+ washes for same benchmark; 10-18 washes previously
  Minimum density: ~3.0e8 particles/mL for successful separation
  Magnetic force : ~470 uN (COMSOL FEA; pellet 7.75 mm from magnet bottom-edge origin)
  Residual liquid: ~5% of origin droplet retained by hydrophilic particles; resuspend immediately

Eight-step On-Chip Immunoassay Protocol:
  Step 1 | Particle dispense and separation
    Volume     : 800 nL unit droplet from reservoir
    Operation  : Supernatant separation (magnet on; diluent actuated to waste; magnet off)
  
  Step 2 | Sample incubation
    Volume     : 3 unit droplets (3 x 800 nL = 2.4 uL)
    Duration   : 6 min at room temperature with continuous circular mixing
    Notes      : 3 droplets chosen for optimal signal vs droplet reliability; evaporation <5%
                 over 30 min (measured by capacitance); TSH: analyte binds Anti-beta TSH particles;
                 E2: analyte competes with E2-HRP for Anti-E2 binding sites
  
  Step 3 | Wash x4 in wash buffer
    Volume     : 4 x 800 nL; supernatant separation each time
  
  Step 4 | Conjugate incubation
    Volume     : 800 nL
    Duration   : 2 min
    TSH        : Anti-TSH-HRP binds TSH captured on particles (non-competitive)
    E2         : E2-HRP binds Anti-E2 sites not occupied by analyte (competitive)
  
  Step 5 | Wash x4 in wash buffer + wash x2 in H2O2
    Notes      : 2x H2O2 wash developed in place of pre-mixing H2O2 + luminol off-chip;
                 pre-mixing caused high inter-assay variability
  
  Step 6 | H2O2 incubation
    Volume     : 800 nL; duration: 2 min
    Notes      : Particles moved to detection region (electrode array aligned to 96-well plate)
  
  Step 7 | Luminol/enhancer merge
    Volume     : 800 nL; on-chip mix (immediately before detection)
    Notes      : Activates HRP-catalyzed chemiluminescence
  
  Step 8 | Chemiluminescence detection
    Duration   : 1 min (signal saturates at 1 min; stable endpoint)
    Settings   : PHERAstar LUM module; focal height 8.6 mm; gain 3600;
                 device taped to 96-well Stripwell plate

Performance vs well-plate ELISA:
  TSH LOD (absolute)   : 2.0 nIU (DMF) vs 3.0 nIU (well-plate)
  TSH LOD (conc.)      : 0.83 uIU/mL (DMF) vs 0.06 uIU/mL (well-plate)
  E2 LOD (absolute)    : 50 fg (DMF) vs 152 fg (well-plate)
  E2 LOD (conc.)       : 21 pg/mL (DMF) vs 6.1 pg/mL (well-plate)
  TSH CV               : 9-21% (DMF) vs 2-13% (well-plate)
  E2 CV                : 5-14% (DMF) vs 4-12% (well-plate)
  Sample volume        : 2.4 uL (DMF) vs 50 uL (well-plate)
  Incubation time      : 6 min (DMF) vs 60 min (well-plate)
  Reagent consumption  : ~100-fold reduction (11.2 uL DMF vs 1.2 mL well-plate total)
  Clinical utility     : TSH detects hypothyroidism (>3.0 uIU/mL); E2 screens ovarian cancer (>20 pg/mL)

Optimized Platform (Chapter 3):
  Hardware     : 90 Pogo pin interface + DropBot automation; integrated motorized PMT;
                 magnetic lens (up to 8 simultaneous separations; precise motor positioning)
  DOE analysis : 3-level full factorial; factors: analyte conc., sample incubation time, volume
                 Optimal: 5 sample droplets (4.0 uL), 3 min incubation
  TSH LOD      : 0.15 uIU/mL (screens hyperthyroidism, TSH < 0.3 uIU/mL)
  TSH CV       : 6-10%; measurement procedure: wash buffer removed post-wash; particles in
                 luminol-H2O2 mixed 4 min; stable signal window ~1 min for sequential reading

Rubella Virus Immunoassay (Chapter 4):
  Analytes     : RV IgG (indirect ELISA, 7 steps) and RV IgM (+ on-chip IgG blocking pretreatment)
  Particles    : Rubella virus-coated paramagnetic particles (Abbott ARCHITECT); 1.5e8/mL in Superblock
  IgG protocol : 7 steps; 4 parallel assays; ~25 min per run
                 Step i: particles dispense; Step ii: sample 1.8 uL, mix 3 min; Step iii: 4x wash;
                 Step iv: HRP-anti-human IgG conjugate (21 ng/mL), mix 2 min; Step v: 4x wash;
                 Step vi: H2O2 (900 nL) + luminol-enhancer (900 nL), mix 2 min; Step vii: PMT 10 s
  IgG LOD/LOQ  : 0.03 IU/mL / 0.1 IU/mL (clinical cutoff: 10 IU/mL)
  IgM protocol : Same as IgG but + pretreatment (sample 1.8 uL + anti-human IgG reagent 900 nL, mix 7 min)
                 and HRP-anti-human IgM conjugate; ~35 min per run
  On-chip dil. : 4 iterations merge-mix-split; generates 2x/4x/8x/16x dilutions; compatible with whole blood
  Panel results: 25 serum/plasma samples (SeraCare PTR201); IgG: 100% sensitivity, 100% specificity
                 IgM: 100% sensitivity / 100% specificity (equivocal omitted); two equivocal mismatches
                 near cutoff (s/co = 0.9 and 1.0); attributed to assay variability + 20-year-old specimens


PROTOCOL 2: DISC (Chapter 5)
-----------------------------
Full name      : DISC -- Digital Microfluidic Immunocytochemistry in Single-Cells
Cell line      : NIH 3T3 (murine fibroblast, primary); MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 for cancer time series
Signaling      : PDGF-BB -> PDGFR auto-phosphorylation (Y857, Y1021) -> PI3K -> PIP3 -> Akt -> p-Akt S473
Seeding density: 500,000 cells/mL -> ~150-300 cells per virtual microwell
Anti-fouling   : 0.05% Pluronic F68 in all culture media, fixing, and wash solutions

Key capabilities:
  Temporal resolution : ~4 s between stimulation and fixation (passive dispense switch)
  Reagent exchange    : 1 exchange removes ~93% of prior solution; 2 exchanges >99%
  Cell reduction      : 150-300 cells/VM vs 15,000 cells/well (flow cytometry): 60-150x fewer cells
  Volume reduction    : 400 nL per VM vs ~200 uL per well: ~500x less volume
  SBR                 : GAPDH signal >=5x background (optimization data, Fig 5.2D)

Passive dispensing mechanism:
  Source droplet translated across vacant lift-off spot (1.75 mm hydrophilic ITO on Teflon-AF top plate);
  hydrophobic-hydrophilic contrast captures a ~400 nL virtual microwell sub-droplet spontaneously.
  Subsequent dispenses displace and replace microwell contents.

Eleven-step DISC protocol (representative arm: Akt phosphorylation at 50 ng/mL PDGF-BB):

  Step 1 | Cell seeding
    Volume   : 3 x 900 nL passive dispenses (2.7 uL) per lift-off spot; VM = ~400 nL
    Incubate : 37 C, 5% CO2, 24 h in humidified chamber; device inverted for cell settling

  Step 2 | Serum starvation
    Reagent  : Starving media (0.5% CS/FBS + 0.05% F68 + pen/strep in DMEM)
    Volume   : 3 x 900 nL; Incubate 37 C, 5% CO2, 24 h
    Purpose  : Synchronizes basal receptor/Akt activity

  Step 3 | Serum-free rinse
    Reagent  : Serum-free DMEM + 0.05% F68; Volume: 3 x 900 nL

  Step 4 | PDGF-BB stimulation
    Reagent  : PDGF-BB 50 ng/mL in serum-free DMEM; Volume: 2 x 900 nL (1.8 uL)
    Duration : 2 min (PDGFR) / 5 min (Akt); ~4 s reagent switch time to fixation
    Dose-response range: 0-200 ng/mL; EC50 ~12.5 ng/mL; Hill n=1.73 (Y857), 2.13 (Y1021)
    Notes    : In time series, Step 4 staggered so Step 5 performed simultaneously for all VMs
               to prevent cross-exposure to paraformaldehyde fumes

  Step 5 | Cell fixation
    Reagent  : 4% paraformaldehyde + 0.05% F68 in DPBS; Volume: 3 x 900 nL (2.7 uL)
    Incubate : 10 min, room temperature

  Step 6 | WB1 rinse
    Reagent  : WB1 (0.05% F68 in DPBS); Volume: 3 x 900 nL (5.4 uL total)

  Step 7 | Permeabilization
    Reagent  : 0.2% Tween-20 in DPBS; Volume: 3 x 900 nL (2.7 uL)
    Incubate : 10 min, room temperature

  Step 8 | WB2 rinse
    Reagent  : WB2 (0.05% Brij 35 in DPBS); Volume: 4 x 900 nL (~8.1 uL)

  Step 9 | Blocking
    Reagent  : 1% bovine NFDM + 0.05% Brij 35 in DPBS; Volume: 3 x 900 nL (2.7 uL)
    Incubate : 1 h, room temperature

  Step 10 | Primary antibody staining
    Reagents : pan Akt (Mouse mAb, 1:50, CST) + p-Akt S473 (Rabbit mAb, 1:200, CST) in BS
               OR PDGFR-beta (Mouse mAb, 1:50, CST) + p-PDGFR Y857/Y1021 (Rabbit pAb, 1:200, SCB) in BS
    Volume   : 3 x 900 nL (2.7 uL); Incubate: overnight (~12 h) at 4 C

  Step 11 | WB2 rinse (unbound primary antibody removal)
    Reagent  : WB2 (0.05% Brij 35 in DPBS); Volume: 3 x 900 nL (5.4 uL)

  Step 12 | Secondary antibody staining
    Reagents : Anti-Mouse IgG AF647 Fab2 1:500 + Anti-Rabbit IgG AF555 Fab2 1:500 in BS (CST)
    Volume   : 3 x 900 nL (2.7 uL); Incubate: 2 h, room temperature

  Step 13 | Off-chip detection (laser scanning cytometry)
    Post-process : Remove top plate; rinse in 10x DPBS/0.5% Tween-20 (30 s); rinse DI water (30 s); air dry
    Scanner      : Axon GenePix 4000B; 532 nm + 635 nm; 5 um resolution; 0 um focus; PMT 500 V
    Analysis     : CellProfiler; Otsu Global thresholding; 15-100 um objects; per-cell p-protein/total ratio
    Normalization: Per-cell ratio normalized to serum-free negative control mean on same device

Key results (DISC):
  PDGFR Y857 max phosphorylation  : 75 s after 50 ng/mL PDGF-BB
  PDGFR Y1021 max phosphorylation : 60 s after 50 ng/mL PDGF-BB
  Akt activation at 3.125 ng/mL   : ~71% despite only ~22% receptor activation (amplification)
  Ligand removal (1 exchange)      : ~93% ligand removed; receptor dephosphorylation confirmed
  Cancer cells                     : MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 differ significantly in Akt hyper-responder
                                     fraction; may correlate with invasion phenotype
