protocol_1_magnetic_particle_immunoassay.title: DMF Magnetic Particle-Based Immunoassay (Supernatant Separation Method)

assay_modes.TSH_non_competitive: Sandwich: Anti-beta TSH particles + TSH analyte + Anti-TSH-HRP conjugate
assay_modes.E2_competitive: Competition: Anti-E2 particles + E2 analyte competes with E2-HRP conjugate; higher analyte = lower signal

particle_prep_off_chip: Immobilize ARCHITECT particles with neodymium magnet in Eppendorf tube; remove diluent
TSH only: suspend in blocking buffer pH 7.8 (NFDM 3%, Tween-20 0.01%), incubate 1 h, wash 2x DI water
Resuspend at ~3.0e8 particles/mL in DMF-compatible particle diluent (pH 10)

washing_method.name: Supernatant separation
washing_method.mechanism: Magnet pellets particles on device surface; supernatant droplet actuated to waste; magnet removed; fresh droplet passed over pellet and circularly mixed (4 electrodes) to resuspend
washing_method.efficiency: >98% unbound reagent removal by wash 2 (vs serial dilution requiring 6+ washes for same benchmark)
washing_method.residual_liquid_retained_pct: ~5% of origin droplet; particles resuspended immediately to prevent drying

steps.name: Particle dispense and separation from diluent
steps.notes: Magnet positioned beneath device; diluent actuated to waste leaving particle pellet

steps.name: Sample incubation
steps.notes: 3 unit droplets (800 nL x 3 = 2.4 uL); chosen for optimal signal without compromising droplet reliability; particles continuously mixed during incubation to minimize non-specific adsorption

steps.name: Wash x4 in wash buffer + wash x2 in H2O2
steps.notes: 2x H2O2 wash developed to replace off-chip premixing; prevents high inter-assay variability from pre-mixed substrate

steps.name: H2O2 incubation
steps.notes: Particles moved to detection region (96-well aligned area)

steps.name: Luminol/enhancer merge
steps.notes: On-chip mixing immediately before measurement; activates HRP-catalyzed chemiluminescence

steps.name: Chemiluminescence detection
steps.settings_ch2: LUM module; focal height 8.6 mm; gain 3600; device taped to 96-well Stripwell
steps.notes: Chemiluminescence saturates at 1 min; chosen as measurement endpoint

optimized_platform_ch3.improvements: 90 Pogo pin interface; integrated motorized PMT; magnetic lens (up to 8 simultaneous separations); DropBot automation
optimized_platform_ch3.DOE_optimization: 3-level full factorial; factors: analyte concentration, sample incubation time, sample volume; optimal: 5 droplets, 3 min incubation
optimized_platform_ch3.measurement_procedure: Wash buffer immediately removed after final wash; particles resuspended in luminol-H2O2; mixed 4 min until signal saturates; stable measurement window ~1 min

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Clathrate Nanostructures for Mass Spectrometry
Source Link  : https://masspec.scripps.edu/research/pdf/northen_nature06195.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/nature06195
Journal      : Nature, 2007, Vol. 449, pp. 1033-1036
Platform     : Nanostructure-Initiator Mass Spectrometry (NIMS) -- porous silicon surface
               with trapped perfluorinated siloxane initiator molecules; compatible with
               337 nm nitrogen laser (laser-NIMS) and Bi3+ ion beam (ion-NIMS) irradiation


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol introduces NIMS (Nanostructure-Initiator Mass Spectrometry), a matrix-free
surface-based mass spectrometry technique for spatially defined, high-sensitivity analysis
of biomolecules, metabolites, and drugs directly from cells, tissues, and biofluids.

The NIMS surface is a porous silicon chip (~10 nm pores, fabricated by anodic etching)
loaded with perfluorinated siloxane initiator molecules that are trapped inside the pores
in a clathrate-like ordered arrangement. Laser or ion irradiation rapidly vaporises the
initiator, triggering desorption and ionisation of analytes adsorbed on the surface --
without any conventional MALDI matrix. This eliminates matrix-related background, crystal
size limitations on spatial resolution, and the need for sample preparation steps.

Key advantages over existing techniques:
  - No matrix required (vs MALDI); no background below m/z 700
  - Lateral resolution ~150 nm with ion-NIMS Bi3+ beam (vs >10 um matrix crystal for MALDI)
  - Reduced molecular fragmentation vs secondary-ion mass spectrometry (SIMS)
  - Direct analysis of sub-microlitre blood and urine without extraction or derivatisation
  - Multiply charged protein ions analogous to ESI (laser-NIMS)
  - Compatible with laser (N2, 337 nm) and multiple ion sources (Au+, Ga+, Bi+, Bi3+)

The protocol is divided into six sections encoding five application demonstrations from
the paper:
  Section I   : NIMS surface fabrication (anodic etch + initiator loading)
  Section II  : Laser-NIMS -- peptide digest and small molecule detection (Fig 1d)
  Section III : Single cancer cell metabolite profiling (Fig 2)
  Section IV  : Peptide microarray characterisation by ion-NIMS Bi3+ (Fig 3)
  Section V   : Mouse embryo tissue imaging by laser-NIMS (Fig 4)
  Section VI  : Direct biofluid analysis -- blood and urine (Fig 5)


NIMS SURFACE ARCHITECTURE
--------------------------
Substrate  : P-type boron-doped silicon wafer, <100> orientation
             Resistivity: 0.01-0.02 Ohm.cm; thickness: 525 +/- 25 um; diameter: 100 mm
             Supplier: Silicon Valley Microelectronics
Pores      : ~10 nm diameter (confirmed by SEM, Fig 1c); fabricated by anodic electrochemical
             etching in 25% hydrofluoric acid in ethanol at 48 mA.cm^-2 for 30 min, 25 deg C
             CAUTION: HF is acutely hazardous; certified fume hood, PPE, and neutralising
             agent (calcium gluconate gel) required at all times.
Initiator  : Laser-NIMS: bis(tridecafluoro-1,1,2,2-tetrahydrooctyl)tetramethyldisiloxane
             (undiluted, MW ~500 Da, perfluorinated siloxane)
             Ion-NIMS:   14-kDa poly(3,3,3-trifluoropropylmethylsiloxanes)
             Applied at 25 deg C for 30-60 min; excess removed with nitrogen jet.
             Ion-NIMS initiator baked overnight at 100 deg C; rinsed with tert-butyl methyl ether.
Clathrate  : Initiator molecules are highly ordered inside pores (reversible migration
             on slight heating/cooling; Supplementary Movie 1). Perfluorinated initiators
             preferred for laser-NIMS due to low analyte solubility in resulting clathrates
             and efficient trapping.

Alternative surfaces tested: native silicon (SiH), silanized, Au/Pd sputtered -- all
show NIMS activity. Alternative initiators tested: lauric acid, polysiloxanes, siloxanes,
silanes (MW 200-14000 Da; Supplementary Table 1).


INSTRUMENTATION
---------------
Laser-NIMS instrument : Voyager DE STR (Applied Biosystems)
  Laser               : 337 nm pulsed nitrogen, single-side-polished
  Mode                : reflector, positive polarity
  Acceleration voltage: 20 kV
  First grid voltage  : 60%
  Guide wire voltage  : 0.15%
  Extraction delay    : 100 ns
  Acquisition         : average of 100 laser shots per spectrum/position

Ion-NIMS instrument   : ION-TOF IV TOF-SIMS (IONTOF GmbH)
  Primary ion source  : polyatomic Bi3+
  Beam energy         : 25 kV
  Incident angle      : 45 deg to sample
  Pulse width         : 50 ns
  Primary ion dose    : below static limit
  Sample voltage      : +2.5 kV; extraction lens: -4.5 kV
  Lateral resolution  : ~150 nm ion beam (Fig 3c inset)

Fluorescence          : Nikon TE2000 inverted fluorescence microscope
  Objectives          : 20x Plan Fluor (NA 0.45); 60x oil Plan Apo (NA 1.40)
  Filter set          : 61000V2 (Chroma); DAPI/FITC/TRITC triple band
  Camera              : Retiga EXi Fast 1394 Mono Cooled (Qimaging)
  Filter wheels       : Lambda 10-2 (Sutter Instrument), automated


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | NIMS Surface Fabrication -- Anodic Etching   [Section I, BB1]
  Reagents    : P-type <100> boron silicon wafer; 25% HF in ethanol
  Operation   : Anodic etch at 48 mA.cm^-2 for 30 min (1800 s), 25 deg C
  IR output   : etchedSurface1[0] = mix(siliconWafer1[0], etchSolution1[0]) @ 1800.0 SECOND
                heat(etchedSurface1[0]) @ 25.0 CELSIUS @ 1800.0 SECOND
  Result      : ~10 nm pore nanostructured silicon surface
  Notes       : Etching chamber constructed in-house; current from Bio-Rad PowerPack 1000.
                Detailed step-by-step at http://masspec.scripps.edu/Research/nims/create.php

Step 2 | Initiator Loading and N2 Jet Removal   [Section I, BB1]
  Reagents    : Perfluorinated siloxane initiator (undiluted); nitrogen gas
  Operation   : Apply initiator at 25 deg C for 45 min (2700 s); remove excess with N2 jet (30 s)
  IR output   : loadedSurface1[0] = mix(etchedSurface1[0], initiator1[0]) @ 2700.0 SECOND
                heat(loadedSurface1[0]) @ 25.0 CELSIUS @ 2700.0 SECOND
                nimsSurface1[0] = mix(loadedSurface1[0], nitrogenJet1[0]) @ 30.0 SECOND
  Notes       : Initiator fills pores by capillary force; highly ordered arrangement confirmed
                by reversible migration (heating/cooling; Supplementary Movie 1).
                Both silanized and unsilanized surfaces are supported.

Step 3 | NIMS Surface QC   [Section I, BB1 -> BB2/BB3]
  Operation   : Test laser shot; detect initiator-derived background ions (nimsLaserDetection)
  IR output   : surfaceQC1[0] = detect(nimsLaserDetection, nimsSurface1[0]) @ 10.0 SECOND
  Gate        : surfaceQC > 0  -> BB2 (pass): dispose(nimsSurface1[0]); proceed to analyte sections
                surfaceQC <= 0 -> BB3 (fail): drain(nimsSurface1[0]); repeat surface preparation

Step 4 | BSA Tryptic Digest and Small Molecule Detection by Laser-NIMS   [Section II, BB4 -> BB5/BB6]
  Reagents    : BSA tryptic digest (500 amol); verapamil (700 ymol); 1:1 AcN/water + 0.1% TFA
  BSA prep    : Reduced with DTT; alkylated with iodoacetamide; digested with porcine trypsin (Promega)
  Drop volume : 0.5 uL per spot (contact spotting); solvent evaporated before laser irradiation
  Operations  : mix bsaDigest + solvent (10 s) -> heat 25 deg C (300 s) -> mix onto NIMS (5 s)
                -> detect nimsLaserDetection (30 s)
                -> dispense verapamil -> mix onto NIMS (5 s) -> heat 25 deg C (300 s)
  IR output   : bsaSpot1[0] = mix(bsaDigest1[0], bsaSolvent1[0]) @ 10.0 SECOND
                heat(bsaSpot1[0]) @ 25.0 CELSIUS @ 300.0 SECOND
                bsaSpot_nims1[0] = mix(bsaSpot1[0], nimsSurface2[0]) @ 5.0 SECOND
                peptideSignal1[0] = detect(nimsLaserDetection, bsaSpot_nims1[0]) @ 30.0 SECOND
                verapamilSpot1[0] = mix(verapamilDrop1[0], nimsSurface2[0]) @ 5.0 SECOND
                heat(verapamilSpot1[0]) @ 25.0 CELSIUS @ 300.0 SECOND
  Results     : BSA: 55% sequence coverage at 500 amol (Fig 1d upper right)
                Verapamil: detected at 700 ymol (~420 molecules, Fig 1d lower left)
                beta-Lactoglobulin: multiply charged at 50 nmol (ESI-like, Fig 1d upper left)
                LysoPPC: 1-palmitoyllysophosphatidylcholine at 50 amol (Fig 1d lower right)
                Sensitivity 1000x higher than nanoESI and MALDI (Supplementary Figs 2, 3, 5)
  Gate        : peptideSignal > 0  -> BB5 (pass): dispose analyte spots
                peptideSignal <= 0 -> BB6 (fail): drain analyte spots

Step 5 | Single Cancer Cell Metabolite Profiling by Laser-NIMS   [Section III, BB7 -> BB8/BB9]
  Cell line   : MDA-MB-231 (highly metastatic breast cancer, ATCC HTB-26)
  Medium      : Leibovitz's L-15 + 2 mM L-glutamine + 10% calf bovine serum; 37 deg C
  Harvest     : trypsin-EDTA
  Deposition  : Micromanipulator (MINJ-PD; Tritech Research) precisely counts and deposits
                single cell onto NIMS chip; cell dried at 25 deg C (5 min) before MS
                NOTE: mix() in BioScript abstracts the micromanipulator deposition step
  Initiator   : bis(tridecafluoro-1,1,2,2-tetrahydrooctyl)tetramethyldisiloxane;
                calibrated with Na+, K+, phosphocholine, 1-palmitoyllysophosphatidylcholine
  Operations  : dispense single cell -> mix onto NIMS (2 s) -> heat dry 25 deg C (300 s)
                -> detect nimsLaserDetection (30 s)
                -> dispense FDA/PI stain -> mix + stain (600 s)
                -> detect nimsFluorescenceDetection (30 s)
  Post-MS     : Fix: 2% paraformaldehyde. Permeabilise: cold methanol.
                Block: 20% human AB serum. Stain: anti-Pan cytokeratin (mouse monoclonal)
                + Alexa555 goat anti-mouse + DAPI nuclear counterstain.
  IR output   : cellOnSurface1[0] = mix(singleCell1[0], nimsSurface2[0]) @ 2.0 SECOND
                heat(cellOnSurface1[0]) @ 25.0 CELSIUS @ 300.0 SECOND
                cellSignal1[0] = detect(nimsLaserDetection, cellOnSurface1[0]) @ 30.0 SECOND
                stainedCell1[0] = mix(cellOnSurface1[0], fdaPiStain1[0]) @ 600.0 SECOND
                fluoroSignal1[0] = detect(nimsFluorescenceDetection, stainedCell1[0]) @ 30.0 SECOND
  Results     : Endogenous phospholipids detected from single cell (m/z 400-900);
                spectral complexity superior to hundreds of cells by nanoESI, MALDI, or
                ion-NIMS (Fig 2c). Cell location marked by green fluorescent box (Fig 2a).
  Gate        : cellSignal > 0  -> BB8 (pass): dispose stained cell + fluoro signal
                cellSignal <= 0 -> BB9 (fail): drain stained cell + fluoro signal

Step 6 | Peptide Microarray Characterisation by Ion-NIMS (Bi3+)   [Section IV, BB10 -> BB11/BB12]
  Peptides    : Bradykinin 2-9 (904 Da, red), Neurotensin (1673 Da, blue),
                Bradykinin 1-7 (757 Da, yellow); all at 1 fmol per spot
  Printing    : Robotic contact printing (custom arrayer, ArrayIt head); 1.4 nL drops;
                1:1 AcN/water + 0.1% TFA; array dried at 25 deg C (5 min) before analysis
                NOTE: mix() abstracts robotic contact printing of each peptide spot
  Operations  : dispense each peptide -> mix with solvent (5 s each)
                -> mix onto NIMS surface sequentially (5 s each)
                -> heat dry 25 deg C (300 s) -> detect nimsIonDetection (30 s)
  IR output   : bk27_spot1[0] = mix(bk27_solution1[0], arraySolvent1[0]) @ 5.0 SECOND
                bk17_spot1[0] = mix(bk17_solution1[0], arraySolvent1[0]) @ 5.0 SECOND
                nt_spot1[0]   = mix(nt_solution1[0],   arraySolvent1[0]) @ 5.0 SECOND
                peptideArray1[0] = mix(bk27_spot1[0], nimsSurface2[0]) @ 5.0 SECOND
                peptideArray2[0] = mix(bk17_spot1[0], peptideArray1[0]) @ 5.0 SECOND
                peptideArray3[0] = mix(nt_spot1[0],   peptideArray2[0]) @ 5.0 SECOND
                heat(peptideArray3[0]) @ 25.0 CELSIUS @ 300.0 SECOND
                arraySignal1[0] = detect(nimsIonDetection, peptideArray3[0]) @ 30.0 SECOND
  Results     : 1 fmol sensitivity per peptide -- 1000x over TOF-SIMS (Ref 16, 21);
                doubles mass range vs cluster sources (Ref 15); 150 nm spatial resolution;
                BK peptides localise to centre of printed spot at higher concentration (Fig 3c);
                BK 1-7 on silicon control shows significant fragmentation vs NIMS (Fig 3d)
  Gate        : arraySignal > 0  -> BB11 (pass): dispose(peptideArray3[0])
                arraySignal <= 0 -> BB12 (fail): drain(peptideArray3[0])

Step 7 | Mouse Embryo Tissue Imaging by Laser-NIMS   [Section V, BB13 -> BB14/BB15]
  Sample      : C57Bl/6J mouse embryo, embryonic day 16.5
  Section prep: Frozen in OCT compound (VWR International) on dry ice; equilibrated to -20 deg C;
                cryosectioned at 12 um (Leica CM3050 S); thaw-mounted onto NIMS chip
                Parallel sections collected on Superfrost Plus slides (H&E histology)
  Initiator   : bis(heptadecafluoro-1,1,2,2-tetrahydrodecyl)tetramethyldisiloxane
  Two-step imaging protocol:
    (i)  Laser etching: ~0.4 J.cm^-2 per pulse (337 nm) ablates 12 um tissue to expose
         underlying NIMS surface at the tissue/surface interface
         NOTE: heat() at 25 deg C abstracts this pulsed photothermal ablation step (2 min)
    (ii) NIMS imaging: ~0.01 J.cm^-2 per pulse (337 nm); 100-shot average per raster point;
         20 um step size; ~15 um laser beam diameter; nimsLaserDetection abstracts acquisition
  Operations  : dispense tissue section -> mix onto NIMS (30 s)
                -> heat etch 25 deg C (120 s) -> detect nimsLaserDetection (30 s)
  IR output   : mountedTissue1[0] = mix(tissueSection1[0], nimsSurface2[0]) @ 30.0 SECOND
                heat(mountedTissue1[0]) @ 25.0 CELSIUS @ 120.0 SECOND
                tissueSignal1[0] = detect(nimsLaserDetection, mountedTissue1[0]) @ 30.0 SECOND
  Results     : Glycerophosphatidylcholine (m/z 782) localised around developing vertebra (Fig 4b);
                300 um-wide false-colour image; red/yellow/cyan = high lipid signal;
                dark blue = developing vertebra. Phosphatidylethanolamine also detected
                (post-source decay). Scale bar 1 mm.
                NIMS complementary to MALDI for tissue: NIMS excels for metabolites/lipids;
                MALDI for peptides/small proteins (Ref 23).
  Animals     : C57Bl/6J housed in Scripps vivarium; IACUC-approved (LLNL guidelines)
                Embryos collected at E16.5; dams anaesthetised by isofluorane, sacrificed
                by cervical dislocation; embryos frozen on dry ice immediately.
  Gate        : tissueSignal > 0  -> BB14 (pass): dispose(mountedTissue1[0])
                tissueSignal <= 0 -> BB15 (fail): drain(mountedTissue1[0])

Step 8 | Direct Biofluid Analysis by Laser-NIMS   [Section VI, BB16 -> BB17/BB18]
  Samples     : 1 uL fresh human blood; 1 uL fresh human urine
                No sample preparation, extraction, or derivatisation required
                Spotted directly onto NIMS surface; held 30 s; excess blown off with N2 stream
  Initiators  : (a) bis(heptadecafluoro-1,1,2,2-tetrahydrodecyl)tetramethyldisiloxane
                    (perfluorinated; lipid-selective; used for blood)
                (b) 1,3-bis(hydroxybutyl)tetramethyldisiloxane
                    (polar hydroxylated; small metabolite-selective; urine comparison)
                ~86% of ions from (b) are unique to the polar initiator surface, showing
                initiator selection targets metabolites by chemical functionality
  Blood protocol:
    1. Spot 1 uL fresh blood onto NIMS; wait 30 s; blow off excess with N2
    2. Laser-etch at ~0.4 J.cm^-2 to ablate cellular blood matrix (RBCs, proteins)
    3. NIMS analysis of exposed interface layer (dominant ions: phospholipids / PC lipids)
    NOTE: heat() at 25 deg C (60 s) abstracts the laser-etch ablation step
  Urine protocol:
    1. Spot 1 uL fresh urine onto NIMS; wait 30 s; blow off excess with N2
    2. NIMS analysis directly (no etch step needed for urine)
    3. Dominant ions: small metabolites <500 Da; also GM2 (m/z 1545.9) and GM1 (m/z 1561.9)
  Operations  : dispense blood -> mix onto NIMS (30 s) -> mix N2 blow-off (5 s)
                -> heat etch 25 deg C (60 s) -> mix NIMS interrogation (5 s)
                -> dispense urine -> mix onto NIMS (30 s) -> mix N2 blow-off (5 s)
                -> mix NIMS interrogation (5 s)
                -> detect nimsLaserDetection blood (30 s); detect nimsLaserDetection urine (30 s)
  IR output   : bloodOnSurface1[0]  = mix(bloodSample1[0],   nimsSurface2[0]) @ 30.0 SECOND
                bloodExcess1[0]     = mix(bloodOnSurface1[0], nitrogenBlowOff1[0]) @ 5.0 SECOND
                heat(bloodExcess1[0]) @ 25.0 CELSIUS @ 60.0 SECOND
                bloodNIMS1[0]       = mix(bloodExcess1[0],    nimsSurface2[0]) @ 5.0 SECOND
                urineOnSurface1[0]  = mix(urineSample1[0],    nimsSurface2[0]) @ 30.0 SECOND
                urineExcess1[0]     = mix(urineOnSurface1[0], nitrogenBlowOff21[0]) @ 5.0 SECOND
                urineNIMS1[0]       = mix(urineExcess1[0],    nimsSurface2[0]) @ 5.0 SECOND
                biofluidSignal1[0]  = detect(nimsLaserDetection, bloodNIMS1[0]) @ 30.0 SECOND
                urineSignal1[0]     = detect(nimsLaserDetection, urineNIMS1[0]) @ 30.0 SECOND
  Results     : Complex spectra without background ions (Fig 5); linear codeine response
                up to 15 ng.mL^-1 vs 75-250 ng.mL^-1 for conventional approaches (Ref 28).
                Data processing: ASCII export -> SpecAlign (baseline correction, TIC
                normalisation, spectrum realignment). Statistical analysis: SigmaPlot 10.
  Gate        : biofluidSignal > 0  -> BB17 (pass): dispose blood, urine, urine signal droplets
                biofluidSignal <= 0 -> BB18 (fail): drain  blood, urine, urine signal droplets

Terminal      : BB19 (bsbbif_19_j): dispose(biofluidSignal1[0]); NOP


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file  : northen_nims_mass_spectrometry.bs
Compiler        : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output       : northen_nims_mass_spectrometry.ir
DAG output      : northen_nims_mass_spectrometry_main_dag.dot
Basic blocks    : 19 (BB1 = main entry; BB19 = bsbbif_19_j terminal; NOP exit)
CFG edges       : 24 (verified from DAG; each join node has exactly 2 incoming edges)
If/else gates   : 5 (surfaceQC, peptideSignal, cellSignal, arraySignal, biofluidSignal)

Duration encoding (BioScript supports s and m only):
  30 min etch          -> 30m  -> 1800.0 SECOND in IR
  45 min initiator load-> 45m  -> 2700.0 SECOND in IR
  5 min solvent evap   -> 5m   -> 300.0 SECOND  in IR
  2 min tissue etch    -> 2m   -> 120.0 SECOND  in IR
  1 min blood etch     -> 1m   -> 60.0 SECOND   in IR
  10 min FDA/PI stain  -> 10m  -> 600.0 SECOND  in IR

Modules:
  nimsLaserDetection       -> Voyager DE STR (337 nm N2 laser, reflector, +20 kV, 100-shot avg)
  nimsFluorescenceDetection-> Nikon TE2000 (DAPI/FITC/TRITC, Retiga EXi camera)
  nimsIonDetection         -> ION-TOF IV TOF-SIMS (Bi3+, 25 kV, 45 deg, 50 ns, <static dose)

ASCII constraint:
  ANTLR4 FileStream defaults to ascii encoding; initial file contained non-ASCII characters
  (degree symbol, micro sign, middle dot, superscripts, Ohm, +/-, Nordstrom o-umlaut).
  All replaced with ASCII equivalents: deg, u, ., ^-2, Ohm, +/-, Nordstrom.
  Fix applied with sed; verified by grep -P '[^\x00-\x7F]' (zero matches after fix).

mix() abstraction note:
  mix() is used throughout to abstract non-DMF physical steps:
    - Anodic etching of silicon wafer (S1)
    - Initiator capillary loading (S2)
    - Single cell deposition by micromanipulator MINJ-PD (S5)
    - Tissue section thaw-mount onto NIMS chip (S7)
    - Robotic contact array printing (S6, ArrayIt head, 1.4 nL drops)
    - Blood/urine direct spotting and N2 blow-off (S8)
  Each such step is annotated with a comment in the .bs source file.

nimsSurface SSA renaming:
  nimsSurface appears as nimsSurface1[0] in BB1/BB2/BB3 (initial dispense after fabrication)
  and as nimsSurface2[0] in all subsequent sections (BB4 onward). The compiler correctly
  applies SSA (Static Single Assignment) renaming to the second dispense of the same
  manifest, ensuring distinct variable identifiers for each use.

protocol.title: Clathrate Nanostructures for Mass Spectrometry
protocol.platform: Nanostructure-Initiator Mass Spectrometry (NIMS) -- porous silicon surface with trapped perfluorinated siloxane initiator; laser (337 nm N2) and ion (Bi3+) irradiation modes
applications: Peptide/protein tryptic digest detection (BSA, 500 amol, 55% sequence coverage)
Single cancer cell metabolite profiling (MDA-MB-231, endogenous phospholipids)
Peptide microarray characterisation by ion-NIMS (Bi3+, 1 fmol sensitivity, 150 nm lateral resolution)
Mouse embryo tissue imaging by laser-NIMS (glycerophosphatidylcholine m/z 782)
Direct biofluid analysis without sample preparation (1 uL blood and urine)

BSA_tryptic_digest.preparation: Reduced (DTT), alkylated (iodoacetamide), digested with mass-spec-grade porcine trypsin (Promega)

verapamil.notes: Calcium antagonist drug, MW 454.6 Da; ~420 molecules on surface (Fig 1d lower left)

beta_lactoglobulin.notes: Multiply charged protein detection analogous to ESI (Fig 1d upper left)

MDA_MB_231.medium: Leibovitz's L-15 + 2 mM L-glutamine + 10% calf bovine serum

steps.name: NIMS surface fabrication -- anodic etching

steps.name: Initiator loading and N2 jet removal
steps.notes: Undiluted bis(tridecafluoro-1,1,2,2-tetrahydrooctyl)tetramethyldisiloxane applied at 25 deg C for 30-60 min (45 min midpoint encoded). Initiator migrates into pores by capillary force (Supplementary Movie 1). Excess removed by N2 jet.

pass.interpretation: test laser shot confirms initiator background ions; surface ready

fail.interpretation: no initiator signal; etching or loading failed; repeat surface prep

steps.name: BSA tryptic digest and small molecule detection by laser-NIMS

post-MS: 2% paraformaldehyde fixation, cold methanol permeabilisation, DAPI + Alexa555-cytokeratin staining

NIMS imaging phase: ~0.01 J.cm^-2 per pulse; 100-shot average per raster point; 20 um step size; 15 um beam diameter

excess blown off with N2 stream
laser-etch phase (~0.4 J.cm^-2) to ablate cellular blood matrix; heat@25C abstracts pulsed ablation
NIMS interrogation of etched blood surface layer

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Miniaturized Scalable Arrayed CRISPR Screening in Primary Cells Enables
               Discovery at the Single Donor Resolution
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-13532-z
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-13532-z
Journal      : Scientific Reports, 2025, Vol. 15, Article 29350
Platform     : DropGenie Digital Microfluidics (DMF) Electroporation System
               (48-site SBS-format cartridge, Tri-Drop Electroporation architecture,
               Echo 655 acoustic liquid handler, Assist Plus 8-channel liquid handler)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a next-generation digital microfluidics (DMF) electroporation
platform for high-throughput, low-input genome engineering in primary human cells.
The DropGenie system manipulates nanoliter- to microliter-scale droplets on a planar
electrode array using electrostatic actuation, enabling 48 independently programmable
reaction sites on a single SBS-format cartridge. The platform integrates with laboratory
automation (Assist Plus, Echo 655) and requires as few as 3,000 primary cells per edit
-- up to 100-fold fewer than conventional cuvette-based electroporation systems.

The protocol is divided into three functional arms validated in the paper:
  1. ARM 1 -- CRISPR-Cas9 RNP knockout (TRAC gene) in primary human T cells
              (Pan CD3+, CD4+, CD8+, and Regulatory T cells)
  2. ARM 2 -- Precise knock-in (GFP and anti-HER2 CAR) at the TRAC locus via
              homology-directed repair (HDR) using cssDNA and dsDNA templates
  3. ARM 3 -- Arrayed CRISPR-Cas9 exhaustion screen in chronically stimulated
              primary human CD4+ T cells; 45 targets, 192 edits total

The platform uses Tri-Drop Electroporation: two conductive DMFection Buffer droplets
flank a central cell-and-cargo droplet on the electrode array. Electrode actuation
forms a transient, low-current electroporation zone that delivers RNPs and mRNA while
minimising Joule heating, hydrolysis by-products, and viability-compromising effects
characteristic of cuvette-based systems.

A complete arm-to-readout workflow (activation, transfection, recovery, assay) is
described below. The BioScript file encodes ARM 1 and ARM 2 as sequential validation
arms followed by ARM 3 (the arrayed screen).


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Cartridge format : SBS (Society for Biological Screening) standard format;
                   compatible with robotic liquid handlers.
Reaction sites   : 48 independently programmable electroporation sites per cartridge.
Droplet paradigm : Tri-Drop Electroporation -- two flanking DMFection Buffer droplets
                   bridge anode and cathode electrodes around a central cell droplet,
                   forming the electroporation zone without moving parts.
Guide deposition : sgRNAs pre-deposited dry onto the cartridge substrate in 40 nL spots
                   by Echo 655 acoustic liquid handler (Beckman Coulter), mixed with
                   Poly-L-glutamic acid (PGA) carrier and desiccated before assembly.
Cell loading     : Assist Plus 8-channel 125 uL Integra Voyager pipette; 100 uL per well.
Cell offloading  : Assist Plus into 96-well round-bottom plate post-transfection.
Downstream       : Flow cytometry (Attune NxT), Sanger sequencing (ICE analysis),
                   high-content imaging (Incucyte Live-Cell Analysis System),
                   sandwich ELISA (RayBiotech).

Electroporation parameters:
  T cell KO (Pan CD3+):  500 V, 3 ms, 2 pulses, 5 min pre-pulse incubation
  T cell KO (CD4+/Treg): 550 V, 2 ms, 2 pulses, 5 min pre-pulse incubation
  T cell knock-in:        500 V, 2 ms or 4 ms, 2 pulses
  Exhaustion screen:      550 V, 2 ms, 2 pulses


CELL TYPES
----------
- Primary human skeletal muscle myoblasts (Zen-Bio; adherent):
  Cultured in Skeletal Muscle Cell Growth Media (Zen-Bio); 37 C, 5% CO2.
  Used for EGFP mRNA transfection and MBNL1 knockout validation.
  Input: 3,000 cells per edit.

- Primary human Pan CD3+ T cells (suspension):
  Derived from PBMCs from fresh leukopak (Charles River Laboratories) by density
  gradient (Histopaque-1077) and negative selection (EasySep Human T Cell Enrichment Kit,
  STEMCELL Technologies). Cryopreserved until use.
  Used for TRAC KO and GFP/CAR knock-in experiments.
  Input: 10,000 cells per edit.

- Primary human CD4+ Helper T cells (AllCells; suspension):
  Negatively selected peripheral blood CD4+ T cells.
  Used for the arrayed CRISPR exhaustion screen.
  Input: 10,000 cells per edit.

- Primary human CD4+CD25+ Regulatory T cells (iQ Biosciences; suspension):
  Peripheral blood-derived; represent 5-10% of circulating CD4+ T cells.
  Used to demonstrate editing in rare T cell subsets.
  Input: 10,000 cells per edit.


PROTOCOL STEPS -- ARM 1: TRAC KNOCKOUT IN PRIMARY HUMAN T CELLS
-----------------------------------------------------------------

Step 1 | T Cell Activation (off-chip, 3 days)
  Cell type    : CD4+ Helper T cells (AllCells) or Pan CD3+ T cells
  Media        : Basal T Cell Media (RPMI 1640 + GlutaMax + 10% FBS + 1% pen/strep)
  Cytokines    : 400 IU/mL IL-2 + 25 ng/mL IL-7 (Miltenyi) + 50 ng/mL IL-15 (Miltenyi)
  Activator    : ImmunoCult Human CD3/CD28 T Cell Activator (STEMCELL) at 25 uL/mL
  Concentration: 1.25e6 cells/mL
  Duration     : 72 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 (= 4320 min; IR: 259200.0 SECOND)
  Purpose      : Expand and activate T cells to permissive state for electroporation.

Step 2 | Cell Wash and Resuspension in Transfection Buffer
  Buffer       : DMFection Buffer (DropGenie proprietary)
  Transfection : 0.01% Surfactant F (ITW Reagents) in DMFection Buffer
  Concentration: 1.0e7 cells/mL in Transfection Buffer
  Purpose      : Remove culture media components that interfere with electroporation.
  Assessment   : Viability > 80% required (NucleoCounter NC-202, ChemoMetec).

Step 3 | sgRNA Pre-Deposition onto Cartridge Substrate
  Method       : Echo 655 acoustic liquid handler (Beckman Coulter)
  Volume       : 40 nL spots per site
  Carrier      : Poly-L-glutamic acid (PGA, Sigma Aldrich) at 100 mg/mL
  sgRNA stock  : 100 pmol/uL (T cells), 200 pmol/uL (myoblasts)
  Mix ratio    : Combined to final sgRNA concentration of 55.6 pmol/uL (T cells)
  Process      : Dry-deposit and desiccate before cartridge assembly.
  Guides       : TRAC sgRNA (ARM 1); ExhaustionTarget sgRNAs (ARM 3; 45 targets)

Step 4 | Cartridge Loading (cells + Cas9 RNP)
  Cells loaded : 10,000 per edit (concentration 1.0e7 cells/mL, 100 uL per well)
  SpCas9       : 0.42 pmol per edit (final concentration 42 pmol in 100 uL, Aldevron)
  sgRNA        : 2.1 pmol per edit (pre-deposited dry on substrate)
  Loading tool : Assist Plus 8-channel 125 uL Integra Voyager pipette
  Incubation   : 5 min at room temperature (pre-pulse; abstraced as heat 25 C, 5 min)
  Note         : RNP complexes form in situ on the cartridge substrate during incubation.

Step 5 | Electroporation (Tri-Drop; 550 V, 2 ms, 2 pulses)
  Method       : Tri-Drop Electroporation on DropGenie electrode array.
                 Two conductive DMFection Buffer droplets flank the central cell droplet.
                 Electrode actuation (550 V, 2 ms, 2 pulses) delivers RNP cargo.
  Parameters   : 550 V, 2 ms pulse duration, 2 pulses (CD4+ / Treg arm)
                 500 V, 3 ms pulse duration, 2 pulses (Pan CD3+ arm)
  Dead volume  : Cartridge dead volume accounted for in total cell input calculation.

Step 6 | Offload and Post-KO Culture (3 days)
  Media        : Basal T Cell Media + 200 IU/mL IL-2
  Format       : 96-well round-bottom plate
  Duration     : 72 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 (= 4320 min; IR: 259200.0 SECOND)
  Offload tool : Assist Plus into 96-well plate

Step 7 | Knockout Detection (flow cytometry)
  Staining     : Anti-TCR alpha/beta antibody (surface); Ghost Dye Violet 510 (viability)
  Instrument   : Attune NxT Flow Cytometer (Thermo Fisher)
  Gating       : Live > Singlets > CD4+ or CD8+ > TCR alpha/beta-negative
  Detection    : knockoutDetection module (BioScript abstraction)
  Results      : CD4+ TRAC KO: 90.41% +/- 3.27; CD8+ TRAC KO: 91.87% +/- 3.13
                 Viability: 97.23% +/- 0.28 (TRAC RNP), 97.83% +/- 0.09 (NTC RNP)
  Branch       : knockoutSignal > 0  -> ARM 2 proceeds (dispose)
                 knockoutSignal <= 0 -> drain (insufficient KO)
  Regulatory T cells: 76.78% +/- 8.62 TCR KO; viability 97.22% +/- 0.89


PROTOCOL STEPS -- ARM 2: GFP KNOCK-IN AT TRAC LOCUS (HDR)
-----------------------------------------------------------

Step 8 | T Cell Activation (Dynabead protocol, separate donor)
  Cells        : Pan CD3+ T cells (separate leukopak donor)
  Media        : Basal T Cell Media + 200 IU/mL IL-2 + 10 ng/mL IL-7 + 5 ng/mL IL-15
  Activator    : Dynabeads Human T-Activator CD3/CD28 (Gibco), bead:cell ratio 2:5
  Format       : 96-well round-bottom plate, 2.5e5 cells/mL
  Duration     : 72 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 (= 4320 min; IR: 259200.0 SECOND)
  Pre-loading  : Dynabeads removed magnetically before cartridge loading.

Step 9 | RNP Assembly (on ice, 20 min)
  sgRNA        : 110 pmol TRAC sgRNA
  SpCas9       : 33 pmol SpCas9 (Aldevron)
  Complexing   : Mix on ice for 20 min (IR: 4 C, 1200.0 SECOND)
  Per edit     : 1.1 pmol sgRNA, 0.33 pmol Cas9

Step 10 | Cartridge Loading (cells + RNP + cssDNA template)
  Cells        : 10,000 per edit (1.0e7 cells/mL, 100 uL per well)
  Template     : GFP cssDNA (Full Circles Therapeutics); 4 kb circular single-stranded DNA
  Concentrations tested: 0.03 ug and 0.06 ug per edit
  Purpose      : cssDNA provides improved genomic integration efficiency vs dsDNA and
                 avoids immunogenic response associated with linear dsDNA.

Step 11 | Electroporation (500 V, 2 ms, 2 pulses)
  Parameters   : 500 V, 2 ms pulse duration, 2 pulses
                 Also tested: 500 V, 4 ms, 2 pulses

Step 12 | Offload and 10-day Expansion
  Media        : Basal T Cell Media + 300 IU/mL IL-2
  Format       : 96-well round-bottom plate
  Duration     : 10 days at 37 C, 5% CO2 (= 14400 min; IR: 864000.0 SECOND)

Step 13 | GFP Knock-In Detection (flow cytometry + fluorescence microscopy)
  Flow         : GFP positivity gating + TRAC KO co-stain (Attune NxT)
  Microscopy   : EVOS Cell Imaging System (Thermo Fisher), Day 10
  Detection    : knockInDetection module (BioScript abstraction)
  Results      : 52.37% +/- 9.70 GFP+ cells at 0.03 ug / 500V / 2ms / 2 pulses
                 41.14% +/- 9.45 at 0.06 ug / 500V / 2ms / 2 pulses
                 Significantly higher than no-template (11.21% +/- 2.83) and
                 off-chip controls (10.62% +/- 4.49) (p < 0.0001)
  Branch       : knockInSignal > 0  -> ARM 3 proceeds (dispose)
                 knockInSignal <= 0 -> drain

Anti-HER2 CAR-T generation (additional validation, same ARM 2 workflow):
  Template     : 3 kb dsDNA encoding anti-HER2 CAR (Integrated DNA Technologies);
                 flanked by TRAC-targeting homology arms.
  Detection    : Protein L staining (GenScript, 1:300 in 4% BSA) + CD3 co-stain
  Results      : HER2 CAR expression up to 40% (average 27.03%); viability > 55%
                 No dose-dependent differences across template concentrations.


PROTOCOL STEPS -- ARM 3: ARRAYED CRISPR EXHAUSTION SCREEN
----------------------------------------------------------

Step 14 | CD4+ T Cell Activation (screen donor)
  Cells        : CD4+ Helper T cells (AllCells), 1.25e6 cells/mL
  Media        : Basal T Cell Media + 400 IU/mL IL-2 + 25 ng/mL IL-7 + 50 ng/mL IL-15
  Duration     : 72 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 (= 4320 min; IR: 259200.0 SECOND)

Step 15 | Guide Pre-Deposition for 45-Target Screen
  Tool         : Echo 655 acoustic liquid handler
  Volume       : 40 nL per site
  Targets      : 45 candidate exhaustion regulators; 4 replicates each = 180 edits
                 + NTC and off-chip controls = 192 total edits (4 cartridge runs)
  Targets include (top hits): SIN3A, PAF1, PRDM1, SETBP1, STAT1, LAG3, ID2, TOX,
                              NR4A1, NR4A2, DNMT3A, EZH2, FOXO1, BATF, TCF7,
                              and 30 additional exhaustion-associated genes.

Step 16 | Cartridge Loading (screen arm)
  Cells        : 10,000 per edit (1.0e7 cells/mL, 100 uL per well)
  SpCas9       : 1 pmol per edit
  sgRNA        : 2 pmol per edit (pre-deposited dry)
  Incubation   : 5 min at room temperature (IR: 25 C, 300 SECOND)
  Vs. conventional: 500,000 cells, 100 pmol Cas9, 50 pmol sgRNA per edit
  Reduction    : 50x fewer cells, ~100x less Cas9, ~25x less sgRNA (Fig. 3G)

Step 17 | Electroporation (550 V, 2 ms, 2 pulses)
  Parameters   : 550 V, 2 ms, 2 pulses (CD4+ T cell optimised parameters)

Step 18 | Post-KO Recovery (3 days)
  Media        : Basal T Cell Media + 200 IU/mL IL-2
  Format       : 96-well round-bottom plate
  Duration     : 72 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 (= 4320 min; IR: 259200.0 SECOND)

Step 19 | Chronic Exhaustion Induction (9 cycles x 3 days = Days 3-28)
  Protocol     : ImmunoCult Human CD3/CD28 T Cell Activator (25 uL/mL) +
                 10 IU/mL IL-2 in 50 uL Basal T Cell Media.
                 Media changed every 3 days with fresh stimulation mix.
  Cycles       : 8 x 3-day cycles (IR: 259200.0 SECOND each = 3 days at 37 C)
                 + 1 final 48 h cycle (IR: 172800.0 SECOND = 2 days at 37 C)
  Total        : 9 cycles covering Days 3-28 of chronic stimulation
  BioScript    : Loop unrolled (no loop primitive in lilott8/BioScript); 9 sequential
                 mix + heat pairs (stimCells_c1 through stimCells_c9).
  Purpose      : Recapitulate progressive T cell dysfunction (gradual exhaustion in vivo
                 model); avoids acute activation-induced cell death.

Step 20 | LAG-3 Staining (exhaustion phenotype readout)
  Stain        : PE-LAG3 (BioLegend) + Ghost Dye Violet 510 + CD4 co-stain
  Incubation   : 20 min in Flow Cytometry Buffer at 4 C in dark
  Readout      : % LAG3-negative CD4+ T cells (exhaustion escape frequency)
  Detection    : exhaustionPhenotypeDetection module (BioScript abstraction)
  Gating       : Live > Singlets > CD4+ > LAG3-
  Branch       : screenSignal > 0  -> escape hit confirmed (dispose stainedForFACS)
                 screenSignal <= 0 -> no rescue (drain)

Step 21 | Cytokine Secretion Readout (ELISA)
  Collection   : Supernatants collected Day 28 (48 h after final re-stimulation)
  Stored       : -80 C until processing
  Kits         : TNFalpha and IFNgamma sandwich ELISA (RayBiotech)
  Dilution     : 3.84x or 2.5x in Assay Diluent B (RayBiotech)
  Curve fit    : 4-Parameter Logistic (4PL) regression for concentration interpolation
  Normalisation: Background-subtracted using media-only (MO) control; normalised to
                 cell count by flow cytometry and adjusted for dilution factor.
  Detection    : cytokineDetection module (BioScript abstraction; detect on screenSignal)

Step 22 | Composite Exhaustion Escape Scoring (off-chip, terminal)
  Metric       : z-score normalized sum of: IFNgamma + TNFalpha + % LAG3-negative CD4+ cells
  Exclusions   : Viability < 70% or CD4+ frequency < 90% deprioritised (confounders)
  Top hits     : SIN3A, PAF1, PRDM1, SETBP1, STAT1 (radar plot; Fig. 3F)
  Output       : Ranked target list; radar plots per top hit across all three axes.


REAGENTS
--------
Electroporation:
  DMFection Buffer         : DropGenie proprietary electroporation buffer
  Surfactant F Buffer      : 0.01% Surfactant F (ITW Reagents) in DMFection Buffer
  SpCas9 Nuclease          : Aldevron; 42 pmol per 100 uL load (KO), 100 pmol (screen)
  Alt-R Cas9 Enhancer      : IDT Alt-R Cas9 Electroporation Enhancer; 0.5 pmol/edit
                             (Regulatory T cells only)
  sgRNAs                   : Custom; Integrated DNA Technologies; PGA carrier (Sigma)
  EGFP mRNA                : TriLink Biotechnologies; 200 ug/mL (myoblasts),
                             100 ug/mL (T cells)
  GFP cssDNA               : Full Circles Therapeutics; 4 kb circular ssDNA; 0.03-0.06 ug/edit
  Anti-HER2 CAR dsDNA      : IDT Alt-R HDR Donor Block; 3 kb; 0.0375-10 ng/edit
  HDR Enhancer V2          : IDT Alt-R HDR Enhancer V2; 15 uM (CAR-T arm)

Cell culture:
  Basal T Cell Media       : RPMI 1640 + GlutaMax (Gibco) + 10% FBS + 1% pen/strep
  ImmunoCult Activator     : Human CD3/CD28 T Cell Activator (STEMCELL), 25 uL/mL
  IL-2 (activation)        : 200-400 IU/mL IL-2 (PeproTech)
  IL-2 (exhaustion screen) : 10 IU/mL IL-2 (PeproTech)
  IL-7                     : 25 ng/mL (activation) / 10 ng/mL (KI) (Miltenyi Biotec)
  IL-15                    : 50 ng/mL (activation) / 5 ng/mL (KI) (Miltenyi Biotec)
  Dynabeads T-Activator    : Gibco; bead:cell ratio 2:5 (KI arm only)

Flow cytometry:
  Flow Cytometry Buffer    : 1X PBS + 2% FBS + 2 mM EDTA (Invitrogen)
  Viability dye            : Ghost Dye Violet 510 (Cytek Biosciences), 1:1000
  PE-LAG3                  : BioLegend (exhaustion screen)
  TCR alpha/beta           : Surface stain (TRAC KO validation)
  FITC-FoxP3               : BioLegend; intracellular (Regulatory T cell characterisation)
  Protein L                : FITC-Protein L (GenScript), 1:300 in 4% BSA (CAR-T)
  Instrument               : Attune NxT Flow Cytometer (Thermo Fisher)

Detection / sequencing:
  Incucyte System          : Sartorius Live-Cell Analysis; 20X (myoblasts), 10X (T cells)
  Sanger Sequencing        : Quintara Bio; ICE analysis v3.0 (Synthego)
  ELISA                    : RayBiotech TNFalpha + IFNgamma sandwich ELISA kits


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : patel_dropgenie_dmf_crispr_screen.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 10 basic blocks, 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
DAG            : patel_dropgenie_dmf_crispr_screen_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations converted to minutes (m) for compiler compatibility.
                 BioScript supports s and m only; h and d tokens are not supported.
                 3 days   -> 4320m   (IR: 259200.0 SECOND)  -- T cell activation,
                                                                KO recovery, each
                                                                exhaustion cycle
                 20 min   -> 20m     (IR: 1200.0 SECOND)    -- on-ice RNP assembly
                 10 days  -> 14400m  (IR: 864000.0 SECOND)  -- KI expansion
                 5 min    -> 5m      (IR: 300.0 SECOND)     -- pre-pulse incubation
                 48 h     -> 2880m   (IR: 172800.0 SECOND)  -- final stimulation cycle

Modules        : transfectionEfficiencyDetection, knockoutDetection, knockInDetection,
                 exhaustionPhenotypeDetection, cytokineDetection

Manifests      : DMFectionBuffer, SurfactantF_Buffer, CD4_T_Cells, SpCas9_Nuclease,
                 TRAC_sgRNA, NTC_sgRNA, ExhaustionTarget_sgRNA, EGFP_mRNA,
                 ImmunoCult_CD3CD28_Activator, IL2_200IU, IL2_10IU, BasalTCellMedia,
                 GFP_cssDNA_Template, AntiHER2_CAR_dsDNA_Template, ProteinL_Stain,
                 PE_LAG3_Stain, FC_Oil

Abstraction notes:
  - `mix` at loading steps: abstracts Assist Plus cartridge well-loading; not bulk mixing.
  - `mix` with FC_Oil:      abstracts Tri-Drop circuit formation on electrode array;
                            the electroporation pulse is implicit in this merge event.
  - `heat` at 25 C, 5 min: abstracts the 5-min room-temperature pre-pulse incubation.
  - `heat` at 4 C, 20 min: abstracts on-ice RNP complexing before cartridge loading.
  - `dispense` for sgRNA:   abstracts Echo 655 acoustic pre-deposition (40 nL dry spots);
                            BioScript has no native acoustic dispense primitive.
  - Loop unrolling:         9 chronic re-stimulation cycles unrolled as 9 sequential
                            mix + heat pairs (stimCells_c1 to stimCells_c9).
                            lilott8/BioScript has no repeat/while primitive.
  - drain vs dispose:       `drain` in .bs source compiles to `dispose` in IR; the
                            compiler treats both identically at IR level. Semantically,
                            false-branch paths route waste to drain reservoir.

Biological scope notes:
  ARM 1 encodes TRAC KO in CD4+ T cells as the representative KO protocol.
  ARM 2 encodes GFP cssDNA knock-in. The anti-HER2 CAR-T arm uses the same
  workflow with AntiHER2_CAR_dsDNA_Template; a separate .bs extension is
  recommended for the full multi-concentration CAR titration experiment.
  ARM 3 encodes one representative screen condition (ExhaustionTarget_sgRNA).
  The full 45-target, 192-edit screen is parallelised across 48 cartridge sites
  (4 runs); BioScript encodes the single-condition logic; parallelism is
  implicit in the DropGenie instrument's independent site addressing.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Computer Vision Reveals Hidden Variables Underlying NF-kB Activation in Single Cells
Source Link  : https://www.science.org/doi/epdf/10.1126/sciadv.abg4135
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abg4135
Journal      : Science Advances, 2021, Vol. 7, Article eabg4135
Platform     : High-throughput microfluidic live-cell imaging (PDMS chip) + image-based SVM machine learning


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a microfluidic live-cell imaging approach to uncover hidden molecular
variables controlling heterogeneous NF-kB (nuclear factor kappa B) activation in single
mammalian cells. The core experiment uses automated PDMS microfluidic chambers to culture
and stimulate NIH 3T3 mouse fibroblasts expressing dual fluorescent reporters (p65-dsRed
for NF-kB dynamics, H2B-GFP as a nuclear marker), combined with a custom image-based support
vector machine (SVM) pipeline that predicts which individual cells will activate NF-kB from
their prestimulation images alone.

The protocol is divided into four functional phases:
  1. Microfluidic device preparation: fibronectin coating and cell seeding
  2. Live-cell imaging: 1.5 h unperturbed prestimulation imaging followed by TNF-alpha
     stimulation (0.1 ng/mL) and 6 h post-stimulation tracking of p65 nuclear translocation
  3. Image-based machine learning: SVM classifier trained on 236 hand-crafted features
     per cell; predicts activation with 79.4% accuracy from prestimulation images alone
  4. Fixed-cell immunofluorescence: validates the IkB-alpha/NF-kB ratio as the primary
     molecular determinant of heterogeneous single-cell activation probability

Key finding: cell-to-cell variability in NF-kB activation is largely explained by a
preexisting difference in the IkB/NF-kB ratio. Cells with a low IkB/NF-kB ratio show
minute "leaky" nuclear p65 localization at rest and are significantly more sensitive to
TNF stimulation. Activated cells show on average a 5-fold higher leaky nuclear p65 level
before stimulation than non-responding cells (P = 1.35e-13). Resting cells dynamically
transition between molecular states but maintain their overall activation probability
(autocorrelation r = 0.78 at 35 min before stimulation, n = 1109 cells).


DEVICE AND IMAGING SETUP
-------------------------
Device material  : PDMS microfluidic chambers
Surface coating  : Fibronectin (FC010-10MG), overnight at room temperature
Cell density     : ~20,000 cells/cm2; cells taken at 100% confluence via 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA
                   (25200-056) for 5 min and cultured 5 h before stimulation
Culture          : 37 C, 5% CO2; standard cell culture conditions maintained during imaging
                   using an on-stage incubation chamber
Microscope       : Nikon Eclipse Ti2
Camera           : Hamamatsu ORCA-Flash4.0 V3 Digital CMOS (C13440)
Magnification    : 20x
Imaging interval : 5 min per field of view
Stimulus delivery: TNF-alpha vials pressurized at 5 psi; connected to chip via PEEK microbore
                   tubing (VICI)
Image analysis   : Custom MATLAB scripts; NF-kB quantified as mean nuclear fluorescence
                   intensity after background correction; peak analysis via MATLAB smooth +
                   z-score normalization + peak detection


CELL LINE
---------
Parental         : p65(-/-) knockout NIH 3T3 mouse fibroblasts
Reporters        :
  p65-dsRed      : NF-kB transcription factor p65 fused to dsRed, expressed under native
                   p65 promotor; minimum fluorescence clone selected to represent endogenous
                   NF-kB pathway dynamics
  H2B-GFP        : Histone 2B fused to GFP, expressed from ubiquitin promotor; serves as
                   nuclear marker for segmentation and cell tracking

In activated cells, cytoplasmic p65-dsRed rapidly translocates to the nucleus in a digital
(switch-like) fashion within ~40 min of TNF stimulation. Non-responding cells show no
translocation and no NF-kB target gene expression.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Fibronectin Chamber Coating
  Reagent  : Fibronectin (FC010-10MG)
  Duration : Overnight (~720 min) at room temperature
  Purpose  : Promotes cell adhesion to PDMS chamber surface prior to loading

Step 2 | PBS Wash of Coated Chamber
  Reagent  : PBS
  Duration : 1 min
  Purpose  : Removes unbound fibronectin before cell seeding

Step 3 | Cell Seeding and Pre-stimulation Culture
  Cell line: NIH 3T3 p65-dsRed / H2B-GFP
  Density  : ~20,000 cells/cm2
  Process  : Cells harvested at 100% confluence with 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA (25200-056) for
             5 min, loaded into coated chamber
  Culture  : 5 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 (= 300 min) before stimulation; allows cell adhesion and
             equilibration to endogenous reporter expression levels

Step 4 | Prestimulation Live-Cell Imaging (t = -90 min to t = 0)
  Duration  : 1.5 h = 90 min; image every 5 min (18 time points)
  Channels  : p65-dsRed (red), H2B-GFP (green), phase contrast
  Output    : 236 hand-crafted features per cell per time point, including:
                - Mean nuclear p65-dsRed fluorescence (top predictor, r = 0.62)
                - SD of nuclear p65-dsRed
                - Nuclear phase entropy
                - Nuclear pixel correlation (information measure)
                - Otsu dimension
                - SFTA (Segmentation-based Fractal Texture Analysis)
                - Major axis length
                - H2B-GFP channel morphology features
  Purpose   : Provides the unperturbed cell image input for the SVM activation classifier.
              Cells are not chemically stimulated during this window.
  Note      : mix step in BioScript abstracts the repeated imaging acquisition loop;
              no reagent mixing occurs at this step.

Step 5 | TNF-alpha Stimulation (t = 0)
  Reagent          : TNF-alpha (PMC3014_3671982503)
  Diluent          : FluoroBrite DMEM (A1896701) + 2x GlutaMAX (35050061) +
                     penicillin/streptomycin (15140-122) + FBS (16140071)
  Concentration    : 0.1 ng/mL (main dataset, n = 2113 cells)
                     Multi-dose: 0.005, 0.05, 0.5, 5 ng/mL (n = 3456 cells combined)
  Delivery         : Pressurized vial at 5 psi; PEEK microbore tubing (VICI); chip inlet
  Time zero        : Stimulation marks t = 0 for all single-cell NF-kB trace analyses

Step 6 | Post-Stimulation Live-Cell Imaging (t = 0 to t = +360 min)
  Duration      : 6 h = 360 min at 37 C, 5% CO2; image every 5 min (72 time points)
  Readout       : Nuclear NF-kB (p65-dsRed) tracked per cell over 6 h
  Activation    : Responding cells show complete cytoplasm-to-nucleus translocation
                  (digital / switch-like behavior); non-responding cells show no change
  Labeling      : Binary threshold on (nuclear p65_peak - nuclear p65_(t=0)) > 500
                  (MATLAB: smooth + z-score normalization, peak detection; Fig. S4A)
  Datasets      : Main: 0.1 ng/mL TNF, n = 2113 cells (independent validation set)
                  Multi-dose: 0.005-5 ng/mL, n = 3456 cells (SVM training set)

Step 7 | NF-kB Activation Detection (QC Gate)
  Module   : nfkbActivationDetection
  Duration : 30 s (image analysis classification)
  Gate     :
    Pass (activationSignal > 0)  -> activated cell; proceed to fixed-cell IF (Step 8-13)
    Fail (activationSignal <= 0) -> non-responding cell; drain

Step 8 | PBS Rinse (pass branch only)
  Reagent  : PBS
  Duration : 1 min
  Purpose  : Removes culture medium before fixation; matches Materials and Methods protocol

Step 9 | Paraformaldehyde Fixation (pass branch only)
  Reagent     : 4% PFA in PBS (ParaformaldehydeFixative)
  Duration    : 10 min at room temperature (25 C)
  Imaging note: Cell image taken at t = -5 min (immediately preceding fixation) used to
                align fixed-cell IF data with live imaging UMAP space (Fig. 5A-B)

Step 10 | Blocking and Permeabilization (pass branch only)
  Buffer   : 10% BSA + 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS (BlockingPermeabilizationBuffer)
  Duration : 1 h (60 min) at room temperature
  Purpose  : Blocks non-specific antibody binding; permeabilizes cell membranes for
             intracellular IkB-alpha antibody access

Step 11 | Primary Antibody - Anti-IkB-alpha (pass branch only)
  Antibody : Rabbit polyclonal anti-IkB-alpha (ab7217)
  Buffer   : 2% BSA + 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS
  Duration : 1 h (60 min) at 37 C
  Target   : IkB-alpha, the main inhibitor of NF-kB; binds p65 and retains it in cytoplasm
             in unstimulated cells; the IkB/NF-kB ratio predetermines activation probability
             (simulation: rho = -0.256, P = 2.7e-11; Fig. 5C)

Step 12 | PBS Wash After Primary Antibody (pass branch only)
  Reagent  : PBS
  Duration : 1 min
  Purpose  : Removes unbound primary antibody before secondary incubation

Step 13 | Secondary Antibody - Alexa Fluor 647 (pass branch only)
  Antibody : Goat polyclonal anti-rabbit IgG H&L Alexa Fluor 647 (G378361)
  Buffer   : 2% BSA + 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS
  Duration : 1 h (60 min) at 37 C
  Read     : AF647 signal (ex ~650 nm / em ~668 nm) quantifies IkB-alpha in nuclear and
             cytoplasmic compartments for IkB/NF-kB ratio analysis
  Validation: Activated (high-scoring) fixed cells show significantly lower IkB/NF-kB ratio,
              higher nuclear NF-kB, and larger cellular area than inactive cells (Fig. 5D)

Step 14 | Immunofluorescence Staining QC Detection
  Module   : immunofluorescenceDetection
  Duration : 30 s
  Readout  : IkB/NF-kB ratio per cell (nuclear + cytoplasmic segmentation of AF647 + p65-dsRed)
  Gate     :
    Pass (ifStainingSignal > 0)  -> IkB/NF-kB ratio quantified; dispose stained sample
    Fail (ifStainingSignal <= 0) -> staining failure; dispose


MACHINE LEARNING PIPELINE
--------------------------
Model            : Support Vector Machine (SVM), cubic kernel
Features         : 236 hand-crafted features per cell (nuclear segmentation, texture,
                   morphology); extracted with custom MATLAB scripts (table S2)
Training set     : Multi-dose dataset: [0.005, 0.05, 0.5, 5] ng/mL TNF, n = 3456 cells
                   10-fold cross-validation, 10% dropout
Validation set   : Independent single-dose dataset: 0.1 ng/mL TNF, n = 2113 cells
Accuracy         : 73% (cross-validation, cubic kernel); 79.4% (independent validation set)
Top predictor    : Mean nuclear p65-dsRed fluorescence prestimulation (r = 0.62, P < 1e-100)
Other predictors : SD nuclear p65, nuclear phase entropy, pixel correlation, information
                   measure, Otsu dimension, SFTA, major axis length
Alternate models : CNN and decision tree outperform SVM in accuracy but lack interpretable
                   feature attribution; SVM chosen for biological insight
Code             : https://github.com/parthivapatel/ML_cellim.git
Dataset DOI      : 10.5281/zenodo.5361956


KEY FINDINGS
------------
1. Prestimulation p65 nuclear leakiness is the primary predictor of single-cell NF-kB
   activation (r = 0.62 with activation probability; Fig. 2C).
2. The IkB/NF-kB ratio is the molecular driver of p65 leakiness and activation probability;
   significant inverse correlation (rho = -0.256, P = 2.7e-11) confirmed by IF (Fig. 5C).
3. Activated cells show on average 5-fold higher leaky nuclear p65 before stimulation than
   non-responding cells (P = 1.35e-13; Fig. 4E). Leakiness represents ~12% of total fluorescence.
4. Unstimulated cells dynamically transition between molecular states but maintain stable
   activation probability (autocorrelation r = 0.78 at 35 min before stimulation, n = 1109).
5. 73.71% of state transitions remain within or adjacent to the same activation-probability
   cluster; TNF sensitivity is stable across the observed prestimulation time window.
6. Counterintuitively, cells with high initial IkB require a smaller TNF dose to achieve
   NF-kB activation, because probability depends on the IkB/NF-kB ratio, not absolute IkB.


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : patel_nfkb_computer_vision_single_cell.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG            : patel_nfkb_computer_vision_single_cell_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations in s or m (BioScript supports s and m only; h not supported)
                 Overnight coating  -> 720m  (IR: 43200.0 SECOND)
                 5 h culture        -> 300m  (IR: 18000.0 SECOND)
                 1.5 h prestim      -> 90m   (IR: 5400.0 SECOND)
                 6 h post-stim      -> 360m  (IR: 21600.0 SECOND)
                 1 h Ab incubations -> 60m   (IR: 3600.0 SECOND)
                 10 min PFA fix     -> 10m   (IR: 600.0 SECOND)
drain          : Normalizes to dispose in IR -- expected compiler behavior, not a bug
Modules        : nfkbActivationDetection, immunofluorescenceDetection
Manifest       : NIH3T3_p65dsRed_H2BGFP_Cells, FibronectinCoating, PBS,
                 FluoroBriteDMEM_TNFalpha, ParaformaldehydeFixative,
                 BlockingPermeabilizationBuffer, IkBa_PrimaryAntibody,
                 AlexaFluor647_SecondaryAntibody
CFG note       : BB3 (activationFail) drain normalizes to dispose in IR; DOT confirms
                 BB1->BB2->BB4 and BB1->BB3->BB4 edges present and correct

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Droplet-based single-cell RNA sequencing of paraformaldehyde-fixed cells (FD-seq)
Source Link  : https://www.protocols.io/view/droplet-based-single-cell-rna-sequencing-of-parafo-n2bvj94k5lk5/v1
Paper DOI    : https://dx.doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.pex-1604/v1
Journal      : Research Square (preprint), posted October 1, 2021
Authors      : Hoang Van Phan, Michiel van Gent, Nir Drayman, Anindita Basu,
               Michaela U. Gack, Savas Tay
Affiliation  : The University of Chicago; Cleveland Clinic
Platform     : Drop-seq microfluidic chip (Macosko et al., Cell 2015)
               Droplet Generation Microfluidic Chip (commercial or custom PDMS)


OVERVIEW
--------
FD-seq (Fixed Droplet RNA Sequencing) is a method for droplet-based single-cell RNA
sequencing (scRNA-seq) of paraformaldehyde (PFA)-fixed, stained, and sorted cells.
Standard high-throughput scRNA-seq methods such as Drop-seq are not compatible with
PFA-fixed cells due to RNA crosslinking. FD-seq resolves this by performing PFA
crosslink reversal inside intact droplets (56 C, 60 min) using heat and Proteinase K
before droplet breaking, thereby releasing intact mRNA for reverse transcription.

FD-seq is designed to work with existing Drop-seq experimental setups and does not
require additional specialized processing equipment. It enables scRNA-seq of cells that
require fixation prior to sequencing, e.g., for biosafety, intracellular staining,
or compatibility with FACS sorting workflows.

The protocol is divided into ten sequential phases:
  1.  Cell fixation (4% PFA, 15 min, RT)
  2.  Cell permeabilization (0.1% Triton X-100, 15 min, RT)
  3.  Pre-droplet preparation (0.01% BSA washes; lysis buffer + bead preparation)
  4.  Droplet generation (Drop-seq chip; co-encapsulation of cells and barcoded beads)
  5.  In-droplet crosslink reversal (56 C, 60 min; Proteinase K + heat)
  6.  Droplet breaking (Perfluorooctan-1-ol + 6X SSC)
  7.  Reverse transcription (Maxima H- RT; 25 C 30 min + 42 C 90 min)
  8.  Exonuclease I digestion (37 C, 45 min; removes unextended primers)
  9.  Whole transcriptome amplification (WTA PCR; Kapa HiFi; 14-cycle program)
  10. Tagmentation and library preparation (Nextera XT; NextSeq paired-end sequencing)


DEVICE AND PLATFORM
-------------------
Chip         : Drop-seq Droplet Generation Microfluidic Chip
               Commercial chip (Macosko 2015) or in-house PDMS fabrication.
               Hydrophobic treatment with Aquapel (cat 47100) required before use;
               chip rested overnight at RT after treatment.
Syringe pumps: Harvard Apparatus Pump 33 DDS and/or KD Scientific model 100.
Inlets       : Cell syringe (3 ml/h), Bead syringe (3 ml/h), Oil syringe (12 ml/h)
Oil          : Bio-Rad droplet generation oil (cat 1864006)
Droplets     : Nanoliter-scale water-in-oil emulsion; single cell + single bead
               co-encapsulated per droplet (stochastic, Poisson-limited).
Beads        : Drop-seq beads (ChemGenes Corp, cat Macosko-2011-10(V+));
               resuspended in TE-TW at 4 C after manufacturer wash.
               Loaded at 120,000 beads/ml in lysis buffer + 50 mM DTT + 800 U/ml Proteinase K.
Cells        : Loaded at 100,000 cells/ml in 0.01% BSA; filtered through cell strainer.
Collection   : ~20 min per sample into 50 ml centrifuge tube.


REAGENTS
--------
Fixation and permeabilization:
  - 4% PFA in PBS (Santa Cruz Biotechnology, cat sc-281692)
  - Triton X-100, molecular biology grade (0.1% in wash buffer)

Wash buffer (prepare fresh):
  - PBS + 1% BSA (molecular biology grade) + 40 U/ml RNase inhibitor (NEB, cat N0447S)

0.01% BSA: molecular biology grade BSA in PBS; prepare at least 10 ml per sample

Lysis buffer (store at 4 C):
  - 22 ml nuclease-free water + 15 ml 20% Ficoll (Sigma F5415) + 10 ml 1M Tris pH 7.5
    + 2 ml 0.5M EDTA + 1 ml 10% Sarkosyl (Teknova S3377)
  - Add 50 ul 1M DTT + 50 ul 800 U/ml Proteinase K (NEB) per 1 ml before use
  - Filter with 40 um cell strainer before use; store on ice

Additional buffers (store at RT unless noted):
  - TE-SDS : 46.9 ml NFW + 500 ul 1M Tris pH 8.0 + 100 ul 0.5M EDTA + 2.5 ml 10% SDS
  - TE-TW  : 49.4 ml NFW + 500 ul 1M Tris pH 8.0 + 100 ul 0.5M EDTA + 5 ul 100% Tween-20
  - 10 mM Tris pH 8.0 : 49.5 ml NFW + 500 ul 1M Tris pH 8.0
  - 6X SSC : 350 ml NFW + 150 ml 20X SSC

Droplet breaking reagent:
  - Perfluorooctan-1-ol (Synquest, cat 2101-3-20)

RT mix (200 ul total):
  - 80 ul nuclease-free water
  - 40 ul 5X Maxima H- RT buffer
  - 40 ul 20% Ficoll
  - 20 ul 10 mM dNTPs (NEB)
  - 5 ul RNase inhibitor (NEB, cat M0314L)
  - 5 ul 100 uM TSO_RNAhybrid primer
  - 10 ul Maxima H- reverse transcriptase (Thermo Fisher, cat EP0753)

Exo I mix (200 ul total):
  - 170 ul nuclease-free water + 20 ul 10X Exo I buffer + 10 ul Exo I (NEB, M0293S)

WTA PCR (50 ul per well):
  - 24.6 ul water + beads (5,000 beads/well)
  - 0.4 ul 100 uM TSO_PCR primer
  - 25 ul Kapa HiFi Readymix (Roche, cat 7958935001)

Tagmentation kit:
  - Nextera XT DNA Library Prep Kit (Illumina, cat FC-131-1024)
  - P5-TSO primer + Nextera_N7XX index primer (custom; see primer sequences)
  - Ampure XP beads (Beckman Coulter, cat A63880); 0.6X bead ratio

Primers:
  - TSO_RNAhybrid  : AAGCAGTGGTATCAACGCAGAGTGAATrGrGrG  (reverse transcription)
  - TSO_PCR        : AAGCAGTGGTATCAACGCAGAGT              (WTA amplification)
  - P5-TSO         : AATGATACGGCGACCACCGAGATCTACACGCCTGTCCGCGGAAGCAGTGGTATCAACGCAGAGT*A*C
  - Nextera_N7XX   : CAAGCAGAAGACGGCATACGAGAT[i7]GTCTCGTGGGCTCGG
  - Custom Read 1  : GCCTGTCCGCGGAAGCAGTGGTATCAACGCAGAGTAC  (NGS)


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Phase 1 | Cell Fixation
  Reagents    : PBS, 1% BSA wash buffer, 4% PFA in PBS
  Step 1      : Wash cells once with 1% BSA in PBS (400g, 5 min)
  Step 2      : Fix with 4% PFA in PBS at RT for 15 min
  Step 3      : Spin (400g, 5 min); discard PFA; wash once with wash buffer
  Storage     : Cells can be stored in wash buffer at 4 C overnight before proceeding
  BS variable : washedFixed (post-fixation, post-wash state)

Phase 2 | Cell Permeabilization
  Reagents    : 0.1% Triton X-100 in wash buffer, wash buffer
  Step 1      : Add 500 ul 0.1% Triton X-100 to cell pellet; incubate RT for 15 min
  Step 2      : Add 1 ml wash buffer; spin (400g, 5 min); discard supernatant
  Step 3      : Wash once more with 1 ml wash buffer
  Optional    : Blocking and intracellular staining can follow; reagents diluted in wash buffer
  BS variable : washed4 (post-permeabilization, post-wash state)

Phase 3 | Pre-Droplet Preparation
  Reagents    : 0.01% BSA, lysis buffer + DTT + Proteinase K, Drop-seq beads
  Cell prep   : Wash PFA-fixed cells 3x with 0.01% BSA (2 ml each); resuspend at
                100,000 cells/ml in 0.01% BSA; filter with appropriate cell strainer
  Bead prep   : Count beads with Fuchs-Rosenthal hemocytometer (20 ul beads + 20 ul 20% Ficoll)
                Resuspend beads at 120,000 beads/ml in lysis buffer (with DTT + ProtK); store on ice
  BS variable : cellsReady, beadsReady
  Compiler note: 3x 0.01% BSA washes unrolled explicitly (no loop construct in BioScript)

Phase 4 | Droplet Generation
  Chip        : Drop-seq Droplet Generation Microfluidic Chip (Aquapel-treated, rested overnight)
  Syringe setup:
    Cell syringe (BD 3 ml Luer-Lok): cells in 0.01% BSA; flow rate 3 ml/h
    Bead syringe (BD 3 ml Luer-Lok + magnetic disc VP 772DP-N42-5-2): beads in lysis buffer;
                  flow rate 3 ml/h; magnetic stirrer (VP710D2) to prevent bead settling
    Oil syringe (BD 10 ml Luer-Lok): Bio-Rad oil; flow rate 12 ml/h
  Start order : Cell pump first, then bead pump, then oil pump
  Collection  : ~20 min per sample into 50 ml centrifuge tube
  QC          : Inspect chip junction under microscope; stable generation = blur at junction
  BS variable : emulsion
  Compiler note: Syringe pump flow and chip geometry are not BioScript primitives;
                 cell/bead co-encapsulation modelled as sequential mix operations

Phase 5 | In-Droplet Crosslink Reversal
  Reagents    : Heat block
  Step 1      : Incubate 50 ml tube with droplets at 56 C for 60 min (heat block)
                KEY STEP: Proteinase K + heat reverses PFA crosslinks inside intact droplets
  Step 2      : Remove from heat block; leave at RT for 10 min
  Step 3      : Place on ice for 5 min
  QC check    : Pipette ~15 ul oil + 5 ul droplets onto Fuchs-Rosenthal hemocytometer;
                verify most droplets contain at most 1 bead
  BS variable : emulsion (in-place heat; heat is void in BioScript)
  Duration    : 56 C for 60m; 25 C for 10m; 4 C for 5m

Phase 6 | Droplet Breaking
  Reagents    : 6X SSC, Perfluorooctan-1-ol (in chemical hood)
  Step 1      : Remove as much oil as possible from 50 ml tube without disturbing droplets
  Step 2      : Add 30 ml 6X SSC + 1 ml Perfluorooctan-1-ol (chemical hood)
  Step 3      : Seal tube; shake vertically 4 times; spin at 1000g for 1 min
  Step 4      : Transfer ~30 ml supernatant (above oil interface) to new 50 ml tube
  Step 5      : Add 30 ml 6X SSC to original tube; wait 2-3 s; transfer 30 ml supernatant
                to second new 50 ml tube
  Step 6      : Spin both new tubes at 1000g for 3 min; pool beads into 1.5 ml DNA LoBind tube
  Step 7      : Wash beads: 2x with 1 ml 6X SSC, 1x with 300 ul 5X Maxima H- RT buffer
                (1000g, 1 min each); discard supernatant
  BS variable : beadWash2 (post-break, post-wash bead fraction)

Phase 7 | Reverse Transcription
  Reagents    : RT mix (200 ul; see Reagents section)
  Step 1      : Add 200 ul RT mix to beads; incubate RT for 30 min with rotation
                (primer annealing and RT initiation)
  Step 2      : Transfer to 42 C for 90 min with rotation (cDNA synthesis)
  Step 3      : Spin beads; discard supernatant
  Washes      : 1x TE-SDS (1 ml), 2x TE-TW (1 ml each), 1x 10 mM Tris pH 8.0
                (all at 1000g, 1 min; modelled as BSA_Wash_Buffer in BioScript)
  BS variable : rtWashed4
  Duration    : RT mix 30m; heat 25c for 30m; heat 42c for 90m
  Compiler note: 90 min = 90m (no h token); 4 wash steps unrolled explicitly

Phase 8 | Exonuclease I Digestion
  Reagents    : Exo I mix (200 ul; see Reagents section)
  Step 1      : Add 200 ul Exo I mix to beads; incubate 37 C for 45 min with rotation
                (removes unextended TSO_RNAhybrid primers from bead surface)
  Step 2      : Spin beads; discard supernatant
  Washes      : 1x TE-SDS, 2x TE-TW (1000g, 1 min each)
  Storage     : If not proceeding immediately: store beads in 1 ml TE-TW at 4 C;
                resuspend in nuclease-free water when ready for WTA
  BS variable : exoWashed3
  Duration    : heat 37c for 45m

Phase 9 | Whole Transcriptome Amplification (WTA)
  Reagents    : Kapa HiFi Readymix, TSO_PCR primer, 96-well plate, Ampure XP beads
  Step 1      : Count beads; resuspend in nuclease-free water at max 5,000 beads per 24.6 ul
  Step 2      : Distribute into 96-well plate (5,000 beads in 24.6 ul per well)
  Step 3      : Set up 50 ul PCR reaction: 24.6 ul beads + water, 0.4 ul 100 uM TSO_PCR,
                25 ul Kapa HiFi Readymix
  Thermocycler program:
    95 C  3 min   (initial denaturation)
    4x  [98 C 20s, 65 C 45s, 72 C 3 min]  (low-cycle amplification)
    10x [98 C 20s, 67 C 20s, 72 C 3 min]  (high-cycle amplification)
    72 C  5 min   (final extension)
    4 C   hold
  Ampure XP purification (0.6X bead ratio):
    Add 10 ul NFW per well; pool 50 ul from each well; add Ampure beads (30 ul equiv per well)
    Incubate 5 min RT; magnetic rack 5 min; wash 4x with 1 ml 80% ethanol
    Dry 5 min; elute in 10 ul NFW per well; recover supernatant
    Store purified WTA at -20 C
  Expected result: Broad band, peak 600-700 bp (TapeStation; Figure 1 in paper)
  BS variable : wtaReaction
  Compiler note: No PCR primitive or loop in BioScript; thermocycler phases encoded as
                 4 sequential heat steps (aggregate cycle durations):
                 95c/3m, 65c/12m (4 cycles x 3 min), 67c/10m (10 cycles x 1 min), 72c/5m

Phase 9 QC Gate | barcodeIntegrityDetection
  Module      : barcodeIntegrityDetection
  Abstracts   : Ampure XP 0.6X cleanup + Qubit/TapeStation quantification of WTA products
  Pass (BB2)  : barcodeSignal > 0 -> valid WTA library (600-700 bp peak); proceed to tagmentation
  Fail (BB3)  : barcodeSignal <= 0 -> amplification or bead failure; drain wtaReaction
  Join (BB4)  : dispose barcodeSignal; fall into tagmentation

Phase 10 | Tagmentation and Library Preparation
  Kit         : Nextera XT DNA Library Prep Kit (Illumina, cat FC-131-1024)
  Input       : 450 pg purified WTA product per reaction (2 parallel reactions)
  Quantify    : Qubit quantification of WTA products before tagmentation
  Step 1      : Tagmentation: Tagment DNA mix (10 ul) + WTA product (5 ul, diluted to 5 ul NFW)
                + Amplicon Tagment mix (5 ul); 55 C for exactly 5 min
  Step 2      : Neutralise: add 5 ul NT buffer; mix; RT for 5 min; place on ice
  Step 3      : PCR amplification:
                add 8 ul NFW + 1 ul 10 uM P5-TSO + 1 ul 10 uM Nextera_N7XX + 15 ul Nextera PCR MM
                Thermocycler: 95 C 30s; 12x [95 C 10s, 55 C 30s, 72 C 30s]; 72 C 5 min; 4 C hold
  Ampure XP purification (0.6X): same protocol as WTA cleanup; store library at -20 C
  Expected result: Broad band, peak ~400 bp (Fragment Analyzer; Figure 2 in paper)
  BS variable : tagReaction1, tagReaction2 (two parallel reactions from same WTA pool)
  Compiler note: Tagmentation PCR encoded as 3 heat steps:
                 95c/30s (init), 55c/6m (12 cycles x 30s), 72c/5m (final extension)

Phase 10 QC Gate | wqaQCDetection
  Module      : wqaQCDetection
  Abstracts   : Ampure XP 0.6X cleanup + BioAnalyzer/Fragment Analyzer quantification
                + NextSeq library loading QC
  Pass (BB5)  : librarySignal > 0 -> valid library (~400 bp peak); dispose tagReaction1, tagReaction2
  Fail (BB6)  : librarySignal <= 0 -> tagmentation failure; drain tagReaction1, tagReaction2
  Terminal (BB7): dispose librarySignal; NOP

Next Generation Sequencing
  Platform    : Illumina NextSeq (>=75 cycles)
  Library QC  : BioAnalyzer quantification; denature per manufacturer guidelines
  Read mode   : Paired-end, single index
  Read lengths: Read 1 = 20 bp (cell barcode + UMI), Read 2 = 60 bp (cDNA), Index 1 = 8 bp
  Custom primer: Custom Read 1 primer (GCCTGTCCGCGGAAGCAGTGGTATCAACGCAGAGTAC)
  Throughput  : One 20-min droplet collection run fully sequenced with high output kit


TIME ESTIMATES
--------------
  Sample fixation, permeabilization, and staining : ~2 hours
  Sample preparation and droplet generation        : ~1.5 hours
  Crosslink reversal (in-droplet)                  : ~1 hour 15 minutes
  Reverse transcription                            : ~2.5 hours
  Exonuclease I digestion                          : ~1 hour
  Whole transcriptome amplification                : ~3 hours
  Sample purification (Ampure XP, WTA)             : ~0.5 hours
  Tagmentation                                     : ~2 hours
  Sample purification (Ampure XP, library)         : ~0.5 hours
  Next generation sequencing                       : ~12 hours
  ---------------------------------------------------------------
  Total (excluding sequencing)                     : ~14.25 hours


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : phan_fdseq_pfa_scrna.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG            : phan_fdseq_pfa_scrna_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations in seconds (s) or minutes (m)
                 (BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported)
                 Key conversions:
                   60 min  -> 60m   (crosslink reversal; IR: 3600.0 SECOND)
                   90 min  -> 90m   (RT cDNA synthesis; IR: 5400.0 SECOND)
                   45 min  -> 45m   (Exo I digestion; IR: 2700.0 SECOND)
                   30 min  -> 30m   (RT primer annealing; IR: 1800.0 SECOND)
Modules        : barcodeIntegrityDetection, wqaQCDetection
Manifests      : PFA_4pct, PBS, BSA_Wash_Buffer, TritonX100_01pct, BSA_001pct,
                 LysisBuffer_DTT_ProtK, DropSeq_Beads, Oil_BioRad, Perfluorooctan1ol,
                 SSC_6X, RT_Mix, ExoI_Mix, WTA_PCR_Mix, NTBuffer, TagmentDNAMix,
                 AmpliconTagmentMix, P5TSO_Primer, NexteraN7XX_Primer, NexteraPCRMasterMix
Compiler fixes applied:
  - Non-ASCII Unicode arrows (U+2192) in comment replaced with ASCII '->'
    (ANTLR4 FileStream is ASCII-only; byte 0xe2 at position 5502 caused UnicodeDecodeError)
  - DropSeq_Beads added as explicit dispense before mix
    (compiler SimpleSymbolVisitor requires all mix operands to be dispense-bound variables;
    manifest names alone are not in-scope without a prior dispense)
Known IR lowering behaviour:
  - drain lowers to dispose in IR (expected; confirmed in prior protocols)
  - bsbbif_2_t (true branch) has no explicit jump in IR; falls through implicitly to BB4
    (standard lilott8 behaviour; CFG edges confirmed correct in DAG)

protocol.title: Droplet-based single-cell RNA sequencing of paraformaldehyde-fixed cells (FD-seq)
protocol.platform: Drop-seq microfluidic chip (Macosko et al., Cell 2015)
protocol.objective: Droplet-based scRNA-seq of PFA-fixed, stained, and sorted cells via in-droplet crosslink reversal using Proteinase K and heat before droplet breaking

device.hydrophobic_treatment: Aquapel Glass Treatment Applicator (cat 47100); treat via cell inlet for 2-3 min; dry with air; rest overnight at RT
