description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Extracellular Vesicle microRNA Quantification from Plasma Using an Integrated Microfluidic Device
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/s42003-019-0435-1
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-019-0435-1
Journal      : Communications Biology, 2019, Vol. 2, Article 189
Platform     : Integrated microfluidics (SAW lysing chip + IEM concentration/sensing chip)
Authors      : Zeinab Ramshani*, Chenguang Zhang*, Katherine Richards, Lulu Chen, Geyang Xu,
               Bangyan L. Stiles, Reginald Hill, Satyajyoti Senapati, David B. Go, Hsueh-Chia Chang
               (* equal contribution)
Institutions : University of Notre Dame; University of Southern California; Jinan University


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a PCR-free integrated microfluidic platform for absolute quantification
of free-floating and extracellular vesicle (EV)-contained microRNAs (miRNAs) directly from
untreated human plasma or serum. The platform integrates two chips in series:

  Chip 1 (SAW lysing chip): Surface acoustic waves (SAWs) generated by interdigitated electrodes
    on a LiNbO3 piezoelectric substrate mechanically lyse EVs under continuous flow, releasing
    their miRNA cargo without chemical reagents.

  Chip 2 (Concentration/sensing chip): Two sets of ion-exchange membranes (IEMs) — a cation-
    exchange membrane (CEM) for electrokinetic concentration and an anion-exchange membrane (AEM)
    functionalized with a target-specific oligoprobe as the sensor — detect and quantify the target
    miRNA via current-voltage curve (CVC) shift in the over-limiting current region.

The two chips are connected by a 500 um diameter, 10 cm Tygon tube enabling uninterrupted sample
transfer with no analyte loss between stages. By conducting two sequential 30-minute measurements
— one with the SAW device OFF (free-floating miRNA only) and one with it ON (total miRNA: free-
floating + EV-released) — the EV-miRNA fraction is directly computed from the difference in
voltage shift (Delta-V) between the two runs.

Target biomarker: miRNA hsa-mir-21-5p (miR-21; sequence: TAGCTTATCAGACTGATGTTGA), associated
with pancreatic, lung, colorectal cancer, and hepatocellular carcinoma.

Key advantages over conventional RT-qPCR:
  - No EV extraction, RNA purification, reverse transcription, or amplification required
  - Assay time: 30 min per measurement (vs. 13 h for RT-qPCR)
  - Sample volume: 20 uL per measurement (vs. 1 mL for RT-qPCR)
  - Quantification uncertainty: <10% (absolute quantification)
  - Detection limit: 1 pM


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Chip 1 — SAW Lysing Chip
  Substrate  : 128 deg YX lithium niobate (LiNbO3), piezoelectric
  Electrodes : 20 pairs of interdigitated aluminum electrodes (200 nm thick; 20 nm Ti adhesion)
               Width-controlled single-phase unidirectional IDT; resonant frequency: 28 MHz
  Channel    : Polycarbonate, 15 x 2 x 0.3 mm (l/w/t); attached with double-sided Kapton tape
               Channel oriented parallel to IDTs; SAW propagates perpendicular to channel
  Operation  : SAW generated at 28 MHz, 1 W (Agilent 33250A + E&I 325LA RF amplifier)
               Acoustic pressure shears EV membranes; ~1 min exposure at 250 uL/h achieves
               ~100% EV lysis (50% more efficient than TRIzol chemical lysis)

Chip 2 — Concentration/Sensing Chip
  Material   : Polycarbonate (three-layer), 60 x 2 x 0.3 mm (l/w/t)
  CEM (x2)  : Cation-exchange membranes (Mega a.s., Czech Republic)
               Implanted at bottom of chip bridging main channel and electrode reservoirs
               200 V DC applied via Keithley 2400 SourceMeter through platinum electrodes
               Reservoir buffer: 10x TAE (400 mM Tris-acetate + 10 mM EDTA)
               Creates depletion zone concentrating negatively charged miRNA up to 1000-fold
  AEM sensor : Anion-exchange membrane (Mega a.s., Czech Republic)
               Polystyrene-divinylbenzene / quaternary ammonium / polyethylene / polyamide support
               Framed by resin mold; positioned in orifice upstream of CEM in main channel
               Functionalized with miR-21 complementary ssDNA oligoprobe via amine-coupling
               Disposable: replaced after each single use to maintain repeatability
  Measurement: Gamry 500 potentiostat; 0-2.5 V CVC sweep; Ag-AgCl reference electrodes;
               platinum measurement electrodes; channel and reservoirs in 0.1x PBS during sweep

Interconnect
  Tygon tube, 500 um diameter, 10 cm length; connects SAW chip outlet to IEM chip inlet


REAGENTS
--------
  PBS 1x          : Injection buffer and driver fluid (Fischer Scientific)
  PBS 4x          : Post-hybridisation wash buffer (removes non-hybridised species from AEM)
  PBS 0.1x        : CVC measurement buffer (low ionic strength maximises Delta-V signal)
  TAE 10x         : Electrode reservoir buffer (400 mM Tris-acetate + 10 mM EDTA)
  miR-21 probe    : ssDNA oligoprobe TCAACATCAGTCTGATAAGCTA (amine-coupled; IDT)
  Plasma samples  : Untreated human plasma (EDTA; Zen-Bio Inc.; 3 healthy donors, 3 runs each)
                    Mouse plasma (Pten-deletion liver cancer model; 15-month-old male mice)
                    Clinical serum (de-identified human liver cancer; USC tissue bank; IRB-approved)

Negative controls:
  NC1: Bare (non-functionalized) AEM exposed to plasma -> no voltage shift
  NC2: 1:1 plasma dilution in 1x PBS -> voltage shift 0.65 V -> 0.6 V (as expected)
  NC3: Non-target miR-196a spike (1 uM; seq: TAGGTAGTTTCATGTTGTTGGG) -> 0.1 V shift (below limit)
  NC4: Man-made probe (GATCGCAGCCAAATGACGTGAC; no known miR complement) -> 0.08 V (below limit)
  NC5: RNAse-treated plasma (free RNA digested) -> no miR-21 detected (confirms signal specificity)
  NC6: Protease-added SAW-lysed plasma (proteins eliminated) -> same shift as untreated (no fouling)


IEM SENSOR CALIBRATION
-----------------------
  Target            : Synthetic miR-21 (IDT) in 1x PBS
  Concentration range: 1 pM to 1 nM
  Replicates        : 3 per concentration point (95% confidence error bars)
  Relationship      : Log-linear over 3 decades of concentration
  Calibration eq.   : C (nM) = exp((Delta-V - 0.76145) / 0.06614)
  Expression level  : ExpressionLevel = exp((Delta-V_target - Delta-V_reference) / b)
                      where b = 0.06614 (calibration fitting parameter)
  Validation        : Synthetic miR-21 at known concentration tested on both integrated device
                      and RT-qPCR; calculated average expression levels nearly identical


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | IEM Sensor Functionalization and Baseline CVC
  Inputs     : PBS 1x, IEM AEM Sensor (oligoprobe pre-functionalized)
  Operation  : Mix (5 s) + detect iemSensorDetection (30 s)
  Purpose    : Acquire baseline CVC for miR-21 oligoprobe in 1x PBS (no sample); used as
               Delta-V = 0 reference for all subsequent measurements.
  Probe seq  : TCAACATCAGTCTGATAAGCTA (amine-coupled to AEM; standard functionalization process)

Step 2 | Measurement 1 - Free-Floating miR-21 Quantification (SAW OFF)
  Inputs     : Plasma Sample (~20 uL untreated), PBS 1x (60 uL driver fluid)
  Operation  : Mix (channel flow; SAW device OFF; 2 s abstraction)
  Flow rate  : 250 uL/h (sample + driver)
  SAW status : OFF; IDT powered down; EVs remain intact
  Inlet      : Sample followed immediately by 60 uL PBS driver fluid
  Notes      : Plasma used as-is; no pre-treatment. Only free-floating miR-21 in plasma
               reaches the AEM sensor. ~1 min transit through SAW channel at 250 uL/h.

Step 3 | IEM Concentration - Measurement 1
  Inputs     : Channel flow 1, IEM CEM Concentrator
  Operation  : Mix (1200 s) + heat at 25 C for 1200 s (IEM electrokinetic abstraction)
  Voltage    : 200 V DC (Keithley 2400 SourceMeter)
  Duration   : 20 min (= 1200 s)
  Temperature: 25 C (ambient; no thermal step; heat models non-thermal IEM operation)
  Effect     : Depletion zone formed upstream of AEM sensor; negatively charged free-floating
               miR-21 concentrates up to 1000-fold directly beneath sensor surface.
               Hybridisation with oligoprobe occurs concurrently during 20-min window.

Step 4 | Post-Hybridisation Wash and Buffer Exchange - Measurement 1
  Wash       : PBS 4x (2 s mix); removes non-hybridised species from AEM surface
  CVC buffer : PBS 0.1x (2 s mix); fills channel and reservoirs for CVC sweep
  Notes      : Low ionic strength of 0.1x PBS maximises over-limiting current Delta-V signal.

Step 5 | CVC Sweep - Free-Floating miR-21 Delta-V Measurement
  Inputs     : readyForCVC1
  Operation  : Detect miR21FreefloatingDetection (30 s)
  Instrument : Gamry 500 potentiostat; 0-2.5 V sweep; Ag-AgCl reference electrodes
  Expected   : Delta-V ~0.1 V for free-floating miR-21 in healthy human plasma (Fig. 3)
  Branch pass (freefloatSignal > 0)  : dispose readyForCVC1 -> proceed to BB4
  Branch fail (freefloatSignal <= 0) : drain readyForCVC1 -> proceed to BB4

Step 6 | Measurement 2 - Total miR-21 Quantification (SAW ON; Free-Floating + EV-miRNA)
  Inputs     : SAW Actuator, Plasma Sample (~20 uL fresh aliquot), PBS 1x (60 uL driver)
  Operation  : Mix (SAW channel flow + acoustic lysis; 60 s) + detect sawLysingDetection (10 s)
  SAW params : 28 MHz, 1 W; Agilent 33250A + E&I 325LA
  Flow rate  : 250 uL/h; ~1 min channel residence time -> ~100% EV lysis
  Notes      : SAWs refract perpendicularly into polycarbonate microchannel and shear EV
               membranes via acoustic pressure. Released EV-miRNA and free-floating miRNA
               both enter the concentration/sensing chip. SAW lysis is 50% more efficient
               than TRIzol and 46% more efficient than Qiagen chemical kit.
               sawLysingDetection module confirms lysis before IEM chip processing.
               Fresh plasma aliquot used; disposable AEM sensor replaced before this run.

Step 7 | IEM Concentration - Measurement 2
  Inputs     : Channel flow 2, IEM CEM Concentrator (fresh)
  Operation  : Mix (1200 s) + heat at 25 C for 1200 s
  Voltage    : 200 V DC for 20 min
  Notes      : Total miRNA pool (free-floating + EV-released) concentrates and hybridises
               with fresh oligoprobe on replaced disposable AEM sensor.

Step 8 | Post-Hybridisation Wash and Buffer Exchange - Measurement 2
  Wash       : PBS 4x (2 s); CVC buffer: PBS 0.1x (2 s)
  Notes      : Identical procedure to Step 4.

Step 9 | CVC Sweep - Total miR-21 Delta-V Measurement
  Inputs     : readyForCVC2
  Operation  : Detect miR21TotalDetection (30 s)
  Instrument : Gamry 500 potentiostat; 0-2.5 V sweep; Ag-AgCl reference electrodes
  Expected   : Delta-V ~0.65-0.7 V for total miR-21 in healthy human plasma (Fig. 3)
  EV-miRNA   : Computed as difference between Measurement 2 and Measurement 1 Delta-V values,
               converted to concentration via: C (nM) = exp((Delta-V - 0.76145) / 0.06614)
               Expression level: exp((Delta-V_total - Delta-V_freefloat) / 0.06614)
  Branch pass (totalSignal > 0)  : dispose readyForCVC2 + dispose lysisSignal -> proceed to BB7
  Branch fail (totalSignal <= 0) : drain readyForCVC2 + drain lysisSignal -> proceed to BB7

Step 10 | Final Cleanup (Terminal)
  Operations : dispose totalSignal; dispose baselineMix; NOP
  Notes      : Off-chip: EV-miR-21 expression level computed and compared to reference.
               Device terminated; experiment ends.


KEY RESULTS
-----------
  Healthy human plasma  : EV-miR-21 ~2 orders of magnitude higher than free-floating miR-21
  Liver cancer mice     : Total plasma miR-21 ~1000x elevated vs healthy mice
                          (tissue upregulation only ~3x, highlighting EV amplification effect)
  Clinical liver cancer : miR-21 ~13x overexpressed in serum vs healthy subjects; no group overlap
  Platform reproducibility: Consistent results across 3 donors x 3 runs x 3 fabricated devices


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file  : ramshani_ev_mirna_integrated_microfluidics.bs
Compiler        : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output       : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG file        : ramshani_ev_mirna_integrated_microfluidics_main_dag.dot
Duration units  : Seconds (s) and minutes (m) only; h token not supported by compiler
Duration notes  : IEM concentration 20 min -> 1200s; SAW lysis 1 min -> 60s

Modules         : iemSensorDetection, sawLysingDetection,
                  miR21FreefloatingDetection, miR21TotalDetection

Manifests       : Plasma_Sample, PBS_1x, PBS_4x, PBS_01x, TAE_Buffer_10x,
                  miR21_OligoProbe, SAW_Actuator, IEM_AEM_Sensor, IEM_CEM_Concentrator

CFG structure   : Diamond-of-diamonds (2 nested if/else gates)
                  BB1 (main) -> BB2/BB3 (freefloat pass/fail) -> BB4 (join)
                  BB4 -> BB5/BB6 (total pass/fail) -> BB7 (terminal)
                  DAG edges: 1->2, 1->3, 2->4, 3->4, 4->5, 4->6, 5->7, 6->7

Key abstractions:
  mix  : Abstracts continuous-flow microfluidic channel injection events (not DMF droplet merging)
  heat : at 25 C for 1200 s models 200 V DC IEM electrokinetic concentration at ambient temperature
  heat : at 25 C for 60 s models SAW channel lysis residence time

Fix applied (v2): lowIonicBuffer (PBS_01x) was dispensed but never consumed in original .bs;
                  removed in revision. PBS_01x is dispensed inline as cvcBuffer1/cvcBuffer2
                  at the exact point of use before each CVC sweep. Confirmed by IR diff:
                  exactly one line removed (lowIonicBuffer1[0] = dispense(PBS_01x));
                  CFG DOT graph byte-for-byte identical before and after fix.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Microfluidic Probe for Single-Cell Analysis in Adherent Tissue Culture
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms4421
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms4421
Journal      : Nature Communications, 2014, Vol. 5, Article 3421
Platform     : Three-layer PDMS microfluidic probe with hydrodynamic confinement lysis,
               pneumatic valve-controlled nanolitre reaction chambers, and fluorescence readout


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a microfluidic probe that selectively lyses single adherent cells
from standard tissue culture using hydrodynamic confinement of a detergent-containing lysis
buffer, captures the resulting single-cell lysate, mixes it with assay reagents in nanolitre-
scale reaction chambers, and performs high-sensitivity fluorescence-based enzyme activity
assays. The platform is demonstrated by measuring Akt kinase activity and GAPDH housekeeping
enzyme activity simultaneously from single HepG2 hepatocellular carcinoma cells in adherent
culture, revealing biological heterogeneity in Akt signalling that correlates with distinct
cell morphology subgroups -- not visible in bulk-level assays.

Hydrodynamic confinement is achieved by simultaneous outflow (Qout, central channel,
5 nL/min lysis buffer) and inflow (Qin, outer channels, 50 nL/min total) at the probe tip,
creating a confined lysis zone of tunable radius R (R/L set by Qin/Qout ratio, confirmed
by COMSOL Multiphysics simulation). The zone is set slightly smaller than the target cell
diameter (~15 um) so that only the targeted cell is lysed; neighbouring cells are unaffected
even in ~80% confluent cultures. The lysate is captured back into the device within ~20 s
and mixed with assay buffers at a 1:4 ratio (set by passive flow resistance ratio) before
pneumatic valves trap the assay mixture in 20 nL reaction chambers at 90 s post-lysis.

The integration of lysis, mixing, and assay in a single chip limits lysate dilution and
maintains sensitivity sufficient to measure enzyme activity from less than half a cell's
worth of total protein. The Akt assay LOD on the device is 0.32 pg active Akt -- approximately
1600x more sensitive than a standard plate reader (LOD 0.51 ng). The device can assay up to
four activities from a single cell (two to four chambers per lysate), and up to four cells
in parallel (one per chamber set), with sequential lysis per cell.

This is, to the authors' knowledge, the first use of hydrodynamic confinement to reclaim
cellular material from adherent culture for biochemical assay.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Material     : Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS, RTV615); three-layer monolithic construction.

Layer 1 (base)     : Bare glass slide; forms base of device except at probe tip region.
Layer 2 (membrane) : ~30 um thin PDMS; forms deformable base of tip (enables close approach
                     to adherent cells on tissue culture surface); contains pneumatic valve
                     lines V1-V4 (15 um SU-8 mould).
Layer 3 (flow)     : ~5 mm thick PDMS; contains all channels, reaction chambers, and
                     flow/control connection ports. Two channel heights:
                       5 um: tip channels + assay buffer mixing regions (tuned for 1:4 mixing
                             by flow resistance ratio)
                      30 um: reaction chambers (maximise fluorescence signal collection)

Fabrication:
  Mask design        : AutoCAD 2000; photoplot film or chrome mask.
  Flow layer 30 um   : AZ4620 photoresist on 6 inch silicon wafer.
  Flow layer 5 um    : SU-8 photoresist on 6 inch silicon wafer.
  Membrane layer     : SU-8 photoresist (15 um valve lines).
  Silanisation       : Heptadecafluoro-1,1,2,2-tetra-hydrodecyl trimethoxysilane;
                       dessicator 1 min vent + 1 h vacuum before casting.
  Membrane PDMS      : RTV615 20:1; spin-coated at 1600 rpm.
  Flow layer PDMS    : RTV615 5:1; cast from Si mould, then plastic replica mould used.
  Partial cure       : 60 min at 65 C; aligned under stereo microscope; baked overnight
                       at 65 C for monolithic bond.
  Final assembly     : Plasma bonded to glass slide with tip protruding over straight edge;
                       baked 95 C 15 min; degassed >= 10 min before use.
  Tip shaping        : Cut with sharp microtome blade to pointed tip with flat front.

Probe tip:
  Channels             : 3 (1 central outflow, 2 outer inflows)
  Channel width (w)    : 100 um
  Channel separation (p): 50 um
  Characteristic length (L = w + 2p): 200 um
  Lysis buffer         : Qout = 5 nL/min (central channel)
  Lysate inflow        : Qin = 50 nL/min total (25 nL/min per outer channel)
  Qin/Qout ratio       : 10 (sets lysis zone R slightly smaller than cell, ~15 um)
  Zone confinement     : COMSOL simulated; detergent diffusivity 6e-11 m2/s; 1% v/v input;
                         R measured as distance from tip where detergent falls to 0.1%

Reaction chambers (AB1-AB4):
  Count            : 4 (AB1-AB4)
  Volume per chamber: ~20 nL
  Assay mix ratio  : lysate:assay buffer = 1:4 (passive flow resistance ratio)
  Travel time      : 90 s from tip to chamber
  Repeatability    : within 10% CV (mixing ratio and travel time)

Pneumatic valves (V1-V4):
  Actuation        : compressed air 30 psi via custom solenoid valve manifold
  Timing           : actuated at 90 s post-lysis (measured travel time)
  Function         : trap assay mixture in selected chamber; optionally split lysate
                     to multiple chambers for multiplexed assays from one cell

Multiplexed chamber assignment (this protocol):
  AB1  : Akt kinase Sox sensor assay
  AB2  : GAPDH NADH formation assay (loading control)
  AB3/4: available for additional activities or parallel cells


CELL LINES
----------
HepG2 (ATCC HB-8065):
  Application    : All enzyme activity assays (Akt, GAPDH, multiplexed); primary cell line.
  Culture medium : Eagle's MEM + 10% FBS (Hyclone, Fisher Scientific)
                   + 1% penicillin/streptomycin (Invitrogen).
  Conditions     : 37 C, 5% CO2; tissue culture treated polystyrene.

MCF-7 (human breast cancer):
  Application    : Single-cell lysis characterisation only (Fig. 3a/b of paper).
  Dye            : Cell Tracker Green (ex 490 nm / em 526 nm).
  Notes          : Used to confirm lysis of target cell and unaffected neighbouring cells;
                   not used for enzyme activity assays. Not encoded in this .bs file.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Device Priming with De-ionised Water
  Reagents     : De-ionised water
  Operation    : Syringe-pump driven flow through device channels
  Duration     : 5 min
  Syringes     : Gas-tight glass syringes 50 uL (lysis buffer and inflow source ports)
  Tubing       : Fused silica OD 360 um / ID 100 um
  Pump         : Harvard Apparatus PHD 2000 syringe pump
  Purpose      : Remove air bubbles; equilibrate channels before BSA coating.

Step 2 | BSA Coating to Prevent Non-Specific Protein Binding
  Reagents     : 1% BSA in 0.5x PBS; de-ionised water (wash)
  Flow rate    : 50 nL/min
  Duration     : >= 60 min (1 h) coating; then DI water wash
  Temperature  : 25 C (ambient)
  Purpose      : PDMS non-specifically adsorbs proteins; BSA blocking is critical to
                 preserve enzyme activity from picomolar single-cell lysate in 20 nL chambers.

Step 3 | UV Photobleaching of Observation Area
  Duration     : >= 30 min
  Wavelength   : ex 377 nm (UV)
  Purpose      : Reduce background autofluorescence in reaction chambers before assay.
                 Done immediately before loading assay buffers.

Step 4 | Load Assay Buffers and Lysis Buffer
  Akt assay buffer (AB1, 20 uL):
    50 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.3, 10 mM MgCl2, 1 mM EGTA, 2 mM DTT,
    4 mM PKC inhibitor peptide, 10 mM Sox substrate peptide,
    1 mM ATP (low metals grade, Calbiochem), 0.4 mM PKItide,
    5 uM GF109203X (EMD)
  GAPDH assay buffer (AB2, 20 uL):
    90 mM sodium pyrophosphate pH 7.1, 20 mM NaH2PO4, 3 mM DTT,
    4 mM NAD+, 10 mM glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate
  Lysis buffer (syringe at lysis port):
    50 mM beta-glycerophosphate, 10 mM sodium pyrophosphate, 30 mM NaF,
    50 mM Tris pH 7.4, 1% Triton X-100, 15 mM NaCl, 2 mM EGTA,
    100 uM sodium orthovanadate, 1 mM DTT,
    1X protease inhibitor cocktail (Merck/EMD 539134),
    1X phosphatase inhibitor cocktail (Sigma P2850),
    20 ug/mL Alexa 488-labelled BSA (lysis zone visualisation)
  Duration     : ~2 min (passive loading)
  Timing       : Immediately before experiment; lysis buffer loaded last.

Step 5 | HepG2 Cell Plating and Attachment
  Seeding density : 5,000-20,000 cells/cm2
  Medium          : Eagle's MEM + 10% FBS + 1% pen/strep
  Substrate       : Standard tissue culture treated polystyrene
  Duration        : 4 h minimum (range 4-16 h; BioScript: 240m -> IR: 14400.0 SECOND)
  Temperature     : 37 C, 5% CO2
  Notes           : Cells fully attached before serum starvation. No effect of seeding
                    density on insulin activation time course (15,000-100,000 cells/cm2).

Step 6 | Serum Starvation
  Medium       : Serum-free Eagle's MEM (no FBS)
  Duration     : 12 h minimum (range 12-24 h; BioScript: 720m -> IR: 43200.0 SECOND)
  Temperature  : 37 C, 5% CO2
  Purpose      : Synchronise Akt signalling baseline; sensitise Akt pathway to insulin.
  Notes        : For bulk assay validation: 16-24 h starvation.

Step 7 | Cell Labelling with Cell Tracker Orange Dye
  Dye              : Cell Tracker Orange (Invitrogen), 2.5 uM in serum-free medium
  Labelling        : 15 min minimum (range 15-45 min) at 37 C, 5% CO2
                     BioScript: 15m -> IR: 900.0 SECOND
  Wash             : PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free)
  Recovery         : Serum-free medium, 20 min minimum (range 20-45 min) at 37 C, 5% CO2
                     BioScript: 20m -> IR: 1200.0 SECOND
  Imaging filter   : Rhodamine (Semrock, ex 540 nm / em 570 nm)
  Purpose          : Cytosolic fluorescent label; drop in target cell fluorescence within
                     ~20 s confirms lysis and lysate capture. Neighbouring cells unaffected
                     (fluorescence constant throughout lysis event; Fig. 3b of paper).

Step 8 | Insulin Stimulation to Activate Akt
  Reagent          : Insulin, 500 ng/mL final concentration in serum-free medium
  Method           : Spiked into medium on plate (medium NOT removed during time-course lysis;
                     cells lysed one by one under continuous stimulation conditions)
  Duration         : 10 min minimum tested (range 10-16.5 min; BioScript: 10m -> IR: 600.0 SECOND)
  Temperature      : 37 C
  Serum-starved control: No insulin; no medium change
  Notes            : Plate brought to microscope and lysis started immediately after
                     desired stimulation time point.

Step 9 | Single-Cell Lysis by Hydrodynamic Confinement
  Flow rates       : Qout = 5 nL/min (lysis buffer, central channel)
                     Qin = 50 nL/min total (25 nL/min per outer channel)
  Lysis zone R     : ~15 um (slightly smaller than HepG2 cell; Qin/Qout = 10)
  Lysis time       : ~20 s (fluorescence drops and lysate captured within 20 s)
  Microscope       : Olympus IX71
  Positioning      : Micromanipulator
  Monitoring       : Rhodamine filter (ex 540 nm / em 570 nm) for Cell Tracker Orange
  Detection module : lysisDetection (BioScript)
  Detection duration: 20 s (BioScript: 20s -> IR: 20.0 SECOND)
  QC gate:
    Pass (BB2): lysisSignal > 0 -> Cell Tracker Orange drop confirmed in target cell,
                neighbouring cells unaffected; dispose lysis zone, proceed to assay
    Fail (BB3): lysisSignal <= 0 -> lysis failure (no drop, or neighbour affected);
                drain lysis zone; retry on next target cell
    Join (BB4): dispose lysisSignal; lysate transport and assay branches begin

Step 10 | Lysate Transport, Valve Actuation, and Akt Kinase Assay (Chamber AB1)
  Mixing           : Lysate + Akt assay buffer at 1:4 ratio by passive flow resistance
                     in 5 um channels (BioScript: mix for 90s -> IR: 90.0 SECOND)
  Valve actuation  : V1/V2 closed at 90 s post-lysis (compressed air 30 psi, solenoid manifold)
  Assay temperature: 30 C (Tokai Hit heating chamber on automated motorised stage)
  Assay duration   : >= 20 min (BioScript: heat + detect 20m -> IR: 1200.0 SECOND each)
  Microscope stage : Prior Scientific H110 motorised; Olympus IX71
  Imaging          : DAPI filter (Semrock, ex 377 nm / em 447 nm); every 30 s;
                     Uniblitz shutter; 200 ms exposure; >= 20 min total
  Readout          : Initial slope of Sox sensor fluorescence vs time (linear region);
                     activity corrected for bleaching by subtracting lysis buffer control mean
  LOD              : 0.32 pg recombinant active Akt (device) vs 0.51 ng (plate reader M2e)
  Single-cell equiv: ~1 ng total protein per HepG2 cell (400,000 cells -> 360 ug total protein)
  Detection module : aktKinaseDetection (BioScript)
  Results:
    Insulin-stimulated 'high Akt' cells: significant Akt increase (p=3.2e-4, n=12)
    Serum-starved / 'low Akt' cells: no Akt response (p=0.35); GAPDH also unaffected (p=0.50)
    Bulk CV: within 7% for Akt lysate measurements
  QC gate:
    Pass (BB5): aktSignal > 0 -> Akt activity above lysis buffer baseline; 'high Akt'
                phenotype confirmed; dispose Akt assay mixture
    Fail (BB6): aktSignal <= 0 -> no Akt above baseline; 'low Akt' phenotype (putatively
                senescent morphology: larger cell area p=0.037, larger min Feret p=0.0003);
                drain Akt assay mixture
    Join (BB7): dispose aktSignal; GAPDH branch begins

Step 11 | GAPDH Housekeeping Enzyme Assay (Chamber AB2) -- Multiplexed Loading Control
  Mixing           : Lysate + GAPDH assay buffer at 1:4 ratio (same resistance ratio)
                     (BioScript: mix for 90s -> IR: 90.0 SECOND)
  Valve actuation  : V3/V4 closed at 90 s post-lysis
  Assay temperature: 30 C
  Assay duration   : >= 20 min (BioScript: heat + detect 20m -> IR: 1200.0 SECOND each)
  Readout          : Initial slope of NADH fluorescence vs time (NAD+ to NADH conversion)
  Imaging          : DAPI filter (same as Akt; automated stage images AB1 and AB2 simultaneously)
  LOD              : Lower than Akt (higher GAPDH expression levels relative to Akt)
  Bulk CV          : Within 18% for GAPDH lysate measurements
  Detection module : gapdhActivityDetection (BioScript)
  Normalisation    : Akt/GAPDH ratio per cell shows same response pattern as raw Akt
                     (Supplementary Fig. 9); GAPDH is valid single-cell loading control
  Notes            : AB1 and AB2 imaged simultaneously on automated motorised stage.
                     Encoded sequentially in BioScript (compiler does not support concurrent
                     parallel detect statements).
  QC gate:
    Pass (BB8): gapdhSignal > 0 -> GAPDH detected; loading control confirmed;
                dispose GAPDH assay mixture
    Fail (BB9): gapdhSignal <= 0 -> GAPDH not detected (lysate loss or chamber failure);
                drain GAPDH assay mixture
    Join (BB10): dispose gapdhSignal; NOP (terminal); single-cell assay cycle complete


BIOLOGICAL FINDINGS
-------------------
Two subpopulations of HepG2 cells identified under insulin stimulation:

'High Akt' cells:
  Akt activity     : Significantly increased upon insulin stimulation (p=3.2e-4, n=12)
  GAPDH activity   : Unaffected (p=0.98; confirms specificity of Akt response)
  Morphology       : Smaller cell area; smaller minimum Feret diameter (caliper width)

'Low Akt' cells:
  Akt activity     : Not increased upon stimulation (p=0.35)
  GAPDH activity   : Also unaffected (p=0.50)
  Morphology       : Significantly larger cell area (p=0.037) and minimum Feret diameter
                     (p=0.0003); consistent with wider, flatter senescent morphology
  Putative identity: Cells in senescence (elevated SA-beta-gal activity confirmed under
                     sparse plating conditions; lower SMP-30 expression promotes lower Akt
                     in HepG2; consistent with literature on Akt in cardiac fibroblast
                     senescence and oncogene-induced senescence)

Key advantage: Morphological phenotype of 'low Akt' cells not observable in flow cytometry.
This probe allows selection of phenotypically distinct cells and direct signalling measurement
from the same individual cell in its adherent context -- connecting intracellular state to
phenotype in a way not achievable with existing suspension-based single-cell methods.


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : sarkar_microfluidic_probe_singlecell_analysis.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
DAG            : sarkar_microfluidic_probe_singlecell_analysis_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations converted to seconds (s) or minutes (m) for compiler
                 compatibility (BioScript supports s and m only; h not supported).
                 Cell attachment 4 h    -> 240m  (IR: 14400.0 SECOND)
                 Serum starvation 12 h  -> 720m  (IR: 43200.0 SECOND)
                 BSA coating 1 h        -> 60m   (IR: 3600.0 SECOND)
                 UV bleach 30 min       -> 30m   (IR: 1800.0 SECOND)
                 Cell Tracker label     -> 15m   (IR: 900.0 SECOND)
                 Post-label recovery    -> 20m   (IR: 1200.0 SECOND)
                 Insulin stimulation    -> 10m   (IR: 600.0 SECOND)
                 Lysis detection        -> 20s   (IR: 20.0 SECOND)
                 Valve travel time      -> 90s   (IR: 90.0 SECOND)
                 Akt / GAPDH assay      -> 20m   (IR: 1200.0 SECOND each)
Modules        : lysisDetection, aktKinaseDetection, gapdhActivityDetection
ASCII rule     : All characters must be 7-bit ASCII; ANTLR4 FileStream opens files in ASCII
                 mode and raises UnicodeDecodeError on any byte > 127, even inside comments.
                 Em-dashes (UTF-8: 0xe2 0x80 0x94) replaced with -- throughout.
                 Other watch items: Unicode superscripts (NAD+, not NAD+U+207A), curly quotes,
                 degree symbols (deg not deg-U+00B0), micro signs (um not u+00B5), +/- signs.
Drain vs Dispose: BioScript compiler normalises drain to dispose at IR level (both are sink
                 operations); distinction is semantic (fail-path waste routing) and does not
                 affect CFG structure or edge count.
Mix abstraction: mix steps model: (a) syringe-pump priming/coating flows, (b) cell/dye
                 incubations on tissue culture plate, (c) simultaneous Qout/Qin tip flows
                 creating lysis zone, (d) passive resistance-ratio mixing of lysate with
                 assay buffer in 5 um channels before valve closure. Not DMF electrode mixing.
Heat abstraction: heat models both 37 C CO2 incubator dwell (cell culture steps) and 30 C
                 heating chamber dwell (assay monitoring steps). Temperature specified per
                 step in BioScript heat statement.
lysisBuffer reuse: In BB4 (Akt mix) and BB7 (GAPDH mix), lysisBuffer1[0] carried from BB1
                 through join nodes; models same physical lysis buffer reservoir feeding
                 both AB1 and AB2 mixing channels in parallel -- consistent with device.
Biological scope: This .bs file encodes the multiplexed Akt + GAPDH arm (Fig. 5, n=12).
                 Single-activity arms (Akt only: Fig. 4a; GAPDH only: Fig. 4b; MK2:
                 Supplementary Fig. 7) differ only in lysate routing to one chamber;
                 each would require a separate .bs file with one assay branch instead of two.
IR verification : All 10 BBs confirmed in .ir output; all 12 CFG edges confirmed in .dot
                 output; all duration conversions verified; zero compiler errors or warnings.

protocol.title: Microfluidic Probe for Single-Cell Analysis in Adherent Tissue Culture
protocol.platform: Three-layer PDMS microfluidic probe with hydrodynamic confinement lysis, pneumatic valves, and nanolitre reaction chambers
cell_lines: MCF-7 (human breast cancer, used for single-cell lysis characterisation only)
protocol.objective: Selective lysis of single adherent cells from standard tissue culture by hydrodynamic confinement, capture of single-cell lysate, and multiplexed fluorescence activity measurement of kinase Akt (Sox sensor) and housekeeping enzyme GAPDH (NADH formation) simultaneously from the same cell; demonstration of biological heterogeneity in Akt activity under insulin stimulation correlating with cell morphology subgroups

layers: Layer 1 (base): bare glass slide, forms base except at tip
Layer 2 (membrane): ~30 um thin PDMS; forms deformable tip base; contains pneumatic valve lines V1-V4
Layer 3 (flow): ~5 mm thick PDMS; contains channels, reaction chambers AB1-AB4, flow and control ports

tip.notes: L = w + 2p = 100 + 2x50 = 200 um. Tip cut with sharp microtome blade to pointed flat front.

lysis_zone.principle: Hydrodynamic confinement of detergent (1% Triton X-100) to a zone of radius R
lysis_zone.zone_radius_R: slightly smaller than cell diameter (~15 um)
lysis_zone.confinement_simulation: COMSOL Multiphysics (Laminar Flow + Transport of Dilute Species); detergent diffusivity 6e-11 m2/s; input 1% v/v
lysis_zone.notes: R/L tunable by Qin/Qout ratio. Lysis zone high-detergent (1% v/v); surrounding surface sees zero detergent. Neighbouring cells unaffected even at ~80% confluency.

mixing.set_by: flow resistance ratio of lysate and assay buffer microchannels

valves.actuation: compressed air, 30 psi, via custom-built solenoid valve manifold
valves.timing: actuated at 90 s after lysis (travel time from tip to chamber)

chambers.parallel_capacity: up to 4 cells in parallel (one per chamber); lysis sequential per cell

fabrication.mask_design: AutoCAD 2000; transferred to photoplot film or chrome mask

photolithography.flow_layer_30um_channels: AZ4620 photoresist on 6 inch silicon wafer

fabrication.silanisation: Heptadecafluoro-1,1,2,2-tetra-hydrodecyl trimethoxysilane; dessicator 1 min vent + 1 h vacuum
fabrication.pdms_flow_layer: RTV615 5:1; cast from silicon mould then plastic replica mould
fabrication.partial_cure: 60 min at 65 C; aligned under stereo microscope; baked overnight at 65 C for monolithic bond
fabrication.final_assembly: plasma bonded to glass slide; tip protruding over straight edge; baked 95 C 15 min; degassed >= 10 min

reagents.culture_medium: Eagle's Minimal Essential Medium + 10% FBS (Hyclone, Fisher Scientific) + 1% penicillin/streptomycin (Invitrogen)
reagents.cell_tracker_dye: Cell Tracker Orange (Invitrogen), 2.5 uM in serum-free medium; rhodamine filter ex 540 nm / em 570 nm
reagents.insulin: 500 ng/mL final concentration in serum-free medium
reagents.bsa_coating: 1% BSA in 0.5x PBS; drawn in at 50 nL/min for >= 1 h; prevents non-specific protein binding to PDMS
reagents.di_water: de-ionised water; device priming and BSA wash

lysis_buffer.composition: 50 mM beta-glycerophosphate, 10 mM sodium pyrophosphate, 30 mM sodium fluoride, 50 mM Tris pH 7.4, 1% Triton X-100, 15 mM NaCl, 2 mM EGTA, 100 uM sodium orthovanadate, 1 mM DTT, 1X protease inhibitor cocktail (Merck/EMD 539134), 1X phosphatase inhibitor cocktail (Sigma P2850), 20 ug/mL Alexa 488-labelled BSA (lysis zone visualisation)
lysis_buffer.syringes: gas-tight glass syringes 50 uL; fused silica tubing OD 360 um / ID 100 um

akt_assay_buffer.composition: 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.3, 10 mM MgCl2, 1 mM EGTA, 2 mM DTT, 4 mM PKC inhibitor peptide, 10 mM Sox substrate peptide, 1 mM ATP (low metals grade, Calbiochem), 0.4 mM PKItide, 5 uM GF109203X (EMD)
akt_assay_buffer.readout: Sox chelation-enhanced fluorescence; DAPI filter ex 377 nm / em 447 nm (Semrock)

gapdh_assay_buffer.composition: 90 mM sodium pyrophosphate pH 7.1, 20 mM NaH2PO4, 3 mM DTT, 4 mM NAD+, 10 mM glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate
gapdh_assay_buffer.readout: NADH fluorescence; DAPI filter ex 377 nm / em 447 nm (Semrock)
gapdh_assay_buffer.notes: LOD lower than Akt due to higher GAPDH expression levels. CV of bulk GAPDH lysate measurements within 18%.

mk2_assay_buffer.composition: same as Akt assay buffer but 25 uM GF109203X instead of 5 uM
mk2_assay_buffer.notes: Analogous LOD to Akt (Supplementary Fig. 7). Not encoded in this .bs file (separate single-activity arm).

steps.name: Device priming with de-ionised water
steps.tubing: fused silica OD 360 um / ID 100 um; gas-tight glass syringes 50 uL
steps.notes: Primed via lysis buffer and inflow source ports. Removes air bubbles and equilibrates channels before BSA coating.

steps.name: BSA coating to prevent non-specific protein binding
steps.notes: 1% BSA in 0.5x PBS. Critical to preserve picomolar single-cell lysate enzyme activity. Washed with DI water after 1 h.

steps.name: UV photobleaching of observation area
steps.operation: heat (25 C, UV light exposure abstraction)
steps.notes: Area of device observed during assay bleached for >= 30 min to reduce background fluorescence in reaction chambers. Done immediately before loading assay buffers.

steps.name: Load assay buffers and lysis buffer into device reservoirs
steps.notes: Lysis buffer loaded into syringe at lysis buffer port. Akt buffer into AB1, GAPDH buffer into AB2, each 20 uL. Done immediately before experiment.

steps.name: HepG2 cell plating and attachment
steps.duration_note: 4 h minimum (range 4-16 h); 240m in BioScript (IR: 14400.0 SECOND)
steps.notes: No changes in insulin activation time course observed for seeding densities 15,000-100,000 cells/cm2 (bulk assay data). Cells allowed to fully attach before serum starvation.

steps.name: Serum starvation
steps.duration_note: 12 h minimum (range 12-24 h); 720m in BioScript (IR: 43200.0 SECOND)
steps.notes: Synchronises Akt signalling baseline. Required to sensitise Akt pathway to insulin stimulation. For bulk assay: starved 16-24 h.

steps.name: Cell labelling with Cell Tracker Orange dye
steps.operation: mix + heat (37 C) + PBS wash + recovery
steps.duration_note: Labelling 15m minimum (range 15-45 m; IR: 900.0 SECOND). Recovery 20m minimum (range 20-45 m; IR: 1200.0 SECOND).
steps.notes: Cytosolic dye; fluorescence drop in target cell confirms lysis and lysate capture. Neighbouring cell fluorescence remains constant throughout lysis event.

steps.name: Insulin stimulation to activate Akt
steps.method: spiked into serum-free medium on plate; medium NOT removed during time-course lysis
steps.duration_note: 10 min minimum tested (range 10-16.5 min; IR: 600.0 SECOND)
steps.notes: For time-course: cells lysed one by one off plate under continuous stimulation conditions. For serum-starved control: no insulin, no medium change. Serum-starved control cells show lower/absent Akt activity ('low Akt' phenotype).

steps.name: Single-cell lysis by hydrodynamic confinement
steps.operation: mix (simultaneous Qout/Qin tip flow abstraction) + detect lysisDetection
steps.notes: Plate placed on microscope immediately after stimulation. Probe positioned near target cell. Lysis confirmed by Cell Tracker Orange fluorescence drop in target cell. Neighbouring cells confirmed unaffected (fluorescence constant). Lysate captured within ~20 s.

steps.name: Lysate transport, valve actuation, and Akt kinase assay (chamber AB1)
steps.operation: mix (resistance-ratio passive mixing) + heat (30 C) + detect aktKinaseDetection
steps.stage: automated motorised (Prior Scientific H110) in heating chamber (Tokai Hit)
steps.readout: initial slope of Sox sensor fluorescence vs time (linear region fitting)

results.p_value_stimulation: 3.2e-4 (stimulated vs starved for high Akt cells)

fail.notes: 'low Akt' phenotype: neither Akt nor GAPDH affected by insulin (p=0.35, p=0.50); morphologically larger cells with higher minimum Feret diameter

steps.name: GAPDH housekeeping enzyme assay (chamber AB2) -- multiplexed loading control
steps.operation: mix (resistance-ratio passive mixing) + heat (30 C) + detect gapdhActivityDetection
steps.readout: initial slope of NADH fluorescence vs time (NAD+ to NADH conversion)

results.conclusion: GAPDH unaffected by insulin stimulation; valid loading control for per-cell normalisation
results.normalisation: Akt/GAPDH ratio per cell shows same response pattern as raw Akt (Supplementary Fig. 9)

steps.notes: Simultaneously acquired with Akt in AB1 on automated motorised stage. Encoded sequentially in BioScript (no parallel detect statements supported by lilott8/BioScript compiler).

high_akt_cells.morphology: smaller cell area, smaller minimum Feret diameter

low_akt_cells.morphology: significantly larger cell area (p=0.037) and minimum Feret diameter (p=0.0003)
low_akt_cells.putative_phenotype: consistent with cellular senescence (wider, flatter morphology; elevated SA-beta-gal activity; lower SMP-30/Akt in HepG2)

heterogeneity_in_akt_activity.note: Morphological differences not observable in flow cytometry; probe enables phenotype-signalling co-measurement from same individual cell

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_7_j
basic_blocks.contents: dispose aktSignal; GAPDH assay mix (90s valve travel) + heat 30C + detect gapdhActivityDetection

basic_blocks.contents: dispose gapdhSignal; NOP

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Automated Microfluidic Platform for Dynamic and Combinatorial Drug Screening
               of Tumor Organoids
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-020-19058-4
DOI          : https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-19058-4
Journal      : Nature Communications (2020), Volume 11, Article 5271
Authors      : Brooke Schuster, Michael Junkin, Sara Saheb Kashaf, et al. (Savas Tay lab)
Platform     : Two-part PDMS microfluidic device: 200-well 3D organoid culture chamber array
               + solenoid-valve multiplexer control device; automated via MATLAB GUI


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes an automated high-throughput microfluidic platform for culturing
patient-derived pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) organoids in Matrigel and performing
individual, combinatorial, and temporal/sequential drug screens. The system supports up to
20 independent fluidic conditions and 10 patient samples in a single experiment across 200
individual culture wells.

The BioScript file encodes three experimental arms:
  (A) Single-agent drug screens: 7 FDA-approved chemotherapies at 72-h continuous exposure,
      with a 48-h media replenishment step (Patient 1).
  (B) Temporal/sequential combination drug regimens: 5 standard-of-care PDAC regimens
      delivered in clinically-mirrored pulse sequences (Patient 1).
  (C) Multi-patient parallel comparison: Gemcitabine + 5-FU temporal arm run simultaneously
      for Patients 1, 2, and 3 (mirrors Fig. 5 heatmap experiment).

All 14 treatment wells converge at exactly 4320 minutes (72 hours) for the apoptosisQC
detect gate, ensuring parallel biological comparison at an identical timestamp.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Chamber layer  : PDMS 200-well array; average well depth 610 um (significantly deeper than
                 typical microfluidic devices of 100-200 um); glass slide base.
Channel layer  : PDMS fluidic channels, 455 um height; reversibly clamped onto chamber layer
                 via polycarbonate plate and six screws; valve-less design allows Matrigel
                 loading by manual pipetting without risk of channel clogging.
Well array     : 200 wells divided into 20 subsets of 10; each subset receives one fluidic
                 condition from the multiplexer.
Multiplexer    : Valve-based reusable control device; up to 30 solutions pre-loaded;
                 solenoid valves controlled by custom MATLAB GUI (CSV/tab-delimited input);
                 supply pressure 5 psi; valve closing pressure 35-40 psi.
Microscope     : Nikon Eclipse Ti inverted microscope; automated translational stage;
                 ORCA-Flash 4.0 CMOS camera (Hamamatsu); 10x objective; NIS-Elements software;
                 imaging every 2-4 h; Life Imaging Service GmbH environmental enclosure
                 (37 C / 5% CO2 / 100% RH).


CELL LINES AND CULTURE
-----------------------
Cell type      : Patient-derived pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) organoids
                 (Patients 1, 2, and 3; IRB12-1108 and IRB13-1149; UCM 2014-2017)
Cell prep      : Tumor samples digested and dissociated; single cells embedded in 70%
                 GFR Matrigel (Corning 356231) / 30% complete organoid media; passed through
                 40 um cell strainer before loading; passaged via mechanical dissociation +
                 TrypLE Express (Fisher Scientific 12605-010).
Complete media : Intesticult (Stemcell Technologies 6005) supplemented with A83-01 (0.5 uM),
                 FGF10 (100 ng/mL), Gastrin I (10 nM), N-acetyl-L-cysteine (10 mM),
                 Nicotinamide (10 mM), B27 (1x), Primocin (1 mg/mL), Y-27632 (10.5 uM).
Growth phase   : 14+ days on platform; organoids grow from single cells to ~500 um glandular
                 structures; automated media exchange every 38 h; continuous time-lapse imaging.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Organoid Culture Establishment (Section 1, BB1)
  Operation  : dispense + mix (abstracts manual pipetting of cells in Matrigel/media mixture
               into 610-um wells, followed by Matrigel gelation and channel layer clamping)
  Arms       : 14 independent wells (one per treatment arm; each with fresh dispensed culture)
  Loading    : 70% GFR Matrigel + 30% complete organoid media + dissociated single cells
  Notes      : Each arm uses independently dispensed cells, Matrigel, and media. No fluid
               variable is shared between arms.

Step 2 | 14-Day Growth Phase (Section 2, BB1)
  Operation  : heat at 37 C for 20160m (14 days = 1209600 s in IR)
  Conditions : 37 C / 5% CO2 / 100% RH (Life Imaging Service GmbH environmental chamber)
  Duration   : 14 days minimum (until organoids reach ~500 um diameter and are visibly mature)
  Feeding    : Automated media exchange every 38 h via multiplexer
  Imaging    : Phase contrast + fluorescence, every 2-4 h, MATLAB auto-segmentation
  Notes      : heat is void/in-place in BioScript (no LHS assignment); same instruction
               applied to all 14 culture wells.

Step 3 | Single-Agent Drug Screen, Patient 1, 72-h Arm (Section 3, BB1)
  Drugs      : Gemcitabine 100 nM, Paclitaxel 10 nM, 5-FU 100 nM, Docetaxel 10 nM,
               CPT-11 100 nM, Oxaliplatin 100 nM, Cisplatin 100 nM
  Markers    : Caspase 3/7 5 uM (Essen Bioscience 4400, apoptosis);
               Propidium iodide 1.5 uM (Thermo Fisher P3566, cell death)
  Phase 1    : Drug exposure 0-48 h (2880m)
  Refresh    : Fresh complete media + drug dispensed and mixed at 48-h mark
  Phase 2    : Continued drug exposure 48-72 h (1440m)
  Total      : 2880m + 1440m = 4320m = 72 h
  QC arm     : Gemcitabine arm used for apoptosisQC detect gate
  Fix A      : Split into two phases to correctly place the 48-h replenishment boundary
               (original 4320m single mix delayed replenishment to 72h+10s)

Step 4 | Temporal FOLFIRINOX, Patient 1 (Section 4, BB1)
  Clinical   : Standard IV FOLFIRINOX for PDAC; mirrors real patient treatment sequence
  Sequence   : CPT-11 100 nM (120m) -> Oxaliplatin 100 nM (120m) ->
               High-dose 5-FU 1 uM (30m) -> Low-dose 5-FU 100 nM (4050m)
  Total      : 120+120+30+4050 = 4320m = 72 h
  Fix B      : Final 5-FU extended to 4050m; paper states "low dose 5-FU continued until
               the end of the 72-h experiment" (not 46h/2760m from clinical text block)

Step 5 | Temporal FOLFIRI, Patient 1 (Section 5, BB1)
  Sequence   : CPT-11 100 nM (240m) -> High-dose 5-FU 1 uM (30m) ->
               Low-dose 5-FU 100 nM (4050m)
  Total      : 240+30+4050 = 4320m = 72 h
  Fix B      : Final 5-FU extended from 2880m to 4050m

Step 6 | Temporal FOLFOX, Patient 1 (Section 6, BB1)
  Sequence   : Oxaliplatin 100 nM (240m) -> High-dose 5-FU 1 uM (30m) ->
               Low-dose 5-FU 100 nM (4050m)
  Total      : 240+30+4050 = 4320m = 72 h
  Fix B      : Final 5-FU extended from 2880m to 4050m

Step 7 | Temporal Gemcitabine + 5-FU, Patient 1 (Section 7, BB1)
  Cycles     : 2 cycles, unrolled (no loop constructs in BioScript)
  Cycle 1    : Gemcitabine 100 nM (240m) -> Low-dose 5-FU 100 nM (2880m)
  Cycle 2    : Gemcitabine 100 nM (240m) -> Low-dose 5-FU 100 nM (960m) [truncated]
  Total      : 240+2880+240+960 = 4320m = 72 h
  Fix C      : Cycle 2 final 5-FU truncated from 2880m to 960m per Fig 4f visual
               truncation at the 72-h assay read boundary

Step 8 | Temporal Gemcitabine + Paclitaxel, Patient 1 (Section 8, BB1)
  Cycles     : 2 cycles, unrolled
  Cycle 1    : Gemcitabine 100 nM (240m) -> Paclitaxel 10 nM (240m) -> Media (1440m)
  Cycle 2    : Gemcitabine 100 nM (240m) -> Paclitaxel 10 nM (240m) -> Media (1920m)
  Total      : 240+240+1440+240+240+1920 = 4320m = 72 h
  Clinical   : Most effective regimen for Patient 1 (Fig 4g); retrospectively consistent
               with clinical outcome (Table 2: gemcitabine+paclitaxel administered last)
  Fix C      : Final media step padded from 1440m to 1920m to reach 72-h boundary
  Note       : Table 1 schedule encoded here; Fig 4g shows a different schedule
               (Cycle1: 2h Gem + 2h Pac + 44h Media; Cycle2: 2h Gem + 4h Pac + 18h Media).
               Table 1 selected as primary encoding per reviewer guidance.

Step 9 | Multi-Patient Parallel Gem+5FU Temporal (Section 9, BB1)
  Patients   : Patient 2 and Patient 3 (Patient 1 encoded in Section 7)
  Mirrors    : Fig. 5 high-throughput simultaneous 3-patient experiment
  Structure  : Identical to Section 7 (same temporal cycle, same 960m truncation)
  QC gate    : Patient 2 arm (p2Finished) used for multiPatQC detect;
               P2 was most sensitive (p=7E-07 vs control, Fig 5b)
  Fix C      : Same 960m truncation applied to p2Finished and p3Finished


QC GATES AND CFG
-----------------

Primary QC gate (apoptosisQC):
  Detect     : apoptosisDetection on gemFinished, 30s
  BB2 (pass) : apoptosisQC > 0 -> dispose all 12 P1 arm droplets
  BB3 (fail) : apoptosisQC <= 0 -> drain all 12 P1 arm droplets
  BB4 (join) : dispose apoptosisQC signal

Secondary QC gate (multiPatQC):
  Detect     : apoptosisDetection on p2Finished, 30s
  BB5 (pass) : multiPatQC > 0 -> dispose p2Finished, p3Finished
  BB6 (fail) : multiPatQC <= 0 -> drain p2Finished, p3Finished
  BB7 (term) : dispose multiPatQC; device disassembled for organoid harvest
               (channel layer removed; wells exposed for sequencing, expansion, or grafting)

CFG edges    : BB1->BB2, BB1->BB3, BB2->BB4, BB3->BB4,
               BB4->BB5, BB4->BB6, BB5->BB7, BB6->BB7
DAG shape    : Two sequential diamond gates converging at terminal BB7


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
--------------------------
BioScript file : schuster_organoid_drug_screening.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG file       : schuster_organoid_drug_screening_main_dag.dot
Duration units : s and m only (h token not supported by BioScript compiler)

Duration conversions used:
  30 min  = 30m    (IR: 1800.0 SECOND)
  2 h     = 120m   (IR: 7200.0 SECOND)
  4 h     = 240m   (IR: 14400.0 SECOND)
  16 h    = 960m   (IR: 57600.0 SECOND)
  24 h    = 1440m  (IR: 86400.0 SECOND)
  32 h    = 1920m  (IR: 115200.0 SECOND)
  48 h    = 2880m  (IR: 172800.0 SECOND)
  67.5 h  = 4050m  (IR: 243000.0 SECOND)
  72 h    = 4320m  (IR: 259200.0 SECOND)
  14 days = 20160m (IR: 1209600.0 SECOND)

Modules        : apoptosisDetection (Caspase 3/7), cellDeathDetection (propidium iodide)
Manifests      : PDAC_P1_Cells, PDAC_P2_Cells, PDAC_P3_Cells, GFR_Matrigel,
                 CompleteOrganoidMedia, Gemcitabine_100nM, Paclitaxel_10nM,
                 FluorouracilLow_100nM, FluorouracilHigh_1uM, Docetaxel_10nM,
                 CPT11_100nM, Oxaliplatin_100nM, Cisplatin_100nM,
                 Caspase37_Reagent, PropidiumIodide
No loops       : All multi-cycle regimens fully unrolled (Gem+5FU x2, Gem+Pac x2)
heat void      : heat is void/in-place; no LHS assignment anywhere
detect SSA     : Each detect result (apoptosisQC, multiPatQC) assigned exactly once
Fluid SSA      : Each arm has independently dispensed cultures, markers, and drugs;
                 no fluid variable used as source in more than one mix/detect on its
                 linear execution chain
ASCII only     : File is strict ASCII; all Unicode removed (checkmarks, arrows replaced
                 with OK and <--) to prevent ANTLR4 FileStream UnicodeDecodeError
Encoding scope : Patient 1 full arm (7 single-agent + 5 temporal);
                 Patients 2 and 3 encoded for Gem+5FU temporal parallel comparison only


FIXES APPLIED (iterative review corrections)
--------------------------------------------

FIX A (Section 3) -- 48-hour replenishment bug:
  Issue  : Original code ran a single 4320m mix then appended replenishment after 72h+10s,
           violating the paper's "48-h mark replenishment" specification.
  Fix    : Each single-agent arm split into:
           phase1 (2880m) + dispense fresh media+drug + phase2 (1440m) = 4320m total.

FIX B (Sections 4, 5, 6) -- Duration deficits in temporal FOLFIRINOX/FOLFIRI/FOLFOX:
  Issue  : Final 5-FU step encoded as 2880m (48h) or 2760m (46h) from Table 1 text,
           leaving each arm 21.5h short of the 72-h endpoint; wells would sit idle.
  Fix    : Final low-dose 5-FU step extended to 4050m in all three regimens.
           Paper explicitly states: "low dose 5-FU continued until the end of the 72-h
           experiment." 120+120+30+4050 = 4320m; 240+30+4050 = 4320m.

FIX C (Sections 7, 8, 9) -- Gem+5FU overshoot and Gem+Pac undershoot:
  Issue  : Gem+5FU two-cycle unroll totalled 6240m (104h), overshooting by 32h.
           Gem+Pac two-cycle unroll totalled 3840m (64h), undershooting by 8h.
           Reviewer first suggested 1200m truncation for Gem+5FU (giving 4560m, incorrect).
           Corrected to 960m (240+2880+240+960=4320m).
  Fix    : Gem+5FU cycle 2 final 5-FU -> 960m; same applied to P2 and P3 in Section 9.
           Gem+Pac cycle 2 final media -> 1920m (240+240+1440+240+240+1920=4320m).

FIX UNICODE -- ANTLR4 UnicodeDecodeError:
  Issue  : UTF-8 checkmark (U+2713, 0xe2 0x9c 0x93) and left arrow (U+2190) in comments
           caused UnicodeDecodeError at byte position 14172 when ANTLR4 FileStream
           attempted ASCII decode.
  Fix    : Decoded file as UTF-8, replaced all non-ASCII chars with ASCII equivalents
           (U+2713 -> "OK", U+2190 -> "<--"), re-encoded as strict ASCII.
