description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : A Microfluidic Device for Measuring Cell Migration Towards Substrate-Bound and Soluble Chemokine Gradients
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/srep36440
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/srep36440
Journal      : Scientific Reports, 2016, Vol. 6, Article 36440
Platform     : Two-layer PDMS microfluidic device with LAPAP photo-patterning and flow-free diffusion gradient generation


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a microfluidic approach for simultaneously generating surface-immobilized
haptotactic chemokine gradients and diffusion-based soluble chemotactic gradients within the same
migration chamber, enabling quantitative single-cell tracking of dendritic cell (DC) migration in
combined and competing chemokine gradient fields.

The device integrates three functional capabilities:
  1. LAPAP (Laser-Assisted Protein Adsorption by Photobleaching) photo-patterning of
     arbitrarily shaped, graded surface-immobilized chemokine patterns (CCL21 24-98 bio)
     with ~0.7 um lateral resolution and ~100:1 dynamic range.
  2. Flow-free diffusion-based soluble chemokine gradients (CCL19) via source-sink
     flow-switching, independently controllable in steepness, mean concentration, and duration.
  3. Precise positioning of immune cells on haptotactic gradients, with simultaneous
     superimposition of opposing or co-directional soluble gradients.

The protocol is divided into three experimental arms:
  ARM 1. Haptotaxis arm: DC migration on immobilized CCL21 gradient (no soluble gradient)
  ARM 2. Chemotaxis arm: DC migration in soluble CCL19 diffusion gradient (no immobilized chemokine)
  ARM 3. Competing gradients arm: DC migration simultaneously exposed to opposing immobilized
         CCL21 (haptotactic) and soluble CCL19 (chemotactic) gradients

Key finding: haptotactic CCL21 gradients dominate at low soluble CCL19 (~0-1 ug/mL), while
increasing CCL19 concentrations (~0-1.2 ug/mL) override the immobilized CCL21 signal and
redirect DC migration along the soluble gradient.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Layer i   : PDMS flow layer; 6 migration chambers (l=1100 um, w=200 um, h_max=28 um).
            Each chamber has one side port at the midpoint of the long axis and two ports at
            the short ends connected to source and sink support channels.
Layer ii  : PDMS control layer; independently controllable PDMS membrane valves on all ports.
            Optimal closing pressure determined per chip by incrementing control channel
            pressure in 0.5 bar steps.
Layer iii : Glass substrate; coated with human plasma fibronectin (250 ug/mL, Millipore)
            for beta2-integrin-mediated DC adhesion and 2D migration.

Inlets  : 9 reagent inlets, 1 cell loading inlet
Outlets : 3 waste outlets

Support channels connect reagent inlets with migration chambers. Flow lines pressurised
at 0.2-0.4 bar. All ports equipped with independently controllable PDMS membrane valves.


CELL TYPE
---------
Bone marrow-derived dendritic cells (DCs) from C57BL/6J mice (C57BL6 strain).
Cultured: GM-CSF hybridoma cell line supernatant (granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating
factor) in non-adhesive petri dish. Bone marrow extracted from femur and tibia; 4500 rpm
spin distally capped bones. 2 x 10^6 cells/10 mL R10 medium per dish.
  - Day 0: seed bone marrow
  - Day 4: add 10 mL R10 + 2 mL GM-CSF supernatant
  - Day 7: replace 10 mL with fresh R10 + 2 mL GM-CSF supernatant
  - Day 8-10: harvest; mature overnight with LPS (200 ng/mL)
Cell culture medium (R10): RPMI 1640 + 10% fetal calf serum + L-Glucose +
Penicillin/Streptomycin (all from Life Sciences, Austria).


REAGENTS
--------
Buffer               : PBS (phosphate-buffered saline)
Surface coating      : Human plasma fibronectin, 250 ug/mL (Millipore, Austria)
LAPAP anchor         : Biotin-4-fluorescein (B4F), 150 ug/mL (Sigma Aldrich, US)
Streptavidin adapter : Streptavidin-Cy3 (SA-Cy3), 10 ug/mL in PBS + 3% BSA (Sigma Aldrich, US)
Immobilized chemokine: CCL21 24-98 bio (biotinylated truncated murine CCL21, aa 24-98;
                       custom synthesized by ALMAC, Craigavon, UK); 250 ng/mL in PBS;
                       stock 25 ug/mL in PBS; stored at -20 C.
                       Truncated to remove basic C-terminal extension (aa 99-134) which causes
                       unspecific binding via heparan sulfate. Max surface density: 157+/-33
                       molecules/um2 (quantified by fluorescence intensity standard curve).
Soluble chemokine    : Murine CCL19 (R&D Systems, USA); 2.5 ug/mL in R10; stock 25 ug/mL in PBS.
Gradient tracer      : FITC-dextran 10 kDa, 200 ug/mL (Sigma Aldrich, US);
                       hydrodynamic radius 2.3 nm (comparable to CCL19: 1.7+/-0.4 nm,
                       CCL21: 1.9+/-0.4 nm).
Cell culture medium  : R10 (RPMI 1640 + 10% FCS + L-Glucose + Pen/Strep)
DC maturation        : LPS, 200 ng/mL


LAPAP SYSTEM
------------
Full name            : Laser-Assisted Protein Adsorption by Photobleaching
Laser                : 355 nm pulsed UV, steerable; pulse frequency 1 kHz
Objective            : Zeiss LD Plan Neo 20x/0.4 (long working distance)
Scanning             : High-speed galvanometric mirror pair; spot spacing ~half focus diameter
                       for continuous pattern; total light dose split into multiple pulses per
                       spot to average pulse-to-pulse power variability
Lateral resolution   : ~0.7 um
Dynamic range        : ~100:1
Pattern specification: Image file; pixel intensity values determine local light dose (bleaching dose)
Calibration          : Compensates for off-center numerical aperture drop and geometric
                       distortions from scan mirrors into objective back aperture
Pattern types        : Uniform patch (haptokinesis control), linear gradient (haptotaxis)
Reference            : Behrndt et al., Science 338, 257 (2012) for hardware description


GRADIENT GENERATION
-------------------
Soluble method       : Flow-free diffusion; source-sink flow-switching strategy
                       (Frank & Tay, Lab Chip 13, 1273, 2013;
                        Mehling et al., Lab Chip 15, 1276, 2015)
Source channel       : Sequentially refilled with R10 + CCL19 (2.5 ug/mL) + FITC-dextran
                       10 kDa (200 ug/mL) via short-end port
Sink channel         : Sequentially refilled with fresh R10 via opposite short-end port
Gradient build time  : ~2.5 h to reach peak CCL19 ~1.8 ug/mL (~190 nM)
CCR7/CCL19 Kd       : 10-100 nM (concentrations in gradient cover dissociation constant range
                       and are sufficient for G-protein loading and downstream signalling)
CCL19 regimes tested :
  CCL19_low    : 0-1.2 ug/mL -> chemokinesis (increased speed, undirected)
  CCL19_medium : 0-1.3 ug/mL -> directed chemotaxis (significantly increased directionality)
  CCL19_high   : 0-1.7 ug/mL -> highly directional chemotaxis (further augmented directionality)
Gradient monitoring  : FITC-dextran fluorescence; spatially averaged over centered
                       longitudinal section of chamber (Fig. 1d in paper)


IMAGING AND ANALYSIS
--------------------
Microscope     : Nikon Ti automated inverted microscope
Objectives     : 10x/NA 0.3 Air Plan Fluor Ph1; 20x/NA 0.5 Air Plan Fluor Ph1 (Nikon, Japan)
Camera         : Digital EMCCD (Hamamatsu C9100-02)
Incubator      : Stage-top; 37 C, 5% CO2, 90% humidity
Tracking area  : 300 x 200 um (corresponds to size of chemokine pattern)
Image software : NIS-AR (Nikon, Japan)
Cell tracking  : Fiji (Schindelin et al., Nat Meth 9, 676, 2012) + Manual Tracking plugin
                 (Cordelieres 2005); manual tracking
Data analysis  : Matlab 2013 (MathWorks Inc., US)


STATISTICAL ANALYSIS
--------------------
Directionality metric : <cos(Theta)>; Theta = angle between gradient direction and current
                        cell direction. Determined every 3 min (cells move ~1 cell diameter).
                        Events without any motion excluded.
Bootstrapping         : 200 resamplings with original sample size
Error bars            : Standard deviation of <cos(Theta)> from bootstrapping


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

ARM 1: HAPTOTAXIS (BB1 -> BB2/BB3 -> BB4)
------------------------------------------

Step 1 | Chip Priming with PBS
  BS variable : chipPrime
  Inputs      : PBS, PBS
  Operation   : mix
  Duration    : 5 min (IR: 300.0 SECOND)
  Pressure    : Flow lines at 0.2-0.4 bar
  Purpose     : Fill entire chip with PBS; determine optimal valve closing pressure
                per chip (0.5 bar increments in control channels).

Step 2 | Fibronectin Coating
  BS variable : fibronectinCoat -> coatedChamber -> chamberReady
  Inputs      : Fibronectin (250 ug/mL)
  Operation   : mix (coat) + mix (PBS flush 1 min) + mix (R10 flush 10 min)
  Duration    : 60 min coat (IR: 3600.0 SECOND); 1 min PBS flush (IR: 60.0 SECOND);
                10 min R10 flush (IR: 600.0 SECOND)
  Temperature : Room temperature
  Purpose     : Fibronectin acts as beta2-integrin ligand enabling DC adhesion and 2D
                migration on PDMS surface. Fibronectin in flow channels flushed with PBS
                after coating; chambers flushed with R10 for 10 min before use.

Step 3 | LAPAP - B4F Loading and PBS Wash
  BS variable : b4fLoaded -> b4fCoated
  Inputs      : PBS (wash, 10 s), B4F 150 ug/mL
  Operation   : mix (PBS wash) + mix (B4F loading 1 min)
  Duration    : 10 s PBS wash + 1 min B4F load (IR: 60.0 SECOND for b4fCoated)
  Purpose     : Chambers washed to remove unbound fibronectin. B4F loaded into assembled
                closed channels via reagent inlets; coats glass surface as LAPAP anchor.

Step 4 | LAPAP - UV Laser Gradient Writing
  BS variable : lapapPattern -> patternWashed
  Inputs      : PBS (used as placeholder in BS for laser event)
  Operation   : mix (abstracts laser scanning event); mix (PBS wash 10 s)
  Duration    : 20 min laser writing (IR: 1200.0 SECOND); 10 s PBS wash (IR: 10.0 SECOND)
  Laser       : 355 nm pulsed UV; Zeiss LD Plan Neo 20x/0.4; galvanometric mirrors;
                1 kHz pulse frequency; ~0.7 um lateral resolution; ~100:1 dynamic range
  Pattern     : Uniform patch (haptokinesis control) or linear gradient (haptotaxis);
                pixel intensity image specifies local light dose; spot spacing ~half focus
                diameter; light dose split into multiple pulses per spot.
  Purpose     : Covalent surface-deposition of B4F in arbitrary graded intensity patterns.
                Unbound B4F washed out with PBS (10 s) after writing.

Step 5 | Streptavidin-Cy3 Incubation
  BS variable : saCy3Bound -> saCy3Washed
  Inputs      : StreptavidinCy3 (10 ug/mL in PBS + 3% BSA)
  Operation   : mix (20 min incubation) + mix (PBS wash 10 s)
  Duration    : 20 min (IR: 1200.0 SECOND); 10 s PBS wash (IR: 10.0 SECOND)
  Temperature : Room temperature
  Purpose     : SA-Cy3 binds to photobleached B4F anchors in laser pattern. SA-Cy3
                fluorescence allows visualization and quantification of printed gradient.
                SA-Cy3 intensity correlates closely with anti-CCL21 antibody staining.

Step 6 | CCL21 24-98 bio Immobilization
  BS variable : ccl21Immobilized -> ccl21Washed
  Inputs      : CCL21_24_98_bio (250 ng/mL in PBS)
  Operation   : mix (30 min incubation at 37 C) + mix (PBS wash 10 s)
  Duration    : 30 min at 37 C (IR: 1800.0 SECOND); 10 s PBS wash (IR: 10.0 SECOND)
  Surface density : max 157 +/- 33 molecules/um2 (0.24 ug/mL equivalent unit volume)
  Supporting channels: kept under constant PBS flow (0.2 bar) to prevent non-specific
                adsorption of CCL21 outside cell culture chambers.
  Purpose     : Biotin tag on CCL21 C-terminus binds streptavidin anchors from LAPAP
                pattern. Truncated aa 24-98 avoids heparan-sulfate unspecific binding.

Step 7 | DC Loading into Migration Chambers
  BS variable : dcLoaded -> dcAdhered
  Inputs      : DendriticCells (10 x 10^6 cells/mL in R10), CellCultureMedium_R10
  Operation   : mix (1 min loading) + mix (30 min adhesion recovery)
  Duration    : 1 min loading (IR: 60.0 SECOND); 30 min recovery (IR: 1800.0 SECOND)
  Loading port: Short-end ports (produces distribution of cells along chamber length)
  Purpose     : DCs adhere loosely to fibronectin-coated PDMS. Round morphology with
                constant protrusions under no-chemokine conditions (undirected migration).

Step 8 | Haptotaxis Detection
  BS variable    : haptotaxisSignal
  Detection module: haptotaxisDetection
  Operation      : detect on dcAdhered
  Duration       : 100 min (IR: 6000.0 SECOND)
  Expected results:
    No chemokine     : Undirected migration; isotropic rose plot; round cell morphology
    CCL21 patch      : Haptokinesis; increased migration speed; no directed migration;
                       tighter adhesion to substrate; isotropic rose plot
    CCL21 gradient   : Haptotaxis; directed migration toward high [CCL21]; rose plot
                       asymmetric toward gradient direction
  Branch:
    PASS (BB2): haptotaxisSignal > 0 -> dispose(dcAdhered); fall through to BB4
    FAIL (BB3): haptotaxisSignal <= 0 -> drain(dcAdhered); jump to BB4


ARM 2: CHEMOTAXIS (BB4 -> BB5/BB6 -> BB7)
------------------------------------------

Step 9 | DC Loading for Chemotaxis Arm
  BS variable : dcLoaded2
  Inputs      : DendriticCells, CellCultureMedium_R10
  Operation   : mix
  Duration    : 30 min adhesion (IR: 1800.0 SECOND)
  Notes       : Fresh DCs loaded into fibronectin-coated chambers without CCL21 patterning.

Step 10 | CCL19 Soluble Gradient Generation
  BS variable : ccl19FitcMix -> gradientSetup -> ccl19Gradient
  Inputs      : CCL19 (2.5 ug/mL), FITCDextran_10kDa (200 ug/mL), CellCultureMedium_R10
  Operation   : mix (source preparation 5 s) + mix (gradient setup 5 s) +
                mix (gradient build 150 min)
  Duration    : 150 min (IR: 9000.0 SECOND)
  Peak CCL19  : ~1.8 ug/mL (~190 nM) after 2.5 h
  CCL19 regimes:
    CCL19_low    (0-1.2 ug/mL) : chemokinesis; cells faster but undirected
    CCL19_medium (0-1.3 ug/mL) : significantly increased directionality toward high [CCL19]
    CCL19_high   (0-1.7 ug/mL) : further augmented directionality
  Control        : R10 medium from both ends -> undirected migration (Fig. 4a)
  Notes       : FITC-dextran traces gradient profile. CCL19 concentrations cover CCR7/CCL19
                Kd (10-100 nM) and trigger G-protein loading and downstream CCR7 signalling.

Step 11 | Chemotaxis Detection
  BS variable     : chemotaxisSignal
  Detection module: chemotaxisDetection
  Operation       : detect on ccl19Gradient
  Duration        : 150 min (IR: 9000.0 SECOND)
  Analysis        : Directionality <cos(Theta)> vs. chamber position (= local CCL19
                    concentration) and time; Fig. 4e in paper
  Branch:
    PASS (BB5): chemotaxisSignal > 0 -> dispose(ccl19Gradient); fall through to BB7
    FAIL (BB6): chemotaxisSignal <= 0 -> drain(ccl19Gradient); jump to BB7


ARM 3: COMPETING GRADIENTS (BB7 -> BB8/BB9 -> BB10)
-----------------------------------------------------

Step 12 | LAPAP Re-Patterning and DC Loading (Competing Arm)
  BS variables  : b4fLoad2 -> lapapWrite2 -> saCoat2 -> ccl21Coat2 -> dcOnCCL21 -> dcRecovered
  Inputs        : PBS, B4F_BiotinFluorescein, StreptavidinCy3, CCL21_24_98_bio,
                  DendriticCells, CellCultureMedium_R10
  Operation     : Sequential mix steps (full LAPAP patterning protocol repeated)
  Durations     : B4F load 1 min (IR: 60.0 SECOND); LAPAP write 20 min (IR: 1200.0 SECOND);
                  SA-Cy3 20 min (IR: 1200.0 SECOND); CCL21 immobilization 30 min
                  (IR: 1800.0 SECOND); DC loading 1 min (IR: 60.0 SECOND);
                  DC recovery 30 min (IR: 1800.0 SECOND)
  CCL21 region  : Lower and middle area of migration chamber; max ~160 molecules/um2
                  (= 0.24 ug/mL equivalent unit volume; Supplemental Figure S6)
  Notes         : DCs positioned to include both CCL21-gradient regions. 30 min recovery
                  before CCL19 gradient generation (Supplemental Movie S3).

Step 13 | Opposing CCL19 Soluble Gradient Superimposition
  BS variables  : conditionAGrad (CCL19_low/CCL21); conditionBGrad (CCL19_medium/CCL21)
  Inputs        : CCL19, FITCDextran_10kDa, CellCultureMedium_R10 (x2 sets)
  Operation     : mix (x2 conditions run in parallel in separate CCL21-gradient regions)
  Duration      : 100 min per condition (IR: 6000.0 SECOND each)
  Gradient direction: Opposing -- CCL19 source at one short end; CCL21 gradient in
                  lower/middle area pointing in opposite direction
  Conditions:
    Condition A (CCL19_low/CCL21):
      CCL19 range : 0-1.0 ug/mL
      Expected    : DC migration toward haptotactic CCL21 gradient at all time points
                    (haptotaxis dominant; Fig. 5a); CCL21 signal not overridden
    Condition B (CCL19_medium/CCL21):
      CCL19 range : 0-1.2 ug/mL
      Expected    : DC migration switches toward chemotactic CCL19 after gradient build-up
                    (chemotaxis dominant, overrides haptotaxis; Fig. 5b)
  Imaging       : SA-Cy3 (CCL21, red) and FITC-dextran (CCL19, green) channels imaged
                  simultaneously to confirm gradient orientation and overlap (Fig. 5a/b)
  Time windows  : Directionality tracked across 0-33 min, 33-66 min, 66-100 min (Fig. 5c)

Step 14 | Competing Gradient Detection and Directionality Resolution
  BS variable     : competingSignal
  Detection module: competingGradientDetection
  Operation       : detect on conditionAGrad
  Duration        : 100 min (IR: 6000.0 SECOND)
  Key result      : Low CCL19 (~0-1 ug/mL) -> haptotaxis dominant;
                    medium CCL19 (~0-1.2 ug/mL) -> chemotaxis dominant;
                    ~1 ug/mL threshold for chemotaxis to override immobilized CCL21 signal.
  Interpretation  : Soluble CCL19 can override immobilized CCL21 haptotactic signal above
                    a concentration threshold. Mechanism may relate to comparable CCR7
                    binding affinities of CCL19 and CCL21, or differential activation of
                    CCR7 binding sites (single amino acid mutation studies show CCL19 and
                    CCL21 can differentially affect receptor activation; Ott et al., 2004).
  Branch:
    PASS (BB8): competingSignal > 0 -> dispose(conditionAGrad, conditionBGrad)
    FAIL (BB9): competingSignal <= 0 -> drain(conditionAGrad, conditionBGrad); jump BB10


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file  : schwarz_chemokine_migration_microfluidics.bs
Compiler        : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output       : 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
DAG file        : schwarz_chemokine_migration_microfluidics_main_dag.dot
Duration units  : s and m only (BioScript constraint); h token not supported.
                  All durations verified against compiler IR SECOND output values.

Duration conversions (bs source -> IR):
  5m   chip prime           ->  300.0 SECOND
  60m  fibronectin coat     -> 3600.0 SECOND
  1m   PBS flush            ->   60.0 SECOND
  10m  R10 flush            ->  600.0 SECOND
  20m  LAPAP write          -> 1200.0 SECOND
  20m  SA-Cy3 incubation    -> 1200.0 SECOND
  30m  CCL21 load           -> 1800.0 SECOND
  30m  DC adhesion recovery -> 1800.0 SECOND
  100m haptotaxis detect    -> 6000.0 SECOND
  150m chemotaxis gradient  -> 9000.0 SECOND
  150m chemotaxis detect    -> 9000.0 SECOND
  100m competing gradient   -> 6000.0 SECOND
  100m competing detect     -> 6000.0 SECOND

Modules   : haptotaxisDetection, chemotaxisDetection, competingGradientDetection
Manifests : PBS, Fibronectin, PluronicF127, B4F_BiotinFluorescein, StreptavidinCy3,
            CCL21_24_98_bio, CCL19, FITCDextran_10kDa, DendriticCells, CellCultureMedium_R10

BioScript abstraction notes:
  LAPAP laser writing  : Abstracted as mix(b4fCoated, PBS); no DMF-sense reagent mixing;
                         represents the UV laser scanning event over the B4F surface.
  Channel flow events  : All source-sink valve actuation and flow-switching steps abstracted
                         via mix operations (consistent with reference .bs file conventions).
  heat statements      : Model temperature-controlled incubations (37 C for CCL21 loading
                         and DC adhesion in competing arm).
  drain vs dispose     : Compiler normalises drain to dispose in IR output; both are terminal
                         fluid operations at IR level. Source .bs correctly uses drain for
                         false branches and dispose for true branches throughout.
  BB2 fall-through     : True branch (BB2) has no explicit jump in IR; compiler handles
                         fall-through to BB4 implicitly. Correct CFG behaviour for this
                         compiler version. Same pattern observed in reference .bs files.

CFG structure (DAG verified):
  BB1  (main)       -> BB2 (T), BB3 (F)    [haptotaxis gate]
  BB2, BB3          -> BB4 (join)
  BB4  (join)       -> BB5 (T), BB6 (F)    [chemotaxis gate]
  BB5, BB6          -> BB7 (join)
  BB7  (join)       -> BB8 (T), BB9 (F)    [competing gradient gate]
  BB8, BB9          -> BB10 (terminal/NOP)
  Total: 10 nodes, 12 edges, 3 sequential diamond-chain if/join pairs.
  No dangling nodes, no unreachable blocks, no missing edges confirmed in .dot output.

protocol.title: A Microfluidic Device for Measuring Cell Migration Towards Substrate-Bound and Soluble Chemokine Gradients
protocol.platform: Two-layer PDMS microfluidic device with LAPAP photo-patterning and flow-free diffusion gradient generation
protocol.cell_type: Bone marrow-derived dendritic cells (DCs) from C57BL/6J mice
protocol.objective: Simultaneous generation of surface-immobilized haptotactic (CCL21) and diffusion-based chemotactic (CCL19) chemokine gradients; single-cell tracking of DC migration in combined and competing gradient fields

layers: PDMS flow layer: 6 migration chambers (l=1100 um, w=200 um, h_max=28 um)
PDMS control layer: independently controllable membrane valves on all ports
Glass substrate: fibronectin-coated (250 ug/mL) for beta2-integrin-mediated DC adhesion

migration_chambers.side_port: one, at midpoint of long axis
migration_chambers.short_end_ports: two; connected to source and sink support channels

device.valves: Independently controllable PDMS membrane valves on all ports; optimal closing pressure determined per chip by incrementing control channel pressure in 0.5 bar steps
device.coating: Human plasma fibronectin, c=250 ug/mL (Millipore, Austria); 1 h incubation; acts as beta2-integrin ligand for DC adhesion and 2D migration

reagents.streptavidin: Streptavidin-Cy3 (SA-Cy3), 10 ug/mL in PBS with 3% BSA (Sigma Aldrich, US)

immobilized_chemokine.name: CCL21 24-98 bio
immobilized_chemokine.truncation_rationale: Removes basic C-terminal extension of full-length CCL21 (aa 1-134) which causes unspecific background binding via heparan sulfate

soluble_chemokine.name: CCL19
soluble_chemokine.gradient_tracer: FITC-dextran 10 kDa (200 ug/mL; Sigma Aldrich, US; hydrodynamic radius 2.3 nm)

gradient_tracer.name: FITC-dextran 10 kDa
gradient_tracer.purpose: Proxy tracer for chemokine diffusion profile; similar hydrodynamic radius to CCL19 (1.7+/-0.4 nm) and CCL21 (1.9+/-0.4 nm)

reagents.cell_culture_medium: RPMI 1640 (R10) + 10% fetal calf serum + L-Glucose + Penicillin/Streptomycin (Life Sciences, Austria)

lapap_system.objective: Zeiss LD Plan Neo 20x/0.4, long working distance
lapap_system.mirror_system: High-speed galvanometric mirror pair for focus spot scanning
lapap_system.pattern_specification: Image file; pixel intensity values determine local light dose
lapap_system.calibration: Compensates for off-center NA drop and geometric distortions from scan mirrors into objective back aperture; total light dose split into multiple pulses per spot to average pulse-to-pulse power variability

gradient_generation.reference: Frank & Tay, Lab Chip 13, 1273 (2013); Mehling et al., Lab Chip 15, 1276 (2015)
gradient_generation.source_channel: Sequentially refilled with R10 + CCL19 (2.5 ug/mL) + FITC-dextran 10 kDa (200 ug/mL)
gradient_generation.sink_channel: Sequentially refilled with fresh R10 medium
gradient_generation.gradient_profiles: Monitored by FITC-dextran fluorescence; spatially averaged over centered longitudinal section of chamber (Fig. 1d)

imaging.image_processing: Fiji (Schindelin et al., Nat Meth 9, 2012) + Manual Tracking plugin (Cordelieres 2005)

statistical_analysis.directionality_metric: <cos(Theta)>; Theta = angle between gradient direction and current cell direction

steps.name: Chip priming with PBS
steps.notes: Flow lines pressurised; entire chip filled with PBS. Control channel pressure incremented in 0.5 bar steps to determine optimal valve closing pressure per chip.

steps.name: Fibronectin coating of migration chambers
steps.notes: Fibronectin incubated 1 h in cell culture chambers. After coating, fibronectin in flow channels flushed with PBS (60 s). Chambers then flushed with R10 medium 10 min.

steps.name: LAPAP - B4F loading and PBS wash
steps.notes: Chambers washed with PBS 10 s to remove unbound fibronectin. B4F (150 ug/mL) loaded into assembled closed channels via reagent inlets and coats glass surface prior to UV patterning.

steps.name: LAPAP - UV laser gradient writing
steps.operation: mix (abstracts laser scanning event over B4F-coated chamber)
steps.notes: Gradient written one spot at a time; spot spacing ~half focus diameter for continuous pattern. Pixel intensity image specifies local light dose. Unbound B4F washed out with PBS (10 s) after writing.

steps.name: Streptavidin-Cy3 incubation
steps.notes: SA-Cy3 binds to photobleached B4F anchors in laser-written pattern. SA-Cy3 fluorescence allows visualization and quantification of printed gradient. Followed by PBS wash (10 s).

steps.name: CCL21 24-98 bio immobilization
steps.notes: Biotin tag on CCL21 C-terminus binds streptavidin anchors. Truncated aa 24-98 prevents heparan-sulfate unspecific binding. Supporting channels kept under constant PBS flow (0.2 bar) during loading. Followed by PBS wash (10 s).

steps.name: DC loading into migration chambers
steps.loading_port: short-end ports (produces distribution along chamber length)
steps.dc_source: C57BL/6J mouse bone marrow; GM-CSF culture day 8-10; LPS maturation overnight (200 ng/mL)
steps.notes: DCs adhere loosely to fibronectin-coated PDMS. Round morphology with constant protrusions under control conditions. 30 min adhesion recovery before gradient initiation.

steps.name: Haptotaxis detection - DC migration on immobilized CCL21 gradient

expected_results.CCL21_patch_uniform: Haptokinesis: increased migration speed, no directed migration; isotropic rose plot
expected_results.CCL21_gradient: Haptotaxis: directed migration toward high CCL21; asymmetric rose plot toward gradient direction

steps.name: DC loading for CCL19 chemotaxis arm
steps.notes: Fresh DCs loaded into fibronectin-coated chambers without CCL21 patterning. 30 min adhesion recovery.

steps.name: CCL19 soluble gradient generation
steps.notes: FITC-dextran traces gradient profile. Control: R10 from both ends (undirected migration, Fig. 4a).

steps.name: Chemotaxis detection - DC migration in CCL19 soluble gradient
steps.directionality_analysis: Directionality plotted vs. chamber position (= local CCL19 concentration) and time; Fig. 4e

steps.name: LAPAP re-patterning and DC loading for competing gradient arm
steps.operation: mix (sequential: B4F load, laser write, SA-Cy3, CCL21 immobilization, DC loading)
steps.ccl21_gradient_region: lower and middle area of migration chamber
steps.notes: Full LAPAP patterning protocol repeated for competing gradient experiment. DCs positioned to include both CCL21-gradient regions. 30 min recovery before CCL19 gradient generation.

steps.name: Opposing CCL19 soluble gradient superimposition

conditionA.label: CCL19_low / CCL21
conditionA.expected_outcome: DC migration toward haptotactic CCL21 gradient (haptotaxis dominant at all time points; Fig. 5a)

conditionB.label: CCL19_medium / CCL21
conditionB.expected_outcome: DC migration overrides toward chemotactic CCL19 after gradient build-up (chemotaxis dominant; Fig. 5b)

steps.gradient_direction: Opposing: CCL19 source at one short end; CCL21 gradient in lower/middle chamber area pointing opposite direction
steps.imaging: SA-Cy3 (CCL21, red) and FITC-dextran (CCL19, green) fluorescence channels imaged simultaneously
steps.notes: Both conditions run in parallel in separate CCL21-gradient regions of the same chip. Directionality measured as <cos(Theta)> vs. position and time (Fig. 5c). CCL19 can override immobilized CCL21 signal above ~1 ug/mL threshold.

steps.name: Competing gradient detection and directionality resolution

basic_blocks.content: Device priming, fibronectin coating, LAPAP B4F loading, UV laser patterning, SA-Cy3 incubation, CCL21 immobilization, DC loading, haptotaxis detection

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Electrochemiluminescence on Digital Microfluidics for microRNA Analysis
Source Link  : https://opensiuc.lib.siu.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?referer=&httpsredir=1&article=1004&context=chem_pubs
Paper DOI    : http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.bios.2015.10.036
Journal      : Biosensors and Bioelectronics, 2015, PII: S0956-5663(15)30500-5
Platform     : DMF (digital microfluidics) with integrated ECL detection on ITO-coated top-plate (EWOD/DMFB)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes the first integration of electrochemiluminescence (ECL) detection with
digital microfluidics (DMF), applied to a magnetic particle-based oligonucleotide hybridization
assay for microRNA analysis. The DMF-ECL system uses sample volumes of ~1.8 uL and targets
microRNA-143 (miRNA-143), a molecule down-regulated in some aggressive cancers, via its
synthetic deoxyribose analogue ds-143.

Magnetic particles pre-coated with single-stranded probe DNA (ss-143) capture complementary
target sequences from solution. The intercalating luminophore [Ru(Phen)3]Cl2 binds double-
stranded DNA formed on the bead surface after hybridization. Tripropylamine (TPA) is then
added as co-reactant. The final bead suspension is actuated to ITO working electrodes on the
DMF top-plate, where 1.5 V DC excites ECL emission detected by a photomultiplier tube (PMT).
ECL signal is proportional to hybridized target; the system achieves an absolute limit of
detection of 1.5 femtomoles (CLOD = 1.1 nM) and discriminates single-nucleotide mismatches
with high specificity. The assay also detects miRNA-143 expression differences between
MCF-7 (less aggressive) and MDA-MB-231 (more aggressive) breast cancer cell lysates.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Configuration : Two-plate DMF (top + bottom plates)

Top plate:
  - ITO-coated glass substrate; remainder of ITO serves as DMF ground electrode
  - 4 x bare (transparent) ITO circular working electrodes (WE), diameter 800 um
  - 2 x Ag/Au/ITO square counter/pseudoreference electrodes (CE/RE), 560 x 560 um
  - Teflon-AF hydrophobic coating globally applied; apertures formed above each WE and CE/RE
  - WEs connected to contact pads via patterned ITO wires
  - Ag/Au/ITO CE/RE formed using gold adhesion layer for mechanical stability

Bottom plate:
  - Glass substrate
  - Chromium array of DMF driving electrodes
  - Parylene-C dielectric layer
  - Teflon-AF hydrophobic layer

Assembly:
  - Top and bottom plates biased by AC voltages (open-source DropBot controller) for droplet
    actuation (move, dispense, mix, split)
  - DC voltages applied between ITO WE and Ag/Au/ITO CE/RE via commercial potentiostat for
    electrochemistry and ECL measurements
  - Permanent magnet positioned below bottom plate for Dynabead immobilization
  - PMT suspended above top-plate to collect ECL photons

Droplet volume : ~1.8 uL per unit droplet


PRE-ASSAY STEPS (off-chip, not encoded in BioScript)
-----------------------------------------------------
1. Probe immobilization: biotinylated ss-143 (21-mer, deoxyribose analogue of miRNA-143)
   immobilized on Dynabeads M-280 Streptavidin via avidin-biotin chemistry.
   Details in supplementary information of source paper.

2. ITO electrode cleaning: cathodic electrochemical cleaning of ITO WEs by cyclic voltammetry
   (10 cycles, -1 V to 0 V, 100 mV/s) in 20 uL PBS (1x) positioned on DMF top-plates using
   ITO WE and Ag/Au/ITO CE/RE. Removes adsorbed organics and reduces oxide layer.


REAGENTS
--------
MagneticParticles : Dynabeads M-280 Streptavidin (Invitrogen Dynal AS, Oslo, Norway)
                    10 mg/mL, ~6-7e8 particles/mL, diameter 2.8 um, in PBS with 0.1% BSA
                    and 0.02% NaN3. Pre-coated with biotinylated ss-143 probe DNA off-chip.
                    Supplemented with 0.05% Pluronic F68 v/v prior to DMF use.

TargetSequence    : ds-143 (synthetic deoxyribose analogue of miRNA-143) in hybridization
                    buffer at test concentration (0, 10, 100, or 1000 nM).
                    Variants: 143-m1 (single nucleotide mismatch), 143-m2 (double nucleotide
                    mismatch), nc-145 (fully non-complementary, deoxyribose analogue of
                    miRNA-145, used as negative control).
                    For cell lysate assays: MCF-7 or MDA-MB-231 lysate diluted 1:10 in sample
                    dilution buffer (pH 8.0: 7.7 mM Tris-base, 12.2 mM Tris-HCl, 200 mM NaCl,
                    5 mM MgCl2, 4% BSA w/v, 0.05% Pluronic L64 w/v).
                    Supplier: Bio Basic Canada Inc. (Markham, ON); HPLC-purified; stock 50 uM
                    in DNase/RNase-free ultrapure water (Invitrogen); working dilutions in
                    respective buffer. All supplemented with 0.05% Pluronic F68.

HybridizationBuffer: 20 mM Tris-HCl, 0.2 M NaCl, 5 mM MgCl2, pH 8.0.
                    Supplemented with 0.05% Pluronic F68.

RuPhen3Cl2        : 200 uM tris(phenanthroline)ruthenium(II) chloride ([Ru(Phen)3]Cl2) in
                    PBS (1x), pH 7.5. Supplemented with 0.05% Pluronic F68.
                    Supplier: Sigma Chemical (Oakville, ON, Canada).
                    ECL luminophore: each Ru(Phen)3(2+) ion intercalates into 4 base pairs of
                    dsDNA double helix; does not bind ssDNA or RNA. Signal tracks dsDNA amount.

PBS               : Phosphate buffered saline (1x), pH 7.5. Supplemented with 0.05% Pluronic F68.

TPA               : 20 mM tripropylamine in PBS (1x), pH 7.5. Supplemented with 0.05%
                    Pluronic F68. ECL co-reactant: oxidized at ITO WE simultaneously with
                    Ru(Phen)3(2+); TPA(+) radical reduces luminophore to excited state,
                    which emits photons (~610 nm) on return to ground state.

PluronicF68       : 0.05% v/v additive in all above solutions prior to DMF use. Reduces
                    droplet fouling of Teflon-AF hydrophobic surface.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Magnetic Particle Dispense and Initial Separation
  Inputs     : MagneticParticles (3 unit droplets, ~1.8 uL each)
  Operations : dispense x3 -> mix x2 (merge to ~5.4 uL) -> heat/magnet 30s -> dispose
  BioScript  : beads1, beads2, beads3 -> beadsMerge1 -> beadsMerged -> [magnet] -> dispose
  IR timing  : mix @ 5.0 SECOND; heat @ 25.0 CELSIUS @ 30.0 SECOND
  Notes      : Paper M&M Sec 2.3: "three unit droplets containing magnetic particles were
               dispensed from their reservoir and merged, and the particles were separated
               from the supernatant." Permanent magnet immobilizes Dynabeads; storage buffer
               supernatant actuated away. heat at 25c for 30s abstracts magnet hold time.
               For cell lysate assays: 5 unit droplets used instead of 3.

Step 2 | Target Hybridization (15 min)
  Inputs     : TargetSequence (2 unit droplets), MagneticParticles (1 unit, pellet model)
  Operations : dispense x2 -> mix (merge) -> dispense pellet -> mix 15m -> heat/magnet 30s
               -> dispose supernatant
  BioScript  : target1, target2 -> targetMerged; pelletForHybrid -> hybridDroplet -> [magnet]
               -> dispose
  IR timing  : mix @ 900.0 SECOND (15 min); heat @ 25.0 CELSIUS @ 30.0 SECOND
  Notes      : Paper M&M Sec 2.3: "two unit droplets of target sequence solution were
               dispensed, merged, and delivered to the immobilized particles for resuspension
               and incubation for 15 min." ds-143 hybridizes to ss-143 probe on bead surface.
               pelletForHybrid re-dispense models bead pellet resuspended by incoming droplet
               (magnet removed; electrode actuation drives resuspension).

Step 3 | Hybridization Buffer Wash x4
  Inputs     : HybridizationBuffer (1 unit droplet per cycle), MagneticParticles (1 unit per cycle)
  Operations : Per cycle: dispense pellet + dispense buf -> mix 1m -> heat/magnet 30s ->
               dispose; repeated 4 times explicitly
  BioScript  : pelletW1-4, washBuf1-4, washMix1-4 (4 independent wash loops)
  IR timing  : mix @ 60.0 SECOND; heat @ 25.0 CELSIUS @ 30.0 SECOND (x4)
  Notes      : Paper M&M Sec 2.3: "particles were washed four times in series by
               re-suspending and mixing with one unit droplet of hybridization buffer
               followed by magnetic separation from the supernatant." Removes unbound
               and non-specifically adsorbed target sequences.

Step 4 | Ru(Phen)3Cl2 Intercalation Labeling (2 min)
  Inputs     : RuPhen3Cl2 (2 unit droplets), MagneticParticles (1 unit, pellet model)
  Operations : dispense x2 -> mix (merge 5s) -> dispense pellet -> mix 2m ->
               heat/magnet 30s -> dispose supernatant
  BioScript  : ruDrop1, ruDrop2 -> ruMerged; pelletForRu -> ruLabelMix -> [magnet] -> dispose
  IR timing  : mix @ 5.0 SECOND (merge); mix @ 120.0 SECOND (incubation);
               heat @ 25.0 CELSIUS @ 30.0 SECOND
  Notes      : Paper M&M Sec 2.3: "two unit droplets of [Ru(Phen)3]Cl2 solution were
               dispensed, merged, and delivered to the particles, where they were re-suspended
               and mixed for 2 min." ECL signal is proportional to dsDNA intercalation level
               (marker for hybridized target amount).

Step 5 | PBS Wash x2
  Inputs     : PBS (1 unit droplet per cycle), MagneticParticles (1 unit per cycle)
  Operations : Per cycle: dispense pellet + dispense PBS -> mix 1m -> heat/magnet 30s ->
               dispose; repeated 2 times
  BioScript  : pelletPW1-2, pbsWash1-2, pbsMix1-2
  IR timing  : mix @ 60.0 SECOND; heat @ 25.0 CELSIUS @ 30.0 SECOND (x2)
  Notes      : Paper M&M Sec 2.3: "particles were washed two times with 2 droplets of PBS
               as in step 3." Removes excess unbound Ru(Phen)3(2+) before TPA addition.

Step 6 | TPA Co-reactant Addition (1 min)
  Inputs     : TPA (2 unit droplets), MagneticParticles (1 unit, pellet model)
  Operations : dispense x2 -> mix (merge 5s) -> dispense pellet -> mix 1m
  BioScript  : tpaDrop1, tpaDrop2 -> tpaMerged; pelletForTPA -> finalDroplet
  IR timing  : mix @ 5.0 SECOND (merge); mix @ 60.0 SECOND (incubation)
  Notes      : Paper M&M Sec 2.3: "two droplets of TPA solution were dispensed, merged, and
               delivered to the particles, where they were re-suspended and mixed for 1 min."
               TPA and Ru(Phen)3(2+) are oxidized simultaneously at the ITO WE; TPA(+)
               radical reduces luminophore to excited state (~610 nm emission).

Step 7 | ECL Measurement
  Inputs     : finalDroplet (bead suspension in TPA + Ru(Phen)3(2+))
  Operation  : detect eclDetection on finalDroplet for 45s
  BioScript  : eclSignal = detect eclDetection on finalDroplet for 45s
  IR timing  : detect @ 45.0 SECOND
  Applied voltage : 1.5 V DC (ITO WE vs Ag/Au/ITO CE/RE)
  Duration   : 45 s total; maximum ECL counts recorded within first 10 s (CV ~10%)
  LOD        : CLOD = 1.1 nM; absolute LOD = 1.5 femtomoles
  Notes      : Paper M&M Sec 2.3: "the final droplet containing TPA and Ru(Phen)3(2+)-labeled
               DNA modified particles was actuated to the ECL electrodes on the top-plate for
               ECL measurements." 1.5 V chosen from cyclic voltammogram plateau (1.4-1.5 V).
               ECL signal decays over time due to irreversible luminophore decomposition;
               maximum within 10 s gives reproducible signal. Two parallel assays run
               simultaneously; total assay time ~40 min.


ECL QC GATE (if/else branch)
-----------------------------
  Condition  : eclSignal > 0
  Pass (BB2) : eclSignal > 0 -> hybridization detected (ECL above blank); dispose finalDroplet
  Fail (BB3) : eclSignal <= 0 -> no signal (below LOD or reagent failure); drain finalDroplet
  Cleanup    : dispose eclSignal (BB4, terminal)
  IR note    : drain in .bs false-branch lowered to dispose() in IR -- known compiler bug;
               .bs source is correct as written.


SELECTIVITY RESULTS
-------------------
  ds-143 vs 143-m1 (single mismatch) : p = 0.002 (distinguishable)
  ds-143 vs 143-m2 (double mismatch) : p = 0.001 (distinguishable)
  143-m1 vs 143-m2                   : p = 0.005 (significant difference)
  ds-143 vs nc-145 (non-complementary): p = 0.2  (indistinguishable from blank, as expected)
  Mechanism: mismatch (1) decreases hybridization efficiency (steric advantage for surface-
  bound probes) and (2) introduces structural distortion reducing Ru(Phen)3(2+) intercalation.


CELL LYSATE RESULTS
-------------------
  MDA-MB-231 ECL counts : 41,000 +/- 6,500 (CV 16%)
  MCF-7 ECL counts      : 95,000 +/- 37,100 (CV 39%)
  Background ECL counts : 17,000 +/- 8,000
  MDA-MB-231 vs MCF-7   : p = 0.03
  Conclusion: MDA-MB-231 (more aggressive, higher metastatic propensity) shows significantly
  lower ECL signal than MCF-7, consistent with down-regulation of miRNA-143 in aggressive
  breast cancer phenotypes.


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : shamsi_dmf_ecl_mirna.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : shamsi_dmf_ecl_mirna.ir
DOT output     : shamsi_dmf_ecl_mirna_main_dag.dot
Modules        : eclDetection
Manifests      : MagneticParticles, TargetSequence, HybridizationBuffer,
                 RuPhen3Cl2, PBS, TPA, PluronicF68
Total variables: 38 (all defined and consumed; zero leaks, zero dangling references)
Basic blocks   : 4 (main, bsbbif_2_t, bsbbif_3_f, bsbbif_4_j)
CFG edges      : 4 (main->2_t, main->3_f, 2_t->4_j, 3_f->4_j)

Duration conversions (all within compiler-supported s/m tokens):
  15 min hybridization -> 15m  (IR: 900.0 SECOND)
  2 min Ru labeling    -> 2m   (IR: 120.0 SECOND)
  1 min wash/TPA       -> 1m   (IR: 60.0 SECOND)
  45 s ECL detection   -> 45s  (IR: 45.0 SECOND)
  30 s magnet holds    -> 30s  (IR: 30.0 SECOND)

Known compiler behaviors (no action required):
  - drain in .bs false-branch lowered to dispose() in IR (known compiler bug; source correct)
  - bsbbif_2_t (true branch) emits no unconditional jump in IR text (known compiler limitation;
    DOT edge 2->4 resolves correctly)

Bead pellet abstraction:
  After each magnetic separation (dispose of supernatant), the bead pellet physically remains
  on-device. BioScript has no 'pellet' primitive; fresh dispense from MagneticParticles
  at each subsequent step models the retained pellet being resuspended by the incoming reagent
  droplet. This is the established pellet re-dispense pattern for this compiler.

protocol.title: Electrochemiluminescence on Digital Microfluidics for microRNA Analysis

top_plate.coating: Teflon-AF hydrophobic layer; apertures above each WE and CE/RE
top_plate.ito_remainder: functions as ground electrode for DMF droplet actuation

Parylene-C dielectric layer
Teflon-AF hydrophobic layer

device.magnet: permanent magnet positioned below bottom plate for magnetic bead separation

magnetic_particles.product: Dynabeads M-280 Streptavidin (Invitrogen Dynal AS, Oslo, Norway)
magnetic_particles.probe_immobilization: ss-143 (21-mer deoxyribose analogue, biotin-conjugated) via avidin-biotin chemistry

variants.nc-145: fully non-complementary negative control (deoxyribose analogue of miRNA-145)

target_sequence.supplier: Bio Basic Canada Inc. (Markham, ON, Canada); HPLC-purified

cell_lysate_samples.on_chip_dilution: 1:10 in sample dilution buffer (pH 8.0: Tris-base 7.7 mM, Tris-HCl 12.2 mM, NaCl 200 mM, MgCl2 5 mM, BSA 4% w/v, Pluronic L64 0.05% w/v)
cell_lysate_samples.cell_lysate_assay_modification: 5 unit droplets of magnetic particles dispensed instead of 3 (step 1)

steps.name: Magnetic particle dispense and merge
steps.notes: Paper M&M Sec 2.3: three unit droplets of magnetic particle suspension dispensed and merged. For cell lysate assays, five droplets used instead of three.

steps.name: Magnetic separation (initial bead pellet)
steps.notes: Permanent magnet below bottom plate immobilizes Dynabeads; supernatant (storage buffer) actuated away by electrode sequence. heat at 25c for 30s abstracts magnet hold.

steps.operation: dispense x2, mix (merge), dispense pellet, mix (hybridization incubation)
steps.notes: Paper M&M Sec 2.3: two unit droplets of target sequence dispensed, merged, delivered to immobilized particles for resuspension and incubation for 15 min. ds-143 hybridizes to ss-143 probe on bead surface. pelletForHybrid re-dispense from MagneticParticles models bead pellet resuspension by incoming target droplet (magnet removed, electrode actuation drives resuspension).

steps.name: Magnetic separation (post-hybridization)

steps.operation: dispense + mix (resuspend) + heat (magnet) + dispose; repeated 4 times
steps.notes: Paper M&M Sec 2.3: particles washed four times in series by re-suspending and mixing with one unit droplet of hybridization buffer followed by magnetic separation from supernatant.

steps.name: Ru(Phen)3Cl2 intercalation labeling
steps.operation: dispense x2, mix (merge), dispense pellet, mix (incubation), heat (magnet), dispose
steps.notes: Paper M&M Sec 2.3: two unit droplets of [Ru(Phen)3]Cl2 dispensed, merged, delivered to particles; resuspended and mixed for 2 min; particles separated from supernatant. Ru(Phen)3(2+) intercalates into dsDNA (4 bp per ion); ECL signal proportional to hybridized ds-143 on beads.

steps.name: PBS wash x2
steps.operation: dispense + mix (resuspend) + heat (magnet) + dispose; repeated 2 times
steps.notes: Paper M&M Sec 2.3: particles washed two times with 2 droplets of PBS as in step 3. Removes excess unbound Ru(Phen)3(2+).

steps.name: TPA co-reactant addition
steps.operation: dispense x2, mix (merge), dispense pellet, mix (incubation)
steps.notes: Paper M&M Sec 2.3: two droplets of TPA solution dispensed, merged, delivered to particles; re-suspended and mixed for 1 min. TPA is ECL co-reactant: TPA(+) radical formed on oxidation at ITO WE reduces Ru(Phen)3(2+) luminophore to excited state emitting at ~610 nm.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Single-Cell Chemoproteomics Identifies Metastatic Activity Signatures in Breast Cancer
Source Link  : https://www.science.org/doi/epdf/10.1126/sciadv.adp2622
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.adp2622
Journal      : Science Advances, 2024, Vol. 10, Article eadp2622
Authors      : Kavya Smitha Pillai, Olivia Laxton, Gang Li, Jing Lin, Olga Karginova,
               Rita Nanda, Olufunmilayo I. Olopade, Savaş Tay, Raymond E. Moellering
Platform     : Single-Cell Activity-Dependent Proximity Ligation (scADPL) coupled to
               valve-based push-up PDMS microfluidic chip with five-chamber assay units


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes an automated chemoproteomic microfluidic platform, scADPL, for
multiplexed endogenous protein activity measurements at single-cell resolution. Unlike
mRNA or bulk protein abundance methods, scADPL directly reports on the active subpopulation
of the proteome, capturing posttranslational regulation invisible to genomic or transcriptomic
approaches.

The platform integrates two components:
  1. Activity-based chemical probes (Cat-Bio for cathepsins; FP-Bio for serine hydrolases)
     that covalently label the active sites of target enzyme families in live cells.
  2. Activity-Dependent Proximity Ligation (ADPL) chemistry that converts probe-protein
     labelling events into amplifiable, barcoded oligonucleotide amplicons, quantified
     by qPCR or ddPCR.

These are coupled to a valve-based PDMS microfluidic chip that automates:
  (i)  Single-cell isolation and brightfield/fluorescence imaging
  (ii) Nanoliter-volume manipulation to achieve optimal proteome concentrations for ADPL
  (iii) Dead volume minimisation for maximum sensitivity and reproducibility

The protocol is organised into four experimental phases:
  PHASE 1 : Single-plex validation of CTSL activity (ddPCR) and NCEH1 target specificity
            (qPCR + JW480 inhibitor) in SKOV3 single cells
  PHASE 2 : Multiplexed Ag-6 panel (NCEH1, MGLL, CTSL, FAAH, CTSB, uPA) profiling in
            SKOV3 single cells with reproducibility and bulk sADPL concordance validation
  PHASE 3 : Heterogeneity profiling across cell lines (HEK293T vs SKOV3;
            aggressive SKOV3 vs non-aggressive OVCAR3 ovarian cancer)
  PHASE 4 : Patient-derived organoid (PDO) profiling from TNBC primary and metastatic
            tumours (between-patient) and ER+ pleural effusion / lymph node (within-patient)

Key quantitative outcomes:
  - sADPL detection threshold: 10 pg whole proteome; single HeLa cell ~2 ng total protein
  - Average scADPL CTSL signal: 54-fold above vehicle-only control (ddPCR)
  - Average scADPL NCEH1 signal: ~64-fold above vehicle-only control (qPCR)
  - JW480 (selective NCEH1 inhibitor, 2 uM): >90% NCEH1 signal inhibition;
    no significant effect on remaining five Ag-6 targets
  - Multiplexed Ag-6 reproducibility (day 1 vs day 2): Pearson r = 0.9981
  - scADPL vs bulk sADPL correlation: Pearson r = 0.9288
  - PCA of SKOV3 vs OVCAR3 scADPL profiles: PC1 = 84.67%, PC2 = 8.37%


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Type       : Valve-based push-up PDMS microfluidic chip
Material   : Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS), 10:1 base:curing agent
Bonding    : Air/oxygen plasma-assisted; PDMS-to-PDMS and PDMS-to-glass
Glass slide: 127.76 x 85.48 x 1 mm

Photoresist layer heights (SU-8 3025 / AZ40XT):
  - 18 mm AZ40XT : dome valve layer (rounded after overnight reflow)
  - 22 mm SU-8-3025 : first channel feature layer (spun at 1372g)
  - 70 mm SU-8-3025 : thick fluidic features (two coats; first at 1372g, second at 448g)

Chip configuration (push-up):
  - Fluidic layer (~72 g PDMS): thick layer; peeled from fluidic mold and bonded on top
    of control layer. Treated with oxygen plasma 18 s (860 mtorr; Harrick Plasma).
  - Control layer (11 g PDMS): thin layer; spun at 448g for 1 min onto control mold;
    bonded to clean glass slide.
  - Assembly incubated at 80 C overnight after bonding.

Punch sizes:
  - Retrieval outlets: 1930 um inner diameter (CR0950765N13R4, Syneoco)
  - All other inlets/outlets: 710 um inner diameter (CR0350255N20R4, Syneoco)

Five chamber zones per assay unit:
  I   - Input fluid artery
  II  - Single-cell trapping chamber
  III - Cell lysis chamber
  IV  - Proximity barcoding element incubation (whole proteome)
  V   - Proximity barcode ligation

Lithography tool: Heidelberg MLA 150 Direct Write Lithographer
                  (Heidelberg Instruments Mikrotechnik GmbH, Germany)
Wafer           : 4-inch photoresist-coated silicon


CELL LINES
----------
SKOV3       : Human ovarian cancer (high-aggressiveness reference line)
              DMEM-F12 + 10% FBS + 1% pen/strep; 37 C, 5% CO2
OVCAR3      : Human ovarian cancer (low-aggressiveness)
              DMEM-F12 + 10% FBS + 1% pen/strep; 37 C, 5% CO2
HEK293T     : Human embryonic kidney (non-cancer control; tissue mismatch)
              RPMI 1640 + 10% FBS + 1% pen/strep; 37 C, 5% CO2
MCF10A      : Non-cancerous breast epithelium (TNBC continuum baseline)
MDA-MB-231  : Aggressive breast cancer (post-EMT); derived from pleural effusion
BM1         : Formed metastatic breast lesion (kindly provided by Dr. Marsha Rosner,
              University of Chicago); RPMI 1640 + 10% FBS + 1% pen/strep
HCC70       : Normal breast cancer cell line; RPMI 1640 + 10% FBS + 1% pen/strep
PDOs        : Patient-derived organoids from:
              - 6 TNBC patients (primary and liver/lung/skin metastases)
              - 1 ER+ patient (pleural effusion L, pleural effusion R, lymph node met)
              IRB protocol 16352A; all samples deidentified; informed consent obtained.
              PDOs grown in BC PDO media (ref. 49); tested for mycoplasma before use.

All lines tested negative for mycoplasma contamination.
All lines except BM1 procured from ATCC; BM1 not STR profiled.


CHEMICAL PROBES AND DETECTION CHEMISTRY
-----------------------------------------

Activity Probes (applied off-chip to live cells before loading):
  Cat-Bio (cathepsin family-wide):
    Concentration  : 5 uM
    Incubation     : 2 h at 37 C in complete media
    Targets        : CTSL (cathepsin L), CTSB (cathepsin B)
    Chemistry      : Biotin-tagged covalent cysteine protease probe

  FP-Bio (serine hydrolase family-wide):
    Concentration  : 2 uM
    Incubation     : 30 min at 37 C in complete media
    Targets        : NCEH1, MGLL, FAAH, uPA
    Chemistry      : Fluorophosphonate biotin; labels active-site serine covalently

ADPL Detection Reagents (added on-chip at Chamber IV):
  Streptavidin-oligo conjugate (SA-oligo) : 4000 pM; binds biotin tag on probe-protein complex
  Antibody-oligo conjugate (ab-oligo)     : 200 pM per target; six antibodies for Ag-6 panel

  Antibodies used:
    NCEH1 : NCEH1 polyclonal antibody (in-house; refs 33, 36)
    CTSB  : Abcam ab58802
    FAAH  : Abcam ab54615
    MGLL  : Abcam no. 24701
    uPA   : Abcam no. 24121
    CTSL  : R&D Systems AF952-SP
    RPE   : Abcam no. 34721 (spike-in control antibody)

Proximity Ligation (Chamber V):
  Splint oligonucleotide : 100 nM; bridges SA-oligo and ab-oligo when both bound to
                           the same probe-protein complex
  Ampligase              : 0.05 U (Lucigen E0001-5D3); seals nick in ligation buffer
  Ligation buffer        : 0.3 mM NAD+, 10 mM DTT, 20 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.3,
                           50 mM KCl, 1.5 mM MgCl2
  Ligation               : 40 C for 45 min (2700 s)

Lysis Buffer (MCP):
  25 mM Tris pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA, 1 mM EGTA,
  0.5% Triton X-100, 0.5% sodium deoxycholate
  Selected after optimisation against Pierce, CST, and TM buffers (fig. S2)

Spike-In Control:
  R-phycoerythrin (RPE): Thermo Fisher Scientific P801
  Added at lysis step; used for inter-cell normalisation
  Outliers: cells with RPE values >2 SD from mean excluded from analysis


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

PHASE 1 | Single-Plex Validation

Step 1 | Device Priming
  Reagents    : PBS, Pluronics F-127
  Operation   : mix 5 min (300 s)
  Purpose     : 2% Pluronics F-127 in PBS; passivates PDMS channel surfaces,
                reduces non-specific cell adhesion before loading

Step 2 | Off-Chip Probe Labelling (SKOV3, single-plex)
  Cat-Bio arm : SKOV3 + Cat-Bio 5 uM; mix 5 s; heat 37 C, 120 min (7200 s)
  FP-Bio arm  : SKOV3 + FP-Bio 2 uM; mix 5 s; heat 37 C, 30 min (1800 s)
  Wash        : PBS wash after labelling; resuspend 50,000-100,000 cells/mL in PBS

Step 3 | On-Chip Single-Cell Trapping (Chamber II)
  Operation   : mix 2 s (abstracts pressure-driven hydrodynamic single-cell capture)
  Notes       : One cell captured per assay chamber; RPE spike-in dispensed at this stage

Step 4 | On-Chip Cell Lysis (Chamber III)
  Operation   : MCP lysis buffer added; mix 60 s; RPE spike added; mix 5 s
  Notes       : Nanoliter dead volume minimised vs bulk sADPL for maximum sensitivity

Step 5 | On-Chip Proximity Barcoding (Chamber IV)
  Operation   : SA-oligo (4000 pM) + ab-oligo (200 pM) premixed 5 s; added to lysate;
                mix 120 s; heat 25 C, 120 min (7200 s)
  Notes       : Both recognition elements bind same probe-protein complex in proximity

Step 6 | On-Chip Proximity Ligation (Chamber V)
  Operation   : Splint oligo added; mix 2 s; ligation buffer added; mix 2 s;
                heat 40 C, 45 min (2700 s)
  Product     : Ligated barcoded amplicons

Step 7 | Off-Chip Amplicon Retrieval and Preamplification
  Flush       : 9 uL water flush off-chip
  Preamplify  : 11 uL reaction (2.5x buffer, 100 nM primers, 200 uM dNTPs,
                9 U Phusion high-fidelity DNA polymerase; NEB M0503L); 18 cycles
  IR abstraction: mix 18m (1080.0 SECOND in IR; cycle count not supported by compiler)

Step 8 | CTSL Detection by ddPCR
  Module      : ddPCRQuantification
  Duration    : 30 s detection window
  Expected    : 54-fold above vehicle-only control (Cat-Bio vs DMSO; Fig. 1B; n=2)
  QC gate     : ctslSignal > 0 -> dispose (BB2); ctslSignal <= 0 -> drain (BB3)

Step 9 | NCEH1 Specificity Validation: JW480 Pre-Treatment
  Cells       : SKOV3; JW480 2 uM pre-treatment 30 min at 37 C (1800 s)
  Probe       : FP-Bio 2 uM, 30 min at 37 C (1800 s)
  On-chip     : Full scADPL workflow (trap -> lyse -> barcode -> ligate -> preamplify)
  Module      : qPCRQuantification (selected over ddPCR from this step forward;
                higher SNR; amenable to multiplexing)
  Expected    : >90% NCEH1-specific signal suppression vs uninhibited control;
                no significant effect on other five Ag-6 targets (Fig. 1C, Fig. 2B)
  QC gate     : nceh1Signal > 0 -> dispose (BB5); nceh1Signal <= 0 -> drain (BB6)


PHASE 2 | Multiplexed Ag-6 Panel (SKOV3, n=8 single cells per condition)

Step 10 | Dual-Probe Pulse Labelling
  Cells       : SKOV3; FP-Bio 2 uM 30 min at 37 C; then Cat-Bio 5 uM added,
                additional 90 min at 37 C (both probes present for final 30 min overlap)
  IR          : labelledFP_Ag6 heat 1800 s; labelledDual heat 5400 s at 37 C

Step 11 | On-Chip Multiplexed scADPL
  Same chamber-by-chamber workflow as Steps 3-7 above.
  Six orthogonal Taqman barcode channels in forward primer sequences enable
  simultaneous target-specific qPCR quantification from the same single-cell lysate.
  All six measurements per isolated cell (n=8 cells; Fig. 2A).

Step 12 | Six-Channel qPCR Quantification
  Instrument  : CFX384 Real-Time System (Bio-Rad); 384-well plates
  Mix         : Luna Universal Probe qPCR Master Mix; 0.9 uM primers, 0.45 uM Taqman probe
  Module      : qPCRQuantification; 30 s detection window
  Expected fold-changes vs no-probe DMSO:
    NCEH1 : >20-fold   MGLL : >20-fold   CTSL : >20-fold
    FAAH  : detectable  CTSB : detectable  uPA  : detectable
  QC gate : ag6Signal > 0 -> dispose (BB8); ag6Signal <= 0 -> drain (BB9)


PHASE 3 | Cell-Line Heterogeneity Profiling

Step 13 | Dual-Probe Labelling of HEK293T and OVCAR3
  HEK293T and OVCAR3 each labelled identically to Step 10.
  Processed on separate chip runs; n > 10 single cells per target per cell line.

Step 14 | On-Chip scADPL for HEK293T and OVCAR3
  Full scADPL workflow (Steps 3-7) for each cell line independently.

Step 15 | qPCR + Fluorescence Imaging Readout; PCA Analysis
  Module      : fluorescenceImaging (abstracts PCA + heatmap analysis; 30 s)
  Normalisation:
    Fig. 3A   : Activity normalised to HEK293T reference population
    Fig. 3B   : Activity normalised to OVCAR3 reference population
    Both      : RPE internal control per cell
  Results:
    SKOV3 vs HEK293T : All six Ag-6 targets significantly higher in SKOV3
                       (p <= 0.0001 to 0.03; Fig. 3A)
    SKOV3 vs OVCAR3  : Five of six targets significant; NCEH1 highest fold-change (Fig. 3B)
    mRNA vs activity : FAAH and CTSB show discordant mRNA vs protein activity profiles
                       (Fig. 3C; Human Protein Atlas mRNA data)
    PCA              : SKOV3 vs OVCAR3 resolved; PC1 = 84.67%, PC2 = 8.37% (Fig. 3F)
    Heatmaps         : Per-cell Z-score activity profiles reveal intra-population
                       heterogeneity across all six Ag-6 targets (Fig. 3D/E)
  QC gate : heteroSignal > 0 -> dispose (BB11); heteroSignal <= 0 -> drain (BB12)


PHASE 4 | Patient-Derived Organoid Profiling

Step 16 | PDO Preparation and Anti-CD45-FITC Immune Cell Staining
  Protocol    : IRB 16352A; fresh core biopsy or pleural effusion specimens
                enzymatically digested (1 h for biopsy) or centrifuged (450g, 10 min
                for pleural effusion); Matrigel 24-well culture to 50-100 mm;
                Dispase 37 C 20 min -> TrypLE 37 C 5-10 min -> 2% FBS stop ->
                40 mm strainer -> 450g 5 min -> 500 uL BC PDO media on ice
  Staining    : FITC-conjugated anti-CD45 antibody; 30 min on ice (4 C, 1800 s)
  Purpose     : CD45+ immune cells identified by on-chip FITC imaging and excluded
                from scADPL analysis; only CD45-FITC-negative tumour cells processed
                (fig. S6 in paper)

Step 17 | Dual-Probe Labelling of PDO Single-Cell Suspension
  Same as Step 10: FP-Bio 30 min at 37 C (1800 s);
  Cat-Bio added, 90 min at 37 C (5400 s)

Step 18 | On-Chip Trapping with Tumour-Cell Imaging Gate
  Trap        : mix 2 s (hydrodynamic capture)
  Imaging QC  : detect fluorescenceImaging 10 s; confirms FITC-negative (tumour) cell
                in chamber before proceeding to lysis

Step 19 | On-Chip scADPL for PDO Tumour Single Cells
  Full scADPL workflow: lyse 60 s -> RPE spike 5 s -> barcode 7200 s at 25 C ->
  ligate 2700 s at 40 C -> preamplify 1080 s

Step 20 | Ag-6 qPCR on PDO Single Cells
  Module      : qPCRQuantification; 30 s
  Normalisation: Z-scores calculated within each target, normalised to:
    TNBC      : PDO1 (primary tumour reference)
    ER+       : Lymph node metastasis reference
    Both      : RPE spike-in per cell
  Results:
    TNBC PDOs : Higher Ag-6 in all metastatic vs primary tumours;
                highest activity in liver metastases (PDO3, PDO4; Fig. 4C)
    ER+ PDOs  : Highest Ag-6 in pleural effusion cells, concordant with MDA-MB-231
                (pleural-derived cell line); left pleural (early stage) shows greater
                intertarget heterogeneity and elevated CTSL; right pleural (later stage)
                shows general Ag-6 increase, decreased variability; lymph node shows
                general decrease in Ag-6 activity (Fig. 4D/E)
    scADPL vs bulk sADPL: concordant in ER+ PDO samples (Fig. 4D)
    General model: Ag-6 activity peaks in cells undergoing EMT or early metastasis;
                   slightly decreases in established metastatic lesions (Fig. 4F)
  QC gate : pdoSignal > 0 -> dispose (BB14, pdoWithQPCR + pdoTumourSignal);
            pdoSignal <= 0 -> drain (BB15)
  Terminal  : dispose(pdoSignal) -> BB16 (NOP; experiment ends)


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : smitha_pillai_scadpl_breast_cancer.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 16 basic blocks (BB1-BB16), 4 if/else gates, 20 CFG edges; terminal NOP
DAG file       : smitha_pillai_scadpl_breast_cancer_main_dag.dot

Duration unit conversions (BioScript supports s and m only):
  Cat-Bio labelling 2 h          -> 120m   -> IR: 7200.0 SECOND
  FP-Bio labelling 30 min        -> 30m    -> IR: 1800.0 SECOND
  JW480 pre-treatment 30 min     -> 30m    -> IR: 1800.0 SECOND
  Barcoding incubation 2 h       -> 120m   -> IR: 7200.0 SECOND (as mix duration, then heat)
  Proximity ligation 45 min      -> 45m    -> IR: 2700.0 SECOND
  Preamplification 18 cycles     -> 18m    -> IR: 1080.0 SECOND (time abstraction; not cycles)
  Cat-Bio overlap addition 90min -> 90m    -> IR: 5400.0 SECOND
  Anti-CD45 staining 30 min ice  -> 30m    -> IR: 1800.0 SECOND (at 4 C)

Modules declared:
  scADPLSignalDetection, ddPCRQuantification, qPCRQuantification, fluorescenceImaging

Manifests (20 total):
  PBS, PluronicF127, MCPLysisBuffer, MCF7_Cells, SKOV3_Cells, OVCAR3_Cells,
  HEK293T_Cells, MDA_MB_231_Cells, PatientDerivedOrganoids, CatBio_Probe,
  FPBio_Probe, StrepAvidin_OligoConjugate, AntiBody_OligoConjugate,
  SplintOligonucleotide, LigationBuffer, PreamplificationMix, qPCR_MasterMix,
  JW480_Inhibitor, FITC_AntiCD45_Antibody, RPhycoerythrin_Spike

Compiler notes:
  - drain vs dispose in IR: BioScript compiler emits both as identical sink operations
    in the IR; semantic distinction (waste channel vs. safe disposal) applies only at
    the physical execution layer
  - Preamplification abstraction: 18m encodes the 18-cycle PCR step as time; the
    BioScript compiler does not support cycle count as an operation parameter
  - Single-cell trap abstraction: `mix @ 2.0 SECOND` in IR represents pressure-driven
    hydrodynamic single-cell capture in Chamber II, not DMF electrode-mediated mixing
  - MCF7_Cells and MDA_MB_231_Cells are declared in manifest for biological completeness
    (referenced in paper but not directly dispensed in this .bs; TNBC cell-line activity
    reported via bulk sADPL in paper Fig. 4B, not encoded as separate scADPL phases here)
  - preamplifiedFPBio variable compiled in IR (Phase 1 FP-Bio arm) but its downstream
    qPCR step is encoded within the NCEH1/JW480 QC branch (BB4); the uninhibited FP-Bio
    signal serves as the reference for the >90% inhibition comparison off-chip

protocol.title: Single-Cell Chemoproteomics Identifies Metastatic Activity Signatures in Breast Cancer
protocol.platform: Single-Cell Activity-Dependent Proximity Ligation (scADPL) coupled to valve-based push-up PDMS microfluidic chip
cell_lines: Patient-Derived Organoids (PDOs) from TNBC primary and metastatic tumors, and ER+ pleural effusion/lymph node
protocol.objective: Automated microfluidic single-cell isolation and on-chip sADPL processing for multiplexed endogenous protein activity measurements at single-cell resolution; identification of a six-enzyme cancer-aggressiveness activity signature (Ag-6) correlated with metastatic breast cancer progression

device.configuration: push-up (fluidic layer thick, bonded on top of thin control layer, bonded to glass slide)
layers: Fluidic layer: ~72 g PDMS (10:1 base:curing agent); photoresist heights 18 mm AZ40XT (dome valve), 22 mm SU-8-3025, 70 mm SU-8-3025 (double-coated)
Control layer: 11 g PDMS (10:1); spun at 448g for 1 min; bonded to glass slide
Glass slide: 127.76 x 85.48 x 1 mm; bonded with air plasma 45 s at 800 mtorr
chamber_zones_per_assay_unit: II  - Single-cell trapping chamber (8 um constriction)
III - Cell lysis chamber (MCP lysis buffer + RPE spike-in)
IV  - Proximity barcoding element incubation (whole proteome; SA-oligo + ab-oligo)
V   - Proximity barcode ligation (splint oligo + Ampligase)

bonding.fluidic_to_control_layer: oxygen plasma 18 s at 860 mtorr (Harrick Plasma); incubated 80 C overnight
bonding.assembly_to_glass: air plasma 45 s at 800 mtorr; incubated 80 C overnight

CatBio.notes: Biotin-tagged; probe-protein complex detected via streptavidin-oligo conjugate in ADPL

FPBio.notes: Fluorophosphonate biotin; covalently labels active-site serine of hydrolases

JW480.selectivity: >90% NCEH1 signal inhibition; no significant effect on other Ag-6 targets
JW480.purpose: Confirm target specificity of NCEH1 scADPL signal (Fig. 1C, Fig. 2B)

StrepAvidin_OligoConjugate.role: Recognises biotin tag on probe-protein complex (one anchor of proximity ligation pair)

AntiBody_OligoConjugate.role: Target-specific recognition element (second anchor); six antibody-oligo conjugates in Ag-6 multiplex

SplintOligonucleotide.role: Bridges SA-oligo and ab-oligo when both are bound to the same probe-protein complex

LigationBuffer.composition: 0.05 U Ampligase, 0.3 mM NAD+, 10 mM DTT, 20 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.3, 50 mM KCl, 1.5 mM MgCl2

lysis_buffer.name: MCP lysis buffer
lysis_buffer.composition: 25 mM Tris pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA, 1 mM EGTA, 0.5% Triton X-100, 0.5% sodium deoxycholate
lysis_buffer.notes: Selected after optimization against Pierce, CST, TM buffers (fig. S2)

spike_in_control.name: R-phycoerythrin (RPE)
spike_in_control.role: Inter-cell normalisation; added at lysis step; cells with RPE values >2 SD from mean excluded as outliers

preamplification.composition: 2.5x buffer, 100 nM primers, 200 uM dNTPs, 9 U Phusion high-fidelity DNA polymerase (NEB M0503L)

qpcr.master_mix: Luna Universal Probe qPCR Master Mix (NEB M3004E)
qpcr.normalisation: RPE spike-in control; values normalised to PBS (simple) or RPE (complex experiments)

ddpcr.notes: ddPCR showed lower SNR vs qPCR for NCEH1 (fig. S2); qPCR selected for all subsequent multiplexing

pdo_media.bc_pdo_media: BC PDO media (ref. 49: Sachs et al., Cell 2018)
pdo_media.dissociation: Dispase 37 C 20 min; TrypLE 37 C 5-10 min; 2% FBS stop; 40 mm cell strainer; centrifuge 450g 5 min
pdo_media.loading_suspension: 500 uL BC PDO media, kept on ice
pdo_media.conditioned_media_for_pdo: PBS + 2% FBS; anti-CD45-FITC staining 30 min on ice before loading

cell_prep_for_chip.pdo_immune_cell_filter: FITC-conjugated anti-CD45 antibody (30 min on ice); CD45+ cells excluded by on-chip FITC imaging

ag6_panel.description: Six-enzyme aggressiveness panel with established ties to cancer cell aggressiveness

phases.name: Single-plex validation: CTSL (ddPCR) and NCEH1 with JW480 inhibitor (qPCR)

steps.name: Device priming
steps.notes: 2% Pluronics F-127 in PBS to passivate PDMS surfaces and reduce non-specific cell adhesion

steps.name: Off-chip Cat-Bio probe labelling of SKOV3 cells
steps.notes: 5 uM Cat-Bio, 2 h (7200 s), 37 C in DMEM-F12 + 10% FBS; labels CTSL and CTSB

steps.name: Off-chip FP-Bio probe labelling of SKOV3 cells
steps.notes: 2 uM FP-Bio, 30 min (1800 s), 37 C; labels NCEH1, MGLL, FAAH, uPA

steps.name: On-chip single-cell trapping (Chamber II)

steps.name: On-chip cell lysis (Chamber III)

steps.name: On-chip proximity barcoding (Chamber IV)

steps.name: On-chip proximity ligation (Chamber V)

steps.name: Off-chip amplicon retrieval and preamplification

steps.notes: Flushed with 9 uL water; preamplified in 11 uL (2.5x buffer, 100 nM primers, 200 uM dNTPs, 9 U Phusion); 18 cycles

steps.name: CTSL detection by ddPCR
steps.expected_result: 54-fold above vehicle-only control (Fig. 1B; n=2 biological replicates)

steps.name: NCEH1 inhibitor specificity QC: JW480 pre-treatment + FP-Bio + on-chip scADPL
steps.expected_result: >90% NCEH1 signal suppression vs uninhibited; no significant effect on other targets (Fig. 1C, 2B)
steps.notes: qPCR selected over ddPCR from this step forward: higher SNR, amenable to multiplexing (fig. S2)

phases.name: Multiplexed Ag-6 panel profiling in SKOV3 single cells

steps.name: Dual-probe pulse labelling (Cat-Bio + FP-Bio simultaneously)
steps.notes: FP-Bio (30 min) then Cat-Bio added for remaining 90 min; both probes present during final 30 min overlap

steps.name: On-chip single-cell scADPL: trap, lyse, barcode, ligate, preamplify
steps.notes: Six orthogonal Taqman barcode channels enable simultaneous qPCR quantification from same single-cell lysate

phases.name: Heterogeneity profiling: HEK293T vs SKOV3; SKOV3 vs OVCAR3

steps.name: Dual-probe labelling of HEK293T and OVCAR3 cells
steps.operation: sequential mix-heat for each cell line

steps.name: On-chip scADPL for HEK293T and OVCAR3 (separate chip runs)
qPCR + fluorescence imaging readout; PCA dimensional reduction

expected_results.SKOV3_vs_HEK293T: All six Ag-6 targets significantly higher in SKOV3 (p <= 0.0001 to 0.03; Fig. 3A)
expected_results.SKOV3_vs_OVCAR3: Five of six targets significantly higher in SKOV3; NCEH1 highest change (Fig. 3B)
expected_results.PCA: SKOV3 vs OVCAR3 resolved at PC1 = 84.67%, PC2 = 8.37% (Fig. 3F)
expected_results.mRNA_vs_activity: FAAH and CTSB show discordant mRNA vs protein activity profiles (Fig. 3C)

steps.normalisation: Activity normalised to HEK293T (Fig. 3A) or OVCAR3 (Fig. 3B) as reference population; RPE internal control

phases.name: Patient-Derived Organoid (PDO) profiling: TNBC between-patient and ER+ within-patient

ER_plus_within_patient.notes: Left pleural effusion: early metastasis detection stage; greater intertarget heterogeneity and elevated CTSL. Right pleural effusion: later stage; general Ag-6 increase, decreased variability. Lymph node: general decrease in Ag-6 activity vs pleural effusions.

steps.name: PDO preparation and anti-CD45-FITC staining for immune cell exclusion
steps.notes: Anti-CD45-FITC staining 30 min on ice; CD45+ immune cells identified and excluded during on-chip brightfield + FITC imaging (fig. S6); PDOs dissociated via Dispase + TrypLE prior to loading

steps.name: Dual-probe labelling of PDO single-cell suspension
On-chip trapping with on-chip tumour cell imaging QC (FITC-negative gate)

steps.notes: Only CD45-FITC-negative (tumour) cells proceed to lysis and barcoding

steps.name: On-chip scADPL for PDO tumour single cells: lyse, barcode, ligate, preamplify
steps.normalisation: Normalised to RPE spike-in per cell; Z-scores calculated within each target relative to PDO1 (TNBC) or Lymph met (ER+)

steps.name: Ag-6 qPCR quantification on PDO single cells

expected_results.TNBC_PDOs: Higher Ag-6 in all metastatic vs primary tumor PDOs; highest in liver metastases (Fig. 4C)
expected_results.ER_plus_PDOs: Highest Ag-6 in pleural effusion cells; concordant with MDA-MB-231 (pleural-derived cell line) (Fig. 4D/E)
expected_results.general_trend: Ag-6 activity peaks during EMT / early metastasis; slightly decreases in established metastatic lesions (Fig. 4F)
