description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : High-throughput co-culture system for analysis of spatiotemporal cell-cell signaling
Source Link  : https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0956566323000313
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bios.2023.115089
Journal      : Biosensors and Bioelectronics, 2023, Article 115089
Authors      : Minjun Son, Andrew G. Wang, Emma Kenna, Savas Tay
Platform     : Two-layer PDMS microfluidics with pneumatic valve control; 192-chamber high-throughput array


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes an automated high-throughput microfluidic co-culture system for
spatiotemporal study of cell-cell signaling. The device enables: (i) chemical stimulation
of sentinel macrophages to initiate cytokine secretion, (ii) formation of diffusion-mediated
cytokine gradients over a receiving fibroblast population, (iii) live single-cell NF-kB
translocation imaging across 192 chambers, (iv) spatially resolved cell retrieval from
near/mid/far regions of the receiving chamber, and (v) downstream gene expression
quantification by RT-qPCR or RNA sequencing.

Two experimental arms are encoded in a single .bs file:
  ARM 1 (main, BB1-BB10): LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages as cytokine source in
                           pre-chamber; paracrine signaling to RelA-DsRed NIH3T3 fibroblasts
                           in receiving chamber.
  ARM 2 (supplemental, BB10-BB16): Fixed-dose 30 ng/mL TNF-a loaded directly into
                                    pre-chamber; no macrophages; controlled distance-dependent
                                    gene expression model. Continues as sequential continuation
                                    from BB10; compiler assigns BB10-BB16.

The protocol reproduces the key experimental conditions of Sections 3.2-3.5 of the paper,
covering macrophage-to-fibroblast paracrine signaling, distance-dependent NF-kB dynamics,
spatially resolved gene expression (Tnfaip3/A20, Casp4, Ccl5/RANTES, GAPDH), and
spatial distribution of sentinel cell density effects on population-level response.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Fabrication : Two-layer PDMS soft lithography; AutoCAD design; bonded to
              127.8 x 85.5 x 1 mm glass substrate (Marienfeld); oxygen plasma (Harrick PDC-001).

Layer 1 (fluid) : Thin PDMS ~50 um height; spun at 2300 RPM from ~10 g mixture on
                  chlorotrimethylsilane-treated fluid mold; contains cell chambers and channels.

Layer 2 (control): Thick PDMS slab; pneumatic valve features; aligned to fluid layer
                   using custom stereomicroscope with XYZ translation stage.

Array format  : 192 chambers in 8x24 arrangement; 96 independently controllable row-column pairs.
                Each unit: small pre-chamber (source) + large receiving chamber.

Receiving chamber: Partitioned into 3 regions (near / mid / far) by pneumatic partitioning valves.
                   Forest of pillars between chamber bottom and sink channel.
                   Cell retrieval side channels (1 per region) lead to dedicated outlets.

Sink channel  : Flushed by gentle peristaltic pumping; provides shear-free cytokine removal;
                mimics capillary clearance of secreted cytokines (Kumar et al., 2019).

Valves        : 88 solenoid-controlled inputs (Festo 197334, Tygon tubes Cole-Parmer ND-100-80).
Control GUI   : Custom Matlab GUI (Gomez-Sjoberg et al., 2010); pre-written scripts for automation.
Imaging       : Nikon Ti2 epifluorescence microscope; temperature/CO2/humidity-controlled enclosure.


CELL LINES
----------
- RelA-/- RelA-DsRed NIH3T3 mouse embryonic fibroblasts (3T3s):
  Receiving chamber cells. NF-kB translocation tracked via nuclear DsRed signal.
  Media: DMEM high glucose (Gibco) + 10% FBS (Omega Scientific) + 2 mM GlutaMAX (Gibco)
         + 1% penicillin/streptomycin (Lonza).
  Loading concentration: 5e5 cells/mL; target ~70% confluency (200-400 cells/chamber).

- RelA-GFP RAW264.7 macrophage-like cells:
  Pre-chamber sentinel cells. NF-kB tracked via GFP.
  Stimulated with 50 ng/mL LPS (InvivoGen, tlrl-3pelps) for 10 min in pre-chamber.

- Primary murine adult fibroblasts (RelA-YFP knock-in mouse):
  Used in cell-patterning experiments (Section 3.5, Fig. 5).

- Bone-marrow-derived macrophages (BMMΦ, RelA-YFP knock-in mouse):
  Used in cell-patterning experiments (Section 3.5, Fig. 5).


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Device Priming and Chamber Coating (Fibronectin)
  Reagents    : Fibronectin (Sigma-Aldrich FC010), PBS, DMEM high glucose
  Operation   : Fibronectin loaded through inlet channels into receiving chambers
  Temperature : 25 C (room temperature)
  Duration    : 30 min (1800 s in IR)
  Wash        : Fresh DMEM flowed through chambers to remove unbound fibronectin
  Purpose     : Promotes fibroblast attachment to glass substrate

Step 2 | RelA-DsRed 3T3 Fibroblast Loading into Receiving Chambers
  Cell line       : RelA-/- RelA-DsRed NIH3T3
  Concentration   : 5e5 cells/mL in complete DMEM
  Target loading  : ~70% confluency, 200-400 cells per chamber
  Operation       : Valve-directed flow through cell loading channel (abstracted as mix in BioScript)
  Adhesion        : 37 C / 5% CO2 for 4-6 h (300 min nominal; 18000 s in IR)
  Notes           : Cells spread evenly before macrophage loading; adhesion verified visually

Step 3 | Hoechst 33342 Nuclear Staining (Optional)
  Reagent         : 1 uM Hoechst 33342
  Incubation      : 10 min at 37 C (600 s in IR)
  Purpose         : Enables nucleus tracking during live-cell epifluorescence imaging
  Notes           : Applied selectively; performed before macrophage loading

Step 4 | RelA-GFP RAW264.7 Macrophage Loading into Pre-Chamber
  Cell line       : RelA-GFP RAW264.7
  Cell number     : 10-100 per pre-chamber; controlled-density experiments use 60 +/- 15
  Suspension      : DMEM high glucose
  Operation       : Flow through source channel; separator valve CLOSED during loading
  Settling        : 30 min at 37 C (1800 s in IR)
  Notes           : Pre-chamber and receiving chamber remain separated by closed separator valve

Step 5 | LPS Stimulation of Macrophages and Wash
  LPS             : 50 ng/mL (InvivoGen tlrl-3pelps)
  Stimulus duration: 10 min (600 s in IR); separator valve CLOSED
  Wash            : Fresh DMEM flowed through pre-chamber to remove LPS before separator opens
  Purpose         : Activates canonical NF-kB via TLR4; triggers TNF-a and cytokine secretion
  Notes           : LPS washed out to prevent direct fibroblast activation by LPS

Step 6 | Separator Valve Opening and Cytokine Gradient Formation
  Operation       : Separator valve opened; peristaltic sink pumping initiated simultaneously
  Tracer (QC)     : Cyanine 5 (Cy5) used to characterise gradient formation kinetics
  Gradient duration: 400 min (24000 s in IR); near region rises by 30 min; full equilibration ~400 min
  Sink pumping    : Gentle peristaltic; removes cytokines at far end; maintains gradient
  Detection       : gradientDetection module; 10 s
  QC gate (BB1->BB2/BB3): gradientSignal > 0 -> dispose(gradientChamber) [BB2];
                           gradientSignal <= 0 -> mix waste + drain [BB3]

Step 7 | Live-Cell NF-kB Translocation Imaging
  Duration        : 200 min (12000 s in IR) post separator opening
  Temperature     : 37 C / 5% CO2 / humidity controlled
  Quantification  : Nucleus/cytosol RelA-DsRed ratio per 3T3 (Kudo et al., 2018)
  Detection       : nfkbTranslocationDetection module; 30 s
  Notes (BB4)     : sinkFlow and gradientJoin are two distinct FreshMedium dispenses;
                    mixed to form imagingChamber (FIX4)
  Findings        : Signaling range correlates with macrophage number; buffered at ~60 macrophages;
                    near cells: rapid strong NF-kB then rapid decay;
                    far cells: slower, lower amplitude, more heterogeneous oscillatory response
  QC gate (BB4->BB5/BB6): nfkbSignal > 0 -> dispose(imagingChamber) [BB5];
                           nfkbSignal <= 0 -> mix waste + drain [BB6]

Step 8 | Spatially Resolved Cell Retrieval (Near / Mid / Far)
  TrypLE flow     : ~10 s (Gibco TrypLE)
  TrypLE incubation: ~60 s (partitioning valves closed before full detachment)
  Total detachment: 70 s (70 s mix duration in BioScript)
  Partitioning    : Pneumatic partitioning valves closed to isolate near / mid / far regions
  PBS retrieval   : Rapidly flowed through cell retrieval side channels to outlet
  Collection      : ~100 cells per region collected as ~2 uL droplet at outlet
  Lysis           : Deposited into 10 uL ice-cold lysis buffer (0.1% Triton-X-100 + RNase inhibitor, Takara)
  Storage         : Biological intent: -80 C long-term cryostorage
                    IR output (v2): heat @ 4.0CELSIUS @ 57600.0SECOND (FIX1; see compiler notes)
  Timepoints      : 0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 h post separator opening; triplicate at each
  Detection       : geneExpressionDetection module on nearLysate; 30 s
  QC gate (BB7->BB8/BB9): geneExprSignal > 0 -> dispose lysates [BB8];
                           geneExprSignal <= 0 -> mix waste per region + drain [BB9]

Step 9 | Downstream qPCR Gene Expression Quantification
  Pipeline        : SmartSeq2 reverse transcription + pre-amplification (Picelli et al., 2014)
  Genes           : Tnfaip3 (A20), Casp4, Ccl5 (RANTES), GAPDH (control)
  Replicates      : Triplicate per timepoint per region
  Normalisation   : Each gene level normalised to maximum across all samples
  Simulation      : NF-kB dynamics input to ODE; degradation rate varied 20-fold (Fig. 4C);
                    degradation rate explains distance-dependent patterns


SUPPLEMENTAL ARM: Fixed-Dose TNF-a Stimulation (Section 3.4, Fig. 4)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
CFG blocks      : BB10 (entry/join from main arm) -> BB11/BB12 -> BB13 -> BB14/BB15 -> BB16 (terminal)
Rationale       : Macrophage variability (Fig. 3C) prevents reproducible NF-kB profiles across
                  samples; fixed TNF-a eliminates this variability
TNF-a dose      : 30 ng/mL (R&D Systems, aa80-235); loaded directly into pre-chamber; no macrophages
Imaging window  : 8 h (480 min; 28800 s in IR)
Retrieval       : Identical TrypLE / PBS / lysis protocol as main arm; heat at 4c for 960m (FIX1)
Timepoints      : 0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 h post separator opening; triplicate
Key finding     : Tnfaip3 peaks 60 min (near) vs 120 min (mid/far);
                  Ccl5 and Casp4 peak 4-6 h with similar magnitude at all positions;
                  degradation rate determines distance sensitivity of NF-kB target gene expression


CELL PATTERNING ARM: Spatial Distribution of Sentinel Cells (Section 3.5, Fig. 5)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Cell lines      : Primary murine adult fibroblasts (RelA-YFP) + BMMΦ (RelA-YFP knock-in mouse)
LPS dose        : 3 ng/mL; sub-threshold for direct fibroblast activation
Patterning      : Macrophages loaded at near (0-0.5 mm) or mid (1-1.5 mm) position via side channels
Finding         : Near-position loading -> strong local fibroblast activation, weak at far;
                  Mid-position loading -> more uniform population-level response, weaker absolute
                  activation; spatial distribution of sentinel cells determines population response


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file   : son2023_coculture_spatiotemporal_v2.bs
Compiler         : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output        : son2023_coculture_spatiotemporal_v2.ir
DOT output       : son2023_coculture_spatiotemporal_v2_main_dag.dot
CFG structure    : 16 basic blocks (BB1-BB16); 4 if/else QC gates
                   Main arm:         BB1-BB10  (3 gates: gradient, NF-kB, gene expression)
                   Supplemental arm: BB10-BB16 (1 gate: imagingChamber QC + 1 gate: lysate QC)
                   Total CFG edges:  20
Modules          : gradientDetection, nfkbTranslocationDetection, geneExpressionDetection,
                   viabilityDetection
Duration units   : BioScript supports s and m only; all durations converted accordingly
                   30m  -> 1800 s   (fibronectin coating, macrophage settling)
                   300m -> 18000 s  (fibroblast adhesion)
                   10m  -> 600 s    (LPS stimulation, Hoechst staining)
                   400m -> 24000 s  (gradient formation)
                   200m -> 12000 s  (NF-kB imaging, main arm)
                   480m -> 28800 s  (imaging window, TNF-a arm)
                   960m -> 57600 s  (lysate staging; biological intent: -80 C cryostorage)

V1 BUGS AND V2 FIXES (all confirmed from IR inspection):

  FIX1 | Negative temperature sign stripped
    v1 IR : heat(nearLysate1[0]) @ 80.0CELSIUS @ 57600.0SECOND  [sign dropped]
    v2 IR : heat(nearLysate1[0]) @ 4.0CELSIUS @ 57600.0SECOND   [correct]
    fix   : `heat at -80c` replaced with `heat at 4c for 960m`
            Biological intent (-80 C long-term cryostorage) noted in .bs comment

  FIX2 | False branches emitted dispose() instead of drain()
    v1 IR : bsbbif_3_f: dispose(gradientChamber1[0])
    v2 IR : bsbbif_3_f: gradientWaste1[0] = mix(gradientChamber1[0], washBuffer21[0]);
                         dispose(gradientWaste1[0])
    fix   : Explicit waste variable in false branch; semantic drain intent preserved in .bs source

  FIX3 | Dead variable lysisBufferStock dispensed but never consumed
    v1 IR : lysisBufferStock1[0] = dispense(LysisBuffer)  [orphaned, never used in mix]
    v2 IR : variable removed entirely
    fix   : Removed standalone dispense; per-region lysis variables (lysisNear, lysisMid,
            lysisFar) are dispensed inline where consumed

  FIX4 | Self-mix in imagingChamber (same variable both operands)
    v1 IR : imagingChamber1[0] = mix(freshMediumFlow1[0], freshMediumFlow1[0])
    v2 IR : imagingChamber1[0] = mix(sinkFlow1[0], gradientJoin1[0])
    fix   : Two distinct FreshMedium dispenses (sinkFlow, gradientJoin) used as operands

REMAINING LIMITATION:
  drain() has no dedicated opcode in lilott8/BioScript IR; all drain() calls compile to
  dispose() on the waste variable. The waste variable pattern (FIX2) preserves semantic
  intent in .bs source even though the IR output is structurally identical to dispose().

protocol.title: High-throughput co-culture system for analysis of spatiotemporal cell-cell signaling
protocol.platform: Two-layer PDMS microfluidics (pneumatic valve control, 192-chamber array)
cell_lines: RelA-/- RelA-DsRed NIH3T3 mouse embryonic fibroblasts (3T3s)
Primary murine adult fibroblasts (RelA-YFP knock-in mouse)
protocol.objective: Automated high-throughput spatiotemporal co-culture platform enabling macrophage stimulation, cytokine gradient formation, live NF-kB single-cell imaging, spatially resolved cell retrieval, and downstream gene expression quantification at 192-chamber scale

device.fabrication: Conventional soft lithography; two-layer PDMS bonded to glass substrate (127.8 x 85.5 x 1 mm, Marienfeld); oxygen plasma bonding (Harrick, PDC-001)
layers: Fluid layer: thin PDMS ~50 um height, spun at 2300 RPM from ~10 g mixture on fluid mold pretreated with chlorotrimethylsilane
Control layer: thick PDMS slab with pneumatic valve features; aligned to fluid layer under custom stereomicroscope with XYZ translation stage

chambers.unit_structure: Pre-chamber (source) + receiving chamber partitioned into near/mid/far regions

valves.actuation: Solenoid valves (Festo, 197334) via Tygon tubes (Cole-Parmer, ND-100-80)

sink_channel.location: Bottom of receiving chamber, separated by pillar forest
sink_channel.function: Peristaltic pumping removes cytokines at far end; mimics capillary clearance
sink_channel.pumping: Gentle peristaltic; shear-free across multiple chambers simultaneously

imaging.environmental_control: Temperature, CO2, and humidity controlled enclosure
imaging.nfkb_quantification: Nucleus/cytosol DsRed intensity ratio per cell (Kudo et al., 2018 method)

reagents.fibroblast_media: DMEM high glucose (Gibco) + 10% FBS (Omega Scientific) + 2 mM GlutaMAX (Gibco) + 1% penicillin/streptomycin (Lonza)
reagents.fibronectin: Sigma-Aldrich FC010; chamber coating prior to cell loading
reagents.lps_high_dose: 50 ng/mL LPS (InvivoGen, tlrl-3pelps); macrophage stimulation in pre-chamber, 10 min
reagents.lps_low_dose: 3 ng/mL LPS; used in cell-patterning experiments (subthreshold for direct fibroblast activation)
reagents.tnf_alpha: 30 ng/mL TNF-a (R&D Systems, aa80-235); loaded directly into pre-chamber for fixed-dose arm
reagents.hoechst: 1 uM Hoechst 33342; nuclear tracking during live-cell imaging
reagents.trypsin: TrypLE (Gibco); cell detachment for retrieval (~10 s flow, ~60 s incubation)
reagents.pbs: Gibco; retrieval wash and channel flush
reagents.lysis_buffer: 10 uL ice-cold; 0.1% Triton-X-100 + RNase inhibitor (Takara); cells collected as ~2 uL droplet
reagents.cy5_tracer: Cyanine 5 (Cy5); used to characterise gradient formation kinetics (Fig. 2C)
reagents.smartseq2_reagents: Reverse transcription and pre-amplification per Picelli et al. 2014 pipeline

qpcr_genes.Tnfaip3_A20: Early NF-kB target gene; fast degradation; peaks 60 min (near) / 120 min (mid/far)
qpcr_genes.Casp4: Late NF-kB target gene; slow degradation; peaks 4-6 h; similar magnitude across positions
qpcr_genes.Ccl5_RANTES: Late NF-kB target gene; slow degradation; gradual rise; highest at mid in macrophage arm

steps.name: Chamber coating with fibronectin
steps.notes: Fibronectin loaded through inlet channels into 192 receiving chambers; incubated 30 min at RT; washed with fresh DMEM to remove unbound fibronectin before cell loading

steps.name: RelA-DsRed 3T3 fibroblast loading into receiving chambers
steps.suspension_buffer: DMEM high glucose + 10% FBS + 2 mM GlutaMAX + 1% pen/strep
steps.operation: flow-through cell loading channel (abstracted as mix in BioScript)
steps.notes: Loaded at ~70% confluency for sufficient single-cell data without significant overlap; 5 h adhesion at 37 C / 5% CO2 (midpoint of 4-6 h window)

steps.name: Hoechst 33342 nuclear staining (optional)
steps.notes: Performed selectively for nucleus tracking in live-cell epifluorescence imaging; 10 min at 37 C

steps.name: RelA-GFP RAW264.7 macrophage loading into pre-chamber
steps.operation: flow through source channel into pre-chamber (separator valve CLOSED)
steps.notes: Separator valve between pre-chamber and receiving chamber remains closed during loading; macrophages allowed to settle 30 min at 37 C before LPS stimulation

steps.name: LPS stimulation of macrophages and pre-chamber wash
steps.operation: mix (valve-directed flow into pre-chamber, separator CLOSED)
steps.wash: Fresh DMEM flowed through pre-chamber after LPS removal
steps.notes: LPS activates canonical NF-kB in RAW macrophages via TLR4; macrophages secrete TNF-a and other cytokines; LPS washed out before separator opens to prevent direct fibroblast LPS exposure

steps.name: Separator valve opening and cytokine gradient formation
steps.operation: open separator valve + initiate peristaltic sink pumping

gradient_kinetics.cy5_characterisation: Fig. 2C; heatmap shows spatial fluorescence decay from source to sink over time

steps.notes: Sink channel flushed by peristaltic pumping establishes and maintains diffusion gradient; mimics capillary clearance. Cy5 used as surrogate tracer for gradient QC; BioScript encodes as mix abstraction of valve-directed flow.

steps.name: Live-cell NF-kB translocation imaging
steps.operation: continuous epifluorescence imaging + peristaltic sink flow
steps.quantification: Nucleus/cytosol RelA-DsRed ratio per 3T3 cell; RelA-GFP tracked in RAW macrophages

findings.signaling_range: Scales with macrophage number (Fig. 3B); buffered at high densities (~60 cells)
findings.fibroblast_heterogeneity: Wide variability in response dynamics even at matched macrophage count (~60)
findings.distance_dependence: Near cells: rapid strong NF-kB activation then rapid decay; far cells: slower, lower amplitude, more heterogeneous oscillations

steps.name: Spatially resolved cell retrieval (near / mid / far)
steps.storage_encoded_in_ir: 4.0CELSIUS @ 57600.0SECOND (heat at 4c for 960m in .bs; biological intent is -80 C long-term cryostorage; compiler cannot represent negative temperatures)
steps.procedure: TrypLE flowed 10 s; partitioning valves closed before full detachment; 60 s further incubation; PBS rapidly flowed through retrieval side channels to flush cells to outlet; collected as ~2 uL droplet; deposited into ice-cold lysis buffer; stored at -80 C

steps.name: Downstream qPCR gene expression quantification
steps.pipeline: SmartSeq2: reverse transcription + pre-amplification (Picelli et al., 2014); then qPCR
steps.normalization: Each gene level normalized to maximum across all samples
steps.simulation: NF-kB translocation dynamics used as input to ODE gene expression model; degradation rate varied 20-fold to explain distance-dependent patterns (Fig. 4C)
steps.notes: Lysates stored at -80 C until processing; suitable for qPCR or RNA sequencing

supplemental_arm.name: Fixed-dose TNF-a stimulation (Section 3.4, Fig. 4)
supplemental_arm.rationale: Remove macrophage variability; use fixed 30 ng/mL TNF-a for reproducible distance-dependent gene expression comparison across samples
supplemental_arm.difference_from_main_arm: No macrophages loaded in pre-chamber; TNF-a loaded directly; otherwise identical fibroblast loading, gradient formation, cell retrieval, and qPCR pipeline
supplemental_arm.key_finding: Tnfaip3 peaks at 60 min (near) vs 120 min (mid/far); Ccl5 and Casp4 peak at 4-6 h with similar magnitude across all positions; degradation rate determines distance sensitivity of gene expression

cell_patterning_arm.name: Spatial distribution and density of sentinel cells (Section 3.5, Fig. 5)
cell_patterning_arm.rationale: 3 ng/mL LPS is sub-threshold for direct fibroblast activation; any fibroblast NF-kB activation is paracrine (macrophage-mediated)
cell_patterning_arm.finding: Macrophages at near position: strong fibroblast activation locally, weak at far; macrophages at mid position: more uniform population-level fibroblast response but weaker absolute activation than near-position loading

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Input Dose Differentiation by NF-kB
Source Link  : https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/752394v1.full.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1101/752394
Journal      : bioRxiv preprint, September 4, 2019 (bioRxiv 752394)
Platform     : Two-layer PDMS microfluidic chip (64 independent chambers, >500 cells/chamber)
               with automated Matlab GUI valve control and live-cell fluorescence imaging


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a microfluidic live-cell analysis pipeline used to investigate how the
NF-kB signalling pathway in single mammalian cells responds to dynamically varying cytokine
concentrations. Using a multiplexed PDMS microfluidic chip, cells expressing p65-DsRed (NF-kB
reporter) and H2B-GFP (nuclear marker) are exposed to TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, or Pam2CSK4 in
precisely controlled temporal profiles: instant step increase, linear ramp, exponential ramp,
and random fluctuating order. Nuclear NF-kB localization is tracked in real time by time-lapse
fluorescence microscopy. Downstream, cells are retrieved from the chip for RT-qPCR measurement
of NF-kB target gene expression.

The central finding is that NF-kB acts as a dose differentiator: its nuclear localization
amplitude (peak height and AUC) is proportional to the logarithm of the change in cytokine
concentration, not the absolute concentration itself. This behaviour is analogous to an
electronic differentiator circuit and is described by:

    NF-kB ~ log(delta_cytokine + 1)   [for delta_cytokine > 0]

A20 and IkBa negative feedbacks are identified as the molecular mechanism providing short-term
memory of prior cytokine level, continuously resetting IKK cycling and receptor sensitivity.
The protocol also includes an A20 CRISPR/Cas9 knockout arm that experimentally confirms A20's
role, and RT-qPCR measurements showing that distinct cytokine input dynamics drive distinct
subsets of NF-kB target gene expression.

The complete experimental workflow covers device fabrication, chip priming, cell loading,
multi-arm cytokine stimulation, live-cell imaging, mathematical modelling inputs, A20 KO
cell generation, and downstream gene expression analysis.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Two-layer PDMS microfluidic chip fabricated by multilayer soft lithography:

Flow layer  : AZ40XT positive photoresist (25 um, 3400 RPM; rounded cross-section by hard-bake)
              + SU-8 3025 negative photoresist (30 um, 3000 RPM) on 4-inch silicon wafer.
Control layer: SU-8 3025 (25 um, 3500 RPM) on 4-inch silicon wafer.
Lithography : Heidelberg MLA150 maskless aligner; 375 nm laser; 280 mJ/cm2 dose.

PDMS layers:
  Flow layer  : RTV-615 (Momentive), 66 g, 10:1 monomer:catalyst; ~2 cm thick slab;
                cured 80 C >5 h; flow pattern grooved on bottom face.
  Control layer: RTV-615, 10 g; spun at 2200 RPM (~50 um thin film); cured 80 C >=1 h.

Assembly:
  1. Flow layer inputs punched.
  2. Both layers treated with oxygen plasma (Harrick PDC-001).
  3. Layers aligned under custom stereomicroscope; cured 80 C overnight for bonding.
  4. Control layer holes punched; chip bonded to 75 x 25 x 1 mm glass slide by plasma + bake.

Chamber specifications:
  - 64 independent sample chambers per chip
  - Chamber size: 3.5 x 0.8 mm
  - >500 cells per chamber
  - Minimum feature spacing: 150 um (robust bonding and alignment)

Actuation:
  - Control layer: pneumatic solenoid valves at 25-30 psi
  - Input media: pressurized at 3-4 psi through PEEK tubing (VICI, TPK.505) to prevent
    shear stress on cells during feeding
  - Automation: custom Matlab GUI; experiment scripts define feeding timing and medium
    type per chamber; greatly improves accuracy, throughput, and reproducibility

Surface coating:
  - 1:3 fibronectin (1 mg/mL) in sterile PBS; loaded into chambers overnight at room
    temperature before experiment day


CELL LINES
----------
Primary experimental cell line:
  - p65-/- 3T3 mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) expressing p65-DsRed and H2B-GFP
    Cultured: DMEM (Gibco 11965092) + 10% fetal bovine calf serum (HyClone) +
              1% GlutaMax (Gibco) + 1x penicillin-streptomycin (Gibco)
    Passaging: Trypsin-EDTA (Gibco); ~1:10 dilution every 2-3 days before 100% confluency
    Conditions: 37 C, 5% CO2
    Imaging media: FluoroBrite DMEM (Gibco A1896702) + same supplements; used during
                   experiments to reduce background fluorescence

A20 knockout cell line:
  - A20 KO MEFs: p65-/- background with p65-DsRed and H2B-GFP; A20 gene edited by
    CRISPR/Cas9 lentiviral delivery; ~90% protein knockdown by Western blot.
    Cultured and maintained under identical conditions to parental MEFs.


REAGENTS
--------
Cytokines:
  TNF-alpha     : Life Technologies, PMC3014
                  Dose range: 0 to 10 ng/mL; instant dose 10 ng/mL;
                  linear step 1 ng/mL/60 min; exponential doubling time 60 min;
                  random range 0-10 ng/mL
  IL-1beta      : R&D Systems, 401ML010CF
                  Dose range: 0 to 2.5 ng/mL; instant dose 2.5 ng/mL;
                  linear step 0.5 ng/mL/60 min; exponential doubling time 60 min
  Pam2CSK4     : InvivoGen, tlrl-pm2s (TLR2 agonist; synthetic diacylated lipopeptide)
                  Dose range: 0.2 to 12.8 ng/mL; doubling every 30 or 60 min
                  Control ligand: NF-kB dose differentiation NOT observed for Pam

Viability stains:
  FDA           : 5 ug/mL; ex 490 nm / em 526 nm; labels live cells (green)
  PI            : 2 ug/mL; ex 488 nm / em 617 nm; labels dead cells (red)

Cell lysis:
  CellsDirect Kit lysis buffer (ThermoFisher); 5 uL per sample;
  snap-frozen at -80 C immediately after retrieval

Surface coating:
  Fibronectin (1 mg/mL) in sterile PBS; 1:3 dilution; overnight room temperature

Trypsin: Trypsin-EDTA (Gibco)

All cytokine-containing media prepared immediately before experiment and kept on ice.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Fibronectin Surface Coating
  Reagents    : Fibronectin 1 mg/mL in sterile PBS (1:3 dilution)
  Operation   : Fill chambers; heat at room temperature (25 C)
  Duration    : 12 h overnight (720 min; IR: 43200.0 SECOND)
  Purpose     : Ensures cell adhesion to PDMS chamber floor before loading

Step 2 | Chamber Flush and Device Equilibration
  Reagents    : FluoroBrite DMEM + supplements
  Operation   : Pressure-driven flush (abstracted as mix); heat at 37 C
  Duration    : 60 min equilibration (IR: 3600.0 SECOND)
  Purpose     : Removes unbound fibronectin; equilibrates to 37 C / 5% CO2 / ~100% humidity

Step 3 | Cell Loading and Settling
  Cell line   : 3T3 MEF p65-DsRed / H2B-GFP
  Concentration: 5 x 10^6 cells/mL; targeting ~50% confluency (>500 cells/chamber)
  Operation   : Gravity-assisted sedimentation (abstracted as mix); heat at 37 C
  Duration    : >=60 min settling before stimulation begins (IR: 3600.0 SECOND)
  Notes       : Chambers closed after loading; cells must adhere firmly

Step 4 | Baseline Imaging (Pre-Stimulation)
  Operation   : detect nfkbNuclearLocalizationDetection
  Duration    : 30 min (IR: 1800.0 SECOND); 5-min imaging intervals = 6 frames
  Purpose     : Establishes pre-stimulus nuclear p65-DsRed baseline (n > 200 cells/condition)

Step 5a | Instant TNF Stimulation
  Reagents    : TNF-alpha 10 ng/mL
  Operation   : Media exchange (abstracted as mix); detect nfkbNuclearLocalizationDetection
  Duration    : 300 min = 5 h (IR: 18000.0 SECOND); replenished every 60 min
  Expected    : Strong NF-kB peak at ~25 min; exponential oscillation decay thereafter
                (desensitisation to constant input; subsequent peaks 10-30% of initial)

Step 5b | Instant IL-1beta Stimulation
  Reagents    : IL-1beta 2.5 ng/mL
  Operation   : Media exchange (abstracted as mix); detect nfkbNuclearLocalizationDetection
  Duration    : 300 min (IR: 18000.0 SECOND)
  Expected    : Parallel dynamics to TNF instant increase

Step 6a | Linear TNF Ramp (5 Steps)
  Reagents    : TNF-alpha; 1 ng/mL increment per step
  Operation   : Sequential media exchange + detect per step
  Duration    : 60 min per step (IR: 3600.0 SECOND); 5 steps total = 300 min
  Expected    : Sustained oscillations; constant AUC at each step; confirms differentiator
                Ramping rates tested: 0.75-10 ng/mL/h (Supplementary Fig. 1)

Step 6b | Linear IL-1beta Ramp (5 Steps)
  Reagents    : IL-1beta; 0.5 ng/mL increment per step
  Operation   : Sequential media exchange + detect per step
  Duration    : 60 min per step; 5 steps total
  Expected    : Constant AUC at each step; differentiator confirmed for IL-1beta (Fig. 2A)

Step 7a | Exponential TNF Ramp (5 Steps)
  Reagents    : TNF-alpha; 2-fold increase per step from starting dose to 10 ng/mL
  Operation   : Sequential media exchange + detect per step
  Duration    : 60 min per step (IR: 3600.0 SECOND); 5 steps total
  Expected    : AUC increases linearly with log(delta_TNF); R-squared ~0.963 (Fig. 2B)
  QC note     : Final step (nfkbExpTNF_s5) used as QC gate anchor for nfkbSignal branch

Step 7b | Exponential IL-1beta Ramp (5 Steps)
  Reagents    : IL-1beta; 2-fold increase per step to 2.5 ng/mL
  Operation   : Sequential media exchange + detect per step
  Duration    : 60 min per step; 5 steps total
  Expected    : Log-linear AUC increase; same differentiator relationship as TNF (Fig. 2B)

Step 8 | Random-Order TNF Fluctuation (4 Steps)
  Reagents    : TNF-alpha; randomly increasing and decreasing concentrations 0-10 ng/mL
  Operation   : Sequential media exchange + detect per step
  Duration    : 60 min per step (IR: 3600.0 SECOND); 4 steps
  Expected    : AUC vs delta_TNF linear for positive changes (correlation ~0.91); sharp drop
                for any concentration decrease; rectified differentiator behaviour confirmed
                (Fig. 2C; Supplementary Fig. 3C for IL-1beta)

Step 9 | Pam2CSK4 Exponential Ramp Control (5 Steps)
  Reagents    : Pam2CSK4; doubled every 60 min from 0.2 to 12.8 ng/mL
  Operation   : Sequential media exchange + detect per step
  Duration    : 60 min per step (IR: 3600.0 SECOND); 5 steps (30 min also tested)
  Expected    : Majority of cells show 1-2 sharp peaks; AUC slopes span negative to positive
                across single-cell clusters; dose differentiation ABSENT for TLR2 ligand
  Analysis    : Single-cell clustering by Matlab linkage (ward method, correlation metric);
                4 groups; TNF slopes all positive (0.037-0.058); Pam slopes mixed
                (-0.048 to +0.035) confirming specificity to TNFR/IL-1R pathway (Fig. 3)

Step 10 | NF-kB Response QC Gate
  Input       : nfkbExpTNF_s5 (final step of exponential TNF ramp)
  Operation   : detect nfkbNuclearLocalizationDetection for 30 s
  Branch:
    Pass (BB2) : nfkbSignal > 0 -> valid oscillatory NF-kB response; dispose; continue
    Fail (BB3) : nfkbSignal <= 0 -> no response (cell death or stimulation failure); drain
  Both branches converge at BB4 (viability join)

Step 11 | Cell Viability Assay (FDA/PI)
  Reagents    : FDA/PI stain (FDA 5 ug/mL, PI 2 ug/mL)
  Operation   : mix (10 min staining, room temperature, dark); detect viabilityDetection 30 s
  Expected    : >80% viability for valid experiment
  Branch:
    Pass (BB5) : viabilitySignal > 0 -> viable cells; dispose; continue to gene expression
    Fail (BB6) : viabilitySignal <= 0 -> low viability; drain
  Both branches converge at BB7 (gene expression join)

Step 12 | Cell Retrieval, Lysis, and RT-qPCR
  Operation   : Trypsinize 1 min; PBS wash to open outlet; 2-3 uL droplet pipetted into
                5 uL CellsDirect lysis buffer; snap-frozen at -80 C
  RT-qPCR     : CellsDirect One-Step RT-qPCR kit; Biorad CFX384
  Targets     : A20, RANTES, Ccl2, Zfp36, Casp4, Serpina3g (TaqMan probes)
  Normalization: GAPDH; 2^(Cq_target - Cq_GAPDH)
  Conditions  : Instant TNF (10 ng/mL, replenished hourly) vs exponential ramp
                (2-fold/60 min for 5 h); cells retrieved at multiple time points during
                and after stimulation (Fig. 7)
  Detection   : detect geneExpressionDetection for 120 min (IR: 7200.0 SECOND)
  Branch:
    Pass (BB8) : geneExprSignal > 0 -> target mRNA detected above GAPDH; dispose lysate
    Fail (BB9) : geneExprSignal <= 0 -> qPCR failure; drain lysate
  Both branches converge at BB10 (terminal cleanup)


KEY RESULTS
-----------
Differentiator equation:
  NF-kB ~ log(delta_cytokine + 1)   for positive changes in cytokine concentration

Linear ramp  : Constant NF-kB AUC at each step (NF-kB responds to constant rate of change)
Exponential ramp : AUC increases log-linearly; TNF R-squared ~0.963; IL-1beta confirmed
Random input : AUC-vs-delta_TNF correlation ~0.91 for increases; sharp drop for decreases
Pam2CSK4    : No dose differentiation (TLR2 pathway); differentiator is receptor-specific

A20 knockout results:
  Exponential ramp : NF-kB saturates at much lower TNF dose; differentiator abolished
  Constant dose    : NF-kB still decreasing at 120 min (vs 60 min for WT);
                     mean oscillation frequency halved; more power at zero frequency
  Random input     : AUC correlation reduced to ~0.76; NF-kB remains nuclear after dose decrease

Gene expression clusters (TNF instant vs exponential):
  Input-responsive (instant only) : Zfp36, Casp4 -- inflammation/apoptosis; require large
                                     initial dose; minimal response during gradual ramp
  Ramp-following                  : A20, Ccl2 -- mirror NF-kB peak height during ramp;
                                     converge to same level when maximum dose is reached
  Late-sustained                  : Serpina3g -- gradual increase only under persistent
                                     high TNF; remains basal during exponential ramp
  Input-independent               : RANTES -- increases continuously under both patterns


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file  : son_nfkb_dose_differentiation.bs
Compiler        : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output       : 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
DAG             : son_nfkb_dose_differentiation_main_dag.dot
Duration units  : All durations converted to minutes (m) or seconds (s) for compiler
                  compatibility (BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported)
                  12 h overnight coating  -> 720m  (IR: 43200.0 SECOND)
                  300 min instant stim    -> 300m  (IR: 18000.0 SECOND)
                  60 min per ramp step    -> 60m   (IR: 3600.0 SECOND)
                  120 min qPCR detection  -> 120m  (IR: 7200.0 SECOND)
ASCII constraint: All non-ASCII characters (kappa, beta, alpha, em-dash, +/- etc.) replaced
                  with ASCII equivalents; ANTLR4 FileStream uses ASCII codec by default.
                  Unicode in comments causes UnicodeDecodeError at byte 0xe2 (e.g. U+03B2).
Negative temp   : -80 C snap-freeze step removed from .bs; compiler silently converts -80c
                  to +80.0 CELSIUS in IR (lilott8/BioScript limitation). Step documented
                  as a comment only.
Modules         : nfkbNuclearLocalizationDetection, viabilityDetection,
                  geneExpressionDetection
Stimulation arms: All 6 arms encoded sequentially in BB1 (main):
                    instant TNF (1 arm), instant IL-1beta (1 arm),
                    linear TNF x5 steps, linear IL-1beta x5 steps,
                    exponential TNF x5 steps, exponential IL-1beta x5 steps,
                    random TNF x4 steps, Pam2CSK4 exponential x5 steps
QC gate anchor  : nfkbSignal keyed on nfkbExpTNF_s5 (final exponential TNF ramp step)
Pam control     : Encoded as separate sequential arm in BB1; not branched independently
Verified outputs: IR and DOT confirmed correct after compilation; all timings, block
                  structure, and CFG edges match expected 10-BB / 12-edge topology.
