description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Processing Stimulus Dynamics by the NF-kB Network in Single Cells
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/s12276-023-01133-7
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/s12276-023-01133-7
Journal      : Experimental & Molecular Medicine, 2023, Vol. 55, pp. 2531-2540
Authors      : Minjun Son, Andrew G. Wang, Bijentimala Keisham, Savas Tay
Platform     : High-throughput programmable valve-based microfluidic platform
               (up to 64 simultaneous experimental conditions; Son et al. Sci. Signal. 2021)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol encodes the core microfluidic single-cell NF-kB signaling experiments
reviewed in Son et al. (2023), covering two main experimental arms:

  (1) Pulsatile TNF-a stimulation - three 15 min pulses at 200 min inter-pulse intervals
      (low-frequency regime), demonstrating full NF-kB system reset and sustained
      full-amplitude oscillatory responses across repeated stimulations.

  (2) Sequential 4-ligand stimulation - TNF-a -> IL-1b -> LPS -> PAM2CSK4, each delivered
      for 2 h in sequence over 8 h total, encoding stimulus identity and order into
      NF-kB dynamics via ligand-specific negative feedback memory (IRAK1, IkBd, A20).

Both arms use fluorescently tagged NF-kB (p65-RFP or p65-GFP) reporter cells and
time-lapse fluorescence microscopy to track nuclear translocation at single-cell resolution
with 3-5 min frame intervals over 8-10 h imaging windows.

A downstream gene expression readout (qRT-PCR or smFISH for NF-kB target genes) and
FDA/PI cell viability QC gate are included as terminal arms.

The BioScript protocol is structured as 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10) with 3 nested
if/else QC gates and 12 CFG edges, matching the DAG output from the lilott8/BioScript
compiler.


BIOLOGICAL CONTEXT: THE NF-kB SIGNALING NETWORK
-------------------------------------------------
NF-kB family transcription factors (RelA/p65, RelB, c-Rel, p50, p52) are activated by
dozens of signals from pathogens and host tissue. The dominant dimer in most cell types
is p65/p50. Prior to stimulation, NF-kB dimers are sequestered in the cytoplasm by
inhibitor of kappa B (IkB) proteins (IkBa, IkBb, IkBe, IkBg, IkBd/p100).

Canonical activation: ligand -> receptor -> ubiquitination/kinase cascade ->
IKK complex activation (IKKa, IKKb, NEMO) -> IkB phosphorylation and degradation ->
NF-kB nuclear translocation -> target gene transcription.

Key negative feedback loops:
  - IkBa (fast; newly translated IkBa exports NF-kB from nucleus; re-synthesised every
    cycle; responsible for oscillatory dynamics)
  - A20 (upstream of IKK; edits ubiquitin scaffolds on TRAF complexes; induced by
    nuclear NF-kB; establishes ~60 min refractory state)
  - CYLD (deubiquitinates IKK scaffolds; upstream of IKK)
  - IRAK-M and MyD88S (TLR/IL-1R pathway specific; induced by nuclear NF-kB)
  - IkBd/p100 homodimer (noncanonical; broad cross-tolerance on 24 h timescale)

Oscillatory dynamics: Under continuous TNF-a, NF-kB undergoes damped oscillations with
~90 min period in fibroblasts. IKK cycling between neutral (n), active (a), and inactive
(i) states is required for sustained translocation cycles. These oscillations are
stimulus-specific: TNF-a drives oscillations in macrophages, fibroblasts, and epithelial
cells, while LPS drives singular (non-oscillatory) activation in fibroblasts.


CELL LINES
----------
- Mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEF), p65-RFP reporter: primary cell type for pulsatile
  and sequential stimulation experiments; oscillatory NF-kB under TNF-a; singular
  activation under LPS; limited polyI:C response. Cultured in DMEM + 10% FBS, 37 C, 5% CO2.
- NCI-H1299 human neuroblastoma, p65-reporter: used in pulsatile and refractory state
  experiments. Cultured in RPMI-1640 + 10% FBS, 37 C, 5% CO2.
- HeLa human cervical cancer, p65-reporter: used for pulse duration vs. cell fate studies
  (NF-kB vs. caspase-8 signaling; Lee et al. Sci. Rep. 2016).
- Mouse macrophages, p65-reporter: oscillatory NF-kB under both TNF-a and LPS;
  NF-kB dynamics drive lasting epigenetic reprogramming (Cheng et al. Science 2021).


REAGENTS
--------
Stimuli:
  TNF-a     : 10 ng/mL (pulsatile arm); 0.1-10 ng/mL range for dose-response
              Signals via: TNFR -> TRADD/RIP1/TRAF2/5 -> TAK1 -> IKK
              Does NOT use IRAK1/MyD88 myddosome.

  IL-1b     : 10 ng/mL
              Signals via: IL-1R -> MyD88/IRAK1/TRAF6 myddosome -> TAK1 -> IKK
              IRAK1 autophosphorylation encodes IL-1b memory (DeFelice et al. 2019).

  LPS       : 100 ng/mL (gram-negative bacterial cell wall component; TLR4 ligand)
              Signals via: TLR4 -> MyD88/IRAK1/TRAF6 AND TRIF-TRAM (endocytosis)
              Shares IRAK1/myddosome with IL-1b -> cross-tolerance after IL-1b exposure.

  PAM2CSK4  : 100 ng/mL (synthetic bacterial lipopeptide analog; TLR1/2 ligand)
              Signals via: TLR1/2 -> MyD88/IRAK1/TRAF6 myddosome -> TAK1 -> IKK
              Does NOT exhibit differentiator-like NF-kB behavior (unlike TNF-a, IL-1b).

Priming agent   : 2% Pluronics F-127 in PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free)
Carrier buffer  : PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free)
Viability stains: FDA (5 ug/mL; ex 490 nm, em 526 nm; live cells, green)
                  PI  (2 ug/mL; ex 488 nm, em 617 nm; dead cells, red)


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Device Priming
  Reagents : PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free), Pluronics F-127
  Mix      : 2% Pluronics F-127 in PBS
  Duration : 5 min
  Purpose  : Prevents non-specific cell adhesion to PDMS microfluidic channel walls.
             Standard pre-conditioning for microfluidic cell culture.

Step 2 | Single-Cell Loading and Equilibration
  Cell line      : MEF p65-RFP NF-kB reporter
  Operation      : Low-density cell perfusion into individual isolated chambers
                   (abstracted as mix in BioScript; no DMF electrode mixing)
  Loading time   : 2 min
  Equilibration  : 30 min at 37 C, 5% CO2
  Purpose        : Single-cell occupancy per chamber; establishes cytoplasmic baseline
                   NF-kB (N:C ratio ~1) before stimulation begins.

Step 3-5 | Pulsatile TNF-a Stimulation (3 Pulses, 200 min Period)
  Stimulus       : TNF-a, 10 ng/mL
  Pulse duration : 15 min (900 s) per pulse
  Wash           : PBS, 5 min, replaces TNF-a to terminate stimulation
  Recovery       : 185 min at 37 C between pulses (total inter-pulse period: 200 min)
  Pulses         : 3 total (Pulse 1 at 0 min, Pulse 2 at 200 min, Pulse 3 at 400 min)

  Biological rationale:
    At 200 min inter-pulse period (low frequency), full NF-kB system reset occurs
    between pulses: IKK returns to neutral state, A20 and IkBa degrade, refractory
    period ends. Full-amplitude NF-kB responses maintained across all 3 pulses.
    (Ashall et al. Science 2009; Kellogg & Tay Cell 2015)

    At high frequency (<100 min period), insufficient time for A20 degradation and
    IKK reset -> diminishing NF-kB amplitude after each successive pulse.

    At resonance (~90 min period, matching intrinsic NF-kB oscillation frequency),
    single-cell NF-kB oscillations synchronise; noise facilitates entrainment and
    increases downstream gene expression across a range of feeding frequencies.
    (Kellogg & Tay Cell 2015)

Step 6 | NF-kB Translocation Detection (Pulsatile Arm)
  Module         : nfkbTranslocationDetection
  Readout        : p65-RFP nuclear-to-cytoplasmic (N:C) ratio; frame rate 3-5 min
  Detection time : 90 s per chamber scan
  QC gate        : nfkbSignal > 0 -> oscillatory NF-kB confirmed (BB2: dispose)
                   nfkbSignal <= 0 -> no translocation detected   (BB3: drain)

Step 7 | Fresh Cell Loading for Sequential Arm
  Operation      : Re-prime device, load fresh p65-RFP MEF reporter cells
  Equilibration  : 30 min at 37 C
  Purpose        : Independent cell population for sequential multi-ligand experiment;
                   ensures no carry-over from pulsatile arm stimulation history.

Step 8-11 | Sequential 4-Ligand Stimulation (8 h Total)
  Ligand 1: TNF-a (0-120 min)
    - 10 ng/mL for 120 min; wash 5 min with PBS
    - Signals via TNFR-TRADD-RIP1-TRAF2/5-TAK1-IKK (no IRAK1 involvement)
    - Induces A20, IkBa, CYLD negative feedback
    - NF-kB: 1-3 damped oscillation peaks

  Ligand 2: IL-1b (120-240 min)
    - 10 ng/mL for 120 min; wash 5 min with PBS
    - Signals via IL-1R-MyD88-IRAK1-TRAF6-TAK1-IKK (myddosome pathway)
    - Reactivates NF-kB despite elevated A20 (different receptor complex)
    - IRAK1 autophosphorylation begins; encodes IL-1b/LPS cross-tolerance memory
    - (Adamson et al. Nat. Commun. 2016; DeFelice et al. Sci. Signal. 2019)

  Ligand 3: LPS (240-360 min)
    - 100 ng/mL for 120 min; wash 5 min with PBS
    - Signals via TLR4-MyD88-IRAK1-TRAF6 AND TRIF-TRAM pathway
    - Shares IRAK1/myddosome with IL-1b; IRAK1 aggregation from L2 creates
      cross-tolerogenic state; LPS-driven NF-kB response attenuated
    - NF-kB: singular activation without oscillation in fibroblasts

  Ligand 4: PAM2CSK4 (360-480 min)
    - 100 ng/mL for 120 min; wash 5 min with PBS
    - Signals via TLR1/2-MyD88-IRAK1-TRAF6 (myddosome; shares with IL-1b and LPS)
    - IRAK1 clustering from L2+L3 further attenuates PAM response
    - PAM does NOT exhibit differentiator-like NF-kB behavior (unlike TNF-a/IL-1b);
      NF-kB response does not track concentration changes in PAM level
    - (Son et al. Sci. Signal. 2021; Wang et al. Cell Rep. 2022)

  Key memory mechanisms encoded in this sequence:
    - IRAK1 autophosphorylation and aggregation (3 h; dose-dependent):
      Triggered by high-dose IL-1b or LPS; creates cross-tolerance for IL-1b AND LPS
      but NOT TNF-a (TNFR does not use IRAK1). Safety mechanism against excessive
      inflammation. (DeFelice et al. Sci. Signal. 2019 - ref 64)
    - IkBd (p100 homodimer; 24 h timescale):
      Genetic deletion eliminates tolerance effect; critical for tolerogenic memory.
      (Shih et al. PNAS 2009 - ref 31)
    - A20 (rapid; upstream of IKK):
      Inhibits TRAF-mediated IKK activation; partially reduces cross-receptor responses.

Step 12 | NF-kB Translocation Detection (Sequential Arm)
  Module         : nfkbTranslocationDetection
  Detection time : 90 s
  Readout        : Composite NF-kB dynamics across all 4 ligands (oscillation period,
                   amplitude, damping coefficient, inter-peak intervals)
  QC gate        : seqSignal > 0 -> sequence-encoded dynamics confirmed (BB5: dispose)
                   seqSignal <= 0 -> no response detected              (BB6: drain)

Step 13 | Downstream Gene Expression Readout
  Module         : geneExpressionDetection
  Duration       : 30 min (lysis + qRT-PCR or smFISH abstraction)
  Target genes   : IL-6, CXCL8/IL-8, IkBa, A20, TNF-a, Casp4, CCL3/4/5
  Key finding    : Different NF-kB translocation dynamics (amplitude, duration, period)
                   produce distinct transcriptional outputs. Subpopulation of
                   proinflammatory genes not upregulated in cells with shorter initial
                   NF-kB oscillation duration. Chromatin remodeling decodes NF-kB
                   activation duration to control gene expression.
                   (Lane et al. Cells 2017; Sen et al. Cell Syst. 2020;
                    Cheng et al. Science 2021)
  QC gate        : expressionSignal > 0 -> target gene upregulation confirmed (BB8)
                   expressionSignal <= 0 -> no expression response detected  (BB9)

Step 14 | Cell Viability QC (Pass Branch Only)
  Stain          : FDA (live) + PI (dead) 1X
  Incubation     : 10 min at room temperature (25 C)
  Detection time : 30 s fluorescence scan
  Target         : >80% viability across 8 h multi-ligand stimulation window
  Purpose        : Confirms NF-kB dynamics represent true signaling responses,
                   not cell death signals. Consistent with Samlali et al. 2020.


IMPORTANT BIOLOGICAL FINDINGS ENCODED IN THIS PROTOCOL
-------------------------------------------------------
1. Pulsatile stimulation reveals hidden network properties:
   Comparing pulsatile vs. continuous TNF-a stimulation revealed that IKK cycling
   between active and inactive states is essential for NF-kB signal transduction
   (Behar & Hoffmann Biophys. J. 2013; Ashall et al. Science 2009).

2. NF-kB acts as a differentiator for TNF-a and IL-1b:
   NF-kB responds to CHANGES in cytokine concentration (delta), not absolute levels.
   This enables spatial interpretation: the network infers relative distance to
   cytokine-secreting sentinel cells from the rate of cytokine concentration change.
   PAM2CSK4 does NOT exhibit this behavior - selective processing of stimulus dynamics.
   (Son et al. Sci. Signal. 2021 - ref 13)

3. Sequential stimulation encodes memory via ligand-specific feedback:
   IRAK1 autophosphorylation creates cross-tolerance between IL-1b and LPS but not
   TNF-a, reflecting receptor pathway topology (shared vs. distinct myddosome use).
   4-ligand sequences produce unique NF-kB oscillation pattern fingerprints.
   (Wang et al. Cell Rep. 2022 - ref 15; DeFelice et al. Sci. Signal. 2019 - ref 64)

4. NF-kB dynamics determine downstream gene expression:
   Different oscillation properties (amplitude, duration, period) produce distinct
   transcriptional outputs in single cells. Stable NF-kB oscillation at fixed period
   increases downstream gene expression.
   (Kellogg & Tay Cell 2015 - ref 17; Lane et al. Cells 2017 - ref 120)

5. Limitation of endpoint measurements:
   Single time-point cytokine measurements (e.g. serum TNF-a in sepsis) show low
   correlation with disease severity. Increasing/decreasing cytokine dynamics are
   far better predictors (e.g. IL-6 kinetics in septic shock mortality).
   Microfluidic dynamic stimulation is required to capture true in vivo signal
   processing. (Abasiyanik et al. Nat. Commun. 2020 - ref 115)


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : son_nfkb_stimulus_dynamics.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
DAG file       : son_nfkb_stimulus_dynamics_main_dag.dot
IR verified    : All 10 BBs present; all time conversions correct (see below);
                 all variables consumed by dispose/drain; terminal NOP present.

Duration conversions (all verified against .ir output):
  15 min pulse           ->  900.0 SECOND
  5 min wash             ->  300.0 SECOND
  30 min equilibration   -> 1800.0 SECOND
  185 min recovery       -> 11100.0 SECOND
  2 min loading          ->  120.0 SECOND
  120 min sequential stim -> 7200.0 SECOND
  30 min gene expression -> 1800.0 SECOND

Modules declared:
  nfkbTranslocationDetection   (pulsatile arm + sequential arm NF-kB imaging)
  geneExpressionDetection      (qRT-PCR / smFISH target gene readout)
  cellViabilityDetection       (FDA/PI live-dead staining)

Unicode fix:
  ANTLR4 FileStream defaults to ASCII encoding; all Greek characters in comments
  replaced with ASCII equivalents before compilation:
  kappa (NF-kB) -> k, alpha (TNF-a) -> a, beta (IL-1b) -> b, delta (IkBd) -> d,
  arrow symbol -> ->

mix abstraction:
  mix operations model programmable valve-gated perfusion of stimulus solution
  into isolated single-cell culture chamber; NOT DMF electrode mixing.

heat abstraction:
  heat steps model physiological temperature incubation/recovery periods (37 C)
  between stimulus pulses or during cell equilibration.

Arms note:
  Two independent experimental arms encoded sequentially in one .bs file:
  (1) Pulsatile TNF-a arm (BB1 -> BB2/BB3 -> BB4)
  (2) Sequential 4-ligand arm (BB4 -> BB5/BB6 -> BB7 -> BB8/BB9 -> BB10)
  Fresh cell populations are loaded for each arm (loadedCells vs. loadedCells2).

protocol.title: Processing Stimulus Dynamics by the NF-kB Network in Single Cells
protocol.platform: High-throughput microfluidics (programmable valve-based multi-condition perfusion)
protocol.objective: Characterise NF-kB signaling responses to pulsatile stimulation, increasing/fluctuating stimulus doses, and sequential multi-ligand combinations at single-cell resolution using live-cell fluorescence imaging in microfluidic devices

device.throughput: Up to 64 experimental conditions simultaneously (Son et al. Sci. Signal. 2021)
device.channel_configuration: Individual isolated cell culture chambers with addressable perfusion inlets
device.imaging: Time-lapse fluorescence microscopy; frame interval 3-5 min over 8-10 h stimulation windows
device.reporter_system: p65-RFP or p65-GFP nuclear translocation; N:C ratio measured per cell per frame
device.flow_control: Programmable syringe pumps or pressure controllers; valve-gated stimulus delivery
references: Gómez-Sjöberg et al. Anal. Chem. 2007 (ref 74) - versatile automated microfluidic cell culture system
Kellogg & Tay Cell 2015 (ref 17) - noise facilitates transcriptional control under dynamic inputs
Son et al. Sci. Signal. 2021 (ref 13) - 64-condition high-throughput microfluidic platform

cell_media.MEF: DMEM + 10% FBS, no antibiotics, 37 C, 5% CO2
cell_media.H1299: RPMI-1640 + 10% FBS, no antibiotics, 37 C, 5% CO2
cell_media.HeLa: DMEM + 10% FBS, no antibiotics, 37 C, 5% CO2

TNFalpha.supplier_note: Human recombinant TNF-a; homotrimer; signals via TNFR-TRADD-RIP1-TRAF2/5-TAK1-IKK

LPS.signals_via: TLR4 -> MyD88/IRAK1/TRAF6 AND TRIF-TRAM (after TLR4 endocytosis) -> IKK
LPS.nfkb_response: Singular activation without clear oscillation in fibroblasts and epithelial cells (vs. oscillatory in macrophages)

PAM2CSK4.description: Synthetic analog of bacterial lipopeptide; TLR1/2 agonist
PAM2CSK4.special_property: Does NOT exhibit differentiator-like NF-kB response to changing concentration (unlike TNF-a and IL-1b)

nfkb_pathway.dominant_dimer: p65/p50 heterodimer (most abundant in almost all cell types)

negative_feedback_proteins.IkBa: Primary fast negative feedback; newly translated IkBa exports NF-kB from nucleus
negative_feedback_proteins.A20: Upstream of IKK; edits ubiquitin scaffolds on TRAF complexes; induced by nuclear NF-kB; establishes refractory state (~60 min post-stimulation)
negative_feedback_proteins.CYLD: Deubiquitinates IKK scaffolds; upstream of IKK; induced by nuclear NF-kB
negative_feedback_proteins.IRAK-M: TLR/IL-1R specific; induced by nuclear NF-kB
negative_feedback_proteins.MyD88S: TLR/IL-1R specific splice variant; inhibits downstream signaling
negative_feedback_proteins.IkBd: Noncanonical; p100 homodimer; mediates broad cross-tolerance on 24 h timescale

ikk_complex.note: IKK cycling between active and inactive states is necessary for NF-kB signal transduction (Behar & Hoffmann Biophys. J. 2013)

oscillation.mechanism: IKK activation -> IkBa degradation -> NF-kB nuclear translocation -> IkBa re-synthesis -> NF-kB nuclear export -> cycle repeats if IKK remains active
oscillation.damping: Oscillations damp under continuous stimulation due to A20/CYLD upstream inhibition

steps.name: Device priming
steps.notes: 2% Pluronics F-127 in PBS; perfused through channels to prevent non-specific cell adhesion to PDMS walls. Standard pre-treatment for microfluidic cell culture (Samlali et al. Small 2020; Son et al. Biosens. Bioelectron. 2023)

steps.name: Single-cell loading and equilibration
steps.operation: flow-through loading into individual chambers (abstracted as mix in BioScript)
steps.notes: Cells loaded at low density to achieve single-cell occupancy per chamber. Equilibration ensures baseline NF-kB is cytoplasmic (N:C ratio ~1) before stimulation. Reporter: p65-RFP enables real-time nuclear translocation tracking (Nelson et al. J. Cell Sci. 2002; Tay et al. Nature 2010)

steps.name: Pulsatile TNF-a stimulation - Pulse 1
steps.notes: 15 min TNF-a pulse delivered via programmable valve. At 200 min inter-pulse period (low frequency), NF-kB system fully resets between pulses; full-amplitude response maintained across all pulses (Ashall et al. Science 2009). At high frequency (<100 min period), response amplitude diminishes after each pulse.

steps.name: Pulsatile TNF-a stimulation - Pulse 2
steps.notes: Second 15 min TNF-a pulse after 185 min recovery. A20 and IkBa fully degraded/reset; IKK back to neutral state. Kellogg & Tay (Cell 2015) showed noise in NF-kB oscillation facilitates entrainment and downstream gene expression across a range of feeding frequencies.

steps.name: Pulsatile TNF-a stimulation - Pulse 3
steps.notes: Third 15 min TNF-a pulse. Confirms sustained full-amplitude NF-kB responses at low-frequency pulsatile regime. Contrasts with high-frequency (60 min period) regime where NF-kB amplitude diminishes progressively (Ashall et al. Science 2009 - ref 72 in paper).

steps.name: NF-kB translocation detection - pulsatile arm
steps.readout: p65-RFP nuclear-to-cytoplasmic (N:C) ratio per cell per frame
steps.notes: NF-kB translocation confirmed by N:C ratio > 1 at peak. Oscillation period ~90 min under continuous TNF-a; single peak under brief pulse; full amplitude maintained at 200 min inter-pulse interval.

steps.name: Fresh cell loading for sequential arm
steps.operation: device re-prime, fresh cell loading, equilibration
steps.notes: Independent cell chamber population for sequential multi-ligand experiment. Same priming and equilibration as Steps S1-S2. Fresh p65-RFP MEF reporter cells.

steps.name: Sequential stimulation - Ligand 1: TNF-a (0-120 min)
steps.signals_via: TNFR -> TRADD/RIP1/TRAF2/5 -> TAK1 -> IKK (does NOT use IRAK1/MyD88)
steps.notes: Primary NF-kB response: 1-3 damped oscillation peaks. A20 upregulation partially suppresses subsequent TRAF2/5-dependent signaling. TNF-a-specific negative feedback does NOT cross-tolerize IL-1b or LPS arms (different receptor complexes). Wang et al. Cell Rep. 2022 (ref 15).

steps.name: Sequential stimulation - Ligand 2: IL-1b (120-240 min)
steps.notes: Despite elevated A20 from prior TNF-a, IL-1b can reactivate NF-kB without attenuation (different receptor complex). IRAK1 begins to autophosphorylate, encoding IL-1b memory. At high dose, IRAK1 aggregation creates cross-tolerogenic state for subsequent IL-1b and LPS but not TNF-a (DeFelice et al. Sci. Signal. 2019 - ref 64). Adamson et al. Nat. Commun. 2016 (ref 73).

steps.name: Sequential stimulation - Ligand 3: LPS (240-360 min)
steps.signals_via: TLR4 -> MyD88/IRAK1/TRAF6 (myddosome) AND TRIF-TRAM (after TLR4 endocytosis)
steps.cross_tolerance_mechanism: IRAK1 autophosphorylation and aggregation from prior IL-1b exposure reduces signaling through shared myddosome complex
steps.notes: LPS and IL-1b share the IRAK1/MyD88 myddosome. If IRAK1 is aggregated from S9, cells enter cross-tolerogenic state: LPS-driven NF-kB response is attenuated. 100 ng/mL LPS drives further IRAK1 clustering, deepening cross-tolerance state for S10. NF-kB response: singular activation without oscillation in fibroblasts. DeFelice et al. Sci. Signal. 2019 (ref 64).

steps.name: Sequential stimulation - Ligand 4: PAM2CSK4 (360-480 min)
steps.notes: PAM2CSK4 shares the myddosome with IL-1b and LPS. After IRAK1 clustering from S9+S10, PAM response is significantly attenuated. Unlike TNF-a and IL-1b, PAM does NOT exhibit differentiator-like NF-kB behaviour (response does not track concentration changes; Son et al. Sci. Signal. 2021 - ref 13). Full 8 h sequence: TNF-a(2h)->IL-1b(2h)->LPS(2h)->PAM(2h) produces distinct NF-kB oscillation patterns per Wang et al. Cell Rep. 2022 (ref 15).

steps.name: NF-kB translocation detection - sequential arm
steps.readout: Composite NF-kB dynamics across all 4 ligands: oscillation period, amplitude, damping, inter-peak intervals
steps.notes: Distinct NF-kB oscillation patterns encode stimulus sequence and identity via IRAK1 and IkBd memory. Wang et al. Cell Rep. 2022 demonstrated 4-ligand sequence encodes unique NF-kB response patterns per ligand-order combination.

steps.name: Downstream gene expression readout
steps.key_finding: NF-kB translocation dynamics (amplitude, duration, oscillation period) correlated with proinflammatory gene expression profiles at single-cell level. Subpopulation of proinflammatory genes not upregulated in cells with shorter initial NF-kB oscillation duration.
references: Lane et al. Cells 2017 (ref 120) - NF-kB signaling dynamics correlated with target gene expression in single cells
Sen et al. Cell Syst. 2020 (ref 16) - duration decoding through chromatin remodeling
Cheng et al. Science 2021 (ref 14) - NF-kB dynamics determine epigenomic reprogramming in macrophages

steps.name: Cell viability QC (pass branch only)
steps.notes: FDA (live, green; ex 490 nm, em 526 nm) and PI (dead, red; ex 488 nm, em 617 nm) staining. Confirms stimulation protocol does not induce significant apoptosis across 8 h multi-ligand sequence. Consistent with methodology from Samlali et al. Small 2020.

low_frequency.effect: Full NF-kB system reset between pulses; sustained full-amplitude responses; A20 and IkBa fully degraded before next pulse

high_frequency.effect: Diminishing NF-kB response amplitude after each pulse; insufficient time for IKK reset and A20 degradation

resonance.effect: Single-cell NF-kB oscillations synchronised; maximum amplitude in subsequent peaks; noise facilitates entrainment across range of frequencies

refractory_period.mechanism: A20-dependent; established upstream of IKK activation; cells do not respond to restimulation with the same ligand during this window

differentiator_behavior.description: NF-kB response tracks the CHANGE in cytokine level (delta), not the absolute dose. Analogous to a differentiator in electronic circuits.
differentiator_behavior.mechanism: A20-mediated upstream IKK inhibition sets a dynamic threshold; cytokine increase overcomes A20 inhibition and resets IKK cycling
differentiator_behavior.reference: Son et al. Sci. Signal. 2021 (ref 13); Cruz et al. Sci. Adv. 2021 (ref 85)

non_differentiator.description: PAM NF-kB response does not track concentration changes; responds to absolute dose levels

cross_tolerance_mechanisms.mechanism: Autophosphorylation and aggregation; inhibits myddosome downstream signaling for both IL-1b and LPS but NOT TNF-a

cross_tolerance_mechanisms.trigger: 24 h prior exposure to LPS, TNF-a, or IL-1b
cross_tolerance_mechanisms.mechanism: Noncanonical NF-kB inhibitor; broad cross-tolerance between multiple stimuli

sequential_stimulation.memory_encoding: Distinct NF-kB oscillation patterns per 4-ligand sequence; feedback remodeling is dose- and ligand-specific

cell_type_specificity.fibroblasts: Oscillatory NF-kB under continuous TNF-a; singular activation under LPS; limited polyI:C response
cell_type_specificity.macrophages: Oscillatory NF-kB under TNF-a AND LPS; polyI:C oscillatory; epigenetic reprogramming by NF-kB dynamics
cell_type_specificity.epithelial: Oscillatory NF-kB under TNF-a; limited LPS and polyI:C response
cell_type_specificity.reference: Adelaja et al. Immunity 2021 (ref 11); Cheng et al. Science 2021 (ref 14)

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.content: Device priming, cell loading, equilibration, pulsatile TNF-a arm (3 pulses at 200 min period), NF-kB translocation detection

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_4_j
basic_blocks.content: dispose(nfkbSignal); fresh cell loading; sequential 4-ligand stimulation arm (TNF-a->IL-1b->LPS->PAM, 2h each); sequential NF-kB detection

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_7_j
basic_blocks.content: dispose(seqSignal); gene expression readout (geneExpressionDetection, 30 min)

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_8_t
basic_blocks.action: FDA/PI viability stain, detect, dispose all

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_10_j
basic_blocks.content: dispose(expressionSignal); NOP

bioscript_compiler_notes.ir_output: 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
bioscript_compiler_notes.duration_units: All durations in seconds (s) or minutes (m); hours not supported
bioscript_compiler_notes.unicode_fix: All Greek characters (kappa, alpha, beta, delta) and arrow symbols replaced with ASCII equivalents; required for ANTLR4 FileStream ASCII codec
bioscript_compiler_notes.mix_abstraction: mix operations model microfluidic valve-gated perfusion of stimulus into cell chamber; not DMF electrode mixing
bioscript_compiler_notes.heat_abstraction: heat steps model inter-pulse incubation/wash recovery periods at physiological temperature (37 C)
bioscript_compiler_notes.arms_note: Two independent experimental arms encoded in sequence: (1) pulsatile TNF-a arm (BB1->BB4) and (2) sequential 4-ligand arm (BB4->BB7). Fresh cell populations used for each arm.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Spatiotemporal NF-kB Dynamics Encodes the Position, Amplitude, and Duration of Local Immune Inputs
Source Link  : https://www.science.org/doi/full/10.1126/sciadv.abn6240
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abn6240
Journal      : Science Advances, 2022, Vol. 8, Article eabn6240
Authors      : Minjun Son, Tino Frank, Thomas Holst-Hansen, Andrew G. Wang, Michael Junkin,
               Sara S. Kashaf, Ala Trusina, Savas Tay
Platform     : Custom two-chamber PDMS diffusion microfluidic chip with pneumatic membrane valve


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a microfluidic coculture platform designed to quantify spatiotemporal
NF-kB signaling dynamics in a model one-way immune communication channel: a signal-sending
macrophage (or soluble TNF source) to signal-receiving NIH 3T3 fibroblasts. The device consists
of two PDMS chambers separated by a pneumatically actuated membrane valve. Cytokine (TNF) is
loaded in the source chamber and released into a receiving chamber filled with fibroblasts by
opening the valve. A peristaltic sink channel continuously perfuses fresh medium at the far end
to simulate capillary clearance, establishing a stable diffusion gradient along the 2.5 mm
chamber axis.

Single-cell NF-kB nuclear translocation is tracked in p65-DsRed-expressing fibroblasts by
time-lapse fluorescence microscopy at 6 min intervals. After the imaging window, cells are
retrieved from three spatially resolved regions (near, mid, far from the TNF source) and
profiled by one-step RT-qPCR for early (A20/Tnfaip3) and late (Casp4, RANTES/Ccl5) NF-kB
target genes.

The BioScript file encodes the primary TNF diffusion experiment (100 ng/mL, 60 min release,
Fig. 3B primary arm) with downstream spatially resolved gene expression measurement (Fig. 6).
The macrophage coculture arm (Fig. 5) is documented in the manifest but not separately encoded.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Fabrication   : Standard soft lithography. PDMS (Momentive RTV-615, 10:1 polymer:catalyst)
                cast on SU-8 masters. Valve regions: positive photoresist MicroChemicals AZ40XT
                (20 um). Channel and control layers: negative photoresist SU-8 3025 (30 or 25 um).
                All photoresists exposed at 375 nm (Heidelberg MLA150 maskless aligner).
                PDMS layers cured overnight at 80 C. Oxygen plasma treatment (Harrick PDC-001,
                30 s) used to bond PDMS slab to clean glass slide.

Chambers      :
  Source chamber    : Cytokine (TNF) or single macrophage loaded here with valve closed.
  Diffusion chamber : Fibroblast receiving chamber, 2.5 mm along diffusion axis, coated
                      with 1:4 fibronectin (1 mg/mL in PBS) overnight before cell seeding.
  Sink channel      : Bottom channel; continuously washed with fresh medium at 0.33 Hz
                      (20 cycles/min) via on-chip peristaltic pumping to deplete cytokine
                      and simulate capillary clearance (bypass refreshed every 1-2 min).

Valve         : Pneumatic PDMS membrane separator; Festo 197334 solenoid valve; controlled by
                custom MATLAB interface (modified from Gomez-Sjoberg et al. Anal. Chem. 2007).
                Reagents delivered via Tygon ND-100-80 tubing + PEEK VICI TPK.505 tubing.

Microscope    : Nikon Eclipse Ti2; stage-top incubator box (Life Imaging Service, Basel);
                maintained at 37 C, 5% CO2, >98% humidity throughout all experiments.


CELL LINES
----------
- p65-/- NIH 3T3 mouse embryonic fibroblasts (signal-receiving population):
    Reporters : p65-DsRed (NF-kB nuclear translocation marker)
                H2B-GFP (nucleus position and boundary marker)
    Medium    : Fluorobrite DMEM (Gibco A1896701) + 10% FBS (Omega Scientific FB11)
                + 1% GlutaMax (Gibco) + 1x penicillin-streptomycin (Gibco)
    Passaging : Trypsin-EDTA (Gibco); 1:10 resuspension before 100% confluency

- p65-/- RAW 264.7 macrophages (signal-sending population; macrophage coculture arm only):
    Reporter  : p65-GFP
    Medium    : DMEM + 10% certified FBS (Gibco A3160401) + 1% GlutaMax + HEPES (Gibco 15630106)
    Passaging : Scraped and resuspended 1:10 before 100% confluency
    Stimulation: LPS 10 ng/mL (InvivoGen tlrl-3pelps) for 10 min; washed with fresh medium


PROTOCOL STEPS (BioScript-encoded TNF diffusion arm)
------------------------------------------------------

Step 1 | Fibronectin Surface Coating of Diffusion Chamber
  Reagents    : Fibronectin (1 mg/mL) diluted 1:4 in PBS
  Operation   : Applied to PDMS diffusion chamber surface overnight at room temperature
  Duration    : 720m (overnight; = 43200 s in IR)
  Purpose     : Promotes fibroblast adhesion and uniform monolayer in diffusion chamber
  Wash        : Channels washed with fresh DMEM before fibroblast seeding
  Paper M&M   : "surface treated with 1:4 fibronectin (1 mg/ml) in PBS solution overnight
                 and washed with fresh medium"

Step 2 | NIH 3T3 Fibroblast Seeding and Attachment
  Cell line   : p65-/- NIH 3T3 (p65-DsRed + H2B-GFP)
  Confluency  : ~80% target seeding density
  Attachment  : 5 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 (= 300m = 18000 s in IR); 1-2 medium feedings during window
  Side channel clearance: Non-adherent cells in side channels flushed out with trypsin
  Note        : `mix` in BioScript abstracts channel flow-through seeding, not DMF electrode
                actuation; no electrode-mediated mixing occurs in this device

Step 3 | TNF Loading into Source Chamber
  Reagent     : TNF (R&D Systems 410-MT); diluted to 100 ng/mL in Fluorobrite DMEM
  Operation   : Loaded into source chamber with pneumatic separator valve in closed position
  Conditions tested in paper: 10, 30, 100 ng/mL (Fig. 3A); this file encodes 100 ng/mL

Step 4 | Valve Opening - TNF Diffusion Initiation
  Operation   : MATLAB-controlled solenoid valve opened; TNF diffuses passively along 2.5 mm axis
  Release duration: 60 min (= 3600 s in IR); valve then closed to stop TNF source input
  Sink perfusion : 0.33 Hz peristaltic pumping (20 cycles/min); bypass washed every 1-2 min
  Diffusion profile (Fig. 1E, fig. S4):
    Near (0-0.4 mm) : Fast TNF rise, high peak concentration, ~0 min NF-kB delay
    Mid  (0.5-0.9 mm): Intermediate TNF kinetics, moderate delay
    Far  (1.0-1.5 mm): Slow TNF rise, low peak, ~25 min NF-kB activation delay;
                        extended NF-kB activation duration (Fig. 1I blue interval)
  Other durations tested: 15 min and 30 min (Fig. 3B)

Step 5 | NF-kB Fluorescence Imaging Window
  Duration    : 200 min total post-valve-open (= 12000 s in IR)
  Interval    : Fluorescence images every 6 min (automated acquisition, NIS Elements)
  Camera      : Hamamatsu ORCA-Flash4.0 V2; p65-DsRed: 555 nm excitation, 0.3 s / 100% LED;
                H2B-GFP: 470 nm excitation, 40 ms / 100% LED; Nikon S plan Fluor ELWD 20x
  Stitching   : 4 FOVs per chamber stitched by custom MATLAB (detectSURFFeatures +
                estimateGeometricTransform)
  Analysis    : p65-DsRed nuclear intensity tracked per cell; basal level (pre-valve) used as
                reference; lowess smoothing applied; threshold = 2 SDs above mean basal per region
  Observations (100 ng/mL, 60 min):
    - Wave-like NF-kB propagation across entire 2.5 mm chamber (Fig. 1H, Movie S2)
    - Sharply defined activation zone: >75% to <25% activation within 0.4 mm (Fig. 1J)
    - 2-3 NF-kB oscillations within activation zone at 100 ng/mL
  QC criterion: >75% of near-region cells (0-0.4 mm) activate above 2 SD threshold

Step 6 | NF-kB Activation QC Gate
  Detection   : nfkbActivationDetection module; 30 s detect on imagingWindow
  Pass (BB2)  : nfkbSignal > 0 -> wave propagation confirmed; dispose(imagingWindow)
  Fail (BB3)  : nfkbSignal <= 0 -> device failure or TNF degradation; drain(imagingWindow)
  Join (BB4)  : dispose(nfkbSignal); proceed to gene expression arm

Step 7 | Continued Incubation to 8 h Time Point
  Duration    : 280m additional (= 16800 s in IR); 200m imaging elapsed; total 480m = 8 h
  Temperature : 37 C, 5% CO2
  Purpose     : Allow late NF-kB target gene expression to accumulate (Casp4, RANTES peak ~4-8 h)
  Timepoints  : Cells retrieved at 0, 2, 4, and 8 h post-TNF release (Fig. 6C)

Step 8 | Spatially Resolved Cell Retrieval
  Method      : Chip outlet PDMS cut with razor; purge medium carries detached cells onto
                glass slide as ~2 uL droplet; pipetted into 10 uL ice-cold lysis buffer
  Valve actuation: Separating valves divide chamber into three spatial zones:
    Near : 0-0.4 mm from TNF source
    Mid  : 0.5-0.9 mm from TNF source
    Far  : 1.0-1.5 mm from TNF source
  Detachment  : TrypLE Express (Gibco); 1-2 min per region (= 2m = 120 s in IR)
  Lysis buffer: 10 uL per region; 0.1% Triton X-100 + RNase inhibitor (Takara); ice-cold
  Storage     : -80 C until qPCR processing
  BioScript note: Three separate PBS + TrypLE + lysis buffer dispenses (one per region) used;
                  continuedIncub staged through chambNear/Mid/Far via distinct PBS dispenses
                  to comply with compiler single-consumption constraint

Step 9 | One-Step RT-qPCR Gene Expression Measurement
  Kit         : CellDirect One-Step RT-qPCR (Thermo Fisher Scientific)
  Targets     : Tnfaip3 (A20) -- early gene; Casp4 -- late gene; Ccl5 (RANTES) -- late gene
  Regions     : Near, Mid, Far (9 total reactions: 3 probes x 3 regions)
  Normalization: GAPDH; DeltaCT method; fold change = 2^(DeltaDeltaCT)
  RT step     : 50 C for 15 min (= 900 s in IR)
  PCR step    : 95 C for 42 min (2 min initial denaturation + 40 cycles; = 2520 s in IR)
  Expected spatial pattern (Fig. 6C):
    A20 (early) : Strongly induced near source at 2 h; drops sharply at mid/far by 8 h
    Casp4 (late): Upregulated across all three regions at 4-8 h (distance-insensitive)
    RANTES (late): Upregulated across all three regions at 4-8 h (distance-insensitive)
  BioScript note: Probes chained sequentially into each lysate to comply with compiler
                  single-consumption constraint: rxnNearA -> rxnNearAC -> rxnNearACR;
                  same chain applied to Mid and Far. Terminal ACR variable carries all
                  three probes and proceeds through RT/PCR heat steps and detect.

Step 10 | Gene Expression QC Gate
  Detection   : geneExpressionDetection module; 30 s detect on rxnNearACR
  QC criterion: A20 near-region signal must exceed 3 SDs above unstimulated baseline at 2 h
  Pass (BB5)  : geneExprSignal > 0 -> dispose(rxnNearACR, rxnMidACR, rxnFarACR)
  Fail (BB6)  : geneExprSignal <= 0 -> drain(rxnNearACR, rxnMidACR, rxnFarACR)
  Terminal (BB7): dispose(geneExprSignal); NOP


KEY FINDINGS
------------
Wave propagation  : TNF diffusion + intrinsic NF-kB network oscillations produce wave-like
                    NF-kB activity propagation; not paracrine amplification by fibroblasts
                    (fibroblasts do not secrete NF-kB-activating signals, fig. S5).

Activation zone   : Sharply defined for all source doses; transition from >75% to <25%
                    cell activation within 0.4 mm (<15% of chamber length) (Fig. 1J).

Dose controls range: Signaling range increases linearly with log(TNF dose);
                    y = 0.89*log(x) - 1.80 mm (Fig. 3C). Dose does not affect oscillation count.

Duration controls oscillations: Number of NF-kB oscillations correlates with stimulus
                    duration, not dose; y = 0.023*x + 1.40 oscillations per minute (Fig. 3C).
                    Duration does not affect signaling range.

Multidimensional decoding: First NF-kB peak height encodes dose; ratio of second to first
                    peak height encodes distance; oscillation count encodes duration -- all
                    decodable simultaneously from single-cell dynamics (Figs. 4D-E).

Single-cell accuracy: Binary decision tree cross-validation yields 0.69-0.94 accuracy
                    distinguishing dose and distance at single-cell level (Fig. 4F).

Gene expression zones: Early genes (A20) restricted near TNF source; late genes (Casp4,
                    RANTES) expressed broadly across all distances. IRF-family target genes
                    (IRF-1, -2, -7, -8, -9) show longer-range expression than NF-kB-family
                    target genes due to lower TNF activation threshold (Figs. 6-7).

Macrophage variability: Single macrophage secretion variability directly determines NF-kB
                    signaling range (0-2 mm) and oscillation count (0 to >3) across 35
                    independent coculture replicates (Fig. 5C).


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : son_spatiotemporal_nfkb_microfluidics.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG file       : son_spatiotemporal_nfkb_microfluidics_main_dag.dot
Duration units : s and m only (h token not supported by compiler)

Duration conversions:
  Fibronectin overnight     : 720m  -> 43200.0 SECOND
  Fibroblast attachment 5h  : 300m  -> 18000.0 SECOND
  TNF diffusion 60 min      : 60m   -> 3600.0 SECOND  (mix + heat)
  NF-kB imaging 200 min     : 200m  -> 12000.0 SECOND
  Continued incubation 280m : 280m  -> 16800.0 SECOND
  RT step 15 min            : 15m   -> 900.0 SECOND
  PCR step 42 min           : 42m   -> 2520.0 SECOND

Compiler constraints resolved:
  1. Bare manifest names in mix: Fixed by adding explicit dispense assignments
     (e.g., freshMedium1 = dispense 1 units of FreshMedium) before every mix operand.
  2. Consumed-variable reuse (continuedIncub): Staged into three independent copy variables
     (chambNear, chambMid, chambFar) via three separate PBS dispenses before TrypLE mixing.
  3. Consumed-variable reuse (lysates): Probes chained sequentially into each lysate
     (rxnNearA -> rxnNearAC -> rxnNearACR) so each variable is consumed exactly once.

drain normalization: BioScript `drain` statements compile to `dispose` in IR output.
                     This is expected compiler behavior, not a bug.

Dead manifest entries: LPS_Stimulant and RAW264_7_Macrophage are declared in the manifest
                       for biological documentation of the macrophage coculture arm (Fig. 5)
                       but are not dispensed in this file. No compile error is raised.
                       Remove for cleanliness if desired.

protocol.title: Spatiotemporal NF-kB Dynamics Encodes the Position, Amplitude, and Duration of Local Immune Inputs
protocol.platform: Custom two-chamber PDMS diffusion microfluidic chip with pneumatic membrane valve
cell_lines: p65-/- NIH 3T3 mouse embryonic fibroblasts (p65-DsRed NF-kB marker + H2B-GFP nucleus marker)
p65-/- RAW 264.7 macrophages (p65-GFP reporter; macrophage coculture arm only)
protocol.objective: Quantify spatiotemporal NF-kB dynamics in fibroblasts responding to a localized TNF cytokine gradient, demonstrate wave-like NF-kB propagation and sharply defined activation zones, decode cytokine dose/duration/distance from single-cell NF-kB dynamics, and resolve distance-specific proinflammatory gene expression patterns by spatially resolved RT-qPCR

device.fabrication: Standard soft lithography; PDMS (Momentive RTV-615, 10:1 ratio) cast on SU-8 masters

photoresist.valve_regions: Positive photoresist MicroChemicals AZ40XT, 20 um thickness
photoresist.channel_and_control_layer: Negative photoresist MicroChemicals SU-8 3025, 30 or 25 um thickness

device.oxygen_plasma_bonding: Harrick PDC-001, 30 s; chip bonded to clean glass slide

chambers.source_chamber: Cytokine or macrophage loading; pneumatically isolated by PDMS membrane valve
chambers.diffusion_chamber: Fibroblast receiving chamber; 2.5 mm length along diffusion axis
chambers.sink_channel: Bottom channel continuously perfused with fresh medium at 0.33 Hz (20 cycles/min) via on-chip peristaltic pumping to simulate capillary clearance

valve.control: Custom MATLAB GUI (modified from Gomez-Sjoberg et al. Anal. Chem. 2007)
valve.tubing: Tygon ND-100-80 with metal pins; PEEK tubing VICI TPK.505

stage_incubator.model: Life Imaging Service, Basel; Nikon Eclipse Ti2 stage-top incubator box

lps_macrophage_stimulation.notes: Used in macrophage coculture arm (Fig. 5) only; not encoded in primary TNF diffusion .bs file

fibroblast_medium.base: Fluorobrite Dulbecco's modified Eagle's medium (DMEM; Gibco A1896701)

fibronectin_coating.application: Overnight coating of diffusion chamber PDMS surface; washed with fresh medium before cell seeding

reagents.cell_detachment: TrypLE Express (Gibco); 1-2 min on-chip before retrieval

lysis_buffer.notes: Ice-cold; lysate stored at -80 C until qPCR

reagents.rt_qpcr_kit: CellDirect One-Step RT-qPCR kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific)

A20_Tnfaip3.kinetics: early gene; rapidly induced and rapidly degraded upon NF-kB activation

Casp4.kinetics: late gene; slow activation, prolonged expression

RANTES_Ccl5.kinetics: late chemokine gene; slow activation, prolonged expression

imaging.stitching: 4 FOVs per chamber; custom MATLAB using detectSURFFeatures + estimateGeometricTransform
imaging.nfkb_analysis: Custom MATLAB image analysis pipeline; nucleus boundary from H2B-GFP; p65-DsRed nuclear intensity normalized to pre-valve basal level; lowess smoothing to reduce noise from cell migration/collisions
imaging.activation_threshold: 2 SDs above mean basal level per subregion

steps.name: Fibronectin surface coating of receiving chamber
steps.notes: 1 mg/mL fibronectin diluted 1:4 in PBS applied overnight to PDMS diffusion chamber to promote fibroblast adhesion. Channels washed with fresh medium before cell seeding.

steps.name: NIH 3T3 fibroblast seeding and attachment
steps.operation: flow-through seeding (abstracted as mix in BioScript)
steps.side_channel_clearance: Non-adherent cells flushed with trypsin from side channels
steps.passaging: Trypsin-EDTA (Gibco); 1:10 resuspension before 100% confluency in flask
steps.notes: Paper M&M: fibroblasts loaded at ~80% confluency; waited at least 5 h with one or two feedings. Cells stuck in other channels removed by flushing with trypsin.

steps.name: TNF loading into source chamber
steps.notes: TNF (R&D Systems 410-MT) diluted in DMEM. Loaded into source chamber with pneumatic separator valve in closed position. 100 ng/mL primary condition encoded; 10 and 30 ng/mL also tested in paper (Fig. 3A).

steps.name: Valve open - TNF diffusion into receiving chamber
steps.operation: valve actuation + passive diffusion (abstracted as mix in BioScript)

diffusion_profile.notes: TNF concentration and kinetics vary with distance (Fig. 1E, fig. S4). Far cells experience lower peak dose and later onset, extending NF-kB activation duration.

steps.paper_ref: Fig. 3B: valve opened and closed after 15, 30, or 60 min. This file encodes 60 min condition.

steps.name: NF-kB fluorescence imaging window

observation.wave_propagation: Wave-like NF-kB propagation across 2.5 mm receiving chamber (Fig. 1H, Movie S2)
observation.activation_zone: Sharply defined; activation rate transitions from >75% to <25% within 0.4 mm (Fig. 1J)
observation.activation_duration_extension: Far cells show longer activation window due to slower TNF ramp (Fig. 1I blue interval)

steps.qc_threshold: >75% of cells in near region (0-0.4 mm) must activate (2 SDs above basal)

pass.interpretation: Wave propagation confirmed; proceed to gene expression arm

fail.interpretation: No detectable NF-kB activation (device failure or TNF degradation)

steps.name: Continued incubation to 8 h for gene expression time course
steps.paper_ref: Fig. 6C: cells collected at 0, 2, 4, and 8 hours after TNF release

steps.name: Spatially resolved cell retrieval from three chip regions
steps.operation: valve actuation + TrypLE detachment + lysis buffer collection
steps.paper_ref: Paper M&M: separating valves actuated to divide cell chamber into top, middle, and bottom sections; each position purged with PBS; cells in ~2 uL droplet collected onto glass slide

steps.name: RT-qPCR gene expression measurement (3 probes x 3 regions)
steps.reaction_assembly: Probes chained sequentially into each lysate to respect compiler single-consumption constraint (rxnNearA -> rxnNearAC -> rxnNearACR; same for Mid and Far)
steps.normalization: GAPDH housekeeping gene; DeltaCT method; fold change = 2^(DeltaDeltaCT)

expected_results.A20_near_2h: Strongly upregulated (early gene); highest near source; drops sharply with distance (Fig. 6C)
expected_results.Casp4_all_regions: Upregulated across near/mid/far at 8 h (late gene; distance-insensitive)
expected_results.RANTES_all_regions: Upregulated across near/mid/far at 8 h (late gene; distance-insensitive)

steps.name: Gene expression QC gate
steps.qc_criterion: A20 signal in near region must exceed 3 SDs above unstimulated baseline at 2 h

pass.interpretation: Valid A20 upregulation confirmed; all three spatial reactions disposed

fail.interpretation: qPCR failure or no detectable induction; all reactions drained

key_findings.wave_propagation: TNF diffusion coupled with intrinsic NF-kB network oscillations drives wave-like propagation of NF-kB activity, not paracrine signaling from fibroblasts (fig. S5)
key_findings.activation_zone: Sharply defined; transition from >75% to <25% activation within 0.4 mm (<15% of chamber length) for all source doses (Fig. 1J)
key_findings.dose_controls_range: Signaling range increases linearly with log(source dose); y = 0.89*log(x) - 1.80 (Fig. 3C)
key_findings.duration_controls_oscillations: Number of NF-kB oscillations correlates with stimulus duration, not dose; y = 0.023*x + 1.40 (Fig. 3C)
key_findings.dose_duration_independent: Dose and duration are two independent, orthogonal control dimensions of the NF-kB spatial response
key_findings.multidimensional_decoding: NF-kB dynamics simultaneously encodes dose (first peak height), distance (ratio of second to first peak height), and duration (oscillation count) in single cells (Figs. 4D-E)
key_findings.single_cell_accuracy: Decision tree cross-validation: 0.69-0.94 accuracy distinguishing dose and distance at single-cell level (Fig. 4F)
key_findings.gene_expression_zones: A20 (early) restricted near source; Casp4/RANTES (late) expressed across all distances; IRF-family genes more distance-insensitive than NF-kB-family genes (Figs. 6-7)
key_findings.macrophage_variability: Single macrophage secretion variability directly translates to variable NF-kB signaling range (0 to 2 mm) and oscillation count (0 to >3) across 35 coculture replicates (Fig. 5C)

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : NF-kappaB Signaling, Dynamic Range and Stochastic Switching under TNF-alpha and LPS Stimulation
Source Link  : https://q-bio.org/w/images/c/c3/038_Tay.pdf
Paper DOI    : N/A
Journal      : IEEE EMBS (conference abstract), Stanford University
Authors      : Savas Tay, Tim K. Lee, Jake Hughey, Anne Leyrat, Markus Covert, Stephen R. Quake
Affiliations : Department of Bioengineering, Stanford University;
               Howard Hughes Medical Institute, Stanford University
Platform     : Fully automated microfluidic cell culture system
               (Gomez-Sjoberg et al., Anal. Chem. 2007, 10:1021-1028)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol encodes a high-throughput microfluidic cell culture experiment for quantitative
single-cell analysis of NF-kappaB nuclear localisation dynamics under TNF-alpha and LPS
stimulation. Using a fully automated microfluidic platform, more than 3000 NIH-3T3 cells
stably expressing a p65-GFP reporter are measured simultaneously under 8 doses of each
ligand spanning 4 orders of magnitude, with 6-minute temporal resolution over 12 hours.

The protocol addresses four key biological questions:

  A. Oscillation continuity: Are NF-kappaB nuclear localisation oscillations under TNF-alpha
     damped or continuous at the single-cell level? Extended 12-hour time-lapse confirms
     they are continuous (not damped).

  B. Dynamic range: How do response threshold, activation fraction, and response time
     scale with dose? Response time decreases from hundreds of minutes near threshold to
     <30 min at saturating doses. The standard NF-kappaB ODE model (Kearns/Hoffman 2009)
     was modified to explain this kinetic dose-response relationship.

  C. Stochastic switching and cell-to-cell variability: High-dose responses are
     stereotyped. Near-threshold doses produce stochastic switching driven by small
     fluctuations in key protein levels (IkBa, IKK), reproduced by the modified
     stochastic NF-kappaB model.

  D. Analog vs. digital signaling: TNF-alpha produces analog signaling (graded nuclear
     localisation intensity proportional to dose). LPS produces digital signaling (full
     all-or-nothing nuclear translocation even at the lowest doses). This distinction
     reflects the biological context: cell-cell communication (TNF-alpha) vs. bacterial
     infection detection (LPS).


CELL LINE AND REPORTER
----------------------
Cell line   : NIH-3T3 mouse fibroblasts stably expressing p65-GFP
Reporter    : p65-GFP (NF-kappaB subunit fused to GFP; nuclear localisation = activation)
Nuclear marker: Co-stain for automated single-cell segmentation and nuclear tracking
Software    : Custom image analysis software for nuclear localisation intensity extraction
              at each 6-min timepoint across >3000 cells per experiment
Microscopy  : Fluorescent time-lapse microscopy; 6-min imaging interval; 12 h total


REAGENTS
--------
- PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free)
- Pluronics F-127 (2% in PBS; device priming)
- Complete growth media (DMEM + serum)
- NIH-3T3 p65-GFP cells
- TNFalpha_Stock: TNF-alpha cytokine solution (near-saturating, intermediate, and near-
  threshold doses encoded as 1:1, 1:10, and 1:100 serial dilutions from stock)
- LPS_Stock: Lipopolysaccharide bacterial product solution (same three dose tiers)
- NuclearMarkerDye: Nuclear co-stain for segmentation
- ImagingBuffer: Isotonic buffer for time-lapse imaging

Dose encoding in BioScript:
  Dose 1 (near-saturating) : 1:1 dilution (1 unit stock + 1 unit PBS)
  Dose 2 (intermediate)    : 1:10 dilution (1 unit stock + 9 units PBS, chained dispense)
  Dose 3 (near-threshold)  : 1:100 dilution (two serial 1:10 steps; 18 PBS units total)


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Device Priming
  Reagents  : PBS, Pluronics F-127
  Operation : mix (300 s = 5 min)
  Purpose   : 2% Pluronics F-127 in PBS passivates microfluidic channel surfaces
              to reduce non-specific cell adhesion before cell loading.
  IR        : primingMix1[0] = mix(primingPBS1[0], primingPluronic1[0]) @ 300.0SECOND

Step 2 | Cell Seeding and Adhesion
  Cell line : NIH-3T3 p65-GFP
  Reagents  : NIH3T3_p65GFP_Cells, CompleteMedia
  Operation : mix then heat at 37 C for 120 min (7200 s)
  Purpose   : Cells loaded into microfluidic culture chambers and allowed to adhere
              for 2 h at 37 C before staining and stimulation.
  IR        : seededChamber1[0] = mix(...) @ 5.0SECOND
              heat(seededChamber1[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 7200.0SECOND

Step 3 | Nuclear Marker Staining
  Reagents  : NuclearMarkerDye, ImagingBuffer
  Operation : mix then heat at 37 C for 30 min (1800 s)
  Purpose   : Nuclear co-stain enables automated cell segmentation and p65-GFP
              nuclear/cytoplasmic ratio extraction at each 6-min imaging timepoint.
  IR        : stainedChamber1[0] = mix(stained1[0], imagingBuf1[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
              heat(stainedChamber1[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 1800.0SECOND

Step 4 | TNF-alpha Stimulation -- Near-Saturating Dose (Dose 1, 1:1 dilution)
  Ligand    : TNF-alpha
  Dilution  : 1:1 (1 unit TNFalpha_Stock + 1 unit PBS)
  Operation : mix then 12 h time-lapse at 37 C then detect
  Duration  : 720 min = 43200 s (time-lapse + detection)
  Detection : nfkbNuclearLocalizationDetection module; 720 min window; 6-min interval
  Expected response:
    - Activation fraction  : ~1.0 (all cells respond)
    - Response character   : stereotyped continuous oscillations (non-damped over 12 h)
    - Response time        : <30 min to first NF-kappaB nuclear peak
    - Signaling mode       : analog (nuclear localisation intensity proportional to dose)
  IR gate   : if tnfHighSignal1[0] > 0 -> bsbbif_2_t (dispose) | false -> bsbbif_3_f (drain)

Step 5 | TNF-alpha Stimulation -- Intermediate Dose (Dose 2, 1:10 dilution)
  Ligand    : TNF-alpha
  Dilution  : 1:10 (1 unit stock + 9 units PBS; chained as p1-p9 -> pbsMix91)
  Operation : serial dilution then fresh cell seeding (120 min) + staining (30 min)
              then mix then 12 h time-lapse at 37 C then detect
  Duration  : 720 min = 43200 s
  Detection : nfkbNuclearLocalizationDetection
  Expected response:
    - Activation fraction  : partial (between threshold and saturation)
    - Response character   : heterogeneous; stochastic switching; some cells oscillate,
                             others remain silent; behaviour varies cell-to-cell
    - Response time        : tens to low hundreds of minutes
    - Signaling mode       : analog (graded)
    - Model                : stochastic ODE (modified Kearns/Hoffman) recapitulates
                             observed switching statistics from IkBa/IKK fluctuations
  IR gate   : if tnfMidSignal1[0] > 0 -> bsbbif_5_t (dispose) | false -> bsbbif_6_f (drain)

Step 6 | TNF-alpha Stimulation -- Near-Threshold Dose (Dose 3, 1:100 dilution)
  Ligand    : TNF-alpha
  Dilution  : 1:100 via two serial 1:10 steps
              Step 1: tnfMidDoseSerial + q1-q9 -> tnfSerial1 (1:10)
              Step 2: tnfSerial1 + r1-r9 -> tnfLowDose (1:100 total)
  Operation : two-step serial dilution then cell prep then 12 h time-lapse then detect
  Duration  : 720 min = 43200 s
  Detection : nfkbNuclearLocalizationDetection
  Expected response:
    - Activation fraction  : very low (near activation threshold)
    - Response character   : rare stochastic switching events; majority of cells silent;
                             on/off switching irregular and unpredictable
    - Response time        : hundreds of minutes for cells that do respond
    - Model                : stochastic NF-kappaB model explains switching from small
                             protein-level fluctuations at low ligand concentrations
  IR gate   : if tnfLowSignal1[0] > 0 -> bsbbif_8_t (dispose) | false -> bsbbif_9_f (drain)

Step 7 | LPS Stimulation -- Near-Saturating Dose (Dose 1, 1:1 dilution)
  Ligand    : LPS (lipopolysaccharide; bacterial product)
  Dilution  : 1:1 (1 unit LPS_Stock + 1 unit PBS)
  Operation : mix then fresh cell prep then 12 h time-lapse at 37 C then detect
  Duration  : 720 min = 43200 s
  Detection : nfkbNuclearLocalizationDetection
  Expected response:
    - Activation fraction  : majority of cells
    - Response character   : digital ON (full nuclear p65-GFP translocation; all-or-nothing)
    - Signaling mode       : digital (complete localisation regardless of dose intensity)
    - Biological context   : LPS detected via TLR4/MyD88 pathway producing switch-like
                             IKK activation; bacterial infection vs. cell-cell communication
  IR gate   : if lpsHighSignal1[0] > 0 -> bsbbif_11_t (dispose) | false -> bsbbif_12_f (drain)

Step 8 | LPS Stimulation -- Intermediate Dose (Dose 2, 1:10 dilution)
  Ligand    : LPS
  Dilution  : 1:10 (1 unit stock + 9 units PBS; chained as s1-s9 -> sbsMix91)
  Operation : serial dilution then cell prep then 12 h time-lapse then detect
  Duration  : 720 min = 43200 s
  Detection : nfkbNuclearLocalizationDetection
  Expected response:
    - Activation fraction  : lower than high dose but still digital in responding cells
    - Response character   : full nuclear localisation in responding fraction (not graded)
    - Key contrast         : TNF-alpha at 1:10 gives graded partial response;
                             LPS at 1:10 gives full ON response in fewer cells
  IR gate   : if lpsMidSignal1[0] > 0 -> bsbbif_14_t (dispose) | false -> bsbbif_15_f (drain)

Step 9 | LPS Stimulation -- Near-Threshold Dose (Dose 3, 1:100 dilution)
  Ligand    : LPS
  Dilution  : 1:100 via two serial 1:10 steps
              Step 1: lpsStock3 + t1-t9 -> lpsSerial1 (1:10)
              Step 2: lpsSerial1 + u1-u9 -> lpsLowDose (1:100 total)
  Operation : two-step serial dilution then cell prep then 12 h time-lapse then detect
  Duration  : 720 min = 43200 s
  Detection : nfkbNuclearLocalizationDetection
  Expected response:
    - Activation fraction  : very low (near threshold)
    - Response character   : DIGITAL ON even at near-threshold dose; responding cells
                             show COMPLETE nuclear translocation (not partial/graded)
    - KEY FINDING          : This is the core analog-vs-digital result. At equivalent
                             sub-threshold doses, TNF-alpha gives weak graded responses
                             while LPS gives full all-or-nothing activation in a small
                             responding fraction. The digital mode is invariant with dose.
  IR gate   : if lpsLowSignal1[0] > 0 -> bsbbif_17_t (dispose) | false -> bsbbif_18_f (drain)


CFG STRUCTURE
-------------
19 basic blocks (BB1-BB19); 6 if/else QC gates; 24 CFG edges; terminal = NOP.

BB1  (main)         -- Entry: priming, cell seeding, nuclear staining, TNF-alpha high dose
BB2  (bsbbif_2_t)  -- TNF-alpha high PASS  : dispose(tnfHighStim)
BB3  (bsbbif_3_f)  -- TNF-alpha high FAIL  : drain(tnfHighStim)
BB4  (bsbbif_4_j)  -- Join: TNF-alpha mid dose dilution + cell prep + stimulation + detect
BB5  (bsbbif_5_t)  -- TNF-alpha mid PASS   : dispose(tnfMidStim)
BB6  (bsbbif_6_f)  -- TNF-alpha mid FAIL   : drain(tnfMidStim)
BB7  (bsbbif_7_j)  -- Join: TNF-alpha low dose 2x serial dilution + cell prep + detect
BB8  (bsbbif_8_t)  -- TNF-alpha low PASS   : dispose(tnfLowStim)
BB9  (bsbbif_9_f)  -- TNF-alpha low FAIL   : drain(tnfLowStim)
BB10 (bsbbif_10_j) -- Join: LPS high dose dilution + cell prep + stimulation + detect
BB11 (bsbbif_11_t) -- LPS high PASS        : dispose(lpsHighStim)
BB12 (bsbbif_12_f) -- LPS high FAIL        : drain(lpsHighStim)
BB13 (bsbbif_13_j) -- Join: LPS mid dose dilution + cell prep + stimulation + detect
BB14 (bsbbif_14_t) -- LPS mid PASS         : dispose(lpsMidStim)
BB15 (bsbbif_15_f) -- LPS mid FAIL         : drain(lpsMidStim)
BB16 (bsbbif_16_j) -- Join: LPS low dose 2x serial dilution + cell prep + detect
BB17 (bsbbif_17_t) -- LPS low PASS         : dispose(lpsLowStim)
BB18 (bsbbif_18_f) -- LPS low FAIL         : drain(lpsLowStim)
BB19 (bsbbif_19_j) -- Terminal             : dispose(lpsLowSignal); NOP

CFG topology: linear chain of 6 diamond patterns (pass/fail -> join), one per dose tier.
Each diamond: BBn -> BBn+1_t and BBn+2_f -> BBn+3_j (join carries next arm's content).


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : tay_nfkb_signaling_dynamic_range.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : tay_nfkb_signaling_dynamic_range.ir
DAG output     : tay_nfkb_signaling_dynamic_range_main_dag.dot
Basic blocks   : 19 (BB1-BB19)
if/else gates  : 6
CFG edges      : 24
Terminal       : NOP in BB19

Duration unit conversions (BioScript supports s and m only; h not supported):
  5 min   priming             ->  5m   -> 300.0 SECOND in IR
  1 min   stain mix           ->  1m   -> 60.0 SECOND in IR
  30 min  nuclear staining    -> 30m   -> 1800.0 SECOND in IR
  120 min cell adhesion       -> 120m  -> 7200.0 SECOND in IR
  720 min 12h time-lapse      -> 720m  -> 43200.0 SECOND in IR
  5 s     reagent mixing      ->  5s   -> 5.0 SECOND in IR

Serial dilution encoding:
  BioScript does not support numeric looping. 1:10 dilutions are encoded as 9 chained
  PBS dispenses (p1-p9, q1-q9, s1-s9, t1-t9, etc.) merged sequentially into pbsMix91,
  qbsMix91, etc. (pattern from moazami_world_to_chip_dmf.bs). 1:100 achieved by two
  successive 1:10 serial steps with separate PBS chains.

ASCII constraint:
  ANTLR4 FileStream defaults to ASCII; any byte > 0x7F causes UnicodeDecodeError.
  All Greek characters replaced: alpha -> alpha, kappa -> kappa, em-dash -> --.

Modules declared:
  nfkbNuclearLocalizationDetection
  cellTrackingAnalysis
  doseResponseDetection

Manifests declared:
  NIH3T3_p65GFP_Cells, PBS, CompleteMedia, PluronicF127,
  TNFalpha_Stock, LPS_Stock, NuclearMarkerDye, ImagingBuffer, FC40_Oil


REFERENCES
----------
[1] Hayden MS, Ghosh S (2004) Signaling to NF-kappaB. Genes Dev. 18, 2195-2224.
[2] Gomez-Sjoberg R, Leyrat A, Pirone DM, Chen CS, Quake SR (2007) Versatile, fully
    automated, microfluidic cell culture system. Anal. Chem. 10, 1021-1028.
[3] Tay S, Lee TK, Hughey J, Leyrat A, Covert M, Quake SR. NF-kappaB signaling dynamic
    range in response to TNF and LPS (in preparation at time of abstract).
[4] Kearns JD, Hoffman A (2009) Integrating computational and biochemical studies to
    explore mechanisms in NF-kappaB signaling. J. Biol. Chem. 284, 5439-5443.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Viral Titer Quantification by Droplet Digital PCR (ddPCR)
Source Link  : https://www.protocols.io/view/viral-titer-quantification-by-digital-droplet-pcr-3byl498p2go5/v1
DOI Link     : https://dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.3byl498p2go5/v1
Platform     : Droplet Digital PCR (Bio-Rad QX200 system)
Vector       : Recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes absolute quantification of rAAV viral genome (vg) copies per mL
using Droplet Digital PCR (ddPCR) with a TaqMan FAM probe targeting the AAV Inverted
Terminal Repeat (ITR) region. The assay partitions each PCR reaction into approximately
20,000 nanoliter-scale droplets, amplifies target sequences within individual droplets,
and reads FAM fluorescence amplitude to count positive (template-containing) and negative
droplets. Absolute concentration is calculated directly by Poisson statistics without
reference standards, making it highly precise for viral vector titer determination.

The workflow consists of five major phases:
  1. Master mix preparation (TaqMan 2x ddPCR Supermix + primers + FAM probe)
  2. Seven-step serial dilution of AAV sample (1:40 then 1:10 x6; D1-D7)
  3. PCR reaction assembly and droplet generation (Bio-Rad DG8 cartridge + QX200)
  4. PCR thermocycling (95C activation / 94C-60C x40 cycles / 98C stabilisation)
  5. Droplet reading (Bio-Rad QX200 reader + QuantaSoft), QC gating, and titer calculation

A positive control (iDreV plasmid DNA, 103 ng/uL, 7453 bp) is run in parallel to validate
master mix composition and cycling conditions before sample titers are reported. Dilutions
D4-D7 (2.5e-5 through 2.5e-8) are loaded into reactions; the linear detection window is
100-10,000 copies/uL. Final titer is calculated by averaging concentrations from dilutions
within the linear range and back-calculating genome copies/mL.


ASSAY DESIGN
------------
Target region  : AAV Inverted Terminal Repeat (ITR)
Chemistry      : TaqMan (FAM/ZEN/IABkFQ dual-quenched probe)
Detection      : Absolute quantification (no standard curve required)
Instrument     : Bio-Rad QX200 Droplet Digital PCR system

Primer Y87 (forward) : GGAACCCCTAGTGATGGAGTT  (100 uM, IDT)
Primer Y88 (reverse) : CGGCCTCAGTGAGCGA       (100 uM, IDT)
Probe (FAM)          : /56FAM/CGCGCAGAG/ZEN/AGGGAGTGG/3IABkFQ/  (100 uM, IDT)


REAGENTS AND CONSUMABLES
------------------------
2x ddPCR Supermix for Probes (no dUTP)    Bio-Rad 1863025  (2112 uL per plate)
Droplet Generation Oil                     Bio-Rad 1863005  (70 uL per well)
Droplet Reader Oil                         Bio-Rad 1863004
DG8 Cartridge for QX200                   Bio-Rad 1864007
DG8 Gasket                                Bio-Rad 1863009
ddPCR 96-Well Plate                        Bio-Rad 12001925
Pierceable Foil Heat Seal                  Bio-Rad 1814040
Nuclease-Free Water
8-strip PCR tubes
96-well non-skirted PCR plate (dilution plate)
Microseal B adhesive seal (Bio-Rad)
Positive control: iDreV plasmid DNA, 103 ng/uL, 7453 bp


MASTER MIX COMPOSITION (per reaction)
--------------------------------------
  1 unit  2x ddPCR Supermix for Probes (no dUTP)
  1 unit  Nuclease-Free H2O
  1 unit  Primer Y87 (100 uM stock)
  1 unit  Primer Y88 (100 uM stock)
  1 unit  FAM Probe (100 uM stock)
  Total master mix volume per reaction : 31.5 uL
  Sample volume per reaction           : 1.5 uL
  Total reaction volume                : 33 uL
  Volume loaded to DG8 cartridge      : 22.2 uL

Per full-plate composition reference:
  2112 uL   2x ddPCR Supermix
  1833.4 uL Nuclease-Free H2O
  38 uL     Primer Y87
  38 uL     Primer Y88
  10.6 uL   FAM Probe

Five independent master mix builds are performed in this BioScript protocol, one per
reaction (D4, D5, D6, D7, positive control). This avoids the split keyword and satisfies
single-static-assignment (SSA) constraints of the lilott8/BioScript compiler.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Master Mix Preparation
  For each of the five reactions, independently combine in a 5 mL Eppendorf tube:
    ddPCR Supermix + Nuclease-Free H2O + Primer Y87 + Primer Y88 + FAM Probe
  Mix each build sequentially (mix for 5 s per addition, 4 additions = 20 s total).
  Vortex briefly; spin down before use. Keep on ice until needed.

Step 2 | Serial Dilution (7 steps, 96-well non-skirted PCR plate)
  Use fresh siliconised tubes or low-binding PCR plate. Change tips between every step.

  Dilution 1 (D1): Add 39 uL nuclease-free H2O to row 1. Add 1 uL of AAV sample.
                   Mix 20 uL by pipetting up and down 20 times. Dilution = 1:40 (2.5e-2).
  Dilution 2 (D2): Transfer 10 uL from D1 into 90 uL H2O. Mix 10x. Factor 1:10 (2.5e-3).
  Dilution 3 (D3): Transfer 10 uL from D2 into 90 uL H2O. Mix 10x. Factor 1:10 (2.5e-4).
  Dilution 4 (D4): Transfer 10 uL from D3 into 90 uL H2O. Mix 10x. Factor 1:10 (2.5e-5).
  Dilution 5 (D5): Transfer 10 uL from D4 into 90 uL H2O. Mix 10x. Factor 1:10 (2.5e-6).
  Dilution 6 (D6): Transfer 10 uL from D5 into 90 uL H2O. Mix 10x. Factor 1:10 (2.5e-7).
  Dilution 7 (D7): Transfer 10 uL from D6 into 90 uL H2O. Mix 10x. Factor 1:10 (2.5e-8).

  Seal plate with Microseal B. Store at 4 C until reaction assembly.
  Reactions are loaded with D4, D5, D6, D7 (linear detection range: 100-10,000 copies/uL).

Step 3 | PCR Reaction Assembly
  Using multichannel pipette, dispense 31.5 uL master mix into each 8-strip PCR tube.
  Add 1.5 uL of the appropriate dilution (D4, D5, D6, D7) to each tube.
  For the positive control tube: add 1.5 uL of iDreV DNA at 2.5e-6 dilution.
  Vortex and spin down each tube twice before loading to DG8 cartridge.
  Bench temperature vortex/spin step modelled as heat at 20 C for 10 s in BioScript.

Step 4 | Droplet Generation (Bio-Rad QX200 Droplet Generator)
  Pour Droplet Generation Oil (Bio-Rad 1863005) into the oil reservoir.
  Load 22.2 uL of each sample reaction into the middle row of a DG8 cartridge.
    IMPORTANT: Pipette slowly. Avoid introducing bubbles. Use reverse-pipetting technique.
  Load 70 uL Droplet Generation Oil slowly into the bottom row of each DG8 well.
  Cover cartridge with the DG8 Gasket (Bio-Rad 1863009).
  Insert cartridge into QX200 Droplet Generator. Run droplet generation.
  Target: approximately 20,000 droplets per well (~0.85 nL each).
  Using a multichannel pipette set to 40 uL, transfer droplets from the top well of
  the DG8 cartridge to the appropriate well of the ddPCR 96-Well Plate (Bio-Rad 12001925).
    IMPORTANT: Pipette very slowly (1 uL/s). Do not tilt or agitate the plate after transfer.
  Seal plate with Pierceable Foil Heat Seal (Bio-Rad 1814040) using the PX1 Plate Sealer
  at 95 C for 5 s.

Step 5 | PCR Thermocycling
  Run the sealed ddPCR plate on a Bio-Rad C1000 Touch Thermocycler (or equivalent).
  Ramp rate: 2 C/s. Lid temperature: 105 C.

  Programme:
    Stage 1: 95 C  for 10 min  (600 s)   -- Hot-start enzyme activation
    Stage 2: 94 C  for 30 s  \
    Stage 3: 60 C  for 60 s   > 40 cycles -- Amplification
    Stage 4: 98 C  for 10 min  (600 s)   -- Droplet signal stabilisation
    Stage 5:  4 C  hold                   -- Until droplet reader transfer

  BioScript IR representation (no loop construct; cycles unrolled as accumulated duration):
    heat at 95 C for 600 s   (stage 1)
    heat at 94 C for 1200 s  (stage 2: 40 x 30 s)
    heat at 60 C for 2400 s  (stage 3: 40 x 60 s)
    heat at 98 C for 600 s   (stage 4)
    heat at  4 C for 60 s    (stage 5 hold abstraction)

Step 6 | Droplet Reader Run (QC Gate 1: Reader Validity)
  Open QuantaSoft software. Load template: ITR-Shenqin-24 (24-sample configuration).
  Per-well template settings:
    Sample name: [sample ID]  |  ABS  |  ddPCR mMix no dUTP  |  FAM  |  Ch1 Unknown
  Load Droplet Reader Oil (Bio-Rad 1863004) into the reader reservoir. Prime reader.
  Place ddPCR plate in reader with black clasps facing down.
  Run experiment in FAM/VIC mode, reading by row.
  Set amplitude threshold to 1000 in QuantaSoft.

  QC Gate (BB2/BB3) -- keyed on D4 (highest expected signal):
    PASS (readerSignal4 > 0): >10,000 droplets per well; clear FAM+/FAM- separation.
                              Proceed to positive control QC.
    FAIL (readerSignal4 <= 0): Insufficient droplets or no FAM signal detected.
                               Repeat droplet generation from Step 4.

Step 7 | Positive Control QC Gate (QC Gate 2: Assay Validation)
  Apply dropletReaderDetection to the positive control well (iDreV at 2.5e-6 dilution).
  Expected result: 300-700 copies/uL.

  QC Gate (BB5/BB6):
    PASS (controlSignal > 0): iDreV within 300-700 copies/uL range.
                              Master mix composition and cycling validated.
                              Proceed to titer calculation.
    FAIL (controlSignal <= 0): iDreV out of expected range.
                               Investigate master mix assembly and cycling programme.
                               Do not report sample titers until positive control passes.

Step 8 | Titer Calculation (off-chip, QuantaSoft)
  In QuantaSoft, identify dilutions D4-D7 within the linear detection range
  (100-10,000 copies/uL). Dilutions outside this range (oversaturated or under-detected)
  are excluded.
  Average the concentrations from dilutions within the linear range.
  Back-calculate viral titer:
    Genome copies/mL = (avg copies/uL) x 1000 / (dilution_factor x (1.5 uL / 33 uL))
  Report titer as vg/mL.

Step 9 | Cleanup
  Discard used DG8 cartridges and gaskets as biohazard waste.
  Wipe down hood and bench surfaces with 70% ethanol.
  Dispose of AAV-containing materials per institutional biosafety guidelines.


CFG STRUCTURE (BioScript)
--------------------------
7 basic blocks, 2 if/else gates, 8 CFG edges:

  BB1  main          (entry) -- Steps 1-6 (BB1 is the sole entry node)
  BB2  bsbbif_2_t    (pass)  -- readerSignal4 > 0:  dispose plateWell4-7
  BB3  bsbbif_3_f    (fail)  -- readerSignal4 <= 0: dispose plateWell4-7
  BB4  bsbbif_4_j    (join)  -- dispose readerSignal4-7; detect controlSignal
  BB5  bsbbif_5_t    (pass)  -- controlSignal > 0:  dispose plateWellCtrl
  BB6  bsbbif_6_f    (fail)  -- controlSignal <= 0: dispose plateWellCtrl
  BB7  bsbbif_7_j    (term.) -- dispose controlSignal; end

  Edges: BB1->BB2, BB1->BB3, BB2->BB4, BB3->BB4,
         BB4->BB5, BB4->BB6, BB5->BB7, BB6->BB7


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file  : vc0005_aav_ddpcr_quantification.bs
Compiler        : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output       : 7 basic blocks, 2 if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG file        : vc0005_aav_ddpcr_quantification_main_dag.dot
Modules         : dropletGenerationDetection, dropletReaderDetection
Manifests       : AAV_Sample, ddPCR_Supermix, PrimerY87, PrimerY88, Probe_FAM,
                  NucleaseFreeH2O, PositiveControl_DNA, DropletGenerationOil, DropletReaderOil

IR operation counts:
  Dispense ops  : 49
  Mix ops       : 43
  Heat ops      : 31  (in-place mutation; not SSA violations)
  Detect ops    :  5
  Dispose ops   : 15
  Branches      :  2
  Jumps         :  2

SSA strategy:
  lilott8/BioScript enforces strict single-assignment. Every variable may be consumed
  (appear as argument to mix/detect/heat/dispose) exactly once. The split keyword
  (syntax: result = split source into N) was avoided because: (a) all N output elements
  must be consumed or the compiler flags stranded droplets, and (b) correct syntax
  requires an integer literal (result = split source into N) which was missing in
  earlier versions causing ValueError in visitSplit. Instead, each manifest is used as
  a reservoir tapped by independent dispense calls; each tap produces a unique SSA token
  consumed exactly once downstream.

drain keyword:
  lilott8/BioScript has no visitDrain method (confirmed from ir_visitor.py). The drain
  keyword in .bs source compiles to dispose() in IR. Both pass and fail branch arms
  emit dispose() in the IR; only one arm executes at runtime (exclusive branches).

heat() in IR:
  heat() is an in-place mutation. The same variable token appears in multiple heat()
  calls (e.g. droplets4 through all 5 PCR stages) then is consumed once by a subsequent
  mix() or detect(). This is correct BioScript IR semantics, not an SSA violation.
  The IR counter showing N>2 appearances for heat-processed variables is expected.

ASCII requirement:
  The ANTLR4 FileStream used by this compiler calls codecs.decode(..., 'ascii') on the
  raw file bytes. Every character in a .bs file, including inside comments, must be
  7-bit ASCII (0x00-0x7F). Non-ASCII characters (em dash U+2014, degree symbol U+00B0,
  Greek mu U+03BC, arrow U+2192, multiplication sign U+00D7) in comments cause a
  UnicodeDecodeError at compile time. All such characters have been replaced with ASCII
  equivalents (hyphen, C, u, ->, x).

Duration units:
  BioScript supports s (seconds) and m (minutes) only. Hours are not supported.
  All durations in this file use seconds.

Biological scope note:
  This .bs file encodes one rAAV sample with 4 serial dilution reactions (D4-D7)
  plus one positive control. For a full 24-sample plate, 24 independent .bs executions
  would be required, or the file can be extended by repeating Steps S2-S6 with
  additional unique variable names per sample.
