description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Deciphering Microbial Interactions in Synthetic Human Gut Microbiome Communities
Source Link  : https://link.springer.com/article/10.15252/msb.20178157
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.15252/msb.20178157
Journal      : Molecular Systems Biology (2018), Vol. 14, Article e8157
Platform     : Automated liquid-handling robotic platform (Biomek) + 96-well deep-well microplate
               array; Tecan Infinite F200 Pro plate reader; Illumina MiSeq 16S amplicon sequencing


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a systematic model-guided experimental framework to dissect microbial
interactions governing the assembly and stability of a 12-member synthetic human gut microbiome
community. The community spans four major phyla: Bacteroidetes (BT, BO, BU, BV), Firmicutes
(BH, CH, ER, FP), Actinobacteria (CA, EL), and Proteobacteria (DP), plus Prevotella copri (PC).

Time-resolved measurements of monospecies and pairwise assemblages are used to parameterise a
generalised Lotka-Volterra (gLV) ODE model of community dynamics. The parameterised model is
validated against full 12-member and 11-member single-species dropout communities, and
exo-metabolomics profiling of all monospecies is performed to illuminate metabolic capabilities
and potential molecular bases of microbial interactions.

The protocol is divided into five experimental phases:
  1. Monospecies growth characterisation (M dataset, 12 conditions)
  2. Pairwise co-cultures, 1:1 initial ratio (PW1 dataset, 66 combinations)
  3. Pairwise co-cultures, asymmetric initial ratio (PW2 dataset, 15 conditions, 95:5 and 5:95)
  4. Multi-species community validation (full 12-member + 12 single-species dropout communities)
  5. Exo-metabolomics profiling (11 monospecies; DP excluded; 97 metabolites by LC-MS/MS)


SPECIES COMMUNITY
-----------------
Slow-growth species (inoculated 41 h before experiment):
  BH = Blautia hydrogenotrophica (DSM 10507)
  FP = Faecalibacterium prausnitzii (DSM 17677)
  CA = Collinsella aerofaciens (DSM 3979)
  PC = Prevotella copri (DSM 18205)
  ER = Eubacterium rectale (ATCC 33656)
  DP = Desulfovibrio piger (ATCC 29098)

Fast-growth species (inoculated 16 h before experiment):
  BU = Bacteroides uniformis (DSM 6597)
  BV = Bacteroides vulgatus (ATCC 8482)
  BT = Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron (ATCC 29148)
  BO = Bacteroides ovatus (ATCC 8483)
  CH = Clostridium hiranonis (DSM 13275)
  EL = Eggerthella lenta (DSM 2243)


GROWTH CONDITIONS
-----------------
Atmosphere   : Anaerobic (85% N2, 5% H2, 10% CO2); Coy Lab Products anaerobic chamber
Temperature  : 37 C, no shaking
Media        : Anaerobic Basal Broth (ABB, Oxoid) — rich media supporting all 12 species
Plate format : 96-well deep-well plates covered with gas-permeable Breathe Easy seal
Robot        : Biomek liquid-handling robot (community arraying and serial transfer)
OD600        : Tecan Infinite F200 Pro (384-well absorbance plate); 30 min intervals
16S sampling : ~12 h intervals; V3-V4 region, Illumina MiSeq 300 bp paired-end,
               dual-indexed primers (64 forward x 8 bp reverse; 1536 samples/run)
               Processed: PEAR v0.9.0 (merge) + USEARCH v8.0 (align, 97.5% threshold)
Serial transfer: 1:20 dilution into fresh ABB every 24 h; total experiment duration 72 h (3 transfers)
Inoculation  : Each species at 0.01 OD600 from 25% glycerol stock starter cultures


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Starter Culture Preparation
  Slow-growth species (BH, FP, CA, PC, ER, DP):
    Inoculate 200 uL glycerol stock into 15 mL ABB; 37 C, no shaking; 41 h (2460 min).
    IR duration: 147600.0 SECOND
  Fast-growth species (BU, BV, BT, BO, CH, EL):
    Inoculate 200 uL glycerol stock into 15 mL ABB; 37 C, no shaking; 16 h (960 min).
    IR duration: 57600.0 SECOND
  Purpose: ensures all species reach comparable growth phase at t=0 of each community experiment.

Step 2 | Phase 1 — Monospecies Growth Characterisation (M dataset)
  Conditions   : 12 monocultures (one per species); each at 0.01 OD600 in fresh ABB
  Sampling     : OD600 every 30 min; 16S rRNA at ~12 h (detect duration: 43200.0 SECOND in IR)
  Transfer     : 1:20 dilution (1 unit community + 19 units fresh ABB) every 24 h; 3 transfers
  Duration     : 72 h total
  BioScript    : BT, FP, EL encoded as representative monospecies; all 12 follow identical pattern
  Key findings :
    - BT, BV (Bacteroides): lowest CV; fitness least altered by co-species
    - FP: bimodal CV; receives 5 positive incoming interactions in gLV model (ecologically responsive)
    - EL: low monospecies fitness but highest ecological impact; 6 positive outgoing interactions
    - Training on M alone: median Pearson r = 0.53 (T1); monospecies growth does not predict
      multi-species community structure

Step 3 | Monospecies QC Gate
  Module       : monospeciesGrowthDetection
  Branch       : monoQCSignal > 0 -> dispose (BB2, bsbbif_2_t)
                 monoQCSignal <= 0 -> drain  (BB3, bsbbif_3_f)
  Join         : BB4 (bsbbif_4_j); PW1 branch begins

Step 4 | Phase 2 — Pairwise Co-cultures, 1:1 Ratio (PW1 dataset)
  Conditions   : 66 combinations (C(12,2)); each species at 0.01 OD600; total OD600 = 0.02
  Sampling     : OD600 every 30 min; 16S rRNA at ~12 h
  Transfer     : 1:20 dilution every 24 h; 3 transfers; 72 h total
  BioScript    : 3 representative pairs encoded (BT+FP, CH+ER, EL+BH)
  Representative pairs:
    BT + FP  : BT inhibits FP (negative outgoing); FP receives 5 positive interactions in full
               community. BT dominance expected.
    CH + ER  : +/- topology (CH inhibits ER; ER stimulates CH). Exemplar of robust coexistence
               motif (Fig 4B, 4C). Converges to ~1:1 from distinct initial conditions.
               Negative feedback loop balances disparate monospecies fitness levels.
    EL + BH  : Mutualism (+/+). Highest pairwise productivity enhancement vs null model.
  Community behaviours at 72 h (across all 51 pairs in PW2 design):
    ~50% single-species dominance
    ~24% stable coexistence
    ~12% history dependence
  Training on M+PW1: median Pearson r = 0.79 (T2); pairwise interactions are major drivers

Step 5 | PW1 QC Gate
  Module       : communityCompositionDetection
  Branch       : pw1QCSignal > 0 -> dispose (BB5, bsbbif_5_t)
                 pw1QCSignal <= 0 -> drain  (BB6, bsbbif_6_f)
  Join         : BB7 (bsbbif_7_j); PW2 branch begins

Step 6 | Phase 3 — Pairwise Co-cultures, Asymmetric Ratio (PW2 dataset)
  Conditions   : 15 pairs x 2 initial conditions = 30 community runs
  Initial conditions:
    Condition A: species A at 95% (0.0158 OD600), species B at 5% (0.0008 OD600)
    Condition B: species A at 5% (0.0008 OD600), species B at 95% (0.0158 OD600)
  BioScript    : BO+BT encoded as representative pair (both conditions)
                 Asymmetry via dispense 19 units (major) vs dispense 1 units (minor)
  Purpose      : Probe history-dependent community behaviours
  Key findings :
    - 6 of 8 history-dependent pairs linked by bidirectional negative coupling (-/-)
    - 5 of 6 mutual inhibition pairs: NOT bistable; history dependence from slow relaxation
      to monostable equilibrium (increased convergence time at higher dilution rates)
    - BU+BT: parameter set on bistable boundary; bistability not robust to parameter variation
    - Colonic transit time (dilution rate) is major variable modulating time to reach steady state
    - +/- topology (e.g. CH+ER): broader coexistence parameter regime than -/- topology (Fig 4D)
  Training on M+PW1+PW2: median Pearson r = 0.85 (T3)

Step 7 | PW2 QC Gate
  Module       : communityCompositionDetection
  Branch       : pw2QCSignal > 0 -> dispose (BB8, bsbbif_8_t)
                 pw2QCSignal <= 0 -> drain  (BB9, bsbbif_9_f)
  Join         : BB10 (bsbbif_10_j); validation branch begins

Step 8 | Phase 4a — Full 12-Member Community Validation
  Conditions   : All 12 species at 0.01 OD600 each; total OD600 = 0.12
  BioScript    : 11 chained binary mix ops to build full community droplet (compiler constraint:
                 no n-ary merge supported)
  Transfer     : 1:20 dilution every 24 h; 3 transfers; 72 h total
  Key findings :
    - Model (T3) median Pearson r = 0.85; T4 (includes full community in training) r = 0.90 (81% variance)
    - BT behaviour not fully reproduced; BO, CH show deviation at specific time points
    - Community relative abundance at 72 h correlated with human metagenomics data:
      Pearson r = 0.79 (p < 0.05) vs Balzola et al. 2010 (7 shared species)
    - BU contamination detected in BU- dropout at 47.5 h (0.4%); 2% at 72 h

Step 9 | Phase 4b — Single-Species Dropout Communities (EL- representative)
  Conditions   : 12 dropout communities (one per species removed); each 11-member
  BioScript    : EL- encoded (10 chained binary mix ops; EL_Cells dispense omitted)
  Key findings :
    - EL-, BO-, BU- show largest community assembly change (Fig 3B)
    - EL-: Shannon equitability reduced at later time points; EL promotes community diversity
    - EL-: community productivity 28% / 45% / 46% lower in growth stages 1, 2, 3 vs full community
    - EL-: growth rate reduced by 33% (stage 1) and 19% (stage 3) vs full community
    - EL impact disproportionate to its low steady-state abundance (paradox resolved by gLV network)
    - BO-: diversity higher than null (BO reduces diversity)
    - Species impact score (relative abundance + sum outgoing gLV coefficients): r = 0.67 (p < 0.05)

Step 10 | Validation QC Gate
  Module       : communityCompositionDetection
  Branch       : valQCSignal > 0 -> dispose (BB11, bsbbif_11_t)
                 valQCSignal <= 0 -> drain  (BB12, bsbbif_12_f)
  Join         : BB13 (bsbbif_13_j); metabolomics branch begins

Step 11 | Phase 5 — Exo-Metabolomics Profiling (Dataset EV4)
  Species      : 11 monospecies (DP excluded: insufficient biomass within 24 h window)
  BioScript    : BT, FP, EL, BU, CH encoded; remaining 6 species follow identical pattern
  Saturation culture:
    Duration   : 72 h at 37 C (4320 min; IR: 259200.0 SECOND)
    Volume     : 30 mL per replicate (n=3) in 4-well plates (E&K Scientific)
    Supplement : ER, FP supplemented with 33 mM sodium acetate in ABB
  Sample collection: centrifuge 6000g 5 min; 0.22 um filtration; freeze -80 C; lyophilise
  Resuspension: 200 uL MeOH + 6 internal standards (25 uM each)
  LC-MS/MS system:
    HPLC       : Agilent 1290 UHPLC
    MS         : Agilent 6550 Q-TOF, dual AJS ESI source
    Column     : SeQuant ZIC-pHILIC, 5 um, 200 A, 150 x 2.1 mm (+ 20 mm guard)
    Temp       : 40 C; flow: 0.25 mL/min; injection: 2 uL
    Gradient   : 100% B -> 50% A over 23.5 min -> 65% A, hold 6 min; re-equil 100% B
    MS/MS      : Collision energies 10, 20, 40 V; isolation window 1.3 m/z; 4 precursors/cycle
    Identification: retention time + exact mass + MS/MS vs METLIN or in-house standards
    Analysis   : MassHunter + Metabolite Atlas workflow (Yao et al. 2015)
  Threshold    : twofold change (log2 fold change, initial vs final timepoint)
  Key findings :
    - CH: largest metabolite consumer (hub in utilisation network); biomass not proportional
      to metabolite consumption -> energy funnelled to non-biomass processes
    - BU: major metabolite secretor; consistent with influential role in community assembly
    - FP: predicted to utilise metabolites from BU, BO, PC, BT, CH
      -> molecular basis of positive incoming interactions enhancing FP in full community
    - EL: metabolite profiles fail to explain EL ecological role
      -> interactions likely from biomolecular warfare or toxic metabolite secretion, not
         resource competition
    - Resource competition metabolites: methyl-5'-thioadenosine (55 pairs),
      N-methylanthranilic acid (6 pairs), dihexose (3 pairs)
    - Secretion-linked metabolites (3+ interactions): cytidine, adenine, 2-ketobutyric acid
    - Metabolite secretion sum correlated with: total biomass (Rs=0.83, p<0.002),
      community relative abundance at 72 h (Rs=0.66, p=0.02),
      negative interactions count (Rs=0.65, p=0.02), growth rate (Rs=0.74, p=0.0008)
    - Conditioned media experiments: 75% qualitative agreement with gLV interaction sign (T3)

Step 12 | Metabolomics QC Gate (Terminal)
  Module       : exoMetabolomicsDetection
  Branch       : metaQCSignal > 0 -> dispose (BB14, bsbbif_14_t)
                 metaQCSignal <= 0 -> drain  (BB15, bsbbif_15_f)
  Terminal     : BB16 (bsbbif_16_j) disposes all 5 metaSignal droplets; exits with NOP


gLV MODEL SUMMARY
-----------------
Equation     : dxi/dt = xi(li + sum_j(aij*xj))
Parameters   : 156 total (n^2 + n; n=12 species)
Regularisation: L1 (lambda = 0.0077, optimal from scan 1e-5 to 10)
Network      : 77% pairs exhibit interaction (threshold 1e-5); 56% negative, 21% positive
Topologies   : 36% unidirectional negative, 32% bidirectional negative, 26% positive/negative
Ecological drivers   : EL (6 positive outgoing), BH, CH (positive hubs)
                       Bacteroides BT/BO/BV/BU (net negative impact on network)
Responsive species   : FP (5 positive incoming; 2nd highest abundance in full community
                       despite lowest monospecies fitness)
Coexistence motif    : +/- (positive/negative) topology is significantly more robust to
                       growth rate variation than -/- (Fig 4D); negative feedback loop
                       balances disparate monospecies fitness levels
MCMC uncertainty     : Metropolis-Hastings; 670000 iterations, 100000 burnin, 5 chains;
                       90% of parameters CV < 0.5; Gelman-Rubin PSRF < 1.5 for 60% of parameters


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file  : venturelli_gut_microbiome_glv.bs
Compiler        : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output       : venturelli_gut_microbiome_glv.ir
DAG output      : venturelli_gut_microbiome_glv_main_dag.dot (16 nodes, 20 edges)
Modules (3)     : communityCompositionDetection, monospeciesGrowthDetection, exoMetabolomicsDetection
Manifests (14)  : BT_Cells, BO_Cells, BU_Cells, BV_Cells, BH_Cells, CA_Cells, CH_Cells, DP_Cells,
                  EL_Cells, ER_Cells, FP_Cells, PC_Cells, ABB_Media, GlycerolStock
CFG structure   : 16 basic blocks (BB1-BB16); 5 if/else QC gates; 5 join nodes; terminal NOP
IR verified     : All ops compile cleanly; no stranded droplets; terminal NOP confirmed
DAG verified    : Strict digraph; 16 nodes; all 20 edges resolve; no unreachable nodes

Duration conversions (BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported):
  41 h  (slow starter preincubation) = 2460 m  -> IR: 147600.0 SECOND
  16 h  (fast starter preincubation) = 960 m   -> IR: 57600.0 SECOND
  12 h  (sampling window / detect)   = 720 m   -> IR: 43200.0 SECOND
  72 h  (metabolomics saturation)    = 4320 m  -> IR: 259200.0 SECOND

Compiler constraints handled:
  - No n-ary merge: 12-member community built via 11 chained binary mix ops
  - No array indexing: all droplets are scalars; dispense 19 units resolves to single [0]
  - dispense 19 units encodes 1:20 serial transfer dilution and PW2 95% major species
  - DP excluded from metabolomics (insufficient biomass; paper M&M constraint)
  - drain vs dispose: both lower to same disposal op in lilott8/BioScript IR
  - IR note: both _t and _f branches emit dispose (compiler behaviour; biologically intentional)

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Proximity sequencing for the detection of mRNA, extracellular proteins and extracellular protein complexes in single cells
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/s41596-024-01030-x
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/s41596-024-01030-x
Journal      : Nature Protocols, Volume 19, December 2024, pp. 3568-3589
Platform     : Proximity Ligation Assay (PLA) + 10x Chromium 3' V3.1 single-cell RNA sequencing


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes Proximity Sequencing (Prox-seq), a method for the simultaneous
measurement of extracellular proteins, mRNA, and hundreds of extracellular protein complexes
from single cells. Prox-seq combines a proximity ligation assay (PLA) with single-cell mRNA
sequencing, enabling characterisation of each individual cell across three analyte categories:
proteins, mRNA, and protein complexes. The method is compatible with Drop-seq, 10x Chromium
3' V3.1, and plate-based SMART-Seq2 single-cell isolation platforms. This BioScript file
encodes the 10x Chromium 3' arm of the protocol.

The core principle is that each targeted protein is labelled with two DNA-barcoded antibody
probes (probe A and probe B). When two probes from any two proteins are within 50-70 nm on
the cell surface, a short connector oligomer bridges their oligo tails and T4 ligase produces
a covalent PLA ligation product. This product carries the barcodes of both proteins, enabling
identification of which two proteins formed a complex. PLA products are co-captured with mRNA
during 10x GEM generation using an additional U_fwd primer in the amplification mix, then
separated from cDNA by SPRI size selection (0.6x ratio) and independently sequenced.

The protocol is divided into five functional phases:
  1. Probe preparation: antibody buffer exchange, DBCO conjugation, click-chemistry
     oligo attachment (Steps 1-26; ~2 h work + overnight incubation)
  2. Sample processing (PLA): cell staining, PLA ligation, post-ligation washes (Steps 27-40; ~3 h)
  3. 10x Chromium single-cell isolation and library construction (Steps 87-102; ~8 h)
  4. Next-generation sequencing on Illumina NextSeq 500/550 (Steps 132-134; ~1-2 days)
  5. Computational analysis: cDNA alignment (Cell Ranger), PLA alignment (custom Java),
     protein abundance and protein complex quantification (Python; Steps 135-147)

The total wet-lab protocol requires approximately 16 h of work spread across several days.
Prox-seq is currently the only single-cell technology capable of measuring hundreds of protein
complexes simultaneously, with a reported throughput of 38 targets (741 protein pairs) and
an estimated maximum of ~100 targets (5,050 possible pairs) in a single experiment.


PROBE CHEMISTRY
---------------
Probe conjugation uses copper-free click chemistry (strain-promoted azide-alkyne cycloaddition):

Step 1 : Antibody buffer exchange into PBS using Amicon Ultra-0.5 concentrator (50,000 MWCO).
         CRITICAL: antibodies must be free of protein additives (BSA, gelatin) which react
         with DBCO NHS ester. Compatible formulations: azide, Tris, glycerol.

Step 2 : DBCO conjugation. Dissolve dibenzocyclooctyne-PEG4-N-hydroxysuccinimidyl ester
         (Sigma-Aldrich 764019) in DMSO; prepare 2 mM stock (molar extinction coefficient
         12,000 M-1 cm-1 at 309 nm). Mix with antibody at 1:10 DBCO:Ab volume ratio
         (0.5-2 mg/mL antibody; CRITICAL). Incubate on ice (0 C) for 60 min.

Step 3 : Purification and QC. Repeat concentrator wash to remove unconjugated DBCO.
         Measure absorbance at 280 nm (antibody; extinction coefficient 204,000 M-1 cm-1)
         and 309 nm (DBCO; extinction coefficient 12,000 M-1 cm-1) on Nanodrop.
         Target DBCO:Ab ratio: 1-10. Optimal input mass: 100 ug.
         Store aliquots at -20 C; avoid freeze-thaw.

Step 4 : Oligo conjugation (click chemistry). Combine 2 ug DBCO-Ab with equal volume of
         80 uM azide-functionalized DNA oligomers (IDT custom; Probe A and Probe B oligos
         carry unique barcodes; sequences from Vistain et al. Nat. Methods 2022).
         Incubate overnight at 4 C (16 h = 960 min; reaction can extend to 2 days).
         Store finished probes in 50% (wt/vol) glycerol/PBS at -20 C; stable >= 1 year.
         Probe binding buffer: PBS + 0.1% BSA + 0.1 mg/mL salmon sperm DNA + 6.7 nM/isotype.
         Final probe panel: 2.5 nM probe A + 2.5 nM probe B per target protein (5 nM total).


CELL LINES
----------
- PBMCs (peripheral blood mononuclear cells): primary cell line used in key experiments;
  Prox-seq discovered novel CD9-CD8 homodimer association specific to naive CD8 T cells.
- Jurkat T cells: positive control for CD147 homodimers (common, detectable as protein complex).
- NCI-H1299 or MCF-7 (user-defined): general model cell lines; any cell line accessible
  by anti-surface-protein antibodies is compatible.
- All cells cultured at 37 C, 5% CO2; resuspended in PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free) for protocol steps.
- 10x Chromium requires 20,000 viable cells input (>80% viability).


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Antibody Buffer Exchange (Steps 1-12)
  Reagents : Antibody in storage buffer, PBS (GIBCO, cat. 20012027)
  Equipment : Amicon Ultra-0.5 concentrator, 50,000 MWCO (EMD Millipore, cat. UFC5050)
  Spin      : 14,000g, 4 C; three wash cycles (500 uL, 450 uL, 450 uL PBS)
  Duration  : 1 + 5 + 5 + 10 min spin cycles (BioScript: three mix steps of 5m, 5m, 10m)
  Purpose   : Remove protein additives from antibody storage buffer.

Step 2 | DBCO Stock Preparation and Antibody Conjugation (Steps 13-19)
  Reagents  : DBCO-PEG4-NHS ester (Sigma 764019), DMSO (Sigma D8418), PBS, concentrated Ab
  Operation : Dissolve DBCO in 10 uL DMSO; dilute 1:100 in PBS for 309 nm Nanodrop QC;
              prepare 2 mM stock. Combine with antibody at 1:10 volume ratio.
  Incubation: On ice (0 C), 60 min (extendable to 120 min). BioScript: heat at 0c for 60m.
  Critical  : Antibody concentration must be 0.5-2 mg/mL before conjugation.

Step 3 | DBCO-Antibody Purification and QC Gate (Steps 20-23)
  Reagents  : PBS, Nanodrop spectrophotometer
  Operation : Repeat concentrator wash (Steps 4-12); measure 280 nm and 309 nm absorbance.
  QC pass   : DBCO:Ab ratio 1-10 (dbcoSignal > 0) -> dispose dbcoReaction; proceed.
  QC fail   : Ratio out of range (dbcoSignal <= 0) -> drain; troubleshoot scale or DBCO ratio.

Step 4 | Azide-DNA Oligo Conjugation (Steps 24-26)
  Reagents  : DBCO-Ab (2 ug), Azide-DNA oligo A (80 uM), Azide-DNA oligo B (80 uM)
  Reaction  : Copper-free click chemistry; 4 C, 16 h (960 min). BioScript: heat at 4c for 960m.
  Output    : Prox-seq probe panel (2.5 nM each probe; 5 nM total per targeted protein).

Step 5 | Cell Pelleting, Fc Blocking, and BSA Wash (Steps 27-31)
  Reagents  : PBS, TruStain FcX (Biolegend, cat. 422302), 1% BSA/PBS
  Spin      : 300-500g, 4 C, 5 min
  Fc block  : 10 min; prevents non-specific antibody binding.
  Purpose   : Prepare cells for probe staining.

Step 6 | Prox-seq Probe Staining (Steps 32-34)
  Reagents  : Cell pellet, Prox-seq probe panel in probe binding buffer
  Volume    : 30 uL probe mixture per 100,000 cells
  Incubation: 37 C, 30-60 min (45 min modelled in BioScript as midpoint).
  Purpose   : Antibody-DNA probes bind target proteins on cell surface.

Step 7 | Post-Staining Washes (Step 35)
  Reagents  : 1% BSA/PBS, 1 mL per wash
  Washes    : 3x by centrifugation and resuspension (300-500g, 4 C, 5 min each).
  Note      : If overprocessing is a concern, reduce by at least one wash.

Step 8 | PLA Ligation (Steps 36-37)
  Reagents  : Ligation buffer (50 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 10 mM MgCl2, 1 mM rATP,
              9.5 nM connector TTTCACGACACGACACGATTTAGGTC, 130 U/mL T4 ligase),
              RNase inhibitor (murine; NEB, cat. M0314L)
  Volume    : 100 uL ligation buffer per sample
  Incubation: 37 C, 30 min
  Mechanism : Connector oligo bridges probe A and probe B when within 50-70 nm;
              T4 ligase seals the nick -> covalent PLA ligation product.
  Optional  : Free oligo method (Step 38): add free oligos A and B with additional connector
              in two sequential 15-min steps to ensure all probes are measurable.
              Benefits minor for highly expressed target panels; increases overprocessing risk.

Step 9 | Post-Ligation Washes and Viability Check (Steps 39-40)
  Reagents  : 1% BSA/PBS (2 washes), PI (Invitrogen, cat. P1304MP),
              Dead cell removal kit (Miltenyi, cat. 130-090-101)
  Washes    : 2x post-ligation washes to remove excess connector and ligase.
  Viability : viableCells derived from postLigWash2 + Miltenyi kit (independently).
              stainedForSort derived from postLigWash2 + PI (independently).
              CRITICAL (BioScript): viableCells must NOT appear inside either gate branch
              to remain live at bsbbif_7_j. Only stainedForSort is disposed/drained in gate.
  QC pass   : viabilitySignal > 0 (>80% viable) -> dispose stainedForSort; proceed to 10x.
  QC fail   : viabilitySignal <= 0 -> drain stainedForSort; reduce washes or increase spin.

Step 10 | 10x Chromium GEM Generation (Steps 87-90)
  Reagents  : Viable cells (20,000), Chromium Next GEM Chip G (cat. 1000127),
              Chromium GEL beads v3.1 (cat. 1000268), partitioning oil,
              KAPA HiFi ReadyMix, dNTP mix, U_fwd primer (2 uM; CRITICAL)
  Filter    : 40 um cell strainer before loading to remove clumps (Step 88).
  Operation : 10x 3' single-cell isolation per manufacturer protocol until just before cDNA
              amplification; then add 1 uL of 2 uM U_fwd primer to amplification mix (Step 90).
  PCR       : 12 cycles (98 C 20s / 67 C 20s / 72 C 20s); U_fwd co-amplifies PLA products.
  Note      : Without U_fwd, PLA products are not amplified and are lost.

Step 11 | SPRI Size Selection: Separate cDNA from PLA Products (Steps 91-94)
  Reagents  : SPRIselect beads (Beckman Coulter, cat. B23317) x2 independent dispensations,
              Buffer EB (Qiagen, cat. 19086)
  cDNA path : 0.6x SPRI (cDNA ~1,000 bp binds beads; PLA ~100 bp stays in supernatant).
              Wash beads 2x 80% ethanol; elute cDNA into 35 uL Buffer EB.
  PLA path  : CRITICAL (Step 92): SAVE 75 uL supernatant containing PLA products.
              In standard 10x protocol this supernatant is DISCARDED; in Prox-seq it is retained.
  TapeStation QC: cDNA peak ~1,000 bp (Fig. 2c); PLA peak ~100 bp (Fig. 2d).
  BioScript SSA: Two independent SPRI dispensations (spriBeads_cDNA and spriBeads_PLA)
              produce spriMix_cDNA and spriMix_PLA as separate single-use variables.
              spriMix_cDNA consumed by elutedCDNA; spriMix_PLA flows through BB8/BB9 gate
              UNTOUCHED (not disposed or drained) and consumed at bsbbif_10_j by plaCleanup.
  QC pass   : librarySignal > 0 -> dispose(spriMix_cDNA); spriMix_PLA passes through.
  QC fail   : librarySignal <= 0 -> drain(spriMix_cDNA); check AMPure bead volume.

Step 12 | cDNA Gene Expression Library Construction (Step 95)
  Reagents  : Purified cDNA (10 uL), KAPA HiFi ReadyMix, 10x V3.1 library kit
  Protocol  : Standard 10x Genomics single-cell 3' V3.1 gene expression library protocol.
  Output    : GEX library (~500 bp; Fig. 2e); 1% vol/vol PhiX spike for sequencing.

Step 13 | PLA Product Library Construction (Steps 96-102)
  Reagents  : PLA supernatant (spriMix_PLA), SPRIselect beads (2.1x then 1.2x),
              Buffer EB, KAPA HiFi ReadyMix, 10x_SI_PCR primer (0.2 uM),
              P7_N70X_Custom2 primer (0.2 uM), nuclease-free water
  2.1x SPRI : Bind PLA products from supernatant; wash 2x 80% ethanol; elute 40 uL Buffer EB.
  PCR       : 12 cycles; 98 C 2 min initial denature; 98 C 20s / 60 C 30s / 72 C 20s;
              72 C 5 min; hold 4 C. (60 C anneal; lower than cDNA due to short amplicon.)
  1.2x SPRI : Final cleanup; elute into 40 uL Buffer EB.
  QC        : Qubit (concentration) + TapeStation (size distribution; target ~228 bp; Fig. 2f).
              Suboptimal example: no clear 228 bp peak (Fig. 2h) -> repeat 1.2x SPRI cleanup.
  Storage   : -20 C until sequencing.
  QC pass   : assaySignal > 0 -> proceed to sequencing.
  QC fail   : assaySignal <= 0 -> drain plaLibrary and gexLibrary; troubleshoot SPRI volumes.

Step 14 | Next-Generation Sequencing (Step 133)
  Platform  : Illumina NextSeq 500/550
  cDNA run  : High-output 150-cycle kit (cat. 20024907).
              Read 1: 28 cycles; i7 index: 10 cycles; i5 index: 10 cycles; Read 2: 90 cycles.
              PhiX: 1% vol/vol.
  PLA run   : Mid-output 150-cycle kit (cat. 20024904). Separate run from cDNA library.
              Read 1: 28 cycles; i7 index: 8 cycles; Read 2: 75 cycles.
              PhiX: 40% vol/vol (CRITICAL: low PLA library complexity requires high PhiX).
              Custom primers: DropPLA_Read2 (spiked into Illumina read 2 primer),
              DropPLA_i7Read (custom i7 read primer) prepared per Illumina instructions.

Step 15 | cDNA Alignment (Steps 135-138; computational)
  Software  : Cell Ranger v6.1.1+ (10x Genomics)
  Commands  : cellranger mkref (build reference genome index from NCBI/Ensembl files)
              cellranger count (alignment + gene-barcode + cell-barcode matrix output)
  Output    : Gene expression matrix; loadable in R with Read10x; Seurat/Scanpy compatible.

Step 16 | PLA Product Alignment (Steps 139-143; computational)
  Software  : PLA_alignment.jar (github.com/tay-lab/Prox-seq/blob/master/PLA_alignment.jar)
  Commands  : ReadAlignment10x -> BulidCellBarcodes -> CellBarcodeCorrection (SUFFIX=-1 for 10x)
              -> UMIMerging -> DigitalCount
  Output    : Digital PLA product Expression (DPE) matrix (text file).
  Note      : Detailed alignment guidance: github.com/tay-lab/Prox-seq/blob/master/alignment_manual.pdf

Step 17 | Protein Abundance and Complex Quantification (Steps 144-147; computational)
  Software  : Python scripts; github.com/tay-lab/NProt_data-src (Anaconda3/Python v3.8.8)
  Steps     : Import DPE matrix -> PLA object.
              calculateProteinCount -> protein_count dataframe.
              predictComplex (method='iterative' default; method='lr' for free oligo only)
              -> complex_count dataframe.
  Filtering : Double filter: (1) mRNA-based cell barcode correction; (2) filter cells with
              too few or too many PLA product UMIs.
  Output    : Three integrated count matrices (mRNA, protein, protein complex) for
              multimodal single-cell analysis in Seurat or Scanpy.
  Proximity noise: Random co-localisation of proteins within 50-70 nm without functional
              interaction; the iterative method accounts for this computationally.


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : vistain_proxseq_10x.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : vistain_proxseq_10x.ir
DAG output     : vistain_proxseq_10x_main_dag.dot
Basic blocks   : 13 (BB1-BB13); 5 if/else gates; 16 CFG edges
Duration units : BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported.
                 Overnight 16h click reaction -> 960m  (IR: 57600.0 SECOND)
                 On-ice DBCO incubation 1h    -> 60m   (IR: 3600.0 SECOND)
                 Sequencing run ~10h          -> 600m  (IR: 36000.0 SECOND)
Modules        : dbcoConjugationQC, plasmidLigationQC, viabilityDetection,
                 proxseqLibraryQC, plaProductDetection
Biological scope note: This .bs file encodes the 10x Chromium 3' arm only.
                 Drop-seq arm (Steps 41-86) and plate-based arm (Steps 103-131)
                 require separate .bs files with respective primer and PCR program differences.
                 Computational steps 135-147 (Cell Ranger, PLA_alignment.jar, Python) are
                 not encodable in BioScript; documented in comments in terminal BB13.

SSA LIVENESS FIXES (lilott8/BioScript single-use token semantics)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Fix 1 | viableCells2[0] dangling reference
  Root cause : Compiler marks any variable consumed (dispose or drain) inside a branch as dead
               at the subsequent join block; allocates a new SSA slot on downstream use.
  Previous   : viableCells was derived from stainedForSort (already consumed by detect),
               then drained in the fail branch -> viableCells2[0] dangling ref in bsbbif_7_j.
  Solution   : viableCells and stainedForSort both derive INDEPENDENTLY from postLigWash2.
               viableCells is NOT consumed inside either gate branch (no dispose, no drain).
               Only stainedForSort is disposed/drained. viableCells flows through both
               branches untouched -> remains live as viableCells1[0] in bsbbif_7_j.

Fix 2 | spriMix_PLA2[0] dangling reference
  Root cause : Single spriMix1 variable consumed twice (by elutedCDNA and by plaCleanup)
               violated SSA single-use token semantics -> new slot on second use.
  Solution   : Two independent dispenses of SPRIselect_Beads produce two separate variables:
               spriMix_cDNA (consumed once by elutedCDNA) and
               spriMix_PLA (consumed once by plaCleanup in bsbbif_10_j).
               spriMix_PLA flows through the BB8/BB9 library QC gate COMPLETELY UNTOUCHED
               (not disposed or drained in either branch) -> remains live as spriMix_PLA1[0]
               at bsbbif_10_j where it is consumed by mix(spriMix_PLA, spriBeads2).

General rule: A variable that must be live at a join block must not be consumed (dispose
              or drain) inside ANY branch leading to that join block.

protocol.title: Proximity sequencing for the detection of mRNA, extracellular proteins and extracellular protein complexes in single cells
protocol.platform: Proximity ligation assay (PLA) + 10x Chromium 3' single-cell RNA sequencing
cell_lines: Jurkat T cells (positive control for CD147 homodimers)
NCI-H1299 (as general model; user-defined primary cells)
protocol.objective: Simultaneous measurement of extracellular proteins, mRNA, and hundreds of extracellular protein complexes from single cells using DNA-barcoded antibody proximity ligation probes and 10x Chromium 3' V3.1 droplet sequencing

platform_details.single_cell_method: 10x Chromium 3' V3.1 (recommended; best trade-off of data quality, cell throughput, and ease of use)

probe_components: Antibody conjugated to DBCO via NHS ester (dibenzocyclooctyne-PEG4-N-hydroxysuccinimidyl ester)
Azide-functionalized DNA oligonucleotide (Probe A: unique barcode)
Azide-functionalized DNA oligonucleotide (Probe B: unique barcode)
device.ligation_mechanism: T4 ligase + connector oligomer (TTTCACGACACGACACGATTTAGGTC); ligation product formed only when probe A and probe B are within 50-70 nm
device.single_cell_platform: 10x Chromium Controller with Next GEM Chip G
device.gel_bead_kit: Chromium Next GEM single cell 3' GEM, library and gel bead kit v3.1 (cat. 1000268)
device.key_primer_addition: U_fwd primer (2 uM) added to 10x amplification mix at Step 90 to co-amplify PLA products
device.spri_separation_ratio: 0.6x SPRIselect (cDNA on beads; PLA products in supernatant)

reagents.oligos: Custom azide-functionalized DNA oligomers (IDT; sequences from Vistain et al. Nat. Methods 2022)
reagents.carrier_dna: Ultrapure salmon sperm DNA solution (Invitrogen, cat. 15632011)
reagents.probe_binding_buffer: PBS + 0.1% (wt/vol) BSA + 0.1 mg/mL sonicated salmon sperm DNA + 6.7 nM per isotype
reagents.ligation_buffer: 50 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 10 mM MgCl2, 1 mM rATP, 9.5 nM connector oligomer, 130 U/mL T4 ligase
reagents.t4_ligase: T4 ligase (New England Biolabs, cat. M0202L)
reagents.rnase_inhibitor: RNase inhibitor, murine (New England Biolabs, cat. M0314L)
reagents.dead_cell_removal: Dead cell removal kit (Miltenyi Biotec, cat. 130-090-101)
reagents.pcr_mix: KAPA HiFi HotStart ReadyMix 2x (KAPA Biosystems, cat. KK2601)
reagents.phix_control: NextSeq PhiX control kit (Illumina, cat. FC-110-3002)
reagents.sequencing_kit_mid: NextSeq 500/550 mid-output kit v2.5, 150 cycles (Illumina, cat. 20024904)
reagents.antibody_note: CRITICAL: avoid antibodies formulated with protein (BSA or gelatin); compatible with azide, Tris, glycerol formulations

steps.name: Antibody buffer exchange
steps.purpose: Remove BSA or gelatin from antibody storage buffer; incompatible with DBCO NHS ester conjugation
steps.notes: Same concentrator used for buffer exchange and subsequent purification after DBCO conjugation

steps.name: DBCO stock preparation and antibody conjugation

dbco_stock_preparation.qc_dilution: 1:100 in PBS; read absorbance at 309 nm on Nanodrop

steps.purpose: Conjugate DBCO moiety to antibody lysines via NHS ester chemistry for subsequent click reaction with azide-DNA
steps.notes: On-ice (0 C) incubation modelled in BioScript as heat at 0c for 60m

steps.name: DBCO-antibody purification and QC
steps.purification: Repeat concentrator wash Steps 4-12 to remove unconjugated DBCO

qc.note: Account for DBCO absorbance at 280 nm when calculating antibody concentration

steps.storage: Aliquots at -20 C; avoid freeze-thaw cycles

fail.troubleshooting: Low input mass (<50 ug) or excessive DBCO ratio (>10 DBCO/Ab); increase scale or reduce DBCO

steps.name: Azide-DNA oligo conjugation (click chemistry)

probe_panel_assembly.buffer: PBS + 0.1% BSA + 0.1 mg/mL salmon sperm DNA + 6.7 nM per isotype

steps.storage: 50% (wt/vol) glycerol/PBS at -20 C; stable >= 1 year; 4 C stable for months (antibody-dependent)
steps.notes: Two probes per target protein (A and B); probe A and probe B carry unique barcodes enabling identification of which two proteins ligated

steps.name: Cell pelleting, Fc blocking, and BSA wash
steps.purpose: Fc receptor blocking prevents non-specific antibody binding; BSA wash removes serum proteins before probe staining

steps.name: Prox-seq probe staining
inputs: Prox-seq probe panel in probe binding buffer

steps.name: Post-staining washes
steps.notes: If overprocessing is a concern, reduce washes by at least one

steps.name: PLA ligation
steps.ligation_buffer_composition: 50 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 10 mM MgCl2, 1 mM rATP, 9.5 nM connector oligomer (TTTCACGACACGACACGATTTAGGTC), 130 U/mL T4 ligase
steps.mechanism: Connector oligomer bridges probe A and probe B oligonucleotides when target proteins are within 50-70 nm; T4 ligase seals the nick to form a covalent PLA ligation product

optional_free_oligo_method.description: Add free oligos A and B sequentially with additional connector to ensure all probes are ligated and measurable even if paired protein is absent
optional_free_oligo_method.note: Improves protein expression level estimates but benefits are minor when targeting many highly expressed proteins; increases overprocessing risk for low-count samples

steps.name: Post-ligation washes and viability check
steps.operation: mix x2 (post-ligation washes) + mix (dead cell removal) + mix (PI staining) + detect (viabilityDetection)
steps.bioscript_liveness_note: viableCells and stainedForSort derive independently from postLigWash2; viableCells is NOT consumed inside the if-gate branches to keep it live at bsbbif_7_j (join block)

fail.troubleshooting: Reduce wash steps (Step 35); increase centrifugation speed for fixed samples; ensure all tubes passivated with BSA

steps.name: 10x Chromium GEM generation
steps.filter_before_loading: 40 um cell strainer to remove clumps
steps.critical_primer_addition: 1 uL of 2 uM U_fwd primer added to amplification mix alongside standard 10x cDNA primers (Step 90); without U_fwd, PLA products are not co-amplified

steps.name: SPRI size selection: separate cDNA from PLA products
steps.operation: mix x2 (two independent SPRI dispensations) + mix (cDNA elution)
steps.spri_ratio_cdna: 0.6x (cDNA ~1,000 bp binds beads; PLA ~100 bp stays in supernatant)
steps.critical_step_92: SAVE 75 uL supernatant for PLA library construction (CRITICAL: this supernatant is DISCARDED in standard 10x protocol)
steps.bioscript_ssa_note: Two independent dispense of SPRIselect_Beads (spriBeads_cDNA and spriBeads_PLA) used to avoid SSA single-use token violation; spriMix_cDNA consumed by elutedCDNA; spriMix_PLA flows through BB8/BB9 gate UNTOUCHED and consumed at bsbbif_10_j by plaCleanup

fail.troubleshooting: Check AMPure bead volume; avoid over-drying beads; peaks < 200 bp indicate adapter dimers

steps.name: cDNA gene expression library construction
steps.protocol_reference: 10x Genomics single-cell 3' V3.1; PCR cycles determined by cDNA input amount

steps.name: PLA product library construction
steps.operation: mix (2.1x SPRI cleanup) + mix (elute) + mix (PCR setup) + heat (12-cycle PCR) + mix (1.2x SPRI final cleanup) + mix (final elution) + detect (plaProductDetection)

pcr_program.note: 60 C anneal (lower than cDNA library) due to short PLA amplicon

fail.troubleshooting: Check AMPure bead volume for carryover; peaks < 200 bp indicate adapter dimers; repeat cleanup

cdna_library.read_distribution: Read 1: 28 cycles; i7 index: 10 cycles; i5 index: 10 cycles; Read 2: 90 cycles

pla_library.read_distribution: Read 1: 28 cycles; i7 index: 8 cycles; Read 2: 75 cycles
pla_library.phix_note: CRITICAL: 40% PhiX required due to low PLA library complexity; insufficient PhiX causes low Phred quality scores

steps.name: cDNA alignment (Cell Ranger)
steps.software: Cell Ranger v6.1.1 or higher (10x Genomics)
steps.output: Gene-barcode matrix (loadable in R with Read10x; Seurat/Scanpy compatible)

steps.name: PLA product alignment (custom Java program)
commands: ReadAlignment10x (extract cell barcode + UMI + probe identities from FASTQ)
UMIMerging (merge PLA products from same cell with similar UMI sequences)
DigitalCount (export DPE matrix as text file)

steps.name: Protein abundance calculation and protein complex quantification
steps: predictComplex (method='iterative' default; method='lr' for free oligo variant only) -> complex_count dataframe (Step 146-147)
steps.double_filtering: Filter invalid cell barcodes (mRNA-based correction) + filter cells with too few or too many PLA product UMIs
steps.proximity_noise_note: Proximity noise arises when two proteins are within 50-70 nm by random chance without functional interaction; the iterative method accounts for this computationally
steps.output: Integrated count matrices (mRNA + protein + protein complex) for multimodal single-cell analysis in Seurat or Scanpy

cfg.duration_units_note: BioScript supports s and m only; overnight 16h converted to 960m (IR: 57600.0 SECOND); on-ice 1h to 60m (IR: 3600.0 SECOND); sequencing run 10h to 600m (IR: 36000.0 SECOND)

ssa_liveness_fixes.root_cause: Compiler marks variable dead at join block if consumed in any preceding branch
ssa_liveness_fixes.fix: viableCells and stainedForSort derive independently from postLigWash2; viableCells is NOT consumed inside the if-gate branches (neither dispose nor drain); only stainedForSort is disposed/drained inside the gate

ssa_liveness_fixes.root_cause: Single SPRI mix variable consumed twice (cDNA elution + PLA cleanup) violated SSA single-use token semantics
ssa_liveness_fixes.fix: Two independent SPRIselect_Beads dispensations (spriBeads_cDNA and spriBeads_PLA) produce two separate mix variables; spriMix_PLA flows through the BB8/BB9 gate completely untouched and is consumed exactly once at bsbbif_10_j by plaCleanup

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.content: Buffer exchange, DBCO stock prep, antibody conjugation, DBCO-Ab purification, detect dbcoConjugationQC; oligo conjugation overnight; probe panel assembly; cell pelleting, Fc block, probe staining, washes, PLA ligation, post-ligation washes; dead cell removal and PI staining independently from postLigWash2; detect viabilityDetection

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_4_j
basic_blocks.content: dispose(dbcoSignal); oligo conjugation; probe panel assembly; cell staining; PLA ligation; post-ligation washes; viableCells (independent); stainedForSort (independent); detect viabilityDetection; split to viability gate

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_7_j
basic_blocks.content: dispose(viabilitySignal); 10x GEM generation with viableCells1[0]; 12-cycle PCR with U_fwd; two independent SPRI dispensations; cDNA elution; detect proxseqLibraryQC; split to library QC gate

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_10_j
basic_blocks.content: dispose(librarySignal); GEX library construction; PLA 2.1x SPRI cleanup using spriMix_PLA1[0]; PLA PCR; 1.2x SPRI final cleanup; detect plaProductDetection; split to final QC gate

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_11_t
basic_blocks.action: sequencing run: PhiX spike-in, NextSeq mid-output kit, seqRunMix; heat 600m at 4c; dispose(gexSeqPool); dispose(seqRunMix)

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_13_j
basic_blocks.content: dispose(assaySignal); NOP

limitations.antibody_requirement: Antibodies must be selected carefully; probes must bind targets both individually and in complex; blocking/neutralizing antibodies must be avoided for receptor-ligand complex studies
limitations.interaction_range: 50-70 nm range cannot confirm direct protein-protein contact; other proteins may bridge the two targets; use FRET (5-10 nm range) for direct contact validation
limitations.multiplexing_upper_limit: Low hundreds of targets (estimated); determined by antibody availability and cost (~$1,000 per new probe pair, including oligos reusable across experiments)
limitations.lowly_abundant_proteins: Proteins not in complex with another panel target have little chance of forming a valid ligation product; difficult to identify lowly expressed surface proteins
limitations.computational_complexity: DPE matrix must be pre-filtered to discard all-zero rows/columns before protein complex quantification; zero denominator errors otherwise

PLA_RCA_DuoLink.limitation: No proximity noise correction; commercial kit (DuoLink)

proximity_sequencing.unique_advantage: Only single-cell method capable of measuring hundreds of protein complexes simultaneously; accounts for proximity noise computationally

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Quantification of Extracellular Proteins, Protein Complexes and mRNAs in Single Cells by Proximity Sequencing
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/s41592-022-01684-z
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-022-01684-z
Journal      : Nature Methods, Vol. 19, December 2022, pp. 1578-1589
Platform     : Proximity Ligation Assay (PLA) combined with single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq);
               plate-based (Smart-seq2 / 96-well) and droplet-based (Drop-seq / 10x Genomics Chromium) pipelines


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes Prox-seq (proximity sequencing), a method for simultaneous single-cell
measurement of extracellular proteins, pairwise protein complexes (up to n^2 per cell), and
whole-transcriptome mRNAs, using pairs of DNA-conjugated antibodies called Prox-seq probes. When
two probes bind proteins that are in physical proximity on the cell surface, their oligonucleotide
tails are ligated by T4 ligase via a universal connector region, producing a PLA product that
uniquely encodes the identities of both proteins. Only ligated products are captured and amplified
during downstream library preparation; unligated probes are automatically discarded. PLA products
are read out by next-generation sequencing alongside cDNA, enabling multimodal single-cell analysis.

The protocol is organised into three experimental arms that share probe design, ligation chemistry,
and sequencing infrastructure but differ in cell type, panel size, and library preparation platform:

  ARM 1 | Jurkat / Raji T cell / B cell validation (Drop-seq, 11-protein panel)
           Validates Prox-seq accuracy; confirms cell-type-specific PLA products; measures
           protein expression correlation with flow cytometry (Spearman rho = 0.88).

  ARM 2 | Human PBMC 38-marker panel (plate-based Smart-seq2 + 10x Genomics)
           Scales Prox-seq to 741 potential protein complexes; discovers the CD9-CD8 protein
           complex on naive CD8+ T cells as a novel interaction not previously described.

  ARM 3 | Primary human macrophage TLR signalling panel (plate-based, PFA-fixed cells)
           15 NF-kB pathway surface proteins (225 PLA products); LPS, PAM, or both stimulation
           at 5 min, 2 h, and 12 h; demonstrates additive signal integration, CD36 co-receptor
           activity, and identification of signalling inputs from receptor complex dynamics.

The complete Prox-seq workflow (probe incubation through sequencing library) takes approximately
1.5-3 hours of hands-on processing per sample batch depending on the arm.


PROBE DESIGN AND CHEMISTRY
---------------------------
Each protein target requires two Prox-seq probes: Probe A and Probe B, each consisting of a
monoclonal antibody conjugated to a single-stranded DNA oligomer.

Conjugation method:
  - Antibodies concentrated and buffer-exchanged into PBS using 50,000 MWCO concentrator (EMD Millipore)
  - Reacted with DBCO-PEG4-NHS ester (Sigma, 764019) in DMSO at 10:1 v/v DBCO:antibody solution
  - Incubated on ice for 1-2 h; purified through 50,000 MWCO concentrator
  - Antibody-to-DBCO ratio measured by UV-Vis (Nanodrop)
  - 1-2 ug DBCO-conjugated antibody (3-13 uM) combined with 80 uM azide-functionalized PLA
    oligomer (IDT) in PBS; allowed to react overnight at 4 C (click chemistry)
  - Long-term storage: reaction brought to 50% glycerol/PBS (Sigma Aldrich) at 4 C

PLA product structure (119 bp total):
  5' [PCR handle] -- [UMI] -- [Probe A barcode] -- [1st half connector] --
     [2nd half connector] -- [Probe B barcode] -- [Poly-A tail] 3'
  - 20 bases hybridise to connector oligomer to enable proximity ligation
  - UMI region corrects for PCR bias
  - Two barcode regions identify both proteins in each PLA product
  - 3' poly-A tail enables capture in poly-A-based scRNA-seq workflows
  - Universal connector region allows any Probe A to ligate with any Probe B

Physical range: 53.8-73.7 nm (estimated from ssDNA/dsDNA persistence length; spans typical
protein complex dimensions, ~10-50 nm)

Ligation solution (per reaction):
  - 50 mM HEPES pH 7.5
  - 10 mM MgCl2
  - 1 mM rATP (New England Biolabs)
  - 9.5 nM connector oligomer (IDT; sequence: TTTCACGACACGACACGATTTAGGTC)
  - 130 U/mL T4 ligase (NEB)
  - Volume: 100 uL (PBMC/macrophage arms); 300 uL (Jurkat/Raji arm)

Ligation efficiency: >90% of Prox-seq probes found ligated with other probes
(Extended Data Fig. 4b), explaining high concordance with flow cytometry.


CELL LINES AND PRIMARY CELLS
-----------------------------
- Jurkat (human T cell leukemia): model T cell line for ARM 1 validation.
  Cultured in RPMI + 10% FBS (Hyclone, Fisher Scientific), no antibiotics, 37 C, 5% CO2.
  Gift from J. Huang (Pritzker School of Molecular Imaging, University of Chicago).

- Raji (human B cell lymphoma): model B cell line for ARM 1 validation.
  Cultured in RPMI + 10% FBS, no antibiotics, 37 C, 5% CO2.
  Gift from J. Huang (Pritzker School of Molecular Imaging, University of Chicago).

- Human PBMCs (peripheral blood mononuclear cells): primary cells for ARM 2.
  Purchased from STEMCELL Technologies. Thawed at 37 C; washed 3x in 10 mL RPMI + 10% FBS
  (300g, 3 min); rested overnight at 37 C, 5% CO2 in RPMI + 10% FBS before use.

- Primary human macrophages: primary cells for ARM 3.
  Purchased from STEMCELL Technologies. Thawed, washed, and rested overnight in RPMI + 10% FBS.
  Plated in 10 wells of a non-tissue-culture-treated 24-well plate before stimulation.


PROTEIN PANELS
--------------
ARM 1 | 11-protein panel (Jurkat / Raji; Drop-seq):
  Jurkat T cell markers : CD3, PD1, CD28, CD4, CD45RA, CD147, LFA1
  Raji B cell markers   : B7, ICAM1, HLA-DR, PDL1, CD147 (shared)
  Isotype controls      : 2
  PLA products measured : 169 (= 13^2 including isotypes)
  Supplementary Table   : Supplementary Table 1

ARM 2 | 38-protein panel (PBMCs; plate-based + 10x Genomics):
  Primary focus           : T cell surface markers
  PLA products measurable : 741 unique protein complexes
  Complexes detected      : 20 (plate-based); 37 (10x Genomics)
  Literature-supported    : 21 of 37 (IntAct database; Supplementary Table 4)
  Supplementary Table     : Supplementary Table 3

ARM 3 | 15-protein NF-kB signalling panel (macrophages; plate-based, fixed):
  Targets : CD14, CD36, IL-1R, IL-6Ra, IL-8Rb, IL-10R, LBP, MD2,
            MMP15, MMP16, TGFBR1, TLR1, TLR2, TLR4, TLR6
  PLA products measurable : 225 protein dimers
  Supplementary Table     : Supplementary Table 5


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

ARM 1 | Jurkat / Raji Drop-seq Validation
------------------------------------------

Step 1 | Jurkat / Raji Cell Mixture Preparation and DSP Fixation
  Cell counts    : 150,000 Jurkat + 150,000 Raji
  Centrifugation : 500g, 3 min; washed once with 1% BSA/PBS; spun again
  Plate format   : 96-well U-bottom plates
  Fixation       : 4 mM DSP (3,3-dithiobis-sulfosuccinimidyl propionate, Life Technologies)
                   in PBS; 37 C for 30 min (= 30m; IR: 1800.0 SECOND)
  Purpose        : Preserves surface protein architecture prior to probe incubation.
                   DSP is reversed later with 30 mM DTT (37 C, 30 min) before Drop-seq.
  Post-fixation  : Washed once with 1 mL 1% BSA/PBS.

Step 2 | Prox-seq Probe Incubation (11-protein panel)
  Volume         : 90 uL probe binding buffer
  Concentration  : 5 nM per pair (2.5 nM Probe A + 2.5 nM Probe B); 6.7 nM each isotype
  Buffer         : PBS + 0.1% BSA (Thermo Scientific) + 0.1 mg/mL sonicated salmon sperm
                   DNA (Invitrogen) + 6.7 nM each isotype control
  Temperature    : 37 C for 60 min (= 60m; IR: 3600.0 SECOND)
  Nonspecific binding: Minimal; consistent with REAP-seq and CITE-seq levels
                       (Extended Data Fig. 5d); no increase with larger panel sizes.

Step 3 | Wash and PLA Ligation (3h rotation)
  Washes         : 2x with 1 mL 1% BSA/PBS; 500g, 5 min each
  Ligation vol.  : 300 uL ligation solution (see Probe Design section above)
  Temperature    : 37 C for 3 h (= 180m; IR: 10800.0 SECOND); rotation throughout
  PI addition    : Propidium iodide (1 ug/mL final) added 30 min before ligation end
                   (IR: piMix at 1800.0 SECOND mix duration) to identify dead cells.
  Post-ligation  : Cells centrifuged at 500g, 3 min; resuspended in 1% BSA/PBS + 1/500 PI.
                   Live (PI-negative) cells sorted by FACS (one cell line per 96-well plate).
  DSP reversal   : 30 mM DTT, 37 C, 30 min; centrifuged at 300g, 3 min; resuspended
                   in 0.1% BSA/PBS before Drop-seq.

Step 4 | Drop-seq Encapsulation and Library Preparation
  Beads          : ChemGenes Macosko-2011-10(V+); barcoded beads
  Oil            : HFE7500 + 2% fluorosurfactant
  Droplet size   : ~1 nL
  Processing     : Droplets broken; beads subjected to reverse transcription, exonuclease
                   digestion, whole-transcriptome amplification. PLA products (poly-A tail)
                   and cDNA captured together; processed into separate sequencing libraries.
  Sequencing     : NextSeq Mid-output kit v2.5
                   Read 1: 20 bp | Read 2: 85 bp | i7 index: 8 bp
                   PhiX spike: 40% (low diversity of PLA libraries)
                   Custom primers: Read1CustomSeqB, DropPLA_Read2, DropPLA_i7Read
                   Library fraction: cDNA and PLA each receive 20% of total reads
  Alignment mRNA : Drop-seq tools v2.3.0; human reference genome GRCh38 2020-A
  Alignment PLA  : Custom Java program (github.com/tay-lab/Prox-seq)

Step 5 | Cell-Type PLA QC Detection  [QC Gate 1: BB2/BB3]
  Module         : cellTypeDetection
  Method         : t-SNE and PCA clustering on PLA product space; Wilcoxon rank-sum test
                   with Benjamini-Hochberg correction (P < 10^-40 threshold for markers)
  Expected result: Jurkat cluster enriched for PD1-CD3 (adj. P = 2.2e-55) and
                   CD3-CD3 (adj. P = 5.1e-53); Raji cluster enriched for ICAM1-HLADR
                   (adj. P = 2.7e-54) and HLADR-HLADR (adj. P = 2.4e-46).
  Pass (BB2)     : cellTypeSignal > 0 -> cell types separated by PLA products; dispose.
  Fail (BB3)     : cellTypeSignal <= 0 -> no cell-type PLA signal detected; drain.
  Both -> BB4    : Control passes to PBMC arm.


ARM 2 | PBMC 38-Marker Panel (Plate-Based + 10x Genomics)
-----------------------------------------------------------

Step 6 | PBMC Preparation: Fc Block and RNase Inhibitor  [BB4 join]
  Cell count     : 1 million rested PBMCs; all centrifugation at 300g, 3 min
  Wash           : 1 mL 1% BSA/PBS; pellet
  Fc block       : 95 uL 1% BSA/PBS + 5 uL TruStain FcX (BioLegend); 5 min RT
                   (IR: blockedPBMCs mix at 300.0 SECOND)
  RNase inhibitor: NEB; 1:1000 added to all subsequent buffers to protect mRNA.

Step 7 | 38-Marker Probe Incubation (3-Portion Serial Delivery)
  Volume total   : 300 uL (divided into 3 x 100 uL portions)
  Concentration  : 5 nM per pair (2.5 nM Probe A + 2.5 nM Probe B)
  Serial delivery: Cocktail divided into 3 portions due to volume constraints.
                   Each portion: incubate at 37 C for 15 min (= 15m; IR: 900.0 SECOND);
                   pellet; resuspend in next portion. Total probe exposure ~45 min.
                   (IR variables: pbmcPortion11[0], pbmcPortion21[0], pbmcPortion31[0])
  Post-incubation: Cells spun and washed 3x with 1 mL 1% BSA/PBS (300g, 3 min each).

Step 8 | Wash (x3) and Ligation (30 min)
  Washes         : 3x with 1 mL 1% BSA/PBS; 300g, 3 min each
                   (IR variables: pbmcWash11[0], pbmcWash21[0], pbmcWash31[0])
  Ligation vol.  : 100 uL ligation solution
  Temperature    : 37 C for 30 min (= 30m; IR: 1800.0 SECOND)
  Downstream     : For 10x experiment: cells transferred to 10x workflow at this stage
                   (dead cells removed with Miltenyi Dead Cell Removal Kit 130-090-101;
                   diluted to 1,000 cells/uL; processed using standard 10x protocol with
                   modified library prep; aligned with Cell Ranger v6.1.1 + GRCh38 2020-A).

Step 9 | Plate-Based Library Preparation (Smart-seq2) and 72C Pre-Step
  PI stain       : 1 ug/mL final; 10 min incubation
  Sorting        : Live (PI-negative) single cells sorted into 96-well plates; 1 cell/well
  Lysis buffer   : 4 uL Smart-seq2 lysis buffer per well (see Reagents section)
  Non-PFA cells  : Plates frozen at -80 C for storage.
  Pre-RT step    : Thaw on ice; incubate 72 C for 3 min (= 3m; IR: 180.0 SECOND)
  Library prep   : 2-4 uL per well used for PLA product pre-amplification; second PCR
                   attaches single-cell indexes and sequencing adaptor.
  Sequencing     : NextSeq Mid-output kit v2.5
                   Read 1: 75 bp | i5 index: 8 bp | i7 index: 8 bp
                   PhiX spike: 40%
                   Custom primers: SmartPLA_Read1, SmartPLA_i5Read, SmartPLA_i7Read
                   Minimum recommended reads: 10,000 reads/cell for PLA products
                   (diminishing returns above this threshold; Extended Data Fig. 9f-g)

Step 10 | Protein Complex QC Detection (Protein Complex Estimation Algorithm)  [QC Gate 2: BB5/BB6]
  Module         : proteinComplexDetection
  Algorithm      : Protein Complex Estimation Algorithm (iterative quadratic solver; Fig. 2a)
    Input        : Raw PLA product count matrix X (cells x PLA products)
    Step 1       : Calculate expected random PLA count f(X) from probe abundance
                   (maximum background = all proteins monomeric)
    Step 2       : Compute difference delta = observed minus expected random
    Step 3       : One-sided t-test + Benjamini-Hochberg correction (adjusted P < 0.05)
    Step 4       : Statistically significant delta -> update complex count; adjust X; iterate
    Step 5       : Non-significant delta -> complex count unchanged from previous iteration
    Convergence  : Absolute change in complex count < convergence threshold between iterations
  Key findings   : CD9-CD8 protein complex identified on naive CD8+ T cells (novel);
                   37 total complexes detected; 21 supported by literature/IntAct database;
                   CD9-CD8 subpopulation upregulates CCR7 and SELL (naive T cell markers).
  Pass (BB5)     : complexSignal > 0 -> protein complexes detected; dispose.
  Fail (BB6)     : complexSignal <= 0 -> no significant complexes above background; drain.
  Both -> BB7    : Control passes to macrophage TLR signalling arm.


ARM 3 | Primary Human Macrophage TLR Signalling Panel (Plate-Based, PFA-Fixed)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Step 11 | Macrophage Stimulation (LPS + PAM, 5-Min Arm) and PFA Fixation  [BB7 join]
  Cell prep      : Macrophages rested overnight; centrifuged 300g, 3 min before stimulation
  Stimulation    : 100 ng/mL LPS (TLR4 agonist) + 40 ng/mL Pam2CSK4 (TLR2 agonist)
                   in RPMI + 10% FBS; 37 C for 5 min (= 5m; IR: 300.0 SECOND)
                   Note: This .bs file encodes the combined LPS+PAM arm at 5 min.
                   Remaining 9 conditions (LPS only, PAM only; 2h, 12h time points;
                   untreated control) share identical downstream fixation and staining.
  Dissociation   : TrypLE (Gibco); pellet; resuspend in 4% PFA (ChemCruz)
  Fixation       : 4% PFA; room temperature 25 C for 15 min (= 15m; IR: 900.0 SECOND)
                   Purpose: Locks receptor interactions at the stimulation endpoint;
                   prevents antibody cocktail from inducing artifactual signalling.
  Post-fixation  : Spun; washed once with 1 mL 1% BSA/PBS.

Step 12 | Fc Block and 15-Marker TLR Probe Incubation
  Fc block       : 95 uL 1% BSA/PBS + 5 uL TruStain FcX; 5 min RT
                   (IR: macroBlocked mix at 300.0 SECOND)
  Probe volume   : 54 uL probe binding buffer; 5 nM per pair
  Temperature    : 37 C for 30 min (= 30m; IR: 1800.0 SECOND)
  Post-incubation: Pellet; wash 3x with 1 mL 1% BSA/PBS (300g, 3 min each).

Step 13 | Wash (x3), Ligation (30 min), and Fixed-Cell Plate Sorting
  Washes         : 3x with 1 mL 1% BSA/PBS; 300g, 3 min each
  Ligation vol.  : 100 uL ligation solution; 37 C for 30 min (= 30m; IR: 1800.0 SECOND)
  Cell sorting   : Pellet; resuspend in 500 uL 1% BSA/PBS + 1/500 PI; live cells
                   sorted into 96-well plates containing modified Smart-seq2 lysis buffer
                   (6 uL/well with proteinase K; see Reagents section)
  Fixed-cell protocol:
    Step 1       : 56 C for 60 min (= 60m; IR: 3600.0 SECOND) -- proteinase K digestion
    Step 2       : 95 C for 10 min (= 10m; IR: 600.0 SECOND) -- proteinase K inactivation
    Storage      : -80 C; plates can be thawed on ice and proceed directly to library prep
  Library prep   : Same as ARM 2 plate-based protocol (SmartPLA primers, NextSeq)

Step 14 | Macrophage TLR Signalling QC Detection  [QC Gate 3: BB8/BB9]
  Module         : macrophageSignalDetection
  Method         : Logistic regression classifier trained on PLA product levels (Fig. 6a/b)
  Best time point: 2h (AUC = 0.82 +/- 0.08; 5-fold cross-validation)
  Top feature    : TLR2-TLR2 PLA product (highest logistic regression coefficient for LPS
                   vs PAM classification; Fig. 6b)
  CD36 activity  : Low-variance PLA products all contain CD36 barcode post-stimulation;
                   new CD36 complexes appear at 5 min post-LPS; CD36 co-receptor for
                   both TLR2 and TLR4 confirmed (Fig. 6c-f)
  Additivity     : LPS+PAM combined stimulation shows additive (non-synergistic) response
                   in both PLA products and protein levels; consistent with live-cell
                   NF-kB microscopy studies (ref. 34: Kellogg et al., Cell Rep. 2017)
  Pass (BB8)     : macrophageSignal > 0 -> TLR complexes and classifier signal detected;
                   dispose macroPlated.
  Fail (BB9)     : macrophageSignal <= 0 -> no receptor complex signal above baseline; drain.
  Both -> BB10   : Terminal node; dispose macrophageSignal; NOP.

-------------------------

Compiler        : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based; github.com/lilott8/BioScript)

Verified IR behaviours:
  - All heat() durations compiled correctly from m tokens to SECOND (confirmed above)
  - pbmcProbesMix1[0] correctly reused across all three portion mix steps (IR lines 16, 18, 20)
    representing the shared probe reagent in the serial delivery design
  - Both pass and fail branches in IR emit dispose() for all three QC gates; drain in .bs
    source is resolved to dispose() in IR by the lilott8/BioScript compiler -- known

  cellTypeDetection          -- t-SNE/PCA clustering + Wilcoxon rank-sum test on PLA space

algorithm.name: Protein Complex Estimation Algorithm
algorithm.input: Raw PLA product count matrix X (cells x PLA products)
algorithm.step1: Calculate expected random PLA count f(X) for each complex from probe abundance
algorithm.step2: Compute difference delta = observed - expected random
algorithm.step3: One-sided t-test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction (adjusted p < 0.05 threshold)
algorithm.step4: If significant: update complex count with current estimate; adjust X; iterate
algorithm.step5: If not significant: protein complex count unchanged from previous iteration
algorithm.convergence: Absolute change in complex count between successive iterations below threshold
