description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Macrophage memory emerges from coordinated transcription factor and chromatin dynamics
Source Link  : https://www.cell.com/cell-systems/pdfExtended/S2405-4712(25)00004-3
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cels.2025.101171
Journal      : Cell Systems, 2025, Vol. 16, Article 101171
Platform     : Automated microfluidic live-cell imaging (PDMS multilayer, 64-chamber device) +
               off-chip ATAC-seq (Illumina NovaSeq SP) + off-chip RNA-seq (Illumina NextSeq550)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a multi-modal experimental pipeline for profiling innate immune memory
in primary bone-marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) from RelA(mVenus/mVenus) (RelA^V/V) transgenic
mice. RelA is the canonical NF-kB transcription factor (TF); its endogenous mVenus tag enables
single-cell live imaging of nuclear translocation dynamics as a direct readout of inflammatory
signalling state.

The protocol is divided into five functional phases:
  1. BMDM differentiation and microfluidic device preparation
  2. Systematic sequential inflammatory ligand stimulation screen (80 conditions;
     two representative arms encoded: polyI:C -> TNF-a and CpG -> TNF-a)
  3. Live-cell NF-kB dynamics imaging and QC gating
  4. ATAC-seq chromatin accessibility profiling (single and sequential stimulus conditions)
  5. RNA-seq transcriptomic profiling and synergy/antagonism classification

A deep-learning multilayer perceptron (MLP) model integrating NF-kB dynamics features (48)
and chromatin accessibility + TF motif features (133) achieves 72.8% accuracy in predicting
memory-conditioned gene expression across four expression classes -- an improvement of >30%
over random assignment (38.7%). The work demonstrates that inflammatory memory is encoded at
two levels: reprogramming of the NF-kB signalling network (network memory) and remodelling of
the chromatin accessibility landscape (chromatin memory), and that both are required for full
predictive power.


MOUSE MODEL
-----------
Strain     : RelA(mVenus/mVenus) C57BL/6J (RelA^V/V); endogenous mVenus-RelA knock-in
Age        : 6-12 weeks (BMDMs); 6-8 weeks (peritoneal macrophage / endotoxemia experiments)
Sex        : Male and female
Housing    : Specific pathogen-free (University of Chicago; UCLA)
Ethics     : NIH Guide for Care and Use of Laboratory Animals; IACUC approval (U Chicago / UCLA)
Reference  : Adelaja et al., Immunity 2021 (original RelA^V/V line description)


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Type       : PDMS multilayer microfluidic device; 64 independent cell-culture chambers; 14 inputs
Control    : Electronically actuated pneumatic solenoid valves; custom MATLAB graphical interface
             or pre-written automation scripts
Tubing     : PEEK (VICI); input pressure 4 psi to minimise cell shearing during feeding
Microscope : Nikon Ti2 epifluorescence; 20x magnification
Camera     : Hamamatsu ORCA-Flash4.0 V2
Channels   : mVenus-RelA (508 nm excitation, 1 s exposure); Hoechst (395 nm, 50 ms exposure)
Interval   : 6-min imaging frames; total window 8-16 h per experiment
Environment: Life Imaging Services apparatus; 37 C / 5% CO2 / 98% humidity
Coating    : 0.2-0.4 mg/mL human fibronectin (R&D Systems 1918-FN) in PBS; overnight coat;
             flushed with complete media before cell loading
Master mold: Silicon wafer; previously published design (Son et al., Sci Signal 2021)

In vivo model (peritoneal macrophages):
  LPS dose : 12.5 mg/kg i.p. in PBS (sublethal endotoxemia)
  Timepoint: 4 h post-injection; peritoneal lavage (ice-cold PBS + 1% FBS + 2 mM EDTA)
  Isolation: Negative selection via Macrophage Isolation Kit (Miltenyi Biotec 130-110-434),
             MACS MS system
  Result   : TNF-a response significantly attenuated; LPS response completely abolished
             vs sham PBS-injected littermates (3 independent pairs)


CULTURE CONDITIONS
------------------
Complete macrophage culture media (RPMI-based):
  RPMI-1640 base
  10% heat-inactivated FBS (Omega)
  1% penicillin/streptomycin (Lonza/Corning)
  1% NEAA (Corning)
  1% HEPES (Gibco/Corning)
  1% sodium pyruvate (Corning)
  1% L-glutamine (Fisher/Corning)
  0.1% beta-mercaptoethanol (Gibco)
  Supplement: 20 ng/mL recombinant murine m-CSF (Peprotech 315-02-10UG)

Live-cell imaging media: phenol-red-free RPMI (Gibco) to minimise background fluorescence.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | BMDM Differentiation (Days 0-7)
  Source     : Femurs and tibias of 6-12 week old RelA^V/V mice
  Protocol   : Bone marrow cells cultured in complete media + 20 ng/mL m-CSF for 7-9 days
  Feed days  : Day 2, Day 4, Day 6 (fresh complete media + m-CSF added)
  Day 7 lift : Wash with PBS; lift adherent BMDMs with 10 mM EDTA (Fisher) in PBS (Gibco)
  Resuspension: 10^7 cells/mL in phenol-red-free RPMI for device loading
  BioScript  : Three sequential culture_D2/D4/D6 mix operations (2880m each = 48 h each);
               lift modelled as mix with PBS (1440m)

Step 2 | Microfluidic Device Preparation
  Coating    : 0.2-0.4 mg/mL fibronectin in PBS; fill chambers; overnight (480m in BioScript)
  Flush      : Complete media; 10 min (10m in BioScript)
  Mount      : Nikon Ti2; set to 37 C / 5% CO2 / 98% humidity before cell loading

Step 3 | Hoechst Staining and Cell Loading
  Stain      : 1 uM Hoechst 33342 in complete media; 5 min (5m); wash with complete media
  Load       : Cells loaded into device; adhere ~30 min before imaging starts
  Tracking   : >99% cell tracking accuracy over 8-h intervals (Video S3, paper supplemental)
  BioScript  : deviceWithCells_arm1 (Arm 1: polyI:C -> TNFa chambers)
               deviceWithCells_arm2 (Arm 2: CpG -> TNFa chambers; separate chamber set)
               NOTE: These are split variables (FIX #3) to prevent double-consumption in IR.

Step 4 | Sequential Ligand Stimulation Screen (80 conditions; 2 arms encoded)
  Design     : Ligand A (identity x dose x duration) -> Ligand B (TNF-a or LPS)
               6 ligands A x 3-4 doses x 2 durations (4h, 8h) x 2 Ligand B = 80 conditions
  Delivery   : Ligands diluted in complete media + m-CSF immediately before use;
               stored on ice; delivered via PEEK tubing at 4 psi
  Controls   : Positive: media -> 10 ng/mL TNFa; media -> 1 ng/mL LPS
               Negative: complete media only
  Replicates : > 300 individual cells per condition; >= 2 independent preparations

  Arm 1 (PRIMING): polyI:C -> TNF-a
    Ligand A : polyI:C (HMW, Invivogen tlrl-pic); 300 ng/mL in complete media + m-CSF
               Duration: 4 h (240 min) via channel perfusion
               Pathway : TLR3/TRIF -> NF-kB activation
               Effect  : Priming; normalised AUC > 1 (> naive Ligand B response)
    Ligand B : TNF-a (R&D Systems 410-MT-010/CF); 10 ng/mL; 4 h (240 min)
               NF-kB Nuc/Cyto ratio tracked at 6-min intervals throughout

  Arm 2 (TOLERANCE): CpG -> TNF-a
    Ligand A : CpG (ODN 1668, Invivogen tlrl-1668); 100 nM in complete media + m-CSF
               Duration: 4 h (240 min) via channel perfusion
               Pathway : TLR9/MyD88 -> NF-kB activation
               Effect  : Tolerance; normalised AUC < 1 (< naive Ligand B response)
    Ligand B : TNF-a; 10 ng/mL; 4 h (240 min)

  Other ligands in full screen (not encoded in .bs; same structural pattern):
    LPS (Invivogen tlrl-3pelps): 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3 ng/mL; tolerising
    TNF-a (R&D 410-MT-010/CF) : 1, 3, 10, 30 ng/mL; tolerising (TNF self-tolerance only)
    PAM2CSK4 (Invivogen)       : 30, 100, 300 pg/mL; tolerising
    IL-1b (R&D 401-ML-010/CF)  : 3, 10, 30 ng/mL; largely indistinguishable from naive

Step 5 | NF-kB Dynamics Imaging and Analysis (Protocol 3)
  Module     : nfkbDynamicsDetection (BioScript); 240m (4h) detect window
  Readout    : RelA-mVenus nuclear/cytoplasmic (Nuc/Cyto) ratio per cell per frame
  Processing : MATLAB 2021a; custom code (GitHub: taylab/macrophage_memory)
               Flat field + dark frame correction
               Hoechst-based nuclear segmentation and multi-frame cell tracking
               Background subtraction from cell-free image regions
               Trace filtering: remove dead, divided, or artefact cells
  Metrics    :
    AUC          : Trapezoidal approximation over 240 min Ligand B window
    Early AUC    : First 120 min (20 frames)
    Late AUC     : Last 120 min (20 frames)
    Max amplitude: Index of max from loess-smoothed trace (3-frame window, min prominence 0.1);
                   Nuc/Cyto ratio at that index from unsmoothed trace
    Peak timing  : First frame at half-maximal amplitude
    Normalisation: AUC' (memory-conditioned) / AUC_0 (mean naive Ligand B AUC)
  Memory classification:
    Normalised AUC > 1 -> priming
    Normalised AUC < 1 -> tolerance
  Mutual information:
    Method : Jetka et al. 2019, PLOS Comp Biol (software package MIToolbox)
    Input  : Dynamic vector of 20 evenly-spaced timepoints over 4 h stimulus interval
    Range  : 0 bits (indistinguishable) to 1 bit (fully distinguishable)
    Finding: Up to 0.9 bits MI between polyI:C-primed vs naive TNF-a responses;
             dynamic trace MI >> single-feature (max amplitude) MI across all conditions

  QC gate (BB2/BB3):
    Pass (BB2): nfkbPrimingSignal > 0 -> dispose(stimulatedArmB)
    Fail (BB3): nfkbPrimingSignal <= 0 -> drain(stimulatedArmB)

Step 6 | ATAC-seq Chromatin Accessibility Profiling (Protocol 4)
  Replating  : 7.5e5 BMDMs/well in 6-well plate; overnight rest in complete media + m-CSF
  Stimulation: Single stimulus (polyI:C 1 ug/mL, CpG 100 nM, LPS 1 ng/mL, TNF-a 10 ng/mL);
               4 h each. Sequential conditions (polyI:C/CpG -> TNF-a/LPS; 4h + 4h).
               Representative encoded in .bs: polyI:C single stimulus (1 ug/mL, 240m)
  Cell lift  : Accutase (ThermoFisher) + gentle scraping; 5e4 cells per reaction
  Nuclei isolation:
    Lysis buffer: 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5 / 3 mM MgCl2 / 10 mM NaCl / 0.1% IGEPAL CA-630
    Temperature : 4 C (cold lysis, on ice)
    Centrifugation: 10 min at 500 x g (BioScript: heat at 4c for 10m)
  Transposase reaction:
    Mix: 25 uL 2X TD Buffer + 2.5 uL TD Enzyme 1 (Illumina) + 22.5 uL nuclease-free water
    Conditions: 37 C, 30 min, 800 rpm shaking (BioScript: heat at 37c for 30m)
    Purification: MinElute PCR purification kit (Qiagen)
  PCR amplification:
    Primers  : Illumina Nextera sequencing primers
    Extension: 72 C initial (5 min); cycles: 98C/30s -> 63C/30s -> 72C/1min (~12 cycles)
    BioScript: heat at 72c for 30m (simplified PCR hold abstraction)
    Pool and sequence on Illumina NovaSeq SP, 50 bp paired-end
  Bioinformatics:
    Alignment        : bowtie2 v2.2.5 (mm10); MAPQ > 30; --very-sensitive --non-deterministic
    Deduplication    : Picard MarkDuplicates v2.18.29
    Peak calling     : MACS3 v3.0.0b1; FDR 0.01; -f BAMPE; -g mm; --nomodel
    Peak merging     : Iterative overlap peak merging (Corces et al. 2018, Science)
    Quantification   : featureCounts (R/Bioconductor)
    Differential acc.: edgeR + limma; vs media control
    Motif enrichment : monaLisa (R/Bioconductor) with JASPAR2022 database
    Peak annotation  : ChIPseeker (R/Bioconductor)
    Track visualisation: Rtracklayer (R/Bioconductor)
  Data deposited: GEO GSE261647

  Key chromatin findings:
    - polyI:C and CpG produce distinct chromatin accessibility patterns (Fig 5B)
    - Shared motifs: kB (RelA, NFKB1/2) and AP-1 (Fos, Jun) in all upregulated groups
    - polyI:C-specific: ISRE (Irf3, Irf8, Irf9) motifs co-occur with RelA peaks
    - CpG-specific: c/EBP (beta, gamma) motifs co-occur with RelA peaks
    - Sequential stimuli: chromatin landscape primarily encodes FIRST stimulus identity
      (Spearman r ~0.79 with first-stimulus-only vs ~0.37-0.44 with second-stimulus-only)

  QC gate (BB5/BB6):
    Pass (BB5): atacSignal > 0 -> dispose(atacLibrary)
    Fail (BB6): atacSignal <= 0 -> drain(atacLibrary)

Step 7 | RNA-seq Transcriptomic Profiling (Protocol 5)
  Replating  : 1.5e5 BMDMs/well in 24-well plate; overnight rest in complete media + m-CSF
  Conditions : polyI:C -> TNF-a; CpG -> TNF-a; polyI:C -> LPS; CpG -> LPS
               (4h Ligand A -> aspirate -> 4h Ligand B -> aspirate -> RLT lysis)
               Representative encoded in .bs: polyI:C -> TNF-a
  Replicates : Triplicate (n=3 per condition)
  Lysis      : RLT buffer (Qiagen) + 1% beta-mercaptoethanol
  RNA extraction: Dynabeads (Invitrogen)
  RT         : Maxima HMinus RT (Thermo Fisher); poly-dT oligo + TSO
               (5'-AAGCAGTGGTATCAACGCAGAGTGAATRGGG-3'); 55 C, 60 min
               BioScript: heat at 55c for 60m
  2nd strand : KAPA HiFi (Roche); primer: 5'-AAGCAGTGGTATCAACGCAGAGT-3'; 1 cycle
  Purification: Ampure XP beads (Beckman Coulter)
  Library prep: Nextera XT (Illumina FC-131-1024); mean fragment size 400-600 bp
  Sequencing : NextSeq550 (Illumina), NextSeq 500/550 high output kit v2 (cat. 20024906)
  Bioinformatics:
    Alignment        : STAR (GRCm38/mm10 reference); default parameters
    Quantification   : featureCounts (R/Bioconductor)
    Differential exp.: edgeR + limma; FDR < 0.01; fold change > 1 vs naive
    Pathway viz.     : Pathview (R/Bioconductor; KEGG mmu04064)
    Overrepresentation: gProfiler (GO:BP and KEGG databases)
    TF enrichment    : ChEA3 (ENCODE ChIP-seq library)
  Data deposited: GEO GSE260996

  Synergy/antagonism classification:
    Formula  : DAB_memory = [AB - (B + dAB + dB)] / (B + dAB + dB)
               AB  = expression under sequential A+B stimulation
               B   = naive media-treated expression
               dAB = change from A-only (A followed by media)
               dB  = change from B-only
    Threshold: synergy if DAB_memory > 0.25; antagonism if DAB_memory < -0.25
  Key findings:
    polyI:C->TNFa: 572 synergistic / 394 antagonistic transcripts
    CpG->TNFa    : 214 synergistic / 366 antagonistic transcripts
    polyI:C->LPS : 800 synergistic / 478 antagonistic transcripts
    CpG->LPS     : 777 synergistic / 630 antagonistic transcripts
    Synergistic genes enriched for NF-kB and TNF signalling (priming) / immune response (all)
    Antagonistic genes enriched for cell adhesion, signal transduction, NF-kB (tolerance)

  QC gate (BB8/BB9):
    Pass (BB8): rnaSignal > 0 -> dispose(rnaLibrary)
    Fail (BB9): rnaSignal <= 0 -> drain(rnaLibrary)


DEEP LEARNING MODEL
-------------------
Architecture : Multilayer perceptron (MLP); TensorFlow framework (Abadi et al. 2016, arXiv)
Input        : 181 features per gene per condition
               133 chromatin features: peak accessibility (CPM) and binding motif counts for
               18 TFs across 3 most proximal ATAC peaks in proximal promoter
               (-1500 to +500 bp from TSS) and distal promoter (-3000 to -1500 / +500 to +3000
               bp from TSS); includes chromatin regulators without motifs (EZH2, HDAC, NELFE)
               48 NF-kB features: peak height, AUC, and activation time per stimulus condition
Output       : 4-class gene expression classification
               Class 1: downregulated (< 0.66x naive)
               Class 2: unchanged (0.87-1.5x naive)
               Class 3: upregulated (3-10x naive)
               Class 4: highly upregulated (>= 20x naive)
Layers       : 2-3 hidden layers; layer 1 = n_input nodes; subsequent = half/quarter prior
Regularisation: 10% dropout after each layer
Activation   : ReLU
Optimiser    : Adam
Validation   : 5-fold cross-validation; 8894 total samples (genes x conditions)
Accuracy     : Combined (chromatin + NF-kB): 72.8%
               Random baseline              : 38.7%
               NF-kB features only          : 61.8%
               Chromatin features only      : 64.7%
               Best 4-motif subset          : 51.2%
Top motifs   : RelA (present in all top-10 motif combinations) > Fos (AP-1) > Stat1/Stat2 >
               c/EBPD > Irf3 > Irf7 > Irf8
Code         : GitHub: taylab/macrophage_memory; DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.14337874


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : wang2025_macrophage_memory.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based; github.com/lilott8/BioScript)
IR output      : wang2025_macrophage_memory.ir
DAG output     : wang2025_macrophage_memory_main_dag.dot
Basic blocks   : 10 (BB1-BB10)
CFG edges      : 12
if/else gates  : 3 (NF-kB QC gate / ATAC QC gate / RNA-seq QC gate)
Modules (3)    : nfkbDynamicsDetection, atacSeqDetection, rnaSeqDetection
Manifests (17) : BoneMarrowCells, PBS, CompleteMCM, MCSF, Fibronectin, HoechstStain,
                 LPS, TNFa, PolyIC, CpG, PAM2CSK4, IL1b, Accutase,
                 TransposaseReactionMix, ATACLibraryPrimers, NexteraXTKit, RLT_Buffer

Duration unit conversions (BioScript supports s and m only; h not supported):
  2880m = 48 h  (BMDM feed intervals D2/D4/D6)         IR: 172800.0 SECOND
  1440m = 24 h  (Day 7 rest post-lift)                  IR: 86400.0 SECOND
  480m  = 8 h   (overnight device coating / RNA plate rest) IR: 28800.0 SECOND
  240m  = 4 h   (ligand stimulation / NF-kB detection)  IR: 14400.0 SECOND
  60m   = 1 h   (reverse transcription)                 IR: 3600.0 SECOND
  30m   = 30 min (transposase / PCR heat steps)         IR: 1800.0 SECOND
  10m   = 10 min (nuclei lysis centrifugation at 4 C)   IR: 600.0 SECOND
  5m    = 5 min  (Hoechst stain / RLT lysis mix)        IR: 300.0 SECOND
  30s   = 30 s   (all three detect calls)               IR: 30.0 SECOND
  5s    = 5 s    (reagent mixing / preparation steps)   IR: 5.0 SECOND
  2s    = 2 s    (cell loading step)                    IR: 2.0 SECOND

Fixes applied (v2 -- confirmed clean in post-compile IR/DOT review):
  FIX #1 : Removed module viabilityDetection (declared but never referenced in any detect call;
            dead code; risk of module-resolution warning in strict compiler mode)
  FIX #2 : Removed manifest TrizolReagent (declared but never referenced in any dispense call;
            RNA extraction uses Dynabeads + RLT_Buffer, both correctly manifested)
  FIX #3 : Split deviceWithCells into deviceWithCells_arm1 and deviceWithCells_arm2.
            Original code caused both stimulatedArmA (polyI:C arm) and stimulatedCpgA (CpG arm)
            to consume deviceWithCells1[0] in the IR -- a double-consumption that would fail
            under stricter compiler modes. Each arm now consumes a distinct IR slot, reflecting
            the separate physical chamber sets on the 64-chamber device.

Biological scope note:
  The 80-condition ligand screen (Figures 1-3) is represented by two arms:
  polyI:C -> TNFa (priming) and CpG -> TNFa (tolerance). All other ligand identity / dose /
  duration combinations follow the same structural pattern and would each require a separate
  .bs file or a parameterised extension of this one.
  The ATAC-seq (Protocol 4) and RNA-seq (Protocol 5) protocols each encode one representative
  condition (polyI:C single-stimulus for ATAC; polyI:C -> TNFa for RNA-seq). All other
  conditions in the paper follow the same dispense -> mix -> heat -> detect block structure.

Data availability:
  RNA-seq  : GEO GSE260996
  ATAC-seq : GEO GSE261647
  NF-kB trace data: Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.14337874

protocol.title: Macrophage memory emerges from coordinated transcription factor and chromatin dynamics
protocol.platform: Automated microfluidic live-cell imaging + off-chip ATAC-seq and RNA-seq
protocol.cell_type: Primary bone-marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) from RelA(mVenus/mVenus) C57BL/6J transgenic mice
protocol.objective: Systematic profiling of innate immune memory in primary macrophages through sequential inflammatory ligand stimulation, live-cell NF-kB dynamics imaging, chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), and transcriptomic (RNA-seq) profiling; deep-learning prediction of memory-conditioned gene expression

device.control: Pneumatic solenoid valves driven by custom MATLAB graphical interface

mouse_model.fluorescent_tag: mVenus fused to endogenous RelA (NF-kB subunit)

LPS.full_name: Ultrapure LPS from E. coli O111:B4

reagents.ligand_storage: -80 C; reconstituted in ultrapure water; single-use aliquots
reagents.ligand_delivery: Diluted in complete media + 20 ng/mL m-CSF immediately before use; stored on ice; 4 psi via PEEK tubing

atac_seq_reagents.lysis_buffer: 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5, 3 mM MgCl2, 10 mM NaCl, 0.1% IGEPAL CA-630
atac_seq_reagents.transposase_mix: 25 uL 2X TD Buffer (Illumina) + 2.5 uL TD Enzyme 1 (Illumina) + 22.5 uL nuclease-free water

rna_seq_reagents.sequencing_platform: NextSeq550 (Illumina), NextSeq 500/550 high output kit v2

steps.name: BMDM differentiation — initial seeding
steps.notes: Bone marrow isolated from femurs and tibias of 6-12 week old RelA^V/V mice. Seeded in complete RPMI + 20 ng/mL m-CSF to initiate macrophage differentiation.

steps.name: BMDM differentiation — Day 2 feed
steps.notes: Fresh complete media + m-CSF added on Day 2.

steps.name: BMDM differentiation — Day 4 feed
steps.notes: Fresh complete media + m-CSF added on Day 4.

steps.name: BMDM differentiation — Day 6 feed and Day 7 lift
steps.notes: Day 6 feed with m-CSF. Day 7-9: adherent BMDMs washed with PBS, lifted with EDTA/PBS, resuspended at 10^7 cells/mL in phenol-red-free RPMI for device loading.

steps.name: Microfluidic device coating and priming
steps.notes: Device chambers coated overnight with 0.2-0.4 mg/mL fibronectin in PBS. Flushed with complete media before cell loading. Device mounted on Nikon Ti2 at 37 C / 5% CO2 / 98% humidity.

steps.name: Hoechst staining and cell loading onto microfluidic device
steps.notes: 1 uM Hoechst 33342 in complete media for 5 min; washed with complete media. Cells loaded and allowed to adhere ~30 min before imaging. No phototoxicity or cell death observed over 12-16 h imaging.

steps.name: Ligand A stimulation — polyI:C (PRIMING arm, Arm 1)
steps.notes: polyI:C activates TLR3/TRIF pathway; primes subsequent NF-kB response to TNF-a. Representative condition from 80-condition screen (Fig 1F, 2A, 2C). Positive controls: media -> 10 ng/mL TNFa; media -> 1 ng/mL LPS. Negative control: complete media only.

steps.name: Ligand B stimulation — TNF-a (PRIMING arm, Arm 1)
steps.notes: Ligand A aspirated; Ligand B delivered via same channel. NF-kB nuclear translocation (RelA-mVenus Nuc/Cyto ratio) tracked at 6-min intervals over 240 min. >300 cells per condition; two independent preparations.

steps.name: Ligand A stimulation — CpG (TOLERANCE arm, Arm 2)
steps.notes: CpG activates TLR9/MyD88 pathway; tolerises NF-kB response to subsequent TNF-a. Parallel run on separate chamber set (deviceWithCells_arm2). Highest tolerising dose (Fig 1E, 2A).

steps.name: Ligand B stimulation — TNF-a (TOLERANCE arm, Arm 2)
steps.notes: CpG arm Ligand B step. NF-kB dynamics tracked identically to Arm 1.

steps.name: Live-cell NF-kB dynamics detection and QC gate
steps.readout: RelA-mVenus nuclear/cytoplasmic (Nuc/Cyto) ratio per cell per 6-min frame

metrics.AUC: trapezoidal approximation over 240 min Ligand B window
metrics.max_amplitude: identified via loess-smoothed trace (3-frame interval, min prominence 0.1)
metrics.normalisation: AUC from memory-conditioned cells divided by mean naive AUC (AUC_0) for same Ligand B

mutual_information.method: Jetka et al. 2019, PLOS Comp Biol
mutual_information.input: dynamic vector of 20 evenly-spaced time points over 4 h stimulus interval

steps.image_analysis: MATLAB 2021a; flat field + dark frame correction; nuclear segmentation from Hoechst channel; cell tracking >99% accuracy over 8 h

steps.name: ATAC-seq — BMDM replating and stimulation
steps.notes: BMDMs replated on Day 7 from matureBMDMs dispense; overnight rest in complete media + m-CSF before stimulation.

steps.name: ATAC-seq — nuclei isolation
steps.lysis_buffer: 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5 / 3 mM MgCl2 / 10 mM NaCl / 0.1% IGEPAL CA-630
steps.notes: Cold lysis to preserve nuclei integrity. Centrifuge step modelled as heat(4C, 10m) in BioScript.

steps.name: ATAC-seq — transposase reaction
steps.transposase_mix: 25 uL 2X TD Buffer + 2.5 uL TD Enzyme 1 (Illumina) + 22.5 uL nuclease-free water
steps.notes: Transposase fragments open chromatin and tags with sequencing adapters. Modelled as heat(37C, 30m) in BioScript.

steps.name: ATAC-seq — PCR amplification, library prep, and QC gate

bioinformatics.peak_merging: iterative overlap peak merging (Corces et al. 2018)

steps.name: RNA-seq — BMDM replating and sequential stimulation
steps.notes: Ligand A applied 4 h; aspirated; Ligand B applied 4 h; aspirated; cells lysed. Media aspirated between each step.

steps.name: RNA-seq — cell lysis and RNA extraction
steps.notes: Aspirate Ligand B; add RLT buffer directly to well; RNA extracted from lysate using Dynabeads.

steps.name: RNA-seq — reverse transcription, library prep, and QC gate
steps.sequencing: NextSeq550 (Illumina), NextSeq 500/550 high output kit v2

bioinformatics.differential_expression: edgeR + limma; FDR < 0.01, fold change > 1 vs naive
bioinformatics.synergy_antagonism_formula: DAB_memory = (AB - (B + dAB + dB)) / (B + dAB + dB); synergy > 0.25, antagonism < -0.25

input_features.atac_detail: Peak accessibility (CPM) and TF motif counts for 18 TFs across 3 most proximal ATAC peaks in proximal (-1500 to +500 bp) and distal (-3000 to -1500 / +500 to +3000 bp) promoter regions; chromatin regulators without motifs (EZH2, HDAC, NELFE)
input_features.nfkb_detail: Peak height, AUC, and activation time per stimulation condition

deep_learning_model.output: 4-class gene expression classification per gene per stimulus condition
deep_learning_model.layers: 2-3 hidden layers; first layer = n_inputs nodes; subsequent layers = half or quarter of prior layer

key_results.chromatin_finding: Initial stimulus dominates chromatin landscape even after re-exposure to second stimulus; first stimulus Spearman r ~0.79 vs second stimulus r ~0.37-0.44

in_vivo_model.model: Sublethal murine endotoxemia (12.5 mg/kg LPS i.p.)
in_vivo_model.readout: Peritoneal macrophages isolated 4 h post-injection; NF-kB dynamics in microfluidic device
in_vivo_model.result: TNF-a response significantly attenuated; LPS response completely abolished in endotoxin-treated mice

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Two-Dimensional Protein Separation with Advanced Sample and Buffer Isolation Using Microfluidic Valves
Source Link  : https://pubs.acs.org/ancham/article-pdf/76/15/4426/37843760/ac0497499.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/ac0497499
Journal      : Analytical Chemistry, 2004, Vol. 76, No. 15, pp. 4426-4431
Platform     : Continuous-flow PDMS microfluidic chip with pneumatic monolith valves (pressure-driven + electrokinetic)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a chip-based two-dimensional (2D) protein separation system that couples
isoelectric focusing (IEF) with capillary gel electrophoresis (CGE) or capillary zone
electrophoresis (CZE) using active pneumatic microvalve control in a double-layer PDMS device.
The key innovation is the use of monolith valves to physically isolate incompatible separation
buffers (ampholyte for IEF vs. high ionic-strength gel/CE buffer), preventing peak interdiffusion
and band dispersion during the coupling step between the two separation dimensions.

The protocol is divided into four functional phases:
  1. Device surface passivation (polyacrylamide + methylcellulose coating to suppress EOF and
     protein adsorption)
  2. Sequential buffer loading: CGE gel buffer into the 2nd-dimension channel (right valves closed),
     then IEF ampholyte-sample mixture into the 1st-dimension channel (left valves closed)
  3. IEF focusing in a 10 mm PDMS channel at 500 V/cm; protein peaks mobilised by EOF into
     the 3 mm peak transfer region; target peaks isolated by closing both valve sets at 80 psi
  4. CGE/CZE 2nd-dimension separation in a 25 mm channel at 250 V/cm; sample stacking at the
     ampholyte/gel buffer boundary narrows the launching band and ensures independence of the
     two separation dimensions

The full 2D separation is completed within 10 min on-chip. A total of four fluorescently labelled
proteins are resolved: GFP (pI 5.6, 26 kDa), ovalbumin (pI 5.1, 45 kDa), low-density lipoprotein
protein (pI 5.11, 179 kDa), and trypsin inhibitor (pI 4.6, 20 kDa).

This BioScript file encodes the IEF-CGE arm as the primary representative experiment (Figures 3
and 4 in the paper). The IEF-CZE arm is structurally identical; a separate .bs file should encode
it with CZE_Buffer (0.375 M Tris-Cl, pH 8.6, 0.1% methylcellulose) substituted for CGE_GelBuffer.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Substrate     : Poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) on flat glass
Fabrication   : Three-process PDMS multilayer bonding:
                (1) Master fabrication by photolithography (AZ-4620 positive + SU-8 50 negative
                    photoresist; Clariant AZ-4620, MicroChem SU-8 50)
                (2) PDMS shaping by spin-coating and casting
                (3) Oxygen plasma bonding (Harrick Scientific, Ossining, NY)

Separation channel mold : 150 um wide, 12 um high; heated to 150 C for 30 min (round-shaped)
Valve control channel   : 300 um wide, 50 um high (square cross section)
Silane treatment        : 30 min hexamethyldisilazane (Sigma-Aldrich) vapor before PDMS casting
PDMS mixing ratio       : 10:1 (Sylgard 184, Dow Corning); degassed at ~5 psi vacuum
Separation layer        : 70 um thick (spin speed 2000 rpm)
Control layer           : ~5 mm thick PDMS
Curing                  : 65 C, at least 2 h; oxygen plasma treatment before bonding
Bonding sequence        : Control layer (5 mm) bonded to separation layer (70 um), then onto
                          PDMS-on-glass substrate
Bonding strength        : At least 2 h rest after alignment-bonding; >50 psi without leakage
Control channel access  : 1/16-in. o.d. metal syringe needle (Hamilton, Reno, NV) for pressure
                          line connection via 1/16-in. Teflon tubing

Channel dimensions:
  IEF channel length      : 10 mm
  CE channel length       : 25 mm
  Peak transfer region    : 3 mm
  Dead volume at junction : 0.1 nL (smaller than commercial microvalves, 10-100 nL)

Valve specification:
  Type                     : Pneumatic monolith valves (Unger et al., Science 2000, 288, 113-116)
  Sets                     : 2 (left: valves 1,2; right: valves 3,4)
  Material                 : Sylgard 184 PDMS (tensile strength 7.1 MPa, elongation 140%)
  Closure pressure         : 80 psi
  Isolation resistance     : 699 MOhm at 30 psi; >1000 MOhm at 100 psi
  No cross-contamination   : Verified over 30 min post-isolation

Valve operation sequence (Figure 1):
  (b) Right valves (3,4) closed -> CGE gel buffer loaded into CE channel (20-60 psi)
  (c) Left valves (1,2) closed, right valves (3,4) opened -> IEF sample mixture loaded
  (d) Both valve sets closed -> target protein peaks isolated in peak transfer region
  (e) Left valves (1,2) opened -> proteins sent into 2nd-dimension CE channel

Note: Control channels must be pre-filled with water before use to prevent air bubbles
during high-pressure valve operation (PDMS is gas-permeable).


SURFACE TREATMENT
-----------------
Static coating  : 3-(trimethoxysilyl)propyl methacrylate (Sigma-Aldrich, St. Louis, MO)
                  as adhesion promoter; followed by acrylamide + TEMED + APS solution
                  introduced into channel; polymerised under N2 purge in vacuum chamber
                  (homemade, N2 purging valve) for 30 min at 25 C to eliminate O2 quenching
Dynamic coating : 0.5% methylcellulose solution as pretreatment; further minimises
                  non-specific adsorption
Outcome         : Protein adsorption reduced to undetectable level by fluorescence microscopy
                  for duration of a single 2D separation experiment
Same silanol (-Si-OH) group in PDMS and glass allows identical acrylamide coating protocol.


MATERIALS AND REAGENTS
-----------------------

IEF sample solution:
  Ampholyte      : 3-10 carrier ampholyte (Beckman Coulter, Fullerton, CA)
  Glycerol       : 10% (BioRad, Hercules, CA)
  Methylcellulose: 1% (Sigma-Aldrich, St. Louis, MO); same concentration in all solutions
                   (anolyte, catholyte, gel buffer) for better mixing in peak transfer region
  Protein samples: Fluorescein- or Alexa Fluor 488-labeled (attached to lysine residues;
                   proteins may acquire multiple dye molecules and exhibit multiple pI values)

Protein samples (100 uM each in IEF-CGE experiment, Figure 4):
  GFP                  : pI 5.6,  MW 26 kDa
  Ovalbumin            : pI 5.1,  MW 45 kDa
  Low-density lipoprotein protein : pI 5.11, MW 179 kDa
  Trypsin inhibitor    : pI 4.6,  MW 20 kDa

IEF linearity markers (separate experiment):
  Source         : Sigma-Aldrich, St. Louis, MO
  pI values      : 3.0, 4.5, 5.1, 6.2, 7.2, 8.1, 9.0, 10.3
  Concentration  : 10 ug/mL each
  Detection      : ex 330-340 nm, em 415-500 nm (fluorescence microscopy)

Buffers:
  Anolyte        : 0.1 M acetic acid, pH 2.5 (+ 1% methylcellulose)
  Catholyte      : 0.5% ammonium hydroxide, pH 10.5 (+ 1% methylcellulose)
  CGE gel buffer : SDS 14-200 gel buffer (Beckman Coulter); 3.0% Tris-hydroxymethylaminomethane,
                   2.0% ethylene glycol; 90% SDS 14-200 + 1% methylcellulose in experiment
  CZE buffer     : 0.375 M Tris-Cl, pH 8.6, 0.1% methylcellulose (IEF-CZE arm only)

Detection system:
  Microscope     : Inverted epi-fluorescence (Olympus, Melville, NY), 100 W mercury lamp
  Filter set     : Standard FITC
  Camera         : Thermoelectrically cooled CCD (Cooke Co., Auburn Hills, MI)
  Acquisition    : IPLab 3.6 (Scanalytics, Fairfax, VA); 1 frame/s


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Surface Passivation - Static Polyacrylamide Coating
  Reagents    : AcrylamideCoating (acrylamide + TEMED + APS + 3-(trimethoxysilyl)propyl
                methacrylate adhesion promoter), GlycerolMethylcellulose (0.5% methylcellulose)
  Operation   : mix; then heat at 25 C for 30 min under N2 purge (5 psi vacuum)
  Duration    : 30 min (1800 s)
  Purpose     : Grow polyacrylamide polymer on PDMS surface to prevent protein adsorption
                and decrease uneven EOF. Follow with dynamic 0.5% methylcellulose coating.
  Note        : One-time chip preparation step before each experiment run.

Step 2 | CGE Gel Buffer Loading into Second-Dimension Channel
  Reagents    : CGE_GelBuffer (SDS 14-200 + 1% methylcellulose)
  Operation   : Pressure-driven injection (abstracted as mix in BioScript)
  Valve state : Right valves (3,4) closed at 80 psi to isolate IEF channel
  Pressure    : 20-30 psi (up to 60 psi applicable without breaking valve seal)
  Purpose     : Fill 25 mm CE channel with gel buffer without contaminating the
                ampholyte-sensitive IEF channel.

Step 3 | IEF Sample Preparation
  Reagents    : Ampholyte_3_10, GlycerolMethylcellulose, GFP_Sample, OvalSample,
                LDLPSample, TrypsinInhibitorSample
  Operation   : Sequential mix steps; ampholyte + methylcellulose/glycerol carrier
                prepared first; all four labeled protein samples then combined and
                merged into the carrier
  Purpose     : Prepare 3-10 ampholyte mixture with 10% glycerol, 1% methylcellulose,
                and all four fluorescently labeled protein analytes.

Step 4 | IEF Sample Loading and Reservoir Buffer Replacement
  Reagents    : AnolyteSolution (0.1 M acetic acid, pH 2.5),
                CatholyteSolution (0.5% ammonium hydroxide, pH 10.5)
  Operation   : Pressure-driven injection (abstracted as mix in BioScript)
  Valve state : Left valves (1,2) closed to isolate CGE gel; right valves (3,4) opened
  Purpose     : Load ampholyte-sample mixture into 10 mm IEF channel; replace reservoirs
                with anolyte (anode end) and catholyte (cathode end).

Step 5 | IEF Focusing (1st Dimension)
  Operation   : Electric field application (abstracted as heat in BioScript)
  Field       : 500 V/cm across 10 mm IEF channel (500 V total)
  Duration    : 130 s
  Temperature : 37 C (abstraction for field-driven step)
  Outcome     : pH 3-10 gradient established; proteins focus to stationary pI bands.
                EOF mobilises focused peaks slowly from anode to cathode.
                Steady state confirmed by monitoring current through channel.
  Speed       : Equilibration <30 s; 2 orders of magnitude faster than CIEF in 25-50 cm
                capillaries (~30 min). Comparable to short fused-silica CIEF (280-360 s,
                Wu et al., Anal. Sci. 2001) but with better S/N and separation properties.
  EOF control : Critical - if too high, peaks are flushed out within minutes.
                Controlled by methylcellulose concentration and polyacrylamide coating.

Step 6 | IEF Peak Detection (QC Gate 1)
  Operation   : iefFocusingDetection module; fluorescence microscopy
  Duration    : 30 s detection window
  Outcome     : Verify focused protein peaks have entered the 3 mm peak transfer region
  Branch      : Pass (iefSignal > 0)  -> dispose(iefChannel); proceed to peak isolation
                Fail (iefSignal <= 0) -> drain(iefChannel); experiment terminated

Step 7 | Peak Isolation by Valve Closure
  Operation   : Pneumatic valve actuation (abstracted as dispense re-entry in BioScript;
                no native valve primitive in lilott8/BioScript)
  Valve state : Both valve sets (1,2 and 3,4) closed at 80 psi
  Dead volume : 0.1 nL (peak transfer region between the two valve sets)
  Isolation   : >1000 MOhm electrical resistance; no protein intercontamination after 30 min
  Purpose     : Physically trap target protein peaks in the 3 mm transfer region, isolated
                from both the IEF channel and the CGE channel. Symmetric channel layout
                prevents valve actuation from mobilising trapped proteins.

Step 8 | CGE Buffer Equilibration
  Reagents    : CGE_GelBuffer
  Operation   : Diffusion equilibration (abstracted as mix in BioScript)
  Valve state : Left valves (1,2) opened
  Duration    : 30 s
  Purpose     : Allow buffer ions to diffuse into peak transfer region to prevent abrupt
                conductivity change at the buffer boundary before CE field is applied.
                Protein diffusion is negligible (large MW, slow diffusion constant relative
                to buffer ions). Small-MW ampholyte co-isolated with proteins is eluted
                rapidly by electrophoresis (lower MW than protein analytes).

Step 9 | CGE Separation (2nd Dimension)
  Operation   : Electric field application (abstracted as heat in BioScript)
  Field       : 250 V/cm across 25 mm CE channel (625 V total)
  Duration    : ~6 min (360 s)
  Temperature : 37 C (abstraction for field-driven step)
  Separation  : Charge-to-mass ratio (non-denaturing CGE, no SDS)
  Stacking    : Proteins enter high-conductivity gel buffer from low-conductivity ampholyte;
                sudden velocity decrease at boundary narrows launching band (stacking effect).
                Highly viscous gel also contributes sieving to stacking.
                Stacking ensures 1st and 2nd dimension separations are fully independent.
  Mobilities  : Ovalbumin (45 kDa): -1.3e-4 cm2/V.s
                GFP (26 kDa): -1.0e-4 cm2/V.s
                Ovalbumin elutes before GFP (higher charge-to-mass ratio, faster mobility)
  Total time  : 10 min for complete 2D separation

Step 10 | CGE Fluorescence Readout (QC Gate 2)
  Operation   : cgeDetection module; fluorescence intensity at end of 25 mm CGE channel
  Duration    : 30 s detection window
  Readout     : Electropherograms (fluorescence intensity vs. time); FITC filter, CCD camera
  Branch      : Pass (cgeSignal > 0)  -> dispose(equilibrated); proceed to cleanup
                Fail (cgeSignal <= 0) -> drain(equilibrated); experiment terminated


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : wang_2d_ief_cge_protein_separation.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG            : wang_2d_ief_cge_protein_separation_main_dag.dot

Duration units : All durations converted to seconds (s) or minutes (m) for compiler
                 compatibility (BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported)
                 30 min coating    -> 30m  (IR: 1800.0 SECOND)
                 130 s IEF         -> 130s (IR: 130.0 SECOND)
                 6 min CGE         -> 6m   (IR: 360.0 SECOND)

Modules        : iefFocusingDetection, cgeDetection

Platform note  : This is a continuous-flow pressure-driven + electrokinetic chip, not a
                 DMF/EWOD device. BioScript primitives are used as abstractions:
                   mix    -> pressure-driven injection and buffer loading steps
                   heat   -> electric field application (IEF focusing, CGE/CE separation)
                   detect -> fluorescence microscopy readout (CCD camera, IPLab 3.6)
                 No native electrokinetic or valve primitive exists in lilott8/BioScript.
                 Valve state changes are modelled as mix steps transitioning between
                 separation phases. Peak isolation (Step 7) uses a fresh dispense to
                 re-introduce the isolated fluid as a new BioScript variable.

Known compiler behaviours observed in IR:
  - drain lowers to dispose() in IR output (known compiler bug; .bs source authoritative)
  - True-branch blocks (bsbbif_2_t, bsbbif_5_t) emit no unconditional jump in IR text
    (known limitation); DOT edges resolve correctly

IEF-CZE arm note : The IEF-CZE arm (paper Section "IEF Coupled with Second-Dimension
                   Capillary Zone Electrophoresis") is structurally identical to this file.
                   A separate .bs file should encode it with CZE_Buffer
                   (0.375 M Tris-Cl, pH 8.6, 0.1% methylcellulose) substituted for
                   CGE_GelBuffer at Steps S2 and S8. All other steps, durations, and
                   CFG structure remain unchanged.

protocol.title: Two-Dimensional Protein Separation with Advanced Sample and Buffer Isolation Using Microfluidic Valves
protocol.platform: Continuous-flow PDMS microfluidic chip with pneumatic monolith valves (pressure-driven + electrokinetic)
protocol.objective: Integrate isoelectric focusing (IEF, 1st dimension) with capillary gel electrophoresis (CGE) or capillary zone electrophoresis (CZE, 2nd dimension) using active pneumatic microvalve control to isolate incompatible separation buffers, prevent peak interdiffusion, and achieve 2D protein separation on-chip within 10 min

fabrication.master: Photolithography using AZ-4620 (positive) and SU-8 50 (negative) photoresist
fabrication.separation_channel_mold: 150 um wide, 12 um high; heated to 150 C for 30 min (round-shaped)
fabrication.valve_control_channel_mold: 300 um wide, 50 um high (square cross section)
fabrication.silane_treatment: 30 min hexamethyldisilazane vapor to prevent adhesion to silicone rubber
fabrication.pdms_mixing_ratio: 10:1 (Sylgard 184, Dow Corning); degassed at 5 psi vacuum
fabrication.bonding: Oxygen plasma (Harrick Scientific); control layer bonded to separation layer, then onto PDMS-on-glass substrate
fabrication.control_channel_access: 1/16-in. o.d. metal syringe needle (Hamilton); 1/16-in. Teflon tubing pressure lines

valves.notes: Right valves (3,4) isolate IEF channel from CGE channel during CE media loading. Left valves (1,2) isolate CGE gel during IEF sample injection. Both sets closed to trap peak transfer region.

static_coating.polymerization_condition: N2 purge, 5 psi vacuum chamber, 30 min

dynamic_coating.purpose: Further minimise protein adsorption and suppress EOF

surface_treatment.outcome: Protein adsorption undetectable by fluorescence microscopy for duration of single 2D separation experiment

ief_sample_solution.notes: 1% methylcellulose suppresses EOF; IEF linearity experiment uses 3% methylcellulose and 5% ampholyte

labeled_proteins.labels: Fluorescein or Alexa Fluor 488 (attached to lysine residues; proteins may acquire multiple dye molecules and multiple pI values)

ief_markers.detection: Fluorescence microscopy, ex 330-340 nm, em 415-500 nm

reagents.anolyte: 0.1 M acetic acid, pH 2.5; contains same methylcellulose concentration as IEF sample
reagents.catholyte: 0.5% ammonium hydroxide, pH 10.5; contains same methylcellulose concentration as IEF sample

cge_gel_buffer.composition: 90% SDS 14-200 gel buffer (Beckman Coulter, Fullerton, CA) + 1% methylcellulose
cge_gel_buffer.notes: Same methylcellulose concentration used across all solutions for better mixing in peak transfer region

cze_buffer.notes: Used in IEF-CZE arm (separate experiment); structurally identical protocol to IEF-CGE arm

steps.name: Surface passivation - static polyacrylamide coating
steps.notes: Coat PDMS channel with 3-(trimethoxysilyl)propyl methacrylate adhesion promoter, then introduce acrylamide + TEMED + APS under N2 purge (5 psi vacuum) for 30 min. Follow with 0.5% methylcellulose dynamic coating. Reduces protein adsorption to undetectable levels.

steps.name: CGE gel buffer loading into second-dimension channel
steps.valve_state: right valves (3,4) closed at 80 psi to isolate IEF channel
steps.notes: CE media loaded into 25 mm CGE channel without contaminating the 10 mm IEF channel. Methylcellulose concentration matched across all solutions.

steps.name: IEF sample preparation
steps.notes: Ampholyte + glycerol/methylcellulose carrier prepared first, then all four labeled protein samples combined and merged into the carrier. All four proteins loaded simultaneously.

steps.name: IEF sample loading and reservoir buffer replacement
steps.valve_state: left valves (1,2) closed to isolate CGE gel; right valves (3,4) opened
steps.notes: Ampholyte-sample mixture injected into IEF channel at low pressure. Reservoirs replaced: anolyte (0.1 M acetic acid, pH 2.5) at anode; catholyte (0.5% ammonium hydroxide, pH 10.5) at cathode.

steps.name: IEF focusing (1st dimension)
steps.notes: pH 3-10 gradient established. Proteins focus to stationary pI bands. EOF slowly mobilises peaks from anode to cathode. IEF steady state confirmed by monitoring current through channel. Equilibration 2 orders of magnitude faster than CIEF in 25-50 cm capillaries (~30 min).

steps.name: IEF peak detection and QC gate
steps.camera: Thermoelectrically cooled CCD (Cooke Co., Auburn Hills, MI)

steps.name: Peak isolation by valve closure
steps.valve_state: both valve sets (1,2 and 3,4) closed at 80 psi
steps.notes: Target protein peaks physically isolated in 3 mm peak transfer region. No protein intercontamination observed after 30 min. Dead volume 0.1 nL is much smaller than commercial microvalves (10-100 nL). Symmetric channel layout prevents valve operation from mobilising proteins in transfer region.

steps.name: CGE buffer equilibration
steps.notes: Buffer ions diffuse into peak transfer region for 30 s to prevent abrupt conductivity jump before CE field application. Protein diffusion negligible (large MW, slow diffusion constant relative to buffer ions). Small-MW ampholyte co-isolated with proteins eluted rapidly by electrophoresis.

steps.name: CGE separation (2nd dimension)
steps.stacking_mechanism: Proteins entering high-conductivity gel buffer from low-conductivity ampholyte experience sudden velocity decrease at buffer boundary; narrows launching band

electrophoretic_mobilities.notes: Ovalbumin (45 kDa) higher mobility than GFP (26 kDa) due to charge-to-mass ratio dependence in non-denaturing CGE

steps.notes: Stacking ensures 1st and 2nd dimension separations are independent (verified by reversing IEF orientation, Figure 5).

steps.name: CGE fluorescence readout and QC gate
steps.readout: Electropherograms at end of 25 mm CGE channel; fluorescence intensity vs. time
steps.expected_elution_order: Ovalbumin before GFP (higher charge-to-mass ratio, higher mobility)

ief_cze_arm.note: The IEF-CZE (capillary zone electrophoresis) arm is structurally identical to the IEF-CGE arm above. CGE_GelBuffer is replaced by CZE_Buffer (0.375 M Tris-Cl, pH 8.6, 0.1% methylcellulose) at Steps S2 and S8. Electric field in 2nd dimension: 250 V/cm. Stacking still occurs at the liquid-liquid conductivity boundary. CE shows higher resolution and faster separation than CGE (lower viscosity, faster liquid-liquid interface mixing). Independence of 1st and 2nd dimension verified by reversing IEF orientation (catholyte/anolyte swap, Figure 5a/5b). A separate .bs file should encode the IEF-CZE arm with CZE_Buffer substituted for CGE_GelBuffer.

ief_linearity.pH_gradient: pH 3-10 established in 10 mm PDMS channel at 500 V/cm
ief_linearity.nonlinearity: Observed at high pH side due to ampholyte mixture optimised for fused-silica capillary (different EOF characteristics from PDMS surface)
ief_linearity.mitigation: Adding 8.1-9.8 ampholyte to wide-range 3-10 ampholyte shifts peaks at high pH side; further study required

peak_isolation.selectability: Any single pI region can be isolated and sent to 2nd dimension by valve operation (Figure 5c: GFP isolated independently)
peak_isolation.multi_transfer: Multiple regions can be transferred simultaneously by integrating additional valve sets

results.validation_method: Reversing IEF orientation (catholyte/anolyte swap); 2nd-dimension separation unaffected by 1st-dimension peak order

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.content: Surface coating, CGE buffer loading, IEF sample prep and loading, IEF focusing, IEF detection

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_4_j
basic_blocks.content: Peak isolation, CGE buffer equilibration, CGE separation, CGE detection

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_7_j
