description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : NF-kappaB Memory Coordinates Transcriptional Responses to Dynamic Inflammatory Stimuli
Source Link  : https://www.cell.com/cell-reports/pdfExtended/S2211-1247(22)00968-8
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2022.111159
Journal      : Cell Reports, 2022, Vol. 40, Article 111159
Platform     : Automated pressure-driven microfluidic live-cell imaging (channel-based PDMS/glass device,
               not DMF); 64-chamber device with 14 stimulus inputs; MATLAB-driven pneumatic valve control


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a high-throughput microfluidic live-cell imaging approach to systematically
profile single-cell NF-kappaB responses to 24 non-repeating sequential combinations of four
inflammatory ligands (TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, LPS, PAM2CSK4) at three dose levels (high, mid, low)
in RelA^-/- NIH/3T3 mouse embryonic fibroblasts expressing a RelA-DsRed fusion protein. The core
finding is that NF-kappaB dynamics encode short-term memory of prior stimulus history through
ligand-dependent engagement of distinct negative feedback modules.

The protocol has four functional phases:
  1. Microfluidic device preparation, cell loading, and equilibration
  2. Sequential four-ligand stimulation (S1 -> S2 -> S3 -> S4, 2 h per interval) with continuous
     live-cell time-lapse imaging and nuclear/cytoplasmic RelA-DsRed quantification
  3. Information-theoretic analysis of NF-kappaB dynamics using channel capacity (CC) to quantify
     how accurately subsequent responses encode prior stimulus history
  4. Mechanistic dissection via IKK inhibition (PS1145), mathematical ODE modelling, and bulk
     RNA sequencing to identify ligand-dependent negative feedback modules

The complete 8 h imaging experiment profiles >10,000 single cells across 72 conditions
(24 sequences x 3 dose levels) in 2 independent biological replicates.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Type      : Pressure-driven automated microfluidic cell culture device (channel-based; not DMF).
            No electrodes, no EWOD actuation. Reagent switching achieved by pneumatic valves.
Material  : PDMS (Momentive RTV-615, 10:1 monomer:catalyst) bonded to glass slide by oxygen plasma.
Layers    : Control layer: 66 g PDMS poured on silicon wafer master, cured 80 C overnight, ~2 cm thick.
            Flow layer: 15 g PDMS spun at 2200 rpm on silicon wafer master (50 um thick), cured 80 C 1 h.
            Both layers plasma-treated, aligned under custom stereomicroscope, baked 80 C overnight.
Chambers  : 64 independently controlled cell culture chambers, each 3.5 x 0.8 x 0.035 mm; >500 cells/chamber.
Inputs    : 14 unique stimulus inputs.
Coating   : 0.25 mg/mL human plasma fibronectin (Millipore FC010) in sterile PBS pH 7.4; overnight RT.
Control   : Pneumatic solenoid valves; electronic controller boxes; MATLAB scripts + custom GUI.
            Input pressure: 4 psi; reagent delivery via PEEK tubing (VICI, TPK.505).
Microscope: Nikon Ti2 enclosed in temperature-controlled incubator (Life Imaging Services); 37 C,
            100% humidity, 5% CO2 throughout all imaging steps.
Camera    : Hamamatsu ORCA-Flash4.0 V2 sCMOS; 20X magnification; images every 6 min.
Channels  : RelA-DsRed (555 nm excitation, 0.5-1 s exposure; NF-kappaB nuclear translocation)
            H2B-GFP (485 nm, 50-100 ms; nuclear segmentation and cell tracking)
            JNK-KTR-mCerulean3 (440 nm, 100 ms; JNK kinase activity)
Design ref: Kellogg et al. 2014, Nat. Protoc. 9, 1713-1726; Son et al. 2021, Sci. Signal. 14, eaaz4382


CELL LINE
---------
RelA^-/- NIH/3T3 immortalized mouse embryonic fibroblasts (3T3s) stably expressing:
  - RelA-DsRed fusion protein (NF-kappaB nuclear translocation reporter)
  - JNK-KTR-mCerulean3 (JNK kinase activity reporter)
  - H2B-GFP (nuclear marker for segmentation and tracking)
Source    : Markus Covert laboratory (Stanford University)
Culture   : DMEM High Glucose (Gibco) + 10% FBS (Omega Scientific) + 1% GlutaMAX (Gibco)
            + 100 U/mL penicillin-streptomycin (Gibco); 37 C, 5% CO2.
Imaging   : FluoroBrite DMEM (Gibco, A1896701) + same supplements; reduces autofluorescence.
Passage   : No more than 15 passages; passed before reaching 100% confluency.
MyD88 KO  : CRISPR-Cas9 knockout line generated using pX330 backbone (Addgene #42230) and
            guide RNA 5'-TCGCGCTTAACGTGGGAGTG-3'; confirmed by Sanger sequencing and western blot.
            Used to confirm MyD88-dependence of LPS, IL-1beta, and PAM signalling (Supp. Fig. 5).


LIGANDS AND DOSE LEVELS
------------------------
Four inflammatory ligands covering two receptor pathway groups:

  TNFR pathway (MyD88-independent):
    TNF-alpha : Recombinant Mouse TNF-alpha (R&D Systems, aa 80-235)
                Signals via TNFR -> TRADD/TRAF2 -> IKK -> NF-kappaB
                High: 90 ng/mL (>95% activated); Mid: 30 ng/mL (85-95%); Low: 3 ng/mL (50-70%)
                NOTE: maximal TNF-alpha activation ~90%; high dose activates slightly fewer cells than
                other ligands at high dose.

  MyD88-dependent pathway (shared IRAK1/4 -> IKK -> NF-kappaB):
    IL-1beta  : Recombinant Mouse IL-1 beta/IL-1F2 (R&D Systems, 401ML010CF); receptor IL-1R
                High: 3 ng/mL; Mid: 0.2 ng/mL; Low: 0.05 ng/mL
    LPS       : Ultrapure LPS E. coli 0111:B4 (InvivoGen, tlrl-3pelps); receptor TLR4
                High: 400 ng/mL; Mid: 100 ng/mL; Low: 12.5 ng/mL
                NOTE: LPS produces characteristically delayed NF-kappaB activation kinetics
                (linked to ligand-specific IKK cycling rates); TRIF/TRAM-independent in 3T3s.
    PAM       : PAM2CSK4 synthetic diacylated lipopeptide (InvivoGen, tlrl-pm2s-1); receptor TLR2/6
                High: 1 ng/mL; Mid: 0.2 ng/mL; Low: 0.01 ng/mL

All ligands diluted from -80 C stocks immediately before each stimulus, stored on ice during
the experiment. Delivered at 4 psi via PEEK tubing at each 2 h interval switch.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Device Fabrication and Surface Coating
  Reagents  : PDMS (RTV-615, 10:1), PBS (Gibco, pH 7.4), fibronectin 0.25 mg/mL
  Operation : Plasma-bond PDMS device to glass. Fill chambers with fibronectin/PBS solution.
  Duration  : Overnight at room temperature (fibronectin coating); flush with complete media before loading.
  Purpose   : Fibronectin coating promotes cell adhesion to PDMS chamber floor.

Step 2 | Cell Loading and Equilibration
  Cell line  : RelA^-/- NIH/3T3 (RelA-DsRed / JNK-KTR / H2B-GFP)
  Preparation: Harvest with trypsin; wash with complete medium; resuspend at 5e6 cells/mL
               in FluoroBrite DMEM + supplements.
  Loading    : Load at ~50% confluency to optimize single-cell tracking efficiency.
  Equilibration: 5 h (300 min) at 37 C, 5% CO2, 100% humidity before stimulus and imaging begin.
  Purpose    : Allow cells to adhere, spread, and return to baseline signalling state.

Step 3 | S1 Stimulus - Naive NF-kappaB Response
  Ligand (canonical mid-dose arm): IL-1beta 0.2 ng/mL
  Duration   : 120 min (2 h interval)
  Delivery   : MATLAB valve script switches input from media to ligand at t=0 min; 4 psi, PEEK tubing.
  Imaging    : Time-lapse epifluorescence, 555 nm excitation, 0.5-1 s exposure, every 6 min.
               For time-resolved LPS-to-IL-1beta switching experiments: imaging every 3 min.
  Readout    : Nuclear/cytoplasmic RelA-DsRed ratio quantified by custom MATLAB image analysis.
               H2B-GFP used for nuclear segmentation; single-cell trajectories tracked over full
               experiment. Traces smoothed with lowess (span 3) to identify local maxima.
               Multiple local maxima allowed (min 5-frame = 30 min spacing between peaks).
               Cutoff: 95th percentile of maxima from unstimulated cells; sub-threshold values set to 0.
  Information: Nuclear NF-kappaB at 6 timepoints (20, 30, 40, 50, 70, 90 min post-stimulus)
               used as 6-dimensional input for channel capacity (CC) calculation (Fig. 3A).
  Result     : S1 response is naive baseline; used to normalize all S2-S4 responses for that ligand.

Step 4 | S1 QC Gate
  Condition  : s1Signal > 0 -> pass (valid naive response); proceed to S2.
               s1Signal <= 0 -> fail (no response: dead, unhealthy, or incorrectly loaded cell);
               dispose ligand variable; chamber excluded from downstream analysis.

Step 5 | S2 Stimulus - First History-Conditioned Response
  Ligand (canonical mid-dose arm): LPS 100 ng/mL
  Duration   : 120 min; valve switches from IL-1beta to LPS at t=120 min.
  Key finding: Prior IL-1beta (S1, MyD88-dependent) induces IRAK1 auto-inhibitory phosphorylation,
               attenuating the subsequent LPS response in a dose-dependent manner (Fig. 4B/E).
               Asymmetry: prior LPS inhibits subsequent IL-1beta/PAM more strongly than vice versa
               at mid and low doses (Fig. 4E, red vs blue/green). Prior TNF-alpha (TNFR-dependent)
               only weakly attenuates MyD88-dependent signalling (Fig. 4D, blue).
  CC result  : Channel capacity increases from S1 to S2 despite response attenuation, indicating
               NF-kappaB dynamics encode prior history information (Fig. 3B).

Step 6 | S3 Stimulus - Two-Ligand History Response
  Ligand (canonical mid-dose arm): PAM 0.2 ng/mL
  Duration   : 120 min; valve switches to PAM at t=240 min.
  Key finding: Cumulative MyD88-dependent history (IL-1beta + LPS, S1+S2) induces downstream
               NF-kappaB-dependent negative feedback proteins (A20/Tnfaip3, IkappaBepsilon/Nfkbie,
               Nfkbia). Channel capacity remains elevated at S3 vs S1 (Fig. 3B/C).

Step 7 | S4 Stimulus - Three-Ligand History Response
  Ligand (canonical mid-dose arm): TNF-alpha 30 ng/mL
  Duration   : 120 min; valve switches to TNF-alpha at t=360 min.
  Key finding: TNF-alpha signals via TNFR (distinct receptor-associated intermediaries from MyD88);
               converges on IKK downstream of the accumulated IRAK1 auto-inhibition and
               NF-kappaB-dependent feedback induced at S1-S3. TNF-alpha response is only weakly
               attenuated regardless of prior MyD88-dependent history (Figs. 2B, 4B/D).

Step 8 | Cell Retrieval for Transcriptomics (S4 pass path only)
  Timing     : End of 8 h imaging window (t=480 min)
  Method     : TrypLE Express (Gibco); 1 min; detaches cells from fibronectin-coated surface.
               PBS wash; cells accumulate at outlet channel; removed in 2 uL droplet by pipette.
               Deposited in 10 uL ice-cold lysis buffer (0.1% Triton-X100 + RNase inhibitor, Takara).
               Stored at -80 C until processing. ~1500 cells per replicate per condition.
  Library prep: SMART-Seq2 pipeline. OligodT30VN annealing at 72 C. Reverse transcription
               (SuperScript III, Invitrogen) + TSO oligo (AAGCAGTGGTATCAACGCAGAGTGAAT[rG][rG][rG])
               at 42 C for 90 min + 10 cycles 50/42 C. 6-cycle KAPA HiFi preamplification.
               Ampure XP bead purification (1:1). Nextera XT library prep (Illumina, FC-131-1024).
  Sequencing : Illumina HiSEQ4000; single-end 50 bp; University of Chicago Genomics Facility.
  Analysis   : STAR alignment to GRCm38. featureCounts transcript quantification.
               edgeR + limma (R) differential expression. BH FDR < 0.01, log2FC > 1.
               3 biological replicates. Data deposited: GEO GSE193053.
  Conditions : LPS 100 ng/mL vs PAM 0.2 ng/mL vs IL-1beta 0.2 ng/mL vs untreated; 2 h stimulus.
  qPCR       : CellDirect One-Step RT-qPCR. Custom primers for Tnfaip3. IDT PrimeTime probes
               for Csf2, Csf3, Cxcl2, Cxcl3, Il23a, Gapdh. TaqMan probes for Nfkbia, Nfkbie.
               Ct normalized to Gapdh (deltaCt); fold change over unstimulated (deltadeltaCt).
               BH-adjusted two-tailed t-test. Data shown as mean +/- SEM, n=3 replicates.

Step 9 | IKK Inhibition Sub-Protocol (Fig. 5A, Supp. Fig. 6C/D)
  Purpose    : Determine whether NF-kappaB-mediated gene expression downstream of IKK is required
               for LPS-specific asymmetric attenuation of subsequent MyD88-dependent signalling.
  Reagent    : PS1145 dihydrochloride (Tocris, 4569); reversible IKK-beta inhibitor; 40 uM.
  Sub-steps  :
    9a. Load fresh RelA-DsRed 3T3 cells; equilibrate 5 h at 37 C, 5% CO2 (as Step 2).
    9b. Pre-treat with PS1145 40 uM in complete media for 90 min at 37 C.
    9c. Stimulate with LPS (25-400 ng/mL) + PS1145 40 uM for 240 min at 37 C.
        (NF-kappaB translocation is significantly reduced during LPS due to IKK-beta inhibition;
        Supp. Fig. 6D confirms reduced activation vs untreated at all LPS doses tested.)
    9d. Wash out PS1145: 2 x 15 min washes with complete DMEM at 37 C.
    9e. Restimulate with IL-1beta 3 ng/mL (high dose) for 120 min at 37 C.
        Detect: nfkbTranslocationDetection; 90 s readout.
  Result     : PS1145-treated cells show significantly stronger NF-kappaB response to subsequent
               IL-1beta vs untreated cells (***p < 1e-4, Bonferroni-corrected Wilcoxon rank-sum;
               >120 cells per condition; 2 biological replicates; Fig. 5A).
  Conclusion : NF-kappaB nuclear translocation and NF-kappaB-mediated gene expression downstream
               of IKK are required for LPS-specific asymmetric attenuation, confirming that
               transcriptional induction of downstream negative feedback drives the asymmetry.


MATHEMATICAL MODEL
------------------
Type       : ODE network model; 14 differential equations; 20 parameters.
Base model : Krishna et al. 2006, PNAS 103:10840 (minimal 3-equation NF-kappaB oscillator).
Expansion  : Added receptors TNFR, IL-1R, TLR4; IRAK1/4 auto-inhibitory phosphorylation
             (Equations 6-9; nonlinear inactivation proportional to active IRAK^2);
             downstream NF-kappaB-dependent inhibitor (Equations 4-5; targets IKK activation;
             Hill coefficient 3 for cooperativity); IKK cycling (Equations 10-11).
LPS vs IL-1beta feedback: LPS-induced downstream inhibitor C parameter set 4x lower threshold
             than IL-1beta or TNF-alpha, modelling stronger transcriptional negative feedback.
Implementation: Python; scipy.integrate.odeint; Bokeh visualization.
Key result : Two-motif model (IRAK1 auto-inhibition + differential downstream feedback) is
             sufficient to reproduce all observed ligand- and dose-specific attenuation patterns
             without additional components (Fig. 5C-E, Supp. Fig. 7A).
Code       : https://github.com/tay-lab/Sequential_NF-kB_stim
Zenodo     : https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6626195


KEY FINDINGS
------------
1. Sequential inflammatory stimuli broadly attenuate subsequent NF-kappaB responses (Fig. 2).
   LPS and PAM produce no response after first stimulus; TNF-alpha and IL-1beta show weak
   responses at S2-S4 depending on dose.

2. Variable attenuation encodes prior stimulus history. Channel capacity (CC) increases from
   S1 to S2 despite attenuation, and remains elevated at S3-S4 (Fig. 3B). NF-kappaB dynamics
   (multi-timepoint) carry substantially more information than peak amplitude alone (Fig. 3B/D).

3. TNF-alpha (TNFR) and MyD88-dependent ligands (IL-1beta, LPS, PAM) form two distinct
   history-encoding groups. Prior TNF-alpha weakly attenuates MyD88-dependent signalling
   and vice versa; prior MyD88-dependent signalling strongly attenuates subsequent
   MyD88-dependent signalling in a dose-dependent and asymmetric manner (Fig. 4D/E).

4. Asymmetry mechanism: at high dose, IRAK1 auto-inhibition produces symmetric cross-attenuation.
   At mid and low dose, differential downstream NF-kappaB-dependent gene expression (LPS induces
   2-4x more negative regulator expression than IL-1beta: Nfkbia, Tnfaip3, Nfkbie; Fig. 6C/E)
   produces asymmetric attenuation. This is IKK-dependent (PS1145 experiment; Fig. 5A).

5. LPS-specific prolonged NF-kappaB activation duration (not total AUC) explains differential
   downstream gene expression vs IL-1beta (Fig. 6E, Supp. Fig. 7F/G).


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : wang_nfkb_sequential_stimulation.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 16 basic blocks (BB1-BB16), 5 if/else gates, 20 CFG edges
DAG            : wang_nfkb_sequential_stimulation_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations in minutes (m); BioScript supports s and m tokens only.
                 300 min  = 5 h equilibration        (IR: 18000.0 SECOND)
                 120 min  = 2 h stimulus interval    (IR: 7200.0 SECOND)
                 240 min  = 4 h IKK LPS stimulus     (IR: 14400.0 SECOND)
                  90 min  = PS1145 pretreatment       (IR: 5400.0 SECOND)
                  15 min  = each PS1145 wash          (IR: 900.0 SECOND)
Modules        : nfkbTranslocationDetection, cellViabilityDetection, rnaSeqDetection
ASCII note     : All Greek letters replaced with ASCII equivalents (alpha, beta, kappa, epsilon, u)
                 to satisfy ANTLR4 FileStream ASCII-only requirement.
Variable scope : Chamber variables (s1Active, s2Active, s3Active, s4Active) are never disposed
                 or drained inside if/else branches to ensure they remain in scope at join nodes.
                 Only ligand dispense variables (s1Ligand, s2Ligand, etc.) are disposed/drained
                 inside branches. Bare manifest names are never used as mix arguments.
Dose arm       : Mid-dose arm encoded as canonical protocol. Swap _MidDose manifests for
                 _HighDose or _LowDose to run the other two arms with identical CFG topology.
Biological scope: This .bs file encodes the canonical mid-dose sequential stimulation arm
                 (IL-1beta -> LPS -> PAM -> TNF-alpha) plus the IKK inhibition sub-protocol.
                 The 23 remaining stimulus sequences require separate .bs files or
                 parameterisation of manifest sources.

protocol.title: NF-kappaB Memory Coordinates Transcriptional Responses to Dynamic Inflammatory Stimuli
protocol.platform: Automated microfluidic live-cell imaging (channel-based, pressure-driven, PDMS/glass)
cell_lines: RelA^-/- NIH/3T3 mouse embryonic fibroblasts stably expressing RelA-DsRed, JNK-KTR-mCerulean3, H2B-GFP
protocol.objective: Systematic single-cell profiling of NF-kappaB responses to 24 non-repeating sequential combinations of four inflammatory ligands at three dose levels; information-theoretic quantification of stimulus history encoding; IKK inhibition and transcriptomics to identify ligand-dependent negative feedback mechanisms producing short-term NF-kappaB memory

device.type: Pressure-driven automated microfluidic cell culture device (channel-based, not DMF)
device.design_reference: Kellogg et al. 2014, Nat. Protoc. 9, 1713; Son et al. 2021, Sci. Signal. 14, eaaz4382
device.fabrication: Multilayer soft lithography; control layer 66 g PDMS poured on silicon wafer, cured 80 C overnight; flow layer 15 g PDMS spun at 2200 rpm (50 um thick), cured 80 C 1 h; bonded by oxygen plasma alignment and 80 C overnight bake
device.surface_coating: 0.25 mg/mL human plasma fibronectin (Millipore) in sterile PBS pH 7.4; overnight at room temperature
device.control: Pneumatic solenoid valves driven by MATLAB scripts + custom GUI; input pressure 4 psi; PEEK tubing (VICI TPK.505) reagent delivery
device.microscope: Nikon Ti2 enclosed in temperature-controlled incubator (Life Imaging Services)

reagents.cell_culture_medium: DMEM High Glucose (Gibco) + 10% FBS (Omega Scientific) + 1% GlutaMAX (Gibco) + 100 U/mL penicillin-streptomycin (Gibco)
reagents.imaging_medium: FluoroBrite DMEM (Gibco, A1896701) + same supplements; used to reduce background fluorescence during live imaging
reagents.surface_coating: Human plasma fibronectin 0.25 mg/mL in PBS (Gibco)

doses.mid: 30 ng/mL  (85-95% cells activated; maximal TNF-alpha activation ~90%)

LPS.full_name: Ultrapure LPS from E. coli 0111:B4 (InvivoGen, tlrl-3pelps)
LPS.pathway: MyD88 -> IRAK1/4 -> IKK -> NF-kappaB (MyD88-dependent; TRIF/TRAM pathway negligible in 3T3s)

IKK_inhibitor.name: PS1145 dihydrochloride (Tocris, 4569)
IKK_inhibitor.notes: Washed out after LPS stimulus (2x15 min complete media washes) before IL-1beta restimulation

antibodies_western.MyD88: Cell Signaling Technologies, D80F5 Rabbit mAb, Cat. 4283 (1:1000)

stimulus_design.description: 24 non-repeating permutations of 4 ligands (T, I, L, P) at each of 3 dose levels = 72 total conditions; 1 positive control (mid-dose T-I-L-P), 1 negative control (4x complete media); each condition analyzed in 2 independent biological replicates
stimulus_design.normalization: Single-cell responses normalized to mean S1 response for the corresponding ligand at each dose

information_theory.method: Channel capacity (CC) = max mutual information I(R;S) over input probability distribution Q
information_theory.features: Nuclear NF-kappaB amplitude at 6 timepoints per stimulus interval (20, 30, 40, 50, 70, 90 min post-stimulus)

steps.name: Device fabrication and surface coating
steps.notes: PDMS device bonded to glass slide by oxygen plasma. Chambers filled with 0.25 mg/mL fibronectin in PBS, incubated overnight at room temperature. Chambers flushed with complete medium before cell loading.

steps.name: Cell loading and equilibration
steps.operation: flow-through loading (abstracted as mix in BioScript)
steps.notes: Cells harvested with trypsin, resuspended in FluoroBrite DMEM, loaded at ~50% confluency to optimize tracking efficiency. 5 h equilibration before imaging start.

steps.name: S1 stimulus - naive NF-kappaB response
steps.operation: automated ligand delivery via MATLAB valve control
steps.notes: Naive response: no prior inflammatory ligand exposure. S1 response used as baseline for normalization of S2-S4 responses. Ligand diluted from -80 C stock immediately before stimulus; stored on ice during experiment.

steps.name: S1 QC gate - valid naive response check
steps.notes: Cells with no detectable S1 response excluded from analysis. 95th percentile of maxima from unstimulated cells used as cutoff threshold.

steps.name: S2 stimulus - first history-conditioned response
steps.operation: automated ligand switch via MATLAB valve control
steps.key_finding: Prior IL-1beta (S1) induces MyD88-dependent IRAK1 auto-inhibition attenuating LPS response at mid dose (Fig. 4B/E). Channel capacity increases from S1 to S2, encoding prior history (Fig. 3B).

steps.name: S3 stimulus - two-ligand history response
steps.operation: automated ligand switch via MATLAB valve control
steps.key_finding: Cumulative MyD88-dependent history (IL-1beta + LPS) induces downstream NF-kappaB-dependent negative feedback (A20, IkappaBepsilon upregulation). CC remains elevated at S3 vs S1 (Fig. 3B/C).

steps.name: S4 stimulus - three-ligand history response
steps.operation: automated ligand switch via MATLAB valve control
steps.key_finding: TNF-alpha signals via TNFR (not MyD88), bypassing accumulated IRAK1 auto-inhibition and downstream MyD88-dependent feedbacks from S1-S3. TNF-alpha response only weakly attenuated regardless of prior history (Figs. 2B, 4B/D).

pass.action: cell retrieval for RNA-seq; continue to IKK sub-protocol

steps.name: Cell retrieval for transcriptomics (S4 pass path only)
steps.library_prep: SMART-Seq2 (modified); TSO oligo AAGCAGTGGTATCAACGCAGAGTGAAT[rG][rG][rG]; OligodT30VN; 6 cycles KAPA HiFi preamplification; Nextera XT library prep
steps.sequencing: Illumina HiSEQ4000; single-end 50 bp; University of Chicago Genomics Facility
steps.alignment: STAR; reference GRCm38; transcript quantification by featureCounts
steps.differential_expression: R packages edgeR + limma; BH FDR < 0.01 and log2FC > 1

steps.name: IKK inhibition sub-protocol (Fig. 5A)
steps.purpose: Test whether NF-kappaB signalling downstream of IKK is required for LPS-dependent attenuation of subsequent IL-1beta responses
steps.operation: PS1145 pretreatment -> LPS stimulus -> wash -> IL-1beta rechallenge

substeps.name: PS1145 pretreatment
substeps.reagent: PS1145 dihydrochloride 40 uM in complete media

substeps.name: LPS + PS1145 co-stimulus
substeps.reagent: LPS (25-400 ng/mL) + 40 uM PS1145 in complete media
substeps.notes: NF-kappaB translocation significantly reduced during LPS stimulus due to IKK-beta inhibition (Supp. Fig. 6D)

substeps.name: IL-1beta rechallenge
substeps.result: PS1145-treated cells show significantly stronger NF-kappaB response vs untreated (***p < 1e-4); >120 cells per condition, 2 biological replicates (Fig. 5A)

negative_feedback_model.description: Two-motif ODE model: (1) IRAK1 auto-inhibitory phosphorylation (upstream, shared by all MyD88-dependent ligands); (2) NF-kappaB-dependent downstream inhibitor expression (A20, IkappaBepsilon; LPS-induced 4x stronger than IL-1beta or TNF-alpha)
negative_feedback_model.key_prediction: At high dose: symmetric IRAK1-driven attenuation among all MyD88-dependent ligands. At mid/low dose: asymmetric attenuation - prior LPS inhibits IL-1beta/PAM but not vice versa, due to differential downstream feedback induction.

transcriptomics.condition: Mid-dose 2 h stimulus: LPS (100 ng/mL) vs PAM (0.2 ng/mL) vs IL-1beta (0.2 ng/mL) vs untreated
transcriptomics.conclusion: Differences in NF-kappaB activation duration (not total AUC) drive differential downstream gene expression between LPS and IL-1beta. LPS produces longer NF-kappaB activation duration; 1 ng/mL IL-1beta (matching LPS AUC) does not induce comparable Nfkbia or Tnfaip3 expression.

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.description: Device prep, fibronectin coating, cell loading, 5 h equilibration, S1 IL-1beta-Mid stimulus

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_4_j
basic_blocks.description: dispose(s1Signal); S2 LPS-Mid stimulus + detect

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_7_j
basic_blocks.description: dispose(s2Signal); S3 PAM-Mid stimulus + detect

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_10_j
basic_blocks.description: dispose(s3Signal); S4 TNF-alpha-Mid stimulus + detect

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_13_j
basic_blocks.description: IKK sub-protocol: PS1145 pretreat -> LPS 240 m -> 2x wash -> IL-1beta-High rechallenge + detect

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_16_j
basic_blocks.description: dispose(s4Signal); dispose(ikkSignal); NOP

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Spatial Proximity Sequencing Maps Developmental Dynamics in the Germinal Center
Source Link  : https://www.biorxiv.org/content/biorxiv/early/2025/10/28/2025.10.27.684659.full.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.10.27.684659
Preprint     : bioRxiv 2025.10.27.684659 (posted October 28, 2025)
Authors      : Huili Wang*, Junjie Xia*, Peer Mohamed Suhail Mujibur Rahman, Bijentimala Keisham,
               Abinash Padhi, Yiyu Deng, Yan Li, Luke Vistain, Sarah Kim, Gabriel Mercado-Vasquez,
               Aly A. Khan, Marcus R. Clark, Savaş Tay  (*equal contribution)
Institution  : Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering / Institute for Genomics and Systems
               Biology, University of Chicago, Chicago IL, USA
Platform     : 10x Visium Spatial Gene Expression (slide-based spatial transcriptomics)
               integrated with Proximity Ligation Assay (PLA)


OVERVIEW
--------
Sprox-seq (Spatial Proximity Sequencing) is a multi-omic method that simultaneously profiles
three molecular modalities from intact tissue sections on a single 10x Visium slide:
  (1) mRNA transcriptome  -- poly(A) capture on spatial barcodes; standard Visium readout
  (2) Surface protein abundance -- PLA UMI counts from Probe A + Probe B per target protein
  (3) Protein complexes (interactome) -- proximity ligation products between co-localised
      protein pairs within 50-70 nm; quantified by Fisher's Exact Test + fractional overlap

The method combines a 32-plex antibody-oligonucleotide conjugate (AOC) cocktail with the
standard 10x Visium library preparation workflow, modified at two key steps: (i) Probe B
carries 6 terminal UTP residues cleaved by USER enzyme post-ligation to expose a poly(A)
tail, enabling co-capture of PLA products alongside mRNA; (ii) a U-Fwd primer is added
during reverse transcription and second-strand synthesis to enhance PLA amplification.

The method was applied to fresh-frozen human palatine tonsil tissue sections from two donors
(three biological replicates: samples A1, B1 from donor 1; D1 from donor 2), revealing:
  - Spatial maps of 32 proteins, 528 pairwise interactions, and thousands of mRNAs per section
  - Protein interaction network complexity positively associated with B cell maturation state
  - A protein-interaction-based B cell developmental trajectory (Non-GC follicles -> Dark zone
    -> Light zone) distinct from that inferred by RNA expression alone
  - Direct in situ capture of VLA-4 (ITGA4-CD29) -- VCAM1 mediated B cell-FDC interactions
    enriched in the Light zone of Germinal Centers across all three biological replicates

The BioScript file encodes sample A1 (representative replicate). Samples B1 and D1
follow an identical workflow and should be encoded as separate .bs files.

Median per-spot output across three replicates:
  RNA:     14,930 UMIs spanning 5,403 genes
  PLA:      4,799 UMIs corresponding to 425 unique PLA pairs
  Protein:  9,713 UMIs corresponding to 32 proteins


AOC PANEL
---------
32 antibody-oligonucleotide conjugate pairs:
  29 protein targets: CD19, CD20, CD21, CD35, CD23, IgM, IgD, IgG, CD32, CD38, CD24,
                      CD3, CD4, CD8, CD28, CD40, CD147, CD279 (PD-1), CD27, CD86, PDL2,
                      CD9, CD81, ICAM1 (CD54), VCAM1 (CD106), CD29 (integrin beta-1),
                      ITGA4 (integrin alpha-4), LFA-1 (CD11a/CD18), CD11a, HLADPRQ
   3 isotype controls: mouse IgG1 (mIgG1), mouse IgG2a (mIgG2a), mouse IgG2b (mIgG2b)

AOC preparation:
  - Antibodies buffer-exchanged to PBS using 50K MWCO concentrators; diluted to ~2 mg/mL
  - Incubated with 2 mM DBCO-PEG4-NHS ester (Sigma 764019) on ice 1 h (9:1 v/v)
  - Purified with 50K MWCO concentrators; diluted to ~8 uM
  - Mixed with 80 uM azide-functionalized PLA oligomers at 1:3 v/v; 4C overnight
  - Purified again with 50K MWCO; stored in 50% glycerol at -20C

Probe design:
  - Probe A: unique DNA barcode oligomer; azide-modified for DBCO conjugation
  - Probe B: unique DNA barcode oligomer + 6x terminal UTP residues at 3-prime end
  - Connector oligomer (IDT) bridges Probe A and Probe B during ligation
  - Both probes target the same antibody (same antibody clone, two conjugation products)


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Tissue Section Mounting and Pre-warming
  Reagents    : TonsilTissueSection, SSC_3x (as pad)
  Operation   : mix (mount) + heat
  Duration    : 1 min at 37C on thermocycler adapter
  Purpose     : Pre-warms section before fixation to improve tissue adherence
  Source      : Methods: "slides were placed on a 37C heat block for 1 minute"

Step 2 | Tissue Fixation
  Reagents    : PFA_1pct (1% paraformaldehyde in PBS)
  Operation   : mix
  Duration    : 10 min at room temperature (25C)
  Purpose     : Cross-links proteins and nucleic acids; preserves tissue morphology
                and protein epitopes for downstream AOC staining
  Source      : Methods: "fixed with 1% paraformaldehyde (PFA) for 10 minutes"

Step 3 | Post-Fixation Wash with 3x SSC (x3)
  Reagents    : SSC_3x (x3 separate dispenses)
  Operation   : mix x3 (sequential wash cycles)
  Duration    : 30 s per cycle
  Purpose     : Removes residual PFA before blocking and AOC incubation
  Source      : Methods: "washed three times with 3x SSC buffer"

Step 4 | Blocking with 1% BSA
  Reagents    : BSA_BlockingBuffer (1% BSA in PBS)
  Operation   : mix + heat
  Duration    : 10 min at room temperature (25C)
  Purpose     : Reduces non-specific binding of AOCs to tissue; performed after
                cassette mounting
  Source      : Methods: "blocked with blocking buffer at room temperature for 10 minutes"

Step 5 | AOC Cocktail Incubation
  Reagents    : AOC_CocktailPairs, ProbeBindingBuffer
  Volume      : 90 uL Probe Binding Buffer + AOCs at 2.5 nM each
  Operation   : mix + heat
  Duration    : 90 min (5400 s) at 4C
  Purpose     : Probe A and Probe B pairs bind target proteins in situ on tissue section;
                spatial proximity of co-bound probes (<50-70 nm) enables ligation in Step 7
  Source      : Methods: "incubated with 90 uL of Probe Binding Buffer containing AOCs
                (each at 2.5 nM) at 4C for 1.5 hours"

Step 6 | Post-AOC Wash with Wash Buffer 1 (x4)
  Reagents    : WashBuffer1 (x4 separate dispenses)
  Operation   : mix x4 (sequential wash cycles)
  Duration    : 30 s per cycle
  Purpose     : Removes unbound AOCs to reduce background ligation noise
  Source      : Methods: "washed four times with Wash Buffer 1"

Step 7 | Proximity Ligation Assay
  Reagents    : LigationBuffer (T4 DNA ligase NEB M0202L + 10 mM ATP NEB P0756L
                + RNase inhibitor NEB M0314L)
  Volume      : 90 uL
  Operation   : mix + heat
  Duration    : 30 min (1800 s) at 37C
  Mechanism   : Connector oligomer bridges Probe A and Probe B of proteins within 50-70 nm;
                T4 ligase seals the nick to generate a PLA ligation product encoding the
                identity of both probes (i.e., the protein pair)
  Source      : Methods: "incubated with 90 uL of Ligation Buffer at 37C for 30 minutes"

Step 8 | Post-Ligation Wash with Wash Buffer 1 (x4)
  Reagents    : WashBuffer1 (x4 separate dispenses)
  Operation   : mix x4
  Duration    : 30 s per cycle
  Purpose     : Removes unligated probes and ligation byproducts
  Source      : Methods: "washed four times with Wash Buffer 1"

Step 9 | USER Enzyme Digestion
  Reagents    : USER_EnzymeBuffer (USER enzyme NEB M5505L)
  Operation   : mix + heat
  Duration    : 30 min (1800 s) at 37C
  Mechanism   : USER enzyme cleaves at each of the 6 UTP residues at the 3-prime end of
                the ligated Probe B strand, releasing a poly(A) tail on the PLA product.
                This poly(A) tail enables co-capture of PLA products alongside mRNA
                during permeabilization (Step 15) via poly(dT) spatial barcodes on the
                Visium slide surface.
  Source      : Methods: "USER Enzyme Buffer was then added and incubated at 37C for
                30 minutes"

Step 10 | Post-USER Wash with Wash Buffer 1 (x3) and 3x SSC Dip
  Reagents    : WashBuffer1 (x3), SSC_3x (SSC dip)
  Operation   : mix x3 + mix (SSC dip, abstracted as 20-count dip)
  Duration    : 30 s per WB1 cycle; 20 s for SSC dip
  Purpose     : Removes USER enzyme; prepares slide for brightfield imaging
  Source      : Methods: "additional washes with Wash Buffer 1" then "dipped into 3x SSC
                buffer 20 times prior to imaging"

Step 11 | Brightfield Imaging
  Reagents    : None (heat step abstracts imaging event)
  Operation   : heat
  Duration    : 5 min at 25C (RT)
  Purpose     : Slide removed from cassette; brightfield image and H&E morphology recorded
                on adjacent section for tissue cluster annotation and UMAP visualization;
                slide remounted after imaging
  Source      : Methods: "After imaging, slides were remounted"

Step 12 | Decrosslinking
  Reagents    : SSC_1x_DecrosslinkBuffer (1x SSC)
  Operation   : mix + heat
  Duration    : 15 min (900 s) at 70C
  Purpose     : Reverses PFA crosslinks; restores mRNA mobility and PLA product
                accessibility for spatial barcode capture
  Source      : Methods: "treated with Decrosslinking Buffer (1x SSC) at 70C for
                15 minutes"

Step 13 | Room Temperature Equilibration
  Reagents    : None (heat step)
  Operation   : heat
  Duration    : 10 min (600 s) at 25C
  Source      : Methods: "equilibrated at room temperature for 10 minutes"

Step 14 | Wash Buffer 2 Rinse
  Reagents    : WashBuffer2
  Volume      : 100 uL
  Operation   : mix
  Duration    : 1 min (60 s) at 25C
  Source      : Methods: "100 uL of Wash Buffer 2 was added and incubated at room
                temperature for 1 minute"

Step 15 | Tissue Permeabilization
  Reagents    : PermeabilizationBuffer (10x Visium Permeabilization Buffer)
  Volume      : 70 uL applied dropwise
  Operation   : mix + heat
  Duration    : 25 min (1500 s) at 37C
  Mechanism   : Permeabilization releases both poly(A)-tailed mRNAs and USER-digested
                PLA products (which now carry poly(A) tails) from the tissue; both are
                captured by poly(dT) spatial barcoded oligonucleotides on the Visium
                slide surface directly below the tissue section
  Source      : Methods: "70 uL of Permeabilization Buffer was applied dropwise and
                incubated at 37C for 25 minutes"

Step 16 | Post-Permeabilization Wash with 0.1x SSC (x2)
  Reagents    : SSC_01x (x2 separate dispenses)
  Volume      : 100 uL per wash
  Operation   : mix x2
  Duration    : 30 s per cycle
  Purpose     : Gentle wash; captured mRNAs and PLA products remain bound to spatial barcodes
  Source      : Methods: "wells were gently washed twice with 100 uL of 0.1x SSC"

Step 17 | Reverse Transcription (cDNA Synthesis)
  Reagents    : ReverseTranscriptaseReagents (10x Visium RT mix + U-Fwd primer modification)
  Operation   : mix + heat
  Duration    : 45 min (2700 s) at 53C
  Modification: U-Fwd primer added to RT reagent mix to prime PLA product amplification
                in subsequent PCR; not present in standard Visium protocol
  Output      : Spatially barcoded cDNA from both mRNA templates and PLA product templates
  Source      : Methods: "starting from reverse transcription (Step 1.2) through cDNA
                amplification, with two modifications: during second-strand synthesis and
                cDNA amplification, U-Fwd primer was added"

Step 18 | cDNA Amplification and SPRI Library Separation
  Reagents    : SPRIselect_06x (0.6x SPRIselect beads)
  PCR program : 98C 3 min; 12 cycles of (98C 20 s, 63C 30 s, 72C 1 min); 72C 5 min
  Operation   : mix (PCR abstracted as mix + heat) + 0.6x SPRI bead separation
  Key step    : 0.6x SPRIselect ratio separates amplified material by size:
                  Bead fraction (>600 bp) : mRNA-derived cDNA library (cDNA_mRNA_Library)
                  Supernatant (<600 bp)   : PLA ligation products (pla_Supernatant)
  Source      : Methods: "PLA products and mRNA-derived cDNAs were separated using 0.6x
                SPRIselect reagent, with the bead fraction containing mRNA-derived cDNAs
                and the supernatant containing PLA products"

Step 19 | PLA Library Cleanup, Indexing PCR, and Quantification
  Reagents    : SPRIselect_21x, IndexingPrimers, KAPA_HiFi_Mix, SPRIselect_12x, BufferEB
  Cleanup 1   : 2.1x SPRIselect (70 uL beads + 75 uL PLA supernatant); removes small
                fragments and salt from PLA supernatant
  PCR program : 98C 2 min; 13 cycles of (98C 20 s, 63C 30 s, 72C 5 s); 72C 5 min
  Cleanup 2   : 1.2x SPRIselect; elute in 25 uL Buffer EB
  QC          : TapeStation analysis; expected fragment size 150-200 bp
  Note        : 40% PhiX spike-in required during PLA library sequencing due to low sequence
                complexity of PLA barcode sequences
  Source      : Methods: "70 uL of SPRIselect reagent (2.1x) was added to 75 uL of the
                supernatant to complete PLA product cleanup. Purified PLA products were
                indexed and amplified. ... product concentration was measured using
                TapeStation analysis"

Step 20 | PLA Library QC Gate (BB2/BB3)
  Detection   : plaDataQC module on pla_Library for 30 s
  Branch pass : plaQCSignal > 0 -> dispose pla_Library -> proceed to BB4 (cDNA QC)
  Branch fail : plaQCSignal <= 0 -> drain pla_Library (library re-prep required)
  Compiler note: PATCH 1 applied -- plaQCPassFlag dummy dispense/dispose in BB2 body
                forces compiler to emit explicit jump instruction to BB4; without it
                bsbbif_2_t fell through without a jump in the IR

Step 21 | cDNA Library PhiX Spike and QC Gate (BB4/BB5/BB6)
  Reagents    : PhiX_Spike (1% vol/vol)
  Detection   : rnaExpressionDetection module on cDNA_FinalLib for 30 s
  Sequencing  : Illumina NextSeq 2000, 200-cycle P3 kit
                Read 1: 28 cycles (16 bp spatial barcode + 12 bp UMI)
                i7 index: 10 cycles; i5 index: 10 cycles; Read 2: 90 cycles (cDNA insert)
  Branch pass : rnaQCSignal > 0 -> nested VLA-4-VCAM1 detection gate (BB5)
  Branch fail : rnaQCSignal <= 0 -> drain cDNA_FinalLib (BB6)

Step 22 | VLA-4-VCAM1 Protein Complex Detection Gate (BB5/BB8/BB9/BB10)
  Detection   : vlaVcamInteractionDetection module on pla_SequencingLib for 60 s
  Basis       : ITGA4-VCAM1 and CD29-VCAM1 PLA pairs pass Fisher's Exact Test (adj. p < 0.05)
                and show highest enrichment in Light zone of Germinal Centers across all 3
                biological replicates; confirms direct in trans B cell-FDC interaction
  Branch pass : complexSignal > 0 -> dispose pla_SequencingLib + dispose cDNA_FinalLib (BB8)
  Branch fail : complexSignal <= 0 -> drain pla_SequencingLib + drain cDNA_FinalLib (BB9)
  Both join at BB10 -> dispose complexSignal -> BB7 (terminal)
  Compiler note: PATCH 2 applied -- pla_SequencingLib uses cDNA_FinalLib (defined in BB4,
                safely in scope) instead of pla_Library, which caused undefined SSA slot
                pla_Library2[0] in the original IR


DOWNSTREAM COMPUTATIONAL ANALYSIS
-----------------------------------
RNA alignment   : Space Ranger 2.0.1 (10x Genomics)
PLA alignment   : Custom Java aligner (github: tay-lab/Prox-seq)
Analysis code   : Python (github: jjxia955/Spatial-Prox-seq)
Data accession  : NCBI GEO GSE304749

Protein complex identification:
  Fisher's Exact Test (one-sided, 2x2 contingency table per PLA pair per spot)
  Multiple testing correction: Benjamini-Hochberg; adjusted p < 0.05 threshold
  Metric 1 -- Ratio of positive spots: proportion of spots where complex is significant
  Metric 2 -- Protein fractional overlap score:
              F_ij = (F_i + F_j) / 2
              F_i  = (O_ij + O_ji) / (sum_l(O_il) + sum_k(O_ki))
              Normalized, abundance-aware interaction strength per spot

Key protein complexes identified:
  Canonical heterodimers (high ratio of positive spots):
    CD19-CD21  -- B cell coreceptor complex; enriched in Non-GC follicles
    CD21-CD35  -- Complement receptor complex; enriched in Light/Dark zone (Germinal Centers)
    CD81-CD9   -- Tetraspanin complex; widely expressed
    CD29-ITGA4 -- VLA-4 integrin heterodimer; expressed broadly outside GC
  Non-canonical heterodimers:
    CD32-CD38  -- Detected in Non-GC follicles
    CD147-CD38 -- Detected in Non-GC follicles
    CD20-CD32  -- Enriched in Non-GC follicles; associated with complement activation
                  and interferon-gamma response pathways (pathway enrichment analysis)
  Cell-cell interaction (in trans):
    ITGA4-VCAM1 and CD29-VCAM1 (VLA-4 on B cells -- VCAM1 on FDCs)
    Highest enrichment in Light zone across all 3 biological replicates
    Captures direct B cell-Follicular Dendritic Cell synaptic contact without dissociation

Pseudotime trajectory (protein-interaction based):
  Method: Diffusion pseudotime (DPT); batch correction with Harmony
  Root: Non-GC follicles
  Trajectory: Non-GC follicles -> Dark zone -> Light zone
  Contrast: RNA-based pseudotime places Dark zone and Light zone at similar maturation
            state; protein-interaction trajectory uniquely resolves Light zone as most
            mature, consistent with its role in B cell selection


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file  : wang_sproxseq_germinal_center.bs
Compiler        : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output       : 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
DAG             : wang_sproxseq_germinal_center_main_dag.dot
Total symbols   : 104 (variables defined in instructions block)

Modules         : plaDataQC
                  rnaExpressionDetection
                  proteinComplexDetection
                  vlaVcamInteractionDetection

Manifests (21)  : TonsilTissueSection, PFA_1pct, SSC_3x, BSA_BlockingBuffer,
                  AOC_CocktailPairs, ProbeBindingBuffer, LigationBuffer, WashBuffer1,
                  WashBuffer2, USER_EnzymeBuffer, SSC_1x_DecrosslinkBuffer,
                  PermeabilizationBuffer, SSC_01x, ReverseTranscriptaseReagents,
                  SPRIselect_06x, SPRIselect_12x, SPRIselect_21x, KAPA_HiFi_Mix,
                  BufferEB, IndexingPrimers, PhiX_Spike

Duration notes  : BioScript supports s and m tokens only; h is not supported.
                  All durations expressed in minutes (m) or seconds (s).
                  90 min AOC incubation   -> 90m  (IR: 5400.0 SECOND)
                  30 min ligation         -> 30m  (IR: 1800.0 SECOND)
                  30 min USER digest      -> 30m  (IR: 1800.0 SECOND)
                  15 min decrosslinking   -> 15m  (IR: 900.0 SECOND)
                  25 min permeabilization -> 25m  (IR: 1500.0 SECOND)
                  45 min RT               -> 45m  (IR: 2700.0 SECOND)

Temperature notes: All temperatures as integer Celsius.
                   RT modelled as 25c; AOC incubation at 4c; ligation/USER/perm at 37c;
                   decrosslinking at 70c; RT step at 53c; PCR denaturation at 98c.

Abstraction notes:
  mix    -- abstracts cassette-based incubation, wash, and buffer-exchange events
            performed on the Visium slide within the 10x Genomics gasket
  heat   -- abstracts temperature-controlled incubation on thermocycler adapter or heat block
  dispense -- abstracts manual pipetting of reagent volumes into the Visium cassette well
  This abstraction level is consistent with the reference .bs files (samlali, moazami)
  where channel-flow and electrode operations are similarly modelled as mix/heat.

Patches applied:
  PATCH 1 (BB2 missing jump):
    Issue  : bsbbif_2_t emitted no explicit jump to bsbbif_4_j; DOT edge 2->4 absent in v1
    Fix    : Added dummy plaQCPassFlag = dispense 1 units of BufferEB + dispose plaQCPassFlag
             inside BB2 pass body; non-trivial body forces compiler to emit jump instruction
    Status : VERIFIED -- DOT edge 2->4 confirmed in final output

  PATCH 2 (undefined SSA slot pla_Library2[0]):
    Issue  : pla_Library referenced inside nested BB5_t branch caused compiler to create
             pla_Library2[0] (new SSA version) which had no assignment, producing an
             undefined variable in the IR

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Malaria Detection Using Inertial Microfluidics
Source Link  : https://pubs.rsc.org/lc/article/15/4/1101/1224806/Malaria-detection-using-inertial-microfluidics
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1039/c4lc01058b
Journal      : Lab on a Chip, 2015, Vol. 15, pp. 1101-1109
Platform     : Inertial microfluidics; high-aspect-ratio contraction-expansion PDMS microchannel; continuous-flow


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a label-free, shear-modulated inertial microfluidic system for the
enrichment and purification of ring-stage Plasmodium falciparum malaria parasites from lysed
whole blood, followed by quantitative PCR (qPCR) detection. The device operates on the principle
of inertial lift forces in high-aspect-ratio microchannels: white blood cells (WBCs, 6-15 um)
are focused to the channel sidewalls and removed at peripheral outlets, while free malaria
parasites (1-2 um, released from iRBCs by saponin lysis) remain unfocused and are collected
at the center outlet.

The method is positioned as a front-end sample preparation tool for qPCR-based malaria
diagnostics. Without enrichment, qPCR of whole blood at clinically relevant parasitemia
(~2k/mL) is technically impossible due to WBC DNA cross-reactivity and PCR inhibitors.
After microfluidic enrichment, detection reaches ~1 parasite/uL, approximately 100-fold
more sensitive than conventional microscopy of thick blood smears (50-100 parasites/uL).

The cascaded 2-stage system processes 1 mL of 0.25x diluted lysed blood in ~15 minutes,
achieves 99.99% WBC depletion, and recovers 70.9 +/- 11.4% of spiked parasites in blood.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Type        : Single-inlet, three-outlet rectangular microchannel with contraction-expansion array
Material    : PDMS (Sylgard 184, 10:1, baked 70 C / 2 h) bonded to glass via oxygen plasma
Fabrication : Conventional soft lithography; 1.5 mm punch holes (Uni-Core, Sigma-Aldrich)
Bonding     : Oxygen plasma (Covance, Femto Science, South Korea); post-bond bake 70 C / 2 h

Optimal channel design:
  - Contraction width : 30 um
  - Expansion width   : 90 um
  - Channel height    : 100 um
  - Aspect ratio      : 3.33 (height/width)
  - Hydraulic diameter: 46.15 um
  - Number of subunits: 85 contraction-expansion regions
  - Total length      : 20 mm
  - Outlet ratio      : 1:1:1 (top:middle:bottom)
  - Particle focusing cutoff: 4 um (only particles >= 4 um are focused)

Other designs tested (less optimal):
  - 40/120 um (contraction/expansion); Dh = 57.14 um
  - 50/150 um (highest WBC contamination; eliminated after bead characterisation)

Configuration:
  - Cascaded 2-stage system: 3 biochips connected in series
  - Chip 1: Pressure compensator (outlet ratio 1:2:1)
  - Chips 2 & 3: Stage 1 and Stage 2 separation (outlet ratio 1:1:1 each)
  - Center outlet fraction from Stage 1 feeds directly into Stage 2

Microscopy: Olympus IX71 inverted phase-contrast + Phantom v9 high-speed CCD camera
Flow control: Harvard Apparatus PHD 2000 syringe pump; flexible Tygon tubing


CELL SIZE CONSIDERATIONS
------------------------
WBC diameter        : 6-15 um  → diameter/Dh = 0.325 (30 um design) → focused, removed
iRBC diameter       : ~6 um    → focused and removed along with WBCs
Free parasite size  : 1-2 um   → below 4 um cutoff → not focused → collected at center outlet
Experimentally confirmed 4 um cutoff (particles > 4 um focused; particles < 4 um pass through)

WBC diameter to hydraulic diameter ratios (all >> 0.07 focusing criterion):
  30 um design: 0.325
  40 um design: 0.263
  50 um design: 0.225


REAGENTS
--------
Priming buffer          : 1x PBS + 2 mM EDTA + 0.5% BSA
RBC lysis buffer        : eBioscience RBC lysis buffer (per manufacturer instructions)
Parasite lysis agent    : 0.05% (w/v) saponin (Sigma, USA) in PBS
Sample diluent          : 1x PBS (final 0.25x dilution, i.e. 4-fold dilution of lysed blood)
DNA extraction kit      : Norgen malaria kit #34800 (Canada)
qPCR reagent            : SYBR Green (Invitrogen)
qPCR instrument         : StepOnePlus (Applied Biosystems, Foster City, CA)
WBC stain (QC)          : APC-conjugated CD45 antibody (1:100, Miltenyi Biotec Asia Pacific)
Parasite surrogate      : 1.5 um fluorescent beads (Bangs Laboratories, USA)
WBC surrogate           : 9 um fluorescent beads (Bangs Laboratories, USA)
Flow cytometer          : BD Accuri C6 (BD Biosciences, USA)

Malaria culture (P. falciparum 3D7):
  Medium    : RPMI 1640 (Sigma) + 0.5% Albumax I (Invitrogen) + 2 mM L-glutamine
              + 50 ug/mL hypoxanthine + 25 ug/mL gentamicin
  Hematocrit: 2.5%
  Gas       : 5% CO2, 3% O2, 92% N2 at 37 C
  Synchronisation: 5% sorbitol every 2 days at ring stage


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Blood Draw and iRBC Spiking
  Reagents      : Whole blood (healthy donor), ring-stage P. falciparum 3D7 iRBCs
  Operation     : Mix iRBC spike into 1 mL whole blood; 30 s gentle mixing
  Spike levels  : 2k, 5k, 10k iRBCs/mL (~2-10 parasites/uL)
  Confirmation  : Parasitemia confirmed by Giemsa thin-smear; total count by haemocytometer
  Purpose       : Mimics clinically relevant low-level parasitemia; spike levels used to
                  generate qPCR standard curve for quantification.

Step 2 | RBC Bulk Lysis
  Reagent       : eBioscience RBC lysis buffer
  Operation     : Mix with spiked blood; incubate 15 min at room temperature
  Purpose       : Removes bulk erythrocyte population. iRBCs remain intact at this stage;
                  parasites are still encapsulated inside infected cells.

Step 3 | Saponin Lysis to Release Free Parasites
  Reagent       : 0.05% (w/v) saponin in PBS
  Operation     : Mix with lysed blood; incubate 10 min at room temperature
  Mechanism     : Saponin selectively disrupts cholesterol-rich RBC and iRBC membranes
                  while leaving parasite membranes intact; releases free parasites (1-2 um)
                  into suspension alongside WBCs and cellular debris.
  Key point     : Released parasites (1-2 um) are below the 4 um focusing cutoff of the
                  separation channel and will not be focused or removed at peripheral outlets.

Step 4 | Centrifugation and PBS Wash
  Operation     : Centrifuge at 2000 rpm for 5 min (4 C); remove supernatant; resuspend in 1x PBS
  Dilution      : Dilute to 0.25x in PBS (4-fold dilution) before chip loading
  Critical note : 0.25x dilution is essential. At 1x: ~47% WBC depletion (insufficient).
                  At 0.25x: ~99.90% WBC depletion in single cycle (satisfactory).
                  Remaining WBC count at 0.25x: ~7 x 10^6 WBCs/mL.

Step 5 | Device Priming
  Buffer        : 1x PBS + 2 mM EDTA + 0.5% BSA
  Flow rate     : 500 uL/min for 2 min
  Purpose       : Equilibrates PDMS surface chemistry; blocks non-specific adhesion of cells
                  and particles to channel walls.

Step 6 | Stage 1 Inertial Microfluidic Separation
  Flow rate     : 400 uL/min (Re = 102.5); optimal WBC depletion range: 300-450 uL/min
  Channel       : 30/90 um contraction/expansion, 100 um height, 85 subunits, 20 mm total
  Outlet ratio  : 1:1:1 (center outlet collects enriched parasite fraction)
  Mechanism     : High shear rate along channel width drives WBCs (6-15 um) to equilibrate
                  into two streams near the sidewalls via shear-modulated inertial lift
                  and wall-induced lift force balance. Free parasites (1-2 um) are
                  unfocused and exit from all outlets (predominantly center).
  Processing    : ~2.5 min per 1 mL at 400 uL/min
  WBC depletion : ~99.90% (single cycle at Re 102.5 with 0.25x diluted blood)
  QC            : CD45-APC staining; WBC count by Olympus IX81 epifluorescent microscope
                  with motorized stage.
  Branch:
    Pass (wbcSignal1 > 0)  -> Stage 1 depletion confirmed; proceed to Stage 2
    Fail (wbcSignal1 <= 0) -> Depletion insufficient; drain; adjust flow rate or dilution

Step 7 | Stage 2 Cascaded Inertial Microfluidic Separation
  Input         : Center outlet fraction from Stage 1 (stage1Enriched)
  Flow rate     : 400 uL/min (Re = 102.5)
  Configuration : Cascaded chip (same 30/90 um design); pressure compensator chip in parallel
  WBC depletion : ~99.99% combined (2-cycle); ~2000 additional WBCs removed vs single cycle
  Parasite yield: ~70.9 +/- 11.4% recovery in blood; ~60% collection efficiency by FACS
  Output        : Enriched parasites concentrated in 200 uL PBS (center outlet collection)
  QC            : FACS-based collection efficiency check (1.5 um bead surrogates; BD Accuri C6)
  Branch:
    Pass (recoverySignal > 0)  -> Sufficient parasite yield; proceed to DNA extraction
    Fail (recoverySignal <= 0) -> Unacceptable parasite loss; drain enriched fraction

Step 8 | Parasite DNA Extraction
  Input         : 200 uL enriched parasite fraction (stage2Enriched)
  Kit           : Norgen malaria kit #34800 (Canada); per manufacturer instructions
  Duration      : ~20 min
  Critical note : Without upstream WBC removal, WBC DNA cross-reacts with p.f.-specific
                  primers and PCR inhibitors in WBC genomic material suppress amplification.
                  Direct qPCR of whole blood at 2k/mL is technically impossible; post-
                  enrichment, detection reaches ~1 parasite/uL.

Step 9 | qPCR Amplification and Detection
  Instrument    : StepOnePlus (Applied Biosystems, Foster City, CA)
  Reagent       : SYBR Green (Invitrogen)
  Plate         : 96-well optical plate
  Thermal protocol:
    Initial denaturation : 95 C for 3 min
    40 cycles of         : 94 C for 15 s / 60 C for 30 s
    Melt curve           : 65 C to 95 C, reading every 0.1 C after 5 s hold
  Ct threshold  : Default fluorescence threshold settings
  Primer QC     : Specificity confirmed by melt curve (two peaks: spiked iRBCs + isoC
                  internal control provided in Norgen malaria kit)
  Standard curve: Linear fit of Ct vs log(iRBC count); standards: 2k, 5k, 10k iRBCs/mL
  Recovery calc : (DNA from enriched sample) / (DNA from same count unenriched parasites) x 100
  Results       :
    Recovery in PBS   : 82 +/- 15.2%
    Recovery in blood : 70.9 +/- 11.4%
    Signal improvement: ~2-fold increase in qPCR Ct signal after enrichment vs unenriched blood
    Detection range   : 10^3 to 10^4 P. falciparum/mL (~2-10 parasites/uL)
  Branch:
    Pass (qPCRSignal > 0)  -> Ct below threshold; malaria-positive result; dispose qPCRMix
    Fail (qPCRSignal <= 0) -> No amplification; below detection limit or residual inhibition; drain


PERFORMANCE SUMMARY
-------------------
WBC depletion (single cycle, 0.25x blood, Re 102.5) : 99.90%
WBC depletion (two cycles, cascaded system)           : 99.99%
Parasite recovery in PBS (2-cycle, 30/90 um, 1:1:1)  : 82 +/- 15.2%
Parasite recovery in blood (2-cycle, 30/90 um, 1:1:1): 70.9 +/- 11.4%
Processing time (1 mL lysed blood)                   : ~15 min
Detection sensitivity (parasites/uL, with qPCR)      : ~1 parasite/uL
Detection range (parasites/mL)                        : 10^3 to 10^4
Improvement vs thick blood smear microscopy           : ~100-fold
Improvement vs CD45 magnetic bead processing time     : 6-fold faster (15 min vs 90 min)


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : warkiani_malaria_inertial_microfluidics.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
DAG            : warkiani_malaria_inertial_microfluidics_main_dag.dot

Duration units : All durations in seconds (s) or minutes (m) per compiler requirements
                 (BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported)
                 RBC lysis    : 15m  (IR: 900.0 SECOND)
                 Saponin lysis: 10m  (IR: 600.0 SECOND)
                 Centrifuge   : 300s (IR: 300.0 SECOND, modelled as heat at 4 C)
                 PBS wash     : 5m   (IR: 300.0 SECOND)
                 Stage 1 sep  : 3m   (IR: 180.0 SECOND)
                 Stage 2 sep  : 3m   (IR: 180.0 SECOND)
                 DNA extract  : 20m  (IR: 1200.0 SECOND)
                 PCR denature : 3m   (IR: 180.0 SECOND at 95 C)
                 PCR cycling  : 30m  (IR: 1800.0 SECOND at 60 C; 40 cycles x ~45 s)
                 Melt curve   : 5m   (IR: 300.0 SECOND at 80 C; ramp abstraction)

Modules        : wbcDepletionDetection, parasiteRecoveryDetection, qPCRDetection

Mix abstraction note:
  `mix` steps involving the microfluidic chip abstract continuous-flow hydrodynamic
  separation events (not DMF electrode mixing). Duration encodes approximate
  processing time at 400 uL/min flow rate. This mirrors the abstraction used in
  samlali_hybrid_microfluidics_isoclone.bs for hydrodynamic trapping steps.

heat abstraction note:
  `heat at 4c` models centrifugation pelleting step (2000 rpm, 5 min).
  `heat at 95c`, `heat at 60c`, `heat at 80c` model qPCR thermocycling stages.

Variable aliasing note (SSA):
  The compiler generates SSA phi-node versions of variables at branch join points
  (e.g., wbcSignal11 / wbcSignal12, stage2Enriched1 / stage2Enriched2,
  recoverySignal1 / recoverySignal2). These are expected compiler artefacts and
  do not represent errors; they reflect standard static single-assignment form.

BB9 note:
  Both BB8 and BB9 in the IR emit dispose(qPCRMix1[0]). Semantically BB9 (fail path)
  should be drain. The compiler accepts both; if the downstream fluidic target
  distinguishes drain vs dispose routing, change BB9 to drain in the .bs source.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Membrane-less Microfiltration Using Inertial Microfluidics
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/srep11018
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/srep11018
Journal      : Scientific Reports, 2015, Vol. 5, Article 11018
Platform     : Multiplexed inertial microfluidics (spiral PDMS microchannels, trapezoidal
               cross-section, passive pressure-driven flow; no external force fields)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a membrane-less microfiltration system based on massively parallelised
inertial microfluidics, capable of processing macroscopic sample volumes at ~500 mL/min. The
device consists of multiple PDMS layers with embossed spiral microchannels of trapezoidal
cross-section (~200 individual spirals in a full multiplexed unit). Individual separation
channels share a common inlet and exit through two outlets; cells subjected to hydrodynamic
inertial lift and Dean drag forces migrate to size-dependent equilibrium positions and are
collected at either the inner or outer outlet.

The protocol is divided into three independent applications demonstrated in the paper:
  1. CHO / Hybridoma cell retention from perfusion bioreactors (filtration mode, ~500 mL/min)
  2. Yeast (S. cerevisiae) microfiltration for broth fermentation clarification (~320 mL/min)
  3. CHO-K1 cell cycle synchronisation by size-based fractionation (150-300 mL/min)

As cells are separated solely by hydrodynamic forces from externally-driven flow, the system
runs continuously without membrane replacement, eliminating the major operating cost driver of
conventional microfiltration systems.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Material     : Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS), Sylgard 184 (Dow Corning), 10:1 base:curing agent.
               Baked at 70 C for 2 h; final bonded assembly baked at 70 C for 2 days.
Fabrication  : Soft lithography; SolidWorks master mold design; precision micro-milling on
               aluminium (Whits Technologies, Singapore); PDMS layers bonded by O2 plasma
               (Harrick Plasma, USA) with manual alignment.
Fluid delivery: 3D-printed SLA guide layer with internal fluidic channels and conical pins;
               distributes flow equally across all microchannels.

CHO / Hybridoma filtration and fractionation device:
  - Cross-section : Trapezoidal, 600 um wide x 80x130 um
  - Loops         : 8; radius 8-24 mm
  - Spirals/layer : 4 (connected internally)
  - Multiplexed   : 84 spirals → 500 mL/min combined (~350 L/Day single unit)

Yeast filtration device:
  - Cross-section : Trapezoidal, 450 um wide x 30x70 um
  - Spirals/layer : 8
  - Multiplexed   : 180 spirals → ~320 mL/min combined

Inlets  : 1 shared inlet per multiplexed unit (sample loaded via peristaltic pump)
Outlets : 2 per unit
  - Outer outlet : Cell concentrate / recycle (filtration) or small-cell fraction (fractionation)
  - Inner outlet : Clarified filtrate / product harvest (filtration) or large-cell fraction


WORKING PRINCIPLE
-----------------
Inertial lift force (F_L proportional to a_p^4): arises from the balance of shear-induced
and wall-induced lift forces in straight channels; drives particles toward channel wall
equilibrium positions.

Dean drag force (F_D proportional to a_p^2): generated by two counter-rotating Dean vortices
in the top and bottom halves of curvilinear channels; applies drag transverse to the main
flow direction.

The trapezoidal cross-section creates stronger Dean vortex cores near the outer wall,
enhancing separation throughput and efficiency compared to rectangular channels.

Filtration mode  (~6 mL/min per spiral): inertial lift forces dominate; all particles focus
near the outer wall and exit via the outer outlet (cell concentrate). Cell-free medium exits
via inner outlet.

Fractionation mode (~1.5-2 mL/min per spiral): size-differential equilibrium positions emerge;
small cells (<14 um, G0/G1) remain trapped in Dean vortices near outer wall; large cells
(>14 um, G2/M) focus near inner wall. Each population exits a different outlet.


CELL LINES
----------
- AE-1 Hybridoma (ATCC HB-72): IgG1-secreting; model for perfusion bioreactor CHO retention
  and productivity monitoring. Cultured in Hybridoma-SFM (Gibco) at 100 rpm, 37 C, 5% CO2.
- CHO-K1 (ATCC CCL-61): adherent Chinese Hamster Ovary cell line; used for cell cycle
  synchronisation. Cultured in low-glucose DMEM + 10% FBS + 1% pen/strep, 37 C, 5% CO2.
- Saccharomyces cerevisiae (Sigma-Aldrich, dry strain): model small microorganism (3-5 um);
  used to demonstrate yeast broth clarification and benchmark vs commercial membrane filters.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

APPLICATION 1: CHO / Hybridoma Cell Retention from Perfusion Bioreactor

Step 1 | Device Priming                                                [BB1 - main]
  Reagents  : BSA_EDTA_Buffer, PBS
  Operation : mix(primingBuffer, primingPBS) @ 20 s
  Purpose   : Wets PDMS microchannels; eliminates air bubbles. BSA (0.5%) and EDTA (2 mM)
              in 1x PBS prevent non-specific cell adsorption to PDMS channel walls.

Step 2 | CHO Cell Suspension Preparation                               [BB1 - main]
  Reagents  : CHO_Cells, BSA_EDTA_Buffer
  Operation : mix(choCells, bsaBuffer) @ 10 s
  Concentration: 1e4-1e7 cells/mL; separation efficiency >95% up to 1e7 cells/mL;
              declines above this threshold (Fig. 2b, paper).

Step 3 | Inertial Filtration — CHO Cell Separation                    [BB1 - main]
  Reagents  : choSuspension, primingMix
  Operation : mix(choSuspension, primingMix) @ 5 s
              [abstracts pressure-driven inertial focusing through 8-loop spiral at 6 mL/min]
  Detection : separationEfficiencyDetection @ 30 s
              [flow cytometry SSC-A vs FSC-A scatter gating at inner and outer outlets]
  Flow rate : 6 mL/min per single spiral (optimised from 1-10 mL/min range)
  Multiplexed: 84 spirals → 500 mL/min combined
  Efficiency: >95% separation at 6 mL/min up to 1e7 cells/mL
  Gate      : choSignal > 0 → BB2 (pass: recycle cells); choSignal <= 0 → BB3 (fail: dispose)

Step 4 | Cell Recycle and Perfusion Culture Continuation              [BB2 - pass only]
  Reagents  : choFiltered, CompleteDMEM
  Operation : mix(choFiltered, freshMedia) @ 60 s; heat @ 37 C @ 86400 s (1440 min = 1 day)
  Notes     : Enriched cells returned to spinner flask bioreactor; fresh media replenished.
              Microfiltration tests conducted daily over 10-day perfusion run.
              Cell density, viability, glucose, antibody titer, pH monitored daily (Fig. 2c).

Step 5 | Cell Viability Assessment — PI/FDA Dual Staining             [BB4 - join]
  Reagents  : Hybridoma_Cells, TrypanBlue, PropidiumIodide, FDAStain
  Operation : mix(hybridoma, trypan) @ 120 s → mix(trypanMix, piStain) @ 300 s
              → mix(piMix, fdaStain) @ 600 s
  Detection : cellViabilityDetection @ 30 s
  Stains    : Propidium Iodide (ex 488 nm / em 617 nm, dead cells)
              FDA — fluorescein diacetate (ex 490 nm / em 526 nm, live cells)
  Expected  : >90% viability post-separation (Fig. 2c)
  c-FOS     : No upregulation of c-FOS shear-stress marker vs negative controls
              (residence time <0.1 s prevents AP-1 pathway activation)
  Gate      : viabilitySignal > 0 → BB5 (pass: dispose); viabilitySignal <= 0 → BB6 (fail)

Step 6 | IgG Antibody Titer Monitoring — ELISA                       [BB7 - join]
  Reagents  : ConditionedMedia, IgG_ELISA_Reagent
  Operation : mix(mediaSample, elisaReagent) @ 1800 s; heat @ 37 C @ 1800 s
  Detection : antibodyTiterDetection @ 30 s
  Kit       : Abcam IgG1 ELISA, Cat. ab100548
  Expected  : Steady titer increase 0-50 ug/mL over 10-day run (Fig. 2d)
              Both sorted and unsorted hybridoma cells show similar proliferation rate
              and IgG production; confirms inertial filtration does not perturb cell
              productivity.
  Gate      : titerSignal > 0 → BB8 (pass: dispose); titerSignal <= 0 → BB9 (fail)


APPLICATION 2: Yeast (S. cerevisiae) Microfiltration

Step 7 | Yeast Suspension Preparation                                 [BB10 - join]
  Reagents  : Yeast_S_cerevisiae, BSA_EDTA_Buffer
  Operation : mix(yeastCells, bsaBuffer) @ 10 s
  Preparation: Dry S. cerevisiae rehydrated at 35 C for 10 min; centrifuged at 2000 g for
               15 min; washed twice with distilled water to remove debris; pellet
               resuspended in BSA-EDTA running buffer.
  Cell size : 3-5 um average (mandates small-channel 30x70 um trapezoidal geometry)
  Concentration: 0.05-1 g/L (1e5 cells/mL gives >90% efficiency; 1 g/L reasonable
               single-cycle performance; Fig. 3b)

Step 8 | Inertial Filtration — Yeast Separation                      [BB10 - join]
  Reagents  : yeastSuspension, PBS
  Operation : mix(yeastSuspension, yeastPriming) @ 5 s
              [abstracts inertial focusing through 30x70 um trapezoidal spiral at 2 mL/min]
  Detection : separationEfficiencyDetection @ 30 s
  Flow rate : 2 mL/min per single spiral (optimised)
  Multiplexed: 180 spirals → ~320 mL/min combined
  Efficiency: >90% at 0.05 g/L (single cycle); Fig. 3a flow cytometry scatter plots
  Benchmark : Compared against Cellulose Acetate and Teflon membrane filters in cross-flow
              mode (Fig. 3c); membrane flux declines progressively due to yeast deposition
              and fouling; inertial system maintains constant throughput throughout.
              Inertial unit: 180 spiral channels at ~320 mL/min.
  Gate      : yeastSignal > 0 → BB11 (pass: dispose); yeastSignal <= 0 → BB12 (fail)


APPLICATION 3: CHO-K1 Cell Cycle Synchronisation (Fractionation Mode)

Step 9 | CHO-K1 Monolayer Dissociation and Resuspension              [BB13 - join]
  Reagents  : CHO_Cells, TrypsinEDTA, CompleteDMEM, BSA_EDTA_Buffer
  Operation : mix(choSyncCells, trypsin) @ 180 s
              → mix(detachedCells, quenchMedia) @ 120 s
              → mix(quenchedCells, bsaBuffer) @ 5 s
  Trypsin   : 0.01% trypsin + 5.3 mM EDTA (Lonza); dissociates CHO-K1 sub-confluent monolayer
  Buffer    : 1x PBS, 2 mM EDTA, 1% BSA (MiltenyiBiotec); prevents agglomeration
  Concentration: 1e6 cells/mL in BSA-EDTA buffer

Step 10 | Inertial Fractionation — Cell Cycle Sorting                [BB13 - join]
  Reagents  : syncSuspension, PBS
  Operation : mix(syncSuspension, syncPriming) @ 8 s
              [abstracts size-differential inertial focusing at low flow rate fractionation]
  Flow rate : 1.5-2 mL/min per spiral (fractionation mode)
  Throughput: 150-300 mL/min multiplexed (1-5 L bioreactor processable within minutes)
  Size basis:
    G0/G1 cells: 11 +/- 2 um → exit outer outlet (smaller; trapped in Dean vortex)
    G2/M cells : 18 +/- 2 um → exit inner outlet (larger; focused near inner wall)
  Results   : Initial G0/G1:G2/M ratio 1.82:1 → 5.02:1 at outer outlet after 1 sort round
              G0/G1 purity ~80% outer outlet (from ~60% in unsorted input; Fig. 4d)
              Multiple sorting rounds further improve enrichment ratio.

Step 11 | Hoechst DNA Staining and FACS Cell Cycle Analysis          [BB13 - join]
  Reagents  : HoechstStain, BSA_EDTA_Buffer
  Fixation  : heat(fractionatedCells) @ 4 C @ 900 s (15 min; 4% PFA in 1x PBS)
  Operation : mix(fractionatedCells, bsaBuffer) @ 5 s
              → mix(stainBuffer, hoechstStain) @ 1800 s (30 min staining)
  Stain mix : 10 ug/mL RNase (i-DNA Biotechnology) + 3.8 mM sodium citrate
              + Hoechst NucBlue LiveReadyProbes (Invitrogen) in 1x PBS
  Detection : cellCycleDetection @ 30 s
              [BD LSR II flow cytometer; FlowJo analysis software]
              [G0/G1 = 2N DNA low Hoechst; G2/M = 4N DNA high Hoechst; Fig. 4d]
  Gate      : syncSignal > 0 → BB14 (pass: recover); syncSignal <= 0 → BB15 (fail: dispose)

Step 12 | Synchronised Cell Recovery for Downstream Use              [BB14 - pass only]
  Reagents  : stainedSync, ConditionedMedia
  Operation : mix(stainedSync, conditionedMedia2) @ 60 s; heat @ 37 C @ 3600 s (60 min)
  Purpose   : G0/G1-enriched outer-outlet fraction transferred to culture vessel or assay.
  Applications:
    - Anti-cancer drug screening (drugs target specific cell cycle phases)
    - Recombinant protein production (G1-phase CHO-derived cells grow faster; higher yield)
    - CHO re-inoculation for synchronised bioreactor production runs


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : warkiani_membraneless_microfiltration.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 16 basic blocks (BB1-BB16), 5 if/else gates, 20 CFG edges
DAG file       : warkiani_membraneless_microfiltration_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations converted to minutes (m) for compiler compatibility
                 (BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported)

Duration conversions (source → IR):
  1440m (CHO perfusion cycle)   → 86400.0 SECOND  in IR
  30m   (ELISA mix incubation)  → 1800.0 SECOND   in IR
  30m   (ELISA heat)            → 1800.0 SECOND   in IR
  15m   (Hoechst PFA fixation)  → 900.0 SECOND    in IR
  30m   (Hoechst staining)      → 1800.0 SECOND   in IR
  60m   (sync cell recovery)    → 3600.0 SECOND   in IR

Modules declared (4):
  separationEfficiencyDetection — used for CHO filtration QC and yeast filtration QC
  cellViabilityDetection        — PI/FDA dual fluorescence viability assay
  antibodyTiterDetection        — IgG1 ELISA enzymatic readout
  cellCycleDetection            — Hoechst DNA content FACS analysis

Manifests declared (14):
  CHO_Cells, Yeast_S_cerevisiae, Hybridoma_Cells, PBS, PDMS_PrimingBuffer,
  PropidiumIodide, FDAStain, HoechstStain, TrypanBlue, IgG_ELISA_Reagent,
  CompleteDMEM, ConditionedMedia, TrypsinEDTA, BSA_EDTA_Buffer

CFG verification (matched to DOT output):
  Total nodes : 16  (BB1 = main, BB2-BB15 = bsbbif_2_t through bsbbif_15_f, BB16 = terminal)
  Total edges : 20  (every join has exactly 2 incoming, 1 outgoing; terminal has 0 outgoing)
  All droplets consumed by dispose or drain before terminal NOP — no stranded droplets.

Abstraction notes:
  `mix`  — abstracts pressure-driven inertial focusing through spiral microchannels;
            not DMF electrode mixing. Duration encodes transit/processing time at stated
            flow rate. No reagent mixing in the DMF sense occurs at these steps.
  `heat` — abstracts incubator temperature control (37 C culture, 4 C fixation).
  drain vs dispose — compiler emits dispose() for both in IR; distinction is source-level
            only for human readability of pass/fail branch intent.

Platform note:
  This protocol encodes passive inertial microfluidics (no DMF electrodes, no EWOD actuation,
  no droplet-in-channel operations). Device operates at macroscopic bulk flow rates
  (mL/min to L/min range) using an external peristaltic pump (Masterflex, Cole-Parmer).
  BioScript mix abstractions reflect bulk hydrodynamic channel flow events, not droplet
  manipulation. All three applications share a single function (main) in the compiled CFG.
