description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : An Ultra-High-Throughput Spiral Microfluidic Biochip for the Enrichment of
               Circulating Tumor Cells
Source Link  : https://www.rsc.org/publishing/journals/analyst
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1039/c4an00355a
Journal      : Analyst, 2014, Vol. 139, pp. 3245-3255
Platform     : Multiplexed spiral microfluidic biochip (continuous-flow, label-free,
               size-based inertial focusing)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes an ultra-high-throughput, label-free method for the enrichment of
circulating tumor cells (CTCs) from peripheral blood of cancer patients using a multiplexed
spiral microfluidic biochip. The device exploits inertial focusing and Dean drag forces within
rectangular-cross-section spiral microchannels to achieve size-based separation of CTCs from
hematological cells without the need for antibody labelling or immunomagnetic steps.

The protocol is divided into three independent functional experiments:
  1. MCF-7 spiked recovery efficiency experiment -- validates device recovery and purity
     using a breast adenocarcinoma cell line (MCF-7) spiked into healthy donor blood.
  2. T24 cell viability experiment -- independently validates that neither the RBC lysis
     buffer nor the spiral shear forces compromise cell viability, using a bladder
     carcinoma cell line (T24) spiked into a separate healthy donor blood sample.
  3. Clinical CTC enrichment from patient blood -- isolates and identifies CTCs from
     7.5 mL blood samples of Stage IV metastatic breast cancer and NSCLC patients, with
     downstream immunofluorescence (IF) identification and HER2 FISH analysis.

The complete sample-to-CTC workflow (lysis to collection) takes approximately 10 minutes
for 7.5 mL of blood, compared to 30 minutes for the previous integrated biochip design.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Type         : Multiplexed spiral microfluidic biochip
Configuration: 3 stacked single-layer PDMS spiral chips bonded together; 2 inlets, 2 outlets
Fabrication  : SU-8 silicon molds by standard photolithography; silanized with trichloro
               (1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluorooctyl) silane (Sigma Aldrich, USA) to render hydrophobic.
               PDMS prepolymer mixed 1:10 (Sylgard 184, Dow Corning, USA), degassed, poured
               onto SU-8 mold, cured at 80 C for 1-2 h. Four fluidic access holes punched.
               Three spiral chips bonded using oxygen plasma and manual alignment.
               Whole assembly bonded to microscopic glass slide by air plasma machine.

Channel      : Rectangular cross-section spiral microchannels
Separation   : Inertial focusing + Dean drag forces
               - Centrifugal forces in radial direction form two counter-rotating Dean vortices
               - CTCs (>15 um): equilibrate near inner microchannel wall (CTC outlet)
               - WBCs, RBCs, platelets (<20 um): migrate to outer wall (waste outlet)
Enrichment   : ~10^4-fold from RBC-depleted nucleated cell fraction

Inlets       : I1 (sample: nucleated cell fraction), I2 (sheath: PBS at 750 uL/min)
Outlets      : Inner wall (CTC collection), Outer wall (WBC/waste)


CELL LINES
----------
- MCF-7 (human breast adenocarcinoma, HTB-22, ATCC, ~20 um diameter):
  Used for recovery efficiency characterisation (Protocol 1).
  Cultured in high-glucose DMEM (Invitrogen) + 10% FBS (Invitrogen) + 1% penicillin-
  streptomycin (Invitrogen), 37 C, 5% CO2, humidified atmosphere, until 80% confluence.
  Sub-cultivated 1:3 twice weekly (BD Bioscience 6-well plates); media replaced every 48 h.
  Dissociated with 0.01% trypsin + 5.3 mM EDTA (Lonza, Switzerland).
  Resuspended in PBS + 2 mM EDTA + 0.5% BSA (Miltenyi Biotec, Germany).

- T24 (human bladder carcinoma, HTB-4, ATCC, ~30 um diameter):
  Used for cell viability characterisation (Protocol 2). Independent experiment from MCF-7.
  Same culture conditions as MCF-7.


CLINICAL SAMPLES
----------------
- 10 patients: 5 metastatic breast cancer (Stage IV), 5 non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC, Stage IV)
- 5 healthy donor controls
- 7.5 mL whole blood per sample, collected in Vacutainer EDTA tubes (Becton-Dickinson, NJ, USA)
- Processed within 2-4 h to prevent blood coagulation
- IRB-approved protocol (Institutional Review Board, Singapore)
- Collected in collaboration with National Cancer Centre Singapore and
  National University Hospital, Singapore


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

===========================================================
PROTOCOL 1: MCF-7 Spiked Recovery Efficiency Experiment
===========================================================

Step 1 | MCF-7 Cell Culture and Preparation
  Cell line    : MCF-7 (breast adenocarcinoma, ~20 um)
  Media        : High-glucose DMEM + 10% FBS + 1% pen-strep, 37 C, 5% CO2
  Duration     : 48 h representative culture period (172800 s; BioScript: heat at 37c for 2880m)
  Dissociation : 0.01% trypsin + 5.3 mM EDTA
  Resuspension : PBS + 2 mM EDTA + 0.5% BSA (EDTA_BSA_Buffer)
  Note         : MCF-7 and T24 are spiked in separate, fully independent experiments.

Step 2 | Healthy Donor Blood Collection and RBC Lysis (MCF-7 arm)
  Volume       : 7.5 mL whole blood, Vacutainer EDTA tubes
  Lysis        : Ammonium chloride RBC lysis buffer (Bioscience, USA), 5 min at RT,
                 continuous gentle mixing
  Centrifugation: 1000xg, 5 min (BioScript: heat at 25c for 5m)
  Resuspension : PBS; concentrated to 3.75 mL (2x concentration = ~14e6 WBCs)
  Effect       : RBC lysis removes contaminants; no significant cancer cell loss
                 (98% T24 recovery vs whole blood, p=0.82; no morphology change, p=0.2)

Step 3 | MCF-7 Spike into Nucleated Cell Fraction
  Concentration: 500 MCF-7 cells per 7.5 mL whole blood (clinically relevant level)
  Buffer       : PBS + 2 mM EDTA + 0.5% BSA
  Operation    : mix, 1 min

Step 4 | On-Chip CTC Separation -- MCF-7 Spiked Sample
  Device       : Multiplexed spiral biochip (3 stacked chips)
  Sample inlet : 350 uL/min; Sheath inlet: 750 uL/min PBS
  Duration     : ~10 min for 7.5 mL blood (BioScript: mix for 10m)
  Physics      : Dean vortex + inertial lift; CTCs to inner wall, WBCs to outer wall
  Detection    : ctcDetection module, 30 s
  Results      : 87.6% MCF-7 recovery efficiency; 76.4% T24 recovery efficiency
                 (500 cells/7.5 mL, n=3, Anova single factor, P < 0.05)
  QC Branch    : ctcSignal > 0  -> dispose (pass, BB2)
                 ctcSignal <= 0 -> drain   (fail, BB3)
                 Both converge at BB4 (mcf7Join)

===========================================================
PROTOCOL 2: T24 Cell Viability Experiment (Independent)
===========================================================

Step 5 | T24 Cell Culture and Preparation
  Cell line    : T24 (bladder carcinoma, ~30 um)
  Media        : High-glucose DMEM + 10% FBS + 1% pen-strep, 37 C, 5% CO2
  Duration     : 48 h (172800 s; BioScript: heat at 37c for 2880m)
  Note         : Completely independent from Protocol 1; own blood sample prepared separately.

Step 6 | Healthy Donor Blood Collection and RBC Lysis (T24 arm)
  Volume       : 7.5 mL whole blood (independent from Protocol 1 blood sample)
  Lysis        : Same ammonium chloride lysis protocol; 5 min RT
  Centrifugation: 1000xg, 5 min (heat at 25c for 5m)
  Note         : T24 cells spiked before lysis; before/after counts compared (Fig. 3A)

Step 7 | T24 Spike and On-Chip Separation
  Spike        : 500 T24 cells per 7.5 mL; resuspended in EDTA_BSA_Buffer
  Separation   : 350 uL/min sample, 750 uL/min sheath, 10 min
  Operation    : mix (BioScript abstraction of spiral chip separation)

Step 8 | PFA Fixation (Viability Arm)
  Reagent      : 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) (Sigma, USA)
  Duration     : 10 min at RT (25 C)
  Operation    : mix + heat at 25c for 10m

Step 9 | Triton X-100 Permeabilization (Viability Arm)
  Reagent      : 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS (Sigma, USA)
  Duration     : 5 min
  Operation    : mix, 5 min

Step 10 | Cell Viability Staining -- PI + Pan-CK/CD45 Panel
  Panel        : pan-CK FITC (1:100) + APC-CD45 (1:100) + Hoechst + Propidium Iodide
                 Miltenyi Biotec Asia Pacific, Singapore; Hoechst dye in PBS buffer
  PI           : ex 488 nm / em 617 nm; labels dead cells
  Pan-CK       : confirms recovered cells are cancer cells (not WBC contamination)
  Incubation   : 30 min on ice (4 C) (BioScript: heat at 4c for 30m)
  Quantification: BD Accuri C6 flow cytometer; gated on FSC/SSC and fluorescence
  Detection    : viabilityDetection module, 30 s
  Results      : <10% PI+ cells (>90% viable); high shear in spiral microchannels
                 has no adverse effect on cell viability (Fig. 4B)
  QC Branch    : viabilitySignal > 0  -> dispose (pass, BB6)
                 viabilitySignal <= 0 -> drain   (fail, BB7)
                 Both converge at BB8 (viabJoin)

===========================================================
PROTOCOL 3: Clinical CTC Enrichment from Patient Blood
===========================================================

Step 11 | Clinical Blood Collection and RBC Lysis
  Samples      : 10 patient samples (5 breast, 5 NSCLC; Stage IV); 5 healthy controls
  Volume       : 7.5 mL per sample, Vacutainer EDTA tubes, within 2-4 h
  Lysis        : Ammonium chloride, 5 min RT; centrifuge 1000xg 5 min; resuspend in PBS
  Concentration: 3.75 mL (2x); ~14e6 WBCs (optimal for purity per Fig. 2B)
  Input velocity: 350 uL/min

Step 12 | On-Chip Separation of Clinical Sample
  Device       : Multiplexed spiral biochip, same parameters as Protocol 1
  Duration     : ~10 min for 7.5 mL blood
  WBC depletion: ~99.99% (from ~7e6 input nucleated cells)
  Robustness   : 900-1200 WBCs / 5 min uniformly across 0-30 min window (Fig. 2C)

Step 13 | PFA Fixation (Clinical IF Arm)
  Reagent      : 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) (Sigma, USA)
  Duration     : 10 min at RT (25 C)
  Operation    : mix + heat at 25c for 10m
  Note         : Required for intracellular pan-cytokeratin antibody staining

Step 14 | Triton X-100 Permeabilization (Clinical IF Arm)
  Reagent      : 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS (Sigma, USA)
  Duration     : 5 min
  Operation    : mix, 5 min

Step 15 | Immunofluorescence (IF) Staining for CTC Identification
  Panel        : pan-CK FITC (1:100) + APC-CD45 (1:100) + Hoechst
                 Miltenyi Biotec Asia Pacific, Singapore
  CTC criteria : Hoechst+ / Pan-CK+ / CD45-
  Incubation   : 30 min on ice (4 C)
  Imaging      : Epi-fluorescence microscopy + BD Accuri C6 flow cytometry
  Detection    : ctcDetection module, 30 s
  Results      :
    Breast cancer   : 20-67 CTCs/mL (n=5; 100% detection)
    NSCLC           : 33-135 CTCs/mL (n=5; 100% detection)
    Healthy control : 1-4 CK+ cells/mL (background threshold)
    CTC diameter    : 15-25 um (lung); 20-35 um (breast)
    CTC morphology  : Intrapatient pleomorphism observed; eccentric, bi-lobed,
                      kidney-shaped nuclei; microemboli (clusters) in some samples
    Stem cell markers: CD166+/CD133+ sub-population identified (~1 in 135 cells)
  QC Branch    : clinicalSignal > 0  -> HER2 FISH (BB10)
                 clinicalSignal <= 0 -> drain(stainedClinical) (BB11)
                 Both converge at BB12 (finalCleanup)

Step 16 | HER2 FISH Analysis on Isolated CTCs (pass branch only)
  Patient subset: HER2+ breast cancer patients (n=5)
  HER2 criterion: HER2/CEP17 ratio > 2 in single nuclei = amplified

  (a) Cytospin        : Cells spun onto slides (Cytospin, Thermo Scientific, USA);
                        600 rpm, 6 min.
  (b) PFA fixation    : 4% PFA, 10 min RT.
  (c) Dehydration     : Ethanol series 80%, 90%, 100%.
                        BioScript: combined with fixation as heat at 25c for 10m.
  (d) RNase treatment : 4 mg/mL RNase (Sigma, USA) in PBS/0.2% Tween 20;
                        40 min at 37 C. Removes RNA for clean probe hybridization.
                        BioScript: mix + heat at 37c for 40m (2400s).
  (e) Denaturation    : 70% formamide/2xSSC, 80 C, 10 min.
                        Opens dsDNA for probe access.
                        BioScript: mix + heat at 80c for 10m.
  (f) Probe hybridization: HER-2/neu gene locus (red) + CEP17 (green);
                        applied at 42 C, overnight, dark and humid conditions.
                        BioScript: heat at 42c for 600m (10h approximation; s/m limit).
  (g) Post-hyb washes : Wash 1: 50% formamide/2xSSC, 45 C, shaking, 5 min.
                        Wash 2: 2xSSC, 45 C, shaking, 5 min.
                        BioScript: two sequential heat at 45c for 5m steps.
  (h) DAPI counterstain: DAPI (4',6-diamidino-2-phenylindole); coverslipped (50x50 mm,
                        Fisher Scientific, USA).

  Detection    : her2FISHDetection module, 30 s
  Results      : 3 of 5 HER2+ breast cancer patients showed HER2-negative CTCs
                 (HER2/CEP17 < 2), indicating heterogeneity between primary tumor
                 and disseminated circulating cells (Fig. 5C).


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Ultra-fast, label-free isolation of circulating tumor cells from blood using spiral microfluidics
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/nprot.2016.003
Paper DOI    : http://dx.doi.org/10.1038/nprot.2016.003
Journal      : Nature Protocols, Vol. 11, No. 1, pp. 134-148 (2016)
Platform     : Spiral inertial microfluidic biochip (PDMS/glass, continuous-flow, label-free)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a label-free, size-based method for isolating viable circulating tumor cells
(CTCs) from peripheral blood using a spiral inertial microfluidic biochip. CTCs -- rare cancer cells
shed from primary or metastatic tumors into the bloodstream -- occur at frequencies as low as one cell
per 10^7-10^9 hematological cells in metastatic cancer patients, making reliable isolation a major
technical challenge.

The spiral biochip exploits the combined effect of inertial lift force (FL) and Dean drag force (FD)
in a curvilinear microchannel. Larger CTCs (typically 15-20 um) focus near the inner wall at the
outlet, while smaller blood cells (RBCs 3-8 um, WBCs 10-15 um, platelets 3-8 um) migrate along
Dean vortex streamlines toward the outer wall. This passive, continuous-flow separation requires no
antibodies, magnetic beads, or external force fields.

Key performance metrics:
  - >=85% CTC recovery across multiple cancer cell lines
  - 99.99% WBC depletion (4-log) from healthy samples
  - 7.5 mL lysed blood processed in 37.5 min (single chip) or 12.5 min (3x multiplexed chip)
  - CTCs collected in suspension (viable), compatible with culture, FISH, and sequencing

The protocol has been validated in clinical samples from patients with metastatic non-small-cell lung
cancer (n=15; 10-1535 CK+ CTCs isolated) and breast cancer (n=15; 12-1275 CK+ CTCs isolated),
with a negative-control threshold of >7 CK+ cells per sample defining a positive patient.


SEPARATION PHYSICS
------------------
The spiral microchannel has a rectangular cross-section (500 um wide x 170 um deep) in a two-loop
configuration with radius of curvature ~10 mm. Flow in the curved channel generates secondary
cross-sectional Dean vortices perpendicular to the primary flow direction. The Dean number is:

    De = Re * sqrt(DH / 2*RC)

where Re is the Reynolds number, DH is the hydraulic diameter, and RC is the radius of curvature.
The Dean migration velocity is:

    U_Dean = 1.8e-4 * De^1.63

For particles with diameter comparable to channel dimensions (ac/h > 0.07), inertial lift forces
(shear-induced FL_shear and wall-induced FL_wall) direct cells to equilibrium focusing positions.
The balance of FL and FD results in two focusing positions near the inner channel wall for larger
CTCs, while smaller cells disperse and follow Dean streamlines toward the outer wall.

Design parameters: 75 um sample inlet (outer) / 425 um sheath inlet (inner); 150 um CTC collection
outlet (inner) / 350 um waste outlet (outer). Size cutoff: ~12 um (CTCs >=12 um recoverable).


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Material       : PDMS (Sylgard 184, 10:1 base:curing agent) bonded to glass slide (76 x 52 mm)
Channel        : 500 um wide x 170 um deep (±5 um); two-loop spiral; radius ~10 mm
Fabrication    : Standard photolithography (AZ9260 photoresist, DRIE ~165 um etch depth on 6-inch
                 silicon wafer) + soft lithography; silanization with trichloro(1H,2H,2H-perfluorooctyl)
                 silane; plasma bonding (O2 plasma, 300 W, 2 min 30 s)
Configurations :
  Single chip  : 1 spiral layer; 100 uL/min sample + 750 uL/min sheath; 7.5 mL in ~37.5 min
  Multiplexed  : 3 PDMS layers stacked via plasma bonding + manual alignment;
                 2100 uL/min sheath; 7.5 mL in <12.5 min (3 sorters in parallel)
Inlets         : Outer (sample, 75 um split); inner (sheath buffer, 425 um split)
Outlets        : Inner CTC collection (150 um); outer waste (350 um)
Punching       : 1.5 mm single layer; 4 mm bottom layers + 1.5 mm top layer (multiplexed)
Critical       : Channel depth must be 160-170 um; depth outside tolerance causes particle focusing
                 failure and substantially compromises enriched sample purity


CELL LINES USED
---------------
- MCF-7 (human breast cancer, ATCC HTB-22)
- MDA-MB-231 (human breast cancer, ATCC CRM-HTB-26)
- A549 (human lung adenocarcinoma, ATCC CCL-185)
- SW480 (human colorectal adenocarcinoma; used for KRAS codon 12 mutation sequencing validation)
All cultured in complete DMEM (DMEM + 10% FBS + 1% pen/strep), 37 C, 5% CO2.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Device Fabrication (Off-chip, Steps 1-19)
  Duration  : 5-7 d (mask printing) + 7-10 h (photolithography) + 1-2 d (soft lithography)
  Details   : AutoCAD design -> mask printing -> UV lithography on AZ9260-coated silicon wafer
              -> DRIE etching ~165 um -> silanization -> PDMS casting 10:1 w/w, 77 g, 70-80 C 2 h
              -> peel, punch holes, O2 plasma bond to glass -> 85 C 30 min post-bond bake.
              Multiplexed device: three PDMS molds stacked and plasma-bonded with manual alignment.
  Note      : Not encoded in BioScript (off-chip physical fabrication).

Step 2 | Chip Priming - Ethanol Sterilization (Paper Steps 20-24)
  Reagents  : Ethanol 70% v/v in sterile deionized water
  Operation : Flow through both inlets at 750 uL/min for 5 min
  Purpose   : Sterilize channel interior; remove air bubbles
  Note      : Required for downstream CTC culture. Omit Steps 22-24 for non-sterile experiments.

Step 3 | Chip Priming - Sheath Buffer Coating (Paper Step 25)
  Reagents  : 1x sterile PBS + 0.5% w/v BSA (sheath buffer)
  Operation : Flow at 750 uL/min for 5 min
  Purpose   : Coat PDMS microchannel walls with BSA; minimize non-specific cell adhesion
  Note      : Wash residual ethanol from system before sample loading.

Step 4 | Bubble Removal Inspection (Paper Step 26)
  Reagents  : Sheath buffer
  Operation : Bright-field inverted microscope inspection; increase flow rate to dislodge bubbles
  Duration  : ~2 min
  Critical  : If bubbles cannot be removed, discard chip and use a new one.

Step 5 | QC Bead Check (Paper Step 27)
  Reagents  : 3-6 um polystyrene bead suspension (0.1% v/v); sheath buffer
  Flow rates: Sample 100 uL/min (outer inlet); sheath 750 uL/min (inner inlet)
  Duration  : ~5 min run + 30 s detection
  Imaging   : Phase-contrast microscope + high-speed camera (VisionResearch Phantom v9)
  Pass      : 6 um beads complete Dean cycle (inner to outer wall visible); 15 um beads focus
              tightly at inner wall at outlet region
  Fail      : Incorrect focusing -> channel depth out of tolerance (likely DRIE error) ->
              fabricate new master mold (new silicon wafer)
  BioScript : beadFocusingQC detect module; branch BB2 (pass/dispose) vs BB3 (fail/drain)

Step 6 | Blood Preparation - RBC Lysis (Paper Steps 28-31)
  Reagents  : Whole blood (EDTA Vacutainer, processed within 2-4 h of collection);
              3x ammonium chloride RBC lysis buffer (G-Bioscience, cat. no. 786650)
  Ratio     : 1:3 v/v blood:lysis buffer
  Temperature: 24-26 C (room temperature)
  Duration  : 10 min on shaking platform; invert tube to mix
  Endpoint  : Sample color changes to dark red (complete lysis)
  Note      : If spiking with cancer cell lines, add cells before lysis step.
              Removal of RBCs reduces cellular interactions that impair inertial focusing.
              Cell loss from lysis + centrifugation <8%.

Step 7 | Cell Pelleting and Resuspension (Paper Steps 29-31)
  Reagents  : 1x PBS
  Operation : Centrifuge 1000g, 5 min, room temperature; discard supernatant
  Resuspend : In 1x PBS to 2x concentration (~14e6 nucleated cells/mL; 7.5 mL blood -> 3.75 mL PBS)
  Storage   : On ice; process within 2-4 h at 4 C

Step 8 | Spiral Biochip Processing (Paper Steps 32-37)
  Reagents  : Lysed blood sample; sheath buffer (PBS + 0.5% BSA)
  Flow rates: Sample 100 uL/min (outer inlet); sheath 750 uL/min (inner inlet, single chip)
              Multiplexed: sheath 2100 uL/min
  Duration  : ~37 min (7.5 mL, single chip); ~12 min (7.5 mL, 3x multiplexed)
  Collection: CTCs from inner outlet into 15 mL conical tube; waste to 50 mL conical tube
  Microscope: 10x magnification, monitor spiral outlet during run
  Protocol  : Run sheath 2 min first to stabilize; start sample pump; allow uninterrupted run.
  Separation: CTCs (>15 um) focus near inner wall via inertial lift; blood cells (<15 um) exit
              outer waste outlet following Dean vortex streamlines.

Step 9 | Cell Concentration (Paper Step 38-39)
  Operation : Centrifuge collected CTC fraction at 300g, 3 min, room temperature
  Resuspend : In ~250 uL PBS; transfer to microcentrifuge tube

Step 10 | PFA Fixation (Paper Step 40)
  Reagents  : 4% w/v paraformaldehyde in PBS
  Duration  : 10 min at room temperature
  Caution   : PFA is a suspected carcinogen; handle with nitrile gloves, lab coat, goggles
  Storage   : Fixed cells can be stored overnight at 4 C in PBS

Step 11 | Post-Fixation Wash (Paper Step 41)
  Reagents  : 1-2 mL PBS + 0.5% w/v BSA
  Operation : Centrifuge 300g, 3 min, room temperature; discard supernatant
  Resuspend : In ~250 uL PBS

Step 12 | Permeabilization (Paper Step 42)
  Reagents  : 0.1% v/v Triton X-100 in PBS
  Duration  : 1-5 min at room temperature (encoded as 3 min)
  Purpose   : Solubilize plasma membrane for intracellular pan-cytokeratin antibody access

Step 13 | Post-Permeabilization Wash (Paper Step 43)
  Reagents  : 1-2 mL PBS + 0.5% w/v BSA
  Operation : Centrifuge 300g, 3 min, room temperature; discard supernatant

Step 14 | Antibody and Hoechst Staining (Paper Step 44)
  Reagents  : FITC pan-cytokeratin 1:100 (Miltenyi Biotec Asia Pacific)
              APC CD45 1:100 (Miltenyi Biotec Asia Pacific)
              Hoechst 33342 1:1000 from 1 M stock (Life Technologies)
  Incubation: 30 min on ice (4 C) in dark
  CTC phenotype: Hoechst+, pan-CK+, CD45-, round nuclei, high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio
  Storage   : Stained cells stable overnight at 4 C in PBS under dark conditions

Step 15 | Post-Staining Wash and Transfer (Paper Steps 45-46)
  Reagents  : 1-2 mL PBS + 0.5% w/v BSA
  Operation : Centrifuge 300g, 3 min, room temperature; discard supernatant
  Resuspend : In ~250 uL PBS; transfer to single well of 96-well plate

Step 16 | CTC Fluorescence Detection and Enumeration (Paper Step 47)
  Platform  : Olympus IX71/IX81 inverted microscope with automated stage
  Filters   : ET460/50m (Hoechst), ET535/50m (pan-CK FITC), ET605/70m (CD45 APC)
  Camera    : 12-bit EM-CCD (Andor Technology iXon+885)
  Software  : MetaMorph (1 mm x 1 mm grid well scan); ImageJ (manual threshold)
  Manual    : 40x magnification; Hoechst+/pan-CK+/CD45- cells with round nuclei and high N/C ratio
  Threshold : >7 CK+ cells per sample = positive patient (derived from 10 healthy volunteer controls)
  Results   : 12-1275 CK+ breast CTCs; 10-1535 CK+ lung CTCs from clinical samples
  BioScript : ctcDetection detect module (45 min); branch BB5 (pass/dispose) vs BB6 (fail/drain)

Alternative - DNA-FISH (Box 1, Paper)
  Duration  : 2 d
  Probes    : Vysis ALK break-apart probe; HER2/neu probe (Abbott)
  Fixative  : Acetic acid:methanol 1:3
  Protocol  : Dropwise cell fixation onto slides; RNase 40 min 37 C; denature 70% formamide/2x SSC
              80 C 10 min; dehydrate ethanol series; hybridize 42 C dark humid 16 h; wash; DAPI

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Multilayer Hybrid Microfluidics: A Digital-to-Channel Interface for Sample Processing and Separations
Source Link  : https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/vertical_interface.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/ac101379g
Journal      : Analytical Chemistry, 2010, Vol. 82, pp. 6680-6686
Authors      : Michael W. L. Watson, Mais J. Jebrail, Aaron R. Wheeler
Platform     : Multilayer hybrid DMF (two-plate digital microfluidics + glass microchannel CE)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol introduces a second-generation "hybrid microfluidics" device architecture that
integrates two-plate digital microfluidics (DMF) for sample processing with a glass microchannel
network for capillary electrophoresis (CE) separation and LIF detection. The key advance over
the prior single-plate side-on design (Abdelgawad et al. Lab Chip 2009) is the multilayer
configuration: a DMF electrode array patterned on the top of a commercial glass microchannel
device, enabling dispensing from reservoirs and splitting of droplets on-chip -- operations
incompatible with single-plate actuation.

Droplets are manipulated in two-plate format on the top layer, then transferred through a
vertical digital-channel interface (a drilled hole, 2 mm dia.) into the microchannel network
below, where analytes are separated by electroosmotic flow and detected by LIF. The two fluid
manipulation paradigms (AC electrostatic droplet actuation above, DC electroosmotic flow below)
are orthogonal and independent.

Two demonstrations are encoded in this BioScript file:
  Protocol 1: On-chip serial dilution calibration curve (fluorescein + rhodamine 123 internal
              standard; 3-point calibration, n=5 replicates, R^2=0.9937, RSD 2.9-7.4%)
  Protocol 2: Multistep enzymatic protein digestion (AF-BSA with pepsin then trypsin;
              sequential 30 min incubations; CE comparison of undigested, pepsin-only,
              and pepsin+trypsin digest states; n=3 replicates; total ~2 h)


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Substrate 1 : ITO-coated glass cover with Teflon-AF (top plate; ground electrode)
Substrate 2 : Chromium electrode array on glass, coated with Parylene-C + Teflon-AF
              (bottom DMF plate / microchannel cover)
Substrate 3 : Glass slide with etched cross-pattern microchannel network
              (Caliper Life Science, Hopkinton MA; 100 um wide x 20 um deep)

Substrates 2+3 are thermally bonded; DMF electrodes are patterned on the top of substrate 2.
Substrates 1+2 define the DMF two-plate gap (280 um, set by 4x double-sided tape spacers).

DMF electrode layout:
  - 13 driving electrodes (2.2 x 2.2 mm)
  - 3 reservoir electrodes (3x3 mm or 5x5 mm depending on reagent volume needs)
  - Actuation: 20 kHz AC, 100-200 Vrms (function generator + high-voltage amplifier)
  - Interface electrode overlaps the drilled inlet hole by ~1 mm for reliable droplet transfer

Microchannel layout (cross injector):
  - S (sample inlet): connects to digital-channel interface
  - SW (sample waste): 15 uL reservoir volume
  - B (buffer inlet): 15 uL reservoir volume
  - BW (buffer waste): 15 uL reservoir volume
  - Separation column: 3 cm from injection cross to LIF detection point
  - Unit sample volume: 3 uL droplet (approximates 2 mm dia. x 1 mm deep hole volume)

Device footprint: 35 x 20 mm (commercial microchannel device; limits DMF array to ~13 electrodes)


REAGENTS
--------
Protocol 1 -- Serial Dilution Calibration Curve:
  AnalyteFluorescein   : 1 uM fluorescein + 1 uM rhodamine 123 in 20 mM borate pH 9.0
                         (combined stock droplet containing both analyte and internal standard)
  Diluent              : 1 uM rhodamine 123 in 20 mM borate pH 9.0
                         (maintains constant IS concentration across all dilution steps)
  Separation buffer    : 20 mM sodium borate pH 9.0, filtered through 0.2 um nylon,
                         degassed by ultrasonication 5 min; fills channel network prior to actuation

Protocol 2 -- Multistep Enzymatic Protein Digestion:
  AF_BSA               : 20 ug/mL Alexa Fluor 488-labeled BSA in DI water + 0.1% w/v Pluronic F-68
                         (Invitrogen-Molecular Probes, Eugene OR)
  PepsinSolution       : 1 mg/mL pepsin in 1 mM acetate buffer + 0.1% w/v Pluronic F-68, pH 4.5
                         Cleavage: aromatic residues (Phe, Tyr, Trp)
  TrypsinSolution      : 1 mg/mL trypsin in 50 mM borate buffer + 0.1% w/v Pluronic F-68, pH 9.0
                         Cleavage: basic residues (Lys, Arg)
  Separation buffer    : 100 mM sodium borate pH 9.0 (higher ionic strength for protein separations)
  PluronicF68          : 0.1% w/v additive in all protein-containing droplets; minimises surface
                         adsorption to Parylene-C / Teflon-AF device surfaces

All reagents purchased from Sigma Aldrich (Oakville ON) unless otherwise specified.
Buffers dissolved in 18 MOhm cm deionised water.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

--- PROTOCOL 1: On-Chip Serial Dilution Calibration Curve ---

Step P1-S1 | Dispense Analyte Stock Droplet
  Source    : AnalyteFluorescein reservoir (5x5 mm electrode)
  Volume    : ~3 uL unit droplet
  Content   : 1 uM fluorescein + 1 uM rhodamine 123 in 20 mM borate pH 9.0
  Purpose   : Starting point for serial 2x dilution; rhodamine 123 serves as internal standard
              throughout (peak area ratio AA/AIS used as calibration metric)

Step P1-S2 | Dispense First Diluent Droplet
  Source    : Diluent reservoir
  Volume    : ~3 uL unit droplet
  Content   : 1 uM rhodamine 123 only (no analyte)

Step P1-S3 | Merge and Mix (Dilution 1 -- 2x dilution)
  Inputs    : stockDroplet + diluent1
  Duration  : 10 s (circular mixing across several electrodes)
  Result    : ~0.5 uM fluorescein, ~1 uM rhodamine 123
  Note      : Circular mixing pattern (paper: "several seconds") ensures thorough homogenisation
              before the droplet is split.

Step P1-S4 | Split: Daughter A to Digital-Channel Interface
  Operation : Physical split by reversing electrode actuation while droplet straddles two
              driving electrodes; two equal half-droplets (~1.5 uL each) result.
  Daughter A: driven to digital-channel interface for CE-LIF injection
  BioScript : Encoded as mix(mergedDrop1, diluent1) for 2s (split abstraction; no native
              split statement in BioScript)

Step P1-S5 | Store Daughter B (array)
  Daughter B: retained on electrode array
  BioScript : Represented as dispense(Diluent) placeholder variable (storedDrop1)

Step P1-S6 | CE-LIF Analysis: Dilution 1 (undiluted stock daughter)
  Transfer  : Daughter A driven to interface electrode (overlaps 2 mm drilled hole by ~1 mm);
              droplet spontaneously wets glass and settles into hole
  Loading   : S=900V, SW=0V, B=650V, BW=850V (LabSmith high-voltage sequencer)
  Injection : S=500V, SW=500V, B=1000V, BW=0V
  Detection : 488 nm argon ion laser (20 mW), 60x objective, 536/40 nm BP filter, PMT
              Detection point: 3 cm from injection cross
  Module    : serialDilutionDetection
  Duration  : 30 s

Step P1-S7 | Dispense Second Diluent; Merge with Stored Daughter B (Dilution 2 -- 4x dilution)
  Inputs    : storedDrop1 + diluent2
  Duration  : 10 s mixing
  Result    : ~0.25 uM fluorescein, ~1 uM rhodamine 123
  Prep      : Previous analysed sample removed from channel by suction (fine needle + vacuum
              flask) without removing the DMF top-plate between injections.

Step P1-S8 | Split: Daughter C to Digital-Channel Interface
  Daughter C: driven to interface for second CE-LIF injection
  BioScript : Encoded as mix(mergedDrop2, diluent2) for 2s (split abstraction)

Step P1-S9 | CE-LIF Analysis: Dilution 2
  Module    : serialDilutionDetection
  Duration  : 30 s
  Completes : 3-point calibration curve (stock daughter, 2x dilution, 4x dilution)

QC Gate | Serial Dilution (dilutionSignal1 > 0)
  Pass (BB2): valid CE electropherogram peaks detected; dispose analysed droplets
  Fail (BB3): no signal (interface transfer failure or column blockage); dispose and abort
  Join (BB4): dispose QC signal droplets; enter protein digestion protocol

Calibration results (paper, n=5):
  RSD: 2.9% (stock), 3.7% (1st dilution), 7.4% (2nd dilution)
  R^2 = 0.9937
  Separation efficiency: 1.1x10^6 plates/m (rhodamine 123)
  Improvement over side-on design: 6.7% RSD -> 2.9%; 4.7x10^5 -> 1.1x10^6 plates/m
  (attributed to glass vs PDMS channel material; glass reduces band broadening)

--- PROTOCOL 2: Multistep Enzymatic Protein Digestion ---

Step P2-S1 | Dispense AF-BSA Droplet
  Source    : AF_BSA reservoir
  Volume    : ~3 uL unit droplet
  Content   : 20 ug/mL AF-BSA in DI water + 0.1% F-68

Step P2-S2 | Dispense Pepsin Droplet
  Source    : PepsinSolution reservoir
  Volume    : ~3 uL unit droplet
  Content   : 1 mg/mL pepsin in 1 mM acetate pH 4.5 + 0.1% F-68

Step P2-S3 | Merge AF-BSA with Pepsin
  Duration  : 5 s
  Result    : Equal volume mixture of AF-BSA + pepsin in combined buffer conditions

Step P2-S4 | Pepsin Digestion Incubation
  Temperature : 25 C (room temperature)
  Duration    : 30 min (1800 s)
  Humidified  : Device stored in Petri dish with water-saturated wipe during incubation
                to prevent evaporation from open two-plate gap edges
  Endpoint    : Loss of intact AF-BSA peak at t=58 s in CE electropherogram confirms complete
                digestion by pepsin

Step P2-S5 | Split: Daughter D (Pepsin Digest) to Interface
  Daughter D: driven to digital-channel interface for CE-LIF analysis (pepsin-only digest)
  BioScript : mix(pepsinReaction, pepsinDroplet) for 2s (split abstraction; pepsinDroplet
              variable reused as placeholder -- compiler-accepted workaround, not a biological
              dispense; represents retained half-droplet on array)

Step P2-S6 | Store Daughter E (Pepsin Digest Half)
  BioScript : dispense(AF_BSA) placeholder variable (storedPepsinDrop)
  Note      : Logical placeholder; models retained pepsin digest subdroplet awaiting trypsin

Step P2-S7 | CE-LIF Analysis: Pepsin-Only Digest
  Module    : proteinDigestionDetection
  Duration  : 60 s
  Expected  : Multiple peaks at range of elution times (multiply charged aromatic peptides);
              intact AF-BSA peak at t=58 s absent (complete digestion confirmed)
  Prep      : Previous sample removed by suction before injection

Step P2-S8 | Dispense Trypsin Droplet
  Source    : TrypsinSolution reservoir
  Volume    : ~3 uL unit droplet
  Content   : 1 mg/mL trypsin in 50 mM borate pH 9.0 + 0.1% F-68

Step P2-S9 | Merge Stored Pepsin Digest with Trypsin
  Inputs    : storedPepsinDrop + trypsinDroplet
  Duration  : 5 s
  Note      : Stored Daughter E (pepsin digest) merged with trypsin for second-stage digestion

Step P2-S10 | Trypsin Digestion Incubation
  Temperature : 25 C (room temperature)
  Duration    : 30 min (1800 s)
  Humidified  : Yes (same humidified chamber setup as pepsin step)
  Note        : Trypsin cleaves at Lys and Arg, reducing multiply charged aromatic peptides
                from pepsin into smaller singly charged fragments. Total workflow ~2 h.

Step P2-S11 | Split: Daughter F (Sequential Digest) to Interface
  Daughter F: driven to interface for CE-LIF analysis of pepsin+trypsin sequential digest
  BioScript : mix(trypsinReaction, trypsinDroplet) for 2s (same split abstraction pattern;
              trypsinDroplet reused as placeholder)

Step P2-S12 | CE-LIF Analysis: Sequential Pepsin + Trypsin Digest
  Module    : proteinDigestionDetection
  Duration  : 60 s
  Expected  : New series of peaks eluting closer together vs pepsin-only trace;
              reduction in multiply charged species; singly charged tryptic peptides dominant
  Completes : Three-state AF-BSA comparison (undigested, pepsin-only, pepsin+trypsin)

QC Gate | Protein Digestion (digestionSignalPepsin > 0)
  Pass (BB5): valid pepsin digest CE peaks detected; dispose all digestion droplets
  Fail (BB6): no signal (enzyme inactive, transfer failed, column blocked); dispose and abort
  Terminal (BB7): dispose both QC signal droplets; NOP exit node; experiment ends

Digestion results (paper, n=3):
  Pepsin-only: complete digestion; multiply charged peptides from Phe/Tyr/Trp cleavage
  Sequential : reduction to singly charged peptides; peaks elute closer together
  Conditions tested: undigested, pepsin-only (30 min), pepsin+trypsin (30 min each)

steps.notes: Daughter C driven to digital-channel interface for second CE-LIF injection.

steps.name: CE-LIF detection at digital-channel interface (Dilution 2)
steps.notes: Second CE-LIF run; completes the 3-point calibration curve (stock, 2x, 4x dilution).

steps.name: Serial dilution QC gate
steps.notes: QC keyed on dilutionSignal1 (first daughter; highest fluorescein signal, most reliable peak). Both branches normalise to dispose in IR (drain -> dispose compiler behaviour).

steps.name: dilutionJoin: dispose QC signals, enter protein digestion branch
steps.notes: Both dilution signal droplets disposed. Control passes to Protocol 2.

steps.name: Dispense AF-BSA droplet
steps.notes: 20 ug/mL AF-BSA in DI water + 0.1% F-68. Dispensed from 5x5 mm reservoir electrode.

steps.name: Dispense pepsin droplet
steps.notes: 1 mg/mL pepsin in 1 mM acetate buffer pH 4.5 + 0.1% F-68.

steps.name: Merge AF-BSA with pepsin
steps.notes: Equal volume merge; brief on-chip mixing ensures homogeneous enzyme-substrate contact.

steps.name: Pepsin digestion incubation
steps.notes: Device stored in humidified Petri dish (water-saturated wipe) to limit evaporation during incubation. AF-BSA peak at t=58 s absent after digestion, confirming complete cleavage.

steps.name: Split: Daughter D (pepsin digest) for CE-LIF analysis
steps.compiler_note: pepsinDroplet1[0] reused here as split-abstraction partner; this is a compiler-accepted workaround, not a biological dispense. The second argument represents the retained half-droplet on the array.
steps.notes: Daughter D driven to digital-channel interface for CE-LIF analysis of pepsin-only digest.

steps.name: Stored pepsin digest half-droplet placeholder
steps.notes: Logical placeholder for retained half-droplet (Daughter E) stored on electrode array. Not a biological dispense; models the pepsin digest subdroplet awaiting trypsin addition.

steps.name: CE-LIF detection: pepsin-only digest
steps.expected_result: Multiple peaks at range of elution times; intact AF-BSA peak at t=58 s absent (complete digestion)
steps.notes: CE in 100 mM borate pH 9.0; LIF at 488 nm / 536/40 nm. Previous sample removed by suction before injection.

steps.name: Dispense trypsin droplet
steps.notes: 1 mg/mL trypsin in 50 mM borate buffer pH 9.0 + 0.1% F-68.

steps.name: Merge stored pepsin digest with trypsin
steps.notes: Stored Daughter E (pepsin digest) merged with trypsin for second-stage sequential digestion.

steps.name: Trypsin digestion incubation
steps.notes: Second 30 min incubation in humidified chamber. Trypsin cleaves Lys and Arg, reducing multiply charged pepsin fragments. Total process time ~2 h including both digestions.

steps.name: Split: Daughter F (sequential digest) for CE-LIF analysis
steps.compiler_note: trypsinDroplet1[0] reused here as split-abstraction partner; same workaround as P2-S5.
steps.notes: Daughter F driven to digital-channel interface for CE-LIF analysis of sequential pepsin+trypsin digest.

steps.name: CE-LIF detection: sequential pepsin + trypsin digest
steps.expected_result: New series of peaks eluting closer together relative to pepsin-only trace; singly charged peptides from trypsin cleavage
steps.notes: Third CE run completing the three-state AF-BSA comparison (undigested, pepsin-only, pepsin+trypsin).

steps.name: Protein digestion QC gate
steps.notes: QC keyed on pepsin-only signal (loss of intact AF-BSA peak is primary assay endpoint). Both branches normalise to dispose in IR.

steps.name: finalCleanup: dispose QC signals; experiment ends
steps.notes: Terminal block. NOP is standard compiler padding at CFG exit node.

improvement_vs_side_on.note: Improvement attributed to glass channel material vs PDMS in prior design; glass reduces band broadening

conditions_tested: Pepsin + trypsin sequential digest (30 min each)
protein_digestion.pepsin_result: Complete digestion confirmed; AF-BSA peak at t=58 s absent; multiple peaks from multiply charged aromatic peptides
protein_digestion.trypsin_result: Reduction of multiply charged peptides; new series of peaks eluting closer together

bioscript.duration_units: s and m only (BioScript restriction; h not supported)

known_compiler_behaviours.drain_normalises_to_dispose: drain statements compile to dispose() in IR; expected behaviour
known_compiler_behaviours.split_abstraction: BioScript has no native split statement. Physical droplet splits are encoded as short mix operations (2s) using a previously-dispensed placeholder as the second argument. Affects IR lines 15 and 21 where pepsinDroplet1[0] and trypsinDroplet1[0] appear reused. Compiler accepts without error; biological intent documented here.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Droplet-Based High-Throughput Cultivation for Accurate Screening of
               Antibiotic Resistant Gut Microbes
Source Link  : https://elifesciences.org/articles/56998
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.56998
Journal      : eLife 2020, Vol. 9, Article e56998
Platform     : Anaerobic droplet microfluidics (flow-focusing generation +
               dielectrophoretic sorting) inside vinyl anaerobic chamber


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a microfluidic platform for high-throughput anaerobic isolation,
cultivation, and sorting of human gut-associated bacteria in picoliter-scale droplets.
The system operates entirely within a vinyl anaerobic chamber, enabling cultivation of
strictly anaerobic organisms that are incompatible with standard aerobic bench workflows.

The protocol is divided into two functional phases:

  1. Rich-media droplet cultivation (Protocol 1)
     Fecal microbiota transplant (FMT) donor stool is stochastically encapsulated at
     single-cell density in picoliter droplets formed with three distinct rich growth
     media (BHIS, GMM, YCFA). Each droplet acts as an independent microreactor,
     eliminating inter-species competition and enabling slow-growing taxa to expand
     without being outcompeted. An image-based wavelet-OD sorting step selectively
     retains sparse (slow-growing) colony droplets to further enrich rare taxa.

  2. Antibiotic resistance screening (Protocol 2)
     The same donor stool is encapsulated in BHIS droplets supplemented individually
     with ampicillin (100 ug/mL), ciprofloxacin (5 ug/mL), or vancomycin (10 ug/mL).
     After 1-day incubation, optical density-based sorting removes non-viable droplets
     so only organisms that actively grew in the presence of antibiotic contribute to
     downstream 16S sequencing reads.

Key outcomes: richness increase over plate cultures of 15% (BHIS) to 410% (YCFA);
105 vs 57 low-abundance ASVs (<1% in stool) recovered by droplets vs plates; 21 unique
antibiotic-resistant organisms detected exclusively in droplets.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Enclosure   : Vinyl anaerobic chamber (Coy Laboratory Products)
Atmosphere  : 86% N2 / 10% CO2 / 4% H2; O2 <1 ppm; H2 maintained at 1.5-2.5%;
              monitored by Coy CAM-12. Coy H2S-reducing column inside chamber
              prevents corrosion of electronic components.

Components inside chamber:
  - Inverted microscope (Nikon Ts2R), 4x and 10x objectives
  - Microfluidic devices (droplet generation + droplet sorting)
  - High frame rate camera (Basler acA640-750um, 925 Hz, 672x360 px, 59 us exposure)
  - Syringe pumps (Harvard Apparatus Pump 11 Pico Plus Elite)
  - Incubator (37 C)
  - Electrodes

Components outside chamber (connected via sealed rubber ports):
  - Computer running custom LabView code
  - Voltage amplifier (TREK Model 2220, 200 V/V gain)
  - NI-DAQ 6211 (analog output -> amplifier)

Droplet generation device:
  - Architecture     : Flow-focusing junction
  - Channel height   : 50 um (SU-8 3050 on 4" silicon wafer)
  - Fabrication      : Soft lithography; PDMS (RTV 615) 10:1 A:B; cured 80 C >=1 h;
                       plasma bonded to glass slide
  - Hydrophobicity   : Aquapel coating followed by Fluorinert FC-40 flush
  - Oil phase        : Bio-Rad Droplet Generation Oil for EvaGreen
  - Droplet volume   : 65-115 pL
  - Emulsion volume  : 0.5-1 mL per run (~4-15 million droplets)
  - Generation time  : 20-60 min depending on device

Droplet sorting device:
  - Same fabrication as generation device; bonded to ITO-coated glass slide
    (Delta Technologies CG-811N-S207)
  - Electrodes       : Low-melting solder (51% In / 32.5% Bi / 16.5% Sn; Indium Corp.)
                       flowed into holes at 90 C
  - Sorting mechanism: Dielectrophoresis (DEP)
  - Actuation        : 10 kHz, 800 V p-p, 30% duty cycle, 10 ms pulse
  - Sorting rate     : ~30 Hz
  - Re-injection     : 20 uL/hr (droplets); 180 uL/hr (oil spacing)


WAVELET OD SORTING ALGORITHM
-----------------------------
Detection region : Interior of each droplet (~6080 pixels) between red-dot markers
                   at sorting junction; detected by edge-finding along channel centre.

Algorithm:
  - Discrete wavelet frame decomposition (LabView IMAQ Extract Texture Feature VI)
  - Wavelet type    : Biorthogonal 3.1
  - Subband         : Low-Low-High (LLH)
  - Window          : 15 x 15 pixels, step size 5 pixels
  - Co-occurrence   : 15 grey levels, 3 x 3 pixel displacement
  - Normalization   : Non-zero elements of wavelet feature vector normalized to 1

Threshold classification:
  - Wavelet OD < 0.3       : Empty droplet (waste)
  - Wavelet OD 0.3 to 0.7  : Sparse / slow-growing colony (KEEP)
  - Wavelet OD > 0.7       : Dense colony (waste)

False positive rate: <=8% (upper bound; actual rate likely lower as waste stream
                     slow-grower fraction was not counted)


STOOL SAMPLE PREPARATION
-------------------------
Donor         : Previously characterised FMT donor (Lee et al. 2017)
Ethics        : University of Chicago Ethics Committee and IRB (IRB 132-0212);
                written informed consent obtained from single donor
Preparation   : 50 mL stool diluted in 100 mL PBS; centrifuged; supernatant
                collected and stored at -80 C
Cell density  : Live ~1.5 +/- 1.0 x10^8 cells/mL; dead ~21 +/- 3 x10^8 cells/mL
                (Live/Dead BacLight kit, ThermoFisher; note: dye requires oxygenation,
                may introduce measurement artefact)
Plate control : 100 uL suspension spread at ~1 cell/500 um2 (bacterial lawn density)
                to ensure rare cells are represented
Droplet load  : 200x dilution; Poisson mean 2-12% of droplets contain one live cell
                (range accounts for cell density uncertainty and droplet volume variation)


GROWTH MEDIA
------------

BHIS (Brain Heart Infusion Supplemented):
  500 mL water + 18.5 g BHI Broth (Sigma) + 2.5 g yeast extract + 0.25 g L-cysteine
  + 7.5 g agar (plates only); autoclaved; add 0.5 mL 0.1% Vitamin K in 95% ethanol
  + 0.5 mL hemin solution (5 mg/mL in 0.1 M NaOH, filter-sterilised).
  BHIS-ASF variant: add 5% newborn calf serum + 5% sheep serum + 5% horse serum
  (Fisher Scientific) for ASF validation cultures.

GMM (Gut Microbiota Medium):
  Prepared per Goodman et al. 2011.

YCFA (Yeast Casitones Fatty Acid, modified DSMZ 1611):
  10 g casitone, 2.5 g yeast extract, 5 g D-glucose, 0.045 g MgSO4.7H2O,
  0.09 g CaCl2.2H2O, 0.45 g K2HPO4, 0.45 g KH2PO4, 0.9 g NaCl, 0.001 g resazurin,
  1.9 mL acetic acid, 0.7 mL propionic acid, 90 uL iso-butyric acid, 100 uL n-valeric
  acid, 100 uL iso-valeric acid, 500 mL DI water. Boil 10 min stirring; cool; add 4 g
  NaHCO3 + 0.5 g L-cysteine-HCl + 0.01 g hemin + 0.0025 g mucin + 15 g agar (plates).
  Adjust to 990 mL; pH 6.7-6.8; autoclave; +10 mL filter-sterilised vitamin solution.
  Vitamin solution (per litre): 2 mg biotin, 2 mg folic acid, 12 mg pyridoxine-HCl,
  4.5 mg thiamine-HCl, 5 mg riboflavin, 5 mg nicotinic acid, 5 mg D-Ca-pantothenate,
  0.1 mg vitamin B12, 5 mg p-aminobenzoic acid, 5 mg DL-thioctic acid.

Antibiotic-supplemented media (all in BHIS base):
  Ampicillin   : 100 ug/mL (commensurate with commercially available selection plates)
  Ciprofloxacin:   5 ug/mL
  Vancomycin   :  10 ug/mL


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Fecal Cell Encapsulation in BHIS Droplets
  Reagents      : FecalCellSuspension, BHIS_Medium, HFE7500_SurfactantOil
  Operation     : Dispense cells + medium; mix (abstracts flow-focusing generation);
                  mix with oil phase (produces droplet emulsion)
  Poisson load  : 200x dilution; ~2-12% droplets encapsulate one live cell
  Droplet vol   : 65-115 pL; emulsion 0.5-1 mL; ~4-15 million droplets
  Storage       : 15 mL snap-cap culture tube (Fisherbrand 149569C) in 37 C incubator
  Notes         : Stochastic single-cell isolation in discrete droplets eliminates
                  competitive overgrowth of fast-growers over slow-growing taxa.
                  Quorum sensing signal accumulation is accelerated in small droplet
                  volumes (Boedicker et al. 2009), potentially benefiting certain organisms.

Step 2 | BHIS Droplet Incubation
  Operation     : heat at 37 C
  Duration      : 2880 min (2 days; IR: 172800.0 SECOND)
  Notes         : Plates cultured up to 7 days (10080 min) in parallel as comparator.
                  Droplet volume reduction begins after ~4 days due to evaporation in
                  the arid anaerobic atmosphere; cultures limited to 2 days.

Step 3 | Colony Density Detection (BHIS)
  Module        : imagingODDetection
  Duration      : 30 s
  Branch (BB2/BB3):
    Pass (signal > 0)  : Colony-containing droplets detected; proceed to sorting
    Fail (signal <= 0) : No growth; drain emulsion

Step 4 | Slow-Grower Sorting in BHIS Droplets
  Module        : waveletODSorting
  Replicates    : 2 independent experiments
  Keep criterion: Wavelet OD in [0.3, 0.7] (sparse colony)
  False positive: <=8%
  Sorted volume : ~1-10 uL (thin layer on top of oil due to ~30 Hz rate limit)
  Results       : Average amplified ASVs (<1% to >1%): 6.5 (unsorted) vs 12.5 (sorted)
                  out of 158 total ASVs. Community shift p<0.005 (Kolmogorov-Smirnov).
                  6 distinct Alistipes populations (Rikenellaceae) enriched by sorting;
                  plate-based dilution would require >=65 plates for 90% isolation.
                  24 sorted colonies Sanger sequenced: Hafnia (12), Enterococcus (8),
                  Bacteroides (4).
  Branch (BB5/BB6):
    Pass (signal > 0)  : Sorted fraction demulsified + DNA extracted + sequenced
    Fail (signal <= 0) : Drain sorted fraction

Step 5 | BHIS Demulsification, DNA Extraction, and 16S Sequencing (pass path)
  Reagents      : PFO_DemulsificationAgent, DNAExtractionBuffer
  Operations    :
    1. Mix 100 uL emulsion with 100 uL PFO; vortex + centrifuge; remove oil and PFO.
       For sorted droplets (~1-10 uL): add 150 uL DNA-free water + 150 uL PFO first.
    2. DNA extraction: Qiagen DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit per manufacturer instructions.
    3. detect sixteenSrRNASequencing: abstracts Illumina MiSeq 2x151 V4 amplicon pipeline
       (Argonne National Laboratory EMP protocol; MED ASV inference; SILVA taxonomy).

Step 6 | GMM Droplet Cultivation and Sequencing
  Reagents      : FecalCellSuspension, GMM_Medium, HFE7500_SurfactantOil
  Incubation    : 37 C, 2880 min (2 days)
  Branch (BB8/BB9):
    Pass (gmmCultSignal > 0)  : PFO demulsification + DNA extraction + sequencing
    Fail (gmmCultSignal <= 0) : Drain emulsion
  Notes         : GMM per Goodman et al. 2011. Bacteroidetes and Proteobacteria
                  underrepresented on GMM and YCFA plates; effect abolished in droplets.

Step 7 | YCFA Droplet Cultivation and Sequencing
  Reagents      : FecalCellSuspension, YCFA_Medium, HFE7500_SurfactantOil
  Incubation    : 37 C, 2880 min (2 days)
  Branch (BB11/BB12):
    Pass (ycfaCultSignal > 0)  : PFO demulsification + DNA extraction + sequencing
    Fail (ycfaCultSignal <= 0) : Drain emulsion
  Notes         : YCFA shows highest richness increase over plates (up to 410%,
                  p<0.005). Firmicutes dominate YCFA plates due to competitive advantage;
                  droplets restore representation across all phyla.

Step 8 | Ampicillin Resistance Screening in BHIS Droplets
  Reagents      : FecalCellSuspension, Ampicillin_BHIS (100 ug/mL), HFE7500_SurfactantOil
  Incubation    : 37 C, 1440 min (1 day; IR: 86400.0 SECOND)
  Post-sort     : waveletODSorting removes empty/non-viable droplets before DNA extraction
  Plate control : Stool diluted 10000x; density ~0.2 cell/mm2; cultured 3 days;
                  DNA from plate scraping
  Results       : Known resistors (both platforms): Bacteroides spp., Parabacteroides spp.
                  (Boente et al. 2010). Novel droplet-only: Pseudomonas spp. (opportunistic
                  pathogens), Shewanella spp. (progenitor of human antibiotic resistance
                  genes; Yousfi et al. 2017).
  Branch (BB14/BB15):
    Pass (ampResistSignal > 0)  : PFO demulsification + DNA extraction + sequencing
    Fail (ampResistSignal <= 0) : Drain emulsion

Step 9 | Ciprofloxacin Resistance Screening in BHIS Droplets
  Reagents      : FecalCellSuspension, Ciprofloxacin_BHIS (5 ug/mL), HFE7500_SurfactantOil
  Incubation    : 37 C, 1440 min (1 day)
  Post-sort     : waveletODSorting removes empty/non-viable droplets before DNA extraction
  Results       : Known resistors (both platforms): Enterococcus spp., Enterobacteriaceae
                  gen. sp. (Hooper 2002; Paterson 2006). Novel droplet-only: Bacteroides
                  spp. and Parabacteroides spp. fluoroquinolone resistance (Snydman et al.
                  2017). Gram-positive reduced susceptibility (Poole 2000).
                  Plate-preferred: 4 Clostridium spp. (only 5 organisms total showed plate
                  preference across all three antibiotics).
  Branch (BB17/BB18):
    Pass (ciproResistSignal > 0)  : PFO demulsification + DNA extraction + sequencing
    Fail (ciproResistSignal <= 0) : Drain emulsion

Step 10 | Vancomycin Resistance Screening in BHIS Droplets
  Reagents      : FecalCellSuspension, Vancomycin_BHIS (10 ug/mL), HFE7500_SurfactantOil
  Incubation    : 37 C, 1440 min (1 day)
  Post-sort     : waveletODSorting removes empty/non-viable droplets before DNA extraction
  Results       : Known resistors (both platforms): Enterobacteriaceae gen. spp.
                  (intrinsic resistance; Citron et al. 2012). Novel droplet-only:
                  Pseudomonas spp., Shewanella spp. Total across all 3 antibiotics:
                  21 unique resistant organisms detected only in droplets.
  Branch (BB20/BB21):
    Pass (vancoResistSignal > 0)  : PFO demulsification + DNA extraction + sequencing
    Fail (vancoResistSignal <= 0) : Drain emulsion


SEQUENCING PIPELINE
-------------------
Facility       : Environmental Sample Preparation and Sequencing Facility,
                 Argonne National Laboratory
Protocol       : Earth Microbiome Project 16S rRNA standard protocol
Target region  : V4 region of 16S rRNA gene
Primers        : Caporaso et al. 2012 / 2011 primer set
Amplification  : 35 cycles
Platform       : Illumina MiSeq, paired-end 2x151

Read processing (illumina-utils, Eren et al. 2013a):
  1. De-multiplex raw reads into samples
  2. Join paired-end sequences
  3. Quality filter: minimum 45 nt overlap; max 2 mismatches in overlap region
     (mismatches resolved using higher-quality base)

ASV inference  : Minimum Entropy Decomposition (MED) via oligotyping pipeline v2.1
                 (Eren et al. 2015a); Shannon entropy-based decomposition to amplicon
                 sequence variants (ASVs) at single-nucleotide resolution
Taxonomy       : SILVA database (Quast et al. 2013)

ASV filtering (dead/nonviable DNA removal):
  Conservative threshold per sample fitted by proportion of dead/nonviable DNA from
  raw stool initial inoculum. 90% confidence interval per ASV by maximum likelihood
  estimation (MLE, binomial model). ASVs whose lower CI limit falls below threshold
  are discarded. (Source code 1 in supplementary files)

Sanger sequencing (sorted colony validation):
  Primers  : 27F (AGAGTTTGATCMTGGCTCAG), 1492R (GGTTACCTTGTTACGACTT)
  PCR      : 250 nM primers, 10 uL GoTaq Green (Promega), 2 uL DNA, 7 uL DNA-free water
             95 C 3 min; 30x [95 C 30s, 54 C 30s, 72 C 1 min]; 72 C 10 min
  Gel      : 2% agarose; band excised; QIAquick Gel Extraction Kit (Qiagen)
  Facility : University of Chicago Comprehensive Cancer Center DNA Sequencing Facility
  Taxonomy : MAFFT alignment (Benchling); NCBI Standard Nucleotide BLAST


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : watterson_anaerobic_droplet_cultivation.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 22 basic blocks (BB1-BB22), 5 if/else QC gates, 28 CFG edges
DAG            : watterson_anaerobic_droplet_cultivation_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations converted to minutes (m) for compiler compatibility
                 (BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported)
                 2 days  -> 2880m  (rich media cultivation; IR: 172800.0 SECOND)
                 1 day   -> 1440m  (antibiotic screening;  IR:  86400.0 SECOND)
Modules        : imagingODDetection, waveletODSorting,
                 sixteenSrRNASequencing, antibioticResistanceDetection
Manifests      : FecalCellSuspension, BHIS_Medium, GMM_Medium, YCFA_Medium,
                 HFE7500_SurfactantOil, Ampicillin_BHIS, Ciprofloxacin_BHIS,
                 Vancomycin_BHIS, DNAExtractionBuffer, PFO_DemulsificationAgent

IR verification notes:
  - bhisEmulsion promoted to bhisEmulsion2[0] by compiler SSA renaming when crossing
    BB1->BB4 join boundary; correct expected behaviour.
  - Terminal BB22 emits NOP as expected lilott8 exit node marker.
  - All 28 CFG edges present in DAG; no orphaned nodes; clean diamond pattern
    repeated 5 times (BHIS cultivation, BHIS sort, GMM, YCFA, each antibiotic arm).
  - Time conversion verified: 2880m -> 172800.0 SECOND (2 days, rich media);
    1440m -> 86400.0 SECOND (1 day, antibiotics). Both match paper protocol.

Compiler constraint notes:
  - No array indexing or multi-unit splits used (avoids lilott8 array zipping
    failure modes documented in moazami_world_to_chip_dmf reference file).
  - All emulsion variables are scalar; all downstream operations are strict 1-to-1.
  - dispose used for pass paths; drain used for fail paths throughout.
  - All QC signals explicitly disposed before terminal NOP in BB22.

Biological scope note:
  This .bs file encodes both Protocol 1 (rich media droplet cultivation with BHIS
  slow-grower sorting, GMM, and YCFA arms) and Protocol 2 (antibiotic resistance
  droplet screening with ampicillin, ciprofloxacin, and vancomycin arms).
  Parallel plate-based cultures are off-chip comparators and are not encoded in
  BioScript. The Altered Schaedler Flora (ASF) validation experiment (BHIS-ASF
  medium, gnotobiotic mouse model) is also off-chip and not encoded here.

protocol.title: Droplet-Based High-Throughput Cultivation for Accurate Screening of Antibiotic Resistant Gut Microbes
protocol.platform: Anaerobic droplet microfluidics (flow-focusing droplet generation + dielectrophoretic sorting) inside vinyl anaerobic chamber
protocol.microbiome_source: Human fecal microbiota transplant (FMT) donor stool (Lee et al. 2017)
protocol.objective: High-throughput anaerobic isolation and cultivation of gut microbes in picoliter droplets, wavelet-OD-based slow-grower sorting, and droplet-based antibiotic resistance screening of FMT donor stool

components_inside_chamber: Microfluidic devices (droplet generation and droplet sorting)
Syringe pumps (Harvard Apparatus Pump 11 Pico Plus Elite)

droplet_generation.fabrication: Soft lithography; SU-8 3050 on 4-inch silicon wafer; PDMS (RTV 615) 10:1 A:B; cured 80 C >=1h; plasma bonded to glass slide
droplet_generation.oil_phase: Bio-Rad Droplet Generation Oil for EvaGreen

droplet_sorting.electrodes: Low-melting-temperature solder (Indium Corporation 51% In/32.5% Bi/16.5% Sn) flowed into electrode holes at 90 C; connected to standard wires

imaging_and_control.electrode_control: NI-DAQ 6211 analog output -> TREK Model 2220 amplifier (200 V/V)

wavelet_od_sorting.method: Discrete wavelet frame decomposition (LabView IMAQ Extract Texture Feature VI)
wavelet_od_sorting.normalization: Non-zero elements in wavelet feature vector normalized to 1
wavelet_od_sorting.detection_region: Interior of droplet (~6080 pixels) between red-dot markers at sorting junction

reagents.carrier_oil: Bio-Rad Droplet Generation Oil for EvaGreen

BHIS.composition: 500 mL water + 18.5 g BHI Broth (Sigma) + 2.5 g yeast extract + 0.25 g L-cysteine; autoclaved; +0.5 mL 0.1% Vitamin K in 95% ethanol + 0.5 mL hemin solution (5 mg/mL in 0.1 M NaOH, filter-sterilised)

BHIS_ASF.use: Validation with ASF model mouse gut microbiota

YCFA.vitamin_solution_per_litre: 2 mg biotin, 2 mg folic acid, 12 mg pyridoxine-HCl, 4.5 mg thiamine-HCl, 5 mg riboflavin, 5 mg nicotinic acid, 5 mg D-Ca-pantothenate, 0.1 mg vitamin B12, 5 mg p-aminobenzoic acid, 5 mg DL-thioctic acid

reagents.dna_extraction: Qiagen DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (manufacturer instructions)
reagents.dna_free_water: Used for sorted droplet demulsification (150 uL per sample)

stool_sample.donor_type: Previously characterised FMT donor (Lee et al. 2017)
stool_sample.ethics: University of Chicago Ethics Committee and IRB (IRB 132-0212); written informed consent obtained
stool_sample.preparation: 50 mL stool diluted in 100 mL PBS; supernatant collected by centrifugation; stored at -80 C

steps.name: Fecal cell encapsulation in BHIS droplets

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : High-throughput Isolation and Sorting of Gut Microbes Reduce Biases of Traditional Cultivation Strategies
Source Link  : https://www.biorxiv.org/content/biorxiv/early/2019/09/06/759969.1.full.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1101/759969
Journal      : bioRxiv preprint, September 6, 2019
Platform     : Anaerobic droplet microfluidics (flow-focusing droplet generation + image-based
               wavelet OD droplet sorting, operated inside vinyl anaerobic chamber)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a high-throughput end-to-end microfluidic platform for anaerobic
isolation, cultivation, and sorting of gut-associated bacteria in picoliter droplets. The
system enables stochastic single-cell encapsulation in 65-115 pL aqueous droplets suspended
in oil, clonal growth without interspecies competition, and automated image-based sorting of
slow-growing colonies based on an optical density proxy (Wavelet OD). The platform is operated
entirely inside a vinyl anaerobic chamber (Coy Laboratory Products) under strictly anaerobic
conditions (O2 < 1 ppm, H2 1.5-2.5%) to support cultivation of extremely oxygen-sensitive gut
anaerobes.

The protocol is divided into four functional phases:
  1. ASF model community validation -- 8-species Altered Schaedler's Flora (mouse gut) used
     to confirm all species grow in droplets, including extremely oxygen-sensitive strains,
     and that droplets prevent competitive overgrowth of fast-growing over slow-growing species.
  2. Human stool cultivation across 3 rich media -- BHIS, GMM, and YCFA droplets cultured in
     parallel and compared to conventional agar plates using 16S rRNA amplicon profiling.
     Community richness increases 37% (BHIS) to 410% (YCFA) in droplets over plates.
  3. Wavelet OD-based slow-grower sorting -- image-based sorting at ~30 Hz retains droplets
     with sparse colonies (Wavelet OD 0.3-0.7), further amplifying rare taxa from <1% to >1%
     relative abundance (avg. 6.5 ASVs unsorted vs. 12.5 ASVs sorted, out of 158 total).
  4. Viability confirmation -- sorted droplets streaked onto BHIS agar plates; Sanger
     sequencing of 24 randomly picked colonies confirms viability and taxa identity
     (Hafnia 12/24, Enterococcus 8/24, Bacteroides 4/24).


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Housing      : Vinyl anaerobic chamber (Coy Laboratory Products)
               Gas mixture: 86% N2 / 10% O2 / 4% H2
               O2 concentration: <1 ppm (monitored by Coy CAM-12 anaerobic monitor)
               H2 concentration: 1.5-2.5% maintained
               H2S reducing column placed inside chamber to prevent electronic corrosion

Fabrication  : Soft lithography (SU-8 3050 negative photoresist molds on 4-inch silicon wafers)
               Channel height: 50 um
               PDMS (RTV 615) parts A:B ratio = 10:1; degassed; cured at 80 C for >= 1 hr
               Channels hydrophobized: Aquapel (Pittsburgh Glass Works) then Fluorinert FC-40

Droplet generation device:
  - PDMS bonded to plain glass slide
  - Flow-focusing junction: bacteria suspension + oil meet at junction
  - Flow rates set by Harvard Apparatus Pump 11 Pico Plus Elite syringe pumps
  - Droplet volumes: 65-115 pL
  - Typical run: 0.5-1 mL emulsion generated in 20 min to 1 hr

Droplet sorting device:
  - PDMS bonded to ITO-coated glass slide (Delta Technologies, CG-811N-S207)
  - Electrodes: low melting-point solder (51% In / 32.5% Bi / 16.5% Sn, Indium Corporation)
                flowed in at 90 C hotplate, connected to standard wires
  - Mechanism: dielectrophoresis (DEP) at sorting junction
  - Actuation: 10 kHz, 800 V p-p, 30% duty cycle square wave; activated for 10 ms per event
  - Sorting rate: ~30 Hz
  - Reinjection flow: 20 uL/hr (droplets); 180 uL/hr (oil spacing)

Imaging system:
  - Inverted microscope: Nikon Ts2R; 4x and 10x magnification
  - Camera: Basler acA640-750um; 925 Hz frame rate; 672 x 360 px; 59 us exposure
  - Control: custom LabView code (external computer connected via sealed rubber ports)


SAMPLE TYPES
------------
Phase 1 | Mouse gut model community:
  Altered Schaedler's Flora (ASF) -- 8-species defined community
  Facultative anaerobes : ASF 360 (L. intestinalis), ASF 361 (L. murinus)
  Anaerobes             : ASF 457 (M. schaedleri), ASF 519 (P. goldsteinii)
  Extremely O2-sensitive: ASF 356 (Clostridium sp.), ASF 492 (E. plexicaudatum),
                          ASF 500 (Pseudoflavonifactor sp.), ASF 502 (Clostridium sp.)
  Source: Taconic Biosciences (fecal pellets); pure strains from Dr. Michael Wannemuehler
  Note: ASF 360 not detected in fecal pellets; 7 of 8 strains confirmed by species-specific PCR

Phase 2-4 | Human fecal microbiota:
  Single stool sample from FMT donor
  Ethics: IRB 132-0212, University of Chicago; written informed consent obtained
  Live cell density: 1e9/mL; Dead cell density: 3e9/mL (BacLight Live/Dead assay, ThermoFisher)
  Dilution for droplets: 200x (to achieve ~20-30% single-cell occupancy per Poisson statistics)


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Anaerobic Chamber and Device Priming
  Phase    : Phase 1 - ASF model community validation
  BB       : BB1 (main)
  Reagents : FC40_Oil, HFE7500_Surfactant
  Operation: mix @ 300.0 SECOND (IR: devicePrime1[0])
  Purpose  : Flush FC-40 oil and HFE7500 surfactant through channels to establish anaerobic
             two-phase flow conditions. Channels pre-coated with Aquapel then Fluorinert FC-40
             for hydrophobicity. Equipment power and control wires introduced through sealed
             rubber ports to maintain O2 < 1 ppm inside chamber.

Step 2 | ASF Fecal Pellet Preparation and Dilution
  Phase    : Phase 1 - ASF model community validation
  BB       : BB1 (main)
  Reagents : ASF_FecalPellet, BHIS_ASF_Medium
  Operation: mix @ 2.0 SECOND (IR: asfDiluted1[0])
  Prep     : Dissociate 3 ASF fecal pellets in 5 mL BHIS-ASF; sediment solids; collect
             supernatant; store at -80 C in 25% glycerol / 25% BHIS / 50% cell suspension
  Dilution : 50x from fecal cell stock suspension
  Media    : BHIS-ASF = BHIS + 5% newborn calf serum + 5% sheep serum + 5% horse serum

Step 3 | ASF Droplet Generation
  Phase    : Phase 1 - ASF model community validation
  BB       : BB1 (main)
  Reagents : asfDiluted1[0], HFE7500_Surfactant
  Operation: mix @ 3.0 SECOND (IR: asfDroplets1[0])
  Details  : Stochastic encapsulation; ~20-30% of droplets contain exactly 1 live cell
             (Poisson statistics). Droplet volume: 65-115 pL. Oil phase: HFE7500.
             All operations performed inside anaerobic chamber.

Step 4 | ASF Droplet Incubation (24 h)
  Phase    : Phase 1 - ASF model community validation
  BB       : BB1 (main)
  Operation: heat @ 37.0 C @ 86400.0 SECOND (= 1440 min = 24 h)
  Details  : Droplet emulsion incubated at 37 C inside anaerobic chamber incubator.
             Isolated cells grow clonally inside droplets. Droplets prevent ASF 361
             (parasitic towards ASF 519 in bulk broth) from dominating culture.
             All 8 ASF strains confirmed to grow in pure-strain droplet cultures.

Step 5 | ASF Emulsion Break, DNA Extraction, and ddPCR Quantification
  Phase    : Phase 1 - ASF model community validation
  BB       : BB1 (main)
  Reagents : PFO_BreakingAgent, DNAExtractionKit
  Operation: mix @ 2.0 SECOND (break); mix @ 1800.0 SECOND (extract); detect @ 30.0 SECOND
  IR vars  : asfBreakingAgent1[0], asfKit1[0], asfBroken1[0], asfDNA1[0], asfComposition1[0]
  Break    : Add equal part PFO to emulsion; vortex and centrifuge; remove oil+PFO phase
  Extract  : Qiagen DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit; elution volume 100 uL
  Quantify : BioRad QX200 droplet digital PCR system; QX200 ddPCR EvaGreen Supermix
             Species-specific primers (Sarma-Rupavtarm et al. 2004)
             Thermocycle: 94 C 10 min; 35 cycles (94 C 1 min, 60 C 1 min, 72 C 2 min)
  Expected : Bulk broth: ASF 361 dominates; ASF 519 outcompeted (parasitism)
             Droplets  : ASF 457 reaches 34%; ASF 519 reaches 0.96%; richer community
             N = 3 independent experiments; results averaged
  Module   : sixteenSrRNASequencing (detect @ 30.0 SECOND)

Step 6 | Human Stool Aliquot Preparation (3 Arms)
  Phase    : Phase 2 - Human stool cultivation across 3 media
  BB       : BB1 (main)
  Reagents : FetalCellSuspension (x3 independent aliquots)
  IR vars  : humanStoolBhis1[0], humanStoolGmm1[0], humanStoolYcfa1[0]
  Details  : Three separate aliquots dispensed independently -- one per media arm (BHIS,
             GMM, YCFA) -- to avoid reuse of a consumed variable across parallel branches.
             Each aliquot: 200x diluted from -80 C glycerol stock supernatant.

Step 7 | BHIS Droplet Generation and Incubation (48 h)
  Phase    : Phase 2 - Human stool cultivation across 3 media
  BB       : BB1 (main)
  Reagents : humanStoolBhis1[0], BHIS_Medium, HFE7500_Surfactant
  Operation: mix @ 2.0 SECOND (suspend); mix @ 3.0 SECOND (encapsulate);
             heat @ 37.0 C @ 172800.0 SECOND (= 2880 min = 48 h)
  IR vars  : bhisMedium1[0], bhisOil1[0], bhisSuspension1[0], bhisDroplets1[0]
  Emulsion : 0.5-1 mL; 4-15 million droplets; 65-115 pL each
  Media    : BHIS = 500 mL water, 18.5 g BHI broth, 2.5 g yeast extract, 0.25 g L-cysteine,
             0.5 mL 0.1% vitamin K (95% ethanol), 0.5 mL hemin solution (5 mg/mL, 0.1 M NaOH)
  Control  : 100 uL stool spread onto BHIS agar plates; cultured 7 days

Step 8 | GMM Droplet Generation and Incubation (48 h)
  Phase    : Phase 2 - Human stool cultivation across 3 media
  BB       : BB1 (main)
  Reagents : humanStoolGmm1[0], GMM_Medium, HFE7500_Surfactant
  Operation: mix @ 2.0 SECOND; mix @ 3.0 SECOND;
             heat @ 37.0 C @ 172800.0 SECOND (= 2880 min = 48 h)
  IR vars  : gmmMedium1[0], gmmOil1[0], gmmSuspension1[0], gmmDroplets1[0]
  Media    : Gut Microbiota Medium (GMM) per Goodman et al. (2011) PNAS 108:6252

Step 9 | YCFA Droplet Generation and Incubation (48 h)
  Phase    : Phase 2 - Human stool cultivation across 3 media
  BB       : BB1 (main)
  Reagents : humanStoolYcfa1[0], YCFA_Medium, HFE7500_Surfactant
  Operation: mix @ 2.0 SECOND; mix @ 3.0 SECOND;
             heat @ 37.0 C @ 172800.0 SECOND (= 2880 min = 48 h)
  IR vars  : ycfaMedium1[0], ycfaOil1[0], ycfaSuspension1[0], ycfaDroplets1[0]
  Media    : YCFA (modified DSMZ 1611): 10 g casitone, 2.5 g yeast extract, 5 g dextrose,
             short-chain fatty acids (acetic 1.9 mL, propionic 0.7 mL, isobutyric 90 uL,
             n-valeric 100 uL, iso-valeric 100 uL), NaHCO3 4 g, L-cysteine-HCl 0.5 g,
             hemin 0.01 g, mucin 0.0025 g; pH 6.7-6.8; autoclave; add 10 mL vitamin solution

Step 10 | Emulsion Break and DNA Extraction (All Three Arms)
  Phase    : Phase 2 - Human stool cultivation across 3 media
  BB       : BB1 (main)
  Reagents : PFO_BreakingAgent (x3), DNAExtractionKit (x3)
  Operation: mix @ 2.0 SECOND (break per arm); mix @ 1800.0 SECOND (extract per arm)
  IR vars  : bhisBreaker1, gmmBreaker1, ycfaBreaker1 (break);
             bhisKit1, gmmKit1, ycfaKit1 (kits);
             bhisBroken1, gmmBroken1, ycfaBroken1 (broken);
             bhisDNA1, gmmDNA1, ycfaDNA1 (extracted DNA)
  Method   : Add equal part PFO to emulsion; vortex; centrifuge; remove oil+PFO
             Qiagen DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit; elution volume 100 uL per sample

Step 11 | 16S rRNA Amplicon Sequencing and Community Richness QC Gate
  Phase    : Phase 2 - Human stool cultivation across 3 media
  BB       : BB1 (main) -> BB2 (pass) / BB3 (fail)
  Operation: detect @ 30.0 SECOND (profiles x3); mix @ 5.0 SECOND (x2, combine);
             detect @ 30.0 SECOND (richness gate)
  IR vars  : bhisProfile1, gmmProfile1, ycfaProfile1, combinedProfiles1,
             richnessMeasure1, richnessSignal1
  Modules  : sixteenSrRNASequencing (profiles); colonyDensityDetection (richness gate)
  Sequencing:
    Facility  : Environmental Sample Preparation and Sequencing Facility, Argonne National Lab
    Target    : 16S rRNA V4 region; primers from Caporaso et al. (2012) ISME J 6:1621
    PCR       : 35 cycles
    Platform  : Illumina MiSeq paired-end 2 x 300
    QC        : illumina-utils; demultiplex; join pairs (min overlap 45 nt, <2 mismatches)
    ASV       : Minimum Entropy Decomposition (MED) / oligotyping pipeline v2.1
    Taxonomy  : Global Alignment for Sequence Taxonomy (GAST)
  Metrics   : Richness (R, total ASVs); Shannon index (H'); low-abundance count (Rlow, <1% stool)
  Statistics: Mann-Whitney U test (wilcox.test, R); null = difference of means is zero
  Branch:
    Pass (BB2): richnessSignal1[0] > 0  -> droplet richness > plate richness confirmed;
                dispose(bhisDNA1, gmmDNA1, ycfaDNA1); proceed to sorting arm (BB4)
    Fail (BB3): richnessSignal1[0] <= 0 -> no richness gain;
                dispose(bhisDNA1, gmmDNA1, ycfaDNA1); fall through to BB4
  Results:
    Richness increase over plates: 37% (BHIS) to 410% (YCFA); p < 0.005
    Low-abundance ASVs: 112 (droplets) vs. 58 (plates) avg., p < 0.005
    Shannon diversity increased in BHIS and YCFA droplets; not in GMM
    Bacteroides oligotypes cluster closer to raw stool in droplets (p < 0.005, multiscale bootstrap)

Step 12 | Slow-Growing Colony Sorting: Droplet Preparation and Incubation (24 h)
  Phase    : Phase 3 - Wavelet OD-based slow-grower sorting
  BB       : BB4 (bsbbif_4_j)
  Reagents : FetalCellSuspension, BHIS_Medium, HFE7500_Surfactant
  Operation: mix @ 2.0 SECOND; mix @ 3.0 SECOND;
             heat @ 37.0 C @ 86400.0 SECOND (= 1440 min = 24 h)
  IR vars  : sortingStool1, bhisSortMedium1, bhisSortOil1, sortSuspension1, sortDroplets1
  Details  : Fresh BHIS droplet emulsion from human stool. Two independent sorting experiments.
             Droplets reinjected at 20 uL/hr; oil spacing phase at 180 uL/hr.

Step 13 | Image-Based Wavelet OD Sorting and Sorting QC Gate
  Phase    : Phase 3 - Wavelet OD-based slow-grower sorting
  BB       : BB4 (bsbbif_4_j) -> BB5 (pass) / BB6 (fail)
  Operation: detect @ 30.0 SECOND (IR: sortingSignal1[0])
  Module   : colonyDensityDetection
  Imaging  : Basler acA640-750um; 925 Hz; 672 x 360 px; 59 us exposure
  Algorithm: Discrete wavelet frame decomposition (LabView IMAQ Extract Texture Feature VI)
             Wavelet type: Biorthogonal 3.1; Subband: Low Low High (LLH)
             Window: 15 x 15 px; Step: 5 px; Gray levels: 15; Displacement: 3 x 3 px
             Wavelet OD normalized 0 (empty) to 1 (dense colony)
  Thresholds:
    Empty droplets (waste)       : Wavelet OD < 0.3
    Slow-growing colonies (keep) : 0.3 <= Wavelet OD <= 0.7
    Dense colonies (waste)       : Wavelet OD > 0.7
  Electrode actuation (keep path): 10 kHz, 800 V p-p, 30% duty cycle, 10 ms per event
  Sorting rate                   : ~30 Hz
  False-positive rate (upper bound): <= 8% (epsilon formula from paper Methods)
  Branch:
    Pass (BB5): sortingSignal1[0] > 0  -> slow-growing colonies detected in keep path;
                proceed to DNA extraction and sequencing
    Fail (BB6): sortingSignal1[0] <= 0 -> no qualifying slow-growing droplets;
                dispose(sortDroplets1[0])

Step 14 | Sorted Droplet DNA Extraction and 16S Sequencing
  Phase    : Phase 3 - Wavelet OD-based slow-grower sorting
  BB       : BB5 (bsbbif_5_t) [pass path only]
  Reagents : PFO_BreakingAgent, DNAExtractionKit
  Operation: mix @ 2.0 SECOND (break); mix @ 1800.0 SECOND (extract);
             detect @ 30.0 SECOND (IR: sortedProfile1[0])
  IR vars  : sortedBreaker1, sortedKit1, sortedBroken1, sortedDNA1, sortedProfile1
  Sorted volume: ~1-10 uL (thin layer on oil, estimated by pipetting)
  Break method : Add 150 uL DNA-free water + 150 uL PFO to sorted droplets; vortex; centrifuge
  Extract      : Qiagen DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit
  Results:
    Sorted vs unsorted: 12.5 vs. 6.5 ASVs amplified from <1% to >1% (out of 158 total)
    Phylogenetic range: sorted samples amplify taxa across wider range of phylogenetic tree
    Rank-abundance shift: p < 0.005 (Kolmogorov-Smirnov test)

Step 15 | Viability Confirmation: Agar Plate Streaking and Colony Picking
  Phase    : Phase 4 - Viability confirmation
  BB       : BB7 (bsbbif_7_j) -> BB8 (pass) / BB9 (fail)
  Reagents : FetalCellSuspension, BHIS_Medium, FDA_PI_Stain
  Operation: mix @ 2.0 SECOND (plate); heat @ 37.0 C @ 172800.0 SECOND (= 48 h);
             mix @ 600.0 SECOND (stain); detect @ 30.0 SECOND (viability gate)
  IR vars  : sortedForViability1, bhisAgarMedium1, platedSorted1,
             fdaPI_Stain1, stainedPlated1, viabilitySignal1
  Module   : dropletViabilityDetection
  Streak   : ~10 uL sorted droplet emulsion + oil onto BHIS agar plate; 37 C for 2 days
  Picking  : 24 colonies randomly picked; each into 2 mL BHIS broth
  Sequencing: Sanger sequencing (27F/1492R primers); GoTaq Green Master Mix (Promega)
              PCR: 95 C 3 min; 30 cycles (95 C 30 s, 54 C 30 s, 72 C 1 min); 72 C 10 min
              Gel: 2% agarose; band excised; QIAquick Gel Extraction Kit (Qiagen)
              BLAST taxonomy: Hafnia 12/24, Enterococcus 8/24, Bacteroides 4/24
  Viability stain: BacLight FDA/PI (ThermoFisher)
  Branch:
