    Pass (BB8): viabilitySignal1[0] > 0  -> colonies viable; dispose
    Fail (BB9): viabilitySignal1[0] <= 0 -> no viable growth; dispose


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : watterson_anaerobic_droplet_gut_microbiome.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based, Python 3.10)
IR output      : 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
DAG file       : watterson_anaerobic_droplet_gut_microbiome_main_dag.dot
Duration units : All durations converted to seconds (s) or minutes (m) for compiler compatibility
                 (BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported)
                 24 h  -> 1440m  (ASF incubation and sorting incubation; IR: 86400.0 SECOND)
                 48 h  -> 2880m  (human stool incubation; IR: 172800.0 SECOND)
                 30 min -> 30m   (DNA extraction; IR: 1800.0 SECOND)
                 10 min -> 10m   (FDA/PI staining; IR: 600.0 SECOND)
Modules        : colonyDensityDetection, sixteenSrRNASequencing, dropletViabilityDetection
Manifests      : FetalCellSuspension, BHIS_Medium, GMM_Medium, YCFA_Medium, FC40_Oil,
                 HFE7500_Surfactant, PFO_BreakingAgent, FDA_PI_Stain, ASF_FecalPellet,
                 BHIS_ASF_Medium, DNAExtractionKit
Bug fixes applied:
  Fix 1 -- DNAExtractionKit manifest used bare in mix (5 occurrences): each replaced with an
           explicit dispense variable (asfKit1, bhisKit1, gmmKit1, ycfaKit1, sortedKit1)
           before its corresponding mix call. Root cause: compiler visitMix requires both
           operands to be previously bound dispense variables.
  Fix 2 -- humanStool variable reused across 3 mix calls (BHIS, GMM, YCFA arms): replaced
           with 3 independent dispense calls (humanStoolBhis, humanStoolGmm, humanStoolYcfa)
           to avoid reuse of a consumed variable across parallel cultivation branches.
IR verification: All mix operands confirmed dispensed before use; no manifest name appears
                 directly inside any mix call; python3 static check passed (0 errors).

protocol.title: High-throughput Isolation and Sorting of Gut Microbes Reduce Biases of Traditional Cultivation Strategies
protocol.platform: Anaerobic droplet microfluidics (flow-focusing droplet generation + image-based droplet sorting inside vinyl anaerobic chamber)
sample_types: Mouse gut microbiota (Altered Schaedler's Flora, 8-species model community)
Human fecal microbiota (single FMT donor stool sample)
protocol.objective: High-throughput anaerobic isolation and clonal cultivation of gut bacteria in picoliter droplets, image-based wavelet OD sorting for slow-growing colonies, and 16S rRNA amplicon profiling to demonstrate enrichment of rare taxa over conventional agar plate cultivation

device.housing: Vinyl anaerobic chamber (Coy Laboratory Products), 86% N2 / 10% O2 / 4% H2 gas mixture
device.fabrication: Soft lithography; SU-8 3050 negative photoresist molds on 4-inch silicon wafers

droplet_sorting_device.substrate: PDMS bonded to ITO-coated glass slide (Delta Technologies, CG-811N-S207)
droplet_sorting_device.electrode_material: Low melting-point solder (51% In / 32.5% Bi / 16.5% Sn, Indium Corporation of America)

reagents.carrier_oil: Bio-Rad Droplet Generation Oil for EvaGreen

BHIS.composition: 500 mL water, 18.5 g Brain Heart Infusion Broth (Sigma), 2.5 g yeast extract, 0.25 g L-cysteine, 0.5 mL 0.1% Vitamin K in 95% ethanol, 0.5 mL hemin solution (5 mg/mL in 0.1 M NaOH)

BHIS_ASF.additives: 5% newborn calf serum, 5% sheep serum, 5% horse serum (all Fisher Scientific)

YCFA.composition: 10 g casitone, 2.5 g yeast extract, 5 g dextrose (D-glucose), 0.045 g MgSO4x7H2O, 0.09 g CaCl2x2H2O, 0.45 g K2HPO4, 0.45 g KH2PO4, 0.9 g NaCl, 0.001 g resazurin sodium salt, 1.9 mL acetic acid, 0.7 mL propionic acid, 90 uL isobutyric acid, 100 uL n-valeric acid, 100 uL iso-valeric acid, 500 mL DI water; boiled 10 min, then: 4 g NaHCO3, 0.5 g L-cysteine-HCl, 0.01 g hemin, 0.0025 g mucin; DI water to 990 mL; pH 6.7-6.8; autoclave; then add 10 mL filter-sterilised vitamin solution
YCFA.vitamin_solution_per_L: 2 mg biotin, 2 mg folic acid, 12 mg pyridoxine-HCl, 4.5 mg thiamine-HCl, 5 mg riboflavin, 5 mg nicotinic acid, 5 mg D-Ca-pantothenate, 0.1 mg vitamin B12, 5 mg p-aminobenzoic acid, 5 mg DL-thioctic acid

asf_strains.source: Taconic Biosciences (fecal pellets); pure strains from Dr. Michael Wannemuehler

steps.name: Anaerobic chamber and device priming
steps.notes: FC-40 oil and HFE7500 surfactant flushed through microfluidic channels inside anaerobic chamber to prime device. Channels pre-coated with Aquapel then Fluorinert FC-40 for hydrophobicity. Anaerobic conditions: O2 < 1 ppm, H2 1.5-2.5%, monitored by Coy CAM-12 anaerobic monitor. H2S reducing column placed inside chamber to prevent corrosion of electronic components.

steps.name: ASF fecal pellet preparation and dilution
steps.stock_preparation: Dissociate 3 ASF fecal pellets (Taconic Biosciences) in 5 mL BHIS-ASF medium; sediment fecal solids; collect supernatant; store at -80 C in 25% glycerol / 25% BHIS / 50% cell suspension
steps.missing_strain: ASF 360 (L. intestinalis) not detected by species-specific PCR in fecal pellets
steps.detection_method: Species-specific PCR; primers from Sarma-Rupavtarm et al. (2004)
steps.notes: Pure ASF strains also cultured independently from stock solutions in liquid BHIS-ASF broth for 1-2 days before separate droplet encapsulation experiments.

steps.name: ASF droplet generation
steps.encapsulation_statistics: Poisson: ~20-30% of droplets contain exactly 1 live bacterial cell
steps.notes: All droplet generation performed inside anaerobic chamber. Bacteria stochastically encapsulated by diluting fecal cell suspension in BHIS-ASF medium to achieve single-cell occupancy per Poisson statistics. Oil phase: HFE7500 with surfactant.

steps.name: ASF droplet incubation
steps.notes: Droplet emulsion placed in 37 C incubator inside anaerobic chamber. Isolated viable strains grow clonally within droplets. Droplets prevent competitive overgrowth of fast-growing ASF 361 (L. murinus) over ASF 519 (P. goldsteinii) observed in bulk broth. Extremely oxygen-sensitive strains (ASF 356, 492, 500, 502) maintained at <1 ppm O2 throughout.

steps.name: ASF emulsion break, DNA extraction, and ddPCR quantification
steps.emulsion_break_method: Add equal part PFO to emulsion, vortex, centrifuge, remove oil+PFO phase
steps.dna_extraction: Qiagen DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit; elution volume 100 uL

quantification.method: Droplet digital PCR (BioRad QX200 ddPCR system)
quantification.thermocycle: 94 C 10 min; 35 cycles: 94 C 1 min, 60 C 1 min, 72 C 2 min
quantification.primers: Species-specific primers from Sarma-Rupavtarm et al. (2004)

expected_results.bulk_broth: ASF 361 (L. murinus) dominates; ASF 519 outcompeted due to parasitism
expected_results.droplets: ASF 361 confined; ASF 457 reaches 34% relative abundance; ASF 519 reaches 0.96%; higher diversity maintained

steps.name: Human stool aliquot preparation
steps.phase: Phase 2 - Human stool cultivation across 3 media
steps.sample_source: Single human stool sample from FMT donor (IRB 132-0212, University of Chicago Institutional Review Board; written informed consent obtained)
steps.aliquot_preparation: Spin down 50 uL stool diluted in 100 uL PBS; carry forward supernatant; store at -80 C
steps.dilution_for_droplets: 200x (to achieve ~20-30% single-cell occupancy per Poisson statistics)
steps.notes: Three independent aliquots dispensed (one per media arm: BHIS, GMM, YCFA) to avoid variable reuse across parallel cultivation branches. Plate controls: 100 uL stool suspension spread onto agar plates, cultured 7 days.

steps.name: BHIS droplet generation and incubation
steps.phase: Phase 2 - Human stool cultivation across 3 media
steps.notes: Brain Heart Infusion Supplemented medium. Parallel agar plate control cultured 7 days. No biological replicate variation detected between replicates or cultivation time for a given condition.

steps.name: GMM droplet generation and incubation
steps.phase: Phase 2 - Human stool cultivation across 3 media
steps.notes: Gut Microbiota Medium prepared per Goodman et al. (2011) PNAS 108:6252.

steps.name: YCFA droplet generation and incubation
steps.phase: Phase 2 - Human stool cultivation across 3 media
steps.notes: Yeast Casitones Fatty Acid medium (modified DSMZ 1611). pH 6.7-6.8.

steps.name: Emulsion break and DNA extraction (all three media arms)
steps.phase: Phase 2 - Human stool cultivation across 3 media
steps.emulsion_break_method: Add equal part PFO, vortex and centrifuge, remove oil+PFO phase
steps.dna_extraction: Qiagen DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit; elution volume 100 uL

steps.name: 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing and community richness QC gate
steps.phase: Phase 2 - Human stool cultivation across 3 media
steps.operation: detect -> mix -> mix -> detect -> if/else gate

sequencing.facility: Environmental Sample Preparation and Sequencing Facility, Argonne National Laboratory
sequencing.qc: illumina-utils: demultiplex, join pairs (min overlap 45 nt, <2 mismatches in overlap)
sequencing.asv_inference: Minimum Entropy Decomposition (MED) / oligotyping pipeline v2.1

metrics.richness_R: Total count of ASVs per sample
metrics.rlow: Count of ASVs <1% abundant in raw stool that are cultivated
metrics.statistical_test: Mann-Whitney U (wilcox.test in R); null: difference of means = 0

expected_results.bacteroides_clustering: Droplet cultures cluster closer to raw stool than plate cultures (p<0.005, multiscale bootstrap resampling)
expected_results.shannon_diversity: Increased in BHIS and YCFA droplets vs. plates; not in GMM

steps.name: Slow-growing colony droplet sorting preparation and incubation
steps.notes: Fresh human stool aliquot in BHIS medium. Two independent sorting experiments. Droplets reinjected at 20 uL/hr; oil spacing phase at 180 uL/hr.

steps.name: Image-based wavelet OD sorting and sorting QC gate

sorting_system.wavelet_transform: Discrete wavelet frame decomposition (LabView IMAQ Extract Texture Feature VI)

steps.name: Sorted droplet DNA extraction and 16S sequencing
steps.sorted_volume_uL: 1-10 (thin layer on oil; estimated by pipetting)
steps.emulsion_break_method: Add 150 uL DNA-free water + 150 uL PFO to sorted droplets, vortex, centrifuge

expected_results.asvs_amplified_unsorted: 6.5 average (out of 158 total ASVs) amplified from <1% to >1%
expected_results.asvs_amplified_sorted: 12.5 average (out of 158 total ASVs) amplified from <1% to >1%
expected_results.phylogenetic_range: Sorted samples amplify taxa across wider phylogenetic range than unsorted

steps.name: Viability confirmation: agar plate streaking and colony growth
steps.operation: mix -> heat -> mix -> detect -> if/else gate
steps.agar_streak_method: Streak ~10 uL sorted droplet emulsion + oil onto BHIS agar plate; culture 2 days at 37 C

colony_picking.method: Random picking; place each colony into 2 mL BHIS broth
colony_picking.sequencing: Sanger sequencing (27F/1492R primers, GoTaq Green Master Mix, PCR: 95 C 3 min; 30 cycles: 95 C 30 s, 54 C 30 s, 72 C 1 min; 72 C 10 min); excise from 2% agarose gel; QIAquick Gel Extraction Kit; sequence at U. Chicago Comprehensive Cancer Center DNA Sequencing Facility

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_4_j
basic_blocks.description: dispose richness QC signals; begin sorting arm

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_7_j
basic_blocks.description: dispose sortingSignal; begin viability confirmation arm

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_10_j
basic_blocks.description: dispose remaining QC signals; NOP

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Computational Prediction of Protein Interactions in Single Cells by Proximity Sequencing
Source Link  : https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011915
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011915
Journal      : PLoS Computational Biology, 2024, Vol. 20(3), Article e1011915
Authors      : Junjie Xia, Hoang Van Phan, Luke Vistain, Mengjie Chen, Aly A. Khan, Savaş Tay
Platform     : Proximity Sequencing (Prox-seq) combined with single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes Proximity Sequencing (Prox-seq), a method for simultaneous quantification
of mRNA, surface protein expression, and protein complexes (dimers) at the single-cell level.
Prox-seq uses a proximity ligation assay (PLA) with DNA-conjugated antibody probes (Probe A and
Probe B) targeting surface proteins of interest. Ligation of the oligos on Probe A and Probe B
occurs only when the two probes are within 50-70 nm of each other — i.e., when their respective
target protein molecules are co-localised or physically interacting. The resulting ligated PLA
products are barcoded, counted by unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) after sequencing, and
provide direct single-cell readout of protein complex formation.

By combining Prox-seq with scRNA-seq, PLA product libraries are sequenced alongside complementary
DNA (cDNA) libraries, yielding multi-omic single-cell data: gene expression, protein abundance,
and protein complex expression simultaneously from the same cell.

The paper introduces a physical simulation model of Prox-seq data and computationally benchmarks
three methods for removing proximity noise (random ligation background) and quantifying true
protein complexes: the iterative method, the linear regression (LR) method, and a new ensemble
method combining both. The ensemble method is demonstrated to be the most accurate and robust
across diverse biological scenarios.

Two cell line arms are encoded:
  ARM 1: Jurkat T cells — known complexes: CD3:CD3 and CD28:CD28 (homodimers)
  ARM 2: Raji B cells  — known complex: ICAM1:ICAM1 (homodimer on cell surface)

Code repository : https://github.com/tay-lab/Prox-seq_computation
Data repository : NCBI GEO accession GSE196130


METHOD DESIGN
-------------
Probe Design:
  Each target protein is stained with TWO DNA-conjugated antibodies:
    - Probe A: antibody conjugated to oligo A (contains barcode for protein i)
    - Probe B: antibody conjugated to oligo B (contains barcode for protein j)
  Ligation of oligo A to oligo B occurs only if Euclidean distance between
  the two probes <= ligation distance (50-70 nm; set to 50 nm in simulation model).
  Result: a PLA product barcode encoding the protein pair i:j.

  Importantly, unligated probes do NOT contribute to PLA signal because both library
  preparation and sequence alignment require barcodes from both the A and B probe.
  UMI counting of PLA products after sequencing gives the number of protein complexes
  per cell per protein pair.

Free Oligo Modification:
  An experimentally modified Prox-seq procedure adds FreeOligoA and FreeOligoB
  (non-antibody-conjugated oligos) alongside the probe panel. These generate PLA products:
    - Protein_X : free_oligo_B  ->  measures non-proximal (unligated) Probe A count
    - free_oligo_A : Protein_Y  ->  measures non-proximal (unligated) Probe B count
  These non-proximal counts serve as explanatory variables in the linear regression (LR)
  method and ensemble method for per-cell proximity noise estimation.

Proximity Noise:
  Random co-localisation of non-interacting proteins produces "proximity noise": ligation
  events between Probe A and Probe B from unrelated proteins that happen to be nearby.
  Theoretical expected proximity noise:
    E(X_ij) = (d_ligation^2 / 4R^2) * A_i * B_j
  where d_ligation = 50 nm, R = cell radius = 5 um, A_i = Probe A count for protein i,
  B_j = Probe B count for protein j.
  Proximity noise scales quadratically with both protein abundance and ligation distance
  (Fig 2e). Identifying and removing proximity noise is essential for accurate complex
  quantification, especially for highly expressed proteins.

Isotype Control:
  Isotype control antibodies with oligonucleotide conjugation are included in both Probe A
  and Probe B panels. This allows direct estimation of nonspecific antibody binding
  probability from observed PLA data. For extracellular Prox-seq assays, nonspecific
  binding constitutes <1% of both-specific PLA counts (e.g. CD147:CD147 in Jurkat cells,
  S4 Fig), and is much less important than proximity noise.


PROBE PANEL
-----------
Targets : CD3, CD28, PD1, CD147, ICAM1, PDL1, HLADR, B7
Control : Isotype control antibody (oligo-conjugated) in both Probe A and Probe B panels
Reference: Same panel as Vistain et al. Nat Methods 2022 (Ref [4])

Jurkat T cells express  : CD3, CD28, PD1, CD147, ICAM1
  Known complexes       : CD3:CD3 (homodimer, Ref [12]); CD28:CD28 (homodimer, Ref [13])

Raji B cells express    : ICAM1, PDL1, HLADR, B7, CD147
  Known complex         : ICAM1:ICAM1 (homodimer on cell surface, Ref [14])
  Specificity check     : Raji cells do not express CD3 or PD1; PLA counts for those
                          targets are near zero, validating probe panel specificity


COMPUTATIONAL METHODS
---------------------

Iterative Method:
  Mechanism   : Solve quadratic equations iteratively for all possible protein dimers.
                Protein complex count = observed PLA count minus expected random PLA count.
                Expected count calculated from protein abundance estimates derived from
                summing PLA product counts per protein.
  Equation    : Y_ij^(m+1) = X_ij - [(sum_A_i - sum_Y_i^m) * (sum_B_j - sum_Y_j^m)] /
                              (total_PLA_sum - sum_Y^m)
  Strengths   : Performs well at high signal-to-noise; no additional experiment required.
  Limitations : Unstable with multiple protein dimers or overabundant proteins;
                sensitive to initialisation (default: all-zeroes matrix).
                Consistently underestimates true complex count (Fig 3c, 3e).
  Best for    : Simpler scenarios with only homodimers or only heterodimers.

Linear Regression (LR) Method:
  Mechanism   : Weighted least squares regression of observed PLA count (X_ij) onto
                product of non-proximal Probe A count (A_i') and Probe B count (B_j').
                Slope beta_1 estimates proximity noise; intercept beta_0 detects complex.
                Protein complex count Y_ij = X_ij - beta_1 * A_i' * B_j'.
  Equation    : X_ij ~ beta_0 + beta_1 * A_i' * B_j'  (weighted by 1 / (A_i' * B_j'))
  Requirement : Free oligo modification experiment required to measure non-proximal counts.
  Strengths   : More accurate than iterative method; performs well in low signal-to-noise
                and multi-dimer scenarios; greater robustness for complex biological cases.
  Limitations : Unstable when non-proximal probe counts are near zero;
                not optimal for high signal-to-noise homodimer/heterodimer-only scenarios.
                Suffers false positives when noise is very low (Fig 4c).
  Best for    : Low signal-to-noise and scenarios with multiple protein dimers or
                overabundant proteins.

Ensemble Method (recommended):
  Mechanism   : Apply LR method first; use LR output (protein complex matrix) as
                initialisation for iterative method instead of all-zeroes matrix.
                Bridges weaknesses of both methods.
  Requirement : Free oligo modification experimental procedure required.
  Strengths   : Robust and consistent across all 8 biological scenario types and both
                high and low signal-to-noise cases (800 randomised tests).
                Highest average prediction score; lowest variance; fewest false positives.
                Most accurate quantification of true-positive complex abundance in single
                cells (Fig 4d).
  Best for    : Recommended default when true biological conditions are uncertain.

Fisher's Exact Test:
  Mechanism   : One-sided Fisher's exact test on 2x2 PLA product contingency table per cell.
                Benjamini-Hochberg correction applied. Identifies enriched protein complexes.
  Use         : Statistical validation of complex enrichment; complementary to quantification.

Prediction Score:
  Formula     : Score = 0.5 * SumPearson - 0.4 * SumMeanDeviation - 0.1 * SumFPrate
  Result      : Ensemble method scores highest and shows lowest variance across all scenarios
                (S10d Fig, S2 Table).


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

--- ARM 1: JURKAT T CELLS ---

Step 1 | Cell Suspension Preparation (Jurkat)
  Reagents    : JurkatCells, PBS
  Operation   : Resuspend Jurkat T cells in PBS at appropriate concentration for staining
  Duration    : 5 min (mix)
  BioScript   : jurkatSuspension = mix jurkatCells with cellPBS for 5m

Step 2 | Nonspecific Binding Block (Jurkat)
  Reagents    : jurkatSuspension, BlockingBuffer
  Operation   : Mix with blocking buffer; incubate 10 min at 4 C
  Duration    : 10 min at 4 C
  Purpose     : Reduces nonspecific antibody binding background
  Notes       : Nonspecific binding <1% of both-specific PLA counts for extracellular
                assays (CD147:CD147 in Jurkat cells, S4 Fig)
  BioScript   : blockedCells = mix jurkatSuspension with blockingBuf for 10m
                heat blockedCells at 4c for 10m

Step 3 | Probe A Staining with Isotype Control (Jurkat)
  Reagents    : blockedCells, ProxSeqProbeA, IsotypeControlAntibody
  Operation   : Mix isotype control into Probe A panel; stain cells 30 min at 4 C
  Duration    : 30 min at 4 C
  Probe A panel: CD3, CD28, PD1, CD147, ICAM1, PDL1, HLADR, B7 + isotype control
  BioScript   : probeAWithControl = mix probeAStain with isotypeControl for 5s
                probeAStained = mix blockedCells with probeAWithControl for 30m
                heat probeAStained at 4c for 30m

Step 4 | Wash Unbound Probe A (Jurkat, 3x)
  Reagents    : probeAStained, WashBuffer (x3)
  Operation   : 3 sequential PBS washes, 2 min each
  Duration    : 3 x 2 min
  Notes       : Unligated probes do not contribute to PLA signal (dual-barcode requirement)
  BioScript   : washedA1 = mix probeAStained with wash1A for 2m
                washedA2 = mix washedA1 with wash2A for 2m
                jurkatProbeAReady = mix washedA2 with wash3A for 2m

Step 5 | Probe B Staining (Jurkat)
  Reagents    : jurkatProbeAReady, ProxSeqProbeB
  Operation   : Stain cells with Probe B panel 30 min at 4 C
  Duration    : 30 min at 4 C
  Notes       : After this step, cells carry both Probe A and Probe B on surface proteins
  BioScript   : probeBStained = mix jurkatProbeAReady with probeBStain for 30m
                heat probeBStained at 4c for 30m

Step 6 | Wash Unbound Probe B (Jurkat, 3x)
  Reagents    : probeBStained, WashBuffer (x3)
  Operation   : 3 sequential PBS washes, 2 min each
  BioScript   : washedB1 = mix probeBStained with wash1B for 2m
                washedB2 = mix washedB1 with wash2B for 2m
                jurkatDualStained = mix washedB2 with wash3B for 2m

Step 7 | Free Oligo Addition (Jurkat, non-proximal probe measurement)
  Reagents    : jurkatDualStained, FreeOligoA, FreeOligoB
  Operation   : Mix free oligos together; add to dual-stained cells; incubate 10 min at 4 C
  Duration    : 10 min at 4 C
  Purpose     : FreeOligoA generates PLA products Protein_X:free_oligo_B (non-proximal Probe A)
                FreeOligoB generates PLA products free_oligo_A:Protein_Y (non-proximal Probe B)
                Non-proximal counts required for LR method: Y_ij = X_ij - beta_1 * A_i' * B_j'
                (Methods: LR method; Ref [4] Vistain et al. Nat Methods 2022)
  BioScript   : freeOligoMix = mix freeOligoADrop with freeOligoBDrop for 5s
                jurkatWithFreeOligos = mix jurkatDualStained with freeOligoMix for 10m
                heat jurkatWithFreeOligos at 4c for 10m

Step 8 | Proximity Ligation Reaction (Jurkat)
  Reagents    : jurkatWithFreeOligos, LigationBuffer, Ligase (T4 DNA Ligase)
  Operation   : Mix ligation buffer with ligase; add to cells; incubate 30 min at 25 C
  Duration    : 30 min at 25 C
  Ligation distance: 50-70 nm (50 nm threshold in simulation model)
  Proximity noise: E(X_ij) = (d_ligation^2 / 4R^2) * A_i * B_j
                   (R = 5 um, d_ligation = 50 nm; Methods: Theoretical calculation)
  BioScript   : ligationReagents = mix ligBuf with ligase for 5s
                jurkatLigated = mix jurkatWithFreeOligos with ligationReagents for 30m
                heat jurkatLigated at 25c for 30m

Step 9 | Ligation Stop and Wash (Jurkat, 3x)
  Reagents    : jurkatLigated, StopSolution, WashBuffer (x3)
  Operation   : Add stop solution (5 min mix); 3x PBS wash, 2 min each
  Duration    : 5 min (stop) + 3 x 2 min (washes)
  BioScript   : jurkatStopped = mix jurkatLigated with stopSol for 5m
                jurkatLigatedReady = (3x wash chain, 2m each)

Step 10 | Single-Cell Encapsulation and Library Preparation (Jurkat)
  Reagents    : jurkatLigatedReady, DNALibraryBuffer, SequencingReagent
  Operation   : Encapsulate cells in individual droplets; lyse; capture mRNA (poly-dT)
                and PLA products (barcoded sequences); prepare combined cDNA + PLA library
  Duration    : 30 min at 37 C (library prep) + 10 min (sequencing reagent addition)
  Output      : Combined scRNA-seq + Prox-seq sequencing library
  BioScript   : jurkatLibPrep = mix jurkatLigatedReady with dnaLibBuf for 30m
                heat jurkatLibPrep at 37c for 30m
                jurkatSeqReady = mix jurkatLibPrep with seqReagentJ for 10m

Step 11 | Jurkat Library QC and Branching Gate
  Reagents    : jurkatSeqReady
  Operation   : detect seqLibraryQC on jurkatSeqReady for 30s
  Detection   : Abstracts fluorometric/electrophoretic QC (Bioanalyzer, Qubit)
                Checks fragment size, library complexity, UMI diversity
  Branch Pass : jurkatLibSignal > 0  ->  dispose(jurkatSeqReady)  ->  proceed to Raji arm
  Branch Fail : jurkatLibSignal <= 0 ->  drain(jurkatSeqReady)    ->  proceed to Raji arm

--- ARM 2: RAJI B CELLS ---
  Steps 12-22 are structurally identical to Jurkat steps 1-11.
  Key differences:
    - RajiCells instead of JurkatCells
    - Raji cells express ICAM1:ICAM1 homodimer (confirmed by all 3 methods, Fig 5d-f)
    - Raji cells do not express CD3 or PD1 (near-zero PLA counts for those pairs)
    - Non-proximal Raji probe counts used to calibrate proximity noise for Raji arm
    - Final QC gate on rajiLibSignal; terminal block disposes rajiLibSignal

Step 12 | Cell Suspension Preparation (Raji)        -- same as Step 1 for Raji
Step 13 | Nonspecific Binding Block (Raji)           -- same as Step 2 for Raji
Step 14 | Probe A Staining with Isotype Control (Raji) -- same as Step 3 for Raji
Step 15 | Wash Unbound Probe A (Raji, 3x)            -- same as Step 4 for Raji
Step 16 | Probe B Staining (Raji)                    -- same as Step 5 for Raji
Step 17 | Wash Unbound Probe B (Raji, 3x)            -- same as Step 6 for Raji
Step 18 | Free Oligo Addition (Raji)                 -- same as Step 7 for Raji
Step 19 | Proximity Ligation Reaction (Raji)         -- same as Step 8 for Raji
Step 20 | Ligation Stop and Wash (Raji, 3x)          -- same as Step 9 for Raji
Step 21 | Single-Cell Encapsulation and Library Preparation (Raji) -- same as Step 10 for Raji
Step 22 | Raji Library QC and Branching Gate
  Branch Pass : rajiLibSignal > 0  ->  dispose(rajiSeqReady)  ->  terminal (BB7)
  Branch Fail : rajiLibSignal <= 0 ->  drain(rajiSeqReady)    ->  terminal (BB7)

Terminal     : dispose(rajiLibSignal)
               Experiment ends. Sequencing data submitted to computational pipeline.
               Code: https://github.com/tay-lab/Prox-seq_computation
               Data: GEO GSE196130


SIMULATION MODEL
----------------
Physical model of PLA product formation per single cell:
  - Non-interacting Probe A points generated as random points on sphere (radius R = 5 um)
  - Non-interacting Probe B points generated as random points on sphere
  - Protein complex points generated as random points; added to both Probe A and Probe B sets
  - Pairwise Euclidean distances computed between all Probe A and Probe B points
  - Pairs within ligation distance threshold (50 nm) are ligated; each probe ligated at most once
  - Non-ligated points returned as non-proximal probe count (measured by free oligo modification)

Variance model:
  - Simulated counts without variance follow Poisson distribution
  - Real data shows overdispersion; negative binomial (NB) variance added: n_NB = 1.5
  - NB formulation: A_i^(t) ~ NegativeBinomial(n_NB, p_NB); p_NB = (1 + A_i/n_NB)^-1
  - NB variance captures positive correlation between PLA product count and non-proximal
    probe count in real data (S1b-S1g Fig)

Calibration:
  - Posterior predictive checks (PPCs): Mann-Whitney U statistic and coefficient of variation
    compared between replicated simulated data and real Jurkat/Raji data (S3a, S3b Fig)
  - n_NB = 1.5 chosen as mean of best-fit n_NB values across all PLA products (S3c Fig)
  - Simulation faithfully captures key aspects of real Prox-seq data


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file  : xia_proxseq_computational_prediction.bs
Compiler        : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output       : 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 sequential if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
DAG file        : xia_proxseq_computational_prediction_main_dag.dot
Duration units  : All durations in s (seconds) or m (minutes); h token not supported by compiler
Duration conversions:
  5m   ->  300.0 SECOND
  10m  ->  600.0 SECOND
  30m  -> 1800.0 SECOND
  2m   ->  120.0 SECOND
  30s  ->   30.0 SECOND
Modules declared  : proxSeqDetection, viabilityDetection, plaDetection, seqLibraryQC
Active QC module  : seqLibraryQC (used in detect statements for both Jurkat and Raji gates)
Manifests (15)    : JurkatCells, RajiCells, PBS, ProxSeqProbeA, ProxSeqProbeB,
                    FreeOligoA, FreeOligoB, LigationBuffer, Ligase, BlockingBuffer,
                    WashBuffer, DNALibraryBuffer, SequencingReagent,
                    IsotypeControlAntibody, StopSolution
Compiler note     : lilott8/BioScript maps both dispose and drain to a unified disposal
                    IR operation (both appear as dispose in IR output). This is expected
                    compiler behaviour and does not affect correctness.
                    Observed in bsbbif_3_f (Jurkat fail path) and bsbbif_6_f (Raji fail path).
CFG arms          : Two sequential arms. ARM 1 (Jurkat) runs in BB1 main. ARM 2 (Raji) runs
                    in BB4 jurkatLibJoin after Jurkat QC gate converges. Both arms share the
                    same 11-step structure: blocking -> Probe A -> wash x3 -> Probe B ->
                    wash x3 -> free oligo addition -> ligation -> stop+wash x3 ->
                    library prep -> QC detect -> branch gate.

protocol.title: Computational Prediction of Protein Interactions in Single Cells by Proximity Sequencing
protocol.platform: Proximity Sequencing (Prox-seq) combined with single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq)
cell_lines: Jurkat (human T cell leukemia; T cell marker panel)
Raji (human Burkitt lymphoma B cell line; B cell marker panel)
protocol.objective: Simultaneous quantification of mRNA, surface protein expression, and protein complexes (dimers) at the single-cell level using dual-antibody proximity ligation assay (PLA) with DNA-conjugated probes, sequenced alongside scRNA-seq cDNA libraries; computational benchmarking of iterative, linear regression (LR), and ensemble methods for proximity noise removal and protein complex prediction

platform_details.assay_type: Proximity Ligation Assay (PLA) with sequencing readout
platform_details.probe_design: Each target protein is stained with two DNA-conjugated antibodies: Probe A and Probe B. Ligation of Probe A oligo to Probe B oligo occurs only when the two probes are within 50-70 nm of each other (i.e., when their target proteins are co-localised or in complex).
platform_details.pla_product: Ligated A+B oligo barcode pair; counted by unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) after sequencing
platform_details.free_oligo_modification: An experimentally modified Prox-seq procedure adds FreeOligoA and FreeOligoB (non-antibody-conjugated oligos) to measure non-proximal (unligated) probe counts. These counts are used as explanatory variables in the LR and ensemble methods for proximity noise estimation.
platform_details.sequencing_platform: Combined scRNA-seq + PLA product library (sequenced together)
platform_details.umi_counting: PLA product UMI counts per cell per protein pair extracted computationally (Python3/Anaconda3 v4.10.3)

cells.jurkat: Jurkat T cells; cultured under standard conditions; resuspended in PBS for staining
cells.raji: Raji B cells; cultured under standard conditions; resuspended in PBS for staining

buffers.PBS: Phosphate-buffered saline; used for cell suspension and wash steps
buffers.blocking_buffer: Blocking buffer to reduce nonspecific antibody binding prior to probe staining; incubated 10 min at 4 C
buffers.wash_buffer: PBS-based wash buffer; used 3x after each probe staining step to remove unbound probes
buffers.ligation_buffer: Ligation buffer compatible with T4 DNA ligase proximity ligation reaction
buffers.stop_solution: Stop solution to quench T4 DNA ligase activity after ligation

probes.probe_A: Prox-seq Probe A: DNA-conjugated antibody panel targeting CD3, CD28, PD1, CD147, ICAM1, PDL1, HLADR, B7 (same panel used for Jurkat and Raji arms; ref Vistain et al. Nat Methods 2022)
probes.probe_B: Prox-seq Probe B: DNA-conjugated antibody panel targeting same proteins as Probe A; B oligo is the ligation partner for A oligo
probes.free_oligo_A: FreeOligoA: non-antibody-conjugated oligo dispensed alongside probe panel; generates PLA product Protein_X:free_oligo_B to measure non-proximal Probe A counts
probes.free_oligo_B: FreeOligob: non-antibody-conjugated oligo dispensed alongside probe panel; generates PLA product free_oligo_A:Protein_Y to measure non-proximal Probe B counts
probes.isotype_control: Isotype control antibody with oligonucleotide conjugation; included in both Probe A and Probe B panels; used to estimate nonspecific antibody binding probability directly from observed PLA data (paper Section 2.2, S4 Fig)

reagents.ligation_enzyme: T4 DNA Ligase; catalyses ligation of Probe A and Probe B oligos when within 50-70 nm proximity

library_reagents.dna_library_buffer: DNA library preparation buffer; used to generate combined cDNA (gene expression) and PLA product sequencing library
library_reagents.sequencing_reagent: Sequencing reagent for combined scRNA-seq + Prox-seq library

probe_panel.control: Isotype control antibody (oligo-conjugated) in both Probe A and Probe B panels

proximity_noise_model.definition: Random ligation of Probe A and Probe B oligos from non-interacting protein molecules that are sufficiently close by random chance; main background source in Prox-seq

variables.R: Cell radius (5 um = 5000 units in simulation)
variables.A_i: Non-proximal Probe A count for protein i
variables.B_j: Non-proximal Probe B count for protein j

proximity_noise_model.distribution: Binomial; X_ij ~ Binomial(n = A_i * B_j, p = d_ligation^2 / 4R^2)
proximity_noise_model.overdispersion: Negative binomial (NB) variance added in simulation (n_NB = 1.5) to capture real data overdispersion
proximity_noise_model.note: Proximity noise scales quadratically with protein abundance and ligation distance (Fig 2e)

iterative_method.mechanism: Iteratively solve quadratic equations for all protein dimers; protein complex count = observed PLA count minus expected random PLA count
iterative_method.strengths: Performs well in high signal-to-noise (homodimer or heterodimer only) scenarios
iterative_method.limitations: Unstable with multiple protein dimers or overabundant proteins; sensitive to initialisation
iterative_method.applicable_situations: Simpler biological scenarios with only homodimers or only heterodimers

lr_method.mechanism: Weighted least squares regression of observed PLA count onto product of non-proximal Probe A and Probe B counts; protein complex count = observed PLA count minus estimated proximity noise (beta_1 * A_i_prime * B_j_prime); requires free oligo modification
lr_method.strengths: Performs well in low signal-to-noise and complex multi-dimer scenarios
lr_method.limitations: Unstable when non-proximal probe counts are near zero; not optimal for high signal-to-noise homodimer/heterodimer-only scenarios
lr_method.applicable_situations: Low signal-to-noise and scenarios with multiple protein dimers or overabundant proteins

ensemble_method.mechanism: Apply LR method first; use LR output as initialisation for iterative method; bridges both approaches
ensemble_method.strengths: Robust and consistent across all biological scenarios; lowest false positive rate; best overall prediction score
ensemble_method.limitations: Requires free oligo modification experimental procedure
ensemble_method.applicable_situations: Robust choice when true biological conditions are uncertain; recommended default

fishers_exact_test.mechanism: One-sided Fisher's exact test on 2x2 contingency table of PLA counts; Benjamini-Hochberg correction; identifies protein complexes occurring at higher frequency than random
fishers_exact_test.use: Statistical validation of complex enrichment; complementary to quantification methods

prediction_score.formula: Score = w1 * SumPearson - w2 * SumMeanDeviation - w3 * SumFPrate
prediction_score.result: Ensemble method has highest average prediction score and lowest variance across all 800 randomised simulation scenarios (S10d Fig, S2 Table)

steps.name: Cell suspension preparation
steps.notes: Resuspend Jurkat T cells in PBS at appropriate concentration for single-cell Prox-seq staining

steps.name: Nonspecific binding block
steps.notes: 10 min blocking at 4 C; reduces nonspecific antibody binding background. Paper Section 2.2: nonspecific binding constitutes <1% of both-specific PLA counts for extracellular proteins (e.g. CD147:CD147 in Jurkat cells, S4 Fig)

steps.name: Probe A staining with isotype control
steps.notes: 30 min incubation at 4 C. Probe A panel targets CD3, CD28, PD1, CD147, ICAM1, PDL1, HLADR, B7. Isotype control antibody (oligo-conjugated) included in Probe A panel to directly define nonspecific binding distribution

steps.name: Wash unbound Probe A (3x)
steps.notes: 3x PBS wash, 2 min each. Removes excess unbound Probe A antibodies. Unligated probes do not contribute to PLA signal (library prep and alignment require barcodes from both A and B probes)

steps.name: Probe B staining
steps.notes: 30 min incubation at 4 C. Probe B panel targets same proteins as Probe A. After this step, cells carry both Probe A and Probe B antibodies on surface proteins

steps.name: Wash unbound Probe B (3x)
steps.notes: 3x PBS wash, 2 min each

steps.name: Free oligo addition (non-proximal probe measurement)
steps.notes: 10 min incubation at 4 C. FreeOligoA and FreeOligoB added to measure non-proximal (unligated) probe counts. Free oligos are not conjugated to antibodies; they produce PLA products Protein_X:free_oligo_B (non-proximal Probe A) and free_oligo_A:Protein_Y (non-proximal Probe B). Required for LR and ensemble methods (Methods: LR method equation Y_ij = X_ij - beta_1 * A_i_prime * B_j_prime). Ref [4] Vistain et al. Nat Methods 2022.

steps.name: Proximity ligation reaction
steps.notes: 30 min at 25 C. T4 DNA Ligase catalyses ligation of Probe A oligo to Probe B oligo only when within 50-70 nm. Random co-localisation generates proximity noise: E(X_ij) = (d_ligation^2 / 4R^2) * A_i * B_j. BioScript mix abstraction represents the proximity ligation event.

steps.name: Ligation stop and wash (3x)
steps.notes: Add stop solution to quench ligase; 3x PBS wash to remove ligation reagents before library preparation

steps.name: Single-cell encapsulation and library preparation
steps.notes: Cells encapsulated in individual droplets and lysed. mRNA captured by poly-dT oligonucleotides; PLA products captured by barcoded sequences. Combined cDNA and PLA product library prepared at 37 C for 30 min. Sequencing reagent added for final library preparation (10 min mix).

steps.name: Jurkat library QC detection
steps.notes: QC check on Jurkat Prox-seq library: fragment size, complexity, UMI diversity (abstracted from fluorometric/electrophoretic QC e.g. Bioanalyzer, Qubit)

steps.name: Cell suspension preparation
steps.notes: Resuspend Raji B cells in PBS. Raji cells express ICAM1 (known homodimer), HLADR, PDL1, B7. Raji cells do not express CD3 or PD1; their PLA products for those targets are near zero, validating probe panel specificity

steps.name: Nonspecific binding block
steps.notes: Same blocking procedure as Jurkat arm

steps.name: Probe A staining with isotype control
steps.notes: Same panel as Jurkat arm. ICAM1:ICAM1 homodimer signal in Raji cells exceeds expected random ligation background (Fig 5d-f)

steps.name: Wash unbound Probe A (3x)
steps.notes: 3x PBS wash, 2 min each

steps.name: Probe B staining
steps.notes: Same procedure as Jurkat arm

steps.name: Wash unbound Probe B (3x)
steps.notes: 3x PBS wash, 2 min each

steps.name: Free oligo addition (non-proximal probe measurement)
steps.notes: Same free oligo modification as Jurkat arm. Non-proximal probe counts for Raji cells used to calibrate proximity noise in LR and ensemble methods for Raji-specific protein complex detection

steps.name: Proximity ligation reaction
steps.notes: 30 min at 25 C. Same conditions as Jurkat arm. ICAM1:ICAM1 homodimer signal in Raji cells exceeds E(X_ij) proximity noise baseline

steps.name: Ligation stop and wash (3x)
steps.notes: Add stop solution; 3x PBS wash

steps.name: Single-cell encapsulation and library preparation
steps.notes: Same procedure as Jurkat arm. After sequencing, UMI counts per PLA product per single Raji cell are primary data for computational analysis (iterative / LR / ensemble methods)

steps.name: Raji library QC detection
steps.notes: Same QC procedure as Jurkat arm

simulation_model.description: Physical model of PLA product formation per single cell; simulates proximity noise and protein complex signal independently
simulation_model.variance_model: Negative binomial (NB); n_NB = 1.5; p_NB = (1 + A_i / n_NB)^-1
simulation_model.calibration: Calibrated against Jurkat (T cell) and Raji (B cell) experimental data; NB variance chosen from mean n_NB fitted to real PLA products (S3c Fig)
simulation_model.posterior_predictive_checks: Mann-Whitney U statistic and coefficient of variation comparison between simulated and real data (S3a, S3b Fig)

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.content: Jurkat cell prep, blocking, Probe A staining, wash x3, Probe B staining, wash x3, free oligo addition, ligation, stop+wash x3, library prep, library QC detect

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_4_j
basic_blocks.content: dispose(jurkatLibSignal); Raji cell prep, blocking, Probe A staining, wash x3, Probe B staining, wash x3, free oligo addition, ligation, stop+wash x3, library prep, library QC detect

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_7_j
basic_blocks.content: dispose(rajiLibSignal); experiment ends; data to computational pipeline

bioscript_compiler_notes.ir_output: 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 sequential if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
bioscript_compiler_notes.duration_units: All durations in s (seconds) or m (minutes); BioScript does not support h token
bioscript_compiler_notes.compiler_behaviour_note: lilott8/BioScript compiler maps both dispose and drain to a unified disposal IR operation (dispose in IR for both pass and fail branches). This does not affect compilation correctness. Observed in bsbbif_3_f (Jurkat fail path) and bsbbif_6_f (Raji fail path) of the IR output.
bioscript_compiler_notes.arms: Two sequential arms encoded in main BB (Jurkat ARM 1) and jurkatLibJoin BB4 (Raji ARM 2). Each arm is structurally identical: blocking -> Probe A stain -> wash x3 -> Probe B stain -> wash x3 -> free oligo addition -> ligation -> stop+wash x3 -> library prep -> QC detect.

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Droplet-based Single-cell Joint Profiling of Histone Modification and Transcriptome (Droplet Paired-Tag)
Source Link  : https://www.protocols.io/view/droplet-based-single-cell-joint-profiling-of-histo-eq2ly6kergx9/v1
Paper DOI    : https://dx.doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.pex-2310/v1
Journal      : Research Square (Method Article preprint), 2023
Authors      : Yang Xie, Chenxu Zhu, Zhaoning Wang, Melodi Tastemel, Lei Chang, Yang Eric Li, Bing Ren
Affiliation  : Department of Cellular and Molecular Medicine, University of California San Diego;
               Ludwig Institute for Cancer Research, La Jolla; Center for Epigenomics, UCSD
Platform     : 10x Chromium Next GEM Single Cell Multiome (ATAC + Gene Expression) with pA-Tn5 tagmentation


OVERVIEW
--------
Droplet Paired-Tag is a rapid multiomic technique for joint single-cell profiling of histone
modifications and gene expression simultaneously at scale. The method adapts the original
combinatorial indexing-based Paired-Tag protocol by incorporating nuclei barcoding on the
commercially available 10x Chromium Single Cell Multiome platform and simplifying the library
preparation process.

Compared to conventional Paired-Tag, Droplet Paired-Tag delivers a higher signal-to-noise ratio
for histone modification data and generates joint modality data with the same efficiency as
single-modality methods such as scRNA-seq and scCUT&Tag. The protocol has been validated on
both cultured mammalian cells (mouse embryonic stem cells, mESC) and primary mouse brain tissue,
where it accurately reconstructs cell type-specific active (H3K27ac) and repressive (H3K27me3)
gene regulatory networks.

The core innovation is a bridged Protein A-Tn5 (pA-Tn5) transposome that carries 10x Genomics-
compatible adapter sequences. Nuclei are first incubated overnight with an anti-histone antibody
bound to pA-Tn5. Tagmentation is then activated by Mg2+, inserting sequencing adapters at histone-
marked genomic loci. Tagmented nuclei are loaded onto the Chromium chip, where each nucleus is
co-encapsulated with a gel bead (GEM) barcoding both the CUT&Tag DNA fragments and the nuclear
mRNA in the same droplet, enabling paired epigenomic and transcriptomic readout per cell.

The three-day protocol produces two independently sequenced libraries per sample:
  - DNA library: histone modification CUT&Tag (200-1000 bp; nucleosome ladder pattern)
  - RNA library: single-nucleus gene expression cDNA (400-500 bp peak, narrow)


DEVICE / PLATFORM
-----------------
Microfluidics : 10x Chromium Next GEM platform (ChromiumX controller)
Chip          : Chromium Next GEM Chip J Single Cell Kit (Cat#1000234)
Encapsulation : Gel-bead-in-emulsion (GEM) droplet generation; each GEM contains one nucleus
                + one gel bead; barcoded RT primer on bead captures both cDNA and tagmented DNA
Sequencing    : Illumina NextSeq 2000
  DNA library : 200-cycle kit (#20046812); cycle config 100+8+24+100
                (Read1 + Index1 + Index2 [cellular barcodes] + Read2)
  RNA library : 100-cycle kit (#20046811); cycle config 28+10+10+72
                (Read1 [cellular barcodes] + Index1 + Index2 + Read2)
Demultiplexing: cellranger-arc mkfastq (10X Genomics); downstream analysis with in-house pipeline


REAGENTS
--------
Buffers (freshly prepared):
  ATAC-RSB Buffer   : 300 uL 1M Tris-HCl pH 7.4 + 60 uL 5M NaCl + 90 uL 1M MgCl2 + 29.55 mL H2O
  OMNI Lysis Buffer : ATAC-RSB 693.75 uL + Digitonin 2% 3.75 uL + IGEPAL-CA630 10% 7.5 uL +
                      Tween-20 10% 7.5 uL + SUPERaseIN 15 uL + RNaseOUT 7.5 uL + 50X PI 15 uL
                      (total 750 uL; freshly prepared on ice)
  MED Buffer 1      : HEPES 1M 20 uL + NaCl 5M 54.2 uL + Spermidine 1M 0.5 uL + 50X PI 20 uL +
                      SUPERaseIN 50 uL + RNaseOUT 25 uL + IGEPAL-CA630 10% 1 uL +
                      Digitonin 2% 5 uL + EDTA 500mM 4 uL + 10% BSA 200 uL + H2O 620.3 uL
                      (total 1 mL; RNase inhibitor doubled for mouse embryos; 50% sufficient for
                      cultured cells and brain tissue)
  MED Buffer 2      : Same as MED1 without EDTA (699.3 uL H2O); Mg2+ must remain free for Tn5
  2X Stop Solution  : 1M Tris-HCl 10 uL + 500mM EDTA 40 uL + 10% BSA 200 uL + H2O 750 uL
  PBS + RI Wash     : 1X PBS 942.5 uL + 50X PI 20 uL + SUPERaseIN 25 uL + RNaseOUT 12.5 uL
  1X Nuclei Buffer  : 20X Nuclei Buffer (PN-2000207) 5 uL + DTT 100mM 1 uL +
                      SUPERaseIN 5 uL + RNaseOUT 2.5 uL + H2O 86.5 uL

Antibody          : Rabbit polyclonal anti-histone modification (1 ug per reaction)
                    e.g. anti-H3K27ac or anti-H3K27me3
Protein A-Tn5     : Assembled bridged pA-Tn5 transposome (0.4 mg/mL; 1 uL per reaction)
                    Assembled from pMENTs-Bridge + AdapterA and AdapterB oligos (IDT)
                    + unloaded Protein A-Tn5 (MacroLab p2409, 0.5 mg/mL)

10X Genomics reagents:
  Chromium Next GEM Single Cell Multiome ATAC + GEX Reagent Bundle (Cat#1000283)
  Barcoding Reagent Mix (PN-2000267); Template Switch Oligo (PN-3000228)
  Reducing Agent B (PN-2000087); Barcoding Enzyme Mix (PN-2000266)
  Quenching Agent (PN-2000269); ATAC Buffer B (PN-2000193)
  20X Nuclei Buffer (PN-2000207); Single Index Kit N Set A (Cat#1000212)
  Dual Index Kit TT Set A (Cat#1000215)

Cleanup reagents  : SPRI beads (Beckman Coulter Cat#B23319); Dynabeads (per CG000338)


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

DAY 1

Step 1 | OMNI Nuclei Lysis Buffer Preparation
  Combine all components (see Reagents above) in order on ice; mix gently.
  Use immediately; do not pre-make. Keep on ice throughout.

Step 2 | Antibody + pA-Tn5 Conjugation
  Mix  : 1 ug rabbit polyclonal anti-histone antibody + 1 uL assembled pA-Tn5 (0.4 mg/mL)
         in 50 uL MED1 buffer per PCR tube.
  Incubation : Rotate 60 min at room temperature (25 C).
  IR duration: 3600.0 SECOND
  Storage : Conjugate can be stored at -20 C if not used immediately.

Step 3 | Nuclei Preparation (Cultured Cells)
  Input    : 250,000 - 1,000,000 cells
  a) Disassociate cells per culture protocol. Spin at 300 RCF / 5 min.
     Wash once with PBS; spin at 300 RCF / 5 min (4 C). [IR: 300.0 SECOND @ 4 C]
  b) Resuspend in 750 uL OMNI buffer (<5 million cells/mL); sit on ice 5 min.
     [IR: mix @ 300.0 SECOND]
  c) Spin at 1,000 RCF / 10 min at 4 C. [IR: 600.0 SECOND @ 4 C]
  d) Resuspend nuclei in 100 uL MED1 buffer. Count using cell counter.

Step 4 | Epitope Targeting (Overnight)
  Input    : 250,000 - 500,000 nuclei
  a) Aliquot nuclei into Maximum Recovery tubes. Spin at 1,000 RCF / 10 min at 4 C.
     [IR: 600.0 SECOND @ 4 C]
  b) Resuspend in 25 uL MED1. Add conjugated antibody-pA-Tn5 (in MED1).
  c) Incubate overnight at 4 C with rotation (~12 h).
     [IR: 43200.0 SECOND @ 4 C; BioScript: 720m]


DAY 2

Step 5 | MED Buffer 2 Preparation (prepare 3 fresh working volumes)
  Prepare three independent 1 mL batches of MED2 (composition in Reagents section above).
  Instance 1 (med2BufferWash1): first MED2 wash
  Instance 2 (med2BufferWash2): second MED2 wash
  Instance 3 (med2BufferTag)  : tagmentation resuspension
  Note: Three fresh builds required; BioScript cannot re-dispense from computed variables.

Step 6 | PBS + RI Wash Buffer and 1X Nuclei Buffer Preparation
  Prepare PBS + RNase Inhibitor wash buffer and 1X Nuclei Buffer (see Reagents above).
  Use within 1 h; do not pre-make the day before.

Step 7 | Nuclei Washing (x2) and Tn5 Tagmentation
  a) Spin nuclei at 300 RCF / 10 min at 4 C. Wash with 50 uL MED2. [IR: 600.0 SECOND @ 4 C]
  b) Repeat wash: add 50 uL MED2; spin 300 RCF / 10 min at 4 C. [IR: 600.0 SECOND @ 4 C]
  c) Resuspend in 50 uL MED2. Add 2 uL MgCl2 (250 mM) to activate Tn5.
  d) Rotate in ThermoMixer at 550 rpm, 37 C, 60 min. [IR: 3600.0 SECOND @ 37 C]
     Note: Thaw 10X Multiome gel beads and barcoding reagents at room temperature during this step.

Step 8 | Stop Tagmentation and Post-Tagmentation Wash
  a) Add 50 uL 2X Stop Solution; mix well.
  b) Spin at 500 RCF / 6 min at 4 C. [IR: 360.0 SECOND @ 4 C]
  c) Wash with PBS + RI buffer.
  d) Spin at 500 RCF / 6 min at 4 C. [IR: 360.0 SECOND @ 4 C]

Step 9 | Nuclei Resuspension and Chromium Chip Loading Preparation
  a) Resuspend in 20 uL 1X Nuclei Buffer. Count nuclei using cell counter.
  b) Aliquot 10,000-16,000 nuclei in 8 uL into PCR tube.
  c) Add 7 uL ATAC Buffer B (PN-2000193). Total volume: 15 uL.
  d) Proceed immediately to droplet generation.

Step 10 | RT Master Mix Preparation and GEM Droplet Generation
  Prepare RT master mix:
    Barcoding Reagent Mix (PN-2000267) : 49.5 uL
    Template Switch Oligo (PN-3000228) :  1.1 uL
    Reducing Agent B (PN-2000087)      :  1.9 uL
    Barcoding Enzyme Mix (PN-2000266)  :  7.5 uL
    Total                              : 60.0 uL
  Add 60 uL master mix to 15 uL nuclei mixture. Load onto Chip J.
  Proceed to droplet generation on ChromiumX per 10X Multiome user guide CG000338.
  Aspirate 100 uL emulsion into new PCR tube after generation.
  Note: `mix` in BioScript abstracts the microfluidic GEM encapsulation event.

Step 11 | Reverse Transcription and Cell Barcoding in Droplets
  Incubate emulsion in Bio-Rad T100 thermal cycler (lid at 50 C):
    Stage 1 : 37 C for 45 min  -- reverse transcription (cDNA synthesis)
              [IR: 2700.0 SECOND @ 37 C]
    Stage 2 : 25 C for 30 min  -- template switching and cell barcoding
              [IR: 1800.0 SECOND @ 25 C]
    Hold    : 4 C
  Note: Both cell barcoding and cDNA synthesis complete during this incubation.

Step 12 | Quench and Products Cleanup
  a) Add 5 uL Quenching Agent (PN-2000269). Pipette mix gently.
  b) Proceed to Dynabeads + SPRI bead cleanup per 10X Multiome user guide CG000338.
     Dynabeads cleanup: 5 min mix [IR: 300.0 SECOND]
     SPRI bead cleanup: 5 min mix [IR: 300.0 SECOND]


DAY 3

Step 13 | Pre-amplification
  Protocol : Per 10X Multiome user guide CG000338 with one modification:
             Elute in 80 uL after SPRI cleanup (instead of standard 160 uL).
  Rationale: Concentrates tagmented fragments; scCUT&Tag library complexity is lower than ATAC;
             higher input increases DNA library complexity.
  Extension: 72 C / 5 min [IR: 300.0 SECOND @ 72 C]
  PCR cycles:
    H3K27ac  : 13 cycles (recommended)
    H3K27me3 : 12 cycles (recommended)
    Adjust based on sample type and estimated recovered nuclei.
  Storage  : Pre-amplified product stable at -20 C for up to 6 months.

Step 14 | DNA and RNA Library Preparation
  Split pre-amplified product:
    DNA library : use 40 uL purified product
    RNA library : use 17.5 uL purified product + 17.5 uL H2O
                  (maintains standard 10X Multiome input volume)
  Both library preps per 10X Multiome user guide CG000338.
  Final SPRI cleanup: 5 min [IR: 300.0 SECOND]

Step 15 | Library QC (Fragment Size Check)
  Instrument : Fragment Analyzer or Agilent TapeStation
  Expected   :
    DNA library (histone CUT&Tag) : 200-1,000 bp; nucleosome ladder pattern
    RNA library (cDNA)            : 400-500 bp peak; narrow distribution
  QC gate    :
    PASS (libraryQCSignal > 0)  -> proceed to sequencing [BB: bsbbif_2_t; dispose]
    FAIL (libraryQCSignal <= 0) -> re-evaluate PCR cycles or nuclei input [BB: bsbbif_3_f; drain]
  Detection duration: 30 s [IR: 30.0 SECOND]

Step 16 | Sequencing
  DNA library : Illumina NextSeq 2000; 200-cycle kit (#20046812)
                Cycle config: 100 (R1) + 8 (I1) + 24 (I2, cellular barcodes) + 100 (R2)
  RNA library : Illumina NextSeq 2000; 100-cycle kit (#20046811)
                Cycle config: 28 (R1, cellular barcodes) + 10 (I1) + 10 (I2) + 72 (R2)
  Demux       : cellranger-arc mkfastq; analysis with in-house pipeline


TROUBLESHOOTING
---------------
Low nuclei yield before chip loading:
  - Increase input cells to >250,000.
  - Check for nuclei clumping during CUT&Tag; fragile nuclei may lyse and aggregate in high-salt buffer.
  - If clumping observed: crosslink nuclei with 0.1% formaldehyde 5 min at room temperature before lysis.
  - Typical yield: 30-60% of input nuclei recovered before loading.

Low library complexity (DNA):
  - scCUT&Tag library complexity is overall lower than snATAC-seq.
  - Increase indexing PCR cycles (13 for H3K27ac, 12 for H3K27me3 as baseline).
  - Confirm elution volume at pre-amplification step is 80 uL (not 160 uL).

Unexpected fragment size distribution:
  - Verify Tn5 activation: ensure MgCl2 was added and tagmentation ran at 37 C / 60 min.
  - Check stop solution was added immediately after tagmentation.
  - Verify antibody specificity and pA-Tn5 assembly quality.


TIME ESTIMATION
---------------
Day 1:
  Antibody + pA-Tn5 conjugation (Step 2)       :  1.0 - 1.5 h
  Nuclei preparation (Step 3)                   :  1.0 - 1.5 h
  Epitope targeting (Step 4)                    :  overnight (~12 h)

Day 2:
  Buffer preparation (Steps 5-6)                :  0.5 h
  Nuclei washing and tagmentation (Step 7)      :  2.0 - 2.5 h
  Stop, wash, and nuclei resuspension (Steps 8-9):  0.5 h
  Droplet generation (Step 10)                  :  0.5 h
  Reverse transcription and barcoding (Step 11) :  2.0 h
  Products cleanup (Step 12)                    :  1.0 h

Day 3:
  Library pre-amplification (Step 13)           :  1.0 - 2.0 h
  DNA and RNA library preparation (Step 14)     :  3.0 - 4.0 h
  Library QC (Step 15)                          :  0.5 h


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file  : xie_droplet_paired_tag.bs
Compiler        : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output       : xie_droplet_paired_tag.ir
DAG output      : xie_droplet_paired_tag_main_dag.dot
Basic blocks    : 4 (main, bsbbif_2_t, bsbbif_3_f, bsbbif_4_j)
CFG edges       : 4 (main->2t, main->3f, 2t->4j, 3f->4j)
Modules         : libraryQCDetection
Manifests       : 29 (all dispense sources declared; no computed variable used as dispense source)

Duration unit convention:
  BioScript supports `s` and `m` tokens only (no `h`).
  All hour and overnight values converted to minutes.
  Key conversions (BioScript -> IR):
    60 min conjugation          ->  60m  -> 3600.0 SECOND
    overnight epitope incubation -> 720m -> 43200.0 SECOND
    60 min tagmentation         ->  60m  -> 3600.0 SECOND
    45 min RT stage 1           ->  45m  -> 2700.0 SECOND
    30 min barcoding stage 2    ->  30m  -> 1800.0 SECOND

Buffer rebuild note:
  BioScript `dispense` is restricted to declared manifests and cannot draw from computed mix
  variables. Buffers needed at multiple protocol sites (MED1 x3 instances for conjugation,
  nuclei resuspension, and epitope prep; MED2 x3 instances for two washes and tagmentation
  resuspend) are each rebuilt independently from their component manifests using distinct
  variable name prefixes (m1a_, m1b_, m1c_ for MED1; m2a_, m2b_, m2c_ for MED2).

drain normalisation:
  `drain` in the .bs fail branch normalises to `dispose` in the IR output.
  This is standard lilott8/BioScript compiler behaviour; consistent with samlali and moazami
  reference protocol IR outputs.

protocol.title: Droplet-based Single-cell Joint Profiling of Histone Modification and Transcriptome (Droplet Paired-Tag)
protocol.platform: 10x Chromium Next GEM Single Cell Multiome (ATAC + Gene Expression) with pA-Tn5 tagmentation
protocol.objective: Simultaneous single-cell profiling of histone modifications (CUT&Tag) and gene expression (RNA-seq) using droplet microfluidics; joint multiomic readout at scale with higher signal-to-noise than combinatorial indexing Paired-Tag

sequencing_platform.dna_cycle_config: 100+8+24+100 (Read1 + Index1 + Index2 + Read2); Index2 carries cellular barcodes
sequencing_platform.rna_cycle_config: 28+10+10+72 (Read1 + Index1 + Index2 + Read2); Read1 carries cellular barcodes
sequencing_platform.demultiplexing: cellranger-arc mkfastq (10X Genomics); downstream analysis with in-house pipeline

ATAC_RSB_Buffer.composition: 300 uL 1M Tris-HCl pH 7.4 + 60 uL 5M NaCl + 90 uL 1M MgCl2 + 29.55 mL H2O
ATAC_RSB_Buffer.use: Base diluent for OMNI lysis buffer, MED1, MED2, and 1X Nuclei Buffer

OMNI_Lysis_Buffer.use: Nuclei lysis; freshly prepared on ice before use

MED_Buffer_1.note: RNase inhibitor concentration doubled vs standard; suitable for mouse embryos. For cultured cells or brain tissue, 50% concentration has no impact on RNA quality.
MED_Buffer_1.use: Antibody-pA-Tn5 conjugation, nuclei resuspension, overnight epitope targeting

MED_Buffer_2.note: Identical to MED1 but without EDTA; Mg2+ must be free for Tn5 tagmentation activity
MED_Buffer_2.use: Nuclei wash (x2) and tagmentation resuspension on Day 2

Nuclei_Buffer_1X.use: Final nuclei resuspension before 10x Chromium chip loading

Stop_Solution_2X.composition: 10 uL 1M Tris-HCl + 40 uL 500mM EDTA + 200 uL 10% BSA + 750 uL H2O
Stop_Solution_2X.use: Terminate Tn5 tagmentation activity (added 1:1 to tagmentation reaction)

protein_a_tn5.assembly_note: pMENTs-Bridge oligo annealed to AdapterA and AdapterB separately at 95C then cooled at 0.1C/s; each annealed adapter mixed with unloaded pA-Tn5 0.5 mg/mL; incubated 30 min RT + 10 min ice; AdapterA and AdapterB assemblies pooled 1:1; stored at -20C

10x_genomics_kit.bundle: Chromium Next GEM Single Cell Multiome ATAC + Gene Expression Reagent Bundle (Cat#1000283)
10x_genomics_kit.chip: Chromium Next GEM Chip J Single Cell Kit, 48 rxns (Cat#1000234)
10x_genomics_kit.index_dna: Single Index Kit N Set A, 96 rxn (Cat#1000212)
10x_genomics_kit.index_dual: Dual Index Kit TT Set A 96 rxns (Cat#1000215)

steps.name: OMNI Nuclei Lysis Buffer preparation
steps.notes: Freshly prepared on ice immediately before nuclei lysis. Three detergents (digitonin, IGEPAL, Tween-20) act synergistically to permeabilise plasma membrane while preserving nuclear integrity.

steps.name: MED Buffer 1 preparation and antibody-pA-Tn5 conjugation
steps.notes: 1 ug antibody + 1 uL pA-Tn5 (0.4 mg/mL) in 50 uL MED1. Rotate 60 min at room temperature (25 C). Product stored at -20 C if not used immediately.

steps.name: Nuclei preparation from cultured cells
steps.operation: mix + heat (centrifugation modelled as heat at 4C)

sub_steps.name: OMNI lysis on ice
sub_steps.notes: Resuspend in 750 uL OMNI buffer (<5 million cells/mL); sit on ice 5 min

steps.notes: Count nuclei using cell counter after MED1 resuspension.

steps.name: Epitope targeting (overnight antibody-pA-Tn5 incubation)
steps.notes: Overnight at 4 C with rotation (~12 h = 720 min = 43200 s in IR). Conjugated antibody-pA-Tn5 binds histone modification epitopes on nuclei.

steps.name: MED Buffer 2 preparation (x3 instances)
steps.notes: Three fresh MED2 instances built sequentially: wash1, wash2, tagmentation resuspend. EDTA excluded vs MED1 to permit Mg2+-dependent Tn5 activity.

steps.name: PBS + RNase Inhibitor wash buffer and 1X Nuclei Buffer preparation
steps.notes: Both buffers freshly prepared from manifests. pbsRIBuffer used for post-tagmentation wash; nucleiBuffer1X for final resuspension before Chromium loading.

sub_steps.name: MgCl2 activation and tagmentation
sub_steps.notes: 10X Genomics Multiome gel beads thawed at room temperature during this incubation

steps.name: Nuclei resuspension and Chromium chip loading preparation
steps.notes: Count nuclei using cell counter after 1X Nuclei Buffer resuspension. ATAC Buffer B added immediately before loading onto Chip J.

steps.name: RT master mix preparation and GEM droplet generation
steps.notes: Chip assembly and reagent addition per 10X Multiome user guide CG000338. `mix` abstracts microfluidic GEM encapsulation; not a bulk mixing step.

steps.name: Reverse transcription and cell barcoding in droplets
steps.notes: Aspirate 100 uL emulsion into PCR tube post-generation. Both barcoding and RT complete during incubation.

steps.name: Quench RT reaction and products cleanup
steps.cleanup_protocol: Dynabeads + SPRI beads per 10X Multiome user guide CG000338
steps.notes: Pipette mix gently after quenching agent addition before proceeding to cleanup.

steps.name: Pre-amplification
steps.modification: SPRI bead elution in 80 uL instead of 160 uL to concentrate tagmented fragments
steps.rationale: scCUT&Tag library complexity is lower than ATAC-seq; concentration maximises DNA library input

cycle_guidance.note: Adjust based on sample type and estimated recovered nuclei

steps.storage: Pre-amplified product stable at -20 C for up to 6 months

steps.name: DNA and RNA library preparation

input_split.note: Water added to RNA input to maintain same total volume as standard 10X Multiome protocol

steps.notes: DNA and RNA library preps run independently. Encoded as single representative SPRI cleanup in BioScript.

fail.action: drain(finalLibrary) [drain normalises to dispose in IR]
fail.notes: Re-evaluate PCR cycle number or nuclei input; check complexity

compiler_notes.duration_unit_convention: BioScript supports s and m only (no h). All durations converted to minutes.
compiler_notes.drain_normalisation: drain in .bs normalises to dispose in IR output; consistent with reference protocols
compiler_notes.buffer_rebuild_note: BioScript dispense is restricted to declared manifests. Buffers needed at multiple sites (MED1 x3, MED2 x3) are each rebuilt from manifests independently using prefixed variable names (m1a_, m1b_, m1c_, m2a_, m2b_, m2c_).

description:
PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : A Digital Microfluidic Method for in Situ Formation of Porous Polymer Monoliths with Application to Solid-Phase Extraction
Source Link  : https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/Yang_2011_A%20Digital%20Microfluidic%20Method%20for%20in%20Situ%20Formation%20of%20Porous%20Polymer%20Monoliths%20with%20Application%20to%20Solid-Phase%20Extraction_Small.pdf
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1021/ac2002388
Journal      : Analytical Chemistry, 2011, Vol. 83, pp. 3824-3830
Platform     : Digital microfluidics (DMF) with in situ UV-polymerized porous polymer monolith (PPM) discs on EWOD electrode array


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes the first combination of digital microfluidics (DMF) and porous polymer
monoliths (PPMs) for on-chip solid-phase extraction (SPE). Circular PPM discs (radius ~1 mm,
height 270 um) are formed in situ on a DMF device by dispensing 1 uL droplets of a C12 monomer
casting solution onto the actuation electrode array, translating them to a designated position,
and polymerizing by UV irradiation (100 W, 365 nm, 5 min). The resulting DMF-SPE method performs
all fluid handling steps -- activation, equilibration, sample loading, washing, and elution --
using microliter droplets manipulated by electrostatic forces on the electrode array.

The protocol is divided into three functional phases encoded in BioScript:
  1. In situ PPM disc formation by UV-initiated photopolymerization (Protocol 1)
  2. Standard four-step DMF-SPE validated against commercial C18 ZipTips (Protocol 2)
  3. Preparative sample cleanup: desalting (Protocol 3a) and surfactant removal (Protocol 3b),
     both validated by off-chip nanoESI-MS detection of angiotensin II at m/z 1047


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Design 1 (Standard SPE device -- Protocols 2 and 3):
  Bottom plate : Patterned chromium electrodes on glass; 88 actuation electrodes (2.2 x 2.2 mm
                 each) + 10 reservoir electrodes (5 x 5 mm each); interelectrode gap 40 um.
                 Coated with 7 um Parylene-C + 50 nm Teflon-AF.
  Top plate    : Unpatterned ITO-glass; Teflon-AF 50 nm coating.
  Spacer       : Three pieces double-sided tape; total thickness 270 um.
  Unit droplet : 1 uL (one 2.2 x 2.2 mm electrode footprint x 270 um height).
  Reservoirs   : Elution solvent, Sample, Monomer (C12), Wash solvent, Activation solvent.

Design 2 (Concentration device -- Protocol 4; preliminary):
  Large electrodes  : 12 x (7.5 x 7.5 mm); unit droplet 12 uL; for sample, activation, wash.
  Small electrodes  : 19 x (2.2 x 2.2 mm); unit droplet 1 uL; for elution solvent and monomer.
  Purpose           : Concentrate large sample volume into a small elution droplet (~9-fold).

Actuation signal : 220-300 V_pp, 18 kHz; amplified output of Agilent function generator.
Fabrication      : University of Toronto ECTI cleanroom; photolithography + chromium etching;
                   Parylene-C by vapour deposition (Specialty Coating Systems);
                   Teflon-AF spin-coated at 1000 rpm 30 s, post-baked 160 C 10 min.


PPM DISC CHARACTERIZATION
--------------------------
Formation     : 1 uL C12 casting solution dispensed, driven to centre electrode position,
                UV-polymerized (100 W, 365 nm, 5 min).
Disc geometry : Radius ~1 mm, height 270 um (equal to device spacer thickness).
Morphology    : Skin-like outer layer; popcorn-like porous interior (SEM, Hitachi S-5200).
Surface area  : 3.7 +/- 0.2 m2/g by BET N2 adsorption (comparable to capillary-formed PPMs).
Reproducibility: Coefficient of variation in disc diameter = 10% (n=5 devices).
Passive dispensing: <10% of droplet volume remains on monolith during actuation;
                >90% of droplet continues moving. PPM not covalently bound to device surface;
                removable/replaceable with tweezers when device is disassembled.


REAGENTS
--------
C12 casting solution (prepared within 3 days of use):
  Butyl acrylate              279 uL
  1,3-Butanediol diacrylate   150 uL
  Lauryl acrylate              69 uL
  Photoinitiator               2.5 mg 2,2-dimethoxy-2-phenylacetophenone
  Porogen                      1 mL (4:1:1 acetonitrile / 95% EtOH / 5 mM phosphate pH 6.8)

SPE solvents:
  Activation                  0.1% v/v formic acid in acetonitrile
  Equilibration               0.5% v/v formic acid in deionized water
  Wash                        0.5% v/v formic acid in deionized water
  Elution (peptides)          0.1% v/v formic acid in acetonitrile
  Elution (fluorescein QC)    500 mM sodium borate in deionized water, pH 9.0

Model analytes:
  Fluorescein                 5 uM in 0.5% v/v aqueous FA (loading time / elution volume QC)
  Angiotensin IV (labeled)    10 uM fluorescamine-labeled angiotensin IV in 0.1% FA (efficiency)
  Angiotensin II + NaCl       1 uM Ang II in 100 mM NaCl (desalting validation)
  Angiotensin II + Pluronic   1 uM Ang II in 0.05% w/v Pluronic F68 (surfactant removal)

Fluorescamine labeling: 100 uL fluorescamine (3 mg/mL in acetone) + 10 uL Ang IV
  (10 mM in 10 mM borate pH 9) + 890 uL acetone; incubate >=2 h; dilute 10x with 0.1% FA.
Deionized water: 18 MOhm cm at 25 C; filtered 0.2 um nylon; sonicated 5 min.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | In Situ PPM Disc Formation  [Protocol 1]
  Reagent    : C12 casting solution (1 uL unit droplet)
  Operation  : Dispense from monomer reservoir -> translate to centre electrode position
               (electrode actuation, 220-300 V_pp, 18 kHz) -> UV polymerize.
  UV params  : 100 W lamp, 365 nm, 5 min exposure.
  Result     : Circular PPM disc; radius ~1 mm, height 270 um, SSA 3.7 +/- 0.2 m2/g.
  BioScript  : Second MonomersC12 dispense used as required second operand for mix (translation);
               heat at 25c for 5m abstracts UV exposure (no UV primitive in compiler).
  Repeated   : Three independent discs formed (disc1, disc2, disc3) for Protocols 2, 3a, 3b.

Step 2 | PPM Activation  [Protocol 2, Step 1a]
  Reagent    : Activation solvent (0.1% v/v FA in ACN); 5 uL.
  Operation  : Dispense -> actuate 5x across PPM disc -> incubate 1 min -> move to waste.
  BioScript  : mix for 1m; dispose activationSolvent.
  Purpose    : Conditions C12 stationary phase for reversed-phase SPE.

Step 3 | PPM Equilibration  [Protocol 2, Step 1b]
  Reagent    : Equilibration solvent (0.5% v/v FA in H2O); 5 uL.
  Operation  : Dispense -> actuate 5x across PPM disc -> incubate 1 min -> move to waste.
  BioScript  : mix for 1m; dispose equilibrationSolvent.

Step 4 | Sample Loading  [Protocol 2, Step 2]
  Reagent    : Fluorescamine-labeled angiotensin IV (10 uM in 0.1% FA); 1 uL.
  Operation  : Dispense -> actuate 5x across PPM disc -> incubate -> move to waste.
  Incubation : 2 min (optimized; Fig. 3a: <20% fluorescence remains in droplet;
               p = 0.30 for 2 vs 4 min -- not significant; 2 min selected for all experiments).
  BioScript  : mix for 2m; dispose peptideSample.

Step 5 | PPM Washing  [Protocol 2, Step 3]
  Reagent    : Wash solvent (0.5% v/v FA in H2O); 2 x 5 uL.
  Operation  : Each droplet dispensed, actuated 5x across PPM disc, moved to waste.
  BioScript  : 2 x (dispense; mix for 30s; dispose washSolvent).
  Purpose    : Removes unbound matrix while retaining analyte on C12 stationary phase.

Step 6 | Analyte Elution  [Protocol 2, Step 4]
  Reagent    : Elution solvent (0.1% v/v FA in ACN for peptides; borate pH 9.0 for fluorescein);
               2 x 5 uL; pooled at sample collection reservoir.
  Operation  : Each droplet dispensed, actuated 5x across PPM disc, moved to collector.
  Incubation : Optimized to 2 elution droplets (Fig. 3b: >90% extracted; p = 0.25 for 2 vs 3
               droplets -- not significant; 2 droplets selected for all experiments).
  Detection  : Plate reader fluorescence (ex 390/em 460 nm peptide; ex 480/em 520 nm fluorescein).
  BioScript  : 2 x (dispense; mix for 30s); detect speExtractionDetection for 30s.
  Branch     : speSignal > 0 -> dispose (BB2); speSignal <= 0 -> drain (BB3).

Step 7 | Preparative DMF-SPE: Desalting  [Protocol 3a]
  Fresh disc : disc2 formed independently (FIX #2: disc1 consumed by Protocol 2).
  Sample     : Ang II 1 uM in 100 mM NaCl; 1 uL.
  Procedure  : Same 4-step DMF-SPE as Protocol 2 (Steps 2-6 above); 2 min loading; 2 elutions.
  Problem    : 100 mM NaCl suppresses nanoESI signal; [M+H]+ at m/z 1047 absent without SPE.
  Result     : Strong [M+H]+ signal at m/z 1047 after DMF-SPE (Fig. 4a).
  Analysis   : Off-chip nanoESI-MS (LTQ Finnigan); spray 1.7-2.0 kV; flow 0.5 uL/min;
               capillary temp 200 C. Eluate resolubilized in 50 uL 50% ACN / 0.1% FA.
  Branch     : desaltSignal > 0 -> dispose (BB5); desaltSignal <= 0 -> drain (BB6).

Step 8 | Preparative DMF-SPE: Surfactant Removal  [Protocol 3b]
  Fresh disc : disc3 formed independently (FIX #2: disc2 consumed by Protocol 3a).
  Sample     : Ang II 1 uM in 0.05% w/v Pluronic F68; 1 uL.
  Context    : Pluronic F68 is standard DMF additive to prevent protein/peptide adsorption to
               Teflon-AF device surfaces (used as 0.05% w/v), but is a strong nanoESI ion
               suppressor; removal prior to MS analysis is critical.
  Procedure  : Same 4-step DMF-SPE as Protocol 2; 2 min loading; 2 elutions.
  Problem    : 0.05% Pluronic F68 suppresses [M+H]+ at m/z 1047 without SPE.
  Result     : Strong [M+H]+ signal at m/z 1047 after DMF-SPE (Fig. 4b).
  Analysis   : Off-chip nanoESI-MS (same conditions as desalting).
  Branch     : surfactantSignal > 0 -> dispose (BB8); surfactantSignal <= 0 -> drain (BB9).


SPE PERFORMANCE SUMMARY
-----------------------
Extraction efficiency (fluorescamine-labeled Ang IV):
  DMF-SPE (C12 PPM)  : 93 +/- 14%  (n=3)
  ZipTip (C18)       : 92 +/- 5%   (n=3)
  Conclusion         : Comparable; no significant difference.

Concentration factor (fluorescein; preliminary; Design 2 device):
  Expected : ~12x (12 uL sample / 1 uL elution)
  Achieved : ~9x
  Range    : Within ZipTip commercial range of 2.5-10x.


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file : yang_2011_dmf_spe_ppm.bs
Compiler       : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output      : 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
DAG file       : yang_2011_dmf_spe_ppm_main_dag.dot
Duration units : BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported.

Duration conversions:
  UV polymerization        5 min   -> 5m   (IR: 300.0 SECOND)
  Activation/equilibration 1 min   -> 1m   (IR: 60.0 SECOND)
  Sample loading           2 min   -> 2m   (IR: 120.0 SECOND)
  Wash / elution           30 s    -> 30s  (IR: 30.0 SECOND)
  Translation mix          10 s    -> 10s  (IR: 10.0 SECOND)

FIX #1 -- heat is void in lilott8/BioScript:
  `heat var at Tc for Td` mutates var in place and returns nothing.
  Original error: UndefinedVariable -- main.ppmDisc is not defined.
  Original code:  heat centredDroplet at 25c for 5m
                  ppmDisc = centredDroplet   <- INVALID
  Fix: centredDroplet / disc2 / disc3 used directly after heat; no alias assigned.

FIX #2 -- each SPE protocol consumes its PPM disc:
  Protocol 2 drives solvents and sample through centredDroplet via sequential mix ops,
  leaving it consumed. Protocols 3a and 3b each form their own independent fresh disc:
    Protocol 2  : centredDroplet  (monomer1a + monomer1b)
    Protocol 3a : disc2           (monomer2a + monomer2b)
    Protocol 3b : disc3           (monomer3a + monomer3b)

mix two-operand constraint:
  BioScript mix requires exactly two operands. The PPM translation step (physical droplet
  movement with no second reagent) uses a second dispense of MonomersC12 as the required
  second operand; same reagent composition, no chemical change introduced.

Modules   : speExtractionDetection, fluorescenceDetection, massSpecDetection
Manifests : ActivationSolvent, EquilibrationSolvent, WashSolvent, ElutionSolvent,
            MonomersC12, FluoresceinSample, PeptideSample,
            AngiotensinII_NaCl, AngiotensinII_Pluronic, PluronicF68
